Title: yieldsApp: Digital Agronomy for Inclusive and Resilient Food Systems
Subtitle: AI-powered agronomy platform enabling farmers and cooperatives to boost yields, ensure compliance, and build resilient, inclusive food supply chains.
Problem Statement: Despite producing much of the world’s food, smallholder farmers and cooperatives remain among the most excluded from the digital economy. Women, youth, and rural communities often lack access to agronomic knowledge, digital tools, and transparent markets. Without connection to global and local agronomic research, farmers rely on guesswork or outdated practices, leading to reduced yields, inefficient fertilizer and pesticide use, and soil degradation. At the same time, they face increasing difficulty complying with stricter regulations and meeting the quality standards demanded by food companies and governments. The result is unstable incomes for farmers, widening inequality, and unpredictable supply for industries. In the face of climate change and growing demand for sustainable production, the absence of inclusive digital solutions threatens both livelihoods and the resilience of global food systems.
Solution Overview:
Solution Overview

yieldsApp is a digital agronomy solution that bridges the gap between farmers and advanced agricultural knowledge. It combines a farmer-friendly mobile app with a data-driven platform for organizations such as food and beverage companies, governments, NGOs and extension services. The solution makes sophisticated science and data accessible to smallholder farmers while providing organizations with the tools to ensure compliance, traceability, and supply chain resilience.

How it Works

For farmers: The mobile app delivers clear, step-by-step guidance. Farmers enter basic information about their fields and crops. yieldsApp then processes information such as soil data, weather conditions, satellite imagery, field observations and agronomic knowledge. AI models analyze these inputs with agronomic expertise to generate precise advice, such as:

Which fertilizers to apply, when, and in what amounts.

What to spray and when to control pests and diseases.

When to plant for optimal growth and yield.

When and how much to irrigate to save water and maximize production.

It also provides early warning alerts for pest and disease risks, helps farmers to identify issues in their fields (image recognition, in combination with agronomic models), all before they cause yield loss.

This transforms complex data into straightforward instructions that farmers can act on immediately, without needing to interpret the underlying science. The app also records fertilizer and pesticide use, enabling farmers to comply with local and international regulations and improve their market positioning. 

For organizations: The platform aggregates and analyzes farm-level data at scale. AI-driven analytics provide yield forecasts, compliance monitoring, and supply chain transparency. This enables food and beverage companies to secure predictable and sustainable sourcing. NGOs and extension services can support smallholder inclusion. Governments can track regulatory compliance and strengthen sustainable agriculture policies.

Methodologies and Technologies Used

Artificial Intelligence and agronomic modeling for yield forecasting, fertilizer optimization, irrigation scheduling, pest and disease risk management and treatment.

Integration of soil data, satellite imagery, weather records, and field observations into actionable insights. Adaptive agronomic protocols that evolve with changing field conditions, connecting global research with local farmer realities.

Traceability and compliance tools that align farm practices with regulations and sustainability standards.


Partnerships and Collaboration Models

Farmers and cooperatives: Can use the mobile app with localized agronomy support.

Food and beverage companies: Using the platform to achieve transparent supply chains and sustainability reporting.

NGOs and development agencies: In Africa, yieldsApp supports programs that include smallholder farmers, particularly women and youth.

Governments and international organizations: For example, projects in the Philippines with the World Bank and national government strengthen adoption of digital agriculture.

Research institutions: Collaborating to ensure that agronomic knowledge is effectively translated into practical recommendations.

Impact
yieldsApp combines a farmer-friendly app with a powerful platform for organizations to create an inclusive digital ecosystem that:

Increases farmer yields by closing the gap between local practices and global agronomic knowledge.

Reduces fertilizer use by 20-45% in certain crops, cutting costs for farmers and lowering environmental impact.

Helps farmers comply with pesticide and fertilizer regulations through built-in recording and traceability tools.

Provides supply chain transparency and predictability for food and beverage companies.

Supports governments in advancing sustainability goals, empowering women and youth, and strengthening the resilience of global food systems.
Solution Provider(s): yieldsApp Ltd. – An stable agritech company specializing in AI-powered crop management. yieldsApp provides a digital agronomy solution that empowers farmers through a simple mobile app and enables organizations such as food and beverage companies, governments, and NGOs to access a powerful platform for compliance, transparency, and supply chain resilience. Sector: Agriculture Technology / Digital Agriculture
Implementation location(s): Solution Implementation Locations The solution has already been implemented in multiple regions worldwide, including:  Latin America: Mexico (barley, vegetables), Guatemala (sugarcane), Brazil (coffee, avocado).  Africa: Ethiopia, Rwanda, Ghana (beans, barley, rice, flowers, vegetables).  Europe: France, Finland, Netherlands, Central and Eastern Europe (barley, sunflower, canola, potatoes, oats, vegetables).  North America: United States, Canada (wheat, oats, corn, vegetables, berries).  Asia: Philippines (rice, banana, vegetables, with government and World Bank support), Israel.  Oceania: Australia (vineyards).
Implementation timeline(s): Initial deployments began in 2019 with farmers and cooperatives in Latin America and North America.  Expanded to Africa (Ethiopia, Ghana) in 2020–2021, in collaboration with NGOs and development agencies.  Implementation in Europe (France, Finland, Netherlands, Central and Eastern Europe) began in 2021–2022, focusing on barley, sunflower, potatoes, and vegetables.  Adoption in North America (United States, Canada) started in 2019e , with corn, wheat, oats, and vegetables.  Projects in Asia (Philippines, Israel) initiated in 2023, including collaborations with the World Bank and government partners.  Ongoing deployments continue through 2025, with active farmer usage and expansion across multiple regions.
Duration to pilot in a new geography: 4-8 months
SDGs addressed: SDG 2 (Zero Hunger);SDG 12 (Responsible Consumption and Production);SDG 13 (Climate Action);
Desired impact:
Solution Objectives

Empower smallholder farmers and cooperatives with easy access to digital agronomy, enabling them to increase yields, reduce costs, and comply with agricultural regulations.

Strengthen food security and resilience by making supply chains more predictable and transparent for food and beverage companies, governments, and NGOs.

Promote sustainable production through efficient use of fertilizers, pesticides, and water, reducing environmental impact while supporting farmer livelihoods.

Key Achievements and Impacts

Yield increase: In barley, corn, and sunflower projects, yields improved while achieving quality targets for food and beverage supply chains.

Resource efficiency: Fertilizer use reduced by 20–45% across multiple geographies, cutting costs for farmers and lowering greenhouse gas emissions from fertilizer production and use.

Compliance and traceability: Farmers supported in complying with pesticide and fertilizer regulations, ensuring food safety and alignment with sustainability standards.

Supply chain resilience: Food and beverage companies gained more reliable sourcing through yield forecasting and transparent farm-level data.

Inclusion and empowerment: Thousands of farmers, including women and youth in Africa and Latin America, accessed digital agronomy for the first time.

Climate impact: More efficient fertilizer use, improved irrigation practices, and reduced input waste contribute to lower greenhouse gas emissions and enhanced resilience of farming systems to climate variability.
Key technologies:
Key Technologies

Artificial Intelligence (AI) and Machine Learning
Used to analyze diverse data sources (soil, satellite, weather, field observations) and generate dynamic, field-specific agronomic protocols. AI also supports yield forecasting, irrigation scheduling, nutrient optimization, and early detection of pest and disease risks.

Remote Sensing and Satellite Imagery
Integrated into the platform to provide insights on crop health, growth monitoring, and stress detection. Farmers do not need to interpret imagery themselves; AI models process the data and deliver straightforward recommendations.

Cloud-Based Digital Platform
Provides scalability, secure data management, and accessibility for farmers through a mobile app and for organizations through a web-based platform. Supports data aggregation for supply chain transparency, compliance monitoring, and program evaluation.

Mobile Application
Designed for ease of use by farmers, including those in low-resource settings. Translates complex data into simple, actionable instructions such as which fertilizers to apply, when and how much to irrigate, and what to spray and when.

Data Integration Interfaces
Capable of connecting with external systems such as farm machinery platforms (e.g., John Deere Operations Center) and weather stations, enabling more advanced implementations where infrastructure exists.
Unique Characteristics:
Unique and Differentiated Characteristics

AI-Driven Agronomy Engine
At the core of yieldsApp is an artificial intelligence engine that integrates soil data, weather, satellite imagery, and field observations. The system translates these inputs into dynamic, field-specific protocols for fertilization, irrigation, planting, and crop protection that adapt continuously to changing conditions.

From Complex Data to Simple Actions
Unlike IoT-heavy or sensor-dependent solutions, yieldsApp requires no specialized equipment. Farmers do not need to interpret datasets or imagery; the platform automatically processes data and provides direct, actionable guidance such as which fertilizers to apply and when, what to spray and when, when to irrigate, and when to plant.

Dual-Layer Architecture (App + Platform)

Mobile App: Delivers actionable, easy-to-understand recommendations directly to farmers, including smallholders with limited digital literacy.

Cloud Platform: Enables food and beverage companies, NGOs, and governments to access aggregated analytics, compliance monitoring, yield forecasting, and supply chain transparency.

Adaptive Agronomic Knowledge Base
yieldsApp combines machine learning with agronomic expertise, creating a continuously improving system that connects global research with local farmer realities. The protocols are not static but evolve with data feedback, ensuring relevance in diverse geographies.

Integrated Traceability and Compliance
Beyond recommendations, yieldsApp records pesticide and fertilizer use to support compliance with regulations and sustainability standards. This provides reliable digital traceability for both governments and food companies.

Ecosystem and Partnership Integration
yieldsApp is not a standalone tool. It is implemented in collaboration with farmer cooperatives, food and beverage companies, NGOs, governments, and international organizations. This creates a reinforcing ecosystem where farmers improve productivity and incomes, companies secure stable sourcing, and governments advance sustainability goals.

Proven Scalability Across Regions
Already deployed in Latin America, Africa, Europe, North America, and Asia, yieldsApp has demonstrated scalability across both advanced and low-resource farming systems. Its cloud-based architecture and modular integrations allow rapid adoption without the need for hardware investment.
Sustainable Change:
yieldsApp does more than improve yields or reduce fertilizer use. It creates the foundation for long-term transformation in agriculture by embedding digital agronomy into the way farmers, companies, governments, and NGOs interact.

System-Level Shifts

Digital inclusion: Smallholder farmers, often excluded from the digital economy, gain access to advanced AI-driven agronomy in a simple mobile format.

Compliance culture: Recording and traceability tools make regulatory compliance the norm, supporting safer food systems and stronger agricultural governance.

Supply chain resilience: With transparent, predictable data, food and beverage companies can plan sourcing more sustainably, reducing disruptions.

Policy innovation: Aggregated platform data supports governments in designing evidence-based agricultural policies and monitoring progress toward SDGs.

Follow-On Effects

A self-sustaining ecosystem emerges where farmers improve income and sustainability, companies gain stable supply, and governments and NGOs advance food security goals.

Knowledge-sharing accelerates: best practices and agronomic models spread across regions, adapted continuously through AI.

Over time, agriculture shifts toward responsible production and climate resilience, reducing the environmental footprint while strengthening food security worldwide.
Funding Sources: yieldsApp has been entirely bootstrapped by its founders and has grown into a profitable business through revenues from farmers, cooperatives, food and beverage companies, and partnerships with  governments and financial institutions. The solution has not relied on external investment or donor funding, which demonstrates its financial sustainability and market-driven scalability.
Testimonials and Endorsements:
Winner of the Burgundy–Israel AgriFood Challenge, recognized for advancing sustainable crop management through AI-powered agronomy.

First place in the Innovation4Morocco Challenge, highlighting yieldsApp as a leading digital agriculture solution in North Africa.

Winner of the OTP Bank Challenge (Hungary), endorsing yieldsApp as a scalable tool for digital inclusion in agriculture and food supply chains.

Recipient of a JDC grant in Ethiopia (Pears project), supporting smallholder farmers with digital agronomy tools for improved yields and sustainability.

Selected by the World Bank to participate in a digital agriculture project in the Philippines, in partnership with the national government, strengthening sustainable production and farmer inclusion.

Featured in international agtech publications such as CropLife and Ineda, cited as one of the best agriculture apps and an innovative partner in climate-smart farming.
Primary thematic focus area: Stable and Resilient Digital Supply Chains
Summary: yieldsApp is a fully implemented, AI-powered digital agronomy platform that bridges the gap between smallholder farmers and advanced agricultural knowledge. It combines a mobile app for farmers with a data platform for organizations, enabling yield optimization, compliance tracking, and supply chain transparency. Already deployed across Latin America, Africa, Europe, North America, Asia, and Oceania, the solution has demonstrated scalability and financial sustainability. Recognized internationally, it empowers farmers—especially women and youth—while helping companies and governments ensure resilient, sustainable food systems.

Title: AI for Her: Transforming Telemedicine Training & Support for Female Providers
Subtitle: Transforming healthcare for underserved communities by equipping female doctors and nurses with AI-powered training & diagnostic tools,while enhancing patient experience through an AI assistant embedded within the Sehat Kahani telemedicine platform.
Problem Statement:
Training and Participation Barrier:

Despite women comprising nearly half of Pakistan's registered medical doctors, around 46.9% (127,468 out of 271,560) (PMC), a striking 35% of female medical graduates are either unemployed or not practicing, equating to over 36,000 qualified physicians (The Nation Business Recorder).
This disconnect between qualification and practice arises from a complex mix of socio-cultural constraints, workplace barriers, and structural inflexibilities that disproportionately affect women. A study reports that 50% of female graduates either never practiced or left the profession shortly after graduation( PMC) The result? A massive under-utilization of public investment, as taxpayers fund education only to see these skilled professionals sidelined, deepening healthcare workforce shortages, especially where they are needed most.

Access and Infrastructure Barrier:

Moreover, in rural Pakistan, healthcare access remains alarmingly sparse. Although the national doctor-to-patient ratio stands at 1:1,300, already worse than the WHO-recommended 1:1,000, rural areas face an even worse picture where the shortage is more acute (pma.org.pk). Rural residents lack stable internet, smartphones, or electricity which are the key components for telemedicine success  (jpma.org.pk).
In today’s era where healthcare can be delivered anywhere and anytime in seconds, these women are held back by outdated systems, while patients in remote areas continue to suffer from preventable illnesses. With the right tools, these professionals can initiate a new era of easily accessible, high-quality healthcare.
Solution Overview:
Introduction of Sehat Kahani

Sehat Kahani is Pakistan’s leading telemedicine platform, redefining healthcare as a universal right. It connects patients nationwide to quality care through two core verticals: a mobile application and e-health clinics.

Telemedicine Platforms
The Sehat Kahani Mobile Application, on Android and iOS, offers remote consultations, prescriptions, and health tracking. Its B2C model runs on a pay-as-you-go basis, while the B2B model partners with corporates and insurers via annual retainers, providing unlimited consultations, counseling, diagnostics, claims support, and medicine delivery for employees and their families.

E-Health Clinics bring care to underserved communities. Supported by nurse intermediaries and diagnostic e-tools, they connect patients to a network of 7,500 licensed doctors, including specialists in maternal health, mental health, and chronic diseases. Consultations start within 60 seconds, with instant prescriptions and same-day medicine delivery in major cities. At an average cost of USD 0.40 per consult, Sehat Kahani reduces household healthcare spending by up to 80%.

AI-Embedded Training for HER
To strengthen healthcare delivery, Sehat Kahani is launching an AI-powered training system for female doctors, nurses, and providers. It addresses barriers to continuous learning with modules on:

Soft Skills & Interaction: AI roleplay enhances empathy and communication.

Medical Knowledge: Refresher modules on diagnostics, prescribing, maternal and child health, and NCD management.

Telemedicine Training: Covers digital etiquette, remote workflows, safe documentation, and referrals.

Features include adaptive learning, AI-simulated patients, real-time copilots, personalized dashboards, offline compatibility, and governance ensuring human oversight.

Dual AI Interface
Sehat Kahani integrates a dual AI interface to enhance patient and provider experiences:

Patient Assistant: Collects symptoms, guides triage, automates scheduling, sends reminders, and delivers follow-up care 24/7.

Provider Copilot: Automates SOAP notes, drafts prescriptions, suggests differential diagnoses, manages referrals, and supports multilingual consultations.

Methodology & Learning Approach
Training is delivered fully online or in blended formats at e-clinics, supported by local nurses. Optimized for low-bandwidth environments, the system provides offline access, adaptive streaming, and AI-driven learning.

Modules use virtual patient simulations and real-world case studies reflecting Pakistan’s underserved areas, focusing on maternal complications, infectious diseases, and NCDs. Dashboards track diagnostic accuracy and communication skills, aligning with WHO and national health standards.

This approach equips providers with clinical, technical, and operational skills for quality telemedicine in fragile contexts while creating a scalable model for nationwide adoption.

Technology Stack

Patient App (Android/iOS): Registration, consultations, prescriptions, and records.

Doctor App (Android/iOS): Manage consults and prescriptions.

Web Frontend (Angular): Responsive browser-based access.

Backend: Koa.js (Node.js) with MySQL and Sequelize ORM.

Integrations: Vonage (video), PubNub (messaging), SendGrid (email), Power BI (analytics).

Infrastructure: Microsoft Azure hosting, encryption, and compliance with data security standards.

Partnerships
Sehat Kahani partners with nursing and physician associations, NGOs, universities, and government agencies. Key collaborators include Ziauddin University, AKU-CIME, Google for AI, Boston Health, PMDC, APPNE, APPNA, and the Federal Ministry of Health.
Solution Provider(s): Google for AI - partner for building AI assisted Patient and physician Assistant  (https://www.linkedin.com/in/esnaong/), Zetsol Consultant (https://www.linkedin.com/in/aftab-saraz-ba69a25b/)
Duration to pilot in a new geography: 1 year
SDGs addressed: SDG 10 (Reduced Inequalities);SDG 3 (Good Health and Well-being);SDG 4 (Quality Education);
Desired impact:
Objectives

Equip female nurses and healthcare providers with telemedicine and AI-assisted skills
Deliver AI-powered training modules for nurses, doctors, and allied health professionals, enabling them to provide remote consultations, use AI diagnostic tools, interpret insights, and integrate them into care workflows. This enhances professional competence, consultation quality, and evidence-based decision-making in virtual settings.

Increase women’s participation in the digital health workforce
Offer accessible learning and flexible work opportunities to qualified but underutilized female healthcare professionals, especially those unable to work in traditional settings. AI-assisted telemedicine roles empower women to re-enter or expand their healthcare careers, achieve financial independence, and contribute to the national health system from home or community hubs.

Improve healthcare access and reduce wait times through AI triage
Integrate AI triage to rapidly analyze symptoms, prioritize urgent cases, and route patients to the right provider. This reduces bottlenecks, prevents unnecessary referrals, and ensures timely care in underserved communities.

Key Achievements & Impacts
Sehat Kahani has reactivated 7,500+ female doctors (85% of its active network) and trained 500+ nurses and allied staff in telemedicine and AI-assisted decision-making. Over 120 nurse intermediaries now serve their own communities, creating trusted access points and boosting women’s role in Pakistan’s digital health sector.

This workforce model has increased consultations delivered by women by 40%, raised nurse intermediary incomes by 45%, and enabled female doctors to earn USD 500–700/month remotely.

The platform operates 65 e-clinics and a mobile app across 317+ cities, including remote tier 3–4 areas. Corporate partnerships with 1,100+ employers extend coverage to 7 million employees and dependents. Since launch, Sehat Kahani has delivered 4+ million consultations, including 1.4 million in 2024, with 65% resolved at first contact—avoiding referrals and treatment delays. Chronic disease follow-ups account for one-third of e-clinic visits, while repeat consultation within six months is 65%, reflecting high trust. Internal audits show 90%+ diagnostic accuracy, matching in-person care.

Preventive health education has reached 6 million people (500,000 in 2024). AI triage has reduced wait times by 25%, connecting patients to doctors in under 60 seconds and enabling same-day prescriptions. Consultations cost USD 0.40, up to 80% cheaper than private GP visits, driving affordability and access.

The model also delivers environmental and social benefits: avoiding 8 million km of travel, preventing 2,400 metric tons of CO₂ emissions, and saving 2 million sheets of paper annually through digital records.

Adoption is strong—60% of app users are first-time digital healthcare users. In new cities, platform adoption reaches 20% of the target population within a year, with 70% retention at 12 months.

Looking ahead, scaling plans aim for 124 e-clinics, 3.5 million consultations annually, and 16 million beneficiaries by 2027, building a gender-inclusive, AI-enabled, community-anchored healthcare system replicable across low- and middle-income and humanitarian settings.
Key technologies: We use AI for adaptive learning, triage, and diagnosis support; a secure telemedicine platform (mobile and web) for video consultations, prescriptions, and health records; cloud-based dashboards for training and performance tracking; IoT diagnostic devices for remote exams; and multilingual, low-bandwidth design to ensure access in underserved areas. All services are hosted on Microsoft Azure with end-to-end encryption for data security.
Unique Characteristics:
Sehat Kahani operates a fully integrated telemedicine ecosystem designed for scale, resilience, and inclusive economic participation. The model unites a secure, AI-enabled digital platform with a nationwide network of permanent e-clinics embedded in rural, peri-urban, and humanitarian communities. Each e-clinic is managed by a locally trained nurse intermediary who serves as the physical point of care, bridging digital literacy gaps, ensuring cultural trust, and enabling on-site diagnostics. This hybrid architecture allows the platform to serve populations with limited connectivity, low literacy, and restricted mobility, reaching groups that traditional digital health models fail to access.
The technical infrastructure is optimised for resource-constrained environments. The platform supports low-bandwidth operation with adaptive video compression and offline functionality, ensuring uninterrupted service in areas with unstable networks. Interoperable electronic medical records allow a patient’s health history to be accessed across all e-clinics and mobile consultations, maintaining continuity of care and clinical safety. IoT-enabled diagnostic devices, including digital stethoscopes, ultrasound probes, and vitals monitors, transmit data instantly to remote physicians for interpretation. AI is embedded into both patient and provider interfaces. Patients receive real-time symptom triage, plain-language medical summaries, and personalised health education in multiple local languages. Providers access AI-assisted differential diagnosis, treatment recommendations, and integrated continuous medical education modules that improve competencies while they work.
The workforce model addresses Pakistan’s gender and labour market challenges. Sehat Kahani has reactivated one of the largest pools of highly qualified but inactive female doctors, overcoming geographic, cultural, and safety barriers that once prevented them from practising. Doctors operate remotely through the platform, supported by nurse intermediaries from the same communities as the patients they serve. This creates gender-concordant care pathways in conservative regions and sustainable income streams for women. The model strengthens the health workforce while increasing women’s participation in the digital economy.
Service integration is a defining feature. Patients can complete the full care cycle including consultation, diagnostics, prescriptions, and medicine delivery within their own community. Embedded e-pharmacy and e-laboratory services eliminate the need for long-distance travel to urban centres, while the interoperable system ensures data from each step is linked to the patient’s record. E-clinics also function as community health hubs, hosting vaccination drives, awareness campaigns, and outbreak responses. Preventive care and chronic disease management are embedded into routine service delivery, decentralising functions that would otherwise depend on centralised hospitals.
This combination of community-anchored infrastructure, AI-powered clinical support, interoperable data systems, IoT diagnostics, and gender-inclusive workforce mobilisation creates a healthcare service model with systemic transformation potential. It reduces pressure on higher-tier facilities, strengthens supply chains for medicines and diagnostics, and generates skilled employment in local economies. The model’s modular design and low operating costs make it directly replicable in other low- and middle-income countries and humanitarian contexts. It demonstrates how locally anchored, technology-enabled healthcare can build resilient, equitable, and economically integrated health systems.
Sustainable Change:
Pakistan’s health system faces structural constraints that limit both access and quality of care. Over 60 percent of the population lives in rural areas where there is less than one doctor per thousand people, and specialist services are concentrated in urban centres. Women represent the majority of medical graduates yet are disproportionately absent from the workforce due to mobility restrictions, safety concerns, and cultural expectations. Infrastructure deficits, unreliable connectivity, and overburdened secondary and tertiary facilities further widen the access gap. Addressing these issues requires a model that simultaneously strengthens the workforce, decentralises care delivery, and integrates technology into every layer of service provision.
Embedding AI into training and clinical workflows creates a direct pathway to build capacity at scale. Adaptive learning modules allow nurses and doctors to acquire new skills without leaving their workstations, while AI-assisted decision support improves diagnostic accuracy, treatment selection, and adherence to clinical guidelines in real time. The same system generates anonymised performance data, enabling continuous quality monitoring and targeted skill upgrades across the network. This integration transforms service delivery from a static consultation model into a dynamic ecosystem where every patient encounter doubles as a training opportunity.
The workforce structure ensures that change is both inclusive and sustainable. Female doctors re-enter the profession through remote practice, delivering care to patients in over 300 cities and towns without leaving their homes. Community-based nurse intermediaries act as the bridge between patients and remote physicians, offering culturally trusted care, ensuring follow-up, and mentoring new recruits in both clinical and digital competencies. Over time, these locally rooted providers form an expanding mentorship chain that grows the system organically, reducing reliance on external recruitment drives.
System-level impact is achieved through decentralisation of services. Primary care, preventive health, and chronic disease management are shifted closer to where people live, alleviating the patient load on urban hospitals. Interoperable electronic health records and AI-driven triage ensure patients are directed to the appropriate level of care, reducing unnecessary referrals and shortening treatment timelines. IoT-enabled diagnostics provide on-the-spot testing that would otherwise require travel to distant labs, while integrated e-pharmacy services ensure timely access to medicines.
This approach creates a resilient digital healthcare infrastructure tailored to Pakistan’s realities. It absorbs the country’s geographic, cultural, and technological constraints into its design, making it effective in both stable and crisis conditions. As the network grows, it strengthens local economies through skilled employment, reduces financial and time burdens on households, and normalises women’s participation in the digital health workforce. The model’s combination of workforce reactivation, technology adaptation, and decentralised service delivery builds a platform for lasting systemic change that can be sustained and expanded without dependence on temporary funding cycles.

Title: Lesson Planning via WhatsApp for Public School Teachers
Subtitle: AI-powered tool delivering free, curriculum-aligned lesson plans to teachers, even in low-connectivity areas
Problem Statement:
In Brazil, public school teachers face enormous challenges that hinder student learning. Overworked and under-resourced, they often lack access to high-quality professional development and practical teaching tools. This results in a critical learning gap: 75% of Brazilian children are behind in reading, according to PIRLS (2021).
One major cause lies in teacher preparation. According to Brazil’s Higher Education Census (2020), 60% of teachers graduate from distance learning programs. Many of these programs are of low quality, offering limited focus on classroom practice. As a result, new teachers often enter the profession without the practical training and support they need, especially those working in underserved public schools.
Nova Escola tackles this systemic problem through a teacher-centered, technology-enabled approach. As a nonprofit, we provide Brazil’s educators with free, curriculum-aligned resources and tools, available online and via platforms like WhatsApp, to improve their daily practice. Our solutions are designed to save teachers time, enhance instructional quality, and respond directly to their real classroom challenges.
This work is grounded in research: investing in teachers is the most cost-effective way to improve education outcomes, according to the World Bank (2020). Moreover, 95% of Brazilian educators see professional development as essential to their careers, and teacher quality accounts for up to 60% of student learning outcomes (Instituto Península, 2023).
Nova Escola’s mission is to ensure that every teacher, no matter where they are, has the tools, knowledge, and support to help every student succeed. We are building the school that supports every public school teacher in Brazil.
Solution Overview:
Our solution delivers free, high-quality, curriculum-aligned lesson plans to public school teachers through WhatsApp, the most widely used messaging app in Brazil. Teachers simply message our WhatsApp number, and an AI-powered assistant guides them to select grade level, subject, and topic. The tool instantly generates a lesson plan aligned with Brazil’s national curriculum guidelines (BNCC), ready to use or adapt, even in low-connectivity environments.
The methodology combines curriculum expertise from our editorial team, co-created with experienced teachers, and AI integration to scale content delivery. All lesson plans are based on pedagogical best practices and inclusive education principles. By leveraging WhatsApp, we meet teachers where they already are, reducing barriers to technology adoption.
The technology stack integrates the WhatsApp Business API, AI language models, and a custom backend for managing and updating lesson plan content. This ensures the solution is scalable, low-cost, and adaptable to other contexts with national curriculum standards.
In 2025, our innovation was recognized by the Meta and Tools Competition awards, which will provide resources to evolve the tool by integrating it with a literacy assessment feature for early-grade teachers. We also partner with Instituto Ultra to deliver regionally tailored mathematics lesson plans via WhatsApp to teachers in São Luís, Maranhão.
Collaboration is at the core of the project. We work with educational organizations, foundations, and technology partners to develop content, ensure technical stability, and expand reach. Key partners include Fundação Lemann, OpenAI, Meta, the World Bank, Instituto Ultra, among others, who support us with funding, technology, and educational expertise.
Solution Provider(s): Fundação Lemann – Brazilian education foundation focused on improving public education, non-profit sector, OpenAI – AI research and deployment company, private sector, Meta – Global technology company and developer of WhatsApp, private sector, World Bank – International financial institution supporting education initiatives, multilateral sector, Instituto Ultra – Brazilian non-profit organization supporting regionalized education projects, non-profit sector
Implementation timeline(s): Apr 2024 – Foundation Nova Escola joined the Chat for GenAI Accelerator (OpenAI + Turn.io) and began exploring how generative AI could support public school teachers in Brazil.  Jun 2024 – First Breakthrough We presented our MVP: AI-generated lesson planning through WhatsApp at the Demo Day, powered by Turn.io as our official BSP. This validated both teacher demand and the feasibility of WhatsApp as a delivery channel.We won the competition.  Jul/Dec 2024 – Iteration & Learning We made significant evolutions to the MVP, refining the experience through ongoing conversations with teachers. We focused on reducing the time needed to generate lesson plans, tested sample outputs to validate the quality of the generated content, and iterated mainly on the user experience, covering onboarding, flow, and feedback. In addition, we conducted initial barrier studies in collaboration with the World Bank to better understand the systemic challenges teachers face when adopting new digital tools.  Feb 2025 – Launch (School Year Kickoff in Brazil) The solution was launched publicly to teachers at the start of the Brazilian school year, maximizing relevance and adoption as educators prepared for their new classes.  Currently Go-to-market phase, with ongoing refinement, expansion of features (adaptation to different learning levels, integration with assessments, regionalization, and didactic sequences), and growth of the teacher base.
Duration to pilot in a new geography: We estimate that piloting our solution in a new geography would take approximately 12 months. This timeframe allows us to (1) understand the specific context and needs of local teachers, (2) adapt lesson plans and resources to align with the national or regional curriculum, (3) test the solution with educators to ensure cultural and pedagogical relevance, and (4) provide a few months of real classroom use. This period is essential to evaluate engagement, measure impact, and gather feedback from teachers before scaling further.
SDGs addressed: SDG 4 (Quality Education);
Desired impact:
Nova Escola’s initiative, the Lesson Planner via WhatsApp, aims to transform the teaching experience and, consequently, student learning. The main beneficiaries, the public school teachers, are expected to experience a significant reduction in workload and greater agility in lesson planning. The tool improves the quality and relevance of materials, adapting them to the specific needs of each classroom, even in low-connectivity contexts.
The initiative has already shown concrete results: 90% of users state that the generated lesson plans can be directly applied in the classroom, validating their pedagogical quality, and 98.3% report saving time when preparing their lessons, confirming one of the most valued benefits by teachers.
It also promotes equitable access to quality teaching resources and supports managing heterogeneous classrooms with students of different ages and levels. In addition, it seeks to strengthen teachers’ confidence and agency by giving them more time and tools to focus on student interaction, personalize instruction, and foster engagement and learning.
Key technologies:
Our solution leverages generative AI, powered by OpenAI’s GPT-4o, and is delivered directly through WhatsApp via an official Business Solution Provider (BSP). This integration allows teachers to interact naturally by sending a simple message, while the AI interprets their request and returns a structured, ready-to-use lesson plan in seconds.
The system runs on a multi-agent architecture. Each agent has a specialized role: some enrich the teacher’s request with pedagogical context, others connect it to Brazil’s national curriculum (BNCC), and others ensure that the output follows a coherent structure. This orchestration guarantees that lesson plans are not generic text, but aligned to curricular standards and adapted to the realities of public school classrooms.
The AI is also grounded in Nova Escola’s proprietary pedagogical assets with more than 6,000 lesson plans created by and for teachers combined with expert input from our pedagogical team. This ensures the generated content is inclusive, culturally relevant, and applicable even in contexts of low connectivity.
Unique Characteristics:
The Nova Escola initiative transforms teaching and learning in Brazilian public schools through the Lesson Planner via WhatsApp. What makes it unique is its combination of artificial intelligence with a platform that teachers already use daily, eliminating the need for new software or complex training. Teachers send a message, select grade and subject, and receive personalized, curriculum-aligned lesson plans based on the BNCC, created by experienced educators and validated by pedagogical experts.
Unlike generic tools, the Planner is rooted in Nova Escola’s rich database, reflecting the real-life challenges and diversity of classrooms across Brazil. It works even in low-connectivity areas, reaching teachers in remote or underserved regions, including rural, indigenous, and quilombola communities, and ensuring equitable access to quality resources.
The project continuously evolves through teacher feedback, pilot testing, and regional adaptation, making the solution responsive to real classroom needs. Partnerships with foundations, technology companies, and innovation awards like Meta and Tools Competition provide funding that keeps the tool free and scalable.
By empowering educators with time-saving, high-quality, and contextually relevant lesson plans, the initiative strengthens their confidence, professional agency, and ability to engage students. Today, it has the potential to reach 1.7 million teachers and 42.7 million students, contributing to a more inclusive, effective, and equitable educational system across Brazil.
Sustainable Change:
Nova Escola’s WhatsApp Lesson Planner contributes to sustainable, systemic change by targeting the core actors in education: teachers. By providing personalized, high-quality, curriculum-aligned lesson plans in an accessible, low-connectivity platform, the solution reduces teachers’ workload and frees time for meaningful interaction with students. This allows educators to focus on effective instruction, personalized support, and fostering student engagement and learning.
As teachers gain confidence and improve classroom practices, student learning outcomes are expected to rise, particularly in literacy and numeracy. The tool also strengthens equity, reaching educators in underserved regions and ensuring access to quality resources regardless of connectivity or school infrastructure.
Over time, the widespread adoption of the tool can influence professional development practices, school management, and curriculum implementation, creating a culture of evidence-informed teaching. By integrating AI with local pedagogical knowledge and continuous feedback from teachers, the initiative fosters an adaptive, scalable, and sustainable model that can be replicated in other contexts with national curriculum frameworks, contributing to long-term systemic improvements in public education.
Funding Sources: The Lesson Plan Generator via WhatsApp has been primarily funded through Nova Escola’s institutional investments as part of its mission to provide free, high-quality resources to public school teachers in Brazil. In addition, the solution has received strategic financial and technical support from key partners. WhatsApp (Meta) and Turn.io have contributed both funding and technology to enable the deployment of the tool in low-connectivity contexts. The Lemann Foundation has supported with financial resources, pedagogical expertise, and articulation with teacher networks. The World Bank has collaborated in projects that strengthened dissemination and large-scale adoption. More recently, international recognition through the Tools Competition has provided funding for the integration of new features, such as literacy-focused teacher surveys. Additional support has come from Microsoft in testing training applications, and from Instituto Ultra in regionalized implementations in the city of São Luís, Maranhão. Together, these financial, technological, and institutional investments have ensured the development, scaling, and continuous improvement of the solution.
Testimonials and Endorsements: https://youtu.be/uHEUqHNni14
Primary thematic focus area: Innovation Acceleration & Knowledge Sharing
Summary: Nova Escola’s Lesson Planner via WhatsApp is an AI-powered tool delivering free, curriculum-aligned lesson plans to Brazil’s public school teachers, even in low-connectivity areas. Teachers interact through WhatsApp, selecting grade, subject, and topic, and instantly receive lesson plans aligned with Brazil’s BNCC curriculum. The solution leverages OpenAI’s GPT-4o, Nova Escola’s proprietary database of 6,000+ expert-created lesson plans, and a multi-agent orchestration system to ensure pedagogical quality. Implemented at scale across Brazil, the solution has already demonstrated impact: 90% of users report direct classroom applicability, and 98.3% report significant time savings. With support from Meta, Fundação Lemann, World Bank, Instituto Ultra, and others, it aims to reach 1.7 million teachers and 42.7 million students, strengthening teacher agency, improving literacy outcomes, and promoting equitable access to quality education.

Title: Digital MicroSchools for the poorest
Subtitle: Teach The World Foundation is a non-profit organization based in Washington D.C, U.S.A, with a bold mission to establish and deploy effective and scalable models of literacy for the developing world, in contexts where there is a lack of teachers and poor infrastructure availability, by leveraging the power of digital technology.
Problem Statement:
The world is experiencing an educational crisis. According to UNESCO’s Education for All Monitoring Report, about 1 in 10 people in the world cannot read or write, adversely affecting achievement of the SDGs. The developing world is the worst hit, with millions of children out of school and millions more poorly educated. When put into this global context, Pakistan's situation stands out even more given that its education crisis is approaching catastrophic levels. It has more than 26 million children out-of-school (UNICEF 2023), the largest in the world. With the population growing by more than 4 million people a year and a literacy rate of 60 percent (Ministry of Finance Pakistan, 2020), 30–40 million more children could be out-of-school by 2030. Meanwhile, learning outcomes for in-school children are very poor, with approximately 40 percent of fifth graders failing to perform at even the second-grade level (DAWN, 2019). 

It is clear that traditional means will not solve this problem in an acceptable time frame — even if the resources existed. There is an imperative need for a rapidly scalable and easily deployable model of education that allows mass access to quality education, with built-in accountability to tackle this global educational crisis with the necessary urgency required. 

It is in response to this ‘wicked’ problem, both for Pakistan and globally, that Teach the World pioneered a breakthrough Differentiated Learning model called the Digital MicroSchool, providing targeted instruction and foundational literacy and numeracy skills to out-of-school children by leveraging digital technologies. By introducing a combination of game-based educational software, tablets, smartphones, and gamification, digital technology has been a game changer in providing foundational literacy to the most marginalized and excluded.
Solution Overview:
Digital MicroSchools transform how foundational education is delivered to out-of-school children in under-resourced and crisis-affected regions. The model combines gamified digital learning, offline-first technology, and community-based micro-classrooms to overcome the infrastructural, economic, and social barriers that prevent children from accessing quality education.

Gamified Learning: 
Children learn core literacy and numeracy skills through interactive, game-based apps, which significantly improve engagement, retention, and independent learning—especially in contexts where traditional methods have failed to hold attention.

Offline, Low-Cost Tech: 
Using solar-powered tablets and local servers, Digital MicroSchools operate entirely offline. This allows deployment in remote areas without internet or electricity, at a fraction of the cost of building and staffing traditional schools.

Community-Embedded Delivery Model: 
Each MicroSchool is facilitated by local community members rather than formal teachers, ensuring cultural relevance, trust, and sustainability.

Data-Driven Learning: 
Devices capture learning progress and attendance offline, enabling personalized feedback, program monitoring, and adaptive instructional support—even without connectivity.

Gender Mainstreaming: 
Enrolling 52% girls, engaging female caregivers, and enabling the professional growth of marginalized women as facilitators, officers, and leaders—advancing their economic participation, decision-making, and social representation.

Franchise for Scale: 
TTWF is building a franchise model for Sindh Government partner organizations to replicate Digital MicroSchools with technical support—dramatically expanding reach without sacrificing quality.

Influencing Policy and Ecosystems: 
TTWF policy advocacy has enabled Sindh Government to consider adding an addendum for Digital Learning to their existing Non-Formal Education Policy, convinced by operational efficiencies and learning outcomes of Digital MicroSchools.

Advancing Digital Equity: 
As children engage with digital content, they also build digital literacy—equipping them with essential 21st-century skills and improving their long-term educational and economic prospects.

Digital MicroSchools offer a replicable blueprint for delivering high-impact learning in disconnected and underserved communities—changing how and where education happens.

To enable further scaling and replication of the model we seek partnerships with other organizations and teams working towards UN SDG's to:
-Leverage advances in AI to personalize learning and adapt content delivery
-Curate high-quality, offline multilingual content aligned with national curricula
-Enhance learning analytics to generate robust evidence and improve real-time decision-making

Ecosystem Buy-In

-Gaining credibility with governments, education authorities, and community stakeholders
-Accelerating trust and ecosystem-wide acceptance of alternative, tech-enabled learning models

Scaling via Franchise Model

We are developing a replicable franchise model to help other education organizations implement Digital MicroSchools with TTWF’s technical assistance. 

-Refine implementation toolkits, training resources, and support systems
-Expand partnerships with NGOs, government bodies, and funders across geographies
Solution Provider(s): Teach the World Foundation
Implementation timeline(s): In terms of timeline, we have already proven the model across multiple geographies now and with 125 Digital  MicroSchools already impacting 15,000 students across Pakistan, Bangladesh and Malawi, we are expanding to an additional 200 schools to be opened in Sindh, Pakistan in 2025-26, impacting 30,000+ out-of-school children and working towards  an ambitious goal to open 1000 such MicroSchools in the next 3 years.
Duration to pilot in a new geography: 18 Months
SDGs addressed: SDG 4 (Quality Education);SDG 1 (No Poverty);SDG 10 (Reduced Inequalities);
Desired impact:
So far, our program has impacted 15000+ students across 3 countries in 140+ deployments.

Our main impact is to teach kids how to read and write. On average, our results were great both on an absolute and a relative basis. Relative to the control group (where students were being taught traditionally), our students in the intervention group scored 2x better on average. 

Moreover, students attendance has improved dramatically and drop-out rates have also reduced in the communities where we have deployed. 

Some crucial benefits that have only been measured qualitatively include 21st century skills like digital literacy and self-learning, increased motivation & confidence, etc.
 
We have a Socio-emotional Learning (SEL) component in our program in refugee environments that helps students manage their emotions better

We believe this program gives them the tools to take control of their own learning and improve their economic trajectories in the 21st Century.
Key technologies:
Core Technological Components:


Educational Software:
We deploy a curated suite of award-winning learning apps (e.g., Enuma, Mathmaker, onebillion, Taleemabad) that use gamification—points, rewards, and levels—to make learning fun and interactive. Many of these apps feature adaptive learning, adjusting content difficulty based on each child’s progress, and provide instant feedback, reinforcing concepts in real time.


Offline-Ready Hardware:
Tablets are robust, affordable, and designed for self-guided use. Paired with solar-powered charging stations and local servers, they operate entirely offline, with 4G connectivity used only for periodic updates and data syncs. Personal headphones enable audio interaction in noisy or shared spaces.


Environment-friendly, off-grid deployability:
MicroSchools are solar-powered, allowing deployment in off-grid communities, and minimizing carbon-footprint of learning


Governance and Monitoring:
MicroSchools are equipped with CCTV cameras for safeguarding and quality monitoring. Selected team members monitor live classroom streams to ensure learning integrity and facilitator accountability.


Data and Analytics:
Devices capture usage data and learning progress offline, which is later synced to centralized dashboards. This supports real-time decision-making, content optimization, and rigorous program evaluation.


Human-Tech Integration:
Local facilitators are trained to support learners, troubleshoot devices, and interpret analytics. This blend of human support and tech-driven content makes the model effective, scalable, and community-owned.


Digital MicroSchools demonstrate how low-cost, context-sensitive technology can transform education for the most excluded children on the planet.
Unique Characteristics:
Our model is a simple and scalable “functional literacy” solution for students in kindergarten to grade 5 (K–5). It has been deployed with excellent results in Pakistan, Bangladesh, and Malawi, in varied settings, from urban slums to refugee camps and remote Himalayan villages. The model delivers world-class reading, writing, and math applications in a gamified format, on low-cost tablets and smartphones, in a facilitated setting. ELAN students outperform students in traditional schools, achieving at least 1.5 times the learning gains, as measured by independent third parties across time, multiple geographies, and environments. As part of a “think big, start small” strategy, Pakistan is our starting point to establish these models. Ultimately, we plan to expand these models globally, to millions, in a disciplined, phased manner.

Using award-winning gamified applications on tablets and smartphones, our technology does not require reliance on a trained teacher. Our strategy is to create game-changing transformation by leveraging the Big Five of digital learning:

1. Universal reach and access: Mobile and global Internet can take the world’s best learning anywhere. We manage learning deployments in three countries, on two continents, from Pakistan.

2. Better, faster “self-learning”: The essence of learning is engagement. Digital educational games provide engagement and motivation in unsupervised settings, promoting “self-learning” and 21st century skills like digital literacy and problem solving.

3. Portability, adaptability, and massive scalability: Digital MictoSchool’s low costs, rapid deployment, and standardized technology and training make our solutions extremely scalable.

4. Transparency and accountability: Built-in tracking in digital applications enables accountability. With data analytics, it enables robust monitoring, evaluation, content adaptation, and personalization.

5. Higher return on investment: High engagement means greater learning. On average, the learning gains are 1.5 times those from traditional teaching. Even at equal cost, the return on investment doubles, and costs at scale can be even lower than they are today.
Sustainable Change:
Our Digital MicroSchools create and enhance lasting social impact by:

1. Enhancing economic and social well-being

• We expect improvements in education to increase employability, improve health, and reduce poverty and crime.

2. Accelerating access to education

• It enables accelerated expansion of access to education, through its strong scalability.

• The Digital MicroSchools have a powerful “democratization” potential. It provides high-quality education to the underprivileged, which is rare in developing countries, reducing the gap between elite schools and under-resourced public schools.

• The “self-learning” feature of the model promotes the development of digital literacy, creative thinking, problem solving, self-confidence, and social-emotional learning.

3. Empowering girls, women, and communities

• A key aspect of the Digital MicroSchools is increased female literacy, as we mandate a 50-50 male-female ratio. In some communities, our at-home program provides education to girls who are kept from going to school because of cultural taboos.

• Our at-home smartphone program focuses on family literacy targeting the child, mother, and father, who are often illiterate themselves. This was an unexpected benefit that emerged from our at-home model.

• The MicroSchools model promotes extraordinarily high community engagement and empowerment. Our first two micro-schools were initiated at the request of communities that have become partners in our mission and have provided space, teachers or facilitators, and other support.
Funding Sources:
Our business model centers on delivering direct value to two core groups: primary beneficiaries (children and communities) and key customers (governments, donors, and implementing partners).

What We Provide:
To children and communities: Access to free, quality, curriculum-aligned education through gamified, offline digital apps delivered on solar-powered tablets in local MicroSchools. These safe and inclusive learning spaces are facilitated by trained women from the community. No money is ever charged to learners or their families.


To governments and education partners: A cost-effective solution that addresses systemic barriers to education. Our offering includes digital content, hardware provisioning, classroom setup, facilitator training, monitoring tools, and learning data dashboards.


How We Provide It:
We implement directly in high-need areas and offer technical assistance to partners through a growing franchise model, enabling replication in other regions.


Services are delivered via standardized implementation toolkits, localized onboarding, and field-based support teams.


Revenue and Funding Model:
We operate as a nonprofit funded through public-private partnerships, including bilateral donors, CSR initiatives, philanthropic foundations, and government programs such as the Sindh Education Foundation (SEF).


Under SEF’s Accelerated Digital Learning Program, we have launched 100 MicroSchools and secured funding for 200 more, reaching 30,000 children for Sindh Government, and 35,000 children in total.


Our long-term model emphasizes cost-efficiency, pooled funding, and scaling through ecosystem partnerships.

Operating fully offline with robust data tracking and facilitator support, the model has been deployed in Pakistan, Bangladesh, and Malawi, reaching 15,000+ children. With government buy-in, a franchise model for replication, and strong policy advocacy, it aims to scale to 1,000 schools in three years, bridging the global education crisis where traditional systems cannot keep pace.

Title: The Visis AI
Subtitle: An assistive reading mobile software that aids the blind to read books independently and conveniently using AI and text-to-speech audio feedback technology.
Problem Statement:
Millions of Blind persons in Africa, espcially in Nigeria face strenous challenges with reading books independently and conveniently, thereby limiting their overall access to quality inclusive education. 

According to the World Health Organization, 26.2 million people suffer from visual impairment in Africa, with most of them being unable to read books and identify scenes around them independently. This has resulted in them having limited access to quality education, job opportunities, and the opportunities to live better quality lives. Also, the National Library of Medicine estimates that over 366 million persons suffer from attention disorders like ADHD and dyslexia, making it more difficult for these victims to enjoy access to read printed books and other published materials conveniently.

At Vinsighte, we currently address this barrier to reading books that is affecting the blind and visually impaired by providing access to our product known as Visis which aids them to read printed books conveniently, giving them access to quality and inclusive education like their sighted peers.
Solution Overview:
To solve this widely overlooked problem, we designed an Artificial Intelligence mobile Assistive reading software called Visis AI.

Visis is an artificial intelligence mobile assistive reading software application that aids the visually impaired and blind in reading printed books and educational materials independently and conveniently. Visis works by using Optical Character Recognition technology to scan the text of books in real-time and convert these texts to audio output for the visually impaired user to listen to. Visis, which can be downloaded from the mobile store and installed on the phone of the user, also leverages Dolby Atmos technology for users who read through our audiobook feature. Visis app also has special features that use computer vision to aid the visually impaired in identifying scenes, colors, and objects in the user's environment.

As part of our product partnership and distribution model, we partner with Schools, institutions, and impact organizations through a B2B2C model to implement our software in their libraries or for their students at a subsidized cost. While individual blind users access Visis through the mobile Play Store. 

Here’s a link to download Visis on the Android and IOS store: 
Apple Store: https://apps.apple.com/ng/app/visis/id6737469649 
Google Play Store: https://play.google.com/store/apps/details?id=com.vinsighte.visis&hl=en
Solution Provider(s): - Vinsighte Limited - Education Sector - https://www.linkedin.com/company/vinsighte-limited/
Implementation location(s): School for the blind Jabi Abuja Nigeria, Pacelli school for the blind Lagos Nigeria, School for the Visually Impaired Benin Nigeria, Omoyeni Home for the blind Oyo Nigeria, Bethesda Home for the blind Lagos, Nigerian Farmcraft center for the blind Lagos, Federal Nigerian Society for the Blind Lagos, Project Enable Nigeria, Rotary Club of Lagos Nigeria, Nigerian Association for the blind.
Duration to pilot in a new geography: 3 Months
SDGs addressed: SDG 4 (Quality Education);
Desired impact:
According to the Nigerian Optometric Association, nearly 7 million Nigerians are blind of which the National Blindness and Visual Impairment survey estimated that 4.25 million of these numbers are children and young adults of reading age (schooling and working age) who need to read books, get access to quality education and live a better life.

Currently, Visis is aiding 15,000+ visually impaired and blind children and young adults in schools, organizations and institutions for the blind across 7 states in Nigeria to read printed books independently and enjoy access to quality education like their sighted peers.

At Vinsighte,  our long term goal is to ensure that 3 million blind and visually impaired persons have access to our AI assistive reading solution which will aid them to read books and get access to quality education and equal job opportunities like their sighted peers by 2029.
Key technologies:
Visis converts documents, images, and real-world text into accessible audio by leveraging AI and cloud technologies. 

The process begins when a user captures printed text, PDFs, or scenes via their smartphone camera. The app preprocesses the image to enhance clarity, adjusting brightness, cropping skewed pages, detecting book edges, and reducing glare or shadows. This cleaned image is analyzed by an Optical Character Recognition (OCR) engine, powered by AWS Textract and Google Gemini, which extracts text pixel-by-pixel, even from complex layouts or multilingual content.

Once text is extracted, the app converts it to audio through a hybrid text-to-speech (TTS) pipeline. For visually impaired users, AWS Polly generates natural-sounding speech with adjustable pacing and multilingual support. For neurodiverse users (ADHD/dyslexia), Dolby Atmos spatial audio adds immersive effects like directional soundscapes (e.g., dialogue centered, ambient noise muted) to minimize distractions and improve focus. Long texts are split into parallel chunks for faster processing, while Redis caching and S3 storage efficiently manage data flow. This blend of robust AI, adaptive audio engineering, and scalable infrastructure ensures Visis delivers high-quality, accessible reading experiences even in regions with limited connectivity.
Unique Characteristics:
Unlike Braille and other traditional reading technology for the blind, Visis uses artificial intelligence technology to aid the blind to read printed texts independently using audio output.

Also, our competitors' solutions such as KNFB reader, and TapTap See which uses AI technology are too expensive for Africa’s low-income visually impaired and blind earners, and are not compatible with low-tech mobile phones commonly used in Nigeria and Africa. However, Visis is built to be compatible with low-end affordable mobile phones and provides an effective UX talkback interface, with an affordable $4/month-$40/annual subscription fee for our users which is also subsidized further by our partners.
Sustainable Change:
In Africa, specifically Nigeria, the general status quo for visually impaired and blind person is to rely on street begging to survive due to the difficulties they face with getting access to jobs as a result of being uneducated because they are unable to afford solutions that can aid them to read books and get access to quality education they deserve just like their sighted peers. 

We understand that blindness has far-reaching implications not just for the affected person, but also for their families, and for progress towards many of the Sustainable Development Goals, one of which is access to quality education. Without education, people are less able to work and earn, more likely to suffer ill-health, and less likely to educate their own children, thereby creating a poverty trap for the entire families. 

At Vinsighte, we are changing this narrative through Visis AI because we believe that the bedrock of every thriving society is quality education for all people irrespective of being visually impaired or blind. As a result of this, we are eliminating the disparities associated with visually impaired persons’ access to digital assistive technology, by designing an affordable, and accessible solution for all visually impaired and blind persons in Africa.

“Mr. Ossai Lawrence, a blind teacher at the School for the Blind in Abuja, stated that Visis reduces the bulkiness of reading Braille books.”

Implemented at scale in Nigeria, it has already reached over 15,000 users across schools and institutions for the blind (Q12, Q15, Q16).

Title: Smart Water Environment Monitoring With AI ＆ Quantum Dot Spectral Sensors
Subtitle: Real-time monitoring and analysis of water environment using advanced AI algorithms and quantum dot spectral sensors for smarter, more digitally economic and more sustainable water management.
Problem Statement: Quantum dot spectral sensing water environment monitoring technology mainly solves the pain points of high cost of traditional water environment monitoring, insufficient space coverage, non-real-time data, and slow emergency response. By realizing miniaturized, portable, and low-power integrated in-situ monitoring, it can obtain real-time water quality data at scale and with high density. This provides core perception capabilities for the construction of an intelligent supervision system for water environment big data, empowers precise pollution control, intelligent decision-making and optimal allocation of environmental resources, and is a key support for promoting the deep integration of digital technology and environmental protection and promoting the development of a green and sustainable digital economy.
Solution Overview:
1.The technology and implementation plan are independently completed by QuantaEye (Beijing) Technologies Co., Ltd.This solution deploys miniaturized, low-power quantum dot spectral smart monitoring terminals for real-time, in-situ acquisition of high-resolution water data. Data is transmitted via the Internet of Things (IoT) to the cloud platform, where big data and AI algorithms conduct in-depth analysis to rapidly parse water quality parameters and detect pollution. This enables continuous monitoring of the water environment, dynamic early warnings, and pollution source tracing, fundamentally transforming traditional approaches and empowering precise, intelligent governance.
2.The core is the internationally pioneering quantum dot spectral sensing technology from QuantaEye (Beijing) Technologies Co., Ltd. It uses quantum dot thin films to replace traditional optical components, achieving miniaturized, high-precision, low-power spectrometers. The system fuses IoT for efficient transmission, cloud computing for scalable processing, and big data for spatio-temporal analysis. AI/Machine Learning is then applied to construct multi-modal water quality models, guaranteeing high accuracy and adaptability.
Solution Provider(s): QuantaEye (Beijing) Technologies Co., Ltd. QuantaEye that specializing in Quantum Dot Chips reseach and development, construction and application of material spectral information big data platforms, is a national high-tech enterprise.As the pioneer and leader of global spectralin for matization,we created Quantum Dot Spectrometer, which stimulated a trend ofresearch and application of mianaturized spectrometry in the world. Based on this, we have successfully developed the world's first high-performance chip-based spectral sensor, making real-time monitoring, identification, and analysis of material information possible. In the era of interconnectedness, QuantaEye combines diverse information such as material information, industy information, and application data in the spectral dimension,expanding the laboratory research-level monitoring methods ofmaterialinformation to daily applications in areas such as Environment, Space Exploration, Healthcare,Agriculture,and Food safety. Bycollectingand accumulating massive basic data,we aims to build a material spectral information big data platform,constantly exploring and opening up innovative intelligent application scenarios , and devotingitselfto opening the "core" era of spectral information with technology and innovation.
