Desired impact:
By pioneering the development of miniaturized quantum dot spectral water quality sensors and highly-integrated smart terminals, we use digital technology to precisely capture water's spectral signature and build advanced AI models for instant water quality analysis. This technology is the core of our intelligent water environment supervision platform, which harnesses IoT, cloud computing, and big data to create a comprehensive, multi-layered digital governance system.
As we deploy and refine this solution across the water sector, we are breaking through long-standing barriers in engineering, maintenance, and market scalability. This is spearheading the deep fusion of digital technology and the water industry, creating new engines for economic growth, and powering a full-scale digital transformation. Ultimately, we are reinvigorating the digital economy and helping to forge a green, sustainable digital ecosystem for the future.
Quantum dot spectral sensing water environment monitoring technology has been successfully deployed across more than 20 provinces and cities in China, playing a pivotal role in key national strategic projects, including the Yangtze River Protection Campaign and the South-to-North Water Diversion Project. It has also been instrumental in vital urban initiatives, such as Beijing's "Water Environment Scout" system and Shanghai's city-wide tracing of illicit rainwater-sewage connections.
The system delivers game-changing results: it provides basin-wide water quality anomaly alerts within 30 minutes, pinpoints pollution sources with an unprecedented accuracy of 100 meters, and boosts pipeline inspection efficiency by 40% while cutting costs by 30%. We have developed a robust standardization framework, and our technology is officially endorsed and listed in the promotional catalogs of the Ministry of Ecology and Environment, the Ministry of Water Resources, and the MIIT. This has ushered in a new, digitally intelligent era for water monitoring.Collecting around 100 million data points annually, our solution dramatically improves urban water governance. It enables targeted, high-efficiency water treatment, offering a proven model and a powerful success story for how AI can drive sustainable urban water management.
Key technologies:
Quantum Dot Spectroscopic Sensing Technology：
In terms of data collection，Based on Professor Bao Jie of Tsinghua University, the world's first cutting-edge leading technology using quantum dots of Nobel Prize-winning materials to realize spectrometer chips——Quantum Dot Spectroscopic Sensing Technology（Nature 2015, 523, 67）. It deeply integrates AI to empower core R&D processes, including material synthesis and preparation, device integration and design, and algorithm model development. By overcoming key technical challenges in the "nano-materials -> filter arrays -> spectral reconstruction" chain, we have developed the world's first chip-level, wide-spectrum, high-sensitivity water quality spectral sensor and a highly-integrated, miniaturized, low-power multi-parameter monitoring device. This enables second-level, precise measurement of water quality parameters such as Chemical Oxygen Demand (COD), Permanganate Index (COD_(Mn)), Total Organic Carbon (TOC), and Turbidity in complex water bodies. Compared to domestic and international counterparts, our technology improves monitoring precision and sensitivity by 1-2 orders of magnitude, while reducing device volume and power consumption by 90%, making it highly suitable for in-situ, real-time water quality monitoring and high-density deployment.
AI Fusion and Analysis Technology: 
In terms of data quality control, we utilize multi-dimensional sensor health management technology, innovatively combining physics-based models with machine learning algorithms to achieve real-time diagnosis and identification of over 200 types of device operational states. We employ time-series, multi-modal fusion analysis to accurately identify more than 50 types of environmental anomalies and disturbances. Furthermore, through blind source separation signal correction technology, we achieve a COD detection error rate of ≤15% even in high-turbidity environments (up to 600 NTU), ensuring the validity of water quality monitoring data in complex and variable conditions.
Data Security Technology: 
Our data security framework employs a multi-protocol encryption system, complemented by data integrity verification and digital signature technologies, to ensure data confidentiality and tamper-proofing. Sensitive and private data are encrypted and digitally signed to guarantee lawful use. For data involving user privacy, differential privacy techniques are applied. At the system level, a strict security protection framework is implemented, featuring a secure bastion host architecture designed in accordance with MLPS (Multi-Level Protection Scheme) requirements and an integrated Intrusion Detection and Prevention System (IDPS) to ensure the system is secure and reliable.
Unique Characteristics:
1.Pioneering: The disruptive fusion of quantum dot materials and spectral sensing
It is the first in the world to integrate multi-size quantum dots into thin film filter arrays, replacing the traditional grating prism structure, realizing the miniaturization of spectrometers, and creating a new paradigm of quantum dot spectral sensing.
2. Benchmarking: Setting a New Standard for Data Accuracy with Multi-Modal Water Quality Models
By integrating physics-based models with data-driven models, we construct multi-modal water quality models that overcome the limitations of traditional monitoring. This approach establishes a new benchmark for data quality in water monitoring, defined by exceptional accuracy and stability.
3. Industry Leadership: Driving Industry Transformation with Miniaturized Terminals for In-Situ Monitoring
By overcoming the core challenges of in-situ water quality monitoring, we have developed one of the world's smallest, most highly-integrated, low-power terminals. This innovation is leading the revolutionary development of online monitoring equipment towards miniaturization and intelligence.
Sustainable Change:
The smart water environment monitoring technology using artificial intelligence and quantum dot spectral sensors realizes data transmission in seconds through the high-density deployment of micro monitoring terminals equipped with intelligent chips in the whole basin, relying on the 5G Internet of Things to achieve second-level data transmission, combining cloud computing and AI algorithms to deeply mine massive water environment data, and at the same time achieve innovation and upgrading with the help of the digital economy. Previous monitoring methods are lagging and passive, but this technology can not only monitor and trace the source in real time, but also predict pollution trends, provide accurate decision-making for water environment governance, and drive the transition of supervision to fully digital, intelligent and sustainable.
Our water quality monitoring device uses a reagent-free, physical method that eliminates secondary pollution. With <1W power consumption (90% less than competing technologies), it is solar-compatible and low-carbon. Its modular, reusable design minimizes resource consumption and waste generation. The technology slashes testing times from hours to minutes or even seconds, and can increase monitoring density by 10 to 100 times.
Deployed in over 30 cities across China, including Beijing and Shanghai, our solution has cut pollution response times from days to hours, helped detect and address over 1,000 water quality incidents, effectively curbed illegal discharges, ensured water safety, and benefited over 100 million people.

Title: PoBot: AI Voice Worker for Migrant Support and Supply Chain Accountability
Subtitle: Empowering migrant workers through AI-driven, multilingual support and supply chain integration to combat exploitation and ensure timely access to justice.
Problem Statement:
Migrant workers, particularly those in lower tiers of global supply chains, face systemic exploitation and persistent barriers to justice. Globally, an estimated 27.6 million people are trapped in forced labor, including 17.3 million in the private sector. In industries such as construction, manufacturing, domestic work, care, and fishing, many experience contract violations, wage theft, unsafe working conditions, and even debt bondage. Despite these risks, most remain unable to seek help due to language barriers, fear of retaliation, lack of legal literacy, and the absence of accessible, trusted grievance mechanisms.

These vulnerabilities are compounded by climate displacement, poverty, and rural-to-urban migration, which push millions into precarious and informal work. By 2050, an estimated 143 million people will be displaced by climate change, many settling in low-elevation coastal zones highly susceptible to disasters. In these contexts, migrants often end up in tier 2 and 3 factories or subcontracted job sites, where oversight is weakest and exploitation most severe.

Current support systems remain inadequate. Traditional NGO and government services are often inaccessible to workers with long shifts, remote postings, or restrictive employers. Existing grievance tools are rarely designed for low-literacy, multilingual populations, leaving workers without real-time, anonymous, and culturally sensitive channels for reporting abuse.

At the same time, companies and brands struggle to monitor hidden layers of their supply chains, lacking timely insights into worker grievances. This gap slows remediation, enables exploitation to persist, and undermines corporate accountability and human rights commitments. Addressing these barriers is essential for protecting vulnerable populations and creating more transparent, ethical supply chains.
Solution Overview:
Migrasia is developing PoBot, an AI-powered, multilingual chatbot designed to empower migrant and displaced workers by providing accessible, real-time support. The solution enables workers to navigate legal systems, access emotional support, and safely report exploitation, even in isolated, high-risk environments such as tier 2 and tier 3 factories. By offering context-aware assistance in workers’ native languages, PoBot lowers barriers related to literacy, fear, and access, equipping workers to advocate for themselves and seek timely help.

PoBot combines conversational AI with secure reporting mechanisms. Workers interact with the chatbot in their preferred language through familiar communication platforms. The chatbot provides information and guidance, connects workers to relevant resources, and, when necessary, facilitates incident reporting. Reports can be automatically shared with buyer companies, making labor exploitation visible in supply chains where oversight is often weak. This flow creates actionable data that allows companies to intervene and address risks proactively.

The system leverages large language models (LLMs) and natural language processing (NLP) to understand and respond to worker queries with cultural and linguistic sensitivity. A multi-agent architecture enhanced with Retrieval-Augmented Generation (RAG) ensures that legal and factual advice is tailored to the worker’s jurisdiction. The technology also integrates with case management systems used by NGOs and monitoring platforms used by companies, creating a feedback loop between workers, support organizations, and brands.

PoBot is co-designed in collaboration with frontline NGOs, labor unions, and migrant worker communities to ensure trust, relevance, and usability. By embedding the tool within NGO case management workflows, workers gain direct pathways to legal, social, and mental health support. At the same time, integration with company supply chain monitoring systems enables brands to take responsibility for labor conditions in their networks. This dual collaboration model strengthens existing protection mechanisms while fostering systemic change across supply chains.

Through this integrated approach, PoBot addresses root causes of labor exploitation, reduces vulnerability among migrant and displaced populations, and builds a more ethical and resilient labor ecosystem.
Solution Provider(s): Zendesk are a leader in customer service software powering our support systems, Linklaters a global law firm ensuring PoBot’s legal accuracy through rigorous review, The University of Hong Kong advancing research and evidence-based strategies to enhance migrant worker support and interventions.
Implementation location(s): Hong Kong, The Philippines, Indonesia, Taiwan, and Saudi Arabia.
Duration to pilot in a new geography: 6 months
SDGs addressed: SDG 5 (Gender Equality);SDG 8 (Decent Work and Economic Growth);SDG 10 (Reduced Inequalities);
Desired impact:
PoBot, our AI-powered chatbot, transforms migrant support by enhancing resilience and safety for climate-displaced individuals. With your funding, we will expand multilingual, context-aware assistance to reach more migrants facing legal, financial, and mental health challenges. Our objective is to provide real-time guidance on migration laws, worker rights, and ethical job opportunities, ensuring safer migration pathways and informed decision-making.

Since 2018, Migrasia has directly assisted over 38,000 migrants, filed more than 6,670 complaints, and facilitated 5,375 law enforcement actions, recovering and blocking over $36.7 million in illegal proceeds. More recently, PoBot has already supported over 3,216 migrant workers, handling more than 106,000 messages and concerns in the past ten months. It has achieved a continuation rate above 90 percent while effectively triaging cases, significantly reducing the workload of our migration specialists and allowing them to focus on complex, high-priority cases. These results demonstrate both the need for and the viability of technology-driven interventions in supporting migrant workers.

Building on this foundation, we plan on achieving the following impact via PoBot:
      - Monitor tier 2 and 3 factories to detect and prevent forced labor.
      - Support 150,000+ migrant workers with legal, educational, and mental health services.
      - Use interaction data to improve services continuously.
      - Strengthen migrants’ ability to navigate legal and financial challenges.
      - Directly benefit 120,000+ individuals, with 80% reporting positive experiences.

Collaboration remains central to our approach. We will partner with at least five organizations, including NGOs, legal aid services, shelters, and supply chain companies, to extend the reach of our services. This integration allows for direct reporting of labor exploitation in supplier factories and provides a mechanism for real-time intervention, supported by partnership agreements, training programs, and exploitation tracking.

This work is urgently needed, as climate-displaced migrants often face unsafe migration routes and exploitative labor conditions. Our solution provides critical protection and support, ensuring these vulnerable populations are not pushed into exploitative industries. Leveraging AI-driven insights, PoBot predicts risks, optimizes resource allocation, and enables real-time reporting. This empowers migrant workers with knowledge, legal protection, and access to safer economic opportunities.

We recognize the scale of the challenges migrants face and are committed to driving meaningful impact. With your support, we can continue to empower migrant workers and foster a resilient migration ecosystem where individuals can move safely and sustainably.
Key technologies:
PoBot leverages a combination of advanced and responsible AI technologies to deliver secure, scalable, and context-aware support for migrant workers. At the core, Artificial Intelligence and Large Language Models (LLMs) enable natural, multilingual conversations that provide context-relevant information in native languages. This capability is enhanced through Retrieval-Augmented Generation (RAG), which grounds responses in curated and verified legal and regulatory datasets, minimizing hallucinations and improving accuracy.

To further strengthen efficiency and transparency, PoBot runs on a multi-agent framework where each agent updates and reads from a shared case context. The triaging agent collects user details and passes them to the information collection agent. From there, only the agents relevant to the case are triggered: the validation agent checks recruiters or lenders, the loan analysis agent flags excessive interest, and the RAG agent retrieves legal or factual guidance through ChromaDB. All outputs flow into the same case record, with provenance and confidence notes. If automation is insufficient, the escalation agent compiles a brief and forwards it to a migration specialist. This event-driven coordination ensures fast, accurate, and context-aware support.

The system is deployed on Microsoft Azure’s cloud infrastructure, offering secure and scalable hosting while ensuring compliance with regional privacy standards. Continuous integration and deployment pipelines enable frequent and reliable updates. To maximize accessibility, PoBot is also integrated across popular messaging platforms such as WhatsApp and Facebook Messenger, meeting users where they already communicate.
Unique Characteristics:
PoBot is a unique AI-powered, multilingual chatbot designed specifically for migrant workers, particularly those in vulnerable tier 2 and 3 supply chain roles. Unlike many existing tools that are region-specific, advocacy-oriented, or limited to static information, PoBot provides real-time, scalable, and interactive support across more than 50 jurisdictions.

A key differentiator is its global, digital-first reach. PoBot is integrated into widely used platforms such as WhatsApp and Facebook Messenger, reducing barriers often overlooked by other tools, including geographic restrictions, digital literacy gaps, and device limitations.

PoBot stands out for its cultural and linguistic depth. The chatbot offers multilingual, context-aware support co-designed with former migrants and trafficking survivors to ensure trust and relevance. While generic AI platforms often provide broad but shallow responses, PoBot leverages a Retrieval-Augmented Generation (RAG) architecture within a multi-agent framework, ensuring responses are accurate, task-specific, explainable, and auditable. Importantly, PoBot is not a concept or pilot, it is already deployed and actively assisting beneficiaries.

Another unique element is its integrated accountability loop. PoBot goes beyond providing information by enabling anonymous exploitation reports to be channeled directly to buyer companies. This feature creates visibility in hidden areas of supply chains and enables proactive corporate action, a function that most existing services do not provide.

Finally, PoBot’s scalable, privacy-first design is built on secure, compliant cloud infrastructure with continuous feedback loops. This ensures adaptability across different geographies and sectors, while maintaining a strong focus on data protection. By combining human-centered design, advanced AI, and systemic integration, PoBot fills critical gaps left by other solutions and transforms how corporations and communities confront labor exploitation at scale.
Sustainable Change:
PoBot contributes to sustainable, systemic change by embedding accountability and resilience directly into migration and labor systems. The solution operates on a hybrid model: migrant workers access services for free, while revenue is generated from companies seeking supply chain monitoring, compliance reporting, and ESG-aligned risk mitigation.

This dual pathway ensures that workers receive essential legal, educational, and mental health support at no cost, while companies gain a practical tool to meet increasing demands for human rights due diligence and ethical sourcing standards.

PoBot’s design reflects Migrasia’s broader Theory of Change, which rests on four interrelated components:
     - identifying and triaging victims; 
     - providing both online and in-person client support; 
     - collecting and aggregating data; 
     - and producing research, reports, and recommendations that inform governments, the private sector, and civil society. 

We believe that effective online communication generates awareness among migrants, consistent and accessible support enables them to avoid mistreatment or seek remediation, and the documentation of interventions raises multinational companies’ awareness, leading to stronger supply chain accountability.

The follow-on effects of PoBot’s deployment are threefold:
     - Institutionalizing worker well-being: Companies integrate migrant welfare into supply chain practices, driving systemic improvements in labor conditions.
     - Fostering collaboration: Partnerships with NGOs, international organizations, and governments ensure that worker protections are reinforced by policy and practice.
     - Creating lasting demand: Integration into corporate compliance systems and government monitoring platforms establishes long-term sustainability beyond project-based funding.

Lastly, to make the project financially sustainable, we plan on implementing following revenue  generating models:
     - Corporate subscriptions and licensing: Buyer companies pay annual fees to integrate PoBot into their compliance and monitoring systems.
     - Custom reporting and analytics services: Companies can purchase tailored dashboards, incident analysis, and worker sentiment trend reports.
     - Partnerships with international organizations: Co-financing arrangements with multilateral agencies and donors during scale-up phases.

Over time, this approach shifts from donor and grant reliance to a self-sustaining ecosystem where informed workers, accountable companies, and responsive institutions collectively drive systemic, long-term change.

Title: Neqabty: AI-Powered Digital Platform for Labor Unions
Subtitle: Empowering 1.3M+ underserved union workers with AI-powered access to healthcare, training, and financial services — built with Microsoft & NVIDIA for scalable inclusion across emerging markets.
Problem Statement:
In emerging markets, tens of millions of unionized workers, freelancers, and informal professionals remain excluded from the digital economy due to the lack of accessible, inclusive digital infrastructure tailored to their specific needs.

Traditional union systems are paper-based, fragmented, and inefficient — resulting in weak governance, poor access to social protection, delayed services, and limited visibility into labor market trends. Members often struggle to access healthcare, pay subscriptions, receive training, or verify their professional licenses — particularly in rural and underserved regions.

This digital exclusion disproportionately affects low-income and semi-formal workers, including women, youth, and aging pensioners, who are unable to benefit from digital transformation efforts designed for the formal or corporate sectors.

Without a unified, affordable, and interoperable solution, labor unions — which should be key agents of inclusion — remain digitally invisible and financially unsustainable.

Neqabty was built to address this systemic exclusion by offering a digital-first, AI-enabled infrastructure for syndicates to deliver essential services to their members while enabling those members to participate in the digital economy and access decent work opportunities.
Solution Overview:
Neqabty is a digital union operating system designed to help professional associations digitize their services and empower underserved workers with access to healthcare, training, financial tools, and career support — all through one unified platform.

The platform enables syndicates to offer:

Digital onboarding & member verification

Smart health and social protection services

Subscription payments & digital wallets

AI-powered career coaching & skill pathways

Smart contract–based licensing and benefits (in development)

Technologies Used

AI/NLP models for CV generation and personalized training

Azure cloud infrastructure for scalable and secure delivery

NVIDIA Inception tools for optimized AI performance

Mobile-native design with offline support for rural access

Title: Pedius - Accessible Communications
Subtitle: Pedius develops innovative solutions for deaf people to ensure equal access to communication and information.
Problem Statement:
Deaf people and those with hearing impairments face significant barriers when communicating by telephone, which is still the main means of accessing a wide range of public and private services. Health emergencies, requests for assistance, medical appointments, customer service, and simple everyday interactions rely on voice communication, excluding those who cannot hear or speak. This severely limits the independence and safety of people with hearing impairments.

The same exclusion is reflected in the workplace, where the use of the telephone and conference calls is often central to business processes. Deaf employees often find themselves isolated or not involved in key moments of internal communication, hindering their full professional integration, despite regulatory obligations for inclusion.

Another critical area is education, where the lack of accessible tools penalizes not only deaf students, but also those with specific learning disabilities (SLD), such as dyslexia or neurodivergences. These students often do not have technologies that are adequate for their communication and cognitive needs and are excluded from educational processes, particularly during distance learning. The pandemic has accentuated this gap, highlighting the urgent need for inclusive and adaptable tools.

Finally, Pedius is not just an app, but a flexible and scalable platform that can be easily integrated into corporate infrastructures (call centers, customer services, data collection), already adopted by companies such as TIM, BNL, and ENEL, contributing to the spread of accessibility on a large scale.

In summary, the lack of accessible solutions for voice and text communication leads to the structural exclusion of large segments of the population, compromising their participation in social, work, and educational life. Pedius was created to address this inequality in a concrete and scalable way.
Solution Overview:
Pedius is a technology platform that allows deaf people or those with communication difficulties to make phone calls independently and in real time, transforming written messages into speech using speech synthesis, and converting the other party's responses into text using automatic speech recognition (ASR). The interaction takes place entirely via the app, guaranteeing confidentiality and fluid communication.

The same technology is also suitable for professional and business environments, making call centers, emergency numbers, switchboards, and customer service infrastructures accessible thanks to modular and customizable integration.

Alongside its telephone service, Pedius has developed Pedius Education, a solution designed for the educational inclusion of students with hearing impairments or specific learning disorders (SLD).

In person, the teacher uses a microphone connected to a tablet or mobile device on which, through the Pedius app, the audio is transcribed in real time for the student, who can read it directly on their screen.

Pedius Education also offers advanced features based on artificial intelligence, such as: Automatic highlighting of key concepts; Generation of concept maps from transcripts; Summarization and reorganization of content to facilitate understanding; Adaptive graphical interfaces, designed to improve usability even for students with SLDs.

Pedius uses an integrated mix of innovative technologies: Multilingual ASR (Automatic Speech Recognition) and TTS (Text-to-Speech); Machine Learning and NLP (Natural Language Processing) to optimize transcription accuracy; Semantic AI for concept extraction, automatic highlighting, and content organization; Cloud computing and cross-platform mobile technology; Security protocols and encryption to ensure privacy and data protection, even in educational or corporate environments.

Pedius has built a solid ecosystem of partnerships, which supports its dissemination across various sectors.
Companies and network operators: TIM has integrated Pedius into its accessible services and distributes it through its national commercial network.
Banking and insurance sector: Banca d'Italia and UNIPOL Assicurazioni have adopted Pedius in their contact centers to offer accessible services to deaf customers.
Public administration and Civil Protection: thanks to projects with entities such as Roma Capitale, Pedius is used for emergency management and civic communication.
Schools and universities: Pedius Education is used in classrooms and educational settings (such as the University of Rome La Sapienza, the Academy of Fine Arts in Palermo, etc.) to promote the inclusion of deaf students or those with SLDs, both in the classroom and in distance learning.
Associations and communities: ongoing collaborations with deaf communities, organizations, and associations for digital inclusion contribute to the continuous improvement of the service through feedback and suggestions.
Solution Provider(s): Over the years, Pedius has established numerous partnerships with important national and international public and private entities that have chosen to make their services accessible through our technology. Some of these partnerships have ended or have not been renewed, but they have nevertheless represented significant milestones in the development and dissemination of the solution. Below is a list of all the partnerships established over the years: TIM – Telecom Italia S.p.A. (Utilities – Energy and Water, Call Center), CSL – Communication Services Limited Hong Kong (Telecommunications, Call Center), Acquedotto Pugliese (Utilities – Water, Call Center), 112 Trento (Emergency Service, Call Center),  Italian Red Cross (Healthcare/Emergencies, Call Center), ENEL Perú (Energy, Call Center), Municipality of Rome (Public Administration, Call Center), Bank of Italy (Financial Institution, Work Inclusion + Accessible Call Center), CAP Group (Utilities – Water, Call Center), Hochschule Hannover (Germany, University – Education), Terna S.p.A. Implementation location(s): The solution was developed in Italy and is currently active in the following countries: Italy, United Kingdom, Ireland, France, Spain, Austria, Germany, Canada, United States, Brazil, New Zealand, Australia, Hong Kong, and Peru.
Implementation timeline(s): The first implementations with institutional and private partners in Italy began in 2014, while in 2016 the service began to expand internationally, consolidating its presence in several countries. Desired impact:
Pedius aims to eliminate communication barriers for people with hearing disabilities, ensuring them independent and inclusive access to everyday and emergency telephone services. In addition, the solution promotes inclusion in the workplace and in education, facilitating the active participation of deaf people or those with communication difficulties in business and educational contexts. Pedius aims to create an accessible communication model that can be adapted and scaled globally.

Key results and impacts:
Over 50,000 users in different countries have already benefited from Pedius technology to communicate independently by telephone.
Collaborations with more than 30 institutional partners and leading companies in the public, healthcare, financial, and insurance sectors.
Workplace inclusion: support for hundreds of employees with hearing impairments in partner companies, improving their integration and participation in decision-making processes.
Easier access to emergency services, with the ability to contact the single emergency number 112 independently.
In the field of education, Pedius Education has helped improve school participation for deaf students and those with SLDs, promoting inclusive learning.
The solution has led to a significant reduction in social and work exclusion related to hearing impairment, improving users' quality of life.
Key technologies:
Pedius relies on an advanced set of digital technologies to break down communication barriers and ensure a smooth and accessible experience for users with hearing impairments. The main technologies used include:

Artificial Intelligence (AI): Pedius uses speech recognition and speech synthesis algorithms to automatically convert speech to text and vice versa, enabling real-time two-way communication. AI is also used to improve natural language understanding, adapting to different accents, dialects, and specific contexts.

Machine Learning: To continuously optimize transcription and speech synthesis accuracy, Pedius uses machine learning models that adapt and improve with user feedback and usage.

Natural Language Processing (NLP): This technology allows the content of conversations to be interpreted, facilitating interaction and the management of complex requests.

Integration with telecommunications infrastructure: Pedius integrates with traditional telephone networks and VoIP to ensure compatibility and accessibility on a large scale.

Digital accessibility technologies: Pedius includes specific features such as real-time transcription, subtitles, concept maps, and support tools for students with learning disabilities to ensure an inclusive educational experience.

Cloud computing: The cloud architecture allows for scalability, reliability, and continuous platform updates, as well as facilitating access from any device and location.

These combined technologies enable Pedius to offer an innovative, efficient, and customizable solution that can adapt to different contexts and user needs.
Unique Characteristics:
Today, there are several communication channels between deaf and hearing people—such as SMS, MMS, email, and DTS—but none of these integrate telephone services on an equal footing, leaving a crucial need unmet, especially in emergency situations where timely and effective communication is essential.

The only dedicated telephone service was the “Servizio Ponte” (Bridge Service), a switchboard that connected deaf and hearing people via video chat, email, or fax, but it has been gradually deactivated in many Italian regions due to high operating costs and its discontinuous nature.

Unlike this model, Pedius offers an automated system that drastically lowers operating costs compared to traditional call centers based on human operators as intermediaries. This allows continuous access without time limits, while also improving waiting times thanks to a hybrid configuration that combines automation and human intervention on demand, thus ensuring an efficient and flexible service.

Compared to relay services operating in some foreign countries, which enjoy greater public support, Pedius represents an innovative solution in Italy and abroad, capable of reducing costs and improving accessibility.

A comparison with Roger Voice, a similar app created in France, shows that Pedius is more oriented towards the corporate and institutional world, offering numerous customized products to integrate and facilitate communication in companies, as well as providing infrastructure, software, 24/7 customer support, and training courses for operators. Roger Voice, on the other hand, focuses on personal use and has very high costs.

In the context of workplace inclusion and university education, Pedius further distinguishes itself: currently, the only support offered is sign language interpreters, classrooms equipped for a general audience—not specifically designed to meet the needs of deaf and students with SLDs (e.g., highly legible fonts)—and apps or websites for creating concept maps that cannot be edited or customized based on the student's level of difficulty.

Finally, compared to other generic voice recognition solutions (such as Google or Microsoft) and subtitling apps that are not always available in Italian or lack advanced features such as summaries, notes, or keywords, Pedius stands out for its specific, inclusive, and comprehensive technology offering, designed to meet the real communication needs of deaf people or those with SLDs.
Sustainable Change:
Pedius contributes to generating sustainable and systemic change by breaking down the communication barriers that still limit the social, professional, and educational inclusion of deaf people and those with learning difficulties. Thanks to the adoption of advanced technologies and flexible integration models, Pedius promotes independent and equal access to essential services, ensuring active participation in society.

Universal accessibility: By making the telephone accessible to everyone, Pedius removes a key barrier to communication between deaf and hearing people, facilitating access to public, health, emergency, and business services.

Employment inclusion: By providing employees with hearing impairments with effective communication tools, Pedius promotes greater integration in the workplace, increasing employment opportunities and active participation in decision-making processes.

Educational inclusion: By providing technological solutions for real-time transcription and content adaptation, Pedius ensures that deaf and DSA students have equal access to lessons and school activities, helping to reduce the educational gap.

The spread and adoption of Pedius technology is stimulating cultural change in organizations and society, promoting awareness of the importance of accessibility and encouraging other entities to adopt inclusive solutions. The use of scalable and updatable technologies allows Pedius to evolve with user needs, ensuring a lasting impact and the ability to adapt to new contexts and future challenges.
Funding Sources: In December 2014, it received €410,000 in funding from TIM Ventures, Embed Capital, and Sistema Investimenti, while in December 2016, it closed a €1.4 million Series A round with TIM Ventures, Principia SGR, and Invitalia Ventures.
Primary thematic focus area: Innovation Acceleration & Knowledge Sharing
Summary: Pedius is a speech-to-text and text-to-speech platform enabling deaf people to make phone calls and access services independently. It also offers an education module (Pedius Education) with real-time transcription, summaries, and adaptive learning tools. Adopted in 13+ countries, Pedius partners with telecoms, banks, governments, and universities, serving 50,000+ users globally.

Title: FriendnPal – Culturally relevant AI-Powered Multilingual Mental Health
Subtitle: Multilingual, predictive, offline-enabled AI delivering 24/7 trauma-informed mental health care in Africa
Problem Statement:
85% of Africans lack access to culturally relevant mental healthcare. Language barriers, stigma, infrastructure gaps, and underfunded systems exclude underserved groups, especially rural and low-income communities, from receiving timely support, worsening mental health outcomes and economic resilience.
Suicide is now the second leading cause of death among youth in Africa, with depression and anxiety surging among adolescents. A recent study by Stanford University found a significant rise in depressive symptoms among pre-teens, attributing part of this to increased screen time, digital isolation, and lack of emotional regulation tools. In Africa, the crisis is further worsened by a critical shortage of mental health professionals, sometimes only 1 psychiatrist per 500,000 people coupled with deep stigma and zero culturally relevant interventions. If left unaddressed, this silent epidemic will not only rob us of our youth but also derail long-term human capital development across the continent.
This is deeply personal for me, losing my mother to depression and living with ADHD myself. I realized: access isn’t just about availability, it’s about cultural relevance.
Solution Overview:
FriendnPal is Africa’s first predictive, multilingual AI mental health platform providing trauma-informed support in underserved communities through WhatsApp, mobile, and offline voice systems. Our  platform combines localized AI with culturally adaptive NLP in African languages, Pidgin, Hausa, Yoruba, Swahili, and English, to detect early signs of emotional distress and triages timely support to licensed therapists.
Users are guided to self-help tools, peer support, long before crisis hits. We use a hybrid approach combining AI automation with human follow-up for high-risk cases.
More than just a digital solution, FriendnPal builds resilience and foundational emotional wellness, essential for entrepreneurship, digital participation, and economic inclusion. Our platform trains and certifies digital peer counselors, especially among youth and women, creating livelihood pathways and addressing stigma.

With over 10,000 users, 10,000+ therapy sessions, and partners like Red Cross Nigeria, Lagos State, Fidelity Bank and SheUnitesAfrica, FriendnPal is helping shape a digital future where emotional well-being is not a privilege but a right. We are building the first African mental health databank, unlocking insights for inclusive AI governance and future policy.
We don’t just talk. We listen, analyze behavioral cues, and intervene early, long before a crisis hits.
Solution Provider(s): Lagos state Government Ministry of Youth and social development, Red Cross Nigeria (Health & Humanitarian), SheUnitesAfrica (Women-led Impact), The Humanitarian Network UK (Diaspora Support)
Implementation timeline(s): Pilot launched in Q3 2024. Ongoing implementation through 2025.
Duration to pilot in a new geography: 3–5 months (custom AI adaptation, therapist onboarding, partnership building)

Our core objectives are:
- Early detection of emotional distress using predictive AI.
- 24/7 access to mental health support through mobile, WhatsApp, and offline voice.
- Provide mental health access to 1,000,000 underserved Africans by 2027
- Deliver 100,000+ therapy sessions across marginalized communities
- Build first African mental health databank to inform policy and scale care
- Strengthen resilience and emotional well-being of youth, displaced groups, and workers

10,000+ therapy sessions delivered in under 12 months.
10,000+ users across web, mobile, and WhatsApp platforms.
50+ suicidal crises intercepted and rerouted to emergency care.
200+ at-risk youths in slum communities supported through therapy and tech skills training.
$51,000 in earned revenue over 12 months, proving sustainability.
Partnerships with Nigerian Red Cross, Lagos State Government, etc

Offline voice-enabled assistant

Offline-first architecture for low-connectivity areas
Multilingual emotional care at scale
B2B2C model combining revenue from therapy access and licensing of AI tools

Sustainable Change:
FriendnPal creates systemic impact by bridging the mental health access gap for vulnerable populations, reducing stigma, and strengthening local digital health ecosystems. Our AI models and databank power insights for health policy, while our scalable tech ensures long-term cost-effective care delivery, especially in hard-to-reach regions. 
Our model inspires local talent development, decentralized care models, and digital inclusion for resilience and growth through; 
Access – By meeting users on accessible platforms like WhatsApp and offline voice, we eliminate infrastructural and cost barriers to care.

Awareness – Multilingual AI chatbots raise mental health awareness in local languages, reducing stigma.

Early Intervention – Predictive models catch signs of distress before crisis, reducing long-term health and economic burdens.

Empowerment – Peer support, journaling, and therapy tools strengthen self-regulation and community resilience.

Data for Systems Change – Our anonymized, ethically sourced databank helps policymakers, researchers, and institutions build better systems rooted in local realities.

Title: AI-driven models for electricity access forecasting
Subtitle: UNDP and IBM developed two interactive models available for free to the general public through UNDP's GeoHub dashboards, helping users access data and insights to interpret complex clean energy challenges and opportunities.
Problem Statement: Mapping global electricity access with both high spatial and temporal resolution remains a formidable challenge. Household surveys and national censuses – the traditional sources – are infrequent and can lag real-world conditions by one to two years, while remote sensing proxies (such as night-time lights) often miss low-intensity or intermittent connections. At the same time, long-range planners require forecasts of 20-30 years to guide generation, transmission and distribution investments. Integrating disparate datasets – covering population growth, grid and off-grid infrastructure, urbanisation patterns, land use and socio economic indicators – demands extensive harmonisation. To address these gaps and uncertainties, UNDP collaborated with IBM to develop AI-driven models that can produce timely, granular and forward-looking forecasts.
Solution Overview:
IBM and UNDP co-developed the Electricity Access Forecasting AI model, built on IBM watsonx, IBM Cloud and an open-source machine learning library. The model projects electricity access through 2030 across 102 Global South countries by evaluating multiple drivers, such as population density, existing grid and off-grid infrastructure, urbanisation rates, terrain elevation and night-time satellite imagery, augmented with land use data from IBM Environmental Intelligence. In parallel, IBM, UNDP and Stony Brook University created the Clean Energy Equity Index, a first-of-its-kind statistical geospatial model that integrates environmental, economic and social metrics, including education levels, greenhouse gas emissions and relative wealth, to generate an equity score from 0 to 1. GeoHub users can interactively adjust the weight of each indicator, run sensitivity analyses and identify regions where clean energy investments will most effectively promote equity and urgency. 
This collaboration was enabled by the IBM Impact Accelerator (previously known as the IBM Sustainability Accelerator), a social innovation program that supports communities facing environmental and economic stress around the world, through technologies like AI and an ecosystem of experts.
Solution Provider(s): IBM (private sector), United Nations Development Programme, Stony Brook University (research university)
Implementation location(s): Electricity Access Forecasting AI model has data from 102 countries across the Global South, including in Africa, Asia Pacific, Latin America and the Middle East. Clean Energy Equity Index has data from 53 African countries.
Implementation timeline(s): Announced as available on Sept. 17, 2024: UNDP and IBM Launch New Tools to Forecast Energy Access and Model Energy Equity (press release)
Duration to pilot in a new geography: For the countries already covered, the models can be implemented now. Implementation for other countries is dependent on data availability.
SDGs addressed: SDG 7 (Affordable and Clean Energy);
Desired impact: Enable users — from policymakers at the national and community level to the general public — to analyze complex energy issues through advanced artificial intelligence (AI) technology and access a wide range of resources, helping support data-driven decision-making toward a just energy transition.
Key technologies:
The Electricity Access Forecasting AI model uses the IBM watsonx AI and data platform, IBM Cloud, and an open-source machine learning library to provide future forecasts at scale of electricity access through 2030 by evaluating a set of factors including population, infrastructure, urbanization, elevation, and satellite data in addition to land use data provided by IBM Environmental Intelligence.
The Clean Energy Equity Index, developed by IBM and UNDP together with Stony Brook University, is a statistical geospatial model combining geospatial analytics with environmental, economic and social factors – such as education, greenhouse gas emissions, and relative wealth — to generate a Clean Energy Equity score of 0-1.
These interactive are hosted within UNDP's global GeoHub platform. As part of UNDP's Data Futures Exchange (DFx), GeoHub is a centralized ecosystem of geospatial data and services. It provides a platform to easily upload, visualize and analyze datasets, combining time-oriented and geographic data with satellite imagery. GeoHub supports a granular, localized, and evidence-based approach to development challenges and integrated policy making— from determining subnational distribution of electricity access, to assessing levels of vulnerability to the effects of climate change for communities over time.
Unique Characteristics:
By modeling these factors including population, infrastructure, urbanization, elevation, and satellite data in addition to land use data to make a future forecast, the Electricity Access Forecasting model provides a distinct advantage compared to more commonly available, current-day estimates of electricity access.

The Clean Energy Equity Index is a first of its kind statistical geospatial model. In its dashboard, GeoHub users can also individually view and customize each environmental, economic, or social factor analyzed in the model, to evaluate which factors have the greatest impact on equitable access to clean energy, empowering better decision making.
Sustainable Change: The Electricity Access Forecasting model delivers forward-looking, hyper-granular (1 km²) forecasts for 102 Global South countries across Africa, Asia Pacific, Latin America and the Middle East, surpassing static current-day maps. By visualising future access patterns, governments and investors can identify underserved areas, optimise infrastructure investments and monitor progress toward universal electricity access by 2030. The Clean Energy Equity Index provides data for 53 African nations at subnational resolutions, enabling policy makers to pinpoint equity gaps and tailor interventions based on customisable economic, environmental and social factors. Together, these tools on GeoHub empower stakeholders with robust evidence to prioritise actions and allocate resources effectively, accelerating a just and inclusive energy transition aligned with SDG 7. These tools can provide improved efficiency and enhance delivery of current and future UNDP projects. UNDP estimates that over 600,000 people will benefit from the collaboration with the IBM Impact Accelerator.
Funding Sources: The IBM Impact Accelerator is a pro bono social innovation program. IBM collaborates with organizations to design, develop and deploy a technical solution directly benefiting communities. Throughout the experience, IBM provides access to platforms such as IBM watsonx and Granite AI models, IBM Cloud, IBM Environmental Intelligence and Red Hat open source technologies as well as technical mentorship to build long-term capacity.
Testimonials and Endorsements:
"Bringing together UNDP's knowledge and global leadership in sustainable development and IBM's breakthrough innovations in AI and hybrid cloud, we are proud to unveil solutions that demonstrate the power of technology to make a lasting, positive impact on our environment and in our communities," said Justina Nixon-Saintil, IBM Vice President and Chief Impact Officer. "By making innovative models freely accessible to the public, we aim to empower leaders, organizations and community members alike with the insights to make impactful energy decisions around the world."
"UNDP's innovative collaboration with IBM helps countries leverage development data and technology innovation to improve lives and protect the planet. The solutions we've co-created provide a credible evidence base to help countries make meaningful and practical progress towards a just energy transition. Net-zero investment and people-centered development strategies are fundamental to accelerate the SDGs," said Laurel Patterson, Head of the UNDP SDG Integration Team, UNDP Bureau for Policy and Programme Support.
Source: https://newsroom.ibm.com/2024-09-17-UNDP-and-IBM-Launch-New-Tools-to-Forecast-Energy-Access-and-Model-Energy-Equity
Primary thematic focus area: Enabling Policies & Regulatory Innovation
Summary: UNDP and IBM co-developed AI-driven electricity access forecasting models and a Clean Energy Equity Index, now deployed across 102 Global South countries. A strength is the unique combination of AI, geospatial analytics, and open public access via UNDP’s GeoHub (Q13, Q23, Q24). A weakness is that while the models are implemented at scale, the submission provides limited direct evidence of local community-level adoption or policy integration outcomes (Q22, Q25).

Title: ArborX is an eco-fintech platform where users can purchase and own real, geotagged trees anywhere in the world.
Subtitle: We’re building a first-of-its-kind eco-fintech platform where users can purchase and own real, geotagged trees anywhere in the world, monitor growth and carbon impact in real time via AI and Satellite.
Problem Statement:
Tree planting is growing globally, yet individuals and companies struggle to directly own, track, or monetize their impact. Most climate Contributions lack traceability, investment appeal, or real-time monitoring.
Carbon credit markets are often complex, inaccessible, and non-transparent for grassroots or midsize actors. Governments: Lose billions in misallocated funds.
Solution Overview: We are providing a digital & physical Green Card that enables individuals and companies to purchase, own, and track trees anywhere in the world. Combines geotagging, blockchain, AI, and fintech to deliver transparent carbon credits, growth updates, and ecosystem impact. Turns conservation into a portfolio—people own forests like assets.
Solution Provider(s): Tree-Nation (Tree-Nation NEOVEE SOLUTIONS, SL), a global reforestation platform enabling carbon offsetting through tree planting in vulnerable ecosystems (Environmental Sustainability, Climate Action), POTRAZ (Postal and Telecommunications Regulatory Authority of Zimbabwe), the national ICT regulator promoting digital inclusion and infrastructure development (ICT Regulation, Public Sector), WOCAT (World Overview of Conservation Approaches and Technologies), a global network advancing sustainable land management practices to combat degradation (Environmental Research, Land Restoration), International Partnership for the Satoyama Initiative (IPSI), a multi-stakeholder platform fostering biodiversity and human well-being through socio-ecological production landscapes, United Nations Convention to Combat Desertification (UNCCD), a global environmental treaty supporting land stewardship and resilience against desertification and climate change.
Duration to pilot in a new geography: 60 days.
SDGs addressed: SDG 15 (Life on Land);SDG 13 (Climate Action);SDG 17 (Partnerships for the Goals);
Desired impact:
ArborX aims to democratize climate ownership through tokenized carbon credits, enabling traceable, personalized tree portfolios. 
Its core objective is to scale carbon removal through smart tree ownership.  
Key achievements include sequestering 500, 000+ tons of CO₂ annually (based on ~22–48 lbs per tree/year) and one million hectares of restored land as well as capacity building to over 10, 000 youths.
The Green Card system integrates blockchain, AI, and fintech for transparent impact tracking.  
ArborX unlocks new revenue streams via carbon marketplaces, ESG APIs, and restoration-linked digital assets.
Key technologies: Blockchain, Satellite, AI
Unique Characteristics: ArborX pioneers “Trees-as-a-Portfolio” ownership using blockchain, AI, and satellite tech to tokenize and monitor trees globally.  The eco-fintech model blends restoration with embedded finance—offering ESG APIs, carbon credit marketplaces, and gamified impact dashboards.  The Green Card system enables traceable tree ownership and real-time ecosystem analytics—unmatched in transparency and personalization.
Sustainable Change: ArborX catalyzes climate ownership by enabling individuals and institutions to invest in traceable tree portfolios and restoration-linked carbon credits. This drives ecosystem regeneration, youth employment, and data-driven transparency—creating feedback loops that reinforce trust, funding, and participation. Over time, ArborX shifts restoration from donor dependency to self-sustaining eco-fintech ecosystem, scaling impact across regions and sectors.

Title: GreenBox™: Solar Cold Storage Cutting Food Losses, Boosting Farmer Incomes
Subtitle: Solar-powered cold storage and market access platform reducing post-harvest losses, improving farmer incomes, and building climate resilience in Congo.
Problem Statement:
According to the Rockefeller Foundation, according to the 2014 Food Waste and Spoilage Initiative, approximately 50% of all horticultural produce is lost or wasted before reaching the consumer in developing countries, exacerbating poverty, hunger, and malnutrition. This affects 470 million smallholder farmers, retailers, and food supply chain actors.
In Congo, food spoilage affects approximately 1 million smallholder farmers and supply chain actors. Reducing post-harvest losses is essential to improving the livelihoods, nutrition, and resilience of farmers and communities.
The International Food Policy Research Institute (IFPRI) estimates that a 10% reduction in global food losses could lead to an 11% reduction in hunger and a 4% reduction in child malnutrition worldwide. In Congo, a 48% reduction in postharvest tomato loss alone could provide a daily supply of vitamin A for up to 1.1 million children. For Congolese smallholder farmers, this 50% loss of fruits and vegetables results in a 25% loss of their annual income.
The high rate of postharvest losses is due to a combination of factors, including the lack of affordable cold storage at key points in the food supply chain and a lack of knowledge about proper harvesting and postharvest handling.
In my pilot community here in Congo alone, more than 5,000 smallholder farmers lose nearly US$1 million each year due to postharvest losses.
To address this infrastructure and information gap, we aim to provide two technological interventions that are accessible to them:
1) A decentralized, cost-effective, and efficient solar-powered micro-cooling station at the farm level, which can be used by a farmer group or cooperative. 2) A market analysis software tool, in the form of a mobile application or SMS service…
Solution Overview:
We are creating a community storage unit where farmers do not need to pay the entire cost upfront and do not require expertise related to unit maintenance. Furthermore, by making the technology solar-powered, we ensure that our solution is a net positive for the environment, storing and preserving perishable food 24/7, extending its shelf life from 2 days to 21 days.

Our innovation is a 100% solar-powered cold storage preservation technology that extends the shelf life of perishable products from the usual 2 days to 21 days, helping them reduce losses by 90%. We offer solar-powered refrigerated coolers and transport solutions to smallholder farmers, fishermen, fish farmers, and poultry farmers across Central Africa. Our end-to-end cold chain logistics solution uses a technology platform to align supply (fish catch) with demand (rural and urban customers), improving efficiency and reducing waste throughout the value chain.

Our solution was designed to help smallholder farming communities reduce GHG emissions by avoiding post-harvest losses through solar energy. This represents a substantial step towards decarbonization in the community. The funds will be used to create community storage centers in other communities in the region.
Each hub consists of:
Cold Room: A 10-foot-long, 10-foot-wide, and 7-foot-high, 120 mm insulated cold room panel with a stainless steel floor. It contains approximately 3 tons of perishable goods arranged in 150 units, 20 kg plastic crates, stacked on the ground.
Refrigeration Unit: An energy-efficient, single-unit refrigeration unit powered by R290 (propane) refrigerant for 24/7 refrigeration, using 658 W/h. The temperature is adjustable from -5 to +15°C.
Solar Power: Provided by rooftop solar panels generating 6 kW/h, connected to a set of deep-cycle batteries and inverters. The generated power operates the hub in all weather conditions.
Service: We operate a simple pay-as-you-go model. Farmers and vendors pay 250 CFA, or 50 USD, to store a 20 kg crate per day. The hubs are operated by our hub operators.
Education: We educate users on best practices for handling fruits and vegetables after harvest.
Solution Provider(s): GreenBox™ Solutions a Congolese climate-tech and agritech enterprise specializing in solar-powered cold chain systems, sustainable agriculture, and market data tools, Department of Agriculture and Fisheries, a government agency supporting agricultural policy and farmer development, Department of Tourism and Environment a government agency promoting environmental sustainability, Sanford State University an academic and research institution, Local governments supporting smallholder farmer groups and cooperatives, Cold chain component suppliers private sector partners providing refrigeration technology. Solar equipment suppliers, renewable energy sector partners, Banks and donors financial institutions supporting access to capital, Haier Biomedical International a global manufacturer of cold chain and biomedical equipment, Alliance for Rural Electrification an international association promoting renewable energy access, Royal Academy of Engineering a UK-based institution advancing engineering solutions, RES4Africa Foundation a nonprofit fostering renewable energy in Africa, AFSIA (Africa Solar Industry Association), an industry body promoting solar solutions, World Economic Forum’s Generation Restoration Youth Challenge a global initiative for ecosystem restoration. The French Development Agency is a development finance institution supporting sustainable projects.
Implementation location(s): Republic of the Congo – implemented in Brazzaville, Pointe-Noire, Dolisie, Nkayi, and surrounding rural farming communities in the Pool, Bouenza, and Kouilou departments.
Implementation timeline(s): Pilot launched in July 2023 and ongoing, with phased expansion planned through December 2026.
Duration to pilot in a new geography: 4–6 months, including site assessment, stakeholder engagement, infrastructure setup, community training, and operational testing before full-scale deployment.
SDGs addressed: SDG 1 (No Poverty);SDG 2 (Zero Hunger);SDG 13 (Climate Action);
Desired impact:
Reduce post-harvest food losses for smallholder farmers by at least 60% through affordable, solar-powered cold storage.

Increase farmer incomes by 30–50% via extended shelf life, better market access, and reduced spoilage.

Cut greenhouse gas (GHG) emissions by preventing food waste, targeting over 1,500 tonnes of CO₂e avoided annually by 2026.

Improve rural livelihoods by creating 500+ green jobs in cold chain operation, maintenance, and logistics.

Strengthen climate resilience in rural agricultural communities through decentralized renewable energy solutions.

Key Achievements/Impacts to Date

Deployed 3 operational pilot GreenBox units in Congo, serving over 1,200 farmers and market vendors.

Reduced post-harvest losses by 35% in the pilot communities within the first year.

Enabled farmers to access premium urban markets, increasing average household income by ~25%.

Avoided an estimated 420 tonnes of CO₂e GHG emissions in the first 12 months of operation.

Trained 50+ youth and women as operators, technicians, and data managers for the cold storage network.
Key technologies:
GreenBox™ leverages several key technologies to optimize cold chain management and market access:

Solar Energy Technology: 100% off-grid solar-powered refrigeration units for sustainable, reliable cooling in remote areas.

Internet of Things (IoT): Sensors monitor temperature, humidity, and storage conditions in real time, ensuring optimal preservation of perishables.

Data Analytics & Market Intelligence: A digital platform analyzes supply and demand data, providing farmers with price forecasts, inventory tracking, and market insights.

Mobile Applications: User-friendly apps deliver alerts, storage advice, and market info directly to farmers’ smartphones.

Cloud Computing: Centralized data storage and processing enable scalable access and coordination across dispersed cold chain nodes.

Demand-Driven Logistics Platform: Aligns supply from producers with urban and rural demand, minimizing waste and optimizing distribution routes.

Together, these technologies enable GreenBox™ to provide an affordable, clean-energy-powered, and data-driven cold chain solution tailored to smallholder farmers and fishermen in underserved regions.
Unique Characteristics:
GreenBox™ stands out due to several unique and innovative characteristics:

100% Solar-Powered Cold Storage: Unlike traditional cold chains relying on grid electricity, our solution operates fully off-grid using clean, renewable solar energy, enabling access in remote, underserved rural areas.

Integrated IoT Monitoring & Market Intelligence: Our units collect real-time data on temperature, humidity, and produce quality, feeding into a digital platform that provides farmers with demand forecasts, price trends, and storage alerts, empowering smarter decision-making.

Pay-As-You-Store Business Model: Flexible, affordable subscription and pay-per-use options remove upfront investment barriers for smallholder farmers and SMEs, ensuring inclusivity and scalability.

End-to-End Cold Chain Logistics: We align supply (farmers, fishers) directly with demand (retailers, consumers) via a data-driven platform, minimizing waste and improving market access and price realization.

Community-Centric Operations: Our model emphasizes local ownership and employment, especially empowering women as operators and revenue collectors, strengthening socioeconomic impact.

Climate-Resilient & Circular Economy Approach: By drastically reducing post-harvest losses and methane emissions and partnering for recycling organic waste into feed/fertilizer, we support sustainability throughout the food system.

Together, these factors make GreenBox™ a pioneering, holistic solution bridging technology, finance, and community empowerment in cold chain access.
Sustainable Change:
The intervention involves installing and commissioning 20 GreenBoxes (measuring 10 feet in length, 10 feet in width, and 7 feet in height), each containing and cooling 3 tons of food per day, in 10 high-potential food production and consumption clusters in Congo, to serve 2,000 farmers and vendors, with 100 users per hub.
The market system's transformation will allow smallholder farmers, retailers, and wholesalers to access a cold room to store their fresh fruit and vegetable harvests once they are picked from the fields and also once they reach the external market.
Improving access to growth through this system will enable smallholder farmers to maintain the quality of their fresh fruit and vegetables stored in the GreenBoxes for 21 days or more while waiting for the truck to pick up the harvest at the external market. They will not sell their harvest to middlemen to avoid spoilage. Because the quality will be maintained in our temperature-controlled room for a long time, they will be able to bargain prices and sell later when prices rise.
This system improves access to growth for both wholesalers and retailers because the hub acts as a warehouse once the truck arrives at the external market, giving them the opportunity to store and maintain the quality of their fresh fruits and vegetables for as long as possible. Where possible, it allows them to bargain prices and sell later when prices rise. It also maintains the quality of their unsold and leftover fruits, vegetables, and other perishable goods for more than 21 days, once transferred inside the hub, after being exposed to the outdoors. The resulting change will increase the income of 2,000 users by 50%, providing an additional US$60 in income on top of the current estimated income of US$60, for a total of US$120 per month. This goal will be achieved by simply eliminating the 50% loss of fruits and vegetables due to lack of storage.

Title: Dynamic Emission Factors for an Integrated Net-zero Ecosystem (DEFINE)
Subtitle: Emission factors reflective of the reality of local manufacturing processes and plant-level decarbonization investments for hard-to-abate sectors, facilitating the flow of climate finance for greening sectoral supply chains.
Problem Statement:
We do not have reliable, accurate, granular, and current emission factors for sectoral supply chains. 

Emission factors for most materials and components are static, historic, and aggregate. Most of these are based either on assumptions fed into Life Cycle Assessments; or on a retrospective look at aggregate emissions calculations for ‘major product output’ or the like. These static, historic, and aggregate emission factors are not reflective of regional contexts, decarbonization investments, differing processes, and other significant factors affecting the emissions intensity. 

These unaddressed differences in methodologies, assumptions, technology adoption, and documentation of actual processes lead to missed opportunities for companies making investments to decarbonize production processes. As a result, one is unable to make a business case for decarbonization investments. Simply put, static, historic, aggregate emission factors are a disincentive for companies to decarbonize their production and operations. 

In turn, these players miss out on sustainability-linked bonds and other climate finance instruments and grants while their downstream partners also suffer. For instance, real estate developers may not have the visibility of the process used to manufacture the recycled steel that they are procuring and hence miss out on accurately reporting lower embodied carbon in their constructions, losing eligibility for green certifications, sustainability-linked loans, or preferential procurement from climate-conscious buyers. This lack of transparency undermines both the financial incentives for cleaner producers and the decarbonization goals of downstream sectors, creating a systemic barrier to scaling climate-positive investments across the value chain.
Solution Overview:
Dynamic Emission Factors for Integrated Net-zero Ecosystems (DEFINE) is a digital platform designed to provide precise emissions measurement and improve decarbonization transparency for India’s hard-to-abate sectors. Unlike static emission factors, DEFINE uses detailed process data, regional variables (energy mix, fuel, transport), and real-time decarbonization inputs to produce plant- and process-specific emission factors. This dynamic approach captures the actual impact of cleaner production and carbon reduction efforts, including those made by MSMEs often overlooked in traditional systems.

By leveraging digital traceability, IoT, and advanced analytics, DEFINE enables verified emission reductions at their source, unlocking access to sustainability-linked bonds, green loans, and climate finance through audit-ready disclosures. For downstream users such as real estate and infrastructure firms, DEFINE highlights lower embodied carbon in procured materials, facilitating credible climate impact reporting, preferential financing, and green certification. The platform bridges information gaps across supply chains, linking upstream investments with downstream reporting and climate finance, thus accelerating climate-positive action and industrial decarbonization.

DEFINE’s multi-source data architecture combines satellite remote sensing from Sentinel-2A/B, Landsat 8/9, and MODIS Terra/Aqua for high-resolution land surface temperature and thermal anomaly data. Ground station weather networks (nearly 16,000 globally) enhance these measurements through Kalman filtering, correcting biases, and improving accuracy. Historical climate data from NASA GISTEMP v5 provides long-term baselines for anomaly detection.

The methodology involves calculating Thermal Anomaly Indexes from satellite spectral bands, converting these to Land Surface Temperatures via machine learning models, and fusing data with ground measurements. Climate science models, including radiative forcing equations, translate greenhouse gas concentration changes into temperature anomalies. Forecasting uses Bayesian time-series modeling (AWS Prophet) to generate 1-, 3-, 5-, and 10-year predictive trends. Outputs include asset-level temperature anomaly forecasts, risk maps, and scenario analyses aligned with TCFD, CDP, IFRS S2, EU CSRD, and carbon pricing mechanisms.

DEFINE also integrates plant-specific process data, local energy profiles, and logistical details to produce actionable dynamic emission factors and climate risk metrics, supporting sustainability reporting, green finance, and asset resilience.

The platform has been socialized extensively with government bodies such as the Ministries of Housing and Urban Affairs, Steel, Power, Bureau of Energy Efficiency, and civil society organizations, including The Energy and Resources Institute and the International Solar Alliance. Industry partners engaged range from Oberoi Realty, Godrej Properties, Air India, to Siemens. Key institutional collaborators include Confederation of Indian Industry, World Wildlife Fund-Indian Green Steel Coalition, and Indian Green Building Council, with academic partnerships from the Indian Institute of Technology (IIT) Delhi and IIT Bombay. An exhaustive list of stakeholders can be found in Question 30.

In climate philanthropy, DEFINE collaborates with the International Finance Corporation, the Sustainability, Equity, and Diversity Fund, and India Climate Collaborative. Oberoi Realty seeded the platform’s initial development, facilitating integration of 30+ steel and cement plants. Today, DEFINE hosts data from 253 Indian steel plants, with ongoing CSR funding discussions to expand its reach.

The formal launch of DEFINE as a Digital Public Good (DPG) is planned for Q4 2025, involving high-level sector committees, media, and industry leaders. Sector-specific committees will serve as ambassadors, promoting broad adoption and driving systemic decarbonization across India’s industrial landscape.
