Title: Mosabi's AI and LLM-Powered Digital Learning for Inclusive MSME Finance
Subtitle: Mosabi empowers grassroots MSMEs with AI-driven, localized microlearning and financial product access to boost livelihoods, resilience, and digital inclusion.
Problem Statement: Grassroots MSMEs and informal sector entrepreneurs in emerging markets face systemic barriers to economic empowerment. They lack access to affordable finance, digital tools, and skills, and traditional training is analog, costly, and not scalable. Financial institutions see them as high risk and expensive to serve, creating cycles of exclusion that disproportionately affect women, youth, and rural populations.
Solution Overview:
Mosabi is an AI-driven, mobile-first edtech-fintech platform that bridges digital upskilling with access to responsible financial services. Through interactive, TikTok-style microlearning in local languages, we provide MSMEs with practical skills for business growth, money management, and digital literacy. Our patented machine learning engine personalizes journeys, links learners to financial products, and generates alternative data that supports creditworthiness and product matching. Mosabi's platform boosts financial decision-making, product access and engagement, and overall financial health.

The omnichannel platform works on smartphones, feature phones, and chatbots, ensuring accessibility for low-literacy and rural users. Gamified assessments, surveys, and chat interfaces drive engagement and monitor impact. We collaborate with banks, fintechs, MFIs, telcos, and NGOs to embed Mosabi into existing ecosystems, lowering customer acquisition costs for providers while empowering end-users. Proven partnerships with UNDP, UNCDF, World Bank Group, FINCA, Société Générale, and local NGOs demonstrate scalability across Africa, Asia, and Latin America.
Solution Provider(s): Mosabi Inc. (U.S. Public Benefit Corporation) is the entity submitting this application, and we leverage partnerships for success in line with SDG 17, recognizing that collaboration is essential for inclusive digital economies. Our model integrates financial providers and fintechs, distribution partners, public sector bodies, and content and research collaborators to ensure lasting impact. We work with banks, microfinance institutions, fintechs, and telecoms such as Société Générale, FINCA Impact Finance, Orange, Ecobank, Santander, and Women’s World Banking to expand responsible product access and reduce customer acquisition costs. We partner with development organizations, NGOs, and multilateral agencies including UNCDF, UNDP, the World Bank, World Food Programme, CAFOD, Jersey Overseas Aid, Trócaire, Irish Aid, USAID, World Vision, Cordaid, and IFAD to extend reach and scale among grassroots entrepreneurs, women, and youth. We also align with public sector institutions to embed our approach within national strategies, including collaboration with AFI, the Alliance for Financial Inclusion, and their member central banks and ministries of finance to advance responsible policy frameworks for financial literacy and inclusion. Finally, we collaborate with content and research partners such as the Financial Alliance for Women and Cenfri, alongside local MSME associations and universities, to co-develop curricula, metrics, and consumer protection frameworks. This blended partnership model ensures that Mosabi connects digital upskilling directly to financial inclusion while creating sustainable, systemic impact at scale.
Implementation location(s): Mosabi has been implemented in Sierra Leone, Ghana, Kenya, Malawi, Zambia, Senegal, and Rwanda, and has pilot initiatives in Latin America and Asia.
Implementation timeline(s): Operations began in 2019 and continue to the present. Country programs typically span 12–36 months with ongoing scaling across regions.
Duration to pilot in a new geography: 6–12 months, covering contextual research, curriculum localization, partnership onboarding, and digital deployment.
SDGs addressed: SDG 1 (No Poverty);SDG 8 (Decent Work and Economic Growth);SDG 15 (Life on Land);
Desired impact: Mosabi’s objective is to democratize financial literacy and digital access for grassroots MSMEs, women, and youth, equipping them to grow resilient livelihoods. To date, Mosabi has reached over 225,000 learners across 7+ countries, with results showing a 70% increase in user incomes, a doubling of savings frequency, and 25% fewer defaults for partner institutions. Our measurable impacts include improved household resilience, stronger MSME revenues, and increased access to credit, savings, and insurance products for excluded populations. By 2027, we aim to expand to 20 countries and 1 million learners.
Key technologies: Mosabi is built as an AI-driven "nerve center" learning management system powered by a cloud-based content delivery network and analytics engine running entirely on Google Cloud Platform. Our architecture leverages machine learning, natural language processing, and large language models (LLMs for inclusion) to personalize learning journeys for underserved MSMEs, tailoring content in local languages and contexts. The omnichannel platform is accessible through Android and KaiOS apps, a mobi-site, desktop portal, and chatbots on WhatsApp, Facebook Messenger, USSD, and SMS, making it inclusive even for low-literacy and low-connectivity users. Core technologies include Google Dialogflow for conversational interfaces, Firebase for content storage and analytics, BigQuery for real-time data insights, and Cloud Firestore for scalability. Our stack also integrates Node.js, Git, TypeScript, React.js, RESTful APIs, Python, R, TensorFlow, and PyTorch for advanced AI and machine learning capabilities, as well as Kubernetes and Apache Spark for deployment and data processing. This combination of cloud infrastructure, AI/ML engines, and inclusive LLMs ensures that Mosabi can scale efficiently, deliver locally relevant microlearning, and generate alternative data for financial inclusion.
Unique Characteristics:
Mosabi uniquely integrates financial education with direct product access through AI-powered matching. Unlike edtechs, we link training with real financial services; unlike fintechs, we embed consumer protection and learning. Our patented model combines behavioral data, gamified engagement, and financial health scoring to create a virtuous cycle benefiting both MSMEs and service providers. This blended edtech–fintech approach is distinctive in scalability, trust-building, and last-mile accessibility.

The speed of inclusive fintech innovation can be breakneck, but central banks and ministries of finance haven't always had the capacity to keep pace. Many new platforms process a tremendous amount of personal data, but client protection and data privacy laws often aren't evolving quickly enough to keep them in check. We have embraced the responsibility to address them head-on. Mosabi even helps our partners deliver better client protection and customer empowerment as part of our core value proposition.
Sustainable Change: Mosabi’s theory of change centers on building knowledge, confidence, and trust so excluded MSMEs become informed participants in digital economies. As entrepreneurs upskill and access products, they improve resilience, incomes, and competitiveness. Service providers reduce costs and risks, expanding services to underserved segments. Over time, inclusive ecosystems emerge, where better-informed consumers demand transparency and innovation, and providers meet those expectations. This systemic shift generates long-term economic empowerment, reduced inequalities, and sustainable digital inclusion.
Funding Sources: Mosabi’s work has been funded through blended finance: impact investment (Finnovista, Startupbootcamp, Grey Matters Capital, Village Capital, Acumen, and the Luxembourg House of Finance & Technology; philanthropic investment and donor grants (UNCDF, World Bank, Sida, GIZ, Jersey Overseas Aid, CAFOD); private sector partnerships (banks, MFIs, fintechs, telcos); and B2B SaaS licensing of the Mosabi platform and scoring engines.
Testimonials and Endorsements: Mosabi's logo files and solution images transmitted via email to das@unido.org will also include a list of media and press clippings with stakeholder/beneficiary testimonials and data.
Further comments/feedback:
For social impact metrics, Mosabi tracks an array of indicators aligned with the IRIS initiative of the Global Impact Investing Network (GIIN). They include the increase in earnings of users, the number of local people employed, living standards measurements, baselines, and progress-out-of-poverty indexing (PPI). Other data that informs and teaches our algorithms include customer engagement survey data and livelihood indicators woven throughout Mosabi gamified quizzing. These help us and our stakeholders monitor and measure impact outcomes and track progress against baselines over time.

We’ve built Mosabi’s platform to be able to track, distill, analyze, and report on all of key performance indicators. Mosabi’s partners – including funders and other stakeholders – have dashboard access for real-time insights, reports, and tracking aggregated and disaggregated performance across segments like gender, geography, age, and other cohorts to monitor and evaluate project success. We can share our full, detailed impact reporting framework in subsequent stages.

Mosabi is a foundationally data-driven organization, and although we are an early-stage inclusive fintech, we think we could be part of some of the global dialogues on how to best collaborate and share insightful and actionable data from the sector. We think there would be tremendous value in sharing and disseminating the data insights Mosabi can generate. We already have research and learning outcome partnerships with thought leaders like Cenfri, Alliance for Financial Inclusion, the Injini EdTech Incubator, FinMark Trust, the Busara Center for Behavioral Economics, Financial Sector Deepening Africa, UNCDF, and the Bharat Inclusion Initiative. We are committed to advancing dialogue on learning and skilling outcomes that run parallel to formal education and we share findings and technology with the broader sector. We have contributed to policy framework development and advocacy in numerous countries, and we would be grateful to extend that based on this framework for UNIDO, UNCTAD, UNDCO, ODET, and partners launching the global call for inclusive digital economy solutions.

At Mosabi, we’re both inspired and challenged by the new pathway we have forged.We feel a tremendous responsibility to be learning every day. Accordingly, we have thrust ourselves into sector working groups and task forces for edtech innovation, grassroots entrepreneurship sector reform and advancing financial inclusion. 

As mentioned in an earlier question, the speed of inclusive innovation can be breakneck, but I think it behooves us to pause to make sure approaches are responsible and inclusive. Innovations like ours should be user-centric, accessible, privacy-oriented, and transparent.
Primary thematic focus area: MSME Empowerment & Local Digital Innovation
Summary: Mosabi is an AI-powered platform that integrates digital upskilling with access to financial products, targeting grassroots MSMEs, women, and youth in emerging markets. The platform’s focus on financial inclusion through gamified microlearning and AI-driven financial product matching is innovative and scalable. However, the solution’s reliance on blended finance and partnerships for funding may limit its long-term scalability without securing a consistent financial model.

Title: SUPPORT TO POTENTIAL AND ESTABLISHED NATURE-POSITIVE MICRO, SMALL, AND MEDIUM ENTERPRISES (MSME) IN NIGERIA AND BEYOND
Subtitle: Supporting MSME’s to sustainably run their operations while looking to expand beyond their local areas of operation.
Problem Statement:
● Sustainability is a major challenge post grant disbursement. This project will help nature focused msme’s to develop sustainability systems to ensure that they do not close programs post grant disbursement. Sustainable Development: The project promotes sustainable economic growth by supporting businesses that prioritize environmental well-being. This aligns with national efforts to achieve the Sustainable Development Goals (SDGs).
● Climate Resilience: By building the capacity of nature-positive MSMEs, the project strengthens the economy's ability to adapt to climate-related challenges like floods and land degradation.
● Environmental Protection: The focus on value chain production and market access encourages MSMEs to adopt practices that minimize environmental degradation like pollution and erosion.
● Improved Governance: The project's approach to training and coaching fosters stakeholder engagement and empowers local communities, potentially leading to better governance around environmental issues.
● Economic Growth: By enhancing the competitiveness of MSMEs, the project helps address economic challenges like food insecurity and inequality by creating jobs and improving livelihoods.
Solution Overview:
SPENM Project Overview
The SPENM project, led by the International Trade Facilitators Association (ITFA) under the UNDP/GEF Small Grants Programme, empowers 470 MSMEs across Nigeria’s six geopolitical zones to excel in sustainable, export-oriented trade. By fostering a technology-driven ecosystem, SPENM promotes inclusive market access, environmental stewardship, and systemic change, aligning with UNCTAD’s trade-led development goals and AfCFTA’s intra-African trade objectives.
A. How the Solution Works
SPENM transforms MSMEs into nature-positive trade leaders through an integrated approach:  

Capacity Building: Delivers blended learning (in-person and virtual workshops via Zoom, plus pre-recorded modules) on sustainable production, financial management, marketing, and Fair for Life (FFL) certification. Targets 500+ MSMEs, with 30%+ women-led, and provides accessible online training materials.  
Market Access: A digital market directory by CNE Graphic Studios connects FFL-certified MSMEs to global sustainable markets, supported by virtual matchmaking events, projecting a 10–20% sales increase per business.  
Sustainability: Embeds eco-friendly practices through FFL certification training and digital checklists, achieving 20–30% carbon reduction and enhanced biodiversity per MSME.  
Collaboration: Partners with government, NGOs, and private sectors to align with AfCFTA, ensuring scalability and replication in 10+ Nigerian states and 1–2 West African countries within 5 years.

B. Methodologies and Technologies
SPENM leverages innovative tools and methods:  

Hybrid Training: Combines live Zoom workshops and pre-recorded modules on the digital directory, supporting 500+ MSMEs with accessible content.  
Digital Tools:  
Market Directory: Showcases certified MSMEs, tracks impacts (e.g., sales, carbon reduction), and targets 500+ listings.  
Virtual Trade Fairs: Hosted on Zoom, connects MSMEs to global buyers, projecting 15–20% more export deals.  
Data Analytics: Cloud-based systems monitor KPIs (e.g., 1,000+ jobs, 20% carbon reduction) via surveys and real-time analytics.  
FFL Tools: Digital checklists and apps by NICERT Consulting and Jordbruk Limited streamline certification.


Social Media: Campaigns on Twitter and LinkedIn boost visibility and partnerships, aligning with UNCTAD’s digital trade strategies.

C. Partnerships and Collaboration

Implementation Partners:  
ITFA: Leads project execution and trade facilitation.  
NICERT Consulting and Jordbruk Limited: Provide FFL certification and eco-friendly production expertise.  
Africa Women Business Network (AWBN): Ensures 30%+ women-led MSME participation.  
Leventis Foundation: Supports agricultural training and evaluation.  
CNE Graphic Studios: Develops the digital directory.


Financial and Policy Partners: The Alternative Bank, AFDB, AFREXIM, NEXIM, NEPC, and ECOWAS provide funding and policy alignment for market access and AfCFTA integration.  
Collaboration Model: Formal agreements with NEPC, AWBN, and Abia State, plus a project manual and media campaigns, enable replication. Partnerships with ECOWAS and UNDP/GEF target expansion to 1–2 West African countries within 5 years.
Solution Provider(s): Partnerships  Implementation: ITFA (lead), NICERT, Jordbruk, AWBN (mobilizing women-led MSMEs), Leventis Foundation, CNE Graphic Studios.  Financial/Policy: Alternative Bank, AFDB, AFREXIM, NEXIM , NEPC, ECOWAS.
Implementation location(s): So far, we have engaged with Nature Positve MSMEs and NGOs on a regional basis across all 6 Geopolitical zones in Nigeria. The contact states per zone are as follows;  North Central region A (Nasarawa, Benue, Plateau) hosted by Nasarawa state, North East region (Adamawa, Bauchi, Borno, Gombe, Taraba, and Yobe) hosted by Bauchi state South West region (Ekiti, Lagos, Ogun, Ondo, Osun, and Oyo) hosted by Lagos state North West region (Jigawa, Kaduna, Kano, Katsina, Kebbi, Sokoto, and Zamfara) hosted by Kano state  South East region (Abia, Anambra, Ebonyi, Enugu, and Imo)  South South region (Akwa Ibom, Cross River, Delta, Edo, Rivers, Bayelsa), and we are now set for North Central region B (Niger, Kogi, Kwara and the FCT) hosted by the FCT, Abuja
Duration to pilot in a new geography: 5 years
SDGs addressed: SDG 8 (Decent Work and Economic Growth);SDG 12 (Responsible Consumption and Production);SDG 13 (Climate Action);
Desired impact:
The SPENM program envisions a thriving, self-sustaining ecosystem where nature-positive MSMEs drive environmental restoration, inclusive economic growth, and social equity across Africa. Having successfully completed a national rollout across Nigeria, delivering trainings in all six geopolitical zones and engaging diverse MSMEs in sustainable and fair-trade practices, we are now poised to scale this foundation into a continental model.

Our desired impact is a transformative ripple effect: empowered businesses, resilient ecosystems, and replicable frameworks that redefine “glocal” trade. This next phase amplifies our proven outcomes in Nigeria, targeting 1,000+ certified MSMEs, 2,500+ jobs, and measurable environmental gains across West Africa within 3–5 years.

a. Environmental Regeneration at Scale
SPENM has embedded sustainability into Nigeria’s MSME and NGO sectors, reducing harm and fostering ecosystem health. Extending this impact to West Africa will deepen these outcomes through:
•	Continental Fair for Life (FFL) Adoption: Building on our collaboration with NICERT Consulting and Jordbruk Limited, we aim to certify 1,000+ MSMEs across West Africa, enabling eco-friendly practices that cut carbon footprints by 20–30% per business.
•	Market-Driven Sustainability: Our online directory, developed by CNE Graphic Studios, will evolve into a continental hub promoting certified MSMEs to global eco-conscious buyers. This will incentivize sustainable practices while improving biodiversity metrics by 10–15% across multiple regions.
Impact: A cross-border model where MSMEs lead environmental stewardship, proving that trade and ecology can reinforce each other.

b. Socio-Economic Empowerment Across Borders
Scaling SPENM transforms MSMEs into engines of inclusive growth, replicating Nigeria’s success across West Africa. Key impacts include:
•	Job Creation and Market Access: Expanding to Ghana, Senegal, and Côte d’Ivoire as entry points, we’ll empower 1,000+ MSMEs, create 2,500+ jobs, and prioritize women-led businesses (50%+ participation). Certification will unlock continental and global markets, increasing revenues by 15–25% per business.
•	Resilient Networks: Regional partnerships with trade promotion councils, women’s business networks, Federal Government parastatals, Nigerian and pan-African financial institutions will connect MSMEs to financing and export opportunities. This ensures independent growth, with 10,000+ households benefiting economically.
Impact: A blueprint for inclusive prosperity, demonstrating how national training success in Nigeria scales into continental resilience.

c. Systemic Transformation: Regional Replication and Legacy
SPENM’s model is ready for systemic adoption across Africa.
•Regional Expansion: Using our refined project manual, we will train local trainers in at least 5 West African countries within 5 years. Co-funded partnerships with governments, NGOs, and ECOWAS will ensure efficiency and sustainability.

•Continental Replication: Lessons from West Africa will be extended to East, North and Southern Africa, aligning with AfCFTA’s push for integrated and sustainable trade.

•Policy Advocacy: Documented success stories will support regional and continental policy reforms, including incentives and tax breaks for green MSMEs. Our directory will expand into a continental trade platform, listing 1,000+ certified businesses.
Impact: A replicable ecosystem model, positioning Africa as a global leader in nature-positive trade.

d. Sustaining Impact: Strategic Foundations
To ensure lasting change, scaling integrates:
•Funding Diversification: Mobilizing impact investors, private sector partners, and regional development banks to sustain certifications and directory operations.
•Capacity Building: Equipping regional partners and institutions for continuity, with clear handover strategies.
•Knowledge Sharing: Disseminating manuals and best practices
Key technologies:
a. Digital Market Directory & Online Platform
Developed by CNE Graphic Studios, the directory showcases Fair for Life (FFL)-certified MSMEs, linking them with global eco-conscious buyers. It doubles as a promotional hub and monitoring tool, enhancing visibility, enabling real-time impact tracking, and breaking geographic barriers. With a projected 10–20% sales increase per MSME, it positions 500+ businesses for export readiness.

b. Blended Learning Platform
SPENM combines online modules with in-person workshops, ensuring accessibility for remote MSMEs while catering to diverse learning needs. Training materials remain available on the directory for refreshers, creating a lasting knowledge base. This inclusive model targets 1,000+ MSMEs (50%+ women-led), boosting trade capacity and resilience.

c. Virtual Matchmaking Platforms
By hosting virtual trade fairs and investor linkages, SPENM connects MSMEs with buyers and partners in a cost-effective, eco-friendly way. This expands market opportunities for underserved regions and is projected to increase export deals by 15–20% per MSME.

d. Data Management & Monitoring Tools
Cloud-based tools integrated with the directory track compliance, job creation (1,000+), and environmental benefits (20–30% carbon reduction). Real-time analytics ensure data-driven decisions, transparency, and accountability.

e. Certification Support (FFL Integration).
Digital checklists and coaching tools developed with NICERT Consulting and Jordbruk Limited simplify audits and guide MSMEs through certification. This makes global standards more affordable and scalable, embedding sustainability into small business practices.
Unique Characteristics:
a. Hybrid “Glocal” Business Model with Fair for Life Certification 
SPENM integrates global fairtrade standards, specifically Fair for Life (FFL) certification administered by Ecocert, into a locally tailored training and coaching model for MSMEs. This “glocal” approach equips Nature positive MSMEs to meet international market demands while addressing Nigeria’s environmental and social contexts.
Unlike traditional MSME support programs focusing solely on local markets, SPENM’s FFL integration (developed with NICERT Consulting and Jordbruk Limited) ensures nature-positive MSMEs achieve globally recognized certifications, enhancing credibility and access to eco-conscious markets. This differentiates SPENM by bridging local production with global trade, targeting a 10-20% revenue increase per certified business.

b. Technology-Driven Market Directory for Scalability and Transparency 
The online market directory, developed by CNE Graphic Studios, is a digital platform that lists FFL-certified MSMEs, connects them to global buyers, and enables real-time monitoring and evaluation. It serves as both a promotional tool and a data hub, tracking impacts like job creation and carbon reductions.
This directory is not just a marketplace but a sustainability engine, integrating promotion, monitoring, and market access in one platform. Unlike typical trade directories, it prioritizes nature-positive businesses, using data analytics to ensure compliance and measure impact. This dual-purpose innovation sets SPENM apart from conventional trade facilitation programs.

c. Strategic Partnership Ecosystem for Mobilization and Replication 
SPENM leverages a network of partners Nigeria Export Promotion Council, AWBN, State governments, Federal Government Parastatals, Pan African Financial Institutions like Afrexim, and private firms like NICERT and Jordbruk to mobilize MSMEs, disseminate knowledge, and ensure post-project continuity. This ecosystem approach formalizes commitments to scale training and certification across the 36 states and potentially West Africa.
The partnership model is differentiated by its multi-stakeholder integration, combining government, private sector, and community networks to create a self-sustaining support system for women-led MSMEs. This contrasts with siloed programs, as SPENM’s collaborative framework ensures scalability and local ownership, with 30%+ participation from women entrepreneurs.
Sustainable Change:
The SPENM program leverages an integrated, technology-driven ecosystem to position MSMEs as leaders in nature-positive, export-oriented trade. By combining a digital market directory, blended learning platform, virtual matchmaking events, data analytics tools, and Fair for Life (FFL) certification support, SPENM enables small businesses to compete globally while advancing sustainability. Building on the successful national rollout across Nigeria, the program now seeks to expand across West Africa, targeting 500+ certified MSMEs, creating 1,000+ jobs, and delivering measurable environmental gains that directly advance SDGs 8, 12, and 13.

a. Breaking Barriers to Global Trade
SPENM removes the structural barriers that limit MSMEs’ access to international markets. The digital market directory, developed by CNE Graphic Studios, together with virtual matchmaking platforms, connects over 500 MSMEs, including 30%+ women-led and rural enterprises to global eco-conscious buyers. Supported by partnerships with the Nigeria Export Promotion Council, AWBN, and other stakeholders, these tools are projected to increase sales by 10–20% per business. By aligning with UNCTAD’s eTrade for All initiative, SPENM ensures inclusive digital trade participation, enabling underserved communities to integrate into the global “glocal” economy.

b. Embedding Sustainability in Trade Practices
SPENM makes sustainability a measurable standard rather than an aspiration. Through real-time data analytics integrated into the directory, businesses track environmental performance, achieving an estimated 20–30% carbon footprint reduction per MSME. With technical support from NICERT Consulting and Jordbruk Limited, MSMEs achieve Fair for Life (FFL) certification, ensuring compliance with international sustainability benchmarks. By promoting FFL-certified products on its directory, SPENM incentivizes responsible production and aligns with UNCTAD’s BioTrade principles, targeting a 10–15% biodiversity improvement in local ecosystems.

c. Scaling Capacity for Lasting Impact
Capacity building remains central to SPENM’s strategy. The blended learning platform delivered through a combination of online modules and in-person workshops equips 1,000+ MSMEs across Nigeria and West Africa with the skills needed for global competitiveness. Digital certification support tools streamline FFL compliance, lowering costs for small businesses. This approach mirrors UNCTAD’s TrainForTrade model, ensuring that trained entrepreneurs become ambassadors of sustainability, replicating best practices across regions and embedding long-term resilience in the MSME ecosystem.

d. Driving Policy Impact with Evidence
SPENM’s data-driven approach provides policymakers with robust evidence of socio-economic and environmental outcomes: 1,000+ jobs created, 5,000+ households uplifted, and measurable biodiversity gains. These verified results strengthen advocacy for incentives such as tax breaks for green-certified businesses, embedding sustainability into Nigeria’s trade policies. Aligned with the AfCFTA agenda, SPENM contributes to building an enabling policy environment that promotes intra-African trade while ensuring nature-positive outcomes. Partnerships with state governments, and Federal Government parastatals, reinforce this systemic shift.

e. Future-Proofing Growth Across Africa
SPENM’s model is designed for scalability and replication. By mobilizing partnerships with ECOWAS, impact investors, and pan-African trade institutions, the program ensures continuity through blended financing models impact investments, private sector co-funding, and market-driven revenue streams. Best practices will be shared through the UNDP/GEF-SGP networks, enabling replication in 1–2 West African countries within 5 years. Name of your organization: KMS ETH Health Trading S.C (TENAWO Digital Health )
Title: TENAWO: Seamless e-Pharmacy, Telemedicine, and Homecare Solutions
Subtitle: TENAWO Digital Health connects patients with nearby pharmacies, doctors, and homecare providers through an AI-powered platform, improving access to affordable and timely healthcare services.
Problem Statement: Millions in Ethiopia face limited access to essential medicines and quality healthcare due to fragmented supply chains, insufficient healthcare providers, and high costs. This disproportionately affects chronic patients, pregnant women, and children, leading to worsened health outcomes and increased preventable complications.
Solution Overview:
How the Solution Works

TENAWO Digital Health is a location-based platform integrating e-pharmacy, telemedicine, and homecare services. Users access the platform via mobile or web apps to search for nearby pharmacies, consult doctors remotely, and schedule homecare visits. The platform’s AI-powered algorithms match patients with the closest verified providers within a 500-meter radius, prioritizing urgency and user needs to ensure timely service delivery. Medication orders are processed through partner pharmacies and delivered via a reliable logistics network, while telemedicine consultations and homecare services provide continuous care, especially for chronic and vulnerable patients.

Methodologies and Technologies Used

The platform leverages AI and machine learning for real-time service matching, demand forecasting, and personalized patient engagement. It uses GPS location services for precise proximity matching and integrates secure digital payment systems for seamless transactions. Data privacy and regulatory compliance are ensured through encryption and adherence to Ethiopian health data laws.

Partnerships and Collaboration Models

TENAWO collaborates with a wide network of 550 doctors, 445 pharmacies, 10 hospitals, 39 clinics, 3 diagnostic labs, and 99 distributors. These partnerships are formalized through MOUs, enabling coordinated service delivery and shared logistics. B2B collaborations with employers, insurance providers, and NGOs extend healthcare access to larger populations through subscription models. Continuous engagement with government bodies such as the Ministry of Health (MOH) and Ethiopian Food and Drug Authority (EFDA) ensures regulatory alignment and support.
Solution Provider(s): 	550 Licensed Doctors — Medical professionals across Ethiopia providing telemedicine and clinical consultations 	445 Partner Pharmacies — Retail and wholesale pharmacies collaborating on medicine supply and e-pharmacy services 	10 Hospitals — Including public and private hospitals partnering on referrals and patient care 	39 Specialized Clinics — Offering specialized medical services and diagnostics 	3 Diagnostic Laboratory Centers — Providing lab testing and integration with telemedicine services 	99 Medical Distributors — Logistics and supply chain partners ensuring medicine availability and last-mile delivery 	Ministry of Health (MOH), Ethiopia — Regulatory authority supporting digital health initiatives 	Ethiopian Food and Drug Authority (EFDA) — Regulatory body overseeing pharmaceutical compliance
Implementation location(s): TENAWO Digital Health has been implemented primarily in Addis Ababa, Ethiopia, with services operational across major urban and peri-urban areas within the city. Plans are underway to expand to additional regions, including Bahir Dar, Mekelle, and Hawassa, to increase healthcare access in Ethiopia’s growing urban centers.
Implementation timeline(s): The implementation of TENAWO Digital Health began in January 2023 and is currently ongoing. Key milestones include the platform launch in March 2023, user growth and partnership expansions throughout 2023, with continued scaling planned through 2025 and beyond.
Duration to pilot in a new geography: The estimated duration to pilot TENAWO Digital Health in a new geography is 4 to 6 months. This timeframe includes initial stakeholder engagement, platform localization, onboarding local healthcare providers and pharmacies, community outreach, and monitoring early user adoption and service delivery to ensure effective implementation and impact.
SDGs addressed: SDG 3 (Good Health and Well-being);SDG 9 (Industry, Innovation, and Infrastructure);SDG 11 (Sustainable Cities and Communities);
Desired impact:
Solution Objectives

•	Improve access to essential medicines, telemedicine, and homecare services for underserved populations in Ethiopia.
•	Reduce patient wait times and out-of-pocket healthcare costs.
•	Enhance medication adherence and continuity of care, especially for chronic patients, pregnant women, and malnourished children.
•	Strengthen healthcare supply chains through AI-driven demand forecasting and efficient logistics.
•	Support Ethiopia’s progress toward Universal Health Coverage (UHC) by leveraging digital innovation.

Key Achievements and Impacts

•	Served over 42,000 clients with more than 71,000 bookings processed in the first 12 months.
•	Reduced medicine delivery times by up to 40% in pilot areas.
•	Achieved $65,000 revenue with sustainable operations at a $5,000 monthly burn rate.
•	Established partnerships with 550 doctors, 445 pharmacies, 10 hospitals, and 99 distributors.
•	Created employment opportunities for over 30 healthcare and logistics professionals.
•	Improved medication adherence by 30% among chronic patients during pilot programs.
Key technologies:
	Artificial Intelligence (AI): Powers real-time service matching, demand forecasting, personalized patient engagement, and predictive analytics for inventory management.
	Geolocation Services (GPS): Enables precise location-based matching of patients with nearby pharmacies, doctors, and homecare providers within a 500-meter radius.
	Mobile and Web Applications: User-friendly platforms designed for accessibility on low-bandwidth networks and diverse devices, supporting multilingual interfaces.
	Secure Digital Payments: Integrated payment gateways facilitating safe and convenient transactions.
	Cloud Computing: Ensures scalable, reliable, and secure data storage and processing.
	Data Encryption & Privacy Protocols: Complies with Ethiopian health data regulations, protecting sensitive patient information.
Unique Characteristics: TENAWO Digital Health stands out through its comprehensive integration of e-pharmacy, telemedicine, and homecare services within a single, location-based digital platform—offering a one-stop solution unmatched by competitors who typically focus on a single service. Our AI-powered real-time service matching ensures users connect with the nearest verified providers, reducing wait times and improving care continuity. The hybrid distribution model combines digital ordering with an on-ground logistics network for reliable last-mile delivery, crucial in underserved urban areas. We also employ a flexible financing mechanism, including pay-per-service and B2B subscription models, enabling broad access across individual and institutional customers. Strategic partnerships with over 1,000 healthcare providers and distributors and regulatory alignment with the Ministry of Health and EFDA strengthen trust and scalability. This blend of technological innovation, operational efficiency, and collaborative ecosystem makes TENAWO a pioneering digital health solution in Ethiopia and beyond.
Sustainable Change:
TENAWO Digital Health contributes to sustainable, systemic change by addressing fundamental barriers in healthcare access through digital innovation. By connecting patients, providers, and pharmacies via an AI-driven, location-based platform, it improves timely access to essential medicines and quality care, reducing preventable complications and hospitalizations. This leads to healthier communities and decreased strain on overburdened health facilities.

The solution strengthens healthcare supply chains through predictive demand forecasting and efficient logistics, enhancing medicine availability and reducing wastage. By fostering partnerships across public and private sectors, TENAWO builds a resilient, scalable healthcare ecosystem that integrates with national health strategies and regulatory frameworks.

Over time, increased digital health adoption empowers patients with better self-management tools, promotes data-driven decision-making among providers, and encourages investment in health infrastructure. This systemic shift advances Ethiopia’s Universal Health Coverage goals and serves as a replicable model for other resource-limited settings, driving long-term equitable health outcomes
Funding Sources: To date, TENAWO Digital Health (KMS ETH Health Trading S.C) has been entirely self-funded through generated revenue, achieving approximately $65,000 USD in revenue over the last 12 months. No external grants, investments, or donor funding have been utilized in the development or implementation phases. This revenue-driven model demonstrates early market validation and operational sustainability.

Title: Dosy: Empowering Women Through Inclusive E-Mobility and Digital Access
Subtitle: Dosy is a digital platform empowering women with e-mobility training, job access, and sustainable transport solutions, bridging gender gaps in the digital and green economy.
Problem Statement: In many of the MENA countries, women experience limited access to cost-effective, safe, sustainable, and reliable transportation. This is due in part to existing gender biases, safety concerns and limited digital and mobility skills. Transportation is necessary for women to reach education, jobs and economic opportunities. Women also tend to be excluded from participation in the growing green and digital economies because they are underrepresented in a tech-driven mobility sector and are limited in training. The compounded impact of digital exclusion, lack of employment and climate change means there is an urgent need for inclusive climate smart mobility solutions that are designed for women.
Solution Overview:
Dosy is a tech-based platform that is creating women-empowered mobility training offerings, accessible, affordable, and eco-friendly in Egypt and the MENA region. Dosy will allow women to access a mobile application and website to book their scooter and bicycle riding lessons with qualified female trainers at their own location at a time that fits their schedule. The platform will also connect them to maintenance and spare parts service providers, and electric vehicle services while promoting green transportation alternatives.

We use location-based matching, online payments, and scheduling tools, plus data analytics to track impact and improve services.

We partner with electric scooter brands, maintenance providers, and delivery services, and collaborate with NGOs and women-focused programs to scale our reach.
Solution Provider(s): Dosy for Micro-Mobility Services – social enterprise in the mobility and gender empowerment sector, Glide – electric scooter provider, clean tech and mobility sector, Atlana – scooter maintenance service, transportation and logistics sector, R2S Logistics – courier and delivery service provider, last-mile delivery sector, Local NGOs – supporting women’s economic empowerment and environmental sustainability.
Duration to pilot in a new geography: 3 to 6 months, depending on local partnerships, infrastructure readiness, and community engagement.
SDGs addressed: SDG 5 (Gender Equality);SDG 8 (Decent Work and Economic Growth);SDG 11 (Sustainable Cities and Communities);
Desired impact:
We work to empower women and youth through digital tools and green mobility training, providing practical skills and employment opportunities in the micro-mobility and delivery sectors. We aspire to make transport safer, more inclusive, and sustainable.  

We have already trained more than 7,000 women to ride scooters and bicycles and supported more than 300 women to earn income as certified riding instructors. We are also improving mobility, reducing traffic congestion, and carbon emissions in crowded cities by promoting the use of electric vehicles and bicycles. Our vision is a cleaner, more inclusive future where everyone (especially women) can move freely, work safely and live sustainably.
Key technologies: Our solution utilizes a mobile-based platform to connect users with local female scooter and bicycle trainers. We draw on GPS and geolocation technology to schedule and structure training sessions. We have inclusive tenets that leverage online payments for secure cashless transactions and a simple LMS to provide safety and maintenance tutorials. As we scale, we plan to include AI to customize training paths and optimize route planning for future delivery and ride hailing uses.
Unique Characteristics: Our solution is the first digital platform in Egypt and MENA focused on training women to operate scooters and bicycles, thus creating job opportunities in mobility for women. It is unique because it is women-led, community-based and focuses on closing the gender gap in transportation through local trainers, flexible scheduling and implementation of a door to door service for those who want to learn from home. This mobility training platform combines micro-mobility solutions with digital training and economic empowerment. Our partnership or co-op model with e-scooter, maintenance and delivery operators creates systems for sustainability of our model. Our future ride-hailing feature for women by women will be another distinguishing feature.
Sustainable Change:
We create pathways to women's empowerment with sustainable mobility and generate lasting economic and environmental impact. Training women to ride a scooter or bicycle and linking them to jobs as trainers, and delivery riders helps tackle gender inequity in transportation and employment. As more women become visible on the road, social norms are altered for greater acceptance and participation.

Increased demand helps to preserve local green transport markets (e.g. e-scooters) and decrease traffic and carbon. Our digital platform allows for scale across regions, not replication. Over time, the solution helps to create a self-sustaining ecosystem where women teach, earn, and lead that leads to systematic change in gender, climate, and economic resilience.

Title: FundingPro: AI Platform for Inclusive Access to Grant Funding
Subtitle: AI-powered platform that helps NGOs, MSMEs, and public entities discover, evaluate, and apply for grant funding faster, cheaper, and more inclusively
Problem Statement: Accessing grant funding is a complex, time-consuming, and resource-intensive process—especially for small NGOs, youth-led startups, and public institutions in developing countries. These actors often lack the expertise, language skills, and tools required to identify relevant opportunities, understand eligibility requirements, and draft competitive proposals. As a result, billions in available funding remain inaccessible to those who need it most, reinforcing existing inequalities and excluding grassroots innovators from the global development ecosystem. Manual grant application processes also create bottlenecks, delays, and high consultant costs, making it nearly impossible for low-capacity organizations to compete for funding.
Solution Overview:
FundingPro is an AI-powered, multilingual digital platform that democratizes access to grant funding by automating the most time-consuming and expertise-intensive parts of the grant application process: discovery, eligibility checks, proposal writing, and submission.

How It Works:
Grant Discovery Engine:
Users input basic information (organization type, country, sector), and FundingPro's AI matches them with relevant funding opportunities from a curated, regularly updated database.

Eligibility Check Assistant:
The platform applies 7 smart filters (e.g., geography, sector, legal status, deadlines) to automatically identify which grants a user qualifies for — avoiding wasted time.

AI-Assisted Proposal Drafting:
FundingPro generates drafts of full proposals, budgets, logframes, and cover letters using contextual data from the user and built-in templates aligned with donor preferences (UN, EU, USAID, etc.).

Multilingual Access:
The platform operates in English, Russian, and Uzbek, ensuring accessibility to underrepresented organizations in Central Asia and beyond.

Referral & Training System:
Youth agents and local digital coaches can earn income by onboarding and assisting users, creating a grassroots-led support network.

Methodologies and Technologies:
AI & Natural Language Processing (NLP):
Custom-trained GPT models for grant writing, donor language optimization, and proposal scoring prediction.

No-code + low-code backend:
Built using Bubble, Make, and integrated with Google Workspace and external APIs (UN, Devex, EU portals).

Automated workflows:
Step-by-step guided process from registration to submission, reducing friction and increasing speed by 60–80%.

Data Protection & Compliance:
GDPR-aligned data handling, with encrypted storage and two-factor authentication.

Partnerships and Collaboration Models:
Uzbekistan Creative Association (UzCA):
Provides outreach to NGOs, women entrepreneurs, and creative economy actors in rural and urban regions.

IT Park Uzbekistan:
Supports technical development, testing, and integration with local tech ecosystems.

Ministry of Employment (pilot phase):
Exploratory collaboration for job creation among youth digital agents and co-financing grant training programs.

EU Youth Sounding Board (Advisory):
Informs inclusion frameworks and outreach strategy for vulnerable groups.

Coaching Network (freelancers & NGOs):
Digital navigators and trainers assist organizations in using the platform.

Outcomes to Date:
12 projects supported, totaling $310,000+ in grant wins

Over 300 users registered during beta phase

100+ hours saved per user on average during application cycles

60%+ of users are from rural or underserved areas
Solution Provider(s): Beta Version Solutions LLC – Lead Organization A private digital innovation company based in Uzbekistan, specializing in AI-powered platforms, grant tech, and public sector digitalization. Sector: ICT, e-Governance, Social Impact Tech.  Uzbekistan Creative Association (UzCA) – Strategic Outreach Partner A nonprofit organization working to promote civic engagement, women’s leadership, and creative entrepreneurship across Central Asia. Sector: Civil Society, Creative Economy, Women’s Empowerment.
Implementation location(s): Uzbekistan – pilot activities conducted in Tashkent, Nukus, and Andijon 2025
Implementation timeline(s): April 2024 – ongoing (prototype tested with real users and early adopters in 3 regions of Uzbekistan)
Duration to pilot in a new geography: 3–6 months, depending on the local digital infrastructure and partner availability.
SDGs addressed: SDG 8 (Decent Work and Economic Growth);
Desired impact:
Solution Objectives:
Democratize access to grant funding for NGOs, MSMEs, and public institutions—especially in underserved, rural, and low-income regions.

Reduce time and cost of grant application processes by automating key tasks such as search, eligibility checks, and proposal writing.

Strengthen local ecosystems by enabling inclusive participation in development funding and donor programs.

Promote digital literacy and job creation through a referral model involving youth agents and grant coaches.

Key Achievements and Measurable Impact (to date):
Over $310,000 in grants secured by early users (12 projects funded between 2024–2025)

More than 300 organizations onboarded during prototype testing phase

60–80% average reduction in time required to complete full grant application cycles

30 digital grant coaches trained and earning income via the platform

60% of users are from rural or underrepresented regions

50% of registered users are women- or youth-led organizations

Projected Impact (by 2027):
Reach 1,000 organizations across 5 countries

Facilitate more than $3 million in total grant funding through the platform

Create income-generating opportunities for at least 500 youth agents

Increase funding access for rural and marginalized actors by a factor of five
Key technologies:
FundingPro leverages artificial intelligence and natural language processing to automate grant discovery, eligibility analysis, and proposal drafting. The platform uses large language models trained on real donor data to generate high-quality content aligned with funder expectations.

It is developed on a low-code/no-code technology stack, enabling rapid iteration and customization. The platform supports multilingual access (Uzbek, Russian, English) and provides localized user experiences for diverse audiences.

Cloud-based infrastructure ensures secure data storage, workflow automation, and seamless integration with external grant databases and APIs. All data processing complies with international data protection standards, including GDPR.
Unique Characteristics:
FundingPro stands out through its combination of advanced AI automation, inclusive design, and a decentralized support model that enables grassroots participation in the funding ecosystem.

Unlike traditional grant platforms, FundingPro not only lists opportunities but actively guides users through the full application process using AI-powered tools that generate tailored proposals, budgets, and logical frameworks. Its multilingual interface ensures accessibility for users in non-English-speaking regions, particularly in Central Asia.

A unique feature is the referral and digital agent model, which engages young people and local experts to earn income by onboarding and supporting new users. This creates a community-based distribution channel and enhances digital literacy at the local level.

The platform also offers a freemium model to ensure financial accessibility for underserved actors, while allowing scalability and integration with public procurement or donor systems via API in future phases.

This holistic approach—combining technology, inclusive business models, and community-driven support—makes FundingPro a differentiated solution in the global digital funding space.
Sustainable Change:
FundingPro contributes to sustainable, systemic change by addressing a structural barrier in development financing: the unequal access to funding opportunities due to digital, informational, and capacity gaps.

By automating and localizing the grant application process, the platform empowers underrepresented actors—particularly rural NGOs, youth-led startups, and women’s initiatives—to access resources previously out of reach. This directly increases their participation in the development ecosystem and builds long-term organizational capacity.

The solution activates a broader support infrastructure by training local digital agents who provide ongoing assistance to users, creating employment opportunities and embedding digital skills in communities. As more organizations gain funding, they are able to launch social impact projects, generate jobs, and reinvest in local development.

Over time, this creates a multiplier effect:
More access → more funded projects → stronger grassroots institutions → greater policy influence and resilience.

By shifting from consultant-dependence to self-service empowerment, FundingPro lays the foundation for systemic inclusivity in the global funding landscape.
Funding Sources:
The initial development of FundingPro has been self-funded by its founder through revenue generated from grant consulting services and partnerships with NGOs and development projects. Additional support was provided in-kind through collaborations with local civil society organizations, IT Park Uzbekistan (for mentoring and infrastructure), and contributions from freelance grant writers and digital coaches during the prototype phase.

No institutional or donor funding has been received to date. However, the platform has facilitated over $310,000 in external grant funding for its early users, validating both its impact potential and revenue model.

FundingPro is currently exploring blended financing opportunities, including grants, social impact investment, and strategic public-private partnerships to support its scaling phase.
Testimonials and Endorsements:
While individual testimonials are not yet formally collected, multiple organizations that have used FundingPro have successfully secured funding from international donors, including UNDP, the EU, and the World Water Challenge.

Key project wins, verified through contracts and official announcements, are publicly documented via the platform’s Telegram channel, which serves as a transparent tracker of impact. The channel currently includes updates on over 12 successful grant applications facilitated by FundingPro since 2024, with a total awarded value exceeding $310,000.

Source (public record): https://t.me/+s1LHM2o42AVmNGZi
Primary thematic focus area: MSME Empowerment & Local Digital Innovation
Summary: FundingPro is an AI-driven platform designed to democratize access to grant funding, especially for NGOs, MSMEs, and public entities in underserved regions. The platform automates the grant discovery, eligibility checks, and proposal drafting process, making it easier and more efficient for organizations in rural and marginalized areas to secure funding. With a focus on digital inclusion, FundingPro empowers local communities through a decentralized support model, fostering job creation and strengthening local ecosystems.

Title: Access to Instant Credit to Keep Africa’s Rural Hospital Stocked and Patients Cared, Powered by AI
Subtitle: An AI-powered credit engine embedded in e-pharmacy systems, providing hospitals and pharmacies across Africa with instant, collateral-free financing—purpose-built for the unique needs of healthcare at scale.
Problem Statement:
As a pharmacist, I witnessed firsthand how small clinics and pharmacies struggle to restock medicine because they can’t get affordable loans. Most lenders see them as too risky because they lack formal credit histories. This leads to long wait times—often over 90 days—to access credit, demands for collateral they don’t have, and extremely high interest rates, sometimes above 30%. The result? Providers delay treatment, lose patients, or shut down entirely.

This is a major issue. In Africa, over 350,000 healthcare providers serve more than 500 million people, yet face a $60 billion funding gap due to poor access to credit. The root cause is fragmented data—lenders can’t assess risk properly, so they avoid lending or charge unfair terms- and the most impacted are healthcare providers in underserved communities.

If nothing changes, the problem will grow rapidly. Africa’s healthcare market is projected to grow at 8% CAGR, reaching $133 billion by 2033. But without financing, providers can’t scale to meet demand. Clinics will remain understocked, health systems will be overwhelmed, and millions could be left without care.

That’s why we built 10mg Health—to fix this. We use AI to create real-time credit scores from inventory, repayments, and procurement data, giving providers instant, collateral-free loans—so they can stock up, grow, and serve patients without delay.
Solution Overview:
At 10mg Health, we’ve built an innovative solution called 10mgCredit that helps clinics and pharmacies in Africa get fast, affordable loans to buy medicines. Just like Experian powers credit scores in Europe, we’ve developed from scratch, Africa’s first AI-powered credit rating system-- an API engine for healthcare providers.

Our system looks at real-time data—like how often a clinic orders medicine, how fast they repay, and what they have in stock. Using this data, our AI gives each clinic a credit score instantly. This score helps lenders safely decide who to give a loan to, without asking for collateral or long paperwork. Our technology is built directly into medicine ordering platforms like mPharma and Remedial Health, so when clinics check out, they can simply click “Pay with 10mgCredit” and get approved in minutes.

We’re a lightweight, plug-and-play solution that’s easy to scale. A great example is our work with PNA in Senegal, where we helped secured $40,000 to support medicine supplies for 764 rural hospitals across 263 communities—using cross-border financing from Fintech Farm UK, all within days. We’re the first movers building this kind of healthcare credit infrastructure in Africa. Our goal is to reach 30,000+ providers, serve at least 1 million patients monthly over the next 3 years, helping to close Africa’s $60B healthcare funding gap—so no clinic ever has to turn a patient away because of empty shelves.
Solution Provider(s): Our key partners include mPharma, Remedial Health, PNA Senegal, and Gigon, who are leading health and logistics platforms helping us embed credit directly at the point of medicine purchase. We also partner with lenders like Fintech Farm, Plend (UK), and Credit Direct, who use our AI-powered credit scores to finance verified healthcare providers. Support partners like Techstars FAST Accelerator and Aston University provide strategic guidance, mentorship, and research backing. Together, these partners help us scale safe, data-driven healthcare lending across Africa.
Implementation location(s): Implemented Locations:  Nigeria – Lagos, Abuja, Ibadan, Kano, and other major cities across 25+ states.  Senegal – Dakar, Saint-Louis, and 263 rural communities through partnership with PNA and Gigon.  These locations represent active implementation of 10mgCredit via integrated pharmacy vendors and cross-border financing pilots.
Implementation timeline(s): Timeline of Implementation:  Nigeria: December 2022 – Present  Senegal: August 2024 – Present  These timelines reflect the active deployment and scaling of 10mgCredit across partner platforms in both countries.
Duration to pilot in a new geography: The estimated duration to pilot 10mg Health’s solution in a new geography is 3 to 6 months.  This includes time for:  Partner onboarding with local pharmacy vendors and lenders  Integration of our AI credit engine into procurement systems  Regulatory checks and localization of credit assessment models  Training and onboarding of initial healthcare providers  First loan disbursements and real-time monitoring setup  With existing templates and proven processes, we can move faster where vendor infrastructure already exists.
SDGs addressed: SDG 3 (Good Health and Well-being);SDG 9 (Industry, Innovation, and Infrastructure);SDG 8 (Decent Work and Economic Growth);
Desired impact:
10mg Health wants to make sure no clinic or pharmacy is left without medicine because they can’t get a loan. Our goal is to help small healthcare providers get fast, safe, and affordable loans, with flexible repayments using AI. This way, they can restock medicines, serve more patients, and grow their businesses. We aim to close Africa’s $60 billion healthcare credit gap, improve access to care, and support economic growth in underserved communities.

Connection to the SDGs:

SDG 3 (Good Health and Well-being): We help clinics and pharmacies stay stocked so they can treat more patients. We currently support over 183,000 patients per month, most of whom are women and children.

SDG 8 (Decent Work and Economic Growth): Our loans help healthcare providers grow and hire more workers. This drives local employment, especially in rural areas.

SDG 9 (Industry, Innovation, and Infrastructure): Our platform is building Africa’s first healthcare credit infrastructure—using real-time data and AI to support smart, sustainable lending and insurance policies.


Key Achievements So Far:

$2.47 million disbursed in healthcare loans

<3% default rate, showing safe lending is possible

Active in 2 countries (Nigeria and Senegal)

Over 5,894 healthcare providers onboarded

Supporting 764 hospitals in Senegal across 263 rural communities alone

Enabled cross-border funding of $40,000 through national partnerships with PNA, Senegal

All these impacts are powered by real-time data and AI scoring, making our solution measurable, scalable, and sustainable.
Key technologies:
10mg Health is pioneering a groundbreaking fintech-healthtech innovation by combining Artificial Intelligence, cloud-based APIs, and secure digital payments to create the first AI-powered healthcare credit infrastructure in Africa.

At the core is our AI credit engine, which instantly analyzes real-time data—such as procurement history, repayment patterns, and stock movement—to generate dynamic credit scores for clinics and pharmacies. This replaces outdated manual assessments with fast, data-driven, and objective risk analysis, enabling loans to be disbursed in under 4 minutes with zero collateral. It's a transformative shift from the 90+ day loan delays common today.

Through cloud-based APIs, 10mgCredit seamlessly integrates into procurement platforms like mPharma, Remedial Health, and Gigon, embedding credit access directly at checkout. Combined with machine learning, our system gets smarter with every transaction—reducing defaults (currently <3%), personalizing credit offers, and building predictive models for safe lending.

Secure, digital disbursements ensure full traceability and lender confidence. Altogether, this solution is a highly scalable, replicable, and AI-enhanced financial breakthrough, driving inclusive access to working capital for underserved providers—especially those in rural communities serving women and children. It’s not just innovation—it’s systemic infrastructure for Africa’s healthcare future.
Unique Characteristics: 10mg Health is a breakthrough solution transforming how healthcare providers in Africa access financing. Through its AI-powered credit engine, 10mgCredit enables clinics and pharmacies to get instant, collateral-free loans at the point of purchase—cutting loan approval time from 90+ days to under 4 minutes. By embedding directly into vendor platforms like mPharma and Remedial Health, the platform makes credit as easy as clicking “Pay with 10mgCredit.” What sets it apart is its ability to generate real-time creditworthiness reports from procurement and repayment data, helping lenders make safe, data-driven decisions and maintain a default rate under 3%. This is safe, smart, and scalable lending—helping over 5,000 clinics restock faster, vendors get paid upfront, and lenders access trustworthy borrowers. With a sustainable revenue model and a growing footprint, 10mgCredit is not just solving a financing gap—it’s laying the foundation for Africa’s first healthcare credit infrastructure.
Sustainable Change:
10mgCredit is more than just a lending platform—it’s a game-changer for healthcare financing in Africa. Most clinics and pharmacies, especially in rural and underserved areas, can’t access loans because they lack credit history or collateral. This leads to 90+ day delays from traditional lenders, with lots of paper-works, empty shelves, and inadequate care—especially for women and children, who make up the majority of patients.

What makes 10mgCredit truly impactful is its AI-driven credit scoring engine, similar to Experian in Europe, which enables instant, collateral-free loans that solutions like PayPal and Klarna extract credit data from—often approved in under 4 minutes. The platform is embedded directly into pharmacy vendor systems through cloud-based APIs, so providers can “Pay with 10mgCredit” right at checkout. Our model also includes flexible repayment options, aligned with the clinic’s cash flow—making it  less risky for lenders and safer for borrowers.

We use real-time data—purchase history, inventory movement, and repayment patterns—to continuously train our machine learning models, helping us improve risk profiles and keep defaults below 3%. By offering secure, traceable digital disbursements and repayments, we’re creating a transparent, scalable system that builds trust among lenders, vendors, and healthcare providers.

The result? Clinics stay stocked, vendors get paid upfront, and lenders deploy capital more confidently. Over time, this approach fuels sustainable healthcare delivery, economic mobility, and inclusive growth across Africa—especially in the communities that need it most.

For this unique, scalable solution contributing to sustainable healthcare in Africa, 10mg Health won the 2025 Financial Times Responsible Business Award, the 2024 Aston University Social Innovation Award, and nominated for AMBA-BGC Global Entrepreneur of the Year 2025 and has also been featured by Springwise, Disrupt Africa, Yahoo News, Empower Africa, TechEstate and African Business.

Title: Empowering Inclusion: A Digital Gateway to Equitable Economic Growth
Subtitle: A digital platform empowering underserved communities with access to online jobs, financial tools, and skills training for inclusive economic participation and growth.
Problem Statement: Millions of people in underserved communities lack access to digital tools, skills, and economic opportunities, leading to exclusion from the digital economy and deepening income inequality.
Solution Overview:
Our solution is an inclusive digital platform designed to bridge the gap between marginalized communities and the digital economy by offering access to skills training, digital tools, and income opportunities in a single, user-friendly ecosystem.

How the Solution Works:
User Enrollment & Onboarding:
Individuals register via mobile or web with minimal barriers (e.g., low digital literacy, language support).

Digital Skills & Literacy Training:
Users are guided through tailored, bite-sized courses in digital literacy, remote work skills, financial management, and entrepreneurship.

Access to Income Opportunities:
After training, users are matched with gig work, freelance projects, remote jobs, or local e-commerce platforms to monetize their skills.

Integrated Digital Wallet:
Users receive payments through a secure wallet and can access savings, payments, and future credit services, fostering financial inclusion.

Ongoing Support & Community Engagement:
The platform features peer support, mentorship, and learning groups to reinforce skills and build confidence.

Methodologies and Technologies Used:
Human-Centered Design: Ensures usability by co-creating with local users and adapting to their specific needs.

Progressive Web Application (PWA): Accessible via low-cost smartphones and limited internet environments.

AI-Powered Personalization: Offers customized learning and job recommendations based on user profiles and performance.

Data Analytics: Tracks progress, outcomes, and helps refine content and user engagement strategies.

Technology Partners: Provide the learning management system, digital wallet infrastructure, and platform maintenance.

Private Sector Employers & Gig Platforms: Offer real-world income-generating opportunities to trained users.

Government & Multilateral Agencies: Collaborate on policy alignment, certification of training, and potential funding for scale and infrastructure.

Title: TreeO2: Bridging Carbon Markets and Smallholders with Smart Tech
Subtitle: TreeO2 is a digital platform that enables smallholder farmers to access carbon markets, verify impact, and earn income through sustainable community forestry.
Problem Statement:
Millions of smallholder farmers in the Global South are excluded from participating in the digital economy, particularly in emerging green finance markets like carbon trading. This exclusion is driven by limited digital infrastructure, low data literacy, and the absence of accessible, trusted tools to measure, verify, and monetise environmental stewardship activities such as community forestry. As a result, small rural communities are unable to access climate finance, derive economic value from their sustainability efforts, or participate meaningfully in the global transition to a low-carbon economy. This digital and economic divide perpetuates poverty, undermines climate action, and reinforces global inequities.

TreeO2 directly addresses this gap by providing an inclusive, community-first digital solution that enables smallholder farmers to participate in the carbon economy, build digital capability, and generate sustainable income through climate-positive practices.
Solution Overview:
TreeO2 is a digital platform that enables smallholder farmers and forest communities to participate in carbon markets by simplifying the measurement, reporting, and verification (MRV) of carbon stored in trees. Designed for low-connectivity and low-literacy environments, TreeO2 bridges the gap between grassroots reforestation efforts and the global digital economy.

Using a mobile app, community-based data collectors geo-tag and monitor individual trees planted and maintained by farmers. The data is synchronised with a cloud-based dashboard that applies geospatial mapping, remote sensing integration, and machine learning to verify carbon sequestration. Crucially, the survival rate of trees is tracked over time to transparently determine how much each farmer should be paid for their role as a long-term steward of the forest.

This verified data feeds into certification pathways, such as the Gold Standard or Plan Vivo, enabling farmers to access carbon finance. TreeO2 integrates open-source technologies, a lightweight offline-first mobile design, and robust data security to ensure inclusivity and scalability.

Collaboration is central to TreeO2’s model. Local partners support implementation and farmer engagement; certification bodies ensure integrity; and international partners help scale and align with global standards. By combining inclusive technology with trusted partnerships, TreeO2 transforms local climate action into measurable, transparent, and monetisable global impact.
Solution Provider(s): xpand Foundation – a not-for-profit social enterprise based in Australia and Timor-Leste, working to advance social equity and environmental sustainability through community-led innovation. xpand leads the development and implementation of the TreeO2 platform, with extensive experience in digital inclusion, community forestry, and international development (Sector: Social Impact, Digital Inclusion, Climate Action).
Implementation location(s): Timor-Leste – TreeO2 has been implemented in Timor-Leste, with the first pilot in Baguia starting in 2019. The tool now supports over 4,000 smallholder farmers currently engaged in community-led reforestation and carbon farming.  TreeO2 is now being scaled nationally through the Rai Matak initiative, in partnership with Foundation Rai Matak and Pollination Group, targeting 20,000 farmers and 10 million trees across Timor-Leste.  Further pilot implementations are underway in Sumatra and Kupang (Indonesia), as well as in Australia, to test scalability and adaptability across diverse social and environmental contexts.
Implementation timeline(s): Implementation began in 2019 with early development and pilot testing in Baguia, Baucau, Timor-Leste with 1000 farmers now using the tool from this pilot. From 2020 to 2025, the solution was refined and scaled to support an additional 3,000 farmers.  In 2025, TreeO2 entered a national scaling phase through the Rai Matak initiative, with full implementation targeting 20,000 farmers and 10 million trees by 2027.  Pilot expansions in Indonesia and Australia commenced in 2025 and are ongoing.
Duration to pilot in a new geography: Onboarding and training usually takes as little as a 1 week training session, with additional remote support.
SDGs addressed: SDG 13 (Climate Action);SDG 15 (Life on Land);SDG 10 (Reduced Inequalities);
Desired impact:
Solution Objectives
- Enable smallholder farmers and forest communities to access carbon markets through a transparent, inclusive digital platform.
- Improve tree survival and climate resilience through long-term stewardship incentives.
- Generate sustainable, verifiable income for rural communities by monetising climate action.
- Strengthen local capacity for digital MRV (measurement, reporting, verification) of carbon stocks.
- Support national and global goals for GHG reduction, ecosystem restoration, and digital inclusion.

Key Achievements and Impacts to Date
- 4000+ smallholder farmers currently participating in Timor-Leste.
- Over 1,000,000 trees registered, monitored, and linked to digital carbon farming payments.
- Verified survival rate over 80%, directly tied to farmer payments.

-100+ local jobs created in data collection, coordination, and digital MRV roles.

Projected to scale to 20,000 farmers and 10 million trees in Timor-Leste by 2027, with estimated GHG removal exceeding 25 million tonnes CO₂e over the trees’ lifetime. Expanding globally, this number would increase significantly.
Key technologies:
Mobile and Cloud-Based Applications
TreeO2 combines an offline-first mobile app for field data collection with a cloud-based dashboard for monitoring, reporting, and verification.

Geospatial Mapping & Remote Sensing
Tree geolocation, satellite imagery, and remote sensing are used to monitor forest cover, verify tree survival, and estimate carbon sequestration.

Machine Learning Algorithms
Machine learning supports analysis of field and satellite data to improve accuracy in tree identification, survival tracking, and carbon calculations.

RFID Tags & NFC Tools
Individual trees are tagged with RFID identifiers and scanned using NFC-enabled devices, ensuring transparent, tamper-proof tracking and verification.

Data Security & Privacy Protocols
End-to-end encryption and secure, role-based access ensure the protection of farmer and environmental data.
Unique Characteristics:
Unique and Differentiated Characteristics of TreeO2
Farmer-Centric, Performance-Based Payments
TreeO2 links verified tree survival to transparent, traceable farmer payments—rewarding long-term stewardship, not just tree planting. This model ensures accountability and sustainable income for communities.

Offline-First + Low-Literacy Design
The mobile app is designed for use in low-connectivity, low-literacy environments, using icons, local languages, and simplified user interfaces to ensure true inclusivity and usability by rural fieldworkers.

Use of RFID + NFC for Tree-Level Verification
Unlike most carbon MRV platforms, TreeO2 uses RFID tags and NFC tools to uniquely identify and monitor individual trees—ensuring high accuracy, traceability, and fraud prevention.

Locally Led Implementation Model
TreeO2 is deployed through a network of local NGOs, farmer groups, and youth data collectors, ensuring community ownership, cost-effective scaling, and deep cultural relevance.

Blended Financing & Certification Pathways
The solution is designed to plug into international certification schemes (e.g., Gold Standard, Plan Vivo) and access a mix of carbon finance, philanthropic capital, and public climate funds.

Integrated National Scaling Pathway
Currently being scaled nationwide in Timor-Leste through the Rai Matak initiative, TreeO2 demonstrates how a digital MRV tool can be embedded in national priorities, local partnerships, and long-term community development.

Contribution to Sustainable, Systemic Change
