Title: Farm Islands: Using AI to connect farmers directly to consumers
Subtitle: Empowering farmers with an AI-powered platform to connect directly with consumers and businesses, increasing their income, reducing food insecurity, and creating a sustainable food supply chain.
Problem Statement:
Farmers in many regions lack direct access to consumers and agro-dependent businesses leaving them reliant on intermediaries like wholesalers, traders, and distributors. According to the UN Food and Agriculture Organization (UNFAO), this system often leaves farmers with just 5–12% of the final consumer price. These middlemen set low purchase prices to maximize their profits, often exploiting farmers who are in weak negotiating positions due to limited capital, small-scale operations, and the perishable nature of their produce. As a result, many farmers are forced to sell at prices that don’t cover their production costs, trapping them in a cycle of poverty. Despite having strong agricultural expertise, most lack the business and marketing skills needed to negotiate fair deals or manage contracts effectively. Additionally, poor access to cold storage—especially in low-income countries— prevents farmers from selling their produce before it reaches the end of its shelf life which leads to significant post-harvest losses, further reducing farmers' income. Compounding this is a lack of access to up-to-date information on sustainable and climate-smart agricultural practices, which limits their ability to adapt to changing conditions and run resilient, profitable farms.

Food Insecurity: 
Limited direct access to farmers impacts not only producers but also consumers and agro-dependent businesses. According to the UN, over 75% of the world’s food-insecure population lives in urban and peri-urban areas. Unlike rural households that can grow their own food, urban residents depend entirely on the cash economy and are highly vulnerable to food price inflation. Since 2020, global food prices have risen by over 35%, according to the UNFAO. In many low-income countries, urban households spend up to 50%—and in the poorest countries, as much as 75%—of their income on food. Agro-based businesses are also affected. Middlemen in the supply chain inflate costs, forcing businesses that don't buy directly from farmers to pay more for raw ingredients which reduces their profit margins. 
Lack of Quality Control and Traceability: 
Middlemen also make it difficult to ensure quality control and product traceability. In the event of a food safety issue, it becomes nearly impossible to trace contaminated products back to their source. This delays response times and undermines consumer trust.
Solution Overview:
Description of how the solution works.
Farm Islands addresses the challenges farmers face by offering an AI powered digital platform that connects them directly with consumers and agro-dependent businesses, eliminating middlemen. This allows farmers to sell at both retail and wholesale prices, helping them retain a larger share of profits and ensuring a more stable, predictable income and attain long-term farm sustainability. Farmers can easily register their farms on the platform, while consumers and businesses can browse, purchase, and set up recurring orders. For buyers, Farm Islands offers access to affordable food and raw materials, reducing food insecurity and boosting business profitability.

Methodologies and technologies used.
Farm Islands leverages artificial intelligence, social media, and the web to create a multi-channel e-commerce, marketing, and resource platform tailored for farmers. With over 85% of farmers already using Facebook, Farm Islands integrates directly with a Facebook AI chatbot to simplify digital adoption. Through a simple chat or button-based interface, farmers can register and set up their online presence without needing any technical skills. The AI handles most of the process, making it easy and unintimidating for farmers to list and sell their products online. In addition to e-commerce, Farm Islands uses AI to provide timely, personalized information on sustainable and climate-smart agricultural practices, helping farmers adapt to climate change and grow their businesses. The AI will also assist with diagnosing issues like pests and plant diseases, all within Facebook Messenger. A companion website will also be available to expand access and provide more functionality for users who prefer web-based interaction.
Consumers and agro-dependent businesses can access the platform via either the Facebook chatbot or the website to browse and make purchases with ease.  

Partnerships and collaboration models 
Farm Islands will collaborate with key solution providers such as cold storage operators, seed and fertilizer suppliers, financial service providers, and irrigation system vendors. These partners will be able to register on the platform, making their products and services easily accessible to farmers. Additionally, Farm Islands will collaborate with governments and development organizations to boost participation of both farmers and agro-businesses.
Solution Provider(s): Meta Platforms Inc. – Provider of Facebook Messenger which serves as the primary access channel for Agrinect’s AI chatbot allowing seamless communication with farmers. (Sector: Social Media), Google (Gemini AI & Climate Platform) – Contributes both generative AI capabilities (via Gemini) and access to climate data through platforms like Google Earth Engine and the Google Climate API. These tools support climate-smart farming recommendations for farmers using the Agrinect platform. (Sector: Artificial Intelligence, Climate Tech, Cloud Services)
Duration to pilot in a new geography: 6 weeks
SDGs addressed: SDG 1 (No Poverty);SDG 2 (Zero Hunger);SDG 13 (Climate Action);
Desired impact:
Farm Islands Main Objectives:

Empower farmers by giving them direct access to consumers and agro-dependent businesses—improving income, ensuring long-term sustainability, and giving them greater control over the agricultural supply chain.
Enhance food security in urban and peri-urban areas by increasing food availability, lowering food prices, and improving access for vulnerable populations.
Boost the profitability of agro-dependent businesses by providing more affordable, direct access to food and raw agricultural materials.
Promote sustainable agriculture by equipping farmers with knowledge and tools for climate-smart and environmentally responsible farming practices, delivered via an AI-powered platform.

Key Achievements and Quantifiable Impacts:

Increase farmer income: 
Raise the average net income of participating farmers by 15–25% within 24 months, by enabling them to retain 30–50% more of the final sale price through direct-to-market sales.
Improve food security: Reduce retail food prices for partner buyers and consumers by 10–15% within the first 12 months.
Reduce post-harvest losses: 
Cut losses by up to 25% within the first 12–18 months through improved market access and partnerships with cold storage providers.
Drive climate-smart adoption: 
Achieve a 30% adoption rate of at least one new sustainable farming practice among registered farmers within 18–24 months, guided by AI recommendations.
Accelerate platform adoption: Onboard a minimum of 1,000 farmers and 5000 consumers and businesses within the first 12 months.
Key technologies:
Artificial Intelligence (AI)
Farm Islands use two key types of Artificial Intelligence; Generative AI and Natural Language Processing (NLP) to automate core processes and provide an enhanced user experience. This helps address barrier caused by digital literacy and accessibility challenges faced by many farmers.

Generative AI
Generative AI enhances the platform by automating key tasks, reducing the manual workload for farmers, and making the system more intelligent, personalized, and proactive.

Product Listing Automation:
When a farmer indicates they want to sell a product e.g., “I want to sell potatoes”, Farm Islands Generative AI automatically creates a complete product listing. This includes generating a product description, suggesting pricing based on real-time market data, and even adding a relevant image, eliminating the need for farmers to do it manually.
Automated Agronomy Advisory: 
Generative AI produces personalized agricultural content such as climate-smart farming tips, sustainability guides, and localized best practices. These recommendations are tailored to each farmer’s location, crop type, and weather conditions, helping them adopt better, data-driven farming practices without the need to search for information themselves.
Conversational Response Generation
Instead of relying on FAQs online, farmer can ask Farm Islands questions and the Generative AI crafts unique, conversational responses to farmer inquiries about topics like pest control, soil health, or market trends. This provides a more engaging and useful experience, especially for farmers seeking timely, situation-specific support.

Natural Language Processing (NLP)
NLP enables Farm Islands to understand and process human language, making the platform intuitive and easy to use. NLP supports multiple local languages and dialects, allowing farmers to communicate in their native tongue. This multilingual capability significantly improves accessibility and adoption, particularly among smallholder farmers in rural areas. Through the Facebook Messenger chatbot, farmers can interact with the system using natural, everyday language, for example, saying, “I want to sell tomatoes.” The AI understands the intent behind the message and responds accordingly.
Unique Characteristics:
What makes Farm Islands innovative is its technological model, inclusive design, and strategic partnerships,.

Embedded Within a Familiar Platform (Facebook Messenger):
Unlike traditional agri-tech platforms that require farmers to download new apps or navigate complex interfaces, Farm Islands is fully embedded within Facebook Messenger, a platform already used by over 85% of farmers across the globe. This drastically lowers the barrier to adoption and ensures faster user onboarding.

Conversational AI for Low-Digital-Literacy Users:
Farm Islands combines Generative AI and Natural Language Processing (NLP) to enable natural, conversational interactions in multiple local languages. Farmers can simply "chat" with the platform to register, list products, or seek farming advice, no technical skills or digital literacy required. This is a major innovation in making digital agriculture tools truly inclusive.

Integrated Agricultural Ecosystem:
Farm Islands is not just a marketplace but an entire ecosystem. It enables registration and participation from:
• Cold storage providers
• Input suppliers (seeds, fertilizers)
• Financial institutions (credit, insurance)
• Government and extension agencies
This collaborative model ensures farmers have access to all the services they need to grow, store, transport, and sell their products more sustainably and profitably.

Scalable and Cost-Effective Model
By building on widely-used platforms like Facebook and leveraging cloud infrastructure, Farm Islands minimizes development and operational costs while maximizing reach and scalability. This makes the model replicable across countries and scalable without requiring massive investments in infrastructure.
Sustainable Change:
Farm Islands aims to drive long-term, systemic change in agricultural value chains by removing structural barriers that trap farmers in poverty while improving food access and affordability for consumers and businesses. Our Theory of Change centers on transforming the agricultural supply chain through digital connectivity, AI-driven tools, and strategic partnerships.

Title: AFRIKABAL – AI-Powered, Blockchain-Verified Trade for Inclusive Economies
Subtitle: AFRIKABAL builds AI-powered, blockchain-verified infrastructure enabling trusted trade, instant payments, and inclusive access to finance across emerging economies.
Problem Statement: In emerging economies, trade is largely informal, unverified, and inaccessible to digital finance excluding millions from markets, credit, and climate-linked opportunities.
Solution Overview:
AFRIKABAL is a programmable, blockchain-powered digital infrastructure designed to make trade verifiable, inclusive, and finance-ready across sectors. The platform issues Decentralized Digital Identities (DIDs) to every participant—farmers, cooperatives, buyers, and logistics providers while recording each transaction on-chain for full transparency and tamper-proof verification.

Through a combination of mobile/web apps and USSD for low-bandwidth regions, users can list products or services, match with verified partners, and transact via escrow smart contracts integrated with mobile money APIs (Flutterwave, MTN, Yellow Card) for instant settlement.

At the core, Anhur AI, our analytics engine, processes transaction, environmental, and behavioral data to:
	•	Forecast prices and demand trends
	•	Assess delivery and credit risk
	•	Generate ESG and climate compliance reports
	•	Provide actionable insights for governments and institutions

Key Technologies & Methodologies:
	•	Blockchain & DIDs: Lisk , Cardano & Peaq for identity and transaction verification; IPFS for encrypted off-chain storage
	•	AI & Oracles: Anhur AI for analytics; Chainlink oracles for real-time market and climate data
	•	Inclusive Access: USSD and offline-first architecture to reach unbanked and underserved communities
	•	Interoperability: APIs for government systems, banks, and carbon markets

Partnerships & Collaboration Models:
AFRIKABAL is co-deployed with UNDP, Google for Startups, and the African Union Youth Start-Up Program, alongside national ICT ministries and cooperative networks. We work on a co-creation model with governments, enabling policy alignment and system integration, while providing private-sector partners with verified supply chains and compliance-ready data.

This combination of trust infrastructure, AI insights, and multi-stakeholder partnerships enables not only inclusive participation in the digital economy but also scalable, cross-sector adoption from agriculture to manufacturing and carbon markets.

Title: AidOS: The Home of Decentralized Aid
Subtitle: AidOS is a secure, decentralized B2B SaaS humanitarian operating system built by Aseel to streamline and decentralize the way aid is delivered, tracked, and managed.
Problem Statement:
The International humanitarian aid sector is failing in fragile and conflict-affected regions. Globally, nearly 300 million people require assistance due to conflict, climate shocks, and systemic fragility. In Afghanistan, over 28 million people need urgent humanitarian support, but aid delivery is inefficient, opaque, and inaccessible, especially in hard-to-reach areas.
AidOS directly addresses the key challenges facing humanitarian operations in fragile and conflict-affected environments such as Afghanistan. Delivering decentralized humanitarian aid involves a complex set of operational and logistical challenges, including:
Fragmented infrastructure, reliant on centralized warehouses, outdated logistics, and high-overhead intermediaries.
Lack of real-time, actionable data, leading to misallocation and exclusion—particularly for the 1.7 billion unbanked.
Accountability gaps, where donors and recipients lack visibility into aid flows.
International aid drying up—USAID has cut their funding and other governments have followed suit
Solution Overview:
Partnerships and collaboration models.
AidOis a secure, decentralized B2B SaaS humanitarian operating system designed to streamline and transform how aid is delivered, tracked, and managed in conflict-affected and hard-to-reach regions. It bridges the gap between donors, humanitarian organizations, and vulnerable communities by providing an end-to-end digital infrastructure that ensures transparency, efficiency, and impact.
AidOS functions as a modular platform where humanitarian actors can deploy tailored aid programs based on real-time needs. Organizations can select from five core modules:
Campaign+: A crowdfunding tool that empowers individuals and organisations to raise funds for causes they care about. Now integrated with the Atalan Network for last-mile delivery and OMID ID for beneficiary verification, Campaign+ makes it possible to move seamlessly from fundraising to impact. Diaspora communities, a prime audience, can use Campaign+ to launch targeted campaigns, mobilise global support networks, and stay directly connected to the people and places they care about — ensuring their contributions lead to timely, transparent, and dignified aid delivery, even across borders and hard-to-reach communities. This approach helps accelerate response efforts, amplifying the impact of localized initiatives.
OMID (Hope) ID: A unique digital identity and QR code system that tracks individual beneficiaries, even in the absence of formal ID or infrastructure. Each person’s aid history, needs, and location are securely stored and updated in real-time.
Hero Network: A volunteer-driven last-mile delivery system activated through Aseel’s mobile platform. Heroes (local volunteers) deliver aid packages directly to beneficiaries, even in rural or insecure areas — without needing physical offices or supply depots.
Real-Time Aid Tracking: Donors, implementers, and government partners can track aid flows — item by item — from dispatch to delivery. Every transaction is digitally logged and verified with GPS, timestamps, and photos.
Data-Driven Decision Support: The platform collects granular, localized data on needs and gaps. This enables aid organizations and donors to make faster, better-informed decisions — reducing duplication and ensuring needs-based distribution.

Title: eLEVATE Lanka: Digital Empowerment for Inclusive Growth of Women, Youth, and MSMEs
Subtitle: eLEVATE Lanka is a scalable digital solution designed to bridge economic and digital divides in Sri Lanka by empowering women, youth, MSMEs, and marginalized communities through targeted digital skills training, access to affordable tech tools, AI-based market intelligence, and inclusive digital platforms for entrepreneurship. The initiative aligns with the Global Digital Compact Objective 2, offering an inclusive, rights-based, and localized model of digital economic participation in Sri Lanka’s underserved sectors, especially in rural, plantation, and conflict-affected areas. The project leverages local innovation ecosystems, public-private partnerships, and open-source platforms to create a digitally empowered, inclusive, and sustainable local economy.
Problem Statement:
Sri Lanka faces a critical juncture in its economic development, where deep-seated socioeconomic inequalities and a rapidly shifting digital landscape risk widening existing divides if left unaddressed. While digital technologies offer transformative potential for inclusive growth, large segments of the population—particularly women, youth, micro and small enterprises (MSMEs), and marginalized communities—remain locked out of these opportunities due to a confluence of structural and systemic barriers.
The root causes of this exclusion are multifaceted:
•	Limited digital infrastructure in rural, plantation, and conflict-affected areas continues to hinder access to online services, training, and market connectivity.
•	Low digital literacy, especially among women and older youth in underserved regions, prevents meaningful participation in the digital economy.
•	Gender norms and unpaid care burdens disproportionately limit women's time, confidence, and autonomy in engaging with digital tools.
•	Many MSMEs operate informally, with inadequate access to affordable digital solutions, e-commerce platforms, or financial technologies (fintech), limiting their ability to scale or compete in modern markets.
•	A lack of localized, inclusive digital policies and regulatory frameworks has resulted in a fragmented ecosystem, where innovation remains concentrated in urban centers, disconnected from community needs and realities.
These root causes are further aggravated by post-crisis economic instability, rising youth unemployment, and the absence of scalable, community-rooted digital interventions.
eLEVATE Lanka responds directly to these challenges. By prioritizing inclusive digital empowerment, the initiative targets the foundational constraints preventing equitable participation in Sri Lanka's digital economy. Through integrated digital skills development, MSME support, and the creation of accessible, culturally responsive platforms, eLEVATE Lanka aims to bridge the digital divide, transform livelihoods, and catalyze inclusive, sustainable economic growth—particularly in those communities historically excluded from the benefits of digital transformation.
Solution Overview:
1. A Detailed Description of How the Solution Works
eLEVATE Lanka operates as an integrated, community-driven digital empowerment program aimed at bridging Sri Lanka’s economic and digital divides. It combines a mobile-first, multilingual Digital Skills and Entrepreneurship Academy with AI-enabled MSME support, local innovation hubs, and policy engagement. Beneficiaries—particularly women, youth, MSMEs, persons with disabilities, and ethnic minorities—gain access to tailored e-learning, digital business tools, and mentorship. The process starts with outreach in rural, estate, and conflict-affected areas, followed by skills training and MSME diagnostics. Learners receive low-bandwidth, offline-accessible training modules in Sinhala, Tamil, and English. MSMEs use an AI-powered diagnostic system to assess their digital maturity, receive personalized solutions, and connect to e-commerce and fintech platforms. Community-based e-Inclusion Labs, hosted in regional universities and youth hubs, drive locally relevant tech innovation. The project also feeds real-time data into a Digital Inclusion Policy Dashboard, enabling evidence-based policymaking and systemic change.

2. Methodologies and Technologies Used
The initiative uses a human-centered design methodology, co-creating solutions with local communities to ensure cultural relevance and accessibility. Delivery is mobile-first, low-bandwidth, and offline-capable to overcome connectivity barriers. The digital learning platform employs modular micro-learning, gamification, and localized case studies to build engagement. An AI-enabled MSME Diagnostic Tool provides real-time business insights and recommended digital solutions. e-Inclusion Labs utilize participatory innovation models, hackathons, and seed-grant mechanisms to foster grassroots problem-solving. Open-source, modular architecture ensures adaptability and scalability, while a Digital Inclusion Policy Dashboard aggregates gender- and youth-disaggregated data for policy use. Technologies applied include AI-driven analytics, cloud-based learning management systems, e-commerce integration, digital payment solutions, and open-source development frameworks.
3. Partnerships and Collaboration Models
eLEVATE Lanka is built on a multi-stakeholder collaboration model involving government, UN agencies, the private sector, academia, and civil society. Core government partners include the Ministry of Technology, Ministry of Women and Child Affairs, and ICTA, which provide policy alignment and infrastructure support. UNDP, UNIDO, and ILO contribute technical expertise and global best practices. Private sector partners such as Dialog Axiata, Daraz Sri Lanka, PickMe, and Hatch support with technology platforms, market access, and mentorship. Local NGOs like Sarvodaya, Emerge Lanka, and Yarl IT Hub ensure grassroots engagement and community mobilization. Regional universities host e-Inclusion Labs, fostering local innovation and research integration. Governance is managed through a Steering Committee with multi-stakeholder representation, supported by Community-led M&E teams and a Digital Ethics and Inclusion Advisory Board to safeguard rights and inclusivity.

Title: kHEALTH : Offline Training & AI Learning Assistant for Community Health Workers
Subtitle: A 100% offline multilingual mobile platform and AI chatbot on microSD that upskills CHWs even without connectivity—co-created with Ministries of Health and local stakeholders
Problem Statement:
Across West Africa, Community Health Workers (CHWs) are the first point of care for prevention, maternal and child health, vaccination and common conditions—yet they rarely receive continuous, up-to-date and context-specific training. Existing offers are often too theoretical and depend on reliable internet, which many CHWs do not have. This creates a skills and information gap that directly undermines the quality and equity of primary care.

Connectivity and cost are structural barriers. “Always-online” products falter at the last mile because they require constant data for video, updates and supervision. By contrast, kHEALTH was engineered to bypass those constraints: the full learning experience and the assistant run 100% offline from a Kajou microSD card, and only sync usage data at a later stage, once the user gets a minimum of internet connection(store-and-forward). This design removes the data-cost barrier and ensures access in low-coverage areas.

In the Senegalese context—representative of much of the sub-region—distance, geographic dispersion and unequal access to services exacerbate those challenges. A natively offline, multilingual and locally aligned solution is therefore essential so CHWs can learn at their own pace and obtain immediate, trustworthy answers at point of need, even without a network.

There is also clear evidence of unsatisfied demand for practical digital training: early cohorts show high adoption and sustained use, well above typical mobile benchmarks on the continent (≈0.5–1 login/week vs. 1.75 for kHEALTH; 3h13 over 3 months vs. 1–2h) and 99% of users engaging beyond 30 minutes. This underscores both the urgency and the feasibility of an offline-first approach.
Solution Overview:
What kHEALTH does
kHEALTH combines (1) a modular, competency-based e-learning pathway (videos, exercises and practical resources) in local languages that is fully accessible offline via Kajou microSD cards, and (2) a multilingual, offline AI assistant that answers CHWs’ questions with sourced, contextualized responses and links back to relevant learning modules.


Why it is truly “offline-first”
All content and the assistant are embedded on the microSD card; the app logs usage locally and syncs automatically when a connection is available. This removes data cost as an adoption barrier and keeps the system reliable in low-coverage settings. Even without the internet, CHWs receive on-device notifications to sustain engagement and completion.


How the offline AI works
The assistant relies on an open-science language model trained on a national medical corpus. To operate completely offline, a lightweight on-card classifier selects the best match from a large, pre-generated Q&A base validated by clinical experts; if the answer is unsatisfying, the user can later opt to fetch a fresh generative answer online, which—after expert review—enriches the offline base. The assistant supports text and audio and is being extended to national languages.

Under the hood, the team uses an open-science ~350M model, pre-generates ~11,500 multilingual Q/A pairs, and embeds a ColBERT reranker on the card; offline TTS enables low-resource audio delivery on entry-level phones.


Monitoring, engagement and measurement
kHEALTH collects more than 70 user datapoints (progress, completions, time-on-task…), powers monthly cohort dashboards (by region and profile), supports individual follow-up and issues certificates upon completion. Targeted messages—in-app and via SMS when offline—nudge specific cohorts and push urgent health information.


Continuous improvement (AI feedback loop)
Every question asked by CHWs is aggregated to surface needs and gaps by region or profile, informing content updates and assistant refinement—a closed loop between field practice and training.


Traction and early outcomes
Côte d’Ivoire (Dec 2024–Feb 2025): ~1.75 logins/week; 3h13 average use over 3 months; 99% >30 minutes; 20% >4h; 13% >6h.

Learning gains: +10% average knowledge improvement after 4 months (baseline vs endline).

Reach and deployment: 5,000 CHWs in Côte d’Ivoire and 2,000 in Senegal already use kHEALTH; in Senegal, 500 are piloting the AI assistant (Wolof version approved in June 2025; rollout in Saint-Louis & Matam).
Solution Provider(s): Kajou (social enterprise; offline digital learning; health/education) — lead developer and implementer, Ministry of Health – Côte d’Ivoire — co-creation, validation, scale-up partner, Operational NGOs (e.g., Save the Children, Enda Santé, PSI) — distribution, supervision, scale.
Implementation location(s): Ivory Coast — national CHW training program (multi-region) with the Ministry of Health and Universal Coverage.   Senegal — Saint-Louis & Matam regions (a total of 2,500 CHWs among which 500 with the AI chatbot option).
Implementation timeline(s): Ivory Coast : Dec 2024 – Feb 2025 usage statistics (baseline/endline study in 2025). Senegal: AI cohort test from end-May 2025; regulatory approval early June 2025; deployment Jun–Aug 2025 to 2,000 CHWs (incl. 500 with AI).
Duration to pilot in a new geography: 6–8 months total, typically: 3–4 months for content localization & AI alignment (national corpus, translations), followed by 3 months of cohort pilot and 1 month for analysis/iteration—consistent with prior planning.
SDGs addressed: SDG 3 (Good Health and Well-being);SDG 4 (Quality Education);SDG 9 (Industry, Innovation, and Infrastructure);
Desired impact:
Objectives :
We aim to roll out kHEALTH to 100,000 CHWs in West Africa by 2030.
Strengthen CHW competencies through modular, competency-based learning and just-in-time offline AI assistance; 2) Improve service quality in maternal/child health, vaccination, malaria and common conditions; 3) Close the digital divide by ensuring full functionality without connectivity; 4) Enable data-informed supervision via dashboards and targeted engagement.


Key achievements to date.
Adoption & engagement (Ivory Coast): ~1.75 logins/week, 3h13 over 3 months; 99% used >30 min; 20% >4h; 13% >6h.
Learning outcomes: +10% average knowledge gain after 4 months (baseline vs endline).
Reach: 2,500 CHWs already trained in Ivory Coast (ramping to 5,000), 2,000 additional in Senegal in 2025 (with 500 using the AI assistant).
Key technologies:

Title: Audiopedia
Subtitle: Voice-first digital financial literacy for last-mile women - mobile money, savings, and fraud safety via QR Access Points, SD Cards and solar audio - localized in Hausa, Kinyarwanda, Twi & more.
Problem Statement: Hundreds of millions of women are still excluded from the digital economy due to low literacy, language barriers, limited data/connectivity, and safety risks (fraud/scams). Existing DFS training often assumes smartphones and reading skills. Women and informal MSMEs need trusted, in-language, phone-based guidance to use mobile money, save, borrow responsibly, and protect themselves—delivered through channels that work offline and on any phone. Audiopedia closes this gap with audio-first content and last-mile distribution.
Solution Overview:
What it is. Audiopedia packages evidence-based DFL into short, dramatized and how-to audio lessons (e.g., SIA’s “Hey Sister! Show Me the Mobile Money!”) and publishes them as open, multilingual playlists on Audiopedia—then delivers them through QR “Access Points,” SD Cards mobile web, ad-hoc Wi-Fi, and solar audio devices so even non-literate users can learn and act. 

How it works (methodologies & tech).
	•	Voice-first micro-lessons mapped to key DFS use cases (open account, send/receive, merchant payments, savings/loans/insurance, privacy & scam avoidance, basic smartphone use). 
	•	Multi-channel delivery: QR Access Points in clinics/markets (scan to play audio), offline solar audio players, SD cards in basic phones, mobile web via ad-hoc Wi-Fi.  ￼
	•	Capacity building via Audiopedia Academy & CBO partnerships for facilitation, outreach, and feedback loops. 

Partnership & collaboration model.
	•	Content & expertise: Strategic Impact Advisors (SIA) provides the “Hey Sister” DFL series (25 episodes, 16 languages). Audiopedia hosts/localizes and integrates into multi-channel last-mile delivery.  
	•	Distribution: Collaboration with local mobile phone providers; Audiopedia’s QR Access Points for community distribution.
Solution Provider(s): Audiopedia Foundation (non-profit; voice-first knowledge platform; Germany; gender equality & inclusive digital skills), Strategic Impact Advisors (SIA) – “Hey Sister! Show Me the Mobile Money!” (digital financial inclusion; USA)
Implementation location(s): Uganda, Rwanda, Nigeria, Tanzania, Ethiopia, Nicaragua, Belize, India, Pakistan, etc.
Duration to pilot in a new geography: 8–12 weeks
SDGs addressed: SDG 5 (Gender Equality);SDG 4 (Quality Education);SDG 8 (Decent Work and Economic Growth);
Desired impact:
Women and informal MSMEs safely adopt and use DFS (mobile money, savings/loans, insurance), increasing income resilience, business formality, and financial health while reducing fraud exposure.

Achievements (selected).
	•	25 DFL audio episodes in 16 languages, open and adaptable; available free online.  
	•	Audiopedia platform 8,000+ audio articles, 80+ languages, and 10M+ people reached, enabling cross-thematic learning (financial literacy, health, livelihoods).  
	•	Deployed through QR Access Points, micro SD cards and solar audio in low-connectivity settings to reach non-literate users.
Key technologies: MediaWiki knowledge platform; Machine Translation + Text-to-Speech (TTS) for rapid localization;  QR Access Points (short-URL); ad-hoc Wi-Fi mobile web apps; solar-powered audio players for offline playback; lightweight dashboards/M&E.
Unique Characteristics:
•	Voice-first + offline-first: Works on any phone, no literacy/data required.
•	Open, modular DPG-style content - adaptable scripts and audio that partners can localize and remix.  
•	Multi-channel last-mile distribution: QR Access Points, mobile web apps, SD cards, ad-hoc Wi-Fi, and solar devices.
•	Women-centered storytelling (e.g., “Hey Sister”) to drive behavior change and trust. 
•	Proven partnerships across NGOs, governments, and telecoms; UN-recognized under SDG Digital Acceleration Agenda.

Activities: Co-create/adapt content; deploy via Access Points; community facilitation; iterative feedback; monitor usage.
Outputs: Multilingual DFL playlists; Access Points placed in markets/clinics; trained facilitators.
Outcomes: Increased DFS knowledge, safer usage (reduced scams), higher mobile money adoption (P2P/merchant), better savings/borrowing decisions for women and MSMEs.
Impact: Women’s economic empowerment, MSME growth/formalization, and reduced inequalities - at population scale through repeatable, low-cost channels.

Title: Farmonaut: Accelerating Local Innovation Through Satellite & Blockchain Intelligence
Subtitle: Empowering developing regions with secure, easy-to-use satellite and blockchain tools to accelerate innovation, improve decision-making, and share digital know-how across local ecosystems.
Problem Statement: Developing countries often lack access to advanced digital tools, real-time data, and secure knowledge-sharing platforms needed to drive innovation. Farmers, small-scale miners, and local institutions still rely on outdated, siloed methods that limit their ability to make informed decisions, share insights, and scale solutions. This results in inefficient resource use, low productivity, and uneven digital transformation across local ecosystems.
Solution Overview:
Farmonaut accelerates local innovation by providing a satellite-powered digital platform that delivers actionable insights to farmers, agribusinesses, and local institutions. The solution works through a web & mobile dashboard that integrates high-resolution satellite imagery, AI/ML models, and geospatial analytics to monitor crops, provide advisory, track environmental change, and forecast risks in near real-time. Users simply select their area of interest and receive automated, easy-to-understand reports and alerts.

Technologies used include multispectral satellite data processing, AI-based classification & prediction algorithms, cloud computing, and APIs for integration with local systems. These tools allow users to access advanced digital capabilities without needing technical expertise.

Farmonaut follows a collaborative model by partnering with local governments, NGOs, multilateral agencies, universities, and MSME cooperatives. These partners help co-design relevant use cases, localize knowledge transfer, and promote adoption. The platform also offers training materials to ensure users generate long-term value from the digital tools.
Implementation location(s): Cameroon, Lesotho, Chile, Zimbabwe, Argentina, Austria, Malaysia, Philippines, Tanzania, Egypt, UAE, Nigeria, Germany, Algeria, USA, Uzbekistan, India, Australia, Netherlands, Israel, Canada, New Zealand, Kenya, Mozambique, Rwanda, Liberia, and the UK.
Implementation timeline(s): Farmonaut began its initial deployments in 2019, with continuous expansion and implementation across additional countries from 2020 to the present (2025). The solution is currently active and ongoing.
Duration to pilot in a new geography: Approximately 6–8 weeks from initial engagement — including needs assessment, area configuration, localization, onboarding of stakeholders, and launch of the dashboard and training materials.
SDGs addressed: SDG 13 (Climate Action);SDG 9 (Industry, Innovation, and Infrastructure);SDG 2 (Zero Hunger);
Desired impact:
Solution Objectives
- Accelerate local innovation by providing real-time, satellite-based analytics and advisory services to underserved agricultural communities and institutions.
- Enable data-driven decision-making for improved crop productivity, resource optimization, and climate resilience.
- Promote widespread knowledge sharing and technology transfer through user-friendly digital tools and training.

Key Achievements / Impacts
- Supported over 300,000 hectares of land with satellite monitoring and advisory services.
- Enabled 15–30% increase in crop yield for farmers using Farmonaut’s platform.
- Helped reduce input costs by up to 25% through precision advisory (fertilizer, irrigation, pesticide).
- Facilitated 10+ cross-border collaborations and pilot projects for technology transfer in developing countries.
- Contributed to early detection of climate risks (drought, pests, extreme weather), improving climate preparedness for thousands of farmers and agribusinesses.
Key technologies:
Farmonaut leverages a combination of advanced digital technologies, including:

- Satellite Remote Sensing – multispectral and hyperspectral imagery for monitoring crops and environmental variables.
- AI / Machine Learning – classification and predictive models to generate real-time crop health, stress detection, and risk forecasts.
- Geospatial Analytics & GIS – spatial analysis and mapping of user-defined areas to deliver location-specific insights.
- Cloud Computing – scalable infrastructure for processing large volumes of spatial data and delivering it through web/mobile platforms.
- APIs / Systems Integration – interfaces for integration with local government systems, agribusiness platforms, and third-party services.
Unique Characteristics:

Title: eNgoma Offline elearning Solution
Subtitle: Empowering schools and communities with offline-first access to quality educational content, anytime, anywhere—no internet required
Problem Statement:
Over the past two decades, the Government of the Republic of Zambia has made notable efforts to integrate Information and Communication Technology (ICT) into the education system, including initiatives to supply computers to schools as part of broader curriculum reforms. These investments were intended to prepare learners for a digital economy, support the implementation of the new curriculum, and bridge the gap between urban and rural education.

However, while the hardware has arrived in many schools, the enabling ecosystem has not kept pace. The majority of schools, particularly in rural and peri-urban areas, lack reliable internet connectivity and have limited or no access to relevant, curriculum-aligned digital content. Many teachers have not received adequate ICT training, which makes it difficult for them to incorporate technology into their lesson delivery. Frequent load shedding further disrupts computer use, while the absence of offline, locally relevant resources means that the equipment often remains idle.

This combination of systemic challenges has undermined the intended benefits of government investment. In many cases, computers and accessories fall into disrepair, are repurposed, or are stolen, leading to wastage and eroding public trust in such programs. For learners in unconnected communities, the result is an even wider education gap, with limited exposure to 21st-century skills and reduced competitiveness in higher education and the job market. Without addressing these barriers: connectivity, content, capacity, and sustainability, the vision of a digitally empowered Zambian education system will remain out of reach.
Solution Overview:
The eNgoma Offline eLearning Solution is designed to overcome Zambia’s persistent barriers to digital education—connectivity, content availability, teacher capacity, and energy reliability—by delivering a self-contained, offline-first learning ecosystem. It enables schools and communities, including those without internet or reliable electricity, to access curriculum-aligned, interactive educational resources anytime, anywhere.
How the Solution Works
1.	Offline Digital Learning Platform
o	At the core is Kolibri, a proven, open-source learning management system optimized for offline environments.
o	Content aligned with Zambia’s curriculum is preloaded onto local servers or computers, allowing learners to access interactive lessons, videos, and quizzes without internet access.
o	The system supports usage tracking and performance analytics, giving educators insights into learner progress.
2.	Adaptable Deployment Models
o	Solutions are installed on low-cost laptops, desktop computers, or network-attached storage devices.
o	In schools without grid power, systems can be paired with solar power kits to ensure uninterrupted learning despite loadshedding.
o	Local Wi-Fi hotspots allow multiple learners to connect simultaneously using any device, without consuming mobile data.
3.	Teacher Training & Capacity Building
o	Teachers receive practical, hands-on training in operating the system, integrating content into lessons, and monitoring learner engagement.
o	Training builds confidence in digital pedagogy, ensuring that technology is used effectively rather than sitting idle.
4.	Community Integration
o	Beyond schools, the solution can be extended to community learning hubs, libraries, or post offices, enabling broader access to lifelong learning resources.

Methodologies & Technologies
•	Kolibri – Offline-first LMS with analytics and customizable content libraries.
•	BeeKee Box – Portable, solar-powered learning hub for remote communities.
•	Solar Integration – Ensures continuous operation in areas affected by loadshedding.
•	Custom Content Curation – Locally relevant and curriculum-aligned resources preloaded to avoid dependency on external downloads.
•	Data-Driven Feedback Loops – Usage statistics and learner performance reports inform teaching strategies and future content updates.
Partnerships & Collaboration Models
•	Zambeef Supported Schools – Deploying offline learning labs in rural schools supported by Zambeef, pairing technology with teacher training to build sustainable capacity.
•	Chongwe, Thornpark, and Chazanga – Successful deployments of Kolibri-powered labs that have increased learner engagement and improved digital literacy.
•	BeeKee – Ongoing discussions to integrate portable, solar-powered eLearning hubs for the most remote and underserved areas.
•	Presidential Delivery Unit – Engaged in exploring a public-private sector-driven national strategy to scale offline eLearning across Zambia, leveraging combined resources, logistics, and policy support.
•	Community Partnerships – Collaborations with local school boards, teachers’ associations, and community and traditional leaders to ensure sustainability and security of equipment.
Why This Approach Works
By combining proven offline learning technologies with solar energy, targeted teacher training, and strong community and corporate partnerships, the eNgoma Offline eLearning Solution ensures that digital education investments deliver real, lasting impact. This model directly addresses the historical challenges of underused or stolen equipment, lack of internet access, and insufficient teacher capacity, transforming past investments into tangible learning outcomes.
Solution Provider(s): eNgoma Solutions : A Zambian technology and innovation company dedicated to leveraging digital tools for social impact. eNgoma specializes in offline-first eLearning platforms, data analytics, connectivity solutions, and ICT infrastructure for underserved communities. The company has a strong track record in deploying education technology in rural and peri-urban areas, integrating renewable energy for sustainability, and designing systems that work even in low-resource environments. Sector: Technology, Education, and Social Impact. L3 provides expertise in teacher training, learning content development, and the deployment of AI-enhanced learning management systems. The organization works closely with schools, governments, and NGOs to ensure technology is effectively embedded into classroom practice for measurable improvement in learner performance. The PDU facilitates collaboration between government ministries, private sector partners, and development agencies to accelerate impactful solutions in education, health, infrastructure, and economic growth. In this initiative, PDU’s role is to foster a public-private partnership model for scaling offline eLearning solutions nationally. Sector: Government, Policy, and Public-Private Partnerships.

Desired impact:
The eNgoma Offline eLearning Solution aims to make quality, curriculum-aligned digital education available to every learner in Zambia, regardless of internet connectivity or location. Our objectives are to:
•	Bridge the digital divide by providing offline access to rich, interactive learning resources in rural, peri-urban, and underserved communities.
•	Strengthen teacher capacity through hands-on training and skills transfer, enabling confident integration of technology into everyday teaching.
•	Transform schools into shared community learning hubs, extending benefits beyond enrolled students to adults and out-of-school youth.
•	Create a scalable, low-cost model for national deployment through public–private partnerships.
Key Achievements and Impacts
Our deployments in Chongwe, Thornpark, and Chazanga, and most recently in Zambeef-supported rural schools, have demonstrated the power of an offline-first approach. In these schools, over 1,200 learners and 45 teachers have gained access to interactive digital resources without the need for internet connectivity. Teacher training sessions have equipped educators with the skills to confidently integrate eLearning into lessons, track learner performance, and even set up and maintain their own lab environments.
By transforming classrooms into community hubs, the solution has also opened opportunities for adult literacy classes and basic digital skills training, directly benefiting community members. Early indicators from partner schools show increases in lesson engagement, improved learner performance in core subjects, and reduced downtime caused by connectivity or power issues.
While our primary focus is educational impact, the solution indirectly supports economic and social outcomes. It encourages local employment for installation, maintenance, and training; fosters technology ownership at the community level, reducing equipment loss and waste; and strengthens human capital by equipping learners with skills relevant to the modern economy.
As the model scales, we envision a Zambia where digital learning is no longer an urban privilege, but a nationwide standard unlocking opportunities for millions of learners and contributing to the country’s long-term social and economic development.

Type: Open-source, offline-first LMS.

Data Analytics & Reporting Tools

Local Wireless Networks

Unique Characteristics:
The eNgoma Offline eLearning Solution stands out because it is built for the realities of Zambia, not just the ideals of a connected world. While most digital learning platforms depend on uninterrupted internet, our solution works entirely offline, yet still delivers rich, interactive, and fully curriculum-aligned content to learners. This means a school in the heart of Lusaka’s suburbs can have the same access to quality resources as a classroom deep in rural Zambia.
Our approach has already proven its worth. In Chongwe, Thornpark, and Chazanga, and now in Zambeef-supported rural schools, we’ve seen students not only engage more with lessons but also develop the digital skills they’ll need for the future. The difference lies in how we combine technology with people. We don’t just install systems and leave; we train teachers in practical, hands-on ways to integrate technology into their daily lessons, track learner progress, and troubleshoot problems. This builds confidence and ensures the investment is used to its full potential.
Another factor that sets us apart is our focus on local relevance. Every resource we deploy is tailored to Zambia’s curriculum and context, using examples that resonate with learners. We avoid the pitfall of relying on generic international content that doesn’t fit our classrooms.
We are also working at a national level to make this a shared success. Through discussions with the Presidential Delivery Unit, we are shaping a public-private partnership model that will make offline eLearning accessible to every child in Zambia. Collaborations with companies like Zambeef demonstrate how corporate infrastructure and community connections can accelerate educational impact.
Finally, our model is sustainable and scalable. By using affordable, locally maintainable hardware and eliminating ongoing data costs, we make it possible to expand from one school to an entire province without waiting for expensive infrastructure upgrades. And because our systems can also serve community learning hubs, post offices, and public libraries, the benefits reach far beyond the classroom, turning technology into a shared community asset.
Sustainable Change:
The eNgoma Offline eLearning Solution is not just a technology package; it is a long-term change-maker for how learning happens in Zambia. By creating a platform that works entirely offline, we remove one of the biggest obstacles to quality education: the need for constant internet access. This means that a child in a rural village has the same chance to access rich, interactive, curriculum-aligned lessons as a learner in the city.
The transformation begins in the classroom. Teachers are not only shown how to operate the system, but also how to weave it into everyday lessons, track student progress, and adjust their teaching to meet different learning needs. A central part of our skills transfer and support model involves both teachers and students participating in hands-on lab setups. This practical involvement gives them the confidence to operate, maintain, and even troubleshoot the system themselves, ensuring the technology becomes an everyday tool rather than a locked-away resource.
As teachers’ skills and confidence grow, so does their ability to inspire curiosity and independent learning among students. Lessons become more engaging, and learners start to take ownership of their education. Over time, these classrooms evolve into community learning hubs. The same technology that powers a mathematics lesson during the day can host adult literacy classes in the evening or provide vocational training for out-of-school youth. This shared access turns schools into places where everyone children, parents, and community members can learn and grow together. With greater involvement comes a sense of ownership, which helps protect and sustain the equipment and resources.
On a national scale, the solution proves that digital learning does not have to wait for full internet coverage or massive infrastructure upgrades to succeed. By working with the Presidential Delivery Unit, corporate partners such as Zambeef, and other stakeholders, we are building a public–private collaboration model that can be expanded across the country and even Africa.
As this approach grows, we expect to see better-equipped teachers, more confident and capable learners, stronger community engagement, and a greater sense of shared responsibility for educational resources. The model’s success will guide government policy, influence investment in ICT for education, and provide a low-cost blueprint for scaling digital learning to every district in Zambia.
In essence, eNgoma’s solution is about shifting digital education from being a privilege of well-connected urban schools to being a fundamental right for every Zambian learner, embedding technology into the heart of teaching, learning, and community life.
Funding Sources:
In its early deployments, the eNgoma Offline eLearning Solution has been funded largely through corporate social responsibility initiatives. Partner companies have donated computer hardware and covered essential costs such as trainer facilitation, transportation, and basic setup. This has allowed us to successfully implement the solution in schools such as Chongwe, Thornpark, Chazanga, and Zambeef-supported rural institutions without relying on public funding.

As we transition into a scaling phase, our funding approach is broadening. We are actively engaging the Presidential Delivery Unit (PDU) and strategic partners such as Zambeef to cover the full scope of implementation costs, including lab setup, teacher training, community skills transfer sessions, ongoing technical support, and the monitoring of learning outcomes.

We are also exploring long-term financing mechanisms through the CSR Forum of Zambia and cooperating partners, with the aim of securing annual funding commitments to sustain and expand the program. In parallel, the PDU is engaging with the Ministry of Education (MoE) and the Zambia Information and Communications Technology Authority (ZICTA) to identify and unlock potential sources of funding, including allocations from the Universal Access and Service Fund and other education-focused budgets.

By combining corporate contributions, public–private partnerships, and community ownership with structured, predictable funding streams, we are building a model that can sustain nationwide deployment and deliver long-term impact.

Title: Verifica: The First EU-Compliant Blockchain for Legal Digital Product Passports
Subtitle: Crypto-free, EU-compliant blockchain enabling legally valid Digital Product Passports, certified data/documents, and AI trained only on trusted enterprise information.
Problem Statement: Most blockchains are crypto-based, energy-intensive, and non-compliant with EU laws, making them unusable for enterprises. Companies lack trusted infrastructure to issue Digital Product Passports, certify data/documents with legal value, and ensure AI compliance.
Solution Overview:
Solution Overview
How it works
Verifica is the first Layer-1 blockchain fully developed and registered in Italy, designed specifically to comply with EU regulations (GDPR, eIDAS, EDPB 02/2025). Unlike crypto-based chains, it is crypto-free, energy-efficient, and enterprise-ready. The platform enables companies to:
Issue Digital Product Passports (DPPs) aligned with the EU Green Deal mandate.
Certify and notarize data, documents, and processes with full legal validity.
Train private LLMs/AI assistants on certified data only, ensuring responsible and compliant AI adoption.
Integrate seamlessly into existing ERP systems and workflows through APIs, reducing adoption barriers for SMEs.
Methodologies and technologies used
Permissioned blockchain governance: nodes hosted by trusted partners such as associations, system integrators, and institutions, rather than anonymous miners.
Optimized Proof of Stake consensus, ensuring scalability and very low energy consumption.
Digital Asset Manager (DAM) for private storage and sovereignty over sensitive data.
Modular APIs for ERP/legal-tech integration and white-label distribution.
AI integration (Verifica Index) for enterprise-grade AI trained exclusively on certified data.
Partnerships and collaboration models
Verifica scales through institutional trust and distribution networks:
Ministry of Enterprises and Made in Italy (MIMIT): recognized interest in leveraging Verifica to safeguard Made in Italy and digital compliance.
Confindustria: collaboration to promote adoption among SMEs and industrial associations.
Regione Friuli Venezia Giulia: local institutional support as the home base of Verifica, strengthening credibility.
University of Trieste: academic collaboration on compliance and blockchain research.
Il Sole 24 Ore: national media partner, distributing Verifica under the brand Valore24 Blockchain, with 150+ sales agents and full media coverage.
Chambers of Commerce (e.g., Italo-Araba): strategic channels to expand internationally, offering Verifica to associated enterprises.
Through this mix of technology, compliance, and institutional partnerships, Verifica lowers barriers for SMEs, builds trust in blockchain, and creates a scalable infrastructure for the inclusive digital economy across Europe and beyond.

Title: Mereka AI Lab
Subtitle: Inclusive AI skilling to empower individuals, MSMEs, and organizations to thrive in the digital economy.
Problem Statement:
Across the globe, participation in the digital economy remains uneven. Millions of workers, small businesses, and underrepresented groups lack access to affordable, practical AI skilling pathways. This creates a widening divide:
For individuals, especially women, youth, and workers in rural or low-income contexts, limited exposure to AI tools reduces their competitiveness in the job market and ability to secure meaningful employment.
For MSMEs, the backbone of most economies, insufficient AI capacity prevents them from modernizing workflows, reaching new markets, and maintaining resilience in times of disruption.


For organizations, digital transformation often falters due to gaps in workforce readiness, where employees lack both the literacy and confidence to adopt AI-enabled processes.
Without inclusive and accessible AI skilling, societies risk reinforcing inequality, limiting economic mobility, and leaving entire communities behind in an era where AI fluency is becoming a baseline requirement for participation in the digital economy.
Solution Overview:
The AI workforce solution addresses the critical challenge of modernizing workflows and processes to meet growing workforce demands and efficiency requirements in an AI-driven economy. We provide a structured pathway to systematically develop AI capabilities across individual and organizational levels, from foundational literacy to executive governance, ensuring organizations can effectively integrate AI tools while building workforce resilience to navigate continuous technological change and prepare workers for the generative AI era.

Detailed Description of How the Solution Works: The AI workforce solution operates through a 5-tiered competency framework progressing from AI Fundamentals Users (beginners using basic tutorials) to AI General Users (professionals using tools like ChatGPT and Microsoft Copilot), AI Team Integrators (managers implementing workflow automation with Zapier and Tableau), AI Specialists (strategists using advanced analytics and AWS AI Services), and AI Business Leaders (executives managing governance and compliance platforms). Each level targets specific audiences with appropriate tools, skills, and responsibilities.

Methodology and Strategy:

Three-Phase Strategic Implementation: Phase 1 focuses on Foundation Building through free AI courses and public programs emphasizing basic literacy. Phase 2 advances to Organizational Integration with custom departmental training and AI culture development. Phase 3 culminates in Advanced Deployment involving AI agent development and strategic organizational transformation.

Pedagogical Methodology: The solution is deployed through five core modules: AI Applications in the Workplace (real-world use cases), Mapping Workflows for AI Integration (identifying improvement opportunities), Practical AI Tools (hands-on low-code/no-code platform training), Implementing AI Solutions (strategic planning and ethics), and Building an AI-Ready Culture (change management and continuous learning). Each module includes practical activities like workflow mapping, hands-on workshops, case studies, and action plan development.

Partnerships and collaboration models: We work closely with foundations and philanthropic organizations to ensure that basic AI literacy and foundational courses remain free and accessible to the larger public, particularly underserved communities, students, and early-career professionals. This inclusive approach ensures that no one is left behind in the AI transformation journey.
For more advanced and specialized training programs, especially in Malaysia, companies can leverage the Human Resource Development Fund (HRDF) funding. The fund enables employers who contribute to the HRDF levy  to claim financial support for employee training and development programs. This mechanism allows companies to upskill their workforce at minimal or no direct cost.
