Title: ANTSA – AI-Enhanced Mental Health Support Between Sessions
Subtitle: Continuous, clinician-guided digital mental health care using AI to bridge access gaps and support resilience in global communities.
Problem Statement: Globally, there are significant gaps in continuous care - especially for women, youth, and marginalised communities. Mental health support often stops at the clinic door, with long waitlists, high costs, and geographical barriers preventing sustained engagement. In low-resource settings, the shortage of qualified practitioners means clients may receive only sporadic or crisis-driven care. Without secure, inclusive, and scalable digital tools that allow clinicians to monitor, guide, and support clients between sessions, vulnerable populations remain at risk of worsening mental health outcomes, reduced productivity, and social exclusion.
Solution Overview:
ANTSA is an award-winning Australian-built digital mental health platform designed to extend therapeutic care beyond in-person sessions, ensuring no client is left unsupported between appointments. Its core innovation is jAImee, the world’s first clinician-supervised AI therapy chatbot, which guides clients through evidence-based, goal-aligned conversations while also detecting and flagging levels of distress in real time. Practitioners can review these interactions, enabling timely, informed interventions and ensuring safety, relevance, and personalisation.

ANTSA directly addresses the global shortage of mental health professionals, the lack of continuous support, and the barriers faced by underserved communities by providing a secure, culturally adaptable, and highly scalable solution. Built from inception with global deployment in mind, ANTSA’s architecture supports multilingual expansion, flexible integration with local health systems, and adaptation to community-specific needs.

By combining real-time mood tracking, daily journalling, automated homework task reminders, and an AI scribe that securely transcribes and summarises therapy sessions, ANTSA reduces practitioner burnout, increases engagement, and delivers actionable insights to guide timely interventions. Its in-house AI technology is hosted on privacy-compliant infrastructure that meets Australian Privacy Principles, HIPAA, and AHPRA standards, ensuring safety and resilience.

Through its readiness for international rollout, ANTSA offers governments, NGOs, and health providers a proven, easily implementable tool to expand access, strengthen resilience, and bridge critical gaps in mental health support.
Solution Provider(s): ANTSA Pty Ltd
Duration to pilot in a new geography: Approximately 6 months
SDGs addressed: SDG 3 (Good Health and Well-being);SDG 10 (Reduced Inequalities);SDG 8 (Decent Work and Economic Growth);
Desired impact:
ANTSA aims to expand continuous, high-quality mental health support beyond in-person sessions through secure, scalable, and culturally adaptable digital tools. The platform is designed to detect and respond to client distress in real time, enabling earlier interventions and reducing the risk of crisis. By automating administrative tasks such as note-taking, homework reminders, and mood tracking, ANTSA reduces practitioner burnout and allows mental health professionals to focus more on direct client care. Its goal is to globally improve client mental health outcomes and to bridge the gap between therapy sessions. 

ANTSA has already shown its ability to make a difference in critical situations. One example comes from a practitioner who described a quiet client who attended monthly sessions and consistently insisted she was fine. However, through her conversations with jAImee, ANTSA’s clinician-supervised AI therapy chatbot, the practitioner was alerted that her mental health was deteriorating towards suicidal ideation. Clients using jAImee are aware that their practitioner will review the chatbot conversations, which encourages openness while ensuring clinical oversight. In this case, the distress indicators triggered an alert, enabling the practitioner to recognise the seriousness of the situation and immediately schedule an appointment. This timely intervention prevented potential harm and demonstrated how jAImee can reveal critical issues that might otherwise remain hidden between appointments.

In other cases, ANTSA has helped clients maintain motivation and progress in therapy by providing daily prompts and reminders to complete therapeutic tasks, which has been particularly valuable for those struggling with depression or executive functioning difficulties. Practitioners have also used ANTSA’s real-time mood tracking to identify emerging patterns of anxiety or low mood and adjust treatment plans before issues escalate. In rural and remote settings, where travel and scheduling can be barriers to consistent support, ANTSA has allowed clients to remain engaged with their treatment plan between infrequent in-person sessions, ensuring continuity of care and reducing the risk of disengagement.
Key technologies: ANTSA uses a combination of in-house artificial intelligence, natural language processing, secure cloud infrastructure, and real-time data analytics to deliver continuous, clinician-guided mental health support. Its core innovation, jAImee, is the world’s first clinician-supervised AI therapy chatbot, engaging clients in guided therapeutic conversations, detecting distress in real time, and alerting practitioners for timely intervention. An AI-powered scribe securely transcribes and summarises sessions, reducing administrative workload. From inception, ANTSA was built with privacy at the forefront to protect the highly sensitive nature of mental health information. The platform is hosted on privacy-compliant infrastructure that meets Australian Privacy Principles, HIPAA, and AHPRA standards, ensuring data sovereignty, confidentiality, and resilience. This secure design allows practitioners and clients to engage with confidence, knowing their data is safeguarded at every step.
Unique Characteristics: ANTSA is the first and only digital mental health platform in the world to feature a clinician-supervised AI therapy chatbot, ensuring every AI-driven client interaction can be reviewed for safety, relevance, and personalisation. Built by Clinical Psychologist and founder Sally-Anne McCormack, who saw a critical gap in client support between therapy sessions, ANTSA is designed by practitioners for practitioners to address real-world challenges such as client disengagement and the growing administrative burden on clinicians. Unlike generic wellness apps, ANTSA is exclusively assigned by practitioners and tailored to individual treatment goals, maintaining a direct therapeutic link. Its AI scribe securely transcribes and summarises therapy sessions, reducing administrative workload and freeing time for client care. Real-time mood tracking, journalling, and automated homework reminders keep clients engaged while generating actionable insights for early intervention, including alerts for elevated distress. Developed entirely in-house with privacy at its core, ANTSA complies with Australian Privacy Principles, HIPAA, and AHPRA standards, making it both secure and globally scalable. Its business model supports adoption by clinics, hospitals, governments, and NGOs, with the flexibility to adapt to diverse cultural and community needs, enabling effective deployment in both developed and developing economies.
Sustainable Change:
ANTSA creates sustainable, systemic change by embedding continuous, digitally enabled mental health support into existing care systems, ensuring that therapeutic engagement does not end when a session finishes. By keeping clients connected through real-time mood tracking, automated therapeutic tasks, and a clinician-supervised AI chatbot, the platform enables earlier intervention, reduces relapse rates, and improves treatment outcomes. This sustained engagement not only benefits individual clients but also relieves pressure on overstretched health services, allowing practitioners to manage larger caseloads without compromising quality of care. Over time, these efficiencies can free up clinical resources for those in acute need, reduce long-term mental health costs, and increase service reach to underserved populations.

The desired follow-on effects include the normalisation of safe, clinician-guided digital tools as a standard part of mental health care, improved practitioner wellbeing through reduced administrative burden, and greater equity of access for women, youth, and marginalised groups. ANTSA’s scalable and culturally adaptable design means it can be integrated into diverse health systems worldwide, creating a replicable model for sustainable digital mental health delivery. As adoption grows, the platform’s anonymised data insights can inform public health strategies, drive policy reform, and support investment in preventative mental health measures, reinforcing a systemic shift towards accessible, efficient, and proactive care.
Funding Sources: To date, ANTSA has been entirely self-funded by its founder, Clinical Psychologist Sally-Anne McCormack. Development has been supported through voluntary input from mental health practitioners, university partnerships with Monash University and Swinburne University, and the expertise of ANTSA’s in-house technology team. Additional support has come from participation in industry accelerator programs such as ANDHealth ACTIVATE 2025, which has provided mentorship, business development resources, and networking opportunities. No external investment or large-scale grant funding has been received to date, ensuring the platform’s design and priorities have remained practitioner-led and client-focused.
Primary thematic focus area: Innovation Acceleration & Knowledge Sharing
Summary: ANTSA provides clinician-supervised AI-driven mental health support between therapy sessions, leveraging AI to engage clients, track mood, and ensure continuous care with real-time insights.

Title: Unlocking Inclusive Finance with AI-Powered Credit Scoring and Alternative Data for Smallholder Farmers and MSMEs
Subtitle: AI-Driven Credit Scoring with Alternative Data to Unlock Fair, Inclusive, and Data-Backed Financing for Smallholder Farmers and MSMEs
Problem Statement:
In Ethiopia, the rapid expansion of digital financial services has not translated into equitable access to credit. Despite a population exceeding 135 million, with over 70 percent under the age of 30, less than 1 percent can access collateral-free loans. Millions of smallholder farmers, women, youth, microbusiness owners, and micro, small, and medium enterprises (MSMEs), particularly in rural and informal sectors, remain systematically excluded from formal financial systems due to rigid, collateral-based lending practices.

This exclusion is reinforced by a convergence of structural and institutional barriers, including low levels of financial literacy, especially among youth and women, fragmented and siloed data systems, the absence of interoperable identity frameworks, limited adoption of automated underwriting tools such as credit scoring models, and regulatory frameworks that are slow to adapt to innovation. Many financial institutions still depend on static, manual processes that lack contextual awareness of borrower behavior. Low digital readiness, minimal trust, and poor coordination among stakeholders further hinder inclusive innovation.

Our AI-driven solution is purpose-built to address these systemic challenges. By harnessing alternative and behavioral data such as mobile usage patterns, informal cash flows, and social trust signals, and embedding them in adaptive machine learning models, we deliver context-aware, inclusive, and risk-sensitive credit assessments. This enables banks, MFIs, and fintechs to serve previously unreachable populations, including MSMEs, without compromising risk management. Our secure, no-code sandbox environment allows institutions to test, configure, and deploy tailored scoring models supported by real-time analytics and fraud detection tools.

This solution responds to urgent societal and economic priorities, including expanding financial inclusion, enabling entrepreneurship, creating jobs, and enhancing resilience for vulnerable populations. In an economy powered by MSMEs and smallholder farmers, inclusive access to finance is not just a development goal but a national economic imperative.
Solution Overview:
At Bahirbits, we are reshaping how creditworthiness is evaluated for underserved and data-constrained populations. Our AI-powered, context-aware credit scoring platform moves beyond traditional, collateral-based lending to deliver dynamic, data-informed risk assessments. It is specifically designed to serve youth-led microenterprises, smallholder farmers, and MSMEs that often fall outside the reach of conventional financial systems.

Conventional credit profiling leaves millions of individuals and small businesses, particularly women-led enterprises, excluded because it relies on limited indicators such as formal credit histories or physical collateral. We address this gap by integrating alternative and behavioral data, including mobile money usage, rent and utility payments, informal income patterns, microenterprise cash flows, and localized demographic signals. When available, we also incorporate structured data such as pension contributions and bank transactions to create comprehensive borrower profiles. This approach allows financial institutions to extend credit confidently to previously overlooked but creditworthy borrowers.

Our platform is built on a modular microservices architecture that ensures flexibility, scalability, and easy integration. Data flows from multiple sources through a robust ETL pipeline into adaptive machine learning models that assess repayment capacity and credit risk with high contextual sensitivity. We partner with institutions using subscription and revenue-sharing models, including co-development, scoring-as-a-service, and white-label deployments. The system integrates seamlessly via API or operates as a standalone no-code platform, with tailored onboarding, data integration, and regulatory alignment. A secure sandbox environment allows partners to simulate, test, and validate models before deployment.

Key components include:
- AI-Powered Scoring Engine: Adaptive models trained on diverse signals, lifecycle-managed with MLflow, supporting real-time and batch scoring.
- No-Code Sandbox: Enables institutions to configure scoring rules without coding skills.
- Fraud Detection and Risk Insights: Real-time indicators capture repayment risks often missed by traditional methods.
- Internal Data Governance framework: PII hashing and compliant sharing frameworks maintain trust and regulatory alignment.

Our scoring models combine interpretable techniques such as gradient boosting, logistic regression, and decision trees with human-in-the-loop processes for complex cases. For borrowers with limited documentation, we extract structured insights from receipts, documents, and images using advanced language and vision models. Continuous monitoring, drift detection, and automated retraining ensure reliable, production-ready operations. Every score is explainable, auditable, and accompanied by a complete history of training and evaluation data.

The platform’s multi-tenant modular design supports isolated workspaces for testing, production, and analytics, and scales across institutions, geographies, and products. Ethical AI principles and bias mitigation ensure fair, transparent, and inclusive scoring. Decision augmentation allows credit officers to review and adjust recommendations, enabling affordable, non-collateralized credit for youth-led enterprises, women entrepreneurs, smallholder farmers, and informal traders.

Bahirbits delivers data-driven, inclusive credit scoring and analytics solutions that strengthen institutional resilience, improve portfolio health, expand access to finance, and foster trust, pioneering the future of inclusive finance in emerging markets.
Solution Provider(s): The following key partners are actively involved in the implementation and scaling of our solution:  Vision Fund Microfinance: A leading microfinance institution in Ethiopia, committed to delivering financial services to underserved and low-income communities. Sector: Microfinance / Financial Services  Elsabi Microfinance: A dynamic provider supporting micro and small enterprises, with a focus on women and youth entrepreneurs, offering accessible and flexible lending products. Sector: Microfinance / Financial Services  The Association of Ethiopian Microfinance Institutions (AEMFI): The national umbrella organization for microfinance institutions in Ethiopia, promoting best practices, policy advocacy, and sector-wide capacity building to advance inclusive finance. Sector: Microfinance / Industry Association  Additional partners may include banks, fintech innovators, and regional financial cooperatives, all contributing to expanding reach, data integration, and technology adoption.
Implementation location(s): Our solution has been successfully implemented in Ethiopia, primarily in Addis Ababa and selected regional towns, focusing on underserved youth-led MSMEs and smallholder farmers. While the platform’s design and core technology are adaptable to other African and Asian markets, expansion into these regions has been limited due to unique local contexts, including differences in data availability, behavioral patterns, cultural factors, and regulatory environments. These factors require tailored adaptations to ensure accuracy and relevance, which are currently being explored for future deployments.
Implementation timeline(s): Our AI-powered credit scoring solution was developed with close engagement of financial institutions and underserved communities in Ethiopia. The design phase began in early 2024, incorporating insights from microfinance institutions such as Vision Fund and Elsabi, which collectively serve over 300,000 clients. Following this collaborative approach, we are preparing a pilot targeting 1,250 borrowers, including small business owners, youth, and women entrepreneurs. Early engagements with partner MFIs have helped us configure scoring models, integrate local data sources, and validate workflows in anticipation of the pilot. This process ensures the platform is user-centered, scalable, inclusive, and aligned with regulatory requirements, while enabling iterative refinement based on real-world feedback once the pilot is launched.
Duration to pilot in a new geography: We estimate a 6 to 8-month pilot period in a new geography. This timeline includes onboarding partner institutions, integrating local data sources, configuring and validating scoring models, training staff on the no-code platform, and conducting real-time testing with an initial cohort of borrowers. The phased approach ensures both operational readiness and iterative refinement, allowing the pilot to generate actionable insights on credit risk, repayment behavior, and financial inclusion outcomes. By the end of the pilot, we will have sufficient evidence to scale the solution across additional regions efficiently while maintaining regulatory compliance and context-sensitive risk assessment.
SDGs addressed: SDG 1 (No Poverty);SDG 5 (Gender Equality);SDG 8 (Decent Work and Economic Growth);
Desired impact:
Our primary objective is to expand equitable access to credit for underserved and traditionally excluded populations, including youth-led microenterprises, women entrepreneurs, and smallholder farmers. We aim to replace outdated, collateral-based lending practices with AI-driven, data-informed credit assessment tools that improve accuracy, reduce default risk, and promote financial inclusion. At the same time, we empower financial institutions with scalable, transparent, and customizable credit decisioning platforms that uphold ethical AI standards and ensure regulatory compliance.
Key Achievements and Impacts
- Enabled partner financial institutions in Ethiopia to provide affordable, non-collateralized credit to over 250 previously underserved borrowers since deployment.
- Achieved credit scoring decision turnaround times consistently under one minute, enhancing operational efficiency and borrower experience.
- Reduced loan default rates by up to 15% through more precise risk profiling using alternative and behavioral data.
- Supported financial inclusion of women entrepreneurs and youth-led businesses, which now represent over 60 percent of our active borrower base.
- Strengthened institutional capacity by delivering no-code tools and secure sandbox environments, enabling rapid model customization and adoption without extensive technical expertise.
- Maintained rigorous data governance and privacy compliance, fostering trust among borrowers and regulators.
Our solution’s impact extends beyond increasing credit access. By combining inclusive credit scoring with actionable insights and operational support, we help build resilient financial ecosystems that empower communities, stimulate local economic activity, and contribute to sustainable development in emerging markets.
Key technologies:
At the heart of our platform is artificial intelligence and machine learning, designed to understand real-world borrower behavior and expand access to inclusive finance. By analyzing alternative and behavioral data such as mobile money activity, utility payments, informal cash flows, and small business operations, our AI generates reliable and explainable credit scores. We combine interpretable models like gradient boosting, logistic regression, and decision trees with human-in-the-loop review for complex or borderline cases, ensuring fairness, transparency, and contextual accuracy. This approach empowers financial institutions to confidently extend non-collateralized credit to underserved populations, including youth, women, smallholder farmers, and MSMEs.

Underpinning this is a secure and robust data infrastructure that integrates ETL pipelines, data warehouses, and data lakes to consolidate information from core banking systems, ledgers, KPIs, and planning tools. A modular, no-code microservices architecture enables institutions to configure scoring rules, integrate seamlessly via APIs, or operate independently, making advanced credit assessment accessible even for organizations with limited technical capacity. Strong data governance ensures personal data is hashed and managed within GDPR-compliant frameworks, supporting auditability and regulatory alignment. Real-time dashboards and analytics provide actionable insights into portfolio health, risk trends, and inclusion metrics, helping lenders make timely, data-informed decisions that improve financial performance while promoting equitable and affordable access to credit.
Unique Characteristics:
Our solution is distinguished by its deep contextualization and adaptability to underserved markets, particularly in emerging economies like Ethiopia. Unlike conventional credit scoring tools that rely predominantly on formal credit histories and collateral, our platform harnesses a rich combination of alternative and behavioral data, including mobile money activity, informal income streams, utility payments, and microenterprise cash flows. This enables financial institutions to accurately assess creditworthiness for traditionally excluded populations such as youth-led microenterprises, women entrepreneurs, smallholder farmers, and informal workers. By generating interpretable and explainable AI-driven scores, our platform builds trust, supports regulatory compliance, and facilitates responsible lending.

Technologically, the platform is built on a modular, no-code architecture that allows institutions with varying technical capabilities to integrate and customize credit decisioning seamlessly. A secure sandbox environment lets partners simulate, calibrate, and validate scoring models and credit policies in alignment with local regulations and institutional priorities. Our AI models incorporate human-in-the-loop review for complex cases, ensuring that contextual insights complement machine efficiency. Ethical AI principles are embedded throughout, including fairness constraints to reduce bias and full transparency in scoring logic.

Beyond its technological innovation, the solution introduces flexible business and partnership models, including subscription services, revenue-sharing arrangements, co-development collaborations, and white-label deployments. These models lower barriers to adoption, foster long-term engagement with financial institutions, and enable rapid scaling across geographies and borrower segments. The combination of advanced AI, operational flexibility, ethical design, and strong institutional support makes our platform uniquely effective at closing financial inclusion gaps in complex, data-constrained environments.
Sustainable Change:
Our solution catalyzes sustainable, systemic change by fundamentally transforming credit evaluation for underserved populations, enabling inclusive access to finance in markets historically excluded from formal lending. By integrating alternative and behavioral data with ethical, transparent AI, we equip financial institutions to provide affordable, non-collateralized credit to youth-led microenterprises, women entrepreneurs, smallholder farmers, and informal workers. This broader access strengthens individual and business capacity, fosters community resilience, and generates a self-reinforcing cycle of economic empowerment.

The anticipated follow-on effects extend beyond immediate lending outcomes. More accurate, context-aware risk assessment reduces default rates and builds healthier loan portfolios, while transparent scoring and human-in-the-loop processes enhance trust between lenders and borrowers. Scalable, no-code deployment strengthens institutional capacity, allowing financial service providers to adopt inclusive credit practices rapidly and adaptively. Over time, these changes drive a systemic shift in lending models, moving away from exclusionary, collateral-based approaches toward equitable, data-informed credit ecosystems.

Ultimately, our platform contributes to long-term economic growth, poverty reduction, and equitable development by embedding fairness, accountability, and sustainability into financial decision-making. By transforming both borrower access and institutional practices, the solution promotes a resilient, inclusive, and scalable financial ecosystem that can be replicated and adapted across emerging markets.

In addition, we leveraged $1,000 in AWS Activate Startup credits to build and host our cloud infrastructure, enabling scalable, secure, and cost-efficient deployment of our AI-driven credit scoring platform. Strategic collaborations with microfinance institutions further enhanced our development process, providing real-world insights and early user engagement. This combination of internal resources, technical support, and partnership-driven input allowed us to design and refine a solution specifically tailored to the needs of underserved communities while ensuring scalability, reliability, and impact.

Title: StudentBuddy: Solar Power for Digital Access and Opportunity
Subtitle: A portable solar lighting and charging solution enabling education, entrepreneurship and digital participation in underserved communities.
Problem Statement: Extreme energy poverty prevents over 660 million people from accessing reliable electricity, limiting education, economic opportunity, and digital inclusion. Without the ability to charge devices, mobile learning, e-commerce and online services remain inaccessible to women, youth, MSMEs, and marginalised communities — deepening the global digital divide.
Solution Overview:
StudentBuddy is a portable, modular solar-powered lighting and charging system designed to close the energy gap that limits participation in the digital economy. It provides safe LED lighting, a portable torch, and dual USB ports for charging phones, tablets, and small devices — enabling education, entrepreneurship, and access to online services in communities without reliable electricity.

Methodologies & Technologies: The system integrates photovoltaic solar panels, long-life lithium-ion batteries, energy-efficient LED lighting, and USB charging. Its modular design allows for local repair and component replacement, reducing e-waste and extending product life to up to 15 years. All aluminium parts are made from 100% recyclable materials.

Partnerships & Collaboration Models: StudentBuddy devices are directly distributed to underserved communities through SolarBuddy’s in-country NGO partners and local delivery networks across the Pacific, Southeast Asia, Sub-Saharan Africa and remote First Nations communities in Australia. These partnerships ensure culturally appropriate deployment, local training for basic maintenance, and long-term support for end users.

SDGs addressed: SDG 4 (Quality Education);SDG 7 (Affordable and Clean Energy);SDG 10 (Reduced Inequalities);
Desired impact:
Desired Impact:
StudentBuddy is a solar-powered, modular lighting and charging system that closes the digital divide for students - especially girls - in off-grid communities. It enables device charging and offline learning, provides safe lighting for after-dark study, prioritises girls’ participation in education, reduces fossil fuel reliance with repairable clean technology, and creates local skills and employment through repair and assembly training.

Key Achievements / Impacts:

Charged up to 500 devices/month per 100 units, enabling digital access in remote areas.

Increased study time by an average of 2 hours/night per student.

Reached 70% female end-users, advancing educational equity and opportunity.

Avoided up to 136 tonnes CO₂e/year per 1,000 units by replacing kerosene lighting.

Delivered over 5 million hours of clean solar lighting/year per 100,000 units.

Built local capacity through training in maintenance and repair, supporting a circular economy.
Key technologies: StudentBuddy utilises integrated solar photovoltaic (PV) panels for off-grid renewable energy generation, modular lithium-ion battery storage for reliable, safe power, and LED lighting for high-efficiency illumination. The system includes USB charging ports compatible with a wide range of devices, supporting digital inclusion in remote areas. Its modular, repairable design enables easy maintenance and local assembly, extending lifespan and supporting circular economy practices.
Unique Characteristics: StudentBuddy combines renewable energy access, digital inclusion, and gender-focused education in a single, scalable solution. Its solar-powered, modular design integrates lighting, device charging, and offline educational content access, making it effective in even the most remote, off-grid settings. The system’s repairable, locally assembled components foster community ownership, create skills training opportunities, and support a circular economy. Distribution is enabled through a global network of NGOs, schools and community organisations, ensuring reach to underserved areas without the need for centralised infrastructure. The prioritisation of girls’ education and safety in design and deployment makes it not only a technology solution but also a social innovation.
Sustainable Change:
Problem: Off‑grid households lack reliable power, limiting study after dark and the ability to keep phones/devices charged for learning, communications, mobile money and essential digital services.

Inputs: Direct distribution of StudentBuddy (solar lighting + USB charging) via in‑country partners; basic user training; localised repair/maintenance with modular spares and planned battery replacement.

Immediate outputs: Safe lighting at home and in community spaces; consistent device charging; reduced spend on kerosene/paid charging; lower exposure to household air pollution.

- Expanded micro‑enterprise activity (e.g., mobile money, market access)
- Local skills and livelihoods from repair/maintenance (circular economy practices)

Long‑term impact:
- More equitable education and digital inclusion
- Increased climate resilience and reduced fossil‑fuel reliance

A scalable, replicable last‑mile model that strengthens community capacity and informs policy and investment in decentralised energy for inclusive digital economies.

Title: Music Technology for All: Digital and Creative Inclusion in Chad
Subtitle: Empowering Chadian youth and women through digital music skills, fostering creativity, inclusion, and cultural heritage preservation
Problem Statement: Chad, with over 50% under 28, sees its youth, especially women, excluded from specialized training and digital tools, in a music sector whose technical side remains male-dominated.
Solution Overview:
The “Music Technology for All” project aims to train young people, especially women, in digital music technologies and related creative skills. The solution operates through practical and theoretical training sessions, covering DAW (Digital Audio Workstation) use, music production, mixing, mastering, and composition. Participants have access to modern digital tools (production software, audio interfaces, digital instruments) and educational resources adapted to the Chadian context.

The methodology relies on an inclusive and participatory approach, combining in-person learning with remote support, practical workshops, mentoring, and collaborative projects. Participants create tangible musical productions, fostering immediate application of the skills learned.

The project leverages partnerships with local and international experts, professional studios, and cultural organizations to ensure high-quality skills transfer and visibility for young talent. Collaboration follows a co-creative model, where trainers and participants develop artistic and digital projects together, enhancing inclusion and youth autonomy.

SDGs addressed: SDG 4 (Quality Education);SDG 5 (Gender Equality);SDG 8 (Decent Work and Economic Growth);

-Train 10 young people, including 6 women, in DAW and digital music production skills.
-Boost female leadership and strengthen women’s inclusion in Chad’s music sector.
-Develop local cultural entrepreneurship and creative capacities.
-Promote Chadian cultural heritage through music production and dissemination.

Key Impacts:
-10 young people trained, including 6 women, with significant enhancement of female leadership.
-5 awardees equipped with basic professional music equipment, including 3 women, enhancing autonomy
-Over 20 original musical works created by participants.

The solution fosters sustainable, systemic change by developing digital and music skills among youth and women, promoting inclusion and empowerment in a still largely male-dominated cultural sector. It generates a multiplier effect through the training of the first generation of young leaders and the networking of local and international mentors, enabling knowledge transfer and best practice dissemination.

-Strengthened female leadership and reduced access barriers for women in Chad’s music sector.
-The creation of new economic and entrepreneurial opportunities around digital music and local culture.

Title: Digital Wallets for Inclusion and Sustainability in the era of Web3
Subtitle: A blockchain-based digital wallet solution. Web3 Digital Wallets are used to empower vulnerable populations and micro and small businesses (MSMEs) by giving them control over their identity, economic and environmental assets.
Problem Statement:
The solution is designed to address key challenges in socioeconomic inequality and asset management for vulnerable populations and MSME in Latin America and the Caribbean. Main challenges include: 

(i) Vulnerable groups, including MSMEs, have limited access to traditional asset management.  This is primarily due to high transaction costs in the "last mile," or the final step of delivering a service to the end customer. Traditional models have a depleted expansion capacity and are characterized by increasing marginal transaction costs as they try to expand their coverage. This unequal access limits the opportunities for vulnerable populations to improve their living conditions. 
(ii) Inefficiencies in Verification and High Service Costs: The high transaction costs in traditional asset management models are rooted in issues including inefficient verification, high service costs and a failure to recognize asset values. These costs impede SMEs from expanding their customer base or accessing credit. 
(iii) Gender and Social Inequality: There is a persistent gender gap in financial inclusion in the LAC region. According to the Global Findex Database 2021, the gender gap in bank account ownership is more than six percentage points, which is unfavorable to women. Regarding MSMEs, women‑owned businesses account for 34% of the global MSME finance gap—estimated at around US$1.9 trillion. Female-owned MSMEs represent 38% or less of all MSMEs globally. These enterprises tend to be smaller, informal, and frequently home-based, and are concentrated in sectors like health, hairdressing, and beauty services—with generally lower turnover and value-added. Even though they are informal, women-led MSMEs re often more profitable, stable, and innovative than their counterparts and commonly reinvest their earnings into family education, health, and nutrition—boosting broader social outcomes. However, the World Bank reports that 7 in 10 women‑owned MSMEs globally cite insufficient access to growth capital as a key barrier, contributing to a $300 billion per year finance deficit.  
(iv) Limited Access to Environmental Asset Valuation: Limitations in the valuation and monetization of environmental assets can hinder market value of products and the subsequent income. 
(v) Informal entities and small MSMEs have limited access to services. The lack of formal documentation, credit history or certifications limit access to attractive services and products.
Solution Overview:
The solution aims to use blockchain technologies to drastically decrease costs and barriers to access to financial and social services for the poor and vulnerable and for MSMEs. By reducing the costs and improving the efficiency of transactions, the solution seeks to increase access to financial services and asset management for people and groups who have been historically excluded. The project's goal is to empower these individuals and MSMEs by giving them full ownership of their data and assets. The solution is a single interoperable digital wallet protocol to improve the management of economic and environmental assets as well as to increase access to credit. This protocol, based on a blockchain network, will allow individuals to manage their tangible and intangible assets through a mobile application. The solution seeks to make individuals the owners of their data under a fully decentralized model. 

By using a single interoperable blockchain-based protocol, MSMEs can reduce credential verification costs from USD 5–8 to USD 0.20–0.40, making compliance and onboarding more affordable. Additionally, digitized credentials allow MSMEs to quickly share verified documents with partners, clients, and regulators, cutting down administrative burdens. 

The digital wallet technology can store a wide range of assets and credentials, including: 

Identity documents  
Property titles  
Environmental certificates  
Vaccination credentials  
Academic diplomas  
Credit history  
Professional certificates  
These wallets also allow users to present credentials via a QR code for transactional purposes, with real-time verification regardless of language or regulatory differences.  

The project's innovation lies in creating the first single interoperable blockchain-based protocol for digital wallets globally. The solution involves and leverages blockchain Technology to provide a decentralized online ecosystem, often referred to as Web3. This technology is key to reducing transaction costs and providing transparency and immutability for transactions. 

The project builds on the success of the existing LACChain Global Alliance focused on developing the blockchain ecosystem in Latin America and the Caribbean. LACChain brings together over 100 solutions across LAC and focuses on collaboration and partnership between these solutions. Stakeholders include members from multilateral agencies (the Inter-American Development Bank (IDB) Group), over 60 leaders in blockchain and technologies from the private sector, and academia (including ConsenSys, NTT Data, RSK, IBM, and Accenture). The model emphasizes a public-private stakeholder partnership to enable digital wallet ecosystems. It promotes an open and competitive market for applications and encourages replication in countries through public-private consortia and open-source protocols.

Agrayú (https://agrayu.com/), a private sector company focused on responding to the needs of rural farmers. Role: provider of digital solutions (loans and financial services) on the digital wallet.   XCapita (https://www.xcapit.com/), provider focused on digital solutions in finance, tokenization, and social impact. Role: ecosystem member.   NTT Data (https://nttdata-solutions.com/), international provider of business solutions focused on systems, applications and products in data processing (SAP). Role: ecosystem member.    Other service providers: could include other banks, universities, agricultural solutions, etc.   Fundación Julio Ricaldoni (https://ricaldoni.org.uy/), not-for-profit focused on linking the Engineering School at the University of Uruguay with farmers and other stakehoolders in the agricultural sector. Role: executing agency.   Inter-American Development Lab (https://bidlab.org/en),  innovation arm of the Inter-American Development Bank. Role: co-funding.   Swiss State Secretariat for Economic Affairs (https://www.seco.admin.ch/seco/en/home.html), Switzerland’s federal government’s center for excellence in all items related to economic and labor market policy. Role: co-funding.
Duration to pilot in a new geography: one year
SDGs addressed: SDG 5 (Gender Equality);SDG 8 (Decent Work and Economic Growth);SDG 10 (Reduced Inequalities);
Desired impact:
The desired impact of the solution is to foster socioeconomic inclusion and sustainability in Latin America and the Caribbean. This is to be achieved by creating a more efficient and equitable digital ecosystem for managing economic and environmental assets. 

(i) By reducing the costs and improving the efficiency of transactions, it seeks to increase access to financial services and asset management for SMEs and people who have been historically excluded. The project's goal is to empower these individuals by giving them full ownership of their data and assets. 
(ii) By applying verifiable digital credentials, it can support SMEs seamlessly participate in cross-border trade, tender processes, and digital marketplaces. Additionally, by offering secure, verifiable credit histories and asset records stored in the wallet, it can help SMEs qualify for loans, microcredit, or investment opportunities they previously could not access. 
(iii) By empowering women, who are currently excluded from asset management, women's participation in the digital economy will be increased, giving them greater control over their assets. By addressing gender gaps in financial and asset management, the solution expands opportunities for women entrepreneurs to grow and formalize their businesses. 
(iv) By enabling the tracking environmental assets, the solution aims to incentivize conservation efforts, reduce greenhouse gas emissions, support the sustainable management of natural resources and improve the income generated from these assets for individuals and communities. 
(v) By creating a single interoperable digital wallet protocol for the region, the solution will facilitate cross-border transactions and create a unified digital ecosystem. The goal is to establish a standard for digital credentials and assets that is recognized across different countries and regulatory bodies, thereby promoting regional economic integration and the seamless flow of goods, services, and information.
Key technologies: Blockchain technologies, digital wallets
Unique Characteristics:
The solution includes business, social and technological innovations: 

(i) Business and Partnership Models: The solution is built on the public-private stakeholder partnership model of the LACChain Global Alliance. This alliance includes over 60 partners, with global leaders in blockchain and technology such as ConsenSys, NTT Data, RSK, and IBM. This model fosters an open and competitive application market by bringing together public, private, and academic stakeholders to enable digital wallet ecosystems. The project also involves 20 organizational units from the Inter-American Development Bank (IDB) Group, ensuring alignment with their strategic mandates and providing technical and leadership support. Additionally, the project aims to achieve scalability by accelerating the development of a competitive market for digital wallet solutions. It provides a core, interoperable protocol that acts as a linchpin for a broad supply side (multiple technology providers) and a large, growing demand side (interested customers).  
(ii) Technological Breakthroughs: The solution’s primary innovation is that it enables the world's first single interoperable blockchain-based protocol for digital wallets. This protocol allows wallets to "talk to each other," enhancing asset management benefits and creating a broader market for digital wallet and complementary service providers. The protocol will allow citizens to manage a wide range of tangible and intangible assets, from identity documents and academic diplomas to environmental certificates, all through a single mobile application. The project utilizes the core technology developed by the LACChain alliance, which uses the IBFT2.0 consensus protocol. This proof-of-authority protocol is differentiated by its low energy consumption, giving it a "near-zero carbon footprint" and making it an environmentally sustainable alternative to other popular protocols like proof-of-work. Additionally, the solution operates on a fully decentralized model that puts vulnerable men and women in control of their own data and destiny. It uses zero-knowledge proof to ensure the protection of personal data, allowing users to share only the minimum necessary information for transactions without revealing all of their personal or medical details. The solution builds on the LACChain project’s foundation, which has been recognized as a model for global blockchain standards by bodies such as the International Telecommunication Union (ITU) and the International Organization for Standardization (ISO). The protocol complies with the Worldwide Web Consortium (W3C) Verifiable Credentials standard, ensuring its interoperability and security. 
(iii) Social Innovation: The solution is innovative in its vision of empowering people and SMEs by giving them ownership of their digital portfolios. This is a departure from traditional models that view this population as passive "beneficiaries" or "recipients". The project enables people to make their own asset management decisions, such as using their professional history for employment or their environmental assets for green credits. The solution has a proactive gender approach aimed at empowering women who are often excluded from managing their own assets. It specifically builds on the experience of a digital wallet project for victims of gender violence (CO-T1594) to offer an integrated solution of empowerment and self-management of assets to women. The project also includes skills development and hackathons to create solutions tailored to women's specific problems.
Sustainable Change:
The solution's central idea is to move beyond the traditional view of vulnerable populations as passive "beneficiaries" or "recipients". By giving people ownership and control of their digital assets and data, it empowers them to make their own decisions about managing their portfolios. The solution brings Web3 to reality for creative inclusive solutions, thus causing a paradigm shift. This opens a new development paradigm where individuals can directly access markets to monetize their assets and gain previously inaccessible income. For example, they could use their professional history to get a job or their environmental assets to obtain green credits. 

The solution's innovation lies in creating the world's first single interoperable protocol for digital wallets. This protocol acts as a linchpin, allowing different digital wallets to "talk to each other". This interoperability will help to build a critical mass of digital wallet and service providers, leading to a broader, more competitive market and lower prices for credential verification. The project aims to reduce the cost of credential verification from US 5−US8 to US0.20−US0.40, making these services more accessible. This market-based approach will drive adoption and scalability beyond the project's direct capacity. 

Additionally, the solution is designed to have a dual impact on both economic and environmental fronts. By valuing environmental assets and the income derived from their improved management, the project seeks to promote their conservation and reduce greenhouse gas (GHG) emissions. This will allow individuals to monetize these assets, creating an economic incentive for sustainable practices. For example, a landowner in the Yucatán Peninsula could obtain green certificates and issue climate bonds using their digital wallet.
Funding Sources: IDB Lab, IFAD, SECO
Further comments/feedback: We are inviting the UN the opportunity to join this powerful and inspiring initiative. Digital wallets are game changers for vulnerable populations and MSMEs, allowing them access to all their data and assets and control of their future. Through cutting-edge technology, the initiative drastically cuts costs for banks to provide services to last-mile populations and allow service providers and users a unique way to connect.
Primary thematic focus area: MSME Empowerment & Local Digital Innovation
Summary: The solution is a blockchain-based digital wallet system designed to empower vulnerable populations and MSMEs, particularly in Latin America and the Caribbean, by giving them control over their economic, environmental, and personal assets. The digital wallet integrates multiple asset types such as identity, property, environmental certificates, and credit history, promoting financial inclusion and sustainability.

Title: MyPiOLE: Digital Marketplace for Eco-Friendly & Inclusive Housing in Africa
Subtitle: "A digital platform connecting displaced people and low-income families to affordable, eco-friendly homes, fostering inclusion and climate resilience in Africa
Problem Statement: In Africa, millions of displaced people and low-income families face barriers to accessing safe, affordable housing due to fragmented markets, high costs, and limited digital connectivity
Solution Overview:
MyPiOLE is a digital marketplace designed to connect displaced people, low-income families, and vulnerable communities with affordable, eco-friendly housing. The platform digitizes housing demand and supply through a participatory database, enabling users to locate available shelters, community housing projects, and rental opportunities in real time via web, mobile app, and USSD for offline accessibility.

How it works

1. Data Collection & Mapping – Local agents, NGOs, and community members submit housing availability and needs via mobile/USSD, which are geotagged and verified.
2. Smart Matching Algorithm – AI-powered search filters match users with relevant housing options based on budget, location, and eco-friendly features.
3. Sustainable Housing Integration – Promotes homes built with local, low-carbon materials, equipped with solar energy systems and biodigesters for waste-to-energy.
4. Inclusive Payment Models – Integrates mobile money, microfinance, and rent-to-own options.

Technologies & Methodologies:
AI and Data Analytics for housing demand/supply matching
Blockchain for secure, transparent rental/ownership contracts
USSD technology for offline access in low-connectivity areas
GIS mapping to visualize housing distribution and gaps
Co-creation approach with community input at every stage

Partnerships & Collaboration Models:
NGOs and UN agencies (HCR, UN-Habitat) for data sourcing and outreach
Local governments for policy alignment and land allocation
Private sector and social enterprises for housing construction and green tech
Microfinance institutions and mobile money providers to enable affordable payment solutions
Community-based organizations for user trust-building and platform adoption

MyPiOLE not only provides digital inclusion but also fosters climate resilience and economic empowerment by creating a transparent, accessible, and sustainable housing ecosystem in Africa.

Title: NATAL CARES
Subtitle: NATAL CARES is a digital organization leveraging power of Mobile Technology, Machine Learning and Low Cost Innovation to combat maternal and infant mortality in Nigeria.
Problem Statement:
According to W.H.O, Nigeria stands as one of the world's most riskiest countries for childbirth, contributing to 19% of global maternal and child deaths. UNICEF reports that Nigeria loses 2,300 children under five and 145 women daily due to pregnancy and delivery complications, making it the LARGEST contributor to global under-five and maternal mortality rates. Our research indicates that a staggering 85% of this mortality is concentrated in underserved rural communities in Nigeria due to three major root causes. Natal Cares aims to address these three major root causes:
	
1.	The healthcare and information gap, leaving Nigerian women susceptible to superstitions and fables.
2.	Unhealthy childbirth practices by untrained community healthcare providers in vulnerable communities.
3.	Lack of child vaccination, contributing to mortality among children aged 0-5.
		

PROBLEM WE ARE TRYING TO SOLVE
1.	HEALTH CARE INFORMATION GAP:
We are tackling the lack of access to basic healthcare information in underserved communities. This information gap leaves many women vulnerable to relying on superstitions instead of medically certified healthcare information, which can lead to poor health outcomes.

2.	UNHEALTHY CHILD-DELIVERY PRACTICES:
We are addressing the prevalence of unhealthy child-delivery practices in underserved communities, where untrained traditional birth attendants and local community caregivers often oversee births, posing significant risks to both mothers and newborns.

3.	LACK OF VACCINATION AND CHILDHOOD RELATED DISEASES:
We are combating the devastating impact of preventable childhood diseases caused by a lack of vaccinations. According to the World Health Organization (WHO), vaccine-preventable diseases remain the most common cause of childhood mortality, with an estimated three million deaths each year in Nigeria alone.
Solution Overview:
At Natal Cares, we have developed a holistic innovative solution that work across the entire care continuum (including education, prevention, detection, treatment, management, follow-up) to solve the three root causes that have been identified and help improve maternal and child health and reduce the risk of maternal deaths and other adverse perinatal outcomes. 

First, we bridge the healthcare information gap in underserved communities through the innovative use of mobile technology. Medically certified healthcare information is delivered to pregnant and nursing mothers via SMS and VOICE NOTES in their preferred local languages accessible on both feature phones and smartphones empowering them to make informed healthcare decisions for themselves and their babies. Through this service, we ensure that no mother, no matter how disadvantaged, is ever truly abandoned by healthcare professionals. 

Secondly, in-order to curb the unhealthy child delivery practices, we have developed Comprehensive DELIVERY KITS containing Sixteen W.H.O recommended critical supplies pregnant women require at childbirth to ensure a safe and hygienic delivery. Also through Onsite and our E-Training Platform, we train and educate frontline health workers and Traditional birth Attendants on latest delivery practices to increase their skillset, knowledge of best practices and build their capacity. 

To combat the devastating consequences of preventable childhood diseases due to insufficient vaccination, we provide adequate Vaccinations for Infants and children also our Mobile Application includes an IMMUNIZATION REMINDER feature through which we meticulously track and ensure that mothers bring their babies for immunization. The App also serves as a comprehensive resource, offering information on nutrition, supplements, and healthy eating habits for pregnant women and nursing mothers. Additionally, it boasts innovative and user-friendly features such as CONNECT-TO-DOCTOR, Natal Cares HELPLINE, DELIVERY KITS ONLINE, and a BLOOD BANK Connect.


Methodologies and Technologies Used
1.	Mobile-first approach leveraging SMS, USSD, and voice for offline users, and WhatsApp/Android apps for online users.
2.	AI-driven personalization to adapt health messages to the woman’s stage of pregnancy and risk profile.
3.	Data integration & dashboards for monitoring maternal outcomes and enabling healthcare partners to make data-driven decisions.
4.	Cloud-based interoperability ensuring scalability and compatibility with health management systems.
5.	Inclusive design methodology – co-created with mothers, TBAs, and local communities to reflect real-world needs.
Partnerships and Collaboration Models


Natal Cares works through a collaborative ecosystem:
1.	Community Health Facilities & TBAs – integrating digital tools and sterile kits into their practices.
2.	NGOs & Development Partners – leveraging networks for outreach, training, and scaling impact.
3.	Universities & Medical Experts – ensuring content accuracy and continuous improvement.
4.	Government & Public Health Agencies – aligning with maternal health programs and national digital health strategies.
5.	Private Sector Partners – including telecom operators for message delivery and logistics partners for kit distribution.
This multi-stakeholder approach ensures sustainability, inclusivity, and scalability, allowing Natal Cares to reach the most vulnerable populations with life-saving care and health information.

By combining digital health innovation, community engagement, and women-focused financial tools, Natal Cares is building healthier families and advancing inclusive digital economies.

Natal Cares leverages a mix of digital health technologies and low-cost innovations to deliver impact at scale:

Unique Characteristics:
Natal Cares provides a Holistic solution that works across the entire care continuum (including education, prevention, detection, treatment, management, follow-up) to help improve maternal and child health and reduce the risk of maternal deaths and other adverse perinatal outcome. 

We provide behavioral change modification using continuous health education and information via our SMS and VOICE Platforms. Therefore, connecting offline and online care for improved maternal and child health. We build strong support systems for mothers using the power of social networking and low cost innovations. This makes it easy for mothers to access services they care about in real time. 

At NATAL CARES, Not only have we developed a disruptive prevention and care delivery model, but we have also developed a unique proprietary technology that helps to replicate our model in other countries to help achieve Universal Healthcare Coverage.

Natal Cares is currently the only Startup in West Africa that provides Live Saving Healthcare information to Users using SMS and VOICE NOTES in preferred Local Languages which is accessible on both Feature Phones and Smart Phones.

Title: From Speech and Language to Mental Health Insights:  Representing and Predicting Disorders
Subtitle: Leveraging AI and social media analytics for early detection, interpretable diagnosis, and scalable mental health interventions in underserved populations.
Problem Statement: Mental health disorders affect 16.6% of the global population, yet diagnosis rates remain below 30% due to inefficiencies in traditional screening (>30 minutes per assessment), lack of objective biomarkers, and systemic healthcare disparities. The stigma surrounding mental illness further limits access to care, particularly in low-resource settings. Social media and digital platforms offer untapped potential for early risk detection and intervention but require robust, interpretable AI frameworks to translate user-generated content into clinically actionable insights while addressing ethical and privacy concerns.
Solution Overview:
Methodologies and Technologies:

Early Risk Detection:

Multimodal AI Models: Integrate acoustic (24-D Mel spectrograms + nonlinear energy entropy), textual (BERT-based symptom networks), and affective features to capture cross-scale pathological markers (e.g., vocal micro-perturbations linked to emotional suppression).

Self-Supervised Learning: Deploy the DEPA framework (Response-level Compression → Contrastive Distillation → Lightweight Decoding) to reduce reliance on labeled clinical data, achieving a 20% F1-score improvement (DAIC-WOZ dataset) and cutting screening time from 30 to 5 minutes.

Interpretable Diagnosis:

Knowledge Graph (PsySym): Map DSM-5 criteria to a computable ontology (7 disorders, 38 symptoms, 2,487 descriptions) using Graph Neural Networks (GNNs) with symptom-level attention, enabling transparent decision-making (e.g., "anhedonia → bipolar risk" pathways).

Causal Analysis: Apply Propensity Score Matching (PSM) to social media data, uncovering symptom-symptom and life-event triggers (e.g., "irritability → weight change" in PTSD), validated by clinical literature.

Scalable Interventions:

Ethical AI Ecosystem: Develop PsyEval (clinical benchmarking) and MedEthicEval (12 ethical scenarios) to ensure safety in LLM-based tools like the "Lingua" companion chatbot (10,000+ users served).

Open Frameworks: Release PsyDial (5 therapy流派 parameterized dialogues) and D4 dataset (4,500 PHQ-9/GAD-7 annotated dialogues), adopted by 20+ institutions.

Partnerships:

Clinical: Collaborate with Shanghai Mental Health Center, Peking Union Medical College, and NIH-funded teams to validate tools in real-world settings (e.g., community smart-speaker systems in Xuhui District).

Academic/Industry: Partner with Alibaba DAMO (chatbot deployment), Princeton (LLM research), and IEEE standards committees to advance ethical AI guidelines.

Global Health: Coordinate with the UN Digital Economy Taskforce to pilot solutions in LMICs, aligning with SDG 3.4 (mental health promotion).

Impact:

Efficiency: 6x faster screenings, 35% misdiagnosis reduction in comorbid cases (AUC=0.91).

Accessibility: Deployed via WeChat Mini-Programs (e.g., "JiaoWoXin") and open-source tools (PsySym, PsyEval).

Policy Influence: Contribute to China’s National AI Ethics Consensus and WHO digital mental health guidelines.

Keywords: AI for mental health, causal symptom networks, ethical LLMs, global health equity.
Solution Provider(s): Mengyue Wu, Associate Professor at School of Computer Science, Shanghai Jiao Tong University; Zhen Wang, Associate Dean, Shanghai Mental Health Center & National Mental Disorder Research Center.
Implementation location(s): Partially in U.S. for screening depression, but using social media and causal graphs for multiple disorder screening and early detection has not been implemented.
Duration to pilot in a new geography: 3 months.
SDGs addressed: SDG 3 (Good Health and Well-being);
Desired impact:
Improve Early Detection & Diagnosis – Reduce the time and cost of mental health screenings while increasing accuracy and accessibility, particularly in underserved regions.

Enhance Clinical Interpretability – Shift from "black-box" AI predictions to symptom-level explainability, aiding clinicians in decision-making.

Scale Affordable Interventions – Deploy AI-driven chatbots and digital tools to provide low-cost, stigma-free mental health support globally.

Advance Ethical AI Standards – Establish safety and privacy frameworks for mental health AI to prevent misuse and ensure responsible deployment.

Reduce Global Mental Health Disparities – Bridge gaps in care by leveraging digital platforms (social media, mobile apps) to reach high-risk populations.
Key technologies:
The solution integrates a suite of advanced artificial intelligence technologies to revolutionize mental healthcare through early detection, accurate diagnosis, and scalable interventions. At its core, multimodal AI combines voice analysis and natural language processing to provide comprehensive mental health assessments. The acoustic analysis component examines subtle vocal biomarkers such as speech rhythm, pitch variations, and energy patterns that correlate with conditions like depression and anxiety. Simultaneously, sophisticated NLP models, including BERT-based architectures and graph neural networks, analyze textual data from social media and clinical conversations to identify symptoms and map them to established diagnostic criteria.

A key innovation is the self-supervised learning framework, which significantly reduces the need for labor-intensive labeled data by employing a three-stage process of response-level compression, contrastive distillation, and lightweight decoding. This approach enables effective model training even with limited clinical annotations. The system's diagnostic capabilities are further enhanced by PsySym, a comprehensive knowledge graph that structures clinical knowledge from the DSM-5, connecting seven major mental disorders with 38 specific symptoms through 2,487 detailed descriptions.

The solution employs causal AI techniques, particularly propensity score matching, to uncover complex relationships between symptoms and life events over time. This allows for predictive insights, such as identifying how specific stressors might lead to particular symptoms. For therapeutic applications, specialized large language models are fine-tuned with therapy-aligned frameworks like PsyDial and Chain-of-Psychotherapy prompting to ensure clinically appropriate, empathetic interactions in mental health chatbots.

To address critical ethical concerns, the solution incorporates robust safety measures including the PsyEval and MedEthicEval benchmarking systems that assess AI models across multiple dimensions of clinical appropriateness, empathy, and safety. These technologies are deployed through accessible platforms like WeChat mini-programs and voice-enabled smart speakers, making mental health support available to broader populations. The system is further supported by open-source datasets and tools that enable global research collaboration and continuous improvement in the field of AI-driven mental healthcare.
Unique Characteristics:
Our solution represents a transformative approach to mental healthcare through several unique and differentiated characteristics that set it apart from conventional methods and existing digital health solutions:

1. Unified Multimodal AI Framework for Mental Health
Unlike current solutions that focus on single modalities (either text or voice analysis), our technology integrates acoustic, linguistic, and behavioral biomarkers into a cohesive diagnostic system. This multimodal approach captures the complex interplay between vocal patterns (like micro-tremors detected through nonlinear energy entropy analysis), linguistic markers (extracted via our specialized BERT-based symptom networks), and behavioral data from digital footprints. The integration of these diverse data streams through our proprietary DEPA self-supervised learning framework enables detection of mental health conditions with 20% greater accuracy than unimodal systems, while reducing screening time from 30 minutes to just 5 minutes.

2. Clinically-Grounded Explainable AI
While most AI mental health tools operate as "black boxes," our solution embeds clinical interpretability at its core through two groundbreaking innovations: the PsySym knowledge graph (mapping 7 disorders to 38 symptoms with 2,487 descriptive relationships) and our symptom aggregation networks. This allows the system to not just predict disorders, but explain its reasoning through symptom-level pathways (e.g., "detected anhedonia + sleep disturbance → 68% depression likelihood"), giving clinicians unprecedented transparency. Our causal AI component further differentiates by revealing how life events may trigger symptom cascades over time, moving beyond static snapshots to dynamic risk modeling.

3. Therapy-Specific Digital Intervention Engine
Our PsyDial framework represents the first parameterization of five major psychotherapy approaches (CBT, DBT, etc.) into AI systems, enabling truly modality-specific digital interventions. Unlike generic chatbots, our solutions can adapt therapeutic strategies based on both clinical best practices and individual response patterns. The Chain-of-Psychotherapy prompting system ensures interventions maintain therapeutic fidelity while our real-time adherence monitoring prevents "concept drift" - a common problem in mental health AI applications.

4. Ethical AI Infrastructure for Sensitive Domains
We've built the first comprehensive ethical framework specifically for mental health AI, including: MedEthicEval benchmark (12 clinical ethics scenarios) , which embedded "circuit breakers" to detect and mitigate harmful outputs. This infrastructure has become a reference standard, adopted by 10+ leading healthcare AI developers and incorporated into national guidelines.

5. Longitudinal Outcome Focus
Unlike point-in-time assessments, our causal AI and continuous monitoring capabilities create the first true longitudinal mental health profiling system, capable of tracking symptom trajectories and intervention effectiveness over months or years - a capability recently validated in our NAACL 2024 study showing 60-day early prediction accuracy.

These differentiated characteristics collectively position our solution not just as another mental health app, but as a new paradigm for global mental healthcare - one that combines clinical rigor with technological innovation while addressing the critical gaps in accessibility, affordability, and stigma that limit current systems.
Sustainable Change:
By redefining mental healthcare as a preventive, data-driven public utility, we move the locus of action from overloaded clinics to the everyday touchpoints—phones, speakers, national clouds—where risk is first detectable. AI screening and forecasting, wrapped in open yet privacy-preserving data standards, become embedded in health policy and digital public infrastructure, creating a virtuous cycle: cheaper early detection funds wider deployment, wider deployment feeds richer anonymized outcomes, richer outcomes sharpen the models and justify further public investment. This structural shift turns mental health from a discretionary expense into an infrastructure line item, much like clean water or broadband, ensuring sustained financing and political priority.

Equally critical is the transfer of ownership outward. Clinicians gain time and trust through transparent, explainable tools; local workers become “AI stewards” who adapt the system to culture and context; open datasets let low- and middle-income countries leapfrog legacy hospitals and catalyze global research consortia. Together these forces collapse the 50 % global diagnosis gap, normalize proactive mental fitness the way step-counters normalized physical fitness, and replace stigma with a resilient, self-improving ecosystem that no single donor or election cycle can dismantle.

Health Equity: Cut global diagnosis gaps by 50% in underserved regions.
Economic Inclusion: Mental health support integrated into digital public infrastructure (e.g., India’s Ayushman Bharat).
Resilient Societies: Address the global economic burden of mental illness through prevention.

This is not incremental improvement—it is rewiring mental healthcare at a systemic level. By aligning technological innovation with clinical practice, policy, and community needs, we create a self-sustaining ecosystem where mental well-being is universally accessible, proactive, and destigmatized.

Name of your organization: Department of Science and Technology Regional Office VI
Title: Strengthening the Regional Startup Ecosystem: Establishment of Provincial and Regional Innovation Hubs (iHubs)
Subtitle: The Innovation Hubs (iHubs) are spaces where individuals and groups can meet, interact, develop new ideas, find solutions that address economic and social problems and be ready to become innovative startups.   The proposed iHubs will act as pre-incubators, helping early-stage startups by offering office space, mentorship, networking, and soft skills development. This project will benefit all startup ecosystem players, including nascent startups, academic and research institutions, TBIs, accelerators, government agencies, and private industries.
Problem Statement:
The Philippines’ startup ecosystem is rapidly growing but remains heavily centralized in Metro Manila, creating regional disparities and limiting nationwide innovation. A key challenge is the lack of pre-incubation support, especially in provinces, which prevents many promising student-led and nascent startup ideas from evolving into viable startups.

Existing Technology Business Incubators (TBIs) are overstretched, while most students view innovation as an academic requirement rather than a potential career path. This results in missed opportunities to cultivate entrepreneurship and commercialize research.

To address this, Innovation Hubs (iHubs) are needed to serve as pre-incubators that bridge the gap between higher education institutions and TBIs. iHubs will nurture early-stage entrepreneurs, promote a startup mindset among students and researchers, and support regional innovation, contributing to a more inclusive and competitive national startup ecosystem.
Solution Overview:
The DOST Innovation Hubs (iHubs) are pre-incubation facilities designed to support early-stage innovators especially students, researchers, and aspiring entrepreneurs at the pre-seed or ideation stage.

Located in the DOST provincial/regional offices or hosted by partner institutions like HEIs, iHubs bridge the gap between academia and formal startup support systems. They offer structured programs based on the 4I Strategies: Inspire, Interact, Ideate, and Initiate, helping individuals transform ideas into viable startup concepts. 

Once ideas are validated, iHubs refer them to Technology Business Incubators (TBIs) for further development. High-growth startups may then proceed to DOST PROPEL, which provides advanced mentorship, funding access, and market support.

The iHub initiative follows this implementation methodology:

Establish iHub Facilities
Set up physical hubs within DOST Offices, HEIs or partner institutions across provinces.
Provide essential infrastructure (co-working spaces, training areas, etc.).

Support Budding Entrepreneurs through Services
Deliver pre-incubation services: idea development, business model design, mentorship, networking, and early validation.
Encourage entrepreneurial mindset through workshops, innovation challenges, and pitch events.

Establish Policies, Guidelines, and Metrics
Develop and implement standardized operational policies and success metrics for effective monitoring and replication.
Promote iHubs in the Regions
Execute campaigns to attract students, faculty, local communities, and researchers.
Strengthen awareness through school visits, webinars, and collaborations with LGUs and industry.

iHubs are more than physical spaces—they are catalysts for regional innovation. By supporting inclusive ecosystems that connect HEIs, local communities, and the private sector, iHubs:

Foster grassroots innovation and entrepreneurship
Promote commercialization of local R&D outputs
Address talent shortages by nurturing entrepreneurial mindsets early
Diversify startup activity beyond Metro Manila
Build a strong national pipeline of startups ready for incubation and acceleration

This cohesive and stage-based innovation support system—comprising iHubs, TBIs, and PROPEL—ensures startups receive the right support at the right time, empowering them to grow locally and scale globally.
Solution Provider(s): The iHubs are built on multi-sector collaboration to ensure sustainability and regional impact:  18 DOST Regional and 82  Provincial Offices: Lead implementers, funders, and coordinators of the iHubs. Higher Education Institutions (HEIs): Host facilities, provide access to students, faculty, and research outputs. Technology Business Incubators (TBIs): Receive referrals for startups ready for formal incubation. DOST PROPEL Program: Supports startups in the growth and scaling phase, offering advanced mentorship and market support. Local Government Units (LGUs): Support local engagement, funding, and promotion. Industry and Private Sector (Philippine Chamber of Commerce and Industry – Iloilo Chapter): Offer mentoring, funding, and market linkages. NGOs and Development Agencies: Support inclusion-focused entrepreneurship and capacity building.

Implementation timeline(s): The implementation of the Innovation Hubs (iHubs) began in January 2024, with 56 hubs successfully launched to date and more currently under development. This is an ongoing, nationwide initiative with no fixed end date, as it is designed for continuous rollout and long-term support of regional innovation ecosystems across the Philippines.
Duration to pilot in a new geography: The estimated duration to pilot the iHub solution in a new geography is 24 months. The timeline covers the establishment of iHub facilities with necessary infrastructure and staffing, and the delivery of pre-incubation services. It also includes the development of policies and success metrics, along with outreach efforts to engage communities, HEIs, and other stakeholders.   After the initial 24-month pilot, iHubs are expected to continue operating as permanent regional innovation support centers, providing ongoing pre-incubation services and serving as long-term catalysts for local startup development and inclusive innovation ecosystems.

The primary objective of the iHubs initiative is to establish a robust and inclusive pre-incubation support system across Philippine regions.

Potential Outcomes
The iHub initiative is expected to significantly increase awareness and engagement in innovation and entrepreneurship, especially in underserved regions. It provides the foundational support for ideas to evolve into market-ready startups.

Projected Impacts (The 2Is)
A. Economic Impact

B. Social Impact
