Title: TODAS em tech: Inclusion of Women in the Digital Economy
Subtitle: Free online bootcamps and a hiring platform for Black, trans, and vulnerable women to enter the technology sector.
Problem Statement:
Brazil faces an estimated shortage of 260,000 programmers, while only 17% of computer science graduates are women and only 25% of the technology workforce is female. The underrepresentation is even more pronounced for Black, Indigenous, and trans women, who account for only 11% of technology jobs. These inequalities have structural roots: socioeconomic, geographic, and educational barriers; a lack of encouragement and security for women in STEM; and a lack of accessible, practical training options aligned with market demands.

The few existing initiatives do not prioritize women in vulnerable situations nor do they offer support to overcome challenges such as internet access, adequate equipment, and professional networks. Universities, in turn, maintain more theoretical curricula that are less responsive to the dynamics of the digital economy, further excluding those who live outside major urban centers.

The situation was exacerbated by the COVID-19 pandemic, which forced seven million women out of the labor market in the country, two million more than men, disproportionately affecting Black women, who rely primarily on informal and in-person employment. Without inclusive and scalable interventions, the technology sector—which represents 6.8% of Brazil's GDP and concentrates nine of the 15 most in-demand emerging professions—will continue to reproduce inequalities and waste the potential of millions of women capable of contributing to innovation and economic growth.
Solution Overview:
Todas em Tech, developed by {reprograma} with institutional support from IDB Lab and a committee of investing companies, is a national solution for the inclusion of Black, trans, and vulnerable women in the technology sector, combining intensive training, an employability platform, and a data system to ensure access and retention in the digital economy.

How it works

- Free 18-week online bootcamps programming, with a 354 hour workload, focused on technical and socio-emotional skills.
- Inclusive selection process with immersive workshops and practical challenges, prioritizing participants from the North and - Northeast regions, with a family income of up to 3 minimum wages, and racial and gender identity.
- Employability platform that connects alumni with companies through a database of resumes, portfolios, and job openings, with integration with ATS systems (e.g., Gupy, Greenhouse).
- Full support: internet scholarships, laptops, and financial support; Weekly pedagogical guidance; mentoring sessions with industry professionals; and a post-bootcamp continuing education program.

Methodologies and Technologies

- Project-based learning and active learning, with question-and-answer sessions, individual and group guidance, and development of socio-emotional skills.
- Technologies: Programming languages, LMS platforms, videoconferencing, microlearning, integration with ATS, and a data module for impact monitoring.
- Content and tools adapted for low-connectivity contexts, ensuring accessibility.

Collaboration Model
The program is supported by a network of partners that work in mentoring, hiring, outreach, and technological integration. Of note is the Committee of Investing Companies (Accenture, Creditas, iFood, Meta, and Nubank), which, together with IDB Lab, provided significant financial resources and contributed market insight, strategic improvements to the program, and a commitment to hiring graduates.
Solution Provider(s): {reprograma} – A Brazilian non-profit civil society organization founded in 2016, specializing in training women in technology with a focus on employability and diversity. Responsible for the design, implementation, and management of Todas em Tech.  IDB Lab (Inter-American Development Bank) – An innovation laboratory that finances and supports inclusive solutions in Latin America and the Caribbean. It invested approximately 50% of the total budget through non-reimbursable technical cooperation, enabling online adaptation, developing the employability platform, and strengthening the data system.  Investing Companies Committee – A group formed by Accenture, Creditas, iFood, Meta, and Nubank, which contributed significant financial resources (approximately 30% of the total budget) and also serves as an advisory board to ensure alignment with market demands. This committee collaborated on defining improvements to the program and platform experience, recommended professionals for mentorships, participated in final project evaluation panels, and committed to hiring graduates.  Tech Communities – AfroPython, Womakers Code, Elas Programam, Cloud Girls, Preta Nerd, Developers Girls, Manas Digitais, Tech Girl BR, among others – supported the program's outreach, mobilization, and candidate referrals, strengthening the program's reach among underrepresented groups.  Educational Partners – Alura and Descomplica, which offered free or discounted access to supplementary courses and learning paths for former students, expanding their technical skills and employability.
Implementation location(s): Brazil – nationwide implementation with a priority focus on the North and Northeast regions. Administrative headquarters: São Paulo, SP.
Duration to pilot in a new geography: 2020 – Structuring and Preparation Adaptation of the in-person model to a 100% online format, ensuring accessibility for women in situations of socioeconomic and geographic vulnerability. Initial development of the employability platform and the data system for impact monitoring. Definition of the remote methodology based on project-based learning and integration with digital teaching tools.  2021 to 2022 – Implementation of the first national cycle (Todas in Tech) Implementation of 10 online bootcamps (front-end and back-end), each lasting 18 weeks. Over 2,160 women were educated in technical workshops and 400 graduated, prioritizing Black women, trans women, and women living in the North and Northeast regions. High completion rate (aprox. 85%) and job placement rate (around 70%) in the first cycle, showing strong alignment between training and employability. Launch of the employability platform (beta version) and beginning of integration with market ATS systems. Activation of the Committee of Investing Companies (Accenture, Creditas, iFood, Meta, Nubank) for strategic co-creation and hiring support.  2023 to 2024 – Expansion and diversification of formats Leveraging the learnings from Todas em Tech to create new training paths in partnership with Google. Expanding the target audience, serving not only women in career transition, but also those already in the market seeking specialization. Implementing courses for female leaders and educators, in addition to technical training specializing in JavaScript. Consolidation of educational partnerships (Alura, Descomplica) and improvement of the employability platform.  2025 to 2026 – New phase of growth and fundraising for emerging areas Ongoing fundraising process to  expand the Todas em Tech program,  now focusing on cybersecurity, artificial intelligence, and data science — strategic and high-demand sectors.  Long-term vision Maintain recurring and thematically diversified cycles, continually training thousands of women prepared for the digital economy, expanding their employability and strengthening diversity in the technology sector. In parallel, we are also investing in early digital education for long-term cultural change through the Futuro em código (Code the Future) , aimed at girls and boys aged 6 to 17 in public school. By starting early, we not only empower girls with foundational skills in technology, but also engage boys in conversations about gender, ethics, and the responsible use of digital tools - key to breaking cycles of digital violence and building a more inclusive future.

Title: From Soil to Cloud: The Future of Farming is Inclusive
Subtitle: A Scalable Digital Public Infrastructure Empowering Farmers, Strengthening Governance, and Driving Global Food Security
Problem Statement:
Agriculture remains the backbone of rural livelihoods and food security in India and across many developing nations, but the sector faces persistent structural and systemic challenges that limit productivity, resilience, and inclusivity.
1. Fragmented and Inefficient Agricultural Ecosystem:
Farmers often operate in isolation with limited access to timely, reliable, and localized information. Advisory services, credit, insurance, and subsidy programs are fragmented, leading to inefficiencies, duplication, and policy leakages.
2. Limited Data-Driven Decision Making:
Policymakers and administrators lack real-time, ground-validated insights into crop health, yield forecasts, pest/disease outbreaks, and resource allocation. This gap restricts proactive governance and results in delayed or suboptimal interventions.
3. Farmer Exclusion and Inequity:
Smallholder farmers, women-led farms, and marginalized communities often remain outside the formal agricultural ecosystem due to lack of digital identity, weak access to finance, and absence of consent-driven data governance frameworks. This perpetuates inequitable access to subsidies, credit, insurance, and market linkages.
4. Climate Vulnerability and Risk Exposure:
Increasing climate variability, pest infestations, and crop stress threaten yields and farmer incomes. The absence of predictive, technology-enabled monitoring and early-warning systems exacerbates risk at both farm and policy levels.
5. Scalability and Replicability Challenges:
Existing pilot solutions in agriculture often fail to scale beyond specific regions due to rigid design, lack of interoperability, and inability to adapt to diverse agro-climatic and governance contexts.
6. Trust Deficit in Digital Transformation:
Farmers are often hesitant to adopt digital tools due to concerns over data misuse, lack of transparency, and limited awareness. Without consent-based frameworks and user-friendly solutions, adoption remains uneven and excludes the most vulnerable.

Without addressing these issues, agriculture will continue to suffer from low productivity, policy inefficiencies, income volatility, and exclusion of vulnerable communities—directly impacting the achievement of SDGs 1 (No Poverty), 2 (Zero Hunger), 8 (Decent Work & Economic Growth), and 13 (Climate Action).

Scalability & Replicability

• Policy Iteration via Sandbox: Safe testing of subsidy, credit, and insurance frameworks before full rollout.

Sustainability & Roadmap

• AI-Driven Compliance: Automated fraud detection, predictive risk analysis, and satellite/drone-based land-use monitoring.

Title: MEKUM: Bridging the Digital Divide in Finance for MSMEs
Subtitle: Inclusive digital finance platform bridging gaps for MSMEs, women, and rural entrepreneurs through affordable accounting and AI tools.
Problem Statement: In Armenia, micro, small, and medium-sized enterprises (MSMEs) are the backbone of the economy but face major challenges in financial management and digitalization. Many lack access to affordable, user-friendly accounting tools, relying instead on manual processes or expensive services that limit transparency, efficiency, and access to credit. This creates barriers to tax compliance, digital participation, and sustainable growth, especially for women-led businesses, youth entrepreneurs, and rural enterprises. The digital divide in financial literacy and accounting capacity reinforces inequality, leaving underserved groups behind in Armenia’s evolving digital economy. Without accessible finance digitalization solutions, Armenian MSMEs struggle to compete, formalize, and integrate into national and global value chains.
Solution Overview:
How it works:
MEKUM is a cloud-based financial management and accounting platform designed to empower MSMEs in Armenia and beyond. It automates bookkeeping, tax compliance, reporting, and cash flow management through an easy-to-use interface accessible even for non-specialists. The platform is available on a low-cost subscription model (approx. $5/month), ensuring affordability for micro-enterprises and NGOs.

Methodologies and technologies used:

Cloud architecture for secure, scalable access from any location.

AI-powered financial assistant that supports decision-making by generating cash flow forecasts, cost analyses, and investment insights.

Localization methodology, adapting to national tax and regulatory systems (already fully adapted to Armenia, scalable to other countries).

Embedded learning tools, providing financial literacy resources and user training to improve digital skills.

Data security standards, ensuring safe and confidential handling of sensitive financial information.

Partnerships and collaboration models:

Local adoption in Armenia: 700+ MSMEs, NGOs, and public entities currently use MEKUM.

Collaboration with accountants and business trainers: MEKUM is integrated into financial literacy and entrepreneurship programs, supporting capacity building.

Governmental cooperation potential: The solution can be linked with national e-governance and tax systems to enhance transparency and compliance.

Scaling model: Open for collaboration with UN agencies, NGOs, development partners, and private sector actors to adapt MEKUM to new contexts (e.g., CIS, Balkans, and other developing economies).

By combining financial digitalization, AI-driven insights, and inclusive design, MEKUM reduces barriers for MSMEs, especially women-led and rural enterprises, fostering greater participation in the digital economy.

Title: Investours: AI Platform for Inclusive Wealth for Underserved Youth and Women
Subtitle: Empowering underserved youth and women with AI-driven financial education, scam detection, and safe pathways to inclusive wealth creation.
Problem Statement: Billions lack access to trusted financial education, vetted investment opportunities, and climate resilience tools—fueling poverty, fraud, and inequality. Women and youth in Africa are most at risk. The World Bank reports 3.5 billion people live under $6.85 per day, while the FBI estimates $16 billion lost to fraud in 2024; in Nigeria, over $1 billion disappeared to Ponzi schemes. Investours responds with free financial education, AI-powered scam detection, inclusive links to licensed firms, and climate-smart literacy—helping underserved people build lasting wealth, withstand shocks, and achieve generational progress.
Solution Overview:
Solution Description
Investours is an AI-powered wealth-tech platform that empowers underserved youth and women with the knowledge, tools, and networks to safely participate in the digital economy while building lasting, climate-resilient wealth.
Our solution rests on three integrated pillars:
1. AI-Powered Financial Education – Investours delivers financial knowledge through a multi-channel learning model designed for diverse literacy levels and learning preferences:
•	Handbooks provide structured reference materials for step-by-step guidance.
•	Podcasts engage mobile-first youth audiences, making financial learning accessible on the go.
•	Cartoons and short videos translate complex financial concepts into relatable, visual stories for children, low-literacy users, and community settings.
•	Interactive digital modules allow users to test understanding, reinforce skills, and track progress.
By combining these channels, Investours ensures that no one is left behind, regardless of education level, language, or access barriers.
2. AI Scam Detection & Investours AI Lab – Our proprietary AI assistant allows users to vet any investment opportunity in real time and flag risks. To strengthen this capability, we are establishing Africa’s first Institute for AI-Powered Financial Scam Detection — the Investours AI Lab. Its flagship solution, NetPolice, will serve banks, fintechs, and regulators to detect and mitigate fraudulent financial activities at scale.
3. Inclusive Access & Climate-Smart Wealth Building –
•	Vetted Opportunities: Partnerships with licensed financial firms give users access to trusted, fraud-free investments.
•	Climate-Smart Literacy: Communities gain knowledge to build wealth resilient to economic shocks and climate risks.
Methodologies & Technologies – We combine:
•	Proprietary AI-driven NLP models tailored for scam detection and opportunity vetting.
•	Cloud-based mobile/web platforms optimized for low-bandwidth environments.
•	Human-in-the-loop validation to combine AI insights with community trust.
Partnerships & Collaboration Models – Our partners include:
•	Licensed financial firms – providing regulated, safe investment pathways.
•	Community cooperatives & grassroots organizations – enabling trust, reach, and adoption at the last mile.
•	Government agencies & regulators – ensuring compliance, fraud prevention, and policy alignment.
•	Academic & research institutions – advancing AI models, scam detection, and climate-finance education.
Together, these partnerships ensure trust, scalability, and measurable impact — positioning Investours as a global model for inclusive wealth access and financial resilience.
Solution Provider(s): Solution Providers are: (i) Investours World Limited – Nigeria-based wealth-tech social enterprise using AI for financial education, scam detection, and inclusive investing across EdTech/FinTech/Climate Resilience, (ii) Licensed Investment Firms (Nigeria, Africa, & Diaspora) – regulated financial institutions providing vetted investment opportunities, (iii) Grassroots Financial Educators (GFEs) – community ambassadors driving financial literacy and access in underserved areas, (iv) NGOs & Women/Youth Associations – civil society partners enabling outreach and trust-building, (v) Academic & Research Institutions – partners for evidence-based insights, innovation, and impact evaluation, (vi) Government Agencies & Regulators – ensuring compliance, consumer protection, and enabling policy support, (vii) Fastcomet Web Hosting (USA) – cloud & AI technology partner supporting secure hosting and scalability.

Implementation timeline(s): Partly implemented during NYSC Orientation Camp, FCT-Abuja, Nigeria; 10-day youth empowerment and immersion from August 5 to 15, 2025.
Duration to pilot in a new geography: The estimated duration to pilot Investours in a new geography is 3–6 months. This includes community engagement, onboarding local partners, recruiting 500+ Grassroots Financial Educators, deploying the mobile/web platform, delivering financial education content, and monitoring early user adoption and impact. Our NYSC partner mobilizes over 30,000 youths annually across 36 states and FCT.
SDGs addressed: SDG 1 (No Poverty);SDG 4 (Quality Education);SDG 8 (Decent Work and Economic Growth);
Desired impact:
Solution Objectives
1.	Financial Inclusion: Empower underserved youth and women with the knowledge, tools, and networks to participate safely in the digital economy.
2.	Fraud Prevention: Reduce exposure to investment scams through AI-powered vetting and the planned Investours AI Lab.
3.	Climate-Resilient Wealth: Equip communities with financial literacy that builds wealth resilient to economic and environmental shocks.
4.	Community Capacity Building: Train Grassroots Financial Educators (GFEs) to expand digital financial access in rural and underserved areas.

Key Technologies Used

Title: LaborHack: Unlocking Verification, Digital Access and Jobs for Africa’s Blue-Collar Workforce
Subtitle: LaborHack is transforming how skilled workers access jobs, training, and finance, using technology to unlock opportunity and dignity for Africa’s underserved workforce.
Problem Statement:
Africa’s skilled workforce is the backbone of its economies, building homes, maintaining infrastructure, and powering industries. Yet this critical talent pool remains undervalued and underutilized, limiting both individual livelihoods and national development. LaborHack tackles three systemic barriers that prevent skilled workers from reaching their full potential.

First, millions of tradespeople remain invisible to opportunity, lacking verified digital identities that employers can trust. Second, hiring is constrained by a fragmented, informal system, with no reliable way to validate skills or credentials, causing inefficiencies and lost matches. Third, vocational schools and training centers, while producing capable graduates, often lack the means to track outcomes or connect learners to jobs.

By addressing these gaps, LaborHack is not just matching people to work. We are building the digital infrastructure of trust and visibility that turns skill into opportunity, restores dignity to blue-collar work, and drives lasting economic impact for workers, families, and communities.
Solution Overview:
LaborHack is a digital infrastructure platform designed to make Africa’s skilled workers visible, trusted, and connected to opportunity. To address the structural barriers holding back this workforce, we have built three core technologies.

First, we verify worker identities and create LaborPasses, which are digital portfolios that capture a worker’s skills, certifications, ratings, and work history. These portfolios replace the outdated paper CV, making workers both discoverable and credible to employers.

Second, we simplify hiring for businesses through LaborHack Recruit, our AI-powered matching tool. Employers gain access to pre-vetted talent, and workers apply directly with their LaborPass, presenting their capabilities in a structured, compelling format. This reduces time-to-hire while ensuring workers put their best foot forward.

Third, we partner with vocational schools through our Digital Logbook and Community Manager tools. The Digital Logbook tracks student projects and skill development in real time, while the Community Manager connects graduates directly to job opportunities, ensuring a seamless transition from training to employment and giving schools visibility into alumni outcomes.

To strengthen worker resilience, we also embed financial tools such as income tracking, savings features, and microloans. These supports help workers remain stable and available for consistent employment, reinforcing the broader labor ecosystem.

In this way, LaborHack is not just a job-matching service, but the infrastructure powering Africa’s next generation of dignified, sustainable blue-collar employment.
Solution Provider(s): OPL Academy – LaborHack’s primary sourcing partner. A vocational training and job placement accelerator that develops and deploys skilled tradespeople across Nigeria. All OPL graduates are onboarded to the LaborHack platform. Sector: Workforce Development / Construction,  Smile ID – LaborHack’s digital identity verification partner. Provides KYC, biometric verification, and fraud prevention tools to securely onboard workers and build employer trust. Sector: Digital Identity / Technology,  Grooming Centre Microfinance Bank – LaborHack’s tool financing partner. Offers microloans and financial services that enable workers to purchase tools and equipment needed for their trade. Sector: Financial Services / Microfinance,  Additional Partners – Employers, recruiters, vocational schools, government agencies, and development partners who collaborate with LaborHack to strengthen the worker ecosystem and expand job access.
Duration to pilot in a new geography: One month
SDGs addressed: SDG 1 (No Poverty);SDG 8 (Decent Work and Economic Growth);SDG 10 (Reduced Inequalities);
Desired impact:
LaborHack aims to:

- Create 1 million+ digital worker identities across Africa to build a trusted, verifiable database of skilled blue-collar talent.

- Match 500,000 workers to decent, dignified jobs locally and globally.

- Double average artisan incomes from around $40 per month to $80 per month, lifting thousands of households out of poverty.
Key technologies: LaborHack's technology stack includes MongoDB for data management, AWS for scalable cloud hosting, ClickUp for project management, GitHub for development workflows, Cursor for AI-assisted engineering, Auth0 for secure authentication, and OpenAI for content automation and intelligent matchmaking. The platform is lightweight and includes offline features to ensure accessibility in low-connectivity regions.
Unique Characteristics:
Most job platforms only work online, but millions of Africa’s blue-collar workers live and operate offline, making them invisible to opportunity. LaborHack is unique because we have built tools that go into communities, schools, and training centers to bring these workers into the digital economy at scale.

We onboard workers directly in their communities through trade associations, unions, and training centers, creating verified digital identities they can use for life.

Our Digital Logbook lets trainees record their projects and skills as they learn, even without internet, so their progress is never lost.

We carry out in-person verification of skills and credentials, building trust for employers.

Our Community Manager tool helps schools and training partners track graduates, connect them to jobs, and prove their impact.

With simple templates that use photos and videos, even workers with little digital experience can showcase their skills clearly.

By turning offline workers into visible, trusted professionals, LaborHack makes it possible for millions of people to be seen, valued, and connected to better work.
Sustainable Change:
LaborHack’s vision is a future where skilled tradespeople across Africa work in a system that recognizes their value, protects their livelihoods, and connects them to steady, dignified work. The desired follow-on effects of our solution go beyond job placement , we aim to help communities thrive by formalizing the blue-collar labor market, creating reliable pipelines from training to work, and driving sustained income growth for households. When workers have verified credentials and, they gain security and respect; when more people in a community are earning stable incomes, local businesses grow, children stay in school, and neighborhoods become safer and more prosperous.

We are building this change through LaborPass (verified digital portfolios), LaborHack Recruit (a recruitment platform for employers), and Community Manager (a shared hub for training and recruitment partners). These tools work together to verify workers at scale, match them quickly to opportunities, and encourage collaboration across the ecosystem. Workers access the platform for free, gaining the ability to present their skills confidently and compete for better opportunities. Employers, recruiters, and training partners subscribe for premium access to verified talent and network tools, generating the revenue that sustains the system. By replacing unreliable, informal hiring with a trusted, transparent, and collaborative framework, LaborHack strengthens not just individual careers, but entire communities.

With the right support, LaborHack can scale its impact to millions more workers, formalizing the labor market, creating sustainable income growth, and unlocking a new era of dignity and prosperity for the people who build and power our societies.

Through verified digital identities, AI-powered recruitment, and community-driven tools, it connects tradespeople to job opportunities, improving livelihoods and empowering underserved communities, particularly women.

Title: SENMER: Blockchain Marketplace Empowering Coastal Communities
Subtitle: SENMER is an inclusive digital marketplace using voice commands to register catches as NFTs.It eliminates middlemen,connecting artisanal fishers directly to EU buyers increasing revenues
Problem Statement: 40% of Senegal's fishing is illegal (FAO) , robbing 600.000 artisanal fishers of livelihoods. Illiteracy(65%) and middlemen trap them in poverty , while untraceable seafood fuels overfishing and $300M per year in economic losses .Coastal communities lack tools to reclaim their ocean' svalue

Solution Overview  
SenMer is an inclusive blockchain marketplace transforming West Africa's blue economy by connecting artisanal fishers, processors (particularly women), and buyers through innovative voice technology, blockchain traceability, and community governance. Here's the detailed breakdown:

"Boat-to-Buyer" Workflow:  
- Step 1: Voice Registration  
  Illiterate fishers (65% of users) record catches in Wolof via mobile app: *"Saxal jën bi, 25kg"* (I caught fish, 25kg). Works offline in low-bandwidth conditions.  
- Step 2: AI Validation  
  Lightweight AI (YOLOv8-nano) pre-trained on 200 West African fish species verifies:  
  - Species via photo  
  - Weight via Bluetooth scales  
  - Quota compliance via government API (ANAMS)  

- Step 3: Blockchain Certification  
  Each catch generates an NFT on hybrid blockchain:  
  {
    "fisher": "Idrissa Ndiaye (Canoe AS-21)",
    "location": "Saint-Louis, 16.2°N, 16.3°W",
    "species": "Yellowfin tuna",
    "weight": "25kg",
    "timestamp": "2024-08-15T06:30:00Z"
  }
- Step 4: Automated Sales & Payment  
  - Processors/PMEs purchase via reverse auctions  
  - Auto-split payments:  
    - 70% to fisher (via Wave/Orange Money in <2hr)  
    - 25% to processor  
    - 5% to community logistics fund

| Blockchain | Hyperledger Fabric (privacy) + Algorand (eco-consensus) | $0.001/tx - 10k TPS |  
| Artificial Intelligence | YOLOv8-nano optimized for Snapdragon 439 | 98% species accuracy |  
| Logistics | IoT temperature/geo sensors + dynamic QR codes | Real-time cold chain monitoring |  
| Governance | $SENMER token (ERC-1155) | Fishers vote on fishing quotas |

Name of your organization: Department of Science and Technology VI
Title: “Providing Access, Resilience, Opportunities and Livelihood to Archipelagic Areas” or PAROLA
Subtitle: PAROLA is a “digital lighthouse”, a beacon of connectivity and access powered by a Locally Accessible Cloud System (LACS). It brings vital information, digital services, and connectivity to remote island communities, enabling access to essential social services and bridging the digital divide.
Problem Statement: Small island and coastal communities in the Philippines face significant economic challenges due to their heavy dependence on fishing. This reliance, coupled with geographic isolation, leaves these communities vulnerable to economic instability and resource depletion. The PAROLA project aims to digitally transform isolated areas, enabling access to education, healthcare, disaster risk reduction and management (DRRM) capabilities, and economic resources. More importantly, it empowers communities to diversify their livelihoods, particularly through sustainable tourism. By strengthening digital infrastructure, PAROLA ensures that these communities are not left behind in the digital age, equipping them to build a brighter and self-reliant future.
Solution Overview:
The project is expected to transform small island and coastal communities (SICCs) into resilient, inclusive, and self-reliant communities by leveraging digital technologies. By the end of the project, the following outcomes are anticipated:

Improved Connectivity and Communication: SICCs will have access to nine (9) fully operational Locally-Accessible Cloud Systems (LACS), enabling seamless communication and the storage and retrieval of critical information (SDG 16.10)

Enhanced Access to Basic Services: Through the PAROLA portal, communities will have improved access to essential services, such as remote education, telemedicine, disaster risk reduction and management (DRRM) resources, and economic opportunities, fostering equitable access across remote areas (SDG 10.2)

Increased Digital Literacy and Capability: Community members will be trained to effectively utilize digital technologies, including digital tourism guides, online educational and informational materials, telemedicine services, and online emergency information and communication platforms, promoting technological empowerment and self-reliance (SDG 16.10 and 13.1)

Strengthened Disaster Resilience: The integration of digital tools for DRRM information and communication will improve disaster preparedness and response capabilities, reducing risks and enhancing recovery in SICCs. For example use of Bantay Panahon for weather information and Project SIGNAL for incident reporting. (SDG 13.1 and 13.1.3)

Title: Bridge for Billions: Gamified, AI-Powered Learning for Inclusive Entrepreneurs
Subtitle: A digital ecosystem that redefines entrepreneurial learning through gamified, AI-powered, and community-driven experiences for underserved founders worldwide
Problem Statement:
Despite the growing number of entrepreneurship support initiatives worldwide, most early-stage entrepreneurs in underserved communities — particularly women, youth, and those in low-income or rural settings — are still not learning in ways that help them succeed. The dominant learning models are passive, fragmented, and disconnected from their realities: generic online content, sporadic workshops, or time-limited accelerators with little practical guidance or follow-up.
These models assume that learners can translate theory into action without support, that mentorship happens organically, or that entrepreneurship is a linear journey. In reality, underserved entrepreneurs face daily uncertainty, limited digital infrastructure, and social and economic constraints — and are being asked to navigate complex business challenges with tools and methods designed for different contexts.
The result is predictable: low engagement, stalled ventures, and wasted potential. To genuinely build inclusive digital economies, we must redesign entrepreneurial learning to be practical, applied, and adaptable — focused not on delivering content, but on developing capacity in real time, with the structure, support, and community that underserved founders need to succeed.
Solution Overview:
Bridge for Billions is a digital incubation platform that reimagines entrepreneurial learning for underserved founders. Our solution delivers a structured, gamified, and community-driven learning journey, supported by AI-powered tools and embedded in local ecosystems. It is designed to bridge the gap between entrepreneurial ambition and tangible business outcomes—especially for youth, women, and early-stage entrepreneurs in low-resource environments.
At the core of Bridge’s model is a step-by-step incubation journey that guides entrepreneurs from idea validation to market-readiness. The platform hosts a modular curriculum of practical business-building tools, available in multiple languages, and accessible via low-bandwidth environments.
Each entrepreneur is paired with a trained mentor using our AI-driven matching system, creating a personalized and human-centered support structure. Throughout the process, entrepreneurs complete real-world tasks such as defining their value proposition, testing their market, building financial forecasts, and designing MVPs — all within a supportive digital environment.
The solution also integrates:
Progress tracking dashboards for both entrepreneurs and program managers
Community features to enable peer-to-peer learning
Localized adaptation of content and support materials
Alumni access to post-program events, resources, and funding opportunities
This methodology is grounded in experiential learning, where participants build while learning, and is designed to be delivered by partners such as NGOs, corporations, governments, and foundations, making it adaptable to diverse contexts and challenges.
✔️ Methodologies
Learn-by-doing pedagogy: Entrepreneurship is taught through the active building of each entrepreneur’s real business.
Gamification: Milestone-based progression, visual feedback, and completion incentives drive engagement and learning retention.
Mentorship as a learning lever: Every entrepreneur is guided by a mentor trained in Bridge’s inclusive mentoring model.
Contextual learning design: Content is locally adapted and culturally appropriate, with flexible pacing and support built in.
Technologies
AI Matching Engine: Automates mentor–entrepreneur pairings based on skills, interests, geography, and availability.
Digital Platform: Cloud-based, mobile-friendly, and accessible with low-bandwidth connections.
Analytics & Reporting Suite: Real-time tracking of progress and engagement for all stakeholders.
Community Layer: Messaging, peer-learning, alumni groups, and partner access to unlock local linkages and post-program continuity.

Title: Agentic Inventory Service: AI-Driven Inventory Optimization to Empower Hospitality MSMEs
Subtitle: An AI-powered solution that helps hospitality MSMEs optimize inventory in real time, improve utilization & revenue forecasting, and access inclusive digital tools for sustainable, competitive growth.
Problem Statement:
Hospitality businesses face increasingly complex challenges in inventory optimization that go far beyond tracking simple availability. Revenue managers must address sophisticated “what-if” scenarios—such as reallocating inventory across diverse customer segments—to maximize yield, ensure financial sustainability, and remain competitive in global markets.
Traditional inventory management systems are not designed to support this complexity. They typically lack the ability to:
•	Assess feasibility of reallocating inventory across segments,
•	Forecast demand shifts and customer behavior,
•	Validate budget compliance and financial tolerance levels, and
•	Calculate revenue displacement and opportunity costs.

This gap is particularly critical in properties managing inventory across dozens of distinct segments. Without advanced analytical capabilities, businesses—especially small and medium-sized operators—struggle to make informed, data-driven decisions that balance profitability, availability, and accessibility for different customer groups.

The absence of such tools leads to underutilized capacity, missed revenue opportunities, and suboptimal strategies that disproportionately affect emerging market operators, women- and youth-led businesses, and MSMEs that lack access to enterprise-grade optimization systems.
There is a pressing need for innovative, inclusive digital solutions that deliver real-time analysis of availability constraints, budget tolerances, and revenue trade-offs—empowering business users to understand not just current availability, but also the strategic, financial, and social implications of inventory reallocation decisions. By democratizing access to advanced digital tools, such solutions will enable hospitality businesses of all sizes to participate more competitively in the digital economy, contributing to the achievement of the Sustainable Development Goals (SDGs) through job creation, financial resilience, optimized utilization, and inclusive growth.
Solution Overview:
1. How the Solution Works

The Agentic Inventory Service is a digital yield optimization engine that transforms complex hospitality inventory reallocation into actionable insights. It uses a modular, agent-based design where each agent performs a specialized function: availability assessment, demand prediction, budget compliance validation, revenue displacement analysis, and final recommendations. Through intelligent feasibility filtering, the system identifies viable moves by combining real-time availability data, predictive demand models, and historical booking patterns. A budget compliance engine enforces tolerance thresholds (±k%), while the revenue displacement calculator quantifies the impact of reallocating units between segments with varying revenue potential. The AI recommendation agent then synthesizes these inputs into explainable, ranked recommendations. Business users can pose natural “what-if” questions—for example, reallocating rooms between segments—and instantly receive comprehensive analysis including feasibility, compliance, revenue impact, and alternative strategies.

2. Methodologies and Technologies Used

The solution combines traditional Machine Learning for demand prediction, deterministic optimization models for feasibility and budget alignment, and large language model (LLM) reasoning for explainable recommendations. It applies parallel processing and intelligent caching to achieve sub-30 second performance in complex scenarios involving up to 100 market segments. Historical time-series analysis (same-day-of-week patterns) is blended with predictive analytics to improve forecasting accuracy. The modular Agentic framework ensures scalability, transparency, and adaptability to different hospitality contexts.

3. Partnerships and Collaboration Models

The service is designed to be deployed in collaboration with hospitality operators, MSMEs, and digital ecosystem partners. Implementation partnerships with hotels and resort groups ensure real-world validation and adoption. Collaboration with cloud technology providers supports continuous model improvement, scalability, and accessibility for small and medium operators. The open architecture also allows integration with existing property management systems, ERP platforms, and digital booking solutions, making the solution interoperable and adaptable to diverse business environments. This collaborative model ensures that innovation remains inclusive, affordable, and aligned with sustainable digital economy principles.

Desired impact:
Solution Objectives
The Agentic Inventory Service aims to empower hospitality businesses—particularly MSMEs—with advanced digital tools that enable real-time, data-driven inventory optimization. The key objectives are:
•	To democratize access to AI-powered yield management traditionally available only to large hotel chains.
•	To enhance revenue resilience and financial sustainability of small and medium operators.
•	To foster inclusive digital transformation by making advanced analytics accessible, explainable, and affordable.
•	To support sustainable growth in the tourism and hospitality sector by improving resource utilization and operational efficiency.

Key Achievements and Impacts
The solution is designed to deliver measurable and scalable impacts:
•	Revenue Growth and Competitiveness: Optimized inventory decisions can increase yield by 10–20% per property annually, improving the profitability of MSMEs and enabling them to compete on a level playing field with larger players.
•	Operational Efficiency: Sub-30 second analysis reduces decision time from hours to seconds, freeing staff capacity and enabling faster responses to market changes.
•	Employment and Skills Development: By lowering the barrier to advanced digital tools, the solution allows smaller operators to retain and upskill staff rather than outsource revenue management functions, potentially creating new digital economy jobs in data-driven hospitality.
•	Inclusivity and Access: Expanding access to cutting-edge AI systems for MSMEs ensures that women- and youth-led enterprises benefit from the same digital opportunities as large corporations. Similarly, technology that is proven in the US can be deployed in developing nations inexpensively. 
•	Sustainability and Resource Efficiency: Smarter allocation of hospitality inventory reduces wasted capacity (empty rooms, underutilized segments), supporting more sustainable business models. Improved utilization indirectly reduces the environmental footprint per guest served, contributing to efficiency gains aligned with SDG 12 (Responsible Consumption and Production) and SDG 13 (Climate Action).

In the long term, the solution strengthens the resilience of hospitality MSMEs, promotes inclusive participation in the digital economy, and contributes to sustainable economic growth through innovation, employment, and competitiveness.
Key technologies:
The Agentic Inventory Service integrates advanced digital technologies to deliver real-time, explainable, and scalable inventory optimization for the hospitality sector:
•	Artificial Intelligence (AI) and Machine Learning (ML):
Traditional ML models forecast demand using historical booking data, seasonality, and same-day-of-week patterns. AI-driven recommendation engines combine deterministic scoring with LLM-based reasoning for explainable, ranked suggestions.
•	Large Language Models (LLMs):
Enhance decision explainability by translating complex optimization outputs into natural language insights for business users.
•	Optimization and Simulation Engines:
Deterministic optimization ensures budget compliance (±k% tolerance) and feasibility filtering. Simulation models compute precise revenue displacement when reallocating units across segments with different revenue per unit (RPU).
•	Cloud-Native and Cloud-Agnostic Architecture:
The solution is designed to be cloud-agnostic, enabling deployment across Google Cloud, Microsoft Azure, AWS, or local cloud service providers (CSPs). This ensures accessibility for MSMEs worldwide, reduces vendor lock-in, and supports diverse regulatory environments.

Together, these technologies make advanced revenue optimization accessible, inclusive, and explainable, bridging the digital divide for MSMEs while driving innovation in the tourism and hospitality industry globally.
Unique Characteristics:
The Agentic Inventory Service stands out through a combination of technological innovation, inclusivity, and practical accessibility that makes it particularly suited for hospitality MSMEs:

•	Agentic Architecture for Yield Optimization
Unlike traditional revenue management tools, the solution employs a modular, agent-based approach (availability, demand prediction, budget compliance, revenue displacement, recommendations). This ensures transparency, adaptability, and explainability at every stage of the decision process.
•	Hybrid AI for Explainable Recommendations
The system uniquely combines deterministic optimization models with large language model (LLM) reasoning, delivering ranked recommendations that are not only accurate but also understandable to non-technical business users. This addresses the critical adoption barrier of “black box” AI.

Title: CROPDOC ANALYTICS
Subtitle: AI-powered digital agronomy tool delivering real-time crop disease detection, advisory, and yield insights for smallholder farmers
Problem Statement: Smallholder farmers, who produce over 70% of Africa’s food, face persistent barriers that threaten food security and economic resilience. Crop diseases, responsible for over $4 billion in annual losses in Sub-Saharan Africa, are often detected late due to limited access to agronomic expertise, inadequate extension services, and lack of affordable diagnostic tools. Climate variability further compounds the challenge by fueling pest outbreaks and unpredictable weather patterns, leaving farmers with poor yields and unstable incomes. Digital technologies exist but remain inaccessible for many rural farmers due to low literacy, poor connectivity, and the high cost of modern solutions. Women and youth, who form the backbone of agricultural labor, are disproportionately affected, limiting their economic empowerment. Without inclusive, accessible, and affordable digital solutions that combine real-time diagnostics with localized advisory, farmers remain trapped in cycles of poverty, vulnerability to climate shocks, and declining productivity.
Solution Overview:
CropDoc is an inclusive digital agriculture platform that empowers smallholder farmers with real-time crop health diagnostics, advisory, and yield optimization. The solution integrates multiple technologies into one accessible ecosystem. Farmers capture field or leaf images via a mobile app or drone surveillance; AI image recognition and spectral analysis detect early signs of stress or disease. For hyper-accurate diagnosis, CropDoc leverages quantum chemistry simulations to model plant–pathogen interactions and recommend targeted, cost-effective treatments.
To bridge the digital divide, CropDoc operates beyond smartphones: USSD and SMS channels deliver disease alerts, weather forecasts, and advisory in multiple local languages, while voice support ensures accessibility for low-literacy users. A cloud-based analytics engine processes satellite and IoT sensor data to generate localized insights, yield predictions, and climate-smart recommendations.
Our model is built on collaboration. We partner with agricultural cooperatives, NGOs, and government extension services to scale adoption, ensure affordability, and embed training. Academic and research institutions strengthen our diagnostic algorithms, while telecom operators enable broad reach through USSD and SMS integration. By combining frontier science with inclusive communication channels, CropDoc creates a resilient, data-driven farming ecosystem that reduces losses, boosts yields, and empowers underserved farmers, especially women and youth.
Solution Provider(s): CropDoc is developed and led by Cropdoc Analytics, a social enterprise leveraging AI and frontier technologies for inclusive agriculture. Key partners include Joseph Sarwuan Tarka University Makurdi (Nigeria), providing agronomic research and validation; Enactus Nigeria, supporting youth-led innovation and farmer training; MTN Nigeria Communications Plc, enabling USSD/SMS delivery and rural connectivity; and NAERLS, strengthening farmer outreach. We also collaborate with UM6P (Morocco) through The Forge and StartGate incubation hubs, providing acceleration, technical mentorship, and pan-African scaling opportunities, alongside local farmer cooperatives across Benue and Kaduna States for adoption and feedback.
Implementation location(s): Ben Gurira morocco , Benue , Kaduna and Nasarawa states Nigeria
Duration to pilot in a new geography: 26 weeks
SDGs addressed: SDG 1 (No Poverty);SDG 2 (Zero Hunger);SDG 13 (Climate Action);
Desired impact:
CropDoc aims to reduce crop losses, strengthen food security, and empower smallholder farmers through inclusive digital agriculture. Our objectives are to cut disease-related losses by 65%, increase yields by 40%, and raise farmer incomes by at least 50% within two farming seasons. We also aim to bridge the digital divide by providing affordable advisory services via USSD, SMS, and multilingual support, ensuring accessibility for women, youth, and low-literacy farmers.
To date, CropDoc has engaged over 15,000 farmers across Nigeria and Morocco, achieving a 25% increase in yields, 30% reduction in treatment costs, and 98% diagnostic accuracy validated by agronomists. These outcomes  boost rural incomes but and reduce chemical misuse, lowering greenhouse gas emissions and environmental damage. By promoting climate-smart agriculture, building digital skills, and fostering rural entrepreneurship, CropDoc contributes directly to the SDGs while advancing inclusive, resilient, and sustainable digital economies.
Key technologies: CropDoc integrates multiple frontier technologies into one inclusive platform. Artificial Intelligence (AI) powers image recognition and spectral analysis for early disease detection. Quantum chemistry simulations model plant–pathogen interactions to deliver precise, low-cost treatment recommendations. Satellite imagery and drone surveillance enable large-scale crop monitoring and geospatial analysis. Cloud-based analytics combine soil, weather, and sensor data for yield prediction and climate-smart advisory. To ensure accessibility, USSD and SMS gateways provide real-time updates to farmers without internet or smartphones, while multilingual voice support enhances inclusivity for low-literacy users. Together, these technologies create a scalable, resilient digital farming ecosystem.
Unique Characteristics: CropDoc is the first agri-tech platform to combine AI diagnostics, drone imaging, and quantum chemistry simulations in a single, farmer-centric system. Unlike conventional tools, it operates inclusively through SMS, USSD, and multilingual voice support, ensuring access for low-literacy and offline users. Its business model blends freemium advisory with affordable subscription services for advanced analytics and drone monitoring, supported by partnerships with telecoms, universities, and cooperatives. This ecosystem enables scalability, gender inclusion, and climate-smart practices. By merging frontier science with accessible communication channels, CropDoc creates a differentiated, resilient model that empowers underserved farmers and strengthens digital economies.
Sustainable Change: CropDoc drives systemic change by embedding digital innovation directly into smallholder farming systems. By making advanced diagnostics accessible via AI, SMS/USSD, and drones, it reduces losses, boosts yields, and raises incomes, creating resilient rural economies. The desired follow-on effects include reduced reliance on chemical pesticides, improved soil and environmental health, and greater adoption of climate-smart practices. As farmers gain digital literacy and trust in technology, they become catalysts for peer learning, expanding impact across communities. This creates a self-sustaining ecosystem where inclusive digital agriculture drives food security, poverty reduction, and long-term socio-economic transformation.

Additional resources have come from self-funding, partnerships with universities, and in-kind contributions from cooperatives and telecom partners for pilot deployments

Title: Bridging the Digital Divide: AI-Powered Financial Inclusion for Women & Youth Entrepreneurs
Subtitle: Democratising access to capital through alternative credit scoring and WhatsApp-first financial and entrepreneurial education
Problem Statement:
Despite global digital transformation, 70% of women-led MSMEs in emerging markets remain excluded from formal finance due to:

1. Credit systems that require asset ownership they often can't access
2. Biased scoring models that ignore non-traditional data (e.g., mobile money history, community reputation)
3. Complex digital platforms that fail to meet users where they are (only 12% of women entrepreneurs in Kenya use banking apps daily vs. 89% on WhatsApp)

Missing links between digital skills training, financial literacy and actionable access to capital

This perpetuates a $42B gender credit gap in Africa alone, stifling economic potential.
Solution Overview:
The heart of our system is the Athena Score™, an AI-powered alternative credit assessment that evaluates business potential beyond traditional metrics. By analysing mobile money history, psychometric data, social capital and learning behaviour, we can identify creditworthy entrepreneurs who lack conventional collateral. This enables women and youth with strong business fundamentals but maybe not property titles, to qualify for financing.

We deliver this through WhatsApp, the platform entrepreneurs already use daily. Users get:

1. Instant loan pre-qualification
2. Bite-sized financial and entrepreneurship coaching
3. Real-time score improvement tips

All in local languages, without needing to download new apps.

Our partnerships multiply the impact. We've integrated with Equity Bank to power their mobile lending, helped Lagos State streamline women's grant programs, and are working with central banks to reform credit systems. Since launch, we've helped 60,000+ entrepreneurs unlock capital while maintaining a 92% repayment rate, proving inclusion and good business can go hand in hand.

This solution directly addresses digital inclusion by meeting users where they are digitally while building the skills and access needed to participate fully in the formal economy.
Solution Provider(s): MasterCard Strive; entrepreneurship & financial literacy content development partnership
Implementation timeline(s): Launched in Kenya (2022), with key milestones: 1. Pilot Phase: Oct–Dec 2022 (7,000 women entrepreneurs, partnership with the Graça Machel Trust) 2. National Scale (Kenya): Jan 2023–present (30,000+ users) 3. International Expansion: Nigeria (2023), UK diaspora (2024) 4. Bank Integration: Partnered with Equity Bank (2023) to embed Athena Score™ 5. Commonwealth Scale: 2023-2024 (60,000+ users cross 27 commonwealth countries)
Duration to pilot in a new geography: 6-8 months
SDGs addressed: SDG 1 (No Poverty);SDG 5 (Gender Equality);SDG 8 (Decent Work and Economic Growth);
Desired impact:
Objectives:

1. Contribute to closing the $42B gender credit gap facilitating $20M in loans annually by 2030
2. Enable 1M women entrepreneurs to access capital using alternative metrics by 2030
3. Shift financial systems to recognise non-traditional data

Key Achievements:

1. 60,000+ women served across 27 market
2. $1M+ unlocked in loans (avg. $500-$5K per entrepreneur)
3. 92% repayment rate (vs. 76% industry avg. for women-led SMEs)
4. 3.2x income increase for users after 18 months
Key technologies:
Core Stack:

1. AI/ML: Athena Score™ analyzes 148 non-traditional variables (mobile money patterns, psychometrics)
2. Conversational AI: WhatsApp-based financial coaching in local languages
3. Blockchain: Secure credit history sharing between partner institutions
4. Cloud: AWS Africa servers ensure low-latency access
Unique Characteristics:
Innovations:

1. Bias-free scoring: Evaluates ambition/community trust as rigorously as financials
2. Ecosystem play: Partners with banks (Equity Bank), governments (Lagos State), and telcos to embed scoring
3. "Phygital" model: Combines AI with human coaches accessible through our Athena ambassadors
4. Gender-smart design: Co-created with 5,000 women entrepreneurs

Differentiator:
Works on basic smartphones via USSD/WhatsApp (no app required)
Sustainable Change:
Athena FundX drives sustainable, systemic change by transforming how financial systems evaluate and invest in women entrepreneurs. In the short term (0-3 years), we have demonstrate women’s creditworthiness at scale through the Athena Score™, enabling banks to lend confidently without traditional collateral. 
Medium-term (3-5 years), we are working with regulators to integrate alternative data into national credit bureaus, currently piloted with Ghana’s central bank. 
Long-term (5-10 years), this shifts institutional capital flows, with 2 partner banks already launching “collateral-light” products based on our model. Beyond finance, our impact will create ripple effects: women reinvest 80% of earnings into education and healthcare, while our data helps policymakers design inclusive economic programs. By proving that inclusion is profitable (92% repayment rates), we’re building a new benchmark for the financial sector, one where ambition and community trust hold as much weight as balance sheets.
