Name of your organization: Webfala Digital Skills for all Initiative
Title: Eko Africa: Digital Skill Development
Subtitle: Closing the Digital Gap: Empowering Mid- and Late-Career Adults Through Digital Skill Development
Problem Statement:
Across Africa, the digital divide continues to widen, particularly among mid and late-career adults who face increasing challenges in adapting to the demands of a rapidly evolving digital economy. The Eko Africa: Digital Skill Development program addresses critical barriers to digital inclusion for this demographic, including displaced workers, career changers, and individuals re-entering the workforce.

According to the International Telecommunication Union (ITU), nearly 60 percent of adults over 40 in sub-Saharan Africa lack basic digital literacy, including the ability to use email, navigate the internet, or operate a computer. In low-income and underserved communities, this figure is even higher due to structural inequalities, limited access to affordable technology, and insufficient opportunities for adult-focused digital education.

As economies across Africa digitize, adults without digital competencies are increasingly excluded from employment, e-governance, financial services, and social participation. A 2023 World Bank report highlights that digital skills are now essential for more than 75 percent of formal sector jobs in Africa, yet training programs are overwhelmingly designed for youth, leaving older populations behind.

Additional challenges include:

Cost barriers: The high price of devices and internet connectivity keeps many adults offline.

Educational gaps: Few adult-focused digital literacy programs exist, especially in local languages or with culturally relevant content.

Technological pace: The speed of innovation makes it difficult for mid and late-career workers to catch up without structured, accessible learning pathways.

The Eko Africa: Digital Skill Development program is designed to close this gap by providing tailored digital literacy and workforce-readiness training. It empowers participants with practical skills to improve employability, support career transitions, and navigate an increasingly digital society.
Solution Overview:
The Eko Africa: Digital Skill Development program is a comprehensive digital literacy initiative designed to close the digital skills gap among mid and late-career adults in underserved African communities. This program delivers a practical, learner-centered approach through an eight-module curriculum that begins with the very basics of computer literacy and gradually progresses to more advanced, real-world applications. Participants are guided through fundamental digital concepts including how to operate a computer, navigate the internet, use email securely, and engage with essential digital tools. As learners advance through the modules, they gain practical skills in job searching, resume writing, online communication, digital financial management, and accessing online educational resources.

The program uses a blended instructional methodology that combines in-person, step-by-step facilitation with guided practice. Each module is led by trained local facilitators who provide personalized support to ensure participants gain both competence and confidence. The curriculum is designed to be culturally relevant and accessible, with content delivered in local languages when necessary. Emphasis is placed on hands-on learning, peer collaboration, and real-life application to reinforce skill retention. At the conclusion of the program, participants receive continued access to internet connectivity, enabling them to apply their new skills in everyday contexts and pursue lifelong learning independently.

Technologically, the program leverages open-source and cloud-based tools, with a focus on the Google Workspace suite, enabling learners to develop digital workplace competencies that are in high demand. Digital safety and responsible online behavior are embedded throughout the program to ensure learners are equipped to navigate the digital world securely. Beyond classroom instruction, Eko Africa provides comprehensive Digital Navigation Services, including two years of post-program technology support. This ensures sustained impact by helping participants troubleshoot challenges, stay up to date, and continue applying their skills meaningfully.

Collaboration is central to the success of the program. Eko Africa partners with local community centers, public libraries, and grassroots organizations to deliver training in familiar, trusted spaces. The program also works closely with local government agencies, adult education providers, and telecommunication companies to secure internet access, digital devices, and broader community engagement. These partnerships strengthen local ownership, expand outreach, and ensure long-term sustainability. By building a collaborative ecosystem of support, Eko Africa ensures that adult learners are not only digitally literate but also digitally empowered.
Solution Provider(s): The Eko Africa Digital Skill Development program will be implemented in collaboration with the following key African partners:   1. Paradigm Initiative – a leading social enterprise that builds ICT-enabled support systems and advocates for digital rights across Africa, operating in the technology and civic engagement sector; 2.  Co-Creation Hub (CcHUB) – Africa’s premier innovation centre dedicated to accelerating the application of social capital and technology for economic prosperity, operating in the innovation and entrepreneurship sector; 3.  African Centre for Women, Information and Communications Technology (ACWICT) – a Kenya-based nonprofit that provides ICT training and employment support for women and youth, operating in the gender equality and ICT sector; 4.  Tech4Dev – a Nigerian nonprofit organisation that empowers people with digital skills to improve access to decent work and bridge the gender digital divide, operating in the technology education sector;  5. AfriLabs – a pan-African network of innovation hubs that supports technology-driven entrepreneurship and fosters knowledge sharing, operating in the innovation and business development sector.
Duration to pilot in a new geography: 12months
SDGs addressed: SDG 1 (No Poverty);SDG 4 (Quality Education);SDG 10 (Reduced Inequalities);
Desired impact:
At Webfala Digital Skills for All Initiative, impact measurement is an integral part of our program design and implementation. Our approach goes beyond simply counting outputs; it focuses on capturing meaningful change in the lives of participants and the communities we serve. Grounded in our Theory of Change, we believe that access to technology and digital literacy opens pathways to economic opportunity, improved quality of life, and social inclusion. To assess how well our programs deliver on this vision, our Impact Team applies a structured, multi-method evaluation framework that combines both quantitative and qualitative data.

For the Eko Africa Digital Skill Development program, we collect data at key intervals to evaluate participant progress and program effectiveness. This includes pre and post training surveys to measure changes in digital skill proficiency, attendance tracking to assess engagement, and focus group discussions to capture participants’ experiences, confidence levels, and real-life application of new skills. Our impact goals are clearly defined: we aim for 80 percent of participants to increase their digital skill proficiency, with a minimum of 80 percent completing the program with strong attendance. We also expect that 70 percent of participants will report improved proficiency, while 60 percent will feel confident using digital tools to support job searches and daily needs. Ultimately, we target a 90 percent satisfaction rate, with participants indicating that the program helped them achieve personal or professional goals.

Insights gathered from ongoing evaluation inform strategic decisions, program design, and continuous improvement. This data-driven approach not only ensures accountability to our funders and partners, but also strengthens our ability to reach and serve those most affected by the digital divide. By using real-time feedback and measurable outcomes, we optimize the impact of our work and build a stronger, more inclusive digital future for underserved African communities.
Key technologies:
Artificial Intelligence / Machine Learning
Crowd Sourced Service / Social Networks
Internet of Things
Software and Mobile Applications
Unique Characteristics:
The Eko Africa Digital Skill Development program stands out for its comprehensive and inclusive design. The structured curriculum guides participants from basic digital knowledge to real-world applications that support both personal growth and career advancement. By focusing on everyday digital tasks such as email use, online safety, and accessing essential services alongside workplace tools like document creation and online job searches, the program delivers a well-rounded and practical learning experience for adult learners.

What makes the program particularly innovative is its community-based delivery model. Eko Africa does not wait for participants to come to a central location. Instead, it brings the training directly into communities by holding sessions in schools, apartment complexes, churches, and other familiar spaces. This approach removes common barriers such as transportation costs and time constraints, especially for those in low-income or underserved areas. All training is provided at no cost to participants and delivered in local languages, ensuring accessibility for learners who may not be fluent in English or have formal education.

In addition, every participant receives internet access support and two years of continued digital guidance to reinforce their learning and encourage long-term use of digital tools. The program is scalable and adaptable to meet the changing needs of different communities and industries. While several organizations in Africa may offer aspects of digital education or internet access, Eko Africa is the only nonprofit delivering a complete and free digital equity solution directly to families. This integrated and barrier-free approach ensures that no one is left behind in the digital age.
Sustainable Change:
Our program is designed not only to equip individuals with essential digital skills but to transform the broader systems that perpetuate digital exclusion. By building strong, strategic partnerships with corporations, foundations, and public agencies, Webfala Digital Skills for All Initiative is laying the foundation for a scalable and sustainable digital equity model that can be replicated across the continent. Our vision is to establish Webfala as the leading provider of comprehensive digital empowerment solutions for underserved children, adults, and families in Africa—all at no cost to beneficiaries.

Sustainability is rooted in our diversified funding strategy, which blends support from individuals, corporations, foundations, and government agencies. We engage partners through financial contributions, in-kind technology donations, and volunteer support, fostering a shared sense of ownership in the communities we serve. Our growing national office infrastructure also enables coordination across multiple locations, positioning us to access large-scale investments and implement regional or national strategies. This integrated model ensures we are not reliant on any single funding stream, reducing risk and strengthening long-term viability.

As the program is deployed and scaled, we expect several key follow-on effects. First, increased digital literacy among adults will lead to greater workforce participation, job mobility, and economic resilience, especially in low-income communities. Second, as digitally literate parents model technology use at home, intergenerational learning will take root, positively influencing children’s digital education. Third, our active engagement in state and national digital inclusion initiatives positions Webfala as a trusted voice in policy discussions, helping to shape systems that prioritize equity and access. Over time, these outcomes will catalyze systemic change—closing the digital divide, expanding opportunity, and creating a more inclusive and connected society.
Funding Sources: As the Eko Africa: Digital Skill Development program is currently in the idea stage, it has not yet received any direct funding. To date, the concept has been advanced through the strategic planning, in-kind contributions, and volunteer efforts of the Webfala Digital Skills for all Initiative team, leveraging the organization’s existing infrastructure, expertise, and community partnerships. While no external financial support has been secured for this specific program, Webfala has a strong track record of attracting funding from individual donors, corporate partners, and foundations for related digital inclusion programs, positioning us to mobilize resources quickly once funding opportunities are identified.
Testimonials and Endorsements: Not available
Further comments/feedback: Our Eko Africa Digital Skill Development program will address the urgent need for digital inclusion among underserved communities in Africa. As an idea-stage initiative, the program builds on Webfala Digital Skills for all Initiative’s proven experience in delivering impactful technology and skills-based programs, while introducing an innovative, community-driven model designed for scalability and sustainability. We appreciate the comprehensive nature of the questions, which allow us to clearly outline our vision, strategy, and anticipated impact, and we are confident that with the right investment, this program will serve as a catalyst for long-term socioeconomic transformation.
Primary thematic focus area: Inclusive Digital Innovation Skills & Entrepreneurial Talent Development
Summary: Eko Africa's Digital Skill Development program aims to bridge the digital divide for mid- and late-career adults in underserved African communities, empowering them with practical digital skills for economic participation and social inclusion.

Name of your organization: Center for Socio-Cultural Research and Heritage Studies, Visayas State University
Title: Smart Traditions: Linking Heritage and Tech for Rural Prosperity
Subtitle: A digital hub preserving local heritage and empowering rural and coastal communities with skills, tools, and market access for sustainable agri-fisheries and inclusive growth.
Problem Statement: Rural and coastal communities face limited digital access, loss of traditional knowledge, weak market linkages, and vulnerability to climate impacts, hindering inclusive and sustainable growth.
Solution Overview: The Digital Heritage and Innovation Hub will create lasting social, economic, and environmental impact by empowering rural and coastal communities with the tools and skills needed to thrive in a digital economy. By preserving indigenous agricultural and fisheries knowledge, the platform safeguards cultural heritage while promoting climate-resilient practices. Immediate impacts include improved market access, increased income for MSMEs, and enhanced digital literacy among women and youth. Over time, the solution will contribute to stronger local economies, reduced post-harvest losses, and greater participation of marginalized groups in sustainable value chains. Scalability is built into the model: the platform’s modular design allows it to be replicated in other agricultural and fisheries-based communities across the Philippines and Southeast Asia. Through strategic partnerships with government agencies, private tech providers, and international organizations, the Hub can expand its reach, integrate with national digital transformation strategies, and contribute to global goals for inclusive and sustainable economic growth.
Solution Provider(s): Center for Sociocultural Research and Heritage Studies – Academic research center specializing in anthropology, cultural heritage preservation, and sustainable development, with a focus on agriculture, aquatic, and natural resources (Education/Research), Department of Agriculture (DA) – Philippine government agency responsible for agricultural policy, farmer support services, and national agricultural programs (Government/Agriculture), Bureau of Fisheries and Aquatic Resources (BFAR) – National agency under the DA managing fisheries development, coastal resources, and fisherfolk welfare (Government/Fisheries), Local Government Units (LGUs) – Municipal and provincial governments facilitating community mobilization, training, and local policy adoption (Government/Local Administration), Private ICT Solutions Providers – Technology companies offering web/mobile development, cloud hosting, and e-commerce tools for agricultural and fisheries value chains (Private Sector/Technology), Food and Agriculture Organization of the United Nations (FAO) – International body providing technical assistance, best practices, and training for sustainable agriculture and fisheries (International Organization/Agriculture).
Duration to pilot in a new geography: Estimated Duration: 12 months  Months 1–3: Community engagement, baseline study, and platform/repository design.  Months 4–8: Platform development, content digitization, and training rollout.  Months 9–12: Market linkage activation, innovation lab events, and monitoring/evaluation.
SDGs addressed: SDG 1 (No Poverty);SDG 2 (Zero Hunger);SDG 8 (Decent Work and Economic Growth);
Desired impact: The Digital Heritage and Innovation Hub will empower rural and coastal communities by preserving indigenous agricultural and fisheries knowledge while equipping over 500 individuals—particularly women and youth—with digital skills and entrepreneurial competencies. Within the first year, the solution will document more than 1,000 traditional practices, provide market access to MSMEs through a traceable e-commerce platform, and increase participant incomes by 15–20%. By integrating climate-resilient and sustainable resource management methods, the Hub will strengthen local economies, promote environmental stewardship, and foster inclusive growth, ensuring that technological advancement benefits even the most marginalized sectors.
Key technologies: The solution leverages a cloud-based knowledge repository integrated with GIS mapping to document and visualize indigenous agricultural and fisheries practices alongside climate-vulnerable areas. A mobile and web application provides digital training modules, market linkage tools, and supply chain traceability, enabling MSMEs to access e-commerce platforms with QR code-based product verification. Digital storytelling and multimedia tools capture oral histories and community innovations, while traceability features ensure transparency, sustainability, and consumer trust.
Unique Characteristics: The Digital Heritage and Innovation Hub uniquely integrates anthropology, cultural heritage preservation, and advanced digital technologies to address agriculture, fisheries, and natural resource challenges. Unlike conventional agri-tech solutions, it combines participatory ethnographic research with GIS mapping, digital storytelling, and e-commerce traceability, ensuring that technology adoption is culturally grounded and community-owned. Its partnership model blends academic expertise, government policy support, private sector innovation, and international development cooperation, creating a scalable, inclusive ecosystem. By preserving indigenous knowledge while enabling MSMEs to compete in global markets, the solution bridges tradition and innovation in a way that is both socially responsible and economically sustainable.
Sustainable Change: The Digital Heritage and Innovation Hub creates sustainable, systemic change by embedding digital skills, market access, and climate-resilient practices into the daily operations of rural and coastal communities. By digitizing and preserving indigenous agricultural and fisheries knowledge, the solution ensures that cultural heritage informs and strengthens modern value chains. Digital literacy training and e-commerce integration build the capacity of MSMEs to compete in broader markets, while traceability systems promote responsible production and consumer trust. Over time, these interventions lead to improved livelihoods, stronger local economies, and reduced resource degradation. As communities adopt and adapt the platform independently, the model becomes self-sustaining and replicable, fostering a culture of innovation and resilience that extends beyond the project’s initial scope and geography.
Funding Sources: The Digital Heritage and Innovation Hub concept has been supported through the proponent’s institutional research grants and small-scale university-funded community engagement projects focused on agriculture, fisheries, and cultural heritage. Additional resources have been leveraged through partnerships with local government units for field activities, as well as in-kind contributions from academic collaborators, such as technical expertise, training facilities, and student research assistance. While the solution’s core components have been piloted in localized contexts, the UNIDO funding will enable full-scale integration of the digital platform, expansion to new geographies, and deployment of advanced e-commerce and traceability features

Title: myStash: Digital Savings & Alternative Credit for Africa’s Informal Economy
Subtitle: A digital platform helping informal workers to save in trickles, access credit without traditional collateral, and build lasting financial security.
Problem Statement:
In Nigeria, over 70% of employment is in the informal sector (these include petty traders, street vendors, artisans) yet most are excluded from the National Pension Scheme, leaving them without social protection or the means to build emergency or retirement savings. During COVID-19, I saw countless families, dependent on informal work, plunged into crisis simply because they had no financial safety net.

Over 40% of these informal workers are women, many of whom are unable to access loans because they do not have collateral like land or other expensive assets, thus perpetuating cycles of poverty and economic exclusion.

This is personal for me because my mother is a single parent and an informal worker, and she faced these same systemic barriers. Watching her work tirelessly while still being financially vulnerable instilled in me a lifelong mission: to empower informal workers, especially women, to build financial resilience and secure a better future.
Solution Overview:
myStash is a digital savings and credit platform designed for informal economy workers who earn daily or irregular incomes. Our solution enables them to autosave small amounts, access credit without traditional collateral, and improve financial literacy, helping them build resilience and long-term security.

How it works:
Users deposit money into their myStash wallet via mobile transfers, agents, or bank integrations. An autosave algorithm (customizable to each user’s earning pattern) automatically transfers small amounts into their savings account. These savings earn interest and can be used as collateral for instant microloans, approved using our AI-powered alternative credit scoring model, which analyzes income flow and spending patterns rather than physical assets.


Methodologies & Technologies:
- AI & Machine Learning for alternative credit scoring and loan approval.
- Mobile-first design for accessibility on basic smartphones.
- Gamification to encourage consistent saving habits.
- Financial literacy micro-modules embedded in the app to promote informed decision-making.


Partnerships & Collaboration Models:
We partner with microfinance institutions, cooperatives, and women’s groups to onboard users at scale, and collaborate with payment providers for seamless transactions. Our inclusive model ensures that even the most financially excluded; particularly women and low-income earners, can access, use, and benefit from digital financial services.
Solution Provider(s): Our  partner organizations include:    Princeps Africa – An investment and venture support firm that has provided strategic funding and business growth support to myStash. Sector:  Financial Technology / Venture Capital / Private Equity,               Paystack (Payment Service Provider) – a technology company enabling seamless bank transfers into myStash wallets. Sector: Payments / Financial Technology,   Women’s Groups & Cooperatives – Grassroots networks that facilitate financial literacy outreach and adoption of myStash among informal workers and underserved women. Sector: Nonprofit / Community Development.
Duration to pilot in a new geography: Based on our current operational model and previous market rollouts, myStash can pilot in a new geography within 6 to 9 months. This timeline includes conducting a market and regulatory assessment (1–2 months), localizing our product to meet cultural and legal requirements (2–3 months), establishing key partnerships with local financial institutions and community networks (1–2 months), and executing a targeted user acquisition and onboarding campaign (2–3 months). Our lean, modular technology infrastructure and experience in cross-border operations allow us to adapt quickly while maintaining compliance and user trust.
SDGs addressed: SDG 5 (Gender Equality);SDG 8 (Decent Work and Economic Growth);SDG 10 (Reduced Inequalities);
Desired impact:
At myStash, our mission is to close the financial inclusion gap for informal economy workers, particularly women, by providing accessible digital savings tools, collateral-free credit, and financial literacy education. Our objectives are to:


- Enable at least 1 million informal workers across Africa to build emergency savings and long-term assets by 2030.


- Expand financial access to underserved communities, especially women, by reducing dependency on predatory lending and informal credit systems.


- Strengthen financial resilience, ensuring that no one’s livelihood is jeopardized by emergencies or income fluctuations.




Key Achievements / Impact:

- Over 20,000+ users onboarded since launch, 68% of whom are women in underserved communities.


- Over $500,000  saved collectively through automated micro-savings in USD and local currency (Naira).


- AI-powered credit scoring has enabled over 3,000 women to access collateral-free loans, increasing business survival rates by over 30% compared to non-users.


- Partnership with microfinance institutions and cooperatives has extended our reach to rural and peri-urban areas, reducing financial service access barriers.


- Created direct and indirect employment opportunities through agent networks, user onboarding, and financial literacy trainers.




By empowering informal workers with tools to save, borrow, and plan, we are contributing to SDGs 1 (No Poverty), 5 (Gender Equality), 8 (Decent Work and Economic Growth), and 10 (Reduced Inequalities), fostering a more inclusive and resilient digital economy.
Key technologies:
We leverage a blend of Artificial Intelligence (AI), API-driven integrations, and cloud-based infrastructure to deliver inclusive financial services to underserved communities.


AI-powered credit scoring: Analyzes non-traditional data such as savings habits, transaction history, and behavioral patterns to generate credit scores for users without formal credit histories. This enables collateral-free lending for women and informal workers who are excluded from traditional financial systems.


Secure API integrations: Seamlessly connect with payment gateways, mobile money platforms, and banking partners, allowing users to save in both local currency and USD


Cloud-based scalability: Ensures high availability, low-cost infrastructure, and rapid scalability across multiple geographies, including rural and peri-urban communities with limited resources.


Data encryption and compliance tools: Safeguard sensitive user information while meeting regulatory standards in multiple jurisdictions.


This technology stack ensures that myStash remains accessible, secure, and scalable.
Unique Characteristics:
What sets myStash apart from other FinTech solutions globally is our laser focus on the informal economy, a demographic representing over 70% of Nigeria’s workforce yet historically overlooked by digital finance. We merge cutting-edge technology with deep cultural understanding to create a solution that is both high-impact and highly adoptable:

- Our AI-driven behavioral credit scoring enables truly collateral-free lending, bypassing the limitations of traditional credit systems.

- Dual-currency savings (Local + USD) shields our users from currency volatility; an innovation rarely offered to low-income earners in emerging markets.

- Community-powered adoption model that blends technology with peer networks and financial literacy, ensuring behavioral change and long-term retention.

- Flexible micro-saving capabilities tailored for daily or irregular earners, enabling participation without penalties or rigid schedules.
Sustainable Change:
myStash is designed to create sustainable, systemic change by breaking the cycle of financial exclusion in the informal economy and ensuring long-term economic resilience for informal economy workers, especially women.


Theory of Change:
If informal workers have access to tools for micro-savings, collateral-free credit, and financial literacy, then they can build emergency funds, invest in income-generating activities, and weather economic shocks without falling into poverty, which leads to increased household stability, better health and education outcomes, and a stronger local economy.


Our desired follow-on effects include:
- Behavioral shift towards consistent saving and responsible borrowing, reinforced by gamified education and peer accountability.

- Gender equity in finance, as more women gain access to credit and investment opportunities, narrowing the economic gender gap.

- Resilient micro-economies in target communities, reducing reliance on exploitative lending and fostering local business growth.
Funding Sources:
Since 2021, myStash has been funded through pre-seed investment from early-stage impact-driven investors who, beyond capital, provide strategic mentorship in product development, financial advisory, and business strategy. This support has powered our product launch, early market traction, and the onboarding of thousands of informal economy workers into formal financial systems.
We are strategically deploying the remaining funds to scale operations, strengthen our technology, and expand into the African diaspora market. To accelerate this growth, we are pursuing grant opportunities and preparing for a Seed round, with a focus on attracting mission-aligned investors.
Testimonials and Endorsements: https://techuncode.com/five-fintech-companies-to-look-out-for-in-2022/
Further comments/feedback: I enjoyed filling the questionnaire, thanks.
Primary thematic focus area: MSME Empowerment & Local Digital Innovation
Summary: myStash is a digital savings and credit platform designed for informal economy workers, especially women, who lack access to traditional banking systems. By leveraging AI for credit scoring and mobile-first technology, myStash enables users to save in small increments, access credit without collateral, and build financial security.

Title: Agir pour le climat et de l'employabilité des jeunes
Subtitle: Connecter le Futur : Solutions Innovantes pour une Économie Numérique Inclusive"
Problem Statement:
Dans le cadre de notre initiative "Agir pour le climat et l'employabilité des jeunes", nous visons à relever plusieurs défis majeurs. 

Premièrement, la crise climatique exacerbe les inégalités socio-économiques, affectant particulièrement les jeunes dans les communautés vulnérables. Ils manquent souvent d'accès à des formations adaptées aux compétences demandées dans un marché numérique en constante évolution, ce qui limite leurs opportunités d'emploi.

Deuxièmement, le fossé numérique persiste, privant de nombreuses jeunes personnes des ressources et des outils nécessaires pour participer pleinement à l'économie numérique. Ce manque d'accès à la technologie et à l'éducation numérique les empêche de développer des compétences clés qui sont essentielles pour leur avenir professionnel.

Enfin, il existe une déconnexion entre les initiatives écologiques et l'employabilité, où les jeunes pourraient jouer un rôle crucial dans la transition vers des pratiques durables. Notre solution vise à intégrer ces enjeux en offrant des programmes qui favorisent à la fois la sensibilisation au climat et le développement des compétences numériques, afin de faciliter l'entrée des jeunes sur le marché de l'emploi tout en répondant aux défis environnementaux.
Solution Overview:
Notre initiative "Agir pour le climat et l'employabilité des jeunes" fonctionne sur un modèle intégré qui combine la formation, la sensibilisation et l'accès aux technologies. La solution se décline en plusieurs étapes :

1. Évaluation des Besoins : Nous commençons par réaliser une analyse des besoins des jeunes dans les communautés ciblées afin d'identifier les compétences numériques et environnementales spécifiques nécessaires.

2. Programmes de Formation : En collaboration avec des experts en éducation et en développement durable, nous développons des programmes de formation pratiques qui incluent des ateliers, des cours en ligne et des sessions de mentorat. Ces formations couvrent des sujets tels que la gestion des ressources durables, les technologies numériques, et les compétences professionnelles.

3. Accès aux Technologies : Nous mettons en place des centres de ressources technologiques où les jeunes peuvent accéder à des ordinateurs, à Internet et à des logiciels pertinents. Ces centres serviront également de lieux de networking et d’échanges d’idées entre jeunes et professionnels.

4. Projets Pratiques : Les participants auront l'occasion de participer à des projets pratiques qui intègrent des solutions climatiques dans des contextes professionnels, ce qui leur permet d'appliquer les compétences acquises tout en contribuant à des initiatives durables.

5. Placement et Suivi : Enfin, nous établirons des partenariats avec des entreprises locales pour faciliter le placement de jeunes dans des stages ou des emplois. Un suivi sera mis en place pour évaluer l'impact des formations sur leur employabilité.

Méthodologies et Technologies Utilisées :

- E-Learning et MOOC: Utilisation de plateformes d'apprentissage en ligne et de MOOC pour fournir des ressources éducatives accessibles à tous.
  
- Apprentissage par Projet: Mise en œuvre d'une approche pédagogique basée sur des projets qui engage les participants dans des situations réelles.

- Techniques de Coaching et de Mentorat: Des sessions de mentorat seront organisées avec des professionnels du secteur pour offrir des conseils pratiques et des retours d'expérience.

- Technologies Vertes: Introduction de technologies durables et d'outils numériques qui soutiennent la transition vers une économie plus verte.

Partenariats et Modèles de Collaboration :

Pour réaliser notre projet, nous envisageons de nouer des partenariats avec :

- Organisations Non Gouvernementales (ONG): Pour co-concevoir et animer les programmes de formation et de sensibilisation.

- Établissements d’Enseignement: Collaborer avec des universités et des écoles professionnelles pour établir des cursus alignés sur les besoins spécifiques des jeunes et du marché du travail.

- Entreprises locales et multinationales: Pour développer des opportunités de stages et de mentorat, et pour fournir des ressources techniques et des soutiens financiers.

- Agences gouvernementales: Pour aligner nos efforts avec les politiques publiques sur l'éducation, l'environnement et l'emploi, tout en maximisant l'impact de notre initiative à un niveau régional et national.

Ce modèle de collaboration permettra de renforcer l'efficacité de notre initiative tout en garantissant que les jeunes acquièrent les compétences nécessaires pour naviguer dans un avenir numérique, tout en jouant un rôle actif dans la lutte contre le changement climatique.
Solution Provider(s): FAO(agricole), ICAT (agricole), REJEPAT (Entrepreneuriat), GIZ
Duration to pilot in a new geography: Durée indéterminée
SDGs addressed: SDG 1 (No Poverty);SDG 8 (Decent Work and Economic Growth);SDG 13 (Climate Action);
Desired impact:
Objectifs de la Solution :

1. Renforcement des Compétences des Jeunes : Former au moins 5 000 jeunes en compétences numériques et environnementales d'ici trois ans, afin de les préparer à un marché du travail en constante évolution.

2. Réduction de la Fracture Numérique : Équiper 1 500 jeunes issus de communautés vulnérables avec les outils technologiques nécessaires pour accéder à des ressources éducatives et des opportunités professionnelles.

3. Promotion de l’Emploi Durable : Faciliter la création de 1 000 postes de stage ou d'emploi en rapport avec les pratiques durables dans des entreprises locales sur une période de trois ans.

4. Contribution à la Lutte contre le Changement Climatique : Sensibiliser 10 000 jeunes aux enjeux climatiques et les impliquer dans des projets de durabilité, ce qui pourrait mener à des initiatives réduisant les émissions de GES.

5. Soutien à l’Entrepreneuriat Vert : Encourager l’émergence de 100 startups ou projets innovants portés par des jeunes, axés sur des solutions durables et l'économie circulaire.

Principales Réalisations ou Impacts de la Solution :

- Formations et Certifications : Au moins 80 % des jeunes participants obtiennent une certification reconnue dans des domaines numériques ou environnementaux, prouvant leur compétence et leur employabilité.

- Emplois Créés : D'ici la fin du projet, nous visons à générer au moins 500 emplois directs et indirects liés aux compétences acquises par les jeunes au sein des entreprises partenaires.

- Réduction des Émissions de GES : Les projets de durabilité mis en œuvre par les jeunes pourraient contribuer à une réduction estimée de 1 000 tonnes de CO2 par an, grâce à des initiatives telles que la gestion efficace des ressources et la réduction des déchets.

- Accès aux Technologies : Augmenter de 50 % l'accès des jeunes aux technologies numériques dans les communautés ciblées, favorisant ainsi leur inclusion dans l'économie numérique.

- Sensibilisation et Engagement Communautaire : Atteindre 10 000 jeunes à travers des campagnes de sensibilisation sur les enjeux climatiques, impliquant un taux de participation de 70 % à des projets communautaires durables.
Key technologies:
1. Plateformes d'E-Learning : Utilisation de solutions d'apprentissage en ligne (LMS) pour dispenser des cours sur les compétences numériques et environnementales, permettant un accès flexible et à grande échelle pour les jeunes.

2. Applications Mobiles : Développement d'applications mobiles pour fournir des ressources éducatives, des outils de suivi des progrès et des plateformes de mise en réseau entre les participants et les employeurs.

3. Outils de Collaboration en Ligne : Utilisation de logiciels de collaboration (comme les tableaux blancs numériques et les plateformes de visioconférence) pour encourager le travail d'équipe et le mentorat à distance.

4. Technologies de Réalité Virtuelle (RV) ou Augmentée (RA) : Intégration de la RV/RA dans les formations pour offrir des simulations immersives qui aident les jeunes à apprendre des compétences pratiques, comme la gestion des ressources durables.

5. Internet des Objets (IoT) : Mise en œuvre de capteurs et dispositifs IoT pour des projets pratiques liés à la durabilité, tels que la gestion intelligente de l'énergie ou le suivi des ressources en eau.

6. Big Data et Analytique : Utilisation de l'analyse de données pour évaluer les performances des jeunes et l'impact des formations, permettant d'ajuster les programmes en fonction des résultats.

7. Blockchain : Potentielle utilisation de la technologie blockchain pour certifier les compétences et les réalisations des jeunes, garantissant la transparence et l'authenticité des certifications obtenues.

8. Outils de Gestion de Projets : Adoption de logiciels de gestion de projet pour structurer les activités, suivre l'avancement et favoriser la collaboration entre les équipes.
Unique Characteristics:
1. Modèle Intégré d’Éducation et de Sensibilisation : Contrairement aux initiatives classiques qui se concentrent soit sur l'éducation soit sur la sensibilisation environnementale, notre solution combine ces deux aspects de manière intégrée. Cela permet aux jeunes d'acquérir des compétences tout en prenant conscience des enjeux climatiques, les préparant ainsi à être des acteurs actifs du changement.

2. Apprentissage Pratique par Projets : Nous adoptons une approche d'apprentissage par projet qui connecte les jeunes à des entreprises locales. Cela leur permet d'appliquer immédiatement leurs compétences dans un cadre réel, favorisant une expérience d'apprentissage concrète et pertinente, tout en créant de la valeur pour les entreprises.

3. Accès Technologique Inclusif : La mise en place de centres de ressources technologiques dans des communautés vulnérables permet un accès direct aux outils numériques et à l'éducation. Cette initiative vise à réduire la fracture numérique en offrant des ressources et des formations là où elles sont le plus nécessaires.

4. Partenariats Multisectoriels : Notre approche repose sur des partenariats innovants entre le secteur privé, le secteur public, et les ONG. Ce modèle de collaboration diversifié favorise un environnement riche en ressources et expertises qui renforce l'impact de l’initiative.

5. Utilisation d’Avancées Technologiques : En intégrant des technologies de pointe comme la réalité virtuelle, l'IoT et la blockchain, nous offrons une expérience d'apprentissage moderne et immersive. Ces technologies permettent une formation plus engageante, efficace et facilement vérifiable des compétences acquises.

6. Mécanismes de Financement Alternatifs : Nous envisageons d'explorer des modèles de financement novateurs, comme le financement participatif et les microcrédits, pour soutenir les jeunes entrepreneurs et les projets innovants liés à la durabilité. Ce soutien financier innovant peut stimuler l’esprit d’entreprise et l’intrapreneuriat chez les jeunes.

7. Focus sur la Durabilité en Entrepreneuriat : La solution ne se limite pas à la formation et à l'emploi; elle intègre également des modules sur l'entrepreneuriat vert. Les jeunes sont encouragés à développer des idées de startups axées sur la durabilité, promouvant une économie circulaire et leur permettant de devenir des agents de changement à long terme.

Ces caractéristiques confèrent à notre solution un avantage distinctif, la positionnant comme un modèle innovant pour répondre aux défis complexes de l'employabilité des jeunes et de la durabilité environnementale.
Sustainable Change:
Notre solution "Agir pour le climat et l'employabilité des jeunes" est conçue pour engendrer un changement systémique durable à plusieurs niveaux en intervenant sur différents leviers clés :

1. Renforcement des Compétences et de l'Employabilité : En formant les jeunes à des compétences numériques et environnementales, notre solution contribue à leur employabilité à long terme, leur permettant de s’adapter à un marché du travail en évolution rapide. Cela peut mener à une génération de jeunes mieux préparés, qui sont capables de s’insérer dans des secteurs économiques en pleine croissance, notamment ceux axés sur la durabilité.

2. Création d’un Écosystème d’Innovation Durable : En intégrant l'entrepreneuriat vert dans notre programme, nous cultivons un écosystème où les jeunes sont stimulés à développer des solutions innovantes qui répondent aux défis environnementaux. Title: Serre Verticale intelligente
Subtitle: AGRO KOOM offers smart vertical greenhouses that use hydroponics to grow plants without soil. Our solution reduces water use by 80% and eliminates chemicals, ensuring healthy and natural crops. With our connected app, monitor the status of your crops in real time, optimizing your yield up to 10 times more than conventional agriculture. Together, we support the Sustainable Development Goals for a better future.
Problem Statement: Senegalese agriculture faces major challenges: limited access to water, rapid urbanization, increasing pressure from insects and diseases, soil salinity, and the devastating effects of climate change. These problems are driving many farmers to abandon their land, with some even turning to irregular migration, such as Mouhamed Ndiaye, a market gardener from the Niayes region, whose tragic story symbolizes the struggle of farmers. In response to this crisis, AGRO KOOM was founded to offer innovative solutions that enable farmers to thrive on their land without being forced to leave their communities.
Solution Overview:
Solution Description
AGRO KOOM offers smart vertical greenhouses that enable plants to be grown hydroponically, without the use of soil. This method offers several advantages:

Optimal Use of Space: Our greenhouses can grow up to 120 plants in a 2 m² area, compared to 30 in conventional agriculture.
Water Management: Thanks to a recycling system, we reduce water consumption by 80% compared to traditional methods.
Real-Time Monitoring: With our mobile app, farmers can monitor the temperature, pH, humidity, and conductivity of their greenhouse. Early alerts inform them about the health of their plants.

Hydroponics and Aeroponics: Our greenhouses use hydroponic and aeroponic systems to feed plants with nutrient solutions, eliminating the need for pesticides and chemical fertilizers.

Artificial Intelligence: An integrated AI model analyzes the collected data to provide accurate recommendations on plant needs and detect potential diseases.

Connected Sensors: Real-time sensors measure environmental conditions and send data directly to the mobile app.

Precision Agriculture Chatbot: Our AI-powered chatbot offers personalized advice and alerts on crop conditions.

Title: Nsengo – Cashless, Circular & Traceable Zero-Interest Microcredit for Smallholder Farmers
Subtitle: A zero-interest, digitally managed microcredit system enabling smallholders to access capital, inputs, and services with full traceability and community accountability.
Problem Statement:
Over 80% of African smallholder farmers lack access to affordable, timely credit.
Microfinance often charges 30%+ interest, while subsidies and grants are short-lived.
Financing is rarely aligned with agricultural cycles or fully traceable.
This traps farmers in low productivity, food insecurity, and climate vulnerability.
Solution Overview:
Nsengo is a zero-interest, fully traceable microcredit platform designed for smallholder farmers. Instead of cash loans, Nsengo provides a virtual credit envelope accessible via mobile money to pay only approved suppliers and seasonal workers. This eliminates cash leakage, ensures that funds are spent on productive inputs, and builds transparent, auditable records.

How it works

Partner producer organizations (OPs) identify and onboard farmers.
Credit envelopes are disbursed digitally, aligned with the crop cycle.
Farmers purchase inputs or labor from pre-approved vendors via Nsengo Wallet.
Repayments are collected through mobile money after harvest and recycled—95% of recovered capital funds the next cycle.

Methodologies & Technologies
Mobile Money Integration (MTN, Orange Money, Moov) for secure, cash-free transactions.
Traceability system linking each transaction to farmer ID, supplier, and location.
AI-powered advisory for agronomic guidance, crop planning, and risk alerts (under development).
Data analytics to track repayment rates, input usage, and impact KPIs in real time.

Partnership & Collaboration Model
Producer Organizations (OPs): handle mobilization, group accountability, and field follow-up.

Local suppliers: provide quality inputs and services, paid directly from the wallet.
Institutional funders (donors, governments, development partners): finance the initial credit envelopes and service fees.

Technology partners: ensure secure integration, AI advisory, and scalability.
This model combines fintech efficiency with local trust networks, creating a scalable, capital-efficient, and farmer-friendly financing ecosystem.
Solution Provider(s): Nsengo SAS – Social fintech company developing inclusive, traceable microcredit solutions for smallholder farmers in West Africa (Agriculture, Financial Inclusion, Technology). Producer Organizations & Cooperatives – Local farmer groups acting as field partners for mobilization, training, and repayment follow-up (Agriculture, Rural Development). Mobile Money Operators (MTN Côte d’Ivoire, Orange Money, Moov Africa) – Digital payment providers enabling secure, cashless credit disbursement and repayment (Telecommunications, Fintech). Input Suppliers & Agri-service Providers – Pre-approved vendors providing seeds, fertilizers, tools, and seasonal labor (Agribusiness, Supply Chain). Institutional Funders (e.g., AFD, FASEP, World Bank projects, government agricultural programs) – Financing initial credit envelopes and operational costs (Development Finance, Public Sector). FAO – United Nations Food and Agriculture Organization, supporting sustainable agriculture, food security, and farmer capacity-building (Agriculture, Policy, Capacity Development). PAM – World Food Programme, working on food security, resilience building, and market access for smallholder farmers (Food Security, Logistics, Rural Development). FIDA – International Fund for Agricultural Development, investing in rural development and inclusive agricultural value chains (Rural Finance, Development, Agriculture). BAD – African Development Bank, financing infrastructure, agriculture, and private sector development in Africa (Development Finance, Agriculture, Climate Resilience). Technology Partners – Developers and integration partners for Nsengo Wallet, traceability system, and AI advisory modules (ICT, AgTech).
Duration to pilot in a new geography: Estimated duration: 6 to 9 months Justification:  Months 1–2 – Identification and contracting with producer organizations (POs) and field partners, plus regulatory and technical adaptation to the target country. Months 3–4 – Initial deployment of the digital platform, training of POs, and farmer onboarding preparation. Months 5–9 – Launch of the first credit cycle, with an average envelope of €305 per farmer for the pilot, field monitoring, data collection, and operational adjustments. This timeline ensures rapid deployment while allowing for local adaptation and measurable results from the first cycle.
SDGs addressed: SDG 1 (No Poverty);SDG 2 (Zero Hunger);SDG 5 (Gender Equality);
Desired impact:
Nsengo delivers 0% interest, fully traceable microcredit to smallholder farmers, starting with an average envelope of €305 per farmer in the pilot. By recycling 95% of repaid funds into 2–3 credit cycles per year, we multiply impact without increasing donor costs.
The pilot will serve 1,500 farmers—50% women—boosting farm incomes by 20–30% and creating seasonal jobs.

At scale, Nsengo will integrate micro-insurance and AI-powered agronomic advice to strengthen climate resilience and productivity. Our capital-efficient, partnership-driven model will scale from Côte d’Ivoire to other African countries, then to Southeast Asia and Latin America—reaching 5 million smallholder farmers by 2030 while ensuring every euro is tracked and maximized for impact.
Key technologies: SaaS platform, Mobile Money integration, AI-powered features (scoring, advisory), and PWA support for low-connectivity environment
Unique Characteristics:
Nsengo combines financial innovation, digital traceability, and embedded local partnerships to create a scalable, impact-driven microcredit model. Our competitive advantage rests on five pillars:

Non-Extractive Model — Zero-Interest, Recycled Credit
No interest or collateral
95% of repayments recycled into new loans, creating a regenerative credit loop
Digital Traceability & Capital Flow Efficiency
Virtual wallet tied to vetted suppliers and farm workers
100% Mobile Money disbursement & repayment
Real-time donor/partner visibility
Embedded in Trusted Local Structures
Work exclusively with cooperatives & producer organizations
Peer accountability & local ownership ensure high repayment rates
Cost-Efficient & Donor-Compatible by Design
Cashless, lean operations with low fixed costs
Fully auditable for ODA, philanthropic, and CSR funds
Strong Field Presence & Co-Creation
Côte d’Ivoire-based pilot team
Product refined with feedback from 300+ farmers
Partnerships with universities, development agencies, and farmer groups
This unique blend makes Nsengo digitally scalable, socially rooted, and financially responsible — a credible alternative to extractive microfinance and ineffective subsidy systems.
Sustainable Change:
Nsengo’s model is designed to move smallholder financing from a cycle of dependency to a cycle of self-reinforcing growth.

1. Immediate Outcomes (0–12 months)

Farmers access zero-interest, traceable credit aligned with agricultural seasons.
Inputs and labor are purchased on time, boosting yields and income within the first harvest cycle.
Digital records build credit history and trust between farmers, cooperatives, and funders.
2. Medium-Term Effects (1–3 years)
Capital recycling (95% of repayments) sustains lending without continuous donor input.
Cooperatives strengthen as economic hubs, improving farmer bargaining power and collective resilience.
Gradual integration of micro-insurance and AI-powered advisory reduces climate and productivity risks.
3. Long-Term Systemic Change (3+ years)
Replication across geographies enables multi-country adoption in Africa, and later South-East Asia & Latin America.
Transparent, cashless microcredit becomes a benchmark for ODA and CSR funding, shifting from subsidies to regenerative finance.
By 2030, up to 5 million smallholders gain lasting access to affordable finance, contributing to food security, poverty reduction, and climate adaptation.
Theory of Change:
Access to affordable, traceable finance → timely farm investment → higher yields & income → cooperative & community strengthening → capital recycling → systemic shift toward sustainable, inclusive agricultural finance.
Funding Sources: Financed through a mix of public grants (Normandie Incubation, AD Normandie, Bpifrance), a Prêt d’Honneur, a bank loan from Crédit Mutuel, and founders’ personal funds.
Further comments/feedback: This questionnaire provides a valuable platform to highlight solutions that bridge systemic gaps in the digital economy. Nsengo’s model addresses not only financial access but also structural inefficiencies, ensuring transparency, scalability, and long-term sustainability. We believe platforms like this are crucial to connect impact-driven innovators with partners who share a vision for systemic change. We welcome opportunities to collaborate, pilot in new geographies, and co-create a pathway toward empowering 5 million smallholder farmers across Africa, and later in Asia and Latin America, by 2030.
Primary thematic focus area: Financial Inclusion and Agricultural Sustainability
Summary: Nsengo is a zero-interest, digitally managed microcredit platform designed to provide smallholder farmers in West Africa with access to capital, inputs, and services. The platform operates using mobile money, ensures full traceability of funds, and offers a revolving credit system that supports sustainable agricultural practices.

Title: DORG: Democratizing Advanced AI Through Ethical Digital Colleagues
Subtitle: An ethical tri-partite ecosystem providing affordable AI colleagues to MSMEs and underserved communities, combining advanced capabilities with built-in compliance and human oversight.
Problem Statement:
MSMEs and underserved communities face a critical AI accessibility gap that perpetuates digital inequality. While large corporations leverage advanced AI for competitive advantage, smaller organizations cannot access these transformative technologies due to prohibitive costs, technical complexity, and lack of ethical frameworks.
Key challenges include:
- Economic barriers: Enterprise AI solutions cost hundreds of thousands annually, excluding 99% of global businesses
- Technical complexity: Implementing AI requires specialized expertise that MSMEs cannot afford or access
Governance vacuum: Most AI tools lack built-in ethical oversight, compliance frameworks, or transparency mechanisms
- Human displacement fears: Workers resist AI adoption due to job security concerns and lack of collaborative integration models
- Fragmented solutions: Organizations must cobble together multiple vendors, creating integration nightmares and security vulnerabilities
- Regulatory uncertainty: EU AI Act compliance requires expensive legal and technical resources beyond MSME reach
- Knowledge asymmetry: Innovation benefits concentrate in developed markets while developing economies lag further behind

This digital divide intensifies global inequality, preventing MSMEs from participating in the AI-driven economy and leaving billions of workers without tools to enhance their productivity and economic prospects. Without inclusive AI access, the promise of digital transformation remains limited to privileged organizations, contradicting sustainable development goals and perpetuating economic disparity.
The challenge demands a systematic solution that democratizes advanced AI while ensuring ethical governance, human-centric integration, and regulatory compliance at affordable scale.
Solution Overview:
How the Solution Works

DORG operates through a tri-partite ecosystem separating ethical governance, knowledge development, and operational delivery to democratize advanced AI access while ensuring responsible deployment.

Core Architecture:

1. DORG Society ETS (Ethical Foundation)
- Non-profit entity providing ethical oversight and regulatory compliance
- Mitigates Environmental and Social Impacts related to Dorg adoption
- Manages EU AI Act compliance frameworks and governance protocols
- Provides training courses for companies and consultants to become certified DORG Onboarders
- Operates DORG Society DAO with blockchain governance using Dorg Ethics Coins (DEC)

2. DORG University (Knowledge Hub)
- Provides marketplace for Competences: Cultural, Agentical, and Actuative
- Enables consulting firms to establish Faculties and develop marketplace Competences
- Creates "local for local" networks with regionally-tailored AI competencies
- Accelerates AI skills in developing countries through locally-delivered training
- Maintains competency registry per Dorg and provides patented Dorg Quality Module

3. DORG Agency SRL (Operational Delivery)
- Delivers "The Apprentice" - foundational AI colleague with 6 core characteristics
- Provides self-onboarding support with dedicated Dorg Onboarder
- Offers technical support to Faculties and operational services

The Apprentice Foundation:
Every DORG begins as "Apprentice" (€6,000/year) featuring:
- Interaction Module: Natural language LLM, calendar, Teams/phone/WhatsApp integration
- SuperAgent: Central orchestrator coordinating intents and requests
- Intent Knowledge Base: Role-based authorizations, interaction memory, shortcuts
- RAG System: Intelligent document access with data quality assessment
- Causal Analysis: Pattern recognition and data correlation
- Structured Output Generation: Traceable, structured responses

Methodologies and Technologies Used

Technical Architecture:
- Modular AI Framework: University competencies integrate into Apprentice base
- Data Sovereignty: Private Cloud on Microsoft AI Foundry/Azure ensuring local data control
- Microsoft Cloud Integration: Native support with Customer Copyright Commitment
- Bounded LLM Systems: Controlled language models with ethical constraints
- Blockchain Governance: Smart contracts for DAO operations

Ethical Methodologies:
- Human-in-the-Loop Design: Role-based behavior and competency availability
- Transparency by Design: All actions in immutable audit trails
- Risk-Based Approach: Automatic EU AI Act compliance classification
- Participatory Governance: Multi-stakeholder DAO with weighted voting

Partnerships and Collaboration Models

Strategic Global Partnerships:

Global AI Association (Accredited Partner)
- AI ethics standards and responsible development frameworks collaboration
- Joint research on governance best practices

AIFOD (Corporate Member)
- AI for Developing Countries Forum participation in Vienna
- Speach on "Regulatory Sandbox and Investment Multiplication Effects"
- Co-Chair at "Invest in SKILL intelligence" session
- Member of Standard Committee of FAIR - Future AI Investment Responsibility certification framework development, chapter "Respectfull entry and Community Engagement"


Ethical Governance Structure:
DORG Society Ethics Committee
- Flavio Bordignon - President DORG Society
- Daniela Leveratto - President Global AI Association  
- Giovanni Vaia - Professor Digital Management, Ca' Foscari University
- Giovanni Grava - Head of Supply Chain Transformation EssilorLuxottica
Solution Provider(s): The solution is built leveraging standard Azure components and internally developed software, we don't have any solution partner. As related to Faculties we are activating partnership with system integrators
Duration to pilot in a new geography: Days for a Dorg Apprentice, specific competencies require development evaluation
SDGs addressed: SDG 3 (Good Health and Well-being);SDG 8 (Decent Work and Economic Growth);SDG 9 (Industry, Innovation, and Infrastructure);
Desired impact:
Solution Objectives
DORG aims to democratize advanced AI as critical digital infrastructure, functioning as a horizontal platform that amplifies human capabilities across all economic sectors. Unlike vertical AI solutions, DORG operates as foundational infrastructure that can be adapted to any industry while maintaining ethical governance and local data sovereignty.

A sick patient in a remote area can call a DORG, which collects symptoms and medical history, provides the doctor with a preliminary diagnosis proposal, and upon physician approval, calls back the patient with results and treatment recommendations. This transforms the Doctor productivity. Similarly, farmers receive personalized crop advice and weather alerts directly on their phones, citizens get instant responses to government service requests, and small business owners access AI capabilities that was previously unaffordable.
Key technologies: DORG leverages Microsoft AI Foundry as the core technological foundation, providing enterprise-grade AI capabilities with built-in safety, compliance, and scalability features. This platform enables the development of bounded Large Language Models (LLMs) with Customer Copyright Committment, advanced natural language processing for multi-channel communication, and secure cloud deployment through Azure infrastructure.
Unique Characteristics:
What are the unique/differentiated characteristics of your solution?

Revolutionary Tri-Partite Ecosystem
DORG's most innovative characteristic is its separation of responsibilities across three integrated entities. Unlike traditional AI companies that combine technology development, ethical governance, and commercial delivery, DORG separates ethical oversight (Society), competency development (University), and operational delivery (Agency). This architecture dramatically reduces costs for individual organizations while ensuring robust governance and enables sharing of massive AI development investments across the entire ecosystem.

Participatory Blockchain Governance
The DORG Society DAO represents a breakthrough in AI governance, using soul-bound Dorg Ethics Coins (DEC) to enable weighted participatory decision-making by all stakeholders - from founders to end users. This decentralized governance model ensures ethical standards evolve through community consensus rather than corporate decree, creating unprecedented transparency and accountability in AI deployment.

"Local for Local" Competency Networks
The Accredited Faculties model enables consulting firms and system integrators to establish their own faculties within DORG University, developing market-specific AI competencies in local languages and cultural contexts. This approach builds indigenous AI capabilities in developing countries rather than imposing external solutions, creating sustainable local expertise and employment.

Data Sovereignty by Design
Unlike cloud-dependent AI services, DORG operates through private cloud deployment on Microsoft AI Foundry, ensuring complete local data control. Organizations maintain full sovereignty over their information while accessing enterprise-grade AI capabilities, addressing critical concerns about data security and regulatory compliance in sensitive sectors.

Democratized Pricing Model
At €6,000/year for the Apprentice, DORG makes advanced AI accessible to organizations with budgets 90% lower than traditional enterprise solutions. This pricing breakthrough enables MSMEs and developing country organizations to access capabilities previously reserved for large corporations, directly addressing economic barriers to AI adoption.

Pre-Integrated Compliance Framework
DORG embeds EU AI Act compliance, ethical governance, and audit trails from day one, eliminating the expensive and complex compliance burden that typically prevents smaller organizations from AI adoption. The built-in governance framework transforms regulatory compliance from a barrier into an enabler.

Human-Centric Collaboration Model
Rather than replacing human workers, DORG operates as a digital colleague requiring human supervision for autonomous decisions. This collaborative approach addresses job displacement fears while actually enhancing human capabilities, making AI adoption socially sustainable.

Platform Infrastructure Approach
Unlike vertical AI solutions designed for specific industries, DORG functions as horizontal digital infrastructure - similar to electricity or internet - that can be adapted across all sectors while maintaining consistent ethical standards and technical reliability.

Conditional Activation Innovation
The dual-payment mechanism ensuring both operational (Agency) and ethical (Society) contributions creates a unique accountability structure where AI capabilities remain active only when both technical and ethical responsibilities are met, preventing misuse or abandonment of governance standards.

This combination of democratic governance, economic accessibility, local capacity building, and built-in ethics creates a fundamentally different approach to AI deployment that prioritizes inclusive development over profit concentration.
Sustainable Change:
How does your solution contribute to create sustainable, systemic change?

Theory of Change: Building Foundational Infrastructure for Autonomous Innovation

DORG was deliberately designed as a neutral "digital employee" platform rather than prescriptive sector-specific solutions. This foundational approach creates sustainable systemic change by empowering organizations to autonomously develop competencies that address their specific needs and local contexts.

Foundation Layer: Creating the Base Infrastructure
The DORG ecosystem establishes fundamental infrastructure comprising ethical governance frameworks, technical platforms, and local capacity-building mechanisms. Rather than directing how organizations should use AI, DORG provides the essential foundations - ethical compliance, data sovereignty, human oversight protocols, and modular competency development tools - that enable safe and responsible AI adoption across any sector or use case.

Autonomous Development Phase: Organizations Drive Innovation
Once the foundational infrastructure exists, companies and organizations independently leverage the platform to develop competencies tailored to their specific challenges. A healthcare organization develops diagnostic assistance competencies, agricultural cooperatives create crop optimization tools, government agencies build citizen service capabilities, and manufacturers develop supply chain intelligence. The platform's neutrality ensures these innovations emerge organically from actual user needs rather than predetermined assumptions.

Ecosystem Effects: Knowledge Sharing and Cross-Pollination
As organizations develop sector-specific competencies within the DORG University marketplace, a natural knowledge-sharing ecosystem emerges. Successful competencies become available to similar organizations globally, while cross-sector applications create unexpected innovations. Agricultural predictive models inform supply chain management, healthcare diagnostic frameworks enhance quality control in manufacturing, and public service optimization techniques improve private sector efficiency.

Local Capacity Building: Indigenous Expertise Development
The Accredited Faculties model ensures that each region develops indigenous AI expertise rather than remaining dependent on external providers. Local consulting firms and system integrators become competency developers, creating employment while building capabilities that reflect regional priorities, languages, and cultural contexts. This distributed development model prevents technological colonialism and ensures sustainable local ownership.

Systemic Transformation: Infrastructure-Driven Change
By functioning as neutral infrastructure rather than directive technology, DORG enables systemic change that is sustainable because it emerges from user needs rather than external imposition. Organizations maintain agency over their AI adoption while benefiting from shared ethical governance, technical reliability, and cost efficiency. This approach creates compound effects where AI capabilities in one sector support improvements across entire local economies.

Long-term Impact: Self-Sustaining Innovation Ecosystem
The desired follow-on effect is a self-sustaining global network where local organizations continuously innovate while sharing knowledge through ethical, democratically-governed infrastructure. The DORG ecosystem provides the foundation - compliance, governance, technical reliability, and affordability - while users determine applications, creating resilient innovation that adapts to changing needs without abandoning ethical principles.

This theory of change recognizes that sustainable transformation occurs when communities have the tools and autonomy to solve their own challenges, rather than having solutions imposed upon them. DORG's role is providing the foundational infrastructure that makes such autonomous innovation possible.
Funding Sources:
Funding Sources

The DORG ecosystem is currently self-funded by the founding team and operates through an asset valorization strategy rather than equity dilution funding models.

Self-Funded Development
All initial development, including the tri-partite ecosystem architecture, Microsoft AI Foundry integration, blockchain governance infrastructure, and foundational competency development, has been financed through internal resources. This self-funding approach ensures complete autonomy in strategic decisions and alignment with the ecosystem's ethical mission without external investor pressure that might compromise the inclusive development objectives.

Asset Valorization Strategy
Rather than seeking traditional venture capital or equity financing that would dilute ownership stakes, DORG pursues a funding strategy focused on valorizing the underlying technological and governance assets. This approach builds sustainable value through operational revenue streams, intellectual property development, and ecosystem network effects rather than speculative investment rounds.

Revenue-Based Sustainability
The economic model generates sustainable funding through the Apprentice subscription fees (€6,000/year to Agency, €600/year to Society), University competency marketplace transactions, and Certified OnBoarder training programs. This operational revenue foundation supports continued development while maintaining independence from external financial pressures that might compromise the inclusive accessibility mission.

Strategic Rationale
The asset valorization approach aligns with DORG's foundational mission of democratizing AI access. Traditional equity funding often requires rapid scaling and profit maximization that could conflict with affordable pricing for MSMEs and developing country organizations. Self-funding preserves the ability to prioritize social impact alongside financial sustainability.

Future Funding Considerations
While maintaining the asset valorization focus, the ecosystem remains open to strategic partnerships and mission-aligned funding opportunities that support global expansion and enhanced local capacity building without compromising the core principles of ethical governance, data sovereignty, and inclusive access.

This funding approach ensures that DORG's development remains aligned with its mission of creating foundational infrastructure for inclusive AI adoption rather than optimizing for investor returns that might exclude underserved communities.
