Title: Zerobionic: Bridging the STEM Gap for Learners with Hearing Impairments
Subtitle: Robotics and AI solution enabling inclusive STEM education for learners with hearing impairments through sign language and gesture-based interaction.
Problem Statement: In many African classrooms, a deaf student’s curiosity often meets an invisible wall. While their peers freely exchange ideas, ask questions, and engage with experiments, they are left struggling to follow along  not because they lack the talent or interest, but because the tools, teaching methods, and resources were never designed with them in mind. In STEM subjects, where complex technical terms and hands-on activities are essential, this gap becomes even more pronounced. Sign language is rarely integrated into the learning process, and the absence of standardized signs for specialized STEM vocabulary leaves students further behind. Beyond the classroom, the challenge deepens. Reliable internet connectivity  often taken for granted elsewhere  is a rare luxury in many rural and underserved areas. Digital learning platforms that could bridge the gap remain out of reach, isolating deaf students from the fast-growing world of technology and innovation. This exclusion does not just limit their education; it limits their future, narrowing career paths and perpetuating socio-economic inequality. Meanwhile, the continent faces another pressing crisis  mounting piles of plastic and e-waste that choke waterways, pollute communities, and damage ecosystems. Ironically, this environmental challenge hides an opportunity: the same materials harming our planet could be repurposed into affordable, life-changing assistive technologies. Yet, without innovative solutions, both the educational divide and the environmental burden will continue to grow, leaving behind not only the deaf community but the promise of a more inclusive and sustainable future.
Solution Overview: Zerobionic is an AI-powered assistive robotics platform designed to break communication barriers for deaf students in STEM education while addressing environmental sustainability. Our solution combines gesture recognition, real-time transcription, and recycled-material manufacturing to create affordable, inclusive learning tools that work even in low-connectivity environments. At the heart of Zerobionic is a gesture-controlled robotic exoskeleton. Using computer vision and deep learning, it recognizes Kenyan Sign Language (KSL) and Rwandan Sign Language (RSL) gestures, translating them into text in real time. For STEM-specific terms that do not yet have standardized signs, we use animation-based visual media to introduce and teach these concepts. This ensures students can fully participate in technical subjects without losing meaning in translation. The exoskeleton also functions as a remote transcription device. In a live or virtual lesson, spoken words are transcribed into text and displayed to the student in real time, with embedded images or diagrams for technical terms. To overcome connectivity barriers, our system transmits lessons over 4G from the training platform to the exoskeleton, then converts them into a 2G-compatible format  ensuring functionality even in remote, underserved communities.
Solution Provider(s): NVIDIA robotics UNDP, Global Learning Council, Kenya National Innovation Agency, Climate Launchpad, KPMG Kenya, Africa Tech Summit, AU,Young Scientist Kenya
Implementation location(s): Nairobi Kenya, Kigali Rwanda, Windhoek Namibia & pilots in Lucern Switzerlans
Duration to pilot in a new geography: 6 months
SDGs addressed: SDG 4 (Quality Education);SDG 10 (Reduced Inequalities);SDG 13 (Climate Action);
Desired impact: Zerobionic was created with a clear vision to ensure that deaf students can participate fully in STEM education, no matter where they live or what resources are available to them. Our objective is to remove communication barriers through AI-powered sign language recognition, real-time transcription, and animation-based visual aids for technical STEM terms. By using recycled plastics and e-waste to manufacture our devices, we also make assistive technology affordable and environmentally sustainable. Connectivity challenges, which often exclude rural learners, are addressed by designing our system to function even on low-bandwidth 2G networks. This vision is already taking shape in classrooms. In Kenya and Rwanda, more than 5,000 deaf students have gained access to interactive and inclusive STEM learning with the help of our devices. Over 500 teachers have been trained to use assistive robotics in their lessons, creating a multiplier effect that will continue to expand our impact. We have also built a dataset of more than 1,000 standardized STEM signs in Kenyan and Rwandan Sign Language, filling a critical gap in technical vocabulary for the deaf community. The impact goes beyond education. By re-purposing over 2,000 kilograms of e-waste and more than 500 kilograms of plastic waste into device components, we are turning environmental hazards into instruments of empowerment. Our low-bandwidth technology has made it possible to bring these tools to some of the most underserved communities, proving that innovation can thrive even where infrastructure is limited. The story of Zerobionic is one of transformation  of classrooms where deaf students are no longer silent observers, but active participants; of waste once destined for landfills now fueling opportunity; and of technology being used not only to teach but to break barriers. It is a story of inclusion, sustainability, and the belief that every learner, regardless of ability, deserves a seat at the table of innovation.
Key technologies: Zerobionic integrates artificial intelligence, computer vision, and deep learning to recognize Kenyan and Rwandan Sign Language in real time, translating it into text or animations for STEM learning. Our robotic exoskeletons use IoT connectivity optimized for low-bandwidth networks, including 2G, ensuring accessibility in remote areas. Machine learning-based natural language processing enhances transcription accuracy for complex technical terms, while 3D printing with recycled plastics and repurposed e-waste keeps devices affordable and environmentally sustainable.
Unique Characteristics: What makes Zerobionic unique is its seamless integration of accessibility, sustainability, and affordability in one solution, built with the community and by the community at large. Unlike traditional assistive tools, our AI-powered system is specifically trained on Kenyan and Rwandan Sign Language, ensuring cultural and linguistic inclusivity. The robotic exoskeleton is optimized to function on 2G networks, overcoming the connectivity barriers that often exclude rural learners. By using 3D printing with recycled plastic and repurposed e-waste, we drastically reduce production costs while addressing environmental waste. Our partnership-driven model works directly with deaf schools, teacher training programs, and policy advocates to ensure adoption is not just technological but systemic, embedding inclusive practices into education itself. This combination of localized AI, low-bandwidth optimization, circular manufacturing, and collaborative, community-led development makes Zerobionic not just a device, but a replicable model for inclusive STEM education worldwide.
Sustainable Change:
When we first brought Zerobionic into a classroom, the change was immediate. A deaf student who once sat quietly in the back, hesitant to ask questions, was now following along with a complex science experiment in real time. His exoskeleton device was transcribing the teacher’s words, animating STEM-specific terms, and giving him the confidence to raise his hand not just to answer, but to debate ideas. That moment wasn’t just a personal victory; it was the start of a ripple effect. Teachers trained to use Zerobionic began to rethink how they approached inclusion, building lesson plans that assumed every student could contribute equally. Local communities, involved in collecting and recycling plastic and e-waste for the devices, started seeing the value of turning waste into opportunity both for the planet and for their own livelihoods. Over time, as more schools adopted the solution, the language of STEM for the deaf is becoming standardized, bridging communication gaps across entire regions. Students who once saw STEM as unreachable are begining to envisioning futures as engineers, researchers, and innovators.
The long-term vision is powerful: a generation of deaf students graduating with the skills to shape industries, inclusive education policies becoming the norm, and communities benefiting from both economic and environmental gains. Zerobionic doesn’t just change classrooms it changes mindsets, systems, and possibilities.
Funding Sources: Zerobionic has been funded through a blend of personal investment, innovation awards, institutional partnerships, and in-kind technical support. Early development was supported by the Young Scientist Kenya (YSK) Award in 2020, which provided initial seed funding. Additional funding and mentorship have come from Kenya’s Ministry of Education and partners in the disability inclusion ecosystem. NVIDIA has provided hardware and AI acceleration resources to power our deep learning models, while Strathmore University, through iLabAfrica, has contributed research facilities, technical expertise, and lab space. We have also received support from the United Nations Development Programme (UNDP) and the Climate Launchpad initiative, which recognized Zerobionic for its circular economy model and environmental impact. Community-led recycling programs further reduce production costs by supplying repurposed plastics and e-waste for device manufacturing. This combination of financial backing, hardware provision, institutional support, and grassroots contributions has enabled us to successfully pilot and scale our solution in deaf schools across Kenya and Rwanda.

Title: Digital Skills & E-Commerce for Youth: Powering Inclusive Growth in Kwara
Subtitle: Empowering Kwara youth through digital skills, e-commerce training, and market access to drive jobs, innovation, and inclusive economic growth.
Problem Statement: The solution tackles youth unemployment, limited digital skills, poor market access for entrepreneurs, and low participation in the digital economy, hindering innovation and economic growth in Kwara.
Solution Overview:
How the Solution Works

Our solution is a mobile-first digital empowerment platform designed for underserved entrepreneurs in low-connectivity areas. Through a lightweight app and offline-enabled learning modules, users gain practical skills in digital marketing, e-commerce setup, financial literacy, and cross-border trade. The platform also provides a marketplace integration, allowing MSMEs to showcase products globally without the need for high-end infrastructure.
Interactive, step-by-step courses are localized into native languages, while AI-driven progress tracking tailors learning paths to each user’s pace and needs.

Methodologies and Technologies Used

Human-Centered Design (HCD): Solution co-created with target communities to ensure cultural relevance and usability.

Blended Learning Model: Combines online and offline content to bridge connectivity gaps.

Lightweight Progressive Web App (PWA): Optimized for low bandwidth and basic smartphones.

AI-Driven Learning Analytics: Personalized recommendations and skill-level adjustments.

Secure Cloud Hosting: Ensures data privacy and easy scalability.

USSD/SMS Integration: Provides critical updates and market alerts to non-smartphone users.

Partnerships and Collaboration Models

Local Community Organizations & Cooperatives: Mobilize participants, provide on-ground support, and facilitate trust-building.

Telecom Operators: Offer subsidized data packages and zero-rated platform access.

E-Commerce Platforms: Enable global product listing and secure payment gateways.

Microfinance Institutions: Provide access to small loans and financial products tailored for MSMEs.

Government Agencies & Policy Advocates: Support policy alignment for digital inclusion and provide regulatory guidance.

International Development Partners & NGOs: Offer capacity building, funding for pilot programs, and technical expertise.
Solution Provider(s): Kwara State Ministry of Business, Innovation & Technology – Government agency driving entrepreneurship, innovation, and ICT adoption in Kwara State; Public Sector.  MTN Nigeria Communications PLC – Leading telecom operator providing connectivity solutions and supporting digital inclusion initiatives; Telecommunications Sector.  Airtel Nigeria – Telecommunications provider offering affordable mobile data and SMS/USSD services for rural and urban communities; Telecommunications Sector.  Jumia Nigeria – Nigeria’s largest e-commerce platform connecting MSMEs to regional and global markets; E-Commerce Sector.  Konga Online Shopping Limited – Nigerian e-commerce company enabling small businesses to sell products online; E-Commerce Sector.  Lift Above Poverty Organization (LAPO) Microfinance Bank – Financial institution providing microloans, savings, and business support to low-income entrepreneurs; Microfinance Sector.  Women in Business, Management and Public Service (WIMBIZ) – NGO advancing women’s leadership, entrepreneurship, and economic empowerment; Nonprofit Sector.  Tony Elumelu Foundation – Africa-focused philanthropic organization empowering entrepreneurs through training, mentorship, and funding; Nonprofit Sector.
Duration to pilot in a new geography: Estimated Implementation Time: 12 months  Months 1–2: Needs assessment, partner onboarding, and localization of training content for Kwara State.  Months 3–4: Platform customization, offline module development, and pilot testing with a small group of entrepreneurs.  Months 5–10: Full rollout across target communities, ongoing training delivery, and marketplace onboarding.  Months 11–12: Monitoring, evaluation, impact reporting, and preparation for scale-up to other Nigerian states.
SDGs addressed: SDG 17 (Partnerships for the Goals);SDG 11 (Sustainable Cities and Communities);SDG 10 (Reduced Inequalities);
Desired impact:
Solution Objectives

Enhance Digital Skills – Equip 1,000 underserved entrepreneurs in Kwara State (60% women, 40% youth) with practical digital business skills.

Improve Market Access – Integrate at least 500 MSMEs into regional and global e-commerce platforms.

Boost Financial Inclusion – Link 70% of trained entrepreneurs to microfinance services for business growth.

Promote Inclusive Growth – Reduce the digital skills and market access gap for marginalized groups in Kwara State.

Enable Sustainable Scale-Up – Develop a replicable digital empowerment model adaptable to other Nigerian states.

Key Achievements / Expected Impacts

Employment Generation: Create or expand 800+ sustainable micro and small enterprises within 12 months.

Income Growth: Achieve an average 30% increase in participants’ monthly income through improved sales and market reach.

Digital Inclusion: Provide digital literacy to entrepreneurs in 10+ rural and semi-urban communities across Kwara.

Financial Access: Facilitate microloans totaling over ₦150 million (USD ~100,000) for business expansion.

Environmental Impact: Reduce travel-related carbon emissions by enabling 20% more online transactions versus in-person sales.

Long-Term Sustainability: Build local capacity so that 70% of trained participants continue independent digital business operations beyond the project period.
Key technologies:
Technologies Utilized

Artificial Intelligence (AI): Used for personalized learning recommendations, adaptive skill assessments, and automated progress tracking.

Progressive Web App (PWA) Technology: Ensures the platform runs efficiently on low-bandwidth connections and basic smartphones common in rural Kwara.

USSD/SMS Integration: Delivers training updates, reminders, and market alerts to non-smartphone users, ensuring no participant is excluded.

Cloud Computing: Provides secure data storage, scalability, and remote access for training materials and marketplace integration.

E-Commerce API Integrations: Connects local entrepreneurs directly to major online marketplaces such as Jumia and Konga.

Data Analytics Tools: Measure user engagement, market trends, and impact metrics to guide continuous improvement.
Unique Characteristics:
What Makes the Solution Innovative

Inclusive-by-Design Technology: Combines AI-powered personalization with offline-enabled modules and USSD/SMS delivery, ensuring both smartphone and non-smartphone users in rural Kwara can fully participate.

Hybrid Learning & Market Access Model: Integrates skills training and direct e-commerce marketplace onboarding in one platform—closing the gap between learning and earning.

Localized Co-Creation: Developed in partnership with Kwara-based cooperatives, women’s groups, and youth associations, making the solution culturally relevant and immediately adoptable.

Innovative Financing Partnerships: Links trained entrepreneurs to microfinance institutions with tailored loan products, creating a direct pathway from skill acquisition to business expansion.

Scalable Public–Private Collaboration: Builds a replicable model leveraging state government agencies, telecoms, e-commerce platforms, and NGOs—allowing fast scale-up across Nigeria and beyond.

Low-Bandwidth Digital Marketplace Integration: Uses lightweight tech to connect rural sellers directly to global buyers without heavy infrastructure investment.
Sustainable Change:
Desired Follow-On Effects (Theory of Change)

If underserved entrepreneurs in Kwara State gain affordable access to digital skills, market platforms, and tailored financial services then they will increase their business capacity, income, and resilience.

This will lead to:

Sustained Digital Inclusion: A self-reinforcing culture of digital adoption in rural and semi-urban communities, inspiring new entrepreneurs.

Economic Growth & Job Creation: Expansion of MSMEs generating new employment opportunities, particularly for women and youth.

Strengthened Local Supply Chains: Increased local production and market connectivity, reducing dependency on external intermediaries.

Policy Influence: Evidence from the project will inform Kwara State and national digital economy strategies, leading to more inclusive policy frameworks.

Scalable Model: A proven, low-cost blueprint for replication in other Nigerian states and across West Africa.

In summary: Skills + Market Access + Financial Inclusion → Higher incomes, reduced inequalities, and resilient local economies.

These funding streams enabled successful small-scale trials, providing the proof-of-concept data and community engagement foundation for the larger, Kwara State–wide rollout proposed to UNIDO.

Title: Bridging the Digital Divide with Solar-Powered Rural community Wi-Fi hotspot
Subtitle: Empowering rural communities with solar-powered Wi-Fi, smart farming, e-learning, digital finance, e-health, and market access to boost productivity and climate resilience.
Problem Statement: In Zambia, only 31.2% of the population, about 5.9 million people, are connected to the internet, leaving 68.8% (over 13 million, mostly rural farmers producing 70% of the nation’s food) offline and excluded from vital digital tools such as smart irrigation, weather alerts, e-learning, market data, and e-health. Across Africa, just 37% of the population, around 547 million people, are online, while 63% (approximately 933 million) remain disconnected, reflecting a severe digital divide. This lack of infrastructure means rural communities cannot benefit from AI innovations, app-based solutions, or digital economies. COVID-19 exposed this gap further: when classrooms closed, rural learners were left stranded without e-learning access, while urban areas adapted. Today, this divide persists, limiting productivity, resilience, and inclusion in the digital economy.
Solution Overview:
Our solution deploys decentralized, off-grid, solar-powered community Wi-Fi hotspots with coverage ranging from 100 meters to 5 kilometers. Each base station can connect 50 to 100 homes and can be expanded to reach 1,000 or more homes by adding additional hardware at each station. These hotspots provide high-speed, reliable, and cost-effective internet with unlimited access, offering reduced speeds once the main data package is depleted to maintain connectivity. Each unit integrates a local cloud server that stores frequently accessed content such as agricultural training videos, e-learning materials, and e-health resources, allowing communities to access key content without requiring broadband data for stored materials.

The hardware is backhauled using satellite internet from partners like Starlink and OneWeb, enabling deployment anywhere regardless of existing infrastructure. We are collaborating with technology partners such as GlobalTT and Bluetown for the supply of specialized hotspot hardware. Through this network, rural communities gain access to real-time weather alerts, market information, agricultural training, educational resources, digital financial services, and e-health consultations.

Our decentralized model ensures that even the most remote communities can benefit from the ongoing AI revolution, digital innovations, and the connected economy. By combining robust satellite connectivity, local content caching, and community-based infrastructure, we provide a sustainable and scalable approach to bridging the digital divide.
Solution Provider(s): Starlink=https://www.starlink.com/ sector satellite broadband, globalTT=https://globalttafrica.com/, bluetown= https://bluetown.com/solution/ all these are in telecom sector
Duration to pilot in a new geography: 2 months
SDGs addressed: SDG 9 (Industry, Innovation, and Infrastructure);SDG 11 (Sustainable Cities and Communities);SDG 17 (Partnerships for the Goals);
Desired impact:
Solution Objectives

Increase digital connectivity for rural communities in Zambia and across Africa by providing reliable internet access through solar-powered community Wi-Fi hotspots.

Enable access to agricultural training, e-learning, e-health services, digital financial services, and market information, improving productivity, resilience, and inclusion in the digital economy.

Promote climate-smart development by using renewable solar energy for off-grid internet infrastructure.

Support equitable access to AI and digital innovations, reducing the rural-urban digital divide.

Key Achievements and Impacts

Expected to connect over 13 million rural Zambians currently offline, including farmers who produce 70% of the country’s food.

Facilitate continuous access to education and training, preventing exclusion during school closures or emergencies.

Enable climate-smart agriculture through timely access to weather alerts, smart irrigation guidance, and crop management tools.

Support local employment and skills development by involving community members in installation, maintenance, and training.

Scalable model: each hotspot covers 100 meters to 5 kilometers, allowing replication in other underserved regions in Zambia and Africa.

Indirectly reduces GHG emissions by promoting solar energy over diesel-powered alternatives for digital infrastructure.
Key technologies:
Key Technologies

Solar-Powered Wi-Fi Hotspots: Off-grid, community-based infrastructure providing reliable internet in remote areas.

Satellite Internet Backhaul: Starlink and GlobalTT ensure high-speed connectivity regardless of location.

Local Content Caching: Bluetown servers store educational, agricultural, and health resources for offline access.

Internet Management & Security: Systems ensure safe, controlled, and fair usage for all community members.

Scalable Mesh Networking: Connects multiple hotspots to expand coverage efficiently. Overall enabler of AI, IoT, e.t.c
Unique Characteristics:
Unique and Differentiated Characteristics

Decentralized, Off-Grid Deployment: Unlike traditional telecom towers, our solar-powered Wi-Fi hotspots can be deployed in the most remote areas without relying on grid infrastructure.

Local Content Caching: Communities can access educational, agricultural, and health resources offline, reducing dependency on continuous broadband data.

Subsidized Bandwidth Model: Internet access is affordable, with options to subsidize costs through targeted ads, making it inclusive for low-income users.

Satellite Backhaul Connectivity: Partnerships with Starlink and GlobalTT ensure high-speed, reliable internet in areas previously unserved by legacy telecoms.

Community-Based Network Management: Local operators are trained to maintain and manage networks, empowering communities and ensuring sustainability.

Scalable Mesh Architecture: Multiple hotspots interconnect seamlessly, enabling flexible coverage expansion as communities grow.

Integrated Digital Services: Supports e-learning, e-health, smart agriculture, digital finance, and market access, bridging the rural digital divide while promoting climate-smart solutions.
Sustainable Change:
If rural communities are provided with decentralized, solar-powered Wi-Fi hotspots with satellite backhaul and local content caching, because they will gain reliable access to e-learning, agricultural training, e-health, digital finance, and market information, then learners will improve their skills and digital literacy, farmers will adopt climate-smart practices and increase productivity, communities will participate more fully in the digital economy, and local operators will gain technical skills and employment.

This systemic approach ensures that connectivity drives sustainable education, economic inclusion, agricultural resilience, and local capacity building, creating lasting social, economic, and environmental impact in underserved regions.

Name of your organization: Bundesministerium für wirtschaftliche Zusammenarbeit und Entwicklung (BMZ)/Federal Ministry for Economic Cooperation and Development
Title: Hamburg Declaration on Responsible AI for the SDGs
Subtitle: The Declaration outlines shared principles and commitments to promote the equitable, inclusive, and sustainable development and deployment of AI worldwide, with particular emphasis on empowering developing countries.
Problem Statement: We stand at a pivotal moment. Despite the progress achieved in recent years, a renewed commitment and active engagement are essential to advance and ultimately achieve the Sustainable Development Goals (SDGs). Digital technologies, particularly Artificial Intelligence (AI), hold transformative potential in this endeavor. In a world characterized by rapid social, political, economic, ecological, and technological changes, AI presents both opportunities and risks. When developed and deployed responsibly, AI can serve as a powerful catalyst for sustainable development, delivering benefits to society, the economy, and the planet.
Solution Overview:
he United Nations Development Programme (UNDP), the German Federal Ministry for Economic Cooperation and Development (BMZ), and key partners from the public sector, business, academia, and civil society have collaboratively developed the ‘Hamburg Declaration on Responsible Artificial Intelligence (AI) for the Sustainable Development Goals (SDGs).’ This landmark initiative—the first global, multistakeholder declaration specifically focused on AI in international development—establishes shared principles and commitments to foster the equitable, inclusive, and sustainable development and deployment of AI worldwide, with a particular focus on empowering developing countries.

The Hamburg Declaration represents an informal global coalition dedicated to advancing a responsible and sustainable AI future. It serves as a platform for facilitating concrete joint initiatives and promoting knowledge sharing. Importantly, it imposes no restrictions on individual collaboration models, allowing for flexible and diverse partnerships.
Solution Provider(s): Yu Ping Chan, Head of Digital Partnerships and Engagement, United Nations Development Programme (UNDP); Theresa Schwarz, Senior Policy Advisor, Digital Technologies, Bundesministerium für wirtschaftliche Zusammenarbeit und Entwicklung (BMZ)
Implementation location(s): Global, with individual commitments by endorsers.
Implementation timeline(s): Overall, the individual commitments of the declaration are to be achieved by 2030 in line with the 2030 Agenda; several individual commitments from endorsers operate on shorter timelines
Duration to pilot in a new geography: The Declaration is open to further endorsements. Endorsers can decide their own timeline for implementation of their commitments in new geographies.
SDGs addressed: SDG 17 (Partnerships for the Goals);
Desired impact:
The desired impact of the solution is to shape a human-centric, human-rights-based, inclusive, open, sustainable, and responsible AI future. Endorsing organizations are committed to advancing AI for the Sustainable Development Goals (SDGs) in alignment with ongoing international efforts.

Solution Objectives:

- Promote equal and meaningful participation in AI development and deployment.
- Ensure fair and equitable access to computing, data, investment, and resources for capacity and talent development, particularly for stakeholders from emerging markets, developing economies, and vulnerable groups.
- Bridge digital divides and empower all nations and communities to co-create and leverage AI solutions that benefit people and the planet.
- Uphold human rights, protect marginalized communities, and combat disinformation through responsible AI technologies.
- Improve the resource efficiency of AI systems and expand access to AI education, particularly for women and girls.
- Support the growth of local AI innovations in developing countries.

Key Achievements or Impacts:

- Advancing the equitable and inclusive development of AI to ensure its benefits are not concentrated among a privileged few.
- Promoting responsible, inclusive, and sustainable AI aligned with the five pillars of the 2030 Agenda for Sustainable Development: people, planet, prosperity, peace, and partnerships.
- Facilitating the co-creation of AI solutions that address global challenges and serve the needs of all communities.

Concrete commitments of the endorsers of the Hamburg Declaration can be found at https://www.bmz-digital.global/wp-content/uploads/2025/06/250603_Hamburg_Declaration_Individual_Commitments-1.pdf
Key technologies: Artificial Intelligence (AI)
Unique Characteristics: First global multi-stakeholder declaration focused specifically on AI in international development
Sustainable Change:
The Hamburg Declaration contributes to sustainable, systemic change by establishing a shared global vision grounded in human rights, inclusion, and sustainability. Its development was informed by extensive and inclusive consultations, with a particular focus on amplifying voices from the Global South and civil society.

Key Contributions to Systemic Change:

- Policy Coherence: The Declaration promotes alignment across policies and strategies, ensuring that responsible AI principles are integrated into innovation ecosystems and future initiatives.
- Multi-Stakeholder Partnerships: By fostering collaboration among governments, businesses, academia, and civil society, it creates a foundation for collective action and shared accountability.
- Locally Relevant Solutions: The approach encourages the development of AI solutions tailored to local contexts, addressing specific needs and challenges.
- Trust and Equity: It aims to enhance trust in AI systems while ensuring that the benefits of AI are equitably distributed, particularly among marginalized and underrepresented communities.

Desired Follow-On Effects:

- A responsible, sustainable, and inclusive AI future that accelerates progress toward the Sustainable Development Goals (SDGs).
- Reduction of inequalities by bridging digital divides and empowering all nations and communities to participate in and benefit from AI advancements.
-Mitigation of risks associated with AI through the adoption of ethical and sustainable practices.

By embedding these principles into global and local frameworks, the Hamburg Declaration seeks to create lasting, systemic change that benefits people, the planet, and prosperity.
Funding Sources: No specific funding was and is necessary for the Declaration itself. Individual commitments and initiatives to implement the Declaration are funded by the respective endorsers.
Testimonials and Endorsements: Please find video testimonials from several endorsers at https://www.bmz-digital.global/en/hsc
Primary thematic focus area: Enabling Policies & Regulatory Innovation
Summary: The Hamburg Declaration on Responsible AI for the SDGs is a global initiative aiming to promote equitable, inclusive, and sustainable AI development, particularly for developing countries. While the declaration offers a strong framework for responsible AI deployment, its long-term impact depends on the individual commitments of endorsers and the broader adoption of its principles.

Title: Digitizing data, supply chain and financial inclusion for smallholder farmers
Subtitle: Building the digital infrastructure that powers farmer data, unlock credit access, and manage the entire agricultural supply chain for transparency, efficiency, and market access.
Problem Statement: Smallholder farmers in Nigeria produce over 80% of the food consumed, yet remain trapped in low productivity and poverty due to fragmented supply chains, lack of access to quality inputs, financial exclusion, and unstructured markets. Most operate without formal records of transactions, making them invisible to investors and financial institutions. Limited data, poor traceability, and reliance on middlemen reduce earnings, increase post-harvest losses, and discourage investment in the sector at scale. The combination of these challenges results in persistent food insecurity, underutilized agricultural potential, and missed economic opportunities for millions of rural households.
Solution Overview:
Agrovesto provides a technology solution designed to increase productivity, profitability, and traceability of smallholder farmers while de-risking investments in Agriculture.

How It Works:
The solution follows a platform-as-a-service model targeting farmer cooperatives or associations, Farmer organizations, financial institutions, and development partners, for cost-effective scaling and trust. The process begins with digital onboarding and verification using the National Identity Number (NIN), biometric capture, and GPS farm mapping. Farmers are then assigned digital wallets to receive payments from buyers, savings, and transfers, building transaction histories that power a credit scoring system.
 
Methodologies & Technologies:
- AI-powered analytics for farmer profiling, yield prediction, and market matching.
- USSD, mobile, and web platforms to ensure accessibility for both tech-savvy and rural farmers.
- Real-time agronomic advisory via SMS, voice, and app notifications.
- End-to-end input disbursement tracking from suppliers to farms.

Partnership & Collaboration Models:
- Farmer cooperatives & associations for member mobilization and group training.
- Input suppliers for verified, quality seed, fertilizer, and equipment distribution.
- Financial institutions to provide credit and input financing.
- Off-takers and processors for structured market access through binding trade agreements.
- Development agencies and government programs for scaling and capacity-building support.
Solution Provider(s): 1. Japan International Cooperation Agency (JICA) – A Japanese government agency providing technical cooperation and development assistance focusing on capacity building, infrastructure, and agricultural productivity. Sector: International Development / Agriculture, 2.Nigerian Women in Agricultural Business Cooperative Society Limited (NiWAB) – A national cooperative organization representing women agripreneurs across Nigeria, focusing on empowerment, agribusiness development, and market access. Sector: Agriculture / Cooperative Development / Women Empowerment, 3. Growth for Sustainable Agriculture Initiative (GSAI) – An agribusiness-focused non-profit dedicated to promoting sustainable agriculture through investment mobilization, capacity building, and technology adoption. Sector: Sustainable Agriculture / Investment Facilitation, 4. Sterling Bank – A financial institution providing banking infrastructure and enabling farmers make and receive payment. Sector: Financial/Payment facilitation, 5. National Agricultural Development Fund (NADF)- A government agency that catalyzes financing and collaboration across the agricultural sector, unlocking its potential to improve productivity, ensure food security, and drive inclusive socio-economic development. Sector: Public/Development partner
Duration to pilot in a new geography: 12 month
SDGs addressed: SDG 2 (Zero Hunger);SDG 8 (Decent Work and Economic Growth);SDG 12 (Responsible Consumption and Production);
Desired impact:
Solution Objectives
- Increase smallholder farmer productivity through timely access to quality inputs, agronomic advisory, and technology-driven farm management.

- Enhance farmer incomes by linking them to premium structured markets and reducing dependency on exploitative middlemen.

- Expand financial inclusion via digital wallets, transaction tracking, and credit scoring for future financing.

- Improve transparency and traceability in the agricultural value chain for investors, buyers, and policymakers.

- Empower women and youth in agriculture through targeted training, market linkages, and access to resources.

- Promote climate-smart agriculture by integrating weather alerts, sustainable practices, and data-driven farm decisions.

Key Achievements/Impacts
- Farmers using the solution have so far recorded about 40 - 60% increases in income through improved yields and market access.

- We have directly supported over 10,000 smallholder farmers across 5 states, creating seasonal and permanent jobs in farming, aggregation, and input supply.

- Facilitated structured offtake deals, reducing post-harvest losses by up to 30%.

- Onboarded and verified thousands of farmers into the formal financial system through digital wallets and transaction-based credit scoring.

- Our partnership with the Nigeria Women in Agricultural Business Cooperative Society (NiWAB) has enabled scaling the solution to over 300,000 women and youth farmers nationwide.

- Through the integrated weather forecasting and pest alerts, it has enabled farmers to adapt planting and reduce crop losses from climate shocks.

- Built a verified farmer database with geo-mapped farms, enabling investors and partners to monitor field activities in real time.
Key technologies:
We integrate advanced and accessible digital technologies to deliver a traceable, efficient, and scalable agricultural value chain platform. These include:

1. Artificial Intelligence (AI)
- For biometric capture and profiling, yield forecasting, and market-matching algorithms.
- For credit scoring based on transaction history, farm performance, and cooperative activity.
- For agronomic advisory, providing tailored crop management recommendations via SMS and app notifications.

2. Offline and online platform technology
- USSD technology for farmers without smartphones or internet access.
- Mobile and web platforms for Cooperatives, Field Agents, Financial institutions, Donor funders, and off-takers to manage funding, operations, transactions, and reporting.
- Cloud-based architecture for secure data storage and real-time analytics.

3. Geo-Mapping and weather technology
- Satellite and GPS mapping of farms for accurate land measurement, production planning, and monitoring.
- Integration with weather data APIs to provide localized climate alerts.
Unique Characteristics:
What makes our solution unique includes:

- Network effect through a group-based partnership model with farmer cooperatives and associations

- Our data-driven investment de-risking model, where we combine farmer identity verification with real-time transaction and yield data for transparency.

-Inclusive technology design through USSD, mobile apps, and web dashboards, accessible to both online and offline rural farmers without smartphones or internet, ensuring inclusivity.

- Innovative credit scoring system that uses transaction history, production data, and performance to determine eligibility for input loans and financing to create sustainable access to credit.

-Multi-stakeholder collaboration system with key players like input suppliers, financial institutions, off-takers, development agencies, and government bodies in an ecosystem.

-Climate-smart processes through the integration of weather data, pest alerts ensure resilience to climate shocks, and transparent farm-to-market tracking.
Sustainable Change:
Our solution’s approach is designed to address the root causes of low productivity, financial exclusion, and market inefficiencies in agriculture, while creating lasting, scalable improvements in the agricultural ecosystem.

Follow-on effects:

-Reliable data enabling investment-readiness, which will attract more private capital and government interventions.
- There will be institutionalized farmer credit histories enabling ongoing access to finance and nationwide adoption of traceable, climate-resilient agriculture.
- Contribution to national food security, reduced poverty, and improved livelihoods.
- Shift from fragmented, informal trade to structured, transparent supply chains.

- We secured $1,000 grant funding from Moolu Venture Lab

- Revenue from operations generated $45,000 in revenue in 2024

While the project has demonstrated strong initial success, its scalability and sustainability depend on further strategic partnerships and long-term financial planning.

Title: A Recruitment Portal For Today's Market.
Subtitle: KAZICONNECT is a digital recruitment platform using smart technology to connect Tanzania seekers with employers, fostering inclusive economic growth.
Problem Statement:
Global's labour market has systemic inefficiencies that disproportionately prevent youth, women, and people with disabilities (PWDs) from obtaining meaningful employment.  Current data show worrying disparities: teenage unemployment rates exceed 30% in numerous African countries, women have a 20% lower hiring probability than identically qualified male candidates, and people with disabilities face 80% underemployment due to accessibility restrictions and discriminatory behaviours.

 These issues are exacerbated by:

Structural Matching Failures: Employers struggle to identify suitable candidates quickly, with typical vacancy lengths surpassing 90 days, while competent job seekers are ignored due to fragmented recruitment channels.
Technological Exclusion: Conventional hiring systems lack the tools to equitably connect marginalized talent pools with opportunities, perpetuating cycles of informality and poverty.
Skills Mismatch: 60% of African employers report difficulty finding candidates with relevant skills, yet training programs rarely align with market needs.

KAZICONNECT solves these limitations by providing an AI-powered recruitment platform that:

1.Reduces the average recruiting time to 7 days for 80% of firms.
2. Actively supports 45,000+ people, including 150+ disabled job seekers.
3. Uses clever algorithms to remove prejudice in applicant shortlisting.
4. Collaborates with governments and non-governmental organisations (NGOs) to prepare youth and women for in-demand occupations.
By altering how talent links with opportunity, we are creating an inclusive digital economy that leaves no one behind, directly furthering SDGs 8 (Decent Work), 10 (Reduced Inequalities), and 17.
Solution Overview:
1. Solution Functionality 

KAZICONNECT provides a comprehensive digital recruitment solution that promotes inclusive hiring practices by strategically matching employers with competent applicants. Fundamentally, the platform makes use of in-house matching algorithms that evaluate corporate needs and candidate profiles to provide the best possible job placements, with an 80% success record in filling openings in as little as seven days. A graduate placement program with integrated employability training, an executive search function for senior posts, and a diaspora recruitment service that takes cross-border employment considerations into account are just a few of the specialised recruitment modules that the system integrates for key populations. To help organisations expedite the hiring process, KAZICONNECT offers a full range of hiring solutions, such as performance analytics dashboards, interview coordination tools, and automated application tracking.

2Technical Execution

The platform's technical architecture integrates a number of trustworthy aspects to deliver scalable and effective services. Its clever matching system, powered by AI-driven algorithms that constantly learn from user interactions, handles an average of 50 applications each job opportunity. 
Reaching Tanzania's diverse population necessitates accessibility across devices and in low-bandwidth environments, which the mobile-optimized interface provides. Employers gain streamlined HR administration capabilities by integrating with Zoho People, and the platform's data analytics engine monitors and evaluates over 37,400 user interactions to give valuable labour market data and drive continual system enhancements. Employers can use dashboards to streamline their entire hiring process.

3.  Strategic Partnerships

KAZICONNECT has built a solid network of partnerships that expands its influence and audience. To create specialised hiring solutions, the platform keeps up direct contact with business partners in a variety of industries. Specialised projects aimed at underserved communities are made possible by ATE's strategic partnerships with development organisations such as Light for the World and Exchange,Youth With Disability Organization, Vocational Education and Training Authority and Salesian DON BOSCO. 

Technology collaborations, especially with Zoho People, enhance the platform's HR administration capabilities, and payroll system connectors guarantee seamless post-hire procedures.
Partnerships with academic institutions and training providers aid in filling skills shortages and preparing applicants for the demands of the labour market. These collaborations are supported by the platform's validated performance metrics, which show the efficacy of the solution and its dedication to inclusive employment practices. These metrics include serving more than 11,000 active users, managing more than 500 job listings at once, and successfully engaging more than 90 people with disabilities.

Through inclusive, tech-enabled hiring practices and the provision of market-relevant skills to women, youth, and people with disabilities (PWDs), KaziConnect seeks to close the skills gap between employers and job seekers. Title: AgriConnect – Inclusive Digital Platform for Rural-Urban Market Linkages
Subtitle: Bridging the digital divide to empower rural farmers and promote sustainable local economies.
Problem Statement: In the Democratic Republic of Congo, many rural farmers lack access to urban markets, resulting in low incomes, post-harvest losses up to 30%, and limited economic inclusion. There is a need for a scalable digital solution that connects farmers to buyers efficiently, even in low-connectivity areas.
Solution Overview:
AgriConnect is a hybrid digital platform combining a web application and USSD/SMS access to ensure inclusivity for low-connectivity regions. Farmers can post products and receive orders; buyers can browse catalogs, place orders, and evaluate suppliers through a rating system.
The platform leverages React, Tailwind CSS, and lightweight backend technologies for web access, and USSD/SMS interfaces for rural users.
Collaboration models include partnerships with local cooperatives, transport and logistics providers, microfinance institutions, and community organizations. The system is designed for scalability and easy replication in other regions.
Solution Provider(s): AgriConnect RDC – Founder & Lead Developer: Manasse Lotafe; Local Cooperatives in Katanga; Chariow Digital Solutions (technical support and e-commerce integration).
Implementation location(s): Lubumbashi and surrounding rural areas, Katanga province, Democratic Republic of Congo
Duration to pilot in a new geography: 6–8 months for adaptation, deployment, and local onboarding
SDGs addressed: SDG 2 (Zero Hunger);SDG 8 (Decent Work and Economic Growth);SDG 9 (Industry, Innovation, and Infrastructure);
Desired impact:
Integrate 500 farmers in Year 1, scaling to 5,000 within 3 years

Increase average farmer incomes by 25% in pilot regions

Reduce post-harvest losses by 15%

Foster digital literacy and market access among rural communities
Key technologies:
React + Tailwind CSS for web interface

USSD/SMS for low-connectivity access

Backend APIs for catalog management, order processing, and rating systems

Optional integration with payment gateways and microfinance APIs
Unique Characteristics:
Hybrid access (web + USSD/SMS) ensures inclusivity in areas with limited connectivity

Integration with local cooperatives and logistics partners for end-to-end service

Community-driven trust model via ratings and feedback

Low-cost, scalable, and replicable model suitable for other African countries

Title: SnooCODE: Offline Digital Addresses For Everyone, Everywhere
Subtitle: SnooCODE lets anyone generate a memorable 5–7 digit alphanumeric address for any location on Earth, even offline, that opens to the exact location on a map when shared.
Problem Statement:
Four billion people around the world live without a formal address, a serious challenge to sustainable development. In much of Africa, even in affluent areas, those who need directions the most – taxi and ambulance drivers, and delivery people – are not literate, hence, do not use street
names. Currently, only 28% of Africa has Internet connectivity, preventing many from accessing essential services via modern means like WhatsApp location. Liberia’s Ministry of Posts & Telecommunications stated in their bid document that inadequate address systems “hampered delivery, commerce, transportation, medical, fire, relief services, and tax collection, etc.”
The problem impacts every gender, all ages, low-income demographics, businesses, and governments. Revenue mobilisation, for example, is ineffective without accurate location data. Even the middle-class urban dweller is denied access to an ambulance if they live some distance away from a popular landmark. 
According to the UNDP, “4 billion people are excluded from the rule of law, as the lack of a legal identity often prevents them from enjoying their rights as citizens. Setting up an addressing system is the 1st step towards tackling that issue.” Not having proper addressing systems costs Africa an estimated $12.6B annually ($9.90 per person). SnooCODE is solving this problem at a one-time cost of $0.5–$1.5 per person.
Solution Overview:
SnooCODE is a digital addressing system that provides 4 main functions: accurate LOCATION; ROUTE OPTIMISATION; information VERIFICATION AND PROOF OF DELIVERY; and INTEGRATION into emerging and future technologies like drones and driverless cars – 99% offline, with a small file size for easy download and storage. 
Once the app is downloaded anyone can generate their SnooCODE with their smartphone wherever they are (even offline and without a SIM in the phone), which gives them a unique 6-digit alphanumeric code e.g. 4BN-8OC, which they can then share with another person, enabling access to a map (chosen by the receiver from their stock of available mobile mapping systems). SnooCODE is accurate to 6.8m on average and ±25cm when used in specialist applications like drone piloting. We considered true literacy levels when designing SnooCODE, enabling an easy-to-use system powered by memorable address codes, so that even a grandmother in the village can have her SnooCODE address pasted on her fridge, ready to share her location address code in an emergency or to get deliveries to her home.

SnooCODE partners primarily with B2B with B2G to gain a critical mass of users for sufficient impact. Our solution, the SnooCODE digital addressing system, has been selected by Liberia as their National Digital & Postal Addressing System (NDPAS). 
We have developed SnooCODE to work in every country on Earth.
Solution Provider(s): The Royal Academy of Engineering (RAENG) funded our launch of a smart waste management logistics app in the Liberian market, we also enjoy the support of the Delegation of German Industry and Commerce (AHK) in Ghana always keen on introducing SnooCODE to potential investors and other interventions.
Implementation location(s): Liberia (National Digital & Postal Addressing System), Ghana, Sierra Leone,  Kenya
Implementation timeline(s): July 2021- Sep 2024: SnooCODE selected as winner through a competitive tender for Liberia’s National Digital & Postal Addressing System with a . Oct 2021- 6-year project contract approved by: Public Procurement & Concessions Commission, Ministry of Finance & Development Planning, Ministry of Justice Mar 28, 2022- Contract notarized Apr 25, 2023- Official public launch Sep 12, 2024- Certificate of Completion signed by the Ministerin 2024 2015- 2024: Customized SnooCODE for the National Ambulance Service of Ghana, Greening ecommerce project with GIZ GHANA 2024 - date: Signed MoU with LFR International to build a responder system in SIERRA LEONE 2020: worked with Opero Services, an NGO in KENYA's solid waste management sector
Duration to pilot in a new geography: 3–6 months: for stakeholder engagement, technical integration, training, and initial rollout excluding government changeover and processes. 1–3 months: for B2B projects
SDGs addressed: SDG 9 (Industry, Innovation, and Infrastructure);SDG 10 (Reduced Inequalities);SDG 11 (Sustainable Cities and Communities);
Desired impact:
Solution Objectives:
SnooCODE is best understood as digital infrastructure. The desired impact of our solution is to serve as a foundation on which other technologies can be built to power logistics and mobility, governance and administration, healthcare, security, and climate action. This digital infrastructure provides anyone in the developing world with an address to access core public and private services and the tools for services and businesses to collect accurate field data, expand their businesses, create more jobs, and improve their service delivery.
Key Achievements/Impacts:
Before our first national contract (i.e., Liberia), we were focused on product development to get our system to world-class levels of service. Our 1st proof-of-concept was a series of time trials with Ghana’s National Ambulance Service and the Komfo Anokye Teaching Hospital (KATH), where we helped reduce response times by as much as 56% with our SnooCODE RED system. After its validation, we worked with the Ambulance Service to train 400 EMTs on its usage. We have also trialled SnooCODE in the last mile delivery, surpassing DHL’s route optimisation system by an average of 19.6%, and that of mom-and-pop operations by as much as 180%. 
In Liberia, our digital addressing system adds approximately 5 million citizens to our existing user base of almost 100,000 Android and iOS users, allowing them to benefit from accurate navigation, quicker emergency response, and successful home deliveries. 
During our 9-month pilot with GIZ addressing excess packaging waste from single-use materials, we completed over 1,500 deliveries and achieved a 58.82% reduction in carbon emissions in Accra, Ghana, using ebikes and our route optimization and verification technology, along with reusable, security-sealed delivery bags. Our pilot projects continue to demonstrate our ability to unlock value for both public and private customers, with significant scaling potential.
 In the long term, our vision is to make SnooCODE the standard for the unaddressed across the developing world. We are currently working towards making SnooCODE it the default standard addressing system in Africa, upon which many other digital systems (e.g., e-commerce apps) can be built for socio-economic development. This will solve the USD 10-14 billion problem of inaccessibility, inefficiency and inconvenience (2018, MIT Emerging World’s Paper) in most African countries.
Key technologies:
SnooCODE works with geocoding technology and a combination of satellite navigation
systems like GPS, GNSS, and GLONASS to assign a memorable 5–7-digit alphanumeric
address code to any location on Earth.
Unique Characteristics:
SnooCODE has the USP of being usable anywhere on earth – online or offline. It can be used by anyone, regardless of their level of education, unlike our top competitor, What3words (W3W), which requires college-level vocabulary to be used; with SnooCODE, all one needs to know is their ABCs and 123s (Language-agnostic). Taking true literacy levels into consideration, SnooCODE is designed as an easy-to-use, memorable address system that can be easily adopted to improve their operations and participate in economic growth. 

Furthermore, SnooCODE provides 3 other capabilities besides accurate location: route optimisation; proof of delivery and compliance verification; and integration into emerging technologies like driverless cars and drones, none of which is offered directly by our competitors. Its small file size makes it versatile for low-resource settings. 
SnooCODE has Prior Art as the first “postal code system and method” for smartphones and other mobile devices(https://patents.google.com/patent/WO2014080186A3/en) ahead of What3words and Google OLC.
Sustainable Change:
SnooCODE turns “addressability” into a national digital public good. A verified, offline-capable address standard becomes the backbone for identity/KYC, service delivery, emergency response, logistics, and revenue mobilization across public and private systems.
Follow-on effects: greater financial inclusion, improved government service delivery and revenue collection, enhanced emergency response and disaster resilience, and stronger foundations for the digital economy in underserved regions. We are in conversation with over 15 other African countries about adopting the system as their national address system. We have close to 100,000 active users, and with our $1.6m Liberia contract, we expect to acquire at least 2 million more users within the next 2 years.
With the emerging market for national addressing on the continent and beyond, if we estimate signing 2 national contracts per year for the next 5 years, this sums up to contracts with 20 countries within the next 10 years, which we estimate will be about a third of the African population, i.e., about 500 million people served in 10 years. Currently, we have close to 100,000 active users, and with our $1.6m Liberia contract, we expect to acquire at least 2 million more users within the next 2 years.
The follow-on effects of this include greater financial inclusion, improved government service delivery and revenue collection, enhanced emergency response and disaster resilience, and stronger foundations for participation in the digital economy in underserved regions and in populations previously cut off from participation.

Primary thematic focus area: Inclusive Digital Innovation Skills & Entrepreneurial Talent Development
Summary: SnooCODE provides a low-cost, offline-capable digital address system for individuals in regions without reliable or formal addressing systems. It helps bridge the location gap for services such as delivery, emergency response, and governance by allowing users to create a memorable alphanumeric address for any location, accessible offline.

Title: Bridging Youth and Communities for an Inclusive Digital Economy
Subtitle: Empowering Sri Lankan youth and MSMEs with digital skills, innovation, and cross-sector partnerships.

Solution Overview:

How it works:

1. Deliver digital literacy and entrepreneurship programs for youth and MSMEs through workshops, mentoring, and online platforms.
2. Connect Sri Lankan youth with international volunteers and experts via AIESEC’s global network (120+ countries).
3. Facilitate public-private partnerships with corporates, universities, and government bodies to co-create sustainable training modules.
4. Establish a digital hub model to provide access to tools, mentorship, and networks.

Methodologies & Technologies:

1. Blended learning approach (in-person + virtual).
2. E-learning platforms, cloud-based collaboration tools, and AI-enabled career readiness modules.
3. Data-driven monitoring to assess impact (tracking employment, MSME growth, and gender inclusion).

Partnership Models:

1. Government institutions for policy alignment.
2. Corporates for technical expertise and funding.
3. Universities for research and curriculum support.
4. NGOs and UN agencies for scaling impact.
Solution Provider(s): AIESEC in Sri Lanka – Youth leadership and project execution (non-profit, youth development sector), Universities – Academic expertise and training support (higher education sector), Government ministries and organizations– Policy alignment and digital strategy.  Private sector partners (e.g., Dialog Axiata, MAS Holdings, Microsoft Sri Lanka) – Corporate expertise, digital tools, and funding.  International AIESEC Network – Global exchange of volunteers, trainers, and best practices.

Desired impact:
Objectives: Build inclusive digital ecosystems by empowering youth and MSMEs with 21st-century skills.

Key Achievements:

1. Train 10,000+ youth in digital and entrepreneurial skills by 2026.
2. Enable 1,000+ MSMEs to adopt digital business models.
3. Reduce gender gap in digital access by engaging 50% female participants.
4. Create sustainable employability pathways through local + international mentorship.
Key technologies:
1. AI-powered career readiness tools.
2. Cloud-based collaboration (Microsoft Teams, Google Workspace).
3. Data dashboards for impact monitoring.
4. E-learning platforms

1. Youth-to-youth training model leveraging AIESEC’s global network.

Title: DigAccess Uganda
Subtitle: Transforming Lives Through Tech for an inclusive digital economy.
Problem Statement: In a world rapidly transforming into digital technology and AI, underserved Population like rural areas and refugee settlements in Uganda risk being left behind due to limited digital skills, poor connectivity, and lack of accessible learning platforms. DigAccess bridges this gap by empowering local digital champions with tools, training, and resources to deliver inclusive, AI-ready digital literacy, ensuring no one is excluded from the opportunities of the evolving digital economy.
Solution Overview:
DigAccess addresses the digital exclusion faced by millions in Uganda’s rural communities and refugee settlements, where limited infrastructure, poor internet access, low digital literacy, and language barriers leave youth and adults unprepared for a rapidly digitizing economy.
Our solution combines a mobile app with offline access, localized content in native languages, solar-powered learning hubs, and community-based Digital Champions trained to deliver hands-on digital and AI skills. This model is innovative because it adapts to the realities of underserved populations, is scalable across diverse contexts, and culturally sensitive, ensuring learning is accessible, relevant, and impactful.
DigAccess is already well-elaborated, with a clear roadmap, mentorship from partners like Refractory Academy, and a growing team.
Solution Provider(s): The DigAccess project is led by DigAccess, a social enterprise focused on digital inclusion and AI literacy in underserved communities. We collaborate closely with Refractory Academy, a leading digital skills training academy in Uganda that provides mentorship and trains our Digital Champions. Additionally, we partner with local community-based organizations (CBOs) to support community mobilization and training delivery.
Duration to pilot in a new geography: 3 months
SDGs addressed: SDG 5 (Gender Equality);SDG 13 (Climate Action);SDG 4 (Quality Education);
Desired impact:
DigAccess aims to close the digital divide in rural and underserved communities by providing accessible, localised, and inclusive digital and AI skills training. The solution seeks to;

Equip youth and adults with job-ready digital skills for the future workforce.

Create sustainable local ecosystems through trained Community Digital Champions.

Foster economic empowerment by enabling participation in the inclusive digital economy.

Key Achievements (Target & Projected):

Skills Development, Train at least 1,000 individuals in the first year, with a focus on women, youth, and marginalised groups.

Employment Generation; Create over 100 direct jobs for trainers and support staff, and empower trained individuals to access remote work opportunities.

Sustainability & Access; Deploy 10 solar-powered learning hubs to ensure continuous access to digital training even in off-grid areas.

Community Empowerment; Increase digital literacy rates in targeted communities by at least 40% within 12 months.

Bridging Gender Gaps; Achieve a minimum of 60% female participation in training programs.
Key technologies: DigAccess leverages a mobile application with offline capability, localised e-learning content, and solar-powered digital hubs to deliver inclusive training in underserved areas. The solution integrates AI-powered learning tools for personalised education, a cloud-based content management system for centralised updates, and secure data analytics to track progress and impact.
Unique Characteristics: DigAccess stands out for its first more localised approach, combining offline mobile learning, solar-powered hubs, and community-based digital champions to overcome infrastructure, literacy, and language barriers. Its innovation lies in integrating AI powered adaptive learning with culturally relevant content in local languages, ensuring accessibility even without internet connectivity. The model blends technology with a sustainable community-led delivery system, making it adaptable, scalable, and cost-effective while directly addressing the realities of underserved populations.
Sustainable Change: DigAccess contributes to sustainable, systemic change by building long-term digital capacity at the community level rather than offering short-term interventions. By training local digital champions and equipping solar-powered hubs, the solution ensures continuous knowledge transfer, ownership, and sustainability. Over time, this will create a digitally literate generation prepared for AI-driven economies, improve youth employability, and empower communities to access opportunities in education, health, and entrepreneurship. The follow on effects include reduced digital inequality, stronger community resilience, and the establishment of a scalable model that can be replicated across East Africa, fostering inclusive participation in the global digital economy.
Funding Sources: The solution has been self funded and also received a grant of 2000 us dollars for doing the research and pilot study of the project.
Testimonials and Endorsements: Not applicable since we have not started the operation of this project.
Further comments/feedback: We would be glad if you supported DigAccess, funding DigAccess is not only promoting digital inclusion but supporting future youth employment, women empowerment and giving hope to the resettled refugees in Uganda.
Primary thematic focus area: Inclusive Digital Innovation Skills & Entrepreneurial Talent Development
Summary: DigAccess Uganda provides a solution to close the digital divide in rural and underserved communities by offering AI and digital literacy training through mobile apps, offline content, and solar-powered hubs. This initiative ensures equitable access to digital skills, fostering economic empowerment and preparing communities for future workforce opportunities.

Title: DPI for Authorship: Programmable Consent for Cultural and Creative IP
Subtitle: A digital public infrastructure that empowers creators, estates, and communities to govern, license, and earn from cultural IP—closing the digital economy divide.
Problem Statement: Billions in cultural and creative value are excluded from the digital economy. Current IP systems are fragmented, inequitable, and blind to sovereign rights, leaving creators and communities underpaid and unprotected. The result is lost income, weakened cultural heritage, and unchecked AI exploitation. Our solution closes this gap by providing sovereign-compliant infrastructure for consent, licensing, and equitable digital participation.
Solution Overview:
Our solution is a sovereign-compliant Digital Public Infrastructure (DPI) for cultural and creative intellectual property (IP). It functions like an authorship “operating system” that enables creators, estates, Indigenous councils, and institutions to register, govern, license, and earn from their IP across borders and platforms.

How It Works

Registration & Verification — Creators and institutions anchor works in the DPI using sovereign credentials (e.g., estates, tribal councils, academic archives). Zero-knowledge proofs ensure privacy while confirming authenticity.

Programmable Consent & Licensing — Dynamic contracts generate terms based on jurisdiction, treaties, and community protocols. Creators can opt in/out of AI training or cross-border use.

Fallback & Risk Protection — If conflicts arise (e.g., treaty overrides, AI misuse), a fallback system pauses licenses, triggers arbitration, or reroutes royalties.

Royalty Routing & Financialization — Payments flow automatically to verified beneficiaries and can be tokenized for insurance, lending, or ESG-aligned impact.

Methodologies & Technologies

- Digital Public Infrastructure design (inspired by Aadhaar, UPI, GovStack standards).
- Blockchain + Zero-Knowledge Proofs for auditability without exposing cultural metadata.
- API Integration Layer connecting to museums, marketplaces, IP offices, and financial platforms.
- Risk modeling + programmable royalty logic to support underwriting and financial inclusion.
- AI Traceability Registry linking training datasets back to source IP.
- Partnerships & Collaboration Models
- Cultural estates & communities: First deployments with iconic author/musician estates and Indigenous councils.
- Universities & HBCUs: Innovation labs at Miles College and Southern University Law Center test governance and policy models.

Financial partners: Early engagement with banks and insurers to co-design IP-backed credit and risk products.

Multilateral DPI networks: Alignment with UNDP + GovStack to ensure interoperability with global public infrastructure standards.
Solution Provider(s): AXM Technologies Corp. — Infrastructure technology company building sovereign-compliant Digital Public Infrastructure (DPI) for cultural and creative IP governance, licensing, and financialization. Sector: Digital Infrastructure / Intellectual Property.  Five Fifths Inc. — Parent IP holding company ensuring authorship sovereignty and long-term stewardship of cultural assets. Sector: Higher Education / Innovation.  Southern University Law Center (AXM x SULC Policy Fellowship) — Civil rights law institution testing governance and policy frameworks for DPI. Sector: Legal / Policy Infrastructure.  Estate Partners (Confidential) — Leading cultural estates in literature, music, and civil rights history serving as pilot clients to validate authorship governance and licensing protocols. Sector: Arts / Heritage / Media.
Implementation timeline(s): 2024 — Provisional patents filed and system architecture developed.  Early 2025 — MVP launched with support for cultural IP registration, licensing, and consent.  Mid 2025 — Innovation Lab established at Miles College; first policy fellowship launched at Southern University Law Center.  2025–2026 — Pilot deployments underway with leading cultural estates and Indigenous councils.
Duration to pilot in a new geography: 6-12 months
SDGs addressed: SDG 9 (Industry, Innovation, and Infrastructure);SDG 16 (Peace, Justice, and Strong Institutions);SDG 10 (Reduced Inequalities);
Desired impact:
Close the digital economy gap for creators, Indigenous nations, and cultural estates by providing sovereign-compliant IP infrastructure.

- Ensure fair licensing, authorship recognition, and royalty flows across borders and digital platforms.
- Establish cultural IP as a recognized, insurable, and bankable asset class for inclusive economic growth.

Key Achievements / Impacts

Economic inclusion: First pilots with HBCUs and cultural estates in 2025 enabled students and communities to register and license 50+ works of cultural IP.

Employment & skills: Fellowship programs at Miles College and Southern University Law Center are training the next generation of digital IP and policy leaders.

Financial empowerment: Pilot clients are testing royalty routing and tokenization models, unlocking new pathways for lending, insurance, and intergenerational wealth transfer.

Governance innovation: AXM has encoded treaty-aware, sovereign-compliant licensing and AI consent into infrastructure—creating a model for scalable, global policy enforcement.

Long-term target: By 2030, AXM aims to bring $10B+ in underutilized cultural IP into the inclusive digital economy, directly benefiting creators, MSMEs, and communities worldwide.
Key technologies:
Blockchain & Zero-Knowledge Proofs (ZKPs): Provide tamper-proof registration, auditability, and privacy-preserving compliance without exposing sensitive cultural metadata.

Smart Contracts & Programmable Licensing Engines: Dynamically generate treaty- and jurisdiction-aware licensing terms and enforce programmable consent (including AI training opt-in/out).

AI Traceability & Model Fingerprinting: Anchors training datasets to cultural IP sources, ensuring accountability and consent in generative AI systems.

API Integration Layer: Connects cultural institutions, IP offices, marketplaces, and financial platforms for cross-border interoperability.

Risk Modeling & Tokenization: Enables royalty routing, insurance underwriting, and the creation of financial instruments backed by cultural IP.

Decentralized & Sovereign-Controlled Storage (e.g., IPFS, Filecoin): Ensures cultural preservation and resilience across jurisdictions.
Unique Characteristics:
Sovereign-Compliant Design: First digital public infrastructure built to respect sovereign, Indigenous, and estate governance, embedding treaty- and jurisdiction-aware logic directly into licensing workflows.

Programmable Consent: Unlike Creative Commons or legacy registries, AXM enforces opt-in/opt-out rights for AI training, remix, and cross-border use through programmable contracts.

Fallback Arbitration Mechanism: Automated “safety net” that pauses or recalibrates licenses when legal conflicts, treaty overrides, or misuse occur—ensuring resilience where current IP systems collapse.

Financialization of Cultural IP: Transforms royalties and rights into bankable, insurable assets, enabling credit, insurance, and ESG-linked financing for communities and creators.

Hybrid Governance Model: Combines community multisig consent (councils, heirs, institutions) with automated compliance engines—bridging human sovereignty and machine enforcement.

Partnership Model: Anchored in universities, law centers, and cultural estates as pilots, ensuring legitimacy, inclusivity, and pathways for scaling globally.
Sustainable Change:
Sustainable, Systemic Change

Our solution transforms cultural and creative IP from a fragmented, underutilized resource into a recognized asset class within the digital economy. By embedding sovereignty, consent, and compliance directly into infrastructure, AXM ensures that creators, Indigenous nations, and estates are not just participants but rule-setters in the digital era.

Theory of Change

Input: Deploy sovereign-compliant DPI for cultural IP (registration, consent, licensing, and royalty routing).

Immediate Outcomes:
- Secure authorship recognition and programmable consent for creators.
- Equitable licensing and royalty flows to communities and MSMEs.
- Training and employment via university innovation labs and fellowships.

Intermediate Outcomes:

- AI and digital platforms are held accountable to enforce consent and attribution.
- Policy innovation spreads through DPI standards aligned with UN frameworks (e.g., UNDRIP, WIPO, GovStack).

Long-Term Impact:
- A global cultural IP economy where billions in currently excluded value flow into sustainable livelihoods, heritage preservation, and intergenerational wealth.
- Shift from extractive models of culture and data toward sovereign, inclusive digital economies.
