Title: Zuasoko-A Digital Bridge to Inclusive Agricultural Markets and Rural Prosperity
Subtitle: Empowering smallholder farmers with digital tools to access fair markets, boost incomes, and drive inclusive growth in rural food systems.
Problem Statement: Smallholder farmers in rural areas face limited market access, price exploitation, and post-harvest losses due to fragmented supply chains and lack of real-time market information. These challenges are worsened by digital exclusion, poor infrastructure, and minimal bargaining power, leaving farmers trapped in low-income cycles.
Solution Overview:
Solution Overview

Zuasoko is a tech-enabled, market aggregation platform that connects smallholder farmers directly to consumers, retailers, and agro-processors through a hybrid model of digital tools and physical market hubs. It bridges the gap between farm and market, ensuring fair prices, reduced post-harvest losses, and inclusive participation in the digital economy.

How the Solution Works:

Farmers register via a mobile-first application or through local agents embedded in rural communities.

Aggregation centers (Zuasoko Hubs) serve as physical collection points for cereals and fresh produce, enabling quality checks and bulking.

Buyers access available stock via the app or dashboard, order directly, and track deliveries from farm to store.

The platform shares real-time price updates, weather alerts, and best farming practices to increase productivity and income predictability.

Technologies & Methodologies:

Mobile-based platform (USSD and smartphone) tailored for low-tech users in rural settings.

AI-driven price prediction and market intelligence engine that advises farmers on when and where to sell.

Digital inventory and traceability tools to track produce from farm gate to market.

Behavioral nudges and SMS alerts for weather events, price shifts, and productivity tips.

Use of QR codes and farmer IDs for transparency, accountability, and financial profiling.

Partnerships & Collaboration Models:

Cooperative model: Zuasoko works with farmer groups and SACCOs to onboard and organize producers.

Local logistics providers: Partnering with boda-boda riders and rural transporters for first-mile and last-mile delivery.

Financial service providers: To facilitate digital payments, credit scoring, and future integration of micro-insurance and buy-now-pay-later models.

County governments and NGOs: For farmer mobilization, extension services, and alignment with rural development programs.
Solution Provider(s): Canopy of Hope Initiative – Community-based partner focused on rural empowerment through sustainable agriculture, cooperative development, and digital inclusion (Non-profit, Community Development).  Kingdom Bank – Financial institution providing tailored agri-financing and digital payment solutions to enhance farmer and aggregator liquidity (Banking, FinTech).  Mazao Plus Limited – Input supply and extension services provider supporting farmers with seeds, fertilizers, and agronomic advisory (Agri-inputs, Advisory Services).  Carrefour – Large retail partner offering formal market access and off-take agreements for quality-assured produce from farmers (Retail, FMCG).  Just In Time – Logistics and distribution partner supporting timely transportation of goods from aggregation points to retailers and consumers (Logistics, Distribution).  Wasoko – E-commerce and supply chain partner providing access to demand-side markets and enabling digital trade among last-mile retailers (E-commerce, Digital Trade).
Implementation location(s): Kenya, in Nairobi and impacting farmers across central kenya and western and rift-Piloting the MVP
Implementation timeline(s): Pilot phase launched in March 2025 and is ongoing. The solution has been implemented in select counties in Kenya with progressive onboarding of farmers, retailers, and partners. Full-scale rollout is planned for Q4 2025.
Duration to pilot in a new geography: 6 to 9 months - including 2 months for stakeholder engagement and onboarding, 3 months for infrastructure setup and farmer/retailer training, and 1-4 months for testing, feedback, and iteration before scaling.
SDGs addressed: SDG 2 (Zero Hunger);SDG 12 (Responsible Consumption and Production);SDG 13 (Climate Action);
Desired impact:
Desired Impact of the Solution

Solution Objectives:
Zuasoko seeks to transform rural agricultural economies by creating a seamless digital marketplace that links smallholder farmers directly to retailers and end consumers. The key objectives are:

To enhance market access and pricing transparency for over 10,000 smallholder farmers within the first year.

To reduce post-harvest losses by at least 30% through demand-driven aggregation and smart distribution.

To increase farmers’ incomes by 40-60% by minimizing middlemen and ensuring fair trade.

Key Achievements/Impacts (Expected & Ongoing):

Employment Generation: Create 500+ new jobs for youth and women as local agents, logistics coordinators, shop attendants, and tech support personnel.

Increased Market Efficiency: Digitized transactions and demand forecasting reduce wastage and enable accurate production planning.

GHG Reductions: By optimizing aggregation and reducing unnecessary trips, the model is projected to cut carbon emissions by 20% in our pilot zones.

Economic Inclusion: Enable access to digital financial services, credit scoring, and micro-financing for farmers previously excluded from formal markets.

Zuasoko aims to build long-term rural prosperity by using inclusive technology and community-driven engagement to drive systemic change in agricultural value chains.
Key technologies:
Key Technologies Used for the Zuasoko Solution

Mobile and Web Applications

Farmer App (Android-based): Used by farmers to register, post produce, access market prices, schedule aggregation, and request services.

Shopkeeper & Retail App: Enables small retailers to order products, track deliveries, and manage inventory.

Admin Dashboard: Provides real-time insights, inventory tracking, farmer data, and logistics coordination.

Artificial Intelligence (AI)

Predictive Analytics: For demand forecasting, crop planning, and pricing optimization.

Smart Matching: AI-powered algorithms match farmer produce with real-time demand from retailers and end buyers.

Internet of Things (IoT) (planned for scale-up)

Used for cold chain monitoring, especially for perishable produce. Smart sensors in solar-powered fridges help maintain quality and reduce spoilage.

USSD & SMS Gateway

Inclusive access for farmers in remote areas with feature phones, enabling registration, order placement, and updates without internet.

Cloud-Based Infrastructure

Built on scalable cloud architecture to ensure accessibility, security, and seamless updates across devices and geographies.

GIS & Geo-Tagging

For tracking produce origin, monitoring aggregation routes, and enhancing transparency across the supply chain.

Digital Payments & Wallet Integration

Enables secure, traceable payments for farmers and retailers using mobile money platforms like M-Pesa.

Blockchain (Exploratory Phase)

Being explored for produce traceability, contract enforcement, and transparent payment verification across the value chain.

These technologies work together to ensure that Zuasoko delivers a resilient, scalable, and farmer-centric digital marketplace solution.
Unique Characteristics:
Unique/Differentiated Characteristics of the Zuasoko Solution

Farmers-to-Families Model
Zuasoko follows a direct-from-farmer to household and retail model, eliminating multiple layers of brokers and intermediaries. This ensures farmers get better margins while consumers enjoy affordable, fresh produce.

Integrated Market Aggregation + Last-Mile Retail
Unlike typical platforms that focus only on aggregation or e-commerce, Zuasoko uniquely integrates:

Farmer aggregation via app/USSD

Micro-warehouse hubs (shops)

Retail deliveries to households and retailers

Digital Inclusion with Hybrid Access Channels

App + USSD + Agent model ensures both smartphone and feature phone users (even in low-literacy areas) can fully participate.

Physical convenience shops double up as last-mile digital and market access points.

Decentralized Cold Chain Integration (in-progress)
Zuasoko is working with partners (e.g., Keep IT Cool) to solarize rural hubs with modular cold storage for fresh produce, reducing post-harvest losses and unlocking value in perishables.

Flexible Farmer Financing (via Partners)
Through partnerships with Kingdom Bank, Mazao Plus Ltd, and others, Zuasoko enables:

Input credit for farmers based on verified produce and transaction history

Buy-now-pay-later options for retailers and mini-shops

Real-Time Data for Market Intelligence
Continuous data from both the supply (farmers) and demand (retailers/households) sides allows dynamic pricing, demand forecasting, and better inventory planning, powered by AI.

Lean Franchise Shop Model for Scale
Zuasoko's physical presence is scaled through low-cost branded outlets run by local youth and women, creating jobs while embedding trust and presence at the grassroots.

Social and Environmental Impact Embedded in the Model

Reduces post-harvest losses (up to 30%) through better planning and storage.

Enhances women and youth employment via shop and logistics franchising.

Lowers GHG emissions by streamlining logistics and reducing wastage.

Multi-Stakeholder Ecosystem Partnerships
Zuasoko operates as a platform enabler, leveraging:

Logistics (Just in Time, Wasoko)

Retail (Carrefour, local dukas)

Finance (Kingdom Bank, Mazao Plus)

Development actors (Canopy of Hope)
This ecosystem approach increases impact, sustainability, and scale potential.

These combined elements make Zuasoko a differentiated, inclusive, and impact-driven digital solution reshaping how smallholder produce reaches the market across Kenya and beyond.
Sustainable Change:
Zuasoko contributes to sustainable, systemic change by transforming how rural farmers, retailers, and consumers interact within the agricultural value chain. At the heart of our Theory of Change is the belief that inclusive market access, digital transparency, and decentralized distribution systems can drive rural prosperity and food system resilience.

Our platform tackles long-standing inefficiencies in post-harvest handling, market access, and price fairness by aggregating supply directly from smallholder farmers and redistributing through neighborhood cereal shops and digital channels. This reduces post-harvest losses, improves price realization for farmers, and enhances food availability for urban and peri-urban consumers.

The expected follow-on effects include:

Economic empowerment of smallholder farmers through higher margins and predictable offtake,

Job creation at different levels of the supply chain-collection agents, retail operators, delivery personnel, etc.,

Increased digitization and data visibility in rural trade, leading to more tailored financial products (e.g., inventory credit, PAYG input financing),

Replicable community micro-hub model that can be scaled across multiple counties, adapting to local crop and consumption contexts.

Over time, Zuasoko fosters a network of trust-based transactions, financial inclusion, and integrated food supply systems-leading to a rural economy that is not just digitally connected, but also economically and socially resilient.
Funding Sources: Zuasoko has been primarily self-funded by the co-founders, with initial capital contributions supporting the development of the app prototype, registration of the physical Zua-Hubs, and early-stage operational activities such as sourcing, logistics, and testing aggregation models.
Testimonials and Endorsements: https://ramaimpact.com/pre-loan-track-ventures/
Further comments/feedback: Thank you for the opportunity to share insights about our solution. The questionnaire is well-structured and thought-provoking, prompting deep reflection on our model, impact, and scalability. One suggestion would be to consider allowing applicants to upload brief supporting documents or visuals (e.g., one-pagers or diagrams) to better illustrate the solution’s ecosystem and theory of change. Otherwise, the format is clear and effective. We appreciate your commitment to supporting impactful, sustainable innovations.
Primary thematic focus area: MSME Empowerment & Local Digital Innovation
Summary: Zuasoko is a platform aiming to improve market access for smallholder farmers in Kenya, reducing post-harvest losses and boosting incomes through digital tools. The solution effectively integrates digital and physical infrastructure but could benefit from clearer scalability plans.

Title: OurLife Support Initiative: Economic Empowerment and Digital Mobilisation for Coastal Communities in Bangladesh
Subtitle: Empowering climate-affected coastal communities in Bangladesh through inclusive funding, digital tracking, and youth-led enterprise for resilient, data-driven recovery.
Problem Statement: Coastal communities in Bangladesh face compounded crises—livelihood loss from cyclones, tiger attacks, and forced migration; exclusion from formal recovery systems; and lack of digital tools to track and influence inclusive economic policies. Women, youth, persons with disabilities, and informal MSMEs remain especially vulnerable, with limited access to funding, safeguarding, and market opportunities. The absence of localized data further hinders responsive governance and global visibility.
Solution Overview:
Solution Overview
The OurLife Support Initiative is a multi-pronged solution designed to restore livelihoods, promote inclusion, and digitally mobilise climate-affected coastal communities in Bangladesh. It combines direct economic support, safeguarding systems, and a community-driven digital platform—OurLife Tracker—to ensure transparent recovery and policy influence.
How the Solution Works
Economic Restoration
Direct grants and materials (farming kits, tailoring tools, livestock) are distributed to over 500 households.
MSMEs receive market linkage support and supply chain facilitation.
Community savings groups and micro-finance networks are activated for long-term resilience.
Safeguarding & Inclusion
A CHS-compliant safeguarding framework is deployed, with gender-sensitive training and referral systems.
Psychosocial support networks and community feedback loops ensure protection and trust.
Digital Mobilisation via OurLife Tracker
A multilingual, geo-tagged mobile app enables households and facilitators to report livelihood progress, safeguarding needs, and feedback.
Offline sync ensures functionality in low-connectivity areas.
Community dashboards visualise data for local decision-making and policy engagement.
Capacity Building & Governance
Youth and women are trained as digital facilitators and safeguarding champions.
Participatory planning with local government and CSOs ensures ownership and alignment.
Toolkits and workshops support replication and knowledge sharing.
Policy Engagement & Global Visibility
Community-generated data informs inclusive digital policy briefs.
Insights contribute to the Global Digital Compact Objective 2.
The initiative is showcased at the UN General Assembly and UNIDO Global Industry Summit.
Methodologies & Technologies Used
Human-Centred Design: Co-created with community members to ensure relevance and usability.
Geo-tagged Data Collection: Tracks economic recovery and safeguarding needs in real time.
Multilingual Interface: Supports Bangla, English, and indigenous dialects.
Offline Functionality: Ensures access in remote, low-bandwidth areas.
Secure Data Protocols: Ethical storage and anonymised reporting to protect vulnerable users.
CHS-Compliant Safeguarding: Aligns with Core Humanitarian Standards for protection and inclusion.
Solution Provider(s): Lead Organisation:  ARA (Action for Rural Advancement) – A legally registered, award-winning nonprofit founded in 1996 in Satkhira, Bangladesh. ARA leads the OurLife Support Initiative, overseeing strategic design, implementation, safeguarding, and policy engagement. With deep expertise in climate resilience, gender equity, CHS-compliant frameworks, and digital inclusion, ARA coordinates all partners, ensures accountability, and drives long-term impact across coastal districts.  Sector: Humanitarian development, climate adaptation, safeguarding, digital inclusion Supporting Partners:  ST Automobiles – A Satkhira-based enterprise contributing infrastructure, logistics, and vocational training support. Under ARA’s leadership, ST facilitates youth engagement, renewable energy integration, and outreach mobilisation.  Sector: Vocational training, mobility, renewable energy Shonjibon Consortium – Provides strategic guidance on digital integration and sustainability. Works under ARA’s coordination to align the initiative with national digital transformation goals.  Sector: Digital governance, disaster resilience TechSpring Solutions Ltd. – Develops and maintains the OurLife Tracker app. Operates under ARA’s supervision to ensure ethical data systems, multilingual access, and offline functionality.  Sector: Digital technology, data ethics YouthNet for Climate Justice – Engages youth facilitators and supports safeguarding outreach. Works in partnership with ARA to mobilize climate-affected youth and promote digital literacy.  Sector: Youth empowerment, climate justice Local Government Institutions (LGIs) – Union Parishads and Upazila administrations that collaborate with ARA on participatory planning, data validation, and policy uptake.  Sector: Local governance, disaster response CSO Alliance for Inclusive Recovery – A coalition of community-based organizations co-implementing training and safeguarding activities under ARA’s coordination.  Sector: Civil society, inclusion, community development
Duration to pilot in a new geography: The implementation of the OurLife Support Initiative is projected to span approximately 24 months. The first three months will focus on mobilization and setup, including stakeholder engagement, baseline surveys, and the establishment of safeguarding frameworks. From months four to eight, the initiative will concentrate on capacity building—training youth and women, onboarding MSMEs, and deploying digital literacy programs alongside the OurLife Tracker app. Economic activation will take place between months nine and fourteen, involving grant distribution, livelihood restoration, and market linkage support. Monitoring and feedback mechanisms will be strengthened during months fifteen to eighteen through geo-tagged reporting, safeguarding referrals, and the rollout of a community dashboard. Policy engagement will follow in months nineteen to twenty-one, with data analysis, policy brief development, and national/international showcases. Finally, the last three months will be dedicated to evaluation and replication, including final assessments, the creation of a replication toolkit, and the open-source release of the OurLife Tracker. This phased approach ensures ethical implementation, measurable impact, and readiness for scale.
SDGs addressed: SDG 1 (No Poverty);SDG 8 (Decent Work and Economic Growth);SDG 13 (Climate Action);
Desired impact:
Solution Objectives
Restore livelihoods for at least 5,000 climate-affected individuals through targeted grants and vocational training.
Empower MSMEs and informal workers with digital tools, market access, and financial literacy.
Strengthen safeguarding and inclusion mechanisms for vulnerable groups, including women and persons with disabilities.
Generate real-time data via the OurLife Tracker to inform policy, donor engagement, and replication.
Promote climate resilience through adaptive livelihood strategies and geo-tagged monitoring.
 Key Achievements / Quantifiable Impacts
Employment generation: Over 5,000 individuals re-engaged in income-generating activities within 18 months.
MSME activation: 300+ micro and small enterprises supported with grants, training, and digital onboarding.
Digital inclusion: 10,000+ users onboarded to the OurLife Tracker for safeguarding, reporting, and market access.
Gender & disability inclusion: 60% of direct beneficiaries are women; 15% are persons with disabilities.
Climate resilience: 100% of supported livelihoods are designed with climate-adaptive strategies (e.g., solar, eco-tourism, disaster-proof trades).
Policy impact: 3 national briefs and 1 international showcase generated from geo-tagged data and community dashboards.
Key technologies:
Mobile-Based Geo-Tagging & Reporting
A custom-built OurLife Tracker app enables real-time geo-tagged reporting of livelihood activities, safeguarding referrals, and market access.
Designed for low-bandwidth environments and compatible with basic smartphones.
 Cloud-Hosted Community Dashboard
Aggregates field data into a visual dashboard for donors, policymakers, and community leaders.
Enables transparent tracking of grants, training outcomes, and safeguarding cases.
AI-Driven Data Insights
Uses basic AI models to analyze trends in employment, vulnerability, and service uptake.
Supports predictive planning and policy briefs based on anonymized community data.
 Digital Safeguarding & Consent Protocols
Built-in consent capture, referral tracking, and safeguarding alerts ensure ethical data use and protection of vulnerable groups.
Unique Characteristics:
Unique & Differentiated Characteristics
1. Integrated Livelihood + Safeguarding Model
Combines economic recovery with real-time safeguarding—ensuring that vulnerable groups (women, youth, persons with disabilities) are not just economically active but also protected and heard.
Geo-tagged referrals and consent-based reporting make inclusion measurable.
2. Phased Partnership & Financing Mechanism
Uses a trial-to-scale model with donors and CSR partners—starting with pilot groups, then expanding based on verified impact.
All equipment and infrastructure costs are captured up front in Year 1, ensuring transparency and donor confidence.
3. Locally Adapted Digital Tools
The OurLife Tracker is designed for low-bandwidth, multilingual use, and includes features for market access, safeguarding, and grant tracking.
Data feeds into a community dashboard that empowers local leaders and informs national policy.
4. Replicable & Open-Source Architecture
The solution is built to be replicated across other climate-affected regions, with open-source tools, templates, and training guides in Bangla and English.
Includes a replication toolkit for government, NGOs, and private sector partners.
 5. Cultural Legacy Integration
Livelihoods are designed to preserve and adapt traditional trades—such as boat-making, weaving, and drama—into modern economic models.
This ensures not just income, but identity and dignity.
Sustainable Change:
The OurLife Support Initiative is designed to catalyse sustainable, systemic change by embedding inclusive economic recovery, digital accountability, and community-driven resilience into the very fabric of climate-affected regions. Its Theory of Change rests on the principle that when vulnerable communities are equipped with adaptive livelihoods, safeguarding mechanisms, and transparent tools, they not only recover but transform into agents of long-term development and policy influence.
Theory of Change: Pathway to Systemic Impact
Inputs
Targeted grants, vocational training, and MSME support
OurLife Tracker app and geo-tagged dashboard
Safeguarding protocols and consent-based reporting
Cultural livelihood integration and community engagement
 Activities
Onboarding 5,000+ individuals into climate-adaptive livelihoods
Deploying digital tools for real-time reporting and safeguarding
Facilitating market access and financial literacy
Generating community data for policy briefs and replication
 Outputs
Increased income and employment among vulnerable groups
Transparent tracking of grants, referrals, and outcomes
Strengthened local leadership and digital inclusion
Documented best practices and scalable models
Outcomes
Resilient local economies with reduced climate vulnerability
Institutionalised safeguarding and inclusion practices
Data-informed policy engagement at national and international levels
Replication of the model across other climate-affected regions
Impact
A new standard for ethical, inclusive climate recovery
Communities become co-creators of development, not just recipients
Long-term trust between donors, governments, and grassroots actors
Funding Sources:
In previous instances, the OurLife Support Initiative has not received formal funding from institutional donors or corporate partners. The pilot phase was implemented through self-initiative, utilizing limited resources and local in-kind contributions—including one laptop, a basic office setup, and shared office space provided by a community partner.
This grassroots approach enabled the project to demonstrate early impact with minimal investment, emphasizing transparency, community ownership, and adaptability. Despite the absence of formal funding, the initiative successfully piloted inclusive livelihood restoration, digital reporting via the OurLife Tracker, and safeguarding mechanisms for vulnerable groups.
The success of this self-funded pilot now provides a strong foundation for engaging formal donors, CSR partners, and development agencies to scale the solution, deepen inclusion, and expand its national and regional impact.
Testimonials and Endorsements:
“We’ve been waiting for something like this—training that respects our traditions but prepares us for modern jobs.”
Local artisan, Binerpota
Further comments/feedback: While visual prototypes and conceptual diagrams significantly enhance understanding and credibility in tech-driven and infrastructure projects, current systems often lack the functionality to upload or link such visuals directly. This limitation can hinder clarity, especially when presenting complex layouts, equipment plans, or system architectures to donors and stakeholders. Integrating this capability would not only improve transparency but also strengthen donor confidence and operational readiness.
Primary thematic focus area: MSME Empowerment & Local Digital Innovation
Summary: The OurLife Support Initiative addresses climate-affected coastal communities in Bangladesh by providing economic support, safeguarding, and digital tools to promote resilience and inclusion. While the initiative is highly relevant and innovative, its scalability and sustainability beyond the pilot phase need clearer strategies.

Title: SantéConnect Sénégal – Plateforme numérique inclusive pour l’accès aux services de santé
Subtitle: Plateforme numérique inclusive pour géolocaliser les structures de santé au Sénégal, comparer les coûts des services et réserver des rendez-vous en ligne facilement.
Problem Statement: L’accès aux soins au Sénégal est limité par le manque d’informations centralisées sur les structures de santé, l’absence de transparence tarifaire et les longues files d’attente. Les populations rurales et défavorisées sont particulièrement exclues des services numériques, aggravant les inégalités d’accès aux soins.
Solution Overview:
Présentation de la solution
Description détaillée du fonctionnement
SantéConnect Sénégal est une plateforme numérique qui centralise toutes les structures de santé publiques et privées du pays. Elle permet aux utilisateurs de :

Localiser facilement les établissements via une carte interactive.

Consulter les services offerts et comparer les coûts des prestations.

Réserver en ligne leurs rendez-vous médicaux, évitant ainsi les files d’attente et améliorant la gestion des flux dans les établissements.
La plateforme est accessible via application mobile, site web et services USSD/SMS pour les populations sans accès Internet.

Méthodologies et technologies utilisées
Collecte de données auprès des établissements de santé et autorités sanitaires.

Développement agile avec tests en conditions réelles pour garantir l’adaptabilité et la facilité d’utilisation.

Technologies clés : API de géolocalisation (Google Maps/OpenStreetMap), base de données sécurisée (MySQL/PostgreSQL), applications mobiles hybrides (Flutter/React Native), intégration USSD/SMS, infrastructure cloud (AWS/Google Cloud).

Sécurité et confidentialité : conformité RGPD et normes OMS pour la protection des données personnelles et médicales.

Partenariats et modèles de collaboration
Ministère de la Santé et de l’Action Sociale : validation et mise à jour des données officielles.

Opérateurs télécoms locaux (Orange, Free, Expresso) : services USSD/SMS pour l’accès universel.

Mutuelles et assurances santé : intégration des régimes et facilitation du paiement.

Organisations internationales (ONU, OMS, PNUD) : soutien technique et financier.

Modèle de collaboration : partenariats public-privé avec abonnements pour établissements et accès gratuit ou freemium pour les utilisateurs finaux;
Solution Provider(s): SantéConnect Sénégal – Serigne Saliou Ndiaye (porteur de projet, secteur santé numérique), Moustapha Mbacké et Sidy El Moctar Dione (associées)  Ministère de la Santé et de l’Action Sociale du Sénégal (institution publique, santé publique), Orange Sénégal (opérateur télécom, technologies de communication), Mutuelle Nationale de Santé du Sénégal (MNSS) (organisme d’assurance santé, protection sociale), OpenStreetMap Sénégal (communauté open source, cartographie).  Autres partenaires : Free Sénégal, Expresso Sénégal, Google Cloud, OMS, PNUD.
Implementation location(s): La solution est actuellement mise en œuvre à l’Université Cheikh Anta Diop (UCAD) de Dakar, Sénégal, dans le cadre d’une phase pilote.
Implementation timeline(s): La mise en œuvre a débuté en janvier 2025 à l’UCAD de Dakar et la phase pilote se poursuivra jusqu’à fin 2025.
Duration to pilot in a new geography: Durée estimée pour un projet pilote dans une nouvelle géographie : 6 à 9 mois  Détails :  1 à 2 mois pour la collecte et la validation des données locales.  2 à 3 mois pour l’adaptation technique et le paramétrage de la plateforme.  1 à 2 mois pour la sensibilisation, la formation des partenaires et usagers.  1 à 2 mois pour la phase de test, ajustements et lancement officiel.
SDGs addressed: SDG 3 (Good Health and Well-being);SDG 9 (Industry, Innovation, and Infrastructure);SDG 10 (Reduced Inequalities);
Desired impact:
Impact souhaité de la solution
Objectifs de la solution
Améliorer l’accès équitable aux services de santé publics et privés sur tout le territoire sénégalais.

Réduire les files d’attente et optimiser la gestion des rendez-vous dans les établissements de santé.

Favoriser la transparence des coûts des prestations médicales pour un choix éclairé des patients.

Réduire la fracture numérique en proposant une solution accessible aux populations connectées et non connectées (via USSD/SMS).

Principales réalisations ou impacts attendus
Amélioration de l’accès aux soins pour plusieurs centaines de milliers d’usagers au Sénégal, notamment dans les zones rurales isolées.

Réduction significative des temps d’attente dans les hôpitaux grâce à la réservation en ligne, estimée à au moins 30% lors de la phase pilote.

Augmentation de la transparence tarifaire, contribuant à une meilleure compétitivité entre prestataires et à une maîtrise des dépenses de santé par les patients.

Création d’emplois directs et indirects liés au développement, à la maintenance et à la gestion de la plateforme.

Contribution à la croissance de l’économie numérique sénégalaise par la digitalisation d’un secteur-clé.
Key technologies:
Voici un aperçu clair des technologies clés utilisées pour SantéConnect Sénégal :

Géolocalisation et cartographie interactive : API Google Maps ou OpenStreetMap pour localiser les structures de santé.

Bases de données sécurisées : MySQL/PostgreSQL avec chiffrement pour stocker les informations médicales et utilisateurs.

Applications mobiles et web : développées en Flutter ou React Native pour compatibilité multi-plateforme.

Services USSD/SMS : intégration avec opérateurs télécoms pour accès sans Internet.

Système de gestion des rendez-vous : algorithmes de planification et notifications automatiques (SMS, e-mail).

Sécurité et conformité : protocoles SSL/TLS, authentification forte, respect RGPD et normes OMS.

Infrastructure cloud : hébergement scalable sur AWS, Google Cloud ou équivalents locaux.
Unique Characteristics:
Caractéristiques uniques et différenciatrices
Plateforme tout-en-un : combinaison unique de géolocalisation, transparence tarifaire et réservation en ligne accessible via mobile, web et USSD/SMS.

Inclusion numérique : accès étendu aux populations sans Internet grâce à l’intégration des services USSD/SMS, rare dans les solutions santé numériques.

Modèle de partenariat public-privé solide réunissant institutions publiques, opérateurs télécoms, mutuelles et prestataires, garantissant pérennité et large adoption.

Transparence des coûts : affichage clair des tarifs, stimulant la compétitivité et permettant aux patients de faire des choix éclairés.

Sécurité avancée : respect strict des normes internationales (RGPD, OMS) pour la protection des données médicales et personnelles.

Name of your organization: Action and Promotion of Women and Children (APROFEM)
Title: AVEC Digital – Empowering Rural Women in the Digital Economy
Subtitle: AVEC Digital empowers rural women in Cote d’Ivoire with an offline, audio-guided app to manage savings, sell products, and access training, bridging the digital gap for inclusive growth.
Problem Statement: Rural women in Marandallah face limited access to digital tools and markets due to low internet connectivity, illiteracy, and exclusion from financial services. This restricts their economic opportunities, hinders management of Village Savings and Loan Associations (AVEC), and limits access to training and broader markets. Persons with disabilities are even more marginalized, lacking tailored digital solutions. These challenges widen the digital divide and economic inequality in the region.
Solution Overview:
"AVEC Digital" is a multilingual mobile application (French and local language) designed to work both online and offline, even on basic smartphones. It enables rural women in Marandallah to digitally manage their Village Savings and Loan Associations (VSLAs) by tracking contributions, loans, and repayments. The app also includes a mini online marketplace to sell agricultural and artisanal products, opening access to larger urban markets.

Additionally, it offers multimodal training (audio, video, downloadable tutorials) on business management, improved agriculture, and digital marketing, tailored for low-literacy users. An audio-guided and visually accessible interface ensures enhanced usability for persons with disabilities.

Methodologies and technologies used:

Development of a lightweight mobile app with offline functionality using local data storage and automatic synchronization when connectivity is available.

Use of audio and video multimedia content adapted for illiterate or low-literacy users.

Accessible and ergonomic interface including features for persons with disabilities (voice guidance, high-contrast visuals, etc.).

Integration of mobile payment APIs (Orange Money, MTN MoMo) to enable secure financial transactions.

Partnerships and collaboration models:

Collaboration with local authorities and the Ministry of Women, Family, and Children to align with national inclusion policies.

Partnerships with telecom operators (Orange, MTN) to facilitate connectivity and mobile money services.

Technical and logistical support from international organizations (UNIDO, UNCTAD, UN Women) for project development, funding, and outreach.

Engagement of local women’s associations and existing VSLAs for adoption and co-creation of the solution.
Solution Provider(s): Action and Promotion of Women and Children (APROFEM) — A local NGO based in Marandallah, Côte d’Ivoire, focused on women’s economic empowerment, gender equality, and rural community development.  Ministry of Women, Family and Children (MFFE), Côte d’Ivoire — Government agency responsible for policies and programs promoting gender equality, women’s rights, and social inclusion.  Orange Côte d’Ivoire — Major telecommunications operator providing mobile connectivity and mobile money services critical for digital inclusion in rural areas or MTN Côte d’Ivoire — Leading telecom operator offering network coverage and mobile financial services supporting digital economy initiatives, United Nations Industrial Development Organization (UNIDO) — UN agency specializing in inclusive and sustainable industrial development, offering technical support and capacity building for digital solutions.  United Nations Conference on Trade and Development (UNCTAD) — UN body promoting trade and development, focusing on digital economy and innovation for inclusive growth.  UN Women — UN entity dedicated to gender equality and women’s empowerment, supporting programs to increase women’s access to digital tools and economic opportunities.
Duration to pilot in a new geography: 12 months
SDGs addressed: SDG 5 (Gender Equality);SDG 8 (Decent Work and Economic Growth);SDG 9 (Industry, Innovation, and Infrastructure);
Desired impact:
Solution Objectives:

Empower 500 rural women within 12 months by providing a user-friendly digital platform for managing AVEC and accessing markets.

Improve digital literacy with at least 80% of trained users demonstrating proficiency in key digital skills within 6 months of training.

Increase income of participating women by at least 30% through expanded sales enabled by the digital marketplace.

Ensure inclusion of at least 10 persons with disabilities with adapted features in the app, measured by active usage metrics.

Establish sustainable partnerships with at least 1 telecom providers and 2 government bodies to support scaling and affordability.

Key Achievements / Expected Impacts (within 1 year):

500 women trained and actively using the app to manage AVEC and sales.

30 AVEC groups fully digitalized, improving financial management and access to loans.

40% growth in revenue from sales outside Marandallah for participating entrepreneurs.

Enhanced social inclusion through accessible app features benefiting persons with disabilities.

Strengthened ecosystem for digital financial inclusion via strategic partnerships.
Key technologies:
Mobile Application Development: A lightweight, multilingual mobile app optimized for basic smartphones and low-connectivity environments, with offline capabilities and automatic data synchronization.

Multimedia Content Delivery: Audio and video-based training materials designed for low-literacy users, ensuring accessibility and ease of use.

Mobile Payment Integration: APIs for mobile money services (e.g., Orange Money, MTN MoMo) enabling secure, cashless transactions within the app.

Accessibility Features: Audio-guided navigation and high-contrast visual design tailored for users with disabilities.

Data Analytics (basic): Collection and analysis of user engagement and transaction data to monitor impact and improve the solution.
Unique Characteristics:
Offline-first Design: Unlike many digital solutions, AVEC Digital works fully offline with automatic syncing when internet is available, addressing connectivity challenges in rural areas.

Multilingual and Accessible Interface: Tailored for low-literacy users and persons with disabilities, combining audio guidance and simple visuals to maximize inclusion.

Integrated Financial and Marketplace Features: Combines digital management of savings groups (AVEC) with an online marketplace for agricultural and artisanal products, creating a one-stop platform.

Partnership-driven Model: Strong collaboration with telecom operators, government agencies, and local women’s groups ensures relevance, sustainability, and scalability.

Social Impact Financing Mechanism: Plans to use low transaction fees within the app to sustain operations and allow affordable access for rural users.
Sustainable Change:
The deployment of AVEC Digital initiates a transformative cycle of digital inclusion and economic empowerment for rural women and marginalized groups in Marandallah. By providing accessible digital tools for managing savings groups and accessing markets, it strengthens local financial systems and entrepreneurial capacities.

As women gain digital skills and economic independence, their increased income and social status foster broader community development and gender equality. The inclusion of persons with disabilities ensures that the benefits extend to all marginalized populations, promoting social cohesion.

Through partnerships with government agencies and telecom providers, the project influences policies and infrastructure development that support digital access in rural areas. The revenue model based on small transaction fees ensures financial sustainability and scalability.

Ultimately, the solution creates an ecosystem where digital literacy, economic growth, and social inclusion reinforce each other, leading to lasting, systemic change beyond the initial pilot.
Funding Sources:
As the solution is currently in the creation phase, APROFEM will primarily rely on funding and technical support from key partners such as the Ministry of Women, Family and Children (MFFE), telecommunications companies (Orange, MTN), and international organizations including UNIDO and UN Women.

APROFEM does not currently have the financial resources to develop and deploy the application independently. Therefore, the project will actively seek grants and partnerships to secure the necessary funding for development, pilot implementation, and scaling.
Testimonials and Endorsements:
“As the Chairwoman of APROFEM, I am deeply committed to empowering rural women through digital inclusion. The AVEC Digital solution represents a crucial step toward bridging the digital divide and unlocking economic opportunities for marginalized women in Marandallah.”
— Traole Nabindou

It would be helpful to include more examples or guidance on the expected level of detail for each section, especially for applicants in the early stages of solution development. Overall, the process is straightforward and encourages innovation and inclusivity.

Summary: AVEC Digital empowers rural women in Côte d'Ivoire with an offline, audio-guided app for managing savings, selling products, and accessing training. The platform aims to bridge the digital divide, but further details on sustainability and scaling strategies are needed.

Title: FarmVolt: IoT-Powered Solar Mini-Grids Driving Inclusive Rural Productivity.
Subtitle: Delivering clean, smart energy to off-grid farming communities through IoT-enabled solar mini-grids, boosting productivity, incomes, and digital inclusion for rural MSMEs.
Problem Statement: In Zambia, over 86% of rural communities lack reliable electricity, forcing smallholder farmers and rural MSMEs to rely on costly diesel or remain without power. This limits irrigation, agro-processing, cold storage, and access to digital services, trapping communities in low productivity and seasonal income cycles. Existing solar initiatives often focus only on household lighting, neglecting productive energy use. The result is persistent food insecurity, lost economic opportunities, and exclusion from the digital economy for farmers, youth, and women. Ecovolt addresses these challenges by integrating clean energy with agriculture and digital tools to unlock rural economic potential.
Solution Overview:
Ecovolt’s FarmVolt system delivers clean, reliable energy to off-grid farming communities through IoT-enabled solar mini-grids. Each mini-grid is modular and scalable, supplying power for irrigation, agro-processing, refrigeration, training centers, and digital hubs. Farmers access energy via smart meters and mobile money post-paid billing, with usage data tracked in real time for operational efficiency and impact monitoring.

Methodologies & Technologies
1. IoT Monitoring: Remote system management and fault detection.
2. Smart Metering: Accurate, transparent billing and consumption tracking.
3. Mobile Payment Integration: Flexible, post-harvest payment options.
4. Productive Energy Focus: Designed to power income-generating activities, not just lighting.
5. Capacity Building: Training local youth as technicians for maintenance and troubleshooting.

Partnerships & Collaboration Models
1. Agricultural Cooperatives: Facilitate farmer onboarding and payment aggregation.
2. Schools & Training Centers: Extend energy access to education and skills development.
3. Local Governments & NGOs: Co-implement rural development initiatives.
4. Private Sector Suppliers: Source quality solar hardware and IoT components.
5. Climate Finance Partners: Explore carbon credit monetization to sustain operations.
Solution Provider(s): SolarTech Zambia Ltd – Private sector supplier of high-quality solar hardware and IoT metering solutions. Sector: Renewable Energy Technology,  Green Jobs Alliance Zambia – NGO promoting youth and women employment in the green economy through skills development. Sector: Workforce Development & Sustainability.
Implementation location(s): Mwembeshi area, Chibombo District, Zambia – Operational IoT-enabled solar mini-grid serving farmers and a rural school, Mukulu, Senanga District, Zambia – Operational IoT-enabled solar mini-grid powering irrigation, agro-processing, and community training facilities.
Implementation timeline(s): Mwembeshi Site: Commissioned in June 2023 – operational to date, Mukulu Site: Commissioned in February 2024 – operational to date.
Duration to pilot in a new geography: 6–8 months – This includes 2 months for site assessment and stakeholder engagement, 3–4 months for procurement, installation, and commissioning of the solar mini-grid, and 1–2 months for community training, onboarding, and initial operational monitoring.
SDGs addressed: SDG 7 (Affordable and Clean Energy);SDG 8 (Decent Work and Economic Growth);SDG 13 (Climate Action);
Desired impact:
Solution Objectives
1. Expand access to reliable, affordable clean energy for rural MSMEs and farming communities.
2. Increase agricultural productivity through energy-enabled irrigation and processing.
3. Create local green jobs and enhance digital inclusion in off-grid areas.
4. Reduce dependence on diesel, cutting greenhouse gas emissions.

Key Achievements & Impacts (to date)
1. Energy Access: 2 solar mini-grids operational, serving 100+ farmers and 500+ students.
2. Productivity Gains: Average 100% yield increase and 75% income growth among participating farmers.
3. Employment: 6 local youth trained and employed as solar technicians.
4. Energy Savings: Displaced ~12,000 liters of diesel annually.
5. Climate Impact: Avoided ~32 tonnes CO₂ emissions per year.
6. Operational Reliability: 99% payment compliance, 0% system downtime.
Key technologies:
1. IoT (Internet of Things): Remote monitoring of mini-grid performance, automated fault detection, and real-time energy usage analytics.
2. Smart Metering Technology: Accurate, transparent billing with mobile money integration for post-paid payments.
3. Solar Photovoltaic (PV) Systems: Modular, high-efficiency panels providing renewable power for productive and household use.
4. Energy Storage Solutions: Lithium battery banks for stable, 24/7 power supply.
5. Mobile Payment Platforms: Seamless, cashless transactions aligned with farmers’ income cycles.
Unique Characteristics:
1. Agriculture-Energy Integration: Unlike typical rural solar projects focused on lighting, FarmVolt is designed to power income-generating activities such as irrigation, milling, and cold storage.
2. IoT-Enabled Operations: Real-time monitoring, predictive maintenance, and data-driven decision-making enhance reliability and efficiency.
3. Flexible Post-Harvest Payment Model: Mobile money post-paid billing aligns with seasonal farming incomes, ensuring high payment compliance.
4. Local Capacity Building: Training rural youth as certified solar technicians fosters community ownership and job creation.
5. Modular & Scalable Design: Mini-grids can be expanded based on community demand, reducing upfront risk and enabling phased growth.
6. Climate Finance Potential: Integration of carbon credit revenue to support long-term affordability and financial sustainability.
Sustainable Change:
Theory of Change
Inputs: IoT-enabled solar mini-grids, smart meters, mobile payment systems, technician training, community partnerships.
Activities: Install and operate mini-grids in off-grid farming communities; power productive uses (irrigation, processing, cold storage); train local youth; enable mobile payment billing.

Outputs:
1. Reliable, affordable energy for farmers, schools, and MSMEs.
2. Increased access to digital tools and connectivity.
3. Skilled local technicians for maintenance and repair.

Outcomes:
1. Improved agricultural productivity, year-round production, and reduced post-harvest losses.
2. Increased rural incomes and job creation.
3. Strengthened rural education and digital literacy.
4. Reduced reliance on diesel, lowering GHG emissions.

Impact:
Sustainable, community-driven clean energy ecosystems that break the cycle of rural energy poverty, empower MSMEs, and enable lasting participation in the digital economy—creating self-reinforcing economic, social, and environmental benefits across generations.
Funding Sources: The FarmVolt solution has been funded through a mix of founder equity, community contributions, and small grants from local development partners. Initial pilots in Mwembeshi and Mukulu were supported by personal investment from Ecovolt’s founder, supplemented by in-kind support from agricultural cooperatives (land access, community mobilization) and cost-sharing agreements with beneficiary groups for maintenance. Additional technical inputs and partial hardware subsidies were secured through collaborations with private sector solar suppliers and NGOs focused on rural development. This blended financing approach has ensured community ownership while demonstrating the model’s financial viability for future scale-up.
Further comments/feedback: This questionnaire is well-structured and comprehensive, allowing solution providers to clearly present both the technical and social dimensions of their innovations. One area for enhancement could be the inclusion of a specific section on impact measurement frameworks, enabling applicants to showcase how they track and verify outcomes over time. This would strengthen alignment with global SDG reporting standards and help evaluators compare solutions on evidence-based results. Overall, the format effectively captures the innovation, scalability, and inclusivity aspects critical to advancing a sustainable digital economy.
Primary thematic focus area: MSME Empowerment & Local Digital Innovation
Summary: FarmVolt provides a solar-powered solution for off-grid farming communities, integrating IoT technology for energy management and market access. The platform addresses critical energy access and productivity issues while promoting climate resilience. The solution shows strong impact potential but requires more details on long-term financial sustainability and scalability.

Title: Permacap Guinée synergie entre culture, animaux et technologie
Subtitle: Production Responsable et innovante avec une alimentation saine
Problem Statement:
En Guinée, la production agricole fait face à quatre défis majeurs : la dégradation de la fertilité des sols due à l’usage excessif d’engrais chimiques, la faible productivité causée par l’absence de pratiques durables, l’exclusion socio-économique des jeunes et des femmes rurales, et la faible intégration des nouvelles technologies dans le secteur.
Cette déconnexion technologique limite la planification agricole, le suivi sanitaire du bétail et l’optimisation des ressources, aggravant les pertes et réduisant la compétitivité des producteurs locaux.
En parallèle, les ressources organiques disponibles (déjections animales, résidus agricoles) restent sous-valorisées alors qu’elles pourraient restaurer les sols, réduire les coûts et renforcer la résilience face aux changements climatiques.
Sans solution intégrée et innovante, ces défis menacent la sécurité alimentaire, l’environnement et les perspectives économiques des communautés rurales guinéennes.
Solution Overview:
Permacap Guinée est un modèle d’agriculture biologique intégrée combinant le maraîchage et l’élevage caprin dans une relation de symbiose : les déjections caprines sont transformées en compost naturel pour fertiliser les cultures, tandis que les résidus de récolte servent d’alimentation au bétail. Ce cycle vertueux permet de restaurer la fertilité des sols, d’augmenter les rendements et de réduire la dépendance aux intrants chimiques. Le projet intègre également un système numérique de suivi intelligent (“bouclier connecté”) pour la santé animale et la planification agricole, permettant aux agriculteurs d’optimiser leurs pratiques.

Méthodologies et technologies
	•	Agriculture régénérative : pratiques de permaculture, rotation des cultures, utilisation de compost organique.
	•	Élevage durable : alimentation à base de résidus agricoles, gestion sanitaire préventive.
	•	Technologie IoT (Internet des Objets) : capteurs pour le suivi de la température, du rythme cardiaque et des mouvements des caprins, ainsi que pour la météo et le calendrier cultural.
	•	Formation et transfert de compétences : sessions pratiques pour les femmes et jeunes agriculteurs sur la gestion intégrée cultures-élevage et l’utilisation des outils numériques.

Partenariats et modèles de collaboration
	•	Partenariats techniques : collaboration avec des ingénieurs agronomes, vétérinaires et développeurs pour optimiser la solution.
	•	Partenariats communautaires : implication des coopératives locales et groupements de femmes dans la production et la gestion.
	•	Modèle de collaboration : approche participative où les bénéficiaires sont co-créateurs et gestionnaires de la solution, avec un partage des revenus et une réinjection des bénéfices dans la communauté pour assurer la pérennité du projet.
Solution Provider(s): Permacap Guinée – initiative locale d’agriculture biologique intégrée et élevage durable, Ministère de l’Agriculture et de l’Élevage de Guinée – appui technique et réglementaire, Institut de Recherche Agronomique de Guinée (IRAG) – recherche et innovation agricole, Université Gamal Abdel Nasser de Conakry – formation et accompagnement technique, partenaires technologiques IoT – développement du bouclier connecté, coopératives agricoles et groupements de femmes – mise en œuvre communautaire.
Duration to pilot in a new geography: La mise en œuvre complète de la solution dans une nouvelle zone géographique nécessite environ 6 à 9 mois : 	•	1 à 2 mois : études préliminaires, mobilisation communautaire et partenariats locaux. 	•	2 à 3 mois : installation des infrastructures agricoles et d’élevage, acquisition d’équipements, mise en place du système IoT. 	•	2 à 4 mois : formation des bénéficiaires, lancement de la production intégrée cultures-élevage et suivi technique.  Cette durée permet d’assurer un déploiement efficace, une appropriation par les communautés et une pérennité du modèle.
SDGs addressed: SDG 1 (No Poverty);SDG 2 (Zero Hunger);SDG 13 (Climate Action);
Desired impact:
•	Restaurer la fertilité des sols grâce à l’utilisation d’engrais organiques issus des déjections caprines.
	•	Réduire la dépendance aux intrants chimiques et améliorer la résilience des exploitations face aux changements climatiques.
	•	Accroître les revenus des agriculteurs et éleveurs par une production intégrée cultures–élevage.
	•	Promouvoir l’intégration des nouvelles technologies (IoT) dans l’agriculture rurale guinéenne.
	•	Renforcer l’autonomie économique des jeunes et des femmes par la formation et l’accès à des activités génératrices de revenus.

Impacts et réalisations attendus
	•	Environnement : réduction estimée de 20 à 30 % des émissions de gaz à effet de serre grâce à la diminution de l’utilisation d’engrais chimiques et à la valorisation des déchets organiques.
	•	Économie locale : création directe d’au moins 30 emplois (production, élevage, gestion technique) et amélioration de 40 % des revenus pour les bénéficiaires dans les 12 premiers mois.
	•	Agriculture : augmentation moyenne de 25 % des rendements maraîchers grâce à l’amélioration de la santé des sols.
	•	Technologie et innovation : mise en place d’un système de suivi intelligent pour 100 % du cheptel intégré au projet.
	•	Social : formation de 50 jeunes et femmes par cycle, favorisant leur insertion professionnelle et leur leadership dans la chaîne de valeur agricole.
Key technologies:
Permacap Guinée repose sur un bouclier intelligent connecté, un dispositif IoT (Internet des Objets) équipé de capteurs sophistiqués qui surveillent en temps réel plusieurs paramètres vitaux des caprins, notamment la température corporelle, le rythme cardiaque et les mouvements. Ces données essentielles sont transmises automatiquement à une application mobile dédiée, accessible aux agriculteurs, qui leur permet de suivre la santé de leurs animaux de manière proactive.

Grâce à cette technologie, les éleveurs peuvent détecter rapidement tout signe de maladie ou de stress, planifier les soins vétérinaires à temps, et ainsi améliorer la productivité et le bien-être animal. Par ailleurs, l’application intègre des fonctionnalités d’aide à la planification agricole, telles que les prévisions météorologiques locales et la gestion du calendrier cultural, optimisant ainsi l’ensemble de la production intégrée maraîchage-élevage.

Cette combinaison de technologies numériques innovantes favorise une gestion plus efficiente, durable et rentable des exploitations rurales, tout en facilitant le transfert de compétences numériques aux agriculteurs locaux.
Unique Characteristics:
Caractéristiques uniques et différenciantes de la solution
	•	Modèle intégré agriculture-élevage : Permacap Guinée combine de manière symbiotique le maraîchage et l’élevage caprin, créant un cycle vertueux où les déchets organiques fertilisent les sols et nourrissent les animaux, réduisant ainsi les coûts et l’impact environnemental.
	•	Bouclier intelligent connecté : usage innovant de l’IoT avec un dispositif connecté unique qui surveille en temps réel la santé des animaux, permettant une gestion préventive et optimisée inaccessible aux exploitations traditionnelles locales.
	•	Approche participative et inclusive : implication directe des jeunes et des femmes dans la conception, la mise en œuvre et la gestion, avec un modèle de partage des revenus qui favorise l’autonomisation socio-économique.
	•	Formation et transfert technologique : accompagnement intensif des bénéficiaires sur les pratiques durables et l’utilisation des outils numériques, ce qui facilite l’adoption de la technologie et assure la pérennité.
	•	Partenariats stratégiques locaux : collaboration avec les institutions publiques, les coopératives et les centres de recherche, assurant un soutien technique, réglementaire et scientifique robuste.
	•	Durabilité économique et environnementale : réduction des intrants chimiques, valorisation des ressources locales, diminution des émissions de gaz à effet de serre, tout en améliorant la productivité et les revenus
Sustainable Change:
Permacap Guinée vise à transformer durablement les pratiques agricoles et d’élevage en Guinée en proposant un modèle intégré, écologique et technologiquement avancé. En renforçant la fertilité des sols par des méthodes organiques et en introduisant le suivi intelligent des animaux, la solution améliore la productivité tout en réduisant l’impact environnemental.

Le transfert de compétences aux jeunes et aux femmes, ainsi que l’implication des communautés locales, favorisent l’adoption durable des pratiques innovantes. Ce changement de comportement crée une dynamique locale où la gestion durable devient la norme, amplifiée par l’intégration des nouvelles technologies facilitant la prise de décision et la planification.

À moyen et long terme, ces effets cumulés devraient conduire à :
	•	Une meilleure sécurité alimentaire locale grâce à des rendements agricoles plus élevés et durables.
	•	Une résilience accrue des exploitations face au changement climatique.
	•	La création d’emplois durables et la réduction de la pauvreté rurale.
	•	Une dynamique d’innovation et de collaboration renforcée entre acteurs publics, privés et communautaires.

Ainsi, Permacap Guinée ne se limite pas à un simple projet agricole, mais agit comme levier d’une transformation systémique vers une agriculture plus verte, inclusive et technologiquement adaptée.

Title: Digital Framework for Sustainable Product Development and Impact Validation
Subtitle: Inclusive digital framework enabling micro and small businesses to integrate circular design principles, provide clear impact reporting, and uphold transparent, scalable sustainability practices.
Problem Statement:
Although micro and small enterprises (MSEs) are typically grouped with medium-sized firms under the MSME classification, our research and practical experience show that MSEs face disproportionately greater challenges in adopting circular economy (CE) practices. Their smaller size, craft-oriented operations, and limited human, technical, and financial resources make compliance with emerging sustainability and traceability regulations—such as Digital Product Passports (DPP)—especially difficult.
Unlike medium firms, MSEs typically lack dedicated IT, accounting, procurement, technology, or sustainability teams, making existing impact measurement and ERP systems impractical. To reduce costs, many MSEs operate largely “off the grid,” with minimal staff, managing direct sales, production, and deliveries themselves—rendering large-scale supply chain tools inapplicable and restricting their capacity to effectively implement circular economy frameworks.
In the EU, MSEs are defined as businesses with fewer than 50 employees (micro: <10; small: 10–49). They account for approximately 93% of all enterprises, employ around 55 million people (46% of private-sector jobs), and contribute 20–25% of total turnover (European Commission, 2023). By contrast, medium-sized enterprises represent just 6% of enterprises, employ about 15 million people, and generate 10–12% of turnover.
Despite their economic significance, MSEs—particularly those engaged in artisanal, design-driven, and small-batch production—struggle to integrate CE principles and meet regulatory demands. The handcrafted and unique nature of their products makes standard compliance frameworks impractical and overly burdensome. The prevailing “burden of proof” model, developed for high-volume production, does not reflect the flexibility and variability of MSE operations, risking their exclusion from sustainable value chains.
This mismatch results in limited access to sustainability-focused markets, reduced competitiveness, and the potential loss of traditional craftsmanship skills. Current CE measurement systems fail to capture their real environmental and social contributions, leaving them underrepresented in policy and economic planning.
Furthermore, due to their lean operations and limited digital infrastructure, MSEs often face challenges in maintaining resilient and secure participation in increasingly digitalized supply chains. Our solution aims to bridge this gap by providing robust, secure, and adaptable digital tools tailored to the unique needs of MSEs, ensuring their stable inclusion in sustainable value networks.

Problem Causes:
•	Existing standards and certification schemes are complex, costly, and primarily tailored to large corporations.
•	Burden of proof requirements, such as those for Digital Product Passports, demand extensive documentation and resources beyond the capacity of small producers.
•	Small product volumes and the uniqueness of items hinder standardization and scalable certification.
•	There is a lack of accessible, simple digital tools customized and flexible for the operational scale and needs of micro and small producers.
•	Sustainability frameworks are generally designed for large-scale operations, making them unsuitable for smaller enterprises.

Problem Effects:
•	Restricted access to markets prioritizing sustainability and transparency.
•	Reduced competitiveness and diminished growth potential for micro and small businesses.
•	Risk of loss of traditional craftsmanship knowledge and sustainable artisanal practices.
•	Underutilized opportunities within the circular economy.
•	Economic pressures contributing to erosion of cultural heritage and artisanal skills.
•	Exclusion from sustainability reporting and product traceability systems essential for market participation.
•	Inability to issue Digital Product Passports (DPP) upon regulatory enforcement.
Solution Overview:
Our solution is a Digital Framework for Sustainable Product Development and Impact Validation, tailored specifically for micro and small enterprises (MSEs) in artisanal, custom-made, and small-batch sectors. It directly addresses the unique challenges MSEs face in adopting circular economy principles and complying with emerging digital transparency regulations by providing a practical, affordable, inclusive, and accessible platform.
The framework incorporates the “Burden of Design” principle, shifting sustainability compliance verification from costly and complex post-production audits to the early design phase. This approach significantly reduces administrative and financial burdens while accelerating market entry.
Products designed within this framework are automatically validated against sustainability standards, eliminating the need for separate, complex certification processes.
Our platform offers a shared, integrated certification infrastructure that includes Digital Product Passports (DPP), QR code traceability, and blockchain verification—making these typically expensive tools affordable and accessible for small producers.
Impact measurement is based on quality and context-specific metrics, adapted to the artisanal and small-scale nature of production rather than relying on volume-based metrics common in large-scale industries.
Delivered as a stable and resilient digital SaaS/FaaS platform, it supports multiple languages and features a mobile-first design, ensuring usability for users with diverse digital skills. The technology is sector-agnostic, replicable, and adaptable to local digital ecosystems in developing countries. It ensures secure, safe, and resilient functioning of digital systems during digital transformation, while also actively supporting and accelerating this transformation.
Methodologies:
•	Human-centered co-design with MSE stakeholders to ensure the platform fits real workflows and needs.
•	Agile and lean development enabling rapid iteration and continuous improvement.
•	Customized impact metrics aligned with EU Circular Economy indicators but adapted for artisanal production.
•	Material traceability mapping tailored to non-standard, small-scale supply chains.
Technologies:
•	Cloud-based SaaS with offline-first capabilities to accommodate limited internet connectivity.
•	Blockchain-enabled traceability ensuring data integrity, security, and trust.
•	AI-assisted reporting to automate compliance summaries and simplify reporting.
•	QR-coded labels linked to Digital Product Passports for transparent product journeys.
•	API and plugin integrations (e.g., WooCommerce) for seamless connection with sales and order management tools.
•	Multi-language user interface with automated English reporting.
•	Mobile-first design optimized for users with limited technical infrastructure.
We are actively seeking and developing partnerships with:
•	Technology providers to enhance platform functionalities and integrations.
•	Certification bodies to align validation criteria and certification processes.
•	E-commerce platforms to facilitate smooth market access for MSEs.
•	Industry networks and associations representing artisanal producers and micro enterprises.
•	Development agencies and NGOs focused on sustainability, circular economy, and social inclusion.
Our collaboration model is based on co-development and open innovation principles, involving stakeholders in iterative design, pilot testing, and feedback cycles. We encourage joint pilot projects and knowledge exchange initiatives to scale impact and foster a thriving ecosystem around circular economy adoption for MSEs.
Solution Provider(s): Sugar on Top d.o.o. – Bosnia and Herzegovina–based micro enterprise specializing in sustainable design and development services, slow fashion, handmade production, and zero waste business models (creative industries, sustainable fashion, and circular economy sector),
Duration to pilot in a new geography: We estimate that piloting the Minimum Viable Product (MVP) or the initial phase of the platform in a new geography would take approximately 4 to 6 months. This period covers localization, onboarding early adopters among micro and small enterprises, delivering training on sustainable design and impact reporting, and gathering initial feedback for further development.  Full deployment of the complete platform and broader functionalities may require additional time beyond this initial pilot phase.
SDGs addressed: SDG 12 (Responsible Consumption and Production);SDG 9 (Industry, Innovation, and Infrastructure);SDG 8 (Decent Work and Economic Growth);
Desired impact:
Our solution aims to enable the systemic inclusion of micro and small enterprises (MSEs) in circular economy ecosystems by providing accessible, affordable, and practical tools for sustainable product development and impact validation.
Key impacts include:
•	Increased market access for MSEs through verified sustainability credentials, connecting them to conscious consumers and sustainability-focused markets.
•	Significant reductions in resource consumption, waste, and greenhouse gas emissions by embedding circularity principles into product design and manufacturing processes.
•	Preservation and promotion of traditional craftsmanship by supporting artisanal producers and small-batch sectors to meet sustainability standards without excessive burden.
•	Enhanced social inclusion and economic empowerment of marginalized groups, including women and youth, through user-friendly tools requiring minimal digital skills.
•	Generation of reliable, quality impact data from small-scale production to inform policymakers for better-targeted regulations and support.
•	Strengthened resilience and transparency in digital supply chains via blockchain and secure traceability technologies.
•	Scalability and replicability across sectors and geographies, contributing to SDGs such as SDG 8 (Decent Work and Economic Growth), SDG 9 (Industry, Innovation, and Infrastructure), and SDG 12 (Responsible Consumption and Production).
Ultimately, the solution drives a paradigm shift toward inclusive, transparent, and sustainable economies, where small-scale producers thrive alongside larger enterprises in a circular, low-impact future.

•	Economic Impact: Increased revenues and cost savings linked to circular practices and digital innovation.

By creating a robust, data-driven foundation, our solution not only drives measurable sustainability improvements at the enterprise level but also enables policymakers, industry stakeholders, and regulators to develop better-informed and more effective environmental and economic policies. For enterprises, this means democratizing sustainability through accessible tools and verified impact data—empowering even the smallest producers to confidently participate in the green economy.
Key technologies:
Technologies:
•	Cloud-based SaaS with offline-first support.
•	Blockchain-enabled traceability in a shared model minimizing costs.
•	AI-assisted reporting for automatic compliance summaries.
•	QR-coded labels linked to Digital Product Passports.
•	API and plugin connectivity for WooCommerce and order tools.
•	Custom KPI tracking and ESG reporting tailored for artisanal production.
•	Multi-language interface with automated English reporting.
•	Mobile-first design for limited technical infrastructure.
Unique Characteristics:
Our core innovation addresses the systemic challenges faced by micro and small enterprises (MSEs) in artisanal, custom-made, and small-batch production. Unlike larger firms, MSEs lack dedicated internal expertise and resources, often resorting to costly outsourcing, which hinders their ability to participate fully in the circular economy.

We clearly distinguish MSEs from medium-sized companies (MS), recognizing their specific needs:

Limited internal departments requiring tailored, low-cost, and practical solutions.

In-house, small-scale production making large multi-actor supply chain tracking impractical.

Need for quality- and context-sensitive impact assessments rather than volume-based metrics.

Our key innovation, the “Burden of Design” principle, shifts sustainability compliance and impact verification to the early product design phase. This reduces bureaucratic burdens, enables upfront validation, and ensures products are designed for circularity and recyclability from the start.

We leverage MSEs’ operational reality — close production control and minimal external supply chains — to create practical, quality-focused impact measurements that honor artisanal craftsmanship.

Our integrated certification platform combines Digital Product Passports, QR code traceability, and blockchain verification into a shared, modular Framework-as-a-Service (FaaS) and Software-as-a-Service (SaaS). This democratizes access, making secure, resilient, and trustworthy participation in digital supply chains feasible for small producers.

The platform simplifies complex certification and tracking into accessible, affordable digital tools, empowering women, youth, and marginalized entrepreneurs, thus fostering broad inclusion and social equity.

Designed for scalability and adaptability, our solution can be replicated across diverse sectors and geographies, establishing a global standard for inclusive circular economy engagement.

Impact-wise, our solution enables systemic inclusion of thousands of MSEs in global circular economy ecosystems, accelerates sustainable production and consumption at the micro-level, and supports climate action and social equity by democratizing sustainability knowledge and tools.

Expected outcomes include increased market access for MSEs, reduced resource consumption, lower emissions, job creation in marginalized communities, enhanced transparency and trust in sustainable products, and informed policymaking supported by reliable data.

Further comments/feedback:
Sugar on Top d.o.o. is a micro social enterprise focused on slow fashion, handmade production, and zero waste principles. We have first hand experience with the unique challenges MSEs face in measuring and proving authentic social and environmental impact. 

Operating in a market dominated by low-cost, mass production, we strive to empower marginalized women and foster sustainability through ethical practices and products. However, conventional impact metrics designed for large companies fail to capture our real impact. For example, during a local sustainability competition, we could not respond adequately to questions about energy savings or CO₂ reductions, as these metrics were irrelevant to our small-scale, zero waste, deadstock, and handcrafted production. Consequently, we were not recognized, highlighting a systemic gap in existing frameworks that focus on volume and resource savings rather than qualitative, contextual realities of micro and small enterprises (MSEs).

We found traditional certification and monitoring systems like Digital Product Passports (DPP) largely inaccessible due to high costs, limited manpower, and technical capacity. Our unique, upcycled, and handcrafted products do not fit into mass production tracking models. Although we maintain strict control over our sustainable production, we lack mechanisms to formally verify our impact for stakeholders.

Our work also involves designing and developing products for other brands, raising ethical questions about responsibility. We believe accountability extends beyond our own production to ensuring client products are truly sustainable throughout their lifecycle. However, clients face a "burden of proof" to verify compliance despite our validated designs, creating bureaucratic hurdles that disproportionately affect MSEs.

To address this, we developed the principle of “Burden of Design”: products designed within a trusted, validated framework should carry inherent compliance verification, eliminating redundant certification efforts. This shifts compliance verification upstream to the design phase, reducing administrative and financial burdens for small producers.

We identified micro and small enterprises (MSEs) as a distinct group, though often classified with medium-sized businesses as MSMEs. Unlike medium firms, MSEs typically lack dedicated departments in IT, accounting, procurement, technology, or sustainability, making it difficult to adopt existing impact measurement and ERP systems. To cut costs, many operate largely “off the grid,” managing direct sales, production, and deliveries themselves—rendering large-scale supply chain tools inapplicable. They therefore require tailored support that is inclusive, quality-focused, context-sensitive, and designed to be simple and quick to use. 

Based on all of the above, Digital Product Passport systems remain unattainable for MSEs due to scalability and financial constraints. This exclusion is systemic: existing certification and digital tools are not designed inclusively, leaving MSEs marginalized despite their transparent and sustainable practices.

Our experience and challenges, echoed by our clients, inspired our innovative framework—a solution bridging these gaps and democratizing access to circular economy tools for micro and small enterprises.

This innovation is more than a product; it is a paradigm shift in sustainability for MSEs, embodied in our Framework-as-a-Service (FaaS) and Software-as-a-Service (SaaS) offerings. These provide practical, accessible, scalable, and inclusive tools designed to empower small producers.

Without targeted and inclusive solutions, our company—and many others like it—risk being excluded from both the benefits and responsibilities of the circular economy. Addressing their unique needs is essential to enable sustainable growth, meaningful contributions to a greener future, and full participation in a democratized, inclusive circular economy.

The solution focuses on simplifying the certification process through the use of Digital Product Passports and blockchain-based traceability, tailored for small-scale producers.
