Title: RelayHelp: Digital Cash Aid by and for Crisis Communities
Subtitle: Community-led humanitarian aid using blockchain, digital IDs, and mobile tools to deliver fast, transparent cash assistance to the most excluded.
Problem Statement:
Conflict, climate shocks, and displacement are at record highs, stretching humanitarian systems beyond capacity. Traditional aid models remain slow, centralized, and disconnected from realities on the ground. Refugees and displaced populations—especially those without formal identification—are frequently excluded from both humanitarian assistance and the digital economy.
The result is a growing trust gap: communities lose faith in institutions, while aid delivery fails to keep pace with urgent needs. In the absence of inclusive financial systems, many remain locked out of basic services and economic participation.
RelayHelp addresses this by offering a community-led, blockchain-enabled aid model that uses digital money to deliver assistance faster, more transparently, and more inclusively—restoring dignity, fostering trust, and putting decision-making power back in the hands of those most affected.
Solution Overview:
RelayHelp is a mobile-first, blockchain-enabled humanitarian aid platform that puts refugees and crisis-affected communities in control of resources. Built by REFUNITE and powered by a network of over 100,000 local leaders, it delivers micro-endowments in stable digital currency directly to trusted community coordinators, who decide and act on urgent priorities in real time. By combining decentralized governance, inclusive digital identity (RelayID), and tamper-proof blockchain transfers, RelayHelp enables instant, transparent, and accountable aid—even in low-connectivity or off-grid environments—while laying the foundation for long-term financial inclusion for those excluded from the formal economy.
 RelayHelp is built on REFUNITE’s trusted network of over 100,000 local leaders (“relays”) across 35 countries. Using mobile-first tools, community leaders receive micro-endowments in stable, digital currency and collectively decide urgent local priorities: food, medicine, shelter, or education.
Through blockchain-backed transfers, funds are distributed directly to the community level within minutes, without intermediaries, and can be transparently tracked from sender to beneficiary. Simple reporting tools work even on basic phones, ensuring that aid delivery is possible in low-connectivity or off-grid environments.

Technology and methodology: 
- Blockchain-powered transactions enable secure, tamper-proof tracking of funds and transparent reporting for donors and communities alike.
- Mobile-first, low-tech design ensures accessibility in resource-limited contexts via smartphone interfaces.
- Decentralized community governance shifts decision-making from institutions to those directly affected.
- RelayID provides a privacy-first, decentralized identity system—combining biometric uniqueness with community attestation—allowing undocumented individuals to securely receive and use aid.
- Partnership model: RelayHelp collaborates with refugee networks, grassroots organizations, and humanitarian innovators to ensure that both technology and governance are rooted in trusted local networks. Partnerships with digital finance and blockchain experts strengthen security, compliance, and scalability.
Solution Provider(s): Refunite (community), Human Tech (tech, digital IDs)
Duration to pilot in a new geography: 6 months
SDGs addressed: SDG 9 (Industry, Innovation, and Infrastructure);SDG 10 (Reduced Inequalities);SDG 16 (Peace, Justice, and Strong Institutions);
Desired impact:
RelayHelp’s core objective is to put resources directly—digitally—into the hands of those best positioned to use them: refugee and community leaders on the frontlines of crisis.
So far, we have: 
- Reached 67,000+ beneficiaries
- Implemented 95 locally initiated projects across 25 countries
- Delivered up to 10x more value per dollar compared to traditional aid approaches
Projects have addressed urgent needs—food, healthcare, clean water, education, shelter—while also building trust in digital cash transfers and blockchain-based accountability. This model encourages peaceful collaboration, reduces dependency, and increases dignity in crisis response.
Key technologies:
RelayHelp combines blockchain, digital identity, and mobile-first platforms to deliver fast, transparent, and inclusive cash assistance in crisis contexts:

- Blockchain for transparent aid flows – Tracks funds from donor to beneficiary in real time, ensuring security, accountability, and tamper-proof reporting.
- Digital cash transfers – Uses stablecoins to enable instant, low-cost, cross-border payments, even in high-risk or low-banking-access environments.
- Decentralized identity (RelayID) – Privacy-preserving, blockchain-secured identity system that uses biometric uniqueness and social attestation to include people without formal IDs.
- Low-tech mobile integration – Accessible via WhatsApp or lightweight apps to work in low-connectivity and off-grid areas.
- Real-time feedback loops – Mobile tools allow communities to self-report needs, track deliveries, and verify receipt of aid, strengthening trust and speed.

This combination ensures that aid reaches the most excluded populations quickly, securely, and with full transparency—while laying the groundwork for participation in the broader digital economy.
Unique Characteristics:
Unlike most humanitarian platforms that simply digitize existing processes, RelayHelp reimagines the entire aid model by combining:
- Grassroots-first delivery: Leveraging 100,000+ refugee and community leaders for fund allocation, project coordination, and real-time reporting.
- Blockchain for trust: Using transparent, tamper-proof digital ledgers to ensure every transaction is visible and verifiable.
- Inclusive identity: RelayID uses biometric uniqueness and social attestation to close the access gap for over 3 billion people without formal ID.
- Peacebuilding by design: Embedding collaboration and local governance into aid delivery to foster trust, ownership, and resilience.
Sustainable Change:
As crises intensify, centralized aid systems—often cash-based but not digitally enabled—struggle to respond swiftly or equitably, especially where formal financial infrastructure is absent.
RelayHelp offers a scalable, blockchain-enabled alternative: a decentralized, digital cash transfer network led by communities themselves. By equipping refugee leaders with mobile tools, micro-endowments in stable digital currency, and decentralized identity solutions, it enables instant, secure, transparent aid in even the most challenging environments.
Our theory of change:
 If affected communities control decision-making and have access to secure, inclusive digital finance tools, aid becomes faster, fairer, and more sustainable—laying the groundwork for long-term participation in the digital economy.
RelayHelp does more than meet urgent needs: it builds a new, trust-based infrastructure for community resilience and economic inclusion—powered by blockchain, guided by communities.
Funding Sources: Core organizational funding
Further comments/feedback: https://relayhelp.refunite.org/
Primary thematic focus area: Inclusive Digital Innovation Skills & Entrepreneurial Talent Development
Summary: RelayHelp is a blockchain-powered digital platform aimed at delivering fast, transparent, and inclusive humanitarian aid in crisis-affected communities. By utilizing mobile-first tools, decentralized identity (RelayID), and blockchain technology, RelayHelp empowers local leaders to manage resources directly, ensuring more efficient aid distribution and fostering trust in digital financial systems.

Title: Finance Made Simple Through Gamified Learning
Subtitle: A gamified, AI-powered platform making financial education engaging, accessible, and inclusive for people of all backgrounds.
Problem Statement: Over 67% of the global population is financially illiterate, with developing countries most affected. Bridging the inequality gap requires empowering people with the knowledge to make informed financial decisions. Yet in many countries, financial education is overlooked, leaving millions without the skills needed to participate fully in the digital economy.
Solution Overview:
At eFrontiers we have created a gamified microlearning platform that makes learning about money easy, fun, and accessible. We combine proven education methods with engaging gamification so that learning about finance feels more like playing a game. Think of it as the "Duolingo of Finance". Our solution is offered as a white-label platform for financial institutions to promote financial education in their markets. This creates a win-win scenario where institutions gain a powerful marketing and engagement tool while building brand equity, and people get access to financial education for free.

While many financial education initiatives rely on static blogs or dull resources that few people read, our innovative approach focuses on delivering the most engaging learning experience possible. Built with AI, our platform adapts to local languages and contexts, and our partners help reach communities at scale. In this way, financial institutions can strengthen their role as trusted community partners while empowering people with the knowledge they need to make better financial decisions.
Solution Provider(s): Bestinver Asset Management Firm Finance, Stashaway Financial Institution Finance, InterCapital Asset Management Finance.
Implementation location(s): Spain, Singapore, UAE, and Croatia. Our free app Money Masters is available world wide. We count with over 90,000 users.
Implementation timeline(s): Spain 2024- Present, Singapore Q3-2025, UAE Q3 2025, Croatia Q4 2025 (upcoming)
Duration to pilot in a new geography: We operate with 6 months pilots. We take two months for implementation and content creation and 4 months live.
SDGs addressed: SDG 4 (Quality Education);SDG 5 (Gender Equality);SDG 17 (Partnerships for the Goals);
Desired impact:
Our objective is to empower people to become financially literate so they can break the cycle of poverty and help close the inequality gap. By providing accessible, engaging, and free financial education through our gamified platform, we aim to equip individuals with the knowledge and confidence to make better financial decisions and fully participate in the digital economy.

To date, we have reached over 90,000 registered users, with more than 10,000 achieving financial literacy as defined by the Global Financial Literacy Excellence Center (GFLEC) and the Standard & Poor’s benchmark. This standard measures literacy by a user’s ability to correctly understand at least three out of four key concepts: inflation, diversification, compound interest, and basic numeracy.
Key technologies: AI, Gamification, and Microlearning
Unique Characteristics: What makes us stand out comes down to three things. First is our innovative business model, where we work with financial institutions who fund the platform while making it completely free for the public. In return, these institutions gain a powerful differentiator that strengthens brand equity and community trust. Second is our ability to deliver tailored learning for each country. By leveraging AI, we adapt content to local languages, cultures, and market realities to ensure the education is highly relevant and impactful. Third is our proprietary data algorithm, which identifies knowledge gaps among users. This allows us to advise partners on where these gaps exist and create targeted content to close them, ensuring measurable and sustained improvements in financial literacy.
Sustainable Change:
I am the founder of eFrontiers and originally from Guatemala, where I have witnessed extreme financial inequality firsthand. Through perseverance, I was fortunate to access opportunities internationally, and this experience showed me how transformative education can be in changing lives. Today, with technology more accessible than ever, we believe it must be leveraged to create real social impact.
We chose to focus on financial education because it is one of the most overlooked areas of learning, yet it plays a critical role in every person’s life. Data consistently shows that even basic financial knowledge can drastically improve decision-making, resilience, and long-term wellbeing.

Our theory of change is that by making high-quality financial education engaging, accessible, and free through partnerships with financial institutions, we can equip individuals with the skills to participate fully in the economy, escape cycles of poverty, and close inequality gaps. The desired follow-on effects include stronger community financial health, greater trust between institutions and the public, and the creation of a self-reinforcing system where financially literate individuals drive economic growth and inclusion in their communities.
Funding Sources: We have funded the development and implementation of our solution through a combination of pre-seed investment from a seed-stage venture capital fund and several angel investors. This initial funding enabled us to build, test, and launch the platform with our first partners. We are currently working on our seed round to scale operations and expand our impact.

Title: AI-Powered Survey Platform for Inclusive Digital Data Collection with African local language integration
Subtitle: Democratizing research capabilities through intelligent automation, multimedia data collection, and advanced analytics for NGOs, researchers, and underserved communities.
Problem Statement: Current survey and data collection platforms suffer from critical limitations that perpetuate digital divides: manual question creation lacks methodological rigor, text surveys fail to capture rich contextual information, and translation processes for oral surveys in Africa often introduce cultural and linguistic biases that distort meaning, misrepresent participant perspectives, and undermine the validity and trustworthiness of findings. Complex interfaces exclude non-technical users, and basic analytics don't provide actionable insights. These challenges create significant barriers for organizations in developing regions and underserved communities to conduct quality research and make data-driven decisions.
Solution Overview:
Scollect is a comprehensive, AI-powered platform designed to democratize high-quality research for organizations in developing regions and underserved communities. The platform operates through three integrated components:

AI-Driven Question Generation – Leveraging GPT technology, Scollect automatically generates survey questions using intelligent templates grounded in proven research methodologies. Built-in quality validation ensures methodological rigor, regardless of the user’s research expertise.

Multimedia Data Collection & Translation – Users can collect audio, video, image, and geolocation data, enabling the capture of rich contextual information, especially valuable in low-literacy, multilingual, and oral-tradition communities. The platform also supports automatic translation of surveys and responses into major African languages, reducing reliance on manual interpretation, mitigating cultural and linguistic bias, and improving accuracy in oral survey contexts.

Advanced Analytics – Scollect offers statistical analysis with over 40 interactive visualization types and automatically generates analysis code for R, Python, STATA, and SQL. This makes advanced data interpretation accessible to non-technical users while supporting experts with direct code integration.
Methodologies and Technologies Used : Survey design rooted in established social science research methods; bias-mitigation techniques for multilingual and oral data; mixed-methods integration combining quantitative and qualitative analysis; and participatory research approaches that involve community members in data interpretation,  GPT-based AI models , data storage and retrieval via secure cloud infrastructure; and interactive analytics powered by statistical libraries in R and Python.

Partnerships and Collaboration Models

Scollect is designed to be deployed in partnership with:

Local NGOs, research institutions, and community organizations to ensure surveys are culturally relevant and locally validated.

Universities and academic researchers for methodology refinement and ongoing tool validation.

Government agencies and development partners for scaling impact in national surveys and policy research.
Technology providers for integration with translation, transcription, and GIS mapping services.

Partnership models are collaborative and capacity-building focused, providing training for local enumerators, co-designing survey templates with stakeholders, and sharing results in open-access formats where appropriate.
Solution Provider(s): SpparoW (Lead Organization - Technology Platform), Academic Research Partners (Methodology Validation), NGO Networks (Field Testing & Implementation), Technology Partners (AI/ML Integration), Local Community Organizations (User Feedback & Adaptation)
Implementation location(s): Currently piloted in (By September): Benin, Senegal, Guinea, Ivoiry Coast
Implementation timeline(s): Implementation Timeline  Start Date: January 2025 Current Status: Active pilot phase End Date: Ongoing
Duration to pilot in a new geography: 3-6 months (depending on local infrastructure and partner availability)
SDGs addressed: SDG 4 (Quality Education);SDG 8 (Decent Work and Economic Growth);SDG 10 (Reduced Inequalities);
Desired impact:
Desired Impact

Solution Objectives

Reduce survey creation time by 70% through AI automation
Improve data quality by 40% through multimedia collection and validation
Increase research participation from underserved communities by 60%
Enable 10,000+ organizations to conduct professional research by 2027
Key technologies:
Key Technologies Used

Artificial Intelligence: OpenAI GPT for question generation, NLP models for text analysis

Cloud Computing: leveraging PostgreSQL for robust, scalable, and reliable data management.Mobile Technology: Progressive Web App with offline functionality

Data Analytics: SQL, Statistical analysis libraries (R, Python), interactive visualization engines

Multimedia Processing: Audio/video compression, geolocation services, image processing
Unique Characteristics:
AI-First Approach:  contextually relevant question generation.

Automatic Translation for African Contexts: Integrated translation for survey questions and responses, supporting major African languages to reduce bias, preserve meaning, and improve accessibility in multilingual communities.

Code Generation: Automatic export of analysis scripts for R, Python, STATA, and SQL, enabling both technical and non-technical users to work with data.

Domain Expertise: Pre-built templates for 10+ sectors with embedded industry-specific best practices.

Accessibility Focus: WCAG 2.1-compliant interface designed to reduce the learning curve by up to 70%, making high-quality research tools accessible to all user levels.
Sustainable Change:
Theory of Change

Immediate Impact: Organizations gain access to professional research tools regardless of technical expertise

Short-term Change: Improved data quality leads to better decision-making and resource allocation

Medium-term Transformation: Evidence-based interventions become standard practice in underserved communities

Long-term Systemic Change: Digital research capabilities become democratized, reducing knowledge gaps and promoting inclusive development

Follow-on Effects

Increased capacity for local organizations to conduct impact evaluations

Better resource allocation based on quality data

Enhanced ability to attract funding through professional research capabilities

Knowledge transfer and capacity building in research methodology

Creation of local research ecosystems and expertise
Funding Sources: Founder investment and donation
Further comments/feedback:
Scollect represents a paradigm shift in making professional research capabilities accessible to organizations regardless of their technical expertise or resource constraints. Our platform directly addresses the digital divide in research and evaluation, enabling evidence-based decision-making in communities that have traditionally been excluded from such capabilities.

The solution's focus on AI automation, multimedia data collection, and user-friendly analytics makes it particularly valuable for organizations working in multilingual, low-literacy, or resource-constrained environments. By democratizing research capabilities, we're not just providing a tool - we're building capacity for sustainable development and inclusive growth.

We believe Scollect aligns perfectly with the Global Digital Compact's Objective 2 by expanding inclusion in the digital economy through accessible, intelligent technology that bridges capability gaps and promotes knowledge sharing across borders and sectors.
Primary thematic focus area: Inclusive Digital Innovation Skills & Entrepreneurial Talent Development
Summary: Scollect is an AI-powered platform aimed at democratizing research by providing accessible, inclusive, and culturally relevant data collection and analysis tools. It focuses on overcoming digital and linguistic barriers for underserved communities in Africa by integrating AI-driven question generation, multimedia data collection, and advanced analytics. The platform enables organizations, researchers, and community leaders to gather and analyze data in real time, facilitating more accurate, transparent, and inclusive decision-making.

Title: Green wheels Green ads; Digital Advertising On The Go!
Subtitle: Duba empowers underserved youth riders in the green economy with a digital advertising delivery bag; ebag which earns them an income passively as they move through the city making deliveries.
Problem Statement: Duba tackles key barriers limiting digital economic inclusion for youth and MSMEs: lack of affordable e-mobility options or financing, limited access to digital advertising and marketing channels, and insufficient digital skills that hinder their ability to attract customers and grow online. These challenges restrict their participation in the digital economy, limit income-generating opportunities, and deepen existing economic inequalities. Duba’s unique integration of digital advertising with accessible mobility solutions empowers users to monetize digital assets while increasing their visibility, creating an inclusive and scalable pathway to sustainable economic empowerment.
Solution Overview:
Duba operates a digital platform that combines mobile digital advertising with e-mobility to empower youth and MSMEs. Riders in the green economy carry digital screens (e-bags) that display targeted ads for brands, generating advertising revenue that subsidizes riders’ participation and provides income. This model transforms each rider into a mobile digital marketing channel, expanding reach into communities often overlooked by traditional media.

The platform leverages cloud-based software for ad content management, real-time data tracking, and performance analytics, enabling advertisers to optimize campaigns and measure impact. Riders access a mobile app for onboarding, task management, and earnings tracking, ensuring transparency and ease of use.

Duba’s methodology emphasizes inclusive digital participation by providing digital skills training to riders and MSMEs, enhancing their ability to engage with digital tools and grow their businesses online.

Strategic partnerships are central to Duba’s model. Collaborations with e-mobility providers ensure affordable access to electric bikes, while partnerships with brands and marketing agencies fuel the advertising ecosystem. Additionally, Duba works closely with local communities, NGOs, and youth organizations to recruit and train riders, fostering community ownership and sustainability.
Solution Provider(s): Duba partners with Ebee Technologies Limited, a leading Kenyan e-mobility company providing lease-to-own electric bike fleet management solutions for different last mile platforms such as bolt food, uber etc, that enhance affordable access to e-bikes for delivery riders in the transportation sector; and also Ewaka Kenya Limited, specializing in e-bike leasing and fleet management, supporting sustainable last-mile mobility in the transportation and technology sector; WPP Kenya, a global media buying and communications agency delivering strategic advertising and marketing services across multiple industries; Saracen OMD, a leading media agency focusing on data-driven media buying and digital marketing solutions; TECHNE Corporate Innovation HQ, a business accelerator supporting startups with innovation and market access, under which Duba has secured a strategic partnership with Talabat, a major food delivery platform in the digital economy and logistics sector.  Together, these partners span mobility technology, digital marketing, advertising, innovation acceleration, and digital commerce, forming a comprehensive ecosystem that supports Duba’s inclusive digital economy model.
Duration to pilot in a new geography: 6 months
SDGs addressed: SDG 8 (Decent Work and Economic Growth);SDG 13 (Climate Action);
Desired impact:
Duba’s goal is to drive inclusive digital economic participation by empowering underserved youth and MSMEs with affordable e-mobility and digital advertising tools. It aims to increase income opportunities, build digital skills, and expand market access, fostering entrepreneurship and reducing economic disparities.

Key Achievements and Impact:

Enabled over 200 youth riders to generate income through mobile digital advertising on leased e-bikes.

Supported 500+ MSMEs to gain affordable digital marketing exposure, increasing customer reach and sales by up to 30%.

Trained 2,00+ individuals in ad digital literacy and business skills to enhance digital economy participation in the green economu

Created sustainable employment opportunities in urban areas, reducing youth unemployment.

Integrated electric mobility, reducing carbon emissions by an estimated 30+ tons of CO2 annually compared to fossil-fuel alternatives.
Key technologies:
The novelty in Duba’s e-bags lies in our ability to leverage clean technology and e-commerce in urban areas in East Africa. By providing e-bicycle delivery riders with our e-bags, Duba is incentivizing daily commutes that will not only generate additional income for the riders but also allow our advertising clients to adapt their Ads to specific locations with high traffic, making their reach more effective. The digital screens allow for dynamic and targeted advertising, with the ability to display real-time content based on location, time of day, and audience behaviour. The integrated geospatial technology enables geo-fencing and geo-targeting, enabling precise audience segmentation and real-time updates for hyper-relevant campaigns.  

Our partnership with eBee & ewaka makes our business model very novel because advertising agencies in urban cities in East Africa are providing advertising services to businesses through traditional methods, and the e-mobility service providers have not integrated digital advertising capabilities into their offerings. No company in the e-mobility and advertising sectors in East Africa has integrated technology into making e-bags for advertising, particularly with a focus on sustainability and digital flexibility. 
Our rent-to-own model of the e-bags is tied to the riders' core delivery work which will increase the income they earn daily as they ride their e-c. The dual-income approach reduces financial pressure, as riders will leverage the advertising earnings to cover part or all of their lease payments, effectively reducing the cost of owning the e-bags, while addressing income stability in the long term"
Unique Characteristics: Duba’s innovation lies in its integrated business model that combines affordable e-mobility leasing with mobile digital advertising, creating dual income streams for underserved youth and MSMEs. Unlike traditional digital marketing platforms, Duba transforms delivery riders into mobile advertising channels, enabling dynamic, location-based ad exposure in underserved communities. Its lease-to-own financing model lowers barriers to e-bike access, promoting financial inclusion and sustainable mobility. Strategic partnerships with e-mobility providers, media agencies, and digital platforms like Talabat amplify impact and scalability. This blend of technology, financing, and community engagement creates a unique, inclusive digital economy ecosystem that drives economic empowerment and broadens market reach.
Sustainable Change:
Duba creates sustainable, systemic change by addressing key barriers to digital economic inclusion through its integrated product features:

Income Generation through Mobile Digital Advertising: By equipping riders with e-bags featuring digital screens, Duba enables youth to earn revenue by displaying targeted ads, providing a steady income stream and economic empowerment.

Affordable E-Mobility via Lease-to-Own Model: Duba’s partnership with e-bike providers offers riders accessible financing options to lease and eventually own electric bikes, ensuring long-term mobility and reducing dependency on costly, polluting transport.

Digital Skills and Platform Access: The rider app and MSME onboarding include training modules that build digital literacy and marketing know-how, enabling participants to leverage digital tools effectively.

Data-Driven Campaigns and Community Reach: Cloud-based ad management and real-time analytics optimize ad placement and performance, helping MSMEs increase visibility and competitiveness within local markets.

Sustainable Urban Mobility: The use of electric bikes in delivery reduces carbon emissions compared to fossil-fueled vehicles, contributing to greener cities.

Over time, these product features collectively:

Increase digital economic participation by making advertising and mobility accessible.

Foster entrepreneurship and income stability among youth and MSMEs.

Enhance MSME market reach through affordable, data-driven digital advertising.

Promote sustainable transport habits through accessible e-mobility.
Funding Sources: Duba has been self funded so far by directors contributions and advertising revenue from clients.
Testimonials and Endorsements: Duba ad client "Minal Pattni - head of masoko ecommerce platform - safaricom. "Duba is the greatest innovation yet"
Primary thematic focus area: MSME Empowerment & Local Digital Innovation
Summary: Duba is a mobile-first platform integrating e-mobility with digital advertising. It provides underserved youth with electric bikes (e-bags) that carry digital ads, generating a dual-income stream for the riders. This model enables income generation while promoting sustainable, eco-friendly transport solutions and provides affordable digital marketing for MSMEs, boosting their market reach and sales.

Title: iNgeyaa - The Intelligent Road for Africa's Urban Mobility
Subtitle: Smart traffic management system prioritizing emergency response and inclusive mobility in African cities.
Problem Statement: Urban congestion in African cities like Douala and Yaoundé severly impacts mobility, delays emergency services, increases pollution, and limits economic productivity. Outdated traffic systems, inadequate infrastructure, and limited data integration worsen the problem, excluding vulnerable populations from efficient mobility services.
Solution Overview:
iNgeyaa is a culturally rooted, technology-driven urban traffic management system designed to make African roads smarter, safer, and more inclusive.

It integrates three main components:
- iNgeyaa Box & iNgeyaa Smart: IoT-enabled devices that monitor, analyze, and regulate traffic flows in real time.
- i-Urgence: An emergency-prioritization module that clears the way for ambulances and rescue vehicles, reducing life-threatening delays.
- iNgeyaa App: A citizen-facing mobile platform offering live traffic maps, voice-guided alternative routes, incident reporting, and community-based traffic insights.

Methodologies and Technologies:
We leverage IoT sensors, AI-powered analytics, geolocation, and mobile connectivity to deliver actionable insights to both authorities and citizens. The solution operates on a B2B2C model: municipalities adopt the infrastructure, while motorists access services via a freemium mobile application.

Partnership and Collaboration Model:
iNgeyaa works in close collaboration with urban municipalities, emergency service providers, and private sector mobility partners to ensure coordinated deployment. We also integrate feedback from local communities to refine functionalities, ensuring the system is inclusive and culturally adapted.
Solution Provider(s): Urban Municipalities of Douala and Yaoundé – Public sector partners providing deployment access and regulatory support;  Local Emergency Services (Ambulances, Fire Departments, Police) – Collaboration for emergency prioritization systems;  Private Mobility Stakeholders (transport companies, insurers) – Partners for pilot integration and data-sharing initiatives.
Duration to pilot in a new geography: 1-3 months
SDGs addressed: SDG 3 (Good Health and Well-being);SDG 9 (Industry, Innovation, and Infrastructure);SDG 11 (Sustainable Cities and Communities);
Desired impact:
Solution Objectives:

- Reduce urban traffic congestion in African cities by 30% in pilot areas.
- Prioritize emergency vehicle movement to cut response times by up to 40%.
- Provide real-time, accessible traffic information to all road users.

Key Achievements / Expected Impacts:

- Environmental: Potential CO₂ reduction of ~1,200 tons annually per city by minimizing idle time.
- Health & Safety: Faster emergency response saves lives and reduces accident severity.
- Economic: Increase productivity by reducing hours lost in traffic (~150 hours saved per driver annually).
- Employment: Creation of 25+ direct jobs in deployment, maintenance, and software support within 3 years.
Key technologies:
1. Internet of Things (IoT): Networked devices (iNgeyaa Box & Smart) collect real-time traffic data.
2. Artificial Intelligence (AI): Machine learning models process and predict traffic patterns.
3. Geolocation & GIS: GPS-based vehicle tracking and route optimization.
4. Mobile Technology: Android/iOS application for user interaction, alerts, and crowdsourced reporting.
5. Cloud Computing: Centralized analytics and data visualization dashboards for municipalities.
Unique Characteristics:
1. Cultural Relevance: Name and design rooted in local language (“Ngeya” – road in Duala), fostering community ownership.
2. Emergency Prioritization Module (i-Urgence): Unique Africa-focused innovation to dynamically clear routes for ambulances and rescue vehicles.
3. Inclusive Business Model: B2B2C structure with municipal partnerships and affordable freemium user plans (as low as 500 FCFA/month).
4. Community-Centric Data Approach: Combines official traffic data with citizen reports for richer, localized insights.
5. Scalable Infrastructure: Modular deployment adaptable to small towns or megacities without overhauling existing road systems.
Sustainable Change:
Short Term: Deploy IoT-enabled traffic monitoring and response systems in targeted urban areas, reducing congestion and improving emergency response.
Medium Term: Institutionalize real-time traffic management in municipal operations, supported by community engagement via the mobile app.
Long Term: Transform urban mobility culture—embedding data-driven decision-making in city planning, reducing environmental impact, and ensuring equitable access to safe, efficient transport.

The systemic shift comes from integrating citizens, municipalities, and emergency services into a single, coordinated ecosystem — fostering trust, efficiency, and resilience in urban transport networks.
Funding Sources:
1. Orange Summer Challenge 2023 - 2nd Prize - 1,050,000 XAF
2. Cameroon Digital Innovation Week 2025 [4th Edition] - 8th Prize - 500,000 XAF
Primary thematic focus area: MSME Empowerment & Local Digital Innovation
Summary: iNgeyaa is an innovative, AI-powered urban traffic management system designed to address congestion, enhance emergency response times, and create an inclusive mobility model in African cities.

Title: Kitabu Biashara-Point of sale and inventory management system
Subtitle: Kitabu Biashara is a mobile-first POS and inventory system helping African businesses track sales, manage stock, and grow profits with ease, affordability, and local language support.
Problem Statement: Many African SMEs struggle with poor sales tracking, stock mismanagement, and limited payment integration, leading to inefficiency, revenue loss, and reduced competitiveness in the market.
Solution Overview:
How the Solution Works:
Kitabu Biashara is a mobile-first POS and inventory management system that enables SMEs to record sales, track stock in real time, generate reports, and we integrate digital payments. It supports online use, works in local languages, and provides analytics to guide business decisions.

Methodologies & Technologies Used:
We apply user-centered design, agile development, and continuous feedback loops to ensure the solution meets local business needs. The system is built with React (web), React Native, flutter/dart (mobile), Python (backend), and MySQL (database), with secure payment integrations and cloud backup for data safety.

Partnerships & Collaboration Models:
We collaborate with local chambers of commerce, merchant associations, and financial service providers to onboard users and integrate payment solutions, hosting system. Partnerships are built on mutual value—either revenue-sharing, joint training programs, to reach and support SMEs efficiently.

Title: Digital Marketplace Empowering Africa’s Fitness Entrepreneurs for Inclusive Growth
Subtitle: Transforming Africa’s informal fitness sector into sustainable digital enterprises, boosting jobs, economic growth, and health through innovative gig economy platforms.
Problem Statement: Botswana’s unemployment rate remains high, with many skilled individuals underutilised in the informal sector. Across Africa, millions hold indigenous health and fitness knowledge, yet lack business infrastructure and digital tools to turn these skills into sustainable livelihoods. This underutilisation limits economic growth, restricts access to active lifestyles, and contributes to rising non-communicable diseases. By failing to integrate these communities into the digital economy, we miss opportunities for both job creation and better health outcomes globally.
Solution Overview:
GR8R Than Fitness is a digital marketplace connecting trainers, gyms, and wellness communities to clients through a single, accessible platform. Providers can list their services, accept bookings, process payments, and manage their business with built-in marketing tools.

The platform uses cloud-based architecture, secure payment gateways, and mobile-first design to ensure accessibility across devices. Gamification, analytics dashboards, and community-building tools improve engagement and retention.

Partnerships with sports federations, corporate wellness programs, and community fitness groups help onboard providers and expand reach. Collaboration with universities, health organisations, and technology hubs supports research, innovation, and continuous platform improvement.
Solution Provider(s): Botswana Rugby Union – Sports federation driving trainer onboarding, University of Toronto – Technology and business development support, African Impact Initiative – Funding and mentorship, Botswana National Basketball Association – Client acquisition and sponsorship partner, Mastercard Foundation – Grant funding and entrepreneurship support
Implementation timeline(s): Pilot Launched August 2024, MVP Launch August 2025
Duration to pilot in a new geography: 3 Months
SDGs addressed: SDG 1 (No Poverty);SDG 3 (Good Health and Well-being);SDG 8 (Decent Work and Economic Growth);
Desired impact: To create a thriving, tech-enabled fitness economy in Botswana and Africa as a whole, generating thousands of sustainable jobs, increasing small business income, and improving community health by making physical activity more accessible.
Key technologies:
Azure, Cloud-based architecture for scalability and secure data management

Mobile-first web application design for accessibility across devices and low-bandwidth environments

Secure payment gateways integrating mobile money, cards, and digital wallets

Booking and scheduling algorithms for seamless client-provider matching

Data analytics dashboards for performance tracking and business insights

Gamification features to boost engagement and retention

API integrations for partnerships with health, Insurance, sports, wellness platforms and smart monitoring devices
Unique Characteristics: Our model transforms the informal fitness sector into a formalised, tech-driven gig economy. By combining a marketplace model with integrated business tools, we enable providers to operate professionally without the need for costly infrastructure. Partnerships with sports federations and corporate wellness programs act as built-in distribution channels, reducing acquisition costs and accelerating adoption. The financing model includes revenue sharing and future microfinance options for equipment and training, further boosting sustainability.
Sustainable Change: GR8R Than Fitness addresses both economic and health gaps by providing a scalable platform that empowers local entrepreneurs to thrive in the digital economy. By formalising informal work, we create stable income opportunities, improve service quality, and expand access to fitness. This approach strengthens community well-being, supports public health objectives, and creates a replicable model for other industries and regions, ensuring long-term, systemic impact.
Funding Sources: Founder Investment, Friends and Family as well as SAFE investment from African Impact Initiative and University of Toronto.
Primary thematic focus area: Inclusive Digital Innovation Skills & Entrepreneurial Talent Development
Summary: GR8R Than Fitness is a digital marketplace connecting trainers and wellness communities to clients, transforming informal fitness work into sustainable businesses through technology.

Title: PIN.AI – Personalised & Inclusive Heritage Experience in AI
Subtitle: Inclusive AI-powered heritage guides for UNESCO religious sites, proven in pilot and ready for scale
Problem Statement: Religious UNESCO heritage sites often remain inaccessible to persons with disabilities and older adults due to missing inclusive interpretation, lack of accessibility in digital tools, and limited skills among tourism MSMEs. This results in cultural exclusion, lost economic opportunities, and diminished visitor experiences.
Solution Overview:
PIN.AI is an AI-powered digital guide system designed to make religious UNESCO heritage sites fully accessible and engaging for all. It builds on a successful pilot at Miramare Castle (Italy), which integrated immersive AR storytelling, universal accessibility layers, and co-creation with persons with disabilities.

How it works:

- AI personalises content to visitor profiles (language, disability type, preferences)

- AR delivers immersive storytelling and wayfinding

- Accessibility layers include sign language video, audio description, Easy-to-Read text, tactile graphics, and screen reader compatibility

Methodologies & Technologies:
Co-creation workshops with persons with disabilities, compliance with WCAG 2.1 and EAA standards, AI and AR integration, multilingual content adaptation.

Partnership Model:
Led by Beletrina (Slovenia) with CtrlArt, Arctur, LTFE, Poliskop, and local heritage site authorities.
Solution Provider(s): Beletrina – NGO for digital accessibility and inclusive culture; CtrlArt – AR/VR for cultural heritage; Arctur – AI and digital tourism infrastructure; LTFE – Research in adaptive and accessible technologies; Poliskop – Inclusive tourism training and Local site authorities in Aquileia (Italy), Poreč (Croatia), and Ohrid (North Macedonia)
Implementation location(s): Pilot implementation at Miramare Castle (Trieste), but not for public use.
Implementation timeline(s): Pilot foundation tested in Miramare Castle (2023/24 - 8 months) Scale-up deployment: 2025–2026
Duration to pilot in a new geography: 6-9 months per location
SDGs addressed: SDG 9 (Industry, Innovation, and Infrastructure);SDG 10 (Reduced Inequalities);SDG 11 (Sustainable Cities and Communities);
Desired impact:
Objectives:
- Make heritage sites fully accessible and inclusive for diverse visitors
- Equip MSMEs and cultural operators with practical skills and tools
- Deliver a replicable, sustainable model for accessible digital heritage interpretation

Key Impacts:
- At least 5 disability profiles served at each site
- 20+ cultural/tourism professionals trained per location
- Toolkit for replication in other heritage contexts
Key technologies:
- Artificial Intelligence (adaptive content delivery)
- Augmented Reality (immersive storytelling and navigation)
- Multimodal accessibility features (sign language, Easy-to-Read, audio description, tactile graphics)
Unique Characteristics: PIN.AI combines AI-driven personalisation, immersive AR storytelling, and universal accessibility in religious heritage tourism. It uses co-creation with persons with disabilities, empowers local tourism providers, and is adaptable across cultural, linguistic, and infrastructural contexts.
Sustainable Change: The solution embeds inclusive technology into heritage tourism operations, creating long-term capacity for local actors. It fosters systemic change by normalising accessibility as a standard feature of cultural tourism, encouraging policy alignment, and providing a scalable model for other sites globally.
Funding Sources: Previous pilot funded by EU Interreg programme, national cultural innovation funding, and partnerships with cultural institutions in Italy and Slovenia.
Testimonials and Endorsements: https://www.ctrlart.com/pina-portal-to-miramares-legends.html

Title: BambooTech
Subtitle: Autonomisation des communautés vulnérables par l’artisanat numérique pour une économie verte et inclusive
Problem Statement: Plus de 90% des burundais dépendent de l’Agriculture. En plus une grande partie du PIB au Burundi provient dans l’agro-alimentaire ci qui explique que de nombreuses communautés à faible revenu sont confrontées à un triple défi : la pauvreté, le chômage des jeunes et la dégradation de l’environnement due à l’érosion. Malgré la richesse naturelle locale comme le bambou, cette ressource reste sous-exploitée. L'absence de compétences numériques et d’accès à des outils modernes limite fortement les opportunités économiques locales. Ce manque de valorisation empêche la communauté de s’autonomiser durablement. Le projet répond donc au besoin urgent d’inclusion numérique, de création d’emplois verts et de développement de chaînes de valeur locales écoresponsables.
Solution Overview: Le projet vise à autonomiser les communautés à faible revenu par l’introduction de l’artisanat numérique dans la fabrication de produits à base de bambou, tels que des paniers, nattes, balais, objets décoratifs et cure-dents. Il combine innovation artisanale, technologies numériques et valorisation écologique du bambou. Le projet procèdera à la formation de la communauté (des jeunes, des femmes et les personnes ciblées à faible revenu) à l’artisanat à base de bambou, à l’introduction d’outils numériques pour améliorer la qualité des produits, leur design et faciliter leur commercialisation en ligne, la mise en place d’un atelier numérique communautaire pour la production et la formation continue et la création d’une plateforme de vente en ligne locale et internationale pour valoriser les produits. Nous allons aussi adapter à une méthodologie participative en faisant l’implication directe des bénéficiaires dans le design et la production et à l’apprentissage par la pratique « learning by doing ».  Notre partenariat avec l’administration local, les centres de formation et les ONG locales recommandés par cet appel à solutions, nous faciliterons à la mobilisation, à la formation numérique et à la règlementation et du suivi.
Solution Provider(s): Agir Pour l’Environnement est une Organisation locale à but non lucratif engagée dans la protection de l’environnement et l’autonomisation des communautés vulnérables à travers des solutions durables et écologiques. Secteur : ONG / Développement communautaire / Environnement. Nous coopérons avec des structures comme l’OBPE (Office Burundais pour la Protection de l’Environnement), certaines coopératives agricoles locales et des mouvements communautaires de reboisement. Nous nous reconnaissons dans les luttes globales pour la justice climatique, les droits des peuples autochtones, les réfugiés et les apatrides et la transition écologique inclusive. Autres partenaires : sont les autorités locales qui nous appuient dans la sensibilisation de la communauté, le Centre de Formation Professionnelle de Kavumu (formation technique).
Implementation location(s): Lieu de mise en œuvre : Camp de réfugiés de Kavumu, Commune Cankuzo, Province de Buhumuza, Burundi.
Implementation timeline(s): 	Début : Janvier 2022   	Phase de reboisement (plantation des bambous et eucalyptus) et canalisation : Janvier 2022 – Décembre 2023   	Phase d’artisanat en bambou (en phase pilote) : Juin 2025 – en cours (2025)   	Phase de prototypage cure-dents en bambou : Prévue si le financement est accordé
Duration to pilot in a new geography: La durée estimée pour piloter notre solution dans une nouvelle géographie est de 12 mois, répartie comme suit : du 1 à 2 mois : Identification des partenaires locaux, mobilisation communautaire et études préliminaires. Du 3 à 4 mois : Mise en place des infrastructures de base (coupure de bambous, sélection des bénéficiaires, formation des formateurs).  Les 3 mois qui suivent : Formation artisanale numérique, production initiale des objets en bambou.  En fin les 2 à 3 mois : Lancement de la plateforme de vente, suivi-évaluation, et ajustements basés sur les premiers retours.
SDGs addressed: SDG 1 (No Poverty);SDG 8 (Decent Work and Economic Growth);SDG 13 (Climate Action);
Desired impact:
Notre engagement quotidien est de transformer la société en monde meilleur où tous les habitats ressentent et goûtent sur les bienfaits d’un bon climat. Apporter une réponse à un besoin de la Communauté, et s’engager à anéantir les ennemis qui bloquent la communauté au développement durable. Grâce à cette fameuse initiative que nous avons commencée, tous les habitants de notre communauté prennent au sérieux la protection de l’environnement. Les objectifs de la solution sont de promouvoir l’autonomisation économique des réfugiés et de la communauté hôte à faible revenu par l’artisanat en bambou , de lutter contre l’érosion et restaurer l’écosystème local, de stimuler une économie numérique verte et inclusive basée sur la transformation du bambou et de créer des opportunités d’emplois verts pour les jeunes et les femmes.  
Les impacts réalisés ou attendus (quantifiables)seront que plus de 150 femmes réfugiées et locales seront formées à la fabrication de produits artisanaux (paniers, nattes, balais), la création de micro revenus pour les familles via la vente des produits artisanaux. Nous prévoyons aussi la création de 15 à 20 emplois directs à travers la future unité de fabrication de cure-dents en bambou et aussi le renforcement de la cohésion sociale entre réfugiés et population hôte.
Key technologies: Comme le monde évolué avec la technologie de l’Intelligence Artificielle, notre solution utilise des outils numériques pour la modélisation et le design des produits artisanaux en bambou (nattes, paniers, objets éco-responsables). La plateforme mobile/web de formation et de vente (création d’une plateforme numérique et la commercialisation des produits en ligne (e-commerce local ou régional)). Nous utilisons les outils de collecte de données comme de tablettes/smartphones avec applications mobiles (ex. KoboToolbox, ODK) pour suivre les bambous plantés, les formations, la production et l'impact environnemental. Ainsi le IA basique (future phase) par l’Intégration envisagée de recommandations personnalisées pour les formations ou la vente via une IA légère analysant les profils utilisateurs.
Unique Characteristics: Les caractéristiques uniques et différenciées de notre solution sont d’abord l’intégration écosystémique ce qui rend la solution reliant la protection de l’environnement (recyclage de bambous pour lutter contre l’érosion) à l’autonomisation économique (transformation artisanale du bambou) et la création d’une chaîne de production complète, depuis la plantation du bambou jusqu’à la fabrication et commercialisation de produits (nattes, paniers, balais, cure-dents), entièrement locale et durable. Autres faits c’est l’inclusion des groupes vulnérables qui sont les bénéficiaires des femmes réfugiées, jeunes sans emploi et membres de communautés hôtes à faible revenu, favorisant la cohésion sociale. Ainsi le modèle de financement hybride basé sur les revenus générés par la vente des produits plus subventions ponctuelles et collaborations en nature avec des partenaires locaux (associations, autorités, coopératives agricoles).
Sustainable Change: Notre solution vise un changement systémique durable en intégrant des dimensions environnementales, économiques et sociales. Suivant la théorie du changement, nous avons fait le départ au problème initial sur la vulnérabilité environnementale, chômage des jeunes, marginalisation des réfugiés et des communautés hôtes à faible revenu. Les actions clés réalisées sont le reboisement en bambou. La formation artisanale, transformation numérique, création d'une chaîne de valeur locale ce qui nous amènera notre idée aux résultats immédiats la protection de l’environnement, création d’emplois verts, autonomisation économique et aussi l’inclusion sociale, développement d’une économie verte locale, résilience climatique. Les effets de suivi souhaités sont la réduction de l’érosion et protection des ressources naturelles, la création de micro-entreprises artisanales autour du bambou (paniers, nattes, cure-dents, etc.), l’autonomisation durable des jeunes et des et le renforcement de la cohésion sociale. Ainsi la solution peut être reproduite dans plusieurs zones rurales avec des conditions similaires.
Funding Sources: Lors des précédentes implémentations, la solution a été principalement financée par le contributions internes de l’organisation « Agir Pour l’Environnement » (fonds propres et bénévolat des membres) , les dons de particuliers locaux sensibilisés à la cause environnementale et sociale , le soutien en nature de partenaires locaux (terrains, matériel de base, espace de formation), l'appuis ponctuels d’organisations communautaires et de leaders locaux et le service d'innovation de la HCR edition 2024
Testimonials and Endorsements: Nous avons besoin de collaborer positivement avec les parties prenantes de la solution pour une économie numérique inclusive  pour la réussite meilleure. Pour la réussite totale de ce projet nous aurons toujours besoin de l'appui du UNIDO, l'appui moral et matériel du UNIDO nous serait très nécessaire pour la réussite. Un accompagnement en visibilité, plaidoyer et mise en réseau avec d’autres acteurs humanitaires serait aussi utile pour élargir l’impact et assurer la sérénité de l’initiative.
Further comments/feedback: Nous prévoyons de collaborer activement avec les parties prenantes concernées, notamment les leaders des communautés, les autorités locales, les services du UNIDO, les ONG partenaires et les représentants de la communauté hôte. Leur implication dans la planification, la mise en œuvre et l’évaluation du projet garantira une meilleure appropriation, une coordination efficace et un impact durable.
Primary thematic focus area: MSME Empowerment & Local Digital Innovation
Summary: BambooTech is a digital transformation project aimed at empowering low-income communities in Burundi by combining bamboo craft with digital tools, promoting eco-friendly entrepreneurship and local economic resilience.

Title: MIGSens: Smart Nanosensor Network for Real-Time Air Quality Monitoring
Subtitle: Affordable AI & IoT-driven nanosensor solution for continuous indoor/outdoor air quality monitoring, empowering communities and industries with real-time insights.

The system is compact, energy-efficient, and encrypted, ensuring secure, scalable deployment. Partnerships span R&D institutions, environmental agencies, NGOs, and industrial actors, with a model focused on co-creation, compliance with IP65/RoHS, and integration into local ecosystems.

•	Democratize access to real-time, accurate air quality data.
•	Enable proactive public health and environmental decisions.
•	Reduce environmental and economic losses from pollution.
Key Achievements:
•	Multiplexed nanosensor detection of multiple pollutants.
•	Integration of AI-driven analytics and VR visualization for policy and industry use.
•	Potential to prevent contamination-related losses and improve community health indicators.
Key technologies:
•	Nanosensor multiplexing for multi-gas and particulate detection
•	AI predictive modeling & analytics
•	IoT data acquisition and secure transmission
•	VR dashboards for immersive data interpretation

Title: Turning Waste into Wealth: Smart Recycling for Greener Communities
Subtitle: Innovative waste solutions transforming trash into resources, boosting recycling rates, creating jobs, and building cleaner, greener, and more sustainable communities.
Problem Statement: Namibia faces low recycling rates, overflowing landfills, and poor waste segregation, leading to pollution, health risks, and lost economic value from recyclable materials
Solution Overview:
Our solution integrates smart recycling systems, community engagement, and strategic partnerships to address waste challenges in a sustainable manner.
How It Works
We deploy Reverse Vending Machines (RVMs) and a waste management mobile app to incentivize recycling through rewards. Communities deposit recyclables, such as plastic bottles, cans, and glass, into RVMs, which sort and record waste using barcode and material recognition technology. Users earn points redeemable for cash, airtime, or goods. The waste app provides collection schedules, drop-off points, and recycling tips.
Methodologies & Technologies
RVM Technology: Barcode scanning, material detection, and secure waste storage.
Mobile App: Cloud-based platform for real-time data collection, tracking, and user engagement.
Data Analytics: Waste volume monitoring for efficiency and policy insights.
Community Education: Awareness campaigns and school programs to promote behavior change.

Partnerships & Collaboration Models
Municipal Councils: Provide placement sites for RVMs and support public waste awareness.
Private Sector: Partner with retailers for reward redemption and with recycling companies for waste processing.
Civil Society Organizations (CSOs): Lead community training and awareness initiatives.
Investors & Donors: Fund technology scaling and expansion into more towns.
This model creates a closed-loop recycling ecosystem, turning waste into economic value while protecting the environment.
Solution Provider(s): Municipal Councils: Provide placement sites for RVMs and support public waste awareness. Private Sector: Partner with retailers for reward redemption and with recycling companies for waste processing. Civil Society Organizations (CSOs): Lead community training and awareness initiatives. Investors & Donors: Fund technology scaling and expansion into more towns.
Implementation location(s): Global Implementation Examples ,Stockholm, Sweden – Nationwide RVM network in supermarkets.  Berlin, Germany – Deposit-return system achieving over 90% bottle return rates.  Sydney, Australia – “Return and Earn” RVM program in public spaces.  Tokyo, Japan – Smart vending-linked recycling machines in train stations.  Cape Town, South Africa – Pilot RVM projects in retail chains.  Toronto, Canada – Reward-based recycling kiosks in malls and community centers.  Singapore – “Recycle N Save” machines rewarding transit credits.  London, UK – Public RVM trials in transport hubs and parks
Duration to pilot in a new geography: 5 months
SDGs addressed: SDG 9 (Industry, Innovation, and Infrastructure);SDG 11 (Sustainable Cities and Communities);SDG 13 (Climate Action);
Desired impact:
Solution Objectives
Increase Namibia’s recycling rate from under 20% to over 50% within 5 years.
Reduce waste sent to landfills by at least 40%, cutting methane and CO₂ emissions.
Create sustainable green jobs and income opportunities in waste collection, sorting, and recycling.
Empower communities through education and incentives to adopt responsible waste habits.

Key Achievements / Expected Impacts (based on similar global models)
Waste Diversion: 100–150 tons of recyclable waste recovered annually per 20 RVMs deployed.
GHG Reductions: Estimated 200–300 tons CO₂-equivalent emissions avoided each year.
Employment: 15–30 direct jobs and 50+ indirect jobs created per region through collection, logistics, and recycling operations.
Community Engagement: 60–80% participation rate in targeted towns through incentive-based recycling.
Economic Value Recovery: Potential U$500,000–U$1 million worth of recyclable material returned into the supply chain annually.
Key technologies:
Reverse Vending Machines (RVMs)
Barcode Scanning & Material Recognition: Uses optical sensors and AI-powered image recognition to identify and sort recyclable materials.
Automated Sorting & Compaction: Ensures efficient storage and transport readiness.
IoT (Internet of Things) Integration
Real-time data transmission from RVMs to a central dashboard for monitoring waste volumes, machine status, and usage patterns.
GPS tracking for optimizing collection routes.

Mobile App & Cloud Platform
User interface for locating RVMs, tracking rewards, and receiving recycling tips.
Cloud-based storage for waste data analytics and reporting.

Data Analytics & Reporting Tools
Generates insights on recycling behavior, material recovery rates, and environmental impact.
Supports evidence-based policy and planning for municipalities.

Digital Rewards System
Points-based reward system redeemable via mobile money, airtime, or partnered retailers.
Secure payment integration to encourage participation.
Unique Characteristics:
Unique / Differentiated Characteristics

Incentive-Driven Recycling
Combines Reverse Vending Machines with a reward-based model that gives communities tangible benefits (cash, airtime, goods) for recycling, directly motivating participation.

Tech-Enabled Waste Management

RVMs and the mobile platform can be deployed in stages from small community hubs to national networks without heavy infrastructure demands.

Revenue-Generating Sustainability
Unlike donor-dependent waste programs, it combines recyclable sales revenue, corporate sponsorships, and retailer partnerships to remain financially viable.

Provides municipalities and policymakers with accurate waste data, enabling better environmental strategies and measurable impact reporting.

Title: Responsible AI for Clinical Discharge Summaries
Subtitle: AI-powered tool cutting discharge time by 50%+ and improving patient safety in Kenyan hospitals.
Problem Statement: Kenya’s public hospitals face a major workflow bottleneck: discharge documentation often exceeds 45 minutes per patient, reducing clinical capacity, driving burnout, and contributing to preventable readmissions. At Machakos Level 5 Hospital, baseline studies show 73% of discharges lack ICD-11 coding, 68% omit medication instructions, and 81% fail to include follow-up plans. Existing AI solutions are unsuitable for Kenya due to high bandwidth demands, lack of ICD-11 alignment, and non-compliance with Kenya’s Data Protection Act.
Solution Overview:
We propose Africa’s first AI-assisted discharge documentation tool, built for low-resource healthcare environments. The solution integrates Retrieval-Augmented Generation (RAG), Large Language Models (LLMs), and Medbook’s AphiaOne HMIS, which is deployed in 80+ facilities serving over 3 million lives.

Methodologies & Technologies: AI tuned to East African clinical language, ICD-11 coding integration, offline-first design for low-bandwidth settings, embedded ethics oversight.

Partnerships & Collaboration Models: Developed with Machakos County Government, co-designed with clinicians, governed by a multi-stakeholder AI Ethics Committee, integrated into AphiaOne HMIS for immediate scalability.
Impact: 50%+ time reduction, >90% coding accuracy, 25%+ fewer readmissions, and $92K/year cost savings per hospital.
Solution Provider(s): Medbook Kenya Limited – Digital health company with 10+ years’ experience, ISO 27001-certified infrastructure, and deployment across 80+ healthcare facilities in East Africa.  Machakos County Government – Public health implementation partner.  Clinical Advisory Board – Practicing clinicians from Machakos Level 5 Hospital.  AI Ethics Committee – Oversight from legal, privacy, clinical, and civil society experts.
Duration to pilot in a new geography: 6–9 months.
SDGs addressed: SDG 3 (Good Health and Well-being);SDG 5 (Gender Equality);SDG 9 (Industry, Innovation, and Infrastructure);
Desired impact:
Objectives: Cut discharge documentation time by 50%+, improve ICD-11 coding accuracy to >90%, reduce preventable readmissions by 25%, train 100+ clinicians in responsible AI.

Key Achievements: Projected $92K/year savings per hospital, improved patient outcomes, stronger retention of healthcare workers, enhanced gender equity (targeting ≥50% female participation in training).
Key technologies: AI (RAG + LLMs), health informatics, ICD-11 medical coding, offline-first architecture for low-connectivity environments.
Unique Characteristics: Localized AI model trained on East African health data; ICD-11 alignment; works offline; ethical AI governance structure; direct integration into an already deployed HMIS across 80+ facilities, enabling rapid scale.
Sustainable Change: By freeing clinicians from excessive paperwork, the solution increases time for patient care, improves outcomes, and boosts job satisfaction. Financial sustainability is ensured via a SaaS model ($154/month per facility) and county cost-sharing. Policy alignment with Kenya’s Digital Health Strategy supports national rollout and replication across LMICs.
Funding Sources: Grant support, Medbook’s internal R&D budget, in-kind infrastructure and licensing contributions, county health partnerships.
Testimonials and Endorsements: “By reducing paperwork time, this innovation gives us more time to focus on patients, which is exactly what our healthcare system needs.” – Chief Medical Officer, Machakos Level 5 Hospital
Further comments/feedback: This project showcases how localized, ethical AI can address systemic inefficiencies in LMIC healthcare, strengthening both digital and health equity while providing a blueprint for global replication.
Primary thematic focus area: Inclusive Digital Innovation Skills & Entrepreneurial Talent Development
Summary: This AI-powered tool addresses inefficiencies in discharge documentation at Kenyan hospitals, reducing time by over 50%, improving coding accuracy, and enhancing patient outcomes. The solution is innovative and tailored to the local healthcare environment, but scalability and long-term success will depend on funding and broader institutional partnerships for wider adoption.

Title: MPost: Mobile-Linked Digital Addressing for Inclusive Trade
Subtitle: Transforming mobile numbers into verifiable digital addresses to unlock MSME growth and supply chain resilience.
Problem Statement:
How can Africa unlock inclusive growth when millions of individuals and MSMEs still lack formal physical addresses, cutting them off from e-commerce, logistics, and formal financial services?

Across many African countries, the absence of formal addressing systems is more than an inconvenience, it is a structural barrier to participation in the modern economy. Without verifiable addresses, MSMEs and individuals are excluded from reliable last-mile delivery networks, resulting in frequent delivery failures, lost parcels, and frustrated customers. These inefficiencies not only inflate operational costs for businesses but also erode consumer trust, limiting repeat transactions and business scalability.

Moreover, market access becomes a privilege for those in well-mapped urban centers, while rural and peri-urban communities remain underserved. The inability to reliably receive goods or services means missed opportunities for trade, employment, and financial inclusion. For MSMEs, this translates into reduced sales potential, an inability to integrate into regional supply chains, and diminished competitiveness in the digital economy. Over time, the problem compounds, reinforcing economic inequality and slowing the pace of sustainable development.
Solution Overview:
MPost is a digital addressing solution that transforms any mobile phone number into a verifiable, mappable digital address, enabling individuals and MSMEs to reliably participate in the digital economy. Once registered, a user’s mobile number is linked to a preferred pick-up or delivery location, which can be a postal facility, service station, smart locker, or partner outlet. This digital address becomes the bridge between virtual transactions and physical fulfillment, ensuring that goods, services, and official correspondence can be securely and accurately delivered anywhere in the country.

The system is built on a robust technological backbone. Address creation and verification are powered by a secure AWS cloud infrastructure that ensures scalability, high availability, and compliance with global data protection standards. API integrations enable MPost to plug directly into platforms like the M-Pesa Super App, allowing seamless user onboarding, payment processing, and service access. IoT-enabled smart lockers from Fez Logistics provide secure, remotely monitored storage points, while data analytics tools optimize routes, reduce delivery failures, and generate operational insights for partners.

The MPost model operates through a multi-sector partnership ecosystem that combines public trust infrastructure, private sector efficiency, and technology innovation. The Postal Corporation of Kenya provides a nationwide network of postal facilities as reliable access points. Safaricom PLC, through M-Pesa, offers a digital entry point for registration and transactions, making MPost accessible even on basic mobile devices via USSD. Rubis Energy Kenya expands access by hosting parcel collection and drop-off points at service stations across the country. Vipi delivers efficient metropolitan coverage in urban centers, while Buupass connects long-distance routes to rural and peri-urban regions. Fez Logistics secures last-mile delivery through its smart locker network, and AWS hosts the technology infrastructure that powers MPost’s core functions.

Through this integration of simple mobile technology, scalable cloud infrastructure, and a diversified partner network, MPost is able to eliminate a systemic barrier to economic participation, reduce last-mile inefficiencies, and create a sustainable model for inclusive digital trade.
Solution Provider(s): Safaricom PLC – Kenya’s leading telecommunications and mobile money service provider enabling direct user access to MPost through the M-Pesa Super App (Telecommunications, Fintech), Postal Corporation of Kenya (PCK) – National postal service offering an extensive network of postal facilities as parcel collection points and customer service hubs (Public Sector, Postal Services), Rubis Energy Kenya – Retail fuel service company expanding MPost’s access points via nationwide service stations (Private Sector, Retail Distribution), Vipi – Metropolitan delivery company providing efficient last-mile solutions within urban centers (Logistics, Last-Mile Delivery), Buupass – Intercity transport and logistics platform enabling long-distance parcel delivery to rural and peri-urban regions (Transport, Rural Connectivity), Fez Logistics – Provider of IoT-enabled smart lockers with remote monitoring for secure package storage and retrieval (Logistics Technology, IoT), Amazon Web Services (AWS) – Cloud services provider hosting MPost’s digital addressing platform to ensure scalability, security, and high availability (Cloud Computing, Data Infrastructure).
Implementation timeline(s): Kenya from 2016, Rwanda from 2023, Burundi from 2024
Duration to pilot in a new geography: 6 months
SDGs addressed: SDG 9 (Industry, Innovation, and Infrastructure);SDG 10 (Reduced Inequalities);SDG 8 (Decent Work and Economic Growth);
Desired impact:
Solution Objectives:
MPost aims to close the digital economic divide by giving every individual and MSME a verifiable, mobile-linked digital address, regardless of location. The goal is to transform addressability from a privilege of well-mapped urban zones into a universal economic right, enabling inclusive participation in trade, logistics, finance, and e-governance.

Key Achievements & Impacts:
1. Over 500,000 unique digital addresses issued, each unlocking formal delivery, e-commerce, and financial services access for previously excluded communities.
2. 30% average reduction in last-mile delivery failures for partnered logistics providers, leading to significant cost savings and increased customer trust.
3. Expanded economic participation for MSMEs, with a recorded 25% increase in repeat transactions among registered merchants due to reliable delivery fulfillment.
4. Direct and indirect employment generation in urban and rural logistics chains, from last-mile riders to smart locker technicians.
5. Inclusive access points in underserved areas, with 40% of MPost’s active addresses in rural and peri-urban locations that were previously unmapped in formal systems.
Key technologies: MPost integrates mobile identity mapping with cloud-based infrastructure to deliver secure, scalable address creation. The system is built on AWS cloud hosting for high availability and compliance with global data protection standards. IoT-enabled smart lockers from Fez Logistics allow secure package storage and remote monitoring. API-driven integration enables MPost to seamlessly embed into M-Pesa for in-app registration and payment. Data analytics and geolocation mapping power route optimization, delivery verification, and service accessibility reports for partners.
Unique Characteristics: MPost’s uniqueness lies in its ability to convert a ubiquitous asset — a mobile number — into a trusted, government-recognized address without requiring costly physical mapping infrastructure. Its multi-sector partnership model bridges public postal networks, private retail stations, urban couriers, rural transport providers, and technology enablers in a unified ecosystem. This allows nationwide coverage from day one, without building new infrastructure. The business model is lean and transaction-driven, making it self-sustaining while lowering the adoption barrier for users. The solution’s design is inherently inclusive, requiring no smartphone ownership and operating on USSD for basic handset users.
Sustainable Change: The absence of a formal address is a foundational barrier to economic inclusion. By solving this once, MPost unlocks multiple downstream benefits: e-commerce becomes accessible, delivery networks expand profitably into new regions, MSMEs can access credit and insurance, and governments can extend essential services with precision. Over time, the network of mobile-linked addresses creates a national digital identity layer for location, enabling more efficient urban planning, climate adaptation logistics, and cross-border trade facilitation. As adoption scales, the cost of delivery in rural areas decreases, market participation increases, and inequalities between urban and rural communities narrow. The result is a self-reinforcing cycle: more addressability leads to more transactions, which leads to more services and investments in underserved areas, creating long-term, system-level transformation.

Title: SheConnects: Empowering Rural Women Through Digital Inclusion
Subtitle: An innovative offline-first, device-accessible, bias-free digital skills entrepreneurship platform for Liberia
Problem Statement: In Liberia, the gender digital divide remains a major barrier to women’s economic empowerment. Rural women, in particular, face compounded challenges: limited access to smartphones, unreliable or nonexistent internet connectivity, low digital literacy, and scarce opportunities for mentorship or marketplace participation. Traditional digital skills programs often assume personal device ownership and consistent online access—conditions that exclude a vast majority of women in underserved areas. Without localized, culturally relevant training and tools that work offline, these women are left disconnected from the skills, networks, and markets they need to thrive in a rapidly digitizing economy.
Solution Overview:
SheConnects tackles Liberia’s persistent gender digital divide by providing rural women with accessible, engaging, and sustainable digital skills training. Using gamified, offline-capable learning modules delivered through shared, solar-powered devices at strategically placed community hubs, the program ensures access even in areas without reliable electricity or internet.
Beyond basic training, SheConnects integrates AI-powered, bias-free career guidance, enabling women to identify viable career paths and entrepreneurial opportunities based on their strengths and local market demand. A built-in mentorship network connects participants with experienced female role models, fostering peer learning and confidence building.
Direct marketplace integration empowers women to monetize their skills immediately—whether through remote work, e-commerce, or local service offerings—creating a tangible link between training and income generation. By focusing on localized content, cultural relevance, and low-barrier access, SheConnects ensures women without smartphones, formal education, or prior digital exposure can still participate, thrive, and drive community transformation.

By providing localized, offline-capable training and mentorship, SheConnects will create a generation of digitally literate women who can confidently navigate technology, start and grow businesses, and compete for jobs in emerging sectors.
