Title: Mkulima AI: Offline Swahili Agri-Tech for Inclusive Rural Prosperity
Subtitle: Empowering Tanzania’s smallholder farmers with offline, AI-driven crop guidance in Swahili, bridging the digital gap and boosting rural food security.
Problem Statement: Smallholder farmers in Tanzania, who produce over 70% of the nation’s food, face systemic challenges: unreliable internet, limited access to agronomic expertise, and rising pest and disease outbreaks that cause up to 40% yield losses annually. High input costs, fluctuating market prices, and climate-induced weather variability deepen rural poverty. Existing digital tools often fail in low-connectivity zones, excluding millions from the digital economy. As Julius Nyerere said, “If real development is to take place, the people have to be involved”—yet without inclusive, accessible technology, these farmers remain locked out of the knowledge and market systems essential for prosperity.
Solution Overview:
Mkulima AI is a fully offline, Swahili-based mobile application designed to empower smallholder farmers with AI-driven, stage-by-stage crop production guidance. It supports 11 major Tanzanian crops, covering land preparation, planting, pest and disease detection, harvesting, storage, and post-harvest handling, ensuring localized, accessible knowledge delivery without dependence on internet connectivity.
How it works:
•	Farmers install Mkulima AI on smartphones through local training sessions.
•	The app uses an AI-powered diagnostic engine (92% accuracy in pilot testing) to identify crop diseases via photo analysis.
•	Content is fully available offline in Swahili, tailored to the farmer’s crop, region, and seasonal calendar.
•	Step-by-step guidance helps optimize input use, reduce losses, and improve yields, with data collected for continuous improvement.
Methodologies & Technologies:
•	AI-powered image recognition for pest/disease diagnosis.
•	Offline-first architecture ensuring full functionality without internet.
•	Human-centered design for rural usability, tested with farmers in Morogoro and Arusha.
•	Localized agronomic content aligned with national agricultural guidelines.
Partnerships & Collaboration Models:
Currently, Mkulima AI is collaborating with Sustainable Agriculture Tanzania (SAT) to launch the pilot phase for 500 farmers, combining SAT’s grassroots network with our technology. The model involves:
•	Capacity building through farmer field schools and local trainers.
•	Co-design workshops with farmers for continuous feature refinement.
•	Joint monitoring & evaluation for measuring adoption, impact, and scalability.
Solution Provider(s): Currently, Mkulima AI operates as the primary solution provider. While no formal partners are engaged at this stage, we actively seek strategic collaborations with agricultural research institutions, farmer organizations, NGOs, and development agencies to enhance content validation, distribution, and long-term sustainability.
Implementation location(s): Morogoro Region, Tanzania; Arusha Region, Tanzania
Implementation timeline(s): Pilot Start: May 2024  Pilot End: August 2025  Duration:  16 months pilot in Morogoro and Arusha regions with 500 farmers trained and supported.
Duration to pilot in a new geography: 6 months – including 2 months for training and app installation, 2 months for field monitoring, and 2 months for data collection and refinement.
SDGs addressed: SDG 13 (Climate Action);SDG 9 (Industry, Innovation, and Infrastructure);SDG 2 (Zero Hunger);
Desired impact:
Solution Objectives:
•	Empower 4,000+ smallholder farmers in underserved rural areas with AI-driven agricultural decision-making tools.
•	Reduce crop loss from pests and diseases through 92% accurate AI disease detection.
•	Lower input costs by at least 30% through precise recommendations and improved resource efficiency.
•	Strengthen resilience of rural farming systems by ensuring access to market prices, weather alerts, and best practices offline.

Key Achievements (Pilot):
•	Trained 500 farmers in Morogoro & Arusha.
•	Achieved 92% accuracy in plant disease identification.
•	Improved yield outcomes by 15% in monitored farms within 3 months.
•	Demonstrated offline capability to serve internet-poor communities.
Key technologies:
Key Technologies Used
•	Artificial Intelligence (AI): Training Deep Machine Learning Models For real-time plant disease detection and tailored agricultural advice.
•	Computer Vision: Image recognition for crop disease identification.
•	Natural Language Processing (NLP): Swahili language interface for inclusivity.
•	Offline-first Mobile Technology: Ensures full functionality without internet access.
Unique Characteristics:
Mkulima AI is the first AI-powered agricultural advisory system in Tanzania built entirely in Swahili and designed to function fully offline, enabling access for farmers in remote, internet-poor areas. Unlike generic agricultural apps, it:
•	Integrates AI-driven disease detection (92% accuracy) with market price alerts, weather forecasts, and crop-specific best practices.
•	Uses a farmer-centered co-design model, developed through field feedback from local smallholders.
•	Supports 11 key crops crucial to East Africa’s food security, from maize and rice to coffee and grapes.
•	Operates on a low-cost, scalable deployment model via village-based training, making it sustainable in low-resource settings.
•	Positions agro-input dealers, NGOs, and government agencies as collaborative stakeholders in both knowledge distribution and market access.
Sustainable Change:
If rural farmers gain access to accurate, localized, and timely agricultural advice in their own language, without needing internet, then they will make better farming decisions, leading to increased yields, reduced losses, and improved incomes.
Mkulima AI drives systemic change by:
1.	Breaking the Digital Divide: Reaching farmers currently excluded from digital agriculture solutions.
2.	Improving Food Security: Reducing pest and disease losses by up to 40% in high-risk crops.
3.	Boosting Rural Economies: Lowering input costs and increasing productivity, creating surplus for local markets.
4.	Strengthening Climate Resilience: Delivering weather-based alerts and crop management advice to adapt to climate shocks.
5.	Fostering Knowledge Transfer: Equipping rural communities with lifelong digital skills and sustainable agricultural practices.
Funding Sources:
To date, Mkulima AI has been entirely self-funded by the founder, with in-kind collaboration from Sustainable Agriculture Tanzania (SAT) during the pilot phase for training 500 farmers.
No institutional or external funding has yet been secured, underscoring both the resourcefulness of the development process and the urgent need for strategic investment to scale.
The limited reach (only 500 out of an estimated 4 million smallholder farmers in Tanzania) is a direct reflection of funding constraints, yet it also demonstrates the untapped potential for impact when adequate resources are provided.

Title: Digital Platform Empowering Women & SMEs in the Circular Green Economy
Subtitle: Empowering women and small businesses with digital tools to turn waste oil into income, stronger local communities, and green energy
Problem Statement: In Egypt and beyond, used cooking oil (UCO) — often dubbed the ‘new liquid gold’ — is largely discarded, leading to water contamination, clogged infrastructure, and lost value from this renewable feedstock. Despite global demand for UCO-driven biofuels surging, the main challenge lies in the absence of efficient collection mechanisms from households, restaurants, and SMEs. Tagaddod bridges this gap with its ‘Green Pan’ digital solution, enabling clean, traceable UCO collection through technology-enabled logistics, empowering communities while securing feedstock for sustainable energy
Solution Overview:
Through an intuitive mobile application "Green Pan" and offline-accessible channels such as the hotline, households, food vendors, and SMEs can schedule the collection of their used cooking oil. Requests are digitally matched with trained women collectors and local micro-entrepreneurs, creating a transparent and traceable last-mile logistics network. By diverting UCO from being illegally resold to restaurants and street food vendors, the service safeguards public health and prevents water contamination. Collected oil is verified, safely stored, and exported to European partners for conversion into sustainable biodiesel. Participants, especially women, earn income for each collection, ensuring both environmental and social benefits.

Methodologies & Technologies
Tagaddod leverages an inclusive, multi-channel digital platform to make participation possible regardless of connectivity or literacy levels, combining a consumer-facing app, and hotline services. This ensures that urban households, rural communities, and informal vendors can easily schedule collections. 

With a data-driven logistics backbone uses GPS-enabled routing, digital weight capture, and real-time dashboards to optimize collector efficiency, track environmental and social impact, and maintain full traceability from source to processing facility. Advanced machine learning and data modelling are integrated into operational systems like the Collectors App, GAP, and Janet, enabling predictive collection patterns, demand forecasting, and optimized resource allocation. This technology underpins a last-mile logistics model that connects waste generators with trained women collectors and local micro-entrepreneurs.

The process transforms a major public health and environmental hazard—improperly disposed or illegally resold used cooking oil—into a high-value, ISCC-certified feedstock for European biodiesel markets. By diverting UCO from drains and the informal resale market, Tagaddod reduces water contamination risks, improves community health outcomes, and prevents adulterated food oil from reaching consumers.

Finally, incentives and environmental awareness campaigns foster long-term behavioral change, turning waste collection into a socially valued and financially rewarding activity for participating households and women collectors.

Partnerships & Collaboration Models

Tagaddod’s impact is driven by strong partnerships across the value chain. Women-led microenterprises and SMEs handle last-mile UCO collection, supported with training, digital tools, and safety gear. Long-term agreements with European biodiesel producers secure stable demand and revenue, while collaborations with development partners like CFYE provide capacity building, funding, and strategic support to expand women’s economic participation.
Solution Provider(s): Challenge Fund for Youth Employment (CFYE) – International development initiative supporting youth employment through capacity building, funding, and skills development (International Development, Employment).
Implementation timeline(s): 2017 – Concept Development & Pilot Phase Shifted from traditional UCO sourcing to a technology-enabled collection model. Early pilots tested digital tracking, GPS routing, and partnerships with local micro-entrepreneurs.  August 2021 – Public Launch of Green Pan App Introduced the Green Pan mobile app, enabling households and SMEs to schedule UCO pickup  2023 – Operational Optimization & Scalability Implemented advanced demand estimation clustering and auto-scheduling algorithms
Duration to pilot in a new geography: 9-12 months
SDGs addressed: SDG 8 (Decent Work and Economic Growth);SDG 13 (Climate Action);SDG 12 (Responsible Consumption and Production);
Desired impact:
Solution Objectives

1- Divert large volumes of used cooking oil (UCO) from unsafe reuse and waterway contamination.
2- Provide businesses with a seamless, traceable UCO disposal solution through the Green Pan app.
3- Supply certified, high-quality UCO to the global biodiesel industry, supporting clean energy transitions.
4- Strengthen the circular economy by transforming waste into a valuable export commodity.

in Egypt, Tagaddod prevents ~2,000 tons of CO₂ emissions/month through UCO collection from 2,000+ businesses and 40,000 households.
A Saudi B2B pilot could avert 20–30 tons CO₂/month and recover 100–200 tons of UCO from 500 businesses in 6 months. Technology-driven logistics deliver ~20% cost savings, enabling profitability within 6–9 months. That would create approximate of 500 job within the first year.
Key technologies:
1- Artificial Intelligence (AI) & Machine Learning
Janet AI: A geospatial growth engine that optimizes demand targeting, collector allocation, and warehouse management for maximum profitability.
Blitz ML: A demand estimator predicting UCO generation for precise scheduling.
ZULU ML: Fraud detection system ensuring data integrity and compliance.


2-GPS-enabled fleet tracking monitors vehicle location, fuel use, and trip progress in real time, enabling dynamic route adjustments and lower operational costs.

3- Cloud-Based Infrastructure
Auto-scaling cloud systems with performance monitoring, real-time alerts, and secure authentication to ensure platform reliability and scalability.

4- Mobile Applications
Collectors App: For field teams to log volumes, upload verification photos, and sync data instantly.

5- Customer-Facing App/Web: For B2B clients to schedule pickups, track service history, and receive notifications.

6- GAP: Real-time tracking service integrating operations, inventory, and campaigns.

7- Digital Traceability & Compliance
QR-based chain-of-custody system tracking each liter of UCO from pickup to export, ensuring ISCC certification compliance and providing auditable reports.

8- Data Analytics & LiveOps Dashboard
Centralized dashboards provide real-time KPIs, operational metrics, and environmental impact reporting for continuous optimization
Unique Characteristics:
Our solution is innovative because it combines advanced technology, social inclusion, and circular economy principles in a single, scalable model:

Technological Breakthroughs: AI-driven demand targeting and UCO prediction, IoT-enabled fleet tracking, and a QR-based traceability system ensure efficiency, transparency, and compliance with international sustainability standards.

Inclusive Business Model: Empowers women to work from home as UCO collectors, while establishing B2B partnerships with businesses for a reliable supply chain.

Impact-Driven Operations: Real-time data allows performance-based resource allocation, turning UCO waste into a valuable export for biodiesel production.

End-to-End Integration: Fully digital collection, verification, traceability, and client engagement create unmatched efficiency, replicability, and profitability.
Sustainable Change:
Theory of Change: Deploying this technology-driven model generates measurable environmental, social, and economic outcomes, creating a self-sustaining, scalable system that benefits communities, businesses, and the planet. Which will result in: 

1- Environmental Impact: Significant reduction in CO₂ emissions and waterway contamination.
2- Economic Inclusion: Creation of jobs, especially for women, and new income streams for households and businesses.
3- Industry Transformation: Establishes a scalable, replicable model for traceable, sustainable waste-to-energy supply chains.
4- Policy & Market Influence: Demonstrates the economic and environmental value of circular economy practices, encouraging wider adoption and regulatory support.

Recently, the Challenge Fund for Youth Employment (CFYE) provided funding to support a specific expansion project. However, the company primarily relies on revenue generated from its core operations to drive growth and scale its impact.

Title: Her Tech Journey: AI-Powered Game to Empower Girls in STEM
Subtitle: Interactive AI-based game inspiring and training girls in underrepresented communities in Peru for future STEM careers.
Problem Statement: Girls from underrepresented communities in Peru face systemic barriers to accessing STEM education and digital skills, leading to a persistent gender gap in the digital economy.
Solution Overview:
Her Tech Journey is an AI-powered, story-driven educational game designed to inspire girls aged 12–25 from underrepresented communities to explore STEM pathways. Through interactive challenges, players learn coding fundamentals, problem-solving and entrepreneurship skills.

- Methodologies & Technologies: Gamification, adaptive AI for personalized learning, open-source coding platforms and interactive storytelling.

- Partnerships: Collaboration with local NGOs, schools and international STEM advocacy organizations like AnitaB for outreach and curriculum validation.

- Model: Hybrid approach, withc offline workshops + online AI-driven platform, ensuring access even in low-connectivity areas.
Solution Provider(s): Her Tech Journey (Founder: Valeria Cerpa), Internet Society (ISOC) – Youth Ambassador Network – Global Digital Inclusion, AnitaB.org – Pass It On Fellow – Women in Technology Advocacy, Local grassroots NGOs for community outreach.
Implementation location(s): Arequipa, Peru (pilot workshops); online platform accessible globally.
Implementation timeline(s): Pilot workshops launched in early 2025; ongoing prototype development with beta testing planned for late 2025.
Duration to pilot in a new geography: 6 months (including localization and partnership building)
SDGs addressed: SDG 4 (Quality Education);SDG 5 (Gender Equality);SDG 9 (Industry, Innovation, and Infrastructure);
Desired impact:
Objectives: Reduce gender gap in STEM education in Peru and in Latin America in the future, by providing accessible, engaging and culturally relevant digital learning experiences.

Key Achievements: In pilot workshops, 80% of participants expressed increased interest in STEM careers; 60% completed at least one coding challenge successfully after playing with the game. Partnerships established with 3 local schools and 2 NGOs in Arequipa city.
Key technologies: Unreal Engine for videogame development, Artificial Intelligence for personalized learning paths, gamification frameworks, open-source coding platforms and offline-first app design for low-connectivity environments.
Unique Characteristics:
- Combines AI personalization with storytelling in the game content, creating a tailored tool to local cultures.
- Offline-first design to bridge connectivity gaps.
- Integrates mentorship from real women in STEM into the game narrative.
Sustainable Change:
Her Tech Journey’s Theory of Change: 
Providing early exposure to STEM skills in an engaging and culturally relevant way. The solution builds confidence, digital literacy and career aspirations among Peruvian girls and young women. Over time, this creates a talent pipeline of women engaing more with tech careers and spaces in the area, entering in the industry and leading in the regional digital economy. The game supports fostering inclusive innovation ecosystems and reducing systemic gender inequalities in Latin America in tech.
Funding Sources: The initial development of Her Tech Journey has been funded through personal contributions from the founder and co-founder, in-kind support from local NGOs from Lima and Arequipa (venue, outreach and facilitation) and a micro-grant of $ 1000 USD from AnitaB.org’s Pass It On Fellowship program. Additional resources were provided by volunteer mentors and partners who contributed time, expertise and technical resources.
Testimonials and Endorsements:
"Her Tech Journey was the first time I saw girls from our school truly believe they could work in technology. The mix of games and real-life role models made a huge difference." – STEM Coordinator, Arequipa.

"I had never written code before, but now I want to study engineering because I saw that I can do it." – Participant, 15 years old, Arequipa, Peru.

Title: "SD Academy: Inclusive Digital Learning for the Deaf in Tunisia"
Subtitle: "An intelligent e-learning platform empowering deaf learners in Tunisia with accessible education, skills training, and socio-economic inclusion opportunities."
Problem Statement: "In Tunisia, 95% of deaf individuals are illiterate due to inaccessible education, social stigma, and lack of qualified support. Rural communities face even greater exclusion, limiting opportunities for learning, skills development, and economic participation."
Solution Overview:
How the Solution Works
SD Academy is the first intelligent e-learning platform in Tunisia dedicated to deaf and hard-of-hearing learners. It offers personalized, interactive courses aligned with the national curriculum, delivered in sign language and supported by expert educators, speech therapists, and psychologists. Learners access the platform from home or community centers, reducing geographic and social barriers. Parents receive tailored coaching to support their children’s education, while professional and vocational training modules prepare learners for the job market and entrepreneurial opportunities.

Methodologies and Technologies Used
The platform applies adaptive learning methodologies, combining diagnostic assessments with customized learning paths. It integrates live video sessions, sign language interpretation, and accessible content formats to ensure inclusivity. The system uses data analytics to track progress and improve learning outcomes, with future plans to embed AI-driven recommendations for personalized skill development.

Partnerships and Collaboration Models
SD Academy collaborates with public institutions such as the Ministry of Social Affairs, Ministry of Education, and Ministry of Health to co-fund enrolments, co-develop content, and train specialized staff. Partnerships with NGOs, psychologists, speech therapists, and ICT providers enable content creation.... These collaborations ensure sustainable scaling, knowledge sharing, and alignment with national inclusion strategies.
Solution Provider(s): Ministry of Social Affairs ,Local Sourd Deaf Organizations
Duration to pilot in a new geography: 24 months
SDGs addressed: SDG 4 (Quality Education);SDG 15 (Life on Land);SDG 16 (Peace, Justice, and Strong Institutions);
Desired impact:
Solution Objectives

Reduce illiteracy among deaf and hard-of-hearing individuals in Tunisia by providing accessible, high-quality digital education.

Equip learners with academic, vocational, and entrepreneurial skills to enable socio-economic inclusion.

Empower parents and caregivers through training to better support deaf learners.

Bridge the digital divide for rural and underserved communities by providing remote learning opportunities.

Key Achievements / Expected Impacts

Enroll and support at least 300 learners within 5 years.

Achieve a minimum 60% reduction in illiteracy among enrolled students.

Provide professional and vocational training to at least 150 individuals, with 50% securing employment or starting a business.

Train 200 parents/caregivers in educational support and communication skills.

Establish partnerships with at least 5 public institutions and 10 private/NGO partners to strengthen sustainability and reach.

Extend access to rural areas, potentially covering over 10 governorates by year 5.
Key technologies:
Key Technologies Used
SD Academy leverages a combination of accessible and advanced digital technologies to ensure inclusive and personalized learning for deaf and hard-of-hearing learners:

E-learning Platform Technology – Web-based learning management system (LMS) with integrated video conferencing tools for live, interactive classes.

Sign Language Video Integration – Embedded interpretation and video overlays for all course content to ensure accessibility.

Adaptive Learning Algorithms – Personalized learning paths based on diagnostic assessments and learner progress tracking.

Data Analytics – Collection and analysis of learning data to monitor performance, improve content, and measure impact.

Future AI Integration – Planned use of artificial intelligence to recommend tailored learning activities, track skill development, and automate certain evaluations.

Cloud Hosting & Security – Secure cloud infrastructure with SSL encryption to ensure data privacy and platform reliability.
Unique Characteristics:
First-of-its-kind in Tunisia: The only intelligent e-learning platform dedicated exclusively to deaf and hard-of-hearing learners, creating a new market segment in inclusive digital education.

Holistic Approach: Combines academic education, vocational training, soft skills development, and parental coaching for comprehensive socio-economic inclusion.

Personalized Learning Model: Adaptive learning paths based on detailed diagnostic assessments, delivered by multidisciplinary experts (teachers, speech therapists, psychologists).

Inclusive Technology Design: Courses fully integrated with sign language interpretation, accessible interfaces, and content adapted to various hearing loss profiles.

Innovative Partnership Model: Co-funding schemes with public institutions and collaboration with NGOs, private ICT providers, and health professionals.

Scalability & Replicability: Designed for deployment in rural areas and replication in other North African countries, leveraging cloud technology and mobile accessibility.
Accredited
Sustainable Change:
The deployment of the SD Academy solution is expected to have the following follow-on effects:


Combating Illiteracy and School Dropout: By providing a personalized, online educational platform, the solution aims to re-integrate students into the school system and fight against illiteracy.


Socio-economic Inclusion: The platform will offer professional training adapted to the demands of the job market, which will help learners find a source of income. The mission is to provide a "second chance" for socio-economic inclusion for deaf and mute individuals.



Empowering Parents: The platform will provide parents with better access to information about issues related to their children's disabilities and offer parental coaching sessions. This will lead to a better involvement of parents in their children's education.






Changing Societal Mindsets: A core mission of SD Academy is to change the mentality and prejudices surrounding deaf and mute people.


Becoming a Reference Point: The vision is for SD Academy to become a reference for the education of deaf and mute individuals, initially in Tunisia and later in the Maghreb region, with comprehensive care from early childhood through high school.


Improving Educational Standards: The project seeks to provide content that meets international standards by hiring qualified and specialized personnel, such as professors, speech therapists, and psychologists.



Expanding Accessibility: The company plans to open regional offices in rural areas in the future to be closer to their clients and complement the educational curriculum on the platform.



Building Trust: The project aims to gain accreditation from the state and the trust of parents, becoming a "refuge" for their children.



Addressing the Gap in Services: The platform addresses the limited and outdated professional training options, insufficient qualified staff, and isolation from the outside world found in existing support centers.

It offers personalized, interactive courses with sign language integration, adaptive learning paths, and support from educators, speech therapists, and psychologists. The platform aims to combat illiteracy and provide vocational and academic training to enhance socio-economic inclusion for the deaf community.

Title: Rayon de soleil pour tous
Subtitle: Une solution numérique itinérante pour le développement - l'extension de "l'impact durable d'une solution photovoltaïque" à une commune
Problem Statement:
À Madagascar, la fracture énergétique et numérique constitue un frein majeur au développement social et économique. En 2023, seulement 33,7 % de la population avait accès à l’électricité (Banque mondiale, 2023), laissant plus de 18 millions de Malgaches non électrifiés (Agence internationale de l’énergie, 2024). Le gouvernement s’est fixé pour objectif d’atteindre 67 % d’ici 2030, grâce notamment à des programmes comme le DECIM (Digital and Energy Connectivity for Inclusion in Madagascar), soutenu par la Banque mondiale (2024).
Sur le plan numérique, les inégalités sont tout aussi marquées : seulement 20,6 % des Malgaches avaient accès à internet début 2024 (Datareportal, 2024), et plus de 70 % de la population ne possède pas de smartphone. Ces contraintes limitent l’accès à l’information, à l’éducation et aux opportunités professionnelles, en particulier dans les zones rurales.
Face à cette situation, le projet RSID (Rayon de Soleil, vers un Impact Durable), porté par ACCESMAD en partenariat avec la Fondation Nexans et le Fonds Watt for Change de Valorem, a apporté une première réponse innovante. Dans 18 lycées photovoltaïques, l’installation de systèmes solaires a permis un désenclavement énergétique et l’accès à la médiathèque numérique EDUCMAD, transformant les conditions d’apprentissage pour des milliers d’élèves et enseignants.
Fort de ce succès, il est désormais possible d’exploiter le potentiel créé par RSID pour dépasser le seul cadre éducatif et atteindre une communauté élargie : jeunes non scolarisés, filles et femmes, associations locales, micro-entrepreneurs et autorités communales. C’est l’ambition de ce projet : « Rayon de soleil pour tous » porté par l’ONG EDUCMAD, en partenariat avec ACCESMAD. En tant qu’ONG malgache, EDUCMAD renforce l’ancrage local du projet et facilite son acceptation par les bénéficiaires. Ce projet d’extension repose sur une innovation clé : la valise numérique, un kit normalisé, autonome en énergie et itinérant.
Solution Overview:
La valise numérique itinérante représente bien plus qu’un simple équipement. C’est un outil de connectivité mobile qui peut circuler dans les quartiers, associations, écoles ou centres communautaires. Elle est conçue pour être rechargeable par énergie solaire ou sur secteur, et contient des ressources modulables selon les besoins de la communauté :
•	La médiathèque EDUCMAD pour l’éducation ;
•	Des modules de sensibilisation au genre et à la santé reproductive ;
•	Des contenus pour renforcer la gouvernance locale ;
•	Des ressources pour l’orientation scolaire et professionnelle des jeunes ;
•	Des modules pratiques pour l’entrepreneuriat et l’agriculture.

Cette démarche s’appuie également sur l’expérience de partenaires techniques comme MIARADIA, qui a participé à la confection des valises numériques EDUCMAD. Cette collaboration démontre que la solution est facilement reproductible, adaptée au contexte malgache, et qu’elle permet de mobiliser un réseau d’acteurs locaux et internationaux.
Ainsi, la valise numérique devient le cœur du projet, une innovation qui permet de dépasser la fracture énergétique et numérique, d’accompagner les établissements scolaires déjà équipés RSID, et surtout d’élargir l’accès à la commune entière.

Méthodologie et activités
Le projet sera mis en œuvre en cinq étapes principales :
a.	Conception et normalisation de la valise numérique
Cette étape consiste au développement d’un kit standardisé : un coffre mobile qui contient un serveur et des tablettes, avec une connexion internet mobile lorsque possible. Il est équipé d’un vidéoprojecteur et de ressources hors ligne.
La conception prendra en compte du modèle déjà expérimenté à Ampangabe comme prototype.
b.	Déploiement et planification : 
Nous allons définir un calendrier de visites de collectes des besoins pour chaque quartier de la commune, en collaboration avec les autorités locales et les associations communautaires.
c.	Centralisation et itinérance
Une valise sera centralisée dans la commune, sous la responsabilité des autorités locales et d’EDUCMAD.
La valise circulera dans les écoles, associations, quartiers et espaces communautaires, afin de toucher divers publics.
d.	Déploiement de formations diversifiées
Nous mettrons en place de sessions de formation interactive et pratique, encadrées par des formateurs d'EDUCMAD et des experts locaux. Les thématiques abordées incluront : des modules d’alphabétisation numérique et bureautique, la santé reproductive, l’égalité de genre, la gouvernance locale, l’orientation scolaire et professionnelle, l’entrepreneuriat et l’agriculture.
Les établissements RSID seront toujours accompagnés pour prolonger l’usage de la médiathèque.
e.	Implication des acteurs locaux
Les partenariats comme avec MIARADIA (association locale d’Ampangabe) seront établis et préservés avec d’autres prestataires pour la confection, la maintenance et l’amélioration continue des valises.
Nous formerons également des jeunes et de femmes comme animateurs et techniciens relais.
La commune, quant à elle sera impliquée dès le début du projet. Son équipe sera formée pour assurer progressivement la gestion et la pérennité du dispositif.
Solution Provider(s): EDUCMAD – Porteur principal du projet – ONG malgache spécialisée dans l’éducation numérique et communautaire – Secteur : éducation, inclusion numérique, développement local; ACCESMAD – Co-implémentation et expertise technique – Organisation à but non lucratif œuvrant pour l’accès aux ressources éducatives – Secteur : éducation, énergie solaire, technologies éducatives; Fondation Nexans – Financement et appui à l’électrification – Fondation d’entreprise du groupe Nexans – Secteur : énergie, électrification rurale, mécénat; Valorem – Watt for Change – Financement et soutien à la transition énergétique – Fonds de dotation du groupe Valorem – Secteur : énergies renouvelables, solidarité internationale; MIARADIA – Partenaire technique local – Association communautaire basée à Ampangabe – Secteur : développement local, éducation, inclusion sociale; GIZ – Fanainga Plus – Appui stratégique et potentiel bailleur – Coopération allemande au développement – Secteur : gouvernance, développement durable, appui aux organisations de la société civile; Schneider Electric – Partenaire technique potentiel – Multinationale spécialisée dans la gestion de l’énergie et l’automatisation – Secteur : énergie, technologie, développement durable.
Geographic focus: 4 regions of Madagascar and the whole nation later
Duration to pilot in a new geography: a minimum of ten months
SDGs addressed: SDG 4 (Quality Education);SDG 5 (Gender Equality);SDG 7 (Affordable and Clean Energy);
Desired impact:
Solution Objectives
General Objective:
Reduce the digital and energy divide in rural Madagascar by deploying an innovative, solar-powered mobile digital solution that supports education, social inclusion, and local development.

Specific Objectives:

OS1: Provide digital and educational access to underserved populations beyond schools.
OS2: Develop digital, social, and professional skills among youth and women.
OS3: Strengthen local governance and community inclusion through tailored digital resources.
OS4: Ensure sustainability by training local actors and transferring ownership to the commune.

Key Achievements or Impacts (Quantifiable and Qualitative)
Educational Impact:

Thousands of students and teachers in 18 RSID-equipped schools now access digital learning via EDUCMAD.
Expansion will reach non-schooled youth and community members through mobile kits.
Social Impact:

Inclusion of women and youth in digital literacy and community leadership.
Awareness raised on gender equality and reproductive health.
Economic Impact:

Training in entrepreneurship and agriculture to boost local income generation.
Creation of local jobs: technicians, trainers, and digital facilitators.
Employment generation: Youth and women trained as community digital facilitators and technicians.
Environmental Impact:

Use of solar-powered kits reduces reliance on fossil fuels.
Energy savings: Deployment of reconditioned equipment and solar panels.

Ce modèle permet un accès numérique sans dépendance à une infrastructure fixe ni à une connexion internet permanente.

Le projet cible les jeunes non scolarisés, les femmes, les associations locales et les autorités communales, élargissant l’impact au-delà du cadre scolaire.

Le projet combine financements privés (fondations d’entreprise) et coopération internationale, avec une stratégie de réplication dans d’autres communes grâce à un guide pratique et une étude d’impact externe.

La solution « Rayon de soleil pour tous » vise à créer un changement systémique durable en s’attaquant simultanément à plusieurs leviers de transformation dans les zones rurales mal desservies de Madagascar. Sa théorie du changement repose sur les éléments suivants :

Accès équitable à l’énergie et au numérique
→ En introduisant une valise numérique autonome alimentée par énergie solaire, le projet permet aux communautés isolées d’accéder à des ressources éducatives, professionnelles et citoyennes, même sans infrastructure existante.

Renforcement des capacités locales
→ En formant des jeunes et des femmes comme animateurs et techniciens, la solution crée un village de compétences locales qui assure la continuité des activités, réduit la dépendance extérieure et favorise l’autonomisation économique.

Appropriation communautaire et gouvernance locale
→ La commune est impliquée dès le départ et formée pour devenir acteur relais, garantissant la pérennité du dispositif et son intégration dans les politiques locales de développement.

Effets multiplicateurs attendus

Éducation : amélioration durable de l’accès à l’apprentissage numérique.
Économie : montée en compétences, création d’emplois locaux, stimulation de l’entrepreneuriat.
Environnement : promotion des énergies renouvelables et gestion responsable des équipements.
Genre : inclusion active des femmes dans les filières techniques et numériques.
Réplicabilité du modèle
→ Grâce à sa simplicité, sa modularité et son faible coût, le modèle peut être répliqué dans d’autres communes rurales, avec un potentiel d’effet d’échelle national.

Title: InovLab Académie : Former les innovateurs numériques africains
Subtitle: Former une génération de jeunes capables de créer des solutions numériques pour transformer l’Afrique et le monde.
Problem Statement: Dans de nombreux pays, dont la Guinée, les jeunes n’ont pas un accès suffisant à une éducation numérique et technologique de qualité. Cette fracture numérique limite leur employabilité, leur capacité à innover et leur participation à l’économie digitale mondiale, creusant les inégalités sociales et freinant le développement local et continental.
Solution Overview:
InovLab Académie forme les enfants, jeunes et étudiants aux compétences numériques et technologiques (programmation, robotique, électronique, entrepreneuriat). Les formations combinent ateliers pratiques en présentiel et contenus pédagogiques adaptés pour favoriser un apprentissage concret et inclusif.

Méthodologies et technologies utilisées :

Pédagogie active et projets pratiques pour apprendre en créant.

Technologies STEM : Arduino, robotique, outils de programmation, modules numériques.

Supports numériques et interactifs pour renforcer l’apprentissage et faciliter l’accessibilité.

Modèle de co-création avec les enseignants et mentors pour adapter les contenus aux besoins locaux.

Préparation à des partenariats internationaux pour l’échange de savoir-faire, le financement et le soutien technique.

Title: AGROSIGN HARMONY : smart collars AI platform to protect crops, empower farmers, and prevent conflicts.
Subtitle: AgroSign Harmony uses connected collars and AI to virtually protect fields, prevent livestock intrusion, support farmers with real-time advice, and promote peace and sustainability in west Africa.
Problem Statement:
In West Africa, thousands of hectares of crops are destroyed each year by stray livestock or wildlife intrusion.  
This leads to recurrent conflicts between farmers and herders, sometimes violent, causing economic losses, social tensions, and population displacement.  
Lacking modern solutions, many farmers cut down trees to build physical fences, accelerating deforestation and threatening biodiversity.  
At the same time, the absence of reliable data on weather, soils, and resource management prevents a more productive and climate-resilient agriculture.
Solution Overview:
AgroSign Harmony is a smart platform combining virtual crop protection, intelligent livestock guidance, and precision agricultural data to foster rural peace and boost productivity.  
AgroProtect : Farmers set their field boundaries virtually via map or by walking around the plot. This “digital fence” activates a monitoring and alert system that detects animal intrusions—even without Internet—through a local IoT network.  
Connected livestock collars : Equipped with GPS and directional alerts, they guide herds to avoid protected zones, reducing conflicts.
Agro-intelligence data : Hyperlocal weather forecasts, soil diagnostics, and farming recommendations, all delivered in local languages through a voice AI.  
Environmental impact : Reduces deforestation and preserves biodiversity by eliminating the need for physical fences.
In short: AgroSign Harmony blends technology, sustainability, and inclusion to transform agricultural practices and strengthen social cohesion.
Solution Provider(s): AgroSign Harmony (Lead Applicant) – AgriTech startup designing and deploying the digital platform (AI, IoT). IoT Manufacturing Partners (China) – Development and supply of connected collars and smart sensors. Ministry of Agriculture and Livestock (Guinea) – Institutional support, regulatory facilitation, and national deployment. National Chamber of Agriculture (Guinea) – Farmers’ representation and integration into cooperatives. Technological Institute of Mamou – Applied research and IT engineering support. Higher Agronomic and Veterinary Institute of Faranah – Agronomic and veterinary expertise, scientific validation. University Gamal Abdel Nasser of Conakry – Research and innovation in AI and data analysis. National Transition Council (Guinea) – Policy framework and advocacy for national digital and agricultural strategy. Community farmers and herders’ networks (Guinea) – Local implementation, pilot testing, and adoption.
Implementation location(s): The project will initially be implemented in Guinea, targeting agricultural regions with high farmer-herder interaction : Mamou, Faranah, Kankan, and Labé.   These pilot zones are strategic as they concentrate livestock intrusion challenges, while offering diverse crops and farming practices.
Implementation timeline(s): Phase 1 (Months 1-3) : MVP technical finalization, language adaptation, and initial training of field teams.   Phase 2 (Months 4-9) : Pilot launch in targeted areas, data collection, and continuous adjustments.   Phase 3 (Months 10-12) : Impact evaluation, feature improvements, and preparation for national scale-up.
Duration to pilot in a new geography: 12 months, to cover a full agricultural cycle and account for seasonal variations in the evaluation.
SDGs addressed: SDG 2 (Zero Hunger);SDG 13 (Climate Action);SDG 15 (Life on Land);
Desired impact:
AgroSign Harmony delivers impact across three key dimensions:  
1. Economic Impact
+30% crop yield through reduced animal intrusion losses.  
Increased rural incomes via secure harvests and sustainable productivity.  
Job creation in manufacturing, installation, maintenance, and training. 
2. Social Impact 
Reduction of farmer-herder conflicts, fostering community peace.  
Inclusion of women and youth through skilled jobs and access to modern tools.  
Local language communication ensuring mass adoption.
3. Environmental Impact
Preservation of thousands of trees annually by eliminating the need for physical fences.  
Lower carbon footprint from reduced travel and agricultural losses.  
Biodiversity protection and ecosystem restoration.
 3-year target: 50,000 farmers protected, 500,000 hectares secured, 20% reduction in agro-pastoral conflicts in covered areas.
Key technologies:
AgroSign Harmony integrates:  
AI (soil data analysis, intrusion detection, real-time voice translation).  
IoT (connected livestock collars, soil sensors, local relay units).  
Geofencing & GPS.  
Offline communication with delayed synchronization.  
Predictive analytics based on weather and historical data.
Unique Characteristics:
AgroSign Harmony stands out through a set of rarely combined innovations: 
1. AgroProtect – Smart Virtual Fencing :  
Farmers set field boundaries via GPS or by walking around the plot.  
Active 24/7 protection against human, livestock, and wildlife intrusion — without physical fences, preventing deforestation.
2. Smart Livestock Guidance:  
Connected collars guide herds to avoid protected areas.  
Immediate reduction of farmer-herder conflicts.
3. Local Multilingual AI:
Voice interaction in local languages, including non-literate populations.  
Natural understanding through continuous learning.
4. Offline Mode & Hybrid Architecture:
Operates without Internet, with later synchronization.  
 Perfect for remote rural areas.
5. Built-in Environmental Impact:
Prevents abusive tree cutting.  
Protects ecosystems and reduces carbon footprint.
Sustainable Change:
AgroSign Harmony is not just a tech tool; it’s a catalyst for structural transformation.*  
Transforming agricultural and pastoral practices:  
Through AgroProtect virtual fencing and smart livestock guidance, we replace destructive methods (physical fences, tree cutting) with a digital, eco-friendly, and collaborative approach.*  
Building trust between communities:  
Our platform acts as a bridge between farmers and herders, reducing historic tensions via a shared alert and prevention system. 
Inclusive rural digitalization:  
With AI-powered, multilingual voice interaction in local languages, we ensure that even non-literate users access digital benefits.  
Integration into national policies:  
AgroSign Harmony provides reliable data (intrusions, weather, soil) to help governments design more effective agricultural, environmental, and land management policies. 
 Targeted shift: moving from a reactive, damage-repair model to a preventive, sustainable, and collaborative model embedded in an inclusive digital economy.
Funding Sources:
Historical funding:  
Personal investment + voluntary support from experts.  
In-kind contributions from local partners (test plots, technical expertise).  
Occasional support from local NGOs.  
Pro bono collaboration from engineers for MVP development.
Testimonials and Endorsements: “If we had this technology earlier, we could have avoided many conflicts.” – Farmers’ cooperative president (Kindia, Guinea).
Further comments/feedback:
AgroSign Harmony is a strategic response to combined challenges of food security, social peace, and environmental preservation.  
Our vision: create an inclusive digital ecosystem connecting farmers, herders, and policymakers.  
With your support, this solution will become an exportable African model for smart, sustainable agriculture.

Summary: AgroSign Harmony uses AI, IoT, and smart collars to prevent crop damage, reduce conflicts between farmers and herders, and promote sustainable agricultural practices in West Africa. The platform offers virtual crop protection, real-time livestock guidance, and precision agricultural data to increase productivity, reduce deforestation, and enhance rural peace.

Title: Asidor App: Unlocking Youth Skills for the Digital Economy
Subtitle: Connecting Africa’s youth to economic opportunities by digitizing skilled trades and making technical services accessible, safe, and affordable.
Problem Statement:
High start-up costs prevent over 1.7 million Ghanaian youth in technical and vocational trades (e.g., electricians, carpenters, beauticians) from launching sustainable businesses. At the same time, over 8 million households and offices lack reliable access to qualified service providers, often resorting to costly, unsafe, and informal artisans.
With 12% youth unemployment and limited digitalization in the sector, skilled workers struggle to monetize their expertise, while communities face poor service access. The problem is two-fold: youth lack affordable pathways to entrepreneurship, and customers lack trust and access to qualified workers.
Solution Overview:
How the Solution Works: 
The Asidor App leverages data science and AI to bridge this gap by creating virtual offices for technical and vocational workers, eliminating costly entry barriers.

For workers:
1. Free digital workspaces to showcase services, advertise skills, and update locations.
2 . Direct calls, chats, and bookings with clients resulting in no agents or middlemen.
3 . Ratings and reviews build trust and credibility.

For customers:
1 . On-demand access to vetted skilled workers nearby for emergencies or projects.
2. Ratings ensure quality and safety.
3 . Transparent, affordable pricing. The app currently demonstrates 98% geo-location accuracy, real-time communication, and robust data security features, ensuring trust on both sides.

Partnerships & Collaboration
1. Local Technical and Vocational Education and Training (TVET) Institutions: to onboard certified graduates.
2. Community-based Organisations & NGOs:  to achieve a nation-wide reach and promote inclusion of women and underserved youth on the Asidor App platform.
3. Government Agencies ( Ghana Enterprise Agency): to recruit certified skilled workers registered with their national associations, e.g. Association of Hairdressers, in line with national digitalization and youth employment goals.
4. Incubators & Accelerators: to provide mentorship, capacity building and access to funding opportunities.
Solution Provider(s): 1. UNICEF StartUp Lab: Innovation accelerator supporting impact-driven ventures in Ghana, providing mentorship, capacity building, and access to global networks (Sector: International Development / Innovation). (,)  2. Civil Society Organisations (CSO) Platform on Sustainable Development Goals (SDGs): A national coalition of NGOs, community-based organizations, and advocacy groups driving inclusive implementation of the SDGs (Sector: Civil Society / Policy Advocacy).  (,) 3. Ghana Enterprise Agency (GEA): Government agency supporting micro, small, and medium enterprises (MSMEs) through training, funding schemes, and entrepreneurship development (Sector: Government / MSME Development).
Duration to pilot in a new geography: 4 - 7 months
SDGs addressed: SDG 8 (Decent Work and Economic Growth);SDG 9 (Industry, Innovation, and Infrastructure);SDG 10 (Reduced Inequalities);
Desired impact:
Desired Impact:
1.Youth Employment & Entrepreneurship: transform 100,000 young people into digital entrepreneurs.
2.Revenue Growth & Livelihoods: increase in skilled workers’ earnings by expanding client access.
3.Service Efficiency: reduce downtime for households and businesses needing urgent services.
4.Gender Inclusion – empower women to launch and scale service-based businesses via the platform.

Quantifiable impact:
1.Targeting 100,000+ skilled workers onboarded in 3 years.
2.Enabling millions of service transactions between workers and households/companies.
3.Contributing directly to SDGs 8 (Decent Work), 9 (Innovation & Infrastructure), and 10 (Reduced Inequalities).
Key technologies:
1.Data Science & AI – for matching and filtering workers according to distance or skill category
2.Geolocation – to connect clients with the nearest workers.
3.Real-time Communication (SocketIO, REST API) – for direct, instant contact.
Unique Characteristics:
1.Inclusion-first design: prioritizes female-led and youth-led enterprises.
2.Zero-cost entry : allows workers to start digital businesses without upfront capital.
3.Nationwide scale : mobile app accessible across Ghana (and replicable across Africa).
4.Trust model: ratings, reviews, and verified digital identities ensure safety and credibility.
Sustainable Change:
By digitizing informal trades, Asidor App transforms the traditional artisan economy into a structured digital marketplace:
1.Short-term: Youth access clients directly, improving income and service reliability.
2. Medium-term: Expanded adoption by MSMEs and contractors boosts job creation.
3. Long-term: A stronger, more inclusive digital economy emerges, reducing youth unemployment and creating systemic pathways for vocational workers across Africa.

Name of your organization: Eastern Visayas State University, Ormoc Campus
Title: Empowering Ormoc’s Upland Farmers Through Digital and Smart Farming Hubs
Subtitle: Enhancing upland farmers’ skills through digital literacy and smart farming hubs for improved productivity, market access, and climate-smart agriculture in Ormoc City
Problem Statement:
In the rural, upland communities of Ormoc City such as the barangays of Lake Danao, Cabintan, and Cabaon-an, farming remains the primary source of livelihood. In fact, according to Ormoc’s Comprehensive Land Use Plan (CLUP) for 2017-2027, upland barangays depend heavily on farming for income and subsistence (Ormoc City Government, 2017). Because of their heavy reliance on agriculture, the Department of Agriculture (DA) prioritizes these upland farmers in poverty alleviation through, for example, its Special Area for Agricultural Development (SAAD) program. However, based on the initial data gathering that the proponents of this proposed project conducted through rapid ethnography, it is revealed that many smallholder farmers face persistent challenges such as limited access to updated agricultural knowledge, climate-resilient technologies, market information, and financial services (Ocay et al., forthcoming 2025). These persistent challenges have been, for the longest time, hindering agricultural productivity, market competitiveness, and sustainable livelihoods among the farmers of the upland barangays of Ormoc City. It is worth noting as well that limited access to modern farming technologies, reliable market information, and climate-smart practices has resulted in low yields, post-harvest losses, and vulnerability to unpredictable weather patterns. It is for this reason that this proposed project aims to address these urgent problems by providing the upland farmers of Ormoc City with access to digital tools, training, and smart farming solutions through the establishment of community-based learning hubs in strategically selected upland barangays in Ormoc City. By bridging technological and knowledge gaps, this proposed project will enhance productivity, improve resilience to climate change, and empower the upland farmers of Ormoc City to actively participate in an increasingly digital agricultural economy. Indeed, these learning hubs will serve as accessible venues for delivering hands-on training in basic digital skills, climate-smart farming technology, e-commerce, mobile banking, and online cooperative platforms.

Ocay, J., Mabitad, A., & Militante, B. (n.d.). Needs Assessment of the Upland Farmers of Ormoc City. Asian Journal of Agriculture and Rural Development (forthcoming 2025).

Ormoc City Government. 2017. Comprehensive Land Use Plan (CLUP). Ormoc City Planning and Development Office.
Solution Overview:
The proposed project envisions a transformative intervention for the upland farming communities of Ormoc City through the establishment of digital and smart farming hubs. Central to this effort is the “Digital Literacy Skills Development” initiative. By equipping farmers with hands-on skills in operating smartphones, computers, and agricultural applications, they gain access to real-time data that informs decision-making and allows them to actively engage in online cooperative platforms. Such empowerment fosters knowledge sharing, collective bargaining, and stronger community solidarity.

Equally important is the “Access to Climate-Smart Farming Technologies” solution, which introduces innovative tools such as soil sensors, automated irrigation systems, and drones. These technologies are designed to combat the persistent issues of low yields and post-harvest losses by promoting precision farming, early detection of threats, and better alignment of planting schedules with weather patterns. 

The hubs will also strengthen farmers’ economic opportunities through “Market Linkages and E-Commerce Integration”. Recognizing that lack of access to reliable market information often forces farmers to rely on exploitative middlemen, the proposed project will provide direct connections to digital marketplaces. Complemented by training in pricing, digital marketing, and online payment systems, farmers can sell produce directly to consumers and institutions, which in turn ensures fairer returns and greater autonomy over their livelihoods.

Another critical aspect is “Financial Inclusion and Mobile Banking”, which addresses the widespread lack of access to formal financial services among upland farmers. Through partnership with banks and microfinance institutions, the hubs will promote mobile banking as a tool to secure savings, access to microloans, and safe transactions without the burden of long travel. This financial empowerment is believed to open pathways for investment in farm improvements and greater economic security.

Sustainability, however, is at the heart of the project, realized through “Community-led Management and Sustainability”. Each hub will be run under a farm-led governance structure, with local leaders trained not only in technology and agriculture but also in hub administration and resource mobilization. This participatory model ensures ownership, trust, and long-term continuity even after external support phases out.

Methodologically, the proposed project will adopt a participatory and context-sensitive approach. Community consultations and rural appraisals will validate local needs, set priorities, and identify farmer-leaders. Training will follow a modular, hands-on format which combines hub-based sessions with on-farm demonstrations to promote learning by doing. Smart technologies will be introduced gradually to ensure mastery and adoption at each stage.

Success of the proposed project will also depend on strong partnerships. The Department of Agriculture, through its SAAD program, will provide technical expertise and inputs. The Ormoc LGU and barangay councils will facilitate site identification, mobilization, and integration into local development plans. Academic institutions such Eastern Visayas State University-Ormoc Campus (EVSU-OC) and Visayas State University (VSU) will contribute research-based modules and monitoring support. Private argri-tech firms will supply and maintain farming tools, while telecom providers will ensure connectivity. Lastly, financial institutions will drive financial inclusion, and farmer cooperatives and NGOs will oversee hub management, which ensures cultural appropriateness and community ownership.
Solution Provider(s): Computer Studies Department of Eastern Visayas State University Ormoc City Campus, Visayas State University, Department of Agriculture, Local Government of Ormoc, Barangay Lake Danao, Barangay Cabaon-an, Barangay Cabintan, Barangay Gaas, ADA Manufacturing Corporation (ADAMCO), CONVERGE, Land Bank of the Philippines, Department of Agrarian Reforms’ Agri-credit and Micro-finance Program, Ormoc-Kananga Leyte Farmers Federation (ORKALEFF), Ormoc City Seeds Growers Agriculture Cooperative (CALCOA), SM Foundation through its Kabalikat sa Kabuhayan (KSK) Program
Duration to pilot in a new geography: The pilot implementation of this proposed project will run for twenty months, which is divided into four key phases, namely: 1) The Preparatory Phase, 2) Capacity-building and Development Phase, 3) Technology Integration and Adaptation Phase, and 4) Monitoring, Evaluation, and Learning Phase.  The first phase will span six months, which will focus on community consultations, participatory rural appraisals, and site identification, alongside partnership building, procurement of smart farming tools, and the development of training modules customized in local dialects. Phase two will also span six months, which includes training of farmer-leaders as peer facilitators through modular workshops and on-farm demonstrations. It is also in this phase that hub management structures will be established and initial technologies such as soil sensors, irrigation systems, and digital tools will be introduced. The third phase, which will also span six months, will gradually expand the use of advanced technologies like drones and digital market platforms, supported by continuous technical assistance and financial inclusion programs through mobile banking and microloans. Finally, the fourth and last phase will span two months. This phase will track adoption rates, measure yield improvements, and gathering farmer feedback. It will also include necessary adjustments to training and technology use, as well as documentation of lessons learned to guide future scaling of the initiative. It must be noted, however, that the Monitoring, Evaluation, and Learning phase will be carried out continuously throughout the pilot implementation.
SDGs addressed: SDG 11 (Sustainable Cities and Communities);SDG 13 (Climate Action);SDG 2 (Zero Hunger);
Desired impact:
At its core, the proposed project aims to harness digital and smart farming technologies to improve agricultural practices, strengthen livelihoods, and create a sustainable ecosystem where upland farmers of Ormoc are not only producers but also empowered community leaders. Its specific objectives, therefore, include: 1) To increase farm productivity through climate-smart technologies, 2) Reduce post-harvest losses with efficient storage and processing systems, and 3) Expand market opportunities via digital platforms, and 4) Promote financial inclusion through mobile banking and microfinance services.

By the end of the pilot phase, the project seeks to achieve measurable outcomes that will serve as indicators of its success. Employment generation is one of the most tangible impacts, as the establishment and management of farming hubs will create direct jobs for farmer-leaders, hub managers, and technical support staff, while indirectly generating livelihood opportunities for input suppliers, transport providers, and local service providers. Hence, it is estimated that each hub can create 10-20 direct and indirect jobs, which provide income opportunities in upland areas of Ormoc City where employment is scarce.

The project will also result in quantifiable improvements in productivity, with participating farmers projected to increase yields by 20-30% through the adoption of soil sensors, automated irrigation systems, and climate resilient inputs. Post-harvest losses are also expected to be reduced by at least 20% through improved storage, processing, and supply chain management, which in turn leads to greater profitability. Access to markets through digital platforms will further enhance farmers’ income by linking them directly to buyers, thus reducing reliance on middlemen. Moreover, at least 100 farmers will be trained in digital literacy and smart farming practices, which equips them with skills that extend beyond farming into broader opportunities within the digital economy.

In the long term, however, the proposed project’s desired impact is to build resilient, self-reliant farming communities that can sustain livelihoods while adapting to climate change and modern market demands. Indeed, the proposed project will not only uplift the socio-economic conditions of upland farmers but also position Ormoc as a model for inclusive and technology-driven agricultural transformation.
Key technologies:
The key technologies needed for this proposed project are the following:

For smart farming tools and equipment: soil sensors, automated irrigation systems, weather monitoring stations, drones, smart greenhouses, and post-harvest storage technologies.

For the digital platforms and software: farm management software, market access platforms, mobile apps for digital literacy and training, data analytics system, monitoring and evaluation tools.

For connectivity and communication infrastructure: stable internet connectivity, Internet of Things (IoT) devices, and telecommunications support.

For financial and inclusion technologies: mobile banking platforms, microfinance and loan management app, and E-commerce platforms.

For training and knowledge-sharing tools: digital hubs (computer/table stations), multimedia training kits, and knowledge repositories.
Unique Characteristics:
The uniqueness and originality of this proposed project lie in its holistic, technology-driven solutions that are carefully tailored to the specific needs and realities of upland farming communities. Unlike conventional agricultural interventions that focus only on inputs or training, this proposed project integrates smart farming technologies, digital literacy inclusion, and community-led governance into a single, cohesive model. Its unique selling point, therefore, lies in the establishment of multi-functional farming hubs that serve not only as training and resource centers but also as access points for technology, markets, and financial services. This hub-based approach ensures that farmers are not passive recipients but active participants, with farmer-leaders trained to operate and manage tools such as soil sensors, automated irrigation systems, and drones, while also leading peer-to-peer learning.

It must also be noted that the urgency of this proposed project stems from the growing vulnerability of Ormoc’s upland farmers to climate change, fluctuating markets, and post-harvest losses. Indeed, traditional farming practices are no longer sufficient to sustain livelihoods, and that without intervention that proposed project offers, upland farmers of Ormoc risk deepening poverty and exclusion. By providing practical, accessible technologies and linking farmers directly to markets and financial services, this proposed project addresses these urgent concerns while at the same time creating sustainable and inclusive growth. In doing so, it positions Ormoc as a model for climate-smart, technology enabled agricultural transformation.
Sustainable Change: By embedding innovation and inclusivity into the very structure of upland agriculture, this proposed project will surely contribute to sustainable and system-wise change. To be specific, indeed, by introducing smart farming technologies, digital tools, and financial services within community-led hubs, this proposed project will address not just immediate productivity gap but also the systemic barriers that keep farmers in cycles of poverty and exclusion. This approach ensures that farmers gain both the knowledge and the means to apply technology, while also at the same time building local leadership and cooperative governance that sustain progress beyond the project period. The desired follow-on effects include a ripple of change where increased yields and incomes strengthen food security, empowered cooperative drive collective bargaining power, and enhanced digital literacy opens pathways to new economic opportunities. Over time, these hubs will inspire replication across other communities, which in turn attracts investment and influence policies toward resilient, technology-enabled rural development.

Title: Digital Innovation Studio for MENA MSMEs
Subtitle: A hybrid R&D hub and marketplace connecting MSMEs to digital tools, new markets, and a direct pathway to venture investment.
Problem Statement: MSMEs in Egypt and the broader MENA region, particularly those led by women and youth, are systematically excluded from the digital economy. They face a "digital ceiling" due to the high costs of technology, a lack of specialized skills, and a fragmented support ecosystem. This suppresses industrial competitiveness, stifles innovation, and prevents inclusive and sustainable economic growth.
Solution Overview:
Our solution is the Sanabil Inclusive Digital Innovation Studio & Marketplace, a hybrid ecosystem designed to solve these challenges.

We operate a physical hub and a digital platform. MSMEs join our program and enter "Digital Co-Creation Labs" where they collaborate with our network of engineers and researchers to develop and implement practical, affordable digital solutions for their specific business needs (e.g., supply chain optimization, IoT for energy monitoring, e-commerce integration).

We use an R&D as a Service (R&DaaS) methodology, providing on-demand access to world-class talent and facilities. The solution includes a Shared Digital Tools Library with open-source and low-code modules to accelerate development. We leverage technologies relevant to MSME needs, including IoT, low-code application platforms, and basic AI/ML models for data analysis.

Our model is built on a three-way partnership: Industry (MSMEs, corporate buyers), Academia (university researchers), and Finance (our sister venture studio, Aria Ventures). High-potential MSMEs from our program are channeled into an "Investment Readiness Track," providing a direct bridge from R&D to venture capital.
Solution Provider(s): Sanabil Tech: The lead organization, an R&D and innovation hub specializing in industry-academia partnerships. Sector: Technology, R&D, Industrial Upgrading. Aria Ventures: Key strategic partner and sister company, a deep-tech venture studio providing an investment pipeline for high-growth MSMEs. Sector: Venture Capital, Finance. Dezign Arena: Sister company and implementation partner, an IoT Design House for prototyping and product design. Sector: Electronics, IoT, Manufacturing. Nawah Scientific: Sister company and implementation partner, an ISO/IEC 17025 accredited lab for advanced scientific testing and R&D. Sector: Biotechnology, Pharmaceuticals, Chemical Industry. Fabri Hub: Sister company and implementation partner, a "Manufacturing on Demand" platform. Sector: Advanced Manufacturing, 3D Printing.
Duration to pilot in a new geography: 24 months. This includes a 6-month setup phase for platform development and partner onboarding, followed by an 18-month implementation and iteration phase with the first two cohorts of MSMEs.
SDGs addressed: SDG 5 (Gender Equality);SDG 8 (Decent Work and Economic Growth);SDG 9 (Industry, Innovation, and Infrastructure);
Desired impact:
The primary objective is to create a scalable model that empowers MSMEs to thrive in the digital economy. Key quantifiable impacts over a 2-year pilot include:

1. Employment Generation: Onboard 150-200 MSMEs, helping them sustain and create jobs through increased competitiveness.
2. Economic Growth: Achieve a measurable revenue increase (targeting 10-15%) through digital channels for at least 60% of engaged MSMEs.
3. Gender Equality & Youth Empowerment: Ensure at least 40% of participating enterprises are women- or youth-led.
4. Innovation & Investment: Graduate 10-15 MSMEs from an Investment Readiness Track, with the goal of advancing at least 5 companies to late-stage investment discussions.
Key technologies: Our solution is technology-agnostic, applying the right tool for the MSME's problem. Key technologies utilized within our network include: Internet of Things (IoT) for monitoring and automation, Low-Code/No-Code Platforms for rapid application development, Additive Manufacturing (3D Printing) for prototyping and spare parts, and foundational AI/Machine Learning for data analysis and process optimization.
Unique Characteristics:
Our solution's uniqueness lies in its integrated, end-to-end business model.

From R&D to Investment: We are not just a training program. Our formal partnership with our sister company, Aria Ventures, creates a complete innovation-to-investment pipeline. We de-risk MSMEs through hands-on R&D and then directly connect the most promising ones to venture capital.

Hybrid "R&DaaS" Model: We combine a digital platform with access to physical, state-of-the-art labs and facilities (including ISO-certified labs), a resource unavailable to MSMEs elsewhere.

Ecosystem Ownership: We are not just connecting partners; we are an ecosystem of sister companies. This ensures seamless execution, shared goals, and deep integration between R&D, manufacturing, and investment readiness.
Sustainable Change:
Our Theory of Change is to create a self-sustaining cycle of innovation.

- By providing affordable access to R&D and digital tools, MSMEs become more efficient and competitive.

- This leads to increased revenues and growth, allowing them to hire more people and invest in further innovation.

- As they succeed, they become role models and create a demand-driven market for digital solutions, inspiring other MSMEs to join the ecosystem.

- The most successful MSMEs attract venture investment through our pipeline, creating major success stories that anchor the ecosystem and generate returns that can be reinvested into the program. The desired follow-on effect is the creation of a permanent, market-driven innovation hub that no longer relies on donor funding and serves as a replicable model for industrial upgrading across the region.

Our goal is to leverage this initial support to build a sustainable, revenue-generating model that can attract further private and impact investment in the future.

Title: AI-driven shopping tourism hub uniting global travelers and local retailers
Subtitle: FashionTouri is an AI-driven platform connecting global shopping tourism with local retail, offering a loyalty system that drives high-spending travelers to invest in the local economy.
Problem Statement:
Local retailers and craftmanship define the economic identity of continents, countries and regions worldwide driving global commerce. They reflect variety and diversity, which in many cases stands for the representation of an entire culture. 
Local companies and brands are under increasing pressure from multiple directions. Rising prices, inflation, and global crises are driving a decline in retail sales, while insolvencies and business closures are becoming more frequent. At the same time, attracting international customers is costly and complex, often hindered by language barriers, fragmented marketing channels, and limited budgets.

Operationally, many businesses struggle with digitization, supply chain disruptions, and the lack of local production capacity. With little time and no common platform to pool resources, small and medium-sized retailers often remain invisible to global shoppers. Brand awareness is low, advertising effectiveness is difficult to measure, and competition with larger players leaves little room for sustainable growth.
Together, these challenges threaten not only individual businesses but also the cultural and economic value that local craftsmanship and retail bring to their regions.

The main shopping streets are often very crowded and there are hardly any parking facilities. In the outlying districts, there are often shopping centers in which almost exclusively large chains are present and hardly any local, individual stores. This is precisely why it is important to take concrete measures together with governments, the cities and town managements, e.g. regarding a decentralization concept. Our app and the bonus system can be used to promote strategic cooperation between retail and tourism organizations and create synergy effects. We also use the app to provide important data on people's movement patterns in the city.

In conclusion, FashionTouri’s innovative approach of personalized tourism experiences with sustainability, local shopping, and global reach makes it a true pioneer in the tourism sector. It redefines how tourists interact with local businesses while promoting conscious consumerism and sustainable practices, all of which set it apart from current industry standards

Title: Digital Business Development Hub: AI Skills & Business Growth for Women, Youth & Refugees
Subtitle: The Digital Business Development Hub integrates AI-driven tools and mentorship to strengthen Business & entrepreneurial skills, market access, and business growth for women, youth, refugees, and underserved groups.
Problem Statement:
Women, youth, refugees, and marginalized communities face systemic barriers that restrict their access to digital skills, AI tools, and business development opportunities. These barriers limit their participation in business growth and innovation-driven markets, including. These barriers include:

- Limited access to quality digital skills training tailored to their socio-economic realities.
- Low AI and emerging technology literacy leaving them unprepared for future job markets.
- Gender and socio-cultural constraints that restrict mobility, leadership roles, and access to entrepreneurship opportunities.
- Fragmented market linkages and lack of affordable platforms to connect with buyers, investors, and business networks.
- Insufficient mentorship and innovation support to translate ideas into market-ready products or services.
- These challenges perpetuate economic exclusion, widen the digital divide, and hinder progress towards SDGs 4, 5, 8, and 9. 

Without targeted, inclusive interventions that combine skills development, AI-driven learning, and market access mechanisms, these populations risk being left further behind in an increasingly digital and innovation-led global economy.
Solution Overview:
The proposed Digital Business Development Hub is an inclusive, AI-powered platform designed to equip women, youth, and refugees in underserved and marginalized communities with market-relevant business development skills, entrepreneurial capacity, and direct access to economic opportunities. By addressing systemic barriers, the Hub integrates AI-driven learning technologies, tailored mentorship, market linkages, and innovation-focused collaboration to drive sustainable business growth, enhance competitiveness, and foster inclusive participation in the digital economy.
How the Solution Works
Participants engage in a structured pathway that integrates AI-personalized training with hands-on entrepreneurship projects and direct market access activities. The Hub delivers:
Adaptive AI Learning Paths – Customized digital training in business development, entrepreneurship, AI literacy, and sector-specific skills, tailored to individual assessments and market demands.
Virtual Business Simulations – Interactive, risk-free environments to practice real business decision-making, supported by AI-driven feedback and performance analytics.
Market Linkages & Networking – Digital showcases, and connections to incubators, accelerators, and financial partners to accelerate business growth and sustainability.
Technologies & methodologies used:
Methodology
Participatory Co-Design – Engage beneficiaries, local NGOs, and private sector partners in designing training content, ensuring cultural relevance and gender inclusivity.
Blended Learning Delivery – Combine mobile-based learning, virtual classrooms, and in-person workshops for flexible access.
Experiential Learning – Use business simulations, project-based assignments, and market challenges to reinforce real-world application.
Mentorship Integration – Pair learners with mentors through AI matching, supported by structured coaching sessions.
Continuous Feedback Loop – Collect real-time learner performance data via platform analytics and mentor reports to adapt learning paths dynamically.
Impact Evaluation – Apply a mixed-method approach (surveys, interviews, analytics, case studies) to measure learning outcomes, business viability, and income generation.
