Summary: Essymart Agtech is a Ugandan social enterprise tackling smallholder farmer challenges through affordable agri-inputs, climate-smart solutions, and digital tools. It integrates e-commerce, fintech, SMS/USSD, advisory services, and last-mile logistics via Village Agripreneurs, ensuring rural farmers access authentic products, financing, and knowledge. By combining biotechnology, mobile money credit, and community-based distribution, Essymart boosts productivity (up to 40% increase in yields), reduces costs (10–20% input savings), and raises farmer incomes (up to $1,000 per year). With 5,000+ farmers already reached, the solution advances food security, resilience, and poverty reduction while promoting gender inclusion and regenerative agriculture.

Title: "Pulsar AgroLink: Solar-Powered Smart Irrigation & Digital Market Access"
Subtitle: A renewable-energy irrigation system paired with a digital platform connecting farmers to markets, boosting productivity and reducing climate impact.
Problem Statement: Smallholder farmers in Togo face unreliable access to water due to climate variability, high fuel costs for irrigation, and limited market access, which reduces productivity and income. Lack of affordable, clean-energy solutions and digital tools further widens the gap, limiting their ability to adapt to climate change and integrate into larger value chains.
Solution Overview:
Our solution integrates solar-powered irrigation technology with a digital e-agriculture platform to enhance agricultural productivity and market access for smallholder farmers in Togo.

How it works

Farmers install solar pumping systems designed to provide reliable, clean, and cost-effective water supply for irrigation.

IoT-enabled controllers allow remote management of water distribution, reducing labor and optimizing resource use.

The digital platform connects farmers directly to wholesalers and retailers, enabling them to sell their produce at better prices, access agronomic advice, and coordinate logistics.

Methodologies and technologies used

Renewable energy systems: photovoltaic pumps designed for low-maintenance rural deployment.

IoT and mobile technology: remote control, water scheduling, and system monitoring via mobile phones.

Cloud-based marketplace: a simple interface that supports SMS for farmers without smartphones.
Solution Provider(s): Pulsar Eco Group (Renewable energy and agri-tech startup, specializing in solar-powered irrigation and digital agriculture solutions), GIZ Togo (International development organization supporting capacity building and technical assistance), UNDP Togo (United Nations agency providing prototype development support), local farmer cooperatives (agricultural associations facilitating rural adoption), microfinance institutions (financial sector partners enabling access to credit)
Duration to pilot in a new geography: The estimated duration to pilot our solution in a new geography is approximately 4 to 6 months. This includes:  1 month for stakeholder engagement, site selection, and feasibility assessment  2 months for installation of solar irrigation systems and system testing  1 month for onboarding farmers onto the digital platform and training  1–2 months for initial operations, monitoring, and feedback collection
SDGs addressed: SDG 13 (Climate Action);SDG 11 (Sustainable Cities and Communities);SDG 7 (Affordable and Clean Energy);
Desired impact:
Solution Objectives

Improve climate resilience for smallholder farmers through clean, reliable solar-powered irrigation.

Increase productivity and reduce post-harvest losses via better water access and digital market integration.

Promote inclusive economic growth by connecting farmers directly to buyers, improving income.

Reduce reliance on fossil fuels in agriculture and lower carbon emissions.

Key Achievements and Impacts (to date)

Over 50 solar irrigation systems installed across rural regions in Togo, reducing dependence on diesel pumps.

Estimated CO₂ emissions reduction of 75–100 tons/year, based on average displacement of fuel-powered systems.

Trained 120+ farmers, with at least 30% women and youth participating in solar irrigation and e-agriculture workshops.
Key technologies:
Solar Photovoltaic (PV) Technology – for powering irrigation systems sustainably without reliance on fossil fuels.

DC Water Pumps – energy-efficient pumping solutions compatible with solar systems for agricultural irrigation.

IoT-Based Remote Monitoring – enables farmers to monitor and control irrigation systems remotely via mobile phones.

Mobile and Web-Based Platform – connects farmers to buyers, provides weather alerts, agronomic tips, and facilitates digital transactions.

Cloud Computing – for secure data storage, system analytics, and seamless access to the e-agriculture platform.
Unique Characteristics:
Integrated Approach: Unlike traditional solutions that address irrigation or market access separately, our solution uniquely combines solar-powered irrigation technology with a digital e-agriculture platform, creating a seamless system that boosts productivity and market inclusion simultaneously.

Renewable Energy Focus: Our use of off-grid solar pumping systems reduces dependence on expensive and polluting diesel pumps, making irrigation affordable and sustainable for smallholder farmers in remote areas.

Inclusive Digital Platform: The platform supports SMS-based access for farmers without smartphones, ensuring digital inclusion for youth and women in rural communities often left behind by tech advances.

Innovative Financing Models: We collaborate with microfinance institutions and local partners to provide affordable financing options, enabling farmers to invest in clean technology without prohibitive upfront costs.

Strong Partnerships: By partnering with international development agencies (GIZ, UNDP), local cooperatives, and financial actors, we ensure both technical expertise and community buy-in, facilitating successful adoption and scale-up.

Scalable and Replicable: Designed for easy adaptation across different geographies and crops, the solution’s modular tech and flexible platform can be replicated in other regions facing similar challenges.
Sustainable Change:
Our solution addresses interconnected barriers in agriculture—limited access to clean energy, water, and markets—by combining solar-powered irrigation with digital market connectivity. This dual approach initiates a chain of systemic change:

Access to clean irrigation technology boosts agricultural productivity and enables year-round farming, improving food security and farmer incomes.

Reduction in diesel use leads to lower greenhouse gas emissions and healthier local environments, contributing to national and global climate goals.

Digital platform integration increases transparency, reduces middlemen, and gives farmers real-time market information, empowering them economically and socially.

Increased farmer income encourages reinvestment in technology and education, while also reducing rural exodus by offering viable livelihoods.

Skills development and local job creation (in solar installation, platform management, and maintenance) strengthens the green economy and fosters community ownership.

Scalability across regions and crops enables replication of impact, creating a resilient, decentralized agricultural ecosystem aligned with SDGs 2, 7, 8, 9, and 13.

The desired follow-on effects include stronger rural economies, improved gender and youth inclusion, a national reduction in fossil fuel reliance, and long-term resilience to climate shocks.
Funding Sources:
Our solution has been funded through a combination of sources including:

Own capital investment from Pulsar Eco Group, supporting initial development and early deployments.

Grant funding and technical support from international organizations such as GIZ and UNDP, which enabled prototype development and pilot projects.

Partnerships with local stakeholders including farmer cooperatives and microfinance institutions, providing financial facilitation for end-users.

In-kind contributions from technology suppliers and community collaborators assisting with training and system installation.
Primary thematic focus area: Innovation Acceleration & Knowledge Sharing
Summary: Pulsar AgroLink integrates solar-powered smart irrigation systems with a digital market access platform to support smallholder farmers in Togo. The solution combines clean energy, IoT-enabled water management, and a cloud-based marketplace (with SMS access for low-tech users) to improve productivity, incomes, and climate resilience. With over 50 systems deployed and 120+ farmers trained (30% women/youth), it reduces reliance on diesel pumps, cuts CO₂ emissions, and strengthens market linkages through direct farmer-to-buyer connections.

Title: Empowering Farmers with Solar-Powered Smart Irrigation Solutions
Subtitle: Affordable solar irrigation systems boosting agricultural productivity and resilience for smallholder farmers in Uganda.
Problem Statement: Smallholder farmers in Uganda face low crop yields due to unreliable rainfall, high irrigation costs, and limited access to modern farming technology. These challenges hinder food security and income generation.
Solution Overview:
Tulima Solar Limited provides affordable, solar-powered irrigation systems designed to help smallholder farmers in Uganda increase crop production, reduce dependence on rainfall, and improve resilience to climate change.

How the Solution Works

1. Site Assessment: Tulima Solar agents assess the farmer’s land to determine water source availability, crop type, and irrigation needs.


2. Customized System Design: Based on the assessment, a tailored solar irrigation system is designed, including either surface or submersible solar water pumps.


3. Installation & Training: The system is installed by trained technicians. Farmers receive hands-on training on system use and maintenance.


4. After-Sales Support: Tulima offers warranty, maintenance, and remote monitoring to ensure continued system efficiency.
Methodologies and Technologies Used

Solar-Powered Pumps: Energy-efficient, sustainable water pumping using solar panels (surface and submersible options).

Pay-As-You-Go (PAYG): Flexible financing model using mobile money platforms (MTN, Airtel) for affordability.

IoT-Enabled Systems: Some systems are integrated with remote monitoring to track performance and detect faults.

Climate-Smart Agriculture (CSA): Farmers are trained in CSA practices such as proper irrigation scheduling, composting, and water conservation techniques.

Partnerships and Collaboration Models

Village Enterprise & Mercy Corps: Provide training in entrepreneurship and link climate-smart agriculture to income-generating activities.

Tulima Agents & Local Technicians: Work within communities to support installation, training, and follow-ups.

Financial Institutions & Mobile Operators: Facilitate PAYG financing and digital payment systems.

Community-Based Organizations (CBOs): Help mobilize farmers and create awareness of the benefits of solar irrigation.
This solution strengthens food security, boosts farmer income, and promotes sustainable agriculture across rural Uganda.
Solution Provider(s): Tulima Solar Limited – A renewable energy company in Uganda providing solar-powered irrigation systems to smallholder farmers; operates in the clean energy and agriculture sectors.  Village Enterprise – A nonprofit organization focused on training rural Africans in entrepreneurship and helping them start sustainable businesses; operates in the poverty alleviation, livelihoods, and economic empowerment sectors.  Mercy Corps – A global humanitarian organization working to help people build secure, productive, and just communities; operates in resilience building, agriculture, and climate adaptation sectors.  Simusolar Limited – Tulima’s parent company, providing solar-powered productive use equipment in East Africa; operates in agriculture technology and solar energy solutions sectors.  MTN Uganda and Airtel Uganda – Telecommunications companies providing mobile money services for pay-as-you-go financing; operate in the digital finance and telecom sectors.
Duration to pilot in a new geography: Six months
SDGs addressed: SDG 13 (Climate Action);SDG 11 (Sustainable Cities and Communities);SDG 17 (Partnerships for the Goals);
Desired impact:
Desired Impact of the Solution

Solution Objectives

Increase agricultural productivity by providing reliable, affordable irrigation powered by clean solar energy.

Enhance food security for smallholder farmers by reducing crop failure linked to inconsistent rainfall.

Promote climate resilience through sustainable, low-carbon irrigation technologies.

Empower rural communities economically by boosting farm incomes and creating jobs through local installation and maintenance services.

Facilitate financial inclusion with accessible pay-as-you-go models via mobile money.
Key Achievements and Impacts

Over 1,500+ smallholder farmers equipped with solar irrigation systems across multiple Ugandan districts, improving year-round crop production.

Estimated increase in crop yields by 30-50% due to reliable irrigation and improved farming practices.

Reduction of approximately 500+ tons of CO₂ emissions annually by replacing diesel pumps with solar-powered alternatives.

Created 50+ direct jobs for local technicians, sales agents, and trainers involved in system installation and support.

Enabled over 70% of users to access financing via mobile pay-as-you-go, improving affordability and adoption rates.

These impacts contribute to sustainable rural development, climate action, and poverty reduction in Uganda’s agricultural communities.
Key technologies:
1. Solar Photovoltaic (PV) Technology

Utilized to power water pumps using renewable solar energy, reducing dependence on fossil fuels and grid electricity.

2. Solar Water Pumping Systems

Includes surface and submersible pumps designed for irrigation, tailored to different terrain and water source conditions.

3. IoT (Internet of Things)

Integrated in select systems for remote monitoring, allowing real-time tracking of pump performance, water usage, and fault detection to ensure efficiency and timely maintenance.

4. Pay-As-You-Go (PAYG) Mobile Technology

Enabled through mobile money platforms like MTN and Airtel, allowing farmers to make small, incremental payments for their systems using their phones.

5. Data Analytics and CRM Tools

Used internally to manage customer data, monitor repayment behavior, and optimize service delivery based on farmer profiles and regional conditions.

These technologies combine to deliver an efficient, scalable, and affordable climate-smart irrigation solution for smallholder farmers.
Unique Characteristics:

Allows smallholder farmers to access solar irrigation systems with no upfront cost, paying gradually via mobile money. This removes financial barriers and promotes affordability.

3. Integrated Climate-Smart Agriculture (CSA) Training

Farmers receive training on sustainable farming practices like composting, drip irrigation, and water conservation, enhancing productivity and environmental resilience.



4. Strong Last-Mile Delivery & Support Network

5. IoT-Enabled System Monitoring

6. Collaborative Partnership Model

The solution thrives through multi-sectoral partnerships with NGOs (e.g., Mercy Corps, Village Enterprise), private sector, and telecom providers, enhancing outreach, training, and financing access.

These features make the solution both accessible and scalable, with a strong impact on agricultural livelihoods, climate adaptation, and economic empowerment.

Title: Digitizing Special Education for Inclusive Growth
Subtitle: Trarrk enables equity in education by empowering schools, teachers, therapists and families to track progress and support  children with learning differences in school and at home.
Problem Statement:
In Sub‑Saharan Africa, an estimated 6.4% of children under 14 have moderate or severe disabilities—but less than 10% of these children actually attend school, and in many countries, the figure is as low as 2%,

Approximately 29 million children with disabilities live across Eastern and Southern Africa. Meanwhile, in Nigeria alone, around 95.5% of children with disabilities are not enrolled in school.

This widespread exclusion is fueled by lack of tools, trained teachers, diagnostics, and data-driven planning, along with stigma and policy gaps. Without systematic support, children with disabilities face lifelong disadvantage from poor learning outcomes to high unemployment and economic exclusion.

Key Challenges:
Lack of assessment and planning tools: Most schools in Africa cannot assess developmental progress or create IEPs due to limited training and absence of structured systems.
Parental and teacher engagement gaps: Families and educators lack accessible platforms to collaborate on interventions tailored to specific needs.
Invisibility in data & policy: The absence of real-time progress tracking limits planning, accountability, and inclusive policy adoption
Solution Overview:
Trarrk is an intelligent, structured digital solution designed to transform how children with disabilities are supported in schools—by enabling real-time progress tracking, personalized educational plans (IEPs), and collaborative engagement between teachers, parents, and specialists.

It addresses the root issues of exclusion by providing tools that make diagnosis, goal setting, daily intervention, and progress documentation accessible even in low-resource African settings.

How the Solution Works:
Assessment & Baseline Mapping:

Children are assessed across 10 developmental domains (e.g., physical, cognitive, social-emotional).

The system uses structured question banks and rating scales to automatically recommend relevant domains and goals for each child.

IEP Generation:

Based on assessment, the platform creates a customized IEP—highlighting specific goals, priority levels (low/medium/high), and timelines.

Each IEP includes recommended school and home activities.

Daily/Weekly Progress Tracking:

Teachers update progress using rating scales per goal and subdomain (no manual text needed).

They can upload photos, videos, or voice notes as evidence of learning or behavior.

Parents view progress in real time and can contribute home-based updates as well.

Analytics & Reporting:

Visual dashboards show progress trends, stagnation alerts, and intervention effectiveness.

Data supports both individual planning and institution-wide reporting to inform inclusion strategy.

Methodologies Used:
Universal Design for Learning (UDL): Adaptable structures to accommodate diverse learners.

Individualized Education Program (IEP) Framework: Aligned with global best practices in special education.

Functional Behavioral Analysis (FBA): Incorporated into behavioral domains.

Caregiver-Teacher Collaboration Models: Based on participatory design with neurodiverse families.

Technologies Used:
Mobile-first Web App (Android-optimized for low-bandwidth environments)

Automated IEP Engine with rule-based AI logic

Cloud-based backend with secure data storage and offline sync

Multilingual interface with voice guidance and visual aids for accessibility

AI-driven recommendation engine for home and school activity suggestions

Partnerships and Collaboration Models:
Schools & Inclusive Education Units: Co-create implementation, provide feedback loops.

Parent Networks & Disability Organizations: Serve as design and testing partners, improving cultural fit and usability.

Government Education Ministries: Aligning Trarrk’s data and goals with national policy frameworks.

Teacher Training Institutions: Integrate Trarrk into pre-service and in-service special education training.

Global and African Research Institutes: For ongoing evaluation, evidence generation, and inclusive policy advocacy.

As we approach the pilot/beta testing phase, Trarrk aims to support over 500 children in 5+ schools across Nigeria during the pilot, helping to streamline IEP implementation and reduce teacher workload by over 60%. Trarrk is designed to scale across underserved regions through an offline-first model, open APIs, and local training partnerships. Early result would indicate a 30% increase in IEP goal achievement rates in pilot environments, demonstrating the platform’s potential to transform special education outcomes at scale.
Key technologies:
Trarrk leverages a blend of AI-powered personalization, cloud-based architecture, and mobile-first design to enable inclusive and scalable special education solutions. The platform uses:

Artificial Intelligence (AI) to auto-generate individualized education plans (IEPs) based on assessment responses and disability categories. AI also personalizes progress tracking and intervention suggestions for each child.

Data Analytics & Visualization to monitor developmental domains in real time, providing insights for teachers, parents, and administrators.

Capacity Building: It equips teachers and careproviders with digital tools to manage IEPs efficiently, reducing burnout and improving accountability.

Community Inclusion: Through parent-teacher collaboration and localized content, we promote community ownership of learning outcomes.

Title: Medify VR: Inclusive Surgical Training Through Virtual Reality
Subtitle: A virtual reality platform providing affordable, immersive surgical training for medical students in underserved and low-resource regions.
Problem Statement: Access to quality surgical training is limited in many low- and middle-income countries due to the high costs of physical infrastructure, lack of cadaver labs, and geographic inequalities. Medical students often graduate without sufficient hands-on experience, resulting in skill gaps and reduced clinical confidence. According to a study published by JAMA Surgery (2019), 30% of young surgeons feel unprepared during their first procedures, significantly increasing the risk of medical errors. Furthermore, research from the National Library of Medicine (2020) shows that surgical simulation can reduce such errors by 40% and improve student performance by 35%. These challenges are even more acute in underserved and rural areas, where access to advanced training tools is minimal.
Solution Overview:
Medify VR is an immersive virtual reality platform that offers realistic surgical simulations for medical students and young healthcare professionals. It enables users to train in a 3D interactive environment, replicating real-life operating room procedures. By removing the need for cadavers, physical labs, or costly equipment, Medify VR makes surgical training more accessible, especially in low-resource and underserved regions.

The platform functions via standalone VR headsets such as the Meta Quest, making it portable and easy to deploy. Learners can select from a growing library of surgical procedures—such as appendectomy or cholecystectomy—and either follow guided tutorials or operate in autonomous simulation mode. Throughout the experience, their performance is monitored through built-in metrics like timing, precision, and procedural accuracy, providing valuable feedback for continuous improvement.

Medify VR is built using advanced virtual reality technology, offering realistic anatomical modeling, intuitive interactivity, and gamified elements to boost learner engagement. All surgical scenarios are co-developed with medical professionals to ensure clinical accuracy and educational relevance. The platform is designed with an offline-first architecture, which allows users to access content without the need for a constant internet connection—a critical feature for use in rural or low-bandwidth environments.

The solution is modular and adaptable, allowing customization based on local curriculum needs or national medical education standards. It also includes a data analytics layer that enables instructors to monitor student progress, identify knowledge gaps, and personalize instruction accordingly.

Medify VR is developed in collaboration with several key partners, including medical universities and teaching hospitals in North Africa (notably in Tunisia and Algeria), as well as a network of experienced VR developers and 3D medical artists. Pilot programs are currently being expanded in partnership with public institutions and NGOs working on healthcare education in West Africa.

Our collaboration model includes institutional licensing for universities, public-private partnerships with ministries and health agencies, and participation in international health and education innovation programs. Through these partnerships, Medify VR seeks to scale its impact globally and contribute to inclusive, technology-driven capacity building in medical education.

Title: iSign: Mobile Sign Language Learning for Inclusive Communities
Subtitle: A mobile-based educational tool promoting basic sign language literacy, inclusivity, and community empowerment for the deaf and mute in the province of Romblon, Philippines.
Problem Statement: Persons with disabilities (PWDs), particularly the deaf and mute, face persistent communication barriers that limit their access to education, public services, and community participation. In the province of Romblon, sign language literacy among families, frontliners, and local officials remains very low, resulting in social isolation, limited opportunities, and vulnerability to discrimination. Existing awareness programs are scarce, and accessible learning tools are lacking, leaving both PWDs and the broader community without the skills to bridge the communication gap. This perpetuates exclusion and hinders the realization of an inclusive local economy.
Solution Overview:
iSign is an Android-based educational mobile application designed to teach basic Filipino Sign Language (FSL) to non-signers, enabling more inclusive communication with the deaf and mute community. The app offers interactive lessons, visual demonstrations, and practice exercises covering greetings, everyday expressions, and essential vocabulary for public service and daily interactions.

The solution is deployed through community-based training sessions across multiple municipalities in the province of Romblon. Participants such as barangay health workers, teachers, local officials, parents, and PWD students are introduced to the app in facilitated workshops that combine guided hands-on use, role-playing, and group activities. These sessions not only build technical sign language skills but also raise awareness about the lived experiences of PWDs, fostering empathy and inclusivity in local communities.

Methodologies and Technologies Used

Mobile Application Technology: Android-based platform ensuring wide accessibility in rural and coastal areas of Romblon where smartphones are common.

Participatory Action Research: Mixed-methods approach involving pre- and post-training assessments, observation checklists, and feedback surveys to evaluate learning outcomes and behavioral change.

Interactive Pedagogy: Role-playing, group challenges, and scenario-based exercises to reinforce skills learned from the app.

Offline Accessibility: Lessons are accessible without internet connection, addressing connectivity gaps in remote municipalities.

IEC Materials: Printed reference guides distributed alongside the app to extend learning beyond the sessions.

Partnerships and Collaboration Models
The iSign initiative is spearheaded by the College of Computing, Multimedia Arts, and Digital Innovation (CCMADI) at Romblon State University, in close collaboration with the Department of Information and Communications Technology (DICT) and the Local Government Units (LGUs) of various municipalities across the province of Romblon. These partnerships ensure alignment with both provincial and municipal inclusion programs and provide logistical, technical, and policy support for implementation.

Community organizations, particularly Persons with Disability Affairs Offices (PDAOs), the Municipal Social Welfare and Development Offices (MSWDOs), barangay councils, and local PWD associations, are directly engaged in planning, mobilization, and evaluation. This multi-sector collaboration promotes community ownership, ensures cultural and contextual relevance, and supports the long-term sustainability of the program.

Duration to pilot in a new geography: 4 months
SDGs addressed: SDG 4 (Quality Education);SDG 9 (Industry, Innovation, and Infrastructure);SDG 8 (Decent Work and Economic Growth);
Desired impact:
Solution Objectives:

-To increase basic sign language literacy among community members, local frontliners, educators, and families in the Province of Romblon.

-To promote inclusivity and social participation of deaf and mute persons by bridging communication gaps.

-To leverage mobile technology as a cost-effective, accessible tool for capacity building in marginalized communities.

-To strengthen local government and community partnerships for sustained inclusive education programs.

Key Achievements / Impacts:

-Improved Sign Language Literacy: Across three phases of implementation (2021–2025), over 600 participants including barangay health workers, municipal employees, teachers, parents, and PWD students gained basic sign language skills. Post-training assessments show 85–90% proficiency in greetings and everyday phrases.

-Increased Awareness & Empathy: In the latest implementation, 95% of participants reported greater empathy toward the deaf and mute community and a stronger commitment to inclusive practices.

-High Satisfaction Rates: Average participant satisfaction rating of 4.80/5 (96.03%) across all project sites, indicating strong perceived value and relevance of the program.

-Capacity Building: Formation of local “iSign Champions” in each implementation site to sustain advocacy, conduct peer-to-peer training, and integrate sign language in daily community interactions.

-Sustainability through Partnerships: Strengthened collaboration between Romblon State University–CCMADI, the Department of Information and Communications Technology (DICT), and Local Government Units, ensuring long-term support and potential scale-up to all municipalities in Romblon Province.
Key technologies:
The iSign solution utilizes:

Android Mobile Application Development – Built using Java and XML on the Android Studio platform for compatibility with a wide range of low- to mid-tier smartphones.

Multimedia Learning Content – Integration of instructional videos, visual illustrations, and interactive modules to teach basic American Sign Language (ASL).

Offline Functionality – Enables access to lessons without constant internet connectivity, ensuring usability in low-connectivity rural areas.

User-Friendly Interface Design (UI/UX) – Optimized for accessibility and ease of use for both tech-savvy and first-time mobile users.

Cloud-Based Content Management – For centralized updates, allowing facilitators to refresh and localize training materials remotely.
Unique Characteristics:
The iSign solution stands out for its community-driven, technology-enabled approach to inclusivity, combining mobile learning with on-the-ground training. Its unique features include:

Localized & Contextualized ASL Content – Adapts American Sign Language (ASL) lessons to the cultural and communication context of Romblon Province, focusing on everyday phrases and practical interactions relevant to local communities.

Hybrid Capacity-Building Model – Blends mobile app-based learning with face-to-face interactive workshops, ensuring both accessibility and practical application.

Inclusive Partnership Framework – Co-developed and implemented by Romblon State University–CCMADI in partnership with DICT and LGUs, ensuring government backing, technical expertise, and local ownership.

Offline-First Technology Design – Operable without internet connectivity, addressing the digital divide in geographically isolated and disadvantaged areas (GIDAs).

Sustainability Through Community Champions – Identifies and trains “iSign Champions” in each municipality who continue advocacy and peer-led training beyond the initial project period.

Scalable & Replicable Model – Modular design allows for easy adaptation in other provinces or countries with minimal re-development cost.
Sustainable Change: The iSign solution fosters sustainable and systemic change by addressing the root causes of communication barriers for the deaf and mute primarily the lack of accessible and practical sign language education and embedding the intervention within community systems to ensure long-term adoption. By combining a mobile-based American Sign Language (ASL) learning platform with in-person training, the project empowers frontliners, educators, parents, and persons with disabilities to acquire and apply essential communication skills. This dual approach not only enhances immediate ASL literacy but also builds confidence, empathy, and awareness among participants, leading to more inclusive interactions in daily life. Sustainability is ensured through the app’s offline functionality, making it accessible even in remote and underserved areas, and through the integration of sign language training into LGU programs, public services, and educational curricula. The identification and mentorship of “iSign Champions” within communities create a multiplier effect, ensuring that advocacy and peer-led training continue beyond the project’s duration. Partnerships with DICT and LGUs across Romblon Province provide institutional support, enabling scalability and replication. Over time, these combined efforts are expected to normalize sign language use in public and community spaces, embed inclusivity into governance and service delivery, and create a lasting culture of communication equity for persons with disabilities.
Funding Sources: The iSign solution has been funded through a Memorandum of Agreement (MOA) between Romblon State University (RSU) and the respective Local Government Units (LGUs) of the implementing municipalities. Under these agreements, RSU provides the technical expertise, training design, and implementation team, while the LGUs allocate financial resources to cover logistical expenses, venue arrangements, participant materials, and other operational costs necessary for the conduct of the program. This co-funding arrangement ensures shared ownership, local commitment, and sustainability of the initiative.

Title: online diagnostic medical kiosk

Project objectives:
1. Creation of a digital platform "Telemedicine Osh" - a mobile application and web portal for remote consultations with doctors.
2. Development of a health monitoring system - installation of smart kiosks in medical institutions for automatic checking of basic health indicators (blood pressure, pulse, temperature).
3. Organization of mobile medical teams - mobile groups of doctors to examine the population in remote areas.
4. Education and prevention - conducting information campaigns on a healthy lifestyle, vaccination and disease prevention.

2. Smart kiosks for health monitoring
Description:
Smart medical kiosks are automated stations for checking basic health indicators. They will be installed in medical institutions, shopping centers and public places so that residents of the Osh region can measure vital parameters for free without visiting a doctor.
Kiosk functionality:
✅ Blood pressure measurement - automatic tonometers for detecting hypertension and hypotension.
✅ Blood sugar level measurement - express analyzer for diabetics and people with prediabetes.
✅ Body temperature measurement - infrared sensors for detecting elevated temperature.
✅ Blood oxygen level measurement (saturation) - pulse oximeter for diagnosing lung diseases and COVID-19.
✅ Weight and body mass index (BMI) - built-in scales and body mass analyzer.
✅ Pulse and heart rate analysis - built-in cardiac sensor.

🔹 Long-term improvement in public health indicators in the region.

Title: Solar-Powered Digital Learning Hubs for Inclusive Education in Rural Eswatini
Subtitle: Empowering rural learners and teachers in Eswatini through solar-powered hubs that provide digital access, educational content and skills for inclusive quality education
Problem Statement: In Eswatini, many rural and underserved communities face limited access to quality education due to a lack of reliable electricity, digital infrastructure, trained teachers, and connectivity. These challenges widen the digital divide, leaving learners and educators without the tools needed to participate in a modern, inclusive learning environment. This gap disproportionately affects women, youth, and marginalized groups, hindering progress toward SDG 4 and digital inclusion.
Solution Overview:
The Solar-Powered Digital Learning Hubs for Inclusive Education in Rural Eswatini is an innovative, scalable solution designed to bridge the digital education divide by bring clean energy and digital learning infrastructure to underserved schools and communities.
1.	How the Solution Works
Each hub is a solar powered unit equipped with: 
•	Laptops or tablets pre-loaded with offline digital education content aligned with Eswatini’s national curriculum.
•	Wi-Fi routers for occasional internet access where feasible.
•	Interactive learning platforms such as Kolibri and government approved e-learning modules.
•	A teacher training program that enhances digital literacy and pedagogical skills.
The hubs are installed at strategically selected rural schools to serve learners and out of school youth. Community members particularly women and youth people can also access the hubs after schools for digital skills training and lifelong learning opportunities 
2.	Methodologies and Technologies Used 
•	Solar Energy Systems: Each hub is powered by stand-alone solar photovoltaic units with battery storage, ensuring 24/7 availability in off-grid areas.
•	Offline e-Learning Platforms: Open-source platforms such as Kolibri are customized with local content, eliminating dependency on stable internet.
•	Modular Deployment: The hub setup follows a plug-and-play design, enabling fast replication in multiple sites.
•	Blended Learning Approaches: Teachers are trained to integrate digital tools into classroom teaching and facilitate learner-centered approaches.
•	Gender-Inclusive Design: The solution includes international outreach to girls and women through safe spaces and targeted programming 
3. Partnerships and Collaboration Models
The initiative is led by the Ministry of Education and Training (MoET) in Eswatini through its Planning Unit in partnership with:
1.	UN agencies (UNESCO, UNICEF) for policy guidance and digital content
2.	Private sector partners for provision of hardware, teacher training and scaling support 
3.	Clinton Health Access Initiative (CHAI) for data monitoring and impact evaluation 
.
Solution Provider(s): 1.	Ministry of Education and Training- Eswatini (Public sector, national government ministry responsible for education policy and service delivery. 2.	UNESCO (United Nations Educational Scientific and Cultural Organisation, intergovernmental organization supporting global education and digital learning initiatives 3.	UNICEF- United Nations Children’s Fund, international organisation focused on child rights and inclusive education.  4.	CHAI – Clinton Health Access Initiative, Non-Governmental Organisation, health and development sector with expertise in data systems and monitoring and evaluation.  5.	Private ICT Service Providers in Eswatini (Private sector, supplying hardware, connectivity solutions and technical support for digital infrastructure
Duration to pilot in a new geography: 24 months
SDGs addressed: SDG 4 (Quality Education);SDG 7 (Affordable and Clean Energy);SDG 10 (Reduced Inequalities);
Desired impact:
Solution Objectives
•	To provide equitable access to quality digital education in rural and underserved communities of Eswatini through solar-powered learning hubs.
•	To build foundational digital skills amongst learners, teachers, especially targeting women, youth, and marginalized groups
•	To enhance teacher capacity in integrating digital tools for effective, inclusive teaching and learning and 
•	To promote sustainable, off-grid energy solutions that ensure continuous access to digital education resources.
Key achievements/expected impacts
•	Reach: enable access to digital learning for at least 5000 and 200 teachers in pilot phase schools with the first 24 months.
•	Digital Literacy: Train at least 150 educators and 1500 learners in basis to intermediate digital skills.
•	Gender Inclusion: Achieve at least 50% participation by girls and young women in digital learning activities and training programs.
•	Energy Impact: Reduce reliance on fossil fuels by providing clean, solar-powered energy to learning hubs, estimated to save approximately 3 000 kWh of grid electricity annually per site.
•	Scalability: Establish a replicable model that can be expanded to at least 20 additional rural locations over 3 years
Key technologies:
Key technologies used in the solution include not limited to, the following:
•	Solar Photovoltaic (PV) Systems: for clean, off-grid power supply ensuring continuous energy access to digital hubs. 
•	Offline Digital Learning Platforms: Open-source software like Kolibri and preloaded educational content aligned with national curricula, enabling access without reliable internet. 
•	Wi-Fi Networking: Local wireless connectivity within learning hubs to connect devices and enable limited online access where feasible.
•	Mobile and Tablet Devices: Laptops, tablets or low-cost computing devices optimized for educational use in low-resource settings.
•	Blended Learning Tools: Digital content delivery combined with teacher facilitation to support interactive and learner-centered approaches. 
•	Data Monitoring Systems. Simple digital tools to track usage, learners' progress, and system performance for ongoing evaluation and improvement.
Whilst this solution does not currently integrate advanced AI, loT or blockchain, it leverages proven digital education and renewable energy technologies that are scalable and sustainable in rural contexts
Unique Characteristics:
Unique and Differentiated Characteristics of the Solution
•	Integrated Solar-Powered Digital Hubs: Combining renewable energy with digital learning infrastructure ensures reliable, off-grid access to education technology in areas with limited or no electricity.
•	Contextualized Offline Learning: Use of open-source platforms customized with locally relevant educational content enables uninterrupted learning without dependency on stable internet connectivity.
•	Community-Centered Model: Strong emphasis on local ownership through collaboration with school committees, community leaders, and faith-based organizations ensures sustainability and responsiveness to local needs.
•	Gender-Inclusive Approach: Targeted outreach and safe learning spaces for girls and marginalized groups address digital and educational inequalities directly.
•	Modular and Scalable Design: The plug-and-play, replicable hub model facilitates rapid deployment across multiple rural sites with relatively low setup costs.
•	Multi-Stakeholder Partnerships: Unique collaboration between government, NGOs, faith-based organizations, UN agencies, and private sector partners creates a comprehensive ecosystem for technical, financial, and social support.
•	Alignment with National and Global Goals: Strong integration with Eswatini’s education strategy and the UN Sustainable Development Goals, enhancing chances for funding and policy support.
•	Capacity Building for Educators: Combining infrastructure with training ensures effective use of technology, not just provision of devices.
This holistic approach distinguishes the solution as both technically feasible and socially sustainable in a challenging rural context.
Sustainable Change:
By deploying solar-powered digital learning hubs, the solution initiates a transformative cycle that addresses core barriers to quality education in rural Eswatini, leading to lasting, systemic impact 
provision of renewable energy-powered digital infrastructure combined with localised educational content and teacher training. Learners and educators gain access to digital tools and skills, enabling inclusive, technology-enhanced teaching and learning. The immediate outputs will be increased digital literacy and engagement amongst students and teachers, and reliable access to educational resources regardless of electricity or internet availability. The desired short-term outcome will be improved learners’ performance, higher school attendance, and greater participation of marginalized groups (especially girls and youth) in digital education access and empowered teachers effectively using digital pedagogy. The medium-term outcomes will strengthen community capacity to maintain and scale digital education solutions, the emergence of local digital innovators and entrepreneurs, and supportive policy environments influenced by demonstrated success. Below is the long-term impact 
•	Sustainable, equitable access to quality education for rural populations, reducing education and digital divides.
•	Enhanced socio-economic opportunities through improved skills, fostering inclusive growth aligned with SDG 4 and related goals.
•	Institutionalization of digital learning as a core component of national education strategy, supported by partnerships and investment.
•	Increased resilience of education systems through decentralized, renewable energy-powered solutions.
This cascading effect fosters systemic change by transforming how education is delivered, accessed and sustained- creating a foundation for ongoing innovation, inclusion and development well beyond the pilot phase.

Summary: The 'Solar-Powered Digital Learning Hubs' program aims to bridge the digital divide in rural Eswatini by offering solar-powered educational hubs. These hubs provide offline access to digital learning resources and training for youth and teachers, focusing on renewable energy and sustainable agriculture. With support from UN agencies, local government, and private sector partners, the program will improve digital literacy, promote gender inclusion, and empower rural communities. (Q13, Q12, Q14)

Title: Congo Plast – Recyclage numérique et inclusif des déchets plastiques
Subtitle: Une solution circulaire numérique qui transforme les déchets plastiques en opportunités inclusives.
Problem Statement: La pollution plastique constitue un fléau majeur en République du Congo. Les déchets plastiques s'accumulent dans les rues, les cours d'eau et les décharges, affectant la santé publique, la biodiversité et les conditions de vie. Le secteur informel de la gestion des déchets est déstructuré et les communautés, en particulier les jeunes et les femmes, sont marginalisées économiquement.
Solution Overview: Congo Plast est une solution technologique inclusive qui repose sur la collecte, la traçabilité, le recyclage et la transformation des déchets plastiques en produits utiles (pavés, briques, etc.). Elle intègre une plateforme numérique permettant la cartographie des zones de collecte, l'enregistrement des collecteurs, la planification des opérations et la gestion de la logistique. Des partenariats avec les collectivités, les entreprises locales, des associations de femmes et de jeunes permettent une approche collaborative durable.
Solution Provider(s): Congo Plast (start-up environnementale), Association Jeunesse Verte Congo (sensibilisation), ITE Congo (partenaire technique et financier), Mairies locales (appui logistique), Collectifs de collecteurs informels, ATELIER 1000 (design et valorisation produits recyclés).
Duration to pilot in a new geography: 9 à 6 mois selon la taille de la zone et les partenariats locaux
SDGs addressed: SDG 8 (Decent Work and Economic Growth);SDG 11 (Sustainable Cities and Communities);SDG 12 (Responsible Consumption and Production);
Desired impact:
Objectifs :

Créer 200 emplois verts directs d'ici 2026 (collecteurs, trieurs, artisans).

Collecter et recycler 1000 tonnes de déchets plastiques par an.

Sensibiliser 5 000 personnes par an sur la pollution plastique et les gestes écoresponsables.


Résultats déjà observés :

15 tonnes de déchets recyclés en pavés depuis le lancement pilote.

36 jeunes formés à la collecte et transformation plastique.

Diminution visible des décharges plastiques sauvages dans les zones ciblées.
Key technologies:
Application mobile pour les collecteurs

Plateforme Web de gestion et traçabilité

Paiements mobiles (Mobile Money)
Unique Characteristics:
Intégration du numérique à chaque étape de la chaîne de valeur

Inclusion active des femmes et des jeunes du secteur informel

Modèle réplicable à faible coût

Approche collaborative avec les autorités locales et les ONG
Sustainable Change: La solution Congo Plast structure une économie circulaire numérique où les déchets deviennent des ressources, tout en créant de la valeur sociale et économique. En outillant les collecteurs avec le numérique, en professionnalisant le recyclage, et en sensibilisant la population, le projet transforme durablement les comportements, génère des revenus et favorise des villes plus propres.
Funding Sources: Congo Plast a été financé principalement par des fonds propres du fondateur, des concours d’innovation remportés (Challenge Startup OSIANE 2024; Challenge startupper de l'année 2024 par Total Energie ; Trophée jeunes entrepreneurs FIAD 2024 etc...), et un soutien technique de ITE Congo. Un processus de levée de fonds avec des investisseurs à impact est en cours pour l’expansio
Primary thematic focus area: Inclusive Digital Innovation Skills & Entrepreneurial Talent Development
Summary: Congo Plast is a digital circular solution that transforms plastic waste into useful products like paving blocks and bricks while providing economic opportunities for marginalized communities in the Republic of Congo. The project includes a digital platform for waste tracking, logistics management, and community engagement.

Title: Digitalizing and Empowering Smallholder Farmers for Sustainable Growth
Subtitle: Connecting Farmers to Markets and Knowledge for Sustainable Growth
Problem Statement: My community, Sanda Magbolontor Chiefdom-Karene District represent 16% of the 8,500 cashew farmers in Sierra Leone, unfortunately these farmers’ faces five critical challenges: digital disconnection, unsustainable farming, no local processing facility, weak market access, and old-age exclusion of women and youth in community development. These issues limit productivity, value addition, and inclusive growth, deterring the sector's potential for rural development. As a result, cashew farmers’ income have dropped from $1,200 to $840 annually, leading  farmers to tap into unsustainable practice like illegal mining, deforestation for timber trading and charcoal burning as a source of fuel.
Solution Overview:
How our Solution Works
This project aligns with Sierra Leone's National Agricultural Transformation 2023-2027 Agenda and the Global Call for Solutions for an Inclusive Digital Economy goals of enhancing Inclusive Digital Innovation Skills & Entrepreneurial Talent Development
Solutions and community-level initiatives, building foundational skills among women, youth, and marginalized groups in digital learning.
Aligned with the Inclusive Digital Economy, our project empowers smallholder cashew farmers by tackling digital disconnection, unsustainable practices, and exclusion. For example, the CashewLink App, a multilingual traceability platform with four main local dialects (including English and French , would connect 8,500 farmers to global markets, tracks carbon emissions, and ensures fair pricing, raising incomes from $840 to $1,200 annually. It would deliver market prices, weather updates, and farming tips via voice commands in Krio, Limba, Temne, Mende English and French, enhancing accessibility in Sierra Leone and Africa. Our sustainable farming workshops currently promote climate-smart agroforestry, replacing deforestation. For example, we have established a 20-acre of demo-farm and transplanted 1,400 cashew polyclonal trees that has the potential to withstand future climate crises. A women-led cooperative processes cashews locally, creating 30 jobs (50% women) and youth participation through volunteering roles, that fosters inclusion. Currently we have 117 farmers trained in our chiefdom (50% women) and three climate awareness campaign held within 45 villages impacting 84 community members in ward 227 and 228.
b) Methodologies and Technologies
Methodologies: our approach is a user-centered design, andragogy and pedagogy (storytelling, group work) ensure app usability for low-literacy farmers. Community workshops train farmers, supply high-yield polyclonal cashew seedlings, coordinate aggregation, and process cashews for sale to buyers like ComCashew. And Zamzam Cashew Company 
Technologies: the CashewLink app (currently a prototype) final designed would be a low-bandit and lightweight mobile app with offline functionality, cloud-based data for real-time updates, with digital traceability system to enhance supply chain transparency within the collapsing cashew sector.


c) Partnerships and Collaboration Models
So far we have partnered and collaborated with the National Federation of Farmers, Ministry of Agriculture, Environmental Protection Agency, UNDP, UNIPod, and Karene District Council support outreach and training. International partners, including the African Cashew Alliance and GIZ-ComCashew/MOVE, fund training in Ghana and Ivory Coast, scaling an inclusive, resilient cashew supply chain.

Title: Smart Waste Collection App & Eco-Solutions for a Cleaner Mali
Subtitle: A digital waste collection app combined with eco-products and community engagement to drive circular economy and climate action in urban Mali.
Problem Statement: The growing urbanization in Mali, particularly in Bamako, has led to an alarming increase in household waste, poor waste management practices, and a lack of structured recycling systems. Communities face health risks, environmental degradation, and low awareness around sustainable waste solutions. Furthermore, many local governments and households lack tools for effective waste monitoring, timely collection, and responsible disposal.
Solution Overview:
ACACH_Mali has developed an innovative digital waste collection platform combining a mobile and web application. Through geolocation and scheduling features, users can easily request waste pickup, track collection, and receive environmental tips. This “smart collection” system improves traceability, increases participation in sorting, and reduces illegal dumping.

In addition to the digital platform, we provide:

Eco-bricks and pavement production from recycled plastic

Reusable eco-bags to reduce single-use plastic

Environmental education workshops for youth and women’s groups


We rely on local partnerships with community leaders, municipalities, and youth organizations. Our model is inclusive, circular, and leverages technology for maximum community impact.
Solution Provider(s): CNJ Mali (Conseil National de la Jeunesse du Mali – youth engagement and community development), Mairie de la Commune I (local government – urban sanitation and waste management), Wildaf Mali (NGO – gender and women empowerment), Intec Sup (private university – education and innovation), Virbyze Venture (international innovation network – entrepreneurship and funding support)
Implementation location(s): ACACH_Mali has been implemented in Bamako, Mali, specifically in Commune I (Marseille neighborhood), a key urban area near the city’s main waste disposal site. This location serves as the pilot area for our awareness campaigns, waste collection services, and eco-product production.
Implementation timeline(s): ACACH_Mali was initiated in January 2024 and activities have been ongoing since then. The pilot phase is planned to continue through 2025 with scale-up starting at the end of 2026.

Title: Empowering Women through Body Literacy and Injury-Free Training
Subtitle: A digital platform designed to empower women with body literacy, reduce injury risks, and replace surface-focused reshaping with smart, confidence-driven training.
Problem Statement:
Most fitness platforms focus on reshaping women’s bodies superficially, ignoring the lack of foundational body literacy and female-specific training knowledge. This not only increases the risk of injury, but also undermines women’s confidence in movement. Over 90% of physical education content is built around male physiology, leaving women underrepresented and underserved.
Women in Gym addresses this gap by translating science into accessible, women-centered learning content, starting from breathing patterns to joint stability. Instead of selling the “perfect shape,” we cultivate understanding, autonomy, and injury prevention.
Our team includes a service designer, a female coach, and tech collaborators from diverse backgrounds, united by lived experience and a shared belief: knowing your body is the first step to owning your power.
Solution Overview:
MusGirlar is a digital solution developed by Women in Gym, an inclusive initiative based at the Royal College of Art that focuses on redefining women’s relationship with fitness through education and empowerment.
MusGirlar is a mobile-first learning platform designed to help women understand their own bodies, avoid injury, and build training confidence, especially in male-dominated gym cultures. Unlike traditional fitness apps that promote body reshaping, we focus on body literacy, helping women understand how their bodies breathe, stabilize, and move.

Our solution integrates principles from functional training, FMS (Functional Movement Screening), STOTT Pilates and female-specific physiology, and translates complex knowledge into visualized content, step-by-step learning journeys, and self-assessment tools. We use mobile UI/UX, anatomical 3D visuals, and behavioral design to promote long-term habit change.

The solution is co-created by a cross-disciplinary team, including a service designers, fitness coach, product designer, and user researcher with lived experiences that span cultures, professions, and body types. We also partner with health professionals, Algorithm Engineers and 30+ female gym-goers to ensure inclusivity, usability, and credibility.
Solution Provider(s): Tianxiao Yuan: Service Designer (Royal Collegof Art)/ Female Fitness Coach, Xiaoqiao Feng: Service/ UI Designer (Royal Collegof Art), Xue Hu: health professionals (Stockholm University)/ National Athlete, Mengqi Yu: Algorithm Engineers/ Technical Developervice Designer
Implementation location(s): London, United Kingdom：Royal College of Art (RCA) campus & Hyde Park（Outdoor prototype sessions focused on breathing and functional movement). Asturias, Spain：Surf camp in a rural setting used as a unique testing environment with women from diverse cultural and physical backgrounds. Online (mainland China and UK): Over 30 participants joined live Zoom sessions covering body literacy and injury prevention.
Implementation timeline(s): April 11, 2025 – June 23, 2025 This includes over 10 rounds of both online and offline prototyping, covering topics like breathing, core, pelvic, shoulder, and knee muscles. Sessions ranged from small group workshops to full interactive Zoom classes, culminating in functional training lesson trials and user feedback collection.
Duration to pilot in a new geography: 3 to 4 months This includes 1 month for contextual and cultural research, 1 month for curriculum localization and testing, and 1–2 months for piloting, community engagement, and iteration based on real-time feedback.
SDGs addressed: SDG 3 (Good Health and Well-being);SDG 4 (Quality Education);SDG 5 (Gender Equality);
Desired impact:
MusGirlar seeks to transform how women engage with movement, not through external reshaping, but through internal understanding. Our core impact is to help more women, regardless of age or background, train functionally and safely. We aim to significantly reduce the high injury risk among women who enter gyms without knowing how their own bodies actually work, and to replace fear with confidence.

Over the years, we’ve seen how women’s bodies are too often misdiagnosed, misrepresented, and misled by systems built around male norms. This has led to widespread injuries, confusion, intimidation and silence. We’re here to change that, not by demanding women fit into old models, but by building a new one from the ground up. A model where women learn how their bodies breathe, stabilize, and move on their own terms.

Through digital reach, we hope to impact thousands of women across different geographies by making body-specific, science-based learning content accessible. We want this knowledge to become common, not niche and ultimately change how fitness is introduced to the next generation of girls and women.
Key technologies:
MusGirlar is a mobile-first learning platform designed to deliver anatomical knowledge in a way that is visually intuitive and emotionally empowering. Our prototype currently includes an interactive interface with modular learning flows,  and self-reflection checkpoints. These elements are intentionally designed to help women absorb complex knowledge without relying on performance metrics or appearance-based rewards.
While AI is not yet embedded in our current prototype, we have already established connections with professionals in the AI for Health space to integrate it into the next development phase. Inspired by the principles in the book Anatomy Trains, which describes the body not as isolated parts but as interconnected fascial and functional systems, we believe AI has the potential to personalize the learning experience from the very beginning.

Many women experience discomfort or injury in one area of the body, when the root cause may lie elsewhere, something even experienced trainers can overlook. With AI support, we envision a system where a user’s body signals, posture, or self-reported pain patterns can help identify likely dysfunction chains before the learning begins. This will not only increase the precision of training advice but also dramatically enhance user retention, as learners will feel that the content is relevant to their own body, not just a generic template.

In essence, we see technology not as a driver of control, but as a tool to deepen self-understanding especially for women who have long been left out of the diagnostic loop.
Unique Characteristics:
What makes MusGirlar truly unique is not just its intention, but the knowledge system behind it. Our training content is built from a carefully curated blend of traditional fitness logic, STOTT Pilates principles from Canada, and insights from medical rehabilitation science, particularly around the role of stabilizing muscles.

But unlike conventional sports science education, our content is not dry, abstract, or divorced from reality. Every concept is tied directly to daily movement experiences, how we breathe, stand, squat, or carry bags. We make anatomy feel lived.

Most importantly, our knowledge architecture does not follow the traditional male-centric model of the body, which has long been used to define “neutral.” Instead, we built a system specifically around female physiology, drawing from the latest literature in women’s health, strength training, and hormonal science. This includes understanding how the four phases of the menstrual cycle influence strength, endurance, and recovery, as well as addressing issues such as pelvic floor dysfunction, which have been long ignored in mainstream training. We no longer treat women as "small men." We design for them on their own terms.

To deliver this content, we use a TTT pedagogical model: Test → Teach → Test. Women begin by self-assessing their functional blind spots, then enter learning modules tailored to those needs, and finally re-test to see their own progression. This model increases learning retention, enhances curiosity, and fosters a deeper emotional connection with the material. It turns movement education into a reflective and empowering process—not a one-size-fits-all curriculum.
Sustainable Change:
MusGirlar is not just a product, it is a shift in the way we teach, talk about, and experience the female body in motion. For too long, women have been training in systems built for men, learning knowledge that wasn’t designed with them in mind. As a result, we’ve seen women’s bodies misdiagnosed, misrepresented, and misled, treated as "small men" in both education and rehabilitation. MusGirlar exists to break that pattern.
By building a movement education system rooted in female-specific physiology, hormone-responsive training, and everyday functionality, we are laying the foundation for long-term, systemic change. This begins by giving women language, structure, and science to understand their own bodies—not through shame or control, but through curiosity and clarity.

Our goal is to normalize a new standard of body literacy, where women no longer wait for external validation or injury to understand their biomechanics, but grow up knowing how to train, breathe, and move in tune with their physiology. When this knowledge becomes widespread, gyms will shift. Coaches will shift. The language of health will shift.

MusGirlar is designed to be scalable, accessible, and adaptable across cultural and linguistic contexts. Our long-term plan includes integrating AI-supported diagnostics that can help users identify hidden physical dysfunctions before training even begins, deepening personalization and user commitment. Over time, this will help dismantle the knowledge asymmetry that keeps women dependent on generic, ineffective models.

Systemic change happens when you don’t just teach people what to do—but help them reclaim the right to ask why. And that is what MusGirlar was created for.
Funding Sources: Our project originated as a student initiative, and we did not receive major external funding in its early stages. However, we were granted £200 from the Student Union to support our initial work. Beyond that, every aspect of our development, including UI design, service blueprinting, prototyping, user interviews, and website development was entirely self-funded and completed by our team members. As women who share similar training experiences and a deep passion for reclaiming women's bodily autonomy, we’ve been fully committed to investing our own time and resources, even without immediate return, because we believe in the long-term impact of this mission.
Testimonials and Endorsements:

Diana, a certified Stott Pilates educator, expressed her admiration for our work and offered to feature our project on her teaching website for her students to access and learn from."https://theinnercore.co.uk/our-team/" "I’m so thrilled to have met you and proud of your work. I will move coming week to get in touch with STOTT teachers and would like you to create a link on my web—it will be amazing!"

Carolyn Runcie, a tutor at the Royal College of Art (RCA)"https://www.rca.ac.uk/more/staff/carolyn-runcie/", acknowledged our team’s clear proposition and impact:
"You've created a strong, clear narrative that communicates the journey you've been on and the impact of your proposition, whole body awareness for function, small fixes for big impact, and understanding pain to work with it. Well done!"

Additionally, we’ve received valuable testimonials from our early-stage users, many of whom report increased body awareness, improved pain conditions, and growing confidence in exercise. The quotes like "I can actually feel the muscle pump more intensely.”“The painful hip click I felt every time I squatted is gone.”"Finally, someone addressed postpartum leakage and it’s improving.”"I’ve learned how to better “My core awareness during movement has become much stronger.”
Further comments/feedback:
We truly appreciate the opportunity to share our work through this questionnaire. As an all-women team, we have poured tremendous effort, time, and heart into this project—not only through the work itself, but also by building meaningful connections with like-minded individuals. Title: Tech for All: Community-Led Digital Inclusion & Economic Empowerment
Subtitle: Community-driven digital skills training, tools, and market linkages empowering rural youth and women to thrive in the digital economy.
Problem Statement: In rural Pakistan, especially in districts like Jacobabad and Kashmore, limited internet access, low digital literacy, and scarce economic opportunities exclude youth and women from participating in the digital economy. Many lack the skills, tools, and networks needed to access online markets, remote jobs, and e-learning platforms. This digital divide deepens economic inequality, limits innovation, and hinders sustainable community growth. Without targeted, community-driven solutions, marginalized groups risk being left further behind in an increasingly digital global economy.
Solution Overview:
How it Works:
“Tech for All” is a community-led initiative that equips rural youth and women with practical digital skills, access to technology, and market linkages to fully participate in the digital economy. The program uses a hub-and-spoke model: central community digital hubs serve as training and innovation centers, while trained youth facilitators cascade knowledge to remote villages. Participants learn digital literacy, e-commerce, freelancing, online safety, and use of productivity tools, enabling them to secure remote jobs, start online businesses, and access global markets.

Methodologies & Technologies Used:

Capacity Building: Structured training modules covering basic to advanced digital skills, delivered in local languages and using interactive, learner-centered methods.

Digital Platforms: Introduction to e-commerce sites, freelancing platforms, and agri-tech/mobile apps for market access.

Blended Learning: Combination of in-person sessions, mobile-based learning materials, and video tutorials.

Offline-Online Integration: Use of portable devices and offline content to overcome poor connectivity in remote areas.

Market Linkages: Facilitation of connections between trainees and digital job platforms, online buyers, and micro-finance providers.

Partnerships & Collaboration Models:

Local Partnerships: Collaboration with schools, women’s groups, and farmer associations to mobilize participants and provide venues for digital hubs.

Private Sector Engagement: Partnerships with local IT companies, mobile network operators, and e-commerce platforms for mentorship, job placements, and reduced-cost internet/data packages.

Government & NGO Linkages: Coordination with vocational training authorities, municipal offices, and NGOs for technical input and sustainability support.

International Collaboration: Potential integration with UN-led initiatives, global digital platforms, and social enterprises for scaling and cross-country learning.
Solution Provider(s): Community Advancement & Support Welfare Association (CASWA) – A registered NGO based in Jacobabad, Pakistan, accredited by the Pakistan Centre for Philanthropy (PCP). CASWA works in digital literacy, youth empowerment, women’s economic inclusion, climate resilience, and community development.  Sindh Technical Education & Vocational Training Authority (STEVTA) – Government body providing technical training accreditation and skill certification in Sindh’s vocational and digital sectors.  Trade Testing Board Karachi – Certifies vocational and digital skills, enhancing employability of trainees for local and global markets.  National Humanitarian Network (NHN) – Civil society network facilitating advocacy, resource sharing, and capacity building for inclusive community development.  Stop-TB Partnership Pakistan – Multi-sectoral platform focusing on community outreach, health awareness, and mobilization, strengthening grassroots engagement.
Duration to pilot in a new geography: Month 1: Community needs assessment, partner engagement, and setup of digital hubs.  Months 2–4: Training of local facilitators, delivery of digital literacy and entrepreneurship modules, and ongoing mentoring.  Month 5: Establishing market linkages, online profiles, and small-scale digital income opportunities for participants.  Month 6: Monitoring, evaluation, and refinement for scale-up
SDGs addressed: SDG 4 (Quality Education);SDG 8 (Decent Work and Economic Growth);SDG 10 (Reduced Inequalities);
Desired impact:
Solution Objectives

Bridge the digital divide for rural youth and women through accessible skills training, technology access, and market linkages.

Increase participation of marginalized groups in the digital economy, enabling sustainable income generation and entrepreneurship.

Strengthen community resilience by integrating digital tools into education, agriculture, and small business development.

Promote gender equality by ensuring at least 50% of beneficiaries are women and girls.

Key Achievements / Expected Impacts (Pilot Stage)

Employment & Income: 300+ rural youth and women trained in digital skills; at least 150 gain remote or local digital jobs within 6 months of training.

Entrepreneurship: 50+ women-led micro-enterprises established or enhanced through e-commerce platforms.

Market Access: 100+ farmers connected to online marketplaces and agri-tech platforms, increasing incomes by 20–30%.

Digital Inclusion: Internet and device access improved for over 500 community members via local digital hubs.

Gender Equality: Equal participation of women and men, with leadership opportunities for female trainers.

Scalability: Model adaptable to other rural districts within 6–12 months with minimal infrastructure investment.
Key technologies:
Key Technologies Utilized

Digital Learning Platforms – Use of e-learning tools (Google Workspace, Learning Management Systems) for delivering interactive, multilingual training content.

Mobile Applications – Agri-tech, e-commerce, and freelancing apps (e.g., Upwork, Fiverr, Daraz) to connect participants with markets and remote job opportunities.

Offline-First Solutions – Portable devices and pre-loaded content to enable training in low-connectivity areas.

Cloud Storage & Collaboration Tools – Google Drive, Microsoft OneDrive for sharing resources, assignments, and tracking participant progress.

Data Analytics & Monitoring Tools – Digital attendance, progress tracking, and impact measurement systems for real-time decision-making.

AI-Powered Learning Support – Introduction to AI chatbots and generative AI tools for content creation, translation, and business automation.

Social Media Marketing Tools – Facebook Business Suite, WhatsApp Business, and Canva for promoting products/services and personal branding.
Unique Characteristics:
Unique & Differentiated Characteristics

Community-Led Model – Unlike top-down digital programs, “Tech for All” trains local youth as facilitators who then cascade skills within their own communities, ensuring cultural relevance and trust.

Inclusive Access Design – Combines online tools with offline-first solutions so even low-connectivity, device-poor communities can participate fully.

Integrated Economic Pathways – Goes beyond skills training by linking participants directly to income opportunities through e-commerce, freelancing, and agri-tech platforms.

Gender-Responsive Approach – Targets at least 50% women beneficiaries, offers women-only training spaces, and builds female leadership within the digital economy.

Public–Private–Community Partnerships – Leverages government vocational boards, local NGOs, and private sector tech companies for training, certification, and job placement.

Sustainability & Scale – Low-cost digital hubs and train-the-trainer models enable rapid replication in new geographies without heavy infrastructure investments.

Emerging Tech Integration – Introduces participants to practical uses of AI, mobile-based agri-advisory systems, and digital marketing automation for small businesses.
Sustainable Change:
Contribution to Sustainable, Systemic Change

Theory of Change:
If rural youth and women gain access to affordable digital tools, targeted skills training, and market linkages, then they will be able to participate in the digital economy, secure sustainable livelihoods, and drive local innovation — leading to reduced poverty, greater gender equality, and inclusive economic growth.

Pathway to Change:

Inputs: Digital hubs, trained facilitators, curriculum, partnerships with tech companies, e-commerce platforms, and vocational certification bodies.

Activities: Digital literacy training, entrepreneurship coaching, AI tool orientation, market linkage facilitation, and ongoing mentoring.

Outputs: Trained community members with digital and business skills, access to online work, and operational online enterprises.

Outcomes (1–3 years):

Increased household incomes through digital jobs and online businesses.

Greater participation of women in economic decision-making.

Reduced migration pressures by creating local income opportunities.

Impact (3–5 years):

Sustained digital inclusion in rural communities.

Strong local ecosystems that continuously generate digital employment.

Communities equipped to adapt to technological change and economic shifts.

Systemic Change Mechanisms:

Community ownership: Local facilitators and hubs become permanent resources beyond project funding.

Public–private linkages: Partnerships create long-term access to markets, certifications, and innovation networks.

Policy influence: Demonstration of scalable, inclusive models can inform national digital inclusion strategies.
Funding Sources:
Funding Sources

Previous pilot implementations of CASWA’s digital literacy and economic empowerment initiatives, which form the foundation of “Tech for All,” have been funded through:

Grants from International Development Partners – e.g., British Council (Pakistan Youth Leadership Initiative) supporting youth digital skills and leadership training.

Local NGO Partnerships – Collaborative funding with networks such as the National Humanitarian Network (NHN) for community mobilization and outreach.

Private Sector Support – In-kind contributions from local IT companies, including refurbished computers, internet packages, and mentorship support.

Community Contributions – Venues, volunteer trainers, and outreach support provided by local schools, women’s groups, and farmer associations.

CASWA Core Funds – Allocations from CASWA’s internally generated resources to co-finance equipment, training materials, and facilitator costs.

These diverse funding streams have enabled small-scale pilots while demonstrating the model’s viability for scale-up through multi-donor and blended financing approaches.
Testimonials and Endorsements:

— Shazia Bibi, Women Entrepreneur, Jacobabad (CASWA Digital Skills Program, 2024)
