Further comments/feedback: Tech for All” is more than a digital skills program — it is a scalable, community-owned model that transforms rural youth and women into active contributors to the global digital economy. With the right partnerships, it can close the digital divide in some of the most underserved regions while creating lasting, inclusive economic growth.
Primary thematic focus area: Inclusive Digital Innovation Skills & Entrepreneurial Talent Development
Summary: Tech for All is a community-driven digital literacy and entrepreneurship training program designed to empower rural youth and women in Pakistan with the skills and tools necessary to participate in the digital economy. By focusing on local digital hubs and market linkages, the initiative promises to bridge the digital divide in rural areas and create sustainable livelihoods.

Title: Digital Bridges Initiative: Empowering Women & Youth for Inclusive Growth
Subtitle: Bridging Afghanistan’s digital divide through skills training, online work access, and inclusive entrepreneurship for marginalized women and youth.
Problem Statement: In Afghanistan, women and youth—especially in rural and underserved areas—face severe barriers to participating in the digital economy due to limited connectivity, restrictive gender policies, low digital literacy, and scarce employment opportunities. This exclusion deepens poverty, widens the gender gap, and limits community resilience. Without targeted, accessible, and safe digital inclusion strategies, millions remain cut off from economic participation and global markets.
Solution Overview:
Bright Destiny empowers Afghan women and girls through an online entrepreneurship and skills development platform that bypasses Taliban restrictions on female education and work. The solution delivers structured, mentor-led training programs in entrepreneurship, career development, and digital literacy, enabling participants to start and manage income-generating projects from home.

How it works:
The program is delivered entirely online through secure channels, ensuring safety and accessibility for women across Afghanistan. Participants join interactive workshops, receive personalized mentoring, and access resource toolkits (business planning templates, marketing guides, and financial literacy materials). Selected participants receive small grants to kickstart their projects, along with access to digital tools like Canva Premium, LinkedIn Premium, and ChatGPT Premium for business enhancement.

Methodologies and technologies used:

Blended learning approach: Combines live sessions, recorded modules, and one-on-one mentorship.

Human-centered design: Training content is adapted to cultural and political constraints, ensuring inclusivity and security.

Digital platforms: Zoom/Google Meet for live sessions, Google Workspace for collaboration, and cloud-based resources for material sharing.

Monitoring and evaluation: Google Forms and progress tracking dashboards to measure learning outcomes and project performance.

Partnerships and collaboration models:
Bright Destiny collaborates with international mentors, grant providers (e.g., APCEIU), and local female professionals to design and deliver training. Partnerships focus on knowledge sharing, funding support, and providing in-kind resources like online tools and expert hours. We adopt a co-creation model, where participants and mentors jointly develop solutions tailored to local challenges.
Solution Provider(s): Bright Destiny Initiative – founded and led by Yaser Yousofi, focusing on socio-economic empowerment of Afghan women and girls through online education, entrepreneurship training, and career development programs. Partner organizations include:  APCEIU (Asia-Pacific Centre of Education for International Understanding) – education-focused UN-affiliated organization providing mentorship and grant support.  Now Bahar Coordination and Reconstruction Organization (NBCRO) – Afghan NGO engaged in community development and humanitarian work.  International volunteer mentors – professionals from Watson Institute, UPG Sustainability, and other global networks.
Implementation location(s): Afghanistan – online platform serving women and girls in Kabul, Herat, Nangarhar, Bamyan, and remote provinces where in-person education is restricted.
Implementation timeline(s): 1st Round: Oct 1, 2022 – Mar 30, 2023  2nd Round: Jul 15, 2023 – Dec 30, 2023  3rd Round: Sep 15, 2024 – Oct 15, 2024
Duration to pilot in a new geography: 3–6 months, including localization, recruitment, and adaptation of training materials.
SDGs addressed: SDG 4 (Quality Education);SDG 5 (Gender Equality);SDG 8 (Decent Work and Economic Growth);
Desired impact:
Objectives:

Provide safe, accessible, and high-quality education for Afghan women under restrictive conditions.

Equip participants with entrepreneurial and digital skills for self-reliance.

Foster microenterprise creation and income generation.


Key Achievements:

80+ women trained in entrepreneurship and career development.

15+ microbusiness ideas developed, some already launched with small grants.

90% participant retention rate despite challenging socio-political environment.
Key technologies:
Online learning platforms (Zoom, Google Meet)

Collaborative tools (Google Workspace, Canva Premium, LinkedIn Premium)

Digital marketing tools for small business growth (social media platforms, WhatsApp for Business)
Unique Characteristics:
Operates entirely online to bypass Taliban restrictions while ensuring safety.

Employs only female trainers and mentors to comply with local regulations.

Provides small grants ($100) directly to participants for immediate project start-up.

Integrates global mentorship networks into local grassroots implementation.
Sustainable Change:
Our Theory of Change:

Inputs: Training, mentorship, online resources, seed grants.

Activities: Deliver entrepreneurship and digital skills workshops online; connect participants to mentors; support business launch.

Outputs: Women-led microenterprises, increased employability, and digital literacy.

Outcomes: Increased household income, reduced economic dependency, expanded local female-led economic participation.

Impact: Breaking cycles of poverty and exclusion, building resilient female entrepreneurship ecosystems despite restrictive environments.
Funding Sources:
Funding Sources
Bright Destiny has been funded through small international grants and mentorship programs.

APCEIU Mentorship & Grant Program – Funded the 3rd round of the Bright Destiny Entrepreneurship Fellowship (2024).

Western Union Foundation Fellowship – Provided seed funding during the first program round (2022).

In-kind contributions from mentors and partner organizations, such as free training hours, technical resources, and software licenses.

Small donations from individual supporters.
Testimonials and Endorsements:
Bright Destiny gave me the courage and skills to launch my own tailoring business from home. The grant and mentoring I received changed my life and allowed me to support my family." — Fellowship Participant, Herat Province (2023)

"In a time when education for women is banned in Afghanistan, Bright Destiny is a lifeline. It offers not just knowledge but a pathway to independence." — Mentor from the APCEIU Program (2024)
Further comments/feedback: The questionnaire is well-structured and allows for detailed explanation of innovative solutions. I particularly appreciate the sections that encourage real-life examples and testimonials, as they help convey the human impact behind the work. However, a short guidance note with sample answers could make it easier for applicants from diverse backgrounds—especially those from low-connectivity regions—to complete the form more confidently. Title: AI and space-base technology application in Education for underserved communities
Subtitle: A SaaS AI-powered platform and deployment of LEO satellite-powered learning hubs in underserved schools and communities.
Problem Statement: When long stay in school and exam preparation after school occurs, secondary school students aged 10–18 in rural & sub-urban areas of Nigeria have daily academic struggles due to poor connectivity, poor facilities, limited access to quality tutors, and the pressure of balancing school with side jobs. Because of this, they feel frustrated, hopeless, and unmotivated due to poor learning resources, and growing self-doubt that affects their confidence and self-esteem, then experience failure in major exams, miss university admission and abandon their aspirations. Currently, they seek help from teachers and peers, attends public tutor houses despite limited resources and uncertainty, have divided academic focus, lacked engagement and had no personalized learning experience.
Solution Overview:
Teachly’s solution proposes development of SaaS AI-powered platform using LEO satellite-powered learning hubs to underserved secondary school students in rural areas. These hubs provide scheduled, low-bandwidth internet access for students to engage with a data-light, cloud-synced educational platform and preloaded learning devices. Value is created for Students through reliable access to structured and engaged community learning via increased digital literacy and local involvement with adaptive and personalized learning.
The technology used will look this way:
1.	AI
2.	Space-based technology i.e LEO/NTN/HTS
3.	React/Flask
4.	AR/VR Tools
5.	GIS Tools
6.	Cloud Services
7.	Payment & Messaging
8.	Security & Scalability: AES encryption, SSL/TLS, Microservice architecture 

Partnerships and collaboration models
1. Freemium Model for Students: We offer basic access to CBT practice, video lessons, and Smart Classroom tools for free, especially through school partnerships. This builds trust, encourages adoption, and reaches low-income students.
2. Subscription-Based Premium Access 
-Personalized tutoring sessions via the Virtual Tutoring Hub
-Advanced CBT features (performance analytics, timed mocks, exam predictions)
-Offline content downloads for independent learning
3. School Licensing / Institutional Sales: Schools or local governments can license the Smart Classroom platform and CBT tools for use across entire classrooms or districts.
-This includes teacher training, device setup (if needed), and ongoing support.
-Potential revenue stream through bulk licenses or per-school/year pricing.
4. Sponsored Access Through NGOs & CSR Programs: We plan to partner with NGOs, education-focused foundations, and corporate social responsibility (CSR) programs that will sponsor access for underserved communities.
5. Add-on Services: Exam Bootcamps & Device Bundling
We will offer seasonal bootcamps (virtual or physical) for WAEC/JAMB prep at a small fee.
6. Community Collaboration: We will partner with individuals and companies in underserved communities.
Solution Provider(s): 1. NIGCOMSAT
Implementation location(s): Implementation in the secondary schools in Ibadan
Duration to pilot in a new geography: 4-6 Weeks
SDGs addressed: SDG 4 (Quality Education);SDG 9 (Industry, Innovation, and Infrastructure);SDG 10 (Reduced Inequalities);
Desired impact:
Solution Objectives
•	Improved Educational Equity and Inclusion
•	Increased Exam Success and Access to Higher Education
•	 Long-Term Socioeconomic Mobility
Impacts
-Reduction in Negative Alternative Means of Economic Growth
-At least 45% of students from underserved areas from 3 pilot states enrolled on the platform in the next one year
-At least Six (6) of rural or low-connectivity schools using Teachly Smart Classroom in each pilot state
-At least 5,000 of students accessing content offline or without data within a year
-At least 65% of Teachly users who pass WAEC/NECO/JAMB
-Average score improvement after 3+ months of use
-At least 50% of students gaining admission to tertiary institutions
-At least 60% of students reporting increased confidence and academic motivation
-At least 65% of users referring Teachly each academic term/year (referral marketing)
Key technologies:
The technology components powering Teachly will look this way:
1. Core Technical Architecture (Modular & Offline-First)
•	Frontend: Mobile-first web app and Android app (React Native/Flutter) optimized for low-bandwidth environments and offline content delivery.
•	Backend: Cloud-based server (Azure, AWS or Google Cloud) for user data, content management, and analytics; with offline data sync capabilities.
•	Data Storage: Local device caching and encrypted SD card support for Smart Classroom and CBT modules; cloud backup for user progress.
•	APIs: RESTful APIs to support modular integration of CBT, tutoring, GIS, and analytics.
2. Proprietary Components
•	Teachly Smart Classroom Engine: Custom offline content delivery system that supports lesson playback, quizzes, and teacher control without internet.
•	AI-Powered Learning Engine (in development): Proprietary algorithm to adapt content and practice tests to student ability, confidence, and engagement.
•	Virtual STEM Lab Modules: In-house developed AR/VR STEM simulations for mobile devices, designed for science subjects in low-resource schools.
•	GIS Mapping Dashboard: Custom-built for planning and targeting underserved schools using geospatial data.
3. Third-Party Technologies and Services
•	AI/ML Libraries: TensorFlow Lite / PyTorch Mobile for on-device learning analytics and AI tutoring.
•	GIS Tools: QGIS for mapping; Google Maps API or Mapbox for visualization; open geo-datasets (e.g., OpenStreetMap, WorldPop).
•	AR/VR Tools: Unity 3D for immersive lab content; WebXR for browser-based simulations; ARCore for Android support.
•	Cloud Services: AWS or Firebase for hosting, real-time database, and content delivery (CDN).
•	Payment & Messaging: Paystack/Flutterwave for subscriptions; Twilio/WhatsApp for user engagement and tutoring access.
•	Learning Management System (LMS) Integrations: Moodle or custom LMS-lite for school deployments.
Security & Scalability
•	Data Protection: AES encryption for offline data; SSL/TLS for all online communications.
•	Scalability: Microservice architecture for modular scaling of CBT, tutoring, and lab components across regions.
Unique Characteristics:
1. Built for the Unconnected: Offline-First, Low-Bandwidth Smart Classroom: Unlike most EdTech tools that rely on consistent internet access, our Smart Classroom works in offline or low-bandwidth environments, making it usable in underserved rural and sub-urban communities. It brings interactive digital learning right into public schools without the need for expensive infrastructure.
2. Personalized, Affordable Virtual Tutoring Hub: Our Virtual Tutoring Hub connects students to trained tutors in their local dialect and curriculum, delivering personalized academic support, emotional encouragement, and mentorship. It simulates a live tutoring experience that is accessible even after school hours thereby bridging the student-teacher gap with empathy and engagement.
3. Localized, Exam-Focused CBT Platform: Our Computer-Based Test (CBT) engine is not just exam practice, it is tailored to WAEC, NECO, and JAMB standards with intelligent feedback and performance analytics. 4. A Holistic Learning Ecosystem, Not Just a Tool: Rather than offering a single product, we provide a cohesive ecosystem that supports student’s academic, emotional, and motivational needs; before, during, and after school. Our integration of learning, testing, tutoring, and mentoring is unmatched in the rural EdTech space.
5. Rooted in Local Reality, Scalable by Design: All our solutions are designed based on field research, piloted in real rural classrooms, and continuously adapted based on student behavior and educator feedback. We are building not just an app, but a movement to unlock the potential of Nigeria’s overlooked learners.
6. Affordable, Flexible Access for Low-Income Families: Our model is built to accommodate families that can’t afford private tutors or high data costs. With ₦500–₦1,000/month pricing, seasonal bootcamps, and freemium options, we are financially inclusive.
7. Community-Driven Approach: We engage schools, parents, and local ambassadors, not just users. This grassroots model builds trust and adoption where other tech-first companies can’t gain traction.
8. Emotional & Motivational Support: Beyond academics, we address the emotional struggle of self-doubt, failure, and low confidence through mentoring and personalized feedback, something most platforms completely ignore.
Sustainable Change:
1. Teachly is addressing Root Causes, Not Just Symptoms: We tackle the structural barriers to quality education in rural and underserved Nigerian communities such as poor connectivity, lack of quality tutors, inadequate facilities, and low exam success rates with an offline-first, affordable, and curriculum-aligned platform that works in the most challenging environments.
2. Building Capacity Within the Education Ecosystem: Our Smart Classroom, Virtual Tutoring Hub, and CBT platform are designed to empower students, teachers, and schools, not replace them. By providing teacher dashboards, localized training, and resource access, we strengthen local education capacity and reduce long-term dependency on external support.
3. Enabling Equitable Access at Scale: Through low-cost subscription models, institutional licensing, and NGO/government partnerships, Teachly ensures that equity is built into the system, making high-quality learning accessible to every student regardless of location or income.
4. Data-Driven Policy and Resource Allocation: Our GIS mapping and analytics will generate real-time insights into where learning gaps exist, enabling government bodies, NGOs, and schools to allocate resources strategically towards transforming not just individual learning but the entire education planning process.
5. Breaking the Cycle of Educational Inequality: By improving exam success rates, we increase university admissions, career opportunities, and lifetime earning potential, creating long-term socioeconomic mobility. This shifts communities away from negative alternative livelihoods toward sustainable economic growth.
6. Creating a Self-Sustaining Model: Teachly’s multiple revenue model balancing direct sales, institutional licensing, and sponsored access which ensures financial sustainability while reinvesting in innovation, content development, and regional expansion.

Title: Satellite-IoT Platform Bridging Ancient Farming Wisdom with Modern Technology
Subtitle: Combining ground-based LoRa sensors with NMD satellite connectivity to help African farmers adapt traditional knowledge to climate change, providing real-time insights for precision agriculture
Problem Statement:
1. Climate Change Disruption: Traditional farming knowledge passed down through generations is failing as climate change creates unpredictable weather patterns, leaving farmers unable to rely on ancestral wisdom for planting, irrigation, and harvest timing.
2. Limited Agricultural Information Access: Remote African farmers lack access to real-time data about soil conditions, weather forecasts, and crop health, forcing them to make critical decisions based on guesswork rather than data-driven insights.
3. Connectivity Gaps: Rural and remote farming communities across Africa have little to no reliable internet connectivity, preventing them from accessing agricultural information, market data, and modern farming techniques.
4. Inefficient Resource Management: Without precise monitoring, farmers struggle with water usage optimization, leading to crop losses from over-irrigation or drought stress, while also wasting precious water resources.
5. Post-Harvest Losses: Lack of early warning systems for diseases, pests, and adverse weather conditions results in significant crop losses that could be prevented with timely intervention and data-driven decision-making.
6. Economic Vulnerability: Unable to access market information and weather forecasts, smallholder farmers remain vulnerable to price fluctuations and climate shocks, perpetuating cycles of poverty in rural communities.
7. Food Security Risks: As traditional farming methods become unreliable and yields decline, food security across Africa becomes increasingly threatened, requiring urgent technological intervention to maintain agricultural productivity.
Solution Overview:
How AgriConnect Works
AgriConnect operates through three integrated layers:
Ground Layer: LoRa-powered sensors monitor soil conditions, weather patterns, and crop health across farms, transmitting data with 15km range and 5+ year battery life.
Satellite Layer: NMD satellite technology ensures reliable data transmission from remote areas, providing weather intelligence and enabling communication where traditional internet fails.
AI Layer: Machine learning algorithms analyze sensor data and traditional farming knowledge to generate real-time insights, automated alerts, and precision recommendations delivered through mobile applications.

Key Technologies
LoRaWAN networks for low-power, long-range sensor communication
NMD satellite infrastructure for remote area connectivity
Multi-parameter sensors (soil, weather, crop monitoring)
Machine learning pipeline for data analysis and predictions
Mobile applications with farmer-friendly dashboards
Smart irrigation systems with automated control

Partnerships
Academic: AIMS Cameroon provides research foundation, student expertise, and institutional support through Roland's research leadership.
Technology: NMD Satellite Technology delivers satellite infrastructure and connectivity solutions for remote farm access.
Implementation: 5-farm pilot program with direct farmer engagement, training programs, and community-based support networks to ensure real-world applicability and traditional knowledge integration.
Training Programs: Comprehensive farmer education on technology use, and access
Solution Provider(s): African Institute for Mathematical Sciences Cameroon (AIMS Cameroon) - Leading Pan-African network of centers of excellence for postgraduate education, research and public engagement in mathematical sciences, Academic/Research Sector, NMD Satellite Technology - Satellite technology company providing connectivity infrastructure and solutions across Cameroon, Telecommunications/Technology Sector

Title: Digital Skills Development for Employment Program (DSDEP)
Subtitle: DisDEP
Problem Statement:
Sierra Leone is on the cusp of a digital transformation, a journey critical for the nation's progress and economic diversification. Yet, a significant challenge currently hinders this potential: a widening skills mismatch within the labor market. There's a clear and growing demand for technologically proficient youth to fill emerging roles in the ICT sector, but a critical shortage of young people with the specific, market-ready skills needed. This fundamental disparity isn't just an abstract concept; it directly translates into high unemployment rates among the country’s eager youth and represents substantial missed economic opportunities that could otherwise accelerate national development. Without targeted and immediate intervention, a generation of promising Sierra Leoneans risks being sidelined, unable to fully participate in the burgeoning digital economy.
The root causes of this critical skills gap are systemic and multifaceted. Firstly, access to quality ICT education remains severely limited, particularly for youth in underserved urban areas and beyond the capital. Even where education is available, the curricula are often outdated, failing to evolve at the rapid pace of technological advancements and industry demands. This means that by the time students complete their programs, the knowledge they've acquired may no longer align with the current needs of employers. This fundamental disconnect leaves many graduates with theoretical understanding but lacking the practical competencies essential for roles in areas like software development, data analytics, digital marketing, and cybersecurity—fields that are increasingly vital for a modern economy.
Furthermore, the absence of sufficient practical training opportunities significantly exacerbates the problem. Many educational and vocational institutions in Sierra Leone struggle with inadequate infrastructure, a lack of up-to-date equipment, and a shortage of instructors with current industry experience. Consequently, students are often deprived of the crucial hands-on experience necessary to translate theoretical knowledge into employable skills. The vital linkages between training institutions and the private sector—such as internships, apprenticeships, and industry-led projects—are either underdeveloped or non-existent. This void prevents youth from gaining real-world exposure and practical application of their learning, rendering them unprepared to meet the tangible skill requirements of the labor market upon graduation.
The consequences of this pervasive skills gap are profound, impacting both individual lives and national development. When youth graduate without the market-relevant skills, they face the harsh reality of unemployment or underemployment, leading to economic disempowerment, diminished self-worth, and increased social exclusion. This not only squanders the immense potential of our young population but also deprives Sierra Leone of a dynamic, innovative workforce critical for driving sustainable economic growth and diversification beyond traditional sectors.
Addressing this challenge is therefore more than just a matter of job creation; it is about empowering a digitally capable generation, unlocking Sierra Leone's full economic potential, and building a more resilient, inclusive society where every young person has the opportunity to thrive in the digital age. This is the urgent call to action our proposal seeks to answer.
Solution Overview:
Sierra Leone aims to leverage digital transformation for socio-economic development, focusing on expanding connectivity and enhancing digital competencies. The ICT sector contributed 3.4% to Sierra Leone's GDP in 2020, and the government is pushing for further growth and job creation through digital transformation. Challenges include limited internet penetration, affordability, reliance on a single submarine cable, and a digital skills gap, which the government is addressing through policies and strategies.
Against this backdrop, there is a widening skills mismatch in Sierra Leone's labor market, with a shortage of technologically proficient youth to fill emerging ICT roles. The root causes include limited access to quality ICT education, outdated curricula, and insufficient practical training opportunities. The consequences include high unemployment among youth and missed economic opportunities, hindering national development.
Project1825 therefor seeks OPEC Fund support for digital skills for Employment initiative to equip Sierra Leonean youth with digital and entrepreneurial skills. The program aims to support and expand the reach of ongoing OPEC Fund interventions, such as the Education Sector Support Project and the Climate Finance and Energy Innovation Hub. The Coding for Employment program can augment the outcomes of OPEC Fund Intervention in the Freetown WASH and Aquatic Environment Revamping Project, and generate new business opportunities for the OPEC Fund’s future investments.
What the project is about
The project aims to transform young people's lives by closing the digital skills gap, helping them find meaningful jobs and build lasting businesses. It will establish accessible digital excellence centers, deliver market-driven ICT skills training, and facilitate direct employment and entrepreneurial pathways. The main activities include conducting feasibility studies, developing training center infrastructure, recruiting trainers, implementing training programs, and establishing private sector partnerships.
The project’s work breakdown structure includes establishing digital excellence centers, designing and developing training center infrastructure, and recruiting and training center management and support staff. Activities also involve developing and localizing demand-driven curricula, recruiting expert trainers, and implementing structured training programs. The project will facilitate direct employment and entrepreneurial pathways, establish private sector partnerships, and provide career development and job placement support.
Project Inputs
The project requires international and national staff, including consultants and experts, along with physical facilities, equipment, and materials. Specialized services, such as architectural and engineering services, construction contractors, and ICT infrastructure specialists, are needed. Essential resources include land for the National Academy, training centers, office premises, equipment, software licenses, and training materials.
Anticipated Impact
The project aims to directly benefit 3,000 young Sierra Leoneans by providing them with digital skills and entrepreneurial acumen. Indirect beneficiaries include tutors, business coaches, guest speakers, employers, consumers, local communities, and the government. Key impact indicators include employment rates of graduates, startup survival rates, gender parity in tech, and improvements in the digital literacy index.
Proposed Project Cost and Financing Plan
The project cost includes direct and indirect costs sum up to $150,000, with a detailed budget provided in the annex.
Why it matters
Before implementation, Sierra Leone faces high youth unemployment and a digital skills gap, which this project addresses. During implementation, the project ensures tangible impact through modern digital centers, enhanced employability, and trained local tutors. Post-project, a skilled workforce and thriving tech sector will boost productivi

For the private sector, the telecommunication agencies like the Orange Sierra Leone and Africel.
Implementation location(s): This is a solution that has already been piloted in the second city of Bo at the Bo Innovation Hub, 147 Old Railway Line, Bo city.

This project aims to transform young people's lives by closing the digital skills gap, helping them find meaningful jobs and build lasting businesses in Sierra Leone's growing digital economy.

To achieve this ambitious goal, the project will pursue the following objectives:

Establish Accessible Centers of Digital Excellence: To set up fully equipped, modern digital training centers in strategic urban which will serve as hubs for high-quality, demand-driven ICT education, ensuring that youth, particularly those from underserved backgrounds, have equitable access to state-of-the-art learning environments and resources.

Unique Characteristics:
Our strategy is informed by lessons learned from previous interventions and aligned with key national and international digital development agendas. We acknowledge that isolated training programs yield limited results without a supportive ecosystem, a lesson reinforced by past evaluations. Our approach directly integrates the vision of Sierra Leone's Directorate of Science, Technology and Innovations (DSTI – see official website https://www.dsti.gov.sl/) by focusing on human capital development as a cornerstone for national digital transformation. It also aligns with the National Digital Development Strategy of Sierra Leone (see https://dig.watch/resource/national-digital-development-strategy-of-sierra-leone), which emphasizes infrastructure, skills development, and digital government.

Our project builds crucial physical digital infrastructure and cultivates the ICT professionals needed to drive these strategic pillars. Furthermore, the International Trade Centre (ITC)'s "READY Salone" project (see: [ITC READY Salone launch https://www.google.com/search?q=https://african.business/2025/01/apo-newsfeed/international-trade-centre-itc-launches-ready-salone-project-to-train-3000-sierra-leonean-youth-for-the-digital-economy/), focusing on empowering youth through digital technologies and entrepreneurial competitiveness, provides valuable insights into demand-driven training and market linkages. Our private sector engagement, curriculum design based on labor market assessments, and dedicated job placement support directly incorporate these lessons to ensure our graduates meet industry needs.

Crucially, our project strategy is designed to complement and build upon existing and ongoing initiatives funded by key development partners like the UN-EU- and OPEC Fund for International Development. Our project complements these by providing specialized, advanced ICT and entrepreneurial skills, taking students beyond basic education to direct economic participation.
By creating a pool of digitally skilled youth, our project fosters the technical capacity necessary to innovate within emerging sectors like blockchain, AI , IOT and renewable energy, providing the human capital to leverage and contribute to such green initiatives. This synergistic approach ensures our investment multiplies the impact of other development efforts, rather than duplicating them.

This project is essential as it directly addresses these gaps by equipping in three years, 3,000 young Sierra Leoneans with critical, market-driven ICT skills, transforming a vulnerable demographic into a productive, self-reliant workforce. The integration of business coaches and industry guest speakers further strengthens the practical relevance, bridging academic learning with real-world demands and fostering an immediate impact on beneficiaries' capabilities.

Title: Green Pay Wallet: Digital Finance for Inclusion & Sustainable CleanTech.
Subtitle: Green Pay Wallet empowers underserved communities with easy digital payments, promoting financial inclusion and supporting sustainable clean-tech livelihoods in Uganda’s slums.
Problem Statement: In Uganda’s slums, marginalized communities lack access to formal financial services, limiting their economic opportunities and growth. Traditional payment methods are inefficient, and many clean-tech initiatives struggle to scale without reliable digital finance tools. This digital divide restricts livelihoods, especially for waste collectors and low-income earners, perpetuating poverty and social exclusion.
Solution Overview:
Solution Overview:
Green Pay Wallet is a simple mobile payment platform designed to help underserved communities in Uganda’s slums access financial services. Users, including waste collectors and small entrepreneurs, can send and receive money, save, and access small loans using their basic mobile phones through USSD codes—no internet required. The wallet also rewards users for adopting clean and sustainable practices, encouraging environmentally friendly behavior.

Methodologies and Technologies:
The platform operates via USSD technology, making it accessible to people without smartphones or internet. It’s easy to use, secure, and works on all mobile networks. The system tracks transactions and rewards to support users’ financial growth and promote green habits.

Partnerships and Collaboration Models:
Green Pay Wallet partners with local businesses, mobile network providers, microfinance institutions, and community groups. These collaborations help reach more users, provide financial products, and promote sustainable livelihoods in the community.
Solution Provider(s): Martyrs Clean Solutions Ltd — A social enterprise focused on clean-tech and community empowerment in Uganda’s slums, specializing in waste management and digital financial inclusion.  MTN Uganda and Airtel Uganda — Leading mobile network operators providing USSD mobile money infrastructure and connectivity services.  Sweepers SACCO, Kampala — A savings and credit cooperative serving waste collectors and informal workers in Kampala, offering microloans and savings products tailored to their needs.  Local Community-Based Organizations (CBOs) — Grassroots groups facilitating community engagement, outreach, and training on financial literacy and sustainable practices.
Implementation location(s): Not applicable. Currently in pilot readiness stage, with planned implementation in Kampala slums, Uganda.
Duration to pilot in a new geography: The estimated duration to pilot the Green Pay Wallet in a new geography is 9 months. This timeframe allows for community engagement, user onboarding, monitoring, feedback collection, and iterative improvements to ensure successful adoption and impact.
SDGs addressed: SDG 1 (No Poverty);SDG 8 (Decent Work and Economic Growth);SDG 11 (Sustainable Cities and Communities);
Desired impact:
Solution Objectives:
Green Pay Wallet aims to promote financial inclusion for marginalized communities in Uganda’s urban slums by offering accessible digital payment services via USSD. The solution will empower waste collectors and small entrepreneurs to save money, access microloans, and adopt eco-friendly practices through incentivization, fostering sustainable livelihoods and cleaner communities.

Key Achievements/Impacts (Planned):

Pilot-ready platform designed to serve users without smartphones or internet access.

Anticipated to improve financial access for  underserved individuals especially in slums.

Expected to promote sustainable waste management and reduce environmental pollution through community incentives.

Plans to build strong partnerships with mobile network operators and local cooperatives to ensure scalability and impact.
Key technologies: Green Pay Wallet uses USSD (Unstructured Supplementary Service Data) technology, enabling users to access digital financial services on any mobile phone without requiring internet or smartphones. This makes the platform highly accessible to underserved communities. The system integrates with mobile money platforms provided by MTN and Airtel Uganda to facilitate secure money transfers, savings, and microloan access. The technology is user-friendly, fast, and secure, designed to work across all mobile networks to ensure broad reach and usability.
Unique Characteristics: Green Pay Wallet stands out for its accessibility, using USSD technology to serve users without smartphones or internet access, which is crucial for underserved communities in Uganda’s slums. Unlike traditional financial services, it integrates digital payments directly with local clean-tech initiatives, incentivizing eco-friendly behaviors through digital rewards. Its unique partnership model combines mobile network operators, local SACCOs, and community groups, creating a supportive ecosystem that promotes financial inclusion and sustainable livelihoods. Additionally, by focusing on informal workers like waste collectors, it addresses a neglected segment with tailored financial products, making the solution both socially impactful and scalable.
Sustainable Change: Green Pay Wallet creates sustainable, systemic change by empowering marginalized communities with accessible financial tools that foster economic independence and resilience. By integrating digital payments with incentives for eco-friendly practices, it encourages behavioral shifts towards sustainable waste management and environmental stewardship. The solution’s partnership with mobile operators, SACCOs, and community groups builds a robust local ecosystem that supports ongoing financial inclusion and entrepreneurship. As users gain financial literacy and access to credit, they can improve their livelihoods, reduce poverty, and contribute to cleaner, healthier communities. Over time, this model can be scaled and adapted to other regions, driving widespread socio-economic and environmental transformation.
Funding Sources:
Funding Sources:
To date, Green Pay Wallet has been primarily self-funded by Martyrs Clean Solutions through internal resources and limited community contributions. We are currently seeking external funding and partnerships to support pilot implementation and scale-up efforts. No formal grants or investment have been received yet, but we have engaged potential partners including mobile network operators and local SACCOs who are interested in collaborating.
Testimonials and Endorsements:
Testimonials and Endorsements:
While Green Pay Wallet is currently in the pilot readiness phase, we have received encouraging feedback from community leaders and local SACCO representatives who recognize the potential impact of the solution on financial inclusion and sustainable livelihoods. As the project progresses, we will gather formal testimonials from beneficiaries and partners to demonstrate its effectiveness and community acceptance.

It would be helpful if future forms allowed saving progress for longer periods and provided examples of strong responses to guide applicants, especially those working in early-stage projects. Overall, the process is very encouraging and motivating for innovators like myself.

Summary: Green Pay Wallet is a mobile-first, USSD-based digital payment platform designed to foster financial inclusion in Uganda’s slums, connecting waste collectors and small entrepreneurs to financial services, microloans, and eco-friendly incentives.

Title: WACOT SmartFarms: Empowering Farmers through Smart Agro Solutions
Subtitle: WACOT’s digital platform is a user-friendly web-based application that facilitates farmer onboarding, farm mapping, input distribution, extension services, market linkage, warehousing, inventory, and supply chain management, fostering inclusive growth in agriculture and rural economies
Problem Statement: Smallholder farmers produce over 80% of rice consumed in Nigeria. However, these farmers and agricultural MSMEs face persistent challenges that threaten their productivity, incomes, and resilience. Many lack reliable access to quality farm inputs and timely extension services with the current extension worker-to-farmer ratio in the country put at 1:8500. This directly impacts yields, especially for vulnerable farmers whose livelihoods depend on a single rain-fed farming cycle increasingly disrupted by climate change. Limited access to markets and affordable financial services, coupled with low digital literacy, leaves them dependent on middlemen and vulnerable to unfair pricing. Manual record-keeping and fragmented supply chains make hinder efficiency and make it difficult to track produce from farm to market. The absence of real-time data on production, logistics, and quality standards undermines traceability, quality assurance, and timely decision-making, leading to signific ant post-harvest losses and missed opportunities especially for women, youth, and rural communities who are disproportionately excluded from the benefits of digital economy reducing their ability to adapt, compete, and grow in an increasingly technology-driven agricultural landscape.
Solution Overview:
The WACOT App is a robust, web-based farming business management platform designed to bridge critical gaps in Nigeria’s agricultural value chain. It seamlessly connects smallholder farmers, input suppliers, labor providers, transporters, and processors, either directly or through a shared agent network, thereby reducing inefficiencies and strengthening value chain linkages. The platform enables comprehensive digital farmer and farm data management, leveraging Internet of Things (IoT) devices, data from the Nigerian Meteorological Agency (NiMet), Artificial Intelligence (AI), and simple text-based channels to deliver tailored extension services.

Through precise farm mapping, farmer profiling, and the capture of key production data, the WACOT App supports real-time monitoring, better planning, and data-driven decision-making. Field agents use the app to geo-map farm coordinates, register farmer profiles, and capture production data such as crop type, planting date, and yield estimates. Farmers can easily dial a universal code to connect with the extension service center, where they receive personalized advisory services in their preferred local language. Extension advisories are also delivered via SMS/voice, WhatsApp, and USSD, aligned to the farmer’s location, crop cycle, and climatic conditions.

The platform enhances market access by providing real-time market price alerts and facilitating direct linkages to buyers, thereby improving farmers’ bargaining power. It also sends alerts on the cost and quality of farm inputs and the nearest access points, with options to purchase in cash or on credit, repayable after harvest.

From 2021 to 2024, WACOT partnered with EveryFarmer under the USAID/WACOT Rice Outgrower Expansion Program, onboarding and managing over 6,000 smallholder farmers across Kebbi State farming communities. This collaboration resulted in a 100% increase in rice yields, the creation of over 7,000 direct and indirect jobs, and improved livelihoods for women and youth farmers. The proven model demonstrates the platform’s scalability, potential for impact, and capacity to transform smallholder agriculture in Nigeria through technology-driven solutions. 

Specific functions of the App include:
i.	Input credit tracking to monitor distribution, usage, and repayment, Traceability modules for supply chain monitoring from production to processing
ii.	Geo-mapping & GIS: Uses GPS-enabled devices to capture accurate farm coordinates and boundaries.
iii.	Farmer Profiling Database: Stores demographic, socio-economic, and production data for analytics.
iv.	Mobile-first Design: Android app for field agents and USSD interface for farmers without smartphones.
v.	Offline Functionality: Allows data capture in rural areas without internet; syncs when connected.
vi.	API Integrations: Connects with weather services, financial institutions, and digital marketplaces.
vii.	Data Analytics: Aggregates and analyzes farm data to improve forecasting, supply planning, and policy alignment.

The solution will be implemented through partnerships with farmer-based organizations and cooperatives for community onboarding, financial institutions to extend credit products linked to app-generated farmer profiles, technology partners for customization and maintenance, research institutions for training and climate-smart agriculture integration, development agencies to build capacity among women and youth, and input suppliers and off-takers to streamline distribution and ensure transparent, traceable procurement.

By digitizing interactions between farmers, aggregators, and buyers, it strengthens transparency, optimizes logistics, and opens up access to markets and services particularly for women, youth, and rural farming communities who are often excluded from the digital economy.
Solution Provider(s): 1. WACOT Limited – Leading agribusiness company in Nigeria specializing in agro-processing, farming, and trading, operating in sesame, maize, rice, and cotton value chains (Agriculture & Agro-processing). 2. EveryFarmer – Digital agriculture platform connecting farmers to markets, finance, and extension services while promoting traceability and inclusive value chains (AgriTech & Market Access), 3. Ahmadu Bello University, Zaria will provide a tailored training and research and climate smart agriculture and technology, as well as Good Agronomic Practices.
Duration to pilot in a new geography: 6–12 months including stakeholder engagement, localization of the WACOT App, farmer onboarding, training, and initial data collection
SDGs addressed: SDG 1 (No Poverty);SDG 2 (Zero Hunger);SDG 5 (Gender Equality);
Desired impact:
Solution Objectives include: 

* Digitally integrate 7000 smallholder farmers and rural MSMEs into inclusive, traceable, and efficient agricultural value chains.
* Improve farmer productivity by 30%, market access, and income through data-driven advisory services, input distribution, and buyer linkages for 7000 smallholder farmers over 12 months.
* Strengthen climate resilience by leveraging EVERYFARMER and NiMet’s localized weather forecasts and climate-smart practices.
* Facilitate access to Agri input financing for 7000 farmers using verifiable digital farmer profiles and transaction histories.

Key Achievements/Impacts (current and projected) include: 

* 7000 rice farmers onboarded and digitally profiled across Kebbi State. 
* 25–30% increase in farmer yields through the adoption of CSA, improved agronomic practices and timely advisory services.
* Average income increase of 20% for participating farmers via direct buyer connections and fair pricing.
* 40% reduction in post-harvest losses by improving supply chain coordination and traceability.
* Reduced GHG  footprint by training farmers on Alternate Wet and Dry, optimizing transport and storage logistics (estimated 5–10% reduction).
* Creation of 2000 direct and indirect  jobs for field agents, extension workers, data operators and laborers across farming communities.
* Strengthened participation of women and youth—with 30% of app users being female farmers and 25% under the age of 35.
Key technologies: The WACOT app leverages mobile technology for field data collection, GIS-based farm mapping, cloud-based data management, and data-driven financing workflows, using predictive analytics for credit scoring to improve smallholder farmer support and program delivery. Additionally, AI-supported prompts are incorporated to provide text- and voice-based tailored advisory support to farmers, taking into account their specific needs and literacy levels.
Unique Characteristics:
The solution stands out for its integrated, partnership-driven model that merges digital technology tailored to farmers’ needs and capacities, while bridging the market access gap, providing tailored advisory service and climate information support, and Agri-input financing within  a single farmer-centric ecosystem. 

Key differentiator include:

* End-to-End Agricultural Digitization: Unlike standalone advisory or trading apps, the WACOT App combines farmer profiling, GPS mapping, climate-smart advisory, input distribution, buyer linkages, and financial access in one seamless platform.
* Verified Data for Financial Inclusion: Creates digitally verifiable farmer profiles with transaction histories, enabling partner banks to extend credit with reduced risk.
* Climate-Smart Integration: Real-time weather forecasts and seasonal planning from NiMet embedded into daily farming decisions.
* Inclusive Value Chain Approach: Strong focus on integrating women and youth into high-value agricultural markets through targeted training and access programs.
* Hybrid Partnership Model: Combines corporate resources (WACOT), digital innovation (EveryFarmer), and research institution for scalable and sustainable impact.

Immediate Outcomes (0–2 years):

* Better informed farming decision through access to climate data and information. 
* Improved income via direct buyer connections and fair, transparent pricing.
* Enhanced climate resilience through localized weather forecasts and adaptive farming practices.
* Access to credit through verified digital profiles and transaction records.

Intermediate Outcomes (2–5 years):
* Establishment of a digitally inclusive agricultural market system where farmers, buyers, and service providers transact seamlessly.
* Reduction in post-harvest losses and logistics inefficiencies through supply chain visibility and efficiency.
* Reduce GHG emission via the adoption of climate smart agriculture practices and technologies. 
* Empowerment of women and youth with digital skills, market access, and entrepreneurial opportunities.
* Generate direct and indirect jobs across farming communities.

Long-Term Systemic Change (5+ years):
* Transformation of rural economies into digitally connected, climate-resilient, and financially inclusive agricultural hubs.
* Strengthened food security and export competitiveness through traceable, quality-assured production.
* Increased school enrollment among children and improved health-seeking behavior across farming communities.

Title: Digital Skills for Grassroots Women & Youth to Drive Inclusive Economies
Subtitle: Empowering underserved women & youth with digital skills, resources & education to drive sustainable, inclusive economic growth
Problem Statement: Many women and youth in underserved communities lack access to affordable digital tools, reliable internet, and the skills needed to participate in today’s economy. This digital gap limits their ability to access online markets, secure remote jobs, and benefit from e-learning opportunities. Without targeted interventions, these groups risk being left further behind in economic growth, deepening poverty and inequality.
Solution Overview:
Solution Overview

Our solution equips underserved women and youth with practical digital skills, affordable access to technology, and market-linked training to unlock economic opportunities. Through community-based Digital Empowerment Hubs, participants receive training in computer literacy, online business tools, e-commerce, and remote work readiness.

How it works
We establish locally managed hubs with internet-enabled computers, solar-powered charging stations, and low-cost device access. Participants undergo structured training programs combining digital literacy, entrepreneurship, and financial inclusion, supported by mentoring and peer learning.

Methodologies & Technologies

Blended Learning: Combining in-person workshops with online courses to ensure flexibility.

Low-bandwidth Digital Platforms: Mobile-friendly tools that work offline and sync online when connected.

Practical Market Projects: Participants apply skills to real-world micro-enterprises and digital freelancing tasks.

Sustainable Tech Use: Solar energy solutions to ensure consistent access in off-grid areas.

Partnerships & Collaboration Models
We collaborate with local schools, vocational centers, and women’s associations to identify participants and deliver training. Partnerships with tech companies provide donated devices, software, and training resources. We also work with microfinance institutions to link graduates to small loans for launching digital-enabled businesses.

This integrated approach ensures that women and youth not only gain digital competency but also have the tools, networks, and financial means to participate fully in the inclusive digital economy.
Solution Provider(s): Cunningham Grassroots Empowerment Initiative (CGEI) – A Nigerian NGO dedicated to empowering underserved women, youth, and communities through education, vocational skills, gender equality advocacy, and sustainable livelihoods. Sector: Nonprofit / Community Development.  National Information Technology Development Agency (NITDA) – Federal agency promoting IT development in Nigeria, providing digital training frameworks, and supporting innovation hubs. Sector: Government / ICT Development.  MTN Nigeria Foundation – Corporate social responsibility arm of MTN Nigeria, supporting community development through digital literacy programs, ICT infrastructure, and educational initiatives. Sector: Private Sector / Telecommunications.  Co-Creation Hub (CcHub) – Nigeria’s premier innovation center providing technology-driven solutions, startup incubation, and training in digital entrepreneurship. Sector: Technology / Innovation.  LAPO Microfinance Bank – Provides microloans, savings schemes, and financial literacy to low-income individuals, especially women entrepreneurs. Sector: Financial Services / Microfinance.
Duration to pilot in a new geography: he pilot implementation in a new geography is estimated to take 6–9 months.  Months 1–2: Community needs assessment, partner engagement, and setup of the Digital Empowerment Hub (infrastructure, equipment, and recruitment).  Months 3–6: Delivery of blended digital literacy, entrepreneurship, and market-linked training programs, alongside mentorship support.  Months 7–9: Business incubation support, linking participants to online marketplaces, and monitoring & evaluation of impact.  This timeline ensures thorough preparation, high-quality delivery, and measurable results before scaling to other locations.
SDGs addressed: SDG 4 (Quality Education);SDG 5 (Gender Equality);SDG 8 (Decent Work and Economic Growth);
Desired impact:
Solution Objectives

Equip underserved women and youth with market-relevant digital skills to increase economic participation.

Bridge the digital divide by providing access to affordable technology, internet connectivity, and practical online business tools.

Foster sustainable livelihoods by linking participants to e-commerce platforms, remote work opportunities, and microfinance support.

Strengthen community resilience through inclusive, tech-enabled solutions that promote gender equality and poverty reduction.

Key Achievements / Desired Impact (Quantifiable Targets for Pilot)

Train 200+ women and youth in digital literacy, entrepreneurship, and online income generation within 6–9 months.

Establish 1 fully functional Digital Empowerment Hub equipped with internet-enabled devices, solar power, and learning resources.

Achieve at least 60% employment or business start-up rate among trained participants within 3 months post-training.

Enable 30+ women-led microenterprises to access online markets, boosting average income by 20–30%.

Provide ongoing mentorship and digital support to ensure sustainable long-term impact beyond the pilot phase.
Key technologies:
Key Technologies Used

E-Learning Platforms: Mobile-friendly learning management systems (LMS) to deliver digital literacy and entrepreneurship courses, accessible even on low-end smartphones.

Productivity & Collaboration Tools: Applications such as Google Workspace, Microsoft 365, and Canva to teach participants practical, market-relevant skills.

Solar-Powered ICT Infrastructure: Renewable energy solutions to power computers and internet hubs in off-grid or low-electricity areas.

Digital Marketing Tools: Social media platforms (Facebook, Instagram, WhatsApp Business) and basic analytics tools to enable online business growth.

Offline-Capable Applications: Training and business tools that function without constant internet access, syncing data when connectivity is available.

Basic Data Analytics Tools: Simple analytics software to track learning progress, measure business performance, and support informed decision-making.
Unique Characteristics:
Unique/Differentiated Characteristics

Community-Centered Digital Hubs: Unlike standard training programs, our model establishes locally managed hubs equipped with solar-powered ICT infrastructure, ensuring reliable access even in off-grid areas.

Blended & Inclusive Learning Model: Combines in-person mentoring with mobile-friendly online training that works on low-end devices and offline, making it accessible to rural women and youth.

Integrated Pathway to Livelihoods: Goes beyond skill acquisition by linking participants directly to online marketplaces, remote work platforms, and microfinance services to support business start-up or job placement.

Cross-Sector Partnerships: Leverages collaborations with tech companies, local government agencies, vocational centers, and financial institutions to pool resources, reduce costs, and expand reach.

Sustainability Focus: Uses affordable, low-maintenance technology and trains local facilitators to ensure continued operation and community ownership after the pilot phase.
Sustainable Change:
Contribution to Sustainable, Systemic Change (Theory of Change)

Our solution tackles the root causes of economic exclusion—limited digital access, low skills, and lack of market linkages—by providing underserved women and youth with practical digital competencies, affordable technology, and direct pathways to income generation.
If we establish community-run Digital Empowerment Hubs,
and provide blended training that is accessible, gender-inclusive, and market-driven,
and link graduates to online job opportunities, e-commerce platforms, and microfinance support,
then participants will not only earn sustainable incomes but also become role models, trainers, and digital service providers within their communities.

Over time, this approach will:
•	Multiply impact as trained individuals transfer skills to peers and family members.
•	Strengthen local economies by increasing the number of small, tech-enabled businesses.
•	Influence policy and partnerships to improve digital infrastructure and inclusion nationwide.
•	Break cycles of poverty and gender inequality by ensuring women and youth have lasting, competitive roles in the digital economy.
The systemic change lies in creating self-sustaining digital ecosystems within communities—where access, skills, and opportunities are continuously generated and maintained locally, long after the pilot phase ends.

Corporate Social Responsibility (CSR) Contributions: Donations of equipment, internet access, and training resources from Nigerian private sector partners in telecommunications and technology.

Community Contributions: In-kind support such as venue provision, volunteer facilitators, and logistical assistance from local leaders and community groups.

Self-Financed Components: NGO operational funds allocated to pilot training activities and basic digital literacy workshops.

These funding models have enabled us to successfully deliver skills training and livelihood projects, laying the groundwork for scaling our digital empowerment solution through new strategic partnerships and larger grant funding.

Through locally managed Digital Empowerment Hubs, the initiative aims to enhance economic participation and foster sustainable livelihoods. Title: Digital Skills for All: Empowering Youth for the Inclusive Digital Economy
Subtitle: Former les jeunes défavorisés aux compétences numériques pour réduire la fracture digitale et stimuler l’inclusion économique.
Problem Statement: In Chad, only 16% of the population uses the Internet (ITU, 2023) and less than 10% of households own a computer. In rural areas, access to digital skills is virtually non-existent. More than 65% of young people are unemployed or underemployed, largely due to a lack of training tailored to the needs of the digital market. This digital divide reinforces inequalities, limits economic opportunities, and hinders local innovation.

Title: Youth-Led Digital Inclusion for Gender-Equal Futures
Subtitle: Partnering with youth-led organizations to drive digital inclusion, close the gender digital divide, and build sustainable economic futures for young people in underserved communities.
Problem Statement: Despite increased digital connectivity, significant disparities persist in access to digital skills, economic opportunities, and safe participation in the digital economy, particularly for young women and marginalized youth. Many youth-led organizations (YLOs), which are best positioned to address these challenges locally, lack the institutional capacity, tools, and support systems to drive inclusive digital transformation. Systemic barriers such as gender-based exclusion, inadequate representation in digital policy spaces, and limited exposure to scalable, context-specific models continue to widen the gender digital divide and constrain youth-driven innovation in underserved communities.
Solution Overview:
The Going Beyond model is a scalable and gender-responsive approach that strengthens Youth-Led Organizations (YLOs) to drive inclusive digital transformation in their communities. DOT acts as a capacity-building hub, equipping YLOs, particularly women-led entities, with the skills, methodologies, and networks to deliver context-relevant digital skills, entrepreneurship, and youth leadership programs.

How the solution works:

- DOT identifies and partners with community-based YLOs, delivering a structured Organizational Development Program (ODP) that builds their institutional capacity.
- These YLOs, in turn, mobilize and train Youth Leaders, 70% of whom are women, who deliver peer-to-peer digital skills training, facilitate safe digital engagement, and lead community-based economic empowerment initiatives.
- Through mentorship, access to digital tools, and integration of gender-responsive strategies, the program ensures that youth, especially women, can participate meaningfully and safely in the digital economy.

Methodologies and technologies used:
- Peer-to-peer learning and youth leadership development
- Gender-sensitive curriculum delivery and training-of-trainers models
- Hybrid training modalities using online platforms, virtual hubs, and locally facilitated sessions
- Monitoring & evaluation frameworks for continuous impact measurement
- Digital resource hubs, including e-learning platforms and toolkits tailored for community adaptation

Partnerships and collaboration models:
- Youth-Led Organizations (YLOs) are central delivery partners, co-designing and implementing local programs.
- DOT serves as the technical and strategic enabler, providing capacity-building, tools, coaching, and quality assurance.

Title: oneAklan
Subtitle: A mobile-first B2B marketplace and AI assistant that connects MSMEs across Aklan and Western Visayas—helping micro, small and medium enterprises find suppliers, customers, funding and local business support.
Problem Statement: MSMEs in Western Visayas face fragmented markets, limited digital visibility, low access to locally relevant business advice, and difficulty finding reliable suppliers and buyers. This results in missed market opportunities, inefficient procurement, and barriers to growth—especially for rural and language-minority entrepreneurs who lack affordable, localized digital tools and business intelligence.
Solution Overview:
oneAklan is a mobile-first platform combining a hyperlocal B2B marketplace (requests/offers), geospatial MatchMaker AI, and an AklanConnect AI chatbot to meaningfully reduce barriers for MSMEs across Region 6.

How it works (high level)

Businesses register or explore in guest mode, post requests/offers, and browse local product listings.

MatchMaker AI uses geolocation, category, intent, historical engagement and preference signals to rank best-fit partners and surface high-quality matches.

AklanConnect AI (GPT-4 based, localized prompts) provides bilingual (English/Bisaya) business advice—pricing guidance, supplier sourcing, government program navigation (DTI/DOST/DA), and step-by-step operational recommendations.

Consumable tokens (Match Boosters, Priority Passes) and subscription tiers (Pro/Premium) let businesses increase visibility and unlock advanced analytics.

Backend is built for data privacy, offline resilience and low-bandwidth operation; includes an analytics dashboard for monitoring performance and match success.

Methodologies & technologies

Mobile-first UX built with React Native / Expo for fast deployment across Android/iOS.

Serverless/postgres-backed backend using Supabase for authentication, real-time DB and secure server-side validation.

Revenue & billing via in-app purchase integrations (platform-native flows) and RevenueCat for cross-platform subscription handling.

AI: fine-tuned prompt engineering and context-aware LLM orchestration (OpenAI GPT-5, Anthropic Sonnet 4, and Gemini) plus lightweight on-device caching for responsiveness.

Geospatial processing and distance-calculation for accurate local matching; ML ranking models trained on anonymized usage data to improve relevance over time.

Security, monitoring and validation: server-side purchase verification, session management, and role-based access control.

Partnership & collaboration model

Public-private collaboration with local government (DTI, DOST, DA), universities for skills/training, and chambers/cooperatives for outreach.

Tech partnerships with cloud and API providers for hosting, analytics and AI services.

Revenue model: freemium marketplace + Pro/Premium subscriptions + consumable token purchases to ensure sustainability while keeping essential features free for micro-enterprises.

Capacity building: local workshops and online help center co-developed with partner agencies to increase adoption and digital skills.

Impact & scalability

Designed to scale from Aklan to the broader Western Visayas and replicateable to other provinces—low-cost deployment and modular components enable regional rollouts.

Focus on inclusion: offline/low-bandwidth features, bilingual support, and guest mode lower barriers for first-time digital users.

Title: AgriPulsr AI — Farm Brain for Climate-Resilient Smallholders
Subtitle: An AI-driven, mobile-first platform that combines hyper-local forecasting, disease detection, dynamic market matching, and finance readiness to reduce losses and raise incomes for smallholder farmers.
Problem Statement: Smallholder farmers across Asia-Pacific face volatile weather, invisible pest and disease outbreaks, fragmented markets, and limited access to affordable finance. These factors lead to unpredictable yields, high post-harvest losses, weak bargaining power, and exclusion from formal credit — perpetuating poverty and food insecurity.
Solution Overview:
How it works: AgriPulsr AI bundles a farmer mobile app, cloud AI models, and partner services into an integrated Farm Brain that continuously reduces risk and maximizes returns. Farmers submit smartphone photos, basic farm telemetry, and optional sensor/satellite data. The platform delivers: instant plant/disease diagnosis, hyper-local short-term weather and pest forecasts, precision input recommendations, and AI-optimized harvest-to-market timing.

Methodologies & technologies:

Computer vision for plant and soil diagnosis.

Spatio-temporal ML models combining satellite imagery, local telemetry, and weather feeds for short-range forecasting and spoilage risk.

Optimization algorithms to map harvest timing and local demand to best available markets and logistics.

Index-trigger logic for automated micro-insurance payouts.

Offline-first mobile design with SMS gateway fallback for low-connectivity areas.

Secure cloud DB for farmer records and consented analytics.

Partnership & collaboration model:

Work with local cooperatives and extension services for farmer outreach and training.

Integrate with telcos for low-cost data/SMS, fintechs and microfinance partners for credit distribution, and insurers for index products.

Collaborate with national ag research institutes to localize crop models and validate recommendations. Deployment follows a co-design pilot approach with government, NGO, and private off-takers.
