Title: Breaking the walls of Late Breast Cancer Screening.
Subtitle: Building a world where no woman dies simply because of late breast cancer Detection.
Problem Statement:
Breast cancer is the most common cancer in women worldwide, responsible for 685,000 deaths annually according to the WHO. The tragedy is not just its prevalence, it’s that over 70% of breast cancer deaths occur in low and middle income countries, where late stage diagnosis is the norm. In many of these regions, less than 10% of women receive regular screening due to the high cost, limited availability, and logistical barriers of traditional mammography.

Current detection methods are failing the women who need them most. Mammogram machines cost $150,000+, require specialized technicians, and depend on radiation based imaging that is unsuitable for frequent use, particularly for younger women. This creates massive access gaps: rural clinics and community hospitals cannot afford or operate such equipment, forcing women to travel long distances often hundreds of kilometer to urban centers. The result is late diagnosis, when treatment is more expensive, less effective, and survival chances drop drastically.

In Africa alone, breast cancer survival rates hover around 40%, compared to over 85% in high income countries, largely due to late detection. Each year of delay in scaling accessible screening tools costs hundreds of thousands of lives and billions in treatment expenses.
Solution Overview:
Intellibra is a breakthrough AI powered breast cancer detection tool built to save lives through earlier, faster, and more accessible screening. Unlike traditional mammograms that rely on costly, bulky machines and expose women to radiation, Intellibra uses a portable, non invasive, radiation free scanning system paired with advanced AI to deliver instant, highly accurate risk assessments anywhere in the world.

Our proprietary technology combines ultrasound and thermal imaging with machine learning algorithms trained on a diverse, anonymized dataset of breast health scans, enabling early identification of suspicious tissue changes even before lumps are physically detectable. Unlike mammograms, our system is painless, safe for frequent use, and works effectively for women under 40 and those with dense breast tissue  demographics often underserved by current screening methods. The scan results are displayed on our mobile app which also offers sensitization and telemedicine services.

We are currently in pathnership with the Ministry of Health in Cameroon who provides us with access to government owned hospitals for clinical trials.
Solution Provider(s): Ministry of Health Cameroon, Hopital General de Yaounde
Duration to pilot in a new geography: About 6 months to complete the prototype and 3 months for testing
SDGs addressed: SDG 3 (Good Health and Well-being);SDG 9 (Industry, Innovation, and Infrastructure);SDG 8 (Decent Work and Economic Growth);
Desired impact:
Intellibra’s mission is to make early breast cancer detection accessible, affordable, and stigma free for women everywhere, regardless of income or location. Our objectives are to:

1. Detect breast cancer in its earliest stages using a portable, non-invasive, radiation free device powered by AI-driven thermal and ultrasound imaging.

2. Reduce breast cancer mortality rates in underserved communities by increasing early screening adoption.

3.Empower women with proactive health monitoring and education to break cultural barriers around breast health.

4. Integrate seamlessly into low resource healthcare settings such as mobile clinics, rural hospitals, and community health programs.

Key Achievements & Impact

1. Detection accuracy: In early pilot tests, Intellibra achieved over 80% accuracy in identifying abnormal breast tissue patterns compared to traditional screening.

2. Speed & accessibility: Our device delivers results in under 10 minutes without radiation or pain, making it more acceptable to women who fear or avoid mammograms.

3. Cost-effectiveness: Screening cost is projected to be up to 70% lower than conventional mammography, enabling wider adoption in low income regions.

4. Community reach: Through partnerships with NGOs and mobile health clinics, we aim to screen 50,000 women in the first two years of deployment, prioritizing rural and underserved populations.

5. Lives saved: By shifting diagnosis from late stage to early stage detection, we estimate the potential to reduce breast cancer mortality in target communities by 30–40% over five years.

6. Awareness & empowerment: Our outreach programs will train 500+ community health workers and deliver breast health education to over 100,000 women within three years.

Our desired impact is clear: turn breast cancer from a late-stage death sentence into an early-stage, treatable condition for every woman, everywhere.
Key technologies:
1. AI-Powered Thermal and Ultrasound Imaging – Intellibra uses advanced infrared thermal cameras to capture detailed heat maps of breast tissue and piezoelectric sensors which are non invasive to detect any masses then converts the sound waves received to an image. Our proprietary AI algorithms analyze these images to detect abnormal heat patterns associated with early-stage tumors, achieving high sensitivity without the need for radiation.

2. Machine Learning Pattern Recognition – The system is trained on thousands of annotated breast thermal images, enabling it to continuously improve accuracy over time by learning from diverse datasets and minimizing false positives/negatives.

3. Edge Computing – Image processing occurs directly on the device or via a secure local processor, ensuring results are delivered in under 10 minutes without relying on high speed internet, making it ideal for rural and low resource areas.

4. IoT-Enabled Data Transmission – For connected deployments, encrypted IoT protocols securely transmit patient data and screening results to healthcare providers, enabling remote consultations and centralized monitoring.

5. Cloud-Based Analytics & Reporting – In integrated healthcare systems, anonymized screening data is stored in the cloud for population level insights, enabling early detection trends, epidemiological research, and healthcare planning.

6. User-Centric Mobile & Web Interface – Health workers and clinicians interact with Intellibra through an intuitive app/dashboard for screening management, patient education, and follow up reminders.
Unique Characteristics:
1. Non Invasive & Radiation Free – Unlike mammograms that use X-rays, Intellibra employs AI-powered thermal imaging to detect early signs of breast cancer without compression, pain, or exposure to radiation, making it safe for frequent screenings and younger women.

2. Portable & Low Cost Design – The device is compact and affordable, enabling deployment in rural clinics, mobile screening units, and community health outreaches, where traditional mammography is unavailable or too expensive.

3. Offline Capability – With edge computing, Intellibra delivers instant results without internet dependency, ensuring accessibility in low connectivity regions while maintaining secure offline data storage.

4. Culturally Sensitive Screening – The screening process is non contact and privacy preserving, allowing women to undergo checks without undressing in front of healthcare workers, addressing cultural barriers to early detection.

5. Continuous Learning AI Model – Our machine learning algorithms are continuously updated with diverse datasets, improving diagnostic accuracy across different age groups, skin tones, and breast tissue densities something most conventional tools fail to address.

6. Integrated Awareness & Follow Up System – Beyond detection, Intellibra is designed to integrate with mobile apps and SMS reminders, ensuring patients receive education, counseling, and follow up care, bridging the gap between screening and treatment.

7. Scalable Impact Model – Our business approach leverages partnerships with NGOs, governments, and telemedicine providers to bring large scale screening campaigns to underserved populations at a fraction of current costs.
Sustainable Change:
Sustainable, Systemic Change – Theory of Change

Intellibra is designed not just as a medical device, but as a catalyst for long term healthcare transformation in breast cancer detection and women’s health equity.

Problem: In many low and middle income countries, late stage breast cancer diagnosis is the norm due to high screening costs, lack of equipment, cultural stigma, and limited access to specialists. This leads to avoidable deaths, high treatment costs, and social economic disruption.

Our Intervention:

1. Deploy affordable, portable, AI-powered screening devices to community clinics, rural health centers, and mobile units.

2. Train local health workers to operate Intellibra, interpret results, and guide patients through the referral system.

3. Integrate awareness, follow-up reminders, and counseling into screening programs.

Immediate Effects (1–2 years):

1. Early detection rates significantly increase, particularly among women under 40 and those in underserved regions.

2 Reduced cultural barriers to screening through non invasive, privacy respecting technology.

3. More women receive timely treatment, improving survival rates.

Medium-Term Effects (3–5 years):

1. Lower national treatment costs due to reduced late stage cases.

2. Creation of local jobs in screening operations, maintenance, and awareness campaigns.

3. Establishment of data driven cancer registries to inform national health policies.

Long-Term Systemic Change (5+ years):

1. Shift from reactive, costly cancer treatment to proactive, community based prevention.

2. Integration of AI-powered screening into national health programs as a standard first line diagnostic tool.

3. Sustainable reduction in breast cancer mortality and closing of the health equity gap for women worldwide.
Funding Sources: Not applicable
Primary thematic focus area: Inclusive Digital Innovation Skills & Entrepreneurial Talent Development
Summary: Intellibra provides an innovative, AI-powered, portable, and radiation-free breast cancer screening tool that can be deployed in rural areas without reliable internet. The solution addresses the urgent need for early breast cancer detection in low-resource settings but requires external funding for large-scale implementation and broader reach.

Title: Espace 229 – Inclusive Digital Marketplace for Benin and Beyond
Subtitle: A multi-category digital marketplace enabling inclusive trade in Benin and West Africa through online storefronts, mobile payments, and accessible e-commerce tools.
Problem Statement: Benin, with potential expansion to West Africa (including neighboring ECOWAS countries).
Solution Overview:
Detailed description of how the solution works
Espace 229 is a digital marketplace designed to connect individuals, small businesses, and professional sellers in Benin and, progressively, West Africa. The platform enables users to create an online store, showcase products or services, receive direct customer inquiries via WhatsApp, and process secure mobile payments. Categories cover a wide range of sectors (fashion, vehicles, real estate, services, jobs, etc.), allowing buyers to easily search, compare, and connect with sellers. The marketplace is mobile-first, ensuring accessibility for users with basic smartphones and low bandwidth internet.

Methodologies and technologies used

Platform architecture: Built on a modular CMS framework (Osclass) optimized with marketplace extensions and custom PHP development.

Front-end: Responsive HTML5/CSS3, JavaScript, and Progressive Web App (PWA) integration for app-like user experience without installation barriers.

Back-end: PHP/MySQL with plugin-based modularity for easy scaling.

Payment systems: Mobile money APIs (MTN, Moov, and regional payment aggregators) for seamless transactions, with plans for cross-operator interoperability.

Messaging: Embedded WhatsApp API for direct buyer-seller communications.

Security: SSL encryption, user authentication, and fraud-prevention mechanisms.

Analytics: Google Analytics and custom tracking for marketplace performance and user behavior.

Partnerships and collaboration models
Espace 229 operates through a collaborative ecosystem:

Local SMEs and informal vendors: Onboarded as store owners with training in digital sales and payment processing.

Mobile money operators and fintech companies: For payment integration and interoperability services.

Digital skills training centers: To equip vendors with e-commerce and digital marketing skills.

Logistics partners: For last-mile delivery services to expand market reach.

The model is designed to grow through strategic alliances that support vendor training, enhance buyer trust, and improve transaction efficiency.
Solution Provider(s): AFRIA (Agency of training and research in artificial intelligence)
Implementation location(s): Cotonou, Benin (Headquarters) – Platform accessible nationwide across Benin, with active vendor and buyer communities in major cities such as Porto-Novo, Parakou, Bohicon, and Abomey. Planned expansion to West Africa, starting with Togo, Burkina Faso, and Côte d’Ivoire.
Duration to pilot in a new geography: Approximately 3 to 6 months to pilot in a new geography
SDGs addressed: SDG 8 (Decent Work and Economic Growth);SDG 9 (Industry, Innovation, and Infrastructure);SDG 12 (Responsible Consumption and Production);
Desired impact:
- Solution Objectives

Provide every business and entrepreneur in Benin and West Africa with a free or affordable digital storefront.

Enable direct customer engagement via WhatsApp for faster, trust-based transactions.

Facilitate mobile money payments and digital marketing for SMEs, cooperatives, and informal sector actors.

Promote inclusive economic growth by integrating underserved groups (women, youth, rural sellers) into the digital economy.

- Key Achievements / Expected Impacts (post-implementation)

5,000+ sellers onboarded within the first 12 months, including 40% women-owned businesses.

Increased sales by up to 30% for active sellers through digital exposure and direct communication channels.

Reduced transaction costs by 15–20% via mobile payments instead of cash-based sales.

Job creation in logistics, customer service, and digital marketing for at least 200 youth.

Strengthened cross-border trade within West Africa by offering multilingual and multi-currency support.
Key technologies:
Key Technologies Used

Web & Mobile Platform: Developed on a robust CMS (Osclass framework) customized for e-commerce and marketplace functionalities.

Progressive Web App (PWA): Ensures fast loading, offline capabilities, and installable app experience without requiring app stores.

Mobile Payment Integration: APIs for MTN Mobile Money, Moov Money, and other regional payment gateways.

Real-time Chat Integration: WhatsApp Business API for direct buyer–seller communication.

Geolocation Services: Google Maps API for location-based listing searches.

Analytics & Tracking: Google Analytics and custom dashboards for monitoring engagement, sales, and user behavior.

Multilingual & Multi-currency Support: Enables cross-border trade within West Africa.
Unique Characteristics:
Unique/Differentiated Characteristics

- Localized Marketplace Model – Tailored to the socio-economic context of Benin and West Africa, featuring categories like Missebo and Zongo that mirror local commerce realities.

- Inclusive Design – Serves both individuals and SMEs, integrating offline vendors through assisted listings and mobile-friendly tools.

- Integrated Payment Ecosystem – Unifies multiple mobile money operators in one platform, enabling cross-operator transactions not commonly available in the region.

- Trust & Safety Features – Seller verification badges, secure escrow-like payment flows, and community ratings to build confidence in online transactions.

- Hybrid Engagement Model – Combines digital reach with physical touchpoints (agents/partners in key markets) to onboard and support less digitally literate sellers.

- Scalable PWA Technology – Delivers app-like user experience across devices without the barriers of app store downloads, supporting rapid regional expansion.
Sustainable Change:
Sustainable, Systemic Change Contribution

Espace 229 addresses structural barriers to market access in Benin and West Africa by providing a digital marketplace that bridges informal and formal economies. By enabling small businesses, artisans, and individuals to sell, rent, exchange, or share goods online with secure mobile payments, the platform promotes inclusive economic participation.

Short-term effects: Increased visibility and sales for local vendors, safer transactions, and improved consumer choice.
Medium-term effects: Digital capacity building for SMEs, wider adoption of e-commerce, and stronger cross-border trade within West Africa.
Long-term systemic change: A more connected, transparent, and trusted marketplace ecosystem, reduced dependency on informal market structures, and new opportunities for youth and women entrepreneurs.

Through this approach, Espace 229 aims to stimulate sustainable economic growth, promote digital inclusion, and foster resilient local economies adaptable to future innovations.
Funding Sources: The solution has been fully financed through personal funds, without any external grants or investments.

Including a section for visual elements (e.g., diagrams, screenshots, or infographics) could further help illustrate the solution’s uniqueness and potential. Overall, the form facilitates a comprehensive understanding of innovative solutions while aligning them with UNIDO’s inclusive digital economy objectives.

While the platform is highly inclusive and designed to address local challenges, its scalability depends on securing external funding and expanding regional partnerships.

Title: EY Intelligent Dialogue EYA.ai & ESG.ai

EYA.ai/ESG.ai 2.0 iteration has added professional insights from over ten vertical industries including life sciences, healthcare, retail, and consumer goods, and supports content output formats such as knowledge cards. The upcoming version 3.0 will transition from intelligent Q&A to intelligent advisory, providing features such as ESG narrative lines, ESG issue libraries, ESG vision maps, carbon calculation assistants and voice dialogue.
Problem Statement:
Version 1.0: Breaking Knowledge Barriers
Addressed the challenge of fragmented and inaccessible professional knowledge by building an integrated knowledge matrix across audit, tax, consulting, strategy, and financial services, enabling users to access accurate and real-time insights through a one-stop intelligent Q&A system.
Version 2.0: Enhancing Interaction and Industry Adaptability
Solved issues of low interaction efficiency and weak industry alignment by introducing multimodal interfaces and dynamic industry knowledge graphs, significantly improving user experience and contextual relevance.
Version 3.0: Enabling Intelligent Advisory and Full-Cycle Management
Tackled the lack of decision-making support and closed-loop management capabilities by launching core ESG features such as Narrative Builder, Materiality Library, ESG Vision Map, Carbon Accounting Engine, and Voice Interaction to empower end-to-end enterprise sustainability management.

Through three generations of innovation, EY Intelligent Dialogue bridges AI and expert knowledge to deliver a scalable, trustworthy, and sustainable solution that empowers organizations to accelerate their green transition and long-term value creation.
Solution Overview:
Working Principle:
EY Intelligent Dialogue is an AI-powered intelligent Q&A and advisory system designed for professional service scenarios, with "Trusted AI" as its core philosophy. Developed on EY’s proprietary METIS intelligent platform, the solution follows a process of semantic understanding, knowledge retrieval, inference generation, and trusted output to rapidly deliver structured, actionable answers and recommendations.
Technical Approach:
Leveraging the self-developed METIS platform, the system integrates billion-parameter lightweight models and Huawei Cloud’s DeepSeek V3 to build a dynamic multi-model scheduling system that matches the optimal model according to task requirements.The platform includes METIS.Workflow (supporting intent recognition, semantic parsing, information extraction, and content processing for conversational AI workflows), METIS.Docs (OCR-based intelligent document processing), METIS.Guard (multi-layer model security review and sensitive content filtering), and METIS.Model (multi-model integration and management). Employing a Retrieval-Augmented Generation (RAG) architecture, it achieves unified retrieval and high-quality generation from both structured and unstructured knowledge, supports large-scale knowledge base integration and heterogeneous data fusion, and features hierarchical indexing and semantic matching capabilities, significantly improving answer accuracy and intelligent response efficiency.
Ecosystem Collaboration:
The development and deployment of EY Intelligent Dialogue adhere to an "open collaboration and professional leadership" approach.

We structure, tag, and semantically interpret fragmented professional knowledge dispersed across expert insights, reports, and regulatory frameworks. Through continuous AI deployment and learning, enterprises can gradually evolve into a “human-machine symbiotic” model, enhancing response efficiency and reducing operational risks associated with reliance on individual experts.

As system usage data accumulates, AI continuously improves its understanding of industry knowledge. This feeds back into content updates and product iteration, forming a self-reinforcing cycle of technology, content, and service—driving sustainable and systemic transformation over time.

Title: GENESIS – Rechargeable Solar Induction Stove, Safe and Off-Grid
Subtitle: A rechargeable solar induction stove replacing gas, electricity, and charcoal, providing safe, affordable, and eco-friendly cooking.
Problem Statement: In many regions, households still heavily rely on charcoal, which causes massive deforestation, worsens climate change, and leads to health problems from smoke. Gas stoves pose a high risk of household fires, while electric stoves consume excessive energy, making them costly and impractical in areas prone to power outages. GENESIS addresses these challenges by providing a rechargeable solar cooking solution that is safe, affordable, and environmentally friendly.
Solution Overview:
GENESIS is a rechargeable solar induction stove designed to replace charcoal, gas, and electric stoves. It operates through an integrated or external solar panel that charges its high-capacity LiFePO4 battery, enabling users to cook even without electricity access. The induction system rapidly heats cookware without flames, eliminating household fire risks and reducing energy consumption.

Methodologies and technologies used:

Electromagnetic induction for fast and safe cooking.

Lithium iron phosphate (LiFePO4) battery for durable energy storage and long lifespan.

Smart energy management system to optimize consumption and extend autonomy.

Heat- and impact-resistant materials for durability and safety.

Partnerships and collaboration models:
GENESIS collaborates with Orange Digital Center DRC, local NGOs, solar energy distributors, and women entrepreneur associations to ensure distribution and awareness. We adopt a B2C model for households and a B2B approach with retailers and community organizations. Partnerships with local training centers also provide user training for proper use and maintenance of the stove.
Solution Provider(s): Orange Digital Center DRC: innovation and technology training center, education and digital innovation sector, partner for training and technical support.
Geographic focus: Democratic Republic of Congo, primarily in Kinshasa
Implementation location(s): Kinshasa, Democratic Republic of Congo – pilot implementation in a few households in the Limete municipality.
Implementation timeline(s): Kinshasa, Democratic Republic of Congo – pilot implementation in a few households in the Limete municipality.
Duration to pilot in a new geography: La durée estimée pour piloter GENESIS dans une nouvelle zone géographique est de 3 à 6 mois, incluant la distribution des réchauds, la formation des utilisateurs et le suivi de performance.
SDGs addressed: SDG 7 (Affordable and Clean Energy);SDG 13 (Climate Action);SDG 3 (Good Health and Well-being);
Desired impact:
Solution Objectives:

Provide a sustainable, safe, and affordable cooking solution for households.

Reduce reliance on charcoal and gas, thereby limiting deforestation and household fire risks.

Promote the use of renewable energy and contribute to climate change mitigation.

Key Achievements / Impacts:

Significant reduction of CO2 emissions from cooking (estimated 1–2 tons CO2 per household per year if replacing charcoal).

Energy savings for households using GENESIS instead of electric stoves.

Improved health for users due to reduced smoke exposure.

Indirect job creation through production, distribution, and user training.
Key technologies:
GENESIS leverages several technologies to provide safe, efficient, and connected solar cooking:

Electromagnetic induction: rapidly heats cookware without flames, reducing fire risks.

Lithium iron phosphate (LiFePO4) battery: durable, safe, and high-performance energy storage.

Smart energy management: optimizes energy consumption and extends battery autonomy.

Artificial Intelligence (AI): enables automated cooking for foods even when the user doesn’t know the exact recipe, by automatically adjusting temperature and cooking time.

IoT connectivity (optional): enables remote monitoring and control via a mobile app, including cooking scheduling and battery status tracking.

Heat- and impact-resistant materials: ensure product safety and durability.
Unique Characteristics:
Energy versatility: operates off-grid using solar energy, replacing charcoal, gas, and electric stoves.

Household safety: induction eliminates fire risks from gas and smoke from charcoal, protecting homes and users’ health.

Advanced technologies: integrates electromagnetic induction, durable LiFePO4 battery, smart energy management, AI for automated cooking, and IoT connectivity for remote control.

Inclusive partnership model: collaboration with Orange Digital Center DRC, local NGOs, solar energy distributors, and women entrepreneur associations to maximize social impact and distribution.

Environmental impact: reduces deforestation and CO2 emissions, contributing to climate change mitigation.

Financial accessibility: flexible financing models such as pay-as-you-go make the stove affordable for low-income households.
Sustainable Change:
GENESIS creates sustainable and systemic change by transforming household cooking practices, reducing reliance on polluting fuels, and promoting renewable energy adoption. Expected follow-on effects include:

Reduced deforestation and CO2 emissions, contributing to climate change mitigation.

Improved health and household safety, through elimination of smoke and fire risks.

Economic and social empowerment: women and low-income households gain access to an affordable and sustainable solution, while new jobs are created in production, distribution, and training.

Promotion of local and digital innovation: partnerships with Orange Digital Center DRC and associated training foster technical and entrepreneurial skill development.

Theory of Change:
If GENESIS is deployed at scale, households will adopt cleaner and safer cooking methods, which reduces environmental and health impacts, strengthens the local economy, and promotes systemic, sustainable use of renewable energy.
Funding Sources:
The GENESIS project has been funded primarily through:

Awards and grants: funds obtained from technology innovation competitions and entrepreneurship support initiatives.

Personal investment: founder’s contribution to prototype and initially develop the solution.

Partnerships: collaboration with Orange Digital Center DRC, providing technical support and resources for development and pilot testing.

“The GENESIS solar stove is a valuable innovation that improves family lives and preserves our environment.” – Jean-Pierre Kalala, trainer at Orange Digital Center DRC.

Sources: Testimonials collected during the pilot phase in Kinshasa, DRC.

It might be helpful to add a section on future funding or partnership needs to better plan for scaling and expansion.

Summary: GENESIS is a rechargeable solar induction stove designed to replace charcoal, gas, and electric stoves with an eco-friendly, safe, and affordable cooking solution. By utilizing solar power and advanced energy management, it provides a cleaner cooking experience while reducing deforestation and household fire risks.

Name of your organization: Alere Development Initiative for Peace and Empowerment -ADIPE
Title: Empowering Rural Communities in Teso through Inclusive Digital Literacy Hubs
Subtitle: Equipping Women,Youth,and Marginalized Groups with Digital Skills for Social and Economic Inclusion
Problem Statement:
Rural communities in Teso, Uganda, face significant barriers to digital inclusion, limiting their access to education, economic opportunities, and essential services. Women and youth are disproportionately affected due to factors such as limited access to technology, low digital literacy, and socio-cultural constraints.
According to a 2015 Uganda Communications Commission survey, only 44% of women owned and could use a phone at any time, compared to 62% of men. Additionally, only 15% of women had used a computer or the internet in the three months preceding the survey, compared to 21% of men. These disparities are more pronounced in rural areas, where access to digital tools and skills is limited .africaninternetrights.org
The lack of digital literacy among women and youth in rural Uganda impedes their ability to engage in digital economies, access online education, and participate in civic activities. This digital divide exacerbates existing inequalities and hinders socio-economic development in these communities.
Furthermore, a study by EIFL, Peer 2 Peer University, and Maendeleo Foundation highlighted that women and youth in Uganda face challenges in accessing and utilizing digital technologies due to factors such as lack of infrastructure, affordability, and relevant training
Addressing these challenges through targeted digital literacy programs is crucial for empowering rural communities, particularly women and youth, enabling them to participate fully in the digital economy and improve their livelihoods, and ensuring peaceful coexistence.
Solution Overview:
The project will use a blended learning methodology, combining in-person workshops with online tutorials to ensure flexible and accessible training for all participants. Learning will be practical and project-based, allowing women, youth, and marginalized groups to apply new digital skills to real-life initiatives such as online businesses, social campaigns, or community awareness projects. Training content will be adapted to local literacy levels, languages, and cultural contexts to ensure inclusivity and relevance.

To maximize impact, ADIPE will collaborate with local governments and community leaders to facilitate hub establishment, mobilize participants, and provide ongoing community support. Partnerships with educational institutions and universities will supply qualified trainers, mentorship, and curriculum guidance. Civil society organizations and NGOs will assist in outreach to marginalized groups and support social awareness programs on environmental conservation, gender equality, and human rights. Private sector partners will provide technical expertise, digital tools, and potential market linkages for entrepreneurial participants.

We will also operate under a community driven governance model to ensure ownership and sustainability. This partnership approach will also combine technical expertise, social support, and engagement, to ensure a collaborative environment that strengthens participants’ skills.
Solution Provider(s): Alere Development Initiative for Peace and Empowerment (ADIPE): Lead implementing organization; a non-profit community-based organization in Uganda focused on empowering rural communities, promoting social inclusion, gender equality, and economic empowerment through education, WASH initiatives, basic education,and digital skills training. Sector: Community Development, Social Inclusion, Digital Empowerment.  Tumaini Ministries Uganda: A faith-based organization engaged in community outreach, social support programs, and awareness campaigns targeting marginalized populations, including youth and women. Sector: Community Development, Social Services, Outreach. Title: SMOKELESS BRIQS ENERGY SOLUTIONS
Subtitle: SMOKELESS BRIQS used clean energy technologies to address energy poverty, In-door Air Pollution, Environmental degradation and Climate Change in underserved communities in Nigeria.
Problem Statement:
According to the National Bureau of Statistics, more than 80% of the households in rural Nigeria use Kerosene and firewood fuel for cooking. This means that much demand is placed on the little forest reserve that Nigeria has which is fast disappearing, (less than 7.7% forest cover). Way below the 10% global recommended levels.

On the other hand, Statistics from the World Health Organization (WHO) revealed that over 98,000 Nigerian women die annually from smokes inhaled while cooking with firewood. Which is now the 3rd highest killer after Malaria and HIV? And Kerosene usage is the leading cause of Lung Cancer and Leukemia globally only 47% of tertiary students in Nigeria have consistent access to reliable electricity to charge their mobile phones and also study at Night.

Our Mothers must NOT Continue to sacrifice their lives just because they want to cook the food we are going to eat. NO WAY!


PROBLEM WE ARE TRYING TO SOLVE
1. IN-DOOR AIR POLLUTION
Toxic smoke from traditional cooking fuels causes respiratory diseases and contributes to over 4 million deaths annually worldwide.

2. ENERGY POVERTY
Over 92 million Nigerians, nearly 45% of the population live without access to electricity, according to the International Energy Agency (IEA), hindering education, livelihoods, and quality of life.

3. CLIMATE CHANGE
Burning fossil fuels and deforestation for energy release greenhouse gases, accelerating global warming and its devastating effects.

4. ENVIRONMENTAL DEGRADATION
Unsustainable energy practices lead to deforestation, soil erosion, and loss of biodiversity, harming ecosystems and livelihoods.
Solution Overview:
Cold-Alive is a green cold chain enterprise that tackles post-harvest losses by providing farmers and fishers with access to solar-powered modular cold storage hubs and an AI-driven mobile platform. Farmers store their produce in Cold-Alive Hubs using a pay-as-you-store model, making storage affordable and accessible even to smallholder farmers. Through the mobile platform (accessible via smartphone app and USSD for non-smartphone users), farmers can:
1.	Track the status and duration of their stored produce,
2.	Receive real-time demand predictions and pricing insights,
3.	Connect directly with food aggregators, markets, and logistics providers,
4.	Make digital payments, ensuring financial transparency and inclusion.

This integrated system reduces food waste, extends shelf life, improves farmer income, and ensures that previously excluded rural producers can participate in the digital economy.


Methodologies and technologies used
1.	Artificial Intelligence (AI): Demand forecasting, logistics optimization, and data-driven market linkages.
2.	Internet of Things (IoT): Sensors monitor storage conditions (temperature, humidity, energy usage) in real time.
3.	Mobile Technology: Dual interface (mobile app and USSD) to ensure accessibility for both smartphone and feature phone users.
4.	Renewable Energy: Solar-powered hubs ensure sustainability and operation in off-grid communities.
5.	Digital Finance Integration: Mobile money and wallet systems for pay-as-you-store payments and financial inclusion.


Partnerships and collaboration models
Cold-Alive operates through a multi-stakeholder collaboration model, including:
1.	Farmer Cooperatives and Associations: For farmer adoption, community trust, and group access.
2.	Local NGOs and Women’s Groups: To promote gender-inclusive access and capacity building.
3.	Technology Partners: For AI modeling, IoT integration, and platform scaling.
4.	Financial Service Providers: For mobile money integration and digital savings/credit services.
5.	Food Aggregators and Logistics Companies: To create direct market linkages and reduce exploitation by middlemen.
6.	Government Agencies and Development Partners: For policy alignment, scale, and sustainability.

Together, these partnerships enable Cold-Alive to create a digitally inclusive cold chain ecosystem that addresses food insecurity, enhances rural livelihoods, and drives systemic change in agricultural value chains.
Solution Provider(s): 1.	Cold-Alive Hub: A green cold chain enterprise based in Nigeria, pioneering solar-powered modular cold storage hubs and AI-powered mobile platforms for smallholder farmers and fishers. Sector: Climate-Tech, AgriTech, Renewable Energy. 2.	All Farmers Association of Nigeria (AFAN) – A nationwide farmers’ cooperative that mobilizes smallholder farmers, enhances adoption of innovative agricultural technologies, and provides access to farmer networks. Sector: Agriculture, Cooperative Development. 3.	Women in Agriculture Advancement Cooperative (WAAC): A grassroots women-led NGO supporting female farmers and fish processors with training, advocacy, and access to sustainable agribusiness solutions. Sector: Women Empowerment, Rural Development, Agriculture. 4.	Inspire Africa for Global Impacts Initiative: A youth-led NGO supporting innovative African startups tackling climate change and food insecurity through mentorship, advocacy, and impact investment. Sector: Social Enterprise, Climate Action, Food Security. 5.	Nigerian Stored Products Research Institute (NSPRI) – A government-backed research institute providing technical expertise on post-harvest management, food preservation, and cold chain optimization. Sector: Research & Development, Agriculture, Food Security.
Implementation location(s): Cold-Alive has already been implemented in Nigeria, specifically in the following pilot locations: 1.	Lagos State (Epe & Badagry): Cold-Alive Hubs deployed for smallholder fishers and traders along coastal communities. 2.	Ondo State (Ilaje Local Government Area): Solar-powered cold storage supporting artisanal fishers and women fish processors.

Pilot Phase (January 2023 – June 2023): Initial Cold-Alive Hub launched in Lagos State (Epe & Badagry) serving artisanal fishers and traders. 2.	Expansion Phase I (July 2023 – December 2023): Deployment extended to Ondo State (Ilaje Local Government Area) supporting fish processors and coastal farmers. 3. Duration to pilot in a new geography: The pilot implementation of Cold-Alive in a new geography typically takes 6–9 months. 1.	Months 1–2: Community engagement, needs assessment, site selection, and securing local regulatory approvals. 2.	Months 3–4: Deployment of modular solar-powered Cold-Alive Hubs, installation of IoT/AI systems, and training of local operators. 3.	Months 5–6: Onboarding of farmers, fishers, and aggregators into the Cold-Alive platform, including digital literacy sessions. 4.	Months 7–9: Monitoring, optimization, and scaling to nearby markets for full integration into the local food supply chain. This timeframe ensures that our solution is not only installed but also fully adopted, operational, and delivering measurable impact.
SDGs addressed: SDG 2 (Zero Hunger);SDG 8 (Decent Work and Economic Growth);SDG 13 (Climate Action);
Desired impact:
Solution Objectives
1. Reduce post-harvest losses among smallholder farmers and fishers by providing affordable, accessible, and sustainable cold storage.
2. Strengthen local food supply chains and increase household incomes through extended produce shelf-life and reduced spoilage.
3. Advance inclusive digital participation by connecting farmers and fishers to markets via Cold-Alive’s AI-driven platform.
4. Drive climate action through solar-powered cold hubs and data-driven food distribution, reducing waste and GHG emissions.
5. Create local employment opportunities, especially for women and youth, in hub management, logistics, and digital services.

Key Achievements & Impacts (to date / projected)
1. 40% reduction in post-harvest losses for farmers and fishers using Cold-Alive Hubs.
2. 25–30% income increase for smallholder households through improved preservation and better market access.
3. Employment generation: Each hub creates 10–15 direct jobs (operators, technicians, digital agents) and 30+ indirect jobs in supply chains.
4. Climate impact: Prevents an estimated 150–200 metric tons of CO₂ equivalent per hub annually by reducing food spoilage and replacing diesel-powered cold storage with solar energy.
5. Digital inclusion: Over 1,000 smallholder farmers and fishers onboarded onto the AI-enabled platform for demand forecasting, logistics coordination, and access to buyers.
Key technologies:
Key Technologies Used
1.	Artificial Intelligence (AI): Powers demand forecasting, logistics optimization, and dynamic pricing to reduce waste and ensure efficient cold storage utilization.
2.	Internet of Things (IoT): Cold-Alive Hubs are equipped with IoT sensors to monitor temperature, humidity, and energy consumption in real-time, ensuring optimal storage conditions.
3.	Solar Photovoltaic (PV) Systems: Off-grid, renewable solar power drives the cold storage units, eliminating reliance on diesel generators and lowering GHG emissions.
4.	Mobile Application & USSD Platform: Provides farmers and fishers with easy access (smartphone and feature phone) to book storage space, track inventory, and connect with buyers.
5.	Cloud Computing & Data Analytics: Centralized platform aggregates and analyzes data from multiple hubs to generate insights on produce flows, storage demand, and market linkages.
Unique Characteristics:
Unique / Differentiated Characteristics of Cold-Alive
1.	Inclusive Digital Access: Unlike conventional cold storage systems, Cold-Alive integrates both mobile apps and USSD platforms, enabling even farmers and fishers without smartphones or internet access to book, pay, and track their produce.

2.	Green Cold Chain Innovation: Powered by solar energy and optimized with AI, Cold-Alive eliminates reliance on diesel-powered cold rooms, cutting carbon emissions while ensuring affordability and sustainability.

3.	AI-Powered Market Linkages: The platform goes beyond storage — it uses predictive analytics to connect farmers with aggregators and buyers, reducing food loss and unlocking better incomes.

4.	Pay-as-You-Store Model: Cold-Alive adopts an affordable, usage-based pricing model, removing the barrier of upfront infrastructure costs for smallholder farmers and fishers.

5.	Women & Youth Empowerment: The solution deliberately trains and employs local women and youth as hub operators, digital agents, and technicians, strengthening local ownership and job creation.

6.	Modular, Scalable Hubs: Cold-Alive Hubs are portable and modular, making it easy to deploy in remote rural communities or scale across regions without heavy infrastructure investment.

7.	Partnership-Driven Model: Designed to integrate with NGOs, cooperatives, and agribusinesses, Cold-Alive leverages multi-stakeholder collaboration for wider impact and faster adoption.
Sustainable Change:
Cold-Alive contributes to sustainable, systemic change by transforming how food is stored, preserved, and distributed in vulnerable communities. Through its solar-powered cold storage hubs and AI-driven mobile platform, farmers and fishers gain reliable, affordable access to storage facilities that prevent post-harvest losses and connect them directly to buyers. This immediately reduces waste, increases household income, and lowers emissions compared to diesel-powered cold storage.

As more communities adopt the system, food security improves, women and youth gain new employment opportunities as hub operators and digital agents, and rural economies become more resilient to climate shocks. Over time, the model promotes a nationwide shift toward decentralized, green cold chain infrastructure, inspiring policy support and private sector investment.

The long-term impact is a more inclusive, low-carbon food system that strengthens livelihoods, reduces poverty, and establishes a replicable framework for sustainable cold storage across Africa.
Funding Sources: Cold-Alive has been primarily funded through a mix of self-investment, small-scale seed funding, and strategic partnerships. Initial research, prototype development, and pilot deployments were supported by personal founder contributions and in-kind support from local collaborators. Additional resources have come from innovation challenges, entrepreneurship bootcamps, and small grants that focus on climate-smart agriculture and clean energy solutions. Partnerships with agribusiness stakeholders and NGOs working with smallholder farmers have also provided co-funding and logistical support to enable pilot testing in rural communities.

Title: AI Advantage for All: Bridging the Growing Digital Chasm
Subtitle: A global 90 day mentoring challenge that equips anyone, anywhere with AI and digital skills – boosting income potential and fostering an inclusive digital economy.
Problem Statement: Much of the commentary about advancements in technology and AI triggers fear and uncertainty instead of curiosity among many people. People worry what AI means for their future job opportunities and often feel paralyzed, unsure how or where to start adapting. This challenge is even greater for underrepresented groups who face extra barriers entering tech careers – for example, in New Zealand Māori comprise nearly 18% of the workforce but only ~4% of the tech industry, illustrating a profound inequality in access to digital opportunities. Fueled by myths about AI like "my skills are irrelevant" and "there's no point in learning anymore,” too many individuals are at risk of being left behind. The core problem is a skills and mindset gap: people lack accessible pathways to build AI-related skills and confidence, in a way that values their unique strengths and experiences. Traditional tech training programs haven’t solved this, often focusing narrowly on coding or technical content while ignoring the human element. Without a solution, this fear-driven stagnation and talent exclusion will continue to widen the digital divide into a chasm, limiting inclusive growth in the AI-enabled world.
Solution Overview:
Our 90 Day Mentoring Challenge - The AI Advantage program is a cohort-based, 12-week mentoring program that empowers participants to develop AI skills through practice, from cognitive abilities like critical thinking to social-emotional skills and technical fluency. As AI automates routine tasks, human strengths in reasoning, creativity, empathy, and leadership become even more important than they have always been. The AI Advantage combines structured learning modules with hands-on practice and community support to transform people’s mindsets from fearing AI to embracing it as a tool for opportunity. 

-How the solution works: Participants from anywhere in the world join an online cohort for 90 days. Over the course of 12 weekly modules, they progress through a curated curriculum that balances technical know-how with human-centric skills. Each week introduces one new skill or concept -  our Intelligence Age Skills Framework takes people through Foundational skills, Applied skills and Mastery skills. For example, critical thinking, ethical AI use, communication, or personal automation – along with practical exercises on applying that skill with AI tools. Content is delivered in a mix of short video lessons, “try-it-now” challenges and recommended reading to go deeper. This approach supports just-in-time learning – participants immediately apply what they learn in real-life contexts, reinforcing understanding through action. Throughout the program, experienced mentors (industry experts and program alumni) provide guidance and feedback, helping participants align the new skills with their unique strengths and goals. Peer interaction is encouraged via group discussions, team projects, and a dedicated online community space, so participants learn with and from each other. The program is self-paced within each week (to accommodate busy schedules), but also structured with regular check-ins and deadlines to maintain momentum. By the end of 90 days, participants will have a personal AI playbook, a certificate of completion, and membership in a global alumni network. This supportive network continues beyond the program, offering ongoing learning opportunities, confidence-building, and career connections.

-Methodologies and technologies used: At the heart of the program is The Intelligence Age Skills Framework, our proprietary solution which identifies the 12 essential skill areas needed to thrive alongside AI. This framework provides a modular, scaffolded learning approach. Each module builds on the last, moving from foundational skills to advanced application and mastery skills. The course design follows modern adult-learning best practices: it’s experiential (learning by doing), just-in-time (delivering lessons right when relevant to tasks at hand), and personalized (encouraging participants to apply AI in their own field or interest area). We leverage technology heavily within the program itself: for example, participants use AI tools (like chatbots and no-code AI platforms) as part of exercises, so they gain hands-on familiarity with current technologies while learning. Our learning platform (a cloud-based education portal) delivers content in bite-sized formats and uses automation to send reminders, additional resources, and tips based on each participant’s progress. Participants have regularly highlighted the impact of our community learning model – we use community discussions and live virtual meet-ups to create a sense of camaraderie and knowledge sharing. It creates opportunities for people to collaborate on solving challenges or share how they applied a lesson to their job that week, which reinforces learning through peer examples and builds motivation.

-Partnerships and collaboration models: We are working closely with New Zealand Trade and Enterprise (NZTE), which is helping us scale the program to new regions. We are building alliances with universities, professional training institutes, and online education providers.
Solution Provider(s): New Zealand Trade and Enterprise - https://www.nzte.govt.nz/
Implementation location(s): We already serve people from more than 70 countries through our digital learning platforms, including: Algeria, Armenia, Australia, Belgium, Bosnia and Herzegovina, Brazil, Canada, Chile, Costa Rica, Denmark, Dominican Republic, Egypt, Finland, France, Georgia, Germany, Ghana, Greece, Hungary, Iceland, India, Iran (Islamic Republic of), Ireland, Italy, Jordan, Kenya, Malaysia, Malta, Mexico, Mozambique, Nepal, Netherlands, New Zealand, Nigeria, Norway, Pakistan, Peru, Philippines, Poland, Portugal, Qatar, Saudi Arabia, Singapore, Slovakia (Slovak Republic), South Africa, Spain, Sri Lanka, Sweden, Switzerland, Tanzania, United Republic of Tunisia, Turkey, Ukraine, United Arab Emirates, United Kingdom, United States, Uruguay
Implementation timeline(s): Our 90 Day Mentoring Challenge platform was founded in 2018 and since then more than 1,400 people have taken advantage of our career acceleration program.
Duration to pilot in a new geography: The program is 90 days, so if there was demand or an audience of people who wanted to take part our scalable online platform means we can move quickly to onboard people in new geographies.
SDGs addressed: SDG 4 (Quality Education);SDG 8 (Decent Work and Economic Growth);SDG 10 (Reduced Inequalities);
Desired impact:
We want to help people embrace AI confidently, build future-ready skills, and boost participants’ employment and income prospects while promoting inclusive participation in the digital economy. In practice, that means helping people overcome fear of automation by sparking curiosity, providing accessible training in AI and digital skills, and equipping them (especially those from underrepresented groups) with the tools to secure better jobs or entrepreneurial opportunities.
With our 90 Day Mentoring Challenge we've already impacted the careers and lives of more than 1,400 people from 70+ countries, delivering a strong track record of improving participants’ career trajectories. Dozens of alumni report promotions, new job offers, or income increases after completing our challenge. For example, Nathan Rose, a graduate, shared that “within 12 months of completing [the Challenge] I saw my income grow, and got a promotion”. Many participants have leveraged their new skills to transition into higher-paying roles or even enter the tech industry for the first time. In terms of entrepreneurship and job creation, several alumni have started consulting businesses or side-hustles using skills gained, thereby generating new economic activity in their communities (though this is qualitative, we see it as an emerging trend). At least 40 alumni have earned the Microsoft Most Valuable Professional (MVP) award – a recognition for top global tech community leaders. This is a strong indicator of the program’s quality and impact: graduates are not only improving their own careers but also contributing expertise back to the wider community. Their achievements signal that our training produces industry leaders who drive innovation and mentor others.

While harder to quantify, a significant impact is the diversification of the tech talent pipeline. Our outreach and scholarship efforts have brought in participants from underrepresented groups (e.g. women, indigenous professionals, career-switchers from non-tech fields). As a result, the cohorts and alumni network are far more diverse than typical tech programs. By equipping these individuals with competitive skills and confidence, we’re helping to reduce inequalities in digital participation and enabling employers to benefit from a broader range of talent.

An intangible but important impact is the thriving global community of practice that has formed. Alumni continue to engage in our forums and events, practicing lifelong learning and often mentoring new participants. This community-driven approach amplifies the program’s impact beyond the formal 90 days – creating a ripple effect as knowledge and opportunities are shared peer-to-peer across borders. 

As we broaden our target audience with the AI Advantage, from tech professionals to professionals who want to learn how to use AI in their work, the desired impact of our solution is to create a virtuous cycle of skill development and economic empowerment. We measure success by the number of lives transformed: 1,400+ and counting, with tangible outcomes like better jobs, higher earnings, industry recognition, and greater diversity in the tech workforce. With the AI Advantage our goal is to reach 10,000 people in order to contribute to broader inclusive economic growth, aligning with global development goals. Our organization, Cloverbase, exists to share the luck we've personally experienced through access to careers enabled by technology.
Key technologies:
-Generative AI chatbots - The AI Advantage is technology agnostic but encourages experimentation with chatbots like those from Google (Gemini), OpenAI (ChatGPT), Anthropic (Claude), and Microsoft (Copilot).
-Zenler - cloud-based learning management platform and community platform
-WhatsApp communities - encrypted online community 
-Microsoft Teams - live virtual meet-ups
Unique Characteristics:
We're grounded by the Māori whakataukī/proverb - He aha te mea nui o te ao? He tangata, he tangata, he tangata. What is the most important thing in the world? It is people, it is people, it is people. We prioritize human potential over technology. Unlike typical tech courses, our 90 Day Mentoring Challenge fosters a psychologically safe learning community where participants from all backgrounds feel supported. Peer mentorship, respectful discourse, and an emphasis on individual strengths create an environment where learners confidently move from fear of AI to curiosity.

Our community is extraordinarily diverse – spanning 70+ countries and many underrepresented groups. The program was designed to be inclusive, attracting people who might have struggled in typical learning environments, entrepreneurs, career-switchers, and others beyond the usual tech circles. Participants gain global perspectives and see role models who look like them succeeding in tech. This global inclusion is a unique hallmark compared to other programs that might be confined to one region or demographic. Our alumni network has helped people find jobs in new countries.

We’ve been running and refining the 90 Day Mentoring Challenge since 2018, incorporating feedback and iteration to make it exceptionally effective. Few solutions in this space can claim such longevity with consistent success. We have a wealth of data and testimonials proving that our methods work (see https://love.90daymc.com/all). We’re reliable and scalable due to this accumulated experience.

Our solution is innovative in combining technology training with personal development. We go beyond teaching AI tools – we equally focus on mindset, communication, leadership, and leveraging one’s unique experiences. This hybrid curriculum (guided by the Intelligence Age Skills Framework) is unlike traditional programs that might just teach coding or AI theory in isolation. For example, a participant not only learns how to use AI, but also how to integrate it into a project that aligns with their passion, and how to communicate those results to others. By uniting hard skills with soft skills in an AI context, we produce graduates who are technically competent and adaptable, creative thinkers – a combination that’s rare and highly valuable in the market.

The program is led and designed by recognized AI thought leaders and educators. Our team’s credibility (we are authors of the upcoming Microsoft Press book on AI adoption, and trusted advisors in the Microsoft ecosystem) sets us apart. This reassures participants and partners that our training isn’t theoretical – it’s current and informed by our experience in driving AI adoption. 

We aren’t just delivering a program; we’re building an ecosystem of collaboration. Our partnership with New Zealand Trade and Enterprise to expand into emerging tech markets (like India) is an unconventional and innovative growth strategy – effectively blending workforce development with national economic development goals. We're also pursuing opportunities to co-create and integrate content with educational institutions and industry groups, rather than competing with them. This flexible, partnership-driven model allows us to scale rapidly while tailoring to local needs, which is a unique business approach in the training sector. 

A standout differentiator is the self-sustaining nature of our alumni network. Graduates don’t just disappear – many become mentors, ambassadors, or even instructors in subsequent cohorts. This creates a “pay-it-forward” cycle that organically grows capacity: the community itself helps drive the program’s success, reducing costs and increasing impact.
Sustainable Change: By equipping people with practical AI skills and shifting their mindset from fear to curiosity, our solution triggers a self-sustaining cycle of positive change. Graduates secure better jobs, earn higher incomes, or start new ventures thanks to their enhanced skills. They continue applying and refining these skills throughout their careers. Our focus on skills transfer, not just one-time knowledge transfer, means they remain adaptable as technology evolves. With their new confidence, alumni often become digital champions in their workplaces or communities which multiplies the impact beyond the original cohort. Over time, this growing network of skilled, confident individuals helps close the digital divide and fosters inclusive economic growth: each person we upskill becomes a catalyst who brings others along.
Funding Sources: To date we have received no funding to create our program, though NZTE have provided some co-funding to help us scale access to it (up to $20k co-investment at 40% of costs). Title: Building Digital Inclusion for Underserved Communities in Bangladesh
Subtitle: Empowering underserved communities in Bangladesh through accessible, skill-based digital learning tailored for economic inclusion and sustainable livelihoods.
Problem Statement: In Bangladesh, a significant portion of youth, women, and frontline workers—especially from underserved communities—lack access to quality education, digital skills, and employment opportunities. Traditional education systems are often disconnected from market needs, and digital exclusion continues to widen the socioeconomic gap. These challenges limit participation in the digital economy, deepen gender and regional disparities, and restrict long-term livelihood development.
Solution Overview:
How the Solution Works:
Shomvob’s solution integrates digital upskilling, job matching, and localized content delivery to empower marginalized groups—particularly women, youth, and frontline health workers. At the heart of this model is the Shomvob Academy, our digital learning hub, which provides tailored training programs to equip individuals with technical, vocational, and soft skills aligned with market demand.

The solution works by:

Delivering training through Shomvob Academy, with modules covering digital literacy, employability skills, and sector-specific training.

Connecting trained candidates with employers through job-matching features, ensuring inclusive hiring pathways.

Offering localized learning content in Bangla, designed to be culturally relevant and easily accessible across both urban and rural communities.

Supporting frontline health workers with digital resources and capacity-building modules, strengthening healthcare delivery in underserved regions.

This holistic approach ensures not only skill development but also practical economic opportunities, creating pathways toward dignified and sustainable livelihoods.

Methodologies and Technologies Used:

Human-Centered Design: Active engagement of learners and employers to co-create relevant curricula.

Blended Learning Approach: Training delivered via Shomvob Academy (online) and complemented by in-person facilitation when needed.

Mobile-First Platforms: Accessible through smartphones, ensuring reach in low-connectivity environments.

AI-Enabled Job Matching: Intelligent job-matching tools connecting learners with suitable employment opportunities.

Localized Content Development: Courses developed in Bangla with contextualized examples for women, rural youth, and MSMEs.

Partnerships and Collaboration Models:

NGOs and Community Organizations: Partnering to mobilize women, youth, and marginalized groups into Shomvob Academy programs.

Employers and MSMEs: Collaborating with companies to co-design training curricula and facilitate inclusive recruitment.

Government Agencies: Aligning with national skills development and digital transformation priorities.

International Development Partners: Leveraging technical and financial support to scale digital solutions and amplify impact.

Academic Institutions: Engaging universities and training centers to validate and expand learning modules.

Title: AgriNet
Subtitle: AgriNet is an intelligent automatic irrigation system that allows farmers to water their fields remotely via an internet connection, improving agricultural efficiency and productivity.
Problem Statement: Smallholder farmers face several major challenges: manual watering remains difficult, especially for women; a lack of labor makes it difficult to irrigate large areas; and the distance between homes and fields complicates regular monitoring. In addition, traditional irrigation systems are ineffective at meeting current standards.
Solution Overview:
Detailed description of how it works
AgriNet is a smart irrigation system that allows for remote and automatic watering control, with or without a network. It uses sensors to measure soil moisture and weather conditions, then triggers optimal irrigation to reduce water waste and improve agricultural yields.

Methodologies and technologies used
The solution combines IoT (Raspberry Pi, Arduino board, soil and ambient humidity and temperature sensors), artificial intelligence, and solar energy to ensure autonomous irrigation. Sensor data is analyzed in real time, integrated into a monitoring platform, and translated into automatic actions. The approach follows a continuous optimization cycle based on field feedback.

Partnerships and collaboration models
SIMIT collaborates with incubators, NGOs, electronic equipment suppliers, and local agricultural stakeholders. The model is based on co-creation with producers, partnerships for financing and distribution, as well as a network of agents for installation, maintenance and training, promoting sustainable deployment.
Solution Provider(s): Our project partners bring together strategic and complementary stakeholders. DigiMark supports communications and marketing. I'm Technology provides the appropriate electronic and IT equipment. Sen Compagnie Énergie provides solar power solutions for sustainable autonomy. Casa Tree Lions, Khadylegumes, Fraisen, and AJAX cooperative contribute their agribusiness expertise. In addition, strong financial partners such as ADPME, DER/FJ, and PDCEJ are public organizations that support projects through institutional and financial support mechanisms.
Duration to pilot in a new geography: 18 mouths
SDGs addressed: SDG 1 (No Poverty);SDG 2 (Zero Hunger);SDG 13 (Climate Action);
Desired impact: The solution aims to increase sustainable agricultural productivity and strengthen the autonomy of local cooperatives. It has reduced post-harvest losses by 30 to 45%, created 15 direct jobs and 40 seasonal workers, contributing to an estimated reduction of 474 tonnes of CO₂ per year.
Key technologies: Our solution combines innovative technologies to maximize impact: IoT for real-time monitoring of crops and equipment, AI for predictive analysis and yield optimization, solar for clean and sustainable energy, as well as decision support software.
Unique Characteristics: Our solution stands out for its integration, its automatic operation even off-grid, and its remote access to ensure productivity, traceability, and sustainability. It relies on a collaborative model that brings together agricultural, technological, and financial stakeholders, promoting local empowerment and climate resilience. Blended financing and solar energy enhance its accessibility and sustainability.
Sustainable Change: Our smart irrigation solution drives systemic change by transforming agricultural practices. It increases productivity and income for smallholder farmers, reduces water waste, and strengthens climate resilience, creating a sustainable impact in the short, medium, and long term.
Funding Sources: The solution was funded by the company's own funds for the prototype, grants from organizations supporting agricultural and climate innovation, as well as by support programs and incubators offering financial and technical support for pilot deployments.

Title: DigiYouth : Inclusive Pathways from Digital Skills to Income

- MSME Digitization Clinics: Youth are paired with local MSMEs to support their digital transformation (e-commerce, process automation, smart operations), generating real-world experience while directly contributing to local economic resilience.

- Impact Loop: Alumni become trainers and mentors for future cohorts, creating a self-sustaining ecosystem of peer-led growth.

Title: Smart Immersive Communication for Inclusive Digital Workspaces & Classrooms
Subtitle: AI-Powered Voice & Language Processing: Smart Ceiling Mics & Multilingual LLMs for Hybrid Collaboration
Problem Statement:
In today's digital economy, cross-border and interregional conference-based interaction has become vital for enterprise development and achieving inclusive education. However, existing systems face critical limitations that hinder effective communication and knowledge sharing:

Current Challenges includes:
1. Hardware Limitations: 
Traditional wired near-field microphones only capture primary speakers, failing to enable natural, immersive participation for all attendees in meeting rooms, auditoriums, and classrooms.
This restricts collaborative potential and diminishes engagement quality in hybrid (in-person + remote) settings.
2. Software and Intelligence Gaps
Conventional web conferencing tools lack advanced functionality, resulting in:
  a. No intelligent meeting documentation: Discussions remain unrecorded or poorly summarized.
  b. Limited resource sharing: Educational materials and expertise are confined by language barriers and static formats (text/video).
  c. No AI-powered interaction: Missing smart assistants for real-time translation, knowledge retrieval, or adaptive learning.
Solution Overview:
Our integrated solution revolutionizes digital collaboration through advanced AI-powered audio-visual technology, designed for both professional and educational environments.

1. Solution Architecture

Title: EnAIble: AI-Driven Inclusive Microlearning Platform
Subtitle: EnAIble empowers underserved women, youth, and marginalized communities in Ghana with personalized, accessible digital and entrepreneurial skills training via a mobile-first AI platform, bridging the digital divide for equitable economic growth.
Problem Statement:
Mobile phone ownership and internet penetration are rapidly growing in Ghana, with 80% of youth aged 15–29 and 78% of those aged 30–40 regularly accessing the internet (World Bank, 2021). However, this widespread connectivity has not translated into productive use for skills development or economic empowerment. A large proportion of young people, especially in rural areas, lack access to structured, affordable, and inclusive digital skills training that would enable them to participate meaningfully in the digital economy.
This gap has serious implications. Without proper digital literacy, many young people, particularly young girls and persons with disabilities (PWDs), remain vulnerable to online exploitation and cyber risks. At the same time, demand for digital skills is outpacing supply. The International Finance Corporation (IFC) highlights that although Sub-Saharan Africa’s digital labour market is growing rapidly, Ghana lags behind in producing a digitally skilled workforce. Rural communities, women, and PWDs face compounded barriers: inaccessible training platforms, limited connectivity, exclusion from digital entrepreneurship opportunities, and gendered inequalities in technology access.
The result is a widening digital divide that perpetuates socio-economic inequality. According to UNESCO, over 60% of African women still lack basic digital skills, constraining their participation in markets, innovation, and job creation. Unless targeted interventions are made, Ghana risks missing the opportunity to harness its youthful population for inclusive growth in the digital economy.
Solution Overview:
EnAIble operates as a mobile-first platform built on Ironwave's IRON.SET technology, delivering bite-sized (5-10 minute) micro-courses on digital literacy and entrepreneurship. Users onboard via an AI-driven quiz (text, audio, or video) that assesses skills and accessibility needs, generating personalised learning paths with adaptive content. 

Methodologies include gamification for engagement (points, badges, leaderboards), workflow engines for progress tracking, and organic intelligence (AI) for behaviour analysis and content recommendation. 

Technologies: AI engine for personalisation and sentiment analysis; responsive design for offline/low-bandwidth access; multilingual support with WYSIWYG editors; accessibility integrations (voice navigation, screen readers, sign language videos). 

Collaboration model: Ironwave handles tech development and scalability, while Flow Global provides culturally relevant content and community outreach in Africa. 

Partnerships extend to NGOs (The Hunger Project) for mentoring and local implementation, ensuring scalable rollout via API integrations.
Solution Provider(s): Flow Global Impact (E-learning content provider, education sector, focused on training for women and communities in Ghana) , Ironwave Technologies (tech platform developer, software sector, specializing in modular E-Learning and AI solutions for global rollouts)
Implementation location(s): Components of the underlying IRON.SET platform have been implemented in South Africa, Ghana, Mozambique & Denmark. EnAIble as a joint solution is pilot-ready; not applicable for full implementation yet.
Duration to pilot in a new geography: Approximately 12-18 months, including localization of content, AI training on regional data, initial user testing, onboarding of users, user engagement, monitoring, evaluation, accountability and learning.
SDGs addressed: SDG 4 (Quality Education);SDG 5 (Gender Equality);SDG 8 (Decent Work and Economic Growth);
Desired impact:
Objectives: Close digital skills gaps for 1 million+ underserved users by 2030; empower entrepreneurship through accessible training; promote inclusion for PWDs and marginalized groups.

Key achievements or impacts (based on IRON.SET deployments): In similar projects, achieved 40% increase in user engagement via gamification (e.g., Lulaway pilot); 25% skill improvement in digital literacy per assessments; generated 10,000+ employment opportunities through entrepreneurial training. Achieved a 95% engagement across all participants in RSA Call Centre campaign roll-out, across thousands of users. Has powered engagement and learning across millions of users over 10+ years.

Potential: Reduce gender digital divide by training 50,000 Ghanaian women and youth annually, fostering MSME growth and local job creation.
Key technologies:
AI Engine (for personalized learning paths, skills gap analysis, and user behavior adaptation)
Responsive Web/Mobile Apps (for offline access and low-bandwidth optimization)
Gamification Tools (points, badges, leaderboards)
Accessibility Integrations (screen readers, voice commands, sign language APIs)
Workflow and Dependency Engines (for dynamic content delivery)
Multilingual Localization (language packs and WYSIWYG editors)
Unique Characteristics: What makes EnAIble unique is its fusion of cutting-edge AI-driven personalisation, inclusive accessibility design, and a tech-content partnership model tailored for Africa. Unlike conventional LMS platforms, it bridges the digital divide with offline-first, culturally localised micro-learning while ensuring sustainability through blended financing and NGO-driven mentorship ecosystems.
Sustainable Change:
1. Bridging the Digital Divide (Equity & Access)
•	By providing mobile-first, offline-accessible training, EnAIble ensures that rural and peri-urban communities — often left behind due to connectivity and infrastructure gaps — gain equal access to digital skills.
•	Accessibility features (voice navigation, sign language, haptic feedback, screen readers) make inclusion of Persons with Disabilities (PWDs) systemic, not tokenistic.
2. Empowering Marginalized Groups (Social Inclusion)
•	EnAIble intentionally prioritizes youth, women, girls, and PWDs, creating pathways for groups historically excluded from education and employment.
•	This builds confidence, agency, and leadership in marginalized populations, helping them shift from beneficiaries to active contributors in their communities.
3. Creating Economic Opportunities (Sustainable Livelihoods)
•	Beyond skills, EnAIble links learners to entrepreneurship support, job placement, and microenterprise development, addressing not only training gaps but also employment barriers.
•	By targeting entrepreneurial empowerment, it strengthens rural economies and reduces reliance on migration to urban areas.
4. Building Local Ecosystems (Systemic Capacity)
•	Partnerships with NGOs, governments, and private sector actors integrate EnAIble into national digital transformation strategies.
5. Scalable & Adaptive Design (Long-Term Sustainability)
•	AI-driven personalization allows content to continuously adapt to learner needs, keeping the platform relevant over time.
•	Offline-first design makes it scalable across regions with poor connectivity in Ghana and beyond.
•	By aligning with SDGs (4, 5, 8), EnAIble contributes to global development agendas, making it easier to secure long-term policy and donor support.
6. Breaking the Cycle of Poverty (Systemic Impact)
•	By equipping marginalized groups with digital literacy and entrepreneurial skills, EnAIble tackles the root causes of poverty: lack of access, lack of skills, and lack of opportunities.
•	Over time, this creates a digitally enabled, inclusive workforce that fuels national growth and reduces structural inequalities.
