The solution targets women, youth, and marginalized groups, offering inclusive features such as offline access and multilingual support. While the platform's AI-driven personalization and focus on accessibility are strengths, its scalability and sustainability will depend on securing funding and long-term partnerships.

Title: AURA: An accessible, advanced, beautiful computing device for severe & profound disability
Subtitle: An inclusive system that’s wheelchair-mountable, featuring collaborative StarGaze app platform to improve independence and connection for people with severe & profound disability, assisting the pursuit of big dreams!
Problem Statement:
Young people with severe and profound disabilities face systemic barriers to independence, education, and employment, particularly in accessing digital technologies that underpin modern life.

Globally, this group experiences:
- Severe exclusion from education and digital skills training: Conventional devices and learning tools are often inaccessible, preventing participation in digital literacy, STEM education, and creative opportunities.
- Unemployment and underemployment: For example, in Australia, only 11.4% of people with severe/profound disability (aged 15–64) are in full-time work (ABS, 2018). Comparable statistics worldwide highlight similarly low participation, primarily due to lack of inclusive technologies and pathways into digital roles.
- Social isolation and mental health impacts: Limited means of communication and engagement with peers leads to higher risks of loneliness, depression, and exclusion from cultural and community life.
- Overpriced, underpowered technologies: Many available assistive devices are prohibitively expensive, technologically outdated, and fragmented across different regions. This leaves families, schools, and healthcare providers struggling to find solutions that are both effective and sustainable.

Without intervention, these challenges perpetuate a cycle of marginalisation, dependency and lost potential. The absence of inclusive digital ecosystems not only affects the individual but also represents a broader social and economic loss, as entire communities are excluded from the innovations, perspectives, and contributions these young people can bring.

Our solution directly addresses these barriers by providing affordable, advanced, and scalable technology designed in collaboration with young people with disabilities themselves, ensuring tools that empower independence, inclusion in education, enable creative expression, and open new digital employment pathways.
Solution Overview:
While most children and young people are learning to read and write, for the many kids who cannot achieve this through physical independence, our AURA and StarGaze solution will be their extension of self as they grow and learn to read and type (with their eyes or even their mind!). Through this we will also open up other crucial areas of day-to-day independence such as:
•	environment control and mobility
•	social connection through communication, community, gaming, and even family and playground games 
•	creative opportunities like music, authoring, art
…and these can all help culminate in better access to digital work opportunities, including the following that we have recently proven AURA can be used for: programming, word processing, graphics design, video editing, web development, internet browsing and even CAD (computer-aided design) and other engineering programs. The list of digital opportunities opened up through easy, accessible, and fast independence in computer control is truly limitless. 

AURA: Our beautiful, advanced computing device we are now applying to complete a space-age production model for. This launch model we’re developing includes a vibrant 15-inch touchscreen with brightness capabilities to even be seen when outside in the sun, a powerful custom computing processor system that can run any application including graphics-intensive programs, quality speakers so speech can be heard even in noisy environments like cafes, systems to encourage face-to-face communication and interaction, plenty of digital storage, long life rechargeable internal battery, sturdy mounting support for wheelchair arms whilst easy to take off and place on a table, and multiple ports with support for eye-trackers, push switches, muscle switches and even brain computer interface – basically any form of control an individual chooses to use over a computer will be compatible with AURA. 

Importantly, we’ve been working with partners like 4Design with the backing of Telstra Foundation to reduce the costs and make this the most advanced yet most affordable and most collaborative inclusive computing system of its kind on the market. 

StarGaze: This is our collaborative inclusive software app store that is bundled with AURA. With access to Psykinetic apps and third-party apps, our users will be able to independently download and launch everything they need from Frontier communication to music to games all from this software hub. Furthermore, through our expanding APIs we provide to third-party developers, it allows many more people and groups to launch their own apps to our community through StarGaze, without having to go through the extensive process we have to understand our users, behaviours, and how these alternate forms of controlling computers work. Our APIs include extensive examples of our unique knowledge, user interface and user experience elements that developers can simply import and make their own. This system has the purpose of helping foster increased collaboration across this very fragmented market, connecting creators and users. 

These solutions aren't just created in collaboration, we build with and for our friends, including a core member of our team who utilises her eye-controlled production prototype for communication, music (she has two singles with an Australian rock legend Steve Balbi and even performs music live on stage), dev-ops programming (she now manages our cloud infrastructure), and is even recently learning 3D CAD modelling.
Solution Provider(s): Telstra Foundation, 4Design
Implementation location(s): Testing conducted in Australia, all major cities, most work done out of Sydney
Duration to pilot in a new geography: Once ready, piloting in a new geography should only take a few months with the right partners
SDGs addressed: SDG 4 (Quality Education);SDG 10 (Reduced Inequalities);SDG 3 (Good Health and Well-being);
Desired impact:
Solution Objectives:

Our initiative seeks to transform independence, inclusion, and digital opportunity for young people with severe and profound disabilities worldwide. By combining advanced inclusive hardware (AURA) with a collaborative digital platform (StarGaze), our objectives are to:

- Increase independence in communication, mobility, and environmental control through accessible computer technologies.
- Expand access to education and digital work opportunities by enabling fast, reliable computing control through eye-tracking, switches, and brain–computer interface.
- Foster social inclusion and mental wellbeing by opening pathways to communication, creative expression, and community participation.
- Create an inclusive digital ecosystem where developers and communities can build, share, and scale applications designed with and for people with disabilities.

Key Achievements and Expected Impacts:

Building on prototypes already trialled, we aim:
- Employment and digital opportunity generation
- Educational empowerment: Children aged 5–25 will gain tools to learn literacy, coding, and digital creativity, aligning with SDG 4 (Quality Education).
- Social and mental wellbeing: By expanding communication, gaming, and creative platforms, the project will foster stronger peer and family connection, aligning with SDG 3 (Good Health & Wellbeing).
- Global collaboration and inclusion: Through StarGaze APIs, we will engage third-party developers to co-create inclusive applications, driving broader systemic change in the assistive technology sector.
- Scalable and sustainable model: By reducing device costs while enhancing performance, we are creating the most advanced yet affordable inclusive computing system in its class, designed to be replicated across regions and integrated into policy frameworks.

Our solution aims to not only deliver transformative impact for thousands of young people but also set a precedent for inclusive digital futures at scale, in line with the UN’s Sustainable Development Goals.

Furthermore, as a documentary presenter I (Jordan Nguyen) have travelled around the world to witness some of the greatest technological innovations for our people and planet. We always knew as a team we continue our decades of work to realise a dream of seeing our friends achieve theirs, and we've worked for years on finding a way to scale the technology to make that happen. We're inspired every day to keep working towards these changes we believe in, so this this is not about the technology or solution itself, it's about our humanity and big dreams for a better tomorrow!
Key technologies: Biomedical technologies, brain-computer interface, eye-trackers, AI, latest computing chips (even looking to harness the NPU neural processing unit for real-time AI), and algorithms that have been created to operate based on natural user behaviour with these systems.
Unique Characteristics:
Our solution is distinct in that it integrates cutting-edge inclusive hardware with a collaborative software ecosystem, creating a scalable model for independence, digital access, and societal inclusion.

1. Technological Innovation

AURA Device: Unlike many assistive devices that are underpowered and overpriced, AURA is a high-performance, affordable computing system designed specifically for accessibility. It supports multiple input methods (eye-tracking, switches, muscle sensors, and even brain-computer interfaces), ensuring that individuals can select the control that best fits their abilities.

StarGaze Platform: An inclusive digital hub where users can access apps for communication, education, creativity, gaming, and work. Crucially, it is open to third-party developers through APIs and SDKs, making it the first collaborative ecosystem designed for people with severe/profound disabilities.

2. Inclusive Co-Design Model

Our products are co-created with friends, with young people with disabilities, not just for them, as seen in our global award-winning documentary 'Becoming Superhuman' where our team creates an eye-controlled vehicle with our friend Riley to achieve his dream of driving a vehicle. A core team member Jess also lives with high-level cerebral palsy and uses AURA daily for communication, work, and creative expression. This ensures authenticity, usability, and dignity at every stage of design.

3. Affordability & Scale

We are partnering with world-class industrial designers and supply chain experts to deliver a space-age level device at a fraction of current market costs. This shifts the market away from niche, expensive products toward mainstream affordability, expanding access globally.

4. Ecosystem Impact Beyond Hardware

Through StarGaze, our platform creates a new market for inclusive apps. By providing developer tools and APIs, we empower other innovators to contribute solutions directly to this community, turning what is now a fragmented sector into a collaborative innovation hub.

5. Alignment with Global Development Goals

Beyond assistive tech, our approach also supports SDGs 3(Good Health & Wellbeing), 4 (Quality Education), 8 (Decent Work & Economic Growth), 9 (Industry, innovation & Infrastructure), and 10 (Reduced Inequalities). This positions the solution not as a single intervention, but as a catalyst for systemic change.

The uniqueness in our solution lies in combining technological breakthroughs, inclusive design, affordability, and a collaborative ecosystem model, aiming to move from isolated devices to a global infrastructure for digital inclusion.
Sustainable Change:
Contribution to Sustainable, Systemic Change

Our solution is designed not only to address immediate needs but has always aimed to also shift the system of inclusion, education, and employment for young people with severe and profound disabilities.

Theory of Change

Inputs
- Advanced, affordable hardware (AURA) and inclusive digital platform (StarGaze).
- Co-design with young people with disabilities and their families.
- Partnerships with industrial designers, educators, clinicians, and developers.

Activities / Outputs
- Distribution of AURA devices globally, beginning with pilot regions (Australia, NZ, USA, Canada).
- Launch of StarGaze as an inclusive app ecosystem, enabling communication, education, creativity, and work applications.
- Release of open SDKs and APIs to allow third-party developers to create inclusive software.
- Training, outreach, and community engagement with families, schools, and healthcare providers.

Short-Term Outcomes (1–3 years)
- Improved independence for young people with disabilities through accessible communication and digital control.
- Educational inclusion via literacy, STEM learning, and digital creativity tools.
- Digital employment pathways, with young people gaining skills and access to remote work opportunities.
- Stronger mental wellbeing and social connection through creative expression, gaming, and peer/family engagement.

Long-Term Outcomes (3–10 years)
- Systemic market transformation: affordable, high-performance assistive devices become the standard, disrupting the current overpriced/underpowered status quo.
- Global developer ecosystem: sustained growth of inclusive apps, ensuring innovation continues beyond our direct efforts.
- Policy integration: governments, NGOs, and education systems adopt and embed inclusive technology within disability, education, and employment frameworks.
- Cultural shift: people with disabilities are increasingly recognised not as passive recipients of care, but as innovators, creators, and contributors in digital society.

Sustainable, Systemic Change
By combining hardware, software, and community co-design, our solution lays the foundation for a self-sustaining ecosystem:
- Devices that scale affordably across markets.
- An open platform where developers, educators, and innovators can continuously expand content.
- User-led co-design ensuring relevance and dignity.
- Measurable improvements in education and employment outcomes that feed back into policy and funding support.

The desired follow-on effect is a new global infrastructure for digital inclusion, where young people with severe and profound disabilities have equal opportunities to learn, work, create, and connect. We'd love to see our friends and the communities we work with benefit further as these impacts spread, driving broader societal benefits in innovation, diversity, as well as more inclusive economic growth.

Testimonials and Endorsements:
Psykinetic AURA:
As a speech pathologist I have partnered with people with complex communication needs for fifteen years, working with them and their families to find and create solutions to enable them to participate in and engage with their worlds the way they would like to.  I offer a letter of support for Psykinetic who are applying to scale their inclusive computing device AURA and StarGaze app platform, to provide faster and more effective AAC (Augmentative and Alternative Communication) options, and to expand collaboration efforts for the growing number of apps to be available with the StarGaze platform.  This device and its platform will create novel and accessible opportunities for independence, social connection, community participation, access to work tools, and entertainment.  It feels quite a privilege to be doing the work that I do in this era of technological and social creativity and imagination. Early in my career I would never have imagined being able to describe the ideal capabilities and outcomes of a piece of technology for one individual and believe it realistic to have that functionality not only made available, but discreetly customised to that client’s unique profile of needs at an accessible cost in a comfortable time-frame. Assistive technology exploration was a matter of finding the “best fit” for the individual from what was a fairly limited and homogenous array of options. The Communication Bill of Rights (Brady et al, 2016) identifies 16 fundamental rights which are essential to enable a person with complex communication needs to participate in communication interactions fully. AAC is more than simply providing an alternative or work-around for a person who cannot or does not use speech as their primary mode of communication. Communication is more than expressing one’s self - it is interaction, advocacy, self-determination, expression, teaching, sharing of wisdom, experiences, emotions and opinions. Therefore, a device which simply “speaks” for its user does not fully serve to bridge the communication gap for users with complex communication needs. I have been involved in comparing and feature-matching a number of available AAC devices controlled with eye gaze for clients and recently worked alongside the Psykinetic team with our client to explore the lived experience of the user and how the currently available devices meet the accessibility, productivity, social and personal needs of the user. The team at Psykinetic have created a device and operating platform which not only gives a person a voice, it enables the user to immerse themselves in their communities and endeavours by providing a degree of efficiency and naturalness of communication not met by other devices. AURA integrates a host of customisable functions and tools which facilitate communication at a level far beyond simply the words spoken. It will grow and adapt with its user as they themselves grow and change with life’s daily, weekly, seasonal and yearly shifts. AURA enables people with complex disabilities to access their environment with a multimodality not easily provided with other available single-unit technology. Integration of functions for mobility, environmental control, communication, productivity and occupation mean that the user can experience a degree of accessibility to their world which independently mobile, verbal communicators experience as their norm. As a disability ally, I believe it is important to foster and advocate for continual, future-focused creativity when it comes to meeting the needs of people with disability and that this creativity is borne of the voices of those whose lives it serves to enhance. Psykinetic’s AURA device and StarGaze platform realise this. Rose Leijten Speech Pathologist BBHSc, BAppSc (Sp Path), MSPA, CPSP

Summary: AURA is an innovative computing device and software platform designed to provide digital inclusion for individuals with severe and profound disabilities, especially in communication, education, and work. Combining advanced hardware with an inclusive software ecosystem, AURA helps users gain independence and engage in digital tasks, while StarGaze offers a collaborative hub for inclusive applications. The technology has immense potential but will need to prove scalability and sustainability through successful piloting and partnership development.

Title: PREMIUM HORTUS
Subtitle: The African Greentech for Agroecology
Problem Statement: In countries like Benin, agriculture is heavily reliant on expensive, highly toxic chemical inputs and a long, traditional distribution system. This inefficiency leads to significant post-harvest losses, with fruits experiencing wastage rates exceeding 45%. Moreover, these practices contribute to high greenhouse gas (GHG) emissions, which exacerbate the vulnerability of producers, particularly women. Around 30% of female farmers in the region earn less than USD 40 annually, and over 32% of children under five years old are food insecure, highlighting a critical issue in terms of both food security and climate resilience.
Solution Overview: Premium Hortus offers a comprehensive solution through FudSup, a blockchain-powered platform available on both mobile and web. This system allows individuals and businesses (households, restaurants, hotels, etc.) to subscribe, plan, and pay online for agroecological and organic foods, with home delivery options. The platform enhances the supply chain by providing traceability from farm to fork. Smallholder farmers benefit from organic inputs, as well as technical and financial support, including our upcoming AI-based cleantech, Agrinov'IA. This AI system will help monitor soil health, optimize fertilization, and manage irrigation, allowing farmers to improve productivity by 45% without fear of climate-related disruptions like droughts or floods.
Solution Provider(s): Our strategic partnerships include prestigious organizations as: AFD, UEMOA, Tony Elumelu Foundation, FAO, Solar Impulse Foundation, CCI Benin, UNCTAD and Initiatives Climat. These partners bring significant expertise in financial support, technical guidance, and a shared commitment to achieving the SDGs.
Implementation location(s): Headquartered in Abomey-Calavi, Benin, our startup is already expanding across the region. We serve an increasing number of clients throughout Africa, including in countries like Togo, Senegal, Nigeria, and Côte d'Ivoire.
Implementation timeline(s): I- Supply Chain Development: By June 2026, we plan to open eight physical stores across Benin (Abomey-Calavi, Cotonou, Godomey, Parakou, Porto-Novo). Alongside, we will deploy eco-friendly logistics solutions such as solar-powered electric vehicles and electric tricycles for deliveries.  II- Cleantech Infrastructure: We will finalize and launch our food supply management technology, FudSup, and complete the development of our AI technology, Agrinov'IA, to ensure sustainable land management, biological pest control, and optimized fertilization.  III- Agroecological Production: By June 2026, we aim to scale agroecological production on a minimum of 10 hectares.  IV- Financial Innovation: Our CALIM+ food credit and insurance system will be developed in partnership with financial institutions, including BCEAO, by March 2027, ensuring wider access to healthy foods for vulnerable populations.  V- International Expansion: Following local success, we plan to expand further across Africa and into international markets.
Duration to pilot in a new geography: We could estimate a nine-month period to pilot our solution in any new geographical region. This timeframe allows us to adapt the Premium Hortus's model to local contexts, test our short-circuits and solutions, and optimize the platform's performance.
SDGs addressed: SDG 2 (Zero Hunger);SDG 9 (Industry, Innovation, and Infrastructure);SDG 13 (Climate Action);
Desired impact:
Our solution aims to increase food security and promote sustainable agriculture, with measurable impact. Notably, we have already achieved:

- A 46.67% reduction in GHG emissions per hectare per year compared to conventional farming.

- A 31.12% reduction in energy consumption related to transport, irrigation, and machinery.

- An average reduction of 5,883 kg of CO2 per year from agricultural operations.

- Reduced crop losses and related GHG emissions.

- Preservation of aquatic ecosystems by reducing water pollution and pesticide use.

- Enhanced soil health and biodiversity by using natural seeds and biological pest control.

In addition, we are contributing to economic resilience by generating green jobs and increasing access to sustainable and healthy food options for vulnerable communities.
Key technologies:
Our solution incorporates cutting-edge technologies not only for stable and resilient digital supply chains but also to optimize agricultural practices.

-	E-commerce Platforms (mobile and web app) for subscription-based food delivery.
-	Blockchain for supply chain transparency and traceability.
-	Fintech (e-payment systems) for secure, seamless transactions.
-	Artificial Intelligence (AI) to manage soil quality, crop yields, and climate resilience.
Together, these technologies create a sustainable, scalable model for agroecology and digital agriculture.
Unique Characteristics:
Our solution stands out due to its:

- Recognition as the first African agritech startup to receive the EFFICIENT SOLUTION 2019 label from Solar Impulse and the Outstanding Practices in Agroecology 2019 award.

- Inclusive circular economy that connects smallholder farmers directly to consumers, ensuring fair prices and supporting local markets.

- Agrinov'IA, the first AI technology in Africa to monitor soil quality, manage fertilization, and assess carbon footprints.

- Diverse and resilient agricultural products, including over 100 varieties of local and exotic organic foods.

- Sustainability: Zero stock model with fast deliveries, secure payment options, and CALIM+, a food insurance credit system aimed at ensuring access to healthy food for children in schools.

- The zero food waste and low-price stability model ensures both affordability for consumers and profitability for farmers.
Sustainable Change: Premium Hortus brings about systemic change by digitizing and democratizing access to sustainable food systems. By re-envisioning the agricultural supply chain through short, digital, and resilient supply circuits, we foster fair trade, sustainable production, and stable food prices. This approach not only supports smallholder farmers but also empowers local economies and preserves biodiversity through eco-friendly agricultural practices.
Funding Sources:
Premium Hortus has been primarily funded through:
-	Equity capital from co-founders and reinvested revenues.
-	Grants received from international competitions, including USD 35,000 from AFD, UEMOA, and the Tony Elumelu Foundation.
-	Financial viability: With a 48.47% margin on variable costs, our business model is designed to be self-sustaining. The subscription model generates 50% of our revenue upfront, ensuring steady cash flow.
We anticipate reaching break-even by day 124 and expect to recoup our initial investment of USD 505,000 by June 2026.
Testimonials and Endorsements:
We have received numerous accolades, including:
- AFD Digital Challenge 2021
- Outstanding Practices in Agroecology Award 2019 by the World Future Council.
- Best Agroecology Innovations at the FAO conference in Rome (2018)
- EFFICIENT SOLUTION 2019 label from the Solar Impulse Foundation
- Recognition by the UNCTAD for our contributions to sustainable development, including being one of the top five green startups showcased  at  UNCSTD 2019, Geneva. These endorsements highlight our leadership in agroecology and innovation in Africa.

Futhermore, We have also received several positive feedbacks, including from Mr. Kouadio A., a client in Paris, who received a delivery of chili pepper seeds for his organic farm project in Côte d'Ivoire. The order was placed in July 2025 from Paris. He wrote:
'Bonjour Monsieur, vous avez été et vous êtes très correct. C'est moi qui vous remercie.'
'Hello Sir, you have been and are very professional. I thank you very much.' This testimonial reflects the reliability and efficiency of our solution, which enables us to successfully support agricultural projects across borders, demonstrating the real-world impact of our service in promoting sustainable farming.

The model connects smallholder farmers directly with consumers while providing them with organic inputs, technical and financial support, and AI-based cleantech (Agrinov'IA) for soil health and climate resilience. The solution reduces GHG emissions, food waste, and chemical dependency while promoting food security, women’s economic empowerment, and sustainable agriculture. Partnerships with AFD, FAO, UNCTAD, Solar Impulse, and others strengthen credibility. Premium Hortus has won multiple awards, operates regionally (Benin, Togo, Senegal, Nigeria, Côte d’Ivoire), and is scaling toward international expansion.

Title: ⁠Igniting Digital Equity: EduSpots’ Community-Led Model & App
Subtitle: EduSpots connects, trains & equips 400+ local changemakers in 50 underserved communities in Ghana and Kenya to ignite future-ready education using digital tools, WhatsApp innovation, and the EduSpots app.
Problem Statement:
Despite the growing importance of digital literacy in today’s world, only 53% of teachers in Ghana have received any form of ICT training, leaving many unable to effectively integrate technology into classrooms; this gap, highlighted by the Ghana National Association of Teachers (GNAT), reflects a persistent challenge dating back to a 2011 study which revealed that 87% of teachers had never used a computer during instructional delivery and only a small minority had integrated ICT into their teaching practices. Today, this continued lack of teacher competence in ICT has severely limited students’ exposure to digital learning, with just 22% demonstrating basic ICT skills, thereby widening the digital divide and threatening the future readiness of young learners.

The 2023 Ghana Population and Housing Census highlights alarming levels of digital exclusion among children. An estimated 188,312 children aged 6 to 11, and 103,047 aged 12 to 17, do not own a functional ICT device. Children aged 0 to 14 accounted for 34.7% of the national digital divide, far exceeding the rates recorded in older populations (0.7% for ages 15–35, and 14.0% for ages 61+). During an EduSpots DigiLit club session in Dulugu, an EduSpots Catalyst found that 18/20 female students did not know how to turn on a computer. 

Stressing the urgency of action, Prof. Edward Appiah, Director-General of NaCCA, stated at a UNESCO workshop in April 2023 that “ICT skills are no longer an optional extra in our education system.” He emphasized that all young people must be equipped with digital skills essential for the future, starting with empowering teachers to integrate ICT in their classrooms (UNESCO, 2023). 

Educators themselves generally do not have the knowledge or equipment to develop these crucial skills in their students, and rely on personal mobile devices to gather the information to teach what they can (ACET, 2022) with a government scheme in Ghana for providing teachers with laptops falling short on delivery expectations. 

From a gender perspective, the digital divide is even more pronounced. In 2018, only 7% of women in Ghana reported using a computer compared to 21% of men, and just 15% of women used the internet for ICT purposes versus 35% of men (Gender Portal, 2021). 

A 2022 World Bank report further underscores the urgency of this challenge, estimating that less than 40% of Ghana’s population possesses the basic digital skills required to effectively use online services. This striking gap between access and actual digital competency demonstrates that without intentional investment in teacher capacity and student digital literacy, Ghana risks leaving a majority of its population unprepared to participate meaningfully in the digital economy and broader knowledge society.

We believe that the talents and ideas of students, teachers and community members are not fully harnessed in addressing digital inequity and promoting future-ready education with digital literacy embedded. Our model changes this through building on the energies, ideas and talents of 400 community-based changemakers, with 50% of our staff team drawn from the Spot community network. The learners of today are fast becoming the changemakers of tomorrow; with 35% of Ghana’s population under 14 (2021 census), this presents a huge future digital leadership opportunity.
Solution Overview:
In 2025, EduSpots connects, trains, and equips over 400 local changemakers (“Catalysts”) in Ghana and Kenya with essential digital tools and skills. Together, they are strengthening community-led education and supporting over 10,000 learners (“Sparks”) to build digital literacy and confidence for the future.

EduSpots invites teams of local changemakers named ‘Catalysts’ to apply to join a grassroots education network with a thorough application process requiring a team of local changemakers, community engagement and support, evidence of existing educational volunteerism, internet connectivity, a space and commitment to our Keeping Spots Safe policy. 

Selected Spot teams embark on a 12-month Ignite Programme. This holistic capacity-building journey includes a 3-day in-person training, monthly virtual workshops, team coaching, mentorship, use of EduSpots’ digital app, and on-site Spot visits. The programme equips teams to establish safe, inclusive, and digitally empowered community learning hubs called ‘Spots’ in schools or community settings.

Selected Spot teams begin their journey with the 12-month Ignite Programme. This holistic journey includes a 3-day in-person training, monthly workshops, team coaching, mentorship, app usage, and Spot visits - all designed to help teams create safe, inclusive change hubs called 'Spots' in schools or community settings. 

Each Spot receives at minimum two tablets, a WiFi kit and resource boxes, and are given access to our Education Hub which is on WhatsApp across a range of WhatsApp groups which Catalysts opt into based on interests. EduSpots has an innovative strategy for learning through WhatsApp that positions Catalysts as knowledge producers and collaborators, rather than purely as trainees. 

All Catalysts and Sparks formally register through the EduSpots app, which includes built-in processes for local reference checks for Catalysts and parental approvals for Sparks. The app allows Spot teams to track key activities such as opening hours, club meetings, book borrowing, and resource usage, while also providing transparency on grants, local fundraising, and expenditure. 

Embedded into this process is EduSpots’ Keeping Spots Safe badge which is compulsory for all Spot teams. This involves completing in person engagement with Sparks, Catalysts, teachers and community members, including events with parents, with a particular focus on Keeping Spots Safe protocols, creating a culture of ‘passing it on’, and online safety.

All active Catalysts gain access to EduBytes, our digital learning platform that builds essential digital skills. Training covers Canva design, career development, basic AI, and practical use of tools such as Microsoft Office Suite and Google Workspace. Catalysts receive certificates upon completing online sessions and submitting tasks, while also being supported to deliver digital skills training in their communities.

Catalyst teams then choose 1- 4 education strands based on local priorities, targeting different age groups: EduKidz (early years), DigiLit (digital literacy), EcoSTEM (STEM and sustainability), and Ignite Equity (gender equity). Each strand offers physical resource kits, mentorship from strand coordinators, and monthly challenges with coaching, competition and certificates, backed by a strong community of practice linking peers across Ghana and Kenya.

In Year 2, selected Catalysts from each Spot join the one-year Catalyse Leadership Programme, where they receive advanced training, particularly in digital skills, and a grant to deliver a Catalyse Project with digitalisation embedded at its core. Looking ahead, we are developing a Year 3 Sustain Programme focused on helping Spots generate local income, strengthen systems, and deepen digital capacity, ultimately preparing them to transition into long-term leadership hubs once they reach self-sustainability.
Solution Provider(s): Our CEO/founder, Cat Davison was recently selected as a UNESCO Youth for Peace fellow with funding awarded and wider professional development support offered towards the development of our online education platforms, which will partly be used to generate sustainable income for EduSpots’ innovation work whilst igniting global intercultural dialogue.  Cat Davison is also a Global Teacher Prize community, working with a community of teachers across the world who have provided technical support to EduSpots’ work, with the support of the Varkey Foundation, and also a Gratitude Network Fellow, who provide coaching and technical business development support.  EduSpots has recently been selected for the second year of the Dovetail Impact Foundation’s Africa Accelerator Portfolio, which has involved a marketing and strategic support programme with MightyAlly, focusing on the theory of change and market position in year 1.  The key partners EduSpots in Ghana works with are local community teams, who build Spot Management Committees comprising representations across students, teachers, headteachers, parents and wider political, religious and educational groups. They sign partnership agreements with EduSpots, depending on whether the Spot is school-based or community-based.   80% of current Spots are within Ghana Education Service schools, in partnership with GES headteachers, teachers and local education authorities with an MOU pending with the wider national Ghana Education Service and the Ghana Library Authority.  We partner with ImpactEd to use their monitoring and evaluation software and reporting, without recent independent evaluation conducted by Expectation State.  We are currently exploring wider partnerships in this process who may support in-person monitoring and coaching, with EduSpots continuing as the main delivery organisation, leading programme design, oversight and evaluation.  Funded by the Gower Street Trust, we are leading a Climate Education Community of Practice, involving 10 local NGOs in collaborative work using digital tools. We are also part of a learning group with the mc2h foundation, which brings together four significant community-led education NGOs in Ghana: Lively Minds, AfriKids, School for Life and EduSpots in a process of learning.
Implementation location(s): Ghana (11 regions), Kenya (1 region), 50 communities in total
Implementation timeline(s): 2023-2025 for the Ignite Programme, App introduced in 2024, EduSpots has been in operation since 2016
Duration to pilot in a new geography: 3 years
SDGs addressed: SDG 4 (Quality Education);SDG 3 (Good Health and Well-being);SDG 10 (Reduced Inequalities);
Desired impact:
In the longer-term we aim to be a transformative global organization championing future-ready learning through community-led, participatory and tech-driven methodologies. 

These are the intended digital skill impact areas in 2025-2026, when we plan to expand our network from 50 to 100 Spots, as part of a research process on our systems, partnerships and exploring diverse scale pathways for our model. 

At least 70 - 80% of Catalysts should demonstrate confidence in integrating ICT tools (laptops, projectors, educational apps, etc.) into lesson delivery at the Spot and in their classrooms.
By 2026, 100% of Catalysts complete online safety training, and 70% of Sparks demonstrate safe online practices through EduSpots’ Keeping Spots Safe assessments and workshops.
By 2026, at least 500 Catalysts create original digital learning content (e.g., Canva posters, AI-assisted resources, short videos), and 50% of Spots run at least one community campaign using these materials.
By 2026, all 400+ Catalysts actively engage in EduSpots’ digital platforms (WhatsApp hubs, EduBytes, EduSpots app) and collaborative tools (Zoom, Google Meet, Teams), with at least 70% contributing monthly to peer learning or resource sharing.
By 2026, at least 40 Catalyse Projects integrate digital tools to address local challenges, with 75% of Spots reporting improved efficiency, transparency, or innovation through digital solutions.
By 2026, 80% of Catalysts and 60% of Sparks can search, assess, and apply digital information for learning and projects, measured through app-based quizzes and project reports.
Close the gender divide so that female Catalysts and learners participate equally in training, access, and usage of digital tools.
Establish peer-support systems and ongoing professional development through our EduBytes programme.

See this link for our wider Theory of Change which shows wider outcomes: https://eduspots.org/about-us/our-vision/

In 2024-2025 we commissioned an independent evaluation of our work with Expectation State, who sampled 10 Spot communities, engaging over 200 parents, community leaders, learners and Catalysts through a mixed methods outcome harvesting approach. Find the report here: https://issuu.com/eduspots/docs/2025_eduspots_model_evaluation_by_expectation_sta

Summary: “The EduSpots programme has successfully transformed educational landscapes across Ghana, fostering a new generation of active, empathetic citizens and catalysing community-driven change.”

Pedagogical transformation: “The shift towards more learner-centred, inclusive, and practical teaching methods has transformed school-based pedagogy, making education more relevant and engaging for students.”

Here are some quantitative findings:
1. There was a 52% increase in Catalysts’ self-reported empathy and cultural sensitivity scores. 
2. 85% of Catalysts felt able to handle complex safeguarding concerns.
3. Trends analysis among learners showed a 40% increase in learners’ participation in civic activities throughout the programme.
4. Parents reported an increase in their ward’s openness in reporting issues they faced at school to them.
5. Classroom observation data showed a 45% increase in student-centred learning approaches among teachers exposed to the EduSpots model.

Findings from internal ImpactEd Studies using validated surveys: 
7.8% increase in ‘environmental action scale’ (2 months, Catalyst Programme post training Academy, 2025) 
13% increase for learners in ‘emotional engagement in maths and science’ (over 10 months, 2024) 
4.8% increase in ‘Sense of Community Index’ (10 months, Catalysts, Ignite Programme, 2024) 
8% increase in ‘interest in reading’ (Over 10 months, DigiLit Learners, 2023) 
12% increase in ‘self-efficacy’ (Over 10 months, Catalysts, Catalyse Leadership Programme, 2021)
2.4% increase in ‘confidence in using digital technology’ scale (Catalysts, March-April 2025)
Key technologies:
Communication & Collaboration Platforms
WhatsApp Groups - used for strategic networking, educational management, peer learning, and knowledge exchange.
Google Workspace - for staff collaboration, peer mentor support and peer-to-peer learning and collaboration for Catalysts.
Zoom - for delivering online training sessions with Catalysts.

Devices & Connectivity
Laptops - Dell Inspiron, 8GB RAM, 512GB storage
Tablets - minimum specifications: 4GB RAM, 64GB storage, 10-inch screen, Android OS (aim: 5 tablets per Spot).
WiFi Kits - to enable reliable internet access for Spots.
Projectors - available in most Spots, paired with tablets for group learning.

EduSpots Digital Platforms
EduSpots App - co-designed with EngagedU to support Catalyst and Spark registration, activity tracking, transparency, and digital learning.

Content Creation & Digital Skills Tools
Canva, Google Workspace, Microsoft Office Suite - for creating locally relevant learning materials.
Basic AI tools (e.g., ChatGPT for education, translation, or lesson ideas) - guided, ethical use for Catalysts and Sparks.
Unique Characteristics:
Innovative use of WhatsApp: We involve Catalysts in training & playful collaboration via 10 structured WhatsApp hubs that use features such as polls, emojis, voice note notes, quizzes, groups calls and more to enable Catalysts to be positioned as knowledge producers; driving their own development and that of others, whilst building an inclusive grassroots education community that increases wider teacher motivation. 

EduSpots App: The EduSpots App is the first of its kind in providing a tool for local people to design, run and track their own educational activities, with systems built in to support parental permissions, whilst tracking references, activities, finance and book borrowing. Among other features, it enables the submission of monthly team challenges to staff members to mark, offer feedback and give recognition.  

Inside-out development: Unlike top-down interventions, our solution empowers Catalysts—parents, youth, and teachers—to envision, lead & sustain the futures they want to see. Their ownership is proven: 25% of our existing Spots were launched by Catalysts expanding the model organically; 60% of staff have Catalyst backgrounds, ensuring lived expertise guides our approach. Learners don’t just benefit—they become Catalysts, creating a self-multiplying effect. 

Affective learning: Through effective use of digital tools, we advance socioemotional learning with students, teachers & parents working together to create safer systems for managing behaviour, with differentiation & inclusive practices embedded in a multimodal approach, which has a ripple effect into schools & communities, addressing root causes of poor mental health and drop-out.
Sustainable Change:
Digital and wider educational inequity is growing and local changemakers - teachers, youth and parents - have untapped talents, energy and ideas, with 35% of Ghana’s population under the age of 14. 

We connect, train and equip local changemakers to ignite future-ready learning through co-curricular clubs in spaces named ‘Spots’, using the app, WhatsApp and digital tools, in both school and community-based spaces.  

School and wider community-based learning becomes more inclusive, interactive, tech-enabled and relevant to their local contexts. 

The change sustains locally, whilst collaborating with government and wider partners to promote future-ready learning, driven by local Catalyst innovations. 

Community members work together to advance future-ready education with diverse voices respected, protected and involved in decision-making. 

Learners, teachers and community members grow their confidence in digital skills, engagement in education and wider optimism. The learners of today, become the future Catalysts of change. 

A growing, self-propelling and sustainable local and global education network enables communities to create the futures they want to see.

Title: Arsela – Unlocking Citizen Development with No-Code AI
Subtitle: Enabling entrepreneurs, SMEs, and institutions to build digital solutions without coding, accelerating growth and access to digital opportunities.
Problem Statement: Many organizations, especially SMEs, face barriers to digital adoption due to high costs, lack of technical talent, and long development cycles. This prevents them from innovating, scaling, and offering better services to citizens and communities.
Solution Overview:
Arsela is a no-code, AI-powered process automation platform that allows non-technical users to create and deploy applications, workflows, and digital services in just a few clicks.

How it works: Users describe processes in natural language, and Arsela’s AI agents transform them into functional applications and automated workflows.

Technologies: Agentic AI orchestration, process mining, low-code/no-code platforms, secure cloud-native deployment, multilingual NLP (English, French, Arabic).

Methodologies: Designed for citizen development, Arsela combines human-in-the-loop oversight with scalable AI agents, ensuring transparency, adaptability, and inclusivity.

Partnerships & Collaboration Models: Arsela collaborates with municipalities, SMEs, and local development agencies to accelerate adoption, offering training and onboarding to empower users. Partnerships with integrators extend the solution’s reach and impact.
Solution Provider(s): Arsela Technologies – Proprietary technology provider, fully developed in-house by Arsela. The platform leverages agentic AI capabilities integrated with OpenAI technologies and is hosted on a secure AWS cloud environment, ensuring scalability, reliability, and compliance.
Implementation timeline(s): 2021–2022 – In-house development of Arsela platform, AI orchestration engine, and no-code builder.  2023 – Pilot implementation with the Ministry of Interior (Tunisia) involving 20 local administrations and municipalities, focusing on digitization of citizen services and process automation.  2024 – Broader deployment across Tunisia and first clients in the UAE, including SMEs and financial institutions.  2025 (ongoing) – Expansion to France & Francophone Africa (Senegal, Côte d’Ivoire) with local system integrators; continuous AI enhancements and multilingual support.
Duration to pilot in a new geography: 2 months
SDGs addressed: SDG 9 (Industry, Innovation, and Infrastructure);SDG 8 (Decent Work and Economic Growth);SDG 11 (Sustainable Cities and Communities);
Desired impact:
- Democratize access to digital transformation by enabling non-technical users (citizen developers) to build applications and automate processes without coding.
- Reduce cost and time barriers for SMEs in adopting and scaling digital solutions.
- Foster local innovation ecosystems by creating training and empowerment pathways that build capacity within communities.

Title: Empowering Tana River County Through Digital Transformation
Subtitle: Leveraging the Desert Stars ICT HUB to equip Tana River's communities with essential digital skills, drive local innovation, and bridge economic divides for a more inclusive digital future.
Problem Statement:
Tana River County, an Arid and Semi-Arid Land (ASAL) in Kenya, faces a profound digital economic divide, with digital literacy rates below 5% and over 76% of its population living in poverty. This severe exclusion disproportionately affects women, youth, and Micro, Small, and Medium Enterprises (MSMEs). They are hindered by:

a) Limited Access: Scarcity of affordable internet, unreliable electricity, and lack of devices in remote areas.

b) Low Digital Skills: Insufficient foundational and advanced ICT knowledge to access online opportunities, government services (eCitizen), or participate in the gig economy.

c) Economic Disadvantage: MSMEs struggle to access new markets, financial services, or enhance productivity due to a lack of digital tools and skills.

d) Vulnerability to Shocks: Communities lack digital information for climate change adaptation (drought/flood early warnings) or to diversify livelihoods, exacerbating existing vulnerabilities.

e) Gender-Based Barriers: Women, in particular, face additional socio-cultural and economic hurdles to digital access and literacy, deepening inequalities.

These systemic barriers prevent Tana River's marginalized communities from meaningfully participating in, and benefiting from, the growing digital economy, perpetuating cycles of poverty and hindering sustainable development.
Solution Overview:
Solution Overview: Desert Stars ICT HUB – Bridging Tana River's Digital Divide

JUHUDI Community Support Center's Desert Stars ICT HUB, based in Hola, is a vital initiative tackling the severe digital and economic exclusion in Tana River County, Kenya. Our mission is to empower women, youth, and MSMEs to thrive in the digital economy.

How Our Solution Works
The HUB acts as a dynamic ecosystem, integrating training, local innovation, and essential resource provision:

Community-Driven Design: We engage local leaders and community groups across Tana River to ensure our programs precisely meet their digital and economic needs, addressing specific challenges like agricultural market access or e-citizen services.

Tiered Digital Skills Training:

Foundational Literacy: Basic computer/smartphone use, internet navigation, and online safety for beginners, especially women.

Applied Skills: Practical training in digital marketing, e-commerce, content creation, and digital financial literacy to boost MSME growth and youth employment.

Advanced ICT: Specialized skills like software development and data analytics, empowering youth to create local digital solutions.

Local Solutions Co-creation: The HUB is a "living lab" where trained youth, with community input, develop digital tools for Tana River's unique challenges. Examples include apps for agricultural market linkages or SMS platforms for water management. Promising ideas receive incubation support.

Access to Infrastructure: We provide reliable internet and computer labs, crucial in areas with limited home connectivity. Solar power ensures continuous operation despite electricity challenges.

Mentorship & Job Linkages: We connect trainees with mentors, facilitate networking, and support online job applications to enhance employment and freelancing opportunities.

Our Approach & Partnerships
We employ a Human-Centered Design (HCD), ensuring relevance and cultural appropriateness. Our training combines in-person, hands-on learning with a mobile-first approach, using open-source technologies for affordability.

Our impact is magnified by strong partnerships:

Local Communities & County Government: Collaboration with Tana River County departments (e.g., Youth Affairs) and local leaders ensures program alignment and community buy-in.

Academic & Private Sector: We engage universities for curriculum development and telcos for affordable connectivity.

NGOs & Development Partners: Partnerships with UN agencies (UNCTAD, UNIDO, UNDP) and other NGOs amplify our reach and impact, ensuring a cohesive approach to digital inclusion in Tana River County.

Title: Filtar is an AI-native security and compliance layer purpose-built for GenAI applications
Subtitle: Filtar combines real-time threat detection, cognitive reasoning, and reinforcement learning to autonomously enforce policies, prevent jailbreaks, and ensure regulatory compliance. Designed for fast-moving companies in regulated industries, Filtar adapts continuously through human feedback and synthetic data augmentation—enabling secure, privacy-first AI deployments without slowing innovation.
Problem Statement:
Security Risks in GenAI: Prevents prompt injection, jailbreaks, and unauthorized system access through real-time threat detection and self-learning filters.

Regulatory & Ethical Compliance: Ensures outputs meet standards like the EU AI Act, NIST, and OWASP via autonomous compliance enforcement and audit-ready logging.

Privacy & Data Protection: Guards sensitive data and user interactions, enabling AI use in regulated environments without exposing private or legal information.

Time-to-Market Delays: Reduces deployment timelines by eliminating manual fine-tuning and integrating out-of-the-box security and policy guardrails.

False Positives & Developer Overhead: Continuously adapts through reinforcement learning, lowering false alerts and minimizing friction for developers.
Solution Overview:
How the Filtar Solution Works

Filtar is a **self-learning, AI-native platform** designed to secure and govern GenAI applications—whether built on LLMs, autonomous agents, or hybrid RAG systems. It acts as a **real-time enforcement layer** that adapts with each interaction to protect systems from malicious use, data leakage, and compliance risks.

1. Intelligent Security & Compliance Layer

Filtar embeds itself at the heart of the GenAI stack and continuously evaluates LLM outputs using:

* **Reinforcement Learning Agents**
Actively learn from real-world interactions, detecting prompt injections, policy violations, and language-based attacks. Agents are rewarded for successfully identifying threats and minimizing false positives.

* **Cognitive Reasoning Models**
Simulate human-like thinking to detect subtle intent (e.g., social engineering, ambiguous prompts). This enables Filtar to catch edge-case jailbreaks or obfuscated attack vectors.

* **Semantic & Psychological Modeling**
Goes beyond keyword filters to understand the *why* behind a prompt—enhancing defense against prompt engineering and adversarial behavior.

* **Real-Time Guardrail Enforcement**
Filtar wraps any LLM or multi-agent setup with guardrails based on:

  * Organizational policies
  * Regulatory requirements (e.g., EU AI Act, HIPAA, NIST RMF)
  * Vertical-specific rules (e.g., healthcare, legal, finance)

---

2. Compliance Stack & Automation Engine

* **Dynamic Risk Scoring & Policy Mapping**
Each model output is scored against pre-mapped regulatory thresholds. Borderline responses are flagged, while clear violations are blocked or escalated.

* **Human-in-the-Loop (HITL) Integration**
Ambiguous or high-risk responses are sent to human reviewers for escalation, labeling, or feedback—feeding back into the learning loop.

* **Anonymized, Auditable Logging**
All actions are logged in a privacy-first, SOC 2–compliant manner, enabling audit trails without compromising user confidentiality.

* **Synthetic Data Augmentation**
  Automatically generates adversarial examples and edge-case scenarios to improve detection accuracy over time—without relying solely on client data.

---

3. Technologies & Methodologies Used

* **Large Language Models (LLMs)** for language understanding and simulation (works with OpenAI, Claude, Mistral, etc.)
* **Reinforcement Learning (RLHF / RL-Secure)** for adaptive threat detection
* **Cognitive Computing Frameworks** (for intent and mental-model simulation)
* **Self-Healing Filters & Auto-Finetuning** for vertical-optimized prompts and filters
* **RAG-Enhanced Context Awareness** via enterprise data integrations
* **On-Prem & In-DB AI** deployment capabilities for high-security environments

---

🤝 4. Partnerships & Collaboration Models

Co-Build & Integration Partnerships

Filtar offers co-development programs with enterprise clients to:

* Extend security filters to new verticals (e.g., legal, insurance, health)
* Customize guardrails based on internal policies
* Jointly build secure agentic workflows tailored to client environments

Pilot & PoC Engagements

* Filtar can be deployed as a lightweight layer in clients’ existing LLM stacks
* Includes validation against client datasets, stress-tested against adversarial inputs
* Validated in environments with real production constraints (e.g., with legal notaries, financial services)

Infrastructure & Model Partners

* **Model Agnostic:** Compatible with OpenAI, Anthropic, Mistral, open-source models
* **Cloud-Neutral Deployments:** Available as SaaS, hybrid cloud, or fully on-prem
* **Data Partners:** Works with client-side data lakes or RAG pipelines to contextualize outputs and personalize guardrails

Title: Facilabio: Connecting Patients and Laboratories, Securely
Subtitle: Facilabio is a digital solution that simplifies the access, management, and sharing of medical test results between patients, laboratories, and healthcare professionals.
Problem Statement: Facilabio provides patients with secure, on-demand access to their medical test results from anywhere, facilitates locating nearby laboratories, and enables comprehensive tracking of their test history. For laboratories, the platform offers direct result delivery, patient statistics monitoring, and automated reminders. Additionally, patients receive personalized health advice and notifications, enhancing patient engagement and continuity of care, particularly in resource-limited settings.
Solution Overview: Facilabio is a comprehensive digital platform designed to enhance the management and sharing of medical test results. It allows patients to securely access their test results anytime and anywhere, track their medical history, and locate nearby laboratories for convenient testing. Laboratories can upload test results through an intuitive interface, monitor patient data and statistics, and automate communications such as appointment reminders and follow-ups. The platform is built using a Python backend Nodejs and modern frontend frameworks like React.js, ensuring a responsive and user-friendly experience across devices, including mobile phones. Data security is a top priority, with encryption protocols and strict access controls aligned with healthcare regulations. Hosted on cloud infrastructure, Facilabio is scalable and reliable, enabling deployment in resource-limited settings. Strategic partnerships with local healthcare providers, laboratories, and NGOs support user training, workflow customization, and community engagement. These collaborations are key to adapting the solution to regional needs and maximizing its impact on patient care and public health.
Solution Provider(s): Bio24 Medical Lab – Clinical diagnostics laboratory, providing expertise in medical testing and patient data management, active in the health sector. Gaindé digital : A company specialized in digital solutions for digital transformation, active in the technology sector. Directorate of Laboratories of Senegal – A public institution responsible for the regulation and coordination of laboratories, active in the public health sector.
Duration to pilot in a new geography: Estimated duration: 2 to 3 months. This includes stakeholder onboarding, platform localization, user training, infrastructure setup, and initial monitoring.
