Title: Empowering Civil Servants with Affordable Solar Through Digital Financing
Subtitle: A digital solar program enabling African civil servants to access affordable, pay-as-you-go solar home systems through salary deduction and mobile monitoring tools.
Problem Statement: In many African countries, civil servants—despite having stable employment—struggle to access clean, reliable electricity due to high upfront solar costs and lack of tailored financing. This leads to continued reliance on expensive and polluting energy sources like kerosene or small petrol generators. The SunWorks Africa Civil Servant SHS Program addresses this by offering solar home systems through affordable, salary-deducted payments, removing financial and technological barriers to adoption while promoting energy access and economic inclusion.
Solution Overview:
The SunWorks Africa Civil Servant SHS Program is a digitally enabled solar financing and deployment initiative that empowers public sector workers in Cameroon to access clean, reliable electricity without upfront cost. By integrating digital identity verification, payroll integration, banking partnerships, and mobile monitoring technologies, the program provides a scalable pathway to last-mile electrification and inclusive participation in the digital economy.

How the Solution Works
Digital Onboarding & Eligibility Screening
Civil servants apply via the SunWorks web portal or USSD system. Their employment status and salary grade are verified through secure integration with government payroll databases.

Financing Through Salary Deduction
Approved users receive solar home systems (SHS) through micro-loans financed by partner banks. Loan repayment is structured as automated salary deductions, removing credit risk and ensuring affordability without collateral.

SHS Delivery & Installation
Tiered solar kits—designed based on typical household loads and user-selected appliance preferences—are installed by certified technicians. Systems support lighting, mobile charging, fans, TVs, radios, and small appliances.

IoT Monitoring & Energy Management
Each SHS includes a smart IoT-enabled controller. Through the MySun mobile/web app, users can:

Monitor energy production and usage

Track repayment progress

Receive maintenance alerts

Access tutorials on energy literacy and financial management

Feed-In Option for Grid-Connected Users
Where policy and infrastructure permit, households with surplus solar energy can sell excess power to the national grid or local mini-grids. Earnings can be credited toward early loan repayment or transferred to user-linked bank or mobile money accounts.

Banking Integration & Digital Wallets
Partner banks provide:

SHS loans backed by payroll data

APIs to monitor repayment

Integration with digital wallets or mobile banking apps to provide users with access to energy credits, balances, and automated reporting

Methodologies & Technologies
Cloud-based registration and user verification platform

API-based payroll integration for secure salary-deducted repayment

IoT-enabled SHS hardware with GSM/SMS connectivity

Offline-compatible load calculator and sizing assistant

MySun app for user energy management and service requests

Multilingual (English/French) interface and localized training content

Geospatial tagging of installations for logistics and monitoring

Analytics engine for repayment risk scoring, usage patterns, and impact tracking

Partnerships & Collaboration Models
Government ministries & payroll departments: Enable automated deductions and user verification

Local and regional banks: Provide energy loans and digital repayment tracking

Telecom providers: Offer GSM channels for IoT and user communication

Solar hardware suppliers: Manufacture modular, scalable solar kits

Energy cooperatives & installers: Conduct last-mile installation and maintenance

NGOs and development partners: Support digital literacy, outreach, and impact evaluation

Power utilities or mini-grid operators: Facilitate net metering and power buy-back programs where permitted

This model not only brings clean, modern electricity to underserved populations, but also creates an inclusive financial footprint for civil servants who may otherwise lack formal credit access. By digitizing the energy journey—from application to repayment and grid participation—SunWorks Africa is enabling public workers to become clean energy consumers and producers in a digitally connected economy.
Solution Provider(s): SunWorks Africa Ltd – A Cameroon-based renewable energy social enterprise focused on solar solutions, last-mile electrification, and digital energy access. SunWorks designs, finances, and deploys solar home systems (SHS) tailored for underserved populations, including civil servants and rural communities. (Sector: Renewable Energy, Digital Finance, CleanTech)  Ministry of Finance – Cameroon – Government payroll integration partner enabling salary-deducted loan repayments for civil servants, ensuring structured, risk-free financing. (Sector: Public Sector / Payroll & Administration)  Ecobank Cameroon S.A. – Financial partner providing tailored microloans for solar systems, repayment APIs, and energy-linked savings and credit products. (Sector: Commercial Banking / FinTech / Clean Energy Finance)  MTN Cameroon – Telecom partner supporting GSM-enabled SHS controllers, USSD services for registration and system alerts, and mobile wallet interoperability for users without traditional banking access. (Sector: Telecommunications / Mobile Finance)  SRNE Solar – Hardware partner supplying advanced, modular solar home system components including IoT-enabled charge controllers and inverters, customized for household and institutional use in African markets. (Sector: Solar Hardware Manufacturing & Distribution)  Eneo Cameroon S.A. – National electricity utility and grid operator supporting grid integration for hybrid solar installations, enabling feed-in tariff structures, net metering, and surplus energy monetization to reduce payback periods. (Sector: Energy Utility / Grid Infrastructure)  Engineers Without Borders – Cameroon Chapter – Technical and capacity-building partner responsible for training local technicians, deploying systems, and maintaining service quality. (Sector: Engineering, Technical Education, Infrastructure Support)  Rural Electrification Agency of Cameroon (AER) – Strategic policy and infrastructure partner supporting grid interaction, mini-grid expansion, and rural deployment approvals. (Sector: Government, Energy Infrastructure)
Implementation location(s): Cameroon – The solution has already been implemented in the following locations:  Yaoundé, Centre Region – Deployment of solar home systems to civil servants across various ministries.  Bamenda, North West Region – Implementation through local technician networks and civil servant outreach programs.
Implementation timeline(s): The solution has been implemented in the following locations since July 2025:  Yaoundé, Centre Region: Initial deployment to civil servant households began in July 2025, focusing on payroll-integrated financing models.  Bamenda, North West Region: Deployment started in July 2025 in partnership with local technicians and community organizations.
Duration to pilot in a new geography: The estimated duration to pilot our solar home system solution in a new geography is approximately 6 to 9 months. This timeframe includes:  Initial stakeholder engagement and partnership formalization (1–2 months)  Community sensitization and user registration (1 month)  System customization, procurement, and logistics setup (1–2 months)  Installation and commissioning of solar home systems (2–3 months)  Training of local technicians and user onboarding (1 month)  Monitoring, troubleshooting, and impact evaluation (1 month)  This timeline can be adjusted based on the size of the target population, geographic accessibility, and local regulatory requirements.
SDGs addressed: SDG 7 (Affordable and Clean Energy);SDG 13 (Climate Action);SDG 11 (Sustainable Cities and Communities);
Desired impact:
Expand access to affordable, clean, and reliable solar energy for underserved households, starting with Cameroonian civil servants.

Enable inclusive digital finance through salary-deducted microloans and mobile payments, especially for unbanked populations.

Foster green employment by training and engaging local technicians in installation and maintenance.

Reduce reliance on fossil fuels and grid instability, improving energy security and lowering household expenses.

Build climate resilience and promote sustainable development through decentralized solar infrastructure.

Key Achievements & Impacts (as of August 2025)
25+ households equipped with modular solar home systems since launch in July 2025 (Yaoundé & Bamenda).

Over 15 local technicians trained and deployed in partnership with Engineers Without Borders – Cameroon Chapter.

Estimated 25–30 metric tons of CO₂ emissions to be avoided annually (based on typical diesel generator replacement).

Monthly energy cost savings of up to 40% for participating households.

Digital inclusion for >70% of users through mobile payments and USSD-enabled support, even for unbanked individuals.
Key technologies:
IoT-Enabled Solar Home Systems
Each system includes smart charge controllers and inverters (from SRNE Solar) that collect and transmit real-time performance data, enabling remote diagnostics, usage tracking, and system control.

Mobile Payment Integration
The solution leverages USSD and mobile money platforms (MTN Mobile Money) for customer registration, balance inquiries, and energy credit payments—facilitating access for users without smartphones or bank accounts.

Payroll-Integrated Fintech API
Through integration with the Ministry of Finance payroll system, loan repayments are automated and deducted at source, minimizing default risk and enabling inclusive credit access.

Cloud-Based Monitoring & Analytics
Back-end systems collect, store, and analyze user and performance data to generate insights on energy usage, maintenance needs, and repayment behavior.
Unique Characteristics:
Payroll-Integrated Financing for Civil Servants
Unlike traditional pay-as-you-go models, our solution uniquely integrates with the government payroll system to offer salary-deducted microloans, making clean energy affordable with minimal risk for both end-users and financial institutions.

Public–Private–Tech Partnership Model
The solution brings together government (Ministry of Energy and Water, AER), private sector (SunWorks, Ecobank, MTN), and civil society (Engineers Without Borders) to co-deliver energy access, financing, and technical support—ensuring sustainability, scale, and trust.

Inclusive Digital Delivery Channels
Through USSD interfaces and mobile wallets, the system enables users—including the unbanked and those without smartphones—to manage their energy usage and make payments, increasing reach across low-income populations.

Smart IoT-Enabled SHS Kits
Systems supplied by SRNE Solar include embedded IoT monitoring, enabling remote diagnostics, usage-based alerts, and preventative maintenance—improving service quality and system uptime.

Energy-for-Income Strategy
The model supports users not only in powering homes but also in generating income (e.g., charging stations, refrigeration for small businesses), creating a pathway out of energy poverty.

Surplus-to-Grid Capability
Through partnerships with Eneo, the system allows for future grid integration and feed-in mechanisms, enabling users to monetize surplus energy and repay loans faster.
Sustainable Change:
Our solution creates long-term, systemic impact by embedding clean energy access within national institutions, digital infrastructure, and financial systems. The desired follow-on effects include:

1. Institutionalized Access to Clean Energy
By integrating with the government payroll system, solar energy becomes a formal, affordable utility for civil servants—turning energy access into a reliable public service rather than a donor-driven intervention. This model can be replicated across ministries and extended to other public or semi-public sectors.

2. Financial Inclusion and Credit History Building
The salary-deducted loan mechanism, supported by commercial banks (e.g., Ecobank) and mobile finance partners (e.g., MTN), enables even low-income, unbanked individuals to access credit for energy systems. As they repay, they build a credit profile, unlocking broader financial services such as housing loans or education financing.

3. Local Green Economy Growth
The program actively trains and employs local technicians, creating skilled jobs in the clean energy sector. This builds a self-sustaining ecosystem of installation, maintenance, and energy entrepreneurship (e.g., solar-powered barbershops, phone charging businesses).

4. Behavioral and Cultural Shifts
Through consistent and visible deployment, the solution normalizes renewable energy adoption, reducing dependence on fossil fuels and generators. This supports a societal shift toward sustainability, especially among public servants who influence broader community behavior.

5. Scalable and Replicable Framework
The model’s integration of policy, technology, and finance provides a blueprint for scale—not only within Cameroon but across sub-Saharan Africa. Once proven, it can be adapted for teachers, healthcare workers, or rural cooperatives in other regions.

By embedding clean energy within existing economic and governance systems, the solution transitions from one-off solar access to a systemic engine for resilience, prosperity, and climate action.
Funding Sources:
The initial implementation of the solution has been funded through a blended finance model, including:

Private Equity and Founder Capital – Seed funding from SunWorks Africa Ltd. founders to launch pilot operations, product development, and partnership engagement.

Commercial Bank Support – Ecobank Cameroon provides credit lines and working capital support tied to the salary-deducted loan program for SHS financing.

Customer Contributions – End-users co-finance systems via structured monthly repayments through payroll deductions or mobile money payments.

In-Kind Support – Technical and training contributions from Engineers Without Borders – Cameroon Chapter, and operational collaboration with public sector partners.

Additional funding applications are underway through international grants and climate finance programs to scale the solution.
Primary thematic focus area: Enabling Policies & Regulatory Innovation
Summary: The SunWorks Africa Civil Servant SHS Program provides affordable, digitally enabled solar systems for civil servants in Cameroon, integrating payroll-based microloans with IoT monitoring and mobile payments. A strength is its strong institutional and private sector partnerships, including the Ministry of Finance and Ecobank (Q14). A weakness is that impact data is still early-stage, with only 25 households served so far (Q22, Q19).

Title: ISLET Connect - Empowering Underserved Communities
Subtitle: The Internet for Sustainable Livelihood e-Education and Tourism Project that will be operated, maintained and sustained by the local residents of the communities empowering them to be self reliant.
Problem Statement:
The ISLET Connect project addresses the critical infrastructure deficit faced by Geographically Isolated and Disadvantaged Areas (GIDAS) in the Philippines. The GIDA communities are physically and socio-economically marginalized, suffering from a profound lack of essential services and infrastructure, particularly in communication, electricity, and supply chains. This digital isolation exacerbates their limited access to fundamental opportunities, including quality e-education, vital e-health services, and viable e-commerce platforms.

Furthermore, the absence of reliable communication infrastructure severely compromises their ability to prepare for and respond to natural disasters, leaving them highly vulnerable during crises. While the Philippine government acknowledges these challenges, support for GIDAS is often hindered by their remote geography, political complexities, and history of conflict. Consequently, these communities remain disconnected from the mainstream economy and social services. The core problem is this persistent digital divide, which perpetuates a cycle of poverty and vulnerability, and which the ISLET Connect project aims to solve by providing a sustainable, community-led connectivity solution.
Solution Overview:
The ISLET Connect project employs a hybrid, multi-layered technical solution designed to deliver reliable and sustainable internet connectivity to Geographically Isolated and Disadvantaged Areas (GIDAS). The core architecture is a robust, community-owned infrastructure that ensures operational longevity and local empowerment.

1. Network Infrastructure & Connectivity: The primary internet source is a high-throughput satellite service (e.g., Starlink), which provides a high-bandwidth backhaul link to a central hub location. From this hub, a wireless multipoint-to-point infrastructure is deployed, using radio frequency technology to distribute the internet signal to surrounding community access points and designated facilities. This hybrid approach circumvents the prohibitive costs and logistical challenges of laying fiber-optic cables in a marine environment.

2. Locally Accessible Cloud System (LACS): A key component is the deployment of a Locally Accessible Cloud System (LACS) at the community level. This localized server hosts essential data and applications, ensuring that services such as e-learning materials, e-health records, and disaster preparedness information remain accessible even during periods of network disruption or intermittent satellite connectivity. The LACS facility provides a resilient platform for critical services.

3. E-Cooperative Model for Operations: The technical solution is sustained through an e-cooperative model where trained community members are responsible for the daily operationalization, maintenance, and basic troubleshooting of the network. This includes managing the local wireless access points and ensuring the LACS and satellite terminal are functioning. This distributed management approach reduces dependency on external technical support and fosters a sense of local ownership.

4. Business & Sustainability Framework: The project establishes community business centers where residents can access the network for entrepreneurial activities. Revenues generated from these activities are directly reinvested into the cooperative to cover operational expenses, purchase new equipment, and upgrade the network. This self-sustaining economic loop ensures the continuous improvement and expansion of the ISLET Connect infrastructure.
Solution Provider(s): Department of Science and Technology (DOST) Philippine Government Agency, Advanced Telecommunications Research Institute International Japan (ATR), Asia Pacific  Network Information Center (APNIC)
Implementation location(s): Gilutongan Island, Cordova, Cebu, Philippines; Cawhagan Island, Lapu-lapu City, Cebu, Philippines; Pangan-an Island, Lapu-lapu, Cebu, Philippines; Barangay Lawis, Inabanga, Bohol, Philippines; Cuaming Island, Inabanga, Bohol, Philippines; Gibitngil Island, Medellin, Cebu, Philippines
Implementation timeline(s): Gilutongan Island, Cordova, Cebu, Philippines (May 2022-present); Cawhagan Island, Lapu-lapu City, Cebu, Philippines (June 2024-present); Pangan-an Island, Lapu-lapu, Cebu, Philippines (Jan 2024-present); Barangay Lawis, Inabanga, Bohol, Philippines (Oct 2024-present); Cuaming Island, Inabanga, Bohol, Philippines (May 2025-present); Gibitngil Island, Medellin, Cebu, Philippines (July 2025-present)
Duration to pilot in a new geography: Five months; one month for survey and  installation; two months for technical training and establishment of e-cooperative; two months for operationalization, maintenance and sustaining the project
SDGs addressed: SDG 4 (Quality Education);SDG 11 (Sustainable Cities and Communities);SDG 13 (Climate Action);
Desired impact:
The primary goal of the ISLET Connect project is to provide a stable broadband internet solution to digitally disadvantaged island and mountainous communities or GIDA areas. By addressing the challenges of limited and expensive connectivity, the project aims to create a positive social impact and promote social responsibility by leveraging the power of Information and Communications Technology (ICT).

The desired impact is multi-faceted, focusing on the following key areas:

1. Enhanced Education
- Improved Access to Learning: The project aims to provide students and teachers with reliable access to online learning materials and resources.
- e-Education Platform: The establishment of a dedicated e-education and Learning Management System (LMS) within the ISLET Connect Portal allows for continuous learning, even with limited internet access.

2. Sustainable Livelihood and Economic Opportunities
- Digital Empowerment: Residents are empowered with essential digital skills and knowledge to engage in the digital economy.
- e-Commerce and Tourism: The project seeks to create a web portal that offers opportunities for livelihood promotion, e-commerce, and the marketing of local tourism. This helps to boost the local economy and create new income streams.

3. Improved Safety and Disaster Preparedness
- Reliable Communication: The project aims to establish a solar-powered Locally Accessible Communication System (LACS) that provides both online and offline instant communication.
- Timely Information: With enhanced connectivity, communities can receive timely updates on natural disasters, such as typhoons, allowing for better preparation and response.

4. Community Engagement and Empowerment
- Community-Based Operations: The project promotes a sustainable community-based support system, including a cooperative-based "COIN" device and a vouchering system for internet access.
- Digital Inclusion: The initiative specifically targets the digitally disadvantaged, including children, women, and persons with disabilities, ensuring they have the necessary ICT solutions to improve their access to information and communication technology.
Key technologies:
Connectivity Infrastructure:
Wireless Point-to-Point (P2P) Links: Used to distribute internet from a mainland hub to the various islands.

Satellite Internet (Starlink): Provides a stable, high-speed broadband connection as both a primary and backup internet source.

Solar Power: Powers all communication facilities to ensure continuous operation.

Software and Systems:
Locally Accessible Communication System (LACS): A local intranet and communication platform that functions both online and offline.

ISLET Connect Portal: A web portal that serves as a central hub for community resources. Using web development frameworks

E-education & Learning Management System (LMS): A component of the portal for local learning using Moodle open source software

"Connect-internet (COIN)" System: A community-based cooperative model that uses a specific device and a vouchering system to manage internet access.
Unique Characteristics:
Hybrid On/Offline System (LACS): The project's "Locally Accessible Communication System" (LACS) is a key differentiator. It's a portable, solar-powered system that provides an intranet and hosts a variety of services (e.g., e-education, e-commerce, disaster information) that can function even in the absence of a live internet connection. This is a critical feature for remote islands where connectivity can be intermittent or completely lost during natural disasters.

Community-Based Sustainability Model ("COIN"): Instead of a purely top-down, charity-based approach, ISLET Connect implements a sustainable, community-managed model called the "Connect-internet (COIN)" cooperative system. A special device and a vouchering system are used to manage internet access, generating revenue to cover operational costs. This model empowers the community to support and maintain the network themselves, ensuring its long-term viability.

Holistic Solution for Community Empowerment: The project goes beyond simply providing internet access. It integrates the technology with a web portal that offers specific, tangible benefits for the community in four key areas:
-Safety: Disaster risk reduction information.
-Livelihood: E-commerce and livelihood promotion.
-e-Education: A Learning Management System for students and teachers.
-Tourism: Promotion of local ecotourism.

Replicability and Scalability: The project is designed with a modular and easily replicable framework. The successful deployment and community engagement in the initial pilot islands have created a proven model that can be expanded to other remote island communities in the region, with the support of local governments. This focus on a scalable, transferable model is a core part of its design.
Sustainable Change:
ISLET Connect's approach to systemic change goes beyond providing a one-time solution. Instead, it focuses on building the capacity of local communities to manage and sustain their own development, creating a ripple effect of positive change.

The Locally Accessible Communication System (LACS) as a Catalyst
The project's technical solution, the LACS (Locally Accessible Communication System), is more than just a communications network. It is a critical tool for empowerment.
- Digital Inclusion: The LACS provides internet access in areas with little to no connectivity, bridging the digital divide for vulnerable populations, including women, children, and people with disabilities. This access is foundational for systemic change, as it enables access to information, education, and economic opportunities.
- Empowerment and Self-Reliance: The LACS is designed to be a portable, solar-powered server system. By providing solar charging stations and immediate, local communication capabilities, it fosters self-reliance. In times of disaster, the community no longer has to wait for external aid to communicate and coordinate, making them more resilient.
- Localized Information Hub: The project created a web portal that functions as a local information hub. It provides an e-education platform, tourism information, and, most critically, disaster risk reduction information. This localized, accessible information stream empowers residents to make informed decisions and prepare for natural calamities, which are a major threat to island communities.

The Community-Based Cooperative Model (COIN)
The economic model of ISLET Connect is designed for long-term sustainability and local ownership.
- Community Ownership: Instead of relying on external providers, the project establishes a community-based support operation. This shifts control and responsibility to the residents themselves, ensuring that the system is maintained and adapted to their needs.
- Economic Viability: The project implements a voucher system and a "COIN Device" (likely a reference to a cooperative internet initiative), which creates an internal, micro-economic ecosystem. By generating local revenue and managing its own finances, the cooperative ensures the long-term viability of the communication system without continuous external funding.
- Livelihood Opportunities: The project's web portal also provides a marketplace for local products and services, fostering e-commerce and diversifying the local economy. This strengthens the community's economic foundation and provides new livelihood opportunities, which is a key component of sustainable development.

3. Governance and Partnerships
ISLET Connect recognizes that systemic change requires collaboration and a supportive policy environment.

Title: Scout is a platform reshaping private market investing from the inside out.
Subtitle: Scout is an AI-powered CRM helping VCs make faster, fairer, and more informed investment decisions—surfacing ESG data, reducing bias, and streamlining dealflow from source to close.
Problem Statement: Venture capital is plagued by slow, biased decision-making and incomplete data, leading to missed opportunities and inequitable funding. Startups generate over 50% of new jobs globally, yet only 2% of VC goes to all-women teams. Research shows diverse founding teams deliver 30% higher returns and faster exits, but are consistently overlooked—hindering inclusive growth and limiting economic potential.
Solution Overview:
Scout is an AI- and ML-powered platform designed to help venture capital investors make faster, more inclusive, and data-informed decisions. It integrates structured and unstructured data—like founder traits, team diversity, and ESG (Environmental, Social, Governance) alignment—early in the deal pipeline to surface high-potential, underrepresented startups. By embedding alternative signals directly into VC workflows, Scout reduces bias and improves capital allocation toward socially and economically sustainable ventures.

Scout’s approach is firmly grounded in equitable principles such as fairness, transparency, inclusivity, and prompt action. These principles guide both the platform’s design, ensuring ethical decision-making and fostering long-term commitment to systemic change in venture capital.

Methodologies & Technologies:
Artificial Intelligence (AI) and Machine Learning (ML) models analyze pitch decks, founder bios, and company narratives to detect founder resilience, team diversity, and ESG alignment beyond traditional financial metrics

Custom ESG & DEI scoring frameworks aligned with SFDR standards

Human-in-the-loop design to maintain transparency and explainability in AI decision processes

Shifting the investment landscape requires collaboration among multiple stakeholders in both the public and private sectors—both top-down and bottom-up. Top-down efforts come through regulations such as SFDR, while bottom-up change is driven by tools like Scout that enable investors to apply these frameworks in their day-to-day work. To drive meaningful change, investors must adopt tools and frameworks that actively reduce bias and promote inclusive, responsible decision-making.

Partnerships and Collaboration Models:
Scout collaborates closely with early-stage VC firms to pilot and validate our platform and AI/ML-driven models. We work with accelerators, ecosystem builders, and organizations focused on diversity to expand access to underrepresented deal flow. Additionally, we have spoken to data providers, government advisors, and legal experts to ensure full compliance with GDPR and responsible AI standards. Through these partnerships, Scout bridges regulatory frameworks with practical tools that support investors in making more equitable and data-driven decisions.
Solution Provider(s): Scout is a primarily bootstrapped for-profit business. While we have not yet formalized official partnerships, we have engaged with over 200 stakeholders including government officials, legal experts, and accelerator program managers. Our current collaboration includes several design partners—early-stage venture capital firms (Ananda Impact Partners, Vowerk Ventures, Proptech 1) providing valuable feedback during product development.  We believe that The Call for Solutions for an Inclusive Digital Economy will help us connect and collaborate with thought leaders and key stakeholders to further embed equitable and inclusive practices within private market investments, driving meaningful change in venture capital.
Implementation timeline(s): Scout was founded in early 2024. The MVP was developed and launched by mid-2024, followed by pilot testing with design partners through late 2024 and ongoing into 2025. The platform is actively used by select VC firms as of early 2025, with continuous iteration and product development planned throughout the year.
Duration to pilot in a new geography: The estimated duration to pilot Scout in a new geography is approximately two weeks from initial setup to active use. After the pilot phase, the solution is designed for ongoing, recurring use with continuous updates and support.
SDGs addressed: SDG 5 (Gender Equality);SDG 8 (Decent Work and Economic Growth);SDG 10 (Reduced Inequalities);
Desired impact:
Increase in funding diversity: Scout aims to raise the share of VC funding going to all-women founding teams by at least 1 basis point (0.01%) annually, contributing to long-term systemic change in capital flows.

Bias reduction: Proprietary AI/ML models surface inclusive indicators (e.g., team resilience, diversity, and ESG alignment), improving equitable deal sourcing and reducing reliance on biased pattern recognition—resulting in up to 30% more diverse founder visibility in pilot usage.

ESG and SDG alignment: Enables VC firms to integrate ESG data into 80%+ of early-stage evaluations, improving regulatory compliance and impact-driven investment strategies.

Economic empowerment: Diverse-led startups typically generate 20–30% higher revenue growth and job creation; Scout helps redirect capital toward these high-potential companies, fostering more inclusive economic development.
Key technologies: Scout leverages advanced technologies including artificial intelligence (AI) and machine learning (ML) to analyze and interpret complex startup and founder data beyond traditional financial metrics. Our platform integrates ESG (Environmental, Social, and Governance) data to provide holistic investment insights. We use secure cloud infrastructure to ensure scalability and data protection, complying with GDPR and responsible AI standards. These technologies enable efficient, unbiased decision-making and support investors in identifying high-potential, diverse startups aligned with sustainable and equitable principles.
Unique Characteristics:
Unique/Differentiated Characteristics of Scout:

Proactive decision support: Unlike traditional VC tools that are passive and reactive, Scout actively surfaces diverse founders, ethical business models, and ESG risks early in the pipeline—prompting action, not just observation.

Bias-aware from the ground up: Scout is purpose-built to reduce systemic bias in venture capital by embedding inclusive metrics like founder resilience, team diversity, and SDG alignment into investor workflows.

Equity-focused AI models: Our machine learning models highlight non-traditional success signals, providing a richer, more equitable understanding of startup potential.

Embedded ESG & SFDR compliance: Scout streamlines integration of ESG and sustainability regulations directly into day-to-day decision-making, supporting both ethical investing and legal accountability.

Built for real-world VC workflows: Co-developed with early-stage VCs, Scout integrates smoothly with existing CRMs and deal processes, ensuring immediate utility without disrupting how investors work.

Independent and values-driven: As a bootstrapped venture, Scout is free from conflicting incentives—enabling us to stay aligned with our core principles of inclusion, fairness, and long-term impact.
Sustainable Change:
Scout addresses systemic bias and inefficiency in venture capital by embedding equitable, sustainability-aligned decision-making directly into investor workflows. By surfacing inclusive, ESG-aligned startups earlier in the pipeline and prompting active recognition of overlooked founders, Scout enables more fair and impactful capital allocation.

Immediate Outputs:

More diverse and SDG-aligned founders are surfaced and considered.

Investors improve ESG and SFDR compliance through built-in analytics.

Time to evaluate and compare early-stage deals is reduced.

Medium-Term Outcomes:

Funding rates for underrepresented founders increase by at least 1 basis point annually.

Capital begins to flow more consistently toward inclusive, impact-driven businesses.

Investors shift toward proactive, data-driven sourcing practices.

Long-Term Systemic Change:

A more inclusive innovation economy emerges, supporting job creation and resilience in underserved communities.

Equity and sustainability become default standards in early-stage investing.

The VC ecosystem becomes more transparent, accountable, and aligned with global development goals.

Title: S4DH (Satellite for Digital Health)
Subtitle: SUSTAINABLE SATELLITE FOR DIGITAL HEALTH IN RURAL AFRICA.
Problem Statement: Nigeria’s health service struggles with brain drain, insufficient infrastructure and inadequate specialist skills on one hand, and affluent patients choosing to be treated abroad. Medical tourism is costing the Nigerian economy in the region of $1.3 billion annually. Hence, the health service for dependent Nigerians, in particular those living in rural and remote areas, is often poor and inadequate. This is prevalent in rural Africa including global south countries. One way to mitigate these shortcomings is to make use of digital solutions enabling shared specialist resources that reside in Nigerian central health facilities and elsewhere.
Solution Overview:
Previous Satellite for Digital Health (S4DH) research project titled Tele-medicine as a Panacea to Medical Tourism in Africa exploiting Communication Satellite Technologies was one of the winning proposals in the international research competition organized by the International Telecommunication Unions (ITU) Connect2Recover initiative; the first ever international research competition organized by the ITU. The competition which received 307 entries from 80 countries across five continents had 15 outstanding winners which include our research project. Connect2Recover is an ITU global initiative that aims to reinforce digital infrastructure and ecosystems of beneficiary countries. 
As Principal Investigator for the $42,000.00 research grant (grant no. 10), I collaborated with international & national universities in United Kingdom and USA, Hospitals and industry including Nigerian Communications Satellite Ltd,  on Digital Health Inclusion Health Project exploiting Communications Satellite Technology for the six (6) months research which draws on a mixed-methods covering case studies, a survey and action research. We assessed past telemedicine projects, Surveys covering interviews, consultations, and discussions with stakeholders on healthcare technologies and deployed ‘Action Research’. The Action Research covered the deployment of VSAT-based internet with a mobile health application (the One2One app) to determine the applicability of satellite technology for telemedicine services. The pilot project facilitated deployment of communications satellite technology with peer-to-peer app for ehealth services including early diagnosis and prompt treatment in unserved areas of Nigeria and rural Africa in general. It effectively delivered telemedicine solutions via the NIGCOMSAT-1R Communications Satellite to guarantee an effective locally delivered health system that reduced the need for medical tourism. https://www.itu.int/en/ITU-D/Pages/connect2recoverresearchcompetition/winners/default.aspx
Aside treating well over 1,000 patients in Northern Nigeria, Southern Nigerian and Internally Displaced Persons (IDP) in Federal Capital Territory of Nigeria, other outcomes include: 
i.	4 Papers publications in various journals and conference proceedings on significance of adopting telemedicine in global south countries.
ii.	Need for Teaching Hospitals to include Digital Health systems as part of their curriculum on benefits of adopting digital health especially in University Teaching Hospitals and other related health organizations fast-track its acceptance and adoption in the country and the continent at large. Framework and policies at local, state, national and regional level are required to drive implementation among other recommendations.
The research project won 2023 Institution of Engineering and Technology (IET) Global impact-in-society Award in healthy lives, assisted living & robotics category received on 28th March, 2023 at IET Headquarters, Savoy Place, London. We leveraged multi-displinary fields comprising of Communications Satellite Systems, Software Application, Cybersecurity, Telemedicine, Health Technology, Informatics and Green Energy. https://www.bawa.tech/blog/iet-impact-in-society-winners/
Solution Provider(s): Dr. Lasisi Salami Lawal, Associate Professor,Department of Information & Communication Engineering, Faculty of Engineering and Environmental Design, Usmanu Danfodiyu University, Sokoto and Acting General Manager, Nigerian Communications Satellite Ltd; Dr. Ubong Udoyen, Department of Psychiatry; Yale University School of Medicine, USA and Managing Director One-to-One Health; Professor Chris R. Chatwin, School of Engineering and Informatics, University of Sussex, Brighton-UK, BN1 9QT and Dr. Theddeus Iheanacho, Department of Psychiatry, Yale University School of Medicine, New Haven, CT, USA.
Implementation location(s): Utilization of Aviation Medical Clinic, Kaduna International Airport with deployment of a pilot for the people of Gwazaye Community; S4DH Mobile Solution for a Cottage Hospital at Ikot Ekpene Udo Community of Akwa Ibom State; Mobile S4DH Clinic for Internally Displaced Persons (IDP) Camp; Kuchingoro, Abuja-FCT
Implementation timeline(s): Deployed as an Action Pilot under a $42,000.00 international research grant for validation in the field for 6 months from 2021 to 2022 after ethical approval covering deployment of VSAT-based internet with a mobile health application (the One2One app) to determine the applicability of satellite technology for telemedicine services. The pilot project facilitated deployment of communications satellite technology with peer-to-peer app for ehealth services including early diagnosis and prompt treatment in unserved areas of Nigeria and rural Africa in general. It effectively delivered telemedicine solutions via the NIGCOMSAT-1R Communications Satellite to guarantee an effective locally delivered health system that reduced the need for medical tourism. https://www.itu.int/en/ITU-D/Pages/connect2recoverresearchcompetition/winners/default.aspx Aside treating well over 1,000 patients in Northern Nigeria, Southern Nigerian and Internally Displaced Persons (IDP) in Federal Capital Territory of Nigeria.
Duration to pilot in a new geography: One week. As a matter of fact, efforts are ongoing to deploy same solution at Usmanu Danfodiyo University, Sokoto School Clinic and ongoing research  effort to incorporate local multilingual translator using deep learning artificial intelligence (AI) to mitigate against language barrier in past field work as well as policy framework and recommendations for digital health systems to Government of African Nations.

Desired impact:
This was a very beneficial solution as it facilitates digital health inclusion for all via Communications Satellite in line with United Nations Sustainable Development Goals (SDG). Goal 3 on “Good Health and Well-being”. The project trial was very useful and helped to provide an essential service to those in the rural areas with limited digital skills. The mHealth Software application effectively deliver tele-medicine consultations locally, which can help reduce medical tourism as confirmed by respondents of the questionnaires administered to healthcare providers and patients.
In underserved communities across Nigeria and other rural African communities, digital health presents a tool to close the gap between the inhabitants of such communities and medical personnel, who are usually based in urban locations including medical consultations with medical professionals anywhere in the world without embarking on physical travel outside the shores especially as it concerns follow-on consultations. Furthermore, the project seeks to explore the creation of a mobile emergency response facility that can quickly be deployed to a disaster location to extend emergency healthcare service delivery. Thus, the project will also make a critical contribution to enhance the nation's disaster response preparedness and effectiveness utilizing communications satellite technology among others including deepening adoption of renewable energy for the digital health systems facilitating GHG reductions and climate future-proof Africa.
Key technologies: To ensure the success of our telemedicine project, our multi-disciplinary team with interdisciplinary excellence contributed expertise on: communications technologies, satellite communications, medicine, software engineering, mechatronics engineering, health policy and management, data & cyber security , whilst at the same time demonstrating a viable advanced technological solution for telemedicine implementation.
Unique Characteristics:
The project made  critical contribution to enhance the nation's disaster response preparedness and effectiveness
utilizing communications satellite technology. 
Other Research Findings are: 
i. Robust networks require taking into account equipment sizing from the gateway of the teleport to the end user equipment for delivery of efficient broadband services end-to-end. 
ii. Major challenges facing the adoption of telemedicine in Nigeria are language barriers and the low literacy level of the population, especially in underserved communities and thus work-in-progress for multilingual deep learning AI translators to major African languages to be facilitated with African super computing initiatives more of South African and Morocco initiatives.
iii. The video call feature of the One2One mobile application was essential for the purpose of physical examination, especially in the case of visible skin conditions. This feature is,
therefore, strongly recommended for any software developed for providing telemedicine services.
iv. Poor sanitary conditions, environmental management and health sensitization and education in IDP camps are major contributor to the prevalent diseases at the camp. 
v. Accessibility of IDP camps to outsiders is not regulated and may pose security challenges to the inhabitants of the camp.

Unique/Differentiated Characteristics are:
i. Our Mobile health application Software built with security features had audio, video and text capabilities to provide telemedicine services in both urban and rural locations using Satellite-based or terrestrial networks.

ii. We had 2 variants of the One2One mobile healthcare application made  available on Google Play Store (One for Doctors with details of their qualifications for registration validation and the other variant for Patients) underscoring the importance of digital mobile apps in the Telemedicine drive and adoption.

iii. The mobile satellite-based solutions can be utilized by the National Emergency Management Agencies and other emergency and disaster management agencies and responders to deliver healthcare services to citizens during disasters and emergency situations.
Sustainable Change: Overall, the optimized ‘one2one’ telemedicine app, effectively delivered via Communications Satellite, can be used in tele-medicine centres and e-health facilities to guarantee an effective locally delivered health system that will reduce the need for medical tourism. The effectiveness of the team and success of the project is not only evident from the number of patients treated but also availability of healthcare professionals and experts from across the world irrespective of their geographic locations. Recommendations also includes the need for University Teaching hospitals to embrace telemedicine and digital-health inclusion in the teaching curriculum of student doctors to fast track e-Health adoption. Policy recommendations are also on course on the National ICT strategy to drive digital health inclusion forward in both Nigeria and Africa in line with United Nations Sustainable Development Goals (SDG) Goal 3 for “Good Health and Well-being”.
Funding Sources: one of the winning proposals in the international research competition organized by the International Telecommunication Unions (ITU) Connect2Recover initiative; the first ever international research competition organized by the ITU. The competition which received 307 entries from 80 countries across five continents had 15 outstanding winners which include our research project. Connect2Recover is an ITU global initiative that aims to reinforce digital infrastructure and ecosystems of beneficiary countries. I was the Principal Investigator (PI) for the $42,000.00 research grant (grant no. 10).
Testimonials and Endorsements: The research project won 2023 Institution of Engineering and Technology (IET) Global impact-in-society Award in healthy lives, assisted living & robotics category received on 28th March, 2023 at IET Headquarters, Savoy Place, London. It was celebrated for leveraging multi-disciplinary fields comprising of Communications Satellite Systems, Software Application, Cybersecurity, Telemedicine, Health Technology, Informatics and Renewable Energy.
Primary thematic focus area: Enabling Policies & Regulatory Innovation
Summary: S4DH deploys satellite-based telemedicine to address Nigeria’s healthcare gaps, with demonstrated pilots treating over 1,000 patients and international recognition from ITU and IET (Q13, Q19, Q28). Its strength lies in validated field pilots and award-winning innovation leveraging communications satellites for rural health (Q13, Q23, Q28). A weakness is that while sustainability and policy recommendations are noted, risk management and a long-term funding pathway are not fully detailed (Q25, Q27).

Title: Digital Food Traceability in Africa.
Subtitle: From Farm to Fork, For people and planet
Problem Statement:
Africa loses approximately 1.2 million hectares of forest per year due to agricultural activities. Agricultural expansion is the primary driver of deforestation in Africa, accounting for over 75% of the continent's forest loss. As demand for cash crops like cocoa, coffee, and palm oil grows, forests are increasingly cleared to make way for farmland. Unchecked expansion accelerates biodiversity loss and carbon emissions. Africa exports $16.5 billion of agricultural produce to the European Union (EU); however, nearly 60% of food produced in the region cannot be traced due to fragmented supply chains and inadequate data collection systems. This lack of traceability results in high rejection rates, with commodities facing rejection rates of up to 45% in the EU, according to Food Tank. With over 200 million farmers, traceability methods used by exporters are predominantly manual, relying on reverse traceability. Paper-based systems are outdated, inefficient, and prone to errors. 

Traceability is a critical component in managing food systems. The lack of traceability erodes consumer trust, compromises food safety, and hinders compliance with quality standards for local and global markets. With the implementation of new EUDR regulations regarding food traceability, many exporters and cooperatives that source their produce from small-scale farmers struggle to meet these standards, risking exclusion. As a major food exporter to the EU, compliance with traceability regulations is crucial for Kenya to maintain its position in the global market.
Solution Overview:
JANI AI is a cloud-based platform that provides end-to-end digital traceability of the food supply chain, from farm to fork, in Africa. JANI AI makes food traceability simple, fast, and affordable. Our platform offers Farm Mapping, Farmer Management, Product Cataloging, and Inventory Management software solutions. We target off-takers, exporters, food processors, and farmer cooperatives in the farming industry. JANI supports critical agricultural value chains in East Africa, including tea, coffee, nuts, and horticulture (fruits and vegetables). 

JANI AI is designed to collect Key Data Elements (KDEs) and monitor critical tracking events throughout the farming process, from production to consumption. Our Farm Mapping Software allows for precise geolocation of farms, capturing GPS points and polygon data for land use verification. Our Farmer Management System assigns unique identifiers and lot numbers to products and producers, ensuring traceability and transparency in the supply chain. Our Inventory Management Software optimizes produce collection and aggregation by consolidating produce into larger batches. JANI AI facilitates compliance with global standards, such as EUDR and FDA. Our system generates certificates of traceability and origin, providing an auditable trail from farm to table. 

JANI operates on a B2B Software-as-a-Service (SaaS) model, offering a subscription-based revenue structure. We offer tiered packages, including Standard, Premium, and Enterprise, with monthly rates ranging from $100 to $1,000. 

JANI AI revolutionizes the way data in food systems is collected, managed, and utilized.  We empower farmers, cooperatives, and exporters to meet global standards and build consumer trust. 



How JANI AI Works
Farmer Registration
 Smallholder farmers are onboarded onto the platform and assigned unique, biometric-linked digital identities. This ensures secure data collection and establishes a foundation for traceability.


Farm Mapping
 Using GPS-enabled mobile tools, farms are geolocated and mapped, capturing polygon data, acreage, and crop details. The platform works offline and syncs automatically when the internet is available.


Produce Collection & Cataloging
 During harvest, produce is collected, tagged, and logged into the system. Data on volume, location, farmer identity, and collection time are recorded for each lot.


Digital Traceability & Compliance Certification
 The system automatically generates digital certificates to validate each batch against global standards such as EUDR. These are verifiable by buyers and regulators.


Batch Traceability Report
 For every shipment or batch, JANI AI produces a traceability report detailing its origin, movement, compliance status, and sustainability metrics, boosting transparency, trust, and market access.

Title: e-BLOOD: Digitizing Every Drop of Blood to Save Lives Faster
Subtitle: An innovative digital platform connecting donors, hospitals, and transporters to ensure fast, traceable, and secure access to blood—anywhere, anytime.
Problem Statement:
In many low- and middle-income countries, blood transfusion systems face major structural challenges. The rapid unavailability of compatible blood, lack of real-time stock data, poor coordination between hospitals, transfusion centers, and donors, as well as the absence of transport and cold chain traceability, lead to preventable loss of lives every day.

The death of my mother, due to the unavailability of a compatible blood bag in time, painfully highlights these failures. This tragic experience revealed the urgent need to rethink and modernize the way blood is collected, stored, distributed, and used.

Even today, in many regions, donor identification, blood transport organization, and emergency management are done manually or with outdated tools. These dysfunctions cause delays, stock shortages, blood wastage due to poor management, and even medical errors.

The e-BLOOD solution addresses these problems systematically by providing digital tools, complete traceability, improved coordination among stakeholders, and faster, more equitable access to blood—especially in remote areas.
Solution Overview:
e-BLOOD
1. Detailed Description of How the Solution Works

e-BLOOD is a mobile and web-based digital platform designed to modernize the entire blood donation, management, and distribution chain. It connects blood donors, healthcare facilities (transfusion centers, hospitals), and transport services, while ensuring traceability, speed, and safety.

Here’s how the solution works:

    Donors: Through a mobile app, donors can create a profile, access their blood type information, view urgent needs in their area, receive targeted notifications, and schedule donations at approved locations.

    Health Facilities and Blood Banks: A web interface allows them to manage their real-time blood stock, report critical shortages, register received donations, and request blood transportation.

    Certified Transporters: A dedicated app enables them to receive transport requests, follow optimized GPS routes, and ensure compliance with blood safety requirements (cold chain, timing).

    Traceability and Safety: Each blood unit is tagged with a QR code to track its full journey from donor to recipient, ensuring transparency, quality, and safety at every stage.

2. Methodologies and Technologies Used

    Cross-platform mobile and web development: Ensures accessibility for all user profiles (Android, iOS, and desktop web).

    Secure cloud-based database: For real-time storage and access to sensitive data (donations, stocks, patient records) with strong data protection measures.

    QR code/barcode system: For unique identification and traceability of each blood unit across all operations.

    Geolocation and interactive mapping: Optimizes blood transport routes and identifies nearby donors or health centers.

    Smart notification system: Sends alerts to eligible donors based on their blood type and location in case of emergencies.

    Real-time dashboards and analytics: For monitoring stock levels, donation trends, logistics flow, and key performance indicators.

    Regulatory compliance: Aligns with national health standards and best practices in blood safety and handling.

3. Partnerships and Collaboration Models

To ensure its success, e-BLOOD is built on a collaborative model involving multiple key stakeholders:

    Partner Health Facilities: Hospitals, clinics, and blood banks using the platform for operational efficiency.

    Public Health Authorities: For approval, integration into national systems, and compliance with legal and ethical standards.

    Nonprofits and NGOs: Support awareness campaigns and mobilize donor communities, especially in schools, universities, and faith-based groups.

    Medical and logistics transport providers: Ensure secure and rapid transportation of blood under proper conditions.

    Tech partners, incubators, and funders: Provide resources, training, mentorship, and financial support for implementation and scaling.

Implementation location(s): Location(s) of implementation: The e-BLOOD solution has been piloted in the Democratic Republic of Congo, in the city of Kinshasa. The initial testing and deployment phases were carried out in several partner health facilities, including blood transfusion centers and urban and peri-urban hospitals in Kinshasa.
Implementation timeline(s): The e-BLOOD solution was piloted from January 2023 to October 2024. This period covered development, pilot testing, gradual deployment, and performance evaluation phases.
Duration to pilot in a new geography: The estimated duration to pilot the e-BLOOD solution in a new geography is approximately 12 to 18 months. This timeframe includes local adaptation, user training, gradual deployment, as well as monitoring and evaluation to ensure effective and sustainable integration.
SDGs addressed: SDG 3 (Good Health and Well-being);SDG 9 (Industry, Innovation, and Infrastructure);SDG 17 (Partnerships for the Goals);
Desired impact:
Intended Impact of the e-BLOOD Solution
Solution Objectives

    Improve rapid access to compatible blood, vaccines, essential medicines, and laboratory samples, especially in emergency situations.

    Optimize the management, traceability, and safety of biological and medical products throughout the supply chain.

    Strengthen coordination among donors, healthcare facilities, laboratories, and transporters through an integrated digital platform.

    Increase engagement of donors and health actors with targeted notifications and user-friendly interfaces.

    Reduce waste caused by poor stock management and failure to maintain transport conditions, particularly the cold chain.

    Support public health in resource-limited areas by modernizing logistical processes and digitalizing operations.

Key Achievements or Quantifiable Impacts

    Reduction of supply delays for blood products, vaccines, and medicines by 30 to 50% in pilot areas.

    Increase of 25% in the number of regular donors and engaged stakeholders via the platform.

    Decrease of 20% in medical product waste through improved management and secure transport.

    Creation of local jobs in logistics, digital management, and awareness campaigns (estimated 10–20 direct jobs during the pilot phase).

    Contribution to health safety through full traceability, reducing medical errors.

    Positive environmental impact through optimized transport routes, lowering CO₂ emissions related to logistics.
Key technologies:
Key Technologies Used for the e-BLOOD Solution

    Cross-platform mobile and web applications: to facilitate access and interaction for donors, health facilities, and transporters.

    Secure cloud computing: centralized storage and real-time updating of sensitive data with high levels of security and privacy.

    Traceability via QR codes / barcodes: unique identification and tracking of each blood bag, vaccine, medicine, or sample at every stage.

    GPS geolocation and route optimization: real-time tracking of transports and optimization of routes to ensure speed and efficiency.

    Smart notification system: targeted alerts to quickly mobilize donors and stakeholders based on urgent needs.

    Advanced analytics and dashboards: for stock monitoring, logistics performance, and decision support.

    Internet of Things (IoT) integration: sensors to monitor the cold chain during transport of sensitive products.

    Blockchain (planned or in development): to ensure data integrity, transparency, and security throughout the supply chain.

    Artificial Intelligence (AI) (planned): forecasting blood demand and optimizing donor mobilization campaigns through predictive analytics.
Unique Characteristics:
Unique and Differentiating Features of the e-BLOOD Solution

    Complete and Transparent Traceability: Each blood bag, vaccine, medicine, or sample is tracked via QR codes, enabling real-time monitoring of its journey to ensure safety and compliance.

    Integrated Digital Platform: Connects donors, health facilities, laboratories, and transporters in a single ecosystem, enhancing coordination and reducing delays.

    Real-Time Data and Analytics: Provides up-to-date information on stock
Sustainable Change:
Contribution to Sustainable Systemic Change

The e-BLOOD solution acts as a catalyst for deep transformation in the management of blood and medical products. By digitizing and automating the supply chain, it improves transparency, speed, and coordination among all key stakeholders (donors, transfusion centers, hospitals, transporters).

This enhanced organization reduces losses, errors, and stockouts while increasing donor mobilization. By integrating analytical tools and real-time data, e-BLOOD enables proactive decision-making tailored to local needs.

Theory of Change:

    Inputs: Digital technology, user training, strong partnerships.

    Activities: Donor registration, stock management, transport coordination, real-time tracking.

    Immediate Outcomes: Reduced supply delays, improved traceability, increased donations.

    Medium-term Effects: Enhanced quality and safety of transfusions, strengthened capacity of health institutions.

    Long-term Impact: Significant reduction in mortality linked to blood shortages and transfusion errors, establishment of a sustainable, integrated, modern, and resilient system.
Funding Sources: The e-BLOOD solution has been funded during previous development and implementation phases primarily through financial support from the company Orange RDC.
Primary thematic focus area: Inclusive Digital Innovation Skills & Entrepreneurial Talent Development
Summary: The e-BLOOD solution is a pioneering platform designed to bridge the gap in blood donation, transport, and management by connecting donors, healthcare facilities, and transporters in real-time. By providing traceable, transparent, and secure access to blood and medical supplies, e-BLOOD enhances operational efficiency, reduces waste, and supports public health in resource-limited areas. The project is piloting in the Democratic Republic of Congo with significant potential for replication across similar regions.

Title: MariaServeur: Offline Smart Hub for Inclusive Digital Public Services Access
Subtitle: A portable, offline-powered solution delivering education, health, and civic e-services to underserved rural, urban communities in Niger without reliable internet access.
Problem Statement: Millions of people in Niger and other low-connectivity regions face systemic digital exclusion due to inadequate internet infrastructure, prohibitive data costs, and limited access to essential digital public services. These communities are disconnected from online education, health information, administrative services, and economic opportunities, exacerbating existing social and economic inequalities. Current solutions typically require stable internet connections and expensive infrastructure, making them unfeasible in remote, sparsely populated, or underserved areas.
Solution Overview:
MariaServeur is a portable offline digital hub developed in Niger by young Nigerien innovators to ensure equitable and inclusive access to essential digital services in areas with limited or no connectivity. The device functions as a local Wi-Fi hotspot, allowing users to connect via smartphones, tablets, or computers without requiring an internet connection or mobile data.
Once connected, users can access a wide range of digital content and services. These include educational resources such as school curricula, educational videos, textbooks, and coding tutorials; health information and services covering maternal health, sexual and reproductive health, mental health, and prevention; civic services including legal rights, administrative procedures, digital identity information, and alert tools; as well as youth empowerment resources such as training in entrepreneurship, crafts, digital skills, and gender-based violence prevention.
The system operates autonomously using solar power, making it especially suited to the Nigerien context. It can be deployed in schools, health centers, public spaces, or mobile units and can be adapted to meet the specific needs of each community.
MariaServeur is built on a combination of open-source technologies and edge computing principles, allowing content to be hosted and distributed directly from the device. It includes a microserver and locally hosted applications and content such as Moodle for education, Kiwix for offline Wikipedia, NextCloud for file sharing, Kolibri, OpenSIS, FarmOS, among others. The device is powered by a hybrid energy system—solar and electric—with an internal battery that ensures energy autonomy. It is also equipped with mesh networking capabilities, enabling multiple units to be interconnected when needed.
The solution is designed to be modular, cost-effective, energy-efficient, and easy to maintain or update, even in remote areas with limited technical resources.
MariaServeur is developed by Agence Capital Humain (ACH – Niger), with support from the National Agency for the Information Society (ANSI) and the Ministry of Posts, Telecommunications and Digital Economy of Niger, aiming for integration into public services. It also benefits from partnerships with several United Nations agencies ( UNWOMEN, UNICEF, etc...) and NGOs, which provide technical support, thematic content, and training. A community of young developers and local actors is engaged to manage and adapt the solution over the long term.
The deployment model is based on community ownership, open access to content, and a participatory approach to co-developing use cases. This framework ensures the sustainability of the solution and its potential for replication and adaptation in other national and regional contexts.
Solution Provider(s): Agence Capital Humain (ACH Niger): A youth-led social organization driving technological innovation, education, community health, and rural empowerment. ACH is the lead implementer of the MariaServeur solution;  Agence Nationale pour la Société de l’Information (ANSI – Niger): A government agency responsible for digital public services and national ICT strategy. ANSI supports the integration of MariaServeur into public digital policies; Ministry of Posts, Telecommunications and the Digital Economy of Niger: The national authority overseeing digital sector development, providing institutional support for the nationwide adoption of the solution.
Duration to pilot in a new geography: Estimated duration to test the solution in a new geography: The deployment of the Maria Serveur MVP in a new location can be completed within 4 to 6 weeks, including needs assessment, adaptation of digital content, local stakeholder engagement, installation, and user training. This timeline may vary slightly depending on the infrastructure and contextual requirements of the target community.
SDGs addressed: SDG 4 (Quality Education);SDG 9 (Industry, Innovation, and Infrastructure);SDG 10 (Reduced Inequalities);
Desired impact: Maria Serveur aims to reduce the digital divide by ensuring equitable access to essential digital services in rural and urban areas with low connectivity. Its main objectives are to promote digital inclusion, improve access to education, health, and civic services, and empower youth and marginalized communities. Moreover, the solution helps create local employment opportunities through the training and involvement of young technicians and community trainers in underserved areas. Its solar-powered operation also reduces the carbon footprint associated with traditional digital infrastructures.
Key technologies: Maria Serveur relies on open-source technologies combined with edge computing principles to provide an autonomous, offline-accessible digital hub. Key technologies include an embedded micro-server, open-source educational and content management platforms such as Moodle, Kiwix, and NextCloud, a hybrid solar-electric power system with integrated battery, and mesh networks enabling interconnection of multiple units. The solution does not currently use artificial intelligence, blockchain, or IoT but remains modular and open to integrating these technologies as needed in the future.
Unique Characteristics: Maria Serveur stands out for being a portable and autonomous solution, designed and locally manufactured by young Nigeriens, operating offline with a hybrid solar power system. This solution is perfectly suited for rural and urban areas with low connectivity in Niger, providing local access to essential digital services (education, health, civic services, agriculture and livestock, etc.) without the need for internet, making it a major innovation.The model is based on the training and involvement of local young technicians who ensure the maintenance and continuous adaptation of the solution according to the specific needs of Nigerien communities, thereby guaranteeing sustainable ownership.Finally, thanks to strong partnerships with Nigerien government institutions and local stakeholders, Maria Serveur benefits from multisectoral support that facilitates its replication and adaptation in other regions.
Sustainable Change: Maria Serveur contributes to sustainable systemic change by breaking the major barrier of digital exclusion in rural and urban areas with low connectivity in Niger. By providing autonomous and local access to essential services such as education, healthcare, civic services, and more, the solution fosters the social and economic inclusion of often marginalized populations. Its theory of change is based on strengthening local capacities through the continuous training of young technicians and community actors, ensuring long-term ownership and job creation; improving social indicators such as literacy rates, access to healthcare, and civic participation; promoting local innovation through adaptable and scalable technology that encourages further digital initiatives; and supporting community resilience through a digital infrastructure that is independent of unstable Internet connections. Thus, Maria Serveur acts as a catalyst for inclusive and sustainable development, fundamentally transforming the social, economic, and technological dynamics of the communities it serves.
Funding Sources: The solution was funded through personal resources, supplemented by a grant awarded for winning 3rd place during Niger’s Digital Week (SENUM Niger).
Primary thematic focus area: Inclusive Digital Innovation Skills & Entrepreneurial Talent Development
Summary: MariaServeur is an innovative offline digital hub aimed at bridging the digital divide for underserved communities in rural and urban areas of Niger. This solar-powered solution provides access to essential services like education, healthcare, and civic resources, all without needing a stable internet connection. By using open-source technologies and empowering local technicians, MariaServeur ensures sustainable digital inclusion, especially for marginalized populations.
