Title: FOMIPYMES: Driving Innovation and Competitiveness in MSMEs
Subtitle: Building MSME capabilities in Paraguay through technical assistance, innovation, and targeted digitalization to boost competitiveness and inclusive growth.
Problem Statement:
MSMEs are the backbone of the region’s economy—99.5% of firms and ~60% of formal jobs in LAC—yet many in Paraguay struggle to adopt modern technologies and reach demanding markets, limiting productivity and inclusive growth. 

Connectivity has improved (81.3% internet penetration in Jan 2024), but advanced technology uptake in firms remains low. In Paraguay’s industry, 8 in 10 companies still use first/second-generation (low) technologies, and only 17% report adoption of more advanced third/fourth-generation tools (Industry 3.0/4.0). 

Customer-facing digitalization is especially lagging: just ~13% of firms are currently implementing concrete actions in the customer/consumer area, even though 52% report using e-commerce platforms (often basic channels like social networks rather than integrated systems). 

Regulatory and trust gaps also hold back the digital economy: Paraguay lacks a dedicated personal data protection law, which firms and analysts identify as a constraint for e-commerce adoption and consumer trust. 

Business dynamism remains subdued: the density of new limited-liability firms is just 0.05 per 1,000 working-age people, far below peers (e.g., Chile 10.7; Costa Rica 4.7; Peru 4.1), limiting the pipeline of innovative, high-productivity firms. 

These gaps—limited advanced tech adoption, weak customer-facing digitalization, regulatory shortcomings, and low firm creation—translate into concrete sectoral bottlenecks: textiles lack access to 3D design tools and functional materials; dairy value chains need low-cost quality/traceability technologies; and diverse MSMEs require product/packaging upgrades plus light digital activation to compete. FOMIPYMES directly targets these constraints through targeted innovation, quality systems, and selective digitalization.
Solution Overview:
FOMIPYMES is a national MSME-strengthening program that combines technical assistance, innovation, and—where it adds value—digitalization across three complementary verticals:

Textiles – 3D design & functional materials

Hands-on upskilling in VStitcher (Browzwear) for digital prototyping and fit validation.
Co-design and pilot runs using functional Taiwanese fabrics (e.g., antibacterial, UV-protective, performance).
Delivery pathway: diagnostic → skills training → 3D prototypes → supplier linkages → market testing.

Dairy – Quality control & traceability for Paraguayan cheese using IoT
 Deployment of IoT kits (temperature, humidity) and digital logbooks in dairy committees.
 Cloud dashboards with current sensors information from IoT devices, with option to export to PDF.
 Delivery pathway: diagnostic → installation & training → supervised operation → continuous improvement.

Potential Industries / Reinventa – Targeted innovation for MSMEs (8 firms)

Short, focused acceleration cycles to reach problem–solution fit and go-to-market readiness.
Interventions: product co-design, packaging/labeling with QR, light digital activation (WhatsApp Business + CRM, simple e-commerce), and channel development (prescribers, gourmet/specialty retail).
Current cohort: Dog Apettit (functional pet snacks), Don Virgilio (flavored hot sauces + gift kit), La Dominica (inulin-based healthy snack), LapataPY (breastfeeding gift kit with QR learning), Sabrosur – Fina la Casera (Paraguayan-cheese sticks), Tujugui (cultural ceramics with 3D/laser molds), Upita Portabebés (hybrid Mei Tai carrier), Desde Casa (hybrid culinary learning + AI assistant).


Methodologies & technologies
Methodologies: competency-based training, learning-by-doing, Human-Centered Design, Lean Startup, and Train-the-Trainer (ToT) embedded within the Vice-Ministry’s extension services.
Technologies: VStitcher / 3D garment simulation; IoT sensors and open protocols (e.g., MQTT) with cloud dashboards; LMS for modular content; AI assistant for routine queries; WhatsApp Business + CRM integrations and low-code automations; QR-linked micro-content (usage, nutrition, stories); 3D printing/laser for molds; digital pattern making; packaging engineering.


Partnerships & collaboration model
Public–public: Ministry of Industry & Commerce (Vice-Ministry of MSMEs) with the Government of Taiwan / TaiwanICDF for technical cooperation, co-funding, and knowledge transfer.
Public–private / ecosystem: Taiwanese Textile Federation (materials/tech transfer); dairy committees/co-ops; local IoT integrators; universities/labs (testing & QA); NGOs and development partners; finance cooperatives; specialty retailers and prescriber networks (clinics, consultants, chefs/influencers).

Operating model: joint diagnostics and roadmaps; co-financing and in-kind contributions; shared M&E (KPIs on adoption, quality, sales, inclusion); ToT to institutionalize capabilities inside the Vice-Ministry for scale-up across regions.

Name of your organization: Alliance for Education and Gender Protection-Sierra Leone
Title: Digital Innovate Hub
Subtitle: A solar-powered, community run tech hub providing digital skills and offline e-learning to underserved youth, students and teachers in Sierra Leone.
Problem Statement: In Sierra Leone, over 70% of the population lacks basic digital literacy and 98% of schools have no access to computers or internet. This digital exclusion limits access to education, reduces employment opportunities, and deepens poverty and inequality. Graduates often leave tertiary institutions without the digital skills needed for today’s job market. Marginalized groups especially rural youth, women and out-of-school children are most affected. Without targeted intervention, this growing digital divide will continue to hinder socio-economic development, innovation and youth empowerment in the country.
Solution Overview:
The Digital Innovate Hub is a scalable, solar-powered, community-centered facility that bridges the digital divide in underserved regions of Sierra Leone by providing access to digital education, tools and infrastructure. Housed in repurposed shipping containers, each hub is equipped with 20–30 installed computers, high-speed Starlink internet, printers, laminators, televisions, and a proprietary offline mobile application that hosts curated digital literacy curricula, e-learning resources, and entrepreneurship modules. 


How it works:
-Hubs are deployed in rural or underserved communities through site assessments, stakeholder engagement and local partnerships.
-Local facilitators are trained using a “train-the-trainer” model to deliver structured digital literacy and entrepreneurship training.
-Teachers receive certified ICT pedagogy training aligned with national curricula.
-Out-of-school youth and students access free foundational digital skills training and use offline learning tools even in connectivity-poor areas.
-Low-cost services such as printing and laminating generate revenue to sustain operations.
-Youth entrepreneurship is fostered through incubation programs, including mentorship, prototyping support, and innovation labs.

Methodologies & Technologies:
-Offline Mobile Application: Contains downloadable educational content compatible with low-end smartphones.
-Solar Energy System: Provides reliable 24/7 electricity in grid-unstable areas.
-Starlink Internet: Ensures high-speed connectivity in remote locations.
-Monitoring & Evaluation Tools: Used to assess impact through surveys and digital skill progression tracking.

Partnerships & Collaboration Models:
-Community ownership is key, each hub is managed by local committees trained in basic maintenance and operations.
-Public-private partnerships support sustainability and scale including collaboration with NGOs, education authorities, and local councils.
-The Ministry of Education provides technical input on curriculum alignment and co-certifies teacher training programs.
-The University of Sierra Leone and Educub provide academic and technological expertise for hub deployment and content development.

https://youtu.be/i_YUbAgZuyo
Solution Provider(s): Alliance for Education and Gender Protection (non-profit, youth-led education and gender equity organization), Educub (education technology organization specializing in digital learning infrastructure), Ministry of Basic and Senior Secondary Education – Sierra Leone (government, education sector), University of Sierra Leone (public tertiary institution – higher education and teacher training), Local Government Councils and Community Leadership Bodies (public sector – local governance and development), NGOs like )Plan International, Unicef) and the Ministry of Technology and Innovation
Implementation location(s): Koidu City, Kono District, Eastern Province, Sierra Leone (With plans to expand to other rural areas including Torwama, Bo Distric
Implementation timeline(s): Start Date: January 2024 Pilot Launch: April 2024 Ongoing Implementation: April 2024 – Present
Duration to pilot in a new geography: 8–10 weeks (from site selection and stakeholder engagement to full infrastructure deployment and training rollout)
SDGs addressed: SDG 8 (Decent Work and Economic Growth);SDG 9 (Industry, Innovation, and Infrastructure);SDG 4 (Quality Education);
Desired impact:
Solution Objectives:
-Bridge the digital divide in Sierra Leone by providing equitable access to digital learning, tools  and internet.
-Improve digital literacy, entrepreneurial capacity, and employability among underserved youth, women, and teachers.
-Create sustainable community-based hubs that foster education, innovation, and income generation.

Key Achievements/Impacts (so far):
-Over 2,000 beneficiaries (in-school students, out-of-school youth, and teachers) impacted since 2024.
-88% of students reported improved digital literacy within 6 months. (Report from our six months ago survey)
-72% of teachers adopted digital tools for classroom instruction.
-93% of users reported greater confidence in using technology for learning and daily life.
-Hub generates 40% of its operational cost via small service fees from printing, laminating and photocopying.
-Enabled local youth to begin tech-based and social innovation projects.
-Empowered teachers to align with modern, ICT-driven curricula.
-Economic Inclusion: from the sstartups incubated; $300 month revenue from printing/laminating services
Key technologies:
-Solar Energy System: Powers all infrastructure in off-grid or energy-poor regions, ensuring 24/7 access.
-Hardware: Repurposed shipping containers; energy-efficient computers/printers.
-High-Speed Satellite Internet (Starlink): Delivers reliable internet connectivity in remote areas.
-Offline Mobile Application: Hosts digital literacy tutorials, national curriculum-aligned learning content, and can be accessed without internet. Syncs when connected to hub Wi-Fi.
-Educational Televisions and Installed Computers: Provide interactive learning experiences and ICT training.
-Monitoring Tools: Data is collected from usage patterns and surveys for continuous improvement and reporting.
Unique Characteristics:
-Shipping Container Model: Modular, mobile and easily deployed even in hard-to-reach rural areas.
-Community Ownership Model: Each hub is maintained and partially operated by trained local committees, ensuring sustainability and buy-in.
-Train-the-Trainer Approach: Builds local capacity and accelerates scale without heavy external staffing.
-Public-Private-Academic Partnership: Collaboration with the Ministry of Education, local governments, Educub, and the University of Sierra Leone ensures alignment with national priorities and educational needs.
-Financial Sustainability Mechanism: Small user fees from printing/laminating services offset operational costs.
-Offline Access to Learning: Proprietary app allows users to download resources and track learning progress even without constant internet access.
Ecosystem Design: Bundles education (SDG 4), entrepreneurship (SDG 8) and green tech (SDG 13) in one hub.
Sustainable Change:
Theory of Change:
By decentralizing digital education infrastructure and embedding it within underserved communities, the Digital Innovate Hub empowers individuals with lifelong digital skills that open pathways to jobs, entrepreneurship, and innovation. This community-rooted model ensures inclusivity, relevance, and resilience.

Systemic Change Outcomes:
-Education Reform Support: Supports national efforts to embed ICT into school curricula and improve teaching standards.
-Workforce Development: Builds foundational digital and entrepreneurial skills among youth, preparing them for future digital jobs.
-Economic Inclusion: Reduces barriers to technology and creates local opportunities for self-employment and business creation.
-Community Resilience: Solar-powered, offline-ready, and community-owned—each hub becomes a long-term asset for digital resilience.
-Replication & Policy Integration: The model is designed to be scaled nationally through government and NGO partnerships, feeding into digital education strategies

-Revenue generated from service fees (printing, laminating, and photocopying) which currently cover up to 40% of operational costs.
-Future scale-up is being designed through public-private partnerships and institutional collaborations with the Ministry of Education, University of Sierra Leone, and potential donor agencies.

Summary: The Digital Innovate Hub provides solar-powered, community-run tech hubs in Sierra Leone offering digital literacy, e-learning, and entrepreneurship training. A strength is the strong multi-stakeholder model (government, university, NGOs) and measurable pilot impacts (2,000+ beneficiaries, 88% literacy gains), while a weakness is its pilot stage and limited long-term financial runway beyond partial cost recovery.

Title: Climate Tech Girls – Empowering Rural Girls with STEM for Climate Resilience
Subtitle: ClimateTechGirls empowers rural Sri Lankan girls (12–17) with STEM skills to tackle climate issues via coding, IoT, and sensors, bridging the digital gender divide and building climate resilience.
Problem Statement: Rural girls in Sri Lanka face multiple barriers to participating in the digital economy, including limited access to technology, gendered social norms, and inadequate STEM education. These challenges are further compounded in climate-vulnerable districts where environmental hazards such as droughts, floods, and changing weather patterns threaten livelihoods and community resilience. Despite their potential, girls are underrepresented in climate innovation and lack opportunities to develop the skills needed for meaningful participation in the green and digital economy. Schools in these regions often lack trained educators, digital infrastructure, and gender-responsive learning approaches. As a result, rural girls are excluded from digital empowerment and climate action processes. ClimateTechGirls addresses these gaps by equipping girls with practical digital and environmental skills, enabling them to become problem-solvers, innovators, and community leaders.
Solution Overview:
ClimateTechGirls is a structured digital inclusion and climate education program that empowers rural girls aged 12–17 through after-school STEM innovation sessions. The program operates in climate-affected districts, Puttalam, Anuradhapura, Monaragala, Hambantota, and Nuwara Eliya, using a locally contextualised, gender-sensitive curriculum.

Girls engage in hands-on learning using Scratch for coding and storytelling, Micro:bit for sensing and logic-based problem solving, and Arduino for environmental monitoring and building smart prototypes (e.g., soil moisture alerts, air quality sensors, and renewable energy trackers). The curriculum includes climate literacy, renewable energy, IoT, and digital storytelling modules, delivered over 32 weeks through community ICT hubs and school-based learning spaces.

The program is co-designed and implemented with local teachers, ICT educators, agriculture and environment instructors, and community-based organisations, ensuring relevance, inclusion, and sustainability. Teachers undergo focused training in digital pedagogy and STEM facilitation to support long-term implementation.

Collaborations with schools, local authorities, and national education and environment stakeholders help embed the solution within existing educational structures. Peer-to-peer learning and community exhibitions foster visibility and inspire other girls to participate, creating a grassroots movement for inclusive digital and climate innovation.
Solution Provider(s): Shilpa Sayura Foundation: A non-profit NGO based in Sri Lanka working at the intersection of education environment and technology. Recognised with global awards for empowering youth and rural communities through digital innovation, APVN (Asia Philanthropy Venture Network): A regional network of social investors focused on closing SDG gaps through strategic partnerships and funding for impactful initiatives, LESG Foundation: A donor organisation committed to supporting youth education and future-ready skills development in underserved regions, Nextgen Interactive (Pvt) Ltd: A technology services company supporting digital infrastructure and services development,  Local Schools: Public schools from project areas that host and co-implement the ClimateTechGirls program, Local ICT Education Service Providers: Community-based organisations and ICT centres delivering hands-on digital training and infrastructure support in rural areas,
Implementation location(s): Implemented in Puttalam, Anuradhapura, Monaragala, Hambantota, and Nuwara Eliya districts of Sri Lanka.
Duration to pilot in a new geography: 1 Year
SDGs addressed: SDG 4 (Quality Education);SDG 5 (Gender Equality);SDG 13 (Climate Action);
Desired impact:
ClimateTechGirls aims to empower 1,000 rural girls with digital and climate innovation skills by 2026, while building the capacity of 100 teachers to deliver gender-responsive STEM education. The solution fosters girl-led climate innovations such as smart farming tools and environmental sensors, promoting green skills and community resilience.
To date, over 300 girls and 30 teachers have been trained across 5 districts, and many tech-based projects have been developed. The program boosts STEM interest and confidence among marginalised girls and contributes to inclusive digital transformation. Long-term, it supports green employment, local innovation ecosystems, and community-driven climate action aligned with SDGs 4, 5, 9, 10, 13, and 17.
Key technologies:
Key Technologies Used
ClimateTechGirls integrates accessible and impactful technologies to enable hands-on learning and climate innovation:
Scratch: A block-based coding platform used to teach foundational programming, storytelling, and digital creativity in local languages.


Micro:bit: A microcontroller used for climate sensing, logic-based computing, and building interactive prototypes such as temperature or soil moisture monitors.


Arduino: An open-source IoT platform that enables girls to create environmental monitoring systems, smart irrigation, and renewable energy trackers.


Internet of Things (IoT): Utilised through Arduino and Micro:bit to connect sensors and build real-time, data-driven climate solutions.


Mobile and Cloud Tools: Used to access learning content, share projects, and collaborate remotely in resource-limited environments.


Artificial intelligence: Using AI tools for weather and hazard prediction to support sustainable agriculture and food production.
These low-cost, high-impact and scalable technologies allow girls to prototype real-world solutions, build digital fluency, and engage in the digital economy while addressing local climate challenges.
Unique Characteristics:
ClimateTechGirls stands out by combining climate resilience, gender empowerment, and digital inclusion through a community-rooted, low-cost, and scalable model. Unlike traditional STEM programs, it is: 

Locally Co-Designed: Developed with teachers, ICT centres, and community partners to ensure cultural relevance, gender sensitivity, and practical application in rural Sri Lankan contexts.

Integrated with Climate Action: Focuses not just on digital skills but on using technology to solve real environmental challenges faced by girls’ communities.

Blended Delivery Model: Combines after-school hands-on sessions, teacher training, and mobile/cloud-based learning, making it accessible in low-resource settings.

Multi-Sector Partnerships: Engages NGOs, schools, donor foundations, tech firms, and local government to ensure sustainability and broad impact.

Youth Innovation Pipeline: Encourages girls to move from learning to prototyping and leadership, enabling future participation in green entrepreneurship, education, and MSMEs.

By embedding innovation into rural education ecosystems, ClimateTechGirls creates long-term value and inclusion where it’s most needed.
Sustainable Change:
ClimateTechGirls contributes to long-term, systemic change by transforming how rural communities engage with digital technology, climate resilience, and girls’ empowerment. The program applies a Theory of Change built on access, capacity, agency, and integration:

Access and Inclusion
By introducing digital tools and climate education through local schools and ICT centres, the program ensures that rural girls, often excluded, gain access to future-focused learning opportunities.

Capacity and Continuity
Training teachers in digital pedagogy and climate tech builds school-level capacity, ensuring the solution is sustained and expanded beyond the initial program. Local ownership is central to the model.


Empowerment and Innovation
Girls become not just users but creators of technology, building real solutions for their communities. This shifts gender norms and fosters a generation of confident, climate-aware innovators.

Community Ripple Effect
Student projects, exhibitions, and local media coverage inspire peers, parents, and policymakers, catalysing broader interest and support for inclusive digital learning.


Policy and Systems Integration
Engagement with ministries and school networks aims to embed the model into national curricula, ensuring scale and policy alignment for systemic transformation.

Title: IRMS: Bridging Africa’s Digital Divide in Public Finance
Subtitle: A digital revenue management system empowering African cities to mobilize resources, boost transparency, and deliver inclusive public services for sustainable local development.
Problem Statement: Many local governments in Africa still rely on manual, paper-based revenue collection systems that are prone to fraud, inefficiency, and poor data management. This undermines their ability to raise sufficient funds for essential services, resulting in service delivery gaps, reduced public trust, and limited local development. These challenges disproportionately affect vulnerable populations, including women, informal traders, and rural communities, who face barriers to accessing fair, transparent, and efficient government services. The absence of digital infrastructure at the subnational level also widens the digital economic divide and hinders inclusive, data-driven governance.
Solution Overview: Levetot is a mobile-first, cloud-based revenue management system that digitizes how African county governments collect and manage local revenue. It supports mobile money payments, offline functionality, and real-time analytics for better governance. Built using human-centered design and agile methods, Levetot partners with local governments, mobile operators, and researchers to deliver scalable, inclusive, and transparent digital public finance solutions.
Solution Provider(s): Safaricom PLC,
Duration to pilot in a new geography: 6 - Months
SDGs addressed: SDG 9 (Industry, Innovation, and Infrastructure);SDG 8 (Decent Work and Economic Growth);SDG 10 (Reduced Inequalities);
Desired impact:
Solution Objectives
Levetot seeks to modernize local government revenue collection by digitizing processes, reducing leakages, and promoting transparency. It empowers African counties to sustainably mobilize Own Source Revenue (OSR) for better service delivery and long-term development. The solution also promotes inclusive access to government services, enabling broader economic participation, especially among women and informal traders.
Key Achievements & Impacts
Counties using Levetot have recorded OSR increases of 15–38% within one year due to better compliance and automation. Over 15,000 informal traders have been digitally onboarded, with 60% being women now receiving transparent services and protection from informal fees. The system has created over 40 direct jobs, reduced permit processing times to under 24 hours, and contributed to institutional capacity and paperless governance.

Kakamega's diverse network coverage 
● Offline Transaction Processing: Essential for revenue collection in remote areas like 
Likuyani's mining regions 
● Automatic Synchronization: Seamlessly updates the central system when connectivity 
returns 
● Multi-language Support: USSD menus in Kiswahili and local languages for broader 
accessibility 
● Location-specific Offline Modes: Customized for different sub-county connectivity 
patterns 
● Encrypted Local Storage: Secure transaction storage during offline periods
Live interaction capabilities and AI-powered chatbots provide round-the-clock support in 
multiple languages.
Unique Characteristics:
Levetot is optimized for low-infrastructure environments, offering offline functionality, seamless mobile money integration, and user interfaces accessible to both clerks and informal traders. Its participatory, human-centered deployment model that ensures rapid adoption, institutional ownership, and sustainability. 
Levetot’s performance-based SaaS model is financially inclusive, allowing counties to scale based on realized revenue gains rather than fixed licensing fees, which lowers barriers to digital transformation. It incorporates real-time analytics for improved transparency, accountability, and fiscal planning, directly enhancing local government capacity to respond to risk and deliver essential services. 
Its gender-inclusive architecture prioritizes usability for women, who dominate informal economies yet remain marginalized in formal public finance systems, thereby fostering equitable access and inclusive growth. This holistic integration of civic technology, adaptive financing, and inclusive design positions Levetot as a pioneering solution for building resilient, data-driven local governance systems aligned with the Sustainable Development Goals.
Sustainable Change:
Systemic change is managed by digitizing and decentralizing revenue collection for local governments, enabling them to generate more Own Source Revenue (OSR) transparently and efficiently. This strengthens institutional capacity, reduces financial leakage, and allows for better service delivery and public investment at the grassroots level. The desired follow-on effects include increased citizen trust, equitable access to services, formalization of the informal economy, and improved fiscal autonomy of counties. 
As county governments become more self-reliant and accountable, they are better equipped to respond to social, economic, and environmental challenges. This creates a reinforcing cycle where inclusive civic technology fosters stronger institutions, leading to long-term improvements in governance, public finance, and development outcomes aligned with the Sustainable Development Goals. Levetot’s scalable model encourages policy adoption at regional and national levels, laying the foundation for broader public sector reform across the continent.

Summary: IRMS (Levetot) is a mobile-first, cloud-based revenue management system digitizing local government revenue collection in Africa. It integrates mobile money, offline transaction processing, USSD, and multilingual support to enhance inclusivity, efficiency, and transparency. Implemented at scale in counties like Kericho, it has increased Own Source Revenue by 15–38%, onboarded thousands of informal traders (60% women), reduced permit processing times, and created jobs. Its SaaS model scales with county revenue gains, lowering barriers to adoption while strengthening local government capacity for inclusive and transparent governance.

Title: DigiHer+: Empowering Girls with Digital Skills, Menstrual Health & GBV Support
Subtitle: A transformative solution that equips underserved girls in Nigeria with digital skills, menstrual health support, and protection against gender-based violence using AI and community-led models.
Problem Statement: In Nigeria, especially in underserved slum communities, adolescent girls and young women face multiple barriers to inclusion. These include lack of access to digital skills and tools, limited or no menstrual health education and resources, and exposure to gender-based violence (GBV) with little or no support systems. These challenges reinforce poverty, school dropouts, and vulnerability to abuse, preventing girls from reaching their full potential and contributing to the economy. There is an urgent need for a holistic, tech-driven, and community-rooted approach to address this triple exclusion.
Solution Overview:
DigiHer+ is a hybrid, community-driven digital empowerment program targeting adolescent girls and young women in underserved Nigerian communities. It aims to bridge the digital divide, promote menstrual health, and reduce gender-based violence (GBV) through accessible and inclusive technologies.

How the Solution Works:

1. AI-Powered Support (via WhatsApp & USSD):
Girls interact with a multilingual chatbot (powered by OpenAI) that delivers digital skills lessons, menstrual health education, and GBV awareness. It also provides psychosocial support and links to local services.

2. Community Safe Hubs:
Safe spaces within communities offer in-person support including digital literacy bootcamps, menstrual hygiene kit distribution, GBV counseling, and peer mentorship.

3. Outreach & Accessibility:
For girls without smartphones or internet, information is shared via radio programs, posters, and SMS/USSD-based engagement, ensuring no one is left out.


Methodologies & Technologies Used:

OpenAI language tools for personalized digital education and chatbot support.

USSD/WhatsApp integration to reach girls with or without smartphones.

Peer-led training for sustainability and trust-building.

Design Thinking & Human-Centered Design to develop content based on real community feedback.

Offline-first strategy using radio, local facilitators, and printed materials to bridge tech gaps.


Partnership & Collaboration Models:

Naomi Helping Hands International Foundation (NHHIF) leads implementation.

Local CSOs, youth groups, and health workers serve as safe hub facilitators and mentors.

Tech experts and volunteers develop and maintain the chatbot and training content.

Women’s health alliances, midwives, and psychologists provide menstrual health and GBV counseling.

OpenAI & EdTech partners support content design and digital curriculum.

Community leaders and schools ensure local acceptance and reach.

Ministry of Women Affairs, Nigeria – The federal government ministry responsible for promoting women’s rights, gender equality, and social welfare programs nationwide.  Women’s Health Alliance Nigeria – A coalition of NGOs focused on advancing menstrual health, reproductive rights, and gender-based violence prevention.  OpenAI – A global leader in artificial intelligence providing advanced AI tools, including language models to power chatbots and digital learning platforms.  EdTech Lagos Network – A consortium of educational technology startups and experts supporting digital skills development and innovative learning solutions. Title: Jitoleze Digital Pathways
Subtitle: Bridging Digital Divides for Youth, Women, and MSMEs in Africa
Problem Statement:
Digital transformation is reshaping economies worldwide, but rural communities, women, and young people in Sub-Saharan Africa remain digitally excluded. Limited access to skills, mentorship, and market opportunities keeps millions trapped in cycles of unemployment and poverty.

In Uganda, youth unemployment remains above 60%, and micro, small, and medium enterprises (MSMEs), which form 90% of businesses, struggle to digitise operations and access competitive markets. Women, who are central to household and community economies, are disproportionately affected by this digital divide.

Without inclusive digital solutions, these groups risk being left behind in the global economy.
Solution Overview:
Jitoleze Digital Pathways is a mobile-first, low-bandwidth platform designed to empower youth, women, and MSMEs in underserved communities by connecting them to skills, mentors, and markets.

E-Learning Hub: Delivers short, practical micro-courses (5–15 minutes) on digital literacy, entrepreneurship, vocational skills, and financial management, designed for low-literacy and rural contexts.

Mentorship Circles: Facilitates virtual mentorship and peer-to-peer learning via moderated groups on WhatsApp, SMS, and in-platform video sessions, connecting participants to local and global professionals.

MSME Digital Marketplace: Provides small businesses with a digital storefront where they can showcase products/services, connect with suppliers, access financial literacy tools, and explore micro-financing options.

Offline Access: Key learning modules are accessible via USSD and SMS, ensuring inclusion for those with limited internet connectivity.

Methodologies & Technologies Used
Human-Centred Design: Co-created with youth, women, and MSMEs to ensure cultural relevance, usability, and accessibility.

Mobile-First Architecture: Optimized for low-data environments, with progressive web app technology and USSD/SMS integration for feature-phone users.

Gamification & Micro-Learning: Uses interactive, bite-sized content with badges and progress tracking to enhance engagement and completion rates.

Data-Driven Insights: Built-in analytics dashboard to monitor user engagement, learning progress, and marketplace activity, guiding continuous improvement.

Integration with Financial & Educational APIs: Partnerships with fintech platforms and educational content providers to expand offerings.

Partnerships & Collaboration Models
Jitoleze Digital Pathways is designed to scale through multi-stakeholder collaboration:

Local Governments & Communities: Aligning with national digital inclusion and youth employment strategies for broader adoption.

Private Sector & Fintechs: Collaborating with mobile network operators, microfinance institutions, and tech companies to integrate mobile payments, provide affordable devices, and enhance service delivery.

Development Partners & UN Agencies: Working with UNIDO, UNCTAD, UNDP, and others to influence policy frameworks and scale digital inclusion programs.

Academic & Training Institutions: Partnering with universities, vocational institutes, and e-learning content providers for high-quality curriculum development.
Solution Provider(s): Jitoleze Foundation (Nonprofit Sector): A Ugandan community-based organization focused on youth empowerment, women’s economic inclusion, and skills development through grassroots programs and digital innovations.  Busia Area Communities Federation (Community Development Sector): A coalition supporting grassroots mobilization and capacity building for marginalized groups in Eastern Uganda.  Local Government of Busia District (Public Sector): Partnering to align Jitoleze Digital Pathways with national youth employment, digital inclusion, and MSME development strategies.  MTN Uganda (Private Sector – Telecommunications): Supporting USSD and mobile integration to reach rural users with limited internet connectivity.  Centenary Bank (Private Sector – Financial Services): Providing financial literacy tools, micro-credit linkages, and digital banking integration for MSMEs and women entrepreneurs.  ChildFund International (Development Partner): Supporting capacity building and content co-creation for youth and women-focused training modules.  Makerere University Business School (Academic Sector): Co-developing curriculum and entrepreneurship content for the e-learning platform.
Duration to pilot in a new geography: Estimated Timeframe: 6–9 months  Breakdown:  Needs Assessment & Stakeholder Engagement (1–2 months): Conduct baseline studies, identify local challenges, and co-create with communities, local governments, and potential partners.  Localization & Platform Adaptation (2–3 months): Customize the platform content (languages, cultural context), integrate local financial and educational partners, and establish mentorship networks.  Capacity Building & Onboarding (1–2 months): Train local facilitators, onboard MSMEs, and recruit mentors for youth and women participants.  Pilot Rollout & Monitoring (2 months): Launch the solution with an initial cohort (1,000–2,000 users) and implement ongoing monitoring and feedback collection.
SDGs addressed: SDG 4 (Quality Education);SDG 5 (Gender Equality);SDG 8 (Decent Work and Economic Growth);
Desired impact:
Empower Youth & Women: Provide accessible digital literacy and entrepreneurship training for at least 10,000 youth and women in underserved communities.

Strengthen MSMEs: Digitize 5,000 small businesses by providing them with tools to access new markets, financial services, and mentorship networks.

Foster Inclusive Digital Transformation: Bridge the rural-urban digital divide by making learning, mentorship, and market access possible even in low-connectivity areas.

Influence Policy: Contribute to the development of inclusive digital strategies at local, national, and regional levels.

Key Achievements / Expected Impacts
By the end of Year 2 of implementation:

Employment Generation: At least 3,000 youth and women gain sustainable employment or start small businesses after training.

Income Growth: Average income increase of 40% for MSMEs and participants who use the marketplace and digital skills acquired.

Business Digitization: 5,000 MSMEs onboarded to the digital marketplace, improving visibility, transactions, and growth potential.

Gender Inclusion: At least 60% of platform users will be women, ensuring gender-responsive digital inclusion.

Community Reach: Indirectly benefit over 50,000 community members through knowledge transfer, employment opportunities, and economic activities.
Key technologies:

Built using Progressive Web App (PWA) architecture to ensure smooth access on low-cost smartphones and offline capabilities for remote areas.

USSD & SMS Integration to reach users with basic feature phones, ensuring full inclusion for rural communities with limited internet access.

E-Learning & Micro-Learning Technology:

Gamified learning modules (short, interactive courses with badges and progress tracking).

Content Management System (CMS) for easy localization and continuous content updates.

Data Analytics & Dashboards:

Real-time analytics to monitor user progress, course completion, mentorship interactions, and marketplace activities.

Scalable & Replicable:

Title: AVECPLUS – Digitizing Community Savings Groups for Financial Inclusion
Subtitle: AVEC+ enables community savings groups to manage savings, loans, and repayments digitally.
Problem Statement: In the Democratic Republic of Congo (DRC), many urban and rural community savings groups (AVECs) still rely on paper-based systems to manage their financial operations, including savings, loans, and deposits. This lack of digital infrastructure makes record-keeping fragile and highly vulnerable to disasters or loss. For example, in 2020, severe floods in Uvira destroyed many AVEC members' notebooks and records, disrupting all group operations. A similar event occurred in April 2025 in Kinshasa, where floods again caused the loss of critical paper-based financial documents. These incidents highlight a recurring challenge: the absence of reliable and secure digital systems to ensure data continuity, transparency, and accountability. As a result, groups struggle to recover, rebuild trust, and maintain access to financial support mechanisms. AVECPLUS directly addresses this problem by providing a digital, resilient, and user-friendly tool for community savings management.
Solution Overview:
AVECPLUS is a user-friendly digital platform designed to modernize the management of Associations Villageoises d’Épargne et de Crédit (AVEC) in both rural and urban communities of the DRC. The solution enables AVEC members to securely record and monitor financial operations such as savings, loan disbursements, repayments, and deposits through a mobile and web-based application.

How it works:

Members or group managers can input transactions directly into the app using smartphones or tablets.

The app supports offline mode, allowing users to operate without constant internet connectivity; data syncs automatically when a connection is available.

The platform provides automatic generation of financial reports and reminders for repayments or meetings, increasing transparency and accountability.

A simple, icon-driven interface caters to users with low literacy levels, and the app supports multiple local languages.

Security features include encrypted data storage and user authentication to protect sensitive financial information.

Methodologies and Technologies:

Built using a progressive web app (PWA) architecture for cross-platform accessibility (Android, iOS, and desktop browsers).

Offline-first design ensures usability in low-connectivity areas.

Use of lightweight databases (e.g., SQLite) for local data storage and synchronization with cloud servers (AWS or Azure).

Developed following a human-centered design approach, involving AVEC members in iterative feedback and testing phases.

Partnerships and Collaboration Models:

Collaborations with local NGOs and community-based organizations facilitate deployment, user training, and ongoing support.

Engagement with local authorities and microfinance institutions to promote acceptance and scaling of the platform.

Potential partnerships with telecom providers to optimize connectivity and mobile data access.

Open invitation to academic institutions for impact research and technical improvements.
Solution Provider(s): New Vision in the World (local NGO supporting community savings initiatives, Community Development), LIZADEEL (organization promoting economic inclusion of vulnerable populations, Social and Solidarity Economy), AFEVEDDI (women-led NGO focused on female entrepreneurship and empowerment, Gender and Entrepreneurship), EMERGENCE (organization active in entrepreneurship and inclusive microfinance, Economic Empowerment), MAMICRE (microcredit enterprise supporting small-scale lending in underserved communities, Microfinance sector)
Duration to pilot in a new geography: Estimated duration: 3 to 4 months  This timeframe includes identifying local AVEC groups, onboarding and training users, configuring the digital platform to local needs, piloting financial operations in real-life conditions, and gathering feedback to improve the system before a full-scale rollout.
SDGs addressed: SDG 1 (No Poverty);SDG 5 (Gender Equality);SDG 8 (Decent Work and Economic Growth);
Desired impact:
Solution Objectives:

To digitally empower community savings groups (AVEC) by providing a reliable, transparent, and accessible tool for managing savings, loans, and repayments.

To increase financial inclusion for rural and urban underserved populations, especially women and youth.

To strengthen the sustainability and autonomy of AVECs by improving record-keeping and accountability.

To create a scalable model for community-based financial management that can be replicated across regions.

Key Achievements and Impacts (expected):

Enhanced transparency and trust within AVEC groups, reducing conflicts and financial mismanagement.

Increased participation of women and youth in financial activities and decision-making.

Facilitation of at least 300 AVEC groups’ transition from paper-based to digital management within the first year of deployment.

Potential to improve income security and reduce poverty for over 5,000 community members through better-managed credit and savings.

Creation of local employment opportunities through training and support roles linked to the digital platform.

Contribution to the achievement of SDGs 1, 5, and 8 by addressing poverty, gender equality, and economic growth.
Key technologies:
AVECPLUS leverages modern but accessible digital technologies designed for low-resource environments:

Progressive Web Application (PWA) technology for cross-platform compatibility (Android, iOS, desktop browsers), enabling easy access without installation.

Offline-first architecture, allowing users to operate the app without continuous internet connectivity; data syncs automatically when a connection is available.

Local data storage using lightweight databases (e.g., SQLite) on devices to ensure data persistence and fast access.

Secure user authentication and data encryption to protect sensitive financial information and maintain privacy.

Human-centered design principles to create an intuitive interface with icon-based navigation, suitable for users with low literacy levels.

Potential for future integration with mobile money platforms and SMS/USSD services to enhance financial transactions and notifications.
Unique Characteristics:
Unique/Differentiated Characteristics of AVECPLUS
Offline-first design ensures usability in rural and low-connectivity areas, addressing a key barrier to digital inclusion often overlooked by other solutions.

User-friendly interface with icon-driven navigation tailored for users with low literacy and limited digital skills, making it highly accessible to marginalized populations such as women and youth.

Community-centered approach, empowering local savings groups to self-manage their finances transparently, fostering trust and social cohesion.

Scalable and adaptable model that can be customized to different community sizes and contexts without heavy infrastructure investment.

Strong partnership network with local NGOs, women’s organizations, and youth groups, ensuring culturally relevant deployment and sustained support.

Focus on financial empowerment rather than only technology, integrating capacity-building and community ownership as core pillars of the solution.
Sustainable Change:
Contribution of AVECPLUS to Sustainable, Systemic Change
AVECPLUS aims to catalyze lasting transformation in community financial management by:

Building digital capacity and financial literacy within underserved populations, especially women and youth, enabling them to take control of their economic futures.

Replacing fragile paper-based systems with resilient digital tools, reducing data loss and improving transparency, which strengthens trust and cohesion within AVEC groups.

Facilitating reliable record-keeping and accountability, which improves the groups’ credibility and opens pathways for accessing formal financial services and external funding.

Creating a replicable and scalable model that local NGOs and authorities can adopt across regions, promoting widespread digital inclusion.

Empowering communities economically, which contributes to poverty reduction, gender equality, and sustainable local economic development.

Theory of Change:
If AVECPLUS is deployed with strong community engagement and training, then AVEC groups will gain reliable tools to manage finances, leading to increased transparency and trust. This improved management will empower members to grow their savings and access credit more confidently, boosting local entrepreneurship and resilience. Over time, this systemic shift will foster economic inclusion and reduce inequalities, supporting broader development goals.

Additional support and guidance have been provided by FAO as part of their broader community financial inclusion programs, although direct funding for AVECPLUS development is still being sought.
Testimonials and Endorsements: Currently, AVECPLUS is at the pilot-ready stage and has not yet been widely deployed; therefore, formal testimonials from stakeholders or beneficiaries are not yet available. However, preliminary feedback from partner organizations such as New Vision in the World and LIZADEEL has been very positive regarding the potential impact and usability of the solution. Further comments/feedback: Thank you for the opportunity to participate in this important call. The questionnaire is clear and comprehensive, allowing us to present the AVECPLUS solution effectively. We appreciate UNIDO and partners’ efforts to promote inclusive digital economy solutions that can create real impact for underserved communities. We look forward to potential collaboration and support to scale AVECPLUS for greater financial inclusion.

Summary: AVECPLUS is a mobile/web-based platform digitizing community savings groups (AVEC) in the DRC. It replaces fragile paper-based records with a secure, offline-capable system to manage savings, loans, and repayments. Designed with icon-driven navigation and local language support, it increases transparency, resilience, and financial inclusion, particularly for women and youth.

Title: EmpowerNet: AI‑Driven Mobile Hub for Inclusive SME Growth
Subtitle: A lightweight, AI‑powered mobile platform delivering training, marketing automation, and strategic insights to underserved small businesses.
Problem Statement: In many emerging economies, small and medium enterprises lack affordable, integrated digital tools and tailored support. They face fragmented service offerings, limited digital literacy, and no real‑time performance data hindering their ability to compete, grow, and participate fully in the digital economy.
Solution Overview:
How the solution works
EmpowerNet is a modular, mobile‑first platform that guides SMEs, startups, and young entrepreneurs through every stage of their digital journey:

    User Onboarding & Profiling: After sign‑up, users complete a brief questionnaire. The system builds a tailored profile—industry, goals, current digital maturity.

    Maxou AI Expert Coaching: Our proprietary AI model, reinforced by OpenAI’s GPT API, serves as an on‑demand digital marketing and entrepreneurship mentor. Maxou AI leverages real‑time data (campaign performance, social insights) and deep knowledge of Metanova’s services to deliver actionable recommendations.

    Training & Knowledge Hub: Interactive micro‑courses and webinars—covering social media strategy, branding, SEO/SEA—are served through an in‑app learning portal. Progress is tracked and next‑step suggestions are generated by Maxou AI.

    Automated Campaign Builder: Users choose objectives (awareness, engagement, lead gen). The platform then:

        Proposes a content calendar (post ideas, optimal timings) based on audience data.

        Generates draft assets (captions, hashtags) with AI.

        Schedules multi‑channel deployment (Instagram, Facebook, LinkedIn).

    Performance Analytics & Feedback Loop: Real‑time dashboards surface KPIs (reach, engagement, conversions). Maxou AI analyzes trends and suggests optimizations—e.g., budget reallocation, A/B test variations—to continuously improve ROI.

    Support & Collaboration: Integrated chat (via StreamChat) connects users to Metanova experts and peer cohorts for live Q&A, fostering community learning and partnership opportunities. 

Methodologies and technologies used

    Frontend: Flutter for a consistent, cross‑platform mobile experience; optimized for low‑bandwidth environments.

    Backend: Laravel PHP framework, offering a secure, scalable REST API and robust user management.

    AI Layer:

        Custom Maxou AI model trained on our proprietary dataset (past campaign performance, sector benchmarks).

        OpenAI GPT‑4 API integration for advanced natural‑language understanding and generation, ensuring rich, context‑aware responses.

        Data pipelines ingest social network metrics (via official APIs), Google Analytics, and client CRM data for real‑time insights.

    Cloud & DevOps: Hosted on AWS (EC2, RDS, S3) with Cloudflare CDN; GitLab CI/CD for automated testing and deployment; Docker for containerized services.

    Security & Compliance: OAuth 2.0 authentication; SSL/TLS encryption; regular security audits; GDPR‑aligned data handling. 

Partnerships and collaboration models

    Technology Partners:

        OpenAI (AI research and API access)

Title: GreenSpark Digital Circular Hub: Transforming Informal Waste into Wealth through Inclusive Tech & Skills in Mombasa
Subtitle: Empowering Women and Youth in Mombasa through Sustainable Green Jobs, Early Childhood Care, and Financial Inclusion.
Problem Statement: In Mombasa’s informal settlements, waste management is fragmented and dominated by informal actors with limited tools, poor incomes, and no digital infrastructure. Women and youth engaged in waste work often lack visibility, fair pay, or access to growth opportunities. This reinforces cycles of poverty, pollution, and exclusion from Kenya’s digital economy.
Solution Overview:
Our solution, "GreenSpark Empowerment Hubs," is a holistic community-based model designed to empower vulnerable women and youth in informal settlements of Mombasa, Kenya, by integrating sustainable income generation, early childhood development, and financial inclusion.

How the Solution Works:
We will establish GreenSpark Empowerment Hubs, modular community centers that offer:

Green Livelihood Training & Production:

Women and youth will be trained to produce eco-friendly briquettes from biomass and charcoal dust, liquid soap, sanitary pads, and organic compost from food waste.

These products are sold to local households, schools, markets, and businesses, providing income and reducing environmental pollution.

On-site Early Childhood Development Center:

While mothers are engaged in training or production work, their children (ages 0–6) will receive nurturing care, nutrition, and early learning from trained caregivers.

The ECD model integrates storytelling, games, nutrition monitoring, and play therapy in safe, child-friendly spaces.

Microfinance and Financial Literacy:

Partnering with a local SACCO and mobile wallet services (e.g., M-Pesa), participants will access group savings, microloans, and training on budgeting, mobile banking, and entrepreneurship.

Circular Economy Integration:

Waste collected from local markets and households feeds into our briquette and compost processes, turning community waste into economic opportunity.

Methodologies & Technologies Used:
Community-Based Participatory Approach (CBPA): Engaging local women, elders, and youth in hub design, implementation, and governance.

Green Technology: Briquette machines (manual & electric), composters, soap mixing units, and simple pad-making kits.

Digital Tools: Use of mobile apps/SMS for microfinance tracking, digital attendance, ECD child progress, and M&E.

Human-Centered Design: Services co-created with end-users for sustainability and ownership.

Inclusive Training Modules: Visual, language-appropriate, and accessible to non-literate participants.

Partnerships and Collaboration Models:
Local Government & Chiefs: For support in land/site identification, local mobilization, and regulatory compliance.

ECD Experts (e.g., Aga Khan Foundation): To design the child care model and train caregivers.

Financial Partners (e.g., Postbank Kenya, Equity Bank, or local SACCOs): For microfinance delivery and digital wallet integration.

Waste Management Firms or County Solid Waste Teams: For waste sourcing partnerships.

Women’s Groups & Youth Associations: For co-ownership, recruitment, and community trust-building.

Technical & Vocational Colleges: For trainers and tool fabrication.

Monitoring & Evaluation Partners (e.g., universities or NGOs): For tracking social impact and learning outcomes.

This integrated model not only creates green jobs and safe child care but also strengthens financial resilience for marginalized families—advancing AGFUND’s mission of inclusive, sustainable human development.
Solution Provider(s): The proposed solution will be led by GreenSpark Initiative, a grassroots social enterprise based in Mombasa, Kenya, focused on sustainable environmental solutions and youth empowerment through green innovation. GreenSpark specializes in clean energy production (eco-briquettes), waste valorization, and circular economy practices, particularly in underserved urban communities.  Key partners include:  TUA Foundation (Transforming Urban Africa Foundation) – a community-based organization operating in Likoni, Mombasa, dedicated to empowering women and youth through skills training, microenterprise development, and social inclusion. TUA Foundation brings deep grassroots networks and experience in community mobilization, social care, and gender-based advocacy.  Likoni Youth Development Association (LIYODA) – a registered youth group active in civic engagement, employment creation, and environmental cleanup campaigns. LIYODA contributes a dynamic youth workforce and supports the mobilization and training of young people for green jobs.  Aga Khan Foundation – Early Childhood Development Program (Kenya) – a leader in holistic child care models, the Foundation will provide technical expertise in designing and operating the Early Childhood Development (ECD) components within the empowerment hubs.  Equity Group Foundation – the social impact arm of Equity Bank Kenya, providing financial literacy training, micro-savings tools, and digital banking services. Equity will support the financial inclusion pillar through mobile-based microfinance and entrepreneurship mentorship.  County Government of Mombasa – Department of Social Services and Environment – providing policy guidance, site support, community waste management coordination, and integration of the solution into the County's urban sustainability strategy.  Together, these partners represent an ecosystem of actors across the green energy, early childhood care, microfinance, and community development sectors—each playing a critical role in ensuring the success, scale, and sustainability of the project.
Implementation location(s): The solution is currently at the pilot implementation stage in Likoni Sub-County, Mombasa, Kenya. Initial activities have been rolled out in Soweto and Timbwani wards, focusing on youth and women mobilization, early-stage briquette production using biomass waste, and setting up a prototype Empowerment Hub that integrates child care services and green job training. This pilot phase is informing the full-scale implementation and refinement of the model.
Implementation timeline(s): Pilot implementation began in March 2025 and is ongoing, with the first phase expected to run until December 2025. This period covers solution design, community engagement, early-stage operations, and performance monitoring in Likoni, Mombasa.
Duration to pilot in a new geography: The estimated duration to pilot the solution in a new geography is 6 to 9 months. This timeline includes stakeholder engagement, infrastructure setup, recruitment and training of beneficiaries, initial production and service delivery, and monitoring and evaluation to ensure scalability and impact.
SDGs addressed: SDG 8 (Decent Work and Economic Growth);SDG 12 (Responsible Consumption and Production);SDG 9 (Industry, Innovation, and Infrastructure);
Desired impact:
The desired impact of our solution is to empower marginalized women and youth in underserved urban communities through sustainable green jobs, early childhood development support, and access to financial inclusion. Our key objective is to create an integrated, community-driven model that addresses unemployment, early childhood neglect, and environmental degradation in one holistic intervention.

The solution seeks to:

Create 150+ green jobs in briquette production, waste management, and early childhood care services within the first 12 months of full implementation.

Improve access to affordable, clean cooking fuel by producing over 100 tons of eco-briquettes annually, reducing dependency on charcoal and deforestation in the target region.

Enhance cognitive, emotional, and physical development of at least 300 children under 5 years through accessible, community-based early childhood development (ECD) centres led by trained local women.

Strengthen financial inclusion by enabling 500+ beneficiaries to access microloans, savings groups, and digital financial literacy through partnerships with local microfinance institutions and digital platforms.

Reduce carbon emissions by an estimated 250 metric tons annually through the use of eco-briquettes and bio-waste circular systems, supporting climate change mitigation.

By uniting economic empowerment, environmental sustainability, and child welfare, our solution offers a scalable and replicable model for inclusive development across Africa.
Key technologies:
Our solution leverages a blend of appropriate, accessible, and scalable technologies to drive social and environmental impact:

Clean Energy Technology – We utilize low-emission briquette production machines that convert biomass waste and charcoal dust into clean, efficient cooking fuel. These machines are energy-efficient and locally operable, designed for ease of use in low-resource settings.

Mobile & Digital Platforms – We are developing a mobile-based ordering and distribution system that enables customers—especially women—to locate vendors, place orders for briquettes, and access clean cooking tips. This improves last-mile access and boosts customer retention.

Digital Financial Tools – Through partnerships with microfinance institutions and fintech providers, we integrate mobile banking, digital wallets, and savings group apps to promote financial literacy and inclusion among our beneficiaries.

Geospatial Mapping (GIS) – We use GIS technology to optimize waste collection routes, identify high-demand zones for briquettes, and strategically locate future Empowerment Hubs for maximum impact.

Data Monitoring & Analytics – A simple data collection dashboard is being piloted to track impact metrics in real time, including briquette production volumes, emissions avoided, child enrollment in ECD centers, and income generated by youth and women.

These technologies ensure that our model remains data-informed, scalable, inclusive, and environmentally resilient.
Unique Characteristics:
Our solution is uniquely positioned at the intersection of climate action, women and youth empowerment, early childhood care, and financial inclusion, offering a holistic and community-driven approach that sets it apart. The following differentiated characteristics make our model both innovative and impactful:

Integrated Multi-Sectoral Model: Unlike siloed interventions, our solution combines eco-briquette production, childcare services, and digital financial tools under one Empowerment Hub—addressing multiple Sustainable Development Goals (SDGs) simultaneously.

Inclusive Employment Model: We prioritize vulnerable women and unemployed youth, not only as beneficiaries but as active co-creators and operators of the model. This participatory approach fosters ownership, sustainability, and dignity-driven employment.

Circular Economy & Waste Valorization: We transform local organic waste and charcoal dust into clean fuel, creating a closed-loop circular economy that reduces urban waste, deforestation, and household energy costs.

Tech-Enabled Accessibility: The integration of mobile platforms, digital wallets, and GIS mapping enhances access to services, optimizes logistics, and empowers communities to participate in the green economy with minimal technological barriers.

Sustainable Financing Mechanism: Revenue from briquette sales, early childhood care fees (tiered by ability to pay), and public-private partnerships fuels a self-sustaining financial model, reducing long-term donor dependency.

Replicable, Scalable, and Locally Rooted: Designed with local ownership and flexibility, our solution can be easily adapted to other urban informal settlements or peri-urban regions across Africa.

Together, these innovations form a resilient, future-ready model that redefines community development by turning everyday challenges into transformative opportunities.
Sustainable Change:
Our solution creates sustainable, systemic change by tackling the root causes of environmental degradation, economic exclusion, and gender inequality—rather than merely addressing the symptoms. It is grounded in a clear Theory of Change that drives lasting transformation across social, economic, and environmental dimensions:

1. Empowerment Through Employment
By training and employing women and youth in green jobs such as briquette production, waste collection, and early childcare services, the solution enables long-term income generation, skills development, and financial independence. This shifts vulnerable groups from dependency to productivity, reducing poverty cycles and boosting household resilience.

2. Waste-to-Wealth Model
Through the circular use of organic and charcoal waste, the project demonstrates a locally scalable model of environmental stewardship. This reduces pressure on forests, lowers CO₂ emissions, and promotes clean urban living—all while generating affordable energy alternatives.

3. Early Childhood Support for Working Mothers
The provision of affordable, safe childcare within the same empowerment hub ensures women can work or pursue training without sacrificing their children’s well-being or development. This leads to greater female workforce participation and improved outcomes for the next generation.

4. Digital Financial Inclusion
By linking participants to mobile banking and savings platforms, the solution fosters formal economic participation. Women and youth gain credit histories, savings habits, and the confidence to invest in micro-enterprises or future ventures, promoting intergenerational financial growth.

5. Policy and Community Influence
Success at the pilot level will serve as a model for policy replication, inspiring local governments, NGOs, and private actors to adopt or invest in similar hybrid models. Community champions trained through the project will also catalyze grassroots change, amplifying the impact organically.

Follow-on Effects include:

Decreased urban waste and deforestation rates.

Increased employment and education levels among women and youth.

Widened access to early childhood care and inclusive finance.

Community-led environmental and social innovation.

In essence, this solution plants the seeds for self-sustaining, regenerative communities that thrive economically while caring for their environment and future generations.

This funding enabled us to establish core infrastructure, conduct community outreach, and initiate key components of the solution, such as briquette production, youth and women training, and early childhood care services. The World Bank support gave us a strong pilot edge, validating our approach and enhancing our credibility with both local stakeholders and potential partners.

Title: TrustMe: Reliable Marketplace Linking Latin-American Tradespeople to Households
Subtitle: Digital platform that vets home-service workers, diagnoses jobs remotely, and secures fair, on-platform payments—boosting MSME income and household safety across Latin America
Problem Statement: Across Latin America, 66 % of families build their own homes because they can afford only informal “building masters” and tradespeople, not architects or engineers. Construction quality hinges on the worker’s skill and honesty, so households often overspend—about 30 % of housing costs go to avoidable repairs—and end up with homes that are unsafe, expensive to maintain, and hard to upgrade. More than 80 % of builders work outside the formal economy, leaving them with erratic income and no path to growth. TrustMe’s first step is a vetted one-day-repair marketplace that matches households with reliable workers, paving the way for a full-cycle construction platform.
Solution Overview:
How it works

1. Client search for the services, describes her needs, choose the tradesman or building master, by looking at their profiles with their ratings and portfolios. 
2. The client can also book a 15-min live diagnostic call or ask an AI chatbot to get cost estimates
3. The building masters / tradesmen selected evaluate the request and, if they want it, they can pay a small US$ 5 fee for the connection with the client. They can keep their relationship for the long term and for as many new jobs they would like.  The platform never takes a share or client payment.
4. Negotiations and type of payment (cash or credit) depends entirely on the client and worker. If the client and worker agree to have the payment via credit card, the payment is released 7 days after job completion to ensure quality. 


Methodologies / technologies (currently)

1. React/TypeScript web & mobile UI, Node/Express API, PostgreSQL & Drizzle ORM (beta)
2. WhatsApp bot using ChatGPT 4.1 API for cost estimates and other consultations (beta)
3. Data dashboards for impact tracking (beta)



Partnership & collaboration model

1. Academia: Stanford Center for Social Innovation (we won the prestigious Stanford Impact Founder Award 2025) & Harvard Kennedy School Latin American Caucus.
2. Government: We are launching a pilot in Merida Yucatan in Mexico during the Thanksgiving break, supported by the Minister of Economics and Labor of the State, Ermilo Barrera Novelo.
3. NGO: Currently working with 3 local NGOs for worker recruitment, vetting and onboarding.
Solution Provider(s): Stanford Center for Social Innovation (Incubator, Higher Education), Latin American Caucus—Harvard Kennedy School (Research, Student and Alumni Networks), Olivares del Castillo Legal & Compliance (Legal Services), Vinculación Social (NGO), Cáritas Esperanza (NGO), Centro Social y Bolsa de Trabajo - Hogar de la Joven (NGO)
Implementation location(s): We are in the beta stage, testing the MVP and vetting workers in Mexico City; We are launching a pilot in Merida Yucatan in Mexico during the Thanksgiving break, supported by the Minister of Economics and Labor of the State, Ermilo Barrera Novelo
Implementation timeline(s): Beta Mexico City - September to November 2025; Pilot Merida - November to December. Full Launch January 2025
Duration to pilot in a new geography: 3–5 months (localized onboarding 2 mo, go-live 1–3 mo)
SDGs addressed: SDG 8 (Decent Work and Economic Growth);SDG 10 (Reduced Inequalities);SDG 11 (Sustainable Cities and Communities);
Desired impact:
Lift earnings of 50 000 tradespeople by ≥30 % within 5 years.
1. Reduce household repair overruns by ≥20 % through transparent pricing & insured workmanship.
Key technologies:
Objectives (5-year horizon)

1. Income uplift: Raise earnings of 50 000 tradespeople by ≥ 30 %.
2. Household savings: Cut repair-and-maintenance overruns by ≥ 20 % through transparent pricing, remote diagnostics, and insured workmanship.
3. Safer self-built homes: Facilitate 250 000+ safe construction and repair projects (measured by # jobs, square-footage improved, and adherence to building-safety checklists), reducing accident risk in informal housing.

Long-term externalities

1. Higher disposable income for education, health, and mobility.
2. Dignified, structurally sound housing that boosts family well-being and lowers disaster vulnerability.
Unique Characteristics:
1. Video-first diagnostic + AI pricing removes 90 % of on-site quote visits.
2. Escrow + delayed payout + insurance creates trust in a segment dominated by cash and informal labor.
3. Dual-sided reputation graphs that reward both craftsmanship and client reliability.
I4. Incubated by Stanford & Harvard networks, providing unusual access to research, talent, and impact capital.
Sustainable Change:
North Star: safe, affordable self-construction for low-income families.

1. Build a trusted workforce. Start with small, one-day repair jobs in higher-income areas; vet tradespeople, log performance, and convert informal labor into credit-ready, insured professionals.
2. Automate design and budgeting. Use video + AI to generate scope, materials lists, and transparent costs for larger renovations, lowering risk and unlocking bulk-purchase discounts.
3. Embed cheap materials and financing. Leverage aggregated demand and verified budgets to secure 5–15 % lower input prices and integrate micro-loans or subsidies directly into digital invoices.
- Expansion path: quick repairs ➜ complex renovations ➜ full self-construction for low-income households.

- Systemic outcomes (5–10 yrs): formal MSME market with e-payments, safer housing stock, inclusive credit for 50 k workers and 1 M+ families.

Title: TropiConnect: Restructuring Agri-trade from the Global South to the world.
Subtitle: An AI and Blockchain powered platform empowering smallholder farmers with direct access to global markets, fair pricing, and sustainable trade opportunities.
Problem Statement: Smallholder farmers across Africa face limited access to global markets due to fragmented supply chains, lack of price transparency, unreliable buyer networks, and minimal digital infrastructure. These barriers trap them in cycles of low income despite producing the world's food in a trillion-dollar industry and dependence on intermediaries who take the lion's share of profit. Without inclusive digital tools, smallholders remain excluded from international trade opportunities, preventing economic growth and long-term sustainability. TropiConnect addresses this by creating a transparent, user-friendly, tech-driven platform that directly links smallholder cooperatives with global buyers.
Solution Overview:
TropiConnect is a digital agri-trade platform that enables smallholder farmer cooperatives across Africa to directly connect with verified global buyers. The platform offers:

Verified Buyer-Cooperative Matching: Farmers list their available crops, certifications, and volumes. TropiConnect matches them with international buyers based on product needs, location, and quality requirements.

Real-Time Market Intelligence: Buyers and cooperatives access real-time pricing, logistics information, and demand forecasts to support transparent, fair trade negotiations.

Digital Trade Facilitation Tools: Integrated digital contract management, export documentation support, logistics and quality assurance tracking reduce friction and errors in trade processes.

Traceability & Certification Verification: TropiConnect supports traceability through blockchain-based records and enables cooperatives to upload certifications (e.g., organic, Rainforest Alliance, Fairtrade) for buyer validation.


Methodologies and Technologies Used:
Blockchain Ledger: Ensures transparent, tamper-proof tracking of product origin, movement, and certification, fostering buyer trust and traceability.

AI-Driven Matching & Price Forecasting: Machine learning models help match supply with buyer preferences and predict market pricing trends.

Mobile-First Design: The platform is optimized for mobile devices to ensure accessibility in rural areas with limited internet access.

APIs & Integration: TropiConnect is built to integrate with logistics, payment, and certification databases, streamlining cross-border trade.

Data Analytics Dashboard: Cooperatives and buyers can track performance, pricing trends, and fulfillment metrics through a user-friendly dashboard.

TropiConnect works through a collaborative, ecosystem-based model involving:
Farmer Cooperatives & Unions: Direct partnerships are formed with vetted cooperatives, offering training and onboarding support.

International Buyers: We engage sustainably oriented importers, processors, and retailers seeking transparency in sourcing.

Universities & Research Institutes: The University of Manchester and Cambridge support and advise TropiConnect on sustainability and R&D for pricing algorithms and tech deployment.
Solution Provider(s): Government and Development Partners: Engagement with national export boards and ministries ensures regulatory alignment and capacity building such as the Ministry of Trade and Co-operatives in Uganda and Innovate UK.  NGOs & Trade Organizations: We partner with entities focused on farmer education, trade policy advocacy, and certification support to ensure inclusivity such as the Inter African Coffee Organisation (received a letter from the Secretary General on the impact we are making).  University of Manchester – Providing R&D support for pricing algorithms and digital infrastructure (Higher Education, Research & Development), Innovate UK – Offering innovation and business growth support (Government, Innovation Support), Ministry of Trade, Industry and Cooperatives – Uganda – Supporting cooperative engagement and trade policy alignment (Government, Trade & Cooperative Development), Inter-African Coffee Organisation (IACO) – Promoting sustainable African coffee trade and value chain development (Agriculture, Trade, Coffee Sector).
