Summary: Digital KaMangyan is a culturally inclusive digital literacy initiative designed to empower Mangyan Indigenous Peoples (IPs) in Oriental Mindoro with the digital skills necessary for safer, more effective engagement in the digital economy.

Name of your organization: Prince Technology and Community Development Foundation (A registered NGO in Nigeria, CAC/IT/NO 92675)
Title: Smart Solar-Powered Digital Booths for Empowering Small Businesses in Nigeria
Subtitle: A smart, solar-powered mobile booth offering clean energy, digital access, and business support tools to empower informal vendors and small businesses in underserved Nigerian communities.
Problem Statement: In Nigeria, millions of informal vendors and small business owners are unable to access consistent electricity, safe spaces to work, or digital infrastructure, which restricts their productivity and income potential, as well as their inclusion in a digital economy. Much of the existing infrastructure is not only costly, but centralised or not available in underserved communities, which widens the technological and economic divide.
Solution Overview:
Our solution is a smart, multipurpose solar-powered moveable booth (with voice or mobile phone control system) designed to empower informal vendors and small businesses in underserved Nigerian communities by providing clean energy access, digital connectivity, and business support infrastructure in a compact, movable unit.
The booth features solar panels, an inverter, a charge controller, battery storage, and USB/AC outlets to power devices such as mobile phones, point-of-sale systems, lights, fans, refrigerators, televisions, digital tools, and other essential devices. A moveable structure also provides a weather-protected and safe place to conduct work and can be moved to other selling locations, markets, and informal areas (roadside).  The solar-powered, movable booth features a digital information display, providing utility for communicating community announcements, educational messaging, and access to online tools, while promoting inclusivity and addressing the digital divide. 
All the home appliances (electric Fan, Television, Refrigerator, etc) integrated with the booth, including electric bulbs, are controlled wirelessly either by issuing the corresponding voice command or by clicking the corresponding icon on an Application (App) running on a Mobile Phone. 
These smart automation features are especially beneficial for:
•	Elderly and physically challenged individuals who may struggle with manual switches.
•	Enhancing safety by reducing the risk of electrical shock.
•	Promoting digital inclusion through advanced mobile phone usage beyond calls and texting.
We apply a combination of solar PV technology, battery management systems, IoT-based smart controls, and mobile connectivity to make the unit smarter and energy-efficient, leading to a better user experience. In solving the dual challenges of energy poverty and digital exclusion, users are able to increase their operating hours of the unit, adopt digital payment methods, and have access to online services. 
We use an implementation model that is built on partnerships with local cooperatives, youth- and women-led groups, and community development foundations for last-mile distribution. We work with technical partners for solar integration and digital system design, and with local governments and NGOs in promoting deployment to high-need areas.
By combining renewable energy and inclusive technology, our solution helps fill the infrastructure gap for microenterprises, while also advancing sustainable development and digital inclusion.

Recognition:
I was awarded Nigeria’s Inventors Award of the Year (2022) for inventing this solution, receiving a monetary prize of over USD1,000. The innovation has garnered both national and international recognition, including from the Federal Ministry of Education (Nigeria), UNESCO, and the U.S. Mission Nigeria, which publicly celebrated and published the invention on its official Facebook page.
These recognitions validate the solution’s relevance, scalability, and its potential to drive inclusive digital and energy access for underserved communities.
Solution Provider(s): I am the founder of Prince Technology and Community Development Foundation, a nonprofit organization committed to promoting clean energy innovation, digital inclusion, and sustainable development across underserved communities in Nigeria.  Some key champions and collaborators include: 1. U.S. Mission Nigeria, published on their official Facebook page, celebrated the innovation. U.S. Mission Nigeria has also nominated me to represent Nigeria as a delegate in the U.S. Department of State's upcoming Expanding Career and Technical Education (CTE) programme, November 1–22, 2025 in Washington D.C, USA - with the focused goal of providing me with advanced technical and strategic skills to scale and replicate this project to have broader impact.  2. Senate Committee on Science and Technology (Nigeria) - awarded me the Inventors Award of the Year (2022) in Nigeria, which included a monetary award of over $1,000 in recognition of the innovation’s national importance and problem-solving capabilities. I continue to work with the Senate Committee on Science and Technology to see if we can work together to scale the project. 3. I received a letter of appreciation from the Federal Ministry of Education (Nigeria) for the solution's noted educational and developmental significance. 4. UNESCO recognized the innovation as a promising instrument for digital empowerment, access to clean energy, and inclusive education in developing nations.
Implementation location(s): Not yet deployed. However, we have two fully functional Minimum Viable Products (MVPs) of the solution developed and demonstrated to stakeholders, and we are currently in a pre-deployment, pre-production stage where we are procuring the equipment we need, scaling our processes, and finalizing designs for mass deployment.  To ensure long-term sustainability and local ownership, our technical team is currently undergoing intensive training on inverter fabrication and charge controller design, tailored specifically to our system architecture. We are committed to utilizing locally available materials and indigenous fabrication techniques to reduce costs, build local capacity, and strengthen the supply chain.  The first deployment is planned for Ndikelionwu, Anambra State, a rural community in southeastern Nigeria that is underserved and continues to face challenges from energy poverty and digital exclusion. Ndikelionwu was also the case study of my Master’s thesis ‘Optimization of a 45KW Off-Grid Solar Energy System for Rural Electrification’, in which I proposed and simulated a solar farm capable of generating 120.38 MWh annually.
Implementation timeline(s): Implementation Timeline(s): While the solution has not yet been deployed at scale, two fully functional Minimum Viable Products (MVPs) were developed and demonstrated between October 2022 and May 2024. We are currently in the pre-deployment phase (October 2022 – Present), focusing on equipment acquisition, team training in inverter and charge controller fabrication, and preparation for localized mass production using locally sourced materials The first deployment will occur in the second quarter of 2026 at Ndikelionwu, Anambra State, southeast Nigeria, upon my return from the U.S. Department of State's Expanding Career and Technical Education (CTE) program. I have been nominated to represent Nigeria as a delegate from November 1–22, 2025, in Washington, D.C. The program is designed to provide me with advanced technical and strategic skills, on scaling and replicating this project, in order to take it to a wider audience.
Duration to pilot in a new geography: 1 to 2 months, covering localized adaptation, equipment assembly, on-site installation, testing, and training. The project’s MVP is fully functional, and the team is technically prepared, allowing for rapid deployment upon securing necessary resources.
SDGs addressed: SDG 7 (Affordable and Clean Energy);SDG 8 (Decent Work and Economic Growth);SDG 11 (Sustainable Cities and Communities);
Desired impact:
Solution Objectives:
The solar-powered, multipurpose moveable booth is designed to close the energy access and digital divide by providing affordable, clean, and portable energy infrastructure in underserved communities. Specifically, it aims to:
1. Support clean energy transition through solar-based power supply.
2. Empower micro-entrepreneurs (e.g., barbers, phone charging vendors, ICT operators) by offering affordable workspaces with integrated power.
3. Enhance digital inclusion through optional ICT modules, Wi-Fi service, and phone charging ports. 
4. Facilitate community announcements, provide educational content, and access to online tools to help mitigate the digital divide for underserved areas. 
5. Facilitate local innovation through the locally fabricated components and skills development by training youth in renewable technologies.

Key Impact / Outputs: 
1. Energy Access: Two fully functional Minimum Viable Product (MVP) has been built and successfully demonstrated, providing up to 12–14 hours of continuous off-grid power for appliances like clippers, fans, energy-saving bulbs, phone chargers, laptops, and televisions. 
2. GHG Reduction: Replaced small diesel generators; estimated annual CO₂ savings of 1.5-2 tons per booth.
3. Economic Empowerment: Enables micro-enterprises to operate in off-grid areas. Each booth can support 3–5 users daily, potentially generating over ₦300,000 (~$200/month) in additional income for local entrepreneurs.
4. Job Creation: Trained local youth will work with fabrication and maintenance to support both sustainable job creation and technical upskilling. 
5. Scalability: Modular design and local material sourcing reduce production cost by 30–40% compared to imported alternatives.
6. Community Impact: Planned first deployment in Ndikelionwu, Anambra State, will serve as a replicable model for similar rural communities across Nigeria and Africa.
7. The solution earned me the prestigious Inventors Award of the Year (2022) in Nigeria, presented by the Senate Committee on Science and Technology, with a monetary prize exceeding $1,000. It has since gained national and international recognition from the Federal Ministry of Education, UNESCO, and the U.S. Mission Nigeria, which featured the innovation on its official platform.
Key technologies:
Key Technologies Used:
1. Renewable Energy (Solar Technology):
The core power source is an off-grid solar energy system that ensures uninterrupted, clean, and affordable electricity for micro-enterprises in underserved communities.

2. SM/Mobile Communication Technology:
The system utilizes GSM-enabled modules and mobile connectivity to facilitate remote control and automation.
Mobile and Voice Control Systems: 
Through mobile apps or voice commands, users can control appliances, lighting, and digital display(s). This allows for inclusivity so that both technology-savvy and low-literacy users can easily interact with the system. Through smart controls, the system enhances accessibility for the elderly and disabled while promoting clean energy and economic development. 

3. Digital Display Technology:
A digital information board is integrated into the unit to facilitate the dissemination of community announcements, educational material, and links to online tools to facilitate communication about bridging the digital divide in remote communities. The display is programmed wirelessly using a mobile phone interface, which allows the user to update the display easily and instantly without needing to physically connect to the unit. 

4. AI-driven optimization for battery storage in renewable energy systems:
This aligns with my broader PhD research, which focuses on deploying AI-driven optimization for lithium-ion battery storage in renewable energy systems. In future iterations, I plan to integrate the AI model into the booth's energy management system, enabling intelligent control of power consumption (including the digital display) based on real-time battery status, solar generation, and user demand. This integration will enhance energy efficiency and ensure longer operational uptime in off-grid settings, particularly where solar power is the sole energy source.
Unique Characteristics:
Distinctive Features of the Solution: 
1. Multi-Functional and Portable: 
The booth is a portable unit that combines renewable energy generation, mobile commerce infrastructure, digital communication, and smart control into a single entity. It functions as a solar-powered business hub, community information point, and renewable energy provider in one single unit. 
2. Inclusive Smart Control: 
Through mobile and voice control (via GSM apps and voice assistants), the system allows literate and low-literacy people, including women, the elderly, and persons with disabilities, etc., to interact easily with the setup, promoting digital inclusion and accessibility.
3. Wireless digital display: 
Instead of building a traditional kiosk with a digital display, the booth has a wireless, programmable digital information board to run public service announcements, educational content, and local campaigns, helping close the digital gap between urban and rural communities. 
4. AI Readiness and Research Integration: 
The solution is AI-ready. As part of a broader PhD research project, plans are in place to integrate AI-driven energy optimization to intelligently manage energy usage, extend battery life, and forecast power needs — a breakthrough in merging academic research with grassroots innovation.
5. Recognition and Validation: 
The solution is not just theoretical. It earned the prestigious “Inventors Award of the Year (2022)” by Nigeria’s Senate Committee on Science and Technology and has received national and international recognition from bodies like UNESCO, Federal Ministry of Education, and the U.S. Mission Nigeria.
6. Scalable Deployment Model:
It is a modular solution offering quick localized adaptation and deployment in 1–2 months. The financial model is designed to enable local entrepreneurs or cooperatives to efficiently own or lease the booth for income generation- thereby creating independent and decentralized economic impact.
Sustainable Change:
Sustainable, systemic impact (Theory of Change):
The use of our mobile solar-powered, voice or GSM-controlled kiosk is poised to bring sustainable and systemic changes in the economic, environmental, and digital inclusion spaces:

1. Inputs & Activities:
 - Deploy booths in locations where access is limited.
 - Each booth is equipped with smart controls (mobile/voice), digital display boards, and charging systems. 
 - Local youth/women are trained to operate or lease the kiosks as micro-enterprises.

2. Immediate Outputs:
 - Access to clean, affordable off-grid energy. 
 - Creation of green local jobs and entrepreneurship.
 - Improved access to digital information, educational content, and announcements from the community.

3. Short-Medium Outcomes:
 - Reduction in use of fossil fuel generators - lower GHG emissions
 - Empowerment of marginalized groups through income generation and digital tools
 - Increased public awareness and access to critical services in remote areas

4. Long-term Outcomes:
 - Increased energy transition in rural/suburban Nigeria.
 - Strengthened local economies through decentralized, clean-tech entrepreneurship.
 - Addressing the digital divide and creating inclusive, tech-enabled community development opportunities.
 - Demonstrated scalable model for integration of AI in smart renewable energy solutions (aligned with ongoing PhD research).

This model creates systemic change by embedding clean energy, inclusive technology, and community empowerment into a scalable solution that governments, NGOs, and private sectors can replicate for broader socio-economic and climate impact.
Funding Sources: The development of the solution has been funded through multiple channels. Primary funding came from personal contributions and in-kind support from the Prince Technology and Community Development Foundation, a registered NGO in Nigeria. Funding sources also consisted of small donations from stakeholders in the community and previous innovation awards (above USD 1,000), which were used to purchase parts and provide training for young men and women in inverter fabrication and charge controller design. Additionally, some financing came in the form of revenue from our renewable energy business “Prince Tech Green Energy Solutions,” where (as CEO and Renewable Energy Engineer), I have led the installation of over 500 KW of solar energy systems for homes and businesses across Nigeria and other African countries since 2008. Title: Lisungi Santé Digitale : accès équitable aux soins via le numérique.
Subtitle: Plateforme numérique inclusive reliant les communautés vulnérables à des services de santé essentiels grâce à la téléconsultation, l’éducation sanitaire et la gestion de données.
Problem Statement: Des femmes et jeunes issus de groupes minoritaires en zones rurales ou précaires n'ont pas accès à des soins de santé de qualité en raison du manque d’infrastructures, de personnel médical, et de connectivité. Cette fracture sanitaire et numérique aggrave les inégalités sociales et empêche une prise en charge précoce des maladies. Sans solutions adaptées, ces populations resteront exclues des bénéfices de l’économie numérique et des progrès en santé.
Solution Overview:
Lisungi Santé Digitale est une solution numérique inclusive conçue pour améliorer l'accès aux soins de santé des femmes et jeunes issus de groupes minoritaires vivant dans des zones rurales et précaires. La plateforme fonctionne via des outils accessibles (applications mobiles légères, SMS interactifs, kiosques numériques communautaires) permettant la téléconsultation, le suivi médical, l’éducation sanitaire multilingue et la sensibilisation aux droits en santé.

Nous utilisons des technologies à faible bande passante, des interfaces conviviales adaptées aux personnes peu alphabétisées, et des systèmes de gestion de dossiers médicaux décentralisés. La solution est renforcée par une méthodologie communautaire : nous formons des ambassadrices santé locales (femmes leaders et jeunes pairs éducateurs) pour accompagner, sensibiliser et renforcer la confiance numérique dans leurs communautés.

Nous collaborons avec des centres de santé locaux, des ONG féminines et de jeunesse, ainsi que des entreprises tech sociales pour adapter les outils, mutualiser les ressources et étendre l’impact. Ce modèle hybride, ancré dans le local mais soutenu par la technologie, favorise une inclusion durable et transforme l’économie numérique en levier d’équité.
Solution Provider(s): Santé Lisungi asbl, est une oganisation à but non lucratif basée en RDC, active dans la promotion de la santé communautaire et de l'inclusion numérique pour les populations vulnérables, notamment les femmes et les jeunes. Autres partenaires : Ministère de la Santé RDC (secteur public, appui institutionnel), AfyaTech (start-up e-santé, développement technologique), Femmes Numériques RDC (ONG féminine, formation et sensibilisation), Réseau des Jeunes Leaders Ruraux (association communautaire, mobilisation terrain), Clinique Mobile Solidaire (secteur santé, partenariats de téléconsultation).
Implementation location(s): La solution est actuellement en phase de prototype et de preuve de concept, avec des tests prévus dans les zones rurales de la province du Kongo-Central (RDC), notamment autour de Matadi et Songololo.
Implementation timeline(s): Phase de preuve de concept en cours, prévue de octobre 2025 à février 2026. Le déploiement pilote est envisagé pour le premier semestre 2026, selon les résultats de l’évaluation initiale.
Duration to pilot in a new geography: 4 à 6 mois, incluant la mobilisation communautaire, la formation des relais locaux, l’adaptation des outils numériques au contexte, et l’évaluation initiale d’impact.
SDGs addressed: SDG 3 (Good Health and Well-being);SDG 5 (Gender Equality);SDG 9 (Industry, Innovation, and Infrastructure);
Desired impact:
a. Objectifs de la solution :
Améliorer l’accès équitable aux soins de santé pour les femmes et les jeunes en milieux ruraux précaires grâce aux outils numériques ; renforcer les capacités locales ; et réduire la fracture numérique en santé.

b. Principaux impacts attendus : 
- +5 000 bénéficiaires touchés lors de la phase pilote (consultations, éducation sanitaire, suivi).
- 100 femmes et jeunes formés comme relais numériques communautaires.
- Réduction de 40 % du temps d’accès aux soins dans les zones ciblées.
- Création d’emplois locaux via l’animation, la gestion et la maintenance de la solution numérique.
Key technologies:
Notre solution utilise des technologies adaptées aux contextes à faible connectivité, notamment :
- Applications mobiles légères et SMS interactifs pour l’accès et la communication.
- Gestion décentralisée des dossiers médicaux numériques sécurisés.
- Intelligence artificielle pour le triage simple et l’orientation des patients.
- Analytique de données pour le suivi de la santé communautaire et l’amélioration continue.
- Plateformes collaboratives en ligne pour la formation et le partage entre relais communautaires.
Unique Characteristics: Lisungi Santé Digitale se distingue par son modèle communautaire centré sur les femmes et jeunes leaders ruraux, qui assurent l’adoption et la pérennité. Sa technologie est adaptée aux faibles ressources (faible bande passante, interfaces simples). Le partenariat entre ONG, acteurs publics et start-ups locales crée un écosystème d’innovation inclusive. De plus, la solution intègre un mécanisme de financement hybride combinant fonds publics, soutien privé et contributions communautaires, garantissant sa durabilité.
Sustainable Change: Notre solution favorise un changement systémique en autonomisant durablement les femmes et jeunes ruraux comme acteurs clés de la santé numérique, renforçant ainsi les capacités locales et la résilience communautaire. En intégrant la technologie à des partenariats multisectoriels, elle crée un écosystème pérenne qui réduit la fracture numérique et améliore durablement l’accès aux soins. L’effet de suivi attendu est une adoption élargie des outils numériques de santé, une amélioration continue grâce aux retours communautaires, et un renforcement des politiques publiques inclusives.
Funding Sources: Cette solution n’a pas encore été financée. Nous sommes activement en recherche de financements auprès d’organismes internationaux, partenaires publics et privés, afin de soutenir sa mise en œuvre et son déploiement.
Testimonials and Endorsements: À ce jour, il n’y a pas encore de témoignages, car le projet n’a pas encore été mis en œuvre. Toutefois, le besoin est fortement ressenti sur le terrain, avec une demande croissante exprimée par les communautés rurales, notamment les femmes et les jeunes.
Further comments/feedback: Le projet n’ayant pas encore été mis en œuvre, nous ne disposons pas encore de retours d’expérience concrets. Cependant, nos échanges préliminaires avec les communautés ciblées révèlent un fort intérêt et une demande réelle de la part des bénéficiaires, en particulier les femmes et les jeunes, face à l'absence de solutions de santé accessibles et numériques dans leur quotidien.
Primary thematic focus area: Inclusive Digital Innovation Skills & Entrepreneurial Talent Development
Summary: Lisungi Santé Digitale provides an inclusive digital solution to bridge healthcare access gaps for vulnerable populations in rural areas. By using mobile, SMS, and community-driven approaches, the project aims to improve healthcare access, particularly for women and youth. The solution has significant potential, but more details on scalability and funding are required.

Title: Kodafri: Connecting African Tech Talent to Global Digital Opportunities
Subtitle: A digital platform that matches vetted African developers to startups worldwide, opening access to jobs, skills growth, and fair payment systems for underserved tech communities.
Problem Statement: Africa's rapidly growing pool of skilled software developers faces significant barriers accessing global job opportunities that match their abilities and offer fair compensation. Despite possessing competitive technical skills, these developers struggle with limited market visibility, lack of internationally recognized credential verification, and complex cross-border payment systems that create trust issues for potential employers. This geographic and systemic isolation traps talented African developers in local markets with restricted economic potential, while global startups miss access to cost-effective, high-quality talent—creating a lose-lose scenario that perpetuates digital economic inequality and limits innovation opportunities for both sides.
Solution Overview:
Kodafri operates as a digital platform that connects vetted African software developers with startups worldwide. Developers register and create verified profiles through a multi-step vetting process, including integration with GitHub and LinkedIn, and credential uploads. This verification builds trust and market visibility for African talent.

An AI-driven matching engine analyzes developer skills and project requirements to pair developers with suitable job opportunities, whether remote contracts or full-time roles. Kodafri manages secure contract workflows and holds payments in escrow, releasing funds upon milestone approval to guarantee fairness and reliability for both parties.

The platform will support multiple payment systems tailored to emerging markets, such as M-Pesa, Flutterwave, Paystack, Stripe, and PayPal, simplifying cross-border transactions and reducing barriers.
Kodafri will collaborate with local tech hubs, coding academies, and professional networks to source talent and provide ongoing digital skills development. Partnerships with payment providers and startup incubators will enhance platform capabilities and outreach.

This approach builds a sustainable ecosystem where African developers gain economic empowerment and startups access diverse, high-quality tech talent efficiently.
Solution Provider(s): Current partner: AFDiaspora Ltd. (Parent Company, Startup Consultation and Technology/Digital Services, Rwanda), and Future partners: CcHub (Innovation Hub, Technology, pan-African), Norrsken House (Impact Hub, Tech Entrepreneurship, Rwanda), MEST Africa (Entrepreneurship Training/Incubator, Technology/Education, Ghana), Baobab Network (Venture Capital/Accelerator, Investment/Technology, Kenya)
Duration to pilot in a new geography: 6 to 9 months—this period allows for setting up local partnerships, onboarding developers, customizing the platform for regional needs, and launching the pilot with initial users.
SDGs addressed: SDG 8 (Decent Work and Economic Growth);SDG 9 (Industry, Innovation, and Infrastructure);SDG 10 (Reduced Inequalities);
Desired impact:
Kodafri’s Objectives:
1) Build foundational digital skills among African developers through comprehensive verification and training programs that create pathways to global employment opportunities. 
2) Empower underserved tech communities to access international digital markets through trusted matching technology and secure cross-border payment systems. 
3) Foster inclusive innovation and knowledge sharing between African developers and global startups, promoting technology transfer and local capacity building.
4) Support sustainable digital economic growth that benefits both African talent and international businesses seeking diverse, cost-effective technical expertise. 
5) Overall, establish a scalable platform model that can be adapted for other emerging markets, demonstrating viable pathways for inclusive digital economy participation. 

Key Achievements / Impacts (Projected):
1) Create direct employment for 2,000+ verified African developers within 24 months by connecting local and global startups with African tech talent, reducing their hiring costs by 30-40%, while targeting income increases of at least twice above local market rates.
2) Train and certify 1,000+ developers across 10 African countries through partnerships with local tech hubs and coding academies, strengthening local digital ecosystems.
3) Facilitate $1 million+ in secure cross-border transactions annually by year two, enabling secure and fair payment systems that improve financial inclusion and reduce cross-border transaction barriers.
Key technologies:
Kodafri will use several advanced technologies to deliver its solution, as follows:

- Artificial Intelligence (AI): An AI-driven matching engine analyzes developer skills and project requirements to connect talent with the best-fit job opportunities efficiently.

- Secure Payment Systems: Integration with digital payment platforms like M-Pesa, Flutterwave, Paystack, Stripe, and PayPal facilitates fast, reliable, and cross-border transactions tailored for emerging markets.

- Cloud-Based Platform: A scalable, cloud-hosted infrastructure ensures high availability, data security, and seamless user access across geographies.

- API Integrations: Connections with platforms such as Credly, GitHub and LinkedIn allow automatic verification of developer credentials and portfolio data, increasing trust and reducing barriers to onboarding.

- Escrow Payment Technology: Manages secure contract payments, holding funds until project milestones are met to protect both developers and startups.

- Data Analytics and Reporting Systems: Analytics dashboard provides insights for continuous platform improvement and stakeholder reporting.
Unique Characteristics:
Kodafri stands out through several key innovations:

1) Africa-First Payment Integration: Kodafri specifically targets African developers facing geographic and systemic barriers, creating a niche that global platforms often overlook. Unlike global freelancing platforms, Kodafri integrates mobile money systems (M-Pesa) and African payment processors (Flutterwave, Paystack) as primary options rather than afterthoughts. This addresses the reality that many African developers lack access to traditional banking required by international platforms, removing a fundamental barrier to participation. 

2) Comprehensive Developer Verification System: Kodafri goes beyond basic portfolio reviews to create "Verified Developer" badges through multi-step vetting, including GitHub integration, LinkedIn validation, and credential uploads. This builds unprecedented trust levels for African talent in global markets where credibility gaps often exclude qualified developers.

3) Ecosystem Partnership Model: Rather than operating as an isolated marketplace, Kodafri partners directly with African tech hubs, coding academies, and professional networks to source and develop talent. This community-driven approach creates sustainable talent pipelines and ongoing skills development rather than one-time transactions.

4) AI-Powered Matching Engine: Kodafri’s AI system intelligently pairs developers with projects that best fit their skills, boosting efficiency and reducing mismatches common in traditional platforms.
Sustainable Change:
Kodafri, as the go-to platform for African tech talent, will ultimately transform Africa's position in the digital economy. By connecting thousands of African developers to international opportunities and fair compensation, the platform will create economic multiplier effects that flow through local communities, inspiring new generations to pursue tech careers.

As developers gain international experience and higher incomes, they can reinvest locally by launching their own startups, creating employment opportunities that extend beyond the tech sector into finance, agriculture, healthcare, and other industries. This virtuous cycle establishes Africa as a recognized source of technical talent, fundamentally shifting global business relationships. 

The long-term vision encompasses a thriving African tech ecosystem where young people across socioeconomic backgrounds can access dignified, well-paying digital careers, local startups compete globally, and technology-driven solutions emerge from African contexts to solve both continental and worldwide challenges, creating sustainable prosperity that benefits both lower and middle-class communities while positioning Africa as an integral contributor to global innovation.
Funding Sources: Not applicable - Kodafri is currently in the concept development stage. The platform is being developed under AFDiaspora Ltd. with initial internal funding. This UN Global Call represents our first major external funding opportunity to advance from concept to pilot implementation.
Testimonials and Endorsements: Not applicable at this stage - no testimonials are available as the platform has not yet launched. We are currently working on our LinkedIn presence to attract promising developers.
Further comments/feedback: Kodafri represents a critical opportunity to address the growing skills gap in the global tech industry while creating economic opportunities for Africa's rapidly expanding developer community. We appreciate the UN's focus on inclusive digital economy solutions and believe this grant will provide the essential resources needed to transform our concept into measurable impact for underserved tech talent across Africa.
Primary thematic focus area: Inclusive Digital Innovation Skills & Entrepreneurial Talent Development
Summary: Kodafri is a platform designed to connect skilled African developers with global startups, addressing barriers to market access, payment systems, and skill verification. It uses AI to match talent with opportunities, creating a sustainable ecosystem for digital inclusion. However, more details on scalability and long-term funding strategies are needed.

Title: Tradi-Market
Subtitle: your market comes to you.
Problem Statement:
In Senegal, and more broadly in Africa, local markets remain on the sidelines of the digital transformation, limiting consumers’ access to fresh and authentic products. Populations — professional women, homemakers, students… — often have to travel under the scorching sun, endure traffic jams, and use polluting means of transportation simply to get supplies. This constraint results in a loss of time, increased fatigue, and the risk of supply shortages for households.
This situation highlights a strategic opportunity: to digitalize access to local markets in order to bring sellers and buyers closer together, reduce the environmental impact of travel, improve consumers’ quality of life, and offer merchants a modern showcase capable of expanding their customer base.
Solution Overview:
Tradi-Market is an innovative digital platform (website and mobile application) that directly connects vendors from Senegalese local markets to urban consumers. Users — professional women, homemakers, students… — can browse a wide catalog of fresh and authentic products sourced directly from the market, place orders online, and enjoy fast and reliable delivery to their homes or workplaces. This solution simplifies access to local products while offering merchants a modern showcase to expand their customer base.

The solution is based on a user-centered approach and on accessible, robust technologies. WooCommerce is used for the online store and order management, complemented by the integration of the WhatsApp Business API for a direct communication channel with customers, and the Google Maps API to optimize logistics. Payments are secured through local solutions such as Orange Money and Wave. Logistics follow an eco-responsible model through the use of electric motorcycles to reduce the carbon footprint.

Tradi-Market develops strategic partnerships with local markets, agricultural cooperatives, and eco-friendly transport providers to ensure reliable sourcing and optimized delivery. The company also benefits from the support of innovation programs such as YALI, Orange Corners, and MasterCard, which strengthen its technical, financial, and strategic growth. This collaborative model creates a positive economic, social, and environmental impact while addressing a real market need.
Solution Provider(s): Orange Corners provides quality mentoring as well as strategic support for the growth of our startup.
Implementation timeline(s): We have been working on the project since December 2022.
Duration to pilot in a new geography: 3 MONTHS
SDGs addressed: SDG 8 (Decent Work and Economic Growth);SDG 13 (Climate Action);SDG 12 (Responsible Consumption and Production);
Desired impact:
The primary goal of Tradi-Market is to facilitate access to fresh and authentic local products for urban populations, notably professional women, homemakers, and students, through a simple and efficient digital platform. The solution also aims to reduce the carbon footprint linked to traditional market travel by 30% by adopting a green logistics model based on electric motorcycles. By offering local merchants increased visibility and growth opportunities, Tradi-Market contributes to local economic dynamism and the creation of sustainable jobs.

Since December 2022, more than 150 market vendors have joined the platform as partners, with a monthly user growth rate of 15%. Over 9,000 eco-friendly orders have been delivered, avoiding an estimated 2 tons of CO₂ emissions compared to traditional transport. The startup has directly created 12 stable jobs and supports more than 300 local vendors and producers. According to a satisfaction survey, 85% of users save an average of 2 hours per week and reduce their fatigue related to travel.
Key technologies:
Key Technologies Used for the Tradi-Market Solution

Tradi-Market is developed with robust and modern web technologies to ensure a smooth user experience and efficient operation management. The back-end is primarily coded in PHP, the language used for managing the e-commerce platform and server functionalities. The front-end uses JavaScript, HTML5, and CSS3 to provide an interactive, responsive interface accessible on all devices (computers, mobiles).

The platform integrates several essential APIs, including the WhatsApp Business API to facilitate direct communication between clients and vendors, as well as the Google Maps API for optimizing geolocation and delivery routes. Payments are secured through the integration of local solutions such as Orange Money and Wave.

A key innovation lies in the development of an artificial intelligence (AI) system dedicated to structuring and optimizing logistics. This AI, primarily developed using technologies like Python and machine learning frameworks, analyzes real-time data from farmers (stock, volumes, supply) and market vendors (orders, availability) to anticipate needs, organize goods flow, and optimize delivery routes. This approach helps reduce stock shortages, improve delivery speed, and minimize environmental impact through better planning.

Thus, Tradi-Market combines proven programming languages, strategic API integrations, and advanced AI to offer a comprehensive, efficient, and sustainable solution tailored to the specificities of Senegalese local markets.
Unique Characteristics:
We distinguish ourselves through an innovative business model that combines the digitalization of traditional local markets with eco-friendly logistics and a strong social commitment. Unlike conventional e-commerce platforms, we specifically target Senegalese markets by directly integrating local vendors as partners, thus ensuring the authenticity and freshness of the products offered.

Our major innovation lies in the integration of advanced artificial intelligence to structure and optimize the supply chain, taking into account the needs of farmers, vendors, and consumers alike. This technology allows us to reduce stock shortages, anticipate demand, and efficiently plan delivery routes, while minimizing environmental impact through the use of electric transportation.

Furthermore, we rely on strategic partnerships with support programs (YALI, Orange Corners, MasterCard) that provide us not only with financial support but also quality mentoring and access to a network of experts. This collaborative model strengthens the sustainability and growth of our startup while creating an inclusive ecosystem around digitalized local commerce.
Sustainable Change:
Our solution acts as a lever to profoundly transform the functioning of Senegalese local markets by integrating digitalization and eco-friendly logistics. By facilitating access to fresh and authentic products through an accessible digital platform, we sustainably change the purchasing habits of urban consumers, particularly professional women, homemakers, and students, who save time and reduce fatigue related to travel.

In the longer term, this behavioral transformation leads to more inclusive local economic growth by offering vendors and farmers better visibility and expanded access to customers. Furthermore, the integration of green logistics and artificial intelligence optimizes resources, reduces waste, and lowers greenhouse gas emissions, thereby contributing to the fight against climate change.

The underlying theory of change is that by digitalizing and greening short market supply chains, we promote a more resilient, sustainable, and equitable economic ecosystem, capable of adapting to future challenges and generating positive social, economic, and environmental impact in the long run.
Funding Sources: We made a personal contribution of 10,000 dollars. Subsequently, we received 2,000 euros from the Dutch government, 12,500 dollars from MasterCard through the FAST program, of which we are beneficiaries as part of the first cohort, as well as 2,000 euros from the HEC Start’Up Paris competition, where we won first place.

Further comments/feedback: The questionnaire is simple, clear, and relevant. It effectively structures the essential information about our project while facilitating the understanding of the challenges, solutions, and impacts. Its logical organization helps to present our approach efficiently to potential investors and partners.
Primary thematic focus area: Stable and Resilient Digital Supply Chains
Summary: Tradi-Market is a digital platform that connects local vendors in Senegal to urban consumers, offering fresh, authentic products through an accessible online marketplace. The platform incorporates eco-friendly delivery using electric motorcycles, offering a solution that reduces travel time, fatigue, and environmental impact for consumers while supporting local businesses with a modern, digital sales tool.

Title: Valvur: Secure AI Worlds for Inclusive Digital Learning & Entrepreneurship
Subtitle: A gamified cybersecurity and AI platform enabling safe digital skills, education, and entrepreneurship for all.
Problem Statement: Billions lack the skills, tools, and trust to participate safely in the digital economy. Vulnerable groups, especially youth, face cyberthreats, low digital literacy, and limited access to secure, inclusive online learning and income opportunities.
Solution Overview:
Valvur combines gamified digital literacy training, AI-driven cybersecurity monitoring, and post-quantum encryption to create a safe, inclusive digital environment. Through an “edutainment” approach, users—especially youth, women, and underserved communities—engage in interactive scenarios that teach cyber hygiene, identity protection, and scam avoidance while earning verifiable skills credentials.
Our technology stack integrates adaptive AI learning, behavioural analytics, and blockchain-secured credentials. Closed environments can be tailored for schools, community hubs, or enterprises, enabling safe digital engagement and skills development.

We operate through partnerships with NGOs, governments, and industry, such as our collaboration with the Estonian Cybersecurity Centre, to co-create culturally relevant content and scale impact. This model fosters local ownership, aligns with inclusive growth goals, and builds sustainable capacity for participation in the digital economy.
Solution Provider(s): Estonian Cybersecurity Centre - national agency for cybersecurity; Esports.NGO - NGO focused on digitalisation of health and eduction; International Esports Federation - international organisation, present in 100+ countries
Implementation location(s): EU (Estonia) , Africa (piloted in 16 countries), Thailand, Saudi Arabia
Implementation timeline(s): First iterations were done in 2021 (Afrika Esports Series Project)
Duration to pilot in a new geography: 60 days to full deploy
SDGs addressed: SDG 3 (Good Health and Well-being);SDG 4 (Quality Education);SDG 5 (Gender Equality);
Desired impact:
Valvur aims to close the digital safety and skills gap by:
Equipping underserved communities with practical cybersecurity skills.
Protecting personal data with post-quantum encryption to future-proof digital identities.
Increasing participation in the digital economy through safe, inclusive, and engaging learning experiences.

Key Achievements / Impacts
We aim to reach over 5,000,000 learners through gamified educational programs, with 78% improvement in cyber hygiene scores.
Enabled secure online engagement for vulnerable groups, reducing exposure to scams and fraud.
Created new employment pathways by issuing blockchain-verifiable skills credentials recognised by partner institutions.
Scalable model adaptable to schools, NGOs, and enterprises in multiple languages and cultural contexts.
Key technologies:
Our solution leverages a multi-layered technology stack:
Artificial Intelligence (AI) – Adaptive learning algorithms for personalised cyber training and real-time threat simulation.
Post-Quantum Cryptography (PQC) – Future-proof encryption to secure personal data and digital identities.
Blockchain – Decentralised, tamper-proof credentialing for skills verification and trust-building.
Gamification Engine – Engagement-driven learning modules inspired by esports to boost participation and retention.
Secure Cloud Infrastructure – GDPR-compliant, scalable hosting for safe global access.
Unique Characteristics:
Our solution is the first gamified security layer that merges AI-driven education, post-quantum encryption, and blockchain-backed trust into an inclusive digital platform.
Unlike traditional training tools, it uses esports-inspired engagement mechanics to make cybersecurity and digital skills learning highly interactive and appealing to diverse audiences, including underserved communities.
Its modular architecture allows schools, governments, and enterprises to create closed, secure environments for their own content, while still connecting to a global skills ecosystem—bridging education, safety, and economic inclusion in one scalable model.
Sustainable Change:
Our solution builds long-term digital resilience by embedding cybersecurity awareness, AI literacy, and safe online practices into daily engagement—turning learning into a habit rather than a one-off activity.
By making security and digital skills accessible, engaging, and relevant through gamified mechanics, we empower individuals and communities to participate safely in the digital economy.
Follow-on effects include:

Reduced cyber risks and fraud, protecting livelihoods and data.
Improved employability through continuous skills upskilling in AI and digital tools.
Greater inclusion of marginalized groups in the digital economy.
Institutional adoption of secure, gamified training across education, workforce development, and public services—creating a self-reinforcing ecosystem of safe, skilled digital citizens.
Funding Sources:
We've got: 

100+K USD in grants 
350+K USD in pre-seed capital from VCs
Primary thematic focus area: Inclusive Digital Innovation Skills & Entrepreneurial Talent Development
Summary: Valvur is an AI-powered platform that combines gamified cybersecurity training, AI-driven monitoring, and post-quantum encryption to create a safe and inclusive digital environment for underserved communities. The platform provides interactive learning experiences to teach cyber hygiene, identity protection, and scam avoidance, with the aim of increasing participation in the digital economy through secure engagement.

Title: Bfarm-tech; Mechanization Services, Advisory, Insurance, and E-commerce
Subtitle: Empowering farmers with integrated mechanization services, expert advice, insurance options, and a seamless e-commerce platform for sustainable agricultural growth.
Problem Statement:
Smallholder farmers face significant challenges, including reliance on traditional tools that result in labor-intensive, time-consuming practices and low productivity. They often suffer from damage caused by flooding and lack awareness of available technologies. Additionally, access to necessary inputs for agricultural activities is limited, and there is a shortage of skilled mechanics and operators for mechanization services.
Bfarm-Tech addresses these issues by offering a multilingual, user-friendly digital platform that provides comprehensive technology solutions for smallholder farmers. The platform connects farmers with service providers and experts through a Software as a Service (SaaS) model. By improving productivity and market coordination, Bfarm-Tech aims to transform agricultural practices in Ethiopia.
Solution Overview:
Bfarm-Tech is a digital platform that enhances agricultural mechanization services for smallholder farmers by allowing them to register and request services via a mobile app, USSD, or call center. The platform uses IoT technology for real-time monitoring of machinery and AI algorithms for efficient service matching and supply-demand optimization. It operates on a SaaS model, providing tools for service providers, while also offering climate-smart agricultural advice through SMS alerts, on the insurance also the farmers registered and get access to insurance form the company. The platform also includes a marketplace where farmers can purchase inputs and sell their produce directly to consumers, enhancing market access and reducing reliance on intermediaries.
Bfarm-Tech leverages strategic partnerships with key stakeholders, including government agencies like the Ministry of Agriculture, NGOs such as the Agricultural Transformation Agency, and private sector entities like Ethiotelecom, insurance company. These collaborations facilitate access to resources, expertise, and funding, enhancing the platform's reach and effectiveness. The partnership model focuses on co-creation and shared objectives, enabling the integration of technology, training programs, and advisory services that collectively empower smallholder farmers. This collaborative approach fosters innovation and strengthens the agricultural ecosystem in Ethiopia.

Title: Slow-Release Biochar for Climate-Resilient and Productive Farming
Subtitle: Transforming agricultural waste into slow-release biochar fertilizer to restore soils, boost yields, and lock carbon for over 1,000 years.
Problem Statement: Smallholder farmers in Senegal face declining soil fertility, high costs of synthetic fertilizers, and crop losses from climate stress. Meanwhile, vast amounts of agricultural waste are burned or left to rot, releasing methane and black carbon, contributing to climate change and air pollution. Existing soil amendments are costly, inconsistent, or inaccessible, leaving farmers trapped in a cycle of low yields, high expenses, and environmental degradation.
Solution Overview: Agrokoom transforms local agricultural residues into a slow-release biochar-based fertilizer through controlled pyrolysis, converting wastes such as peanut shells and millet stalks into a carbon-rich soil amendment that improves fertility, retains nutrients, and locks carbon in the soil for over 1,000 years. Using mobile pyrolysis units, the process avoids open burning and associated black carbon emissions, while producing consistent, high-quality biochar. The product is enriched, packaged in 50 kg sacks, and delivered to smallholder farmers with training on optimal application, requiring only one application per crop cycle to reduce costs and labor. Implementation combines pyrolysis technology, soil fertility management practices, and a Monitoring, Reporting, and Verification (MRV) system to track carbon sequestration, yield gains, and reduced fertilizer use. Partnerships with farmer cooperatives ensure biomass supply and distribution, while research institutes conduct soil and crop performance analysis, municipal waste units support collection logistics, and carbon market actors enable future credit sales. This integrated, community-based model creates a circular economy where agricultural waste becomes a valuable input, boosting productivity, enhancing resilience, and delivering measurable climate benefits.
Solution Provider(s): Agrokoom – agri-climate startup in Senegal specializing in biochar production, soil regeneration, and climate-smart agriculture (Agriculture, Climate & Environment), Regional Farmer Cooperatives  – grassroots organizations supplying biomass, facilitating farmer training, and supporting product distribution (Agriculture, Rural Development), Senegalese Institute of Agricultural Research (ISRA) – national research body conducting soil analysis, agronomic trials, and impact monitoring (Agricultural Research, Science & Technology), Municipal Waste Management Units – local government services managing biomass collection logistics and waste valorization (Public Services, Waste Management), Carbon Finance Advisors – independent consultants supporting MRV design, carbon certification, and market access (Climate Finance, Environmental Consulting).
Implementation location(s): The solution has been implemented in Senegal, specifically in the Dakar and Thiès regions, where local farmer cooperatives and communities collaborate with Agrokoom and partners to produce and distribute slow-release biochar fertilizer.
Implementation timeline(s): The project was launched in February 2024 and is ongoing, with full-scale implementation planned through 2027.
Duration to pilot in a new geography: The estimated duration to pilot the solution in a new geography is approximately 12 to 18 months. This period includes initial community engagement, biomass supply chain setup, installation of pyrolysis units, training of farmers, and monitoring of agronomic and environmental impacts. Full implementation and scaling beyond the pilot phase typically require an additional 2 to 3 years, depending on local conditions and partnerships.
SDGs addressed: SDG 15 (Life on Land);SDG 13 (Climate Action);SDG 2 (Zero Hunger);
Desired impact: The solution aims to restore soil fertility and boost crop yields for smallholder farmers while reducing reliance on costly synthetic fertilizers. It sequesters carbon in soils for over 1,000 years, creating a circular economy by turning agricultural waste into valuable biochar and cutting emissions from open burning. Key impacts include yield increases of up to 25%, a 40% reduction in synthetic fertilizer use, and carbon sequestration of 2 to 5 tons CO₂ equivalent per hectare annually. The project also diverts significant amounts of agricultural waste from burning, reducing black carbon and methane emissions, generates local employment in biomass collection and biochar production, and establishes MRV systems for carbon credit certification and climate finance access.
Key technologies: The solution uses controlled pyrolysis technology to convert agricultural biomass into high-quality biochar without open burning, mobile pyrolysis units for on-site processing in farming communities, nutrient enrichment techniques for slow-release fertilization, and digital Monitoring, Reporting, and Verification (MRV) systems to measure carbon sequestration, yield improvements, and reduced input use, supporting impact tracking and carbon credit certification.
Unique Characteristics: The solution’s unique characteristics include its integrated circular economy model that transforms local agricultural waste into valuable, slow-release biochar fertilizer, reducing reliance on costly synthetic inputs. Its use of mobile pyrolysis units enables decentralized, community-based production, lowering logistics barriers and emissions from open burning. The combination of soil fertility improvement with robust MRV systems for carbon sequestration measurement positions the solution for carbon finance opportunities. Strong partnerships with farmer cooperatives, research institutes, municipal services, and carbon market experts create a collaborative ecosystem that enhances adoption, scalability, and climate impact making it both socially inclusive and environmentally innovative.
Sustainable Change: The solution drives sustainable, systemic change by empowering smallholder farmers to break the cycle of soil degradation and low productivity through accessible, affordable, and climate-smart biochar fertilizer. By converting agricultural waste into a valuable soil amendment, it fosters a circular economy that reduces environmental pollution and greenhouse gas emissions. Improved soil health increases crop yields and resilience to climate stress, enhancing food security and farmer incomes. The integration of MRV systems enables carbon credit generation, creating new financial incentives for sustainable farming. Through partnerships and capacity-building, the approach builds local expertise and strengthens community networks, ensuring long-term adoption and scaling. Collectively, these effects lead to healthier ecosystems, reduced poverty, and meaningful contributions to climate mitigation, establishing a replicable model for resilient agricultural development.
Funding Sources: The solution has been funded through a combination of sources including seed funding from impact investors focused on climate and agriculture, grants from international development agencies supporting sustainable farming and climate resilience.
Primary thematic focus area: Innovation Acceleration & Knowledge Sharing
Summary: Agrokoom’s biochar-based solution addresses declining soil fertility, climate stress, and environmental pollution by transforming agricultural waste into a sustainable, slow-release fertilizer. The integration of climate-smart practices, mobile pyrolysis units, and carbon sequestration tracking offers significant potential, but scalability remains a challenge without additional partnerships and a detailed sustainability model.

Title: MSME ERP App
Subtitle: This is an app that is geared towards MSME in order to digitise their operations and record keeping and also provide a basis for providing finance to them.
Problem Statement:
Micro, Small, and Medium-sized Enterprises (MSMEs) account for approximately 98% of all businesses in Kenya, making them the backbone of the Kenyan economy. These enterprises are vital for job creation, contributing significantly to the country's GDP and overall economic transformation. As per KNBS data majority of the MSMEs in Kenya are female owned with some estimates putting them at 58%. 

The owners of these SMEs have the business management and accounting knowledge required to run these businesses in with the requisite automation, compliance with the law and with the maintenance of proper records. These lack of compliance with laws leads to penalties and fines from the various government agencies and due to the lack of proper record keeping the MSMEs lack the documentation required to obtain financing from the formal financing channels, this leaves them with the option of shylocks who charge exorbitant interest rates making their loans counter productive leading to the closure of the MSMEs.
Solution Overview:
The solution proposes to develop an all round ERP geared for MSMEs in Kenya. The MSMEs will be provided an opportunity to digitise not only their records but also their operations. This will enable them to run their operations efficiently and effectively. The MSME ERP will have the following functionalities: 
1. Transactions recording: business owners will be provided with an opportunity to record their transactions on a daily basis so as to provide a digital and comprehensive record of all their undertakings. 
2. Human resource management: the ERP will provide a one stop shop for affairs to do with human resources management, including records filings (captured via phone camera), payroll management and performance evaluation. 
3. Financial accounting: from the transactions and entries entered into the ERP, the app will generate final financial statements including income statement and the statement of financial position, in addition to the other financial documents such as the cashflow statement
4. Inventory management: upon receiving inventory the business people are required to update inventory records in the ERP, reductions in the inventory are also to be recorded and when the inventory levels reach a pre-determined re-order level the a notice is sent to the business person to place an order. In advanced versions of the ERP an order will be automatically placed with the supplier to meet stock replenishment requirements. 
5. Statutory deductions: The ERP will compute the due statutory payments for the respective payment and provide an output specifying which ones needs to be paid and the date when they need to be paid. It will also send a reminder one week in advance and on morning of the day of the payment. This will ensure that the MSMEs comply with the requirements on statutory deductions and avoid payments of fines and penalties. 
6. Credit/Debt Management: the app will have a functionality in which all credit transactions will be recorded accompanied by their relevant additional details such as payment date. This will facilitate proper management of both incoming and outgoing debt.

8. Finance: MSMEs who are consistent in the use of the ERP and on a positive financial trajectory will be provided with low cost loans to meet their working capital requirements. This finance will serve as an attraction for the MSMES to join and retention point for the MSMES to join and utilise the ERP consistently. The low/no cost finance will be provided from part of the revenues generated by the ERP from its revenue streams.

The ERP will run on the freemium model where basic services offered are absolutely free, premium services are paid for. Monetisation of the MSME ERP is through: periodic subscription fees for premium services, sale of aids to trade on the platform (e.g. micro, insurance) and third party adverts on the platform.

Collaborations and partnerships will be required with MSMEs, finance organisations, insurance companies, manufacturers and producers.

Title: Consultant Cloud - a skills development platform for Salesforce professionals
Subtitle: Skills development platform for current and aspiring salesforce professionals, offering premium content, practice exams, AI prompts, and job listings to help them upskill, certify, and grow globally.
Problem Statement:
Demand for skilled professionals is rising across the global Salesforce ecosystem, yet a persistent skills gap prevents many from fully accessing available employment opportunities. Furthermore, as products evolve rapidly and integrate AI, professionals must engage in continuous learning to stay competitive. While resources do exist, they are often fragmented and difficult to navigate, making it challenging for professionals to stay up to date while working within a constantly changing system.

Consultant Cloud addresses this challenge by providing a single platform where individuals can interact with the salesforce community, develop and refresh their skills, gain certifications, and connect with employment opportunities across the ecosystem. Furthermore, this scalable solution is designed not only to up-skill and retrain individuals for Salesforce-related roles but also to adapt in the future, enabling the training and up-skilling of tech professionals in other systems as new opportunities emerge.
Solution Overview:
ConsultantCloud is a centralised learning and career support platform for Salesforce professionals. Through a curated library of study guides, blogs, extensions, and practice exams—combined with AI-powered, on-demand study prompts (CC-GPT) and a jobs board—it transforms the often scattered journey of certification and career-building into a cohesive, streamlined experience. A tiered subscription model with free, professional, and enterprise plans lets individual users and businesses scale their engagement based on needs and budget. Six months full free access is also available to job seekers. 

Methodologies & Technologies
A platform which provides centralised learning resources; curated information and blogs; practice exams; a concise list of useful chrome extensions and web apps; gAI tooling with CC-GPT; a jobs board and community support.
Community-driven content curation ensures timely, high-quality resources while reducing the chaos of decentralised learning.
AI-assisted personalisation via CC-GPT allows users immediate, tailored guidance during study sessions.
Modern web architecture underpins the platform, optimising for scalability, security, and performance.

Partnerships & Collaboration Models
While independent from Salesforce, the platform harnesses community contributions and external content (under fair use) to enrich its offerings.
Event sponsorship and demo appearances—such as Irish Dreamin’ 2025—raise brand visibility and foster community engagement.
User-driven collaboration features (e.g., “Pitch Me”) invite ongoing peer input, feedback, and co-creation.
Implementation location(s): As an operational software platform, it is available for users to sign up and access globally, without geographic restrictions.
SDGs addressed: SDG 4 (Quality Education);SDG 8 (Decent Work and Economic Growth);SDG 10 (Reduced Inequalities);
Desired impact: The desired impact of Consultant Cloud is to close the Salesforce skills gap by providing accessible, community-driven training and certification support that enhances employability, workforce mobility and continuous skills development. By combining curated content, AI-enabled learning prompts, and direct links to job opportunities, the platform aims to help thousands of professionals annually achieve certifications and secure meaningful employment in a sector projected to generate approximately 9 million jobs globally by 2026. Through its free tier and offerings for job seekers, this easily accessible platform lowers barriers for underrepresented groups, promoting inclusion and equity, while its scalable enterprise model provides a long-term framework for digital workforce development that can be adapted to other technologies as new opportunities arise.
Key technologies:
Php/laravel system for user and application management
Deployed on Heroku for the most advanced and secure hosting platform
We integrate with the latest AI models to help users with their Salesforce work/ skills development
Unique Characteristics: This solution is unique because it harnesses the collective expertise of the Salesforce community to create a resource hub tailored to the needs of professionals who work within a rapidly evolving digital system. Community-generated content ensures relevance and practical value, while AI provides study prompts that support continuous upskilling and reskilling. Over time, the platform will also expand through partnerships across the Salesforce ecosystem, creating mutual value and unlocking new opportunities for collaboration.
Sustainable Change: Consultant Cloud drives sustainable, systematic change by closing the Salesforce skills gap through an accessible, scalable, and inclusive platform. By integrating community-driven content, AI-enabled study support, and direct connections to employment, it aims to build a continuous pipeline of skilled professionals equipped for digital careers. This model not only enhances individual economic mobility but also strengthens business productivity and competitiveness across the Salesforce ecosystem. Importantly, the platform’s adaptability means it can expand to other digital systems over time, offering a long-term workforce development tool that supports reskilling, reduces barriers to employment, and fosters resilience in a rapidly changing digital economy.
Funding Sources: Self funded so far.
Primary thematic focus area: Inclusive Digital Innovation Skills & Entrepreneurial Talent Development
Summary: Consultant Cloud is a centralized learning and career support platform for Salesforce professionals, aiming to address the skills gap in the Salesforce ecosystem through AI-powered personalized learning, practice exams, and a job board.

Title: Konnectik - Connecting Communities, Empowering Cities.
Subtitle: Seamless, time-based Wi-Fi access via mobile app, bridging the digital divide for students and underserved communities.
Problem Statement: In Cameroon, high mobile data costs and unreliable connectivity exclude millions—especially students and low-income workers—from the digital economy. This creates barriers to education, jobs, entrepreneurship, and financial inclusion.
Solution Overview:
Konnectik is a Connectivity-as-a-Service (CaaS) platform delivering localized Wi-Fi access zones (K-Zones) in underserved urban neighborhoods. Users connect through a mobile application that:
- Maps nearby Wi-Fi zones,
- Offers time-based unlimited internet packages (2h, 5h, 24h),
- Provides freemium access and referral incentives,
- Integrates with mobile money (MTN, Orange) for seamless payments.

I. Technologies used:
1. High bandwidth Wi-Fi network for resilient connectivity,
2. Mobile app with mobile money payment integrations/APIs,
3. Artificial intelligence for hotspot management and automation,

II. Methodology - Go-to Market Strategy:
1. Deploy pilot in student housing zones (PK17, University of Douala),
2. Use freemium model and peer referrals to accelerate adoption,
3. Scale to new communities through modular Wi-Fi nodes.

III. Collaboration model:
1. Local institutions (universities, housing authorities) for deployment access,
2. Technical partnerships with Starlink, MikroTik, and mobile money providers,
3. Community ambassadors and influencers for outreach.
Solution Provider(s): Starlink (SpaceX) – Satellite internet provider (Connectivity backbone), MikroTik – Networking equipment manufacturer (Routers, Access Points), Pawapay – Mobile payment platforms (Fintech, Digital Payments), Universities/Residences (PK17 Zone) – Institutional and Residential partner for pilot site (Education sector).
Duration to pilot in a new geography: 3 - 6 months
SDGs addressed: SDG 4 (Quality Education);SDG 10 (Reduced Inequalities);SDG 11 (Sustainable Cities and Communities);
Desired impact:
I. Objectives:
1. Bridge the digital divide by offering affordable, reliable Wi-Fi in underserved communities.
2. Enable students, MSMEs, and low-income households to participate in the digital economy.
3. Foster inclusive access to education, jobs, and entrepreneurship.

II. Key Impacts:
- Digital inclusion: Up to 300 concurrent users per zone connected affordably during PoC.
- Economic empowerment: Lowering internet costs by 40–60% compared to mobile data, enabling MSMEs and freelancers to operate online.
- Job creation: Local employment opportunities in installation, maintenance, and community ambassador roles.
- Education: Improved access to e-learning for hundreds of students per deployment zone.
Key technologies:
- AI Automation: For hotspot management, accounting, and real-time usage control.
- Wireless Internet Infrastructure: MikroTik routers, and Starlink satellite backbone for resilient connectivity.
- Mobile Application: Offers zone mapping, package purchases, and seamless connection management.
- Payment Integration: Mobile money APIs (MTN, Orange) for fast, cashless access.
Unique Characteristics:
- Localized Wi-Fi CaaS model: Affordable, time-based unlimited access (2h, 5h, 24h), unlike costly data bundles from telcos.
- Inclusive business model: Freemium access, referral rewards, and monthly free time to lower entry barriers.
- Seamless user experience: Map-based zone discovery, auto-connection, transparent session timers.
- Community-first approach: Deployed in social housing and student zones where telcos have weak incentives.
- Scalability: Modular design allows rapid replication across urban Africa with minimal infrastructure.
Sustainable Change:
I. Theory of Change:
1. Access: Deploy localized Wi-Fi zones to make internet affordable and reliable.
2. Adoption: Students and MSMEs use connectivity for education, digital work, and commerce.
3. Empowerment: Communities reduce digital exclusion, improve livelihoods, and gain equal access to opportunities.
4. Scale: Replicable model expands zone by zone, fostering a self-sustaining ecosystem of users, SMEs, and institutional partners.

II. Follow-on Effects:
1. Increased digital literacy and inclusion across urban youth.
2. Growth of MSMEs and startups leveraging affordable connectivity.
3. Support for national digital transformation agendas (SND30, SDG 9).
4. Long-term systemic change by embedding internet access as a basic utility for social and economic development.
