Title: ClimaTerra Créatif: FinTech et storytelling pour une économie digitale inclusive
Subtitle: An integrated digital solution combining FinTech, agroecology, and visual storytelling to boost financial inclusion and creative entrepreneurship in the DRC.
Problem Statement: In the Democratic Republic of the Congo, rural communities face limited access to financial services, low digital literacy, and underutilized creative potential. These challenges hinder inclusive economic growth, especially for youth and women. Climate vulnerability further exacerbates poverty and marginalization. There is a pressing need for integrated solutions that bridge the digital divide, promote financial inclusion, and empower local innovation through culturally resonant tools.
Solution Overview:
ClimaTerra Créatif is a hybrid digital solution developed by ADE RDC that integrates FinTech, agroecology, and creative storytelling to foster inclusive growth in underserved communities of the DRC.

How the Solution Works
ClimaTerra Pay and TikaWallet provide secure, mobile-based financial services tailored to rural users, enabling access to savings, payments, and climate-linked incentives.

Agroecological training modules are delivered through visual content and community workshops, promoting sustainable farming practices.

TikTok and other digital platforms are used to disseminate educational and inspirational content, created by local youth and artists, to raise awareness and drive engagement.

The solution is designed to be low-bandwidth friendly, multilingual, and culturally adapted to local realities.

Methodologies and Technologies
Human-centered design ensures the tools are intuitive and accessible to users with limited digital experience.

Blockchain-inspired transparency in TikaWallet supports traceable transactions and builds trust.

Open data mapping helps identify climate risks and tailor agroecological responses.

Creative storytelling methodologies empower youth to produce content that reflects local challenges and aspirations.

Partnerships and Collaboration Models
ADE collaborates with local cooperatives, youth groups, and community leaders to co-create content and ensure adoption.

Strategic partnerships with UNESCO, FAO, and GIZ provide technical support and validation.

Engagement with digital influencers and artists amplifies reach and cultural relevance.

ADE is building alliances with financial institutions and mobile operators to scale the FinTech components.

UNESCO – United Nations Educational, Scientific and Cultural Organization – International organization supporting cultural innovation, education, and youth engagement.  FAO – Food and Agriculture Organization of the United Nations – International organization providing technical expertise in agroecology and sustainable food systems. TikTok Creators and Digital Influencers – Independent creatives amplifying ADE’s messaging through culturally resonant visual campaigns.

Title: TARO INNOV’FOOD – Transformation numérique et durable du taro en super-aliments
Subtitle: Plateforme agroalimentaire inclusive valorisant le taro local grâce à la transformation durable, aux outils numériques et à l’inclusion des femmes et des jeunes
Problem Statement: En RDC, l’insécurité alimentaire, les pertes post-récolte et la dépendance aux importations alimentaires sont aggravées par la faible transformation des produits locaux et un accès limité aux marchés numériques. Le taro, tubercule nutritif (Mbala ya Langa), reste sous-exploité, privant les producteurs et consommateurs d’une opportunité économique et nutritionnelle.
Solution Overview: En RDC, l’insécurité alimentaire, les pertes post-récolte et la dépendance aux importations alimentaires sont aggravées par la faible transformation des produits locaux et un accès limité aux marchés numériques. Le taro, tubercule nutritif (Mbala ya Langa), reste sous-exploité, privant les producteurs et consommateurs d’une opportunité économique et nutritionnelle.
Solution Provider(s): ,GEEC SARL – Groupe d’Expertise Environnementale et de Conservation Secteur : Agroalimentaire durable et économie circulaire  AGRIFED – Appui au développement agricole et agroalimentaire  ONU Femmes – RDC – Inclusion et autonomisation économique des femmes  Ecosynerge Afrique – Innovation verte et énergies renouvelables
Implementation location(s): République Démocratique du Congo (RDC) – Kinshasa :  Commune de Mont-Ngafula – Site principal de transformation et de conditionnement.  Commune de Limete – Point de distribution et coordination logistique.  Commune de Gombe et Kasa-Vubu – Points de vente et partenaires distributeurs.   Province du Kongo-Central – Kisantu et Kasangulu :  Zones d’approvisionnement en taro auprès des producteurs locaux et coopératives agricoles partenaires.
Implementation timeline(s): Lieu(x) de mise en œuvre  République Démocratique du Congo – Kinshasa : Production et transformation dans nos installations locales ; distribution dans plusieurs communes (Mont-Ngafula, Limete, Gombe, Kasa-Vubu).  RDC – Province du Kongo-Central : Approvisionnement en taro auprès des producteurs locaux (Kisantu, Kasangulu).    ---  Calendrier de mise en œuvre  Phase pilote : Janvier 2025 – Mars 2025 (tests de recettes, validation des procédés de transformation, premiers retours consommateurs).  Phase opérationnelle actuelle : Avril 2025 – en cours (lancement commercial, développement de la distribution et des ventes physiques & en ligne).   .

SDGs addressed: SDG 2 (Zero Hunger);SDG 3 (Good Health and Well-being);SDG 1 (No Poverty);
Desired impact:
22. Impact souhaité de la solution

Objectifs de la solution

1. Valoriser le taro (Mbala ya Langa) en le transformant en une gamme de produits alimentaires nutritifs, modernes et accessibles.


2. Réduire le gaspillage post-récolte grâce à des procédés de conservation et de transformation adaptés.


3. Créer des emplois verts et inclusifs pour les femmes et les jeunes, en particulier dans les zones rurales et périurbaines.


4. Renforcer la sécurité alimentaire en offrant des alternatives locales et saines aux produits importés.


5. Promouvoir une production durable à faible empreinte carbone grâce à l’utilisation d’équipements écoénergétiques et d’emballages écologiques.

 Principales réalisations / impacts attendus (quantifiables)

1. Impact économique et emploi

+50 emplois directs créés d’ici 3 ans (production, emballage, logistique, vente).

+150 emplois indirects générés dans la chaîne de valeur (agriculteurs, transporteurs, revendeurs).

Augmentation de 30 à 40 % des revenus des agriculteurs partenaires grâce à la revalorisation du taro.


2. Impact social et nutritionnel

1 500 à 2 000 ménages bénéficiaires directs par an, ayant accès à des produits nutritifs à base de taro.

Amélioration de l’apport nutritionnel (fibres, vitamines, minéraux) dans les foyers ciblés.

Formation de 200 femmes transformatrices et 100 jeunes aux techniques de transformation et de gestion agroalimentaire.


3. Impact environnemental

Réduction de 35 % des pertes post-récolte de taro grâce au séchage solaire et à la transformation.

Utilisation d’équipements écoénergétiques réduisant la consommation d’énergie de 40 % par rapport aux procédés traditionnels.

Adoption d’emballages recyclables ou biodégradables réduisant les déchets plastiques.
Key technologies:
La solution TARO INNOV’FOOD intègre plusieurs technologies adaptées au contexte local et axées sur l’efficacité, la durabilité et l’accessibilité :

1. Technologies de transformation agroalimentaire écoénergétiques :

Séchoirs solaires pour la déshydratation du taro, réduisant la consommation d’énergie et les pertes post-récolte.

Mini-extrudeuses pour la fabrication de spaghetti, biscuits et snacks à base de taro.

Broyeurs et moulins à faible consommation pour la production de farine fine.

2. Technologies de conservation et conditionnement :

Emballages alimentaires écologiques (biodégradables ou recyclables) adaptés à la conservation des produits.

Procédés de mise sous vide pour prolonger la durée de conservation sans additifs chimiques.

3. Technologies digitales :

CRM simplifié (WhatsApp Business, Airtable, Trello) pour la gestion des clients et commandes.

Plateforme web pour la présentation des produits et la prise de commandes.

Marketing digital via réseaux sociaux pour le ciblage et l’engagement des clients.
Unique Characteristics:
Notre solution est unique par :

1. Diversification inédite du taro : transformation en une large gamme de produits modernes (farine, spaghetti, bouillie, biscuits, beignets, pain).

2. Modèle économique inclusif : intégration directe des agriculteurs, femmes transformatrices et jeunes dans la chaîne de valeur.


3. Technologie frugale et durable : utilisation d’équipements simples, à faible consommation, adaptés au contexte congolais.


4. Approche locale et culturelle : valorisation d’un produit patrimonial (Mbala ya Langa) tout en le modernisant pour répondre aux attentes des consommateurs urbains.


5. Distribution hybride : combinaison de ventes physiques (marchés, points de vente) et digitales (site web, réseaux sociaux).
Sustainable Change:
Notre théorie du changement repose sur trois effets majeurs :

1. Économique

Création d’emplois verts pour les femmes et les jeunes.

Augmentation des revenus des agriculteurs grâce à la valorisation d’une culture locale.

Développement d’une filière taro compétitive en RDC.


2. Social et nutritionnel

Amélioration de l’accès à des produits alimentaires locaux, nutritifs et abordables.

Réduction de la dépendance aux importations alimentaires.

Renforcement de l’autonomie économique des groupes marginalisés.


3. Environnemental

Réduction du gaspillage post-récolte.

Promotion d’une production et transformation à faible empreinte carbone.

Adoption d’emballages durables et réduction des déchets alimentaires.

Title: Harnessing AI to Empower Women in Tech in Northeast Nigeria
Subtitle: An inclusive AI-powered digital skills training initiative for women to close the gender gap in tech and promote sustainable economic growth in underserved regions of Nigeria.
Problem Statement: In Northeast Nigeria, women, especially those displaced by conflict, face a painful reality: limited access to digital education, employment, and leadership. This systemic exclusion silences their potential and deepens inequality in a fast-moving digital economy.
Solution Overview:
Our solution, Empowering Women in Tech, is more than a program, it’s a lifeline. In a region devastated by insurgency and poverty, we offer hope through technology.

We provide women and girls with hands-on training in software development, digital literacy, and artificial intelligence. Through peer mentorship, emotional support, and leadership coaching, we help women reclaim their confidence, tell their stories through code, and build solutions for their communities.

This project integrates AI-powered learning platforms, cloud-based tools, and locally adapted training materials. Each cohort receives devices, data access, and real-world project experience to ensure learning is practical and lasting.

We work hand-in-hand with traditional leaders, grassroots groups, international innovation centers, and women-led tech networks. Our strength lies in collaboration, uniting voices across sectors to create a digital economy where no woman is left behind.
Solution Provider(s): Future Prowess Foundation (NGO, Tech & Empowerment), Dunin-Deshpande Queen’s Innovation Centre (Academia, Entrepreneurship Accelerator), Women Techmakers (Tech, Community Support), Development Hub (Local ICT training organization)
Implementation location(s): Maiduguri, Borno State, Nigeria – a region where many of our participants are internally displaced women, widows, or survivors of gender-based violence.
Implementation timeline(s): Phase I: March – November 2023 (Initial pilot in Maiduguri, focused on digital literacy and software development) Phase II: August 2024 – July 2025 (Ongoing phase, integrating AI and expanding to additional states in Northeast Nigeria)

Title: Medmum Digital Hub: Empowering Women Through Health, Skills and Tech
Subtitle: A low-tech digital platform supporting maternal health, local skills, and economic independence for vulnerable women and girls in climate-affected areas of Northeast Nigeria.
Problem Statement: In Northeast Nigeria, maternal deaths, malnutrition, early marriage, and poverty are widespread. Many women and girls lack access to health care, digital tools, education, and economic opportunities. Climate change especially flooding makes things worse by displacing families, destroying farms, and increasing food insecurity. Girls are often forced into marriage early, silencing their voices and limiting their futures.
Solution Overview:
Medmum Digital Hub is a simple, mobile-accessible platform that supports pregnant and nursing mothers and empowers young women in underserved communities.

How it works:
• Provides voice-enabled maternal health tips and climate-resilient nutrition advice.

• Offers offline-first digital skill training (tailoring, soap making, agro-processing, solar installation, Henna decor, modern kitchen utensils installation).

• Shares flood alerts and health guidance using local languages.

• Features storytelling campaigns “Ripe Before Sow” to delay early marriage.

Technologies Used:
• Mobile-friendly platform with voice and pictorial UI for low literacy

• Offline LMS (learning system) powered by solar digital kiosks

• USSD/SMS and IoT for flood early warning and health alerts

Partnerships:
• Collaboration with local midwives, community health workers, women's groups, and digital inclusion engineers.

• In discussion with tech NGOs and local radio stations for content delivery.
Solution Provider(s): Medmum and Infant Care – Civil Society NGO focused on maternal health and women empowerment, Local Women’s Cooperative Associations – Livelihood training and peer support, Community Health Extension Workers – Health outreach and maternal care, Radio Gombe (proposed) – Broadcast of digital health content,  Engineers, Without Borders Nigeria (potential partner) or Nascom Embedded – Technical design of digital kiosks
Duration to pilot in a new geography: 6 to 9 months, depending on infrastructure and partner engagement
SDGs addressed: SDG 3 (Good Health and Well-being);SDG 5 (Gender Equality);SDG 13 (Climate Action);
Desired impact:
Objectives:
• Improve maternal health and nutrition in rural, flood-prone areas

• Reduce early marriage through digital awareness

•Build self-reliance in women through digital skills and entrepreneurship

Key Impacts (3-year projection):
• Reach 10,000+ women with mobile health and climate education

• Train 5,000 women and girls in livelihood skills

• Reduce maternal deaths and early marriage in pilot areas by 30%

• Provide solar-powered kiosks in 50 underserved villages
Key technologies:
• Mobile Web App with voice and image-based UI

• Offline Learning Management System (LMS)

• USSD/SMS for rural engagement

• IoT sensors for local flood alerts

• Solar-powered digital kiosks
Unique Characteristics:
• Combines engineering, digital health, local economy, and gender advocacy in one platform

• Designed for low-connectivity, low-literacy users

• Uses community storytelling and cultural sensitivity (“Ripe Before Sow”) to change harmful traditions

• Tech-enabled but community-powered—built with and for local women

• Low-cost, modular, and scalable across rural regions
Sustainable Change:
This solution addresses root causes of poverty, exclusion, and inequality. It helps women gain knowledge, voice, and income. As women contribute to their households, they gain respect and decision-making power. Delaying early marriage leads to healthier mothers and children. Tech-enabled awareness reduces maternal deaths and increases food security.

The long-term effect is a more equal, resilient, and digitally included society, where local women are not just beneficiaries, but leaders of change.
Funding Sources: The solution has been self-funded so far, through personal savings and small community contributions. We are currently exploring partnerships with NGOs, development organizations, and local government bodies for pilot-stage support and technical collaboration. Our aim is to attract both grant funding and social impact investment to scale the solution across Northeast Nigeria and similar vulnerable regions.

Title: santéConnect jeunes: Inclusive digital platform for adolescents and young people to access sexual and reproductive health services in Goma
Subtitle: Empowering youth with access to quality sexual and reproductive health services though digital tools, community education, and advocacy in vulnerable settings
Problem Statement:
santéConnect jeunes – Project Statement (UNDCO style)
The santéConnect jeunes project aims to improve access to quality sexual and reproductive health (SRH) services for adolescents and young adults, particularly in vulnerable areas of the Kivu region in the Democratic Republic of Congo. By combining digital tools, community education, peer mobilization, and advocacy, the project seeks to strengthen knowledge, reduce risky behaviors, combat gender-based violence, and promote youth empowerment. It supports national efforts in advancing sexual and reproductive health and rights, HIV/AIDS prevention, and meaningful youth participation in social transformation.
Solution Overview:
Detailed Description of How the Solution Works

The proposed solution is an integrated community-based system combining awareness-raising, proximity services, and digital innovation, aimed at improving sexual and reproductive health (SRH), ecological resilience, or sustainable resource management in vulnerable areas.

Overall Functioning:
Initial Participatory Assessment: A multidisciplinary team (health, environment, ICT, sociology) conducts data collection in target areas through surveys, focus groups, and interviews with local leaders.
Field Activity Deployment: Activities include awareness campaigns, training of community outreach workers, distribution of kits/services, mobile medical or environmental interventions, and installation of digital tools (depending on project scope).
Use of a Community Digital Tool (e.g., mobile app, USSD platform, or web-based system) to:
Inform and educate beneficiaries,
Collect and centralize local needs,
Track service delivery,
Monitor impacts in real time using interactive dashboards.
Feedback and Continuous Improvement: Quarterly evaluation meetings are held with stakeholders to adjust and optimize implementation.

2. Implementation Methodology

The implementation follows five key phases:

Phase 1: Planning and Stakeholder Mobilization
Identification of specific needs in the target areas.
Selection and engagement of local actors (authorities, CSOs, youth, women, schools, etc.).
Initial training of the core project team and field collaborators.

Phase 2: Co-Design and Local Adaptation
Co-creation workshops with communities to define interventions, key messages, and tools.
Cultural and linguistic adaptation of materials and technologies (e.g., translations, pictograms, audio formats).

Phase 3: Field Implementation
Launch of field activities (awareness, environmental or health diagnostics, etc.).
Ongoing sessions facilitated by trained community agents.
Technical interventions (e.g., ecological restoration, mobile health clinics, contraceptive distribution).

Phase 4: Digital Integration and Monitoring
Deployment of an information management system (mobile app or dashboard).
Participatory monitoring using qualitative and quantitative indicators.
Regular assessments with local partners and program adjustment.

Phase 5: Capitalization and Sustainability
Documentation of achievements, best practices, and lessons learned.*
Organization of local or regional exchange forums.
Capacity building of local actors for long-term ownership.

3. Technologies Used
Depending on the project domain, the following technologies are applied:
Area	Technologies Used
Data Collection	KoboToolbox, ODK, SurveyCTO
Awareness-Raising	Community radio, SMS, USSD, interactive posters
Monitoring & Evaluation	Power BI, Google Data Studio, GIS dashboards
Digital Services	SRH or environment mobile app, WhatsApp chatbot, QR codes
Mobile Health	Digital health records, telemedicine, automated SMS alerts
Environment	Drones for mapping, GPS, satellite monitoring systems

4. Partnership and Collaboration Model

Key Partners:
Local organizations: Traditional leaders, CSOs, youth/women groups involved in grassroots implementation.
Technical partners: Universities, research centers, local tech startups.
Funding partners: Foundations, development agencies, bilateral donors (e.g. Klarna, G20, UNDP, European Union).
Public institutions: Sector ministries, health zones, environmental divisions, education institutions.

Collaboration Model:
The project operates under a co-management model:
Project coordination is led by a main implementing organization (e.g., Uhakika Medical Foundation).
Technical partners provide specialized expertise (training, technology, M&E).
Community members are involved at every step via local steering committees.
A multistakeholder steering committee oversees results and strategic decision-making.
A collaboration charter is signed with each stakeholder to define roles, respons
Solution Provider(s): 1.	Technological Solution Providers 2.	SRH Content and Education Providers 3.	Medical Kits and Supplies Providers 4.	Logistics and Connectivity Providers 5.	Communication and Media Providers 6.	Capacity Building Providers  a)	Sexual and Reproductive Health and Rights (SRHR) b)	Digital Health and Innovation c)	Youth Empowerment and Participation d)	Community Health Systems Strengthening e)	Health Equity and Inclusion f)	Environmental and Climate-Responsive Health g)	Monitoring, Research and Data-Driven Decision-Making
Implementation location(s): Implementation Location – santéConnect Jeunes  The santéConnect Jeunes project is implemented primarily in the cities of Goma and Bukavu, as well as in the Nyiragongo territory, all located in the eastern part of the Democratic Republic of Congo (DRC). These areas were selected due to their significant youth populations, high unmet needs in sexual and reproductive health (SRH), and challenges in accessing quality youth-friendly health services.  More specifically, the project targets:  Urban and peri-urban areas of Goma and Bukavu, where youth populations are dense and digital connectivity is relatively better.  Rural and remote communities within Nyiragongo territory, including isolated areas around Lake Kivu, where access to SRH information and services is limited.  Displaced and vulnerable youth populations, including those living in internally displaced persons (IDP) camps and settlements affected by conflict.   These locations align with the project’s goal to reach marginalized and underserved youth through innovative digital and community-based solutions.

Desired impact:
Intended Impact of the santéConnect Project

Solution Objectives:
Improve access to sexual and reproductive health (SRH) services for youth and vulnerable populations in targeted areas (Goma, Bukavu, Nyiragongo territory).
Strengthen awareness and education on SRH to reduce risky behaviors.
Facilitate coordination between healthcare providers, local partners, and beneficiaries through an interactive digital platform.
Reduce rates of sexually transmitted infections (STIs), early and unwanted pregnancies, and other reproductive health issues.

Key Expected Results:
Increase SRH medical consultations via the santéConnect platform by at least 40% within the first 12 months.
Raise awareness among at least 15,000 youth on good sexual health practices through digital and community campaigns.
Reduce unwanted pregnancies by 20% among young women in intervention zones after 2 years.
Lower new STI infections by 15% through improved prevention and access to treatment.
Enhance coordination and service tracking with a real-time digital monitoring system for better resource allocation.

Long-term Impacts:
Sustainable improvement in reproductive health of target populations.
Strengthened local capacities in community health and digital solutions.
Contribution to achieving the Sustainable Development Goals (SDGs), particularly SDG 3 (Good Health and Well-being) and SDG 5 (Gender Equality).
Key technologies:
Technologies Used in santéConnect

1. Cross-Platform Mobile Application (Android & iOS)
Overview: A mobile app accessible on smartphones and tablets, developed using frameworks like Flutter or React Native to ensure easy and fast access to the santéConnect platform, even in areas with low connectivity.
Role: Allows users (patients, health professionals) to register, access information, receive reminders, and communicate with health experts.

2. Secure Centralized Database
Overview: A secure cloud database (e.g., Firebase, PostgreSQL, or MongoDB) to store personal data, medical histories, and consultation results.
Role: Ensures confidentiality, availability, and data integrity with encryption protocols and controlled access.

3. Authentication and Access Management System
Overview: Implementation of secure authentication systems (such as OAuth 2.0, two-factor authentication) to ensure that only authorized users can access sensitive data.
Role: Protects against unauthorized access and complies with privacy standards.

4. Instant Messaging and Teleconsultation Technology
Overview: Integration of instant messaging and video conferencing tools (e.g., WebRTC, Twilio) to enable direct communication between patients and healthcare providers.
Role: Facilitates remote consultations, quick advice, and care coordination.

5. Data Collection and Analytics Modules
Overview: Use of analytics tools and artificial intelligence (AI) to process data, detect trends, and personalize health advice.
Role: Optimizes medical decision-making and public health prevention efforts.

6. Administrative Web Interface
Overview: A web platform accessible to managers and partners for monitoring, user management, and reporting.
Role: Ensures operational oversight and project management.

7. Connectivity and Network Infrastructure Optimization
Overview: Designed to operate even with limited internet connection (offline mode, delayed synchronization).
Role: Enables wide geographic coverage and continuous accessibility in rural areas.
Unique Characteristics:
Unique and Differentiated Features of santéConnect

1. Youth- and Vulnerable-Group-Centered Approach
santéConnect specifically targets young people, including adolescent girls, internally displaced youth, and those living in rural or peri-urban areas who are often excluded from traditional health services.

2. Digital Accessibility in Low-Connectivity Environments
The platform is designed to function offline with delayed data synchronization, making it usable in areas with limited or no constant internet access.
It is also compatible with low-cost smartphones.

3. Integration of Telehealth and Psychosocial Support
In addition to medical consultations, santéConnect offers access to mental health and psychosocial support services, crucial in humanitarian and post-conflict settings.

4. Multilingual and Culturally Adapted Platform
Content is available in local languages (such as Swahili, Lingala, or Kinyarwanda) in addition to French, with audio-visual formats adapted for low-literacy users.

5. AI-Powered Personalized Health Recommendations
Using artificial intelligence, the solution provides customized health reminders (e.g., vaccines, screenings, contraception) and advice based on the user’s age, gender, and personal health profile.

6. Hybrid Model: Digital Platform with Community-Based Support
santéConnect combines digital services with the support of peer educators and community health workers, ensuring a vital human connection in health education.

7. Data Collection for Advocacy and Health Policy Improvement
Aggregated data is used to identify unmet health needs, measure project impact, and inform local public health strategies and decision-making.

8. Sustainable Local Partnerships
The solution is built on strong collaborations with local health centers, NGOs, schools, and public health authorities, ensuring community ownership and long-term sustainability
Sustainable Change:
1.	Improving Equitable Access to Health Services
By breaking down geographic, financial, social, and cultural barriers, santéConnect ensures continuous and inclusive access to essential health services, especially in marginalized and underserved areas.
This helps correct persistent structural inequalities within the healthcare system.

2.	Driving the Digital Transformation of Community Health
santéConnect introduces innovative digital tools that modernize how healthcare is delivered, monitored, and evaluated—bridging the gap between on-the-ground services and digital platforms.
This model supports the development of new national digital health policies.

3.	Empowering Youth and Strengthening Local Capacity
The solution promotes health education, bodily autonomy, and active youth engagement in managing their own health.
By training peer educators and community health workers, santéConnect strengthens long-term local human resources.

4.	Creating a Reliable Data System for Public Decision-Making
The platform collects disaggregated and reliable data on youth health needs, behaviors, and trends, helping inform public strategies, health policies, and funding allocations.
It contributes to evidence-based governance and long-term health planning.

5.	Shifting Social Norms and Addressing Taboos
santéConnect serves as a catalyst for social change by addressing often-taboo topics (such as sexuality, contraception, and mental health) through culturally sensitive, youth-friendly formats.
It helps shift perceptions and practices over time, creating a lasting cultural impact.

6.	Ensuring Sustainability Through Partnerships and Public Integratio
By involving public institutions, local NGOs, and schools, the solution is designed to be integrated into existing systems and policies.
It is scalable and replicable across other regions or health sectors, ensuring long-term sustainability.

Title: Laying the Foundations for Inclusive Digital Health Policy: A Situational and Regulatory Mapping Study Toward the Development of a Cancer Center EHR System in Zamboanga City Medical Center
Subtitle: This research constitutes Phase 1 of a larger, multi-phased initiative to design and implement a regulatory-aligned, locally adaptable Electronic Health Record (EHR) system at the Zamboanga City Medical Center (ZCMC) Cancer Center. This initial phase focuses on conducting a situational assessment and regulatory landscape mapping, with the goal of informing the policy and institutional readiness necessary for sustainable digital health transformation in regional cancer care.  Through a mixed-methods approach, the study will examine the interplay between existing digital health policies, institutional capabilities, data governance protocols, and frontline needs. This research aims to surface policy gaps, ethical concerns, and systemic barriers that must be addressed before EHR adoption and to recommend a policy-responsive pathway forward. The outcomes will provide an evidence-based foundation for Phase 2, which involves prototype development and pilot implementation.
Problem Statement:
This initiative directly addresses the challenges below by laying the regulatory and institutional foundation for a locally developed, policy-informed, and inclusive EHR system, with long-term scalability for other regional hospitals across the Philippines and the Global South:
1. Unequal Access to Digital Health Tools
Regional public hospitals, especially in underserved areas like Zamboanga Peninsula, lack the infrastructure and systems to adopt inclusive digital health solutions such as Electronic Health Records (EHRs).
2. Policy-to-Practice Disconnect
National digital health and data protection laws exist, but institutional capacity to implement them remains low, leading to fragmented or delayed digital transformation in healthcare.
3. Regulatory and Institutional Readiness Gaps
Public healthcare institutions often operate without clear frameworks for data privacy, patient consent, and digital governance, increasing risks for both patients and providers.
4. Lack of Locally Adaptable EHR Models
Existing EHR systems are either donor-dependent or misaligned with local needs. There is a need for modular, policy-compliant, and scalable EHR solutions that reflect regional workflows and realities.
5. Underutilization of Local Digital Talent and MSMEs
Health digitalization efforts rarely engage local developers, health informatics graduates, or MSMEs—missing opportunities for economic inclusion, innovation, and long-term system sustainability.
Solution Overview:
Detailed Description of How This Solution Works
          This solution lays the foundational groundwork for an inclusive, policy-aligned Electronic Health Record (EHR) system tailored to the needs of a regional cancer center in the Philippines. Specifically, it focuses on Phase 1: conducting a situational analysis and regulatory landscape mapping at Zamboanga City Medical Center (ZCMC) Cancer Center to ensure that the future EHR system is grounded in ethical, legal, and operational realities.
          The solution works by:
     1. Diagnosing the institutional and regulatory environment to determine how existing digital health laws and policies (e.g., Data Privacy Act, UHC Act) apply—or fail to apply—in the regional cancer care context.
     2. Assessing the hospital’s digital readiness, clinical workflows, and health information systems to inform the structure and policy compliance of the future EHR.
     3. Engaging with key stakeholders from health, technology, and policy sectors to co-develop data governance recommendations, institutional protocols, and a framework for system implementation.
     4. Generating policy briefs and institutional recommendations that will guide Phase 2 (prototype design) and inform broader digital health policy development for public hospitals.
          The ultimate goal is to ensure that when the EHR is built and deployed in future phases, it will be:
     > Locally relevant
     > Legally compliant
     > Ethically grounded
     > Technically sustainable
     > Scalable across other regional settings

Methodologies and Technologies Used
Methodologies:
     1. Mixed-Methods Research Approach
     2. Policy Landscape Mapping
     3. Stakeholder Engagement
     4. Institutional Readiness Assessment
     5. Gap and SWOT Analysis
Technologies (for future development phases but factored in now):
     1. Google Open Health Stack
        Open-source, modular framework supporting secure, interoperable, standards-based EHR systems.
     2. FHIR (Fast Healthcare Interoperability Resources) Standards
        For ensuring future data interoperability across healthcare systems.
     3. Consent Management and Data Privacy Protocols
        To be designed in alignment with RA 10173 and ethical frameworks.
     4. Cloud-Based and On-Premise Hosting Models (to be evaluated):
        Depending on institutional capacity and DOH/DICT recommendations.

Partnerships and Collaboration Models

     - Zamboanga City Medical Center (ZCMC) Cancer Center
          > Main pilot institution for the study
          > Provides access to systems, staff, and cancer care workflows
          > Will benefit from the eventual system integration
Regulatory and Policy Stakeholders:
     - Department of Health (DOH) – Health Facility Development Bureau & KMITS
          > Policy alignment and eventual endorsement of EHR models
     - Department of Information and Communications Technology (DICT)
          > For integration into national digital infrastructure and HIE standards
     - National Privacy Commission (NPC)
          > To ensure compliance with data privacy and consent protocols

(Public Health Sector), Department of Health – Knowledge Management and Information Technology Service (DOH-KMITS) – The digital health arm of the DOH responsible for health information systems, digital infrastructure policy, and interoperability standards in the Philippine healthcare system. (Government – Health Policy and ICT), Department of Information and Communications Technology (DICT) – The national agency overseeing digital infrastructure, cybersecurity, and the implementation of the Philippine eHealth Strategic Framework; provides alignment with national digital transformation policies. (Government – ICT Sector), National Privacy Commission (NPC) – The Philippine authority on data privacy and personal information protection, responsible for enforcing RA 10173 (Data Privacy Act); ensures ethical and legal compliance of the EHR system. (Government – Legal and Regulatory Sector),  Western Mindanao State University (WMSU) – A state university based in Zamboanga City, with active programs in nursing, public health, and ICT; provides academic and research support, health informatics expertise, and digital talent development. (Higher Education Sector),  WMSU College of Nursing – A leading nursing institution in Mindanao with faculty expertise in public health, systems research, and care delivery; contributes research personnel and contextual healthcare insights. (Higher Education – Health Sciences Sector),  WMSU College of Computing Studies – Provides technical support in ICT, systems analysis, and software development for future prototyping and digital literacy training. (Higher Education – ICT Sector),  Local MSMEs in Health IT and Software Development (to be formally identified in Phase 2) – Small and medium technology enterprises and freelance developers based in Zamboanga Peninsula to be engaged in co-designing and potentially co-developing the EHR system. (Private Sector – Digital Innovation and MSME Development),  Cancer Patient Advocacy Groups and Civil Society Organizations (to be onboarded) – Local groups representing cancer patients and their families to ensure ethical considerations, inclusive consent protocols, and patient-centered feedback during system design. (Civil Society Sector)
Duration to pilot in a new geography: Thirty-six months (three years)
SDGs addressed: SDG 3 (Good Health and Well-being);SDG 9 (Industry, Innovation, and Infrastructure);SDG 10 (Reduced Inequalities);
Desired impact:
Solution Objectives
1. Digitize and streamline cancer care workflows
Improve clinical documentation, continuity of care, and access to patient information through a secure, context-sensitive Electronic Health Record (EHR) system.
2. Strengthen digital health capacity of public health institutions
Enable regional cancer centers and their personnel to transition from paper-based records to digital systems with full ownership and contextual relevance.
3. Advance inclusive digital innovation
Localize open-source technologies using co-creation with local IT experts, health professionals, and patients, promoting digital equity and innovation at the grassroots level.
4. Generate health system data for decision-making
Support analytics for planning, policy, cancer surveillance, and service improvement through structured and real-time data collection.
5. Build a scalable and replicable model
Establish a pilot that can be adapted and deployed across other disease-specific centers or geographically similar healthcare facilities.

Key Achievements or Impacts (Projected and Early Evidence)
1. Health System Efficiency
     > Reduction in time spent on documentation; improved coordination of patient care
2. Digital Capacity Building
     > Training of health professionals and staff in EHR use and digital workflows
3. Innovation and Local Employment
     > Engagement of local software developers and health informatics experts; jobs created
4. Data for Policy and Research
     > Establishment of a structured cancer data registry; improved reporting and audit trails
5. Replication Potential
     > Modular system design allows adaptation to other specialties (e.g., maternal care, TB)
6. Digital Inclusion
     > Improved access to records for patients and providers in underserved areas via cloud tech
7. Sustainability and Ownership
     > Stakeholder co-design ensures institutional buy-in and long-term sustainability
Key technologies:
Key Technologies Used in the EHR Solution
1. Open Health Stack (OHS) by Google
     > A suite of open-source digital health components designed for LMICs.
     > Supports interoperability, modular development, and standards-based health data exchange (e.g., HL7 FHIR).
     > Includes components like:
          - OpenMRS or FhirEngine for health record management
          - Android FHIR SDK for mobile data capture
          - DHIS2 integration for analytics and reporting
2. Artificial Intelligence (AI)-Ready Architecture
     > Prepares the system to support AI modules for:
          - Clinical decision support
          - Risk stratification
          - Cancer care pathway optimization
          - Natural language processing for faster encoding in future phases
      > AI modules may not be fully implemented in Phase 1 but are part of the system roadmap for future scalability.
3. Cloud Computing and Edge Storage
     > Hybrid architecture with cloud-hosted backend (e.g., Google Cloud / AWS / local servers), and offline capabilities to ensure reliability in low-connectivity environments.
     > Data sync mechanisms ensure continuity of operations even in unstable bandwidth conditions.
4. Data Privacy & Security Technologies
     > End-to-end encryption of patient data
     > Role-based access control (RBAC)
     > Audit logging to monitor and secure sensitive information
     > Compliance with Philippine Data Privacy Act (RA 10173) and global health data standards
5. Mobile Health (mHealth) Integration
     > Android-based health worker apps for real-time bedside documentation and community outreach
     > Enables decentralized, inclusive participation in the healthcare process
6. Data Analytics and Visualization Tools
     > Integration with DHIS2 or custom dashboards for monitoring, reporting, and evidence-based decision-making
     > Real-time analytics on patient outcomes, service utilization, and cancer treatment trends
Optional (for Phase 2+):
7. Interoperability Frameworks & Blockchain Potential
     > Exploration of blockchain for immutable health records and patient consent management
     > Use of FHIR APIs for future interoperability with national health databases or insurance systems
Unique Characteristics:
Unique / Differentiated Characteristics of the Solution
1. Cancer-Specific, Context-Aware EHR System
     - First-of-its-kind EHR designed specifically for oncology in a government cancer center setting in the Philippines.
     - Custom workflows based on the local cancer patient journey, including chemotherapy regimens, diagnostics, and survivorship care plans.
     - Incorporates psychosocial care components, palliative tracking, and Filipino patient cultural considerations.
2. Phase-Based, Scalable Implementation Model
     - Designed as a multi-phased digital health transformation initiative, beginning with foundational EHR, and scaling toward:
          > Mobile health (mHealth)
          > AI-powered clinical decision support
          > Interoperability with national health insurance and DOH registries
     - Offers a replicable model for other disease-specific verticals (e.g., HIV, TB, maternal health).
3. Inclusive Design and Capacity Building
     - Developed using human-centered design, engaging cancer patients, nurses, doctors, and IT staff in co-creation.
     - Prioritizes usability for non-tech-savvy users in resource-constrained settings.
     - Includes a training and digital upskilling component for local health workers and administrative staff.
4. Open Health Stack Utilization for LMICs
     - Builds on the Open Health Stack (OHS) ecosystem, ensuring:
          > Open-source technology
          > Low-cost implementation
          > Global standardization (e.g., HL7 FHIR)
     - Eliminates dependency on costly proprietary systems while allowing modular growth and international interoperability.
5. Strong Public Health + Tech + Academia Partnership Model
     - Collaboration between:
          > Zamboanga City Medical Center (ZCMC) – health service provider
          > Western Mindanao State University (WMSU) – research and academic partner
          > DOH IX / CHD IX – regulatory and integration facilitator
          > Local tech innovators and developers – system developers using open-source stack
     - Promotes a multi-sectoral digital health ecosystem anchored in public sector resilience.
6. Offline Functionality for Geographically Isolated Areas
     - Designed with hybrid online-offline data syncing, making it resilient in regions with unstable connectivity.
     - Addresses healthcare access gaps in geographically isolated and disadvantaged areas (GIDAs).
7. Foundation for Health Equity and AI Readiness
     - Lays the groundwork for future AI integration focused on predictive care and personalized cancer treatment.
     - Champions equity in digital health transformation, ensuring marginalized and cancer-vulnerable populations are prioritized in digital system inclusion.
Sustainable Change:
Theory of Change: Building Sustainable, Systemic Change through Cancer-Centered EHR
Ultimate Goal
> To strengthen equitable, digitally empowered, and patient-centered cancer care systems in underserved regions through sustainable health technology innovation.

Inputs
     - Digital infrastructure and cloud-enabled architecture (via Open Health Stack)
     - Multidisciplinary human resource: health informatics experts, oncologists, nurses, developers, researchers
     - Partnerships with government (DOH, ZCMC), academia (WMSU), and local tech ecosystem
     - Training modules for digital literacy and system use
     - Seed funding for Phase 1 development and piloting

Activities
     - Co-design of EHR prototype tailored to the cancer patient journey
     - Deployment of Phase 1 EHR system for core patient records and treatment documentation
     - Capacity-building for frontline health workers
     - Community and stakeholder engagement sessions
     - Monitoring, evaluation, and iteration of the system for usability and impact
     - Documentation for scale-up and replication

Outputs
     - A fully functional, cancer-specific EHR deployed at ZCMC Cancer Center
     - Health workers trained in digital record-keeping and system use
     - Improved patient documentation, care coordination, and data retrieval
     - Governance and data security policies introduced at institutional level

Immediate Outcomes
     - Reduced paperwork and redundant patient interviews
     - Faster access to patient data, leading to more timely treatment decisions
     - Enhanced communication among departments (oncology, pathology, pharmacy, billing)
     - Improved continuity of care, especially for long-term cancer management

Long-Term Outcomes
     - Establishment of ZCMC as a regional model for digital oncology care
     - Institutional readiness for health data interoperability with PhilHealth, DOH, and national cancer registries
     - Empowered health workforce with digital competencies
     - Emergence of local digital health innovators using open-source architecture
     - Foundational data layer for future AI integration and personalized medicine

Systemic Impact (Sustainable Change)
     - Shift from paper-based to evidence-based digital cancer care
     - Greater health system resilience through tech-enabled service delivery
     - Contributes to inclusive digital transformation of public health in underserved regions
     - Establishes feedback loops for policy and R&D on digital health tools in oncology
     - Paves the way for scaling to other clinical departments and regions, enhancing universal health coverage (UHC)

Follow-On Effects
     - Development of disease-specific modules (e.g., HIV, TB, mental health)
     - Integration with national insurance and cancer surveillance systems
     - Policy influence on digital health standards for LMICs
     - Job creation in health IT and local tech industries
     - Bridging digital divide in healthcare access and equity

Summary: The project aims to lay the groundwork for a locally adaptable, policy-compliant Electronic Health Record (EHR) system for cancer care at Zamboanga City Medical Center, Philippines. Its strengths lie in its focus on inclusive digital health and local capacity building, but scalability and long-term funding remain unclear.

Problem Statement:
Globally, a significant number of people lack access to safe drinking water, with an estimated 2 billion individuals lacking access to safely managed drinking water services. Many more drink water from sources that are not adequately protected against contamination. The lack of access to clean water disproportionately affects populations in South Asia and Sub-Saharan Africa, as well as in parts of Oceania and Southeast Asia
Pakistan is the country where 80% rural population drinks contaminated water, while the situation in urban cities also not good, nearly 16 million individuals do not have access to safe drinking water and in 2016, Dawn published that about 84% to 89% of water sources in Pakistan do not meet water quality standards for human consumption. Correspondingly, in 2017 the Daily Times reported that nearly 39,000 children under 5 die annually due to diarrheal ailments. Because of these kinds of high numbers, the poor quality of drinking water has forced a large cross-section of citizens to buy bottled water. However, many of the mineral water companies were found selling contaminated water. To monitor and improve the quality of bottled water, the Government of Pakistan through the Ministry of Science and Technology has designated the task for quarterly monitoring of bottled/mineral water brands to PCRWR. According to the monitoring report PCRWR for the quarter January-March 2022 following the brief overview of the findings however, many of the mineral water companies were found selling contaminated. 
According to Sindh Bureau of Statistics, unsanitary condition, polluted water, illiteracy among rural mothers, high fertility, small budgetary allocation and inadequate administrative structures have been identified as the main hurdles in the progress of health conditions. There are also clear differentials in health conditions by rural and urban areas and socio-economic groups. Majority of the diseases in the rural areas are caused by malnutrition and the use of unsafe water.

Title: Mauritech Connect : Le numérique au service de tous
Subtitle: Une plateforme innovante reliant formation, e-commerce et services en ligne pour réduire la fracture numérique et stimuler l’inclusion sociale et économique en Mauritanie.
Problem Statement: En Mauritanie, de vastes zones rurales restent exclues de l’économie numérique en raison d’un accès limité à Internet, d’un manque d’infrastructures et de compétences numériques, accentuant les inégalités sociales et économiques.
Solution Overview:
Description du fonctionnement
Mauritech Connect est une plateforme hybride (en ligne et hors ligne) qui permet aux communautés, notamment rurales, d’accéder à :

Formations numériques (alphabétisation numérique, bureautique, marketing digital, codage de base).

E-commerce local pour vendre et acheter des produits artisanaux, agricoles et de services.

Services en ligne essentiels : démarches administratives, téléconsultation médicale, paiement électronique.

Ces services sont accessibles via :

Une application web/mobile multilingue (arabe, français, pulaar, soninké, hassaniya, wolof) optimisée pour faible débit.

Des centres numériques communautaires équipés d’ordinateurs et d’Internet par satellite, alimentés par énergie solaire.

Méthodologies et technologies utilisées

Approche communautaire : implication des leaders locaux et des associations pour assurer l’adhésion et la pérennité.

Technologies adaptées : plateformes légères fonctionnant hors ligne avec synchronisation automatique, utilisation de panneaux solaires pour alimenter les centres, connexion VSAT dans les zones non couvertes.

Formation participative : modules pédagogiques interactifs, mentorat par des experts, auto-apprentissage guidé.

Innovation inclusive : interface intuitive, adaptée aux personnes peu alphabétisées.

Partenariats et modèles de collaboration

Institutions publiques : Ministère de la Transformation numérique, Ministère de l’Éducation, Ministère de la Promotion féminine.

Secteur privé : opérateurs télécoms (Mauritel, Mattel, Chinguitel), entreprises TIC locales pour le développement et la maintenance.

Organisations internationales : ONU (PNUD, UIT, UNESCO), ONG spécialisées en inclusion numérique.

Modèle de collaboration : co-financement initial par bailleurs + génération de revenus via services premium (formations spécialisées, abonnements e-commerce) + implication communautaire pour la gestion locale des centres.
Solution Provider(s): Ministère de la Transformation Numérique, de l’Innovation et de la Modernisation de l’Administration – Institution publique chargée de la mise en œuvre des politiques numériques et de l’extension de la connectivité.  Mauritel S.A. – Opérateur national de télécommunications, fournissant connectivité et solutions techniques adaptées aux zones rurales.  PNUD Mauritanie (Programme des Nations Unies pour le Développement) – Agence onusienne soutenant l’innovation inclusive et le développement durable. Autres partenaires : Mattel S.A., Chinguitel S.A., UNESCO Mauritanie, Raddo Technologie, ONG locales de développement communautaire.
Duration to pilot in a new geography: 12 mois
SDGs addressed: SDG 4 (Quality Education);SDG 8 (Decent Work and Economic Growth);SDG 9 (Industry, Innovation, and Infrastructure);
Desired impact:
Objectifs de la solution
Réduire la fracture numérique en Mauritanie en facilitant l’accès aux outils, compétences et services numériques, en particulier pour les jeunes et les femmes rurales.

Stimuler l’entrepreneuriat local et l’intégration des producteurs au marché numérique.

Améliorer l’accès aux services publics et privés via des solutions numériques adaptées aux zones isolées.

Principaux impacts attendus
Formation de 3000 bénéficiaires (jeunes et femmes) aux compétences numériques d’ici 3 ans.

Création d’au moins 200 micro-entreprises numériques ou e-commerçantes soutenues via la plateforme.

Réduction de 15% des déplacements physiques pour les démarches administratives grâce aux services en ligne, contribuant à une moindre empreinte carbone.

Installation de 15 centres numériques solaires, générant une économie d’énergie fossile et favorisant l’accès dans des zones hors réseau.

Augmentation de 25% des revenus des artisans et producteurs locaux grâce à la vente en ligne.
Key technologies:
Plateforme web/mobile légère : conçue pour fonctionner avec une faible connexion Internet, optimisée pour les zones à faible débit.

Connexion VSAT (satellite) : pour garantir l’accès Internet dans les zones rurales isolées où la couverture mobile est faible ou inexistante.

Énergie solaire : panneaux photovoltaïques pour alimenter les centres numériques de manière autonome et écologique.

Modules d’e-learning interactifs : intégrant des outils pédagogiques adaptatifs pour faciliter l’apprentissage.

Système de gestion de contenu multilingue : pour proposer des formations et services dans plusieurs langues locales (arabe, français, pulaar, soninké, hassaniya, wolof).

Outils de e-commerce intégrés : gestion sécurisée des transactions et suivi des commandes.

Plateforme sécurisée avec authentification pour garantir la confidentialité des données utilisateurs.
Unique Characteristics:
Approche hybride : combinaison d’une plateforme numérique légère et de centres communautaires alimentés à l’énergie solaire, pour toucher à la fois les populations connectées et déconnectées.

Multilinguisme local : contenu et interface adaptés aux principales langues parlées en Mauritanie, assurant une accessibilité culturelle rare dans ce type de projet.

Modèle communautaire de gestion : implication directe des leaders locaux et associations dans la gestion des centres, garantissant l’appropriation et la pérennité.

Financement mixte et durable : financement initial par partenaires internationaux, complété par des revenus générés via services premium (formations spécialisées, e-commerce) pour assurer l’autonomie financière.

Énergie renouvelable intégrée : utilisation systématique de l’énergie solaire pour rendre les centres autonomes, écologique et adaptés aux zones hors réseau.

Plateforme modulaire et évolutive : conçue pour intégrer facilement de futures innovations (intelligence artificielle, blockchain) selon les besoins et opportunités.
Sustainable Change:
Mauritech Connect vise à instaurer un changement systémique durable en transformant profondément l’accès et l’usage du numérique au sein des communautés mauritaniennes.

Théorie du changement :
Accès équitable aux infrastructures numériques (centres solaires + connectivité satellite) →

Acquisition de compétences numériques par les populations clés (jeunes, femmes, artisans) →

Inclusion économique renforcée via l’accès au e-commerce et aux services en ligne →

Dynamisation des économies locales et autonomisation des acteurs communautaires →

Modification des comportements sociaux et économiques : valorisation des compétences numériques, réduction des inégalités, meilleure gouvernance locale grâce aux outils digitaux →

Effet de levier régional et national : duplication du modèle dans d’autres régions, influence sur les politiques publiques et intégration dans les stratégies nationales de développement numérique.

Effets de suivi souhaités :

Adoption durable des outils numériques par au moins 70 % des bénéficiaires dans les zones ciblées.

Création de filières économiques locales liées au numérique, avec croissance mesurable du chiffre d’affaires des micro-entreprises.

Amélioration continue des compétences grâce à des formations renouvelées et adaptées.

Réduction notable de la fracture numérique et sociale, avec un impact visible sur l’éducation, l’emploi et l’accès aux services publics.

Renforcement des capacités institutionnelles locales et adaptation des politiques publiques au nouveau paysage numérique.

En somme, Mauritech Connect ne se contente pas d’apporter des outils, il crée un écosystème où le numérique devient un levier durable de développement inclusif et équitable en Mauritanie.
Funding Sources: Mauritech Connect n'a pas encore été finance par aucun bailleurs
Primary thematic focus area: Inclusive Digital Innovation Skills & Entrepreneurial Talent Development
Summary: Mauritech Connect is a digital inclusion platform designed to bridge the digital divide in Mauritania by providing digital training, e-commerce access, and online services to underserved communities, focusing on rural youth and women.

Title: Marketplace for the vulnerable and disabled
Subtitle: To create a socially inclusive ecosystem that will help people with disabilities in the Fergana region, produce inexpensive handicrafts that will be sold through a digital platform.
Problem Statement:
1. Limited access to markets — artisans with disabilities often lack the opportunity to sell their products due to a lack of sales channels, high competition, and barriers to online trading.
2. Low digital literacy — many potential beneficiaries do not have the skills to work with electronic platforms, which limits their participation in e-commerce.
3. Social isolation — the lack of platforms for interaction with clients and other artisans leads to low community engagement and decreased self-confidence.
4. Economic vulnerability — limited employment and income opportunities increase financial instability among people with disabilities.
5. Insufficient public awareness — consumers are poorly informed about the quality and value of products created by people with disabilities, which reduces demand for such goods.
Solution Provider(s): "Texno-Soft" LLC - software, Association of Disabled People of Fergana Region - association of disabled people, Khokimiyat of Fergana Region - assistance in organizational matters
Duration to pilot in a new geography: 3 months
SDGs addressed: SDG 1 (No Poverty);SDG 4 (Quality Education);SDG 17 (Partnerships for the Goals);
Desired impact:
To create an inclusive platform that will provide people with disabilities with the opportunity to sell their handicrafts, increase their income and develop professional skills, as well as raise public awareness of the value of their work and creative potential.
Creation of more than 600 jobs within 1.5 - 2 years
Key technologies: Enables inclusive participation of both technical and non-technical users. Cloud computing: Provides secure data storage, remote access, and integration with other platforms for data sharing and cross-industry collaboration.
Unique Characteristics:
1. State and civil society — assistance in scaling up and inclusion in state programs of sustainable agriculture.
2. Educational and demonstration format. Laboratory for knowledge exchange between regions.
3. Inclusiveness and social orientation. Emphasis on involving women and vulnerable groups in the decision-making process and income generation.
4. Financial sustainability. Self-sufficiency model through product sales, conducting training courses.
Sustainable Change:
Key systemic changes and long-term impacts are as follows:
1. Democratization of access to markets — artisans gain direct access to a wide range of buyers without intermediaries, which increases their income and competitiveness.
2. Increased transparency — a single digital environment with supplier verification and supply chain tracking helps build trust and reduces the risk of unfair practices.
3. Stimulating the local economy — an increase in the number of orders and partnerships in the region increases employment and develops local businesses.
4. Sustainable business models — the marketplace creates conditions for long-term development due to built-in services (logistics, electronic payments, seller training).
5. Digital transformation of the industry — the introduction of technologies (e.g. data analytics, IoT for supply monitoring) increases efficiency and predictability.
6. Social impact — expanding opportunities for women entrepreneurs, rural residents and other socially vulnerable groups.
As a result, the launch of a marketplace becomes a catalyst for sustainable change, transforming traditional models of trade and interaction into more environmentally friendly, fair and technologically advanced formats.
Funding Sources: European Union, IPHR
Testimonials and Endorsements: At two seminars held in Fergana in the NGO House (June 23, August 1, 2025) on the launch of a social marketplace, the participants spoke out with great enthusiasm in favor of launching the platform. They noted that the launch of such a social marketplace will allow vulnerable groups of the population to find themselves in society and learn how to work on the marketplace and earn money from their labor.
Further comments/feedback: Supporting our project will improve the socio-economic situation of vulnerable groups of the population and create new jobs for them and raise their status
Primary thematic focus area: Inclusive Digital Innovation Skills & Entrepreneurial Talent Development
Summary: This initiative creates an inclusive digital marketplace for artisans with disabilities, enabling them to sell their products directly to consumers, increase their income, and gain skills. While it addresses a critical need for social inclusion, further details on scalability and long-term financial sustainability are required.

Title: Digital Music Therapy for Inclusive Health and Youth Empowerment
Subtitle: Providing remote, accessible music therapy to underserved patients and youth via innovative digital platforms.
Problem Statement: Many patients in hospitals, nursing homes, and underserved communities lack access to therapeutic music due to physical, scheduling, or geographic barriers. Youth musicians also face limited opportunities to develop skills and engage digitally.
Solution Overview: Solis and Luna Arts delivers music therapy and education through digital platforms, including the LunaTunes: Songs by Request program and the Healing Beats app. Patients can request personalized music remotely, improving emotional well-being. The solution uses interactive web apps, digital content, and community engagement to expand access. Partnerships with hospitals, veterans’ homes, and youth ensembles support implementation and feedback to refine services.
Solution Provider(s): Solis and Luna Arts (Nonprofit organization focused on music therapy and digital inclusion, Arts and Health sector), Karma for Cara Foundation (Nonprofit supporting youth leadership and community service, Youth Development sector), Youth Service America (Global nonprofit empowering youth volunteers, Education and Civic Engagement sector), AmeriCorps (U.S. federal agency promoting national service and community programs, Public Service sector), Riley’s Way Foundation (Nonprofit supporting youth-led social change and advocacy, Health and Youth Empowerment sector).
Implementation location(s): Bergen County, New Jersey--hospitals, veterans homes, nursing homes, and community centers.
Duration to pilot in a new geography: 2 months
SDGs addressed: SDG 3 (Good Health and Well-being);SDG 4 (Quality Education);SDG 10 (Reduced Inequalities);
Desired impact: Solis and Luna Arts aims to improve the emotional and mental well-being of over 20,000 patients annually by providing accessible creative therapy through digital and in-person platforms. Having already positively impacted 5,000 patients through physical events, the organization is expanding its reach by integrating innovative digital solutions to overcome barriers to access. Additionally, the program empowers more than 2,000 youth musicians by developing their digital skills and offering meaningful performance opportunities that foster confidence, community engagement, and professional growth. By broadening access to therapeutic arts in underserved and marginalized communities, Solis and Luna Arts actively contributes to reducing health inequities and promoting social inclusion through creative healing.
Key technologies: The solution utilizes a suite of digital technologies to facilitate remote and personalized music therapy. This includes interactive web applications that allow patients to request songs and engage with therapy content digitally. Integration with digital music platforms such as the Spotify API enables curated, real-time music streaming tailored to patient preferences. Remote interaction tools facilitate live virtual sessions and feedback collection, while online surveys and data collection methods track patient outcomes, engagement, and satisfaction, enabling continuous refinement of the therapy experience.
Unique Characteristics: Solis and Luna Arts stands out by uniquely combining arts, healthcare, and digital innovation into a cohesive, patient-centered music therapy model. Unlike traditional in-person therapy, this scalable digital approach overcomes physical barriers such as mobility, geographic distance, and scheduling conflicts, making therapy more inclusive and widely accessible. The solution integrates youth empowerment by involving young musicians in digital skill development and community outreach, fostering intergenerational collaboration and sustainability. This blend of technology, creativity, and social engagement differentiates the program as an innovative model for delivering therapeutic arts at scale.
Sustainable Change: By leveraging digital tools and platforms, Solis and Luna Arts establishes a sustainable model that extends therapeutic music access beyond traditional physical and geographic constraints. This approach contributes to systemic change by addressing health inequities through inclusive, remote care options that empower underserved populations. The solution promotes community resilience by fostering digital literacy and engagement among youth musicians, creating a pipeline of empowered individuals who can sustain and expand therapeutic arts initiatives. Ultimately, this model supports long-term growth in accessible, arts-based health solutions that integrate technology, education, and social justice principles to transform care delivery and community well-being.
