Title: Job Guru Africa: Unlocking Freelancing In The Kenyan Digital Economy
Subtitle: Enabling economic inclusion through a platform that supports freelancing, skill development, and job access for Kenya’s next generation of digital workers.
Problem Statement: In Kenya, a new generation is redefining success, moving beyond the old job market in pursuit of meaningful careers and flexible lifestyles. Yet many face barriers to income opportunities due to limited exposure, inadequate skills training, and lack of access to trusted digital platforms. The fragmented gig economy fails to cater to their specific needs and potential.
Solution Overview:
Job Guru Africa is an end-to-end digital platform designed to connect Kenyan and African freelancers with meaningful work opportunities while supporting SMEs and organizations seeking freelance talent. The platform is a dual-sided marketplace offering services, jobs, and projects with the aim of providing both visibility and income-generating channels to users. 

The platform leverages WordPress and automations for onboarding, analytics, and SEO to create a scalable infrastructure that remains accessible for users with minimal tech barriers. Manual quality control ensures each listing meets credibility standards.

Our growth model is based on a community-first approach. We manage an online freelancer group, host webinars, and build relationships with recruiters and entrepreneurs. Through our business development manager, we are working on driving grassroots partnerships and representation at organisations like Rotary and Ajira.
Solution Provider(s): We have not signed any official partnerships as yet.
Implementation timeline(s): The solution has already been implemented in Kenya since 2023 and is currently operational.
Duration to pilot in a new geography: To pilot the solution in a new geography, the estimated duration is 3–6 months. This would include conducting local research, adapting platform content and compliance to the local context, establishing initial partnerships, and onboarding early users (freelancers and employers). The core platform and operational model are already in place and scalable, allowing for a faster and cost-effective rollout.
SDGs addressed: SDG 8 (Decent Work and Economic Growth);SDG 10 (Reduced Inequalities);
Desired impact:
Solution Objectives:

To empower Kenyan and African youth with access to dignified, flexible, and sustainable freelance work opportunities by bridging the gap between local talent and global digital demand.

Key Achievements and Impact:

• Over 200 freelancers registered on the platform since 2023, with a growing focus on youth.
• Created income-generation pathways.
• Weekly job listings and skills content have contributed to an increase in platform engagement and repeat visits.
• In the next 12 months, we aim to support 500+ new freelance earners, catalyzing digital employment and economic inclusion across Kenya and beyond.
Key technologies: Our technology stack includes a WordPress framework with multi-user capabilities, that allow users to create profile, jobs, projects, and service listings. We've embedded real-time analytics (Clarity, GA4), scalable payment integration (M-Pesa, PayPal-ready), and are building toward future integrations with AI-powered tools and automations for freelancers and employers alike.
Unique Characteristics:
Job Guru Africa combines a localized freelance marketplace that is tailored to operate in the Kenyan and African markets, allowing for physical, remote, and hybrid freelance work. 

We have integrated with regionally dominant payment systems like M-Pesa, combined with manual vetting and community building, which allows for scalability and bridges the gap between local and global gig opportunities and the underrepresented African digital workforce. 

We are also working on cultivating a grassroots partnership model to work with local freelancers, affiliates, and organizations to grow organically, expand reach, and co-create solutions based on lived experience.
Sustainable Change:
Job Guru Africa aims to redefine employment pathways by shifting how African youth perceive and access work. We equip freelancers with tools, income-generating opportunities, and digital skills; and educate employers on hiring sustainably and inclusively.

Our Theory of Change follows a four-stage ripple model:

1. Access – Remove barriers to joining the digital economy.

2. Skills & Income – Provide meaningful income + digital skills.

3. Community & Mentorship – Foster peer support and knowledge sharing.

4. Leadership & Advocacy – Create empowered digital leaders who shape future systems.

This model lays the foundation for long-term systemic change in how Kenya and Africa works, earns, and grows in the digital era.
Funding Sources: The platform has been fully self-funded by the founder, Harveen Bansal, since its inception.
Primary thematic focus area: Inclusive Digital Innovation Skills & Entrepreneurial Talent Development
Summary: Job Guru Africa is a digital platform designed to connect Kenyan and African freelancers with meaningful work opportunities, providing skill development, income-generating channels, and supporting local SMEs and organizations seeking freelance talent.

Title: The Leap Project – Enabling bold steps into the digital world.
Subtitle: Helping underserved communities take the leap into the digital economy through skills, innovation, and opportunity.
Problem Statement: According to the International Telecommunication Union, over 2 billion people remain offline, with women and marginalized groups more severely affected by the digital divide. In Nigeria and many developing regions, limited access to digital tools, poor infrastructure, and low digital literacy continue to rise daily, excluding millions—especially women, youth, and persons with disabilities—from opportunities in education, jobs, and markets. This deepens socio-economic inequalities and undermines progress toward the Sustainable Development Goals. Without targeted, inclusive digital interventions like The Leap Project, these communities risk being permanently left behind in the rapidly evolving global digital economy.
Solution Overview:
The Leap Project is a community-driven digital inclusion initiative designed to equip women, youth, and marginalized groups in Nigeria and similar developing regions with the skills, tools, and opportunities needed to participate fully in the digital economy.

How our solution works:
We deliver blended learning programs that combine in-person training in underserved communities with access to offline and online digital tools. Our curriculum covers:

✅ Foundational digital literacy (basic computer use, internet navigation, email communication)

✅ Entrepreneurial and employability skills (e-commerce, digital marketing, project management)

✅ Assistive technology training for persons with disabilities

✅ Mental well-being modules to promote resilience in digital entrepreneurship

Training is delivered quarterly in rural and peri-urban locations through local hubs, schools, and community spaces( community town halls) . For communities with poor connectivity, we use offline-enabled platforms (e.g., Kolibri, Learn My Way) and distribute preloaded devices containing learning materials.

Methodologies and Technologies Used

✅ EdTech Platforms: Google Workspace for Education, Microsoft Learn, Canva for Education, Scratch, and offline tools like Kolibri for low-connectivity areas.

✅ Project-Based Learning (PBL): Participants apply new skills to real-world projects, such as designing a digital business plan or setting up an online shop.

✅ Inclusive Design: Accessible content formats (screen reader–friendly documents, captioned videos, sign language support where possible).

✅ Blended Training Model: Combines instructor-led sessions, peer learning, and self-paced assignments.

Partnerships and Collaboration Models

✅ Local Implementation Partners: Collaboration with schools, faith-based organizations, and grassroots NGOs to mobilize participants and provide safe training venues.

✅ Technical Support Partners: Engagement with EdTech companies and open-source communities to provide tools, licenses, and training content.

✅ Capacity Building with Government & UN Agencies: Working with relevant ministries, UNDP, and local authorities to integrate our model into existing digital inclusion strategies.

✅ Volunteer Network: Skilled volunteers from universities and our trained Corp members act as trainers, mentors, and peer coaches.
Solution Provider(s): Springs of Good-Health Initiative– Nonprofit/Education/Health, Google Workspace for Education – Technology/Education, Microsoft Learn – Technology/Education, Kolibri (Learning Equality) – Nonprofit/EdTech, Secondary Education Management Board (SEMB) – Government/Education, United Nations Development Programme (UNDP) – Nigeria, Multilateral/Development, Faith-Based and Educational Institutions – Education/Community Development, The Pollination Project.
Implementation timeline(s): Our pilot phase was launched in October 2022; expanded implementation from January 2023 to present (ongoing).
Duration to pilot in a new geography: 📅 Month 1–2:  ✅ Community Needs Assessment and Stakeholder Engagement  ✅ Map target communities and identify local partners.  ✅ Conduct baseline surveys on digital literacy, access to tech, and entrepreneurship readiness.  ✅ Sign MoUs with local authorities, schools, women’s groups, and youth networks.  ✅ Secure locations for training (community centers, schools, or mobile hubs).  📅 Month 3–7:  ✅ Infrastructure Setup and  Training Rollout  ✅ Install and configure digital learning tools (computers, internet access, solar backup if needed).  ✅ Train trainers (TOT) from the local community for sustainability.  ✅ Launch core training in digital literacy, entrepreneurship, and market access tools.  ✅ Provide special accessibility tools for learners with disabilities.  📅 Month 8–9: ✅ Monitoring, Feedback and Adaptation  ✅ Track learner engagement, completion rates, and skill uptake.  ✅ Hold focus groups with participants for feedback.  ✅ Adjust training content and delivery based on insights.  ✅ Document impact stories and key metrics for funder reporting.
SDGs addressed: SDG 4 (Quality Education);SDG 8 (Decent Work and Economic Growth);SDG 5 (Gender Equality);
Desired impact:
The desired aim of the Leap Project is to create a ripple effect of socio-economic empowerment, unlock opportunities for hundreds of marginalized individuals while building resilient, future-ready communities through the enablement of digital inclusion and entrepreneurship in underserved communities.

✅ Solution Objectives: 

📌 To bridge the digital divide by providing underserved women, youth, and persons with disabilities with access to digital tools and training.

📌 We would equip at least 500 beneficiaries in the pilot phase with digital literacy and entrepreneurship skills to increase employability and income-generation opportunities.

📌 We would promote inclusive participation in the digital economy by ensuring at least 50% female participation and accessible learning for persons with disabilities.

📌 We would strengthen local capacity by training community-based facilitators who can sustain the program beyond the pilot phase.

Our Key Achievements / Expected Quantifiable Impacts (Pilot Phase Projection)

✅ Digital Literacy Advancement: At least 80% of participants demonstrate measurable improvement in basic-to-intermediate digital skills.

✅ Employment and Entrepreneurship: At least 30% of trained participants start income-generating activities or secure jobs within 6 months after training.

✅ Community Empowerment: Establish 3 functional digital hubs equipped with accessible learning tools in underserved communities.

✅ Gender Inclusion: Maintain a minimum of 50% women participation in all training sessions.

✅ Accessibility: Provide assistive technologies for at least 20 participants with disabilities, enabling equal participation.

✅ Our SDG Contribution: Directly contributes to SDG 4 (Quality Education), SDG 5 (Gender Equality), SDG 8 (Decent Work and Economic Growth), and SDG 10 (Reduced Inequalities).
Key technologies:
Our Key Technologies Used for 
The Leap Project would leverage on low-cost, accessible, and adaptive digital tools to ensure inclusivity and scalability in underserved communities. Which are:

📌 Google Workspace for Education – for collaborative learning, cloud-based assignments, and remote training.

📌 Microsoft Learn / Office Suite – for productivity skill-building and professional readiness.

📌 Canva for Education – for accessible design and creative entrepreneurship training.

📌 Khan Academy and Kolibri – for offline/online self-paced learning in areas with low internet connectivity.

📌 Assistive Technologies – including screen readers, voice-to-text, and adaptive keyboards to support persons with disabilities.

📌 Offline Learning Kits & Preloaded Devices – ensuring digital learning continuity in areas without reliable electricity or internet.
Unique Characteristics:
✅ Blended, Inclusive Learning Model: We combine in-person, peer-led training with offline and online digital tools, making it adaptable to communities with limited or no internet access.

✅ We focus on Marginalized Groups: prioritizes women, youth, and persons with disabilities through accessible content and assistive technologies, ensuring no one is left behind.

✅ Community-Driven Partnerships: We works closely with local schools, faith-based organizations, government agencies (like SEMB), and grassroots groups to co-create culturally relevant training and sustain impact beyond initial phases.

✅ Use of Open-Source and Low-Cost Technologies: We employ platforms like Kolibri and free educational resources to reduce costs and expand scalability without sacrificing quality.

✅ Mental Health Integration: Incorporates mental well-being modules alongside digital skills training to build resilience and holistic empowerment for participants.

✅ Sustainability Through Capacity Building: We train local trainers and community facilitators to ensure ongoing program delivery and scalability with minimal external support.

✅ Flexible Deployment: We are able to implement in diverse settings—from urban to remote rural areas.
Sustainable Change:
The Leap Project fosters sustainable, systemic change by addressing the root causes of digital exclusion and building lasting local capacity through inclusive digital skills training and entrepreneurship development, to empower marginalized groups—especially women, youth, and persons with disabilities—to actively participate in the digital economy.

We partner with local institutions, government bodies (such as SEMB), and community organizations in ensuring that culturally relevant and scalable delivery models are integrated into existing education and development frameworks. Training local facilitators and leveraging low-cost, accessible technologies creates a self-sustaining ecosystem that continues beyond initial project funding.

Our expected follow-on effects include:

📌 Increased digital literacy and economic participation within underserved communities, leading to improved livelihoods and reduced poverty.

📌 Enhanced gender equality and social inclusion by empowering women and marginalized groups with equal access to digital opportunities.

📌 Strengthened local institutions and ecosystems capable of delivering ongoing digital education and support services.

📌 Replication and scaling potential across other regions and countries through adaptable training models and partnerships.

Title: AI-Powered Data Platform Closing the Analytics Gap in Emerging Markets
Subtitle: We help businesses in emerging markets make sense of fragmented data by centralizing, cleaning, and analyzing it, making digital tools accessible where they're needed most.
Problem Statement: In emerging markets, businesses struggle to access timely, reliable insights due to fragmented data, limited technical talent, and underinvestment in digital infrastructure. Traditional analytics tools assume centralized, clean data and in-house data teams, conditions that are often unavailable in emerging ecosystems. This creates a significant barrier to data-driven decision-making, reinforcing economic exclusion and inefficiency.
Solution Overview:
Our platform combines AI agents and modern data infrastructure to help businesses in emerging markets unlock the value of their data without needing in-house data teams. The platform automatically connects to various data sources (e.g., spreadsheets, databases, CRMs, PDFs), cleans and structures the data, and enables users to query it in plain language to generate insights and analytics reports, dashboards, etc.

We use a local-first lakehouse architecture (DuckLake + DuckDB + Google Cloud Storage) for resilience in low-connectivity environments. Our agentic system includes:

*Pipeline Engineer: Automates data ingestion and orchestration using Prefect 2.0

*Schema Engineer: Uses Cube.dev to create semantic layers for consistent metrics

*Analytics Assistant: Enables natural language querying and insight generation

Our methodology prioritizes ease of use, low compute costs, and adaptability to infrastructure constraints common in emerging markets.

We are currently working with early users across Africa through a design partnership model. This includes co-building features, receiving implementation support, and influencing our roadmap. We are also exploring collaborations with regional innovation hubs and policy organizations to support digital inclusion efforts.
Solution Provider(s): We do not yet have partners
Duration to pilot in a new geography: 3-6 months
SDGs addressed: SDG 8 (Decent Work and Economic Growth);SDG 9 (Industry, Innovation, and Infrastructure);SDG 10 (Reduced Inequalities);
Desired impact:
Our goal is to democratize access to data-driven decision-making for businesses in emerging markets by replacing the need for costly data teams and infrastructure. By doing so, we help reduce operational inefficiencies, accelerate digital transformation, and unlock new economic opportunities.

Key impacts include:

*Reducing the time to actionable insights from weeks to minutes

*Cutting data operations costs by up to 80% by automating data prep and analysis

*Enabling 10,000+ business users to make informed decisions without technical training

*Supporting job creation by helping local businesses grow sustainably with better insights

*Catalyzing local digital innovation by equipping underserved markets with foundational data tools
Key technologies:
Artificial Intelligence (AI): Multi-agent system that automates data ingestion, cleaning, modeling, and analysis. Users can interact with data through natural language queries.

Cloud Computing: We use a local-first lakehouse architecture (DuckLake + DuckDB + Google Cloud Storage) to enable cost-effective, scalable, and resilient data storage and processing even in low-connectivity settings.

Workflow Orchestration: Prefect 2.0 powers dynamic, event-driven pipelines managed by our AI agents.

Semantic Modeling: Cube.dev enables the automated creation of semantic data models, ensuring consistency and ease of access for business users.

LLMs: Language models are integrated for conversational analytics and automated data documentation, enabling no-code access to insights.
Unique Characteristics:
Our solution is built specifically for the infrastructure, talent, and regulatory realities of emerging markets, something most analytics tools overlook. Unlike traditional BI platforms, we use AI agents to fully automate data ingestion, cleaning, modeling, and querying.

Technologically, our local-first lakehouse architecture enables resilience in low-connectivity environments. Our multi-agent system (built with Prefect, DuckDB, Cube.dev, and LLMs) allows us to deliver high performance at low cost.

We also offer a design partnership model co-building the product with early users to ensure the solution aligns with real-world needs while providing affordability and shared ownership of outcomes.
Sustainable Change:
By making advanced data infrastructure and analytics accessible to resource-constrained businesses, our solution unlocks a ripple effect of long-term, systemic change. When MSMEs and local enterprises gain the ability to make data-informed decisions, they become more efficient, competitive, and sustainable.

This leads to greater economic participation, job creation, and reduced dependency on foreign technology and expertise. Over time, widespread adoption of our agentic platform can help shift entire markets toward more inclusive digital economies, where innovation is locally driven and data is treated as a shared asset.
Funding Sources: We have been bootstrapping so far.
Primary thematic focus area: Innovation Acceleration & Knowledge Sharing
Summary: AI-powered platform that automates data cleaning, modeling, and analysis to help businesses in emerging markets unlock insights without needing in-house data teams.

Title: WorkWith: A Global Digital Toolbox for Accessible Work & Economy
Subtitle: WorkWith is an online platform that empowers worldwide employers, entrepreneurs, economic service providers, and nonprofits to create accessible work environment, tools, and work methods for job seekers with disabilities. Its global toolbox is a comprehensive resource designed to remove barriers for persons with disabilities by offering practical tips and reasonable accommodations for creating accessible work environments. These are categorized by job tasks and types of impairments or functional limitations. The toolbox features both software and hardware solutions that support access to information and communication technologies (ICT). Additionally, dedicated sections highlight good practices and recommendations for fostering inclusive employment and services as well as digital accessibility in line with international web accessibility standards (WCAG). This initiative aims to break the cycle of economic exclusion and accelerate global disability inclusion in key economic sectors. Link: www.WorkWithDisability.org
Problem Statement:
There is an inextricable link between disability and poverty. Over a billion people globally, approximately 15 percent of the world’s population, have disabilities and 80 percent of them live in developing countries (WHO and World Bank 2011). According to the World Bank, the employment rates of persons with disabilities are a third to half of the rates for persons without disabilities, with unemployment rates as high as 80 to 90 percent in some countries (including developed and developing economies) . 
This nexus between disability and poverty has devastating impacts on individuals with disabilities as well as massive collective costs: The global unemployment rate of persons with disabilities results in an annual loss of USD $1.37-1.94 billion GDP.
One of the many barriers to employment for people with disabilities is the lack of accessibility and reasonable accommodation. Some employers and service providers consider that disability inclusion is too complex, and they don’t know from which point to start. 
Companies and services from American, Nordic and European countries usually benefit from additional support and dedicated services to help them move forward on the path to inclusion. However, examples of accommodation can be found in many countries. What lacks is that they are not shared in a a broad and systematic way. 
Additionally, people with disabilities—already traditionally disadvantaged in the labor market—are further marginalized in an economy undergoing digital transformation. They face a persistent digital divide driven by a combination of factors, such as outdated or unequal access to technology, limited internet availability, low income, insufficient digital literacy, and a lack of accessible digital tools and services. According to The State of Web Accessibility in 2024, 88% of websites still fail to meet current web accessibility standards, with the average site scoring just 60 out of 100 in accessibility.
As digital technologies rapidly advance and reshape the world of work, it is essential to provide inclusive solutions that enable people with disabilities to access economic services and employment opportunities, so that they can participate in emerging economic sectors, and fully benefit from digital innovations to enhance their social and economic participation.
Solution Overview:
WorkWith is the world’s first digital database showcasing reasonable accommodation solutions for employers, economic services providers (skill trainings, job placement, micro-finance, etc.), nonprofits and entrepreneurs.
WorkWith provides technical information about workplace inclusion and reasonable accommodation and allows users to develop a personalized guide to help them make their project, business, or organization more inclusive. The platform presents reasonable accommodations that can be categorized by disability and work tasks and includes photo documentation of different methods of accommodation from around the world. As part of the reasonable accommodations, software and hardware solutions are presented for supporting people with disabilities in accessing and using ICT (such as speech recognition software, task-management apps, image description tools, and adaptive keyboards and mice, etc.). The solution aims to highlight reasonable accommodation from a variety of countries around the world so that companies based in low- and middle-income countries can find solutions that are relevant to their context and easily applicable.
Also included are general fact sheets with tips on accessibility, reasonable accommodation and task adaptations targeting economic inclusion stakeholders and employers or entrepreneurs. A specific focus will be made on how to improve accessibility of digital tools and services to increase persons with disability connectivity and reduce the digital divide they face.
The WorkWith platform aims to help non-experts understand that accommodation can be easy and to increase the ability of companies, services providers and nonprofits to work with people with disabilities around the world. The proposed solution is interactive and scalable: it allows reasonable tips and ideas for development to be shared with a large community of interested parties, who in turn can also share the developments they have tested and implemented.
Solution Provider(s): All economic actors that are interested in developing inclusive and accessible workplace can be part of it: Employers and services providers such as vocational training centers, micro-finance institutions, business incubators, etc. The WorkWith platform also aims at establish strategic partnerships with stakeholders active in the field of employment for people with disabilities and accessibility such as the Global and Business Disability Forum established by the International Labor Organizations (ILO GBDN) and the Zero project, an organization that finds and shares solutions that improve the daily lives and legal rights of all persons with disabilities.
Duration to pilot in a new geography: 1 year
SDGs addressed: SDG 1 (No Poverty);SDG 5 (Gender Equality);SDG 8 (Decent Work and Economic Growth);
Desired impact:
This solution ultimately serves persons with disabilities in low- and middle-income countries who will benefit from the expanded inclusive employment opportunities and accessible workplace and digital tools offered by employers and service providers who utilize WorkWith. The impact of attaining employment is nothing short of transformational - from attaining an income to increased independence and self-esteem. Family members also gain when a person with disabilities is able to work.
Employers and services providers (vocational training centers, micro-finance institutions, business incubators) will directly benefit from the WorkWith solutions by accessing a network of resources and a list of reasonable accommodations for making their workplace or services more accessible. The ones using digital solutions will be able to use tips and recommendations for improving digital accessibility.
WorkWith will also support development actors to make their projects more inclusive, reaching an even larger audience. Users will include:
•	Entrepreneurs or job seekers with disabilities wishing to develop their own business
•	Mainstream economic development practitioners (those working in NGOs, local nonprofits or community-based organizations) who want to include participants with disabilities in their programs, giving people with disabilities more access to the benefits of development projects. 
•	Organizations of persons with disabilities who are supporting people with disabilities in their communities as well as advocating for employment and accessibility
Key technologies: Online platform - dedicated internet site
Unique Characteristics:
WorkWith offers a first-of-its-kind, user-friendly solution to two massive problems across low- and middle-income countries: lack of employment opportunities for people with disabilities and lack of employers and service providers’ knowledge regarding making workplace and service accessible.
Currently, companies and service providers lack a centralized platform to access and share practical examples of reasonable accommodations tailored to diverse contexts. While existing networks disseminate reports, studies, and project outcomes aimed at improving employment access for persons with disabilities, they often fall short of offering concrete, actionable solutions. Moreover, employers and service providers frequently lack the time to engage with theoretical literature to develop effective medium-term strategies. Although companies and financial actors in both developed and middle-income countries (Bolivia, China, Columbia, India, Morocco, Philippines, etc.) are implementing inclusive solutions, these efforts often remain fragmented and invisible.
Our proposed solution addresses these gaps by offering an accessible online database where users can quickly discover practical workplace and reasonable accommodation options. This significantly lowers the entry barrier for employers and service providers to implement inclusive practices. The platform is also designed to be cost-effective, leveraging contributions from its user network to continually expand and enrich the resource base.

The tool box was initially developed in 2019 with funding from and in partnership with human-centered design firm IDEO.org. Dozens of stakeholders, including organizations of persons with disabilities (OPDs), international nongovernmental organizations (INGOs), vocational training centers, businesses, and others from Nepal, Kenya, and the United States, contributed their time, expertise, and attention to the development of the tool. Persons with disabilities were directly involved throughout the process, contributing to both the design and content development, and participating in user testing as volunteers. In the initial stage, over 100 unique accommodations—including hundreds of photos—from Bangladesh, Nepal, Kenya, Senegal, and Tunisia were collected and shared. Convinced of the project's merits from the outset, HI has been seeking adequate funding to bring the project to its next phase. While feedback from test users has been very positive, the platform requires additional content and refinement to deliver sufficient value to its users.

To enhance the value of the platform, several improvements are considered. These include:
•	Adding more diverse examples that reflect different contexts, sectors, and user experiences—particularly from developed, middle income and and low-income countries to offer a starter package with sufficient content
•	Content will be translated into additional languages to increase accessibility for a global audience. 
•	The platform’s structure and functionality have to be reorganized and refined to make it easier for users to search for and identify relevant solutions. 
•	Additionally, the section on recommendations and tips for mainstreaming accessibility—including digital accessibility and alignment with international WCAG standards—has to be strengthened. 
•	Finally, a business model will be reviewed and tested to ensure sustainability, enabling a wide range of users to contribute content, whether through financial support or proposition of reasonable accommodations documented with descriptions and pictures.
Sustainable Change:
1. Shifting mindsets through awareness and accessibility of knowledge
WorkWith challenges the misconception that disability inclusion is complex or expensive. By presenting practical, low-cost, and globally relevant solutions in an easy-to-use platform, it empowers employers, service providers, and entrepreneurs to take action, especially in low- and middle-income countries where information and resources are often scarce.

2. Building capacity for long-term inclusion
The platform is designed for non-experts, helping mainstream stakeholders (such as small business owners, training centers, or government programs) understand and implement inclusion without needing specialized background knowledge. This fosters sustained behavior change and builds internal capacity within institutions and communities.

3. Encouraging innovation and local adaptation
By collecting and sharing accommodation examples from around the world, WorkWith promotes peer learning and local adaptation. Users can both access and contribute solutions, creating a feedback loop that keeps the platform dynamic and responsive to real-world needs.

4. Supporting inclusive digital transformation
With a strong focus on digital accessibility, WorkWith addresses a critical barrier to inclusion: the digital divide. By promoting ICT tools and solutions for persons with disabilities, the platform helps ensure that disability inclusion is built into the growing digital infrastructure, not added as an afterthought.

5. Influencing systems through cross-sector engagement
WorkWith targets multiple sectors—employment, economic services, entrepreneurship, and nonprofits—ensuring that disability inclusion becomes a cross-cutting priority. This multi-sector approach supports systemic change, embedding inclusion in key systems that drive economic and social development.
Funding Sources: WorkWith was born out of a competitive, disability-focused “design challenge” in which Humanity & Inclusion was one of the six organizations out of 480 submissions that won and received seed funding. The tool box was initially developed in 2019 with funding from and in partnership with human-centered design firm IDEO.org.
Primary thematic focus area: Inclusive Digital Innovation Skills & Entrepreneurial Talent Development
Summary: WorkWith is an innovative platform designed to remove barriers to employment for people with disabilities by providing practical, accessible solutions for workplace accommodations. It leverages a centralized digital resource to share best practices, guidelines, and technical tools for inclusion. While the solution has significant potential, its scalability and long-term sustainability depend on securing funding and expanding its network of partners and users.

Title: Inclusive Digital Marketplace for Underrepresented Artisans
Subtitle: A digital platform connecting women-led artisan brands to global buyers, bridging the digital divide through e-commerce access, training, and market visibility.
Problem Statement: Millions of women artisans in MENA face digital exclusion. Without access to online tools, e-commerce platforms, or marketing expertise, their businesses remain invisible, limiting income and growth.
Solution Overview:
Ptah is a digital marketplace that consolidates women-led artisan brands into one online platform, providing them with visibility, sales channels, and digital training. Our methodology combines e-commerce infrastructure, digital marketing, and storytelling to connect artisans to global customers. 

We plan to collaborate with local NGOs, women entrepreneur networks, and logistics partners to streamline onboarding and delivery. 

Technologies used include a mobile-responsive web app, social commerce integrations, and analytics tools for performance tracking.
Solution Provider(s): Ptah Crafts (E-commerce & Digital Inclusion – Egypt), Local artisan cooperatives, Women-led SME partners
Implementation location(s): Egypt, serving artisans nationwide; scalable to MENA region.
Duration to pilot in a new geography: 6–9 months for adaptation, onboarding, and launch.
SDGs addressed: SDG 5 (Gender Equality);SDG 8 (Decent Work and Economic Growth);SDG 10 (Reduced Inequalities);
Desired impact:
Objectives: Increase market access and income for women artisans in MENA through digital inclusion.
Key Impacts: In pilot phase, 3+ artisans onboarded, long-term target to reach 10,000 artisans and create sustainable income opportunities (with average 30% revenue increase in 6 months).
Key technologies: E-commerce platform, social commerce integration (Instagram/Facebook shops), analytics dashboard, digital payment systems.
Unique Characteristics: Combines a niche product focus (handcrafted décor) with social impact for women entrepreneurs, localized onboarding, and storytelling to preserve cultural heritage while creating market competitiveness.
Sustainable Change: By equipping women artisans with digital sales channels and skills, Ptah shifts them from informal, low-revenue activities to formal, scalable businesses. This fosters inclusive economic growth, preserves cultural heritage, and sets a model replicable in other emerging markets facing similar digital gaps.
Funding Sources: Bootstrapped by founders; small in-kind contributions from local partners (e.g., marketing collaborations, event participation). Currently seeking grants and strategic partnerships for scale-up.
Primary thematic focus area: MSME Empowerment & Local Digital Innovation
Summary: Ptah is an inclusive digital platform aimed at empowering women artisans in the MENA region by providing them access to global markets, digital sales channels, and capacity-building tools. This solution addresses the digital exclusion faced by women artisans in MENA by enabling them to showcase and sell their handcrafted goods online while preserving cultural heritage.

Title: Portable Digital Identity & Compliance Infrastructure for Industrial Workforces
Subtitle: Real-time worker verification, permit issuance, and site compliance for high-risk, high-volume industries.
Problem Statement: Industrial sites in emerging markets face significant operational delays, safety incidents, and compliance gaps due to manual, fragmented systems for verifying worker identity, credentials, and permits. This causes billions in productivity losses and exposes organizations to regulatory and reputational risks.
Solution Overview:
Nashid is a modular, identity-first workforce management platform designed for industrial ecosystems such as construction, oil & gas, logistics, and manufacturing. It digitizes and automates the “who, where, when, and what” of site operations through:

- Worker Wallets (cloud or mobile) holding verifiable credentials (permits, training, ID, safety records) anchored to decentralized identifiers and verifiable credentials standards.
- Site Management Dashboard for real-time permit issuance, access control, task assignment, muster tracking, and compliance monitoring.
- API Layer for integration with access hardware, government data sources, and enterprise systems (ERP, WMS, safety systems).

Methodology & Technology:

- Decentralized identity (DIDs, VCs) for tamper-proof credentials
- NFC, QR, and biometric authentication
- Offline-first architecture with cloud sync
- Integration with national ID systems and training providers

Partnerships & Collaboration:

- Government: Oman’s regulators governing the local IT infrastructure
- Industry: NEOM (KSA), OQ (Oman), ADNOC (UAE) pilots
- Technology: Access control hardware vendors, AI-driven safety analytics providers
Implementation location(s): We have been approved for pilots in NEOM out of Saudi, and in ADNOC out of UAE
Duration to pilot in a new geography: 8 to 12 weeks (adhere to data regulations, site assessment, setup, onboarding, training, live testing)
SDGs addressed: SDG 8 (Decent Work and Economic Growth);SDG 9 (Industry, Innovation, and Infrastructure);SDG 10 (Reduced Inequalities);
Desired impact:
Key Objectives:
- Increase workforce safety, compliance, and trust through real-time verification
- Reduce operational delays and fraud in workforce management
- Enable worker mobility and recognition across projects and geographies

Key impact:
- To empower 10 million blue-coller economy, by providing workers and tradespeople the visibility, recognition, and trust they deserve — enabling fair access to opportunities and ensuring their skills and contributions are valued across projects and employers, and that they are catered to and accounted for.
Key technologies:
- W3C Decentralized Identifiers (DIDs) 
- W3C Verifiable Credentials (VCs)
- The Blockchain
- Near Field Communication (NFC)
- AI for facial recognition and matching
Unique Characteristics:
- Only platform unifying identity, access, time, and task workflows at the workforce level
- Portable worker identity wallets enabling cross-project mobility and faster onboarding
- Privacy-preserving, decentralized credential model ensuring trust without centralized data hoarding
- Hardware-agnostic integration model for rapid, low-disruption deployments
Sustainable Change: By becoming the trusted identity and compliance layer across industrial ecosystems, Nashid creates a reusable, verified workforce pool recognized by multiple employers, contractors, and regulators. This reduces onboarding friction, increases labor mobility, strengthens safety culture, and drives a shift from paper-based, reactive compliance to proactive, data-driven workforce governance.
Funding Sources: Through VCs like NEOM's Tonomus, Cyfr Capital, and Oman Technology Fund (OTF)
Primary thematic focus area: Stable and Resilient Digital Supply Chains
Summary: Nashid is a workforce management platform designed to streamline identity verification, permit issuance, and compliance monitoring across high-risk industries. The platform leverages decentralized identifiers, biometrics, and real-time data synchronization to enhance workforce safety, reduce operational delays, and improve compliance. It integrates with national ID systems and industrial hardware to ensure efficiency and security in worker management.

Name of your organization: Réseau Soutien aux Entrepreneurs de Guinée (RSEG)
Title: Numérique Vert pour Tous ( Numérique Vert pour Tous est une innovation digitale qui place le numérique au service de l’action climatique. Elle s’appuie sur une plateforme web et mobile conçue pour sensibiliser, former et accompagner les jeunes et les femmes entrepreneurs dans l’adoption de pratiques écologiques.)
Subtitle: Éco-Tech pour Tous
Problem Statement: En Guinée, l’action climatique se heurte à deux défis majeurs : le manque d’accès des jeunes et des femmes, surtout en zones rurales, aux outils numériques et aux connaissances écologiques, et l’insuffisance de solutions locales adaptées aux réalités environnementales. Cette double fracture — numérique et écologique — limite l’adoption de pratiques durables, freine l’innovation verte et aggrave les impacts du changement climatique sur les communautés vulnérables.
Solution Overview:
Numérique Vert pour Tous est une plateforme web et mobile (accessible en ligne et hors ligne) qui sensibilise, forme et accompagne jeunes et femmes entrepreneurs vers des pratiques écologiques.
Elle combine :
Bibliothèque numérique verte (guides, vidéos, fiches pratiques).
Formations hybrides (cours en ligne + ateliers terrain).
Espace collaboratif digital pour échanges, co-création et mise en relation avec experts et investisseurs.
Méthodologies et technologies : apprentissage par la pratique, mentorat, suivi-évaluation continu, application web responsive (PWA), contenus légers adaptés aux faibles débits, synchronisation hors ligne/ligne.
Partenariats : Orange Digital Center Conakry (logistique, salles), associations locales (mobilisation), médias (sensibilisation), experts bénévoles (agriculture durable, tech). Modèle collaboratif basé sur la co-création et l’adaptation aux réalités locales.
Solution Provider(s): Fournisseur(s) de solutions Orange Digital Center Conakry – Centre d’innovation et de formation numérique, secteur : télécommunications et TIC. Africa Connexion TV – Média audiovisuel spécialisé dans la sensibilisation et la valorisation des initiatives africaines, secteur : médias et communication. Associations communautaires de jeunes et de femmes – Organisations locales engagées dans le développement communautaire, secteur : économie sociale et solidaire. Experts bénévoles en agriculture durable et TIC – Professionnels indépendants, secteurs : agroécologie et technologies de l’information. Autres partenaires : réseaux panafricains en discussion pour extensions, développeurs web bénévoles, formateurs indépendants.
Implementation location(s): Guinée – Conakry (commune de Ratoma, quartier Nongo) et zones rurales de Dubréka et Coyah.
Implementation timeline(s): Phase pilote lancée en janvier 2025 et en cours, avec une première évaluation intermédiaire réalisée en juin 2025.
Duration to pilot in a new geography: Environ 6 mois, incluant la phase de diagnostic local (1 mois), l’adaptation des contenus et outils (2 mois), la formation initiale des bénéficiaires (2 mois) et l’évaluation intermédiaire (1 mois).
SDGs addressed: SDG 4 (Quality Education);SDG 13 (Climate Action);SDG 11 (Sustainable Cities and Communities);
Desired impact:
Démocratiser l’accès au numérique vert pour les jeunes et les femmes, en particulier en zones rurales.
Renforcer les compétences en pratiques écologiques et entrepreneuriat durable.
Réduire l’empreinte écologique locale par des actions concrètes et mesurables.
Principales réalisations (phase pilote) :
150 jeunes et femmes formés au numérique vert, compostage, agriculture durable.
20 mini-projets écologiques lancés (jardins urbains, recyclage, biofertilisants).
3,2 tonnes de déchets organiques traités par compostage (janv–juin 2025).
80 % des bénéficiaires ont modifié leurs pratiques environnementales, 45 % ont formé d’autres personnes localement.
Création de 5 emplois directs et mobilisation de 2 experts bénévoles.
Impact attendu à l’échelle régionale :
Extension à 500+ bénéficiaires en 2 ans.
Réduction estimée de 20 tonnes de déchets organiques par an.
Création de 20 à 30 emplois verts directs et indirects.
Key technologies:
Plateforme web et mobile responsive (PWA) : permet un accès facile sur smartphone et ordinateur, en ligne et hors ligne.
Synchronisation hors ligne / en ligne : les contenus sont accessibles même avec une connexion faible et se synchronisent automatiquement.
Contenus multimédias légers : vidéos, guides et infographies optimisés pour faibles débits internet.
Formulaires numériques et tableaux de bord : suivi des bénéficiaires et collecte de données pour évaluer l’impact.
Outils collaboratifs digitaux : forums, messagerie et espaces de co-création pour interaction entre bénéficiaires, experts et mentors.
Technologies exploratoires (en phase de développement) :
Data analytics pour suivi des comportements et ajustement des programmes.
Modules e-learning interactifs pour personnaliser l’apprentissage.
Unique Characteristics:
Approche hybride et inclusive : combinaison de formation en ligne, ateliers terrain et mentorat, adaptée aux zones rurales et aux populations marginalisées.
Accès hors ligne : la plateforme fonctionne même sans connexion internet, ce qui est rare dans les solutions numériques vertes en Afrique.
Co-création et collaboration : espace digital interactif favorisant le partage d’expériences, l’innovation collective et le lien direct avec experts et investisseurs.
Double impact social et environnemental : inclusion numérique, autonomisation des jeunes et femmes, et réduction tangible des déchets et pratiques non durables.
Auto-financement initial et modèle scalable : la phase pilote a été auto-financée par la communauté RSEG, avec un potentiel de déploiement régional grâce à des partenariats stratégiques.
Adaptabilité locale : contenus et programmes modulables selon les réalités écologiques, économiques et culturelles des communautés bénéficiaires.
Sustainable Change:
Numérique Vert pour Tous vise à créer un impact durable en transformant les comportements, les capacités et les structures locales :
Renforcement des compétences et autonomie : en formant les jeunes et femmes aux pratiques écologiques et à l’entrepreneuriat vert, la solution crée une génération capable de prendre des décisions durables et d’influencer leur communauté.
Diffusion des bonnes pratiques : les bénéficiaires deviennent des relais locaux, multipliant les formations et inspirant d’autres initiatives vertes, générant un effet boule de neige.
Création d’écosystèmes collaboratifs : l’espace digital et les partenariats permettent un réseau d’acteurs locaux et régionaux engagés, facilitant l’innovation et l’adoption de solutions durables à grande échelle.
Impact environnemental concret : réduction des déchets, adoption de l’agriculture durable et promotion de l’économie circulaire contribuent à la résilience climatique locale et régionale.
Durabilité financière et sociale : modèle évolutif et partenariats stratégiques assurent la continuité des projets, la mobilisation de ressources et la pérennisation des actions.
Théorie du changement : formation → adoption de pratiques vertes → diffusion communautaire → émergence d’entrepreneurs verts → réduction des impacts environnementaux et renforcement de l’inclusion numérique, générant un cercle vertueux durable.
Funding Sources:
La phase pilote de Numérique Vert pour Tous a été auto-financée par les membres du Réseau de Soutien aux Entrepreneurs de Guinée (RSEG – Conakry), incluant :
Contributions financières personnelles des membres pour le développement de la plateforme et l’organisation des formations.

Manque d’accès au financement local pour les startups, TPE et commerçants informels.

Dépendance excessive aux financements extérieurs (aides internationales, dette publique, bailleurs étrangers).

Difficulté à mobiliser l’épargne citoyenne et diasporique pour le développement économique.

Manque de transparence et de traçabilité dans les circuits de financement actuels.

Faible culture d’épargne et de réinvestissement productif dans les communautés locales.

Absence d’offres d’épargne éthiques et rémunératrices orientées vers le développement.

Insuffisante mobilisation des collectivités locales et institutions dans le financement de proximité.

Fracture numérique entre entrepreneurs formels et informels (peu d’accès aux outils digitaux).

Faible maîtrise des compétences numériques chez les artisans, PME et personnes vulnérables.

Manque de plateformes en ligne adaptées aux besoins réels des petites entreprises africaines.

Exclusion des porteurs de projets non connectés des opportunités de financement et de formation.

Insuffisante création d’emplois durables faute d’un soutien financier et social adapté.

Inégalités d’accès aux financements responsables entre grandes entreprises et petits porteurs de projets.

Manque d’outils digitaux sécurisés et accessibles pour démocratiser le financement participatif en Afrique.
