Title: BRIDGE (Breaking Reproductive Inequities Digitally for Global Equity)
Subtitle: A youth-led digital health platform using USSD and telemedicine to close SRHR gaps, empower adolescents from age 15, and turn policy into practice.
Problem Statement:
Young people in Rwanda face persistent barriers to accessing sexual and reproductive health (SRH) services, despite major policy progress. The 2025 national law lowered the age of consent for SRHR services to 15 and officially recognized telemedicine, e-consultations, and e-medical records. Yet in practice, adolescents and youth still encounter stigma, judgment, and long travel distances when seeking care. According to the 2020 DHS, only 40% of young women aged 15–24 felt confident to seek contraception, and 7% of girls aged 15–19 are already mothers or pregnant with their first child.

Healthcare providers are also overloaded with high patient volumes, leaving little time to explain SRHR issues or answer youth questions. As a result, many young people rely on misinformation from peers or social media, further exposing them to risky decisions. While 87% of Rwandans own mobile phones, there is no trusted, private, youth-centered digital platform that translates these new rights into accessible care.

This gap between law and lived reality is what BRIDGE seeks to address, ensuring that every young person can access confidential, accurate, and timely SRHR support, starting from the age of 15.
Solution Overview:
BRIDGE is a youth-led digital health platform designed to transform Rwanda’s 2025 reforms on sexual and reproductive health (SRHR) and digital health into practical, accessible services for young people. The new law lowered the age of consent for SRHR services to 15 and officially recognized telemedicine, e-consultations, and e-medical records. While this policy shift was groundbreaking, its impact will only be felt if young people can access these rights in ways that are private, youth-friendly, and inclusive. BRIDGE provides exactly that turning law into lived reality.

The platform works through a simple USSD code, for example *909#, which any young person can dial from a basic phone, even without internet. Once connected, they are presented with a confidential menu in Kinyarwanda, English, or French. From there, they can explore accurate SRHR information, request a call back from a youth-friendly doctor, or click a link to join a real-time chat. A built-in chatbot provides immediate answers to common questions, while live consultations with certified doctors and counselors offer personal support and counseling. For ongoing needs, users can also access an optional e-health locker a secure, PIN-protected space where they can save reminders, notes from consultations, or track their menstrual cycle. This digital health record is fully user-controlled, giving young people ownership of their health information for the first time.

The methodologies that guide BRIDGE are centered on inclusivity, youth empowerment, and digital innovation. By combining USSD technology, telemedicine integration, real-time chat support, and secure e-health records, the platform is designed to reach young people where they are whether in urban or rural settings, with or without internet. Recognizing that many youth prefer quick conversations over reading long texts, the solution emphasizes call and chat options, ensuring information is delivered in a way that is accessible, convenient, and engaging for a digital generation.

Partnerships are central to the success of BRIDGE. We will work with the Ministry of Health to ensure alignment with national SRHR and digital health priorities. District-level Youth SRHR Champions will act as peer educators, raising awareness and guiding their peers to use the platform. Healthcare providers will be directly engaged to provide live consultations and counseling, while telecom companies will host the USSD service. Private sector actors such as menstrual health product companies or youth-focused financial services will be invited to support free access for rural users through sponsorships. Finally, development partners and NGOs including UNFPA, AmplifyChange, and other SRHR-focused organizations will provide technical input, funding support, and pathways to scale.

By combining low-tech access, high-quality telemedicine, and youth-led outreach, BRIDGE ensures that young people starting from the age of 15 can access confidential, accurate, and timely SRHR services. It is an affordable, inclusive, and legally compliant model that not only addresses Rwanda’s pressing challenges but can also be adapted and scaled across Africa to break reproductive health inequities digitally and drive global equity.
Solution Provider(s): URUNGANO Initiative – A youth-led organization co-founded by young Rwandan medical doctors and SRHR Champions who believe in the power of digital health to transform lives. The Initiative was established to close gaps in sexual and reproductive health access, particularly for adolescents and young people, by leveraging innovation, advocacy, and community-driven solutions. With its leadership rooted in both medical expertise and grassroots activism, URUNGANO is uniquely positioned to spearhead BRIDGE. The team is ready to lead this initiative with passion, credibility, and technical know-how, ensuring youth voices are not only represented but actively shape policy-to-practice solutions. (Sector: Civil Society, Youth-led SRHR Innovation)  Rwanda Biomedical Center (RBC), Ministry of Health – The government body responsible for health systems, policy, and digital integration. RBC will ensure the solution aligns with Rwanda’s national e-health strategy and SRHR priorities. (Sector: Government, Public Health)  AfriYAN Rwanda (African Youth and Adolescents Network on Population and Development) – A coalition amplifying adolescent and youth voices in SRHR advocacy. AfriYAN will support peer-led mobilization, training of SRHR Champions, and advocacy for equitable access. (Sector: Youth Network, Advocacy)  MTN Rwanda & Airtel Rwanda – Leading telecom operators that will provide the USSD infrastructure to ensure national reach, bridging the gap for rural and underserved youth. (Sector: Telecommunications, Private Sector)  Rwanda Telemedicine Society (RTS) – A network of health professionals advancing digital healthcare delivery. RTS will provide medical experts for teleconsultations and contribute to building an integrated e-medical records system. (Sector: Healthcare, Digital Health)  UNFPA Rwanda (United Nations Population Fund) – A key development partner in SRHR, UNFPA will provide technical guidance, knowledge-sharing, and potential resourcing to strengthen the innovation’s impact. (Sector: Development Partner, UN Agency)
Duration to pilot in a new geography: We anticipate that piloting BRIDGE in a new geography will take 12 months.
SDGs addressed: SDG 3 (Good Health and Well-being);SDG 5 (Gender Equality);SDG 10 (Reduced Inequalities);
Desired impact:
The BRIDGE solution seeks to transform the sexual and reproductive health (SRH) landscape for young people in Rwanda by reducing unintended pregnancies, increasing contraceptive uptake, and lowering maternal mortality associated with unsafe abortion. Rwanda’s youth face a pressing SRH crisis: nearly half of all pregnancies are unintended, with around 114 unintended pregnancies occurring annually per 1,000 women aged 15–44. Alarmingly, almost 22% of these unintended pregnancies end in induced abortion, many performed under unsafe conditions that endanger the health and lives of young women. The consequences are reflected in maternal mortality statistics, with unsafe abortion and related complications accounting for an estimated 18% of maternal deaths in the country.

At the same time, while awareness of contraception is relatively high, uptake among young people remains strikingly low. Only 18.1% of sexually active adolescents aged 15–19 and 38.7% of those aged 20–24 use a contraceptive method, leaving a wide gap between knowledge and consistent practice. This gap is fueled by stigma, privacy concerns, and poor access to youth-friendly services especially in rural communities where over 70% of Rwandan youth live. The recent 2025 legal reform that now allows adolescents from the age of 15 to access SRH services provides an unprecedented opportunity to address these challenges, but translating policy into meaningful practice requires innovative, inclusive solutions.

BRIDGE directly responds to this need by leveraging USSD technology, telemedicine, and youth-led peer support to deliver confidential, real-time SRH information and counseling. By giving adolescents the ability to connect discreetly with trained providers, the platform lowers barriers of stigma, mistrust, and distance. Our approach not only empowers young people with accurate knowledge but also supports them in making informed choices that can prevent unintended pregnancies and reduce reliance on unsafe abortion. In doing so, BRIDGE contributes to lowering maternal complications and deaths while aligning with national strategies for adolescent health and digital transformation.

The desired impact of BRIDGE is clear: to double contraceptive uptake among youth in our pilot cohort, to reduce unintended pregnancies by at least 20% within the first year of implementation, and to contribute to a measurable decline in unsafe abortion-related complications. Beyond health outcomes, the solution also aims to empower adolescents through digital literacy and leadership opportunities, with at least 100 Youth SRHR Champions trained to drive change within their communities. By addressing structural barriers through technology and peer-led engagement, BRIDGE will not only save lives but also reshape how Rwanda’s young people access and experience sexual and reproductive healthcare.
Key technologies:
The BRIDGE solution is powered by simple yet impactful digital technologies designed to reach young people regardless of their device, location, or connectivity. At its core, we use USSD (Unstructured Supplementary Service Data) technology, which allows even those without smartphones or internet access to interact with our platform through any mobile phone. This ensures inclusion of rural and low-income adolescents, who often face the greatest barriers to SRHR services.

To complement USSD, we integrate telemedicine platforms that enable remote consultations with youth-friendly doctors and counselors through secure digital channels. These consultations are supported by electronic medical records (EMRs), allowing for secure, confidential, and continuous documentation of adolescent health interactions, which improves follow-up and continuity of care.

The platform also leverages chatbot technology embedded within the USSD and web interfaces to deliver instant SRHR information, reminders, and referrals in multiple languages. Over time, the chatbot will be enhanced with artificial intelligence (AI) capabilities to personalize information based on user needs and behavior, making the system smarter and more responsive with each interaction.

For monitoring and evaluation, BRIDGE employs data analytics tools to aggregate anonymized usage data. This enables us to generate insights on youth SRHR trends, service uptake, and emerging needs while maintaining strict privacy protections. These insights are valuable not only for service delivery but also for informing policy and programming at national and regional levels.

Together, these technologies USSD, telemedicine, EMRs, chatbots, and analytics form a robust ecosystem that bridges the gap between policy and practice, ensuring equitable access to sexual and reproductive health for adolescents starting at age 15.
Unique Characteristics:
What makes BRIDGE truly unique is that it is born from the lived realities of young people in Rwanda, designed by youth leaders who understand the barriers their peers face when seeking sexual and reproductive health (SRH) services. Unlike many digital health solutions that require smartphones and internet connectivity, BRIDGE prioritizes inclusion through USSD technology, making it accessible on even the most basic phones. This means that a girl in rural Nyagatare or a boy in Rusizi without internet access can still dial a simple code and connect to life-saving information and support. In Rwanda, where over 70% of youth live in rural areas, this approach is not just innovative it is essential.

Another distinctive feature of BRIDGE is its alignment with the 2025 legal reforms that lowered the age of consent for SRHR services to 15 and formally recognized telemedicine and e-medical records. While many projects stop at advocacy, BRIDGE moves quickly to turn policy into practice, offering a ready-to-use system that gives effect to these progressive reforms. This direct connection between national policy change and grassroots service delivery sets the platform apart as a timely and contextually relevant innovation.

Our business model is also different. Instead of relying solely on donor funding, BRIDGE integrates blended financing mechanisms that include affordable micro-payments from youth, institutional partnerships with schools and NGOs, and corporate sponsorships from youth-friendly brands. This not only ensures sustainability but also creates a sense of ownership among young users, schools, and the private sector. By balancing affordability with institutional support, the model creates a financially viable pathway for long-term growth.

BRIDGE’s uniqueness also lies in its youth-centered design and governance. The platform is co-founded and led by young Rwandan medical doctors and SRHR champions who bring both technical expertise and community trust. Young people are not just users but also co-creators and champions trained to support their peers as “Youth SRHR Champions.” This model builds a multiplier effect: each trained champion extends the platform’s impact far beyond the digital space, reaching classrooms, communities, and families.

BRIDGE is distinguished by its human-centered use of technology. While it uses digital tools such as USSD, telemedicine, and chatbots, it never loses sight of the human connection. The platform ensures that young people speak to real, youth-friendly providers when needed, receive reminders that fit their daily lives, and know that their privacy is respected. This balance of digital innovation and human care makes BRIDGE not just a technology, but a trusted partner in young people’s health journey.

BRIDGE is innovative not because it introduces flashy technology, but because it combines low-tech accessibility, policy alignment, sustainable financing, and youth leadership into a single solution that responds directly to Rwanda’s unique context.
Sustainable Change:
BRIDGE is designed not as a short-term project but as a driver of systemic transformation in Rwanda’s sexual and reproductive health ecosystem. Its sustainability lies in the way it connects progressive national policies to real community needs through inclusive technology, while empowering young people to become both beneficiaries and agents of change.

The starting point is Rwanda’s 2025 legal reform, which lowered the age of consent for sexual and reproductive health (SRH) services to 15 and formally recognized telemedicine and e-medical records. These policies opened an unprecedented window of opportunity, but laws alone do not guarantee access. BRIDGE transforms this policy into practice by offering a youth-led digital health platform that works through USSD and telemedicine. This ensures that every young person, whether in urban Kigali or in a remote rural village, can confidentially access accurate SRH information, counseling, and services without stigma or unnecessary barriers.

The immediate effect of this approach is to break down geographical, cultural, and systemic obstacles that prevent adolescents from seeking care. With a simple USSD code accessible on basic phones, young people are connected to trained health providers and youth champions, while anonymized data feeds into national health systems to inform decision-making. This creates a reliable digital-first infrastructure for SRH services that is inclusive, scalable, and trusted.

Over time, the ripple effects grow. By normalizing confidential digital access, BRIDGE empowers adolescents to make informed choices, which in turn increases uptake of contraception, reduces unintended pregnancies, and helps lower maternal mortality from unsafe abortions an issue that still accounts for about 13% of maternal deaths in Rwanda. The platform also reduces school dropout rates among girls by preventing early, unintended pregnancies, contributing to broader goals of gender equality and educational attainment.

At the institutional level, BRIDGE builds a culture of evidence-based policymaking by generating real-time data on youth SRH behaviors and needs. Schools, NGOs, and even local governments can integrate the platform into their programs, ensuring that digital SRHR becomes embedded into Rwanda’s wider health and education systems. Partnerships with telecom companies and private sponsors provide financial resilience, while youth co-founders and champions ensure local ownership and long-term commitment.

Ultimately, the systemic change envisioned is both cultural and structural. Culturally, BRIDGE helps shift norms by reducing stigma and making youth SRHR a normal, accepted part of healthcare. Structurally, it strengthens Rwanda’s digital health system and demonstrates how progressive laws can be successfully translated into practical services. The desired follow-on effects include policy reinforcement, stronger health equity, and Rwanda’s positioning as a regional leader in youth-led digital health innovation.

In this way, BRIDGE is not just a solution to today’s gaps but a sustainable pathway toward an inclusive, rights-based health system, one where no young person is left behind and where digital innovation ensures that policy translates into practice for generations to come.
Funding Sources: Not yet Funded. It's an Idea.
Primary thematic focus area: Inclusive Digital Innovation Skills & Entrepreneurial Talent Development
Summary: BRIDGE is a youth-led digital health platform using USSD and telemedicine to close gaps in sexual and reproductive health (SRH) access for young people in Rwanda. The solution is innovative, leveraging low-tech accessibility and a human-centered design, but its potential for scalability and financial sustainability needs further clarity.

Title: R Universal – Solutions for a Resilient Recycled Plastics Supply Chain
Subtitle: R Universal is an in-house cloud-based, model-driven, IoT- and AI-enabled solution, combining rERP, rMES, and DPLUS to cover production, operations, and equipment management, providing end-to-end visibility, cost traceability, and predictive maintenance for recycled plastics.
Problem Statement:
The recycled plastics manufacturing sector, although essential for the circular economy, struggles with structural barriers caused by limited digitalisation and weak ESG alignment:
Production
•	Raw materials are highly variable and non-standard, which is often inconsistent in type, quality, and contamination levels, making it difficult to achieve consistent product quality.
•	Manual or outdated systems for tracking workflow stages (e.g., sorting, washing, shredding) can lead to bottlenecks and inefficiencies.
Operations
•	Plastic waste often needs to be stored temporarily, requiring space and creating risks of contamination or degradation.
•	Critical production and operational data are often manually recorded, delayed, fragmented, or inaccurate.
•	Managers cannot make precise, evidence-based decisions due to a lack of real-time visibility.
•	Limited ability to trace the origin of plastic waste to verify whether it meets regulatory and sustainability requirements, and access requirement to ESG-aligned markets.
Equipment
•	Frequent Maintenance: Recycling machinery experiences significant wear and tear due to abrasive contaminants in plastic waste, leading to frequent maintenance and downtime.
•	Lack of real-time monitoring leads to unplanned downtime and inefficient energy use.
•	Operating and maintaining advanced recycling equipment requires skilled workers, which can be a challenge in regions with limited training resources.
Others
•	A significant challenge is the absence of specialised software designed to address recyclers' specific needs.
•	Advanced software solutions often involve significant upfront costs, licensing fees, and maintenance, making them less friendly for SMEs.
•	Traditional solutions often lack compatibility with IoT technologies and fail to incorporate advanced AI for enabling predictive maintenance.
Solution Overview:
Our solution provides a fully integrated digital platform for production, operations, and equipment management, enabling end-to-end visibility and coordinated control across recycled plastics manufacturing. By managing key production factors — people, machines, and materials — it ensures stable production, efficiency, and product quality.
rERP – Operational Platform:
•	Tailored for recycled plastics manufacturers, covering the full process from procurement to sales.
•	Fully integrated with the production system (rMES) to support production scheduling and execution.
•	Provides precise tracking of raw material consumption, product generation, and special product markings, ensuring accurate operational and cost data.
rMES – Production Platform:
•	Captures the full production process from input to output, updating inventory and cost in real time.
•	Supports reverse supply chain workflows and other industry-specific processes.
•	Displays production data in real time, enabling managers to monitor and optimise the shop floor continuously.
DPLUS – Intelligent Equipment Maintenance Platform:
•	Monitors PLC data and core equipment components operational parameters via IoT sensors, enabling unified line-wide monitoring.
•	Allows users to define custom operational rules and alerts for predictive maintenance, while building a knowledge base for equipment management.
•	Uses machine learning to learn equipment patterns and provide actionable maintenance recommendations, improving uptime and operational reliability.
Technologies & Methodologies:
•	Integrated ERP/MES framework, IoT sensor networks, real-time dashboards, AI/ML analytics.
•	Provides digital visibility across production, operations, and equipment, with optional ESG data collection (energy usage, waste tracking) as a complementary feature.
Collaboration & Implementation:
•	Designed for MSMEs, with modular architecture allowing easy deployment, training, and future scaling.
•	Works with local manufacturing partners to make the light bespoke to each production environment.
Solution Provider(s): Golden Data (provider of digital transformation solutions for sustainable manufacturing, specialising in rERP, rMES, and IoT for circular industries), AWS (provider of cloud service)
Implementation timeline(s): UK: Feb 2024 – Feb 2025, China: Jul 2025 – Present
Duration to pilot in a new geography: 6–9 months per site, including installation, training, and data integration
SDGs addressed: SDG 9 (Industry, Innovation, and Infrastructure);SDG 12 (Responsible Consumption and Production);SDG 13 (Climate Action);
Desired impact:
Objectives:
Improve operational efficiency, reduce downtime, enhance cost visibility, and deliver traceable, ESG-ready data.

Key Impacts:
•	15~20% reduction in raw material waste through digital quality mapping.
•	10~20% reduction in energy consumption via IoT-enabled predictive maintenance.
•	15~20% increase in labour productivity and onboarding efficiency for new staff.
•	60~70% reduction in internal data collection, analysis, and third-party audit time.
•	Automated ESG metrics embedded in production reports, ensuring compliance with global sustainability standards.
•	Greater buyer confidence and supply chain traceability, strengthening MSME participation in ESG-certified markets.
Key technologies:
•	IoT sensors and digital dashboards for real-time ESG and production data.
•	AI and predictive analytics for energy optimisation and waste reduction.
•	ERP/MES cloud platforms with built-in ESG performance modules.
•	Blockchain-ready architecture for transparent ESG reporting across supply chains.
Unique Characteristics:
Our solution is unique because it is purpose-built for recycled plastics manufacturers operating in fragmented, non-standardised, and ESG-driven environments. Unlike conventional industrial software designed for standardised production lines, our solution integrates sector-specific digital tools, model-driven flexibility to meet the realities of reverse supply chains.

Key differentiators include:

Production
•	Purpose-built for recycled plastics, capturing complex workflows and heterogeneous raw materials.
•	Allows digital standardisation and traceability where generic ERP/MES solutions fail.

Operations
•	Integrated digital ecosystem combining rERP, rMES, and DPlus (IoT) for real-time, evidence-based operational decisions.
•	Centralised data visibility bridges gaps in cost control, production tracking, and supply chain accountability.

Equipment
•	Equipment model-driven foundation allows custom machinery to be digitally monitored and optimised.
•	AI/ML-powered predictive maintenance reduces unplanned downtime and energy consumption.
•	Supports customised event rules, comparative analysis, and knowledge retention, ensuring operational knowledge is preserved and shared across teams.

ESG-Linked Innovation
•	Utilises IoT technology to collect energy consumption data， such as current usage, and gas emissions.
•	Supports ESG audits and helps enterprises perform self-evaluation, reducing the risk of greenwashing.
•	Provides actionable insights to optimise energy use while maintaining production efficiency.

Overall Innovation
•	Sector-specific, model-driven, fully integrated platform covering production, operations, and equipment.
•	Scalable, modular design for MSMEs and replicable. Lightweight bespoke development enables scalability to other production environments and circular economy industries.
•	Data visualisation supports evidence-based decision-making, improving transparency and management efficiency.
Sustainable Change:
Production:
•	Digital standardisation and traceability of raw materials and products reduce waste and improve quality consistency, supporting sustainable manufacturing practices.

Operations:
•	Real-time visibility of production, cost, and inventory enables evidence-based decision-making, strengthening management capacity in MSMEs.
•	Data-driven insights foster continuous process optimisation and operational efficiency.

Equipment:
•	Predictive maintenance and knowledge retention from IoT and AI/ML monitoring reduce unplanned downtime and extend equipment life.
•	Customisable event rules and comparative analysis ensure operational knowledge is preserved and shared across teams.

Systemic Impact:
•	By integrating production, operations, and equipment into a unified digital platform, the solution creates a scalable, replicable model for other circular economy industries.
•	Optional ESG data collection (energy use, emissions) helps enterprises align with sustainability reporting standards and reduce greenwashing risk.

Overall, the solution enhances transparency, efficiency, and resilience, fostering a more sustainable, data-driven, and competitive industrial ecosystem.
Funding Sources: Funded through internal R&D investment and pilot partnerships with selected recycled plastics MSMEs.
Primary thematic focus area: MSME Empowerment & Local Digital Innovation
Summary: R Universal is an IoT- and AI-powered platform designed to improve the efficiency, traceability, and sustainability of the recycled plastics supply chain. The solution is tailored for MSMEs, addressing industry-specific needs and ESG alignment. Its key strength lies in integrating digital tools for production, operations, and equipment management, but more details on scalability and long-term financial sustainability are needed.

Name of your organization: Tisuka Incorporated Limited (Trading as Tisuka Group)
Title: Vendi: Empowering Entrepreneurs with Disabilities Through Inclusive E-Commerce
Subtitle: The online marketplace for all: zero upfront capital, full support, and real opportunities to grow.
Problem Statement:
All across Africa, people with disabilities face huge barriers to earning a living. According to The Zambian Federation of Disability Organizations and ILO, in Zambia over 60 percent of people with disabilities live below the poverty line, compared to the 50% of the population without disabilities living below the poverty line, and the unemployment rate for youths with disabilities sits around 16.8%, compared to 12.5% of youths without disabilities. 
Over 80% of Africans with disabilities are unemployed, not because they aren’t capable, but because society makes it difficult for them to work. Many cannot access loans or startup capital because banks and investors see them as high-risk. Even those who try to start businesses struggle to reach customers, as most marketplaces and online platforms are not designed to be accessible. Physical limitations, lack of digital tools, and social stigma make it hard to compete with others who don’t face these barriers.
On top of that, many people with disabilities are isolated from networks, mentorship, and support systems that could help them grow. They often have ideas and products, but no practical way to make a living or reach buyers. This leaves talented, capable African entrepreneurs stuck in poverty and prevents communities from benefiting from their skills and contributions.
Solution Overview:
How it works:
Vendi is an online platform that helps people with disabilities start businesses. People can join as suppliers who sell products at wholesale prices, or merchants who add their profit and sell the supplier products to customers without needing any money to start. Buyers come to Vendi to buy products at retail prices. When someone buys something, the money is shared between the supplier, the merchant, and Vendi. Vendi also takes care of delivery. This way, people with disabilities can earn money and become financially independent, even if they don’t have money to start a business.

Technology:
Tisuka built Vendi during one of our many social impact programs which was a mentorship program we have for Zambian entrepreneurs with disabilities. 
It has text-to-speech, speech-to-text, keyboard navigation, and screen reader tools so everyone can use it. We keep improving the platform by asking users for feedback and testing new ideas to make sure it works well.

Partnerships and Collaboration:
We work with organizations like Challenges Zambia and Sight Savers to find and support entrepreneurs with disabilities. We partner with suppliers to offer products and with delivery services to get items to customers. We also give mentorship and guidance through Tisuka Group’s network, and we never leave our entrepreneurs behind, but rather guide them through various different ways in which they are building their businesses.
Solution Provider(s): Challenges Zambia – A Zambian non-profit organization that supports entrepreneurs and innovation through training, mentorship, and business incubation. Sector: Entrepreneurship & Innovation Support.  Sight Savers – An international non-governmental organization working to prevent avoidable blindness, promote equality for people with disabilities, and support inclusive development. Sector: Disability Rights & Inclusion.
Implementation timeline(s): Between May 2025 and July 2025, 3 entrepreneurs with disabilities have used the platform and made sales
Duration to pilot in a new geography: 12 months
SDGs addressed: SDG 10 (Reduced Inequalities);SDG 9 (Industry, Innovation, and Infrastructure);SDG 8 (Decent Work and Economic Growth);
Desired impact:
Objectives:
-Empower entrepreneurs with and without disabilities to start and grow businesses with no upfront capital.
-Increase financial independence and economic participation among marginalized groups.
-Provide a fully accessible digital platform with mentorship, guidance, and tools to succeed.
-Expand the reach of small local businesses and suppliers, creating a sustainable marketplace.

Achievements:
-Generated ZMW 187,000 in sales in the pilot stage, demonstrating market demand.
-100 entrepreneurs with disabilities are set to be onboarded on the platform by December 2025 through partnerships with Challenges Zambia and Sight Savers.
-Shortlisted for Standard Chartered Women In Tech Zambia Program and given the opportunity to pitch Vendi
Key technologies:
1. AI-Powered Accessibility Enhancements
Vendi Africa employs the following AI-driven solutions to enhance web accessibility:
-Screen Reader Optimization: Facilitates navigation for users with visual impairments.
-Keyboard Navigation Support: Enables users to interact with the site using keyboard shortcuts.
-Font and Contrast Adjustments: Allows users to modify text size and contrast for better readability.
-Speech-to-Text and Text-to-Speech: Assists users with hearing or speech impairments in communication and navigation.

2. AI-Driven Product Recommendations
The platform utilizes machine learning algorithms to analyze user behavior and preferences, offering personalized product suggestions. 

3. Automated Order Management and Payment Processing
Vendi streamlines transactions through automated systems that manage orders and payments efficiently.

4. Real-Time Analytics and Feedback Mechanisms
The integration of analytics tools allows for the collection of user feedback and behavior data, enabling continuous improvement of the platform's features and services.
Unique Characteristics:
What makes Vendi truly innovative is that it breaks down barriers for entrepreneurs with disabilities in ways no other platform has done before. First, our business model is unique: entrepreneurs can start selling and earning without any capital. They don’t need loans, savings, or external funding- just a smartphone and the drive to succeed. The fact that we deliver makes it easy for our entrepreneurs to earn from home. And our business model alone opens doors that traditional business models simply don’t.

Secondly, Vendi is technologically inclusive. With AI-powered accessibility plug-ins like text-to-speech, speech-to-text, keyboard navigation, and screen readers, our platform ensures that entrepreneurs with visual, hearing, or mobility impairments can use it independently. This is not just a tech feature; it is a tool for empowerment.

Finally, we combine digital innovation with personal, ongoing mentorship. One could argue that anyone can take their successful e-commerce platform and add accessibility plug-ins to it, and we challenge that by showing that true impact comes from the deep, trusting relationships we’ve built with our entrepreneurs; our users, through ongoing mentorship, support, and understanding their real needs. We don’t just put entrepreneurs on a platform and leave them. Our team works with them in person, helping them grow skills, build confidence, and navigate challenges.
Sustainable Change:
Economic empowerment: Entrepreneurs gain sustainable income, improving their financial independence and quality of life.

Social inclusion: As more people with disabilities succeed in business, communities begin to recognize their capabilities, reducing stigma and promoting equity.

Skills development: Entrepreneurs gain digital literacy, marketing, and business management skills that last beyond the platform.

Marketplace transformation: Suppliers, merchants, and buyers adapt to more inclusive business practices, setting a new standard for accessible commerce.

Scalability: The model can be replicated across regions and countries, creating systemic change in how society supports entrepreneurs with disabilities.
Funding Sources: So far, Vendi has been fully funded by Tisuka Group. Following production of our MVP, we made sales during pilot testing and are now seeking funding to scale up (app development, customer acquisition, etc.)
Further comments/feedback:
I may not have much, but I have a vision, determination, and a deep love for the people I serve. I started this business as a 24-year-old dreamer; now, at 26, despite all my achievements I am still just trying to make a real difference in the world. My father is hard-of-hearing, my niece is a paraplegic, and through Vendi, I have grown to love my entrepreneurs like family. I eat in their homes, attend the weddings of their children, and celebrate their successes.

Tisuka has always been built on social impact, and that is why our projects succeed: at our core is care for people and solving problems no one else cares to address. Vendi is more than a platform- it’s a lifeline, a path to independence, and a way to change lives.

With your support, I promise I can do this. Give me the chance, and together we can create something lasting and transformative.
Primary thematic focus area: Inclusive Digital Innovation Skills & Entrepreneurial Talent Development
Summary: Vendi is an innovative e-commerce platform aimed at empowering entrepreneurs with disabilities by providing them with the tools to start and grow businesses without upfront capital. The solution integrates accessibility features and mentorship to ensure inclusive participation. The main challenge lies in securing funding for scaling and ensuring long-term sustainability beyond the pilot phase.

Title: SuiviVital – Inclusive Digital Health for All
Subtitle: An AI-powered digital health platform bridging healthcare access gaps through mobile and WhatsApp integration.
Problem Statement: In Africa and other underserved regions, healthcare systems remain fragmented, heavily paper-based, and inaccessible to large segments of the population. Rural and low-income communities, especially women and children, face barriers to timely care, lack of follow-up, and exclusion from digital health innovations. This deepens inequalities in health and economic participation.
Solution Overview:
How it works: SuiviVital digitizes healthcare access by combining AI, mobile applications, and WhatsApp-based health services to reach populations regardless of internet or literacy levels. Patients register via phone, receive automated reminders for appointments or medication, and access maternal and chronic disease support. Providers benefit from electronic health records, voice-to-text transcription for radiology, and real-time monitoring dashboards.

Methodologies and technologies:

AI for health risk prediction, maternal health monitoring, and anomaly detection in medical imaging.

Natural Language Processing for multilingual support (French, Moore, and local languages).

Cloud-based interoperability for healthcare facilities, pharmacies, and laboratories.

Integration with RoyalPay for secure digital payments, enabling affordable teleconsultations.

Partnerships and collaboration models:
SuiviVital partners with health ministries, NGOs, and local clinics to integrate services into national healthcare frameworks. We also work with telecom providers for SMS/WhatsApp delivery and with financial service providers for payment inclusion.
Solution Provider(s): AI-KING GROUP  Software development, AI models, and platform deployment, Minister of Health Hosting our patient data, Telecom company for sms service
Implementation location(s): Preparing to deploy at  Clinic Espoire in Ouagadougou Burkina Faso
Duration to pilot in a new geography: 6–9 months (including customization, training, and local partnerships).
SDGs addressed: SDG 3 (Good Health and Well-being);SDG 5 (Gender Equality);SDG 9 (Industry, Innovation, and Infrastructure);
Desired impact:
Objectives: Expand inclusive healthcare access, reduce missed appointments, empower women through maternal health support, and strengthen digital public health systems.

Achievements/Impacts:

a) Digitized medical records for pilot clinics, reducing paper burden.

b) 40% reduction in missed follow-up appointments in pilot areas.

c) Hundreds of women enrolled in maternal health monitoring programs.

d) Creation of jobs for health data officers and local developers.
Key technologies:
Artificial Intelligence (AI) for health predictions and imaging.

Natural Language Processing (NLP) for multilingual health support.

Cloud-based digital health infrastructure.

WhatsApp Business API and SMS for accessibility.

Digital payments integration (RoyalPay).
Unique Characteristics:
Inclusive by design: works on basic phones via WhatsApp/SMS, reaching populations with limited internet access.

AI-driven maternal and chronic disease support, tailored to local languages.

Integrated digital payment system for affordable and secure care access.

Partnership-first approach: works with ministries, clinics, and telecoms for systemic adoption.
Sustainable Change: SuiviVital fosters a digital health ecosystem that replaces manual, fragmented healthcare processes with interoperable, inclusive digital systems. By empowering patients to actively manage their health, reducing administrative burdens for providers, and integrating payment inclusion, the solution creates lasting systemic change. The theory of change: digital inclusion in healthcare → stronger health outcomes → improved productivity and economic participation → reduced inequalities in the digital economy.
Funding Sources: SuiviVital has been primarily funded through founder contributions and self-investment from AI-KING GROUP. We are now actively seeking partnerships, grants, and equity-free funding opportunities from global organizations, accelerators, and UN-led programs to scale implementation.
Testimonials and Endorsements:
Response from early tester: “SuiviVital has made it easier for me to store and track my diabetes data,  appointments, and vaccinations for my child. I receive reminders on WhatsApp, which reduces my stress of forgetting.” – Pregnant mother, Ouagadougou

“Our clinic reduced missed appointments significantly since using SuiviVital. The digital health records save us time and allow us to focus more on patients.” – Healthcare provider, Burkina Faso
Further comments/feedback: The questionnaire is comprehensive and aligns well with UN priorities on inclusive digital innovation. For early-stage African startups like SuiviVital, it is valuable that the call emphasizes matchmaking, technical support, and global visibility beyond funding. One suggestion would be to allow startups to submit short video pitches directly in the form, as this can help showcase solutions more dynamically to the expert jury.
Primary thematic focus area: Inclusive Digital Innovation Skills & Entrepreneurial Talent Development
Summary: SuiviVital bridges healthcare access gaps using AI, WhatsApp, and SMS to improve maternal health, chronic disease management, and appointment follow-ups. A notable strength is its inclusive design, making healthcare accessible via basic phones. However, the limited funding details and the lack of a proven track record in diverse geographies raise questions about long-term scalability.

Name of your organization: National Higher Polytechnic School of Douala
Title: Faith'SchooLab : VR Medical Training Revolution for Africa
Subtitle: Transforming medical education across Africa through ultra-affordable cardboard VR headsets and immersive 3D learning, bridging the digital divide in healthcare training.
Problem Statement: Across Africa, a deep educational crisis is crippling healthcare systems and endangering lives. In Cameroon and similar resource-limited settings, medical students graduate with dangerous gaps in practical skills, despite years of theoretical study. This isn’t just an inconvenience, it’s a life-or-death issue. A study by the West African Health Organization found that 76% of medical graduates feel “underprepared” for basic clinical procedures. This translates into preventable medical errors, contributing to 83,000 avoidable deaths annually in Sub-Saharan Africa. The root cause? Severe resource limitations that render traditional medical training unsustainable. At the University of Douala’s Faculty of Medicine, one anatomical model serves over 100 students. Cadaveric dissection, long considered the gold standard is nearly nonexistent due to cultural, financial, and ethical barriers. Advanced simulation tools remain out of reach when a single high-fidelity mannequin costs more than an entire department’s annual budget. The environmental impact is just as alarming. When specimens are available, they require formaldehyde and toxic preservatives, posing serious health risks and creating environmental hazards. Plastic anatomical models, beyond their prohibitive cost, contribute to growing waste problems in regions lacking proper recycling infrastructure. The result? Students dedicate years to medical training yet graduate unprepared for real-world clinical demands. A 2023 survey found that 63% of recent medical graduates in Cameroon suffer from severe anxiety about their competence. This crisis of confidence further weakens an already fragile healthcare system. But this problem isn’t limited to medicine. Across African education systems, practical, hands-on learning is a privilege, not a right. Students study science without experiments, agriculture without fieldwork, and technical disciplines without access to equipment. The consequences ripple across society: undertrained doctors, stagnant innovation, fragile economies, and wasted human potential. The gap between theory and practice remains a structural barrier that traditional educational models simply cannot overcome.
Solution Overview:
Faith'SchooLab is not just an innovation it’s an educational revolution. In many developing countries, hands-on learning is a luxury. We provide a clear, sustainable, and eco friendly solution that works without expensive infrastructure, without internet, and with a major social impact. Our approach is built on three key innovations : 
1.	Locally-produced, ultra-affordable VR technology: We’ve designed a cardboard VR headset made from recycled materials, which can be produced anywhere at minimal cost. At less than $2 per unit, it turns an ordinary smartphone into an immersive learning tool, making interactive education accessible to all. Local production creates jobs and reduces the carbon footprint. 
2.	A powerful and intuitive educational software: Our application allows students to see, interact with, and engage in their learning: Ultra-realistic 3D models, derived from real medical imaging Interactive scenarios, placing students in real-world situations Step-by-step guided training, teaching essential skills hands-on Personalized learning, adapting content to each student’s needs 
3.	100% offline access: No internet needed. Once downloaded, the application works without connectivity and can be updated through simple peer-to-peer sharing. Education becomes possible anywhere, even in the most remote areas

Title: REVA : AI-Powered Financial Platform for Informal & Gig Workers
Subtitle: Helping Africa’s gig and informal workers track income, manage taxes, and access financial services with AI-powered tools.
Problem Statement: In Tunisia, over 400,000 informal and gig workers struggle with irregular income, complex tax rules, and unaffordable accounting services. Most still rely on paper or Excel for bookkeeping, leading to frequent errors, missed deadlines, and costly penalties. Without proper financial records, they remain excluded from credit, insurance, and social protections. These challenges are not unique to Tunisia—across Africa, millions of informal workers face the same barriers of financial exclusion, weak digital tools, and heavy bureaucracy, which lock them out of formal economic participation
Solution Overview:
Reva is an AI-powered financial platform built to solve Tunisia’s informal and gig workers’ challenges, with a model that can scale across Africa where the same barriers exist.
* How it works: Reva automates income tracking through AI-powered receipt scanning and direct API integration with gig platforms like Glovo. A Tunisia-specific tax engine pre-calculates VAT, CNSS contributions, and deductions, enabling near-error-free one-click tax filing. The app also offers “domiciliation lite” to simplify business registration.
* Technologies: AI + OCR for real-time expense categorization, mobile-first design optimized for offline use, Arabic/French interface, and gig platform API integrations.
* Methodology: A subscription at 21 TND/month =7$(80% cheaper than traditional accountants) makes compliance affordable for low-income workers. The pilot will measure adoption, error reduction, and user satisfaction to validate the business model.
* Partnerships & Collaboration: Reva partners with gig platforms to integrate earnings data, accounting firms to validate compliance, and microfinance institutions to provide access to loans, savings, and social protection. At scale, Reva empowers millions of African informal workers to formalize, reduce penalties, and access financial services.
Solution Provider(s): (Reva Project Team) – Tunisian fintech startup led by entrepreneurs with experience in FMCG, digital platforms, and accounting innovation. The team is building REVA, an AI-powered financial platform to serve informal and gig workers.  Future Collaboration Partners (under discussion): local accounting firms (for tax compliance validation), gig platforms such as Glovo and Poslik (for earnings integration), and microfinance institutions (to expand access to credit and savings).
Duration to pilot in a new geography: Estimated Duration: We estimate 6–9 months to pilot REVA in a new geography. This includes 1–2 months for market research and regulatory adaptation, 2–3 months for app localization and testing, and 3–4 months for pilot rollout with 100–200 workers to validate adoption, retention, and compliance outcomes
SDGs addressed: SDG 8 (Decent Work and Economic Growth);SDG 9 (Industry, Innovation, and Infrastructure);SDG 10 (Reduced Inequalities);
Desired impact:
* Solution Objectives:
Automate income tracking and bookkeeping for informal and gig workers.
Simplify tax compliance through Tunisia-specific pre-loaded VAT/CNSS rules and one-click e-filing.
Enable access to financial services such as loans, savings, insurance, and retirement plans.
Reduce time and costs associated with manual bookkeeping and traditional accounting.
Support formalization of Tunisia’s informal economy and promote financial inclusion.
* Key Achievements / Impacts (Quantifiable):
Time savings: Users save 7–8+ hours per month compared to manual bookkeeping.
Cost reduction: Subscription at 21 TND/month, 80% cheaper than traditional accounting.
Financial compliance: Reduce tax penalties by over 90% through AI-driven filing.
Access to financial services: Enables informal workers to access loans, savings, and insurance, unlocking economic opportunities.
Economic impact: Targets the $2.3B informal economy in Tunisia, helping formalize previously untapped transactions.
Scalability: Potential to reach hundreds of thousands of informal workers across Tunisia and North Africa, increasing household income, financial stability, and economic mobility.
Key technologies:
Artificial Intelligence (AI): Powers receipt scanning, auto-categorization of expenses, and the Arabic/French chatbot for user guidance.
Optical Character Recognition (OCR): Converts paper receipts and invoices into digital data for automated bookkeeping.
API Integrations: Connects with gig platforms like Glovo and YASSIR to automatically track earnings in real-time.
Mobile-First Offline Design: Ensures usability in low-connectivity areas, enabling continuous access for informal workers.
Localized Tax Engine: Pre-loaded with Tunisia-specific VAT, CNSS, and deduction rules for automated, compliant e-filing.
Cloud Backend: Securely stores financial records and supports scalable deployment for large user ba
Unique Characteristics:
Unique / Differentiated Characteristics:
First AI-powered financial platform for Tunisia’s gig economy: Tailored specifically for 400,000+ informal workers, unlike generic accounting software.
Zero-effort bookkeeping: Automated receipt scanning, expense categorization, and real-time income tracking via gig platform APIs.
Localized compliance: Pre-configured Tunisia-specific VAT/CNSS rules with one-click e-filing, reducing errors and penalties.
Affordable subscription model: 21 TND/month—80% cheaper than traditional accounting services, making financial management accessible.

Integrated financial ecosystem: Future partnerships with microcredit banks and insurers provide loans, savings, and insurance for informal workers.
Time and cost efficiency: Saves users 7–8+ hours/month and dramatically lowers compliance costs.

By automating bookkeeping, tax compliance, and income tracking, workers gain visibility and legitimacy, enabling access to loans, savings, insurance, and retirement plans. This reduces errors, penalties, and time spent on manual bookkeeping, while improving household financial stability. Over time, REVA fosters greater participation in the formal economy, boosts tax compliance, reduces systemic inequalities, and can be scaled to replicate a digitally empowered financial ecosystem for millions of informal workers.
