Title: BloomFem
Subtitle: BloomFem is a nursing management system designed to streamline health records for vulnerable pregnant women at clinics across Kampala, ensuring better care and follow-up.
Problem Statement:
BloomFem addresses key challenges in maternal and child healthcare in Kampala, including:

Poor record management: Replaces paper-based systems with digital records for accuracy and easy access.

Fragmented care: Ensures continuity of care through centralized data tracking.

Delays in treatment: Reduces time lost searching for or recreating patient histories.

Limited follow-up: Supports alerts and reminders for immunizations, antenatal visits, and check-ups.

Data loss & security: Minimizes risks of lost or damaged files with secure cloud storage.

Understaffed clinics: Eases workload for nurses by automating routine data tasks.
Solution Overview: BloomFem is a digital nursing management system designed to improve healthcare delivery for vulnerable women and children at clinics in Kampala. It digitizes patient records, streamlines clinical workflows, and supports timely follow-ups through appointment scheduling and automated SMS reminders. Built using human-centered design and agile development methodologies, BloomFem features a secure, cloud-based platform with offline capabilities and multilingual support, making it accessible and reliable for low-resource settings. The system is interoperable with national health information systems like DHIS2 and OpenMRS. BloomFem is developed in collaboration with local clinics, nursing associations, and district health offices, ensuring contextual relevance and sustainability. Partnerships with technology providers, NGOs, and the Ministry of Health enable training, deployment, and scaling efforts, with a shared goal of strengthening maternal and child health systems across Uganda.
Solution Provider(s): The implementation of the BloomFem Nursing Management System is driven by a strong partnership between organizations with expertise in healthcare, digital technology, and community-centered innovation.  Lead Partner: Martian Ventures – An innovation and venture studio focused on building inclusive, tech-enabled solutions for underserved communities. Wyke Bazirake, Director of Martian Ventures, leads strategic oversight and stakeholder coordination, engaging with health facilities, community health workers, and nursing associations to promote adoption and long-term scalability of BloomFem.  Ms. Mariah Miranda, Software Developer, leads frontend development, crafting user-friendly and multilingual interfaces optimized for clinic staff.  Ms. Vanessa Shumbusho, Backend Developer, is responsible for maintaining a secure and efficient server-side infrastructure to support sensitive health data.  Mr. David Egessa, Senior Developer, oversees software architecture, integration with national health systems, and ensures the platform follows best practices for performance, scalability, and reliability.  Mr. Emmanuel Samanya, Website Developer, ensures smooth platform functionality, responsive UI design, and continuous technical support for diverse user environments.  Secondary Partner: Cyber Tap Africa – A digital solutions firm with a focus on scalable innovations in health and environmental systems. Francis Kamau, Director of Cyber Tap Africa, brings deep expertise in digital health innovation and oversees strategic integration of cutting-edge tools within BloomFem. His team supports backend technology development, security architecture, and real-time data processing to ensure the system remains robust, scalable, and aligned with Uganda’s digital health priorities.  Additional Partner: Mara Scientific – A research-driven health tech organization that contributes clinical data management expertise. Mara Scientific plays a key role in ensuring that the BloomFem system adheres to maternal and child health care protocols and national health reporting standards.  Together, these partners enable BloomFem to transform how vulnerable women and children receive care in Kampala’s clinics—through improved record-keeping, timely follow-up, and enhanced decision-making by healthcare providers.
Implementation timeline(s): The BloomFem Nursing Management System is scheduled to launch in May 2025, followed by a phased rollout over 1 year and 2 months, concluding in July 2026. This staged deployment allows for pilot testing, feedback integration, staff training, and gradual scaling across targeted clinics in Kampala to ensure system effectiveness, sustainability, and user adoption.
Duration to pilot in a new geography: 1 year roll out
SDGs addressed: SDG 3 (Good Health and Well-being);SDG 5 (Gender Equality);SDG 9 (Industry, Innovation, and Infrastructure);
Desired impact: The BloomFem Nursing Management System aims to enhance maternal and child healthcare by improving clinic efficiency, ensuring continuity of care, and strengthening data accuracy through digital health record management. Over a 14-month rollout beginning in May 2025, BloomFem is expected to reduce patient record retrieval time by 75%, increase on-time maternal checkups and child immunizations by 40%, and improve data accuracy to 95%, compared to traditional paper-based systems. By training over 150 nurses and health workers, the solution also supports workforce digital empowerment. Environmentally, BloomFem contributes to sustainability by significantly reducing paper use and medical form waste across participating clinics, helping to lower the sector’s carbon footprint and promote greener healthcare practices. The system is projected to support care for over 50,000 women and children annually by 2027, with measurable improvements in health outcomes and service delivery.
Key technologies:
BloomFem leverages a combination of modern digital technologies to deliver an efficient, secure, and user-friendly nursing management system. The core platform is built on a cloud-based infrastructure, ensuring scalable and reliable data storage with strong encryption to protect patient confidentiality. The system is developed as a Progressive Web App (PWA), enabling easy access across devices such as tablets, smartphones, and computers, with offline functionality to support low-connectivity clinic environments.

To enhance clinical decision-making, BloomFem integrates basic AI-powered alerts and reminders that notify healthcare workers of upcoming appointments, immunizations, and potential health risks based on entered patient data. Additionally, the platform supports API integrations with national health information systems like DHIS2 and OpenMRS, ensuring seamless data exchange and compliance with Uganda’s health data standards.

While BloomFem does not currently use IoT or blockchain, its modular design allows for future integration of these technologies—for example, IoT devices for remote patient monitoring or blockchain for enhanced data integrity and traceability as the system scales.
Unique Characteristics:
BloomFem stands out through its holistic approach combining technology, partnerships, and community engagement to address maternal and child health challenges in low-resource settings. Unlike traditional paper-based or fragmented digital systems, BloomFem offers a user-friendly, offline-capable Progressive Web App tailored specifically for nursing workflows in Kampala’s clinics. Its integration with national health systems ensures data consistency and supports government health initiatives.

The solution’s innovative partnership model—led by Martian Ventures with Cyber Tap Africa as technical lead—blends local tech expertise with deep community and clinical involvement, ensuring the platform is both contextually relevant and scalable. Financing is structured around phased rollout and capacity-building, enabling cost-effective scaling without heavy upfront investment.

Additionally, BloomFem incorporates AI-driven clinical decision support and automated patient follow-up reminders, which improve care outcomes while reducing staff workload. Its focus on reducing paper waste also introduces an environmentally sustainable element rarely prioritized in similar health solutions. This combination of tailored technology, collaborative partnerships, and sustainable design makes BloomFem a uniquely impactful innovation in the FemTech and digital health space.
Sustainable Change:
BloomFem contributes to sustainable, systemic change by digitizing and streamlining maternal and child health record management within clinics, improving data accuracy, care continuity, and clinical decision-making. By empowering healthcare workers through user-friendly technology and training, it strengthens the health system’s capacity to deliver timely, quality care. The increased efficiency reduces missed appointments and health risks, fostering better health outcomes for vulnerable women and children.

Theory of Change:
If clinics adopt BloomFem’s digital system, then nurses and health workers can manage patient information more accurately and efficiently. This leads to improved monitoring of maternal and child health indicators, enabling timely interventions such as immunizations and antenatal care. Better data drives stronger health system planning and resource allocation at district and national levels. Over time, this results in reduced maternal and child morbidity and mortality, enhanced workforce capacity, and a culture of data-driven healthcare. The environmental benefit of reduced paper waste further supports sustainable healthcare practices. Collectively, these changes build resilient, scalable health systems that can sustainably improve population health outcomes beyond the initial rollout.

Title: Responsible Digital Inclusion: The Palau Model
Subtitle: Palau's pioneering framework for safe, ethical, and empowering digital engagement, fostering an inclusive economy through responsible online behavior.
Problem Statement:
This solution that has been refined and tested out to thousands of Palauans over 8 years addresses the following challenges/issues:

- With the infrastructure investment by international partners in a fiber optic cable in 2017, Palauans suddenly became chronically online on social media, acting outside of culturally appropriate norms leading to a rise of image-based abuse, scams, and cyber bullying.

- Those who take advantage of online shopping and other fintech-related services, naively provide their data and have been scammed.

- Young entrepreneurs interested in selling their products online often get overwhelmed and give up during the set-up phase of their endeavors due to barriers in fintech infrastructures that leave out some global south countries like Palau. 

- Professionals like police, lawyers and judges, and educators often lack the capacity to monitor or solve crises that are digital in nature.
Solution Overview:
The Palau Digital Citizenship Initiative, founded on a unique Responsibility-based Approach, directly addresses the multifaceted challenges arising from Palau's rapid digital transformation following the 2017 fiber optic cable infrastructure investment. This solution, refined and tested over eight years with thousands of Palauans, tackles issues ranging from unchecked online behavior and financial scams to entrepreneurial roadblocks and institutional capacity gaps.

At its core, the Initiative empowers individuals and institutions through a comprehensive and culturally sensitive framework.
Recognizing that simply prohibiting certain online behaviors is insufficient, the Responsibility-based Approach fosters critical thinking and encourages individuals to understand the impact of their digital actions on themselves, their communities, and Palau’s culture. This methodology is particularly effective in addressing sensitive "taboo" subjects prevalent in Pacific contexts, such as image-based abuse and revenge porn, by reframing them within a broader discussion of digital ethics, respect, and personal accountability, rather than solely focusing on punitive measures and “freedom of speech.”
The Initiative's practical implementation involves the development and delivery of tailored educational classes, papers, and networking. These are designed to be relevant and accessible to diverse audiences, including:
• Senators: Advocating with policymakers and testifying against rushed and harmful bills that don’t take into account gendered nuances in the image-based abuse space.
• Students: Equipping the younger generation with foundational digital literacy, critical thinking skills, and an understanding of responsible online conduct from an early age.
• Parents: Providing tools and knowledge to guide their children's online experiences, recognize digital risks, and foster open communication about online safety.
• Educators: Building the capacity of teachers to integrate digital citizenship into their curricula and serve as frontline mentors for
students.
• Police Academy, Lawyers, and Judges:
Enhancing the capacity of law enforcement and legal professionals to understand, monitor, and effectively address digitally-rooted crises, including cybercrime, image-based abuse, and online fraud.
• Entrepreneurs: Offering guidance and resources to navigate fintech infrastructures,
overcome setup barriers, and safely leverage online platforms for business endeavors.

This multi-pronged strategy is reinforced by continuous desk research and policy advocacy. The Initiative actively monitors emerging digital trends, identifies new risks, and contributes to the development of national policies that  support a safer and more inclusive digital environment that considers Palau and the Pacific context.

Methodologies and technologies used:

The solution employs a mixed-methods approach research, curriculum development, advocacy, and program delivery:

• Mixed-Methods Research: This involves combining qualitative research (e.g., focus groups, interviews with community members, victims, and professionals to understand lived experiences and cultural nuances) with quantitative data (e.g., surveys on online behavior, scam prevalence, and digital literacy levels of entrepreneurs and small business owners). This comprehensive research informs the design of interventions and ensures their cultural appropriateness and effectiveness.

• Responsibility-based Approach: This unique pedagogical methodology moves beyond rules-based and the dominant rights-based approach to digital literacy to emphasize personal accountability, ethical decision-making, and understanding the consequences of online actions within a cultural context. It facilitates open discussions on sensitive topics by framing them within a framework of respect and
“the village” well-being.
• Curriculum Design and Authoring: As the founder, I meticulously design and author bespoke materials and recommendations.
Solution Provider(s): Palau Bureau of Communications, Ministry of Education, Ministry of Justice, Senate, Civil Society, traditional women groups, schools and youth, ITU, FAO, and UNOPS.
Duration to pilot in a new geography: 6 months in other Pacific Islands
SDGs addressed: SDG 5 (Gender Equality);SDG 9 (Industry, Innovation, and Infrastructure);SDG 4 (Quality Education);
Desired impact:
The desired impact of the Palau Digital Citizenship Initiative that I want to introduce as a model to similar Pacific Island states, is to cultivate a responsible, safe, and inclusive digital economy in the Pacific, empowering individuals and institutions to thrive in the digital age while preserving their unique cultural values and mitigating online risks.

Solution Objectives:
1. To foster critical thinking and responsible digital behavior among Pacific islanders of all ages and professions.
 2. To enhance the capacity of institutions (government, law enforcement, education, legal) to understand, monitor, and address digital challenges effectively.
 3. To promote a culturally sensitive approach to digital literacy that addresses "taboo" subjects like image-based abuse within a framework of ethics and community well-being.
 4. To equip entrepreneurs with the knowledge and resources to safely and effectively leverage digital platforms for economic growth.
 5. To inform and influence national digital policies that support a safer and more inclusive online environment tailored to the Pacific context.

Key Achievements or Impacts of the Solution (Quantifiable):
 - Behavioral Change: Increased understanding and adoption of responsible online conduct among thousands of Palauans and other Pacific Islanders. While specific quantifiable data on reduced instances of unchecked online behavior or scams is not provided, the eight years of refinement and testing with thousands of Palauans suggest a significant reach and presumed positive impact on digital literacy and behavior that’s ready to be scaled and adopted to other Pacific island contexts.
 - Policy Influence: Successful advocacy with policymakers, leading to more nuanced and culturally sensitive legislation (e.g., preventing harmful bills related to gendered nuances in image-based abuse). Quantifiable impact could include the number of bills successfully opposed or amended due to the Initiative's advocacy and the number of consultation with policymakers. 
- Institutional Capacity Building: Enhanced capacity of law enforcement, legal professionals, and educators to address digitally-rooted challenges and crises. Quantifiable impact could include the number of professionals trained.
 - Entrepreneurial Empowerment: Improved ability of Palauan entrepreneurs and small businesses to navigate fintech and leverage online platforms safely, potentially leading to increased digital business creation and reduced instances of online fraud impacting businesses. Quantifiable impact could be the number of entrepreneurs trained and results of online polls and surveys. 
 - Cultural Preservation: Integration of culturally sensitive frameworks into digital literacy and economic inclusion, fostering discussions on sensitive topics within a framework of respect and "the village" well-being. This is a qualitative impact that is fundamental to the solution's approach.
Key technologies: I use low tech such as power points, traditional literature reviews, etc. Lately, I’ve been using AI research assistants such as Perplexity and Claude to help streamline my research. I am testing out AI content creation tools to help transform my lectures into more engaging content.
Unique Characteristics: I believe the core of my solution is the most unique part because it works for Palau and answers clarion calls from other Pacific Islanders in this space: The Responsibility-based Approach to Digital Literacy and Inclusion. This approach allows my project to address often taboo subjects in the Pacific such as sex, revenge porn, LGBTQ, gender and sexuality, as well as navigating other nuances like religious expectations vs real life dilemmas.
Sustainable Change:
The Palau Digital Citizenship Initiative contributes to creating sustainable, systemic change by embedding a responsibility-based approach to digital literacy and economic inclusion, fostering a self-reinforcing cycle of informed digital citizenship. The desired follow-on effects, outlined below as a Theory of Change, demonstrate how the solution aims to create lasting positive transformation rather than out-of-touch  interventions. TOC:

- Culturally-Grounded Behavioral Norms: By moving beyond a punitive or purely rights-based approach, the "Responsibility-based Approach" cultivates an intrinsic understanding of digital ethics rooted in Palauan and Pacific cultural values like "the village" well-being and respect. This shift from external rules and individual rights to internal ethical frameworks makes responsible online behavior more sustainable and self-perpetuating. When individuals internalize these values, their actions are guided by a deeper understanding of collective impact, leading to more resilient behavioral change.
 - Institutional Capacity Building & Integration: The initiative targets a diverse range of institutions (senators, police, lawyers, judges, educators, parents). By building their capacity and providing tailored knowledge, the solution ensures that digital citizenship principles are integrated into legal frameworks, educational curricula, law enforcement protocols, and parental guidance. This institutionalization means that the knowledge and practices are not dependent on a single program or individual, but become embedded within the fabric of society.
 - Proactive Policy Advocacy: Continuous desk research and policy advocacy enable the initiative to anticipate emerging digital trends and risks. By actively contributing to national policy development, the solution ensures that the regulatory environment evolves in tandem with technological advancements, preventing future harms and fostering an inclusive digital space. This proactive stance hopes to ensure  that the system is continually adapting and improving, rather than reacting to crises.
 - Empowered Digital Citizens & Leaders: Equipping students from an early age with foundational digital literacy and critical thinking skills creates a generation of digital citizens who are inherently responsible and capable of navigating and adapting to complex online environments. Simultaneously, educating policymakers and legal professionals ensures that leaders are informed and equipped to make sound decisions regarding digital governance. This creates a pipeline of informed citizens and leaders who can sustain the desired digital ecosystem.
 - Economic Resilience & Inclusivity: By addressing entrepreneurial roadblocks and providing guidance on fintech infrastructures, the solution directly contributes to a more resilient and inclusive digital economy. When entrepreneurs can safely and effectively leverage online platforms, it fosters innovation and economic growth, which in turn reinforces the need for a safe and ethical digital environment.

Desired Follow-on Effects:
IF: 
the Palau Digital Citizenship Initiative delivers comprehensive, culturally-sensitive education and advocacy across diverse stakeholders (students, parents, educators, law enforcement, legal professionals, policymakers, entrepreneurs) based on a Responsibility-based Approach,
THEN: 
we expect the following immediate outcomes:
 - Increased digital literacy and critical thinking skills among Palauans and other Pacific island communities.
 - Enhanced understanding of online risks and responsible online conduct.
 - Improved capacity of institutions to address digital challenges and implement relevant policies.
 - Greater engagement of policymakers in developing informed and culturally appropriate digital legislation.
 - Increased confidence and safety for entrepreneurs utilizing digital platforms.
LEADING TO: 
An inclusive digital economy and ecosystem in Pacific Islands.

Summary: The Palau Digital Citizenship Initiative is an eight-year, nationally embedded program that addresses the risks of rapid digital adoption in Palau by fostering a responsibility-based approach to online behavior. Strengths: proven long-term implementation, deep cultural contextualization, institutional partnerships, and systemic impact. Weaknesses: limited quantitative evidence of behavior change, modest use of advanced technologies, and reliance on project-based funding.

Title: AQUALOOP: The AGRITEKTURA Circular System for Inclusive Agri-Aqua Innovation
Subtitle: A digital circular system integrating smart farming, design, and innovation to empower inclusive, tech-driven agri-aqua communities through AGRITEKTURA System
Problem Statement: AGRITEKTURA's AQUALOOP Circular System addresses key challenges in food security, low local agri-aqua production, lack of access to smart technology, fragmented supply chains, limited training, and rural economic exclusion. It provides an integrated, tech-enabled circular system that empowers communities through smart farming, modular infrastructure, and inclusive capacity-building.
Solution Overview:
1. How the Solution Works

AGRITEKTURA thru its AQUALOOP is a digital circular system that integrates architecture, smart aquaculture, and agri-based innovations to address local food insecurity and rural livelihood gaps. The core of the system is the portaSHIP, a modular, prefabricated smart aquafarm unit designed for hatchery and grow-out operations. These units are deployed in target communities and can be scaled based on local demand and terrain.

AQUALOOP ensures the sustainability of each project by offering a complete ecosystem: from training and design development to installation, monitoring, and market linkage. Beneficiaries (e.g., youth, farmers, fisherfolk, agri-preneurs) are onboarded into a closed-loop system where they receive technical assistance, tools, and shared infrastructure to sustainably produce, process, and profit from their agri-aqua ventures.

The solution operates under a hub-and-spoke model, where regional hubs serve as command centers for training, fabrication, and data consolidation, while satellite farms replicate the model using locally available materials and workforce.

2. Methodologies and Technologies Used

- Design Thinking & Systems Innovation: Applied in the planning, customization, and prototyping of each solution to adapt to different site conditions and community needs.
- Internet of Things (IoT): Sensors monitor water quality, temperature, fish growth, and energy usage, allowing real-time decision-making and predictive maintenance.
- AI and Data Analytics: Supports smart forecasting, inventory tracking, and performance analysis to improve production yield and efficiency.
- Prefabrication & Modular Construction: Used in portaSHIP units for fast deployment, scalability, and cost efficiency.
- Circular Economy Principles: Waste is minimized and outputs (e.g., water, organic materials) are reused or recycled within the system.
- Digital Literacy & Training Programs: Empower local users to manage and scale the system using practical digital tools and micro-credentials.

3. Partnerships and Collaboration Models

AGRITEKTURA + AQUALOOP thrives through multi-stakeholder collaboration, with partners across government, academia, and the private sector:

Government Partners:

- TESDA: Technical training, curriculum development, and certification for operators.
- DOST & DTI: R&D support, equipment grants (e.g., Shared Service Facilities), and innovation funding.
- DA-BFAR: Aquaculture support services and linkage to fisheries programs.

Academia & Innovation Hubs:

- Collaborates with state universities and colleges (SUCs) to pilot portaSHIP units as learning labs and R&D incubators.
- Joint development of training modules and co-managed innovation hubs (e.g., HIVE Creative Hub at John Paul College).

Private Sector & Community-Based Enterprises:

- Partners with local fabricators, suppliers, and tech providers (e.g., IoT system developers like Anihan Tech) for localized production.

Establishes coop-led or LGU-led implementation models with revenue-sharing and reinvestment schemes.
This collaborative model ensures inclusive participation, shared ownership, and long-term sustainability, positioning AGRITEKTURA as a scalable, community-anchored innovation for the inclusive digital economy.
Solution Provider(s): AGRITEKTURA ENTERPRISES – A multi-sectoral social innovation enterprise specializing in sustainable agritecture, smart aquafarming, and circular systems for food security, operating in the Agriculture, Architecture, and Innovationsectors.  AQUALOOP Circular Systems Department – The business development and ecosystem management arm of AGRITEKTURA, focused on implementing digital, inclusive, and scalable agri-aqua circular systems across regions, under the Agritech and Sustainability sectors.  TESDA (Technical Education and Skills Development Authority) – A national government agency that provides technical-vocational education, certification, and workforce development programs. Sector: Education and Skills Training.  DOST (Department of Science and Technology) – Government agency supporting research, technology development, and innovation funding. Sector: Science, Technology, and Innovation.  DTI (Department of Trade and Industry) – Through the Shared Service Facilities (SSF) Program, DTI supports MSMEs and innovation initiatives. Sector: Trade, Industry Development, and MSME Support.  DA-BFAR (Department of Agriculture – Bureau of Fisheries and Aquatic Resources) – Provides technical support and regulatory guidance for aquaculture-based projects. Sector: Agriculture and Fisheries.  John Paul College (JPC) and Mindoro State University (MinSU) – An academic institution in Oriental Mindoro and home of the HIVE Creative Hub, where AGRITEKTURA incubates student-led innovation projects. Sector: Education and Creative Industry.  Local Fabricators and Co-Farming Partners – MSMEs and community-based enterprises engaged in the localized production of portaSHIP systems and implementation of AQUALOOP farms. Sector: Manufacturing, Construction, and Community Development.
Implementation location(s): The CRIB (AGRITEKTURA HUB) @ Roxas, Oriental Mindoro
Duration to pilot in a new geography: 6 Months - 1 year
SDGs addressed: SDG 11 (Sustainable Cities and Communities);SDG 2 (Zero Hunger);SDG 9 (Industry, Innovation, and Infrastructure);
Desired impact:
Solution Objectives

- Empower underserved communities through inclusive access to smart agri-aqua systems and digital technologies.
- Enhance local food security by boosting sustainable aquaculture production using IoT-integrated systems.
- Generate green jobs in agriculture, design, fabrication, and training through circular enterprise models.
- Promote digital transformation in rural areas by training beneficiaries in data-driven aquaculture and agritecture.
- Reduce environmental impact through circular systems that minimize waste, optimize resource use, and promote sustainability.
- Create scalable innovation hubs that serve as incubation centers for student-preneurs, farmers, and tech developers.

Key Achievements / Impacts (Current & Projected)

1. Employment Generation
- Over 150+ indirect jobs created (fabricators, local contractors, trainers, operators).
- Projected 50+ direct jobs per hub in roles such as aquatech operators, trainers, data monitors, and farm technicians.

2. Food Security & Local Production
- Each portaSHIP system produces up to 1,500–2,000 kg of fish per cycle, meeting community-level demand.
- Integrated hatchery reduces dependency on external fingerling suppliers.

3. Training & Digital Inclusion
- Trained 120+ students and youth on IoT in aquaculture, smart farming, and design-based problem-solving.
- Projected 300+ community trainees annually through expansion of training hubs.

4. Environmental Impact (Circular System Benefits)
- Designed for low-energy consumption via solar power integration (20–30% energy savings).
- Minimizes water waste through recirculating aquaculture systems (RAS) and closed-loop reuse of water.
- Future modules include integration of organic waste-to-energy systems.

5. Scalability & Replication
- One operational prototype hub in MIMAROPA, with ongoing expansion efforts in CALABARZON.
- Targeting 5 regional hubs by 2026, each serving as a node in a digitally connected agri-aqua ecosystem.
Key technologies:
Key Technologies Utilized

1. Internet of Things (IoT)
- Real-time monitoring of water quality parameters (e.g., temperature, pH, dissolved oxygen) through connected sensors.
- Enables predictive maintenance, feeding optimization, and early warning systems to reduce fish mortality and increase yield.

2. Data Analytics & Cloud-Based Dashboards
- Aggregates sensor data into a centralized system for performance tracking and decision-making.
- Visual dashboards help farmers, students, and operators analyze trends and take action in real time.

3. Artificial Intelligence (AI) – Experimental Integration
- Used for pilot applications in predictive analytics (e.g., fish weight estimation, feed conversion ratios, growth cycles).
- Future AI modules aim to automate climate adaptation, harvest timing, and resource management.

4. Modular & Prefabricated Construction
- portaSHIP Aquatecture System (Portable Smart Aquafarm Facility) units are designed using CAD/BIM for precision, speed, and scalability.
- Prefabrication reduces costs, construction time, and environmental disruption.

5. Renewable Energy Systems (Solar-Powered Setup)
- Integrates off-grid solar solutions for pumps, sensors, and aeration, lowering carbon footprint and ensuring resilience in remote areas.

6. Digital Learning Platforms & Micro-Credentials
- Training modules delivered through blended platforms with digital badges and TESDA-aligned certifications.
- Expands access to technical education in agri-aqua innovation.
Unique Characteristics:
Unique & Differentiated Characteristics

1. Integrated Circular System for Agri-Aqua Innovation - AGRITEKTURA's portaSHIP is not just a smart farming solution — Integrated with the AQUALOOP digital circular system that integrates design, technology, sustainability, and entrepreneurship. It closes the loop from production to training, to community enterprise, making it a holistic model for inclusive rural development.

2. Modular Innovation through portaSHIP Systems - The portaSHIP is a patented-ready, modular smart aquafarm designed for rapid deployment, low-footprint construction, and adaptability to diverse geographies. It combines hatchery and grow-out functions in one prefabricated, IoT-integrated unit, making it suitable for both rural and peri-urban settings.

3. Human-Centered Design Meets Tech-Enabled Impact - The solution is co-designed with communities using design thinking methodologies, ensuring local relevance while layering in high-impact technologies like IoT, AI, and solar power. This hybrid of traditional wisdom and modern systems design creates contextual yet scalable solutions.

4. Inclusive Enterprise & Capacity-Building Approach - AGRITEKTURA trains local youth, fisherfolk, and agri-preneurs through micro-credential programs co-developed with TESDA, SUCs, and industry experts. This builds a grassroots innovation workforce capable of managing and replicating the model.

5. Scalable Hub-and-Spoke Replication Model - The system uses a regional hub for fabrication, training, and data management, with satellite farms or "spokes" deployed in target communities. This ensures efficiency, scalability, and localized implementation without high capital overheads.

6. Multi-Stakeholder Ecosystem Partnerships - The project thrives on a dynamic collaboration among government agencies (TESDA, DTI, DOST, DA-BFAR), academic institutions, private tech startups, and community cooperatives—creating a shared-ownership model where every stakeholder has skin in the game.

7. Accessible Financing and Hybrid Ownership Models - The solution offers flexible financing schemes such as co-investment, shared service facilities (SSF), and cooperative-owned hubs, allowing inclusive entry for micro-entrepreneurs and local governments without heavy upfront costs.

8. Designed for ESG, SDG, and Resilience Alignment - AGRITEKTURA is purpose-built to advance SDGs 1, 2, 8, 9, 11, 12, and 13, while enabling local implementation of ESG principles in agriculture, education, and infrastructure development.
Sustainable Change:
How the Solution Creates Sustainable, Systemic Change

AGRITEKTURA + AQUALOOP fosters long-term, systems-level transformation by addressing the root challenges in food production, livelihood access, and digital exclusion—especially in rural and underserved areas. It does this by integrating technology, training, design, and inclusive enterprise models into one scalable circular solution.

Theory of Change

If we provide modular, tech-enabled agri-aqua systems (portaSHIPs), and equip communities with the skills, infrastructure, and digital tools to operate them then we empower local farmers, fisherfolk, and youth to sustainably produce food, generate income, and participate in the digital economy.

Resulting in improved food security, employment, environmental resilience, and inclusive local innovation ecosystems.

Desired Follow-On Effects

1. Empowered Local Economies - Communities evolve from passive recipients to active producers, generating income through localized, tech-enabled food systems.

2. Decentralized Innovation Ecosystems - Regional hubs become centers of learning, fabrication, and innovation, seeding further entrepreneurship and local IP development.

3. Increased Digital Inclusion & Literacy - With IoT, data dashboards, and training, communities gain digital skills and begin to interact with markets, supply chains, and services online.

4. Sustainable Production Systems - Through circular approaches and climate-smart technologies, communities transition to low-waste, regenerative farming systems.

5. Scalable Replication and Franchising - The model is designed to be replicated across provinces using co-ownership or micro-franchise models, multiplying its impact without centralized control.

6. Policy Alignment and Public-Private Engagement - By working with government, SUCs, and private partners, the system helps inform better agritech policies, investment flows, and training standards.

Title: EcoFert : Des déchets à l’or liquide pour une agriculture durable
Subtitle: EcoFert valorise déchets et urine en engrais bio, via une appli mobile, pour fertiliser les sols, réduire la pollution et renforcer la sécurité alimentaire en Guinée.
Problem Statement: En Guinée, la gestion des déchets constitue un défi environnemental majeur, en raison de la qualité produite et la capacité limitée de collecte, de transport et de traitement. les déchets  s'accumulent dans les quartiers sans être valorisés, contribuant à l'insalubrité urbaine et à la pollution. Parallèlement, les agriculteurs manquent d'engrais accessibles et durables pour fertiliser leurs sols, ce qui compromet la productivité agricole et la sécurité alimentaire. L'utilisation d'engrais chimiques, lorsqu'elle est possible, appauvrit les sols et pollue les nappes phréatiques. Le lien entre ville et campagne reste faible, et l'économie circulaire quasi absente.
Solution Overview: EcoFert Guinée est une solution innovante qui valorise les déchets organiques et l'urine en les transformant en engrais liquides biologiques destinés à l'agriculture locale. Le processus commence par la collecte des déchets organiques (ménages, restaurants, marchés) et de l'urine, via un système d'abonnement géré par une application mobile. Ces matières sont ensuite acheminées vers des unités de traitement où elles subissent un processus de fermentation anaérobie combiné à des activateurs biologiques pour produire un engrais liquide riche en nutriments. La solution repose sur une double méthodologie :	 •	 Méthode biologique : compostage liquide contrôlé, sans additifs chimiques, respectueux des normes environnementales.	 •	 Méthode numérique : application mobile (en développement) permettant l'abonnement des ménages, la géolocalisation des points de collecte et le suivi des livraisons. EcoFert fonctionne selon un modèle d'économie circulaire, reliant :	 •	 Les ménages urbains (producteurs de déchets),	 •	 les agents de recouvrement (formés et équipés),	 •	 Les agriculteurs (bénéficiaires d'un engrais bio, moins coûteux et plus durable). Nous collaborons avec des acteurs communautaires (chefs de quartier, restaurateurs, agriculteurs), des structures locales, et nous bénéficions actuellement de l'appui du Programme de Développement de Prototype (PDP) du PNUD Guinée, avec le soutien du gouvernement japonais. Ce programme accompagne le projet en phase de prototypage technique et stratégique. Cette solution répond à la fois à des enjeux écologiques, agricoles, sociaux et numériques, tout en créant des opportunités économiques inclusives pour les jeunes et les femmes.
Solution Provider(s): Programme des Nations Unies pour le Développement (PNUD Guinée) – Agence onusienne de développement, partenaire stratégique à travers le Programme de Développement de Prototype (PDP), secteur : développement durable, innovation sociale. Saboutech Incubateur – Centre d’innovation et d’accompagnement pour entrepreneurs et porteurs de solutions technologiques, appui en incubation, renforcement des capacités et réseautage, secteur : entrepreneuriat, innovation numérique. Chefs de quartier et leaders communautaires – Facilitateurs d’accès aux ménages et relais pour la sensibilisation à la gestion des déchets, secteur : mobilisation communautaire, environnement urbain.
Duration to pilot in a new geography: La mise en œuvre pilote d’EcoFert Guinée dans une nouvelle zone géographique peut être réalisée en 3 à 4 mois, répartis comme suit : 	•	Mois 1 : Sensibilisation communautaire, identification des ménages, restaurants et agriculteurs, recrutement et formation des collecteurs. 	•	Mois 2 : Installation du dispositif de collecte, adaptation logistique, premiers tests techniques du traitement. 	•	Mois 3 : Lancement opérationnel, suivi des flux, ajustements techniques, premières livraisons d’engrais bio. 	•	Mois 4 : Évaluation de l’impact, collecte des données terrain, optimisation du modèle.  Ce calendrier peut être réduit à 2 mois dans une zone disposant déjà de relais communautaires actifs et d’un cadre logistique minimal.
SDGs addressed: SDG 2 (Zero Hunger);SDG 12 (Responsible Consumption and Production);SDG 13 (Climate Action);
Desired impact:
Objectifs de la solution	 
•	 Réduire la pollution urbaine liée aux déchets organiques et aux rejets d'urine non valorisés.	
 •	 Offrir aux agriculteurs un engrais bio, abordable et local, pour améliorer la fertilité des sols.	
 •	 Promouvoir une agriculture durable, sans engrais chimiques nocifs.	
 •	 Créer des opportunités d'emploi vert pour les jeunes et les femmes dans la collecte, la transformation et la distribution.	
•	 Renforcer l'économie circulaire locale en reliant les zones urbaines et rurales. 

Impacts attendus (quantifiables et concrets)	
•	 Réduction de 10 à 15 tonnes de déchets organiques par zone pilote, chaque trimestre.	 •	 Production mensuelle de 500 à 800 litres d'engrais bio liquide en phase initiale.
•	 Création de 10 à 20 emplois directs (collecteurs, transformateurs, agents logistiques).	
 •	 Réduction des émissions de GES : en limitant les décharges à ciel ouvert et les fermentations anarchiques (méthane), EcoFert contribue à une baisse mesurable des émissions locales.	 
•	 Amélioration de 20 à 30 % de la productivité agricole chez les premiers bénéficiaires utilisant l'engrais bio (selon les tests préliminaires).
Key technologies:
Notre solution repose sur l'intégration de technologies simples mais adaptées au contexte local, avec une vision d'évolution progressive vers des outils plus avancés : 

1. Application mobile (en développement) Permet aux ménages, restaurants et points de collecte de :	 
•	 s'abonner au service de collecte,	
 •	 géolocaliser les collectionneurs,	
 •	 suivre les livraisons d'engrais bio. Technologies impliquées : développement mobile, base de données en ligne, géolocalisation (GPS). 
2. Technologies de traitement biologique Le cœur de la transformation repose sur :	 
•	 La fermentation anaérobie,	
 •	 des activateurs microbiens naturels pour accélérer la décomposition,	
 •	 Des cuves de traitement artisanales optimisées. 
Ce processus respecte les normes environnementales sans recourir à des produits chimiques. 
3. Prévisions futures : intégration de capteurs (IoT) À moyen terme, EcoFert prévoit d'intégrer des capteurs intelligents pour :	 
•	 suivre la température et le pH des cuves de fermentation,	
 •	 automatiser certaines étapes du traitement. Cela reposera sur des solutions IoT adaptées aux environnements à faible connectivité
Unique Characteristics:
EcoFert Guinée se distingue par sa capacité à combiner innovation locale, impact environnemental et inclusion sociale dans une solution intégrée, évolutive et adaptée au contexte urbain africain. 
1. Modèle circulaire hybride (ville-campagne) EcoFert relie directement les producteurs de déchets urbains (ménages, restaurants) aux besoins des agriculteurs en zone périurbaine ou rurale, créant une boucle verte qui n'existait pas encore à ce niveau.
2. Valorisation de l'urine humaine Contrairement à la majorité des projets de compostage, EcoFert intègre la récupération et la transformation de l'urine en engrais bio liquide, une ressource peu exploitée en Afrique de l'Ouest mais riche en azote, phosphore et potassium. 
3. Numérisation du service via l'application mobile Le système d'abonnement, de collecte et de suivi est numérisé pour améliorer l'efficacité, renforcer la transparence et faciliter l'accès au service, même dans les quartiers défavorisés. 
4. Faible coût de déploiement et d'adaptation Le modèle est conçu pour être déployé rapidement dans différentes zones, avec des équipements locaux, une main-d'œuvre locale et une formation simplifiée, ce qui le rend accessible aux communes ou aux groupes de jeunes. 
5. Inclusion des jeunes et des femmes dans le modèle économique EcoFert crée une chaîne de valeur verte inclusive : collecte, transformation, logistique, distribution. Ces maillons offrent des emplois directs, valorisants et durables à des populations souvent marginalisées. 
6. Soutien institutionnel dès la phase de prototypage La solution bénéficie de l'accompagnement du PNUD Guinée à travers le Programme de Développement de Prototype (PDP), renforçant sa crédibilité, sa viabilité et ses perspectives de mise à l'échelle.
Sustainable Change:
EcoFert Guinée agit comme un levier de transformation systémique en instaurant une économie circulaire locale qui reconnecte les enjeux urbains (gestion des déchets) et ruraux (sécurité alimentaire), tout en générant de la valeur sociale, environnementale et économique. 
Théorie du changement : Si les déchets organiques et l'urine sont collectés, valorisés localement et distribués sous forme d'engrais bio abordable, alors les agriculteurs disposeront d'alternatives durables aux intrants chimiques, les sols seront enrichis naturellement, la pollution urbaine sera réduite, et des opportunités économiques seront créées, Ce qui contribuera à renforcer la sécurité alimentaire, à améliorer la santé publique, à professionnaliser la filière « déchets-agriculture » et à instaurer un modèle reproductible à grande échelle dans les zones urbaines africaines. 
Effets de suivi attendus :	 
•	 Changement de comportement des ménages et restaurateurs vis-à-vis des déchets organiques (de nuisance à ressource).	 •	 Adoption durable de pratiques agroécologiques par les petits agriculteurs grâce à un engrais local, bio et économique.
•	 Renforcement des politiques locales sur la gestion décentralisée des déchets et l'agriculture urbaine.	
 •	 Émergence de micro-entreprises vertes autour de la collecte, transformation et distribution, notamment pour les jeunes et les femmes.	 
•	 Modèle reproductible à l'échelle régionale pour d'autres villes confrontées aux mêmes défis

Le projet a été lancé grâce à l’engagement de l’équipe fondatrice qui mobilise ses ressources propres (contributions personnelles, moyens logistiques, compétences techniques) pour le prototypage, les premières expérimentations et les actions de sensibilisation.

Cette approche autofinancée démontre notre motivation, résilience et capacité à démarrer avec peu de moyens, en attendant de mobiliser des partenaires techniques et financiers pour l’extension. Title: Agrisense : Connecter les sols, protéger les récoltes, nourrir l’avenir
Subtitle: Agrisense est une solution intelligente qui connecte les sols agricoles via des capteurs pour améliorer les rendements, protéger les cultures et renforcer la résilience des zones rurales sensibles.
Problem Statement:
Agrisense répond à plusieurs défis majeurs :

Le manque d’accès aux données agricoles fiables en zones rurales.
Les pertes de rendement dues à un suivi inadéquat des sols et des cultures.
L’absence d’outils adaptés aux agriculteurs peu lettrés pour comprendre et agir.
La difficulté à détecter tôt les maladies ou stress des plantes.
Le besoin d’adapter l’agriculture aux effets du changement climatique
Solution Overview:
Fonctionnement de la solution :

Agrisense est une solution agro-technologique intégrée qui s'appuie sur des capteurs intelligents installés directement dans les champs pour surveiller en temps réel les paramètres critiques du sol (pH, humidité, température, nutriments). Ces capteurs collectent les données, qui sont transmises via un réseau IoT (LoRa ou GSM) à une plateforme centralisée.

L’application mobile associée (Android) permet aux agriculteurs de visualiser simplement ces données, recevoir des conseils personnalisés (fertilisation, irrigation, etc.) et être alertés en cas de maladie ou de déséquilibre du sol. Pour les zones à faible alphabétisation, l’application intègre une interface audio et visuelle multilingue (soussou, malinké, poular), facilitant la compréhension et l’action.

Méthodologies et technologies utilisées :

Capteurs sur mesure : capteurs 4-en-1 (température, humidité, pH, nutriments) adaptés aux réalités des sols guinéens.

IoT (Internet des Objets) : transmission des données via LoRa ou GSM pour couvrir les zones reculées.

Mobile et Web App : plateforme mobile pour les utilisateurs finaux, et back-office web pour les techniciens.

Intelligence artificielle (en développement) : détection précoce des maladies des plantes via reconnaissance d’images.

Pédagogie visuelle/audio : kit de sensibilisation simplifié (illustrations + audios en langues locales).

Tableaux de bord d’aide à la décision : pour les techniciens agricoles et partenaires (ONG, institutions).
Solution Provider(s): Partenaires principaux :  1. TRUSTEE – Think and Do Tank Organisation panafricaine spécialisée dans l’innovation sociale et l’inclusion numérique. TRUSTEE accompagne Agrisense à la fois en incubation et en phase d’accélération, en appui stratégique, prototypage et mise en réseau.  2. Orange Digital Center – Guinée Programme de soutien à l’innovation porté par Orange, offrant des formations, mentorats et ressources techniques. Agrisense est actuellement en incubation au sein de leur programme, bénéficiant d’un accompagnement technologique.  3. Toogueda – Programme CATALIST Incubateur guinéen axé sur l’entrepreneuriat à impact. Agrisense est incubé dans le cadre du programme CATALIST, un dispositif d’appui à la structuration et au financement des projets à fort potentiel.
Implementation location(s): Le projet à été mis en place en République de Guinée dans la région de BOKE et la sous préfecture de kamsar
Duration to pilot in a new geography: La durée nécessaire est de trois mois
SDGs addressed: SDG 2 (Zero Hunger);SDG 1 (No Poverty);SDG 9 (Industry, Innovation, and Infrastructure);
Desired impact:
Principaux impacts (réalisations ou attendus) :

Jusqu’à 30 % de réduction des pertes de rendement sur les cultures ciblées grâce à un meilleur suivi.

Économie de 25 à 40 % d’eau en optimisant l’irrigation selon l’humidité mesurée par les capteurs.

Réduction des émissions de GES : baisse de l’usage excessif d’engrais et intrants grâce aux recommandations précises.

Création de 15 emplois directs et 50 indirects (agents techniques, poseurs de capteurs, formateurs, développeurs, etc.) en phase pilote.

Intégration de 3 langues locales (soussou, poular, malinké) dans l’application pour une meilleure inclusion.

Favorise l’adoption des pratiques agricoles durables (fertilisation raisonnée, agriculture de conservation).
Key technologies:

Technologies clés utilisées dans AGRISENSE :

1. IoT (Internet of Things)

Utilisation de capteurs connectés 4-en-1 (humidité, pH, température, nutriments) déployés dans les champs.

Title: DigiHustle Hub: Empowering Rural Youth through Digital Innovation.
Subtitle: A digital empowerment platform providing rural youth and women with skills, tools, and market access to thrive in the inclusive digital economy.
Problem Statement: Despite the growing digital economy, rural youth and women remain excluded due to limited access to digital tools, low digital literacy, and lack of market connections. This digital divide deepens inequality, stifles innovation, and prevents marginalized groups from participating in economic opportunities and decision-making processes.
Solution Overview:
Solution Overview.
Our solution, DigiHustle Hub, is a blended digital empowerment platform tailored for rural youth and women in underserved communities. It offers practical digital literacy training, entrepreneurship incubation, and access to digital tools and markets. Participants are equipped with essential skills such as mobile-based digital marketing, e-commerce navigation, financial literacy, and low-code app development to turn local ideas into income-generating ventures.

How it works:
The program combines in-person community-based bootcamps with mobile-accessible e-learning modules to reduce access barriers. After training, participants receive mentorship and are linked to local and global digital marketplaces and financing platforms through curated partnerships. The platform also includes a "Digital Hustle Tracker"—a simple tool for monitoring progress, earnings, and skills advancement.

Technologies & Methodologies:
Mobile-first e-learning design
WhatsApp-based chatbot support
Open-source learning management systems (LMS)
Peer-to-peer learning and storytelling
Human-centred design (HCD) approach
Community participatory mapping tools

Partnerships & Collaboration Models:
We collaborate with local youth organizations, SACCOs, women’s groups, and digital service providers. Key partners include community ICT centres, grassroots trainers, and fintech providers who enable safe digital transactions. We are also in conversation with universities for certification and with NGOs for replication across different regions. Our model thrives on co-creation with the community to ensure relevance, scalability, and sustainability.
Solution Provider(s): Broad Borders Hope Foundation - A youth-led NGO working at the intersection of digital inclusion, climate justice, and community empowerment in rural Kenya. (Civil Society/NGO), Ajira Digital Kenya - A government-backed initiative supporting youth employability through digital skills training and online job opportunities. (Public Sector/ICT), Chamasoft Ltd. - A fintech company providing digital financial tools for informal community savings groups (Chamas), helping integrate rural women into the digital economy. (Private Sector/Fintech), Masinde Muliro University of Science and Technology (MMUST) - Academic partner offering technical curriculum support and certification for digital skills training. (Academia), Digital Opportunity Trust (DOT) Kenya - Empowering young leaders with digital and entrepreneurial skills to create grassroots change. (NGO/Youth Empowerment.
Implementation location(s): Pilot implementation conducted in Bungoma County and Kakamega County, Kenya.
Implementation timeline(s): Pilot phase implemented from March 2024 to June 2025. Ongoing expansion planned for late 2025.
Duration to pilot in a new geography: The estimated duration to pilot our solution in a new geography is 4 to 6 months. This includes stakeholder engagement, localized content adaptation, recruitment and training of participants, deployment of digital tools, and initial monitoring and evaluation.
SDGs addressed: SDG 4 (Quality Education);SDG 5 (Gender Equality);SDG 8 (Decent Work and Economic Growth);
Desired impact:
Solution Objectives:

The DigiHustle Hub aims to bridge the digital divide by equipping rural youth and women with relevant digital skills, entrepreneurial knowledge, and access to digital marketplaces. The core objectives are:
•	To enhance digital literacy and confidence among marginalized groups.
•	To increase the number of youth-led digital enterprises in rural areas.
•	To connect small-scale entrepreneurs with national and global digital economies.
•	To foster inclusive digital innovation for sustainable livelihoods.

Key Achievements / Impacts (so far):
•	Trained over 150 rural youth and women across Bungoma and Kakamega counties in digital entrepreneurship and financial literacy.
•	Facilitated the creation of 30+ micro-digital ventures, including online craft shops, virtual assistant services, and digital farming advisories.
•	Enabled 40% of trainees to access income-generating digital work within 3 months post-training.
•	Built partnerships with 4 local institutions and 2 fintech platforms to improve digital access and secure transactions.
•	Set a foundation for scaling the model across underserved communities in Kenya and beyond.
Key technologies:
The DigiHustle Hub leverages accessible and inclusive technologies to reach underserved communities. Key technologies include:
•	Mobile-First Learning Platforms: Optimized for low-bandwidth areas, enabling users to access content via basic smartphones.
•	WhatsApp Chatbot: Offers interactive guidance, mentorship access, and learning reminders in local languages.
•	Open-Source LMS (e.g., Moodle): Delivers structured training modules with tracking features for progress monitoring.
•	AI-Powered Recommendation Tools (Pilot): Suggests relevant digital job opportunities and learning pathways based on user input and engagement history.
•	Digital Mapping & Survey Tools (like KoboToolbox): Used for needs assessments, impact tracking, and community participation.
These technologies are selected for their affordability, ease of use, and scalability across rural and low-resource environments.
Unique Characteristics:
DigiHustle Hub stands out for its community-rooted, mobile-first model that combines digital skill-building with localized entrepreneurship and direct market access. Unlike traditional digital training programs, our solution integrates human-centred design and peer learning to ensure cultural relevance and user ownership.

Key differentiators include:
•	Blended learning delivery using WhatsApp chatbots and offline toolkits to serve areas with poor connectivity.
•	Community-based trainers and digital mentors who ensure ongoing local support and inclusion.
•	Integrated digital hustle tracking tool that helps participants monitor income, skills, and progress over time.
•	Collaborative partnership model involving universities, SACCOs, fintechs, and youth groups to ensure sustainability and scale.
•	Gender-responsive approach tailored to address digital and social barriers faced by rural women and girls.

This solution doesn’t just teach tech it builds pathways to income, dignity, and long-term participation in the digital economy.
Sustainable Change:
Theory of Change:

At the heart of DigiHustle Hub is the belief that digital inclusion is a catalyst for economic justice and community transformation. By equipping rural youth and women with relevant digital skills, tools, and entrepreneurial support, we enable them to become active participants in the digital economy moving from passive consumers to empowered creators and earners.

Inputs:
Training curricula, mobile-based platforms, local mentors, and community partnerships.

Activities:
Digital literacy training, entrepreneurial incubation, peer mentoring, and connection to digital marketplaces and financial tools.

Immediate Outcomes:
•	Increased digital confidence and skills among marginalized groups.
•	Creation of micro-enterprises and access to online income streams.
•	Strengthened local digital ecosystems.
•	Long-term/Systemic Change:
•	Reduction of digital and economic inequality by integrating marginalized voices into digital value chains.
•	Gender and youth empowerment through sustained income and visibility in the digital space.
•	Increased resilience of rural economies, as communities build localized digital solutions and reduce dependency on traditional, fragile sectors.
•	Policy influence, as grassroots innovation demonstrates scalable models for inclusive digital development.

By embedding the solution within community structures and building capacity from the ground up, DigiHustle Hub fosters a ripple effect of opportunity, equity, and innovation that continues well beyond the pilot.

Title: SMARTFARM: The Digital Brain for Smallholder Agriculture
Subtitle: A smart agriculture platform combining IoT, AI, and marketplace access to empower African smallholder farmers.
Problem Statement: Smallholder farmers in Africa face low yields, poor market access, limited technical knowledge, and vulnerability to climate shocks due to lack of affordable, data-driven agricultural support tools.
Solution Overview:
SMARTFARM is an all-in-one digital platform designed for smallholder farmers. It combines a SMARTFARM Box equipped with IoT sensors and AI algorithms, a mobile app, and an online marketplace.
The SMARTFARM Box collects real-time data (soil moisture, temperature, humidity) and uses AI to provide actionable insights on irrigation, fertilization, pest control, and harvesting. Farmers receive alerts and recommendations directly on their phones.

The mobile app also connects them to a digital marketplace where they can sell produce at better prices, access agricultural inputs, and receive online training.

Title: FermaTech: Automated Low-Electric System for Coconut Wine
Subtitle: Revolutionizing traditional winemaking with science-based automated electro-fermentation to boost quality and support rural enterprises.
Problem Statement: Traditional coconut wine fermentation is slow, inconsistent, and highly dependent on manual processes, making it prone to microbial contamination and variable product quality. The lack of modern tools limits productivity, scalability, and market competitiveness for local producers. Additionally, inefficient fermentation leads to energy and resource waste, hampering sustainability. This project addresses these issues by developing an automated low-electric current fermentation system to improve process control, reduce production time, ensure product consistency, and empower local winemakers with accessible, science-based technology.
Solution Overview:
This project introduces an automated low-electric current (LEC) fermentation system designed specifically for coconut wine (cocowine) production. The system integrates electro-stimulation technologies with an automated fermentation setup to optimize microbial activity, improve ethanol yield, enhance sensory qualities, and ensure consistency of the final product.

The LEC system will apply either continuous low-voltage direct current (DC) or pulsed electric fields (PEF) to the fermentation medium in controlled settings. These electrical inputs stimulate yeast cell activity and enhance fermentation efficiency by increasing cell membrane permeability and improving nutrient uptake. The process will be managed by a microcontroller-based unit that automates voltage levels, pulse frequency, and stimulation intervals.

Sensors embedded in the system will monitor fermentation parameters such as temperature, pH, °Brix (sugar content), and ethanol concentration in real time, allowing for adjustments without human intervention. The automated approach reduces contamination risks, minimizes manual labor, and improves the repeatability of production cycles.

1. Experimental Design

A Randomized Complete Block Design (RCBD) will be used with three groups:

T0: Control (traditional fermentation)

T1: LEC stimulation (1–3V DC)

T2: Pulsed electric field stimulation (0.5–1.5 kV/cm)


2. Materials

Fresh coconut sap (with barok)

Glass fermentation vessels with airlocks

LEC and PEF apparatus: DC power supply, electrodes (stainless steel/graphite), pulse generator

Sensors and data loggers for monitoring temperature, pH, °Brix

Analytical tools: ethanol assay kits, spectrophotometer, digital refractometer


3. Automation Components

Microcontroller (e.g., Arduino or Raspberry Pi) to regulate:

Electric current flow

Pulse duration/frequency

Data collection from sensors

User interface (basic LCD or web dashboard) for system control and display


4. Evaluation Methods

Daily sampling for ethanol yield, pH, microbial count, and fermentation rate

Sensory evaluation using a trained panel and 9-point hedonic scale

Statistical analysis using ANOVA and Tukey’s HSD


5. Partnerships and Collaboration Models

5.1Internal Collaborators: Samar State University (SSU) through the Environmental Science Research and Development Center (ESRDC): Project implementation, lab resources, and training. SSU Colleges (CAS, CIT, CoEd): Provide interdisciplinary expertise in biology, engineering, education, and sensory analysis.

5.2 External Partners: DOST-Samar: Technical support, equipment access, potential co-funding, and support for utility model/patent application. LGU Paranas: Site coordination, community mobilization, and engagement of local coconut wine producers.

6. Community Engagement
Local cocowine producers will be involved in pilot testing, feedback collection, and eventual technology adoption. Training modules and manuals will be co-developed with input from producers to ensure usability and cultural relevance.

7. Future Collaboration Opportunities
The project aims to formalize linkages with other R&D agencies (e.g., DA-BAR, PCAARRD), and explore scalability options through industry-academe-government partnerships.

This pilot timeline ensures thorough testing while allowing for contextual adjustments and local capacity-building.
SDGs addressed: SDG 1 (No Poverty);SDG 9 (Industry, Innovation, and Infrastructure);SDG 5 (Gender Equality);
Desired impact:
The desired impact of the solution is to modernize and improve the efficiency of local coconut wine (cocowine) production through the application of automated low-electric current (LEC) and pulsed electric field (PEF) fermentation technologies. The primary objectives are to shorten fermentation time, enhance ethanol yield, and improve the overall sensory quality of the product, while promoting energy-efficient and sustainable processing methods suitable for small-scale producers. By introducing automation, the project aims to reduce fermentation time by 30–50%, increase alcohol yield by 10–20%, and improve product acceptability based on sensory evaluation scores exceeding 80%.

The solution is also expected to result in energy savings of approximately 25–40% through the use of low-voltage systems (1–3V DC), contributing to more sustainable production practices. In terms of social impact, the project targets the generation of 10–20 new livelihood opportunities during pilot implementation and scale-up, with at least 50 local coconut wine producers trained ensuring equitable participation of women-led enterprises. The initiative will also deliver a functional fermentation prototype, support utility model registration, and encourage responsible use of natural additives such as barok. Ultimately, the project aligns with national priorities for innovation, rural enterprise development, and climate-resilient food processing systems.
Key technologies:
The key technologies used in this solution focus on automated electro-stimulation systems integrated with basic Internet of Things (IoT) components and microcontroller-based automation. These technologies are tailored for small-scale, sustainable fermentation applications in rural settings.

Overview of Technologies Utilized
	Low Electric Current (LEC) Stimulation Technology- Applies a constant low-voltage direct current (1–3V DC) using submerged electrodes to stimulate yeast activity, enhance microbial metabolism, and accelerate fermentation.
	Pulsed Electric Field (PEF) Technology- Delivers short bursts of high-voltage pulses (0.5–1.5 kV/cm) to increase cell membrane permeability (electroporation), improving nutrient uptake and fermentation kinetics.
	Microcontroller-Based Automation (Arduino or Raspberry Pi)- Manages electric current flow, pulse timing, and voltage levels. Controls the stimulation process and ensures consistent operation without manual intervention.
	Internet of Things (IoT) Sensors- Integrated sensors monitor key fermentation parameters such as temperature, pH, °Brix (sugar content), and ethanol concentration. Enables real-time data logging and process optimization.
These technologies are adapted to be low-cost, scalable, and locally maintainable, making them ideal for community-level implementation in rural fermentation enterprises.
Unique Characteristics:
The proposed solution stands out through its unique combination of technological innovation, local adaptability, and inclusive design. It introduces a low-cost, automated electro-stimulation system using low electric current (LEC) and pulsed electric fields (PEF)- a first-of-its-kind application in coconut wine (tuba) production in the Philippines. While similar technologies have been explored in industrial winemaking, this project customizes the approach for small-scale, rural producers, making advanced fermentation tools accessible through microcontroller-based automation and real-time monitoring of key parameters such as pH, temperature, and sugar content.
What makes the solution further distinctive is its energy efficiency and sustainability. Operating at only 1–3 volts, the system significantly reduces energy consumption compared to conventional methods, while also improving product consistency and reducing waste. Beyond the technology, the project leverages a collaborative partnership model involving Samar State University, DOST-Samar, LGU-Paranas, and local coconut wine producers. This inclusive co-development framework ensures that the solution is not only technically sound but also socially accepted and community-owned.
Moreover, the project integrates gender-responsive strategies by targeting equal participation of women in training, piloting, and eventual adoption. It is designed to deliver dual outcomes: improved cocowine quality and a transferable, patentable fermentation system for broader commercialization. These combined features position the solution as an innovative, locally grounded model that advances sustainability, livelihoods, and rural enterprise development.
