Summary: FermaTech est un système automatisé de fermentation à faible courant électrique (LEC) et champ électrique pulsé (PEF) conçu pour moderniser la production traditionnelle de vin de coco aux Philippines. En stimulant l’activité microbienne grâce à de faibles impulsions électriques et en intégrant des capteurs IoT et un microcontrôleur (Arduino/Raspberry Pi), la solution améliore le rendement en éthanol, accélère la fermentation de 30–50 %, et réduit les risques de contamination. Développé par l’Université d’État de Samar (SSU) et ses partenaires (DOST-Samar, LGU Paranas), le projet inclut des formations communautaires, un co-développement avec les producteurs locaux et une approche de genre. Il vise à accroître la productivité, réduire les pertes post-récolte, économiser 25–40 % d’énergie et améliorer la qualité sensorielle du cocowine. (Q12, Q13, Q17, Q18, Q19).

Title: CultivaHub: Digital Solutions for Organic Fertilizer & Waste Management
Subtitle: Transforming food waste into organic fertilizer via CleanerBox smart bins and WasteBank trash-to-cash platform, empowering African farmers and promoting circular economy.
Problem Statement: African smallholder farmers face declining soil fertility due to overuse of chemical fertilizers and poor waste management. Food waste is abundant but underutilized, worsening environmental and economic challenges.
Solution Overview: CultivaHub converts food waste into high-quality organic fertilizer (CultivaFert) using decentralized processing. Our CleanerBox smart bins collect segregated waste, enabling efficient recycling. WasteBank incentivizes community participation by rewarding waste deposits. We collaborate with local farmers, municipalities, and NGOs to co-develop sustainable waste-to-fertilizer ecosystems that restore soil health, increase yields, and improve livelihoods.
Solution Provider(s): CultivaHub (Eco-innovative startup), Local Farmers Associations (community partners), Municipalities (waste collection), Environmental NGOs (technical support).
Implementation location(s): Goma, North Kivu, Democratic Republic of Congo
Duration to pilot in a new geography: 6 months for setup, community engagement, and initial operations
SDGs addressed: SDG 1 (No Poverty);SDG 8 (Decent Work and Economic Growth);SDG 12 (Responsible Consumption and Production);
Desired impact:
• Restore soil fertility and increase crop yields by 20-30%
    • Divert tons of organic waste from landfills, reducing methane emissions
    • Generate green jobs and empower 300+ smallholder farmers
    • Promote circular economy models for sustainable agriculture in Africa.
Key technologies: IoT-enabled CleanerBox smart bins for waste segregation and monitoring, mobile platform WasteBank for incentivizing participation, data analytics for impact tracking.
Unique Characteristics: CultivaHub integrates physical waste management hardware with a digital trash-to-cash platform, creating economic incentives for community participation. The decentralized organic fertilizer production model is tailored for local resource cycles, ensuring affordability and environmental sustainability.
Sustainable Change: By empowering communities to manage organic waste digitally and transform it into fertilizer, CultivaHub fosters circular economy practices, enhances food security, and creates replicable green jobs. This systemic shift reduces dependence on chemical inputs and promotes environmental stewardship aligned with global SDGs.
Funding Sources: Our solution has been funded through a combination of personal investment, trainings and revenues, grants from local and international development programs, and support from impact-focused competitions and awards (e.g., GreenTech Program by UNDP Kenya, Omega Resilience Award by the HOMEF). We are currently exploring additional partnerships and impact investors to scale.
Primary thematic focus area: MSME Empowerment & Local Digital Innovation
Summary: CultivaHub is a circular economy initiative that transforms food waste into organic fertilizer through IoT-enabled smart bins (CleanerBox) and a digital trash-to-cash platform (WasteBank). Piloted in Goma, DRC, the solution empowers smallholder farmers with affordable organic inputs, reduces waste-related emissions, and creates green jobs by integrating hardware, digital platforms, and local community partnerships.

Title: Améliorer l'Accès et la Gestion du Gaz Domestique au Cameroun pour un Développement Durable
Subtitle: Le projet vise à contribuer à l'atteinte des Objectifs de Développement Durable (ODD) en améliorant l'accès des ménages camerounais au gaz domestique, une source d'énergie propre et abordable. Plus spécifiquement, le projet cherche à améliorer l'efficacité de la gestion des bouteilles de gaz au Cameroun, en réduisant les coûts et les pertes liés à la gestion des bouteilles de gaz, et en améliorant l'accès des clients aux bouteilles de gaz de leur marque préférée. En mettant en place un système de gestion des bouteilles de gaz qui permet aux clients d'échanger leurs bouteilles de gaz d'une marque contre une autre marque, le projet vise à rendre l'accès au gaz domestique plus facile et plus abordable pour les ménages camerounais, tout en réduisant les coûts et les pertes.
Problem Statement:
1. Gestion des Bouteilles de Gaz :   Transport inefficace des bouteilles de gaz, entraînant des coûts élevés et un manque à gagner. Distribution non optimisée, limitant l'accès des clients aux bouteilles de gaz. Manque d'efficacité globale dans la gestion des bouteilles, se traduisant par une disponibilité irrégulière et un accès difficile pour les clients.

2. Réduction des Coûts et des Pertes : Processus d'échange des bouteilles de gaz vides contre des bouteilles pleines inefficace, entraînant des pertes de temps et des coûts supplémentaires pour les fournisseurs et les consommateurs. Contraintes importantes pour les ménages, obligés d'abandonner leurs activités et de parcourir de longues distances pour se procurer du gaz.

3. Amélioration de l'Accès des Clients : Difficulté pour les clients d'acheter du gaz indépendamment de la marque de leur bouteille, limitant leur choix et les obligeant à se conformer aux exigences des fournisseurs. Manque d'efficacité globale dans la gestion des bouteilles, se traduisant par une disponibilité irrégulière finale et un accès difficile pour les clients.
Solution Overview:
1. Solutions à la Gestion des Bouteilles de Gaz  :
  •  Transport Collectif : Mettre en place un système de transport indépendamment mutualisé et optimisé, permettant de regrouper les bouteilles de gaz de différentes marques et de réduire les coûts de transport.
  •  Distribution Massive : renforcer le réseau de distribution pour qu’il soit plus étendu et plus performant, avec des points de vente stratégiquement situés pour garantir une couverture géographique optimale.
  •  Amélioration de l'Efficacité : Mettre en œuvre des outils de suivi et de gestion des stocks en temps réel, permettant d'anticiper la demande, d'optimiser les tournées de livraison et de garantir la disponibilité des bouteilles de gaz pour les clients.

2. Solution à la Réduction des Coûts et des Pertes :
 •  Échange Efficace : Mettre en place un système d'échange rapide, simple et transparent, basé sur des procédures standardisées et des outils informatiques performants.
  •  Réduction des Contraintes : Renforcer le réseau existant en réseau de points d'échange de proximité, permettant aux ménages de se procurer du gaz sans avoir à parcourir de longues distances ni à abandonner leurs activités. Proposer des services de livraison à domicile pour les personnes les plus éloignées ou les plus vulnérables.

3. Solutions à l’amélioration de l'Accès des Clients :
  •  Disponibilité : Mettre en place un système permettant aux clients d'acheter du gaz indépendamment de la marque de leur bouteille, favorisant ainsi la concurrence transparente et la satisfaction des consommateurs.
  •  Amélioration de l'Efficacité : Mettre en œuvre des outils de suivi et de gestion des stocks en temps réel, permettant d'anticiper la demande, d'optimiser les tournées de livraison et de garantir la disponibilité des bouteilles de gaz.
Solution Provider(s): -	La SCDP (Société Camerounaise de Dépôt Pétrolier) est le premier partenaire ;  -	Les stations-services qui ont une marque de gaz telles que Tradex, TOTAL, NEPTUNE OIL, GREEN OIL, BOCOM ; -	Les opérateurs de téléphonie mobile (Orange Cameroun, MTN Cameroun) - MINFI (Ministère des Finances) qui donnera l’agrément de paiement à partir de notre application
Duration to pilot in a new geography: 10 mois
SDGs addressed: SDG 9 (Industry, Innovation, and Infrastructure);SDG 7 (Affordable and Clean Energy);SDG 12 (Responsible Consumption and Production);
Desired impact:
-	Contribution aux Objectifs de Développement Durable (ODD) : Le projet participe à la protection de l'environnement, l’accès à une énergie propre et abordable, à l’industrie, innovation et infrastructures, à la consommation et production responsables
-	Réduction de la déforestation et de la pollution : Moins de recours au bois et au charbon de bois, bénéfique pour l'environnement et la santé.
-	Création d'emplois locaux : Le projet générera des emplois dans la logistique, la distribution, la gestion du réseau et la manutention.
-	Gain de temps et confort pour les consommateurs : Moins de déplacements et plus de flexibilité dans le choix des marques.
-	Soutien aux commerces de proximité : Les points d'échange agréés verront leur activité et leurs revenus augmenter.
-	Accès facilité au gaz domestique : Plus de ménages, y compris les plus modestes, pourront facilement accéder au gaz.
-	Coût total (Cout d’achat + Charge d’acquisition + Risques éventuels) du gaz réduit pour les familles : L'optimisation de la logistique et la concurrence entre marques feront baisser les prix.
-	Image positive pour les entreprises participantes : Les fournisseurs de gaz et les partenaires du projet renforceront leur image de marque en s'engageant pour le développement durable.
Key technologies: Nous utiliserons comme technologie une application mobile et web client serveur pour nous permettre de connecter les client fonctionnant sur la plateforme Android et IOS. Chaque client pourra télécharger gratuitement notre application disponible sur Play Store ou APP STORE et avoir accès à nos ressources.
Unique Characteristics: Notre concept original et novateur ne cherche pas la rivalité, mais à solidifier l'offre de valeur auprès des clients. En plus, ce projet est unique grâce à son approche innovante, sa concentration sur la gestion des bouteilles de gaz, sa participation aux ODD et son potentiel impact sur les familles modestes. Son modèle économique permet de de faire gagner de l’argent et de créer plus de valeur aux différents parties prenantes
Primary thematic focus area: Inclusive Digital Innovation Skills & Entrepreneurial Talent Development
Summary: This project aims to improve access to and management of domestic gas in Cameroon, reducing costs, enhancing availability, and ensuring sustainability. The solution focuses on optimizing gas bottle distribution and exchanges, but further details on the scalability and long-term financial sustainability are needed.

Title: Mon Artisan: Connecting Skilled Workers to Instant Opportunities
Subtitle: A digital platform linking qualified artisans to customers, offering skills training, pre-financing, and reliable home and business services across Francophone Africa.
Problem Statement: In Francophone Africa, skilled informal workers lack visibility, certification, and stable income, while customers struggle to find affordable, trustworthy services quickly and securely.
Solution Overview:
Mon Artisan is a digital skill-on-demand platform that connects customers to vetted, qualified artisans and gig workers for services such as plumbing, electricity, carpentry, painting, IT support, and more. Users can search, compare, and book services instantly via mobile or web, with integrated mobile and card payment options. The platform also offers after-sales customer service, dispute resolution, and service guarantees to ensure satisfaction.

For artisans, Mon Artisan provides a profile to showcase skills, receive job requests, and manage bookings. They benefit from skills-building programs, official certification pathways, pre-financing for tools or materials, and logistical support to complete jobs efficiently.

Methodologies and technologies used : 
- Platform architecture: Web and mobile application built for accessibility in low-bandwidth environments.
- Artisan vetting process: Manual screening, reference checks, and skills assessments to ensure quality.
- Secure transactions: Integration of mobile money and bank card payments for ease and transparency.
- Customer experience design: Simple, pleasant, and secure UX/UI to promote adoption.
- Impact measurement: Tracking completed jobs, customer ratings, artisan earnings, and training outcomes.

Partnerships and collaboration models : 

-Training & Certification: Partnerships with vocational training institutes to provide official certification for artisans.
- Financial Support: Agreements with microfinance institutions for artisan pre-financing.
- Service Ecosystem: Collaborations with insurers and home equipment distributors for bundled offers.
- Expansion Partnerships: Engagement with government agencies and accelerators (e.g., Catalyst Jobtech Accelerator by Mercy Corps & BFA Global) to scale operations across Francophone Africa.)
Solution Provider(s): Mercy Corps – global humanitarian organization supporting inclusive jobtech solutions, BFA Global – impact innovation firm focused on fintech and jobtech in emerging markets, vocational training institutes – technical and professional education providers, microfinance institutions – financial services providers for underserved communities, insurers and home equipment distributors – companies offering complementary products and services.
Duration to pilot in a new geography: One month
SDGs addressed: SDG 8 (Decent Work and Economic Growth);SDG 1 (No Poverty);SDG 10 (Reduced Inequalities);
Desired impact:
Solution Objectives: 
- Create sustainable income opportunities for artisans and gig workers in the informal sector.
- Improve access to affordable, reliable, and high-quality services for households and businesses.
- Strengthen artisans’ skills through training, certification, and digital literacy.
- Facilitate financial inclusion via secure payments and pre-financing options.
- Expand the reach of the platform across Francophone Africa to connect millions of users.

Key Achievements / Impacts : 
- Employment generation: Hundreds of uncertified but skilled workers accredited and connected to steady work opportunitiesIvory Coast’s Mon Artis….
- Income growth: Increased earnings for artisans by enabling more frequent and higher-value jobs.
- Skills development: Partner-led training and certification programs improving professional standards.
- Market access: Bridging the gap between underserved informal workers and the middle-class customer base.
- Social inclusion: Expanding opportunities at the bottom of the pyramid through technology-enabled connections.
- Regional expansion: Operational in Côte d’Ivoire and Burkina Faso, with planned entry into Senegal and other Francophone West African countriesIvory Coast’s Mon Artis….
Key technologies:
Key Technologies Used :

- Web and Mobile Applications: Core platform accessible via smartphone and desktop, optimized for low-bandwidth environments.
- Mobile Money & Card Payment Integration: Secure, seamless transactions through mobile wallets and bank cards.
- Artisan Management System: Database with vetting records, job history, ratings, and performance tracking.
- Geolocation Services: Matchmaking between customers and nearby vetted artisans for faster service delivery.
- User Experience (UX/UI) Design: Intuitive interface ensuring simple, pleasant, and secure navigation.
- Data Analytics: Monitoring service quality, user behavior, artisan performance, and training outcomes to inform improvements.
Unique Characteristics:
- End-to-End Support for Artisans: Goes beyond job matching by offering skills training, official certification, pre-financing, and logistical assistance, enabling artisans to grow sustainablyIvory Coast’s Mon Artis….

- Inclusive Market Access: Bridges two traditionally disconnected socio-economic groups — skilled informal workers and middle-class customers — through an accessible, tech-enabled marketplace.

- Quality Assurance Mechanism: Vetting process, performance tracking, and customer ratings ensure trust and service reliability.

- Integrated Financial Ecosystem: Combines secure mobile/card payments with microfinance partnerships to fund tools, materials, or working capital.

- Scalable Regional Model: Already operational in Côte d’Ivoire and Burkina Faso with a framework for rapid expansion across Francophone West Africa.

- Multi-Sector Collaboration: Works with vocational institutes, insurers, distributors, and development accelerators to create a holistic service and income-generation ecosystem.
Sustainable Change:
1. Problem Context
In Francophone Africa, the informal sector employs the majority of the workforce, yet artisans often lack visibility, certification, financial support, and consistent income. Customers face challenges in finding trustworthy, affordable, and skilled service providers.

2. Pathway to Change

Access & Trust: The platform connects vetted artisans with customers, ensuring transparent transactions, quality standards, and guaranteed payments.

Capacity Building: Through partnerships with vocational institutes, artisans gain new skills, certifications, and digital literacy, raising the overall quality of services in the market.

Financial Inclusion: Pre-financing and secure digital payment systems integrate artisans into the formal financial ecosystem, unlocking access to credit and insurance.

Market Expansion: The regional rollout increases service demand and job opportunities, boosting incomes and reducing underemployment.

3. Desired Follow-On Effects

Improved Livelihoods: Steady, better-paying jobs for artisans, lifting households out of poverty.
Sector Formalization: Transition of informal workers into recognized, certified professionals.
Gender Inclusion: Greater participation of women artisans in traditionally male-dominated trades.
Local Economic Growth: Increased productivity and spending power in communities served.
Replicable Model: A scalable blueprint for digitizing and formalizing artisan services across Africa.

4. Long-Term Impact
A self-sustaining ecosystem where skilled work is valued, service quality is standardized, and technology permanently transforms how informal labor is accessed, managed, and rewarded
Funding Sources: Grants, love money, personal capital contributions
Primary thematic focus area: MSME Empowerment & Local Digital Innovation
Summary: Mon Artisan is a digital platform that connects skilled artisans in Francophone Africa to customers, providing essential services like skills training, pre-financing, and market access. The solution empowers artisans while increasing service quality, but requires more details on scalability and long-term sustainability.

Title: FinancIA – Intelligent Financial Empowerment Platform
Subtitle: AI-powered digital platform enabling women, youth, and MSMEs to manage budgets, achieve savings goals, and access financial literacy.
Problem Statement: Millions of women, youth, and micro-entrepreneurs lack access to affordable, user-friendly tools for managing their personal or business finances. This digital gap limits their ability to plan, save, invest, and access credit, perpetuating cycles of poverty and exclusion from the formal economy.
Solution Overview:
How it works: FinancIA is a web and mobile-ready platform offering AI-driven tools to create budgets, set financial goals, track expenses, and simulate investments or loans.
Methodologies: User-centered design for low digital literacy; financial literacy frameworks aligned with OECD and UN financial inclusion guidelines; AI for categorization and recommendations.
Technologies: Next.js, Tailwind, SQLite/PostgreSQL, Chart.js, OpenAI API for natural language support and personalized insights.
Partnerships: Designed for collaboration with NGOs, universities, cooperatives, and local financial institutions for last-mile outreach.
Collaboration model: Freemium model with free core features for underserved communities and optional enterprise/MSME modules through partners.
Solution Provider(s): Rico Gutierrez y Cía. S. en C. – Private company, financial consulting and technology solutions, Colombia.  Potential partners: Universidad del Rosario (Colombia) – Higher education and research in business and technology.
Duration to pilot in a new geography: 3–4 months, including localization, partner onboarding, and community training.
SDGs addressed: SDG 4 (Quality Education);SDG 5 (Gender Equality);SDG 8 (Decent Work and Economic Growth);
Desired impact:
Objectives:
Increase financial literacy among women, youth, and MSMEs.
Improve budgeting, savings, and investment practices in underserved communities.

Key impacts (targets within 12 months):
Reach 5,000+ active users in pilot regions.
Increase average monthly savings by 15% among active users.
Improve MSME cashflow predictability by 20% through integrated tools.
Key technologies:
AI (OpenAI API) for expense categorization and recommendations.
Modern web stack (Next.js, Tailwind, Chart.js) for responsive, accessible UI.
Database engines (SQLite/PostgreSQL) for scalable storage.
Export/analytics modules (XLSX, PDF) for offline and reporting use.
Unique Characteristics:
Combines personal finance and MSME cashflow tools in one platform.
Designed for low digital literacy users with visual, step-by-step guidance.
AI-assisted categorization and contextual financial tips.
Modular architecture allowing NGOs or governments to white-label and deploy quickly.
Sustainable Change: By equipping underserved individuals and small businesses with digital financial management skills and tools, FinancIA reduces the risk of debt traps, fosters savings culture, and facilitates access to formal credit. The long-term change is a more financially resilient population that participates actively in the digital economy, creating multiplier effects in household stability, entrepreneurship, and community development.
Funding Sources: FinancIA has been self-funded to date by Ivan Rico and our family company: Rico Gutiérrez y Cía. S. en C., with in-kind contributions of development time, design, and hosting. Additional support from personal funds of the founders. We are seeking partnerships and grant opportunities to expand the pilot and reach underserved communities.
Testimonials and Endorsements:
As FinancIA is at Prototipe stage, initial feedback has been collected from small business owners and youth participating in financial literacy workshops in Bogotá:

“This platform makes it easy to understand my monthly cashflow and set savings goals, even from my phone.” — Pilot participant, Bogotá, Colombia.
“For the first time, I can see clearly how much I spend on supplies versus sales.” — MSME owner, informal retail sector.
Further comments/feedback: This questionnaire covers all the key aspects for evaluating inclusive digital solutions. We suggest that future calls could include an optional section for describing planned pilot metrics and expected return on inclusion, as these are critical for measuring long-term impact.
Primary thematic focus area: Inclusive Digital Innovation Skills & Entrepreneurial Talent Development
Summary: FinancIA is an AI-powered digital platform aimed at enhancing financial literacy and improving financial management for women, youth, and MSMEs in underserved communities. While the solution is innovative, it is still in the prototype stage and faces challenges related to scalability, funding, and partnerships necessary for wider adoption.

Title: EcoTrace : Transforming Waste into Rewards for a Cleaner Cameroon
Subtitle: A digital platform empowering citizens to recycle, track, and earn rewards for a cleaner, greener Cameroon.
Problem Statement: In Cameroon, over 600,000 tons of plastic waste are generated annually, but only 15% is recycled. Improper waste management pollutes urban areas, harms communities, and contributes to greenhouse gas emissions.
Solution Overview:
EcoTrace is a digital platform designed to transform urban waste management in Cameroon. Citizens can report and recycle plastic waste using the app, earning rewards for their participation. The system tracks each contribution, enabling real-time monitoring of waste collection and recycling rates.

Methodologies and technologies:

Mobile and web application with an intuitive interface for reporting and tracking waste.

Data analytics to monitor recycling trends and community engagement.

Gamification and rewards system to incentivize participation.

IoT and QR code tagging (where available) to track larger waste collection points.

Partnerships and collaboration models:

Ukuzola: Supports environmental education, awareness campaigns, and sustainable practices promotion.

Collaboration with municipal authorities to integrate EcoTrace into urban waste management strategies.

Engagement with local communities and youth groups to encourage active participation and ensure inclusive impact.
Solution Provider(s): Ukuzola – An association dedicated to social and climate transitions, supporting environmental education, sustainable practices, and community engagement in Cameroon.
Implementation location(s): Pilot locations: Implemented in select urban neighborhoods in Yaoundé, Cameroon.
Implementation timeline(s): Implementation timeline: Pilot phase initiated in March 2025 and currently ongoing in select urban neighborhoods of Yaoundé, Cameroon.
Duration to pilot in a new geography: Estimated duration to test in a new geography: Approximately 3 to 6 months, including setup, community engagement, training, and monitoring of waste collection and citizen participation.
SDGs addressed: SDG 11 (Sustainable Cities and Communities);SDG 12 (Responsible Consumption and Production);SDG 13 (Climate Action);
Desired impact:
EcoTrace aims to improve urban waste management, increase recycling rates, and foster sustainable behaviors among citizens. The solution empowers communities, particularly youth and women, to actively participate in creating cleaner, more resilient cities.

Key achievements and impacts:

Plastic waste collected and recycled: Approximately 1.2 tons during the pilot phase in selected neighborhoods of Yaoundé.

Citizen engagement: Over 600 individuals trained or actively participating in waste reporting and recycling initiatives.

Reduction of greenhouse gas emissions: Estimated 1.8 tons of CO₂ avoided through recycling and reduced plastic production.

Economic opportunities: Rewards system incentivizes participation and creates small-scale economic benefits for community members involved in collection and recycling.

Behavioral change: Increased awareness and adoption of responsible consumption and waste management practices.
Key technologies:
Mobile and web application: Intuitive interface for reporting, tracking, and managing waste.

Data analytics: Monitoring recycling trends, user engagement, and impact metrics.

Gamification and reward system: Incentivizes citizen participation and promotes behavioral change.

IoT (Internet of Things) and QR code tagging: For tracking large waste collection points and improving traceability where available.

Cloud-based infrastructure: Ensures scalable, real-time data management and accessibility.
Unique Characteristics:
Citizen-driven approach: EcoTrace actively engages communities, especially youth and women, turning waste management into a participatory and rewarding activity.

Gamification and rewards: Innovative incentive system encourages continuous participation and behavioral change.

Digital tracking and analytics: Real-time monitoring of waste collection and recycling rates ensures transparency and measurable impact.

Inclusive partnership model: Collaborates with local associations, municipal authorities, and community groups to strengthen social engagement and sustainability.

Scalable and adaptable platform: Technology designed for replication in other cities and regions, making the solution flexible for diverse urban contexts.
Sustainable Change:
EcoTrace aims to create a sustainable shift in urban waste management by engaging citizens, local authorities, and community organizations in a participatory and data-driven process. By turning waste collection into a rewarding activity, the platform changes behaviors, increases recycling rates, and reduces environmental pollution.

The theory of change is as follows:

Awareness and engagement: Citizens, especially youth and women, learn the importance of waste management and climate action.

Behavioral change: Continuous participation through rewards leads to habitual recycling and responsible consumption.

Community and institutional adoption: Municipalities and local organizations integrate EcoTrace into urban waste strategies.

Scalable impact: Replication across other urban areas amplifies waste reduction, lowers greenhouse gas emissions, and promotes circular economy practices.
Primary thematic focus area: Sustainable Cities and Communities
Summary: EcoTrace is a digital platform designed to improve urban waste management and increase recycling rates in Cameroon. The platform incentivizes citizen participation through a gamification and rewards system, allowing users to report and recycle waste. Using mobile and web applications, EcoTrace offers real-time monitoring, tracking, and analytics to ensure transparency and accountability in waste management. The system is designed to promote sustainable behaviors and empower marginalized communities, particularly youth and women, to actively engage in environmental conservation.

Title: Digi-Equal Africa
Subtitle: Connecting African women in tech with mentorship and speaking opportunities to share expertise, raise visibility, and advance digital gender equality.
Problem Statement: Across Africa, gender stereotypes and limited visibility of female role models in technology discourage girls and women from pursuing and thriving in STEM careers. These barriers begin early in education and persist into professional and entrepreneurial spaces, resulting in a lack of representation, mentorship, and access to networks for women in tech. Existing initiatives often operate in isolation, making it difficult for role models and organisations to connect, collaborate, and maximise their impact on digital gender equality.
Solution Overview:
How the Solution Works:
Digi-Equal Africa is a digital platform that connects African women in tech with organisations (such as digital skills initiatives and innovation hubs) that are working to advance digital skills and gender equality.

On the platform, role models create profiles highlighting their expertise, career journey, and availability for mentorship, speaking engagements, advisory roles, and other collaborations.

Organisations add their programs and opportunities to the platform, then search and filter the role model directory by sector, skill set, region, and language.

The platform facilitates direct connections, enabling engagements that raise the visibility of female tech leaders and inspire the next generation.

Methodologies and Technologies Used:

User-Centred Design: Developed with input from both role models and intermediaries to ensure relevance and ease of use.

Cloud-Based Web Platform: Accessible across devices to ensure reach across Africa.

Search & Matching Functionality: Tag-based filtering by expertise, location, and sector.

Analytics & Feedback Tools: Embedded to measure engagements, reach, and user satisfaction.

GDPR-Compliant Data Management: Ensuring privacy and trust for all users.

Partnerships and Collaboration Models:

Core Research Partnership: The platform was built on insights from the UKRI/GCRF funded “Bridging the Digital Gender Divide” project, led by the University of Leicester which led to the establishment of Coalition for Digital Equality (CODE) Network.

Technology & Inclusion Partners Africa Technology Business Network (ATBN), Ishango.ai and Co-Catalyst provides platform development, digital marketing, community engagement, and impact strategy.

Community Partnerships: Collaboration with existing women-in-tech networks, STEM mentorship programs, and educational institutions across Africa.

Events & Outreach: Engagement through the African Business Chamber UK and the annual Digi-Equal Africa Awards to expand visibility and partnerships
Solution Provider(s): University of Leicester – A leading UK higher education and research institution : Higher Education & Research, Africa Technology Business Network (ATBN) – A social impact organisation committed to enabling inclusive digital transformation in Africa; sector: Technology, Digital Inclusion, Social Impact: Co-Catalyst – An organisation dedicated to fostering collaborative solutions for social change, with a focus on equity, inclusion, and sustainable development; sector: Social Innovation, Inclusive Development, Capacity Building:Ishango.AI – An impact-driven technology company creating AI and data solutions while developing African data science talent; sector: Artificial Intelligence, Data Science, Digital Skills Development.
Implementation location(s): Target countries initially include Ghana and Uganda with aim to expand across Africa
Duration to pilot in a new geography: 3 months
SDGs addressed: SDG 5 (Gender Equality);SDG 9 (Industry, Innovation, and Infrastructure);SDG 8 (Decent Work and Economic Growth);
Desired impact:
Enhanced Representation – At least 100 African female role models onboarded and actively engaged on the platform within the first 12 months.

Expanded Opportunities – Facilitation of 50+ mentorships, speaking engagements, or advisory roles linking role models with schools, universities, and innovation hubs.

Organisational Impact – At least 25 participating organisations reporting improved gender inclusion practices as a result of engagement with role models.

Geographic Reach – Role model and intermediary participation from 8+ African countries, ensuring diversity in language, region, and expertise.

Visibility and Engagement – Annual Awards celebrating African women in tech and raising public awareness of women’s role in shaping Africa’s digital future.
Key technologies:
Cloud-Based Web Platform – Provides secure, scalable, and device-agnostic access for users across Africa.

Advanced Search & Filtering – Tag-based and sector-specific matching to connect role models and organisations efficiently.

Data Analytics & Reporting Tools – Capture engagement metrics, user activity, and impact data for continuous improvement.

Secure Data Management (GDPR-Compliant) – Protects user information through encryption, secure authentication, and privacy-by-design practices.

Integration with Communication Tools – Enables seamless coordination for mentorship, speaking engagements, and events via embedded scheduling and messaging features.
Unique Characteristics:
Pan-African Scope with Local Relevance – Connects women and organisations across multiple African countries, with filters for language, region, sector, and career stage to ensure culturally and contextually relevant matches.

Research-Led Approach – Built on evidence and frameworks developed from the UKRI/GCRF “Bridging the Digital Gender Divide” project, ensuring activities are grounded in proven strategies to tackle gender stereotypes.

Partnership Model for Sustainability – Leverages collaborations with innovation hubs, digital skills initiatives and women-in-tech networks to expand reach and ensure post-grant longevity.

Impact Measurement Integration – Captures engagement, reach, and outcomes via in-platform analytics and feedback loops, enabling transparent reporting and iterative improvement.
Sustainable Change:
Digi-Equal Africa addresses a key driver of gender inequality in Africa’s digital economy - the lack of visible, accessible female role models in technology - by building a structured, scalable, and evidence-based mechanism for connecting them with organisations working to advance digital gender equality.

Theory of Change:

Inputs – Creation of a pan-African, GDPR-compliant digital platform; onboarding of diverse female role models; partnerships with innovation hubs, and digital skills initiatives.

Activities – Facilitate mentorship, speaking engagements, advisory roles, and public recognition through events such as the Digi-Equal Awards.

Outputs – Increased connections between role models and organisations; wider dissemination of women’s success stories; stronger gender equality practices in partner institutions.

Short-Term Outcomes:

Enhanced visibility and influence of women in tech.

Increased access for girls and women to relatable mentors and career pathways in STEM.

Improved inclusivity in participating organisations’ programs and policies.

Long-Term Impact:

Growth in the number of women pursuing and thriving in tech careers and entrepreneurship.

Strengthen gender inclusion practices in innovation hubs and digital skills initiatives across Africa.

A self-sustaining, cross-sectoral network that continually fosters digital gender equality.

Desired Follow-On Effects:

Institutionalisation of gender-inclusive practices in the African digital sector

Creation of a virtuous cycle where today’s mentees become tomorrow’s role models.

Expanded adoption of the model across other regions and sectors, supported by ongoing partnerships and revenue-generating activities for platform maintenance.
Funding Sources:
The Coalition for Digital Equality (CODE) network was established as part of an 18-month project " Bridging the Digital Gender Divide to Stimulate Growth in African Digital Economies" funded by UK Research and Innovation (UKRI) and the Global Challenges Research Fund (GCRF)
The Digi-Equal Africa platform development was funded by the Economic and Social Research Council (ESRC)'s Impact Acceleration Account (IAA)

Summary: Digi-Equal Africa is a pan-African digital platform designed to connect women in technology with mentorship, speaking engagements, and advisory opportunities. By showcasing female role models, the initiative aims to dismantle stereotypes, provide visibility, and enhance career pathways for women in STEM. Built on research from the UKRI/GCRF-funded 'Bridging the Digital Gender Divide' project, the platform uses cloud-based infrastructure, advanced search and matching tools, and GDPR-compliant data management. It partners with universities, NGOs, women-in-tech networks, and innovation hubs to ensure inclusivity and sustainability. The project also features events like the Digi-Equal Africa Awards to expand visibility and institutionalise gender equality practices in Africa’s digital economy.

Title: Rural Women Biogas Production Utilisation and Commercialisation
Subtitle: This is a project to assist women in rural areas in biogas production for their own domestic use and sale of the excess production. The production and stored capacities are monitored digitally and remotely via an app.
Problem Statement: Women in Kenya and Africa generally have for eons spent alot of time gathering firewood for their cooking, needless to say, this is not only detrimental to the environment due to deforestation and air pollution but also not sustainable because of the reducing forest cover across Africa and the world generally. Additionally, firewood poses serious medical threats in terms of respiratory, cardiovascular issues, carbon monoxide poisoning and eye problems occassioned by the smoke from the firewood. These medical issues also lead to an increase in medical expenses on funds which are already too limited to meet daily survival.
Solution Overview:
The solution to the above above is as detailed below: 
Most women in rural communities in Kenya have livestock which they rear for milk, meat, leather and sale. The solution works by providing women in the rural areas of Kenya with bio-digesters for the production of biogas from animal waste with a specific emphasis on cow dung. Cow dung is in most rural communities treated as waste and dumped, used as organic manure on crops or used for smearing on house walls for its aesthetic value (it is an African thing). The biogas produced from the bio digestors shall first and foremost be used by the household for their own domestic consumption and any excess production will be collected in storage facility located within the homestead for collection, transportation to a compression facility and packaging to be sold to urban area dwellers for their own use as fuel.  Since a single homestead may not be able to produce the biogas in commercially viable quantities, the project foresees the inclusion of multiple households into the programme and their organisation in to a biogas producing co-operative where each household/woman members shall be paid according to the volume of biogas that is collected from their homestead for a given period of time, usually a month. The bio digestors and storage facilities for the homestead shall initially be provided to the households free of charge, but their cost shall be recouped from the revenues accruing to the households from the sale of biogas sold by them. The membership to the biogas production and selling co-operative shall be restricted to only women. This solution shall save the women from spending too much time collecting firewood, eliminate the medical problems associated with the firewood and at the same time provide them with an income. Additionally, this solution will create a positive footmark by reducing deforestation for firewood. An app shall be developed and utilised to monitor the gas production and capacities in the storage tanks and report on any problems in the systems at the homesteads. This app shall inform when corrective action needs to be taken and when collection of the gas is necessary. 
 
Methodologies and Technologies used
Biogas production is based on anaerobic digestion, where biomass is broken down in the absence of oxygen to produce methane rich gas. The primary feedstock for this solution shall be domestic animal droppings with an emphasis on cow dung. A biodigestor tank shall be provided to each of the households in the programme accompanied by a storage facility in which excess biogas shall be stored. The excess biogas shall be collected on a fixed interval for transportation to a central purification, compression and storage facility. In this facility the gas shall be purified, compressed and packaged in gas cylinders for sale to urban dwellers for use in their cooking requirements. A percentage of the net sales proceeds shall be remitted to the members of the co-operative via mobile money. The gas may also be sold to factories which require fire to undertake their activities. 

Partnerships and Collaboration 
For this solution there shall be need to first of all partner with the women in rural areas who have livestock especially cows, county/local and central governments in Kenya and across Africa, non-governmental organisations, relevant United Nations entities, International Finance Corporation, among many other organisations who maybe interested in clean energy.
Solution Provider(s): 1. Denis Kamau Muthoni, Senior Lecturer of Supply Chain Management and Director, Board of Postgraduate Studies of the The Co-operative University of Kenya Qualifications: PhD in Supply Chain Management, Master’s in Procurement and Logistics, Bachelor’s in Economics and Business Studies, 2. Professor Peter Kinyanjui, PhD. Biochemistry/Molecular Biology, York University, Toronto, Canada. MSc Biochemistry, University of London. BSc. Second Class Honors (Upper Division) Biochemistry/Entomology, University of Nairobi. 3. Ezra Opande,  Qualifications: Software Engineering, ALX Experience: 10+ Years
Duration to pilot in a new geography: One (1) year
SDGs addressed: SDG 7 (Affordable and Clean Energy);SDG 1 (No Poverty);SDG 13 (Climate Action);
Desired impact:
The objectives of this solution are: 
1. To promote the use of clean energy in rural Kenya and Africa. 
2. To provide women in rural Kenya with a sustainable source of income.
3. To reduce deforestation occasioned by use of trees as firewood.
4. To reduce the negative medical effects of use of firewood.
5. To provide women in rural areas with an opportunity to spend their time more productively instead of using it searching for firewood. 
6. To bring women in rural areas under the umbrella of a co-operative for the sale of biogas which they can use to improve the social economic status. 

The targeted achievements of this solution are: 
1. By the end of the first year to recruit over 1,000,000 households into the programme.
2. By the end of the first year to produce at least 1000 tonnes of biogas for domestic use and sale.
Key technologies:
Block chain technology shall be utilised to monitor the gas production and capacities in the storage tanks and report on any problems in the systems at the home steads 

Plastic drum digestors shall be used for the production of the biogas, while balloon bag storage tanks shall be used for storage of the excess biogas in the homesteads.
Unique Characteristics:
The most unique characteristic of this solution are: 
1. The solution utilises animal waste especially cow dung to generate fuel for use in cooking and sale which has for centuries been dumped, used as organic fertilizer or as beautifier for earthen walls
2. The solution organises the homesteads into co-operatives which ensures that their individual productions when aggregated become commercially viable. This maybe the first co-operative in the world dedicated to the production of biogas for both domestic use and sale. 
3. The solution provides the benefits of eliminating the medical problems associated with use of firewood and also creates an environment where it reduces deforestation simultaneously. 
4. The solution frees up the time used in searching for firewood to be used in more productive activities.
Sustainable Change: The solution contribute to a sustainable systemic change by making use of clean energy thereby conserving the environment by reducing deforestation and also provides a sustainable income to the women in rural areas since as long as they have a cow or cows they will produce biogas which they use at home and also get to sell.
Funding Sources: Not funded.
Testimonials and Endorsements: None.
Primary thematic focus area: MSME Empowerment & Local Digital Innovation
Summary: This project empowers women in rural Kenya by providing biogas production systems using cow dung, offering both domestic use and income generation opportunities through the sale of excess biogas. While the model is innovative and environmentally sustainable, its scalability and long-term sustainability will depend on securing funding and partnerships for wider implementation.

Title: Rescam – AI-Powered Scam-Baiting Intelligence System
Subtitle: Turning the tables on scammers through automated engagement and intelligence gathering to protect vulnerable communities at rescam.org.nz
Problem Statement: Scams are a global epidemic costing individuals and businesses billions annually, disproportionately impacting vulnerable and digitally underserved communities. Traditional awareness campaigns struggle to keep pace with scammers’ evolving tactics, leaving individuals exposed and unable to detect or report fraudulent approaches effectively.
Solution Overview:
Rescam is an innovative scam-baiting and intelligence system developed by Netsafe to disrupt online fraud at scale. It works by engaging scammers in realistic, automated email conversations that waste their time, divert them from targeting real victims, and gather critical intelligence about scam operations.

Using natural language processing and AI-driven personas, Rescam replies convincingly to scam emails submitted by the public. As scammers respond, their language, tactics, and infrastructure are mapped and analysed. This intelligence informs public awareness campaigns, strengthens law enforcement efforts, and contributes to global scam-prevention databases.

The platform’s methodology includes:
	•	AI persona-based engagement engines trained on scam communication patterns.
	•	Automated conversation threading to maximise scammer time-wasting without human intervention.
	•	Secure storage and analysis of scammer emails, domains, and tactics for actionable insights.
	•	Public-facing submission portal at rescam.org.nz enabling anyone to forward suspected scams.

Partnership and collaboration models:
	•	Public participation – anyone can forward scams for the system to engage with.
	•	Law enforcement cooperation – insights shared with agencies combating cybercrime.
	•	International knowledge sharing – data shared with global anti-fraud networks.
	•	Academic collaboration – scam dataset access for research into fraud prevention.
Solution Provider(s): Standard Security NGO, 501 Charity,
Implementation timeline(s): Prototype in 2017, AI enabled and tested 2023, launched at scale in New Zealand in 2024 and now online
Duration to pilot in a new geography: 3-6 months
SDGs addressed: SDG 16 (Peace, Justice, and Strong Institutions);SDG 9 (Industry, Innovation, and Infrastructure);SDG 8 (Decent Work and Economic Growth);
Desired impact:
Solution Objectives:
	•	Reduce the economic and emotional harm caused by online scams by intercepting and disrupting scam operations before they reach victims.
	•	Generate actionable intelligence to strengthen law enforcement and global anti-fraud efforts.
	•	Empower individuals worldwide to actively contribute to the fight against online fraud by forwarding scam emails to Rescam.

Key Achievements / Impacts:
	•	Engaged with scammers in millions of automated conversations since launch, wasting thousands of scammer hours.
	•	Poised to disrupt  fraudulent operations targeting vulnerable communities and small businesses.
	•	able to share scam intelligence with global partners, improving the speed and accuracy of scam detection.
	•	Raised public awareness through media coverage in over 100 countries, increasing scam recognition rates among internet users.
Key technologies:
Artificial Intelligence (AI) – NLP-driven persona conversations trained on scammer linguistic patterns.
	•	Automation & Workflow Engines – to process public submissions, initiate scam-baiting responses, and manage conversation flow without human intervention.
	•	Data Analytics – for scam trend identification, metadata extraction, and infrastructure mapping.
	•	Cloud-based Systems – for secure and scalable global engagement.
Unique Characteristics:
Scalable Disruption – Rescam is one of the first public-facing, AI-driven scam-baiting systems capable of handling thousands of concurrent conversations.
	•	Crowdsourced Participation – anyone can contribute simply by forwarding scam emails.
	•	Dual Impact Model – combines real-time disruption of scammer operations with intelligence gathering for prevention and prosecution.
	•	Humour-Infused Engagement – unique AI personas use wit and absurdity to prolong scammer engagement, adding a psychological deterrent.
	•	Nonprofit-led Initiative – driven by a mission-focused organisation (Netsafe), not a commercial enterprise, ensuring public benefit over profit.
Sustainable Change:
Theory of Change:
	•	Short-term – Reduce the immediate harm from scams by wasting scammers’ operational time and diverting them from real targets.
	•	Medium-term – Build a comprehensive database of scammer tactics and infrastructure, enabling faster global detection and disruption.
	•	Long-term – Foster a more scam-aware global citizenry and strengthen cross-border cooperation against cyber-enabled fraud, leading to reduced scam prevalence and increased trust in digital systems.

The systemic change comes from creating a self-sustaining loop: public participation feeds scam data → AI disrupts scammers and produces intelligence → intelligence informs prevention, prosecution, and education → more people join the effort → scammers’ cost of operating increases, reducing profitability and prevalence.
Funding Sources: Rescam was initially funded through Netsafe’s operational budget with support from public donations.   In-kind technical support from partner Standard Security. Additional support has come from international collaborations, pro bono media promotion, and charitable donations to Netsafe.
Testimonials and Endorsements:
The Investigators NZ

“This innovative tool is a simple yet clever way for the public to turn scam emails into a weapon against the very criminals trying to trick them.”
— The Investigators, June 2024 (theinvestigators.co.nz)

Best Awards Judges (Re:Scam 2.0 entry)

“A brilliant example of using creativity and AI to protect people, while making it entertaining to fight back. Re:Scam 2.0 shows how tech can serve the public good at scale.”
— Best Awards 2024 entry feedback (bestawards.co.nz)
Primary thematic focus area: Inclusive Digital Innovation Skills & Entrepreneurial Talent Development
Summary: Rescam is an AI-driven scam-baiting platform developed by Netsafe to disrupt online fraud by engaging scammers in automated conversations, gathering critical intelligence, and protecting vulnerable communities. The platform uses AI personas, NLP, and automation to waste scammers' time and contribute to global anti-fraud efforts.

Title: Teriya Market
Subtitle: Teriya Market empowers farmers, youth, and women-led businesses with AI-driven tools for market access, finance, and growth across the Global South.
Problem Statement:
In many countries of the Global South, small agriculture producers and informal businesses are Excluded from global trade due to low digital access and poor platform fragmentation
Smallholder farmers, women, and youth-led businesses often lack digital skills, trust in online systems, and access to digital payments and logistics.
Solution Overview:
Teriya Market is a digital platform that helps smallholder farmers, women, and youth-led businesses across the Global South sell their products, access financial tools, and get business insights.

It works as a web based, mobile-friendly marketplace where users can list products, find new buyers, and receive payments. It also provides tools to help users set prices, plan logistics, and improve their sales using market insights from AI based analyses.

Additionally, local partners such as SOVIECAP International and Ireme Green Innovation Hub provide mentorship and capacity-building support to ensure users can fully leverage the platform for sustainable business growth.
They train Women and Youth in agriculture to take advantage of the platform and increase the sales of their products. They also provide technical support in rural areas, including product registration and management assistance.
Solution Provider(s): 1. Teriya Management Inc.: A US Based company specializing in AI and Data-driven solutions, 2.SOVIECAP International: A Social enterprise Based in Burkina Faso specializing in inclusive youth mentorship across West Africa, 3 Ireme Green Innovation Hub: A Rwanda-Based company specializing in inclusive youth mentorship and community empowerment across Eastern Africa.

Duration to pilot in a new geography: Six (06) months
SDGs addressed: SDG 1 (No Poverty);SDG 10 (Reduced Inequalities);SDG 2 (Zero Hunger);

Our Objectives:

1. Facilitate market access for smallholder farmers, women, and youth-led businesses across the Global South through a digital platform that connects them with local and international buyers.
2. Promote economic inclusion by providing tools, training, and financial integration for marginalized communities with limited access to digital markets.
3. Strengthen food systems and reduce inequality by improving the visibility, pricing power, and sustainability of rural producers.
4. Lay the groundwork for South–South trade by enabling cross-border product visibility and trade linkages within the Global South.

5. 200+ products registered across agricultural, craft, and processed goods, creating visibility for producers in more than 3+ countries.

Artificial Intelligence:
We use Artificial Intelligence to support our local partners for farmers, women, and youth training. 

Cloud Computing:
The platform runs on secure and scalable cloud services, which helps us grow and reach more countries.

Our approach is different because we put women and young people first, build communities from the ground up, and have tech that can grow with us.

Title: Responsible Generative AI for Inclusive Technical Education in Sub-Saharan Africa
Subtitle: Leveraging Generative AI to empower inclusive technical education and entrepreneurship in Sub-Saharan Africa through university incubation programs.
Problem Statement:
Technical and vocational education in Sub-Saharan Africa faces significant challenges in delivering quality, inclusive, and relevant training. Many TVET institutions have limited access to up-to-date digital learning tools, resources, and high-quality course materials. Students and instructors struggle to design or access tailored content that meets diverse learning needs, which limits skills development, employability, and entrepreneurship opportunities. Women, youth, and marginalized communities are particularly disadvantaged, often lacking equal access to learning opportunities and digital technologies. Traditional curriculum development processes are slow, resource-intensive, and unable to respond quickly to evolving industry demands, further widening the skills gap.

This situation hinders the ability of TVET institutions to equip learners with the competencies required for the modern workforce and to foster locally-driven innovation and entrepreneurship. There is a critical need for inclusive, scalable, and responsible AI-driven solutions that can support content creation, enhance personalized learning experiences, and ensure equitable access for all learners. By integrating AI tools into incubation programs and education ecosystems, institutions can bridge the educational gap, accelerate skills acquisition, and empower underserved communities, ultimately contributing to a more inclusive and resilient digital economy in the region.
Solution Overview:
Our solution, Responsible Generative AI for Inclusive Technical Education in Sub-Saharan Africa, leverages AI-powered tools to enhance TVET learning, skills development, and entrepreneurship through university-led incubation programs. Generative AI produces interactive learning materials, technical guides, simulations, and exercises tailored to diverse learner needs in mechanical, electrical, and IT domains. Personalized learning pathways adapt content based on skill levels, preferences, and progress, enabling self-paced, competency-based learning. The AI tools are embedded into incubation programs, supporting student-led startups and MSMEs to access digital resources, prototype solutions, and develop entrepreneurial skills. Ethical and inclusive AI practices ensure content is contextually relevant, accessible, and aligned with local education standards.

The solution combines Generative AI, NLP, adaptive learning algorithms, and digital collaboration platforms to create an inclusive and scalable education ecosystem. Key partnerships include Jimma University Innovation Incubation Center (JUIIC) as the host, local TVET institutions for pilots, industry partners for mentorship and tools, and UNIDO/UNCTAD/ODET for technical support, funding, and global visibility. This approach is fully replicable across Sub-Saharan Africa, bridging the skills gap, empowering underserved communities especially women and youth and fostering inclusive digital entrepreneurship.
Solution Provider(s): Jimma University Innovation Incubation Center (JUIIC) : Host organization; provides incubation programs, entrepreneurship support, and innovation ecosystem development for students, youth, and MSMEs in Ethiopia; Sector: Education, Innovation, Entrepreneurship.  Jimma University, College of Technology : Academic partner; provides technical expertise in mechanical, electrical, and IT education; Sector: Higher Education, Technical Education.  Local TVET Institutions in Sub-Saharan Africa: Pilot and implementation partners; provide vocational training programs and learner access for AI-driven content integration; Sector: Technical and Vocational Education.  Industry Partners :  Companies providing mentorship, access to AI tools, digital infrastructure, and market linkages for student startups;  UNIDO (United Nations Industrial Development Organization) : Provides technical support, funding opportunities, and visibility on international platforms;  ODET (UN Office for Digital and Emerging Technologies) : supports AI integration, responsible technology adoption, and capacity building;
Duration to pilot in a new geography: 12 months
SDGs addressed: SDG 17 (Partnerships for the Goals);SDG 4 (Quality Education);SDG 10 (Reduced Inequalities);
Desired impact: The solution aims to empower women, youth, and marginalized communities in Sub-Saharan Africa by enhancing technical and digital skills through AI-driven learning, improving the quality and accessibility of TVET education, and fostering entrepreneurship via university incubation programs. Expected impacts include measurable skills development in mechanical, electrical, and IT domains, increased participation of underserved learners (targeting 40–50%), the creation of 10–15 new student-led startups or MSMEs during the pilot phase, and the development of scalable AI-powered learning modules and incubation models that can be replicated across the region. By promoting responsible and inclusive AI adoption, the solution strengthens local capacities, supports equitable access to digital tools, and contributes to building inclusive, resilient, and sustainable digital economies, aligned with the SDGs.
Key technologies: The solution leverages Generative AI and Natural Language Processing (NLP) to create interactive, personalized learning materials, simulations, and technical guides for TVET students. Adaptive learning algorithms tailor content to individual learner needs, supporting competency-based education. Virtual Reality (VR) and Augmented Reality (AR) are integrated to provide immersive, hands-on training experiences, enhancing understanding of complex technical concepts. Digital collaboration platforms enable mentorship, knowledge sharing, and engagement within incubation programs, while data analytics and monitoring tools track learner performance and program outcomes. Together, these technologies create an inclusive, scalable, and responsible AI-driven educational ecosystem, bridging skills gaps and fostering entrepreneurship in Sub-Saharan Africa.
Unique Characteristics: The solution is unique in its integration of Generative AI, VR, and AR technologies to create immersive, personalized, and interactive learning experiences for TVET students, a first in many Sub-Saharan African contexts. Unlike traditional curriculum development, the solution is scalable, adaptive, and rapidly deployable, allowing tailored content for diverse learners, including women, youth, and marginalized groups. Its integration with university-led incubation programs connects skills development directly to entrepreneurship, fostering MSME creation and local innovation ecosystems. The solution also employs a responsible and inclusive AI approach, ensuring ethical, transparent, and contextually relevant use of technology. Additionally, the partnership model—linking academic institutions, TVETs, industry, and UN organizations—enables knowledge sharing, mentorship, and access to global platforms, providing both technical and financial support. This combination of cutting-edge technology, inclusive design, and ecosystem-based implementation differentiates it from conventional technical education solutions.
Sustainable Change: The solution fosters sustainable, systemic change by transforming technical education and incubation ecosystems in Sub-Saharan Africa. By providing AI-driven, VR/AR-enhanced, and personalized learning, it equips learners with high-demand technical skills and promotes entrepreneurship and MSME creation, directly addressing the regional skills gap. As trained students and startups apply these skills, they generate local innovation, economic growth, and job creation, particularly for women, youth, and marginalized communities. The integration of incubation programs with digital tools ensures long-term capacity building, enabling institutions to continuously update curricula and adopt new technologies. Through partnerships with academic institutions, industry, and UN agencies, knowledge, mentorship, and best practices are shared widely, making the approach replicable and scalable across the region. The desired follow-on effects include an inclusive and resilient digital economy, increased employability, strengthened local innovation ecosystems, and equitable access to technical education, contributing to the SDGs and leaving a lasting, systemic impact.

Title: Système informatiser de gestion scolaire "Impacter votre école sans crainte".
Subtitle: logiciel de gestion scolaire IV-SCOOL" impacter votre école sans crainte"
Problem Statement:
Dans un monde de plus en plus numérisé, la transformation digitale du secteur éducatif devient une nécessité pour garantir une éducation de qualité, inclusive et adaptée aux réalités du XXIe siècle. À Goma, comme dans plusieurs autres villes de la République Démocratique du Congo, les établissements scolaires fonctionnent encore majoritairement selon des méthodes traditionnelles de gestion, reposant sur des documents papier, des registres manuels et des processus administratifs longs, souvent sujets aux erreurs, aux pertes d’informations et à une faible traçabilité.
Ce mode de fonctionnement limite l’efficacité des services scolaires, tant sur le plan administratif que pédagogique. Il engendre des retards dans la communication, complique le suivi des élèves, freine la planification pédagogique, et rend difficile l’analyse fiable des données scolaires (telles que les résultats, la fréquentation, les besoins en formation ou les évaluations de performance). Par ailleurs, l’absence de systèmes numériques intégrés freine l’innovation pédagogique, limite l’interactivité entre enseignants, élèves et parents, et rend les écoles moins résilientes face aux situations de crise comme les conflits ou les pandémies.
Face à ces défis, le projet de numérisation du système de gestion administrative et pédagogique dans les écoles de Goma se veut une réponse concrète et durable. Il vise à moderniser le fonctionnement des établissements scolaires par l’introduction d’outils numériques, de plateformes de gestion scolaire, et de bases de données centralisées. L'objectif est de renforcer la gouvernance scolaire, d'améliorer la qualité de l'enseignement en fournissant des manuels scolaires adaptés à chaque niveau et mettre en place des laboratoires informatiques à la pointe de la technologie moderne adapté aux écoles primaires et secondaire, de faciliter l'accès à l'information et de créer un écosystème éducatif plus transparent, efficace et résilient.
Ce projet s’inscrit également dans la vision nationale d’un système éducatif performant, aligné sur les Objectifs de Développement Durable (ODD), notamment l’ODD 4 qui prône une éducation de qualité pour tous. Il ambitionne enfin de favoriser l’inclusion numérique, en réduisant la fracture technologique entre les écoles publiques et privées, urbaines et périphériques, tout en renforçant les capacités des acteurs éducatifs à utiliser les TIC à bon escient.
Solution Overview:
La ville de Goma, capitale de la province du Nord-Kivu en République Démocratique du Congo, fait face à de nombreux défis socio-éducatifs liés à son contexte géopolitique instable, à la croissance rapide de sa population scolaire et à la faiblesse des infrastructures éducatives. Le système éducatif y demeure largement dépendant de procédés manuels, avec des écoles qui peinent à assurer une gestion administrative et pédagogique efficace, transparente et adaptée aux exigences contemporaines.
Dans la majorité des établissements scolaires de Goma, les dossiers des élèves, les relevés de notes, les bulletins, les plannings de cours, les rapports d’inspection, ainsi que les archives administratives sont tenus de manière manuelle, sur support papier. Ce mode de gestion entraîne non seulement une surcharge de travail pour les équipes administratives, mais aussi des risques élevés de perte ou de falsification de données, une lenteur dans le traitement des informations, et un accès limité ou inexistant aux statistiques fiables pour orienter la prise de décision.
Par ailleurs, dans une ville confrontée à des crises récurrentes (conflits armés, déplacements de populations, épidémies, éruption volcanique, etc.), l’absence d’un système numérique résilient limite considérablement la continuité pédagogique et le suivi efficace des apprenants, notamment ceux en situation de vulnérabilité.

La numérisation du système de gestion scolaire apparaît donc comme une réponse stratégique et innovante face à ces enjeux. Elle permettra :
•	D’améliorer la gestion des données scolaires (informations sur les élèves, les enseignants, les présences, les notes, les décisions administratives, etc.) 
•	De renforcer la transparence et la traçabilité dans la gestion des écoles.
•	De faciliter le suivi pédagogique individualisé des élèves, y compris ceux déplacés ou ayant changé d’établissement.
•	De favoriser une meilleure communication entre les directions d’écoles, les enseignants, les parents et les autorités éducatives.
•	D’encourager l’intégration des TIC dans l’enseignement, en préparant progressivement les écoles à une transformation pédagogique plus large.
•	Mettre en place un laboratoire au standard international pour les séances pratiques des élèves et la formation continue des enseignants.

Ce projet s’inscrit dans une volonté de modernisation du système éducatif local, en lien avec les priorités nationales en matière d’éducation, les politiques provinciales du Nord-Kivu, et les engagements internationaux pour une éducation inclusive, équitable et de qualité

Suite à ce défit, impact-asbl à développer une solution web ( logiciel scolaire ) en utilisant des nouvelles technologie stacks: react, Laravel.

IV-SCOOL : est une application à la fois simple et complète conçue pour faciliter la gestion efficace des activités d’enseignement Primaire, secondaire et professionnel.
Ce logiciel offre une solution tout-en-un avec des fonctionnalités adaptables aux besoins spécifiques des départements en fonction de leurs domaines d’expertise.
IV-SCOOL  permet de centraliser, au sein d’une interface unique, l’ensemble des aspects liés à la gestion d’une institution. En ce qui concerne la gestion des élèves, elle propose un service d’inscription en ligne et en présentiel permettant de suivre les demandes en temps réel. Du côté de la gestion du personnel enseignant et des intervenants, IV-SCOOL  offre un service de suivi pédagogique regroupant toutes les informations nécessaires sur les plans de cours, les synthèses, les feuilles de présence, les évaluations et les emplois du temps
IV-SCOOL  facilite les mouvements de paiement des élèves et le contrôles.

Desired impact: Contribuer à l'amélioration de la qualité de l’éducation dans la ville de Goma par la modernisation, la digitalisation et l’optimisation des systèmes de gestion administrative et pédagogique au sein des établissements scolaires.

stacks: react, Laravel
base des données: mysql

Sustainable Change:
La pertinence de ce projet repose sur le besoin urgent de moderniser les systèmes éducatifs pour les rendre plus efficaces, transparents et résilients, particulièrement dans des contextes fragiles comme celui de Goma. Le recours aux outils numériques dans la gestion scolaire s’impose aujourd’hui comme un levier fondamental pour améliorer la qualité de l’éducation, optimiser la gestion administrative et renforcer la gouvernance dans les établissements.
Dans la ville de Goma, où de nombreuses écoles sont confrontées à des difficultés liées à la surcharge des effectifs, à l’insuffisance d’infrastructures, à la mobilité fréquente des élèves et à l’instabilité socio-politique, la numérisation permettra d’assurer un suivi rigoureux et permanent des données scolaires. Elle facilitera également la centralisation des informations, la génération automatisée des bulletins et rapports, la gestion des absences, et une meilleure communication entre les parties prenantes (direction, enseignants, parents, autorités éducatives).
De plus, ce projet contribue directement à la réduction des inégalités d’accès à l’information, à l’amélioration des performances scolaires, et à la mise en œuvre progressive de la digitalisation du système éducatif congolais, conformément aux orientations du Ministère de l’EPST et aux Objectifs de Développement Durable (ODD), notamment l’ODD 4.

Notre solution apporte un changement durable en rassemblant toutes les données de l’école au même endroit, en rendant la gestion plus claire et transparente. Elle aide la direction à mieux décider grâce à des informations fiables et crée une culture numérique simple et utile, que d’autres écoles peuvent aussi adopter.

Title: MASOCs: Empowering Local Communities and Small Business in Cyber Resilience
Subtitle: A scalable network of local cyber centres to monitor, alert, and build safety & digital resilience in communities to protect assets & infrastructure. They uplift women, youth & marginalized groups.
Problem Statement:
The MASOCs solution addresses several key challenges for small businesses and individuals:
* Financial, digital and technical literacy
* Increasing success in cyber threats targeting capacity and monies from community small businesses and those involved in critical infrastructure.
* Lack of foundational skills in cyber safety and digital responsibility in local workforces.
* Insufficient resilience to digital disruptions within communities.
* The need for fundamental, practical and globally recognised training to build local capacity for cyber protection and response.

MASOCs are designed to empower women, youth, and marginalized groups by providing inclusive digital learning and micro-credentials, building essential cyber safety and resilience skills at the community level - teaching new skills and supporting their local communities. 


The MASOCs Powered by HEULDINS solution aligns with several United Nations Sustainable Development Goals (SDGs):
• Goal 4: Quality Education – By providing accessible, scalable and nationally recognised micro-credentials and digital learning opportunities, MASOCs enhance foundational cyber skills and lifelong learning.
• Goal 8: Decent Work and Economic Growth – The initiative supports small and micro businesses and boosts local employability in cybersecurity, fostering inclusive economic participation and sustainable growth.
• Goal 9: Industry, Innovation, and Infrastructure – MASOCs build resilient behaviours and promotes innovative and secure digital solutions for small businesses and critical infrastructure sectors.
• Goal 10: Reduced Inequalities – By focusing on digital inclusion and community-driven upskilling, particularly for women, youth and marginalized groups, MASOCs work to narrow the digital divide.
• Goal 16: Peace, Justice, and Strong Institutions – Strengthening community and national cyber resilience contributes to safer, more secure institutions and societies.
• Goal 11: Sustainable Cities and Communities - enables a master-planned area social opportunity centre (MASOC) to foster inclusive, resilient, and sustainable communities by integrating accessible facilities, green spaces, affordable services, and economic opportunities.
Solution Overview:
MASOCs establish a nationwide tapestry of scalable Monitoring & Alert Security Operations Centres dedicated to local small businesses. These centres provide continuous cyber threat monitoring, rapid alerts, and expert guidance tailored to local needs. The program delivers immediate data on emerging trends and threats, and also delivers a nationally recognised micro-credential based on the Critical Energy Infrastructure Cyber Resilience framework. This micro-credential equips local workers with foundational skills in cyber safety, digital responsibility, and infrastructure resilience, creating a more secure business environment and stronger, digitally resilient communities. It allows women, youth, and marginalized groups the opportunity to develop inclusive lay-person baseline digital learning and micro-credentials, building essential cyber safety and resilience skills at the community level. These new skills support local communities.  

Methodologies and Technologies Used: 
• Centralised Monitoring: MASOCs deploy scalable, real-time cyber threat detection and alert systems, leveraging Security Operations Centre best practices.
• Micro-Credential Training: By aligning learnings to focus on foundational skills in cyber safety, digital awareness, and operational resilience.
• Digital Learning Platforms: Accessible, user-friendly e-learning technologies ensure small businesses and community members can engage in upskilling regardless of size and location.
• Community-Focused Model: “Locals helping locals” empowers communities to support and reinforce cyber resilience together.
• Scalable Architecture: Cloud-based infrastructure supports rapid scaling and tailored deployment across different regions.

Partnerships and Collaboration Models:
• Industry Collaboration: The program is developed in partnership with Energy Skills Limited and local businesses to ensure relevance and practicality.
• Local Workforce Engagement: By involving community members, including women, youth, and marginalized groups, MASOCs builds a diverse tapestry of awareness and talent for ongoing cyber resilience.
• Training and Education Partners: Collaboration with education and training providers ensures the micro-credential is nationally recognised and of the highest quality.
• Public-Private Partnership: MASOCs encourages participation from government, industry associations, and critical infrastructure operators for sustainable implementation and long-term impact.
