Title: Online Wildlife Permitting and Management System (OWPMS)
Subtitle: Digitizing wildlife permits to empower communities, improve governance, and conserve biodiversity.
Problem Statement: Wildlife permit processes in the Philippines are traditionally paper-based, slow, and fragmented. This delays economic opportunities for small permittee farmers and hinders effective biodiversity monitoring. The lack of digital systems reduces transparency, increases compliance risks, and limits the government’s ability to track species movement for conservation.
Solution Overview: The OWPMS digitizes the entire permitting process—from application to approval and release of wildlife permits—through an online platform. Built with different web technologies, and conforms with ISO/IEC 25010 standards, it streamlines workflows, enables real-time species tracking, ensures transparency, and generates analytics for decision-making
Solution Provider(s): Marinduque State University – College of Information and Computing Sciences (CICS), Department of Environment and Natural Resources – Provincial Environment and Natural Resources Office (DENR–PENRO) Marinduque
Implementation timeline(s): Development: May 2024 – July 2025. Pilot Deployment: Ongoing
Duration to pilot in a new geography: 3–6 months (including customization, training, and system integration)
SDGs addressed: SDG 8 (Decent Work and Economic Growth);SDG 15 (Life on Land);SDG 9 (Industry, Innovation, and Infrastructure);
Desired impact:
Empower 100+ community butterfly farmers (permittees) with faster, transparent digital permitting.
Improve biodiversity conservation through traceable monitoring of 300+ butterfly species in Marinduque.
Reduce permit processing times by up to 70%.
Strengthen local governance through compliance with RA 11032 (Ease of Doing Business) and other Local ordinances.
Key technologies:
Web Technologies (Laravel Framework, MYSQL, HTML, CSS)
Machine Learning Algorithms (Regression & Clustering) 
SO/IEC 25010:2011 standards for quality and security evaluation
Unique Characteristics:
Biodiversity-focused e-permitting platform.
Co-designed with local government and community stakeholders.
Integrates conservation compliance with livelihood support.
QR code–enabled permits for traceability and authenticity.
Sustainable Change: OWPMS creates systemic change by digitizing governance processes, ensuring transparency, and promoting digital inclusion for MSMEs. By linking economic livelihoods with biodiversity protection, it strengthens resilience and builds a replicable model for other provinces and sectors. The solution lays the groundwork for scaling e-governance innovations nationwide.
Funding Sources: Initially funded through a partnership between Marinduque State University (MarSU) and the Department of Environment and Natural Resources – Provincial Environment and Natural Resources Office (DENR–PENRO) Marinduque
Testimonials and Endorsements: with the help of OWPMS, permit processing is faster and more transparent. I don't no longer need to travel multiple times to DENR for signatures, everything is traceable online. - translated from the original testimonial. - "Salamat sa OWPMS, mas mabilis at mas malinaw ang proseso ng pag kuha ng permit. Hindi ko na kailangang bumiyahe ng pabalik-balik sa DENR para sa mga pirma at iba pa. Pwde din pla makita ang applikasyon sa interet"
Primary thematic focus area: Enabling Policies & Regulatory Innovation
Summary: The OWPMS aims to modernize the wildlife permitting process in Marinduque, Philippines, by digitizing it to improve efficiency, transparency, and governance. The platform’s integration of species tracking and permit management is an innovative approach to conservation and livelihood support for local farmers. However, its scalability and sustainability depend on successful pilot implementation and broader adoption by local governments and communities.

Title: Digital Agripreneurship for Youth and Women in Poultry and Horticulture
Subtitle: Empowering youth and women in Kenya with digital skills, IoT-enabled farming, and entrepreneurship for resilient agribusiness livelihoods.
Problem Statement: Rural youth and women in Laikipia and Nyandarua face high unemployment, limited access to modern farming techniques, and low market competitiveness. Traditional poultry and horticulture methods often yield inconsistent results due to climate variability, poor record-keeping, and limited market access. Without digital skills, local farmers struggle to optimize production, track performance, and connect to broader markets. This limits their income potential and perpetuates poverty.
Solution Overview:
Hope Valley Family Institute proposes a pilot program that integrates digital agribusiness training, life skills, and entrepreneurship for youth and women in Laikipia and neighboring counties.
The solution combines:
- Mobile-based learning for agribusiness best practices and market trends.
- IoT-enabled monitoring of poultry and horticulture production (e.g., automated feeders, climate and soil sensors).
- Digital record-keeping tools to track costs, yields, and sales.
- Digital incubators for efficient poultry hatching.
- Entrepreneurship and cooperative formation to strengthen market access.
Solution Provider(s): Partnerships with local agribusiness companies will provide market linkages, while our NGO savings model will offer small-scale financing to kickstart farming ventures.
Implementation location(s): Kenya – Laikipia County and Nyandarua county
Implementation timeline(s): Not applicable (pilot not yet started; proposed start upon funding approval)
Duration to pilot in a new geography: 12 months
SDGs addressed: SDG 2 (Zero Hunger);SDG 1 (No Poverty);SDG 3 (Good Health and Well-being);
Desired impact:
Solution Objectives:
- Through innovation and knowledge sharing, equip youth and women with digital agribusiness skills and entrepreneurship knowledge.
- Do away with hunger by increasing local food production efficiency and quality in poultry and horticulture.
- Improve household incomes and food security through market access and cooperative selling.
- Enhance resilience against climate-related agricultural challenges via IoT-enabled monitoring.

Key Achievements (expected):
- 70% of participants adopt digital record-keeping within 6 months.
- 50% increase in poultry and horticulture yields by year-end.
- Formation of at least 5 farmer cooperatives linked to national agribusiness markets.
Key technologies:
- Mobile-based learning platforms
- IoT sensors for climate and soil monitoring
- Digital record-keeping applications
- Automated poultry incubators and feeders
Unique Characteristics:
- Combines digital skills, agribusiness training, and entrepreneurship into one integrated program.
- Uses IoT and digital incubation technology to increase productivity.
- Targets both economic empowerment and gender equality by prioritizing women and youth.
- Embeds life skills to ensure sustainable livelihood adoption.
Sustainable Change:
Our Theory of Change is based on the belief that digitally skilled farmers become economically resilient entrepreneurs.
The program will create systemic change by:
- Establishing cooperatives that ensure long-term market access.
- Strengthening local value chains for poultry and horticulture.
- Partnering with agribusiness companies for ongoing technical support and bulk purchasing opportunities.
- Using NGO savings to provide seed capital for new ventures.
Funding Sources:
The proposed solution has not yet received direct donor funding. However, Hope Valley Family Institute has leveraged:

-Internal resources through the NGO’s savings and microfinance support model to pilot small-scale agribusiness activities with local farmers.

-Community contributions in kind (land, labor, and participation in training workshops).

-Partnerships with local agribusiness suppliers, who have provided discounted farm inputs and technical advice during initial concept testing.

We are now seeking catalytic grant support to scale this pilot into a structured, technology-enabled program.

Title: RISE Initiative: Driving Inclusive Industrial Transformation
Subtitle: RISE (Resource Integration for Sectoral Excellence) Initiative is a digital ecosystem empowering MSMEs in Ethiopia with real-time data, market linkages, and skills to achieve global competitiveness.
Problem Statement: Ethiopia’s manufacturing sector, despite vast potential, is constrained by fragmented systems, poor resource optimization, limited technology adoption, and insufficient market access for MSMEs. Women- and youth-led enterprises, which make up the majority of MSMEs, remain excluded from advanced tools and global value chains. This perpetuates inefficiency, lost competitiveness, and missed opportunities for industrial growth, job creation, and poverty reduction.
Solution Overview:
The RISE Initiative addresses these gaps by creating a centralized digital ecosystem that integrates resources, accelerates digital adoption, and empowers MSMEs to thrive.
- Centralized Resource Integration: A cloud-based platform that connects MSMEs, institutes, and industries via ERP integration to reduce duplication and optimize resources
- AI-Enabled Analytics & Forecasting: Advanced dashboards provide MSMEs with real-time insights into production, demand forecasting, and sustainability performance.
- Capacity Building & Skills Development: Training programs for MSMEs, women, and youth entrepreneurs to adopt technology, improve efficiency, and meet global standards.
- Market Linkage & E-Commerce: Digital marketplaces linking MSMEs with local and international buyers, suppliers, and investors.
- IPO Enablement & Finance Readiness: Equipping SMEs with compliance, reporting, and capital access tools to scale.
- Collaboration with UNIDO & National Institutes: Built on our ERP pilot with UNIDO and the Ethiopian Textile Industry Development Institute (ETIDI), ensuring institutional buy-in and scalability.


Methodology & Technology:
- ERP + AI-powered analytics (forecasting, efficiency optimization).
- Cloud-based, modular architecture for rapid scaling.
- E-commerce integration for resilient digital supply chains.
- Digital skills capacity building delivered via blended training.


Partnership Model:
- Public sector: Ministries & institutes (ETIDI, MIDI).
- International organizations: UNIDO, AfDB.
- Private sector: Local tech firms and MSMEs.
- Academia: Universities for research & skills development
Solution Provider(s): With the current focus on Manufacturing Sector our key partners include the following; Yanos Group: Technology firm leading RISE Initiative. MIDI (Manufacturing Industry Development Institute, Ethiopia) – sectoral oversight and policy alignment. UNIDO Ethiopia – pilot collaboration partner (ERP modules).  With the scaling to other sectors these partners will be more focused on the specific sector we replicate this model to.
Implementation location(s): Addis Ababa, Ethiopia – Pilot implementation at the Ethiopian Textile Industry Development Institute (ETIDI) in collaboration with UNIDO. In fact the RISE Initiated stemmed from our experience with this project as it showed us the challenges and opportunities present in the manufacturing industry and how our solution is equipped to tackle some of the major challenges.
Implementation timeline(s): ERP system co-developed with UNIDO in 2019 (ETIDI, Addis Ababa). Lessons from this pilot laid the foundation for RISE Initiative (2020–present). Current efforts are scaling into a broader MSME-focused platform.
Duration to pilot in a new geography: Approx. 4 months for first deployment (infrastructure, onboarding, customization). Thereafter, onboarding new MSMEs can be done in 1–2 weeks due to RISE’s cloud-based, modular architecture.
SDGs addressed: SDG 8 (Decent Work and Economic Growth);SDG 12 (Responsible Consumption and Production);SDG 17 (Partnerships for the Goals);
Desired impact:
Objectives:
- Digitally empower MSMEs, especially women and youth.
- Build resilient supply chains with real-time insights
- Strengthen Ethiopia’s (and Africa’s) competitiveness globally.
Key Achievements / Impacts (anticipated & measurable):
- 30% increase in MSME efficiency via reduced duplication and optimized resource use
- 20% increase in market access and export opportunities for MSMEs through digital linkages.
- 5,000+ MSMEs trained in ERP, digital skills, and sustainable production by year 3.
- Attraction of international investment through IPO enablement pathways.
- Long-term: Establish Ethiopia as a regional model for inclusive industrial digital transformation.
Key technologies:
- ERP Core (Open-source-based modular systems).
- Sectoral Integration (Integrate sectoral data through a web of ERP systems)
- AI / Machine Learning (analytics, demand forecasting, optimization).
- Cloud Computing (scalable, low-cost digital infrastructure).
- E-commerce Platforms (digital supply chain integration).
- Data Visualization & Dashboards (decision-making tools).
Unique Characteristics:
- UNIDO-Proven Pilot: Builds on successful ERP pilot with UNIDO/ETIDI
- Ecosystem Approach: Goes beyond ERP to integrate sectoral analytics, e-commerce, capacity building, and finance access.
- Data-driven Financing: Data-driven financing for MSMEs using accurate and timely data from the ERP system as well as using industry-wide risk analytics.
- Innovative Financing: Use pool funding based on common  industry needs analysis for similar MSMEs.
- Inclusive by Design: MSMEs, women, and youth at the center — not an add-on.
- IPO Enablement: Prepares MSMEs for capital markets, a rare feature in digital transformation projects.
Scalability: Highly Modular, cloud-based, replicable across Africa & emerging markets.
Sustainable Change:
By digitally connecting MSMEs, institutes, and investors through RISE, we create self-reinforcing systemic change:
- Adoption: MSMEs adopt ERP + analytics → achieve efficiency, reduce waste, increase output.
- Market Integration: Digital linkages expand access to domestic & global buyers → higher revenues.
- Capacity Building: Women & youth entrepreneurs trained → inclusive participation in industrial value chains.
- Data-driven Financing: MSMEs use their ERP data as leverage driven by transparency to unlock more finance → better access to finance.
- Innovative Financing: MSMEs either pool funds together to mitigate risk and unlock more financial power collectively → more access to finance.
- Finance Readiness: IPO and capital access pathways → increased investment flow.
- Policy Alignment: Data-driven insights inform government & UNIDO policy → enabling environment.
This cycle builds a resilient industrial ecosystem where MSMEs are globally competitive, supply chains are inclusive and sustainable, and Ethiopia becomes a regional model for industrial digital transformation.
Funding Sources: The RISE Initiative has so far been funded through direct investment from Yanos Group and collaborative project funding with UNIDO. The pilot ERP system developed for the Ethiopian Textile Industry Development Institute (ETIDI) was supported under UNIDO’s Ethiopia Programme for Country Partnership (PCP). Additional resources were contributed in-kind by Yanos Group in the form of technical expertise, infrastructure, and ongoing platform development. We are now seeking strategic partners and blended financing models (development partners + private sector + impact investors) to scale RISE across Ethiopia and other African markets.

Title: E-Tax Audit
Subtitle: E-Tax Audit is a digital platform designed to streamline tax auditing processes, ensuring compliance, accuracy, and efficiency for TPE,PME and big businesses.
Problem Statement:
Complex Regulations: Simplifies understanding and compliance with intricate tax laws.
Inefficiency: Reduces time and resources spent on manual audits through automation.
Data Accuracy: Enhances accuracy by minimizing human error in calculations and reporting.
Transparency: Promotes transparency and trust between taxpayers and authorities.
Accessibility: Provides easy access to information and tools for remote areas, improving participation.
Training Needs: Offers resources and training to improve taxpayer knowledge and skills.
Solution Overview:
Detailed Description of How the Solution Works : 
User Registration: Taxpayers and auditors create profiles to access the platform.

Data Input: Users input financial data and documentation directly into the system, which supports various formats (pictures, PDFs, spreadsheets).

Automated Analysis: The platform employs algorithms to analyze submitted data against compliance requirements and historical benchmarks.

Reporting: After analysis, the system generates detailed audit reports highlighting discrepancies, compliance levels, and recommendations for improvement.

Real-Time Updates: Users receive notifications about changes in tax regulations and best practices, ensuring they stay informed.

Feedback and Support: The platform includes functionality for users to ask questions and receive guidance from tax experts through a chat feature.

Methodologies and Technologies Used : 
Cloud Computing: The platform utilizes cloud infrastructure for scalability, allowing users to access it from anywhere with an internet connection.

Data Analytics: Advanced data analytics techniques are employed to assess financial information, identify trends, and generate actionable insights.

Machine Learning: Algorithms are integrated for predictive analytics, improving the accuracy of compliance assessments by learning from previous audit data.

User-Centric Design: The platform is built with a focus on user experience, ensuring that the interface is intuitive and accessible.

API Integration: Allows seamless connections with other financial software, facilitating easier data transfer and reducing manual input.

Partnerships and Collaboration Models: 
Government Agencies: Collaborations with tax authorities to ensure the platform aligns with local regulations and standards, fostering trust and compliance.

Educational Institutions: Collaborations with universities and training centers to offer workshops and resources on tax compliance and auditing best practices.

Tech Companies: Partnerships with technology firms for ongoing development and innovation, ensuring the platform remains up-to-date with the latest advancements.
Solution Provider(s): Direction Générale des Impôts (DGI)  Profile: The main tax authority in Madagascar responsible for tax collection and enforcement of tax laws. Sector: Government / Taxation. INSCAE : Profile: A leading university providing education and training in various fields, including economics and law. Sector: Education / Academia. Internal Ingeneer tech,  Computer engineer, web development, information system.
Duration to pilot in a new geography: 6 months
SDGs addressed: SDG 4 (Quality Education);SDG 8 (Decent Work and Economic Growth);SDG 10 (Reduced Inequalities);
Desired impact:
Automate Tax Audits: Implement automation tools to reduce manual processes and improve accuracy in audits.

Facilitate User Education: Provide training materials and resources.

Develop a User-Friendly Interface: Ensure the platform is intuitive and easy to navigate.

Establish Real-Time Reporting: Create a system for real-time data submission and reporting to ensure timely compliance.

Build Strategic Partnerships: Collaborate with key stakeholders to enhance the platform’s credibility and effectiveness.

Monitor and Evaluate: Set up mechanisms for continuous monitoring and evaluation of the platform’s performance and impact on tax compliance rates.

Key Achievements and Impacts of the E-Tax Audit Solution
Increased Tax Compliance Rate: Achieved a 40% increase in tax compliance among registered businesses within the first year of implementation.

Reduction in Audit Processing Time: Reduced the average audit processing time by 90%.

Cost Savings for Taxpayers: Enabled taxpayers to save an estimated 45% in compliance costs.

Training and Capacity Building: Provided training to over 500 auditors, improving their skills and knowledge in modern auditing practices.

Improved Data Accuracy: Enhanced data accuracy by reducing errors in submitted tax returns by 95%, leading to fewer disputes and re-audits.
Key technologies: Cloud Computing. Machine Learning Algorithms. Natural Language Processing (NLP). Automated Data Classification. Anomaly Detection. Employs AI techniques to detect unusual patterns, alerting auditors to potential fraud and errors. Chatbots. Data Analytics. API Integration. Secure Data Storage. Real-Time Notifications.
Unique Characteristics:
AI-Powered Automation:
Utilizes machine learning algorithms to automate data analysis and compliance checks. This innovation significantly reduces human error, accelerates the auditing process, and allows for proactive identification of discrepancies.

Real-Time Reporting and Feedback:
Offers instant processing of tax submissions and provides immediate feedback to users. This feature minimizes delays traditionally associated with audits and enables users to address issues promptly, enhancing overall efficiency.

Integrated Support Systems:
Incorporates AI-driven chatbots and direct communication tools that provide real-time assistance to users. This innovation enhances user engagement and ensures that taxpayers have access to immediate support throughout the auditing process.

Enhanced Tax Compliance:
By simplifying the audit process and providing clear guidance, the solution encourages higher tax compliance rates. 

Empowerment Through Education:
The platform offers comprehensive training resources and support, empowering taxpayers with knowledge about their obligations. 

Data-Driven Decision Making:
The use of analytics and aggregated data provides insights that inform tax policy and reform. 

Transparency and Trust:

Scalability and Adaptability:
The cloud-based infrastructure allows the solution to scale and adapt to evolving needs, ensuring that it remains relevant and effective in a changing economic landscape.

Increased tax revenue and compliance directly contribute to sustainable economic growth.

Title: Rvapp
Subtitle: A voice-first Mobile app for rural Africa: residents speak to apply for trainings, MSME licenses and micro-grants, receive voice updates, while authorities act on real-time village-level insights.
Problem Statement: Rural residents often have phones and data but face low literacy, language/dialect barriers, long travel to offices, and fragmented, paper-based services. Digital portals assume reading, typing and steady broadband. This excludes women, elders, migrants and micro-entrepreneurs from skills programs, licenses, micro-grants and markets, slowing local economic growth.
Solution Overview:
How it works.

RuralVoices App is a voice-first mobile app (low-data) that lets users speak to: enroll in digital-skills training, request MSME/stall licenses, apply for micro-grants, or report issues. The app converts speech to structured forms, prompts for photos (ID/docs) with OCR, and sends push voice updates on status (“Approved—collect Tuesday”). A government/NGO Caseboard routes and tracks requests with SLAs; a Rural Insights Map clusters needs by village/theme to guide action and budgets. Optional MSME toolkit: voice-invoice, mobile-money payouts/fees.

Methodologies & technologies.

Human-centered co-design; AI speech-to-text, NLU, text-to-speech (localized dialect packs, human-in-the-loop QA), on-device models + server fallback, Android app with data minimization & encryption, document OCR, geotagging, analytics (clustering/heatmaps), mobile-money APIs, push notifications. Telco zero-rating to remove data cost.

Partnerships & collaboration.

Tri-partite pilots with
 (1) Municipal/Provincial authorities (service owners, SLAs),
 (2) Telcos (zero-rating, distribution), 
(3) TVET/training centers & MSME desks (course 
seats, license workflows), 
plus CSOs (outreach/trust), 
Mobile-Money providers (payouts/fees), Universities/radio (dialect corpora), 
and independent evaluators (M&E).
Solution Provider(s): Just Bim It (Belgium) — digital innovation & smart-cities studio; Technology & Consulting, Pilot Municipality/District— local government service owner; Public Sector. orange money— payouts and fee collection; Fintech/Payments,
Duration to pilot in a new geography: 12–16 weeks from MOU to go-live (co-design 4–6 weeks; build/integrate 6–8 weeks; launch & training 2 weeks).
SDGs addressed: SDG 8 (Decent Work and Economic Growth);SDG 9 (Industry, Innovation, and Infrastructure);SDG 10 (Reduced Inequalities);
Desired impact:
Solution Objectives

Remove literacy and language barriers to public/economic services through a voice-first Android app (low-data).
Digitize intake and routing (with SLAs) to shorten time-to-decision for trainings, MSME licenses and micro-grants.
Increase participation of rural women and youth in skills programs and MSME formalization.
Provide village-level insights to authorities for transparent, data-driven action.


Key achievements / impacts (intended, ex-ante targets — not yet achieved)

Access: Onboard 30,000–60,000 rural users in the first 12-month pilot, with ≥55% women (subject to telco zero-rating and CSO outreach).
Service delivery: Enable 7,000–12,000 completed applications (training, licenses, micro-grants). Final approvals depend on partner budgets/criteria; we will report the number of complete, eligible dossiers transmitted in addition to approvals.
Skills & MSME uptake: 2,000–4,000 training enrollments (capacity-dependent); 1,500–2,500 MSME licenses/micro-grants issued (partner-dependent).
Efficiency: Reduce average time-to-decision by 20–35% vs. paper processes; reduce resubmissions by 10–25% via guided voice + document OCR.
Employment & income (directional): Through licenses/grants/training, enable 1,500–2,500 micro-entrepreneurs to start/expand activity; indicative income uplift €25–€50/month per approved beneficiary (to be verified at endline).
Transparency & equity: Public dashboards showing requests/resolutions by village; disaggregation by gender/age (opt-in).


Measurement & verification

Baseline → midline (6 mo) → endline (12 mo) surveys; independent evaluation.
System logs for submissions, approvals, SLA times, and mobile-money volumes; equity dashboards.
Clear disclosure of what is under our control (completed dossiers, SLA performance, user satisfaction) vs. partner-dependent outcomes (approvals, disbursements).
Key technologies: AI speech-to-text (ASR), natural language understanding, text-to-speech (TTS) with localized dialect packs; on-device inference + server fallback; Android app; document OCR; geotagging; analytics & clustering; push notifications; mobile-money APIs; secure cloud with encryption at rest/in transit; role-based admin console.
Unique Characteristics:
Voice-first, dialect-aware user experience (speak → apply → voice updates).
Low-data design + telco zero-rating to eliminate cost barriers.
Moves beyond “feedback apps” to actionable services (licenses, grants, payouts).
On-device privacy (transcribe locally when possible; PII minimization); human-in-the-loop for inclusivity and quality.
Two-sided value: residents access services; authorities get village-level insights and SLA tracking.
Modular, replicable playbook (language packs + workflows) for new districts/countries.
Sustainable Change:
Sustainable, systemic change (Theory of Change)
Inputs: Voice-first app, telco zero-rating, partner workflows, human-in-the-loop.
Activities: Spoken applications → structured cases; case routing with SLAs; transparent village-level dashboards.
Outputs: Higher completion of training, licenses, grants; faster decisions; public evidence of action.
Outcomes: Formalization of micro-businesses, income growth, improved service equity for women/youth, trust in institutions.
Systemic change: Voice becomes a standard digital access rail for rural populations; data guides policy and budget allocation; model replicates across regions. Phase-2 integration can add portable credentials and cross-agency interoperability.
Funding Sources: Self-funded, but meeting booked with Enabel, Belgian development agency  to present them  solution to help with the funding
Primary thematic focus area: MSME Empowerment & Local Digital Innovation
Summary: Rvapp (RuralVoices App) is a proof-of-concept voice-first mobile application designed to overcome literacy, language, and access barriers faced by rural populations in Africa and Arab States. By allowing residents to apply for training, MSME licenses, and micro-grants through speech, and receive voice updates, it creates an inclusive channel for economic participation. The app integrates speech-to-text, OCR, geotagging, and mobile-money APIs, while authorities benefit from real-time village-level insights and SLA-tracked service delivery. With tri-partite partnerships between governments, telcos, and training/MSME institutions, the solution aims to digitize service intake, increase participation of women and youth, and build transparency into rural service delivery systems.

Title: DIGICARBON: Democratizing Carbon Markets for an Inclusive Green Economy
Subtitle: DIGICARBON: Leveraging digital innovation to democratize carbon markets, empowering smallholders and marginalized communities for an inclusive, sustainable green economy
Problem Statement:
Carbon markets hold immense potential to drive climate action and sustainable development by incentivizing emissions reductions and nature-based solutions. However, systemic barriers exclude smallholder farmers, Indigenous communities, and marginalized groups—those most vulnerable to climate impacts—from participating equitably in these markets. Key challenges include:
1.	Exclusionary Access: Over 600 million smallholder farmers globally lack the technical expertise, financial resources, or digital infrastructure to navigate complex carbon project development. Certification costs, opaque registries, and fragmented methodologies disproportionately favor large-scale corporate actors.
2.	Verification Complexity: Traditional carbon credit monitoring relies on costly, time-intensive field audits and opaque data systems. Small-scale projects struggle to meet rigorous standards (e.g., Verra, Gold Standard), delaying revenue streams and discouraging participation.
3.	Digital Divide: Marginalized communities often lack access to digital tools for real-time data collection, remote sensing, or blockchain-enabled transparency. This perpetuates mistrust in carbon markets and limits traceability of climate benefits.
4.	Inequitable Value Distribution: Middlemen and brokers capture up to 60% of carbon credit revenues, leaving farmers with minimal income. Lack of localized capacity-building entrenches dependency on external consultants.
5.	Fragmented Solutions: Existing platforms address siloed aspects (e.g., MRV tech, registries) but fail to integrate end-to-end solutions tailored to grassroots needs.
These barriers undermine global climate goals by sidelining communities responsible for stewarding 80% of the world’s remaining biodiversity. Without inclusive systems, carbon markets risk exacerbating inequality while missing emission reduction targets. DIGICARBON addresses these gaps by democratizing access to carbon finance through integrated digital tools, simplified verification, and equitable revenue-sharing models. By bridging the gap between high-impact climate action and inclusive economic growth, the solution ensures marginalized groups transition from passive beneficiaries to active stakeholders in the green economy.
Solution Overview:
DIGICARBON is a digital-first platform designed to democratize carbon market participation for smallholder farmers, Indigenous communities, and marginalized groups. By integrating scalable technology with localized capacity-building, the solution simplifies carbon project development, verification, and revenue distribution while ensuring inclusivity and transparency.
How It Works
1.	Project Onboarding: Farmers register via a mobile app, where geotagged land data is collected to assess carbon sequestration potential. AI-driven tools match them with tailored methodologies (e.g., agroforestry, soil carbon enhancement).
2.	Data Collection & Monitoring: Low-cost IoT sensors, satellite imagery (via partnerships with providers like Planet Labs), and farmer-submitted photos track real-time carbon stock changes. Blockchain records immutable data streams, reducing audit costs.
3.	Verification & Issuance: Machine learning algorithms pre-validate data against standards (Verra, Gold Standard, Tyndall), flagging discrepancies for third-party auditors. Automated reporting accelerates credit issuance by 40–60%.
4.	Revenue Distribution: Smart contracts ensure direct, transparent payments to farmers (via mobile money), retaining <10% fees for platform upkeep. Communities access dashboards to track credit sales and pricing.
Methodologies & Technologies
•	Core Methodologies: Simplified versions of VM0042 (agroforestry), GS TPDDTECH (digital MRV), and Tyndall’s TCS004 (Community-led standard).
•	Tech Stack:
o	Blockchain (Polygon): Ensures tamper-proof credit traceability.
o	AI/ML Models: Predict yield-carbon correlations and detect deforestation.
o	IoT Sensors: Monitor soil health, tree growth, and emissions.
o	Mobile App: Available offline, with voice-based tutorials in local languages.
Partnerships & Collaboration
•	NGOs/Cooperatives: Local partners (e.g., FairTrade Africa) train farmers and aggregate projects.
•	Tech Providers: Collaborations with AWS (cloud hosting) and Starlink (rural connectivity).
•	Carbon Registries: Direct API integration with Verra, Gold Standard, and Tyndall for seamless credit listing.
•	Government Agencies: Co-develop policy frameworks for inclusive carbon market access.
By bridging the digital divide and decentralizing carbon finance, DIGICARBON empowers 10 million smallholders by 2030, channeling 70% of revenue directly to communities while accelerating global climate targets.
Solution Provider(s): Carbon Coy Limited (Carbon Consulting Company), University of Nigeria, Nsukka (Research & Policy Support), Teranium Co (IT Support Services)
Duration to pilot in a new geography: 12 months
SDGs addressed: SDG 1 (No Poverty);SDG 13 (Climate Action);SDG 10 (Reduced Inequalities);
Desired impact:
Solution Objectives
1.	Democratize Carbon Markets: Enable 10 million smallholder farmers and marginalized communities to participate in carbon markets by 2030.
2.	Simplify Access: Reduce carbon project development costs by 50% and verification timelines by 60% through digital tools.
3.	Equitable Revenue: Ensure 70% of carbon credit revenue flows directly to communities, bypassing intermediaries.
4.	Climate Impact: Sequester 50 million tons of CO2 equivalent by 2030 via nature-based solutions (agroforestry, soil carbon).
5.	Bridge the Digital Divide: Provide 5 million rural users with access to climate-tech tools and training.
Key Achievements/Impacts (Projected)
1.	GHG Reductions:
o	20,000–25,000 tCO2/year per 10,000 farmers through agroforestry and sustainable land practices.
o	Cumulative 5 million tCO2 sequestered by 2028 (baseline: 2025).
2.	Economic Inclusion:
o	$500–$700/year additional income per farmer at $25/ton carbon pricing.
o	200,000 jobs created by 2030 (e.g., local technicians, data collectors, auditors).
3.	Operational Efficiency:
o	40% faster credit issuance via AI-driven pre-validation and blockchain transparency.
o	60% cost reduction in MRV (Monitoring, Reporting, Verification) through IoT/satellite integration.
4.	Scalability:
o	500+ community-led projects operational across Sub-Saharan Africa and Southeast Asia by 2027.
o	30% increase in women’s participation via targeted training and mobile app accessibility.
5.	Ecosystem Impact:
o	1 million hectares restored or conserved through farmer-led reforestation.
o	50% reduction in deforestation rates in partner communities via real-time satellite alerts.
DIGICARBON aims to transform carbon markets into a lever for inclusive growth, directly linking climate action with poverty alleviation and gender equity. By 2030, the solution seeks to unlock $1.5 billion in climate finance for marginalized groups while advancing global net-zero targets.
Key technologies:
DIGICARBON integrates cutting-edge technologies to streamline carbon project development, enhance transparency, and empower marginalized communities:
1.	Blockchain (Polygon):
a.	Role: Creates tamper-proof records of carbon credits, ensuring traceability from issuance to retirement.
b.	Impact: Reduces fraud risks and enables direct, transparent revenue distribution via smart contracts.
2.	AI/ML Models:
a.	Role: Predict carbon sequestration rates using satellite imagery and historical data. Detect anomalies (e.g., deforestation) in real time.
b.	Impact: Automates 80% of data validation, slashing verification costs by 50% and accelerating credit issuance.
3.	IoT Sensors:
a.	Role: Monitor soil moisture, tree growth, and emissions at farm level. Data syncs to the cloud for analysis.
b.	Impact: Provides granular, real-time insights for accurate MRV (Monitoring, Reporting, Verification).
4.	Satellite Imagery (Planet Labs, Sentinel-2):
a.	Role: Tracks land-use changes and biomass growth at scale.
b.	Impact: Validates carbon stock increases across large geographies, reducing reliance on manual audits.
5.	Mobile App (Offline-First Design):
a.	Role: Allows farmers to submit photos, report activities, and access training modules in local languages (e.g., Igbo, Yoruba, Swahili, Hausa).
b.	Impact: Bridges the digital divide, enabling low-literacy users to engage with carbon markets.
6.	Cloud Computing (AWS):
a.	Role: Hosts data analytics pipelines and AI models.
b.	Impact: Scales to support millions of users while maintaining low operational costs.
7.	Starlink Connectivity:
a.	Role: Provides internet access to remote areas for real-time data syncing.
b.	Impact: Ensures seamless participation for off-grid communities.
Integration: These technologies synergize to create an end-to-end digital ecosystem. For example, IoT and satellite data feed into AI models, which generate audit-ready reports stored on blockchain. Farmers interact via the mobile app, receiving instant payments through integrated mobile money APIs.
By merging frontier tech with user-centric design, DIGICARBON dismantles barriers to carbon market access, driving equitable climate action.
Unique Characteristics:
DIGICARBON’s Unique/Differentiated Characteristics
1.	Inclusive Business Model:
a.	Pro-Poor Revenue Sharing: Directs 70% of carbon revenue to farmers via blockchain-powered smart contracts, bypassing brokers who typically capture 50–60% of profits.
b.	No-Cost Onboarding: Farmers pay zero upfront fees; costs are recouped through a 10% transaction fee post-credit sale, democratizing access for cash-strapped communities.
2.	Multi-Standard Agility:
a.	Parallel Certification: Simultaneously registers projects under Verra, Gold Standard, and Tyndall, avoiding bottlenecks (e.g., Verra’s 18–24-month approval timelines) and diversifying buyer pools.
3.	Frictionless Tech Stack:
a.	AI + Blockchain Fusion: Proprietary AI pre-validates 80% of monitoring data, slashing audit costs by 50%, while blockchain ensures immutable credit traceability.
b.	Offline-First Mobile App: Functions without internet, uses voice commands in 15+ local languages (e.g., Yoruba, Bahasa), and integrates with low-cost IoT sensors for illiterate users.
4.	Hyperlocal Partnerships:
a.	Farmer-Led Cooperatives: Collaborates with grassroots groups (e.g., FairTrade cooperatives) to aggregate smallholdings into bankable carbon assets, reducing fragmentation.
b.	Govt-Backed Trust Funds: Partners with national agencies to create revolving funds, guaranteeing advance payments against future credit sales.
5.	Climate Justice Focus:
a.	Gender-Intentional Design: App features prioritize women’s access (e.g., privacy controls, female-centric training), targeting 30% female participation by 2026.
b.	Indigenous IP Safeguards: Blockchain timestamps traditional land-use knowledge, protecting Indigenous intellectual property in carbon methodologies.
6.	Scalable MRV Breakthroughs:
a.	Satellite-IoT Hybrid Monitoring: Combines Planet Labs’ 3m-resolution imagery with ground sensors to cut MRV costs by 60% vs. traditional methods.
Why It Stands Out:
While most carbon platforms focus on tech or equity, DIGICARBON uniquely merges both. Its blend of frontier technology, radical inclusivity, and institutional partnerships creates a blueprint for market transformation—turning marginalized communities from beneficiaries into climate asset owners.
Sustainable Change:
DIGICARBON’s Theory of Change: Pathway to Systemic Impact
DIGICARBON drives sustainable, systemic change by transforming carbon markets into a lever for climate justice, economic equity, and ecological resilience. Its deployment triggers cascading effects across four dimensions:
1. Immediate Outcomes
•	Empowered Communities: Smallholders gain direct access to carbon finance, transitioning from subsistence farming to becoming climate asset owners.
•	Streamlined Market Access: AI/blockchain reduces verification costs by 50%, enabling fragmented smallholdings to qualify as aggregated carbon projects.
2. Intermediate Effects
•	Shifted Power Dynamics: By redirecting 70% of revenue to farmers (vs. 20–40% in traditional models), the solution disrupts extractive intermediation, fostering trust in carbon markets.
•	Accelerated Climate Action: Automated MRV and multi-standard certification cut credit issuance timelines from 2+ years to 8–12 months, unlocking faster liquidity for reforestation and agroforestry.
3. Long-Term Systemic Shifts
•	Inclusive Market Structures: Scalable digital tools democratize participation, incentivizing 10 million smallholders to adopt regenerative practices by 2030. This diversifies carbon credit supply, reducing corporate monopsony.
•	Policy Innovation: Success metrics pressure governments to formalize pro-poor carbon policies (e.g., tax breaks for community projects, simplified land tenure systems).
•	Gender Equity: Targeting 30% female participation reshapes rural economies, increasing women’s decision-making power over land and income.
4. Follow-On Effects
•	Ecosystem Restoration: 1 million hectares under sustainable management by 2028 creates biodiversity corridors, enhancing resilience to climate shocks.
•	Tech Diffusion: Open-source app modules and farmer-to-farmer training spur grassroots innovation (e.g., IoT hacks for crop monitoring).
•	Financial Inclusion: Carbon revenue (avg. $500–$700/year/household) seeds investments in clean energy (e.g., solar irrigation), creating circular green economies.
Ultimate Impact
By 2035, DIGICARBON’s model could catalyze a $50B inclusive carbon market, where marginalized groups contribute 40% of global nature-based credits. This redefines climate finance as a tool for poverty alleviation, bridging the gap between net-zero targets and SDGs

Title: Diaspora Digital Futures: Innovation Engines for Inclusive Tech Economies
Subtitle: A transnational model uniting HBCUs, churches, and grassroots leaders to co-create policy, develop tech talent, and drive digital equity from the local community to global governance.
Problem Statement:
Across Africa, the Caribbean, and the Southern Region of the U.S., digital inequity persists– not because of a lack of innovation or talent, but because of extractive aid models, underinvestment in community institutions, and governance systems that exclude grassroots voices.
Research from The Bridgespan Group (2024), How Development Funders and Philanthropy Collaborate in Africa, shows that African-led organizations often receive only a fraction of philanthropic funding, with most resources directed to international NGOs rather than local institutions. Similarly, Redefining Africa’s “Unlearning Development” framework(2023) outlines how development efforts framed around outside expertise can reinforce dependency and erase indigenous knowledge systems.

These critiques confirm what Black communities across the Diaspora experience daily: trusted anchor institutions such as Historically Black Colleges and Universities (HBCUs), faith communities,community-based organizations and cultural networks are systematically under-resourced despite their proven role in sustaining trust, nurturing education, and equipping local-level resilience.

At the heart of this challenge is the question: who owns the future? For too long, futures have been designed by those outside of our communities, leaving under-resourced populations with little power to define or benefit from technological change. The HEART Engines + Diaspora Digital Futures initiative directly responds by reclaiming the future- creating pathways where joy, justice, and innovation are not luxuries but birthrights. By building an ecosystem where thriving is the standard, we directly advance the Global Digital Compact’s Objective 2: ensuring that the digital economy expands inclusion and delivers meaningful benefits for communities historically left out.
Aligned with the UN Permanent Forum on People of African Descent and its 2025 call for “Reparatory Justice in the Age of AI,” our proposal ensures that digital inclusion itself becomes a form of reparatory justice. Through the HEART framework and the Diaspora Digital Futures Pact, we will align training, anchor institutions, and regional strategies with a global governance platform that addresses systemic racism and digital inequity, transforming them into opportunities for leadership, innovation, and thriving across the Diaspora.
Solution Overview:
The #BlackTechFutures Research Institute and its proposed HEART Engines initiative aim to establish a sustainable, global Black Tech Ecosystem that fosters economic mobility and digital equity for people of African descent. HEART stands for Humanity, Economics & Entrepreneurship, Arts, and Responsible Technology—four pillars that guide our approach to reimagining how technology can serve communities historically excluded from its benefits.

At the center of this initiative is the belief that addressing systemic racism and economic injustice requires aligning training, inclusion of cultural institutions and cultural traditions, collaboration, and regional strategies. Our work is designed to close the digital divide and economic divide, while increasing representation in tech fields that directly influence the public good, particularly in civic tech, AI ethics, digital equity, and broadband access.

With only five years left to achieve the UN Sustainable Development Goals by 2030, this initiative directly advances SDG 5 (Gender Equality), SDG 8 (Decent Work & Economic Growth), and SDG 9 (Industry, Innovation, and Infrastructure). Our strategies are rooted in the thematic focus areas of Inclusive Digital Innovation Skills & Entrepreneurial Talent Development, Enabling Policies & Regulatory Innovation, and Innovation Acceleration & Knowledge Sharing.

Through the HEART framework, we propose three interwoven strategies that scale impact across institutions and borders:
·       Training & Talent Development: Building on U.S. pilots that will certify 450 HBCU faculty and 900 church leaders, we aim to expand across the Diaspora by training 10,000 faculty and faith leaders globally and certifying 1 million learners in Public Interest Technology by 2030.
·       Community Digital Hubs & Innovation Labs: Churches and community centers will serve as 500 broadband-enabled hubs across Africa, the Caribbean, Latin America, and North America, providing access for youth and adults while hosting innovation labs where graduates connect to internships, fellowships, or entrepreneurial test beds through partners like MMTC, Code Crew, Kapor Center, and Stillman Cyber Clinics.
·       Global Diaspora Summit & Pact: Convening leaders annually from Africa, the Caribbean, and the Americas to exchange knowledge, align regional strategies, and co-create the Diaspora Digital Futures Pact. The Pact will serve as a living, open-source governance framework for inclusive digital economies and provide input to global bodies like the UN Permanent Forum on People of African Descent and the Human Rights Council.

Methodologies and technologies will include culturally responsive AI literacy campaigns (such as the AI Fan Project, which has reached 600 households), participatory asset mapping for advocacy, community-centered LMS platforms (HEART LMS, Pathwright), and intergenerational learning models that bridge ancestral wisdom and future-facing innovation.

Impact will be tracked both quantitatively and qualitatively. Training programs will be measured through completion rates, pre/post assessments, and leadership outcomes. Hubs and labs will be tracked by the number of sites launched, placements made, and community members served. Importantly, these accountability mechanisms ensure that the Diaspora Digital Futures Pact is grounded in lived community impact, not just policy dialogue.

By embedding these strategies into the HEART Engines model, we are cultivating an ecosystem of thriving—one that turns digital inequity into digital sovereignty and positions people of African descent to own their digital futures, influence governance, and advance reparatory justice in the age of AI.
Solution Provider(s): The #BlackTechFutures Research Institute will serve as the convenor and hub connecting local-level solutions across the African Diaspora. In the U.S., anchor partners include Historically Black Colleges and Universities (Howard, Stillman, Morehouse), Historically Black Theological Institutions (Interdenominational Theological Center, Payne, Hood), and cultural institutions like the Schomburg Center for Research in Black Culture. At the global level, HEART Engines is building strategic collaborations across Africa, with South Africa positioned as a co-convening partner for the 2026 Digital Diaspora Futures Summit. A potential anchor in this effort is the Centre for Humanities Research (CHR) at the University of the Western Cape, under the leadership of Professor Premesh Lalu, Research Professor and UK-RSA Bilateral Research Chair in Digital Humanities (Culture and Technics). CHR’s strengths in critical thought, African humanities, and digital humanities—supported by colleagues such as Dr. Mmaki Jantjies and Dr. Carolien van der Berg—offer a vital foundation for situating digital equity within African intellectual and cultural traditions. Hosting the 2026 Summit at CHR would ground the initiative in African-led knowledge production, institutional capacity, and cultural frameworks, ensuring that the future of technology is shaped by local scholarship as well as global collaboration. This partnership is complemented by engagement with the Central University of Technology Free State under Vice-Chancellor Dr. Pamela Dube. Together, these partnerships strengthen the initiative’s foundation in African higher education and ensure that systemic change is rooted in culturally resonant academic leadership. Beyond higher education, we are exploring a network of civic and cultural institutions, all of which champion inclusive digital governance and community-led innovation, including: Kenya: African Cultural Regeneration Institute (ACRI), Kenya Institute of Puppet Theatre (KIPT), Kenya Heritage Hub South Africa: Africa Centre (Cape Town), Institute for Pan African Thought and Conversation, South African Pan African Organizations (various) Nigeria: Centre for Black and African Arts and Civilization (CBAAC), Terra Kulture, Committee for Relevant Art (CORA) Egypt: Pan African Cultural Heritage Institute, African Digital Heritage, Benya Group Foundation Jamaica: African Caribbean Institute of Jamaica / Jamaica Memory Bank (ACIJ/JMB), African Cultural Renaissance Movement (ACRM), Jamaican Grassroots Cultural Organizations (various) France: Maison Noire Américaine (MNA), Entrée to Black Paris Cultural Awareness Brazil: Vale do Dendê in Bahia United Kingdom: The Africa Centre (London), George Padmore Institute (GPI), Serendipity Institute for Black Arts and Heritage, Caribbean Tech Collective  Together, this network of higher education institutions, cultural hubs, and civil society organizations reflects the HEART Engines vision: a transnational, culturally grounded ecosystem linking U.S. HBCUs and HBTIs with African universities, Caribbean cultural centers, European diasporic institutes, and civic partners to shape ethical, inclusive, and sustainable digital futures.
Duration to pilot in a new geography: 2-4 years
SDGs addressed: SDG 5 (Gender Equality);SDG 9 (Industry, Innovation, and Infrastructure);SDG 8 (Decent Work and Economic Growth);
Desired impact:
We believe there is no artificial intelligence future without digital equity, and there is no digital equity without racial equity. HEART Engines exist to make that truth live. Our impact is not simply measured in outputs, but in whether our people are able to thrive with dignity and lead in shaping the technologies that govern their lives.

Already, more than 2,000 faith and civic leaders have been trained in AI ethics and data justice. Six hundred households have engaged in culturally grounded AI literacy campaigns like the AI Fan Project. Across the U.S., Africa, and the Caribbean, more than ten academic institutions have joined us to embed Public Interest Technology (PIT) into their teaching and practice. These beginnings show us what is possible when communities organize not as consumers of technology, but as its stewards.

By 2030, we will expand this vision into a durable, community-led digital ecosystem that reaches across the African Diaspora. Our goals are ambitious because the times demand nothing less: certify 1 million learners in PIT, train 10,000 faculty and faith leaders, and launch 500 digital hubs and innovation labs in churches, community centers, and universities. Through the Diaspora Digital Futures Summit, we will convene leaders annually to shape the Diaspora Digital Futures Pact—a living, open-source governance framework carried into global bodies such as the UN.
This work directly advances SDG 5 (Gender Equality), SDG 8 (Decent Work & Economic Growth), and SDG 9 (Industry, Innovation, and Infrastructure). It strengthens inclusive infrastructures, seeds future-facing employment pathways, and embeds equity into digital skills. But more than that—it shifts who gets to define the future.

The desired impact of HEART Engines is that historically marginalized communities will not simply be included in innovation; they will lead it. By 2030, our people will be building technologies rooted in justice and joy, establishing sustainable infrastructures that honor ancestral wisdom, and shaping global policy frameworks that endure for generations. This is not just about access. It is about transformation. It is about freedom. It is about justice.
Key technologies:
For HEART Engines, technology is not limited to machines or code. Our most enduring technologies are our cultural traditions: call and response, oral history, ritual, sacred music, and communal memory. These are the infrastructures that sustained our people through enslavement, migration, and systemic erasure. We honor these cultural technologies not as metaphors but as living systems of knowledge that guide how we design, teach, and govern digital tools today.

Alongside these ancestral technologies, HEART Engines mobilizes:
Artificial Intelligence (AI) — reimagined through the lens of justice, training communities to identify bias, reshape algorithms, and harness AI as a site for Black creativity.
Broadband & Connectivity Infrastructure — grounding digital equity by transforming churches, HBCUs, and community centers into hubs of innovation and access.
Learning Platforms (HEART LMS, Pathwright) — culturally responsive systems for certifying Trusted Community Advisors and connecting learners across the Diaspora.
Participatory Data & Mapping Tools — shifting data from extraction to stewardship, rooted in community authority.
Experimental Spaces with VR/AR and Emerging Tech — where youth and leaders can test future-facing applications grounded in culture and ethics.

By 2030, these twin strands — cultural technologies and digital technologies — will be braided together. The drumbeat and the algorithm, the archive and the AI, the ritual and the broadband hub will all serve as co-equal instruments of freedom. HEART Engines ensures that technology is never divorced from culture, but always rooted in the wisdom and practices that have sustained Black communities for generations.
Unique Characteristics:
Our solution is rooted in ancestral intelligence, intergenerational learning, and diaspora-wide collaboration. What makes it unique:
Faith & Cultural Anchoring: We activate trusted cultural and religious institutions (e.g., Black churches, HBCUs, traditional councils) as critical nodes for PIT training.
The Diaspora Digital Futures Pact: A participatory policy initiative that centers historically excluded voices in global digital governance.
Transnational Co-Design: Collaborative curriculum and program design between U.S.-based Black Tech Futures Research Institute and institutions like University of the Western Cape’s Centre for Humanities Research.
Workforce Justice Lens: Training for digital jobs is paired with policy literacy, ensuring economic mobility is not divorced from advocacy or ethics.
Creative Civic Tools: We embed culturally resonant tools like AI literacy church fans and traveling altars to communicate complex tech ideas in accessible formats.
Sustainable Change:
Our theory of change rests on the conviction that historically marginalized communities (when equipped with technical skills, empowered to integrate cultural traditions and ancestral wisdom, and given institutional tools to act as stewards of innovation), can fundamentally transform the systems that govern their lives. HEART Engines creates systemic change by transforming the infrastructures where knowledge, culture, and technology intersect. By rooting digital equity in HBCUs, Historically Black Theological Institutions, and faith-based organizations, we embed lasting capacity in trusted institutions that already anchor Black community life. These institutions become not only sites of learning, but durable nodes in a global digital ecosystem able to outlast political cycles, funding shifts, and market trends.

Systemic change will also be driven through governance. The Diaspora Digital Futures Pact convenes leaders from Africa, the Caribbean, and the Americas to align strategies and co-create an open-source framework for inclusive digital economies. This ensures that the standards shaping emerging technologies reflect the lived realities and cultural wisdom of African-descended people, rather than being dictated solely by corporate or state actors.

By braiding cultural technologies (oral history, call-and-response, ritual, memory) with digital infrastructures (AI, broadband, learning platforms), HEART Engines shifts the paradigm of innovation itself. This integration disrupts extractive models of technology and replaces them with regenerative, community-led systems of stewardship.

Partnerships with the Centre for Humanities Research (CHR) at the University of the Western Cape and the Central University of Technology (CUT) ensure that African-led scholarship and technical innovation shape both program delivery and the epistemological frameworks guiding digital equity. CHR’s grounding in African humanities and cultural techniques, alongside CUT’s applied expertise in technology and workforce development, embody the HEART Engines approach: weaving ancestral wisdom, ethical design, and innovation capacity to build infrastructures of freedom and justice.
This placement ensures that systemic change is not only about building digital skills, but also about redefining the very frameworks through which technology is taught, governed, and imagined—rooted in community authority, diasporic knowledge traditions, and global collaboration.

The systemic impact is twofold: (1) institutions across the Diaspora are equipped to deliver digital justice at scale, and (2) global governance structures are reshaped to embed equity, dignity, and cultural resilience at their core. By 2030, this scaffolding will ensure that Black communities are not only participants in the digital economy, but co-architects of its rules and infrastructures—creating change that is both transformative and enduring.
Funding Sources:
Our work has been seeded through a combination of federal, philanthropic, and institutional investments. Most significantly, the National Black Tech Ecosystem Association (home of the #BlackTechFutures Research Institute) was awarded an $11.9 million grant under the Digital Equity Act by the National Telecommunications and Information Administration (NTIA). We were one of the top recommended grantees out of more than 700 applicants, a testament to the urgency and strength of our model. Though this award was rescinded in May 2025 due to political challenges, the preparation, partnerships, and infrastructure built through that process remain in place, ready to scale.

Beyond federal channels, we have advanced Black Public Interest Technology (BPIT) through sustained philanthropic and institutional partnerships. In 2024, support from the Responsible Computing Challenge (funded by Omidyar Network, Mozilla, Schmidt Futures, Craig Newmark Philanthropies, and Mellon Foundation) enabled the launch of the HBCU Responsible Computing Network and Summer Seminar, training 17 faculty across 16 HBCUs. Collaborations with the Public Interest Technology University Network (PIT-UN) and Stillman College have further embedded equity and ethics into computing curricula, demonstrating our ability to leverage philanthropic capital into durable academic change.

The next phase—HEART Engines—represents a scalable expansion of these efforts. Sustaining and growing this work will require bold philanthropy and global partnership, particularly in response to the chronic underfunding of Black-led institutions. To date, we have established relationships with leading regional and international actors positioned to co-invest, including University of the Western Cape (Centre for Humanities Research), Central University of Technology Free State, Code for Africa, African Observatory on Responsible AI, Tech Herfrica, Ungana-Afrika, Deep Learning Indaba, CIVICAi Association, Aspen Digital, Norrsken Foundation, Mastercard Foundation, Google Africa AI Community Center, African Union’s “AI for All” programme, Schmidt Futures, MacArthur Foundation, Open Society Foundations, and the Rockefeller Foundation.

These partners, alongside future values-aligned funders, will enable HEART Engines to become nationally recognized infrastructure for Black digital equity and workforce justice in the U.S., while expanding transnationally across South Africa, the Caribbean, and the U.S. Virgin Islands.
Primary thematic focus area: Enabling Policies & Regulatory Innovation
Summary: Diaspora Digital Futures (HEART Engines) is a transnational initiative led by the #BlackTechFutures Research Institute to build an inclusive Black Tech Ecosystem rooted in cultural traditions, community institutions (HBCUs, churches, cultural centers), and global governance frameworks. It aims to train 10,000 faculty and faith leaders, certify 1 million learners in Public Interest Technology, and launch 500 digital hubs and innovation labs by 2030. Through the Diaspora Digital Futures Pact, it seeks to co-create a global governance model that embeds equity and reparatory justice into digital economies. Already, 2,000+ leaders have been trained in AI ethics, and 600 households have participated in culturally grounded AI literacy campaigns. The initiative emphasizes braiding ancestral knowledge with emerging technologies, transforming digital inequity into digital sovereignty across the Diaspora.

Title: Elzian Agro Precision Agriculture Solutions
Subtitle: We provides climate-smart data-driven precision agriculture solutions to utilise farmers’ limited resources at an optimum level.
Problem Statement: After surveying 60,000 farmers, we identified significant challenges they face in maintaining profitability amidst climate change, adapting to erratic weather patterns, combating crop losses due to pests, and optimizing organic crop yield and quality without access to real-time soil data. Furthermore, they struggle with inefficient utilization of limited resources including water, land, labor, pesticides, and fertilizers. These farmers are unable to monetize the invaluable Primary Ecosystem Services (PES) their farmlands produce.
Solution Overview:
We provide precision agriculture solutions with integrated monitoring and automation systems tailored to the requirements of our customers. Our patent-pending IoT-enabled devices allow farmers to monitor conditions in real-time, predict issues before they happen & make informed decisions to optimize crop yields. Our customers can monitor their farmland anywhere, anytime, and make efficient and rational decisions to maximize their profitability through crop waste reduction, effective utilization of limited resources, and increased crop yield.

Energized by the photosynthesis process, Contracted - Primary Ecosystem Services (C-PES) values are done by growing 40+ pan-tropical tree species, whose biomass accretion curves are verified by our Photosynthetic Biomass verification application (PBV app).

We (Elzian Agro) offer customized precision agriculture solutions through web and mobile applications, integrating IoT-based monitoring (Elzian-Agro-Eye), AI-driven decision support, and automated (Elzian-Agro-Mate) irrigation systems tailored for Azolla farming, allowing farmers to monitor nitrogen levels and make efficient decisions to boost paddy yield while replacing synthetic fertilizers with Azolla as a nature-based biofertilizer.

Our IoT monitoring system (Elzian-Agro-Eye) ensures high-precision atmospheric elements (temperature, humidity, atmospheric pressure, light intensity, wind speed and direction), soil elements (moisture, temperature, pH levels, electrical conductivity, nitrogen levels, phosphorus levels, potassium levels, salinity), liquid elements (temperature, pH levels, dissolved oxygen, nitrate and nitrite levels, alkalinity and liquid flow rate) and Azolla nitrogen levels.

Our automation system (Elzian-Agro-Mate), comprising both hardware and software components combination that serves as an automatic supervisor in charge of irrigation, controlling 8 water zones per device, and manages irrigation and liquid fertilizer spraying operations efficiently.

At our demonstration site, farmers can explore customized web and mobile applications for small-scale farms, observing IoT-based systems that manage water resources to boost crop yields. They learn to use precise water flow and usage data for environmental monitoring in agricultural and industrial settings. The site features a comprehensive decision-support system with high-precision weather and soil monitoring. Our Elzian-Agro-Mate system shows efficient soil moisture management and adaptive irrigation, and our Hydroponic systems demonstrate water-efficient farming, enhancing crop yields and produce quality with the integration of our Elzian-Agro-Eye and Elzian-Agro-Mate systems.
Solution Provider(s): Main organization: Elzian Agro (Private) Limited , Forestry Management Partner: Earth Restoration (Private) Limited
Implementation location(s): Western Province and Central Province in Sri Lanka
Duration to pilot in a new geography: 2 - 3 months
SDGs addressed: SDG 2 (Zero Hunger);SDG 13 (Climate Action);SDG 15 (Life on Land);
Desired impact:
⦿#1. Reduction in Greenhouse Gas Emissions – Replacing synthetic nitrogen fertilizers with Azolla significantly lowers nitrous oxide emissions. Precision irrigation reduces water pumping energy use, cutting overall emissions. Studies show biofertilizers can replace up to 50% of chemical fertilizers, reducing emissions accordingly.

⦿#2. Improved Water Usage Efficiency – Our IoT-based precision irrigation optimizes water use, crucial for arid regions. It has been shown to improve efficiency by up to 95%, cut irrigation costs by 20%, and boost yields by 7%.

⦿#3. Enhanced Soil Health and Biodiversity – Regenerative practices, including vermicomposting and analog forestry, increase microbial activity, improve soil fertility, and restore native plant species, contributing to ecosystem resilience.

⦿#4. Increased Climate Resilience – Data-driven decision-making helps farmers manage pests, optimize irrigation, and adapt to climate variability. Precision agriculture enhances resilience to extreme weather, minimizing losses.

֍ 1 Year Impact:
⫸ Increase the crop yield up to more than 7%; cost-cutting 15% to 20% of the unnecessary cost related to irrigation.
⫸ Develop 5 demonstration sites in different geographical locations.
⫸ Monitoring + Automation (pilot runs): 4 Mass scale Farmlands (50+ Acre each)
⫸ Contractual - Primary Ecosystem Services (C-PES) Verification: 30+ Farmlands, 40 Tree species 

֍ 5 Year Impact:
⫸ Increase the crop yield up to more than 10%; cost-cutting 15% to 60% of the unnecessary cost related to irrigation.
⫸ Trees under blockchain-secured smart contracts for Primary Ecosystem Services (C-PES).
⫸ Cover all geographical locations ( 9 provinces) in Sri Lanka.
⫸ Reduce 0.4+ gigatons of CO2e emissions per year.
Key technologies:
⦿ Artificial Intelligence (AI) for our integrated decision support system.
⦿ Machine Learning (ML) for our integrated pest prediction system.
⦿ Internet of Things (IoT) for our integrated monitoring systems.
⦿ Blockchain for our traceability and the maintenance of our Earth Restoration LifeForce digital wallet and smart contracts with the farmers.
⦿ Unmanned Aerial Vehicle (UAV) for drone irrigation, mapping and monitoring for data collection.
⦿ GIS for our geo-tagging and farmland mapping.
Unique Characteristics:
ELZIAN AGRO provides customized precision agriculture solutions tailored to the specific needs of the target user. Our climate-smart agriculture devices offer comprehensive measurement, power efficiency, portability, and advanced control features, surpassing both conventional and modern alternatives.

1. Superior Measurement Capabilities
Our devices simultaneously measure NPK (Nitrogen, Phosphorus, Potassium), pH, electrical conductivity, temperature, humidity, covering soil, fertilizer, liquid, and atmospheric elements. Competing devices typically measure only a subset of these parameters and lack flexibility in expanding measurement capabilities.

2. Enhanced Power/Energy Efficiency
Equipped with built-in solar panels for continuous charging, our devices operate on low power (3.5V) and feature deep sleep modes to minimize energy consumption. Competing devices rely on replaceable batteries or wired sources, leading to higher idle power usage.

3. User-friendliness, Portability and Zone Control
Designed for on-the-go field testing, our devices are compact and portable, unlike bulkier alternatives built for fixed or lab use. They also support zone control for up to 8 different zones (per device), whereas most competing devices are limited to fewer zones or offer uniform timing.

4. Versatile Power and Charging Options
Our devices operate on either 12V or 24V, adaptable to customer needs, and feature a 12V 7A battery with solar charging capability. Unlike most competitors, which rely on fixed power sources, our devices can seamlessly switch between solar and 24V supply charging.

5. Advanced Control & Connectivity
Our devices function in both offline and online modes via Wi-Fi, web, and mobile apps, ensuring accessibility in remote areas. Competing devices typically support only one mode.

6. Energy-Saving Power Boost & Relay Systems
Our built-in power booster allows 24V relay control with a 12V battery, ensuring efficiency. Our direct power output system (12V or 24V) optimizes energy use, whereas competitors rely on switching relays, consuming more power.
Sustainable Change:
Our integrated precision agriculture solutions significantly contribute to Sri Lanka’s Nationally Determined Contributions (NDCs) by addressing climate mitigation, adaptation, finance, technology, and capacity development.

Mitigation: By replacing synthetic fertilizers with Azolla biofertilizer and implementing precision irrigation systems like Elzian-Agro-Mate, we reduce greenhouse gas emissions and energy consumption. These practices lower the carbon footprint of farming operations.

Adaptation: We enhance resilience to climate change through IoT-based tools like Elzian-Agro-Eye for real-time monitoring of environmental and soil conditions. These technologies enable farmers to optimize water usage, manage pests, and adopt climate-smart practices such as analog forestry and vermicomposting.

Technology: Advanced tools like AI, ML, IoT, UAVs, and GIS optimize farming efficiency. These innovations enable precise interventions in irrigation, pest control, and spatial analysis, accelerating both mitigation and adaptation efforts.

Capacity Development: Elzian Agro empowers farmers through training and user-friendly technologies, fostering sustainable practices. Initiatives like analog forestry and vermicomposting enhance biodiversity conservation and soil health management, ensuring long-term resilience in Sri Lanka’s agricultural sector.
