Title: SkillUp Africa: Driving Inclusive Growth Through Digital Empowerment
Subtitle: A digital skills and entrepreneurship program equipping underserved youth and women in Africa for meaningful participation in the digital economy.
Problem Statement: In Kenya, communities in Kibera (Nairobi), Kitui, and northeastern counties face limited access to quality, affordable digital skills training. While urban centers like Nairobi have basic connectivity, informal settlements and rural regions lack inclusive infrastructure and locally relevant digital learning platforms. Youth, especially young women, encounter multiple barriers—including gender norms, digital illiteracy, and limited access to devices or mentorship—hindering their participation in the digital economy. These challenges deepen unemployment, poverty, and inequality.
Solution Overview:
Solution Overview
SkillUp Africa is a grassroots digital empowerment initiative designed to equip marginalized youth and women in underserved regions—including Kibera (Nairobi), Kitui, and parts of northeastern Kenya—with practical digital skills, entrepreneurial knowledge, and job readiness training. The solution uses a blended learning model that combines mobile-first digital content with in-person mentorship and community-based hubs to ensure accessibility, relevance, and sustainability.

How It Works
Learners are enrolled through local community outreach and undergo modular training in areas such as digital literacy, online work, basic coding, entrepreneurship, and financial inclusion. The program includes both online self-paced content and facilitated in-person sessions delivered through partner organizations or trained local mentors.

a. Methodologies and Technologies

Human-centered instructional design tailored to low-literacy and low-resource settings
Mobile-friendly LMS platforms (Moodle, Rise 360) and offline learning kits
SMS-based microlearning and WhatsApp for learner support

b. AI-enabled career guidance chatbot (pilot)

Gamified learning modules and digital storytelling for engagement
Blockchain-based certification for learner records and credentials (in testing phase)

c. Partnerships and Collaboration Models:

Local community organizations and youth groups for learner mobilization and support
TVET institutions and ICT hubs for technical training delivery
Government agencies like the Youth Enterprise Development Fund and Ajira Digital for policy alignment and job linkages
Private sector partners for mentorship, digital tools, and internship pathways
Donors and NGOs supporting funding, scalability, and evaluation
Solution Provider(s): Impact Frontiers (Community-Based Organization, youth and women empowerment, civil society sector), Ajira Digital Program – Ministry of ICT and the Digital Economy (Government initiative, digital skills and online work, public sector), Youth Enterprise Development Fund (YEDF) (Government agency supporting youth entrepreneurship, public sector), SafeSpace Africa (NGO focused on mental health and gender-based empowerment, civil society sector), Kitui ICT Innovation Hub (Local tech hub providing ICT training and community innovation support, private-public partnership), TotoSci Africa (STEM and digital education provider for underrepresented communities, education/technology sector), Digital Opportunity Trust Kenya (DOT Kenya) (NGO fostering digital inclusion and youth leadership, civil society sector)
Implementation location(s): Kenya – Kibera (Nairobi County), Kitui Town (Kitui County), and pilot outreach in Wajir and Garissa (Northeastern Kenya)
Duration to pilot in a new geography: Approximately 3 to 4 months, including needs assessment, stakeholder onboarding, localization of content, capacity building, and initial training rollout.
SDGs addressed: SDG 1 (No Poverty);SDG 5 (Gender Equality);SDG 8 (Decent Work and Economic Growth);
Desired impact:
Desired Impact of the Solution

Solution Objectives:
SkillUp Africa aims to bridge the digital divide by equipping marginalized youth and women—especially in informal settlements and rural counties—with the digital literacy, entrepreneurial skills, and mentorship needed to access dignified work, start businesses, and contribute to the local digital economy.

Key Achievements / Impacts:

1. Trained over 500 youth and women in foundational and intermediate digital skills across Nairobi (Kibera), Kitui, and Northeastern Kenya
2. Facilitated 150+ work linkages through internships, freelancing, or job placements
3. Supported 25+ youth-led microenterprises with digital business skills, startup kits, or funding referrals
4. Maintained an average 60% female participation rate
5. Improved digital literacy scores among participants by 70% (pre/post assessments)
6. Created local digital champions to extend impact through peer mentoring and community outreach
Key technologies:
SkillUp Africa integrates a mix of accessible and innovative technologies to ensure inclusive, scalable learning:

1. Mobile-First Learning Management Systems (LMS): Platforms like Moodle and Rise 360 deliver interactive, self-paced training accessible via smartphones, even in low-bandwidth environments.
2. SMS-Based Microlearning: For learners in areas with limited internet access, SMS delivery supports lesson summaries, quizzes, and reminders.
3. WhatsApp & Chatbots: AI-powered chatbots (pilot stage) offer career guidance and learner support via WhatsApp, improving engagement and personalized learning pathways.
4. Gamified eLearning & Digital Storytelling: Tools like Vyond and Articulate Storyline are used to make learning interactive, relatable, and engaging, especially for low-literacy users.
5. Blockchain-Based Certification: Piloted for issuing tamper-proof digital certificates to enhance credibility and job market acceptance of learners’ credentials.
6. Data Dashboards & Analytics: Used to track learner progress, generate reports, and inform real-time program adjustments.
Unique Characteristics:
Unique/Differentiated Characteristics:
SkillUp Africa stands out through its community-driven, gender-responsive, and tech-enabled approach to digital inclusion. Key differentiators include:

Female-First Design: Training schedules, content, and mentorship are tailored to accommodate the needs of young women, including flexible learning options, safe spaces, and female-led facilitation.

Last-Mile Accessibility: Combines mobile-first LMS, SMS microlearning, and offline kits to reach learners in low-connectivity and rural areas, especially in Kitui and Northeastern Kenya.

Hybrid Delivery Model: Merges digital training with localized, in-person mentorship via community-based hubs and partners—ensuring both reach and depth of learning.

Inclusive Partnerships: Leverages cross-sector collaboration—civil society, government agencies (like Ajira & YEDF), local TVETs, and grassroots organizations—to localize and scale impact.

Sustainable MSME Integration: Links youth to digital microenterprise development through entrepreneurship training, digital marketing, and funding referrals.

Credential Innovation: Pilots blockchain-backed digital certificates to boost job-readiness and verifiability of learner achievements in both formal and informal labor markets.

Low-Cost Scalability: Designed to scale with minimal infrastructure investment using existing community networks and open-source technologies.
Sustainable Change:
How the Solution Contributes to Sustainable, Systemic Change (Theory of Change):
SkillUp Africa creates sustainable, systemic change by equipping underserved youth and women with relevant digital skills, entrepreneurial capacity, and job readiness—laying the foundation for inclusive participation in the digital economy.

The solution’s Theory of Change is grounded in the belief that when marginalized communities gain access to market-aligned digital learning and supportive ecosystems, they can become agents of change in their own local economies.

Key systemic effects include:

Empowered youth-led ecosystems: Trained youth become digital champions, peer mentors, or MSME founders, fostering a culture of innovation and skills transfer within their communities.

Reduced gender and regional disparities: By intentionally targeting rural and peri-urban areas, especially women, the model closes gaps in access to technology, training, and income opportunities.

Stronger local economies: MSMEs benefit from digital enablement, leading to increased productivity, job creation, and resilience.

Institutional learning: Collaborations with local TVETs and policy bodies help embed inclusive digital skills training into government and NGO frameworks.

Scalability with community ownership: Community-driven implementation ensures adaptability and long-term sustainability without dependence on external actors.

In the long term, the solution contributes to a more inclusive, digitally skilled workforce that drives economic growth, innovation, and social equity across Kenya and beyond.
Funding Sources:
Grants from nonprofit organizations and foundations supporting digital inclusion and youth empowerment

In-kind contributions from implementation partners such as training venues, volunteer trainers, and digital platforms

Public-sector collaboration, offering access to content, outreach support, and program alignment

Internal organizational fundraising, including proposal development, resource mobilization, and community-based support
Primary thematic focus area: Inclusive Digital Innovation Skills & Entrepreneurial Talent Development
Summary: SkillUp Africa is a grassroots digital empowerment initiative providing mobile-first training, mentorship, and entrepreneurial support to underserved youth and women in Kenya. Using blended models (online/offline), SMS microlearning, WhatsApp chatbots, and blockchain certification, it delivers market-relevant digital literacy, coding, entrepreneurship, and financial skills. Piloted in Kibera, Kitui, and Northeastern Kenya, it has already trained 500+ youth and women, facilitated 150+ job placements, and supported 25+ youth-led microenterprises. The initiative emphasizes gender inclusion (60% female participation), last-mile accessibility, and cross-sector partnerships to scale digital and economic empowerment sustainably.

Title: Ability Meets Opportunity: Uganda’s women and female youth with disabilities online
Subtitle: "Ability Meets Opportunity" is a targeted intervention designed to advance digital inclusion for Ugandan women and female youth with disabilities by providing tailored skills training, accessible technologies, and sustained access to digital platforms, enabling their active participation in the inclusive digital economy.
Problem Statement:
Women with disabilities in Wakiso District face significant digital exclusion, despite the widespread digitalization of basic, social, and public services in Uganda, including healthcare, education, financial services, and government platforms (Uganda Ministry of ICT, 2023). Nationally, only 19% of women use the internet compared to 27% of men, with women with disabilities encountering even greater barriers to accessing digital technologies and services (Data for SDGs, 2023; Paradigm Initiative, 2022). 

Persons with disabilities, who represent approximately 12% of Uganda’s population, account for 22% of the unemployed and often live in households with poverty rates 30% higher than the national average (DevInit, 2021). Uganda’s digital skills readiness stands at a low 33%, limiting the ability of these women to engage with essential digital platforms such as mobile internet, digital payments, e-commerce, and e-government services (UNCDF, 2021). 

Moreover, women with disabilities are frequently excluded from digital policy frameworks and data collection efforts, resulting in inadequate inclusive program implementation (G3ICT, 2022; DevInit, 2021). These challenges are further exacerbated by economic inequality, entrenched gender and disability biases, insufficient ICT infrastructure, and weak enforcement of legal protections (ActionAid Uganda, 2023). 

The “Ability Meets Opportunity” initiative addresses these systemic barriers by providing targeted digital skills training, accessible technologies, and sustained support, complemented by community engagement and policy advocacy to promote meaningful and sustainable digital inclusion for women with disabilities in Wakiso District.
Solution Overview:
A Detailed Description of How the Solution Works
“Ability Meets Opportunity” is a comprehensive, multi-dimensional initiative aimed at closing the digital divide for women and female youth with disabilities in Wakiso District by tackling barriers related to access, skills development, and systemic exclusion. The program delivers tailored digital skills training designed to meet the diverse needs of participants, covering essential competencies such as basic device operation, internet navigation, online safety, mobile money usage, digital entrepreneurship, e-government services, and remote work capabilities. Training is provided in accessible formats, including screen readers, sign language interpretation, and simplified visual aids to ensure inclusivity. Participants receive assistive technologies—such as adapted smartphones, Braille displays, hearing aids, and voice recognition software—and benefit from affordable internet connectivity through partnerships with local service providers. To sustain digital engagement and skills application, the program establishes peer support networks, mentorship by digital champions with disabilities, and helpdesk services for ongoing technical assistance. The initiative also conducts community awareness campaigns to challenge stigma and entrenched gender and disability biases, while engaging local government, disability organizations, and service providers to advocate for inclusive digital policies, infrastructure improvements, and enforcement of disability rights.

The “Ability Meets Opportunity” initiative adopts a strategic, inclusive approach to skills development, employing participatory and learner-centered methodologies anchored in Universal Design for Learning (UDL) principles. Designed to meet the diverse needs of women and female youth with disabilities, the program delivers tailored instruction through multiple modes of representation, engagement, and expression. A blended learning model—incorporating in-person workshops, mobile learning, and radio outreach—ensures broad accessibility across both high- and low-connectivity settings. Training will be provided in accessible formats, including sign language, screen reader-compatible materials, and simplified visuals, supported by a comprehensive suite of assistive technologies such as NVDA, JAWS, Braille displays, and accessible mobile devices. Peer interaction and community-building will be fostered through commonly used digital platforms like WhatsApp, Telegram, and Facebook. To support practical outcomes, the program links training to digital public services and financial platforms, including e-government systems and MTN Mobile Money. 

Partnerships and Collaboration Models 
The success of the “Ability Meets Opportunity” initiative is anchored in inclusive, cross-sector collaboration, drawing on the strengths of diverse partners to advance digital inclusion for women and female youth with disabilities. Central to this approach are partnerships with local and national Disabled Persons Organizations (DPOs), which co-design training, identify participants, and ensure disability-inclusive practices. The initiative works closely with government bodies—including the Ministry of ICT and National Guidance, Ministry of Gender, Labour and Social Development, and Wakiso District local government—to align with national digital strategies and leverage public infrastructure. Collaborations with technology and internet service providers support access to affordable, accessible devices and connectivity, while civil society organizations contribute to advocacy, awareness, and community engagement. Academic and research institutions provide data and policy insights, and private sector actors, social enterprises, donors, and impact investors help secure financial sustainability and integrate digital skills within broader economic empowerment frameworks. This collaborative model ensures relevance, scalability, and long-term systemic impact.

Sector: Disability Rights and ICT.  Wakiso Women Empowerment Network (WWEN): A community-based organization focused on advancing the social and economic rights of women and female youth in Wakiso District. Sector: Gender Equality and Community Development.  Ministry of ICT and National Guidance, Uganda: Government agency responsible for national ICT policy formulation, digital infrastructure development, and coordination of digital inclusion initiatives. Sector: Government/Public Sector.  MTN Uganda: Leading telecommunications company providing internet connectivity and digital financial services across Uganda. Sector: Education and Research.  ActionAid Uganda: International NGO working on gender justice, disability inclusion, and poverty alleviation through community mobilization and advocacy. Sector: Human Rights and Development.
Duration to pilot in a new geography: 24 months
SDGs addressed: SDG 1 (No Poverty);SDG 5 (Gender Equality);SDG 10 (Reduced Inequalities);
Desired impact:
Desired Impact of the Solution
“Ability Meets Opportunity” aims to empower women and female youth with disabilities in Wakiso District by fostering equitable access to digital technologies, enhancing digital literacy, and promoting sustainable economic participation in Uganda’s digital economy. The initiative seeks to reduce systemic barriers, promote social inclusion, and contribute to poverty alleviation by enabling beneficiaries to leverage digital platforms for education, entrepreneurship, employment, and access to essential services.

Solution Objectives
Enhance Digital Literacy: Provide tailored, disability-inclusive digital skills training to at least 1,000 women and female youth with disabilities in Wakiso District within the first two years.

Increase Access to Assistive Technologies: Distribute accessible digital devices and assistive technologies to participants, ensuring 90% have reliable tools to engage effectively with digital platforms.

Facilitate Affordable Connectivity: Partner with internet service providers to subsidize data packages and expand affordable internet access for 95% of program beneficiaries.

Strengthen Support Networks: Establish ongoing mentorship, peer support groups, and technical helpdesk services to sustain skills application and promote confidence in digital environments.

Influence Policy and Community Norms: Engage local government, disability organizations, and communities to advocate for inclusive digital policies and reduce stigma, aiming for measurable improvements in policy implementation and social attitudes.

Desired Achievements or Impacts
Within a 24-month implementation period, the “Ability Meets Opportunity” initiative aims to deliver measurable and sustainable outcomes for women and female youth with disabilities in Wakiso District. The program seeks to train over 200 participants in foundational and advanced digital skills, with at least 85% demonstrating measurable improvements in digital literacy, usability of assistive technologies, and the confidence to independently navigate digital platforms.

As a result of targeted capacity building, the initiative envisions at least 50 women securing digital-based employment, remote work, or establishing online micro-enterprises, contributing to increased economic self-reliance and local digital entrepreneurship among persons with disabilities.

The project also targets a significant shift in digital adoption, aiming to increase internet use among participants from below 20% to at least 75%, enabling consistent access to digital public services, including e-government platforms, online education, health information systems, and mobile financial services.

To address accessibility gaps, the program will distribute a minimum of 200 assistive technology devices, such as screen readers, Braille-enabled tools, adapted mobile phones, and hearing aids, ensuring women with sensory, physical, or cognitive disabilities can engage fully with digital tools and services.

At the community level, the initiative will conduct 15 targeted sensitization campaigns aimed at reducing stigma and shifting negative social norms. These are expected to result in at least a 40% improvement in community attitudes towards women with disabilities participating in digital and economic spaces.

On the policy front, the program will engage local and district stakeholders to influence the inclusion of disability-responsive measures in at least two district-level digital inclusion strategies. This advocacy will promote long-term systems change and institutional commitment to inclusive digital development.

Finally, the initiative anticipates that beneficiaries will experience an average income increase of 25%, within the project period, attributable to increased digital access, improved employment opportunities, and strengthened digital entrepreneurship skills.
Key technologies: The key technologies underpinning the “Ability Meets Opportunity” initiative focus on enhancing accessibility, connectivity, and user engagement for women and female youth with disabilities. These include assistive technologies such as screen readers (e.g., NVDA, JAWS), Braille displays, speech-to-text and text-to-speech tools, and mobile devices pre-configured with accessibility features like voice control and magnification. The initiative employs a blended learning platform combining mobile-based learning modules, radio broadcasts, and in-person workshops to ensure broad reach across varied connectivity environments. While the solution does not currently incorporate advanced technologies like AI, IoT, or blockchain, it leverages widely accessible digital communication platforms (e.g., WhatsApp, Telegram, Facebook) to facilitate peer support and community engagement. Additionally, integration with e-government services and digital financial systems (such as MTN Mobile Money) supports practical application of digital skills, fostering economic empowerment within an inclusive digital ecosystem.
Unique Characteristics: The “Ability Meets Opportunity” initiative stands out through its comprehensive, inclusive design that specifically targets women and female youth with diverse disabilities, an often-underserved demographic in digital skills programs. Its uniqueness lies in the integration of Universal Design for Learning (UDL) principles, ensuring training is fully accessible and tailored to individual learning needs through multiple modalities. The blended learning model, combining in-person, mobile, and radio delivery, innovatively addresses connectivity challenges across urban and remote areas. Strategic partnerships with Disabled Persons Organizations, government agencies, technology providers, civil society, academia, and the private sector create a collaborative ecosystem that aligns digital inclusion with national policies and sustainable economic empowerment. Furthermore, the program’s use of assistive technologies alongside accessible digital platforms fosters meaningful participation and peer support, while its rights-based, data-driven monitoring framework ensures accountability and continuous improvement. This multi-dimensional approach combines inclusive pedagogy, diverse delivery methods, strong partnerships, and practical digital integration, differentiates the solution as both innovative and scalable.
Sustainable Change: The “Ability Meets Opportunity” initiative drives sustainable, systemic change by empowering women and female youth with disabilities through inclusive digital skills development, enabling their meaningful participation in the digital economy and society. By applying Universal Design for Learning principles and accessible technologies, the program ensures equitable access to training, fostering increased digital literacy and confidence among participants. Through strong partnerships with government, civil society, and the private sector, the initiative aligns with national policies and integrates beneficiaries into existing digital platforms and services, promoting long-term inclusion. The anticipated follow-on effects include enhanced economic empowerment, improved access to public and financial digital services, and strengthened social networks that support ongoing learning and advocacy. Over time, these outcomes contribute to shifting societal attitudes, reducing barriers, and embedding disability-inclusive practices within institutional frameworks, thereby creating a replicable model that catalyzes broad digital inclusion and drives systemic transformation.
Funding Sources: It was first funded by Defend Defenders Organisation who funded the training of 10 women and female youth with disabilities in digital security training.
Primary thematic focus area: Inclusive Digital Innovation Skills & Entrepreneurial Talent Development
Summary: ‘Ability Meets Opportunity’ is an inclusive digital literacy and empowerment initiative targeting women and female youth with disabilities in Uganda’s Wakiso District. It combines skills training, assistive technologies, affordable connectivity, and systemic advocacy. Strengths: deep contextual relevance, strong disability-inclusive design (UDL principles, multi-modal learning, assistive tech), and broad multi-sector partnerships. Weaknesses: still at idea/concept stage with minimal track record, resource limitations, and unclear long-term funding model beyond initial support.

Title: ReLink: Empowering Digital Access, Visibility & Job Creation
Subtitle: Addressing youth unemployment and MSME digital exclusion through a dual-impact model: local youth earn income by helping small businesses build digital presence via mobile-friendly tools.
Problem Statement: Across developing economies, over 400 million micro and small enterprises lack digital presence, limiting their market reach and economic resilience. At the same time, 73 million youth globally face unemployment despite possessing digital literacy skills. This Interlinked challenges perpetuates economic inequality and undermines inclusive growth. ReLink addresses this systemic challenge through an innovative workforce development model that transforms unemployed youth into Digital Guides who provide accessible digitization services to underserved MSMEs, creating sustainable employment while enabling business growth.
Solution Overview:
Solution Overview
ReLink is a community-powered digital platform that bridges the digital divide for underserved local businesses and informal workers by providing them with mobile-optimized microsites and searchable profiles. Through a Digital Guide Job Creation Model, ReLink trains local youth to identify, onboard, and support these micro-entrepreneurs, transforming digital inclusion into scalable employment.
How It Works:
Digital Guides use ReLink's web/mobile app to discover and onboard informal businesses without an online presence. They help create simple profile pages that include photos, services, pricing, and contact options. Consumers can then search by category, location, or keywords to discover and connect with service providers in their vicinity. Guides earn rewards based on verified sign-ups, engagement metrics, and impact delivered.
Core Technologies:

Frontend: React + Tailwind CSS for responsive, mobile-first UI
Backend: Supabase for real-time database, authentication, and storage
AI tools: Help Guides auto-generate content like business descriptions and tags
Offline-first capability: Enables onboarding in low-connectivity areas
Gamification: Encourages Guide performance through points and levels

Partnerships & Collaboration:

Local NGOs & Cooperatives: e.g., Fantsuam Foundation (Kaduna) for grassroots mobilization and training
State and Local Governments: e.g., KADEDA (Kaduna) and Kano State Ministry of Commerce for MSME digitization and youth job creation
SMEDAN: Enables ReLink to support national MSME programs with data, tools, and inclusion pathways
GIZ-DTC Nigeria: Offers innovation bootcamps and digital transformation mentorship
Solution Provider(s): Relink Technologies Limited (Lead technology developer and implementer, digital innovation for social impact sector, Nigeria), Fantsuam Foundation (Rural development NGO specializing in ICT for Development and community empowerment, based in Kaduna State, Nigeria), Kaduna State Enterprise Development Agency (KADEDA) (State government agency focused on youth employment and MSME development programs), Kano State Ministry of Commerce (Public sector partner enabling local business digitization and economic development initiatives), Small and Medium Enterprises Development Agency of Nigeria (SMEDAN) (Federal government agency supporting micro, small and medium enterprise growth and formalization), GIZ - Digital Transformation Center Nigeria (GIC-DTC Nigeria) (Innovation hub advancing inclusive digital transformation and technology entrepreneurship), Youth and Women Cooperatives Network (Community-based organizations facilitating grassroots mobilization and Digital Guide recruitment across target communities)
Implementation location(s): Current Locations: Kaduna State, Nigeria – Initial pilot implementation in communities across Kaduna South LGA and Chikun LGA, including collaboration with local cooperatives and youth associations for onboarding Digital Guides and MSMEs. Kano State, Nigeria – Ongoing onboarding and field testing in Nasarawa LGA and Kumbotso LGA, with support from community-based organizations and state commerce agencies.
Implementation timeline(s): Pilot Start: March 2024 Current Phase: Ongoing scaling and refinement (as of May 2025),  June 2024 – First cohort of Digital Guides trained in Kaduna,  August 2024 – Launch of MVP platform and first user profiles onboarded,  March 2025 – Expansion into Kano State
Duration to pilot in a new geography: 6–9 months, including 1 month for stakeholder engagement, 2 months for Digital Guide recruitment and training, 3–6 months for onboarding and field testing.
SDGs addressed: SDG 1 (No Poverty);SDG 8 (Decent Work and Economic Growth);SDG 9 (Industry, Innovation, and Infrastructure);
Desired impact:
Solution Objectives:

Bridge the digital divide for underserved businesses and informal workers
Create youth employment through the Digital Guide Model
Improve visibility and customer access for local MSMEs
Promote inclusive digital transformation at the grassroots level

Key Achievements & Impact (as of July 2025):

120+ local businesses onboarded across pilot communities in Kaduna and Kano States
25+ Digital Guides trained with 15 actively earning supplementary income through ReLink
70% of onboarded businesses report receiving new customer inquiries within first month
45+ women-led enterprises now have their first online presence through the platform
8 cooperatives and trade associations have adopted ReLink for member visibility
Partnership established with KADEDA for integration into youth employment programs
Pilot recognition by SMEDAN as innovative approach to MSME digitization
Key technologies:
AI (Artificial Intelligence): Auto-generates business descriptions, service tags, and suggestions to assist Digital Guides in creating engaging profiles
Mobile-First Progressive Web App (PWA): Built using React, Tailwind CSS for fast, responsive, offline-capable experiences
Supabase Backend (PostgreSQL + Realtime DB): Provides secure authentication, real-time data syncing, and scalable infrastructure
Offline Functionality & Data Sync: Ensures onboarding continues in low-connectivity environments
Geo-Tagging & Mapping Tools: Uses GPS and map APIs for location-based service discovery
Gamification System: Incentivizes Digital Guides via point-based progress and reward system
Unique Characteristics:
ReLink is unique in combining no-code digital tools with a built-in job creation strategy. It's more than just a platform — it's a movement powered by local Digital Guides who activate adoption in underserved areas. Key differentiators include:

Digital Guide Job Creation Model: Transforms digital inclusion into youth employment opportunities
Community-Led & Hyperlocal Approach: Uses boots-on-the-ground model ensuring grassroots inclusion
Offline-First & Low-Bandwidth Design: Built for intermittent connectivity and rural areas
AI-Assisted Onboarding: Helps Guides generate compelling content faster
Public-Private-Community Ecosystem: Strategic collaboration enhances trust, scale, and sustainability
Built-in Impact Metrics & Gamification: Transparent incentive model ensures accountability
Sustainable Change:
Theory of Change: Sustainable Systemic Impact

Immediate Inputs & Activities:

Recruit and train local youth as Digital Guides. Partner with grassroots NGOs, cooperatives, and government agencies. Deploy the ReLink platform to support offline and online MSME onboarding.
Short-Term Outcomes:
Thousands of informal businesses gain digital identity. Digital Guides earn income, increasing youth livelihood opportunities. Consumers easily find and connect with local services online.
Medium-Term Systemic Outcomes:
MSME digitization increases across underserved communities, enhancing market access and income. Youth workforce grows in digital economy with transferable skills. ReLink becomes real-time economic visibility tool for governments, aiding policy planning and resource targeting.
Long-Term Systemic Change:
Digital exclusion reduces as visibility and digital trust improve across the informal sector. Self-reinforcing ecosystem created where public and private actors co-invest in youth-led digital enablement. ReLink data supports national economic mapping and evidence-based policymaking.

Community-driven approach (locals recruit locals)
Offline-first tech built for real-world challenges
Integration with existing systems rather than bypassing them

Local 'Digital Guides' are trained to onboard small businesses onto ReLink, creating microsites and searchable profiles, thereby generating income for youth and visibility for businesses. Title: Incmenda d’ Terra
Subtitle: Incmenda d’ Terra” embodies the mission to connect tourists and consumers with authentic Cape Verdean products from the land, promoting culture, tradition, and local sustainability. It also supports family economies and fosters digital inclusion in the financial sector among artisans and farmers.
Problem Statement:
Cape Verde has a population of approximately 526,000–527,000 inhabitants and over 1 million emigrants living abroad, many of whom visit the country every year. Additionally, Cape Verde welcomes more than 1 million tourists annually, making tourism one of the nation’s most significant economic pillars.
However, small local producers, especially women who are heads of households and create cultural and artisanal products, struggle to access these lucrative markets. Many tourists stay in large hotels with limited exposure to authentic local goods. At the same time, small producers lack the digital tools and structured channels to connect with visitors or sell their products effectively.
This disconnect limits income generation, reduces opportunities for cultural promotion, and hinders digital and financial inclusion in rural communities.
The project aims to establish a digital ecosystem that connects small local producers with tourists and emigrants, thereby promoting Cape Verdean culture, strengthening family economies, and driving digital inclusion across various sectors, including artisanal and agricultural.
Solution Overview:
The proposed solution is the creation of a comprehensive digital platform that connects small local producers from every island in Cape Verde with tourists, emigrants, and national consumers. The platform will serve as a centralised marketplace where all producers can register and showcase their products online.

How it works:

Producer Registration & Product Validation: Producers from all islands will register on the platform, and all listed products will go through a validation process to ensure quality standards and authenticity.

Customer Purchase: Clients (tourists, emigrants, or locals) browse the catalogue and place orders online, paying directly through a secure payment gateway integrated into the platform.

Real-Time Order Assignment: The system automatically identifies the producer with the requested product in stock.

Centralized Processing: Before delivery, products are collected from producers and sent to a central hub on each island. Here, orders are packaged with customized kits that highlight Cape Verde’s culture and identity.

Delivery: Orders are delivered by a specialized logistics team. Customers can also purchase products from islands they are not visiting, as the platform will be integrated with the Cape Verde Post Office (Correios de Cabo Verde) for national and international deliveries.

Methodologies & Technologies:

Technologies: Cloud-based e-commerce platform, real-time inventory management, QR Code integration, secure digital payments, and tracking systems for logistics.

Methodology: Agile development with continuous validation of producers and products to ensure quality and authenticity.


Collaboration Models:

Central hubs on each island will manage quality control, packaging, and distribution.

A dedicated logistics team will handle last-mile delivery, ensuring reliable and timely service.

Partnerships with financial institutions will facilitate digital and financial inclusion for small producers, especially women-led businesses in rural areas.

This integrated solution not only connects producers directly to tourists and emigrants but also creates a robust ecosystem that promotes Cape Verdean culture, supports family economies, and drives sustainable community development.
Solution Provider(s): Ministry of Agriculture and Environment (MAA) (Government & Agriculture), Ministry of Tourism and Transport (MTT) (Government & Tourism), Correios de Cabo Verde (National Postal Service) (Logistics & Postal Services), Producers’ Associations and Local Cooperatives (Agriculture & Artisanal Production), Hotels, Airports and Tourist Agencies in Cape Verde (Tourism & Hospitality), Cultural NGOs (Culture & Creative Industries), Pro-Empresa (Institute for Business Promotion) (Entrepreneurship & Business Support), Câmara de Comércio de Sotavento e Barlavento (Chambers of Commerce) (Business Development), IEFP – Instituto do Emprego e Formação Profissional (Employment & Training), Universidade de Cabo Verde (Uni-CV) and other Higher Education Institutions (Research & Innovation), Financial Institutions and Microcredit Organizations (Digital & Financial Inclusion).
Duration to pilot in a new geography: We estimate that the pilot phase of our solution in a new geography will take approximately 6 to 9 months. This period includes the following key activities:  Months 1-2: Local market research, stakeholder engagement, and registration of producers in the new region.  Months 3-4: Platform customization and integration with local logistics and payment systems.  Months 5-6: Launch of pilot operations, including onboarding producers, activating sales channels, and initiating marketing campaigns.  Months 7-9: Monitoring, data collection, user feedback, and iterative improvements to optimize the platform and delivery operations.  This timeline ensures a controlled, scalable rollout with sufficient time for adaptation to local specificities, guaranteeing quality and customer satisfaction while minimizing risks.
SDGs addressed: SDG 5 (Gender Equality);SDG 8 (Decent Work and Economic Growth);SDG 9 (Industry, Innovation, and Infrastructure);
Desired impact:
The Incmenda d’ Terra project aims to establish a scalable and sustainable digital platform that empowers small-scale local producers—particularly women-led family businesses—by connecting them directly with tourists, emigrants, and national consumers across Cape Verde. The solution promotes authentic cultural products while driving economic inclusion, digital literacy, and financial access in underserved rural communities. By leveraging innovative technology, efficient logistics, and strict quality control, the project fosters entrepreneurship, preserves Cape Verde’s cultural heritage, and opens new revenue streams through expanded market access.

Expected Impact and Key Achievements:

Job creation: Generate sustainable employment opportunities for over 200 local producers and artisans, emphasizing youth and women's empowerment.

Income growth: Increase earnings for small producers through direct sales and fair trade practices, reducing economic disparities.

Digital & financial inclusion: Enhance adoption of digital tools and online payment systems among rural producers, enabling broader financial participation.

Cultural preservation & promotion: Strengthen Cape Verdean identity and cultural tourism by showcasing authentic, high-quality products to tourists and the diaspora.

Sustainable economic development: Support balanced regional growth by improving market access and fostering resilient local economies.
Key technologies:
Our platform leverages a suite of modern, robust technologies designed to ensure security, scalability, and sustainability, enabling effective connection between local producers and consumers:

Cloud Computing: Utilized for hosting the e-commerce platform, providing high availability, scalability, and cost-effective infrastructure management to support growth across all islands.

Responsive Web and Mobile Applications: Built using modern frameworks (e.g., React.js, Next.js) to deliver seamless, user-friendly experiences for producers and customers on multiple devices.

Secure Payment Gateways: Integration with trusted digital payment systems to enable safe, transparent, and efficient online transactions, fostering financial inclusion.

Real-Time Inventory and Order Management: Automated tracking of product availability across producers, ensuring accurate order fulfilment and optimized logistics.

QR Code Technology: Enables easy product access and purchase via displays in tourist hotspots, enhancing customer engagement and omnichannel presence.

Data Analytics and Reporting: Tools for monitoring sales, customer behavior, and supply chain performance, supporting informed decision-making and continuous improvement.

Cybersecurity Measures: Implementation of encryption, secure authentication (e.g., multi-factor authentication), and compliance with data protection standards to safeguard user data and build trust.

API Integration with Logistics Partners: Seamless connection with Correios de Cabo Verde and other delivery services to enable efficient, trackable shipments both locally and internationally.
Unique Characteristics:
Incmenda d’ Terra is not just a marketplace; it is a transformative ecosystem that redefines how Cape Verdean cultural heritage and local entrepreneurship thrive in the digital age. Unlike traditional commerce models, our platform uniquely integrates a multi-island network of small producers, ensuring authentic products are curated, validated, and delivered with uncompromising quality.

Our innovative omnichannel approach combines cutting-edge e-commerce technology with strategic physical touchpoints—QR code-enabled displays in key tourist hubs, bridging the gap between digital convenience and tactile cultural experience. This hybrid model ensures accessibility for tourists and locals alike, regardless of geography.

Moreover, our partnership-driven model empowers small-scale producers, especially women-led family businesses, by facilitating fair trade, digital and financial inclusion, and capacity building. We integrate seamless logistics through collaborations with national postal services and local delivery teams, enabling efficient, transparent, and scalable operations.

Financially, the introduction of subscription-based packages tailored to emigrants represents a novel revenue stream that fosters sustained economic growth and strengthens the cultural ties of the diaspora to their homeland.

Long-term, Incmenda d’ Terra is poised to become a national cultural brand and economic catalyst, promoting sustainable development, preserving Cape Verde’s intangible heritage, and generating inclusive prosperity for generations. This blend of cultural preservation, innovative technology, and social impact positions our solution as a flagship project aligned with global Sustainable Development Goals and funding priorities.
Sustainable Change:
Incmenda d’ Terra is designed to ignite a transformative ripple effect across Cape Verde’s social, economic, and cultural landscapes. By bridging the gap between small local producers and global consumers through innovative digital platforms and strategic partnerships, our solution lays the foundation for enduring, systemic change.

At its core, the solution empowers marginalized producers, especially women-led family businesses, fostering economic inclusion, digital literacy, and fair trade practices that uplift entire communities. As producers gain direct market access and increased income, a virtuous cycle of entrepreneurship, skill development, and community resilience is triggered.

The integration of technology and logistics modernizes traditional commerce, enhancing transparency, efficiency, and scalability. This catalyzes a sustainable local economy that values cultural heritage and environmental stewardship, ensuring long-term prosperity without sacrificing identity.

Furthermore, by connecting the diaspora and tourists to authentic Cape Verdean products, Incmenda d’ Terra strengthens cultural pride and global awareness, creating a dynamic brand that fuels tourism and export growth.

The follow-on effects include:

Empowered, digitally skilled producers with sustainable livelihoods.

Strengthened local economies with diversified income streams.

Enhanced cultural preservation and international visibility.

Inclusive growth that narrows economic and gender gaps.

A replicable model of community-driven innovation and sustainability.
Funding Sources: Until now, all development and preliminary work related to the project have been fully funded by the four founding partners. This self-financing approach has enabled us to advance key activities, including market research, concept development, initial platform design, and stakeholder engagement. No external funding has been received to date, highlighting the commitment and confidence of the founders in the project's potential.
Primary thematic focus area: MSME Empowerment & Local Digital Innovation
Summary: Incmenda d’ Terra is a digital ecosystem designed to connect Cape Verdean small producers—especially women-led artisans and farmers—with tourists, emigrants, and national consumers. The platform serves as a multi-island marketplace integrating product validation, logistics, cultural packaging, and digital payments. By leveraging partnerships with government, postal services, and financial institutions, the project promotes local entrepreneurship, cultural preservation, and digital inclusion.

Title: BridgeFund: Blockchain and AI for Refugee-Led Financial Inclusion
Subtitle: AI and blockchain-powered microfinance ecosystem enabling refugees and marginalized entrepreneurs to launch, grow, and repay zero-interest loans sustainably.
Problem Statement: Over 1.7 billion people lack access to formal financial services. Refugees and marginalised communities face compounded barriers—such as the lack of formal identification, credit history, or banking access—trapping them in cycles of poverty and exclusion.
Solution Overview:
BridgeFund is a digital innovation of Bridging Gaps Microloans gUG, a UNHCR Refugee-Led Innovation Fund awardee. It is a full-cycle, AI and blockchain-powered platform that equips refugees and marginalised entrepreneurs with entrepreneurial training, verified identity, and automated microloan systems.

Key Components:
- AI-powered multilingual training tailored to literacy levels and business stages.
- Blockchain-based KYC-lite identity system using biometrics, mobile authentication, and community endorsement.
- Direct microloan disbursement using blockchain smart contracts.
- Smart Pay-it-Forward zero-interest loan pool, tracked and reallocated using AI and blockchain.
- Digital wallet integration for savings, repayments, and credit scoring.
- Personalized AI mentorship and monitoring.

BridgeFund is driven by a global, volunteer-powered team with strong ecosystem partnerships, ensuring both cost-efficiency and community ownership.
Solution Provider(s): Bridging Gaps Microloans (enterpreneurship training & microloan provider), Tech To The Rescue (support directly or through accelerator program to find a suitable partners)- AI & blockchain providers, eWorkForce ( mobil app), The Information Lab (impcat dash boaerd),  refugee-led local partners (several local partners in Sub-Saharan africa and Latin America)

SDGs addressed: SDG 1 (No Poverty);SDG 8 (Decent Work and Economic Growth);SDG 5 (Gender Equality);
Desired impact:
- Train 50,000+ refugee and marginalised entrepreneurs by 2028
- Disburse 10,000+ zero-interest loans
- Sustain a self-replenishing $1M+ pay-it-forward fund
- Enable $5M+ in economic activity in marginalised communities
- Unlock $20M in inclusive capital by 2028
Key technologies: Artificial Intelligence (AI), Blockchain, Mobile Fintech/Digital Wallets
Unique Characteristics:
- Community-governed, blockchain-tracked Pay-it-Forward microloans
- Freemium model providing free access for refugees and low-income users
- AI mentorship tailored to individual business journeys
- Volunteer-powered global team reducing costs and promoting inclusion
Sustainable Change: BridgeFund builds decentralised financial ecosystems by integrating financial access, identity verification, entrepreneurship, and digital trust. It empowers communities to sustain and scale their economic participation. The model’s self-reinforcing ecosystem (pay-it-forward lending, AI-based support, blockchain transparency) creates a virtuous cycle of empowerment, reinvestment, and accountability.

Name of your organization: Initiative Africaine pour le developpement durable
Title: Bridging the Digital Divide: Empowering Youth & Women Through Digital Hubs
Subtitle: Establishment of digital hubs to train youth and women in digital skills, promote entrepreneurship, and foster inclusion in the digital economy.
Problem Statement: Many communities, especially in rural and underserved areas, face limited access to digital infrastructure, digital skills training, and economic opportunities. Youth and women are disproportionately affected by this digital divide, limiting their participation in the modern economy. The lack of digital literacy, affordable internet access, and relevant technological tools hinders inclusive development, perpetuating poverty and unemployment. This solution aims to tackle these barriers by creating accessible digital spaces that empower marginalized groups through training, connectivity, and entrepreneurship support.
Solution Overview:
Solution Overview
Our solution involves the creation of community-based digital hubs in underserved and rural areas to provide equitable access to digital tools, skills training, and entrepreneurship support for youth and women. These hubs act as local centers for digital empowerment, economic inclusion, and innovation.

1. How the Solution Works
The digital hubs are designed to function as multi-purpose centers where participants can:
•	Access the internet and digital devices (computers, tablets, printers, etc.).
•	Receive structured training in basic digital literacy, coding, e-commerce, financial inclusion, and digital entrepreneurship.
•	Participate in mentoring and incubation programs to develop and scale income-generating digital projects or small businesses.
•	Engage in awareness sessions on cyber safety, digital rights, and civic participation.
Each hub is managed by trained local facilitators and supported through a community-led approach to ensure relevance, sustainability, and ownership.

2. Methodologies and Technologies Used
•	Human-Centered Design (HCD): The solution is tailored to the specific needs of local beneficiaries through community consultations and participatory planning.
•	Blended Learning Approach: Combines in-person training with access to open educational resources (OER) and e-learning platforms.
•	Digital Tools & Platforms: Open-source software and affordable tech solutions are used to reduce costs and promote scalability.
•	Solar Power Integration: To ensure consistent access to electricity in off-grid or energy-insecure areas.
•	Monitoring & Evaluation Systems: Digital dashboards are used to track participation, outcomes, and impact over time.

3. Partnerships and Collaboration Models
•	Local Government & Community Leaders: Engage in site selection, awareness, and mobilization of participants.
•	NGOs and Development Agencies: Provide technical assistance, curriculum development, and capacity-building support.
•	Private Sector Partners: Contribute with hardware donations, mentorship programs, and funding for infrastructure.
•	Telecom Operators and ISPs: Facilitate affordable or subsidized internet access for hubs.
•	Educational Institutions: Collaborate to offer certifications and scale learning outcomes.

Sectors: ICT, education, social inclusion.  **Ministry of Posts and Digital Economy of Chad** – A government institution responsible for national digital inclusion strategies. Title: GreenGrid DigiRoots: A Circular Digital Pathway for Youth Inclusion
Subtitle: Empowering underserved Kenyan youth with digital tools, green skills, and access to circular economy opportunities.
Problem Statement: In Kenya, rural and peri-urban youth—especially those from informal settlements—face systemic exclusion from the digital economy. This is due to limited access to infrastructure, low digital literacy, and insufficient pathways into emerging green sectors such as circular economy, e-mobility, and clean energy. Consequently, youth unemployment, plastic pollution, and poverty persist, reinforcing inequality and limiting the potential for inclusive, climate-resilient development.
Solution Overview:
GreenGrid DigiRoots is a community-driven digital platform and training ecosystem designed to equip marginalized youth with the tools and networks to participate meaningfully in the green and digital economy.

How it works:

Youth are onboarded into a mobile-first platform offering localized digital literacy, circular economy education, and entrepreneurial skills.

The platform uses gamified micro-learning modules, quizzes, and badges to motivate participation.

Trained youth are then matched with opportunities—from internships and seed funding to recycling partnerships, clean energy sales, or plastic waste recovery enterprises.

A community dashboard tracks plastic collection data, micro-enterprise growth, and employment outcomes.

Methodologies and Technologies Used:

Progressive Web Application (offline-enabled for low-connectivity areas)

Mobile surveys & dashboards to track youth outcomes and plastic flows

AI-powered profiling for personalized learning and job matching

Blockchain-lite traceability in plastic-to-product pathways (pilot stage)

Partnership & Collaboration Model:

Academia: Provide technical training in green innovation (e.g., Masinde Muliro University)

Private Sector: Plastic off-takers and recyclers (e.g., TakaTaka Solutions)

Local Government: Infrastructure support and youth group mobilization

CBOs/Youth Groups: Implement grassroots outreach, mentorship, and scaling

The solution fosters inclusive digital access while promoting sustainable livelihood generation in line with SDG 8, 9, and 13.
Solution Provider(s): GreenGrid Youth Alliance – Youth-led NGO championing green jobs and civic engagement  Masinde Muliro University of Science and Technology – Renewable energy and circular economy technical partner  TakaTaka Solutions – Private sector recycling partner supporting waste valorization  DigitalMatatu – Tech firm supporting mobility data and digital infrastructure  Village Capital – Accelerator partner for youth-led green enterprises
Implementation location(s): Pilot activities conducted in Kakamega County, Kenya, specifically targeting peri-urban youth in Lurambi and Shinyalu sub-counties. Local schools, youth groups, and informal plastic collection networks were engaged in the initial co-design and field testing.
Implementation timeline(s): Initial design and field testing phase: February 2024 – June 2025 Pre-pilot and prototype trials: July 2025 – August 2025
Duration to pilot in a new geography: 3 to 6 months, depending on infrastructure availability and stakeholder onboarding. This includes contextual adaptation, digital onboarding, training of trainers, and baseline data collection.
SDGs addressed: SDG 8 (Decent Work and Economic Growth);SDG 9 (Industry, Innovation, and Infrastructure);SDG 13 (Climate Action);
Desired impact:
Solution Objectives:

Empower underserved youth and women in peri-urban Kenya with digital entrepreneurship skills.

Digitize and formalize community-based plastic waste collection through a smart platform.

Reduce plastic pollution by integrating digital tools in the circular economy.

Key Achievements / Expected Impacts (Quantifiable):

Train 1,000 youth and women in digital skills for circular entrepreneurship within 12 months.

Deploy a digital platform that registers 5,000 kg/month of plastic waste diverted from the environment.

Create 150 new green jobs directly (digital recyclers, collectors, agents) and 300+ indirectly in the first year.

Improve income for local waste collectors by 20-40% via digital visibility and direct market access.
Key technologies:
Mobile and Web-Based Platform: For digital tracking, registration, and payments to plastic collectors.

QR Code Scanning and Geo-Tagging: To record waste origin and link collectors to recycling agents.

Digital Wallet Integration: To facilitate micropayments and financial inclusion.

Data Analytics Dashboards: To track environmental impact (GHG reductions, volumes collected, etc.) in real time.
Unique Characteristics:
Inclusive Design: Co-developed with informal waste collectors, youth groups, and women-led cooperatives.

Mobile-First Technology: Adapted to low-connectivity and low-literacy users in peri-urban Kenya.

Blended Value Model: Combines social impact (jobs, skills) with environmental benefit (plastic removal).

Public-Private-Civil Collaboration: Linking local youth-led organizations with recyclers, county governments, and green startups.

Impact Tokenization (In Progress): Piloting a system to tokenize verified plastic collection as tradable social impact credits.
Sustainable Change:
Theory of Change:

Problem: Youth unemployment and plastic pollution co-exist in underserved areas, yet opportunities for digital inclusion are lacking.

Intervention: Introduce a digital platform that formalizes and financially rewards plastic collection, while delivering entrepreneurship and digital training.

Outputs: Digitally connected green micro-enterprises; plastic diverted from dumpsites; increased incomes.

Outcomes: Strengthened local circular economies, digital inclusion of youth and women, scalable model for replication across regions.

Impact: Long-term reduction in plastic pollution and youth unemployment through systemic shifts in informal waste economies and digital value chains.
Funding Sources:
The solution has primarily been self-funded by GreenGrid Youth Alliance, with additional in-kind support from local stakeholders including:

Community-based organizations (e.g., space for trainings and mobilization)

Technical volunteers (platform developers and environmental engineers)

Small grants and donations from environmentally conscious local enterprises interested in extended producer responsibility (EPR) practices

We are currently seeking strategic funding to scale up the digital infrastructure, expand coverage, and enhance the impact across multiple counties

Name of your organization: Actions Contre les Souffrances des Orphelines et des Veuves (ACSOV-ONG/RDC)
Title: Inclusion Numérique et Innovation Locale : Autonomisation des femmes et des Jeunes victimes de Guerre dans le Territoire de Nyiragongo et Ville de Goma
Subtitle: Renforcer les compétences numériques des femmes et jeunes victimes de guerre pour stimuler l'innovation, l'emploi et l'inclusion économique à Goma et Nyiragongo
Problem Statement:
A Goma et dans le Territoire de NYiragongo, les milliers de femmes et de jeunes portent encore les blessures visibles et invisibles des conflits armés. Arrachées à leurs foyers, privées d'accès à l'éducation, au travail et aux ressources de base, beaucoup luttent chaque jour pour reconstruire leur vie dans la dignité. 
Dans ce contexte, le numérique pourrait-être une passerelle vers l'espoir : un moyen de se former, de créer, d'entreprendre, de retrouver une place active dans la société. Mais ces opportunités restent hors de portée pour une grande majorité d'entre elles et eux, faute d'accès, de formation ou d'accompagnement. 
Ce manque d'inclusion numérique renforce leur isolement, perpétue la pauvreté et compromet leur avenir. Il est urgent d'agir, non seulement pour réduire la fracture numérique, mais aussi pour rendre justice à ces vies brisées, et leur ouvrir de nouvelles perspectives d'autonomie et de résilience.
Solution Overview:
1. Description détaillée du fonctionnement de la solution
Face à l’exclusion numérique qui frappe durement les femmes et les jeunes victimes des conflits à Goma et Nyiragongo, notre solution propose un parcours d’inclusion numérique adapté, humain et durable. Elle repose sur la mise en place de centres communautaires d’innovation numérique, mobiles et fixes, où les bénéficiaires recevront gratuitement des formations de base et intermédiaires en informatique, communication digitale, entrepreneuriat numérique et protection en ligne.
Ces centres ne sont pas de simples espaces d’apprentissage. Ils sont pensés comme des lieux d’écoute, de reconstruction et d’espoir, où chaque participante et chaque participant est accompagné avec bienveillance, en tenant compte de son vécu, de ses capacités et de ses rêves. En parallèle, des cycles d’ateliers pratiques permettront aux bénéficiaires de développer des microprojets digitaux (boutiques en ligne, services locaux, communication sociale, etc.), avec un accès encadré à des outils et connexions Internet.
Cette approche vise à redonner aux survivants de la guerre les moyens d’agir, de créer, de se reconstruire par le savoir et la technologie. Elle les aide non seulement à devenir compétents dans un monde numérique, mais aussi à retrouver confiance en elles/eux-mêmes, à se relever et à prendre part activement à la vie économique et sociale de leur communauté.
2. Méthodologies et technologies utilisées
Notre méthodologie repose sur une approche participative et bienveillante, axée sur l’autonomisation progressive :
-	Identification communautaire participative des bénéficiaires les plus vulnérables, en collaboration avec les leaders locaux, structures de base et centres pour déplacés.
-	Formation par modules adaptés aux réalités locales : alphabétisation numérique, bureautique, marketing digital, cybersécurité, outils collaboratifs, entrepreneuriat numérique, storytelling digital.
-	Apprentissage actif par la pratique, avec des simulations, des mini-projets collectifs, des plateformes locales d’échange, et des sessions de mentorat.
-	Suivi psychosocial discret, intégré dans l’approche pédagogique pour tenir compte des traumatismes vécus.
-	Technologies utilisées : ordinateurs portables reconditionnés, smartphones, connexions Internet locales (4G ou Wi-Fi communautaire), logiciels libres et accessibles (LibreOffice , WhatsApp Business, etc.).


3. Partenariats et modèles de collaboration
Notre solution ne peut réussir qu’à travers une dynamique collective et solidaire. C’est pourquoi elle s’appuie sur un réseau de partenariats locaux, nationaux et internationaux :
-	Partenariats communautaires : collaboration étroite avec les chefs de base, associations de femmes, groupes de jeunes déplacés et comités locaux pour assurer une mobilisation inclusive et respectueuse.
-	Partenariats techniques : coopération avec des centres de formation locaux, des écoles techniques, des jeunes informaticiens de la région, et des volontaires du numérique pour le renforcement des capacités.
-	Partenariats institutionnels : collaboration avec la Division provinciale du Genre, les autorités locales, et des structures humanitaires présentes sur le terrain pour renforcer la cohérence et la pérennité de l’intervention.
- Modèle de collaboration durable : les bénéficiaires formés seront à leur tour mobilisés comme formateurs/trices communautaires, créant ainsi une chaîne solidaire d’inclusion numérique, et contribuant à la transformation locale.
Solution Provider(s): Le projet sera mis en œuvre en partenariat avec des acteurs engagés dans la résilience communautaire, l’autonomisation numérique et la protection des populations vulnérables : 1.	Actions Contre les Souffrances des Orphelines et des Veuves – RDC (ACSOV-RDC) : organisation de la société civile locale, active dans l’accompagnement psychosocial, la formation, et la réinsertion socioéconomique des femmes et jeunes affectés par les conflits armés. ACSOV-RDC assurera la coordination communautaire, la sélection des bénéficiaires, et le suivi terrain du projet. 2.	 (EDS-SUD) : structure spécialisée dans la formation numérique et entrepreneuriale inclusive, engagée dans la démocratisation des compétences numériques en milieu vulnérable. Elle fournira les modules de formation, les experts formateurs ainsi que l’appui technique et pédagogique. 3.	Corporación Fe Mundo Social ODS (Colombie) : organisation internationale travaillant sur les Objectifs de Développement Durable (ODD), spécialisée dans l’innovation sociale, l’éducation et la coopération Sud-Sud. Elle apportera une expertise méthodologique, un soutien en innovation digitale locale, et facilitera les échanges interrégionaux d’expériences. 4.	MenEngage DRC : réseau engagé pour l’égalité de genre et l’implication positive des hommes et garçons dans la lutte contre les violences basées sur le genre (VBG). Dans le cadre de ce projet, MenEngage appuiera l’intégration d’approches sensibles au genre et facilitera les séances de sensibilisation communautaire autour du numérique éthique, de la masculinité positive et de la cohabitation pacifique. 5.	Autres partenaires : Division Provinciale du Genre, Famille et Enfant (DPGFE) – Nord-Kivu, Réseau des Jeunes pour le Numérique Inclusif (RJNI), Groupe d'Ingénieurs Volontaires de Goma, StartHub Goma, Comité local des déplacés de Kanyaruchinya, Fondation Femme Numérique, Village Tech Solidaire, Lycée Mwanga.

L’objectif principal est de favoriser leur réinsertion socioéconomique, leur autonomisation, et leur participation active à une économie numérique inclusive et durable.
2.	 Impacts clés de la solution :

Subtitle: AI-powered mental health support for underserved African populations - multilingual, accessible, and stigma-free
Problem Statement: Africa faces a severe shortage of mental health professionals, high stigma, and limited culturally relevant solutions, leaving millions without access to quality care. In Kenya, there is only 1 psychiatrist per 500,000 people, and across Sub-Saharan Africa, more than 75% of individuals with mental health conditions receive no treatment at all. Stigma prevents nearly 60% of youth from seeking help. Most existing digital solutions are non-localized or depend entirely on human therapists, making them inaccessible or ineffective for underserved populations. These gaps have contributed to rising suicide rates, untreated depression, and a deepening mental health crisis across the continent
Solution Overview: CogniXpert AI is a mobile and web-based LLM-based mental health assistant that provides 24/7, culturally sensitive emotional support across Africa. Key features include AI-powered therapy support, mood tracking, journaling, crisis support, and seamless connection to professional therapists when needed (in development). The platform is designed to be inclusive, easily accessible, and easy to integrate into higher-learning institutions, workplaces, and healthcare systems. CogniXpert AI is supported by strategic partnerships with AWS for Startups, Redington, Meta, Ministry of ICDE (KE), We Make Change, and clinical advisors to ensure impact, scalability, and community relevance.
