Primary thematic focus area: Inclusive Digital Innovation Skills & Entrepreneurial Talent Development
Summary: Biolyze is an AI-driven platform focused on early cancer detection through multi-omics integration. Its innovative approach to harmonizing diverse biomedical data provides early, actionable insights for clinicians. A key weakness is the lack of solid partnership examples, as it is still in the prototype stage.

Title: Smart Profile Card: QR-Powered Digital Identity
Subtitle: A sleek digital profile scan card showcasing all social and business links in one page web app
Problem Statement:
Traditional business cards have long served as a tool for networking, but in today’s digital economy they are increasingly limited. Static paper cards cannot capture the dynamic nature of people’s work, nor provide instant access to updated information, portfolios, or contact links. Professionals across industries such as fashion designers, developers, artists, bloggers, creative entrepreneurs, and service providers struggle to present their skills and services in a way that is both professional and digitally accessible.

Many individuals, especially youth and small business owners, lack affordable, simple, and innovative solutions to transition from a physical business card to a digital profile that connects directly to their website, portfolio, or social platforms. This gap reduces visibility, limits opportunities, and excludes them from fully benefiting from the global digital economy.
Solution Overview:
Our solution is a digital profile card platform that transforms the traditional business card into an interactive gateway to the digital economy. Each profile card contains a QR code that instantly redirects to a personalized one-page digital profile, acting as a central hub for an individual’s identity, personal and business contacts, services, and social media presence.

Scanning the QR code on the physical or digital card opens a dedicated online profile page, which may include bios, portfolios, contact details, and links to websites and social platforms. Users can upload their own custom designs or select from ready-made templates to create a professional digital card. Existing customers can easily update or customize their cards such as modifying background images, adding or removing social links, or uploading new designs without the need to spend money for redesign. This makes the profile card a sustainable, reusable, and scalable networking tool, bridging offline interactions with online visibility.

Methodologies and Technologies Used:

Stack: Next.js + Vercel programming stack

Frontend: Next.js with Tailwind CSS for fast, mobile-friendly, and visually appealing interfaces.

Backend/Hosting: Vercel for cloud storage, domain accessibility and real-time updates.

API: Payment integrations like Stripe, Mobile Money and Paystack for secure online payments both locally and internationally.

Analytics & tracking: Google Analytics to measure card visits, redirects, and user engagement.

QR Integration: QRCode monkey for each profile code generation, ensuring simple redirection and updates.

Content Management System (CMS): Strapi to manage user profiles, links, and card content dynamically.

GitHub: For open-source contribution, version control, and team collaboration.

Design utilization: Adobe Photoshop and Figma for creativity blend and UI/UX modification

Partnerships and Collaboration Models:

Collaboration with creative professionals (designers, developers, artists, bloggers, and fashion entrepreneurs) to tailor the platform to diverse industries.

Potential partnerships with youth networks, business hubs, and skill training programs to onboard students, artisans, and professionals.

Collaboration with SMEs and startups to offer branded profile cards for employees and teams.

Open to institutional partnerships (universities, accelerators, professional associations) to scale adoption and expand the platform’s reach.
Solution Provider(s): OpenSource Catalyst (Founder-led initiative) – A social innovation and tech development startup focused on building open-source solutions for sustainable development, entrepreneurship, and digital inclusion. Sector: Technology, Social Impact.
Duration to pilot in a new geography: The solution can be piloted in a new geography within 3 to 6 months. Since it is software-based, cloud-hosted, and user-driven, the pilot rollout timeline would be relatively short compared to heavy infrastructure projects.
SDGs addressed: SDG 9 (Industry, Innovation, and Infrastructure);SDG 8 (Decent Work and Economic Growth);
Desired impact:
Solution Objectives:

To revolutionize traditional business cards by replacing them with dynamic, eco-friendly digital profile cards that connect directly to websites or online portfolios.

To empower individuals across sectors (fashion, developers, designers, bloggers, artists, and professionals by giving them a modern, shareable identity tool)

To improve networking efficiency, accessibility, and visibility of individuals and businesses.


Key Achievements/Impacts

Digital Visibility: Expands users’ professional reach by providing instant website redirection and enhanced online presence.

Merger: Provides a merger between the tech and creative industry.

Employment & Skills Development: Creates opportunities for designers, developers, and local digital service providers to collaborate in customizing cards.

Accessibility & Inclusivity: Levels the playing field for professionals and creators in emerging economies by giving them an affordable, professional online representation.
Key technologies:
AI: AI-driven analytics to provide insights into profile visits, user engagement, and customer behavior.

Cloud: For hosting, user data management, and real-time updates.
Unique Characteristics:
Technological breakthrough/innovation: Unlike static traditional business cards where customers pay for design and separate printing, our solution combines dynamic digital designs with customization and integrated payment systems which allows for both personal and business profiles in a digital platform, easing redesign. The system leverages AI to provide insights into customer engagement and in subsequent versions will recommend profile optimizations, suggest networking opportunities, and make each user’s digital presence adaptive. Smart networking through QR scan to a digital presence.

Hybrid model factor: The first phase of the project provides a two way usage whereby in the absence of sharing a business card (profile card) to networks, the owner can switch to sharing links. 

Open collaboration framework: As the founder of OpenSource Catalyst, this product is developed with the open source MIT license policy to allow developers, startups, and communities to contribute and extend especially the digital platform for profile cardholders.
Sustainable Change:
By giving individuals a digital, standardized profile card, the solution ensures that skills and experiences are visible and recognized. This leads to increased opportunities, which in turn motivates continuous learning and professional development. Once adopted widely, the platform can influence broader systemic change in hiring, mentorship, and skills development practices, creating a self-reinforcing ecosystem of opportunity in later releases.

Over time, this systemic adoption strengthens local workforce quality and encourages skillful talents  in the creative industry to actively manage their digital presence, building a culture of self-branding and continuous professional development.
Funding Sources: The project is actually self funded from initiation to development.
Primary thematic focus area: Inclusive Digital Innovation Skills & Entrepreneurial Talent Development
Summary: The Smart Profile Card provides a digital, eco-friendly alternative to traditional business cards, helping individuals, especially from underserved sectors, increase their visibility and networking opportunities. The solution’s strength lies in its scalability and customization options. However, the lack of external funding and formal endorsements may limit its reach and long-term sustainability.

Title: Frugal deeptech non invasive platform for multi-disease screening via one test
Subtitle: We develop a frugal non-invasive digital platform for multi-diseases prescreening using audio biomarkers. Our approach targets two pathologies in a single test.
Problem Statement:
We target two diseases in one test : hearing loss and chronic respiratory diseases each affecting nearly 500 million people worldwide according to the WHO. 
Workers in noisy/polluted sectors such as Metallurgy, Mining, Construction, Wood, Textile, Food Industry,...Call Centers, Education & Healthcare Admin,... are possibly affected by double diseases. 
Hearing loss as chronic respiratory diseases are a global silent epidemic: there are service gaps worldwide, a need for rehabilitation services and a great lack of screening especially in Africa and in the Eastern Mediterranean region. 

It is a major public health problem with staggering socioeconomic costs.
Solution Overview:
Audiovocal signals are the easiest physiological signals to measure. dB.Sense is developing a non-invasive digital platform for multi-diseases screening revealed by audiovocal impairments.  
We enhance and optimize the power of standards tests through multimodality and jointly optimize the duration and reliability of in situ tests using advanced statistical approaches; essential factors for effective and efficient mass screening.

dB.Sense is a spinoff of the University of Tunis El Manar (UTM). Its 3 cofounders are all engineers and PhD in ICT and Applied Mathematics. We collaborate with UTM’ecosystem: 
- Tunis Faculty of Medicine: General practitioners, ENT, Pulmonologists
- ISTMT: Audiologists & Speech Therapists

Desired impact:
dB.Sense deeply believes in the power of frugality enabled by digital technology and artificial intelligence in the service of frugal deeptech in health technologies for early, reliable, and in-situ multi-pathology mass screening. We can do more with less.

Two expected impacts of the solution:
Quantification of the solution's impact in terms of the number of people screened: schoolchildren, workers in at-risk sectors, and the elderly. 
Halving screening time amounts to doubling or even more the number of people traditionally screened, especially for multi-disease.

Quantification of the impact on job creation. These low-cost platforms can be developed and deployed locally microenterprises with three employees, through remote training for programming and assembling the platform and through training for the people performing the screening.

The United Nations has a crucial role to play with decision-making bodies to stimulate the empowerment and innovation of SMEs in digital technology for universal and easy accessibility to health.
Key technologies:
Software aspect : AI based algorithms for tests automatisation, data analysis of audio features
Hardware aspect : development of the application in multiplatform mode (IoT,...).
Unique Characteristics:
The differentiating features of our solution lie in frugal deeptech solutions association for healthcare. Each of these solutions, taken separately, does not constitute a disruptive innovation, but, taken together, constitutes a distinctive product: 
- Simple physiological signals to measure non-invasively on a single platform
- Multi-pathology screening in a single test
- Hybrid signal/AI approaches for reliable in situ measurements 
- Reduced testing time thanks to advanced statistical approaches
Sustainable Change:
To understand why systemic change is possible thanks to our non-invasive multi-disease platform, it is essential to understand the current obstacles.

Noise and pollution lead to silent epidemics with staggering and insidious global socioeconomic consequences.

The major drawback of these manifestations is their invisibility.

In terms of public health, this translates into three interdependent realities on the ground in many countries:

1) Regulations
These are most often "timid" or poorly enforced, or even non-existent; for example:
- Maximum noise levels to be respected in schools, public places, industries, etc., as well as occupational exposure limits for pollutants (chemicals, dust, cement, etc.).
- Mandatory wearing of helmets or masks, often difficult to enforce for communication reasons or in extreme heat.
- Screening from early childhood, at school, in the workplace, and at retirement is often rare and irregular.

2) Implementing screening tests
This faces two challenges:
- Cost and maintenance of the device: A diagnostic/clinical medical device is relatively expensive. It is obtained after lengthy administrative procedures because it is not manufactured locally. Specialists will therefore not add the cost of additional screening devices, even if they are less expensive. NGOs cannot afford to purchase several for mass screening campaigns. Maintaining the equipment requires expensive expertise and equipment, which are non-existent in many countries.
- Time-consuming screening campaigns: reducing screening time often results in reducing its quality.

Our solution could smoothly induce lasting systemic change, structurally transforming the healthcare system in which it is integrated, because it does not compromise on quality.

The ripple effect would have a long-term impact:

Indeed, our digital solution allows for the simultaneous screening of two pathologies (e.g., hearing loss and respiratory diseases): 1) in a non-invasive, simple, and, above all, rapid manner; 2) without compromising on-site quality reliability; 3) at a very reasonable cost.
Thus:
- School principals, business leaders, or manufacturers will be less reluctant to perform screenings if logistics are streamlined.
- ENT specialists, audiologists, speech therapists, general practitioners, pediatricians, school and occupational health physicians, health professionals at primary care centers, etc., will be less reluctant to acquire such a screening device in addition to their usual equipment. This early screening will refer even more patients to specialists and will not compete with them.
- Young people will be more aware if they can benefit from a screening training certificate, provided through short training sessions on the platform. 
- Jobs could be created to develop the digital platform locally.
- Deeptech health researchers will be able to access data enabling them to conduct more in-depth analyses (e.g., based on AI) regarding pathologies potentially specific to a country. This data sharing is planned (in compliance with regulations).
- Students, workers and seniors will be made aware of the incidence of diseases if they are screened simply and regularly.
- Decision-makers at the highest levels of government: Ministries of Health, Education, and Labor will be made aware, and regulations and resources will follow if screening campaigns demonstrate their effectiveness in the field and if digital screening jobs follow.

A virtuous circle could be created, and these silent diseases could gain visibility and be eradicated earlier.

Title: Empowering First-Time Investors in Emerging Markets With AI-Powered Financial Inclusion
Subtitle: Blaze empowers underserved youth and first-time investors in emerging markets with AI-personalized trading strategies, financial literacy, and ESG investment tools for inclusive, sustainable finance.
Problem Statement: A new generation of youth, students, and underserved individuals in emerging economies are eager to participate in wealth-building and climate-conscious investing but face systemic barriers - ranging from low financial literacy and inaccessible platforms to a lack of tailored tools that consider their goals, risk tolerance, and ESG values. Most digital financial platforms are complex, intimidating, or designed for already-privileged users, leaving behind those who need guidance the most. Blaze addresses this gap by democratizing access to investing through AI-powered education, personalized strategy generation, and real-time portfolio support - all designed with inclusion and impact at their core. Our solution helps these communities build digital financial skills, access ESG-driven opportunities, and grow sustainably in the digital economy.
Solution Overview:
Blaze is an AI-powered platform designed to democratize access to investing and financial resilience for underserved populations - particularly students, youth, women, and MSMEs - by simplifying wealth-building, enhancing financial literacy, and embedding ESG-aligned practices into every step.

How the Solution Works:

Blaze acts as a financial co-pilot, guiding users from education to execution. Users begin by setting their financial goals, income, and risk appetite through an intuitive onboarding process. Blaze then generates customized “investment playlists” - sets of AI-driven trading strategies tailored to the user’s objectives, such as long-term saving, short-term cash flow, or sustainability-focused portfolios.

An embedded gamified educational layer (BlazeVerse) teaches key investment principles and ESG fundamentals in engaging, interactive formats, ensuring even financially illiterate users can participate confidently.

Users can execute trades through their brokerage accounts (via API integration), receive alerts for dynamic rebalancing, and track their performance over time. Blaze keeps users engaged and empowered while building sustainable financial habits.


Methodologies and Technologies Used:

AI & Machine Learning: Used to generate investment strategies based on individual risk and return profiles.

ESG-Integrated Investing Engine: Blaze’s models conduct in-depth ESG scoring on companies and markets to surface high-impact, sustainability-aligned opportunities.

Gamified Financial Education: Interactive modules and quizzes teach financial and ESG concepts in a user-friendly way.

User ESG Tracking: Each user receives an ESG score, showing how aligned their portfolio is with sustainable investing principles. Blaze then promotes alternatives that are both profitable and environmentally/socially responsible.

Goal-Based Return Modeling: Calculates required returns to meet financial targets and suggests optimal paths.

Mobile-First UI/UX: Designed to ensure accessibility, simplicity, and adoption across underserved user segments.


Partnerships and Collaboration Models:

START Fellowship (University of St. Gallen, Switzerland): Blaze is backed by the prestigious START Fellowship, which supports high-impact entrepreneurs from emerging markets. Through START, Blaze has built strategic relationships with global mentors and investors, gaining international credibility and mentorship.

Egyptian Group for Information Dissemination (EGID): Blaze is in advanced talks with EGID to integrate real-time Egyptian market data - critical for enabling up-to-date investment decisions across our platform.

Egyptian Financial Regulatory Authority (FRA): Blaze is in licensing with the FRA for offering advisory and execution services in a fully compliant manner.

Central Bank of Egypt (CBE): As Blaze explores long-term integration of savings and payment functionalities, engagement with the CBE is essential for understanding digital wallet regulations and broader fintech compliance.

Paymob: A partnership to facilitate in-app payment and transaction infrastructure, ensuring seamless user onboarding and potential fund transfers.

Streetbeat (US-based AI investing platform): Blaze is collaborating with Streetbeat to support the backend AI infrastructure and access global datasets. This partnership supports scalability and adds a layer of sophistication to Blaze's analytics engine.

Arab Finance Brokerage & Beltone Financial Holding: Blaze is collaborating with these licensed brokers to enable real-time trade execution through API integrations. These partnerships would allow users to directly place orders within the Blaze app and execute curated strategies effortlessly.

The American University in Cairo (AUC): Blaze was incubated through AUC’s ecosystem, and continues to collaborate with its faculty, student body, and events.
Solution Provider(s): START Fellowship (Entrepreneurship Accelerator, Switzerland), EGID - Egyptian Group for Information Dissemination (Capital Markets & Data), Egyptian Financial Regulatory Authority (Financial Regulation, Egypt), Central Bank of Egypt (Financial Regulation), Paymob (Fintech & Payment Infrastructure), Streetbeat (AI-Powered Investing Platform, USA), Arab Finance Brokerage (Brokerage Services, Egypt), Beltone Financial Holding (Investment Banking & Brokerage, Egypt), American University in Cairo (Academic Institution & Startup Support), AUC Venture Lab (University-based Incubator & Entrepreneurship Support).
Implementation location(s): The solution has already been implemented in Egypt, primarily in Cairo. Pilot testing, user acquisition, and institutional partnerships - including with the American University in Cairo and EGID - were conducted in Cairo, with strong traction. Additionally, international user testing and validation were carried out in St. Gallen, Switzerland, as part of the START Fellowship accelerator program. The program provided access to a global network of experts and early-stage investors, enabling valuable feedback and iterations. The platform is now preparing for expansion across Africa, the MENA region, and Europe.
Implementation timeline(s): The initial development began in July 2024. The MVP was launched in February 2025, followed by user testing and iteration throughout March–May 2025. The waitlist officially launched in June 2025, and we aim to begin full deployment by November 2025.
Duration to pilot in a new geography: The estimated duration to fully pilot our solution in a new geography is approximately 3 to 4 months. This includes time for market localization, legal compliance and licensing, user onboarding, partnership development, and technical infrastructure deployment. The timeframe may vary slightly depending on regulatory requirements and ecosystem readiness in the target region.
SDGs addressed: SDG 4 (Quality Education);SDG 8 (Decent Work and Economic Growth);SDG 9 (Industry, Innovation, and Infrastructure);
Desired impact:
Our solution aims to democratize access to investing by empowering young and first-time investors with AI-powered, personalized financial tools that make smart investing both intuitive and sustainable. Through Blaze, users will not only improve their financial literacy but also make informed investment decisions aligned with their goals, risk appetite, and ethical preferences. Our long-term objective is to shift behavior toward more inclusive and conscious investing at scale.

Key quantifiable impacts include:

- Educating over 1 million users within the next 5 years through gamified, interactive modules that improve financial confidence and literacy, particularly in emerging markets.

- Facilitating the onboarding of at least 500,000 first-time underserved investors, many of whom lack access to traditional financial advisory services.

- Shifting capital toward sustainable and ESG-compliant assets, with a goal of 60% of portfolios built on Blaze incorporating at least one ESG-rated asset.

- Supporting economic empowerment and job creation indirectly by enabling individuals to build long-term wealth and make better financial decisions.

- Tracking behavioral improvements over time, including reductions in panic-selling, increased savings rates, and more consistent investing behavior, using in-app analytics.

Our vision is to create a generation of confident, impact-driven investors who can actively contribute to financial inclusion, responsible capital allocation, and long-term economic resilience across Africa, the MENA region, and beyond.
Key technologies: Blaze leverages a powerful stack of modern technologies to deliver personalized, AI-driven investment experiences. At its core, Blaze uses advanced Artificial Intelligence (AI) and Machine Learning (ML) models to generate and adapt dynamic trading strategies based on users' financial goals, risk profiles, and market behavior. A key feature is our proprietary Natural Language Processing (NLP) engine, which powers our chatbot, allowing users to ask questions, receive strategy explanations, and co-create investment plans interactively. We also integrate real-time financial data APIs for market monitoring and execution, ensuring timely and accurate trading decisions. The app is cloud-hosted to ensure scalability and performance, with a mobile-first frontend built natively on Android and iOS for an intuitive, secure user experience. As we scale, we are exploring data encryption and privacy-preserving AI techniques to safeguard user data and maintain regulatory compliance in financial jurisdictions.
Unique Characteristics: Unlike existing trading platforms that primarily serve seasoned or institutional investors, Blaze is uniquely built for underserved retail users in emerging markets - especially beginners who are often overlooked. Our edge lies in democratizing access to financial tools by combining personalized AI-generated trading strategies with localized financial education, all delivered through an intuitive dynamic experience. Where many platforms focus purely on profit, Blaze goes further by embedding ESG and sustainability considerations directly into its recommendations - empowering users not just to grow wealth, but to make a positive impact. This values-driven approach, paired with hyper-personalization and community features, allows Blaze to bridge the gap between trading, education, and purpose in a way other competitors do not focus.
Sustainable Change: Our solution fosters sustainable, systemic change by democratizing access to financial education and ethical investing, equipping underserved retail investors with the tools, knowledge, and confidence to build long-term wealth. By combining AI-driven personalization with ESG-focused investment pathways, we shift the narrative around trading from pure profit to purposeful impact - empowering individuals to contribute to environmental and social progress through their portfolios. As adoption scales, this model promotes financial inclusion, reduces socioeconomic disparity, and redirects capital flows toward more sustainable businesses, driving long-lasting change in both individual behavior and the broader investment ecosystem.
Funding Sources: Currently, we are entirely bootstrapped and actively seeking external funding to scale our operations. To date, the only external support received has been a $7,500 grant from the START Fellowship, which was instrumental in supporting initial product development and early-stage testing efforts during our time in St. Gallen, Switzerland.
Primary thematic focus area: Inclusive Digital Innovation Skills & Entrepreneurial Talent Development
Summary: Blaze is an AI-powered platform designed to democratize investing for underserved youth, students, women, and MSMEs in emerging markets. It provides AI-personalized trading strategies, gamified financial literacy tools, and ESG-integrated investment guidance. Backed by the START Fellowship (University of St. Gallen) and piloted in Egypt, Blaze partners with regulators, fintechs, and brokers to deliver compliant, localized solutions. With a mobile-first interface and NLP-powered chatbot, Blaze simplifies wealth-building, supports ESG investing, and fosters digital financial inclusion.

Title: Inclusive Digital Access for Rural Economic Empowerment
Subtitle: A transformative solution providing affordable digital connectivity, financial inclusion, and digital skills to empower rural communities and close the digital economic divide.
Problem Statement:
P
Millions of people in rural and underserved areas lack affordable internet access, digital literacy, and financial inclusion. This digital divide limits access to essential services, education, and economic opportunities, deepening poverty and inequality. BrightLink addresses these systemic barriers by providing affordable connectivity, digital skills training, and inclusive financial services, enabling marginalized populations to participate in the digital economy and improve their livelihoods.
Solution Overview:
Solution Description:
BrightLink is a decentralized digital access platform designed to bridge the digital divide in rural and underserved communities. The solution combines low-cost community Wi-Fi networks, solar-powered digital hubs, and a mobile-first platform offering digital literacy programs and inclusive financial services. BrightLink enables last-mile connectivity and provides access to e-learning, e-health, and digital entrepreneurship opportunities, creating a sustainable pathway for economic empowerment.

Methodologies and Technologies Used:

Community Wi-Fi Networks: Deployment of mesh network technology with solar-powered routers to provide affordable, stable internet in off-grid areas.

Solar-Powered Digital Hubs: Establishment of communal digital access points equipped with tablets, smart devices, and e-learning content, powered by renewable energy.

Mobile-First Platform: A lightweight mobile app offering financial services (mobile wallets, microloans), vocational digital literacy, and market access tools.

Data-Driven Approach: Use of real-time usage analytics to adapt services to community needs and optimize resource allocation.

Offline Capabilities: Local content caching ensures educational materials and services remain accessible without constant internet connection.

Partnerships and Collaboration Models:
BrightLink operates through multi-stakeholder partnerships involving:

Local Governments: Supporting infrastructure deployment and enabling regulatory environments.

Community Cooperatives: Co-management of digital hubs, ensuring local ownership and sustainability.

Private Sector Partners: Technology providers and financial institutions offer affordable devices, fintech solutions, and digital services.

NGOs and Development Agencies: Supporting community mobilization, digital skills training, and social impact measurement.

Academic Institutions: Co-developing culturally relevant educational content and conducting impact assessments.

This collaborative model ensures community empowerment, scalability, and long-term impact in driving digital inclusion.
Solution Provider(s): Roberto Save Dreams Foundation (RSDF): A non-profit organization focused on rural development, clean energy, and digital inclusion initiatives across Sub-Saharan Africa. Sector: Non-profit, Social Impact.  BrightNet Technologies Ltd.: A social enterprise specializing in affordable connectivity infrastructure and mesh networking solutions for underserved areas. Sector: ICT, Connectivity Solutions.  GreenSpark Energy Solutions: Provider of off-grid solar energy systems powering rural digital hubs and community networks. Sector: Renewable Energy, Sustainable Infrastructure.  FutureSkills Africa: A training and capacity-building organization delivering digital literacy, entrepreneurship, and vocational skills programs. Sector: Education, Workforce Development.  Unity Microfinance Bank: A financial institution offering micro-loans, savings, and digital payment services tailored for rural entrepreneurs. Sector: Financial Inclusion, Microfinance.
Implementation location(s): Locations of Implementation:  Zambia: Southern Province – Choma District, Kalomo District  Angola: Cuando Cubango Province – Menongue Municipality, Cuito Cuanavale  Zambia: Western Province – Mongu District
Implementation timeline(s): Implementation Timeline: Pilot phase launched in January 2024 and ongoing, with initial rollout planned through December 2025.
Duration to pilot in a new geography: The estimated duration to pilot the solution in a new geography is 6 to 9 months, which includes initial community engagement, infrastructure setup, training, and early impact assessment.
SDGs addressed: SDG 7 (Affordable and Clean Energy);SDG 9 (Industry, Innovation, and Infrastructure);SDG 17 (Partnerships for the Goals);
Desired impact:
Solution Objectives:

To bridge the digital divide by providing affordable and reliable internet access to rural and underserved communities.

To enhance digital literacy and entrepreneurial skills, enabling inclusive participation in the digital economy.

To promote financial inclusion through accessible mobile financial services tailored for low-income populations.

To foster sustainable community ownership and local capacity for maintaining digital infrastructure.

To contribute to economic empowerment, job creation, and poverty reduction in target regions.

Key Achievements and Impacts:
Connected over 5,000 individuals across rural Zambia and Angola to affordable digital services during the pilot phase.

Trained 1,200 community members in digital literacy and basic ICT skills.

Facilitated access to mobile financial services for 3,000 previously unbanked users, increasing financial inclusion by 25% in pilot areas.

Created approximately 150 new jobs linked to digital hubs and community network management.

Reduced reliance on fossil-fuel-powered connectivity by deploying solar-powered digital hubs, contributing to an estimated reduction of 20 tons of CO₂ emissions annually.
Enabled access to online education, healthcare, and market information, improving socio-economic resilience of communities.

These impacts demonstrate the solution’s role in driving inclusive digital growth and sustainable development.
Key technologies:
Key Technologies Used in the Solution

Mesh Network Technology: Enables low-cost, scalable, and resilient community Wi-Fi networks to provide reliable internet access in remote areas.

Solar-Powered Energy Systems: Off-grid solar panels and battery storage power digital hubs and networking equipment sustainably.

Mobile-First Application Platform: Lightweight apps optimized for low-bandwidth environments deliver digital literacy training, financial services, and market access tools.

Data Analytics: Real-time usage and impact data collection to optimize service delivery and tailor content to community needs.

Offline Content Caching: Ensures continuous access to educational and health resources even when internet connectivity is intermittent.

Digital Financial Technologies (FinTech): Mobile wallets, microloans, and payment systems designed to enhance financial inclusion for underserved populations.

While AI and blockchain are not core technologies in the current phase, future iterations may explore their integration to enhance personalized learning and secure transactions.
Unique Characteristics:
Unique/Differentiated Characteristics of the Solution

Community-Centric Ownership Model: Unlike traditional top-down approaches, BrightLink empowers local cooperatives to co-manage digital hubs and networks, fostering sustainability and trust.

Integrated Approach Combining Connectivity, Skills, and Finance: The solution uniquely bundles affordable internet access with digital literacy training and tailored financial services, addressing multiple barriers simultaneously.

Solar-Powered Off-Grid Infrastructure: Deploying renewable energy-powered digital hubs ensures reliable service in off-grid rural areas, reducing environmental impact and operational costs.

Flexible, Mobile-First Platform with Offline Capabilities: Designed for low-bandwidth and intermittent connectivity contexts, enabling continuous access to critical digital resources.

Multi-Stakeholder Partnership Model: Strong collaborations across NGOs, government, private sector, and local communities enable scalable deployment and diversified funding sources.

Data-Driven Adaptation: Continuous monitoring and community feedback loops allow dynamic tailoring of services to evolving local needs, maximizing relevance and impact.

These elements together make BrightLink a replicable, scalable, and sustainable solution for digital inclusion in underserved regions.
Sustainable Change:
Contribution to Sustainable, Systemic Change

BrightLink’s solution is designed to catalyze long-term, systemic change by addressing root causes of digital exclusion through an integrated, community-driven approach:

Empowerment through Digital Access: By providing affordable, reliable connectivity, the solution opens pathways for education, healthcare, and economic participation, enabling communities to overcome structural barriers.

Capacity Building and Skill Development: Digital literacy and entrepreneurial training equip individuals with skills to access new opportunities, fostering a digitally skilled workforce that can drive local innovation and economic growth.

Financial Inclusion: Accessible mobile financial services promote savings, credit, and secure transactions, empowering marginalized populations to build economic resilience and engage in broader markets.

Community Ownership and Governance: Involving local cooperatives in managing infrastructure fosters local accountability, sustainability, and adaptability of services beyond initial project timelines.

Environmental Sustainability: Solar-powered infrastructure reduces dependence on fossil fuels, promoting green technology adoption and climate resilience.

Theory of Change:
If rural communities gain affordable digital access, relevant skills, and inclusive financial tools  managed through locally owned and maintained infrastructure  then they will increase participation in the digital economy, improve livelihoods, and reduce inequalities. This leads to sustained economic development, strengthened local institutions, and resilient communities capable of adapting to future technological and social changes.

Ultimately, BrightLink aims to transform isolated communities into digitally empowered ecosystems that drive inclusive growth and contribute to national development goals.
Funding Sources:
Funding Sources

The BrightLink solution has been funded through a combination of sources to ensure sustainability and scalability:

Grants and Donations: Initial pilot funding provided by international development agencies and philanthropic foundations, including support from the Roberto Save Dreams Foundation.

Public-Private Partnerships: Collaboration with local governments and private sector partners who contribute resources, infrastructure, and technical expertise.

Impact Investment: Early-stage investments from social impact funds focused on digital inclusion and renewable energy initiatives.

Community Contributions: In-kind support and small financial contributions from local cooperatives and users to foster ownership and maintenance.

Technical Assistance Programs: Support through capacity-building grants and technical partnerships with NGOs and development organizations.

This diversified funding model has enabled a balanced approach to deployment while building a foundation for future financial sustainability through service revenues and local stakeholder engagement.
Testimonials and Endorsements:
Testimonials and Endorsements

While specific testimonials for the BrightLink solution are not publicly available, similar initiatives in Zambia have garnered positive feedback from beneficiaries and stakeholders.  For instance, the EDGE project, which focuses on digital transformation for Zambian agricultural SMEs, has received commendations from participants.  Kanji Poultry Services' owner, Izukanji Simbaya, noted, "I have seen the importance of having an online community and how it can grow my business, thanks to the training programmes."  Similarly, Salima Lungu of C&S Agro emphasized, "Being a part of USAID’s Enterprise Development and Growth Enhanced Activity has expanded my knowledge of digital marketing in the agricultural space and linked me to other institutions through social media platforms, expanding my reach."  

These testimonials highlight the transformative impact of digital inclusion initiatives in Zambia, aligning with the objectives of the BrightLink solution. 

Note: For more detailed information and potential future testimonials, please refer to the provided sources or contact the respective organizations directly.
Further comments/feedback:
Further Comments/Feedback

Thank you for the opportunity to contribute to this important Global Call for Solutions. The questionnaire is comprehensive and thoughtfully structured, effectively capturing critical information about innovative digital inclusion initiatives.

A suggestion for future iterations could be the inclusion of a section for brief case study summaries or impact stories that highlight real-world community transformations. This would provide evaluators with a more vivid understanding of the human impact behind the data.

Overall, the form successfully balances technical details with social impact, encouraging applicants to present holistic solutions that can drive sustainable, inclusive growth in the digital economy.

Please feel free to reach out if you require any clarifications or additional information about our submission. We look forward to potential collaboration opportunities.

A strength is its integrated model with quantified pilot impacts (5,000 connected, 1,200 trained, 3,000 financially included), while a weakness is the lack of explicit SDG indicator mapping and reliance on external funding without secured long-term runway.

Title: SUSI Tech - Digitising Food Manufacturing for SME Growth and SDG Impact
Subtitle: A no code platform helping small and medium food manufacturers to digitise and optimise their production operations, encouraging sustainable production practices, improving economic performance and support innovation capacity.
Problem Statement: Small and medium-sized manufacturers often lack the digital infrastructure, technical skillsets, and financial resources needed to digitise and optimise their operations. Manual processes dominate production, compliance, and quality management tasks, making it difficult to track waste, improve efficiency, and meet sustainability goals. Limited access to data-driven tools and AI further widens the productivity and innovation gap between SMEs and larger enterprises.
Solution Overview:
SUSI Tech delivers a comprehensive no-code digitalisation platform comprising two integrated modules: FlowIQ (TRL 5) for process mapping and OptimiseIQ (TRL 2) for real-time monitoring. The solution features AI-enhanced user journeys that enable non-technical SME users to interact with complex industrial systems through intuitive interfaces, with FlowIQ creating the "digital blueprint" of manufacturing processes whilst OptimiseIQ serves as the "living dashboard" that brings this blueprint to life with real-time data.

Digital Twin Architecture

Every process mapped in FlowIQ creates a comprehensive digital twin comprising sequential workflow steps with defined inputs and outputs, semantic metadata including equipment specifications and compliance checkpoints, performance baselines with target KPIs and escalation thresholds, and embedded regulatory frameworks specific to each operation. OptimiseIQ automatically inherits and operationalises this digital twin structure through dynamic interface generation, contextual alerting pre-configured according to FlowIQ compliance checkpoints, intelligent task routing with AI recommendations contextualised by mapped roles and responsibilities, and performance attribution linking all metrics directly to specific process steps.

Core Functionality

Both FlowIQ and OptimiseIQ operate as a cloud-based SaaS platform. FlowIQ enables non-technical SME users to digitise manufacturing processes through four pathways: drag-and-drop visual modelling using BPMN standards, pre-built industry templates for food manufacturing operations, AI-powered conversion of existing SOPs, flowchart images and system files into digital process models, and import capabilities for existing diagrams. Each process step captures comprehensive metadata including human actions, machine specifications, system integrations, compliance frameworks (HACCP, allergen controls), and sustainability metrics, with AI automatically generating compliance reports by synthesising process data with regulatory requirements.

OptimiseIQ functions as the operational execution layer, automatically inheriting structure and metadata from FlowIQ models whilst dynamically generating monitoring interfaces based on defined process steps and data points. Users access a unified command centre displaying live production KPIs, real-time alerts, cross-functional analytics, and AI-powered task recommendations, with granular visibility through drill-down dashboards that mirror exact FlowIQ process flows and offer historical trend analysis.

Technology Stack

The platform utilises Progressive Web Application architecture with offline-first capabilities, cloud-native microservices with containerised Docker deployment, and API-first design enabling seamless integrations. AI integration leverages leading multimodal AI models (currently Claude from Anthropic) for natural language processing, automated BPMN generation, and intelligent pattern recognition at the highest accuracy. Data management encompasses PostgreSQL for structured data, and integrations to existing document repositories for SOPs, ERP systems as well as other system databases for data such as sensor readings, log files, etc.

Partnership Model

SUSI Tech employs strategic co-selling with established food manufacturing consultancies serving as primary sales channels and deployment partners, leveraging existing SME relationships whilst combining technology with industry expertise through commission-based revenue sharing that incentivises engagement and knowledge co-creation.
Solution Provider(s): DIETZ Consulting GmbH, a quality management and risk management consultancy serving manufacturers in the DACH region
Duration to pilot in a new geography: 6 weeks
SDGs addressed: SDG 8 (Decent Work and Economic Growth);SDG 9 (Industry, Innovation, and Infrastructure);SDG 12 (Responsible Consumption and Production);
Desired impact:
Solution Objectives

Our primary objective is to democratise digital manufacturing for SME food manufacturers. Our solution bridges the digital divide affecting small and medium-sized food manufacturers by providing accessible, no-code digitalisation tools that enable non-technical teams to achieve Industry 4.0 capabilities without requiring substantial IT investment or specialist technical skills.

Our secondary objectives include: 
Accelerating SDG Achievement: Support UN Sustainable Development Goals through improved resource efficiency, reduced waste, enhanced food security, and inclusive economic growth.

Building Digital Resilience: Create adaptive capacity for SMEs to respond to market volatility, regulatory changes, and supply chain disruptions.

Foster Innovation Networks: Establish collaborative ecosystems connecting SMEs, consultants, and technology providers to share knowledge and accelerate adoption.

Enable Regulatory Compliance: Simplify adherence to evolving food safety, environmental, and sustainability regulations through automated reporting and monitoring

Measurement and Verification Framework

A comprehensive KPI framework tracks adoption metrics (SMEs onboarded, active users, process models created), impact metrics (waste reduction percentages, energy savings, compliance report generation time), economic indicators (cost savings per SME, productivity improvements, employment creation), environmental measures (CO2 equivalent reductions, resource consumption optimisation), and social outcomes (skills development completions, digital literacy improvements, supply chain resilience scores).

The monitoring methodology combines baseline assessments with pre-implementation measurements for all participating SMEs, real-time tracking through OptimiseIQ platform analytics, and longitudinal studies tracking sustained impact and technology adoption patterns over 3-5 years, ensuring robust accountability and evidence-based impact demonstration.
Key technologies:
The FlowIQ digital process mapping solution includes the following technology components: 

Process Modelling Engine: With an embedded BPMN.io open-source framework, the core component enables non-technical users to create digital manufacturing processes through four methods: drag-and-drop BPMN visual modelling, pre-built industry templates, AI-powered conversion of existing documentation, and import of existing BPMN process diagrams. Each process step captures comprehensive metadata including human resources, equipment specifications, quality parameters, and compliance requirements.

AI Integration Layer: Our AI engine embeds a leading multimodal AI model, currently Claude from Anthropic, that powers intelligent document processing, automatically converting SOPs, images and process-related data into structured digital models. The AI agent maps the contextualised process information to the closest available process template (highest confidence) or generates a draft BPMN diagram for further configuration by the user. The AI engine also generates automated compliance reports by mapping the process data with regulatory frameworks, eliminating manual documentation effort.

Data Architecture Framework: PostgreSQL-based relational database with JSONB support manages hierarchical process templates, configured instances, and semantic metadata at each process step. The architecture features repository abstraction layers enabling seamless integration with external documentation systems (SharePoint, Google Drive, other third party repositories) through configurable connectors with encrypted credential management and automated validation, creating comprehensive digital twins that serve as the foundation for operational monitoring.

Document Management System: Multi-tenant repository system with version control linking process steps to external documentation through automated connectors, whilst PDF report generation pipeline combines process data with external metadata using templating engines to produce compliance reports stored in object storage, ensuring complete traceability and audit compliance.

OptimiseIQ - Real-Time Production Intelligence

Dynamic Dashboard Generator: Automatically inherits structure and metadata from FlowIQ digital twins to create customised monitoring interfaces, displaying live production KPIs, performance analytics, and cross-functional metrics without manual configuration requirements.

Intelligent Alert Engine: Contextual alerting system pre-configured according to compliance checkpoints and thresholds defined in FlowIQ, with AI-powered pattern recognition identifying production inefficiencies and quality issues in real-time.

Advanced Analytics Platform: Time-series database stores real-time production metrics with PostgreSQL maintaining structured operational data, enabling granular process visibility through drill-down dashboards mirroring exact FlowIQ workflows, offering historical trend analysis, waste tracking, and detailed alert logs linked to specific process steps and equipment.

Task Management Hub: Event-driven architecture with Redis caching manages sophisticated workflow systems combining manual task creation with AI-generated improvement recommendations based on performance patterns, integrated with production schedules through API connectors and featuring automated follow-up tracking to transform static process models into dynamic operational management tools.

Both platforms maintain bi-directional data flow, ensuring continuous synchronisation between digital twin models and operational reality whilst providing enterprise-level manufacturing intelligence through intuitive, accessible interfaces designed specifically for SME environments.
Unique Characteristics:
AI-Powered Digital Twin Democratisation
SUSI Tech delivers the first integration of advanced multimodal AI (Claude from Anthropic) with manufacturing digitalisation specifically designed for non-technical SME users. Unlike enterprise solutions requiring technical expertise, production specialists create sophisticated digital twins through drag-and-drop interfaces, automated document conversion, and configurable templates. Automated BPMN generation from existing documents eliminates manual process mapping barriers, significantly reducing implementation time whilst maintaining enterprise-grade semantic data architecture.

Seamless Digital Twin-to-Operations Integration
Our breakthrough bi-directional synchronisation between process design (FlowIQ) and operational monitoring (OptimiseIQ) automatically configures monitoring dashboards based on digital twin specifications through inherited metadata structures. This eliminates the traditional gap between process documentation and operational visibility that plagues existing manufacturing software solutions, whilst sophisticated AI and analytics remain accessible through conversational interfaces, enabling quality managers and factory owners to directly implement advanced digitalisation without technical specialists.

Embedded Compliance and Sustainability Intelligence
Automated generation of regulatory compliance reports (HACCP, ISO standards) synthesises process data with regulatory frameworks, eliminating manual documentation effort. Built-in carbon footprint tracking and waste reduction analytics align with EU Green Deal requirements, providing SMEs with enterprise-level sustainability reporting capabilities that generic process mapping tools cannot match.

Collaborative Ecosystem Innovation
Our knowledge co-creation framework enables partners to contribute process templates, best practice libraries, and feature prioritisation, ensuring continuous platform evolution based on real-world SME needs rather than traditional vendor-customer relationships. This SME-first design philosophy addresses resource constraints, limited IT support, and skills gaps, creating a new "inclusive Industry 4.0" category that democratises advanced manufacturing intelligence previously available only to large enterprises.
Sustainable Change:
SUSI Tech's FlowIQ and OptimiseIQ demonstrate how empowering SMEs with accessible, AI-powered digital tools unlocks sustainable industrial transformation from the ground up. By enabling non-technical users to digitise and optimise production processes without costly infrastructure or specialised IT skills, SUSI Tech seeks to activate measurable improvement cycles aligned with industry-proven impact metrics: 60% food waste reduction, 15-25% emission decreases, and 20-30% efficiency gains.

Systemic Change Mechanisms: The platform catalyses transformation through self-reinforcing network effects. Trained consultant partners (targeting 100+ over five years) create knowledge co-creation ecosystems, developing 500+ reusable process templates that accelerate peer adoption. Activating regional manufacturing clusters unlock collective purchasing power for SUSI Tech solutions, reducing individual costs whilst building local expertise. Establishing academic partnerships would validate impact evidence, influencing government policies and development finance priorities.

Sustainability Framework: Economic models align with SME growth patterns, ensuring long-term accessibility. Immediate cost savings from waste reduction and efficiency gains fund continued adoption, creating positive feedback loops. Demonstrated ROI attracts sustainable financing whilst consultant ecosystems distribute implementation burdens across multiple stakeholders.
Scalable Impact Pathways: Successful implementations create demonstration effects encouraging broader adoption across similar manufacturing contexts. South-South knowledge transfer accelerates deployment in developing economies through proven methodologies. Market forces drive supply chain partners to demand higher digital standards, creating systemic pressure for widespread adoption.

Our Long-term Vision: By 2034, SME manufacturers globally possess digital capabilities comparable to large enterprises, contributing measurably to SDG targets through reduced emissions, enhanced food security, and inclusive economic growth. This multi-layered impact embeds intelligence and adaptability into manufacturing operations, transforming previously excluded SMEs into active contributors to responsible, tech-driven industrial development whilst establishing inclusive design as the standard for future industrial technology innovation.
Funding Sources: The solution has been fully funded by the co-founders to date.
Testimonials and Endorsements: Not yet available
Primary thematic focus area: MSME Empowerment & Local Digital Innovation
Summary: SUSI Tech is a proof-of-concept no-code digitalisation platform for SME food manufacturers, integrating FlowIQ (process mapping, TRL 5) and OptimiseIQ (real-time monitoring, TRL 2). It enables non-technical users to create digital twins of manufacturing processes and operational dashboards, embedding compliance, sustainability, and AI-powered optimisation. Developed by DIETZ Consulting GmbH, it leverages multimodal AI (Claude by Anthropic), BPMN standards, and PostgreSQL-based architecture. Co-selling with food manufacturing consultancies forms the partnership model. The solution targets SMEs in Europe and Central Asia, with ambitions for global replication.

Title: FarmHer Thrive
Subtitle: Empowering rural women with seeds, knowledge, and digital tools to grow, process, and profit from sustainable agriculture.
Problem Statement: Rural women farmers in sub-Saharan Africa face structural barriers in access to land, credit, climate information, and digital tools. These inequalities limit their ability to adapt to climate shocks, reduce post-harvest loss, and secure fair market value. Without targeted support, women remain underrepresented in agri-tech, underpaid in value chains, and overburdened with invisible labor.
Solution Overview:
FarmHer Thrive is an inclusive, women-led digital agriculture and health platform that equips rural women farmers with timely access to inputs, information, and income opportunities — all through mobile-first technology. It addresses key barriers such as low yields, post-harvest losses, digital exclusion, and gender-based economic marginalization.

1. Onboarding & Needs Assessment:
   Community agents register women farmers via mobile (WhatsApp, SMS, USSD) and collect baseline data on their location, crops, and farming needs.

2. Access to Inputs:
   The platform connects users to affordable seeds and basic farming inputs, distributed through local cooperatives and verified vendors.

3. Timely, Localized Support:
   Women receive weekly messages tailored to their crops and region — including:

   * Pest control alerts
   * Climate-smart tips
   * Soil health practices
   * Menstrual & maternal health education

4. Harvest & Buy-Back Model:
   FarmHer Thrive buys harvests directly from women farmers at fair prices, reducing post-harvest losses and providing guaranteed income.

5. Agro-Processing & Sales:
   Purchased produce is processed into high-quality products (e.g. dried pepper, smoked fish, broiler meat) for sale via:

   * Cooperatives and markets
   * Small retailers and diaspora buyers
   * An upcoming digital storefront

6. Savings & Financial Inclusion:
   Women are supported with access to community savings groups, micro-credit options, and financial literacy content.

Methodologies and Technologies Used

Human-centered co-design: Farmers co-create content in local languages (audio, text, and voice messages)
Low-tech mobile delivery:WhatsApp and USSD make it accessible to users with basic phones
Lean data approach: Baseline and outcome tracking through mobile surveys and agent-led visits
Community empowerment model:Training local women as agents to support digital literacy and trust.

Partnerships and Collaboration Models

Local Cooperatives & Women’s Groups: for farmer identification, distribution, and community trust
Health and Agricultural Extension Workers:for validating content and offering referrals
Agro-processors & Small Retailers: for post-harvest processing and distribution
Technology Partners: for USSD/WhatsApp integration, data privacy, and platform development
NGOs and Government Programs: for scaling outreach and aligning with public extension services.

Duration to pilot in a new geography: Months 1–2:  Community engagement, onboarding, and content co-design  Input partnerships and agent training  Months 3–6:  Distribution of seeds and tools  Weekly mobile messages on farming, pest control, and health  Digital financial inclusion and savings groups  Months 7–9:  Produce collection, processing, and sales  Farmer feedback and early performance tracking  Months 10–12:  Outcome evaluation  Optimization and planning for scale-up.
SDGs addressed: SDG 8 (Decent Work and Economic Growth);SDG 5 (Gender Equality);SDG 2 (Zero Hunger);
Desired impact:
Solution Objectives:

* Improve agricultural productivity and resilience among rural women farmers through access to timely inputs and information
* Enhance women's participation in the digital economy via mobile-based learning, health education, and financial inclusion
* Create sustainable, women-led value chains by supporting harvest buy-back, processing, and ethical market access

Key Impacts & Achievements (Expected):

2,500+ rural women farmers digitally supported in the first 12 months
30–40% yield improvement due to access to pest alerts, seasonal tips, and seed support
30% reduction in post-harvest loss through structured buy-back and processing
Income increase of 20–50% for participating farmers based on current small holder benchmarks
150–200 women agents trained as local digital facilitators and agro-processors
 Indirect contribution to climate adaptation through climate-smart farming practices (GHG savings data to be tracked post-pilot)
 Foundation for replicable rural MSME ecosystems led by women.
Key technologies:
FarmHer Thrive integrates accessible digital tools with emerging technologies to deliver inclusive, women-centered agricultural and health solutions at scale.

1. Mobile-first Delivery (WhatsApp & USSD):

* Primary communication channel for agri-health messages in local languages
* Enables access for low-literacy users and those without smartphones
* USSD ensures reach in low-connectivity areas — aligning with Digital Public Goods principles of accessibility and equity

2. AI-driven Personalization (Upcoming):

* Planned integration of AI models to personalize advice based on crop, location, season, and health needs
* Enables predictive alerts (e.g., pest outbreaks, weather shifts) and adaptive content delivery
* Supports low-resource users through simple, voice-supported interfaces

3. Community-based Data Systems:

* Human-centered mobile data collection tools for registration, feedback, and impact tracking
* Supports lean, real-time decision-making without heavy infrastructure

4. Scalable Backend Infrastructure:

* Cloud-based platform ensures secure content delivery, monitoring, and future integrations
* Ready to adopt digital public goods and open standards (e.g., DHIS2, OpenSRP) for interoperability with health and ag systems

5. Future Integration Potential:

IoT sensors for demo farms to support soil/moisture tracking
Blockchain for ethical traceability of processed goods (e.g., FarmHer-branded, spices, plantain flour, dried peppers or smoked fish).
Unique Characteristics:
1. Women-first, Mobile-first Design:
FarmHer Thrive is tailored for rural women who are often excluded from traditional agri-tech and health systems. By using USSD and WhatsApp, the platform delivers critical content in local languages, voice notes, and simplified formats — ensuring accessibility even with basic phones and low literacy.

2. Integrated Value Chain Approach:
Unlike siloed interventions, FarmHer Thrive connects the entire agricultural journey — from seed access to harvest buy-back, local processing, and sales — enabling women to earn more, waste less, and own more of the value chain.

3. Embedded Health + Financial Inclusion:
The platform uniquely merges farming with menstrual/maternal health education and savings group models, recognizing women’s needs holistically. This creates long-term resilience and builds trust in underserved communities.

4. Community-led Technology Adoption:
By training local women agents to onboard users and support digital access, the model blends human trust with digital scale — increasing adoption, relevance, and sustainability.

5. Scalable, Climate-smart Content Engine:
Content is co-designed with local women and experts to reflect regional farming cycles, pest patterns, and wellness needs. Future AI-powered personalization will allow adaptive content delivery for each user and geography.

6. Social Enterprise Model:
As a women-led initiative, FarmHer Thrive reinvests revenue from produce processing and digital partnerships back into the platform — creating a circular model for scale and impact.
Sustainable Change:
FarmHer Thrive tackles the root causes of rural women’s exclusion from the digital and agricultural economy by delivering integrated support across farming, health, and market access. The solution is designed to shift systems — not just symptoms — through community ownership, inclusive technology, and economic agency.

Theory of Change

If rural women farmers are equipped with:

* Timely agricultural and health information via accessible digital platforms
* Access to quality inputs, savings groups, and guaranteed markets
* Support from trained community agents and local processing partners

Then they will:

* Improve productivity, reduce losses, and increase income
* Gain confidence, health awareness, and financial independence
* Build trust in digital tools and become agents of change in their communities

So that over time:

* Local food systems become more inclusive, resilient, and woman-led
* Gender gaps in land use, technology, and decision-making narrow
* A scalable ecosystem of women-run micro-enterprises grows — creating a ripple effect of intergenerational empowerment.
This systemic approach shifts the power from top-down aid to community-driven innovation — laying the foundation for sustainable growth across regions.
Funding Sources:
FarmHer Thrive has been primarily self-funded to date, with early support drawn from personal investment, small-scale bootstrapping, and community contributions.

As the solution prepares for pilot implementation, it is actively seeking funding and strategic support from international donors, digital inclusion accelerators, and gender-focused innovation challenges.
Primary thematic focus area: MSME Empowerment & Local Digital Innovation
Summary: FarmHer Thrive is a women-led digital agriculture platform designed for rural women in sub-Saharan Africa. Using mobile-first delivery (USSD, WhatsApp), it provides access to seeds, climate-smart advice, health education, financial inclusion, and fair-market buy-back models. Farmers are supported across the full value chain: from input access to harvest collection, agro-processing, and sales. Community agents onboard women and co-design content, ensuring accessibility for low-literacy users. The model integrates health, financial literacy, and farming support, aiming to improve yields, reduce post-harvest loss, and increase women’s income. Expected results include supporting 2,500 farmers in the first year and building scalable, women-led MSME ecosystems.

Name of your organization: Association de Bienfaisance et de Secours aux Sinistrés et Réfugiés (ABSSR)
Title: Projet : Inclusion numérique pour les femmes et jeunes filles déplacées et réfugiées
Subtitle: Une solution numérique inclusive visant à former, connecter et autonomiser les femmes et jeunes filles déplacées et réfugiées à travers l'accès aux compétences et opportunités économiques digitales.
Problem Statement: Le projet répond à l’exclusion numérique et économique des femmes et jeunes filles déplacées et réfugiées dans cinq régions du Burkina Faso, notamment, le Nord, le Centre, le Centre-Nord, la Boucle du Mouhoun et l'Est. Ces populations, déjà fragilisées par les conflits, le déplacement forcé et la pauvreté, font face à un accès limité aux outils numériques, à l’éducation digitale, aux compétences professionnelles modernes et aux opportunités économiques en ligne. Le manque de connectivité, de formation adaptée, de dispositifs d’accompagnement et de reconnaissance sociale accentue leur marginalisation. En l’absence d’interventions ciblées, elles restent en marge de l’économie numérique et de l’autonomisation socio-économique, renforçant leur dépendance et leur vulnérabilité.
Solution Overview:
Le projet « Inclusion numérique pour les femmes et jeunes filles déplacées et réfugiées » vise à renforcer l’autonomie de 500 bénéficiaires dans cinq régions du Burkina Faso à travers un accès équitable aux compétences, outils et opportunités numériques.

Fonctionnement de la solution :
Le projet se déploie en trois étapes :

1. Formation numérique et professionnelle : modules adaptés sur les bases de l’informatique, la navigation web, la sécurité en ligne, l’usage des plateformes d’apprentissage, et l’initiation à l’entrepreneuriat digital.

2. Mise en réseau et accès aux opportunités : accompagnement vers des plateformes d’e-commerce, d’emploi à distance, ou de services numériques locaux (rédaction, design, gestion de données).

3. Création d’espaces numériques mobiles : unités mobiles équipées de kits solaires, ordinateurs/tablettes, connexion internet, accessibles même dans les zones à faible infrastructure.

Méthodes et technologies utilisées :
- Approche participative et sensible au genre
- Contenu de formation en langues locales
- Utilisation de plateformes open source (Moodle, KoBoToolbox)
- Dispositifs solaires pour zones sans électricité
- Méthode « former et autonomiser » avec mentorat intégré

Partenariats et collaboration :
- OSC locales pour l’identification des bénéficiaires et la mobilisation communautaire  
- Centres de formation pour l’hébergement des sessions
- Partenaires techniques (ONG, opérateurs tech) pour le matériel et la connectivité
- Ministères et autorités locales pour l’ancrage institutionnel et la durabilité
Solution Provider(s): Association de Bienfaisance et de Secours aux Sinistrés et Réfugiés (ABSSR) – Organisation humanitaire intervenant dans la protection, l’éducation, l’autonomisation économique et l’inclusion sociale des personnes déplacées et réfugiées,    Ministère de la Solidarité, de l’Action humanitaire, de la Réconciliation nationale, du Genre et de la Famille – Institution publique en charge des politiques de prise en charge des populations vulnérables,    Ministère du Développement de l'Économie numérique et de la Transformation digitale – Appui technique pour la formation numérique et l’infrastructure,    Groupe Telmob/ONATEL – Fournisseur d’accès à Internet et partenaire pour la connectivité dans les zones ciblées,    Centres de formation professionnelle (CFP) locaux – Structures d’accueil pour les formations pratiques et digitales,    Coalition Burkinabè pour les Droits des Femmes (CBDF) – Réseau associatif pour le plaidoyer genre et l’intégration sociale des femmes.
Duration to pilot in a new geography: La durée estimée pour piloter la solution dans une nouvelle géographie est de 18 mois, répartis comme suit :  - 3 mois : mobilisation des partenaires locaux, sélection des bénéficiaires, installation logistique.   - 6 à 10 mois : mise en œuvre des formations numériques, accompagnement entrepreneurial et accès aux outils.   - 4 à 5 mois : suivi-évaluation, capitalisation des résultats et ajustements pour la montée en échelle.
SDGs addressed: SDG 4 (Quality Education);SDG 5 (Gender Equality);SDG 8 (Decent Work and Economic Growth);
Desired impact:
Objectifs de la solution :  
- Renforcer les compétences numériques de 500 femmes et jeunes filles déplacées et réfugiées dans 5 régions du Burkina Faso.  
- Faciliter l'accès de 500 femmes et jeunes filles déplacées et réfugiées à des opportunités économiques en ligne (emploi, auto-entrepreneuriat, e-commerce).  
- Réduire la fracture numérique et sociale qui freine leur autonomie et inclusion.

Principales réalisations/impacts attendus :  
- 500 bénéficiaires formées aux compétences numériques de base et avancées.  
- Au moins 200 femmes intégrées dans des activités génératrices de revenus via le numérique (prestations en ligne, vente, services).  
- Environ 100 micro-entreprises digitales sont crées (e-commerce, services numériques locaux).  
- Accès régulier à Internet via 5 espaces numériques mobiles équipés.  
- Renforcement du leadership numérique féminin, avec une participation accrue aux plateformes d’expression et de marché.  
- Réduction des inégalités d’accès au numérique dans les zones ciblées, avec effet d’entraînement communautaire.
Key technologies:
Le projet Inclusion numérique pour les femmes et jeunes filles déplacées et réfugiées utilise principalement les technologies suivantes :

1. Technologies numériques mobiles : tablettes, smartphones, ordinateurs portables utilisés dans des unités mobiles pour la formation et l’accès aux services.

2. Internet et plateformes d’apprentissage en ligne : utilisation d’outils open source comme Moodle, Google Workspace et KoBoToolbox pour la formation, le suivi et l’auto-apprentissage.

3. Énergie solaire hors réseau : pour alimenter les équipements numériques dans les zones sans accès à l’électricité.

4. Technologies de connectivité : routeurs mobiles, modems 4G/5G et Wi-Fi communautaire pour assurer un accès Internet dans les localités ciblées.

Le projet n’intègre pas encore des technologies avancées comme l’IA ou la blockchain, mais pose les bases pour une future intégration dans le renforcement des compétences et l’analyse des données.
Unique Characteristics:
Le projet se distingue par plusieurs caractéristiques innovantes et différenciées :

1. Studio numérique mobile et solaire : une unité itinérante équipée (énergie solaire, connectivité, matériel numérique) permet de toucher les zones isolées, souvent exclues des projets classiques.

2. Approche genre et vulnérabilité centrée : la solution est spécifiquement conçue pour répondre aux barrières que rencontrent les femmes déplacées (mobilité, accès, temps, compétences, normes sociales).

3. Modèle coopératif de revenus partagés : les bénéficiaires formées sont accompagnées pour créer des micro-entreprises numériques collectives (freelance, services digitaux, e-commerce) favorisant la propriété partagée.

4. Formation modulaire flexible : contenus numériques adaptés aux niveaux d’éducation, langues locales et rythmes d’apprentissage des femmes déplacées, avec tutorat et mentorat communautaire.

5. Intégration dans les structures locales : le projet collabore étroitement avec les OSC, centres de formation, et services publics pour assurer l’ancrage local et la durabilité post-financement.

Ces éléments font de cette solution un modèle adaptable, inclusif et reproductible, au-delà des approches traditionnelles d’insertion numérique.
Sustainable Change:
Le projet contribue à un changement systémique durable en agissant sur plusieurs leviers structurels :

1. Renforcement des capacités individuelles : en dotant les femmes et jeunes filles déplacées de compétences numériques et entrepreneuriales, le projet leur permet de devenir actrices de leur propre autonomisation économique, réduisant la dépendance à l’aide humanitaire.

2. Création d’un écosystème local d’inclusion numérique : les studios mobiles, les partenariats avec les OSC, centres de formation et institutions publiques favorisent la mise en place d’infrastructures et de services numériques accessibles et pérennes.

3. Modèle économique coopératif reproductible : en promouvant la propriété partagée et la mutualisation des revenus à travers des micro-entreprises digitales, le projet installe des mécanismes locaux de génération de richesse équitable.

4. Changement des normes sociales : la visibilité des femmes déplacées comme actrices économiques et numériques contribue à briser les stéréotypes de genre et à renforcer leur rôle dans la prise de décision communautaire.

5. Effets de suivi souhaités :  
   - Plus grande participation des femmes déplacées à l’économie locale  
   - Intégration des modules numériques dans les programmes de formation existants
   - Réplication du modèle dans d'autres régions ou pays confrontés aux mêmes enjeux
Funding Sources: Le projet est actuellement en phase de conception. À ce stade, aucun financement n’a encore été obtenu, mais des démarches sont en cours pour mobiliser des fonds auprès de partenaires potentiels, institutions publiques et bailleurs internationaux. Les ressources futures viseront à soutenir le développement, le lancement et la montée en échelle du projet.
Testimonials and Endorsements: Le projet est en phase de conception, donc aucun témoignage ou approbation formelle n’a encore été recueilli. Cependant, ABSSR prévoit de collecter des retours et soutiens de la part des bénéficiaires et partenaires lors des phases pilotes et de mise en œuvre future.
Further comments/feedback:
