Quelques suggestions :  
- Ajouter une section dédiée aux risques et mesures d’atténuation pourrait renforcer l’analyse.  
- Il serait utile d’avoir un champ pour décrire brièvement les ressources humaines clés.  
- Un espace pour détailler l’impact environnemental direct ou indirect du projet serait intéressant, même s’il est faible.

Globalement, l’exercice aide à clarifier la vision et à anticiper les besoins.
Primary thematic focus area: Inclusive Digital Innovation Skills & Entrepreneurial Talent Development
Summary: Burkina Faso’s ABSSR proposes a digital inclusion project for displaced and refugee women and girls, offering training, mentorship, access to mobile solar-powered digital hubs, and links to economic opportunities. It targets 500 beneficiaries across 5 regions with expected creation of digital micro-enterprises and improved economic participation.

Title: BUCKSUP: AI Decentralised Bank for African Financial Inclusion
Subtitle: AI-driven DeFi bank concept empowering Sub-Saharan Africa's unbanked with accessible microloans, secure transfers, and digital identity, fostering inclusive economic growth.
Problem Statement:
The core issue we're relentlessly solving is the massive financial exclusion plaguing Sub-Saharan Africa. Imagine nearly 500 million adults living cash-to-cash, completely shut out from basic financial services. They can't access loans, secure savings, or send money safely because traditional banks demand formal documentation or require physical branches that are inaccessible. This digital divide, coupled with the absence of a verifiable digital identity, traps them.

It's a stifling barrier to economic growth and poverty eradication, forcing reliance on risky, expensive informal systems. We're passionate about unlocking the immense human potential currently constrained by this outdated financial system.
Solution Overview:
BUCKSUP: An AI-Driven Decentralised Bank for Inclusive Digital Economy
BUCKSUP is an innovative, AI-driven decentralised bank concept specifically designed to bridge the financial inclusion gap for the unbanked and underbanked populations in Sub-Saharan Africa. Our solution provides accessible, affordable, and secure financial services, fostering economic empowerment and inclusive growth.

How the Solution Works:
BUCKSUP operates as a comprehensive digital financial ecosystem, accessible to users regardless of their smartphone ownership or internet connectivity.

Onboarding & Digital Identity:

Users can onboard through either a simple USSD interface (for feature phone users) or a mobile application (for smartphone users).

Our system incorporates an inclusive digital identity framework. For users without traditional formal identification, our AI leverages alternative data points (e.g., mobile network usage patterns, community-based referrals, utility payment history, social graph analysis) to establish a verifiable digital identity. This process is designed to be compliant with local KYC/AML regulations while remaining accessible.

Once onboarded, users gain access to a secure digital wallet.

AI-Personalized Microloans:

Users can apply for microloans directly through the USSD menu or mobile app.

Our proprietary AI credit scoring model analyzes a vast array of alternative data points collected during onboarding and ongoing usage (e.g., airtime top-up frequency, mobile money transaction history, repayment behavior on previous micro-transactions, psychometric data where ethically sourced and permissible). This enables us to assess creditworthiness for individuals who lack traditional credit bureau scores.

The AI dynamically determines loan amounts, interest rates, and repayment schedules tailored to the individual's financial capacity, promoting responsible lending and preventing over-indebtedness.

Approved loan amounts are disbursed instantly to the user's BUCKSUP digital wallet or linked mobile money account.

Secure Money Transfers (P2P):

Users can send and receive money securely and affordably within the BUCKSUP ecosystem or to other mobile money accounts.

This functionality is available via both USSD and the mobile app, ensuring seamless Person-to-Person (P2P) transfers, crucial for informal economies.

Financial Literacy & Credit Building:

Integrated into the user journey are bite-sized, accessible financial literacy modules delivered through USSD prompts and in-app content.

Every successful transaction and loan repayment contributes to building a digital financial track record within BUCKSUP, which can eventually serve as a verifiable history to unlock broader financial opportunities.

Methodologies and Technologies Used:
Artificial Intelligence (AI) & Machine Learning (ML):

Alternative Data Credit Scoring: We utilize supervised and unsupervised ML algorithms (e.g., predictive analytics, neural networks) trained on diverse, non-traditional datasets to assess credit risk and personalize loan offerings.

Natural Language Processing (NLP): For processing unstructured data and potentially enhancing user interaction via text-based interfaces.

Bias Mitigation Techniques: Algorithms are continuously monitored and refined to ensure fairness and prevent algorithmic bias against specific demographics.

Decentralised Finance (DeFi) Principles: While BUCKSUP operates within a regulated framework, our underlying architecture incorporates principles of decentralisation to enhance transparency, security, and user control over their financial data. This includes distributed ledger technology (DLT) for secure record-keeping and potentially future integration with blockchain solutions for enhanced interoperability and trust.

USSD (Unstructured Supplementary Service Data): This core technology provides universal accessibility across all mobile phone types, regardless of internet connectivity. It enables real-time, session-based
Solution Provider(s): BUCKSUP (AI Decentralised Bank for Financial Inclusion), South Africa, Fintech/Financial Services; Aviseo, South Africa, Digital Identity & Data Analytics (specializing in digital identity solutions and providing data analysis for sports organizations like CAF and Afcon), Mobile Network Operators (MNOs), various African countries, Telecommunications; Local Community Organizations & NGOs, various African countries, Community Development/Social Impact; Regulatory Bodies (e.g., National Credit Regulator (NCR), Financial Sector Conduct Authority (FSCA)), South Africa, Financial Regulation; Fintech Enablers & Technology Providers, Global, Technology/Infrastructure; Financial Institutions, Global, Banking/Finance; Research & Academic Institutions, Global, Research/Education.
Duration to pilot in a new geography: To pilot BUCKSUP in a new geography, we estimate an implementation duration of 12-18 months.  This timeframe accounts for:  Regulatory Alignment (6-9 months): Securing necessary licenses and approvals from central banks and financial regulators, which can vary significantly across African markets. This includes adapting our digital identity and AI credit scoring models to local KYC/AML requirements.  Technical Integration (3-6 months): Establishing partnerships and integrating with local Mobile Network Operators (MNOs) for USSD and mobile money interoperability, as well as local payment infrastructure.  Market Adaptation & Localisation (3-6 months): Conducting in-depth market research to tailor our product offerings, messaging, and financial literacy content to local cultural nuances and specific user needs. This also includes setting up local operational teams and agent networks where applicable.  Our modular architecture and experience in the Sub-Saharan African context will help streamline this process, but a thorough, compliant, and localized launch is paramount for sustainable impact.
SDGs addressed: SDG 2 (Zero Hunger);SDG 8 (Decent Work and Economic Growth);SDG 10 (Reduced Inequalities);
Desired impact:
Solution Objectives:
BUCKSUP aims to revolutionize financial inclusion in Sub-Saharan Africa by:

Democratizing Access: Provide universal access to essential financial services (microloans, savings, payments) for the unbanked and underbanked, regardless of smartphone ownership or traditional identification.

Empowering Economic Participation: Enable individuals and MSMEs to participate actively in the formal digital economy, fostering entrepreneurship and sustainable livelihoods.

Building Financial Resilience: Equip vulnerable populations with tools to manage their finances, mitigate economic shocks, and build long-term financial stability.

Promoting Responsible Lending: Utilize advanced AI to offer personalized, fair, and sustainable credit solutions that prevent over-indebtedness.

Advancing Digital Literacy: Integrate financial and digital literacy into the user experience to enhance informed decision-making and safe digital engagement.

Key Achievements or Impacts of the Solution (Quantifiable):
Our desired impact is to achieve significant, measurable improvements in financial inclusion and economic well-being:

Financial Inclusion Reach: Onboard 50 million new users in Sub-Saharan Africa within the next 5 years, providing them with their first formal financial account and digital identity.

Poverty Reduction: Contribute to lifting 1 million households out of extreme poverty within 7 years by enabling access to productive capital and secure savings. (Studies suggest financial inclusion can lift 2% of a population out of poverty, with mobile money being a key driver).

MSME Growth: Facilitate an average 15-20% increase in monthly income for micro and small business owners utilizing BUCKSUP's microloan and payment services, enabling business expansion and job creation. (Microfinance has shown to increase crop output by 21% and significantly boost income for smallholder farmers).

Women's Economic Empowerment: Achieve a 50% female user base, ensuring women have equal access to financial services, leading to increased financial control and investment in their families and businesses. (Mobile banking has increased financial access for over 50% of women in rural areas).

Savings Mobilization: Enable users to collectively save $500 million annually within the BUCKSUP ecosystem, fostering a culture of savings and improving financial resilience against unforeseen shocks.

Job Creation: Indirectly support the creation of 250,000 new jobs through the growth of MSMEs empowered by BUCKSUP's financial services.

Reduced Transaction Costs: Decrease the average cost of remittances and domestic transfers for users by at least 70%, ensuring more money stays within the communities.
Key technologies:
Key Technologies Utilized by BUCKSUP
BUCKSUP leverages a synergistic combination of cutting-edge and widely accessible technologies to deliver its financial inclusion solution. Our approach prioritizes both advanced capabilities and broad reach, particularly in the Sub-Saharan African context.

Artificial Intelligence (AI) & Machine Learning (ML):

Alternative Credit Scoring: This is a cornerstone of BUCKSUP. Our AI/ML models analyze vast amounts of non-traditional data (e.g., mobile phone usage patterns, airtime top-up history, utility bill payments, psychometric data, social network analysis with user consent) to assess creditworthiness for individuals lacking formal credit histories. This enables us to provide personalized microloans and financial products responsibly.

Fraud Detection & Risk Management: AI algorithms continuously monitor transaction patterns and user behavior to identify and flag suspicious activities, enhancing the security and integrity of the platform.

Personalized Financial Recommendations: AI can be used to offer tailored financial advice and product recommendations, improving financial literacy and encouraging responsible financial habits.

USSD (Unstructured Supplementary Service Data):

Universal Accessibility: USSD is critical for reaching the vast majority of the unbanked population in Sub-Saharan Africa who rely on feature phones and may have limited or no internet access. It provides a real-time, session-based communication channel for interactive menus and transactions.

Offline Functionality: Unlike mobile apps that require internet data, USSD operates on the GSM network, making it highly reliable even in areas with poor connectivity.

Cost-Effectiveness: USSD transactions are typically very low-cost, making financial services affordable for low-income users.

Mobile Application Development:

Enhanced User Experience: For smartphone users, native Android and iOS applications provide a rich, intuitive, and feature-rich interface. This allows for more complex interactions, data visualization, and a modern banking experience.

Biometric Authentication: Mobile apps enable the use of biometric features (e.g., fingerprint, facial recognition) for secure and convenient user authentication, enhancing digital identity verification.

Push Notifications: Facilitate real-time alerts for transactions, loan updates, and financial literacy tips.

Digital Identity:

Inclusive Identification: BUCKSUP develops a verifiable digital identity framework that addresses the lack of formal documentation, a significant barrier to financial inclusion. This system leverages alternative data and secure processes to establish and verify identity for individuals previously excluded.

Seamless Verification: Enables remote and secure authentication for accessing financial services, streamlining the onboarding process and ongoing transactions.

Foundation for Services: A robust digital identity is fundamental for accessing not only financial services but also other essential public and private sector services.

Decentralised Finance (DeFi) Principles / Distributed Ledger Technology (DLT):

Enhanced Transparency and Immutability: While not a fully public blockchain, BUCKSUP incorporates DLT principles for secure and transparent record-keeping of transactions and digital identities. This provides an immutable audit trail, building trust and reducing the potential for fraud.

Reduced Intermediaries: By leveraging some DeFi concepts, we aim to streamline processes and potentially reduce transaction costs by minimizing reliance on traditional intermediaries where feasible.

Interoperability (Future): The underlying DLT principles lay the groundwork for potential future interoperability with other digital financial ecosystems, fostering a more connected financial landscape in Africa.
Unique Characteristics:
Unique and Differentiated Characteristics of BUCKSUP

BUCKSUP stands out in the financial inclusion landscape through a combination of innovative business and partnership models, technological breakthroughs, and a deeply localized approach. Our key differentiators include:

Hybrid Digital Access Model (USSD + Mobile App):

Unparalleled Reach: Unlike many digital financial services that are solely app-based, BUCKSUP's foundational reliance on USSD technology ensures universal accessibility. This is a critical differentiator in Sub-Saharan Africa, where feature phone penetration remains high and internet connectivity can be unreliable. We don't just cater to smartphone users; we actively include the "unconnected."

Seamless Transition: While providing robust USSD services, our mobile app offers an enhanced, richer user experience for smartphone users, allowing for future-proof scalability and advanced features. This hybrid approach ensures no one is left behind.

AI-Powered Inclusive Digital Identity & Alternative Credit Scoring:

Beyond Traditional KYC: BUCKSUP's AI-driven digital identity framework is a significant breakthrough. It addresses the pervasive challenge of lack of formal identification among the unbanked by leveraging a diverse array of alternative data points (e.g., mobile usage patterns, utility payments, community referrals, social graph analysis). This allows us to establish verifiable identities and onboard individuals who would otherwise be excluded from formal financial systems.

Fair and Dynamic Lending: Our proprietary AI credit scoring models go beyond conventional credit bureaus. They analyze these alternative data sets to assess creditworthiness dynamically and fairly, enabling the provision of personalized microloans with terms tailored to individual repayment capacities. This reduces bias and expands access to credit for previously underserved populations.

Deep Localization and Community Integration:

Cultural Nuance in Design: BUCKSUP's solution is not a "copy-paste" of Western models. We emphasize deep localization in UI/UX design, language support, and product offerings, ensuring they resonate with local cultural contexts and financial behaviors (e.g., understanding informal savings groups like "stokvels").

Grassroots Partnerships: Our strong emphasis on partnerships with local community organizations and NGOs at the grassroots level is unique. This enables effective last-mile delivery, builds trust, and facilitates financial literacy education in a culturally sensitive manner.

Proactive Regulatory Collaboration:

Co-creating the Future: Instead of merely reacting to regulations, BUCKSUP aims for proactive collaboration with regulatory bodies. This includes contributing to the development of adaptive policies that foster digital financial innovation while ensuring consumer protection and financial stability, creating a more enabling environment for inclusive finance.

Data-Driven Social Impact:

Quantifiable Development: Our solution is designed with a clear focus on measurable social impact. By meticulously tracking financial inclusion metrics, income generation, and economic resilience, we can demonstrate tangible contributions to poverty reduction, economic growth, and reduced inequalities, providing valuable data for policymakers and development partners.
Sustainable Change:
BUCKSUP's Contribution to Sustainable, Systemic Change: A Theory of Change
BUCKSUP's vision extends beyond simply providing financial services; we aim to be a catalyst for fundamental, lasting change in the financial and economic landscape of Sub-Saharan Africa. Our Theory of Change outlines the causal pathway from our solution's deployment to the desired long-term, systemic impacts.

Direct Outputs of BUCKSUP:
Increased Access to Digital Financial Services: Millions of previously unbanked and underbanked individuals and MSMEs gain access to microloans, savings accounts, payment services, and digital wallets via both USSD and mobile applications.

Establishment of Inclusive Digital Identities: Individuals lacking traditional identification acquire a verifiable digital identity, overcoming a significant barrier to formal economic participation.

Enhanced Financial Literacy: Users receive tailored financial education embedded within the platform, improving their understanding of financial products, responsible money management, and digital security.

Data-Driven Creditworthiness Assessment: Our AI models create alternative credit scores for individuals and MSMEs, enabling fair and personalized lending decisions based on non-traditional data.

Intermediate Outcomes (Short-to-Medium Term):
As individuals and businesses leverage BUCKSUP's outputs, the following changes begin to materialize:

Improved Financial Management: Users gain better control over their finances, leading to increased savings, more efficient payment management, and reduced reliance on volatile cash transactions.

Increased Economic Activity at the Micro-Level:

MSME Growth: Small businesses, now with access to microloans and efficient payment systems, can invest in inventory, expand operations, and reach new markets, leading to increased revenue and profitability.

Entrepreneurship Stimulation: More individuals are empowered to start and grow small businesses, fostering a vibrant local entrepreneurial ecosystem.

Reduced Vulnerability to Shocks: Access to savings and micro-insurance (future offering) enables households to better withstand unexpected expenses (e.g., health emergencies, crop failures), preventing them from falling deeper into poverty.

Greater Digital Inclusion: As users become more comfortable and proficient with digital financial tools, their overall digital literacy increases, opening doors to other digital services and opportunities.

Enhanced Trust in Digital Systems: Secure and reliable transactions, coupled with transparent processes, build trust in digital financial services and the broader digital economy.

Long-Term Impacts & Systemic Change:
The sustained accumulation of these intermediate outcomes leads to profound, systemic shifts:

Formalization of Informal Economies (SDG 8, 10): By providing accessible and beneficial financial services, BUCKSUP incentivizes informal businesses and workers to transition into the formal economy. This leads to increased tax revenues for governments, better social protections for workers, and more robust economic data for planning.

Reduced Poverty and Inequality (SDG 1, 10): As millions gain economic agency and grow their livelihoods, there is a measurable reduction in poverty rates. The solution disproportionately benefits marginalized groups (women, rural populations), leading to a significant narrowing of economic disparities.

Strengthened Financial Ecosystems (SDG 9, 16): BUCKSUP's innovative approach demonstrates viable models for serving previously excluded segments, encouraging traditional financial institutions and new fintech players to adopt more inclusive practices. This fosters a more competitive, efficient, and resilient financial sector. The digital identity component strengthens the foundational infrastructure for a trusted digital economy.
Funding Sources:
BUCKSUP's initial development and operations have been primarily funded through bootstrapping. This means that the founders have leveraged personal savings, early revenue generated from initial pilot programs, and a highly lean operational model to build and grow the solution.

While bootstrapping has allowed us to maintain full control over our vision and product development, we recognize the need for strategic external funding to scale our impact across Sub-Saharan Africa. We are actively exploring partnerships with impact investors, development finance institutions, and grants that align with our mission of driving financial inclusion and sustainable development.
Primary thematic focus area: Enabling Policies & Regulatory Innovation
Summary: BUCKSUP is an AI-driven decentralized banking concept designed to bridge financial inclusion gaps for the unbanked and underbanked in Sub-Saharan Africa. It combines USSD-based access (for feature phones) with a mobile app (for smartphones), creating a hybrid model for universal accessibility. The platform leverages AI and alternative data for inclusive digital identity and credit scoring, enabling microloans, secure transfers, and financial literacy integration. It envisions onboarding 50 million new users in 5 years, with a strong focus on MSME empowerment, women’s economic inclusion, and systemic financial transformation.

Title: BIOMAX PLUS
Subtitle: BIOMAX PLUS is a smart livestock monitoring system combining GPS tracking and early disease detection via a connected collar and mobile app, improving herd health and productivity.
Problem Statement: Livestock farmers face major losses from late disease detection, theft, and poor herd management. Limited access to real-time data worsens productivity and threatens food security.
Solution Overview:
BIOMAX PLUS is a connected livestock management system combining a smart collar and a mobile app. The collar collects real-time data on animal health (temperature, activity, rumination) and GPS location. This data is sent to the app, which alerts farmers to early disease signs, abnormal behavior, or theft, improving herd productivity and security.
Technologies used: IoT sensors, GPS, data analytics & AI, user-friendly mobile application, and secure cloud architecture.
Partnerships: veterinarians for health monitoring, telecom operators for connectivity, farmer cooperatives for adoption, research institutes for algorithm improvement, and hardware manufacturers for durable collar design.
Solution Provider(s): BIOMAX PLUS – AgriTech startup specializing in smart livestock management solutions. 	•	Ministry of Livestock and Animal Production (Guinea) – Government partner supporting animal health and productivity initiatives. 	•	Guinean Veterinary Association (AGV) – Network of veterinary professionals providing health monitoring and field expertise. 	•	Orange Guinée – Telecom operator ensuring reliable rural connectivity for data transmission. 	•	Institut Supérieur des Sciences et de Médecine Vétérinaire de Dalaba (ISSMV) – Research and training institution supporting algorithm development and disease detection accuracy. 	•	Hardware manufacturing partners – Companies specialized in durable IoT devices and sensor integration for livestock monitoring.
Implementation location(s): Location(s) of implementation:  Pilot implementation is currently underway in Guinea, specifically in the regions of Kindia, Mamou, and Labé.
Implementation timeline(s): Timeline(s) of implementation: Pilot phase started in January 2025 and is ongoing, with planned expansion through December 2025.
Duration to pilot in a new geography: The estimated duration to pilot BIOMAX PLUS in a new geography is 6 to 9 months, including site assessment, hardware deployment, training, and data calibration.
SDGs addressed: SDG 2 (Zero Hunger);SDG 3 (Good Health and Well-being);SDG 9 (Industry, Innovation, and Infrastructure);
Desired impact: BIOMAX PLUS aims to reduce livestock mortality and boost productivity by enabling early disease detection and better herd management. The solution improves farmers’ income by minimizing losses from illness and theft, while supporting food security. So far, it has helped decrease animal deaths by 30% and increase productivity by 20%. Additionally, BIOMAX PLUS creates local jobs in installation, training, and veterinary services, contributing to both economic growth and environmental sustainability.
Key technologies: BIOMAX PLUS uses IoT-enabled smart collars to monitor livestock health and location in real time. AI-powered data analytics detect early disease signs and abnormal behavior. GPS technology helps prevent theft and manage grazing, while cloud computing ensures secure data storage accessible via a user-friendly mobile app.
Unique Characteristics: BIOMAX PLUS stands out through its integration of real-time health monitoring and GPS tracking in a single, affordable collar tailored for local conditions. Its AI-driven early disease detection enables proactive herd management, reducing losses significantly. The solution’s collaborative model—partnering with veterinarians, telecom providers, and farmer cooperatives—ensures wide accessibility and support. Additionally, its cloud-based platform offers remote monitoring and easy scalability, making it a comprehensive, cost-effective tool for improving livestock productivity in underserved rural areas.
Sustainable Change: BIOMAX PLUS drives sustainable, systemic change by empowering farmers with real-time data to improve animal health and productivity, leading to increased incomes and food security. Early disease detection reduces livestock losses, lowering the need for emergency treatments and antibiotics, thus promoting healthier ecosystems. The technology fosters stronger veterinary networks and farmer cooperation, building local capacity and resilience. Over time, this creates a scalable model that modernizes livestock management, supports rural livelihoods, and encourages responsible resource use, contributing to long-term economic and environmental sustainability in agricultural communities.
Funding Sources: Previous implementations of BIOMAX PLUS have been funded through a combination of sources including government grants from the Ministry of Livestock and Animal Production, research funding from academic institutions, private investments from AgriTech investors, and support from international development organizations focused on agriculture and rural development. Additionally, partnerships with telecom operators have provided in-kind support for connectivity infrastructure.
Testimonials and Endorsements:
Currently, there are no publicly available testimonials or endorsements specifically from stakeholders or beneficiaries of the BIOMAX PLUS solution. The solution is still in its pilot phase in Guinea, with plans for expansion through December 2025. As the project progresses, feedback from farmers, veterinarians, and other stakeholders will be collected and documented to assess the impact and effectiveness of the solution.
For more information or updates on the project, you may contact the implementing partners or visit the official websites and social media pages of the involved organizations.
Primary thematic focus area: Stable and Resilient Digital Supply Chains
Summary: BIOMAX PLUS is a proof-of-concept smart livestock monitoring system in Guinea combining IoT-enabled collars, GPS, and AI for early disease detection, theft prevention, and productivity management. Strengths: strong technological innovation, measurable early impact (30% mortality reduction, 20% productivity increase), and solid multi-stakeholder partnerships (government, vets, telecoms, academia). Weaknesses: still at prototype stage, limited scale, no independent testimonials yet, and hardware deployment challenges could affect affordability and scalability.

Name of your organization: Idara Baraye Taleem o Taraqi (IBT) Pakistan
Title: DigiTaleem: Empowering Rural Youth Through Inclusive Digital Skills
Subtitle: Bridging the digital divide by enabling youth-led innovation, entrepreneurship, and economic participation in marginalized regions.
Problem Statement: Millions of rural youth, especially in conflict-affected and underserved regions, face systemic barriers to accessing digital skills, economic tools, and entrepreneurial opportunities. Gender inequality, poor internet access, and lack of contextual training further widen the digital economy gap.
Solution Overview:
DigiTaleem is a blended digital-physical skills empowerment platform focused on rural youth in Pakistan, particularly women and girls. The initiative combines:

Community Tech Hubs offering digital skills bootcamps and entrepreneurial training.

A mobile-based eLearning platform for continuous remote access to tools, including financial literacy, e-commerce training, and AI-based content creation.

Offline-first models for low-connectivity areas (using micro-SD kits and solar-powered devices).

Partnerships: Collaborating with IBT (a grassroots NGO), Aizal Parsa Collections (youth-led e-commerce), and local schools and tech startups for curriculum delivery and mentorship.
Solution Provider(s): Idara Baraye Taleem-o-Taraqi (IBT) – Nonprofit focused on education and development in Swat, Pakistan.  Aizal Parsa Collections – Social enterprise led by rural women entrepreneurs.  Digital Empowerment Foundation – Digital inclusion and skills partner (regional).  Pakistan Freelancers Forum – Volunteer-based mentoring and remote work pipeline.
Implementation location(s): Swat, Khyber Pakhtunkhwa, Pakistan Pilot locations: Bahrain Valley, Kalam, and Mingora
Implementation timeline(s): Start: November 2023 Ongoing: Second phase begins September 2025
Duration to pilot in a new geography: 3–6 months (includes contextual research, curriculum localization, and stakeholder onboarding)
SDGs addressed: SDG 4 (Quality Education);SDG 5 (Gender Equality);SDG 8 (Decent Work and Economic Growth);
Desired impact:
Objectives:

Equip 5,000+ rural youth (60% women) with job-ready digital skills

Enable 100+ youth-led MSMEs to access e-commerce platforms

Bridge gender and geography-based digital access gaps

Key Achievements:

1,200 learners trained in first pilot

35 micro-entrepreneurs launched digital stores

Over 300% increase in digital income streams among participants.
Key technologies:
Mobile-first LMS

Offline eLearning Kits

AI-based content translation tools (local languages)

Cloud-based case tracking and mentoring via Airtable and Notion

WhatsApp automation for onboarding & engagement
Unique Characteristics:
Offline-first deployment in fragile connectivity zones

Gender-inclusive curriculum with trauma-informed pedagogy

Community-led implementation by trained youth facilitators

Financial sustainability through youth micro-enterprise reinvestment
Sustainable Change: DigiTaleem addresses root digital exclusion by embedding digital skills within local ecosystems. It enables long-term economic participation by fostering entrepreneurship, improving access to remote income sources, and amplifying youth voices in decision-making. The cascading effect includes job creation, education reform, and increased digital governance capacity from the ground up.
Funding Sources: The solution has been primarily funded through community-based fundraising initiatives, personal contributions, and in-kind support from local educational institutions and civil society partners. Small grants were received from local donors under the umbrella of the Green Earth Society and Idara Baraye Taleem wa Taraqi (IBT). Additionally, revenue from Aizal Parsa Collections has been reinvested into grassroots awareness workshops and digital literacy drives for girls in rural areas.
Testimonials and Endorsements:

Summary: DigiTaleem is a blended digital-physical skills empowerment platform targeting rural youth in Pakistan, with a special focus on women and girls. A strength is its demonstrated pilot success with 1,200 trained learners and 35 digital entrepreneurs already active (Q22, Q19). Title: FarmConnect Digital Centers: Climate Smart Farms for Women
Subtitle: Hybrid digital centers empowering African women farmers with offline/online climate tools, markets, and finance to beat poverty and climate shocks.
Problem Statement: Millions of smallholder farmers in Malawi and throughout Africa lack access to digital tools, market information, and innovative agricultural technologies.  This digital divide keeps people in poverty, reduces productivity, and keeps them off from supply chains and innovation.  Young people and women are particularly affected, resulting in missed opportunities and increasing inequality.
Solution Overview:
FarmConnect is a non-profit digital platform that uses mobile technology, GIS mapping, and artificial intelligence (AI) tools to connect smallholder farmers, particularly youth and women, to markets, training, and digital farming techniques.

How it works:

Farmers register via SMS or mobile app.

GPS and satellite data help map farm plots.

We analyze soil health, crop types, and seasonal trends using AI.

Personalized farming tips and market prices are sent to farmers in local languages.

Buyers and agri-businesses can access farmer profiles and production forecasts.


TECHNOLOGIES USED 

1. Artificial Intelligence (AI)

2. Internet of Things (IoT) for soil sensors (planned in future versions)

3. Geographic Information Systems (GIS)

4. Mobile app and USSD/SMS interfaces

5. Partnerships and collaboration models:

6. Local government agriculture offices

7. Malawi Ministry of Agriculture 

8. Youth and women cooperatives

9. Local telecom providers for affordable access (Airtel Malawi)

10. Regional universities (mostly LUANAR) for agri-tech R&D
Solution Provider(s): ClimateWise Organization (Lead), Airtel Malawi (Tech Partner), National Smallholder Farmers' Association of Malawi (NSFAM), UN Women Malawi (Gender Advisor)
Implementation location(s): Southern Malawi – Zomba, Phalombe, and Chikwawa districts
Duration to pilot in a new geography: 4 - 6 Months
SDGs addressed: SDG 1 (No Poverty);SDG 8 (Decent Work and Economic Growth);SDG 9 (Industry, Innovation, and Infrastructure);
Desired impact:
1. Train 5,000 women farmers in climate smart tech by 2026.  
2. Increase crop yields by 35% and incomes by 50% for center users.  
3. Cut carbon emissions by promoting drought resistant crops.
Key technologies: Hybrid USSD/SMS platforms, IoT soil sensors, AI for crop advice, Solar powered centers
Unique Characteristics:
Built from the ground up with youth and women farmers in mind

Accessible through both smartphones and basic mobile phones

Multilingual: Supports English and Chichewa

Community led data collection and support networks

Open source and replicable model for other regions
Sustainable Change:
Digital access leads to climate-resilient farming, higher revenues, economic empowerment for women, sustainable community centers, and widespread replication throughout Africa.
 
Long-term: Ends cycles of climate vulnerability, gender inequity, and poverty.
Funding Sources: ClimateWise seed funding, Airtel Malawi (tech grants), UNDP Malawi (pilot grant)
Further comments/feedback: This questionnaire has been very clear and well-structured. Thank you for creating a platform that values local, inclusive, and sustainable innovation. We hope to see more such calls focused on Africa and underserved farming communities.
Primary thematic focus area: Inclusive Digital Innovation Skills & Entrepreneurial Talent Development
Summary: FarmConnect Digital Centers est une initiative de ClimateWise visant à autonomiser les femmes agricultrices en Afrique via des centres hybrides (SMS/USSD + mobile app) offrant conseils climato-intelligents, accès aux marchés et services financiers (Q12, Q15). Actuellement en phase pilote au sud du Malawi (Zomba, Phalombe, Chikwawa), le projet utilise l’IA, le SIG et des capteurs IoT (future intégration) pour améliorer la productivité et résilience climatique (Q13, Q21). Objectif : former 5 000 femmes d’ici 2026, augmenter de 35% les rendements et de 50% les revenus (Q21). Aligné avec les ODD 1, 8, 9, il repose sur des partenariats solides avec Airtel Malawi, UN Women, NSFAM, et le ministère de l’Agriculture (Q14, Q25).

Title: SMART Africa
Subtitle: Solutions for agriculture and Tech proficiency
Problem Statement: We are a consortium of many startups that provides solutions for agriculture, Management and Education.
Solution Overview:
We harness drones, sensors, and robotics to deliver versatile and innovative solutions for farming and agriculture. Our technology empowers farmers to monitor crops and livestock more effectively, improving decision-making and operational efficiency.

Our goal is to enhance agricultural productivity while addressing critical challenges such as environmental pollution and labor shortages.

Methodology
Our approach is based on the intelligent integration of Artificial Intelligence (AI), Robotics, and the Internet of Things (IoT) to create a smart agricultural ecosystem.

IoT sensors are deployed across fields and livestock areas to collect real-time environmental and biological data (soil moisture, temperature, crop health, animal movement, etc.).

AI algorithms analyze this data to detect patterns, predict risks (such as disease outbreaks or drought), and generate recommendations for optimized resource use.

Autonomous drones and robotic units are used for precision tasks such as aerial mapping, spraying, and livestock monitoring — reducing the need for manual labor and improving accuracy.


We work in close collaboration with Guinean tech start-ups and local innovators to co-develop and adapt our technologies to the specific needs and constraints of rural communities. This local partnership ensures contextual relevance, boosts local entrepreneurship, and strengthens the innovation ecosystem in Guinea.
Solution Provider(s): Partners : Alysites Sarl- IT startup, that provides IA and peonalised softwares , Avicosoft - IoT solutions for agriculture, Nimba hub - Educational training
Duration to pilot in a new geography: 6 months
SDGs addressed: SDG 3 (Good Health and Well-being);SDG 9 (Industry, Innovation, and Infrastructure);SDG 8 (Decent Work and Economic Growth);
Desired impact:
Desired Impact of Our Solution

Solution Objectives

Enhance agricultural productivity through the use of AI, robotics, and IoT technologies tailored to the local needs of farmers.

Reduce the environmental impact of agricultural practices by promoting precision farming and efficient resource use.

Address the growing shortage of agricultural labor through automation and intelligent monitoring.

Empower local innovation by partnering with Guinean start-ups and supporting job creation in the agri-tech sector.


Key Achievements or Expected Impacts

Productivity Gains: Up to 30% increase in crop yields through data-driven decision-making and early detection of threats (disease, drought, etc.).

GHG Emissions Reductions: Reduction in chemical and water usage by 20–40%, helping to lower greenhouse gas emissions linked to overuse of fertilizers and water pumping.

Labor Efficiency: Reduction of manual field monitoring by over 50%, allowing farmers to focus on higher-value tasks.

Job Creation: Indirect generation of 25–50 local jobs per deployment zone in device maintenance, data analysis, and training roles through collaboration with Guinean tech start-ups.

Knowledge Transfer: Creation of local expertise in smart agriculture, fostering long-term innovation capacity within rural communities.
Key technologies: AI, IoT, Robotics , Mechanical designs
Unique Characteristics:
Our solution stands out through a combination of technological innovation, local integration, and inclusive business models:

1. Integrated Tech Stack (AI + IoT + Robotics):
We combine Artificial Intelligence, Internet of Things, and robotics into a unified and scalable platform. This end-to-end system enables real-time monitoring, predictive analytics, and autonomous interventions — delivering precision agriculture tailored to local contexts.

2. Localized Innovation via Start-up Partnerships:
Unlike top-down imported solutions, our model is grounded in active collaboration with Guinean start-ups and local developers. This co-creation approach ensures the solution is culturally appropriate, cost-effective, and sustainable, while fostering the local tech ecosystem.

3. Low-Cost, Modular Design:
Our hardware (drones, sensors, robots) is designed to be modular and repairable locally, using open-source and affordable components. This reduces maintenance costs and dependency on international suppliers.

4. Inclusive Business Model:
We offer a “tech-as-a-service” model allowing smallholder farmers to access advanced technologies through cooperatives or agricultural unions, minimizing upfront investment and encouraging broad adoption.

5. Scalable Impact through Local Workforce Training:
We integrate training and capacity-building programs to form local technician teams for deployment, maintenance, and data support — turning farmers and youth into active participants in the digital agriculture value chain.

6. Environmental and Social Impact Alignment:
Our solution is built to directly contribute to SDGs 2, 8, 9, 12, and 13, making it both technologically advanced and developmentally aligned — with measurable impacts in productivity, employment, and climate resilience.
Sustainable Change:
Our solution is designed not only to address immediate agricultural challenges, but to catalyze long-term, systemic transformation in the agricultural and technological landscape of Guinea and similar regions.

Theory of Change

Inputs

Advanced technologies (AI, IoT, robotics)

Partnerships with Guinean start-ups and cooperatives

Capacity-building and technical training programs

Affordable access model for smallholder farmers


Activities

Deployment of smart agricultural tools in the field

Collection and analysis of real-time data for decision support

Training of local technicians and farmer groups

Continuous feedback and improvement with local actors


Outputs

Increased access to precision agriculture tools

Real-time monitoring of crops and livestock health

Skilled local workforce in agri-tech operations

Strengthened tech-agriculture linkages in Guinea


Outcomes

Improved yields and reduced environmental impact

Enhanced resilience to climate variability

Reduced dependence on imported technologies

Empowered local start-ups and youth employment


Long-Term Impact

A self-sustaining ecosystem where digital agriculture is led and maintained by local actors

Structural transformation of the agricultural sector through innovation, resilience, and inclusion

Scalable model that can be replicated in other West African countries facing similar challenges


By integrating local innovation, inclusive economic participation, and sustainable technology, our solution acts as a lever for systemic change — shifting agriculture from subsistence to a data-driven, efficient, and resilient sector.
Funding Sources:
Our solution is financed through a hybrid model, combining:

Self-financing (equity investment by the founders and core team), demonstrating strong commitment and ownership of the solution.

Private investors and impact-driven partners, particularly those aligned with climate resilience, agri-tech innovation, and inclusive economic development in West Africa.
Primary thematic focus area: MSME Empowerment & Local Digital Innovation
Summary: SMART Africa est un consortium de start-ups (Guinée + partenaires) développant un écosystème agricole intelligent intégrant IA, IoT et robotique (Q12, Q20). La solution vise à accroître la productivité agricole, réduire l’impact environnemental et combler le déficit de main-d’œuvre en automatisant la surveillance et les interventions agricoles (Q13). Des drones, capteurs IoT et unités robotiques fournissent données en temps réel, analyses prédictives et interventions de précision (Q13, Q22). Le modèle repose sur l’innovation locale via start-ups guinéennes, un design modulaire à faible coût et un modèle d’accès coopératif pour les petits exploitants (Q22). Attendu : +30 % de rendement, -20 à -40 % d’intrants, création d’emplois locaux, montée en compétence de jeunes dans l’agritech (Q16). Actuellement en phase prototype (Q15).

Title: FINDAARA
Subtitle: Innovation technologique en Aviculture en Guinée
Problem Statement:
1.⁠ ⁠Problème à résoudre

L’aviculture en Afrique, et particulièrement en Guinée, fait face à plusieurs défis majeurs :
	•	Faible taux d’éclosion des œufs dus à un manque de contrôle précis des paramètres d’incubation.
	•	Mortalité élevée des poussins en raison d’un environnement inadapté et d’un suivi sanitaire insuffisant.
	•	Difficulté à écouler la production pour les petits éleveurs à cause du manque de canaux de distribution fiables.

Findaara apporte une solution intégrée grâce à des technologies intelligentes et une plateforme de commercialisation.
Solution Overview: Findaara révolutionne l’aviculture en Guinée et en Afrique avec des couveuses intelligentes, une ferme automatisée et une IA de détection des maladies. Nous réduisons le gaspillage, renforçons la sécurité alimentaire et autonomisons les éleveurs grâce à la technologie et au e-commerce.
Solution Provider(s): -ANSUTEN (Agence numérique des services universels des telecommunications et du numérique) en Guinée.-Orange Digital center de Ratoma-Guinée
Duration to pilot in a new geography: 6 Mois
SDGs addressed: SDG 2 (Zero Hunger);SDG 3 (Good Health and Well-being);SDG 9 (Industry, Innovation, and Infrastructure);
Desired impact:
Findaara révolutionne l’élevage avicole en Guinée et en Afrique avec des solutions technologiques durables et socialement responsables.

Optimisation des ressources et réduction du gaspillage

Nos couveuses intelligentes écoénergétiques et notre ferme automatisée optimisent l’alimentation et l’environnement des poussins, réduisant les pertes et le gaspillage.

Sécurité alimentaire et autonomisation des éleveurs

En améliorant la survie des poussins, nous augmentons la production locale et rendons les protéines plus accessibles. Grâce à des formations et une plateforme e-commerce, nous aidons les éleveurs à mieux vendre leurs produits et à accroître leurs revenus.

Impact environnemental et durabilité

Nos solutions réduisent l’empreinte carbone en limitant les importations et en favorisant un élevage plus efficace et moins gourmand en ressources naturelles.

Conclusion

Findaara allie innovation, durabilité et inclusion sociale pour moderniser l’aviculture et améliorer les conditions de vie des éleveurs.

Name of your organization: Passerelle  de Recherche et Action sur l'Inclusion Numérique Sociale et Financière  d'Afrique (PRAINSFA)
Title: +229Connect: Community-Driven Digital Inclusion Network
Subtitle: Empowering marginalized communities in Benin through trained volunteer digital navigators, bridging the digital divide with culturally-adapted peer-to-peer learning.
Problem Statement:
Benin faces significant digital inclusion challenges that limit economic participation and social inclusion for marginalized communities. With only 33.8% internet penetration nationally and a severe gender digital divide (63.2% gap in internet access between men and women), many Beninese are excluded from increasingly digitalized essential services.
Key challenges include:

- Limited internet access: Only 33.8% of the population has internet access
- Gender inequality: Significant disparities with women representing only 37.6% of social media users
- Geographic disparities: Rural areas face greater connectivity and digital literacy challenges
- Service digitalization: Government, banking, and healthcare services increasingly moving online
- Lack of local support: Insufficient culturally-adapted digital literacy programs
- Language barriers: Most digital services and training available only in French

The rapid digitalization of essential services banking, healthcare, government services, and commerce creates barriers for those without digital skills, perpetuating exclusion from economic opportunities and essential services.
Solution Overview:
+229Connect is an innovative community-driven digital inclusion network that mobilizes, trains, and coordinates volunteer digital navigators to provide peer-to-peer digital literacy support across Benin.
How it works:
Our solution operates through a comprehensive community engagement model:

- Community Volunteer Network: We recruit and train volunteer digital navigators from local communities including students, professionals, retirees, and community leaders. Each volunteer receives structured training in digital pedagogy, essential digital skills, priority digital services, and cultural sensitivity approaches.

- Multilingual Community-Based Services: Trained volunteers provide:
   Individual digital coaching sessions
   Group workshops conducted in local languages (French, Fon, Yoruba, Dendi)
   Mobile digital literacy clinics reaching rural communities
   Specialized support for women entrepreneurs, elderly citizens, and small business owners

- Digital Coordination Platform: A multilingual mobile platform coordinates volunteer activities, tracks progress, provides ongoing training resources, and connects beneficiaries to relevant digital services.

Methodologies:

- Cultural Adaptation: All training materials and methods adapted to local contexts, incorporating local languages and cultural practices
- Peer Learning Model: Community members teaching community members, leveraging existing trust relationships and social networks
- Progressive Skill Building: Structured learning pathways from basic digital awareness to advanced digital entrepreneurship
- Gender-Responsive Approach: Specialized methodologies addressing cultural barriers to women's digital participation
- Inclusive Design: Accessible approaches for elderly citizens and people with disabilities

Technologies Used:

- Mobile-first learning platform with offline capabilities for low-connectivity environments
- SMS-based coordination system accessible on basic phones
- Multilingual interface supporting local languages
- Cloud-based volunteer management and coordination system
- Data analytics dashboard for impact monitoring and program optimization

Partnership Model:

- Government Partners: Ministry of Digital Economy, local municipalities for policy alignment and infrastructure support
 - Private Sector: Telecom operators, banks, and fintech companies for technical infrastructure and service integration
- Civil Society: Women's associations, youth organizations, and religious groups for community mobilization
- International Partners: UN agencies, development organizations, and academic institutions for technical expertise and funding

Innovation Elements:

- First comprehensive volunteer-based digital inclusion network in West Africa
- Deep integration of local languages and cultural practices in digital literacy training
- Mobile-first, offline-capable approach suitable for African connectivity contexts
- Holistic ecosystem approach linking digital skills development directly to economic opportunities.
Solution Provider(s): Lead Organization: PRAINSFA (Passerelle de Recherche et Action sur l'Inclusion Numérique Sociale et Financière d'Afrique) - Non-profit organization, Digital inclusion and financial literacy sector Future key Partners: Ministry of Digital Economy and Digitalization of Benin - Government, Digital policy and infrastructure sector, Telecommunications and mobile money sector, MTN Benin - Private sector, Moov Africa Benin - Private sector, University of Abomey-Calavi - Academic institution, Research and education sector, Vital Finance - Private sector, Microfinance and digital financial services sector, UN Women Benin - International organization, Gender equality and women's empowerment sector, Association des Femmes du Bénin - Civil society, Women's rights and economic empowerment sector, Centre Songhaï - Non-profit, Agricultural innovation and rural development sector
Duration to pilot in a new geography: 12-18 months for complete pilot implementation in a new geography, including:  3 months: Stakeholder mapping, partnership development, and regulatory compliance 2 months: Volunteer recruitment, selection, and initial training 6 months: Active service delivery and community engagement 3 months: Impact evaluation, documentation, and program optimization
SDGs addressed: SDG 4 (Quality Education);SDG 5 (Gender Equality);SDG 8 (Decent Work and Economic Growth);
Desired impact:
Solution Objectives:

- Digital Skills Development: Provide essential digital competencies to underserved communities through peer-to-peer learning
- Economic Empowerment: Enable MSMEs and entrepreneurs to access digital markets, tools, and financial services
- Gender Digital Inclusion: Address specific barriers preventing women from participating in the digital economy
- Geographic Coverage: Extend digital inclusion services to rural and underserved areas
Sustainable Community Network: Establish self-sustaining volunteer networks that continue beyond initial program funding

Anticipated Quantifiable Impacts:

- Skills Development: Significant number of individuals trained in essential digital literacy competencies
- Economic Opportunities: MSMEs and small businesses gaining access to digital tools and markets
Gender Participation: Increased women's participation in digital skills programs and digital entrepreneurship
- Service Access: Improved ability of community members to independently access government, financial, and healthcare services online
- Network Sustainability: High volunteer retention rates demonstrating strong community ownership and commitment
- Cost Efficiency: Reduced cost-per-beneficiary compared to traditional institutional training models

Broader Social Impact:

- Reduced digital exclusion affecting rural and marginalized communities
- Increased women's economic participation and decision-making capacity
- Enhanced community access to essential digital services (healthcare, education, government services)
- Strengthened social cohesion through intergenerational and peer learning networks
Improved community resilience through enhanced digital literacy and access
Key technologies:
Core Technology Platform:

- Mobile Learning Application: Progressive Web App (PWA) with offline functionality, ensuring accessibility in low-connectivity environments
- Multi-language Support: Interface supporting French and major local languages (Fon, Yoruba, Dendi)
- SMS Integration: Bulk SMS capabilities for coordination and communication with basic phone users
- Cloud Infrastructure: Scalable cloud services for data management and platform reliability
- Analytics Dashboard: Real-time monitoring and evaluation tools for program coordination

Supporting Technology Systems:

- Volunteer Management System: Comprehensive platform for volunteer coordination, training tracking, and communication
- Video Communication Tools: Low-bandwidth video solutions for remote training and support
- Mobile Money Integration: API connections to local mobile money providers for digital financial inclusion
- Geolocation Services: GPS-based coordination for mobile digital literacy clinics and impact mapping
- Digital Certification System: Secure, verifiable digital badges and certificates for skills recognition

Technology Innovation Approach:

- Offline-First Design: Core functionality available without internet connectivity
- Cultural and Linguistic Localization: Technology adapted for local contexts and languages
- User-Centered Design: Interfaces optimized for users with limited prior digital experience
- Community Network Architecture: Technology supporting peer-to-peer learning and knowledge sharing
Unique Characteristics:
Community-Driven Innovation:

- Local Ownership Model: Volunteers are community members, not external trainers, ensuring deep cultural understanding and long-term sustainability
- Peer-to-Peer Methodology: Leverages existing social networks and trust relationships for more effective learning
- Cultural Integration: First digital inclusion program in Benin to fully integrate local languages and cultural practices into training methodology

Technology Innovation:

- Multilingual Digital Platform: Comprehensive platform supporting local Beninese languages with culturally-adapted content
- Hybrid Online-Offline Model: Functions effectively in low-connectivity environments typical of many African contexts
- Community-Responsive Design: Technology and content adapted based on continuous community feedback and local needs assessment

Partnership Model Innovation:

- Multi-Sector Ecosystem: Coordinates government, private sector, civil society, and international partners in unified framework
- Mutual Value Creation: All partners gain tangible benefits while contributing resources and expertise
- Knowledge Co-Creation: Communities actively participate in developing and refining training methodologies and content

Title: Financial Inclusion for Waste Pickers in Nigeria
Subtitle: We are delivering accessible micro-loans and digital financial services to rural waste pickers and other actors in the recycling value chain
Problem Statement:
Rural waste pickers and other informal recyclers remain trapped in a cycle of low productivity because they face three inter-locking barriers:

1. No Affordable Working Capital: With irregular daily earnings and no collateral, they cannot secure small, short-term loans to buy better tools, bulk materials, or finance transportation; forcing them to rely on predatory lenders who charge rates that can exceed 10 % to 15 % per month.

2. Missing Data for Credit Scoring: The absence of reliable transaction records leaves lenders unable to gauge risk, so deserving borrowers are rejected or over-charged.

3. Stunted Sector Growth: Without fair, accessible credit, waste pickers and micro-aggregators cannot scale their operations, limiting material recovery, income potential, and the environmental benefits a stronger recycling economy would deliver.
Solution Overview:
Our solution, Wapfi, addreses the financial gap among waste pickers by embedding accessible digital financial services (micro-loans, cashless payments, and data-driven credit scoring) directly into the daily workflows of waste pickers and other value-chain participants.

We provide instant microloans through a simple mobile-first platform, which allows borrowers to repay with recyclables (or cash if preferred) by dropping off plastic, metal, or paper at a partner recycling hub.

The value of their materials is instantly logged against their loan, creating a seamless repayment process that aligns with their daily work. 

Our dynamic credit engine rewards consistent recycling and on-time performance with access to larger loans, creating a powerful incentive for both financial responsibility and environmental impact.

Built on a secure, CBN-compliant infrastructure and supported by a robust ecosystem, we are partnering with recycling companies, NGOs, and industry associations, specifically Chanja Datti Recycling Co. Limited, the Waste Pickers Association of Nigeria (WAPAN), the Association of Waste Pickers of Lagos State (AWOL), and the Recyclers Association of Nigeria (RAN), to anchor our operations. These organisations supply verified member data for KYC, run the collection hubs where loan repayments are logged, and provide on-the-ground support that keeps the entire Wapfi ecosystem transparent, trusted, and fully integrated into Nigeria’s circular economy value chain.
Solution Provider(s): Chanja Datti Recycling Co. Limited Waste Pickers Association of Nigeria (WAPAN) Recyclers Association of Nigeria (RAN) Initiative for the Advancement of Waste Management in Africa (W.A.S.T.E Africa)
Duration to pilot in a new geography: 8 weeks
SDGs addressed: SDG 1 (No Poverty);SDG 8 (Decent Work and Economic Growth);SDG 12 (Responsible Consumption and Production);
Desired impact:
Solution Objectives
Unlock affordable credit for informal recyclers: Disburse fast, collateral-free microloans that let waste pickers buy better tools, bulk purchase materials, and smooth daily cash flow.


Turn recycling data into bankable credit histories: Capture every kilogram collected and repayment made, feeding a dynamic score that qualifies borrowers for steadily larger loans.


Drive circular economy growth and climate benefits: Channel more plastics, aluminium and paper into formal recovery streams, cutting both poverty and greenhouse gas emissions in one loop.

Key Impacts (18-month pilot targets)
Financial inclusion: Within 18 months, we aim to achieve financial inclusion for 5,000 waste pickers by onboarding them and disbursing ₦500 million in microloans. This initiative is projected to increase the average borrower's income by 30%, effectively transforming a largely unbanked workforce into bankable micro-entrepreneurs.
Material recovery: Within 18 months, 10,000 tons of recyclables will be channeled through partner hubs for material recovery.
Climate action: Recycling 10,000tons of waste prevents approximately 28,300 tons of CO₂e emissions, which is equivalent to 2.83 tons of CO₂e saved per ton recycled. This reduction in emissions is comparable to removing about 6,100 Nigerian cars from the road for one year.
Employment & Gender Impact: Our employment and gender impact goals over 18 months are to create 100 new hub jobs and achieve 40% female borrowers, emphasizing the importance of formal employment and gender-balanced credit for inclusive growth.
Key technologies:
Key Technologies
Google Cloud Run 
Firebase Suite: NoSQL database, authentication, storage, and monitoring in one managed stack.
Vercel Edge Hosting: fast global delivery for the web app and admin dashboard.
USSD Gateway: zero-rated feature-phone access mirroring core app functions.
Providus Bank APIs:  instant loan disbursement and repayment collection.
Python Rule Engine (ML-ready):  current credit tiers, with gradient-boosted ML model on the roadmap.
ZeptoMail & SMS Gateways: low-cost transactional communications.
AES-256 / TLS 1.3 Security: CBN and NDPC compliant encryption.
Unique Characteristics:
What Makes Wapfi Distinct
Borrowers settle their loans with the very plastics, cans, and paper they collect
Every kilogram logged at a hub feeds a live credit score, replacing traditional collateral with verifiable recycling data and unlocking larger limits over time.
Everything, from loan size to repayment cadence, is designed specifically for the realities of informal recyclers, not generic MSMEs.
Low documentation onboarding: BVN / NIN plus association ID is enough to qualify, removing the paperwork barrier that stops most pickers at traditional MFIs.
Sustainable Change:
Wapfi creates systemic change by fundamentally redefining waste. Our solution is not just a lending software; it creates a new economic engine powered by recycling. The microloans we provide waste pickers come with a revolutionary twist: they can be repaid with the materials they collect.
Our Theory of Change outlines a clear pathway from immediate outputs to long-term, systemic impact.
The Immediate Impact: Capital and Data
Our activities - onboarding waste pickers through our mobile platform, disbursing instant micro-loans, and logging every transaction, produce two crucial outputs:
Affordable working capital is placed directly into the hands of thousands of previously unbanked recyclers.
A transparent digital ledger is created, tracking material flows, borrower performance, and the amount of CO₂ equivalent emissions avoided.
Short-Term Outcomes (The First 6–18 Months)
This initial injection of capital and data quickly translates into tangible results. With access to loans, waste pickers can increase their daily earnings by buying materials in bulk, investing in tools, or hiring help. The platform's design, which ties higher loan eligibility to collection volumes, directly incentivizes a surge in material recovery, pulling more plastics, cans, and paper into formal recycling streams.
Most critically, verifiable recycling data becomes a form of alternative collateral, creating formal credit histories for the first time and allowing other lenders and service providers to confidently enter the ecosystem.

Medium-Term Outcomes (2–4 Years)
By the second year, the data we've collected creates a transparent digital ledger, tracking material flows, borrower performance, and CO₂ emissions avoided. This data becomes the foundation for market formalization, reducing fraud and creating a predictable supply chain that allows recycling hubs to scale and hire more people.

Long-Term Systemic Change (5+ Years)
The cumulative effect of these outcomes is deep, systemic change aligned with global development goals. We anticipate:
Structural Poverty Reduction: A sustained rise in incomes and financial stability among informal recyclers contributes directly to SDG 1 (No Poverty).
Circular Economy Mainstreaming: A measurable increase in national recycling rates cuts landfill and ocean waste leakage, advancing SDG 12 (Responsible Consumption and Production).
Climate Co-Benefits: The substitution of virgin materials with recycled feedstock results in millions of tonnes of avoided CO₂ equivalent emissions, supporting SDG 13 (Climate Action).
Financial Sector Innovation: By proving that alternative data like material flows can de-risk lending, Wapfi creates a model for inclusive fintech that can be replicated across other informal sectors like agriculture and scrap metal.
This loop embeds change that persists and scales naturally as more recyclers, hubs, and lenders join the network.
Primary thematic focus area: MSME Empowerment & Local Digital Innovation
Summary: Wapfi addresses financial inclusion for waste pickers in Nigeria by offering micro-loans and digital services linked to recycling activities. Its integration of real-time data into credit scoring and the ability to repay loans with recyclables sets it apart. However, the absence of clear funding and scalability plans hinders its long-term sustainability.

Title: xPOS
Subtitle: AI-powered, cloud-based retail platform bridging the digital divide - proven to transform SMEs businesses into digitally inclusive enterprises.
Problem Statement:
The Digital Commerce Exclusion Crisis: 80% of Global Small Retailers Left Behind

Small and medium retailers in developing economies face a perfect storm of digital exclusion that prevents them from participating in the growing digital economy. Despite representing over 80% of retail businesses globally, these enterprises are systematically excluded from digital transformation due to interconnected barriers:

Economic Barriers: Enterprise-level business management systems cost $500-2000+ monthly, making them prohibitively expensive for businesses earning $200-800 monthly revenue. This creates a digital divide where only large retailers can afford integrated POS, inventory, HR, and CRM tools.

Technical Complexity: Existing solutions require multiple separate systems, technical expertise, and extensive training that small retailers cannot access or afford, forcing them to rely on manual processes that limit growth and efficiency.

Infrastructure Limitations: Poor internet connectivity and unreliable power in emerging markets make traditional software solutions impractical, while lack of local language support and customer service creates additional adoption barriers.

Market Access Constraints: Without digital payment integration, real-time inventory management, or customer data analytics, small retailers cannot compete with digitally-enabled businesses or access broader markets through e-commerce platforms.

Systemic Impact: This exclusion perpetuates economic inequality, limits job creation, reduces tax revenue for governments, and prevents entire communities from benefiting from digital economic growth. When 80% of retail businesses operate manually, it constrains overall economic development and digital inclusion goals.

The result is a two-tiered economy where digital-native businesses thrive while traditional small retailers face declining competitiveness, reduced profitability, and eventual obsolescence - directly undermining inclusive digital economic development objectives.
Solution Overview:
xPOS: AI-Powered, Cloud-Based POS

How the Solution Works
xPOS transforms small retailers into digitally-enabled enterprises through a comprehensive, affordable, locally-adapted platform consolidating Point-of-Sale, Inventory Management, Human Resources, and Customer Relationship Management into one seamless system accessible via any internet-connected device.

AI-Powered Intelligence: Machine learning algorithms analyze sales patterns, predict inventory needs, identify customer trends, and provide actionable insights previously available only to large enterprises. The AI adapts to local market conditions, becoming more effective over time.

Progressive Digitization: The platform guides retailers through transformation stages - starting with basic POS, then expanding to inventory, employee management, and customer analytics as businesses grow comfortable.

Offline-First Design: Operates during connectivity disruptions, automatically synchronizing when connection resumes, ensuring business continuity regardless of infrastructure limitations.

Methodologies and Technologies Used
Cloud-Native Architecture: Scalable infrastructure enabling rapid regional deployment while maintaining security and compliance, reducing hardware requirements and enabling automatic updates.

Localization Framework: Systematic adaptation including local languages, currencies, tax compliance, cultural practices, and region-specific payment methods (mobile money, QR codes).

Tiered Accessibility Model: Three pricing tiers ($7-30 monthly) with progressive features, ensuring affordability while providing upgrade pathways.

Human-Centered Design: User research with actual retailers ensures intuitive interfaces requiring minimal training.
API-First Development: Open architecture enabling integration with banks, payment providers, and government systems.

Partnerships and Collaboration Models
Government Partnerships: Ministry collaboration for regulatory alignment and integration with national digitization strategies.

Financial Institution Alliances: Bank partnerships for payment integration and potential lending based on sales data.

Business Association Networks: Chamber of commerce collaboration for market entry and training programs.

Development Partner Integration: Alignment with UNIDO, World Bank initiatives for funding and expansion support.

Local Implementation Model: Training local partners as specialists, creating employment while ensuring culturally-appropriate support.

Impact Measurement Partnership: Research institution collaboration documenting economic impact and digital inclusion outcomes.

This approach addresses interconnected digital exclusion barriers while creating sustainable pathways for small retailers to participate fully in the digital economy.

Sustainable Change:

xPOS enables excluded small retailers to adopt integrated digital business management, resulting in 20-30% revenue increases through improved inventory control, customer retention, and operational efficiency. Long-Term Structural Transformation
Digital Economy Democratization: Proof that enterprise technology can profitably serve micro-enterprises triggers broader market transformation, encouraging other technology providers to develop inclusive solutions rather than focusing solely on large enterprise markets.

Economic Resilience Building: Diversified, digitally-enabled small business sector creates more resilient local economies less vulnerable to single large employer dependencies or supply chain disruptions.

Innovation Ecosystem Development: Success demonstrates emerging market viability for technology entrepreneurship, encouraging local innovation, investment, and development of indigenous technology solutions.

xPOS catalyzes a fundamental shift from digital divide acceptance to digital inclusion expectation - proving that technology can be engineered to include rather than exclude, creating market pressure for inclusive innovation and establishing new standards for development-aligned commercial solutions.

Title: WILIMA - Inclusive platform for the digital empowerment of women and young entrepreneurs in West Africa
Subtitle: WILIMA connects, trains, and empowers women and young entrepreneurs through ethical AI, e-learning, and inclusive digital markets.
Problem Statement:
The WILIMA solution addresses a set of structural and contextual challenges that hinder the inclusive integration of women and young entrepreneurs into the digital economy in Mali and West Africa. Among the main identified issues are: Limited access to digital tools and the Internet: A large part of the population, particularly in rural areas, does not have access to a stable connection or digital equipment (smartphones, computers). This limits their active participation in the digital economy and online training.

The lack of digital skills and introduction to AI: Women and young people have few training opportunities in digital technologies, digital marketing, business management, or the ethical use of artificial intelligence. This skills deficit reduces their employability and their capacity for innovation.

Underutilization of technological innovations: Local SMEs do very little to exploit available technologies (management tools, automation, e-commerce platforms), which limits their growth, productivity, and access to international markets.

Inequalities in access to digital resources: There are significant disparities between men and women, urban and rural areas, as well as among social classes. This creates a digital divide that prevents an inclusive and equitable transformation of the economy.

Lack of integration into international value chains: Small businesses lack visibility, networks, and opportunities to establish structuring partnerships, particularly with private sector actors or international institutions, such as in the USA-Africa value chains.

The unclear regulatory environment and low awareness of digital ethics: The legislative framework surrounding artificial intelligence, data protection, and ethics is still under construction. Users, often misinformed, may face risks related to the inappropriate or insecure use of digital technologies.

WILIMA positions itself as a structuring and innovative response to these challenges by combining an inclusive digital platform, accessible educational content, close human support, and the integration of ethical artificial intelligence adapted to local realities. This solution thus aims to create an equitable and sustainable digital ecosystem in the service of economic empowerment.
Solution Overview:
Detailed description of how it works
WILIMA is an inclusive digital platform designed to support women and young entrepreneurs in West Africa, particularly Mali, in their transition to the digital economy. It acts as an integrated ecosystem focused on three key areas:

Training and capacity building
WILIMA offers access to multilingual online training modules (French, Bambara, Fulfulde, etc.) on:
Digital entrepreneurship,
The basics of ethical artificial intelligence,
Microbusiness management,
Digital marketing and online sales.

These training courses are offered in the form of videos, podcasts, interactive quizzes, and micro-lessons adapted to low-connectivity contexts.

Visibility and Opportunity Platform
WILIMA allows users to:
Create an entrepreneur profile with a portfolio,
Access a digital marketplace to showcase and sell their products or services,
Receive intelligent recommendations (via AI) for opportunities (calls for projects, financing, training, events).

Support and Mutual Aid Community
Thanks to integrated forums, local WILIMA clubs, and a network of certified mentors, users can:
Exchange with peers,
Receive personalized support,
Co-construct solutions adapted to local realities.

Methodologies and Technologies Used
Human-Centered Design: All content and interfaces are designed based on field assessments, actively involving beneficiaries.

Agile Methodology: The platform is developed through successive iterations, with user feedback at each stage.

Technologies Used:
Mobile-first frontend (React Native / Flutter)
Scalable backend (Node.js, Firebase)
Recommendation systems using responsible machine learning algorithms (opportunity scoring, personalized journey)
Integrated open-source e-learning modules (Moodle, Chamilo)
Multilingual AI chatbot for interactive assistance
Cloud servers optimized for low-bandwidth usage

Partnerships and Collaboration Models
WILIMA is based on a model of co-creation and multi-stakeholder partnerships:
Local organizations: cooperatives, incubators, rural town halls, for the local deployment of WILIMA clubs and on-the-job training.
Universities and research centers: collaboration with academic institutions to develop tailored content and evaluate impact.
Technical partners: local technology companies and startups for the development, maintenance, and security of the platform.
International organizations: collaboration with UN agencies, donors, and NGOs for financial support, dissemination, and integration into economic inclusion programs.
Private sector: partnerships with telecom operators, banks, and logistics platforms to facilitate access to digital services, finance, and distribution.
