Founded to meet the growing need for technical support, evaluation, and development of high-impact projects, the firm specializes in advising NGOs, public institutions, and local authorities. Its approach is rooted in a detailed understanding of local realities, combined with multi-sector technical expertise and a strong ability to mobilize high-level experts.; Cluster Digital Afrique : Pan-African network of technology innovation centers, hubs and incubators – sector: innovation and technology; Orange Digital Center Mali (technological innovation and digital inclusion center supported by Orange Mali – sector: telecommunications and digital training); University of Social Sciences and Management of Bamako (USSGB) (public university institution involved in research and co-creation of adapted educational content – sector: higher education and research),

The WILIMA solution aims to:

Unique Characteristics:

Lightweight, open-source, and energy-efficient infrastructure, compatible with low-end smartphones.

Automated performance dashboards (social impact, gender, employment, climate).
- Continuous community feedback mechanisms, integrated into the platform.
Sustainable Change:

Its theory of change is based on a progressive, inclusive, and replicable dynamic, structured as follows:

-Lack of economic opportunities
-Isolation from innovation networks

🌀 Systemic Change (Long-Term Impact)

-Transformation of training, financing, and networking systems for MSMEs

Title: EduNiger
Subtitle: EduNiger: an online library offering books in physical, PDF, and audio formats, providing access to knowledge and culture in Niger and beyond.
Problem Statement: EduNiger addresses limited access to educational resources, the scarcity of diverse book formats, and geographic barriers, while also promoting local authors by providing dedicated spaces to showcase their works. It offers physical, PDF, and audio books accessible to everyone in Niger and beyond.
Solution Overview:
Solution Overview

How the solution works:
EduNiger is an online library platform that provides users with access to a wide range of books in three main formats: physical copies, PDFs, and audio books. Users can browse, search, and access content tailored to their preferences and needs. The platform also offers dedicated spaces for local authors to upload, promote, and share their works, helping to foster a community around Nigerien literature and knowledge sharing. Physical books can be requested or reserved for delivery or pickup, while digital formats (PDF and audio) are instantly accessible online or via app.

Methodologies and technologies used:

Digital Content Management: A robust database system stores metadata and files (PDFs, audio) securely, enabling fast retrieval and smooth user experience.

Multi-format Support: The platform supports seamless integration and delivery of physical, PDF, and audio formats to accommodate diverse user needs and preferences.

User Interface: Responsive web and mobile applications built using modern frameworks (e.g., Flutter, React) ensure accessibility across devices.

Author Spaces: Dedicated author portals allow for content management, analytics, and community interaction.

Cloud & Hosting: Use of scalable cloud services to handle traffic and data storage with high availability and security.

APIs & Integrations: For delivery management, payment gateways (for physical book orders), and third-party audio streaming services.


Partnerships and collaboration models:

Local Authors and Publishers: Collaboration agreements to host and promote their works, ensuring fair visibility and support.

Educational Institutions: Partnerships to enrich the content library and integrate EduNiger as a resource for students and educators.

Libraries and Cultural Centers: For physical book lending, events, and outreach programs.

Technology Providers: Collaborations for infrastructure, app development, and digital rights management.

Community Organizations: To promote literacy, local culture, and digital inclusion across Niger and neighboring regions.
Solution Provider(s): Abdou Moumouni University of Niamey (UAM) Profile: The main public university in Niger, a leading institution in research and higher education. Sector: Higher education and research. Role: Principal partner who requested the integration of the UAM portal within EduNiger, enabling public access to the university’s scientific outputs.
Implementation location(s): The solution is already deployed and accessible to a wide audience across the entire Niger territory. The application is available for download at www.eduniger.com.
Implementation timeline(s): The solution has been deployed since April 2025 and is continuously operational to date.
Duration to pilot in a new geography: The estimated duration to pilot EduNiger in a new geography is approximately 3 to 6 months.  This timeframe includes:  Setting up necessary local partnerships and infrastructure  Customizing the platform to local needs and content  Training local users and authors  Running the pilot phase with continuous monitoring and adjustments before scaling up.
SDGs addressed: SDG 4 (Quality Education);SDG 9 (Industry, Innovation, and Infrastructure);SDG 10 (Reduced Inequalities);
Desired impact:
Solution Objectives:

Facilitate equitable and inclusive access to educational resources through multiple formats (physical, PDF, audio).

Promote and support local Nigerien authors to strengthen national cultural and scientific production.

Reduce the digital and geographic divide by enabling broad and accessible knowledge dissemination.

Encourage local digital innovation and entrepreneurial skill development around reading and culture.


Key Achievements / Impacts:

Over 500 active users since the launch in April 2025.

Integration of Abdou Moumouni University’s scientific portal, increasing visibility of hundreds of university publications.

Availability of several thousand books in diverse formats, enhancing inclusion for varied audiences, including those with reading difficulties (via audio format).

Creation of dedicated spaces for more than 15 local authors, significantly boosting cultural production and dissemination.

Contribution to improving education and culture in Niger, indirectly fostering employment through the development of digital and entrepreneurial skills.

Reduction of geographic barriers through online access, minimizing the need for physical travel to access resources.
Key technologies:
EduNiger leverages a set of modern technologies to provide an accessible digital library experience. Key technologies include:

Cloud Computing: for secure and scalable storage of digital content (PDFs, audio files).

Mobile development with Android Studio: to build a performant native mobile app tailored for Android users.

Web development with React: for a responsive, fast, and interactive web application.

MySQL database: for reliable and structured management of user data, content, and metadata.

Content Management System (CMS): to efficiently organize, manage, and update book collections and author spaces.

APIs: to integrate third-party services such as payment gateways, digital rights management, and content delivery networks.

Multimedia support: enabling audio streaming and downloadable formats to meet diverse user needs.

Data analytics: to monitor user engagement, content popularity, and continuously improve the platform.
Unique Characteristics:
EduNiger stands out through its inclusive and multi-format approach, combining physical books, PDFs, and audio formats within a single accessible platform. Unlike many traditional digital libraries, it specifically values and promotes local Nigerien authors by providing them dedicated spaces to showcase their works, thereby fostering local cultural and scientific production.

Its innovative partnership model, which involves universities like Abdou Moumouni University and plans for collaboration with telecom operators and community organizations, ensures wide accessibility and relevance. The platform supports digital inclusion by addressing barriers related to geography, literacy (through audio books), and technology.

Technologically, EduNiger combines mobile native apps (Android), responsive web applications (React), and a robust backend with MySQL, enabling seamless user experiences across devices. While not yet integrating AI or blockchain, its modular architecture allows easy future enhancements.

Furthermore, EduNiger uses flexible financing mechanisms to support both free access and potential revenue for local authors, contributing to sustainable cultural development.
Sustainable Change:
EduNiger aims to foster sustainable and systemic change by addressing core barriers to equitable access to knowledge and cultural resources. By providing an inclusive digital library that supports multiple formats (physical, PDF, audio), it enables diverse populations—including those in remote areas or with literacy challenges—to access educational content.

The solution empowers local authors, enhancing their visibility and economic opportunities, which encourages ongoing cultural and scientific production. This strengthens the local knowledge economy and supports community development.

By partnering with educational institutions, telecom providers, and community organizations, EduNiger builds an ecosystem that promotes digital inclusion, literacy, and innovation. This ecosystem effect creates lasting change beyond individual users, impacting institutions and communities.

The desired follow-on effects include:

Increased literacy rates and educational attainment across target regions.

Strengthened local cultural identity and pride through greater access and promotion of indigenous works.

Development of digital skills and entrepreneurial talent connected to content creation and distribution.

Expansion of digital infrastructure and services that support inclusive growth.

Sustainable economic opportunities for authors and related sectors, reducing inequalities.


Overall, EduNiger’s Theory of Change envisions that by democratizing access to knowledge and empowering creators, it contributes to long-term social, educational, and economic development in Niger and similar contexts.
Funding Sources: The development and deployment of EduNiger have been carried out without external funding, relying primarily on internal resources from the development team. No grants or external financial assistance have been sought to date.
Testimonials and Endorsements: Numerous positive feedbacks are already available directly on the EduNiger website, expressing user satisfaction regarding ease of access, the diversity of formats offered, and the promotion of local authors. These testimonials highlight the platform’s positive impact on knowledge access and cultural promotion in Niger. We continue to collect and publish endorsements to build trust and encourage more users to join the community.
Further comments/feedback: The questionnaire is clear and comprehensive, effectively covering all essential aspects needed to present innovative digital solutions like EduNiger. It encourages detailed explanations which help showcase the solution’s strengths and impact. We appreciate the opportunity to share our work and look forward to potential collaborations and support to scale our platform further.
Primary thematic focus area: Inclusive Digital Innovation Skills & Entrepreneurial Talent Development
Summary: EduNiger is an inclusive digital library offering physical, PDF, and audio books to users in Niger and beyond, with a special focus on promoting local Nigerien authors. While it addresses geographic and digital inclusion, the solution's lack of AI or blockchain integration limits its scalability and innovation potential.

Title: Appolos: La Crypto qui Finance les agriculteurs Africains
Subtitle: Une institution de microfinance innovante, dédiée aux agriculteurs exclus du système bancaire traditionnel, en leur offrant un accès simplifié au financement sans exigence de garantie; grace à la crypto Appolos
Problem Statement:
Les mutations numériques et technologiques ont transformé le monde en un univers dominé par le High-Tech et le tout numérique. Cependant, si ces innovations ont ouvert de nouvelles opportunités dans les pays développés, elles ont également exacerbé les inégalités et les vulnérabilités dans les pays en développement, en particulier en Afrique.
L’accès aux services financiers y reste un défi majeur. Selon la Banque mondiale, en 2017, 68 % des populations, notamment les agriculteurs et les éleveurs en zones rurales, n'ont pas accès aux comptes bancaires ni aux financements nécessaires pour développer leurs activités économiques. En outre, l'inflation galopante et le coût de la vie toujours plus élevé amplifie les difficultés économiques. À ce sujet, en Afrique subsaharienne, l'inflation des prix alimentaires a dépassé 20 % dans plus d'un quart des pays, ralentissant la progression des revenus réels et de la demande des consommateurs, et aggravant l'insécurité alimentaire (Banque mondiale). Cela met en évidence l'incapacité des systèmes financiers traditionnels à répondre aux besoins d'inclusion et de développement économique.
Solution Overview:
Pour répondre aux multiples défis identifiés, Cryval a développé un token innovant, Appolos, conçu pour  mettre en place une microfinance innovante, dédiée aux agriculteurs exclus du système bancaire traditionnel, en leur offrant un accès simplifié au financement sans exigence de garantie afin de stimuler l’activité économique et renforcer l’inclusion financière.
Ce dispositif repose sur l’utilisation de la cryptomonnaie Appolos (lever des capitaux), adossée à la blockchain, garantissant transparence, traçabilité et inclusion.
Au total lever 10 milliards FCFA à travers la vente du token Appolos afin rendre accessible les crédits 2 000 000 d’agriculteurs sur 10 ans.

A ce jour plusieurs agriculteurs ont beneficié de notre solution de crédit sans garantie et avec des option de remboursement en nature ou espèce
Solution Provider(s): - Etat du Cameroun (MINJEC, OSSP, APME, - CMPJ Yagoua) : incubation et Accompagnement technique  VISA pour les carte débit en cryptomonnaie - Binance : API de cryptomonnaie  -  OAPI : déposer la marque COSUMAF : octroi de l’agrément des prestataires des services sur actifs numériques (PSAN) - CONFEJES : accompagnement technique et financière - GATNA : formation en cryptomonnaie - Binance, CoinMarketCap, pancakeswap, Bscscan: listing Appolos - Metamask, Trust wallet : portefeuilles numériques, Ets OSEVALO: logistique et transort de la remboursement en nature, Commune de Gobo: partenaire technique
Implementation location(s): À ce jour, le projet Appolos est mis en œuvre à petite échelle dans la localité de Yagoua, au Cameroun, avec des résultats particulièrement encourageants. Sur les bénéficiaires actuels, 82 ont choisi de rembourser leurs crédits en nature, principalement sous forme de sacs de riz et de maïs, confirmant la pertinence de cette option adaptée aux réalités agricoles locales. La grande majorité, soit environ 90 %, vit en zones rurales, où l’accès au financement traditionnel est quasi inexistant. Ce déploiement pilote démontre non seulement l’adhésion des communautés ciblées, mais aussi l’efficacité du modèle Appolos pour répondre aux besoins des petits producteurs, renforcer leur autonomie et faciliter leur inclusion financière grâce à un mécanisme de remboursement flexible et localement pertinent.
Implementation timeline(s): Actuellement, notre solution est particulièrement sollicitée par les agriculteurs durant la saison des pluies, d’avril à novembre, période cruciale pour leurs activités. Cependant, cette demande saisonnière limite notre impact économique et social. Nous envisageons donc d’étendre notre offre sur toute l’année afin d’assurer un soutien continu aux producteurs, optimiser leur productivité, stabiliser leurs revenus et renforcer la résilience face aux aléas climatiques et aux fluctuations du marché agricole.
Duration to pilot in a new geography: 6 mois
SDGs addressed: SDG 2 (Zero Hunger);SDG 8 (Decent Work and Economic Growth);SDG 9 (Industry, Innovation, and Infrastructure);
Desired impact:
Appolos vise une inclusion financière massive, permettant à 10 millions d’agriculteurs d’accéder à des crédits sur 10 ans via sa banque inclusive. Le projet dynamise l’économie locale en facilitant l’accès aux financements et aux paiements numériques, favorisant l’entrepreneuriat et l’autonomisation économique. Les populations vulnérables bénéficient de projets éducatifs, sanitaires et sociaux, notamment pour les femmes, enfants et déplacés. Cryval accélère l’adoption de la blockchain en Afrique en soutenant les initiatives technologiques et les projets innovants.

La startup, actuellement composée de 4 hommes et 2 femmes, prévoit d’élargir son équipe avec des développeurs, experts marketing, commerciaux, financiers, comptables, spécialistes DeFi, traders et secrétaires pour accompagner sa croissance et garantir une gestion efficace.

Appolos contribue à la protection de l’environnement en utilisant la Binance Smart Chain, qui consomme moins d’énergie que les systèmes PoW, et en favorisant des transactions virtuelles réduisant les déplacements et infrastructures polluantes.
Key technologies: Blockchain, SWIFT, mobile banking, IA
Unique Characteristics:
Cryval (Appolos - APS) se distingue des autres projets crypto-financiers en CEMAC par son positionnement unique et son approche hybride, conçue pour répondre aux défis spécifiques de la région. Contrairement aux cryptomonnaies mondiales qui ignorent les réalités locales, APS est pensé pour s'intégrer dans un contexte où le Franc CFA domine et où l'inclusion financière reste un enjeu majeur.
 
L'un des problèmes majeurs traités par Cryval est l'exclusion financière, particulièrement marquée en CEMAC. En combinant les avantages de la DeFi et de la Finance Traditionnelle, APS offre des services accessibles aux populations non bancarisées, aux jeunes entrepreneurs et aux petites entreprises. Par exemple, la tokenisation d'actifs permet de financer des projets locaux sans recourir aux garanties traditionnelles, tandis que les paiements numériques facilitent les transactions quotidiennes. De plus, Cryval intègre des mécanismes de récompenses et des programmes éducatifs pour encourager l'adoption de l'APS et former les utilisateurs aux technologies blockchain. Cette démarche éducative et communautaire est essentielle pour ancrer APS dans l'économie réelle et favoriser une transition douce vers une économie numérique inclusive.

CRYVAL ne se limite pas à la création d’une cryptomonnaie : au contraire, nous bâtissons un écosystème financier inclusif, reliant finance traditionnelle et DeFi pour libérer le potentiel économique de l’Afrique.
Sustainable Change: Appolos crée un changement systémique durable en favorisant l’inclusion financière et la transition vers une économie numérique accessible à tous. En combinant finance traditionnelle et DeFi, la solution réduit l’exclusion des populations vulnérables, soutient les petites entreprises et dynamise l’entrepreneuriat local. Les mécanismes de tokenisation, paiements numériques et programmes éducatifs assurent l’adoption progressive de la blockchain. À long terme, cela génère une économie plus résiliente, transparente et connectée, tout en renforçant l’autonomie financière des communautés. Le suivi visé inclut l’augmentation du nombre d’utilisateurs bancarisés, l’amélioration des flux économiques locaux et l’essor d’une culture numérique inclusive et durable.
Funding Sources: La solution a été majoritairement financée en fonds propres. Actuellement, nous explorons des pistes de financement pour permettre son déploiement à grande échelle. À ce jour, nous avons développé et lancé le token Appolos, créé le site web du projet, rédigé le livre blanc et mis en place les pages officielles du projet. De plus, nous avons constitué un fonds de roulement destiné à garantir les crédits, facilitant ainsi l’accès aux financements pour les utilisateurs et assurant la viabilité du projet.
Testimonials and Endorsements:
Témoignages d’agriculteurs bénéficiaires:

Témoignages de partenaires:

Title: YOMA -- a blockchain-powered digital ecosystem that connects youth to skill-building opportunities, verifies their impact through decentralized technology, and creates pathways to jobs and income.
Subtitle: YOMA connects youth to skills & jobs via blockchain. 5M+ engagements, 460K users, 50K+ certificates. Offers digital, ambassadorial & green pathways. Expanding across Africa with UNICEF & partners.
Problem Statement:
Despite Africa’s growing youth population—projected to reach 830 million by 2050—young people face systemic barriers to opportunity. Over 60% of African youth are underemployed or working in informal jobs, while 1 in 5 are Not in Education, Employment, or Training (NEET). Traditional education and labor systems fail to equip them with future-ready skills, livelihood opportunities, or pathways to meaningful participation in the digital economy. Without intervention, this risks perpetuating cycles of poverty, inequality, and social exclusion—even as global challenges like climate change and digital transformation demand youth-led solutions.

How might we unlock the untapped potential of Africa’s youth by reimagining access to skilling, earning, and community impact at scale? This is where YOMA comes in:

Key Challenges Yoma Addresses:

Youth Unemployment – Bridges the gap between skills and job opportunities, particularly in underserved regions.

Lack of Verifiable Credentials – Uses blockchain (YoID) to validate skills and achievements, boosting employability.

Limited Access to Green Jobs – Connects youth to climate action roles (e.g., reforestation, clean energy) in growing sectors.

Financial Exclusion – Rewards participation with digital rewards and tokens, offering unbanked youth redeemable digital/physical incentives.

Fragmented Learning Pathways – Provides structured "learning-to-earning" tracks (digital, ambassadorial, green) for scalable impact.

Displacement & Marginalization – Supports refugees (e.g., Fair Chance program) with skills, entrepreneurship, and community integration.

Impact: Scalable, tech-driven solutions for youth empowerment aligned with SDGs.
Solution Overview:
Technology Developments
Yoma has undergone several upgrades, culminating in V3 in April 2024. The new version features a redesigned homepage showcasing Yoma’s core value proposition and key partner solutions, along with the Yoma ID (YoID) and a digital passport that stores youth credentials on the blockchain. The team conducted in-person and online user testing, integrating feedback into the platform (see consolidated feedback here). Yoma currently offers Single Sign-On (SSO) with partners such as atingi and Goodwall, and is developing deeper Self-Sovereign Identity (SSI) integration to embed YoID into platforms like SA.youth.mobi, UReport/RapidPro, and FunDoo. The SSI system prioritizes data privacy and gives youth control over their credentials. With V3, Yoma also upgraded its Partner Portal, providing real-time reporting and monitoring of opportunities. Partners can generate “magic links” for participants upon opportunity completion, enabling easy credential claiming and efficient verification.

Design Workshop and Impact Marketplace
To align with youth aspirations, Yoma held a design workshop with the D-School in early 2024, focusing on impact-gigs. Participants expressed strong interest in community- and environment-focused opportunities that also provide a sustainable livelihood. Therefore, in September 2024, Yoma partnered with IXO to develop the Yoma impacts marketplace, to pilot three use cases with Greater Stellenbosch Trust, Duzi-uMngeni Conservation Trust (DUCT), and Harambee. The design sprint introduced mechanisms for “impact certificates,” allowing youth to apply for tasks, submit evidence, and receive verified payments. While no impact certificates have been generated yet, this feature is planned for the second phase in 2025. IXO has already gathered experience in outcome-based funding together with UBS Foundation in India. The team also have an existing business model built into the platform where 10% of all claims processing fees originated through the impact-gig platform accrue to Yoma as the platform operator.
Solution Provider(s): None of this would be possible without core YOMA partners such as RLabs, Goodwall, Umuzi, DIDx, Ixo, Generation Unlimited and UNICEF – who share our vision for an inclusive digital future.Financial and strategic partners include, Accenture, SAP, PwC, Fondation Botnar, GIZ, BMZ, Capgemini, UNICEF Innovation, UNICEF Switzerland and Lichtenstein, Austrian Development Agency, Government of Canada, Harambee and Presidency of South Africa
Implementation location(s): By December 2024, Yoma was operational in eight African countries and had a light presence in the Philippines, supporting global expansion. UNICEF offices such as Madagascar, Uganda, Tanzania, Lesotho, and Botswana are preparing to adopt Yoma, underscoring its potential for further scaling. However, Yoma recently shifted its focus for scale to three countries (South Africa, Nigeria, and Kenya) to ensure quality of implementation and the learnings from this implementation will help in scaling more to other countries.
Duration to pilot in a new geography: 2 years
SDGs addressed: SDG 8 (Decent Work and Economic Growth);SDG 10 (Reduced Inequalities);SDG 13 (Climate Action);
Desired impact:
Desired Impact of Yoma

Solution Objectives:

Bridge the Skills-Jobs Gap – Equip youth with market-relevant skills and connect them to employment/entrepreneurship opportunities.

Enable Verifiable Credentials – Use blockchain (YoID) to validate skills, boosting trust and employability.

Drive Green Economy Participation – Prepare youth for climate-smart jobs (renewable energy, conservation, sustainability).

5M+ youth engagements and 500,000 + registered users (2020–2025).

50,500+ blockchain-verified certificates issued, enhancing employability.

81,500+ youth engaged in climate/entrepreneurship challenges via Goodwall.

8 African countries + Philippines operational, with UNICEF scaling to Madagascar, Uganda, Tanzania, and Botswana.

144+ free learning/impact opportunities from partners like SAP, Accenture, and GIZ.

Ultimate Goal: A future where youth lead sustainable development through dignified work, climate action, and digital empowerment (aligned with SDGs 4, 8, 10, 13, and 17).

Unique Characteristics: 1. Uses innovative finance to fund and measure social impact, 2. uses innovative digital identity protocols to bring together and convene entire youth ecosystems and link youth to opportunities to help solve the issue of fragmentation.
