Title: greentech venture studio
Subtitle: Enabling Greentech Innovation in the Global South
Problem Statement:
Although environmental problems are global, Armenia illustrates how climate and digital divides intersect to hinder inclusive development. Yerevan’s extreme air pollution (AQI 165) and outdated water and energy infrastructure highlight urgent environmental challenges, with direct consequences for health, safety, and economic prosperity. At the same time, youth, women, MSMEs, and marginalized groups often lack access to the digital tools, skills, and resources needed to design or adopt solutions that address these issues.

Current innovation initiatives in the region are often fragmented and one-off, failing to provide continuous support for scaling promising ideas. MSMEs struggle with limited financing, market access, and capacity to integrate digital cleantech. As a result, opportunities to build inclusive, green digital economies are missed, leaving vulnerable communities behind.

There is a pressing need for a systematic, repeatable model that empowers underrepresented innovators, strengthens MSMEs, and generates scalable digital cleantech solutions to tackle pressing environmental problems locally while being replicable globally.
Solution Overview:
The Cleantech Venture Studio is designed to tackle Armenia’s most pressing environmental challenges—such as Yerevan’s severe air pollution, inefficient energy use, and outdated water systems—by placing youth, women, and underrepresented innovators at the center of the solution-making process. Rather than organizing isolated events, the studio provides a continuous cycle of innovation that transforms early ideas into viable cleantech ventures and connects them to real-world markets.

Each cycle begins with an open call for diverse participants who are eager to work on solutions to concrete environmental problems. Through hackathons and bootcamps, teams co-create digital and technological prototypes, drawing on mentorship from experts in engineering, sustainability, and business development. The most promising ideas enter a structured three- to six-month incubation program, where participants refine their solutions, test them with users and communities, and build sustainable business models. The studio then helps ventures take the next step by connecting them with investors, offering access to regional and global cleantech ecosystems, and creating opportunities for international exposure.

The methodology combines digital innovation—such as IoT-based monitoring, AI-driven optimization, and data-driven planning—with a strong focus on human-centered design. This ensures that solutions are not only technically sound but also inclusive, accessible, and tailored to the needs of MSMEs and vulnerable communities.

Partnerships are at the heart of the initiative. Universities and research institutions involve young scientists and engineers; local enterprises and MSMEs provide the testing ground for solutions; civil society organizations mobilize women and marginalized groups; international organizations such as UNIDO and UNCTAD create pathways for knowledge sharing and global replication; and investors are engaged from the start to secure financial sustainability and scaling opportunities.

By combining local urgency with a scalable venture studio model, this solution builds a pipeline of cleantech innovations that can be repeated across cycles in Armenia and replicated in other regions, creating long-term impact in both environmental resilience and inclusive digital economic growth.
Solution Provider(s): FAST (Foundation for Armenian Science and Technology) Foundation's B-ON biotech prototyping lab, Armenian Bioinformatics Institute-research institute in life sciences, Sience and Technology Angel Network-an Armenia-based angel-investor network
Duration to pilot in a new geography: 7 months
SDGs addressed: SDG 3 (Good Health and Well-being);SDG 13 (Climate Action);SDG 9 (Industry, Innovation, and Infrastructure);
Desired impact: The objective of the proposed program is to catalyze innovation in cleantech by bridging the gap between academia, businesses, and the youth. The anticipated impact of the project is a continuous flow of science-based, innovative, and economically viable ventures that address the urgent challenges of climate change, public health, and well-being. The model allows for replicability in other areas of the Global South, where there is a need to bridge the gap between academia, the underrepresented parts of society, and the businesses.
Key technologies:
Our solution leverages a combination of advanced and emerging technologies to address environmental challenges and foster digital inclusion in climate innovation. Key technologies include the Internet of Things (IoT) for real-time monitoring of air quality, energy consumption, and water usage, enabling data-driven interventions that improve efficiency and reduce waste. Artificial Intelligence (AI) and machine learning are applied to analyze large datasets, optimize resource management, and predict the environmental impact of proposed solutions.
Importantly, our venture studio approach allows these technologies to be applied iteratively across multiple projects, ensuring that each solution benefits from previous learnings and can be replicated or adapted in other contexts. This model maximizes impact, supports continuous innovation, and strengthens the potential for scalable, sustainable solutions in Armenia and beyond.
Unique Characteristics: The uniqueness of our program lies in its combination of a venture studio model, technology-driven innovation, and inclusive engagement of local talent. Unlike conventional incubation programs, our approach does not stop at one-off projects; instead, it continuously nurtures multiple cleantech initiatives in parallel, iteratively refining and scaling solutions based on real-world results. This model allows proven concepts to be replicated in other communities or adapted for different environmental challenges. By including investors and research institutions in the mix of partners, our proposed program is uniquely placed to contribute to producing viable solutions for the environmental challenges.
Sustainable Change:
The proposed program seeks to create lasting, systemic change by building a vibrant ecosystem for climate innovation in Armenia, with the potential to be replicated in other regions. The idea is simple: by giving young innovators, entrepreneurs, and MSMEs access to mentorship, technology, and engagement with investors and local stakeholders, they can turn their ideas into real solutions for pressing environmental challenges. These solutions, once developed and scaled, will improve energy and water efficiency, reduce emissions, and enhance urban environmental quality—all while equipping participants with skills, experience, and networks that help them continue innovating on their own.

The impact doesn’t stop with the first generation of projects. Each successful initiative becomes a model that inspires others and encourages knowledge sharing. By promoting best practices and accessible technologies, the program strengthens local innovation capacity, accelerates the adoption of clean solutions, and fosters inclusive economic growth. Over time, this creates a ripple effect, embedding a culture of sustainable innovation, building resilient communities, and supporting environmental stewardship that lasts well beyond the life of the program itself.
Funding Sources: The solution is still in the idea stage, so far, no funding has been available yet, although the organizing team is constantly looking for suitable funding sources from both public and private sources.
Primary thematic focus area: Inclusive Digital Innovation Skills & Entrepreneurial Talent Development
Summary: The Greentech Venture Studio aims to empower youth, women, and MSMEs in Armenia by providing a continuous cycle of cleantech innovation, connecting local talent to technology and investors. The program’s strength lies in its holistic, inclusive approach, combining digital innovation, local capacity-building, and scalable solutions. The main challenge lies in securing funding and ensuring scalability beyond the initial phase.

Name of your organization: University of Science and Technology of Southern Philippines
Title: Digital Stories, Indigenous Futures
Subtitle: Empowering Indigenous youth through digital storytelling to unlock entrepreneurial potential and cultural innovation
Problem Statement: The solution addresses systemic barriers Indigenous youth face in accessing entrepreneurship opportunities, including limited resources, geographic isolation, cultural disconnection, and underrepresentation in mainstream economies. It also tackles the digital divide and lack of culturally relevant education, empowering youth to share their stories while building skills, confidence, and sustainable livelihoods through technology and self-expression.
Solution Overview:
Solution Overview

How the Solution Works:
"Digital Stories, Indigenous Futures" is a youth-centered program that combines cultural storytelling with digital media training to foster entrepreneurship among Indigenous youth aged 15–25. The solution delivers hands-on workshops in communities—both in-person and virtually—where youth learn to create compelling digital stories (short videos, podcasts, animations) rooted in their language, traditions, and lived experiences. These stories are then leveraged as creative assets to launch micro-enterprises, such as content creation, cultural education platforms, or artisanal brands. Participants receive mentorship in business planning, digital marketing, and financial literacy, enabling them to turn their narratives into sustainable ventures.

Methodologies and Technologies Used:
The program uses a culturally responsive, land-based, and intergenerational learning approach, integrating Indigenous pedagogies with experiential education. Workshops are co-facilitated by Elders, knowledge keepers, and youth mentors to ensure cultural authenticity. Technologically, the solution utilizes accessible tools such as smartphones, free editing software (e.g., DaVinci Resolve, Audacity), and platforms like YouTube, TikTok, and Shopify to support content distribution and e-commerce. Cloud-based collaboration tools (Google Workspace, Zoom) enable remote participation. Digital literacy, creative design, and entrepreneurial skill-building are scaffolded through modular, self-paced learning paths.

Partnerships and Collaboration Models:
The initiative partners with Indigenous communities, schools, and governance bodies to ensure local ownership and relevance. Collaborations include:

Community Organizations & Tribal Councils: For program delivery, space, and recruitment.
Post-Secondary Institutions: For curriculum development, certification, and access to labs.
Tech Companies & NGOs: For equipment donations, platform access, and digital safety training.
Indigenous Artists & Entrepreneurs: As mentors and role models.
A co-design model ensures communities shape program content, while a hub-and-satellite network allows scalability across urban, rural, and remote regions. Ongoing evaluation and storytelling feedback loops ensure continuous improvement and cultural integrity.
Solution Provider(s): Solution Providers and Key Partners for the Pilot in Barangay Tagbak, Talakag, Bukidnon:  Save the Children Philippines, Inc. – A child rights organization with extensive experience in youth empowerment, education, and community development in Indigenous communities across Mindanao. Active in Northern Mindanao, they support programs that integrate culture-based learning and digital inclusion for Indigenous youth. Sector: Non-Governmental Organization (NGO), Child & Youth Development. Bukidnon State University (BukSU) – A public higher education institution based in Malaybalay City, Bukidnon, with strong outreach programs in Indigenous Peoples’ education and cultural preservation. The university’s College of Education and College of Computer Studies can provide technical support, student facilitators, and training space. Sector: Education, Research, Public Institution. Tebtebba (Indigenous Peoples’ International Centre for Policy Research and Education) – A global Indigenous organization with national networks in the Philippines that supports Indigenous youth leadership, climate resilience, and cultural rights. Tebtebba can contribute culturally grounded methodologies and training frameworks. Sector: Indigenous Rights, Advocacy, Capacity Building. Mindanao State University – Iligan Institute of Technology (MSU-IIT), Center for Alternative Development Initiatives (CADI) – Engaged in community-based innovation and digital literacy programs for marginalized youth. CADI has experience in participatory media and social entrepreneurship training in Mindanao. Sector: Education, Technology, Community Development. Philippine Computer Society, Inc. (PCS) – The national professional organization for IT practitioners, which supports digital literacy and tech-for-social-good initiatives. Can assist in providing trainers, open-source tools, and digital safety modules. Sector: Technology, Professional Association. Lupong Tagapangasiwa ng Katutubong Punso (LTKP), Talakag Chapter – The local Indigenous Peoples’ Mandatory Representative Organization (IP-MRO) in Barangay Tagbak, recognized under the Indigenous Peoples’ Rights Act (IPRA). LTKP ensures community consent, cultural integrity, and local coordination. Sector: Indigenous Governance, Community Leadership. Gawad Kalinga (GK) Village Builders Foundation, Inc. – A poverty alleviation organization with active community hubs in Bukidnon. GK’s youth development arm, Kabataan Konek, promotes digital skills and entrepreneurship among rural youth. Sector: Social Development, Youth Empowerment. These partners collectively provide cultural authority, technical expertise, educational resources, and community trust essential for the pilot’s success in Tagbak.
Implementation location(s): "not applicable". this is to be piloted in Barangay Tagbak, Talakag, Bukidnon, Northern Mindanao, Philippines.
Duration to pilot in a new geography: The estimated duration to pilot the solution in a new geography, such as Barangay Tagbak, Talakag, Bukidnon, is 6 to 8 months.  Breakdown of Implementation Timeline: Month 1–2: Community Engagement & Co-Design Conduct consultations with the local Indigenous community (via LTKP), secure Free, Prior, and Informed Consent (FPIC), co-design the curriculum with Elders and youth, and finalize partnerships. Month 3: Capacity Building & Training Setup Recruit participants, train local facilitators, procure equipment (tablets, audio kits), and prepare digital platforms and learning materials adapted to local context and language. Months 4–6: Workshop Delivery & Story Creation Implement a 12- to 16-week program of weekly workshops covering digital storytelling (video, audio, animation), cultural expression, and foundational entrepreneurship skills. Month 7: Enterprise Development & Mentorship Guide youth in developing micro-enterprise ideas based on their stories (e.g., cultural content channels, crafts, eco-tours), and connect them with mentors and market access opportunities. Month 8: Showcase, Evaluation & Sustainability Planning Host a community storytelling showcase, evaluate impact, document lessons, and establish a local youth-led hub or peer network to sustain the initiative. This timeline allows for culturally responsive pacing, seasonal considerations, and integration of traditional knowledge systems, ensuring meaningful and community-owned outcomes.
SDGs addressed: SDG 4 (Quality Education);SDG 8 (Decent Work and Economic Growth);SDG 10 (Reduced Inequalities);
Desired impact:
Desired Impact of the Solution

Solution Objectives:

Empower Indigenous youth in Barangay Tagbak with digital storytelling and entrepreneurial skills to create sustainable livelihoods.
Strengthen cultural identity and intergenerational knowledge transfer through technology-enabled narrative expression.
Bridge the digital divide and foster inclusive innovation by providing access to tools, training, and market opportunities.
Key Achievements and Impacts (Pilot Target – 6–8 Months):

Youth Empowerment: Train and support at least 30 Indigenous youth (ages 15–25) in digital storytelling, cultural entrepreneurship, and digital literacy.
Enterprise Creation: Facilitate the launch of 15+ youth-led micro-enterprises (e.g., cultural content channels, eco-craft brands, local tour guides) with basic income-generating capacity.
Content Production: Produce 30+ culturally rooted digital stories (videos, podcasts, animations) in local Indigenous languages (e.g., Talaandig, Higaonon), archived for community and educational use.
Skill Development: Achieve a 90% skill proficiency rate in core competencies (digital media, business planning, communication) as measured by pre- and post-training assessments.
Employment & Income: Enable at least 10 youth to earn supplemental or primary income (average ₱3,000–5,000/month) from their ventures within 6 months post-training.
Community Engagement: Engage 20+ Elders and knowledge keepers as co-facilitators, strengthening intergenerational dialogue and cultural continuity.
Digital Access: Distribute or provide shared access to 15 digital kits (tablets, audio recorders, editing tools) to establish a community youth media hub.
This impact model ensures measurable social, cultural, and economic outcomes while laying the foundation for scalability across other Indigenous communities in Mindanao and beyond.
Key technologies:
Key Technologies Used in the Solution

The solution leverages accessible, user-friendly digital tools and platforms to empower Indigenous youth in storytelling and entrepreneurship—prioritizing affordability, ease of use, and cultural relevance. The technologies are selected to work within the infrastructure realities of rural and remote communities like Barangay Tagbak, Talakag, Bukidnon.

Overview of Key Technologies:
Mobile Devices & Digital Creation Tools
Smartphones and Tablets: Used for recording video, audio, and photography—low-cost and widely available.
Free/Open-Source Software:
DaVinci Resolve (video editing)
Audacity (podcast/audio editing)
Canva and Krita (graphic design and digital illustration)
These tools enable youth to produce professional-quality digital stories without expensive software.
Digital Storytelling & Content Platforms
YouTube, TikTok, and Facebook: Used to share stories widely, build audiences, and promote youth-led brands. These platforms support vernacular content and offer monetization pathways.
Anchor.fm or Spotify for Podcasts: To distribute oral histories and language-based storytelling.
E-Commerce & Business Enablement Tools
Shopify and Facebook Marketplace: Enable youth to sell crafts, digital content, or cultural experiences online.
GCash and Digital Payment Systems: Facilitate financial transactions and build financial literacy in cash-light economies.
Cloud-Based Collaboration & Learning
Google Workspace (Drive, Docs, Meet): Supports remote learning, file sharing, and mentorship across distances.
Offline-First Learning Modules: Content is downloadable for use in low-connectivity areas via USB drives or local servers.
Digital Safety & Data Sovereignty Practices
Training in digital privacy, consent, and IP rights ensures youth protect their cultural content.
Use of local data storage (community servers or encrypted drives) to uphold Indigenous data sovereignty.
Technology Approach:
The solution does not rely on advanced technologies like AI, blockchain, or IoT, but instead emphasizes appropriate, low-barrier digital tools that are sustainable, culturally safe, and scalable in resource-limited settings. The focus is on human-centered design, where technology serves as a bridge for cultural expression and economic opportunity—not an end in itself.
Unique Characteristics:
Unique and Differentiated Characteristics of the Solution

Culture-Centered Innovation
Unlike conventional digital literacy or entrepreneurship programs, this solution places Indigenous knowledge, language, and storytelling at the core—using technology not to replace tradition, but to amplify and sustain it. Stories become both cultural preservation tools and entrepreneurial assets, creating a powerful fusion of identity and income.
Youth-Led, Elder-Guided Co-Design Model
The program is co-developed and facilitated by youth, Elders, and knowledge keepers, ensuring cultural authenticity and intergenerational exchange. This dual mentorship model strengthens community ownership and trust, setting it apart from top-down or urban-centric tech initiatives.
Low-Cost, High-Impact Digital Access Strategy
Designed for remote and under-resourced areas, the solution uses affordable, widely available devices (e.g., smartphones) and free/open-source software, minimizing infrastructure needs. A shared “community media kit” model enables sustainability without requiring individual ownership of tools.
Story-to-Enterprise Pathway
The innovation lies in the direct link between storytelling and entrepreneurship—youth monetize their narratives through content platforms, cultural education services, or craft-based brands. This transforms personal and cultural expression into tangible economic opportunity, a model rarely applied in Indigenous youth development.
Localized Digital Sovereignty Framework
The solution integrates training on digital rights, consent, and cultural IP protection, empowering youth to control how their stories are shared. Content is stored locally and shared on community-approved terms, promoting data sovereignty—a critical but often overlooked aspect in digital inclusion projects.
Hybrid Delivery with Scalable Hub-and-Spoke Network
The pilot in Barangay Tagbak can evolve into a regional hub, training youth facilitators who replicate the program in neighboring Indigenous communities. This peer-to-peer model reduces long-term costs and increases cultural relevance across diverse ethnic groups in Mindanao.
By blending tradition with technology, centering community voice, and turning stories into sustainable livelihoods, this solution offers a culturally grounded, scalable, and youth-driven approach to digital empowerment—distinct from mainstream tech-for-development initiatives.
Sustainable Change:
How the Solution Contributes to Sustainable, Systemic Change
Theory of Change and Follow-On Effects

The solution is designed not only to empower individual youth but to catalyze sustainable, systemic change within Indigenous communities by transforming how culture, technology, and economic opportunity intersect. The long-term vision is a self-renewing ecosystem where Indigenous youth are recognized as cultural leaders, innovators, and entrepreneurs—driving community resilience and intergenerational prosperity.

Theory of Change:
If Indigenous youth are equipped with digital storytelling tools and entrepreneurial skills in a culturally safe, community-led environment,
and they are supported by Elders, local institutions, and strategic partnerships,
then they will create meaningful enterprises rooted in their identity,
which will lead to stronger cultural continuity, increased economic self-reliance, and greater youth participation in local decision-making,
ultimately resulting in systemic shifts in education, economic development, and digital inclusion policies for Indigenous communities.

Desired Follow-On Effects:
Cultural Revitalization & Intergenerational Dialogue
As youth document and share stories in their native languages (e.g., Talaandig, Higaonon), Elders become valued knowledge partners, reversing language loss and strengthening cultural pride. This fosters a renewed sense of belonging and identity across generations.
Emergence of Youth-Led Innovation Hubs
Successful participants become peer mentors and trainers, establishing community-based digital storytelling and entrepreneurship hubs. These hubs serve as ongoing centers for skill-building, reducing dependency on external facilitators and ensuring long-term sustainability.
Influence on Local Education & Policy
The program’s success can inspire local government units (LGUs) and schools to integrate culture-based digital literacy and entrepreneurship into formal and non-formal curricula, creating institutional change in how Indigenous youth are educated and supported.
Increased Access to Digital Economies
Youth who launch micro-enterprises (e.g., cultural content creators, eco-tourism guides, artisan brands) contribute to a local digital economy, attracting investment, tourism, and market linkages. Over time, this shifts perceptions of Indigenous communities from “marginalized” to “innovative and resilient.”
Amplified Indigenous Voices in National Discourse
As stories gain visibility on platforms like YouTube and TikTok, they challenge stereotypes, inform public understanding, and position Indigenous youth as agents of change, influencing media narratives and policy conversations on inclusion and equity.
Replication Across Indigenous Communities
The modular, low-cost model can be adapted by other IP communities in Mindanao and beyond, supported by networks like Tebtebba and LTKP, leading to a regional movement of culturally grounded youth entrepreneurship.
By starting with storytelling—a foundational element of Indigenous worldviews—and linking it to tangible economic outcomes, the solution creates a virtuous cycle of cultural pride, skill development, and community-led development. This approach doesn’t just deliver short-term training; it plants the seeds for lasting systemic transformation rooted in Indigenous self-determination.
Primary thematic focus area: Inclusive Digital Innovation Skills & Entrepreneurial Talent Development
Summary: The 'Digital Stories, Indigenous Futures' initiative empowers Indigenous youth through digital storytelling, blending cultural expression with entrepreneurship. This program fosters self-confidence and sustainable livelihoods while preserving cultural heritage. A key strength is its community-centered approach, involving both youth and Elders. However, the lack of formal funding sources and endorsements limits its long-term sustainability and impact potential.

Title: Fully integrated digital platform unlocking opportunities for youth and MSMEs
Subtitle: XValley is a digital ecosystem that equips youth and MSMEs with skills, finance, markets, and growth opportunities to thrive in the digital economy.
Problem Statement:
Across Africa, up to 50% of young people are unemployed or underemployed. For many, entrepreneurship and self-employment are the only viable path to economic empowerment. Yet access to finance, skills, and markets and opportunities remains very limited, particularly in Francophone West Africa, where entrepreneurship ecosystems are still underdeveloped.

This calls for structural solutions designed to connect young entrepreneurs with the skills, networks, and resources that enable inclusive growth.
Solution Overview:
XValley addresses the challenges mentioned above through a 4-pillar approach:

1.Federate: A digital platform that acts as a hub for entrepreneurs and self-employed youth and consolidates growth resources and ecosystem actors in one platform.

2.Equip: A Startup Academy offering curated training programs and an AI-powered financial tool (FinAI) that helps entrepreneurs build financial statements, manage cashflows, and gain financial literacy, even with no prior financial expertise.

3.Connect: A comprehensive database of investors, accelerators, as well as training, funding and grant opportunities, freely accessible to MSMEs to expand access to finance and partnerships.

4.Promote: A “Hero of the Month” spotlight and ecosystem visibility campaigns that showcase remarkable entrepreneurs and self-employed youth, and connect them to markets, partnerships, and contracts.

Partnerships & Collaboration:

Collaborations with universities, accelerators, and NGOs to deliver training.

Partnerships with investment networks and grant programs to channel financing opportunities.

Co-creation with youth entrepreneurs to ensure solutions meet real needs.
Solution Provider(s): For the time being, we deliver our programs directly to entrepreneurs but we are seeking partnership opportunities with universities, accelerators, financial institutions and NGOs to deliver training and financing to young entrepreneurs and self-employed youth.
Duration to pilot in a new geography: 3 months
SDGs addressed: SDG 1 (No Poverty);SDG 8 (Decent Work and Economic Growth);SDG 10 (Reduced Inequalities);
Desired impact:
Objectives:

Empower youth and MSMEs to actively participate in the digital economy.

Reduce barriers to finance, markets, and capacity building.

Strengthen entrepreneurship ecosystems across Francophone West Africa and beyond.

Expected Impacts (2025–2027):

5,000+ youth and MSMEs onboarded onto the platform.

1,000 startups trained through the Startup Academy.

$5M+ in financing opportunities unlocked through investor/startup connections.

Increased visibility for 100+ entrepreneurs through monthly promotions.

Long term: Increased youth employment, financial inclusion, and regional innovation capacity.
Key technologies:
Cloud-based web platform 

AI-powered learning (X-academy) and financial literacy tools (FinAI).

Data-driven opportunity matching and investor–startup linkage.
Unique Characteristics:
Unique / Differentiated Characteristics:

Platform-first ecosystem: Unlike single-service solutions, XValley integrates skills, finance, markets, and visibility into one inclusive platform.

AI-enabled financial literacy: The FinAI tool provides MSMEs with financial structuring and forecasting, breaking a key barrier to investment readiness.

Francophone-first focus: Few platforms target Francophone Africa, where ecosystems are fragmented, XValley fills this strategic gap. Our platform and tools are still accessible in both English and French.
Sustainable Change:
XValley’s Theory of Change rests on the belief that equipping youth entrepreneurs with the right tools, networks, and visibility leads to systemic economic empowerment.

Pathway of Change:

Inputs: Digital platform, training academy, FinAI tool, investor database, promotion campaigns.

Activities: Entrepreneurs gain access to digital tools, financial literacy, growth networks, and investment opportunities.

Outputs: More startups become investment-ready, more MSMEs connect with markets and financing, and more youth access income-generating opportunities.

Outcomes: Expansion of a resilient entrepreneurship ecosystem in Francophone West Africa.

Impact: Sustainable, inclusive participation in the digital economy, leading to reduced unemployment, stronger MSME growth, and broader economic resilience.

Follow-on effects include:

Policy influence by showcasing digital models that work.

Replication and scaling across Africa through partnerships.

Cultural shift towards valuing entrepreneurship as a driver of inclusive growth.
Funding Sources: Self-funded
Primary thematic focus area: Inclusive Digital Innovation Skills & Entrepreneurial Talent Development
Summary: XValley is a fully integrated digital platform designed to empower youth and MSMEs in Francophone West Africa by addressing systemic barriers to skills, finance, and markets. Operating in Côte d’Ivoire and Senegal, it delivers a 4-pillar model: (1) a federated hub consolidating entrepreneurship resources; (2) a Startup Academy with AI-powered financial literacy and management tool (FinAI); (3) a database of investors, accelerators, and funding opportunities; and (4) promotion campaigns showcasing entrepreneurs. The initiative aims to onboard 5,000+ youth and MSMEs by 2027, train 1,000 startups, unlock $5M in financing opportunities, and strengthen inclusive entrepreneurial ecosystems.

Title: Chamalink: Inclusive Digital financing for Climate Resilience
Subtitle: Chamalink empowers community groups with digital financing to access clean technologies, building climate resilience, boosting incomes, and advancing inclusive growth.
Problem Statement: Low-income households across Africa struggle to access clean technologies due to high upfront costs, limited financing, and fragmented distribution systems. This perpetuates reliance on unsafe energy sources, low agricultural productivity, and unsafe water access, increasing health risks, poverty, and vulnerability to climate shocks. The lack of inclusive digital financing solutions prevents communities from unlocking the benefits of climate-resilient technologies at scale.
Solution Overview:
Chamalink is an inclusive digital financing and e-commerce platform designed to leverage existing community structures such as self-help groups, cooperatives, and savings associations. Through the platform, these groups can discover clean technologies, pool resources, and finance adoption via personal savings, peer-to-peer lending, or crowdfunding. By digitizing traditional group models, we empower members to connect with life-changing solutions while strengthening financial inclusion.
The platform provides access to a wide range of climate technologies, including clean cooking solutions, solar home systems, agricultural innovations, and water purification technologies. It also enables groups to track and maximize the socio-economic benefits of these technologies such as improved productivity, health outcomes, and income opportunities helping communities build long-term resilience.
Technologically, Chamalink integrates mobile payments, blockchain for transparent group savings and transactions, and AI-enabled tools to assess creditworthiness and optimize financing pathways. The solution is accessible both via web and mobile, ensuring usability across diverse contexts.
We are building strategic partnerships with government agencies, non-profit organizations, and financial institutions to expand financing options and align with national climate resilience priorities. Additionally, we are developing a nationwide agency network in collaboration with small businesses, creating local jobs and driving adoption through community ownership.
Solution Provider(s): We are currently establishing partnerships with manufacturers of clean technologies, and still dont have signed agreements with any partners, at the moment its just Kawilab Energy systems, a social enterprise bulding a pilot for the project as we try and bring in more players.
Implementation timeline(s): Pilot Started in January 2025 aimed at lasting till April 2026
Duration to pilot in a new geography: 12 months
SDGs addressed: SDG 6 (Clean Water and Sanitation);SDG 7 (Affordable and Clean Energy);SDG 10 (Reduced Inequalities);
Desired impact:
Solution Objectives
Chamalink aims to accelerate inclusive access to climate technologies by enabling community groups to finance and adopt clean energy, agricultural, and water solutions. Our objectives are to (i) reduce barriers to affordable clean technologies, (ii) empower communities to achieve socio-economic resilience, and (iii) create new green jobs through local agency networks.

Key Achievements / Impacts

Access & Adoption: 100+ groups enrolled and 1,500+ groups on the waitlist, collectively saving over USD 20,000 toward climate technologies within the last 6 months.

Climate Impact: By supporting the adoption of clean cooking, solar, and water solutions, Chamalink contributes to reducing household GHG emissions and improving energy efficiency.

Economic Impact: Over USD 30,000 mobilized in early-stage investments (combining equity, grants, and awards). Anticipated revenue growth of 50–65% annually as adoption scales.

Employment: Building a distributed agency network that partners with small businesses, creating local jobs in distribution, after-sales support, and financing services.

Social Impact: Improved health outcomes from clean cooking, enhanced productivity through access to energy and water, and stronger financial inclusion for underserved communities.
Key technologies:
Chamalink leverages a suite of digital technologies to deliver inclusive financing and access to climate solutions:

Blockchain: Ensures transparent, secure, and traceable community savings, peer-to-peer lending, and crowdfunding transactions.

Mobile Payments (USSD, M-Pesa, mobile money): Enables seamless contributions, withdrawals, and payments, even for users with basic phones.

Web & Mobile Applications: Provide user-friendly interfaces for groups to discover clean technologies, track savings, manage loans, and access financing options.

Data Analytics & AI: Supports credit scoring, demand forecasting, and personalized financing models for underserved communities.

IoT Integrations (future roadmap): Planned to monitor usage and performance of distributed climate technologies like solar home systems and water pumps, improving reliability and after-sales support.
Unique Characteristics:
Chamalink is unique because it does not simply provide access to clean technologies — it transforms the way communities finance and adopt them. Unlike traditional models that rely heavily on subsidies or external loans, our platform leverages existing community structures such as self-help groups and cooperatives, enabling them to pool resources through digital savings, peer-to-peer lending, and crowdfunding. This bottom-up approach creates a self-sustaining financing ecosystem rooted in trust and social capital.

We also integrate blockchain for transparency, mobile money for accessibility, and digital marketplaces that connect communities directly to vetted clean technology providers. By building an agency network of local entrepreneurs and SMEs, we ensure last-mile distribution and local ownership, which most financing platforms overlook.

This combination of inclusive financing, community-led adoption, and technology-enabled transparency makes Chamalink a scalable and replicable model for accelerating climate resilience across Africa.
Sustainable Change:
The biggest barrier to clean technology adoption is affordability and access. By removing these barriers through digital financing, Chamalink enables communities to directly own and benefit from clean technologies. Increased adoption of solar, clean cooking, agricultural, and water solutions reduces reliance on polluting fuels, improves health outcomes, enhances food security, and lowers household energy costs.
For communities and livelihoods: Access to clean energy and climate-smart technologies increases productivity, creates new income streams, and empowers local businesses and women-led groups to thrive.
For the environment: Greater adoption of clean solutions leads to measurable GHG reductions, improved air quality, and more sustainable natural resource use.
For the wider ecosystem: By digitizing group savings, lending, and crowdfunding, we create a scalable, community-driven financing model that reduces dependence on external aid, accelerates technology distribution, and strengthens resilience. Closing this access gap with digital tools unlocks systemic change  transforming underserved populations from passive recipients into active participants in the green economy.
Funding Sources: The development and early implementation of Chamalink has been financed through a combination of founder investment and small grants. We have committed our own resources to build and test the platform, complemented by support from programs such as the Tony Elumelu Foundation, GIZ’s Women Entrepreneurship for Africa program, and an award from the Social Shifters Global Innovation Challenge. These funds have enabled us to pilot the solution with community groups, refine our digital platform, and demonstrate early traction in mobilizing savings and investments toward clean technologies.
Further comments/feedback: The questionnaire was comprehensive. One suggestion would be to include more space for describing local implementation contexts, since community-driven solutions are often highly dependent on regional dynamics
Primary thematic focus area: MSME Empowerment & Local Digital Innovation
Summary: Chamalink is an inclusive digital financing and e-commerce platform that helps community groups in Africa access clean technologies such as solar, clean cooking, agricultural, and water solutions. By digitizing traditional group models (self-help groups, cooperatives, savings associations), it enables members to pool resources through savings, peer-to-peer lending, and crowdfunding. The platform integrates blockchain for transparency, mobile payments for accessibility, and AI for credit scoring and demand forecasting. With 100+ groups already enrolled, $20,000 in collective savings, and 1,500 groups on the waitlist, Chamalink is demonstrating strong traction. It aims to reduce barriers to climate technology adoption, improve health and productivity, create local jobs, and accelerate community resilience through inclusive financing.

Title: mAIté: Bridging the Digital Divide in Public Services
Subtitle: mAIté breaks language and tech barriers, offering multilingual, secure, and easy access to public services for everyone, especially the digitally excluded.
Problem Statement: Millions of people—especially migrants, non-native speakers, and those with limited digital skills—struggle to access public services due to language barriers, complex bureaucracy, and inaccessible digital systems. Public institutions, meanwhile, are overwhelmed by demand, under-resourced, and pressured to comply with new accessibility laws. This dual burden results in inefficiency, exclusion, and growing inequality.
Solution Overview:
mAIté is a multilingual, multimodal administrative assistant designed to make public services truly accessible to all. It operates on familiar platforms like WhatsApp, SMS, and Messenger, eliminating the need for users to install new apps or navigate complex websites.

How It Works:
1. A user sends a question—via text, voice, or image—to mAIté in their own language.

2. The system detects the language, anonymizes the input, and understands the query using natural language processing (NLP).

3. An agentic AI framework identifies the relevant institution, procedure, or service using a semantic knowledge graph.

4. A personalized, step-by-step response is generated and delivered in the user's language, with links to translated, trusted sources.

5. Users can request reformulations or translations to help them interact more effectively with public institutions.

Methodologies and Technologies:
- Agentic AI Orchestration: Using Model Context Protocol (MCP) to manage modular AI agents.

- Multimodal Input Processing: Accepts and processes text, speech, and image inputs.

- Semantic Knowledge Graphs: Tailored mappings of administrative institutions and services.

- Open-source, EU-sovereign LLMs: Fine-tuned on administrative data, ensuring accuracy and independence from non-EU platforms.

- Privacy-by-Design: Real-time anonymization, encrypted transport, and full GDPR compliance.

- Explainable AI: Each output includes traceable logic and audit trails to ensure transparency.

- Interoperability by Design: Aligned with the European Interoperability Framework, mAIté enables plug-and-play integration with institutional systems and cross-border public service reuse.

Partnerships and Collaboration:
- NGOs (e.g., Belrefugees): Co-design and testing of domain-specific instances to meet real-world needs.

- Public Institutions: Validation of knowledge graphs and onboarding of use cases for compliance and service optimization.

- Academic Spinoffs : Supporting research and model evaluation and finetuning of vocabularies and ontologies.

- Tech and Sustainability Consultants (e.g., Axoly Tech): Ensuring environmental efficiency and compliance with the Sustainable IT Charter.
Solution Provider(s): Vucable SRL, librAIry.es - IT, Belrefugees - NGO
Duration to pilot in a new geography: 3 months
SDGs addressed: SDG 10 (Reduced Inequalities);SDG 11 (Sustainable Cities and Communities);SDG 16 (Peace, Justice, and Strong Institutions);
Desired impact:
Bridge the Digital Divide: Reach up to 199 million EU residents (within 5 years) with limited digital skills, offering accessible administrative assistance through low-tech channels like SMS and WhatsApp.

Advance Multilingual Inclusion: Support interaction in 250+ languages, enabling true linguistic equity across Europe’s diverse populations.

Reduce Public Sector Strain: Cut frontline administrative workload by 10–30% by automating routine queries, improving service efficiency and reducing burnout.

Enhance Service Navigation Accuracy: In Brussels, for instance, where up to 33% of citizens are misdirected during service visits, mAIté improves first-contact accuracy, saving time and resources.

Promote Sustainable and Sovereign AI: Implement frugal AI techniques (e.g., model pruning and lightweight compute) to minimize energy use and reduce carbon footprint of digital public services.

Ensure Compliance with EU Accessibility Laws: Help institutions meet European Accessibility Act and GDPR requirements—avoiding penalties and boosting inclusivity.

Strengthen Institutional Trust: Provide transparent, explainable responses with traceable sources to counter misinformation and improve citizen confidence in public institutions.
Key technologies:
Artificial Intelligence (AI):

- Natural Language Processing (NLP): Understands user queries in 250+ languages, including speech and text.

- Agentic AI Orchestration: Coordinates specialized AI agents using the Model Context Protocol (MCP) for dynamic, context-aware workflows.

- Multimodal Processing: Handles inputs from text, speech, and images to interpret administrative documents and user needs.

Semantic Technologies:

- Knowledge Graphs: Models public institutions, service catalogs, and legal frameworks, enabling precise query resolution.

- Ontologies & Vocabularies: Built to EU standards (e.g., DCAT-AP), allowing for structured, interoperable knowledge representation.

Privacy and Security

- Privacy-by-Design Anonymization: Combines named entity recognition and token masking to ensure user data remains confidential.

- End-to-End Encryption: Secures all communication channels and infrastructure to meet GDPR and EU AI Act compliance.

Interoperability Frameworks

European Interoperability Framework (EIF): Ensures plug-and-play compatibility with public-sector systems across borders and jurisdictions.

Sustainable IT

- Frugal AI Practices: Uses model pruning, quantization, and lightweight infrastructure to minimize energy consumption and environmental impact.

Open-Source Technologies

- EU-Sovereign LLMs: Fine-tuned on administrative content and deployed on EU-hosted infrastructure to ensure data sovereignty.
Unique Characteristics:
Semantic Intelligence for Public Services
At the heart of mAIté is a semantic knowledge graph, mapping the structure, roles, and service pathways of public institutions across jurisdictions. This enables deep contextual understanding of user queries—far beyond keyword matching—allowing precise, jurisdiction-specific answers that generic LLMs cannot deliver.

Human-Centered by Design
mAIté is co-designed with frontline workers, NGOs, and real users, ensuring that every interaction reflects lived realities. It doesn’t replace people—it augments them, by translating complex procedures into step-by-step guidance that users can act on with confidence, regardless of their language, literacy, or digital skills.

Truly Inclusive Access
Available via WhatsApp, SMS, and Messenger, mAIté supports 250+ languages and accepts text, voice, and image inputs, making it usable by nearly anyone—no downloads, logins, or advanced literacy required.

Transparent and Trustworthy AI
Every inference in mAIté is explainable and traceable, with human-in-the-loop checkpoints and logic paths visible for audit or review. No black boxes—only accountable intelligence built for public trust.

Interoperable and Scalable by Design
Conforming to the European Interoperability Framework, mAIté can be easily adapted and scaled across institutional and national boundaries, supporting consistent service delivery and policy compliance across the EU.

Ethical, Frugal, and EU-Sovereign
mAIté is built on open-source European infrastructure, prioritizing ethical AI principles, data sovereignty, and sustainability through low-carbon tech practices.
Sustainable Change:
Problem:
Millions across Europe—especially migrants, people with disabilities, and digitally excluded populations—face systemic barriers in accessing public services. Public institutions, in turn, are overburdened, under-resourced, and struggling to meet rising accessibility demands.

Intervention:
mAIté introduces a human-centered, multilingual AI assistant that translates complex bureaucratic systems into accessible, actionable guidance. Built on semantic knowledge graphs and deployed via low-tech channels, it reaches users where they are—regardless of language, literacy, or device.

Outputs:
Public institutions onboarded to interoperable, AI-powered knowledge frameworks.

Citizens receive real-time, trustworthy administrative support in 250+ languages.

Frontline staff are relieved from repetitive tasks and can focus on complex cases.

NGOs and local actors integrate mAIté to better serve vulnerable groups.

Short-Term Outcomes:
Immediate improvement in access to services for marginalized groups.

Reduction in misdirected public queries and associated delays.

Greater institutional capacity to meet demands without extra staffing.

Early compliance with the European Accessibility Act and digital inclusion mandates.

Medium-Term Outcomes:
Cultural shift in public service delivery: from rigid systems to flexible, user-centric support.

Systematic reduction in digital inequality, leading to better social integration.

NGOs and municipalities gain data-informed insights to adapt services in real time.

Long-Term Impact:
A more inclusive, efficient, and transparent public sector across Europe.

Sustainable cost savings and emissions reductions via frugal AI and fewer in-person visits.

Increased institutional trust and democratic participation, especially among historically excluded populations.

A scalable model for ethical, sovereign, and accountable AI in public services—positioning the EU as a global leader in responsible digital transformation.
Funding Sources: Bootstrapped
Primary thematic focus area: Inclusive Digital Innovation Skills & Entrepreneurial Talent Development
Summary: mAIté is a multilingual, multimodal AI assistant designed to make public services accessible for migrants, non-native speakers, and digitally excluded populations. A key strength is its integration of semantic knowledge graphs, EU-sovereign LLMs, and low-tech channels (WhatsApp/SMS) for maximum inclusion. A weakness is that the solution is still at pilot stage, bootstrapped, and lacks demonstrated large-scale institutional adoption.

Title: Inclusive digital futures for  Rwanda's youth
Subtitle: A digital inclusion initiative equipping Rwandan youth with skills, SDG knowledge, and reintegration support, with a focus on vulnerable groups including juveniles and youth post-rehabilitiation.
Problem Statement: In Rwanda, vulnerable youth including juvenile detainees, young girls, individuals recovering from substance use disorders, and those recently released from correctional or rehabilitation facilities face compounded barriers to digital inclusion and socio-economic reintegration. These challenges are exacerbated by limited access to digital infrastructure, inadequate skills development pathways, and persistent stigma and cultural norms that disproportionately affect girls and young women. Social exclusion, gender-based discrimination, and the absence of targeted psychosocial and vocational support contribute to high rates of unemployment, recidivism, and relapse into substance abuse. The digital divide further marginalizes these groups, restricting their participation in the evolving digital economy. There is an urgent need for inclusive, gender-responsive, and context-adapted digital solutions that foster resilience, build relevant competencies, and enable dignified reintegration into society.
Solution Overview:
Inclusive Digital Futures for Rwanda's Youth is a digital empowerment initiative by UNA Rwanda targeting vulnerable youth including juvenile detainees, post-rehabilitation youth, and young women. The program addresses digital exclusion through a trauma-informed blended learning approach using accessible technologies, WhatsApp, SMS, and mobile platforms to deliver digital literacy, entrepreneurship, and SDG education. For low-connectivity areas, we provide offline solutions.
Our curriculum covers market-relevant skills: mobile content creation, social media management, graphic design, digital marketing, basic coding, and ethical AI applications. Through project-based learning and mentorship, participants develop real-world solutions while building professional portfolios and career pathways.
Strategic partnerships with Rwanda Correctional Service, kLab innovation hub, and Rwanda ICT Chamber provide access to target populations, technical expertise, and direct employment connections. This scalable model transforms digital divides into economic opportunities, directly advancing SDGs 4, 8 and 10, by creating pathways from vulnerability to digital participation for Rwanda's most marginalized youth.
Solution Provider(s): 1. United Nations Association of Rwanda (UNA Rwanda): A civil society organization promoting UN values, SDG awareness, and youth empowerment in Rwanda. Sector: Non-profit/Development. 2. Rwanda Correctional Service (RCS): A government institution responsible for the rehabilitation and reintegration of inmates, including juveniles. Sector: Public/Security & Social Reintegration. 3. Rwanda ICT Chamber – A private sector umbrella body promoting ICT development and digital talent in Rwanda through policy advocacy, capacity building, and ecosystem support. Sector: Private/ICT.
Duration to pilot in a new geography: 6-9 months
SDGs addressed: SDG 4 (Quality Education);SDG 8 (Decent Work and Economic Growth);SDG 10 (Reduced Inequalities);
Desired impact: The primary objective of this proposal is to empower Rwanda’s most vulnerable youth especially young girls and those reintegrating from detention or rehabilitation by equipping them with the skills, confidence, and opportunities to thrive in the digital economy as active, innovative citizens. To achieve this, our project will deliver practical training in market-aligned digital skills and entrepreneurship, deeply integrated with dedicated mentorship and psychosocial support to replace stigma with confidence and break the cycle of recidivism. The program will build direct bridges to economic independence through guaranteed internships and job placements. During its 12-month pilot phase, this initiative will engage a minimum of 200 young people, with the goal of achieving at least a 75% program completion rate and connecting over 100 graduates to tangible income-generating opportunities through our vital partnerships with kLab, the Rwanda ICT Chamber, and other private sector allies.
Key technologies:
Our proposed solution is a community-led digital empowerment project to be implemented by UNA Rwanda through its Youth Empowerment and SDG Awareness Program. We envision a future where no young person regardless of their background is left behind in the digital era. This project will focus on supporting vulnerable youth, including juvenile detainees, youth recovering from substance abuse, including young girls, by equipping them with practical digital skills, confidence, and renewed hope for a better future.
At the heart of the project is a blended learning model that will leverage accessible technologies such as mobile phones, WhatsApp, and SMS to deliver interactive lessons on digital literacy, entrepreneurship, and SDG awareness. For participants in low-connectivity environments, such as correctional and rehabilitation facilities, the program will provide preloaded tablets and offline audio kits to ensure inclusive participation. Youth will receive hands-on training in marketable digital skills such as mobile content creation, social media management, graphic design, online marketing, and basic coding. They will also be introduced to artificial intelligence in simple and ethical ways, learning how to apply AI tools for design, storytelling, and real-life problem solving.
Through mentorship and guided learning, participants will work on small, community-based projects that address local challenges. They will also learn how to build digital CVs, apply for job opportunities, and explore pathways to self-employment or micro-entrepreneurship.
This future project will be delivered in close partnership with the Rwanda Correctional Service (RCS), enabling access to correctional and rehabilitation centers; kLab, which will support with innovation, digital mentorship, and incubation opportunities; and the Rwanda ICT Chamber, which will help connect trained youth to job placements and entrepreneurial ecosystems in Rwanda’s growing digital economy.
Together, we aim not just to teach skills, but to spark transformation reigniting hope, building resilience, and preparing a generation of tech-savvy, socially conscious young Rwandans to lead and thrive in their communities.
Unique Characteristics:
Our uniqueness lies in the way this future project meets young people where they are especially those often forgotten in digital programs: juvenile detainees and youth recovering from substance abuse, many of them young girls facing stigma and isolation. Instead of relying on complex or expensive technology, we will use simple, accessible tools like mobile phones, WhatsApp, SMS, and offline audio kits to reach them, no matter where they are.
What makes this solution truly different is that it’s not just about learning digital skills it’s about rebuilding confidence, creating second chances, and turning potential into purpose. Youth will learn how to create content, manage social media, design graphics, market products online, and even explore the basics of AI in ways that are ethical, empowering, and practical.
And we’re not doing it alone. With the support of the Rwanda Correctional Service, kLab, and the ICT Chamber, we will make sure learning leads to real opportunities mentorship, internships, and income-generating paths. This is not just a training program; it’s a bridge back to society, a spark of hope, and a chance for young people to rise and lead in Rwanda’s digital future.
Sustainable Change:
Our solution contributes to sustainable, systemic change by addressing the root barriers that keep vulnerable youth especially juvenile detainees, youth recovering from substance abuse, and young girls from fully participating in Rwanda’s digital and economic future. It does more than teach digital skills; it restores confidence, builds community, and opens real pathways to reintegration and income generation.
The theory of change is simple but powerful: If we provide marginalized youth with accessible, relevant, and empowering digital education and connect them to mentorship, markets, and job opportunities then they will be better equipped to break cycles of poverty, reduce recidivism, overcome stigma, and become leaders and innovators in their communities.
Over time, this will shift how society views and supports formerly excluded youth. Schools, correctional centers, and community programs will have a scalable model for reintegration and digital inclusion. Our partnerships with institutions like RCS, kLab, and the ICT Chamber will help embed this work into national systems ensuring long-term ownership, growth, and policy alignment.
This project is a seed for lasting change planting new possibilities in the lives of young Rwandans and helping build a more inclusive, resilient, and opportunity-rich society.
Funding Sources: This is a new and proposed solution that has not yet been implemented. As such, it has not received prior funding. However, UNA Rwanda intends to mobilize support through partnerships with UN agencies, private sector actors, and innovation-focused development partners. The project is designed with a scalable and collaborative model to attract funding through grants, sponsorships, and blended financing aligned with youth empowerment, digital inclusion, and SDG implementation priorities.
Primary thematic focus area: Inclusive Digital Innovation Skills & Entrepreneurial Talent Development
Summary: The 'Inclusive Digital Futures for Rwanda's Youth' initiative, led by UNA Rwanda with partners including the Rwanda Correctional Service and ICT Chamber, aims to equip vulnerable youth (juvenile detainees, post-rehabilitation youth, and girls) with digital skills, entrepreneurship training, and psychosocial support. A key strength is its unique focus on highly marginalized groups combined with strong institutional partnerships. A weakness is that it is still at concept/MVP stage with no prior funding or implementation experience.

Title: DigiHustle
Subtitle: Empowering Entrepreneurs through AI and Digital Literacy
Problem Statement:
Despite global advances in digital innovation, substantial economic and digital divides persist in many marginalized communities, disproportionately affecting women and youth. According to the International Telecommunication Union (2023), nearly 2.6 billion people remain offline, with women 17% less likely than men to use mobile internet in low- and middle-income countries. In sub-Saharan Africa and the Caribbean, these disparities are even more pronounced, where structural inequalities intersect with poor infrastructure, limited digital literacy, and exclusion from financial ecosystems (GSMA, 2023; World Bank, 2022).
Women and youth in rural and underserved communities face unique barriers to entrepreneurship, including lack of access to affordable digital tools, limited financial literacy, and inadequate business support systems (UN Women, 2022). These constraints not only restrict economic mobility but also exacerbate gender-based and age-based inequalities in wealth, employment, and innovation. For example, women-owned MSMEs often operate informally and are less likely to benefit from digital financing, market intelligence, or AI-driven innovations (UNCTAD, 2022). Similarly, youth unemployment remains a pressing challenge, with many young people excluded from formal economies and underrepresented in digital upskilling initiatives (ILO, 2021).
The absence of inclusive digital infrastructure and support perpetuates a cycle of exclusion that undermines resilience, productivity, and participation in the global digital economy. In light of the United Nations Global Digital Compact and Sustainable Development Goals (SDGs), especially SDG 5 (Gender Equality), SDG 8 (Decent Work and Economic Growth), and SDG 9 (Industry, Innovation and Infrastructure), there is an urgent need to address these gaps through inclusive, scalable, and locally adaptive solutions.
DigiHustle responds to this need by targeting the intersection of gender, age, and digital exclusion with a mobile-first platform that delivers AI-powered business tools and contextualized digital literacy. By fostering entrepreneurial resilience and expanding access to digital value chains, the initiative directly contributes to closing opportunity gaps and enabling inclusive digital transformation in the Global South.
Solution Overview:
Solution Overview: DigiHustle Platform

1. How the Solution Works:
DigiHustle is a mobile-first, AI-enabled platform designed to empower marginalized entrepreneurs—particularly women, youth, and persons with disabilities—with the digital tools, knowledge, and skills needed to thrive in the digital economy. The platform offers:

AI-Powered Business Coaching: A chatbot mentor provides enterprise advice tailored to user inputs, local context, and business stage.

Smart Inventory & Market Forecasting Tools: Automated tracking and predictive analytics assist micro-entrepreneurs with restocking decisions and demand projections.

Localized Learning Modules: Interactive, multilingual courses in financial literacy, e-commerce, digital marketing, and basic tech skills.

Offline Functionality: Content is downloadable and usable offline to address connectivity gaps in remote or underserved regions.

Title: YouScreen VIBE
Subtitle: YouScreen Voices integrated for Better Empowerment
Problem Statement: In many underserved communities, particularly in rural Uganda, women and girls face persistent barriers to accessing sexual and reproductive health (SRH) information, gender-based violence (GBV) support, and mental health services. These challenges are compounded by digital exclusion, social stigma, low health literacy, and weak health system responsiveness. Traditional health outreach methods often fail to reach marginalized women especially adolescents, survivors of violence, and women in remote areas leaving them without timely, confidential, and life-saving information or support. The result is a cycle of silence, poor health outcomes, and social vulnerability that digital tools could break if designed with inclusion at the core. YouScreen VIBE addresses this gap by providing a trusted, tech-enabled pathway for women to access SRH and GBV services safely and anonymously.
Solution Overview:
How the solution works:
YouScreen VIBE is a user-friendly digital platform—accessible via mobile app and SMS that empowers women and girls to confidentially report gender-based violence, access cervical cancer screening information, request HPV vaccination appointments, and receive mental health support. Beneficiaries can register anonymously, connect with local healthcare providers, counselors, and legal aid, and receive real-time assistance through toll-free calls and encrypted SMS messaging. The platform integrates a geo-location feature to link users with the nearest available services, ensuring timely intervention.

Methodologies and technologies used:

- Mobile app and SMS interface: Designed for low-bandwidth and non-smartphone users to maximize reach.

- End-to-end encryption: Protects privacy and confidentiality of users’ data and communications.

- AI-powered chatbots: Provide 24/7 guidance, basic counseling, and initial triage.

- Data analytics dashboard: For monitoring trends, service delivery, and impact assessment, accessible only to authorized health and social service providers.

- User-centered design: Developed through participatory approaches involving women survivors, healthcare workers, and local leaders to ensure cultural sensitivity and usability.

Partnerships and collaboration models:
YouScreen VIBE collaborates closely with local health facilities, community-based organizations, women’s groups, and government ministries to ensure integration with existing health and social services. Partnerships with telecom providers enable free access to the platform via SMS and calls. The project also engages advocacy groups and legal aid organizations to provide holistic support for survivors. Regular coordination meetings with partners ensure continuous improvement and sustainability.
Solution Provider(s): YouScreen Initiative — A community-based health organization in Uganda focused on improving women’s access to cervical cancer screening, HPV vaccination, and gender-based violence support through innovative digital solutions. Sector: Community Health and Digital Innovation, Local Health Facilities in Northern and Eastern Uganda — Public and private clinics partnering to provide cervical cancer screening, HPV vaccination, and counseling services. Sector: Healthcare Services, Telecom Partner (e.g., MTN Uganda) — Provides free SMS and toll-free call services to ensure accessibility of the platform to low-income and rural populations. Sector: Telecommunications, Ministry of Health Uganda (MOH) — Provides policy guidance, technical support, and integration with national health programs. Sector: Government/Public Health.
Duration to pilot in a new geography: 3 months
SDGs addressed: SDG 3 (Good Health and Well-being);SDG 5 (Gender Equality);SDG 9 (Industry, Innovation, and Infrastructure);
Desired impact:
Solution Objectives:

- To increase equitable access to cervical cancer screening, HPV vaccination, and gender-based violence (GBV) support services for women across Northern and Eastern Uganda, especially in rural and underserved communities.

- To empower women and communities through digital technology by providing a secure, user-friendly platform for reporting GBV, accessing health information, and scheduling screening and vaccination appointments.

- To enhance data collection and monitoring through encrypted digital dashboards for better program management, impact evaluation, and timely intervention.

- To foster multi-sectoral partnerships that strengthen health service delivery and community engagement for sustained impact.

Key Achievements / Impacts (Projected):

- Increase cervical cancer screening rates by 30% within the first 18 months in targeted districts.

- Facilitate access to HPV vaccination for at least 1000 girls aged 9-14 within 2 years.

- Enable timely reporting and support for over 500 GBV survivors through the digital platform annually, ensuring confidentiality and connection to relevant services.

- Improve health data accuracy and availability with real-time encrypted dashboards, leading to a 25% reduction in reporting delays and enhanced resource allocation.
Key technologies:
YouScreen VIBE uses AI-powered tools and an SMS-based chatbot to expand access to care, especially for women in remote areas. The AI system helps triage reports, assess risk, and prioritize urgent GBV cases, while offering automated guidance on self-care, legal steps, and referrals.

The SMS chatbot allows women to report GBV anonymously, book screenings, and access localized support—even without smartphones or internet. It’s linked to our M&E dashboard for real-time follow-up and data-driven decision-making.
Unique Characteristics:
YouScreen VIBE stands out by seamlessly integrating women’s health services with gender-based violence (GBV) support through a privacy-first, AI- and SMS-powered digital platform. Unlike conventional models, it offers:

Dual-impact approach: Combines cervical cancer screening access with real-time GBV reporting and support—two often siloed issues—into a single, community-driven system.

No-internet accessibility: Our SMS-based chatbot ensures even women in rural or low-connectivity areas can safely engage with the platform in their local language.

AI-driven triage: Risk assessment and response prioritization using AI ensures rapid, tailored interventions.

End-to-end encrypted M&E dashboard: Enables secure, real-time tracking, follow-up, and trend analysis for both health and protection outcomes.

Collaborative delivery model: Engages grassroots health centers, women-led CSOs, and tech innovators in a shared-value ecosystem to ensure scale, trust, and local ownership.
Sustainable Change:
YouScreen VIBE is designed to catalyze long-term, systemic change by empowering communities to normalize preventive screening and GBV reporting as part of routine care. Our Theory of Change is grounded in three key outcomes:

Behavioral Shift: By integrating cervical cancer screening and GBV support into everyday conversations through local language SMS and trusted women-led networks, we reduce stigma and increase early help-seeking behavior.

Capacity Building: Training health workers, mentor mothers, and local CSOs strengthens decentralized systems for prevention, care, and referral—building community resilience.

Data-Driven Policy Influence: Real-time, anonymized data collected via the platform informs local governments and partners, helping to optimize services and influence national health strategies.
