Title: Digital lending to SMEs through invoice discounting and LPO financing
Subtitle: SELF Microfinance Fund Partners with Cashme Tanzania to Provide Short-Term Loans to MSMEs through Invoice Discounting and LPO Financing
Problem Statement: Micro, Small, and Medium Enterprises (MSMEs) in Tanzania face significant barriers in accessing timely and affordable short-term financing to meet their working capital needs. Traditional financial institutions often require collateral and lengthy approval processes, which limit MSMEs’ ability to seize immediate business opportunities. This financing gap constrains growth, disrupts cash flow, and undermines the potential of MSMEs to contribute effectively to the economy. There is a pressing need for innovative, technology-driven lending solutions that offer quick, flexible, and accessible financing tailored to the unique needs of MSMEs.
Solution Overview:
SELF Microfinance Fund will partner with Cashme Tanzania Ltd, a licensed peer to peer lending platform to bridges the gap between lender and borrowers through digital lending.
The platform provides an opportunity for both individual and institutional lenders to extend short term financing to SMEs through invoice discounting and LPO financing. The sought funds from UNIDO will be used for on lending to MSMEs through the platform and for creating a credit guarantee fund to cover for credit risks resulting from the unsecured lending.
The model operates as follows;
(i)	The business (borrower) sells on credit to a reputable company/off taker and issue an invoice
(ii)	The borrower posts and discounts the invoice on the platform
(iii)	Cashme Tanzania sends letter to the company/off taker to confirm the invoice and payment date. This includes the notes of assignment of receivables
(iv)	The company/off taker confirms the invoice (amount, payment date and if there is any partial payment and no performance claim) in writing. This includes notes of acknowledgement of receivables
(v)	Cashme Tanzania approves the invoice for trading, and lenders bid on the invoice and transfers their bid amount to Cashme Tanzania collection account
(vi)	Cashme Tanzania disburses the loan to the borrower’s account. This account is charged by Cashme Tanzania, with the right to view and restrict withdraw
(vii)	On maturity date the company/off taker pays to the borrower’s account
(viii)	The borrower pays the loan to Cashme Tanzania collection account
(ix)	Cashme Tanzania pays the lender the principal loan amount and interest earned
Solution Provider(s): There are two key partners, (i) SELF Microfinance Fund which is a government owned microfinance institution regulated by the Central bank and (ii) Cashme Tanzania Ltd a company licensed by the Capital Market and Security Authority to operate as a peer to peer lending platform
Implementation location(s): The solution is implemented in Tanzania, East Africa
Implementation timeline(s): The Cashme Tanzania platform is operation but SELF MF has not yet joined as a lending pertner
Duration to pilot in a new geography: 6  months
SDGs addressed: SDG 1 (No Poverty);SDG 8 (Decent Work and Economic Growth);SDG 5 (Gender Equality);
Desired impact:
a)	Improved access and convenience: Beneficiaries will gain better access to credit through the platform
b)	Enhanced financial inclusion: The increased availability of credit will enable more MSMEs to access formal financial services, contributing to greater economic participation
c)	Poverty Reduction and Job Creation: Increased access to finance will catalyse business growth, 
d)	Job creation: Increased access to finance will catalyse self-employment, and job creation contributing directly to national poverty alleviation efforts.
Key technologies:
The technology used mostly is the development of the platform and API (Application Programming Interface) so that the platform can communicate with other devices.
An API is a set of rules and protocols that allows different software applications to communicate with each other. It defines how requests and responses should be structured between systems.
Unique Characteristics: It is the only digital invoice discounting and LPO financing platform in the country
Sustainable Change:
The partnership between SELF Microfinance Fund and Cashme Tanzania introduces a technology-enabled financing solution that addresses the persistent challenge of limited access to short-term working capital among MSMEs. By leveraging a digital lending platform, the solution provides fast, collateral-free loans for invoice discounting and LPO financing critical for MSMEs to maintain cash flow, fulfill orders, and grow their businesses.

This solution contributes to sustainable and systemic change in the following ways:
1.	Digitization of MSME Finance:
A fully digital lending model enhances transparency, efficiency, and scalability of financial services. 
2.	Financial Inclusion and Empowerment:
MSMEs that were previously excluded from formal finance due to lack of collateral or complex procedures will gain access to tailored financial products. This leads to increased income generation, job creation, and local economic development.
3.	Data-Driven Credit Scoring:
As MSMEs use the platform, digital transaction data will support alternative credit scoring methods. This reduces reliance on traditional collateral and enables responsible, risk-based lending over time.
4.	Crowding in Private Sector and Innovation:
The success of this digital lending model can serve as a proof of concept for other financial institutions and fintechs to adopt similar approaches, fostering competition and innovation in MSME finance.

Theory of Change (Follow-On Effects):
•	Short-Term: MSMEs receive quick access to affordable working capital, improving business continuity and order fulfillment.
•	Medium-Term: Increased business revenues allow MSMEs to expand operations and hire more employees.
•	Long-Term: Improved access to finance leads to formalization of businesses, stronger MSME ecosystems, and a more inclusive financial sector—ultimately contributing to national goals of poverty reduction, job creation, and economic resilience.
Funding Sources: This is the first time we are seeking funding for this solution
Testimonials and Endorsements: We have not issued any loan yet through the platform
Further comments/feedback: Thank you for this opportunity
Primary thematic focus area: MSME Empowerment & Local Digital Innovation
Summary: SELF Microfinance Fund (government-owned) and Cashme Tanzania (licensed P2P lending platform) are partnering to provide MSMEs with short-term financing via digital invoice discounting and LPO financing. The model leverages a fully digital platform with API integration to connect MSMEs, lenders, and off-takers, reducing reliance on collateral and lengthy approval processes. UNIDO funding would support on-lending and a credit guarantee fund to mitigate risks, enabling broader financial inclusion and economic participation.

Name of your organization: Association pour la Défense des Personnes Vulnérables (ADPV)
Title: Inclusion numérique pour les jeunes défavorisés
Subtitle: Un programme de formation numérique pour autonomiser les jeunes défavorisés et réduire les inégalités d'accès à l'économie numérique dans les zones isolées, province de Moundou (Tchad).
Problem Statement: Au Tchad, de nombreux jeunes, en particulier ceux vivant dans les zones rurales et reculées comme la province de Moundou, sont confrontés à une exclusion numérique persistante. L’Association pour la Défense des Personnes Vulnérables (ADPV) a mené en 2025 une enquête de terrain qui a révélé que plus de 78 % des jeunes interrogés n’avaient jamais reçu de formation en compétences numériques, et près de 65 % n’avaient aucun accès régulier à un ordinateur ou à Internet. Ce déficit d’accès et de connaissances empêche ces jeunes de s’insérer dans l’économie numérique, d’accéder à des emplois décents ou de développer des initiatives entrepreneuriales. Ce manque de compétences numériques de base creuse davantage les inégalités sociales, économiques et technologiques entre les jeunes des centres urbains et ceux des zones reculées. La fracture numérique devient ainsi un frein majeur à l’inclusion sociale et au développement durable au Tchad.
Solution Overview:
La solution "DigitAll : Inclusion numérique pour les jeunes défavorisés" est un programme structuré de formation et d’accompagnement visant à doter les jeunes tchadiens, en particulier ceux des zones rurales comme Moundou, des compétences numériques essentielles pour leur inclusion sociale et économique.

Comment fonctionne la solution ?

La solution repose sur trois volets complémentaires :

1. Formation aux compétences numériques de base et avancées : alphabétisation numérique, bureautique, navigation Internet, cybersécurité, conception graphique, création de contenus, initiation au codage, etc.

2. Sessions pratiques et projets communautaires : les jeunes formés réalisent des mini-projets (création de CV numériques, lancement de pages professionnelles, etc.) pour mettre en application leurs acquis.

3. Orientation professionnelle et accompagnement post-formation : aide à la recherche de stages, de bourses, de formations complémentaires ou d’opportunités de travail indépendant en ligne.

Les sessions sont organisées dans des centres de formation locaux ou dans des espaces communautaires équipés temporairement. Pour les zones très reculées, des kits mobiles de formation sont déployés (ordinateurs portables, connexion Internet mobile, vidéos pédagogiques hors-ligne).

Méthodologies et technologies utilisées

- Pédagogie participative : les jeunes sont acteurs de leur apprentissage via des exercices pratiques, du travail en groupe et des jeux éducatifs.

- Outils numériques open source : utilisation de logiciels libres comme LibreOffice, GIMP, Scratch, Moodle, etc.

- Technologies mobiles et hors-ligne : formation possible via tablettes, clés USB éducatives, et contenus téléchargeables utilisables sans Internet.

- Suivi individualisé : carnet de progrès, fiches de compétences, évaluation continue.

Partenariats et modèles de collaboration

La mise en œuvre repose sur un modèle collaboratif :

- Collectivités locales : mobilisation des jeunes, mise à disposition de lieux pour les formations.

- Établissements scolaires et religieux : relais communautaires pour le recrutement et la sensibilisation.

- Organisations partenaires : collaboration avec des ONG locales et internationales pour l’appui technique, le co-financement et le renforcement des capacités.

- Secteur privé : recherche de soutien auprès d’opérateurs télécoms et de fournisseurs de matériel numérique pour l’équipement et la connectivité.

- Volontaires et mentors : mobilisation de professionnels du numérique pour encadrer, inspirer et accompagner les bénéficiaires.
Solution Provider(s): L'Association pour la Défense des Personnes Vulnérables (ADPV) : Organisation de la société civile tchadienne créée en 2023. À travers son programme pilote lancé en 2024, l’ADPV a déjà formé plus de 20 jeunes à N'Djamena en leadership des jeunes, compétences numériques de base, et sensibilisation à l’économie digitale. Elle assure la coordination générale de la solution, le déploiement des modules de formation et le suivi des bénéficiaires. Secteurs : éducation, inclusion numérique, développement communautaire.  Maison Digitale de Moundou : Structure locale d’inclusion numérique fournissant un cadre d’apprentissage équipé et des formateurs spécialisés. Elle contribue activement aux sessions pratiques et au suivi des jeunes. Secteurs : éducation numérique, autonomisation des jeunes.  Centre Martin Luther de Moundou : Centre d’accueil communautaire fournissant des espaces confortables et sécurisés pour la tenue des sessions de formation. Secteurs : développement communautaire, appui aux initiatives sociales.  Société Airtel Tchad : Fournisseur privé de services de télécommunications. Elle appuie le projet par des dons de forfaits Internet, de cartes SIM et de solutions de connectivité pour les jeunes apprenants. Secteurs : télécommunications, inclusion numérique.  Centre Culturel de Moundou : Institution culturelle locale soutenant le projet par la mise à disposition de matériels (chaises, tables, projecteurs) et de locaux en appui logistique. Secteurs : culture, éducation informelle.  Radios locales de Moundou (Radio Bonne Nouvelle, Radio Kàr Uba, etc.) : Médias partenaires diffusant des messages de sensibilisation, des témoignages de jeunes bénéficiaires et des appels à participation, favorisant ainsi la visibilité et l’adhésion communautaire. Secteurs : médias, éducation populaire.
Implementation location(s): Lieu de mise en œuvre de la solution :  Province de N'Djame, République du Tchad – ville de N'Djamena, 7ème Arrondissement  Quartiers ciblés : Chagoua, Habena, Kamnda, Atrone   Centres utilisés : Siège social de l'ADPV, immeuble 1
Implementation timeline(s): Période de février 2024 à avril 2024 Le projet pilote a été mis en œuvre sur une période de trois mois dans la ville de N'Djamena, avec des sessions de formation hebdomadaires, des ateliers pratiques et des activités de sensibilisation communautaire.
Duration to pilot in a new geography: La durée estimée pour piloter la solution dans une nouvelle zone géographique est de 6 à 8 mois. Ce délai inclut l’identification des bénéficiaires, la mobilisation des partenaires locaux, l’installation logistique (matériel, connectivité), la mise en œuvre des modules de formation, ainsi que le suivi et l’évaluation des résultats.
SDGs addressed: SDG 4 (Quality Education);SDG 8 (Decent Work and Economic Growth);SDG 10 (Reduced Inequalities);
Unique Characteristics:
La solution "DigitAll : Inclusion numérique pour les jeunes défavorisés" se distingue par plusieurs éléments innovants et adaptés au contexte local :

1. Approche communautaire décentralisée
Plutôt que de centraliser la formation dans des centres urbains classiques, la solution s’appuie sur des espaces communautaires existants (églises, centres culturels, maisons digitales) pour amener le numérique au plus près des jeunes en zones reculées, notamment à Moundou. Cela permet d’atteindre les publics les plus exclus sans dépendre d’une infrastructure coûteuse.

2. Partenariats multi-acteurs à impact local
Le projet mobilise un écosystème local de partenaires publics, privés et communautaires : radios locales, centres culturels, opérateurs télécoms (Airtel), et organisations de jeunesse. Cette synergie locale permet une mise en œuvre à faible coût, durable et ancrée dans les réalités sociales.

3. Formation inclusive et flexible
La solution combine des technologies low-tech (contenus hors-ligne, clés USB, logiciels libres) avec un apprentissage progressif, participatif et pratique, adapté au niveau des jeunes sans expérience préalable du numérique. L’accompagnement post-formation (mentorat, orientation) constitue une valeur ajoutée souvent absente dans les programmes classiques.

4. Résultats concrets dès le pilote
Dès sa phase pilote, la solution a généré des impacts mesurables et concrets :
- Obtention d’une bourse internationale (IAS 2025) pour le Président national de l’ADPV grâce aux compétences acquises ;
- Création du site web officiel de l’organisation www.adpv-td.org par les jeunes bénéficiaires eux-mêmes, démontrant ainsi leur autonomie numérique ;
- Élaboration de CV numériques, profils professionnels en ligne et accès à des opportunités concrètes pour plusieurs participants.

Ces résultats illustrent le potentiel de la solution pour être répliquée et étendue à d’autres localités.
Sustainable Change:
La solution "DigitAll : Inclusion numérique pour les jeunes défavorisés" vise à instaurer un changement durable et systémique en s’attaquant aux causes structurelles de l’exclusion numérique des jeunes au Tchad. Sa logique de transformation repose sur une théorie du changement articulée en quatre niveaux :
1. Accès équitable aux compétences numériques :
En formant les jeunes marginalisés, notamment ceux des zones rurales comme Moundou, la solution garantit un accès équitable à des compétences devenues essentielles dans le monde moderne. Cela leur permet de devenir acteurs à part entière de l’économie numérique.

2. Autonomisation économique et sociale :
Grâce aux compétences acquises (bureautique, Internet, création de contenu, réseautage professionnel), les jeunes peuvent :
- accéder à des emplois numériques ou en ligne,
- créer leurs propres initiatives (ex. : création de sites web, services digitaux),
- élargir leur réseau et leurs opportunités à travers des outils numériques professionnels.

3. Effet multiplicateur local
Les jeunes formés deviennent à leur tour agents de changement : ils sensibilisent, forment ou accompagnent d’autres jeunes de leur communauté. Cela crée un effet boule de neige, renforçant l’inclusion numérique à l’échelle communautaire sans dépendance extérieure prolongée.

4. Renforcement des systèmes locaux
La solution s’inscrit dans un modèle communautaire et institutionnel durable, en collaboration avec :
- les centres culturels et éducatifs,
- les radios locales,
- les opérateurs télécoms,
les collectivités territoriales. Elle contribue ainsi à renforcer les capacités locales à intégrer durablement le numérique dans les politiques de jeunesse, d’éducation et de développement.

Impact attendu à long terme :

Un environnement numérique inclusif au Tchad, où les jeunes, même issus des milieux les plus défavorisés, accèdent aux outils numériques, deviennent compétents, autonomes et contribuent activement à la croissance économique et à la transformation sociale.
Testimonials and Endorsements:
À ce jour, nous n’avons pas pu recueillir formellement des témoignages écrits ou vidéo des bénéficiaires. Toutefois, plusieurs retours positifs ont été exprimés oralement par les jeunes formés, les membres de la communauté et les partenaires locaux, témoignant de l’impact réel de la solution sur le terrain.

Des photos illustrant les activités de formation ainsi que d’autres résultats visibles du projet sont disponibles sur le site web officiel de l’ADPV à l’adresse suivante : www.adpv-td.org.
Further comments/feedback:
Le questionnaire est bien structuré et permet de présenter de manière détaillée la solution proposée. Il favorise une réflexion approfondie sur les impacts, les partenariats et la durabilité de l’initiative. Il serait toutefois bénéfique d’ajouter deux options importantes :

1. La possibilité de sauvegarder le formulaire comme brouillon, afin de permettre aux candidats de le compléter progressivement sans perdre les informations déjà saisies.
2. L'ajout d'une section pour joindre des documents justificatifs (rapports, brochures, attestations, etc.), ce qui renforcerait la crédibilité des candidatures et faciliterait la vérification des informations.

Merci pour cette opportunité qui valorise les actions locales et communautaires.

It combines practical training, community-based delivery, and mentorship to reduce the digital divide. The pilot trained 21 youths, with tangible outcomes such as CV creation, internships, and job opportunities.

Title: AHISSA: Smart Access to Agricultural Markets for Small Producers
Subtitle: A digital platform that connects smallholder farmers to buyers, improves price transparency, and reduces post-harvest losses in West Africa.
Problem Statement: Smallholder farmers in Benin and neighboring countries face significant challenges in accessing stable markets, receiving fair prices, and avoiding post-harvest losses. With limited visibility and no direct link to urban or cross-border buyers, over 35% of harvested maize and cassava derivatives are wasted. This leads to income insecurity and discourages youth engagement in agriculture. Furthermore, the absence of digital infrastructure for inclusive market access perpetuates rural exclusion from the growing digital economy.
Solution Overview:
AHISSA is a mobile-first digital platform developed by AGROTRADE BENIN SARL that facilitates real-time connections between agricultural cooperatives and urban or cross-border buyers. It aggregates demand, provides price transparency, and enables digital transaction tracking.

Methodology & Technology Used:

    Progressive web app optimized for low-connectivity zones

    Integration of mobile money and USSD features for non-smartphone users

    Data-driven dashboards to track supply, pricing, and logistics

Partnerships & Collaboration Models:

    Cooperatives: Provide regular stock data

    Market traders & cross-border buyers: Source products on-demand

    Youth-led logistics partners: Manage last-mile delivery

    Public agriculture platforms: Feed market trends into the system
    AHISSA is also supported by the Centre pour l'Employabilité et l'Entrepreneuriat des Étudiants de l’UAC and the Resolution Project.
Solution Provider(s): AGROTRADE BENIN SARL (AgriTech social enterprise, Benin), Centre pour l’Employabilité et l’Entrepreneuriat des Étudiants de l’UAC (Academic entrepreneurship support, Benin), Resolution Project (Global social impact incubator, USA)
Implementation location(s): Benin – Departments of Plateau (Kétou, Ifangni), Ouémé (Porto-Novo), and Littoral (Cotonou)
Duration to pilot in a new geography: 3 to 4 months, including onboarding of producers, technical setup, and buyer engagement
SDGs addressed: SDG 9 (Industry, Innovation, and Infrastructure);SDG 8 (Decent Work and Economic Growth);SDG 2 (Zero Hunger);
Desired impact:
Solution Objectives:

    Facilitate direct and digital access to markets for smallholder farmers

    Reduce post-harvest losses and price volatility for maize and cassava

    Empower women and youth through inclusive digital tools

    Digitize informal trade and supply chains in rural areas

Key Achievements (as of mid-2025):

    10 agricultural cooperatives onboarded (≈300 smallholder farmers, 70% women)

    Over 70 tons of maize traded with digital traceability

    16 temporary and 4 permanent jobs created (logistics, sales agents)

    Reduction of post-harvest losses by an estimated 25% in pilot zones
Key technologies:
Progressive Web App (PWA) optimized for low-connectivity areas

USSD and SMS integration for inclusive access

Mobile money integration (MoMo, MTN, Moov, Celtiis) for transactions

Data dashboards for cooperative inventory and pricing

Planned use of AI for demand forecasting and market insights (future roadmap)
Unique Characteristics:
AHISSA stands out through its hybrid last-mile model that bridges the digital divide in rural agricultural trade. Unlike traditional platforms, AHISSA combines a mobile-first web app, USSD/SMS access, and a physical logistics network to connect farmers many of whom lack smartphones or internet with urban buyers. The platform is specifically tailored for low-income, low-tech environments, leveraging community-based logistics agents for collection and delivery.

Our inclusive business model removes financial barriers: registration is free for farmers, and revenues are generated through a small transaction fee from buyers and service partners. We reinvest part of the margin into rural capacity building.

AHISSA’s co-development approach with local cooperatives ensures high adoption, while partnerships with platforms like Agrosfer and Afrimarket extend market reach. Our offline-first tech stack, youth-led distribution model, and embedded financial tools (MoMo, Celtiis, MTN, Moov) create a seamless value chain integration that is both scalable and replicable across West Africa.
Sustainable Change:
AHISSA’s model addresses systemic exclusion of rural farmers from the digital economy. By digitizing market access and integrating financial inclusion tools (mobile payments, pricing intelligence), the solution empowers producers, improves income stability, and fosters entrepreneurial ecosystems in rural zones.

Theory of Change:

    Digital connection → Increased visibility and access to buyers

    Market access → Better prices, reduced losses, and motivation to scale

    Youth employment → Logistics agents, platform support, sales roles

    Replication model → Expand to similar regions with high post-harvest loss

    Systemic shift → Informal trade becomes traceable, inclusive, and efficient
Funding Sources: The solution has been entirely self-funded by the founder, without any external grants or institutional investment to date. This reflects a strong personal commitment to the solution’s development and deployment.
Testimonials and Endorsements: Not available at this stage. However, positive informal feedback has been consistently received from early users and cooperative members engaged through the platform. Formal testimonials will be collected during the upcoming pilot expansion.
Primary thematic focus area: Stable and Resilient Digital Supply Chains
Summary: AHISSA is a mobile-first agri-marketplace developed in Benin that connects smallholder farmers with buyers through an offline-first digital platform and youth-led logistics. Strengths: strong local problem alignment (post-harvest losses, market exclusion), inclusive tech stack (PWA, USSD, mobile money), and demonstrated early results with measurable trade volumes and job creation. Weaknesses: still at MVP stage, self-funded with limited external financing, and AI-driven forecasting still in roadmap phase.

Title: Smart Porridge: AI-Driven Flour Production for Nutrition and Inclusion"
Subtitle: "Using AI and local grains, we produce nutritious porridge flour that boosts health, supports farmers, and drives inclusive growth in Rwanda’s digital economy.
Problem Statement: Many rural communities in Rwanda face limited access to nutritious food, inefficient grain processing, and lack of market data, hindering both health outcomes and smallholder farmer income.
Solution Overview:
Solution Overview

Our solution combines traditional grain processing with digital innovation to produce high-quality porridge flour while supporting local communities and driving inclusive economic growth.

How the Solution Works:
We source grains (such as maize, sorghum, millet, and soy) directly from smallholder farmers in Rwanda. These are then cleaned, blended, and milled into nutritious porridge flour using improved, hygienic processing methods. AI technologies are integrated into several stages of the value chain to enhance efficiency and quality:

Grain Selection & Sorting: AI-powered image recognition tools help identify and sort high-quality grains, reducing waste and improving product consistency.

Quality Control: Machine learning algorithms monitor moisture levels, contamination risks, and nutrient composition during production.

Market Forecasting: AI models analyze sales data, seasonal trends, and market demands to forecast production needs and optimize distribution.

Digital Training & Farmer Support: A mobile platform shares best practices, weather alerts, and market prices with partner farmers, increasing productivity and resilience.

Methodologies and Technologies Used:

Artificial Intelligence (AI) for predictive analytics and quality control

Image recognition for sorting and grading grains

Cloud-based mobile platform for farmer communication and data sharing

Data analytics for market trend analysis and production planning

Partnerships and Collaboration Models:

Farmer Cooperatives: We collaborate with local farmer groups to ensure consistent grain supply and fair pricing.

Tech Partners: We work with local and international AI developers and data science experts to adapt digital tools to our context.

NGOs & Development Agencies: Partnerships support farmer training, gender inclusion, and nutritional awareness campaigns.

Government & Regulatory Bodies: We align with national food safety and economic development policies to scale responsibly.

Sector: Technology, Artificial Intelligence, Digital Inclusion.  Rwanda Agriculture and Animal Resources Development Board (RAB) – A government agency that supports agricultural research, extension services, and farmer development. Sector: Public Sector, Agriculture, Research.  GIZ Rwanda – A German development agency supporting sustainable economic development and digital transformation in Rwanda. Sector: Development Cooperation, Digital Economy, Capacity Building.

Increase access to affordable, nutritious porridge flour in Rwanda.

Empower smallholder farmers through fair trade and digital tools.

Enhance food quality and production efficiency using AI.

Promote inclusive participation in the digital economy, especially among women and youth.

Unique Characteristics:

AI-Enhanced Traditional Agriculture:
We blend traditional grain processing with advanced AI technologies—an uncommon approach in Rwanda’s agrifood sector. This enables precision in quality control, reduces waste, and improves nutritional standards.

Title: Innovative Blood Bank Management System for Tanzania's Healthcare Efficiency.
Subtitle: The Highlands MOS Health Facility's Blood Bank Management System in Tanzania efficiently tracks blood donation, storage, and transfusions, ensuring safe, timely blood supply and inventory control.
Problem Statement:
The Highlands Mos Health Facility aims to develop an innovative blood bank management database system that transcends the limitations of the traditional methods currently employed by the National Blood Transfusion Service (NBTS) in Tanzania. The existing approach often faces challenges such as inefficient inventory tracking, delayed blood availability, and data inaccuracies, which can lead to critical shortages and adversely affect patient outcomes, particularly among economically disadvantaged populations.

Our proposed system seeks to address these key issues by providing a real-time, integrated platform for blood donations tracking and inventory management. This will enhance the accuracy and timeliness of data, streamline the blood collection, storage, and distribution processes, and ensure that life-saving blood supplies are readily available when needed. 
Ultimately, this revolutionary approach aims to save lives by reducing blood shortages and improving access to safe and sufficient blood supplies for all Tanzanians, especially the vulnerable communities who are most affected by current limitations.
Solution Overview:
The proposed solution is a revolutionary Blood Bank Management Database System designed to transform the current blood supply and management practices employed by the National Blood Transfusion Service (NBTS) in Tanzania. Recognising the critical gaps and inefficiencies in the existing system, this innovative platform aims to streamline blood inventory tracking, enhance donor engagement, facilitate real-time data sharing among health facilities, and ultimately improve patient outcomes, especially for the economically disadvantaged living below $5 per day.
>HOW THE SOLUTION WORKS
1. A Centralised, Real-Time Database System
- At its core, the system is a centralised digital database that consolidates information from all registered health facilities of all levels (dispensaries, health centres, polyclinics, and hospitals) across Tanzania. It continuously updates data on blood stock levels, donor records, blood types, expiration dates, and distribution history.
2. Intelligent Inventory Management and Forecasting
-Using advanced algorithms and machine learning techniques, the system analyses historical data to predict future blood demand patterns. This enables health facilities to plan inventory replenishments efficiently, reducing wastage and ensuring a steady supply of blood for emergencies.
3. Donor Engagement and Recruitment Module
-The platform incorporates features to identify reliable donors, schedule donation drives, and sends reminders to existing donors. It encourages community participation through awareness campaigns integrated into the system, making it easier to reach more donors especially those from underserved communities.
4. Inter-Facility Blood Exchange Platform
-A key feature is the ability to facilitate quick "blood exchanges" among facilities. When one health centre has surplus blood of a particular type, and another faces scarcity, the system enables secure and efficient transfer requests, minimising delays and ensuring patients receive timely care.
5. Accessibility and User-Friendly Interface
-Designed with simplicity in mind, the system is accessible via web and mobile platforms, allowing health workers and administrators in remote areas to access critical information without requiring sophisticated infrastructure or extensive technical skills.
METHODOLOGIES AND TECHNOLOGIES USED
>Cloud Computing and Data Hosting
The system leverages cloud infrastructure for scalability, security, and accessibility, ensuring data is safely stored and available across the country.
>Mobile and Web Application Development
User-friendly interfaces are developed for both Android and web platforms, allowing widespread access even in areas with limited connectivity.
>Secure Authentication and Data Privacy
Robust security protocols, including encryption and role-based access controls, protect sensitive donor and patient data.
>Partnerships and Collaboration Models
The system is designed to collaborate with government health agencies, local NGOs, international health organisations like WHO, and private sector partners. 
IMPACT ON POOR LIVES IN TANZANIA
This system aims to directly improve health outcomes for Tanzania's most vulnerable populations by: 
i) Lowering Costs
-By streamlining processes and reducing wastage, the system minimises operational costs, making blood more affordable and accessible.
ii) Enhancing Donor Participation
-Encouraging community-driven blood donation campaigns helps build a sustainable donor base among low-income populations.
iii) Empowering Rural and Remote Areas
With mobile access and real-time data sharing, health facilities in underserved regions can coordinate better.
-Highlands Mos Health Facility based in Dar es salaam has firsthand experience with the challenges faced in healthcare delivery. This innovative system represents a significant leap forward in Tanzania's healthcare landscape. By harnessing modern technology, fostering collaborations it promises to save lives

SDGs addressed: SDG 3 (Good Health and Well-being);
Desired impact:
The desired impact of our innovative blood bank management database system in Tanzania is to significantly enhance the efficiency, accuracy, and responsiveness of blood bank operations nationwide. The solution aims to modernise the current traditional approaches employed by the National Blood transfusion Service (NBTS), leading to improved health outcomes and operational sustainability.

Solution Objectives:

a)Streamline Blood Inventory Management: Implement real-time tracking of blood stocks to reduce shortages and wastage.
b)Enhance Data Accuracy and Accessibility: Provide a centralised digital platform for better data management, retrieval, and reporting.
c)Improve Donor and Recipient Management: Facilitate efficient donor registration, screening, and recipient matching processes.
d)Ensure Blood Safety and Traceability: Incorporate safety protocols and traceability features to prevent transfusion-transmissible infections.
e)Support Decision-Making: Enable data-driven decisions through analytics and reporting tools.

Key Achievements and Impacts:

a) Increased Efficiency: Reduces blood processing time by approximately 30% ensuring faster availability for patients.
b) Reduction in Blood Wastage: Achieves a 80%decrease in expired or unused blood units through better stock management. Unlikely the existing paper approach used by NBTS that leads to extremely wastage of blood units due to poor stock management.
c)Enhanced Data Accuracy: Minimizes errors in donor and recipient information, improving safety and compliance.
d)Employment Generation: The system is assured to create about 200 new jobs related to system maintenance, data management, and technical support within Highlands Mos Health Facility and associated regional centres.
e)Improves Service Coverage: Through expanding access to safe blood services to underserved regions, increasing transfusion availability by 25% compared to the existing approach used throughout the country.

Overall, this innovative database system is expected to contribute to a more resilient, transparent, and effective blood transfusion service in Tanzania, ultimately saving more lives and strengthening the country's healthcare infrastructure.
Key technologies:
The innovative blood bank management database system developed for deployment in Tanzania leverages a suite of advanced technologies to enhance efficiency, accuracy, and collaboration among stakeholders such as the National Blood Transfusion Service (NBTS), Government agencies, health NGOs, and Health facilities (both Public & Private). The key technologies utilised in our system include:

1. AI (Artificial Intelligence):
-AI algorithms are employed to optimise blood inventory management, predict demand patterns, and automate data analytics. This enables proactive planning, reduces wastage, and ensures timely availability of blood supplies across facilities.

2. Database Management Systems (DBMS):
-A robust, secure, and scalable database underpins the system, facilitating real-time tracking of blood units, donor information, and inventory status. Technologies such as SQL or NoSQL database will be used, depending on scalability and data complexity requirements. 

3. Web and Mobile Application Technologies:
-User-friendly interfaces are built using web frameworks (like React, Angular or Vue.js) and mobile app development platforms (such as Android and IOS) to ensure accessibility and ease of use for health workers, administrators, and donors.

4. Cloud Computing:
-Cloud services such as AWS or Azure provide scalable infrastructure for data storage, processing, and backup, ensuring high availability and disaster recovery.

5. Internet of Things (IoT):
-IoT devices, such as temperature sensors in storage units and RFID tags on blood bags, enable real-time monitoring of storage conditions and asset tracking, ensuring blood safety and integrity.

6. Data Security and Privacy Technologies: 
-Implementation of encryption, access controls, and compliance with data protection standards to safeguard sensitive donor and patient information. 

7. Interoperability Standards:
-Adherence of healthcare data standards to facilitate seamless data exchange between the blood bank system and other health information systems across Tanzania.

8. Collaborative and Communication Tools: Integration of communication platforms (email, SMS,alerts, notifications) to streamline coordination among stakeholders and facilitate timely updates.

This integrated technological approach aims to create a reliable, efficient, and secure blood bank management system that supports Tanzanian's health sector in saving lives and improving blood transfusion services. The project is led by the Highlands Mos Health Facility based in Dar es salaam, in collaboration with NBTS and other key stakeholders, ensuring local relevance and sustainable implementation.
Unique Characteristics:
Our innovative blood bank management database system introduces several unique and differentiated features that set it apart from the existing approach used by NBTS in Tanzania. These features enhance efficiency, accuracy, and responsiveness in blood support services across the country. These advancements include:

1. Integrated Real-Time Data Management: The system offers a centralised platform that consolidates blood inventory, donor information, and transfusion records in real-time, enabling swift decision-making and reducing delays.

2. Advanced Donor and Blood Tracking: Leveraging barcode and RFID technologies, the system ensures precise tracking of blood units from collection to transfusion, minimising errors and enhancing traceability.

3. Predictive Analytics and Demand Forecasting: Incorporating machine learning algorithms, the system analyses historical data to predict future blood demand in various regions, optimising inventory levels and reducing wastage.

4.Automated Replenishment and Supply Chain Optimisation: The system automates alerts for low stock levels and coordinates with regional centres to facilitate timely replenishment, ensuring consistent availability.

5. Enhanced Data Security and Privacy: Utilising robust encryption and access controls, the system safeguards sensitive donor and patient information, complying with national and international data protection standards.

6. User-Friendly Interface with Mobile Accessibility: The system will feature a user-friendly accessible via web and mobile devices, enabling easy access for field staffs and health workers to input and retrieve data efficiently in remote areas.

7. Partnership and Business Model Innovations: The system establishes a collaborative platform connecting hospitals, clinics, and mobile blood collection units, fostering partnerships that optimise resource sharing and expand outreach. The system also supports innovative financing mechanisms, such as subscription-based access for smaller health facilities, ensuring sustainability and scalability.

8. Technological Breakthroughs in Cloud Integration and Scalability: Leverages cloud technology for scalable storage and processing, ensuring high availability, disaster recovery, and seamless updates, which are critical for a nationwide healthcare support system.

This comprehensive, technologically advanced, and partnership-oriented approach makes our blood bank management system a groundbreaking solution that enhances efficiency, safety, and sustainability in blood support services across the country.
Sustainable Change:
The implementation of the innovation blood bank management database system in Tanzania, spearheaded by the Highlands Mos Health Facility team in collaboration with the National Blood Transfusion Service (NBTS) and key health stakeholders, contributes to creating sustainable, systematic change through several interconnected mechanisms aligned with our theory of change.

How our solution contributes to sustainable, systematic change:

1. Enhance Data Management and Decision-Making: The new system provides real-time, accurate, and centralised data on blood inventory, donor information, and transfusion needs. This improves the efficiency and reliability of blood supply management, reducing wastage and shortages. Overtime, this fosters a culture of evidence-based decision-making that is embedded within the health system.

2. Capacity Building and Local Ownership: By involving the Researchers, Medical team and Country's local health authorities in system deployment, training, and maintenance, the solution builds local capacity. This empowers the local staffs to manage and adapt the system independently, ensuring long-term sustainability beyond external support. 

3. Standardisation of Processes: The system introduces standardised workflows for blood collection, testing, storage, and distribution across facilities. Standardisation reduces variability and errors, leading to improved safety and quality of blood transfusions which becomes institutionalised within the health system.

4. Strengthening Collaboration and Coordination: The platform facilitates better communication and coordination among hospitals, blood donation centres, and national authorities. This interconnectedness promotes a more integrated blood management network in Tanzania that enhances resilience and responsiveness in crises.

5. Data-Driven Policy and Planning: Aggregated data from the system informs policymakers and health planners about blood usage patterns, donor trends, and gaps. This supports the development of targeted interventions, policies, and resource allocation strategies, fostering a proactive approach to blood safety and sufficiency.

Desired Follow-on-Effects (Theory of Change):

>Immediate Effect: Improved accuracy, efficiency, and safety of blood management processes at participating facilities.

>Medium-Term Effect: Increased availability of safe blood, reduced wastage, and strengthened capacity of local health teams to manage blood services independently.

>Long-Term Effect: Establishment of a sustainable, resilient blood management system integrated into the national health infrastructure. This leads to improved patient outcomes, reduced mortality from blood-related conditions, and the creation of a replicable model for other regions in Tanzania and beyond.

Overall, our solution aims to embed a culture of systematic, data-driven blood management within Tanzanian health systems, fostering sustainable improvements in blood safety, availability, and health outcomes for generations to come.
Funding Sources: The innovative blood bank management database system for Tanzania currently in the idea phase has primarily been funded through internal sources. To date, the project has made initial progress by engaging with key stakeholders, including health leaders in the country, mutual NGOs such as AMREF and SIGHT SAVERS, as well as the board of the National Blood Transfusion Service (NBTS). While these engagements have provided valuable support and validation, the development and implementation of the system rely mainly on the project's own funding. Securing external funding would be crucial in advancing the system from the conceptual stage to full deployment, enabling swift action and a more robust upgrade to the existing blood bank management approach used by NBTS in Tanzania.
Further comments/feedback:
During the meeting held on 14th October 2024 at NBTS headquarters, which was organised by the late National Director of WHO Africa, Dr. Faustine Ndugulile, Dr. Juma Programme Manager from NBTS provided remarks on the new system. He highlighted that the prospects discussed and the ideas behind the innovative system could be a life-changing development for NBTS, significantly enhancing efficiency, data accuracy, and overall management of blood supplies.

However, Dr JUma also noted that a major hindrance is NBTS's tight budget constraints. The organisation is currently unable to fund the development and implementation of the new system immediately. It is planned that a comprehensive system funding proposal will be prepared and included in the budget for the new fiscal year starting in July 2025. As of now, NBTS has yet to receive confirmation or further communication regarding the funding approval.

Overall, while the system holds great promise, financial limitations remain a key challenge that needs to be addressed to realise this innovative solution.
Primary thematic focus area: Stable and Resilient Digital Supply Chains
Summary: The Highlands Mos Health Facility proposes an AI-powered Blood Bank Management Database System for Tanzania to address inefficiencies in the National Blood Transfusion Service (NBTS). The platform integrates real-time inventory management, predictive analytics, donor engagement, and inter-facility blood exchanges, accessible via web and mobile (Q13, Q16). It aims to reduce shortages, wastage, and errors, while ensuring equitable access to safe blood, especially for underserved populations (Q11, Q17).

Title: CLIMATE VOICES DL
Subtitle: Climate Voices Digital Lab is  is a mobile-first platform designed to empower women journalists and grassroots storytellers by enabling them to create, publish, and amplify climate justice narratives, even in offline or low-bandwidth environments.
Problem Statement:
In East Africa, women journalists and grassroots storytellers face systemic barriers to participating in the digital economy and shaping climate narratives. Despite making up 44% of the media workforce in Uganda, only 33% hold editorial leadership roles, and a staggering 55% of front-page stories exclude women entirely. And if a climate story involves a  woman, she is interviewed as a victim and not as an expert. This underrepresentation limits their ability to influence public discourse and policy.

Digital exclusion compounds the issue. While 64% of the region is covered by high-speed internet, only 24% of the population actively uses it, with rural women disproportionately affected by cost, infrastructure gaps, and digital illiteracy. Even mobile access, though widespread, lacks the functionality needed for advanced storytelling and advocacy.

Climate change intensifies these challenges. East Africa is experiencing rising temperatures of up to 0.5°C per decade, increased droughts, and erratic rainfall patterns that threaten food security, water access, and livelihoods. Yet, the voices of those most impacted especially women in vulnerable communities remain largely absent from climate policy and media coverage.
Solution Overview:
Let me imagine im pitching it in 5 minutes, this is how it would flow
Come with me to Karamoja in the deep ends of Uganda’s geographical discoveries, a place many global climate conversations forget, where the sun scorches wetlands, the internet is a luxury, and stories are passed from mother to daughter, never reaching decision-makers in Brussels or Addis Ababa. That’s where Climate Voices Digital Lab begins.

Without inclusive digital tools and platforms, these women are locked out of the very conversations that shape their futures.

Climate Voices D L  is a mobile-first platform designed to empower women journalists and grassroots storytellers by enabling them to create, publish, and amplify climate justice narratives, even in offline or low-bandwidth environments. It operates through a three-part framework: 
1.	A Story Creation Hub with voice-to-text tools, data visualizations, and writing templates; a Capacity building Portal that offers micro-courses and mentorship in native languages; and a Story Syndication Engine that connects local stories to regional and international policy networks. 
2.	Built using human-centered design, the platform leverages AI and progressive web app technology for offline compatibility, while employing NLP and multilingual transcription tools to enhance accessibility. 
3. Its impact is monitored through participatory evaluation frameworks involving local media clubs and journalists. 
The exclusive Podcast Feature allows users to produce and distribute climate-focused audio stories, interviews, and field reports. This enhances emotional resonance, expands accessibility for low-literacy audiences, and supports storytelling in diverse languages and formats. Core podcast segments include Field Dispatches, Policy Pulse, Mic Drop Moments, and Behind the Story, all anchored in lived experiences and advocacy narratives.

Implementation follows a hub-and-spoke model anchored in Central Uganda and expanding via rural community storytellers. Strategic partnerships with organizations like  Centre for Gender Equality (CEGE), Women of Uganda Network(WOUGNET), African Center for Media Excellence, , local online radio stations like Luweero radio, Northern Uganda Media Club (NUMEC), , and regional allies such as Amshamsha Foundation, AfriLabs,  and  ensure the Lab's sustainability, reach, and integration into broader advocacy and development ecosystems.
Solution Provider(s): Women of Uganda Network (WOUGNET) is  civil society organization advancing women's rights through ICT and digital inclusion; active in digital safety advocacy, research, and community capacity building (Gender Equality & Technology), African Centre for Media Excellence (ACME) is a leading Ugandan nonprofit dedicated to strengthening journalism and promoting media freedom. ACME provides training in investigative reporting, climate journalism, and ethical media practices, Northern Uganda Media Club (NUMEC) a  leading media development organization based in Gulu, Uganda. NUMEC strengthens journalism in northern Uganda through training, press freedom advocacy, and climate storytelling,  Center for Gender Equality (CGE) is a community based organization that was established in 2016 to defend rights of women and girls. Based in Kasese- Western Uganda, Climate Talk Uganda with Josephine Karungi  is a biweekly podcast exploring climate change impacts in Uganda through community voices, agriculture, and innovation. Hosted by journalist Josephine Karungi, it features grassroots stories and climate solutions from across the country. Luweero Online radio is a community online radio which supports and work by sharing local stories, climate issues, and educational program.
Duration to pilot in a new geography: Not Applicable
SDGs addressed: SDG 13 (Climate Action);SDG 5 (Gender Equality);SDG 17 (Partnerships for the Goals);
Desired impact:
The solution aims to
1.	Amplify marginalized voices in climate discourse.
2.	  Build media capacity for accurate and compelling climate reporting. 
3.	 Foster civic engagement and policy influence through localized storytelling.
4.	 Promote inclusive climate action by bridging digital divides. These goals are pursued through a mobile-first platform that operates even in offline or low-bandwidth environments, using AI-powered voice-to-text tools, multilingual transcription, and human-centered design.
Quantifiable impacts from pilot phases and projected outcomes include:

o	Over 150 climate stories published across East Africa and Europe

o	More than 300 journalists and media professionals trained in climate reporting and digital tools

o	2.5 million plus social media impressions from campaigns like #ClimateVoicesAfrica

o	Engagement of 40 plus grassroots organizations in co-creation and dissemination.

o	Creation of annual youth-led media fellowships, contributing to climate innovation in the media.
o	60% of content adapted for offline access, expanding reach in low-connectivity areas
o	Survey-based evidence of increased public understanding of GHG mitigation strategies
Long-term, the Lab seeks to influence climate adaptation policies, integrate community narratives into regional frameworks like COMESA, and scale its model across other geographies.
Key technologies:
AI tools
Climate Voices Digital Lab leverages a mix of accessible technologies to drive inclusive climate storytelling. Its backbone is a mobile-friendly web application built to function seamlessly in low-bandwidth settings. Through natural language processing and multilingual transcription tools, it allows users to convert spoken language into written text, navigate the platform in local dialects, and communicate across linguistic barriers. The platform’s progressive web framework ensures offline compatibility, enabling creators in remote areas to publish and interact with climate content without constant internet access. AI-enhanced features offer support with writing suggestions and layout options, while embedded data visualization tools help users illustrate climate trends with clarity. Designed with community input and user feedback, the system’s architecture prioritizes usability and security, supported by scalable cloud infrastructure and APIs that connect storytellers to larger networks. Every technological element works together to ensure the platform remains relevant, resilient, and empowering to voices that have long been unheard.
Unique Characteristics:
The Climate Voices Digital Lab is an inclusive, mobile-first platform designed to bridge the digital divide by equipping women journalists and grassroots storytellers, especially in low-bandwidth regions with AI-powered tools to create and syndicate climate justice narratives.

 Built using progressive web technology and human-centered design, the Lab operates fully offline and supports voice-to-text transcription and multilingual content creation, ensuring accessibility for low-literacy and linguistically diverse communities. Its integrated podcast feature expands narrative formats to audio, enabling rebroadcast through local radio and mobile listening hubs. Structured around a hub-and-spoke model anchored in Central Uganda, the Lab leverages community-led scaling and strategic partnerships with COMESA, WOUGNET, ACME, NUMEC, and Amshamsha Foundation, a Tanzanian nonprofit advancing climate restoration, clean energy, and community resilience through youth-led innovation and cross-sector collaboration.

 The Lab’s hybrid financing mechanism blends donor funding with monetizable training toolkits and syndicated content services, ensuring long-term sustainability. By combining digital accessibility, gender equity, and localized storytelling with AI innovation, the Climate Voices Digital Lab advances an inclusive digital economy where climate narratives can influence policy, shift behavior, and drive equitable development at scale.
Sustainable Change:
If underserved women journalists and grassroots storytellers are equipped with mobile-first, offline compatible digital tools enhanced by AI, localized languages, and accessible formats, they will produce climate narratives that reflect lived realities and overlooked policy gaps. By integrating storytelling into community capacity building and syndicating content to regional platforms, the Lab enables narratives to influence climate policy, reshape development priorities, and foster inclusive media ecosystems.

This leads to:

	Increased civic engagement in climate discourse from underrepresented communities

	Strengthened media pluralism and gender representation in environmental reporting

	Policy shifts informed by localized, evidence-rich storytelling

	Scaled digital inclusion through community-led replication and strategic partnerships

Sustainable media innovation through hybrid financing and ecosystem co-ownership
In the long run, Climate Voices Digital Lab catalyzes an inclusive digital economy by embedding local voices into global climate decision-making structures, fostering resilience and equity through systems that are community-rooted, AI-enabled, and policy-linked.

Testimonials and Endorsements: Not Applicable

I'm particularly inspired by the project's alignment with the UN Sustainable Development Goals and its emphasis on inclusive, purpose-driven innovation. Regardless of the outcome, we remain committed to supporting this vision, whether through strategic partnerships, technical collaboration, or amplifying shared goals. We're excited by the potential for collective impact.
Primary thematic focus area: Innovation Acceleration & Knowledge Sharing
Summary: Climate Voices Digital Lab (DL) est une plateforme mobile-first conçue pour autonomiser les femmes journalistes et conteuses locales en Afrique de l’Est. Elle permet la création, la publication et l’amplification de récits sur la justice climatique, même en environnements à faible connectivité (Q12, Q19). Grâce à l’IA, à la transcription multilingue et aux podcasts, elle comble l’exclusion numérique, renforce les capacités locales, et connecte les récits communautaires aux réseaux régionaux et internationaux.

Title: Digital Solutions to Turn Plastic Waste into Economic Value
Subtitle: A community-driven solution using smart bins, digital points, and local incentives to transform plastic waste into income and impact.
Problem Statement: In many African communities, plastic waste is both an environmental and economic burden. Most households lack access to structured waste collection systems. Young people remain excluded from green jobs, and recycling value chains are disconnected from communities. There’s a missing link between behavior change, local incentives, and traceable impact.
Solution Overview:
Rôbalôtô is a community-based digital solution that incentivizes households to sort and sell plastic waste through a gamified, traceable system.

We use: QR-coded smart bins assigned to each household for waste tracking, A mobile platform where users earn green points based on the weight of sorted plastics, A local EcoMarket that connects plastic sellers (households) with recyclers and social enterprises, Environmental education clubs in schools to raise awareness and scale behavior change.

Methodologies and Technologies: Community-based data collection, Gamification of waste collection, Integration of IoT (QR-code enabled tracking), Mobile-first digital interface for low-bandwidth environments

Partnerships: CDQs (Neighborhood Development Committees), Local schools and educational authorities, Recyclers and plastic-processing SMEs, Municipalities for policy alignment
Solution Provider(s): - Rôbalôtô (Lead Innovator – Waste-Tech & Community Mobilization)  - Bras Ouverts Luna (NGO – Social Project Management & Local Education)  - CDQ (Neighborhood Development Committees – Local Governance)  - eco-citoyennete.org (Digital platform – Marketplace & Data Analytics)
Implementation location(s): Lomé, Togo (specifically Golfe 4 district and surrounding urban communities
Implementation timeline(s): Start: January 2023 Current phase: Ongoing pilot expansion through 2025
Duration to pilot in a new geography: 4 to 6 months
SDGs addressed: SDG 11 (Sustainable Cities and Communities);SDG 12 (Responsible Consumption and Production);SDG 13 (Climate Action);
Desired impact:
Solution Objectives: 

Digitize and incentivize plastic waste collection, Promote youth employment in the circular economy, Connect recyclers to reliable, traceable waste streams.

Key Achievements:

Over 200+ tons of plastic diverted from the environment during pilot.
50+ schools and 300+ households onboarded with smart bins.
15 youth employed as local collectors and EcoMarket agents.
Schools integrated into environmental education campaigns.
Key technologies:
QR-code enabled IoT smart bins

Mobile-first web platform

Gamification algorithm for point-based rewards

Geo-tagging and community-based tracking
Unique Characteristics:
Community-embedded approach with local development committees.

Dual platform: Education + Economic value creation.

Plastic as currency: Citizens can convert waste into digital points redeemable for rewards or services.

Scalable model: Adaptable for other materials or urban challenges (e.g., e-waste, compost).
Sustainable Change:
Rôbalôtô changes the perception of plastic from "waste" to "economic resource." By incentivizing households and youth to actively engage in waste management, the solution builds a new local ecosystem of value around plastic. This encourages inclusive entrepreneurship, strengthens circular economy networks, and fosters a mindset shift across communities.

Our Theory of Change is based on behavior change, digital empowerment, and economic inclusion, leading to long-term environmental resilience and social transformation.
Funding Sources:
The Rôbalôtô solution has been funded through a combination of awards, private grants, and in-kind contributions from local partners.
Notable funding and support include:

TotalEnergies Startupper of the Year Award 2024 (Pan-African Winner) – cash prize and mentorship

GIZ Startup Togo – 1st Prize 2024, including financial and technical support

Togo Digital Awards – 3rd Prize

In-kind technical assistance from the Bras Ouverts Luna NGO
Primary thematic focus area: MSME Empowerment & Local Digital Innovation
Summary: Rôbalôtô is a community-driven digital waste-tech initiative in Lomé, Togo that transforms plastic into economic value through QR-coded smart bins, a gamified mobile platform, and local EcoMarkets (Q13). Its strengths are demonstrated pilot results (200+ tons diverted, 50+ schools onboarded, 15 youth employed) (Q22) and strong recognition through awards (Q27). Weaknesses include limited geographic scope and lack of external testimonials (Q28).

Title: AI-powered nonprofit growth tool
Subtitle: Kweet helps nonprofits get new donors and save hours weekly
Problem Statement:
There are over 10 million nonprofit organizations worldwide, and most of them struggle to reach new donors due to limited marketing resources, ineffective acquisition strategies and lack of data-driven insights.

Charitable giving is set to grow 20% in the next 20 years. With 79% of Gen Z donors discovering causes online, the future of fundraising depends on effective outreach and donor acquisition strategies.

According to Google for Nonprofits survey, 75% of nonprofit believe GenAI has the potential to transform their marketing and donor outreach efforts.

Our beneficiaries are nonprofit organizations worldwide looking to get new individual donors and optimize their time and budget. In a way, our end beneficiaries are also those receiving support from our users - underserved communities, underrepresented causes.
Solution Overview:
Kweet is an AI-powered nonprofit growth tool that helps get new donors and save hours weekly.

Kweet assists with donor-centric writing across communications, marketing and fundraising. Unlike generic AI tools, Kweet focuses on donor psychology and will become the only tool nonprofits need for donor acquisition and retention.

By adding agentic AI to Kweet, we are looking to cut donor acquisition and marketing costs by 25% for our users, driving millions in additional donations while boosting donor engagement.

Our pilot study will 5 nonprofit ranging from $150k-9M in annual revenue have shown up to 80% time saved for writing donor-centric comms, allowing nonprofit workers to invest their freed time into building relationships with donors and corporate partners.
Implementation location(s): Germany, Spain, Ukraine, United States, Mexico
Implementation timeline(s): We ran a pilot from February to July 2025 - now opening doors to new users
Duration to pilot in a new geography: 1 week. Kweet is intuitive by design, we provide personalized onboarding, learning materials and guides, as well as 24/7 founder support.
SDGs addressed: SDG 8 (Decent Work and Economic Growth);SDG 16 (Peace, Justice, and Strong Institutions);SDG 10 (Reduced Inequalities);
Desired impact:
In the short term, Kweet streamlines content creation, saving users up to 3 hours a day and reducing donor acquisition costs by around 30%. These immediate outputs translate into increased donor engagement and better campaign performance.
Over time, the cumulative effect of these improvements means nonprofits can run more effective fundraising campaigns, leading to higher donation volumes and expanded outreach.

Main KPI: Average time saved per user per week
We measure the cumulative hours saved through user activity tracking, feature usage data, and self-reported surveys.

Saving time translates directly into:

- More capacity for the most impactful work
- Reduced burnout for nonprofit teams
- Faster fundraising and growth outcomes

Revenue growth (secondary KPI)
    - Measures financial gains resulting from time reallocated toward strategic fundraising.
    - Indicates whether time saved is contributing to tangible organizational outcomes.
    
    Tracked through: user surveys and feedback loop.
Key technologies: AI, with agentic AI implementation planned for 2025
Unique Characteristics: Kweet helps nonprofits get new donors and save hours weekly by assisting them with donor-centric writing across communications, marketing and fundraising. Unlike generic AI tools, Kweet focuses on donor psychology and will become the only tool nonprofits need for donor acquisition and retention.
Sustainable Change:
We contribute to SDGs 5, 8, 10 and 16.

SDG 5 Gender Equality
Target 5.5: Ensure women’s full and effective participation and equal opportunities for leadership at all levels of decision-making in political, economic and public life.

We track the gender identity of nonprofit founders and executive leadership among our users.
Our KPIs include:
- % of women-led nonprofits using Kweet.
- Revenue growth rate among women-led organizations using our platform.
- Retention and engagement rates for women-led nonprofits.

By helping women-led organizations grow more efficiently, Kweet enables greater economic and leadership participation for women in the nonprofit sector.

SDG 8 Decent Work and Economic Growth
Target 8.3: Promote development-oriented policies that support productive activities, decent job creation, entrepreneurship, creativity and innovation.

We analyze annual revenue growth for nonprofits using Kweet.
Additional metrics include:

- Number of new grant/funding opportunities secured.

These indicators show how Kweet supports nonprofit economic resilience, job security, and expansion.

SDG 10 Reduced Inequalities
Target 10.2: Empower and promote the social, economic and political inclusion of all, irrespective of age, sex, disability, race, ethnicity, origin, religion or economic or other status.

Key impact indicators:

This allows us to assess how equitably Kweet is distributing AI-powered growth support to nonprofits that need it most.

SDG 16 Peace, Justice and Strong Institutions
Target 16.6: Develop effective, accountable and transparent institutions at all levels.

We help strengthen civil society by increasing the financial sustainability of nonprofit institutions.

Metrics include:

Title: We aim to install a biodigester to convert organic waste from our drying process (peels, branches, leaves) into renewable energy. The resulting biogas will power our drying operations, reducing our carbon footprint. The by-product, digestate, will be distributed as natural fertilizer to our network of agricultural suppliers, promoting a circular, sustainable, and eco-friendly model while significantly reducing methane emissions from our processing activities.
Subtitle: As part of our eco-responsible approach, we plan to install a biodigester to recover organic waste generated during the drying of our fruits, vegetables, and tubers (peels, branches, and plant residues). This system will produce biogas, which will be used as a renewable energy source to power our drying process, thus reducing our reliance on fossil fuels and lowering our carbon footprint.  The biodigester will also help reduce methane emissions generated by the natural decomposition of these wastes. In addition, it will produce digestate, a nutrient-rich natural fertilizer. This by-product will be redistributed—free or at low cost—to our network of agricultural suppliers, helping improve soil fertility and boosting local productivity.  This project follows a circular and sustainable model, combining economic performance, environmental responsibility, and positive social impact. It is easily replicable in other agricultural zones and contributes to building a more resilient and climate-conscious agri-food production system.
Problem Statement: The implementation of a biodigester presents several key challenges, including the high initial investment cost and the need for technical expertise to ensure optimal operation. Consistent supply of quality organic waste, ongoing maintenance, and compliance with regulatory standards also pose significant constraints. Additionally, social acceptance may be impacted by concerns related to odors or sanitary risks. To succeed, the project will require careful planning, strong technical partnerships, and effective engagement with local stakeholders to build understanding and support.
Solution Overview:
The biodigester breaks down organic waste (peels, plant residues) in the absence of oxygen. This anaerobic process produces biogas used for energy and digestate, a natural fertilizer. It transforms waste into a resource while significantly reducing greenhouse gas emissions.
The project uses continuous anaerobic digestion with automated control of temperature, pH, and pressure. Organic inputs are sorted, shredded, and fed into a sealed digester tank. The resulting biogas is captured, stored, and used for drying operations or injected into the national power grid.
The project will be implemented in partnership with Bio Energy, responsible for technical studies and system installation. ARSEL will oversee regulatory compliance for grid connection. EDC will manage the injection of surplus energy into the national grid, while ENEO will purchase and resell the excess power. The Pasteur Center will conduct digestate quality tests and environmental impact monitoring. Lastly, the Hintel Institute will support the initiative through student immersion programs, providing hands-on training in renewable energy and circular economy practices.
Solution Provider(s): Our key partner is Bio Energy, a company wich has an experience in biodigester installation and management.
Implementation location(s): Bio energy our partner already impliment this solution in some area of Cameroon
Implementation timeline(s): it can take three months to implement this solution
Duration to pilot in a new geography: we need six lonths to start
SDGs addressed: SDG 4 (Quality Education);SDG 7 (Affordable and Clean Energy);SDG 9 (Industry, Innovation, and Infrastructure);
Desired impact: Installing a biodigester aims to eliminate energy-related costs, which account for 8% of our production expenses. This sustainable solution will help reduce operational costs, enhance profitability, and ultimately allow us to keep our selling prices unchanged despite energy market fluctuations
Key technologies: We just une a biogigestor with a generator working with methane
Unique Characteristics: Our solution stands out by converting all our waste into energy. This benefits three key links: our suppliers, who gain access to affordable organic fertilizers; our clients, who enjoy stable prices as energy costs are offset by fertilizer sales; and our company, which can sell surplus energy to the state. This circular model strengthens both our economic and environmental sustainability while creating shared value across the entire chain.
Sustainable Change: Our solution shows that waste should not be seen as pollution, but as a real source of income. By turning waste into value, we transform an environmental challenge into an economic opportunity supporting our competitiveness, empowering our partners, and driving the transition to a more sustainable model.

Summary: The project aims to install a biodigester to convert organic waste into renewable energy, reduce greenhouse gas emissions, and produce natural fertilizer. The solution’s strengths include its circular model and sustainability focus, but it faces challenges related to high initial investment, technical expertise, and social acceptance.
