Title: Projet de digitalisation de 425 organisations de la société civile (OSC) du Burkina Faso
Subtitle: Digitalisation des OSC burkinabè , facteur contributif à la réalisation des piliers population, planète, prospérité, paix et partenariat de l'agenda 2030 des NU
Problem Statement: La non digitalisation des organisations de la société civile (OSC) dirigées par des femmes, des jeunes ou des personnes en situation de handicap au Burkina Faso, ne facilitent pas l'efficacité de leurs interventions dans la durée . Cet état de fait résulte de la faible capacité financière de ces organisations et partant constitue une barrière dans la conception de sites web adapté à leurs besoins spécifiques. En conséquence, la vulnérabilité économique des OSC ciblées aggrave les inégalités régionales et amplifient le fossé numérique. Or sachant que le numérique s'impose dans toute politique publique dans ce 21ème siècle et surtout dans la réponse aux crises, catastrophes naturelles et risques de changement climatique, il en résulte que sa faible appropriation réduit leurs contributions à la réalisation des ODD. En conclusion, sachant que le numérique est devenu essentiel dans toutes les politiques publiques au 21ème siècle, notamment pour gérer les crises, les catastrophes naturelles et les risques liés au changement climatique, il est évident que le faible usage de ces outils par les OSC diminue leurs efforts pour atteindre les Objectifs de Développement Durable.
Solution Overview:
La solution proposée au problème identifié au sous point 12 porte sur la réduction des inégalités régionales au niveau des OSC dirigées par des femmes, des jeunes ou des personnes en situation de handicap au Burkina Faso à travers la digitalisation de 425 d'entre elles. La durée de réalisation du projet est de 24 mois consécutifs . La méthodologie d'approche opérationnelle proposée pour la réalisation des activités du projet est structurée en trois étapes clés (phase préparatoire, phase opérationnelle et phase de livrables):
  Étape 1 : phase préparatoire 
Elle consistera en la tenue d'une réunion de cadrage entre l’Association MANN-GÃƆ et les experts de l'UNIDO. Ensuite, il s'agira de former les agents recenseurs mobilisés pour la collecte des données primaires et secondaires se rapportant aux OSC éligibles au projet. Enfin, une réunion de prise de contact aura lieu entre l’Association MANN-GÃƆ et les potentiels consultants chargés de concevoir de digitaliser les potentiels OSC bénéficiaires du projet

  Étape 2 : phase opérationnelle dite de terrain du projet
Il s'agira de mobiliser les ressources humaines (06) et 17 consultants pour respectivement le pilotage du projet et la conception des sites web au profit des 425 OSC identifiées . Ensuite, il sera organisé 17 ateliers de renforcement des capacités des 425 responsables d'OSC bénéficiaires dont en moyenne 25 participants dans chacune des 17 Régions administratives du pays. Enfin, les 17 Consultants mobilisés assureront la conception des sites web 

  Étape 3 : phase de livrables ou de bilan du projet
Il s'agira , à ce niveau d'assurer le monitoring , les évaluations à mi-parcours et de fin du projet , conformément au cahier de charge signé d'accord partie. En somme, les évaluations du projet se feront en application des critères d'évaluation de l'OCDE et en appropriation du guide méthodologique national d'analyse et d'évaluation des politiques publiques au Burkina Faso. Quant à l'évaluation d'impact du projet, elle se fera un an après la réception officielle des 425 sites web développés

Le budget Total du projet est USD 987,996, USD dont USD 948,584 représentant la subvention sollicitée à l'UNIDO et USD 39,412 provenant de l'apport en nature et en industrie des bénéficiaires

S'agissant du partenariat , l’Association MANN-GÃƆ , dans sa vision de ne laisser personne de côté dans toute thorine du changement, opte pour une approche inclusive et participative sensible aux jeunes, aux femmes et aux personnes en situation de handicap. A l'évidence, l'Etat et ses démembrements, les délégations spéciales communales , les OSC partenaires , les consultants accrédités dans le domaine du digital et le Bureau de coordination des NU à Ouagadougou seront impliqués dans tout le processus de cocréation de l'initiative
Solution Provider(s): Ministère en charge des libertés publiques du Gouvernement du Burkina Faso, Ministère de la Transition Digitale, des Postes et des Communications Électroniques du Gouvernement du Burkina Faso, Ensemble des 17 Régions administratives du Burkina Faso, Ensemble des 351 collectivités territoriales du Burkina Faso, Association Banw Baar et l'Association la Perche de l'Inclusion
Geographic focus: Burkina Faso (ensemble des 351 collectivités territoriales du Burkina Faso)
Implementation location(s): La solution est actuellement en phase pilote, mettant en avant la digitalisation de l'Association MANN-GÃƆ, située à Ouagadougou, au Burkina Faso, dans la région de l'Alliance des États du Sahel (AES) en Afrique de l'Ouest francophone. Depuis 2024, le portail numérique de l'Association MANN-GÃƆ est disponible à l'adresse suivante : https://www.mann-ga.org/
Implementation timeline(s): Le projet pilote de digitalisation de l'Association MANN-GÃƆ a été réalisé au Burkina Faso. La conception du site web de l'association a nécessité trois semaines de travail à temps partiel.
Duration to pilot in a new geography: 24 mois consécutifs
SDGs addressed: SDG 10 (Reduced Inequalities);SDG 16 (Peace, Justice, and Strong Institutions);SDG 17 (Partnerships for the Goals);
Desired impact:
	Objectifs spécifiques (OS) du projet :
      -  OS 1: combler le fossé numérique dans les domaines de l'humanitaire, du développement et de la paix en assurant la digitalisation d'au moins 425 organisations de la société civile dirigées par des femmes, des jeunes et des personnes en situation de handicap, et ce, dans un délai de 26 mois
      -  OS2: renforcer les compétences de 425 responsables des 425 OSC bénéficiaires du projet dans l'utilisation et l'animation de leurs plateformes numériques respectives, pour des interventions humanitaires rapides, Flexibles sécurisées, innovantes et assorties du devoir de redevabilité citoyenne pour les générations actuelle et future.
      -  OS3: Capitaliser chacune des 425 plateformes numériques construites pour booster la mobilisation des partenaires et des ressources autour de projets de lutte efficace, coordonnée et durable contre les crises, les catastrophes naturelles et les risques climatiques 

	Résultats attendus (RA):
      -  RA1 de l'OS1: le fossé numérique dans les domaines de l'humanitaire, du développement et de la paix, comblé, à partir de la digitalisation d'au moins 425 organisations de la société civile dirigées par des femmes, des jeunes et des personnes en situation de handicap, et ce, dans un délai de 24 mois
       -  RA1 de l'OS2 : renforcer les compétences de 425 responsables des 425 OSC bénéficiaires du projet dans l'utilisation et l'animation de leurs plateformes numériques respectives, pour des interventions humanitaires rapides, flexibles sécurisées, innovantes et assorties du devoir de redevabilité citoyenne pour les générations actuelle et future
      -  RA3 de l'OS3 : chacune des 425 plateformes numériques construites capitalisées, participent à booster la mobilisation des partenaires et des ressources autour de projets de lutte efficace, coordonnée et durable contre les crises, les catastrophes naturelles et les risques climatiques
Key technologies:
Les technologies numériques clés qui seront utilisées dans le présent projet sont: 
	L’IA: elle est la pièce maitresse qui sera utilisée pour la conception des 425 sites internet au profit des 425 associations bénéficiaires 
	Le Cloud Computing: Permet d'accéder à des ressources informatiques (serveurs, stockage, applications) via Internet, plutôt que de les avoir localement. 
	Les réseaux sociaux : il s’agit de l’utilisation de plateformes sécurisées pour les actions de visibilité des interventions de chacune des 425 OSC bénéficiaires du projet. Les réseaux sociaux serviront également de source de mobilisation des partenaires et des ressources pour le financement des projets sociaux. 
	 Blockchain: il s’agira de se doter à titre onéreux des espaces de partage et de sécurisation des données primaires et secondaires utiles à chaque association et à la communauté internationale et surtout aux populations vivant en milieu décentralisé. 
	 Cybersécurité : Technologies et pratiques visant à protéger les systèmes informatiques et les données contre les menaces numériques. 
	 Électronique numérique : Il s’agit d’équiper les 425 OSC d’ordinateurs portables pour l’exploitation informatisée des données statistiques
Unique Characteristics: L'initiative de digitalisation des plateformes, destinée à soutenir les 425 organisations dirigées par des femmes, des jeunes et des personnes en situation de handicap, repose sur une approche unique.  Autrement dit, chaque site web sera conçu de manière personnalisée, même si deux associations opèrent dans le même domaine. En somme, ce projet intègre les identités culturelles propres à chaque organisation tout en mettant l'accent sur les principes d'inclusion, de genre et de jeunesse . Les plateformes seront réalisées par des experts locaux, en utilisant un langage clair et accessible, garantissant ainsi une facilité d'utilisation pour tous.
Sustainable Change:
Les fractures numériques au Burkina Faso représentent une problématique réelle qui freine l'efficacité des acteurs humanitaires, notamment ceux issus de la société civile aux moyens financiers limités. Cette situation est particulièrement préoccupante dans un contexte marqué par une crise sécuritaire ayant généré plus de deux millions de Personnes Déplacées Internes (PDI). 

Face à cette crise humanitaire, la mobilisation des parties prenantes, en particulier les OSC dirigées par des jeunes, des femmes et des personnes en situation de handicap, s'avère essentielle. A ce titre, la digitalisation des 425 OSC vulnérables constitue une démarche alignée sur les Objectifs de Développement Durable (ODD) 10, 16 et 17 inscrits dans l'agenda 2030 des Nations Unies.

 En outre, la création de sites internet pour les OSC disposant de faibles capacités financières apparaît comme une solution concrète pour réduire les inégalités, renforcer l'efficacité des interventions humanitaires et favoriser des partenariats durables. 

A l'évidence, le présent projet contribuera à la réalisation des ODD, de l'agenda 2063 de l'Union Africaine, ainsi qu'au pilier 2 "Répondre à la crise humanitaire du plan d'action pour la stabilisation et le développement (2023-2026) du Gouvernement du Burkina Faso, du plan d'action intérimaire des NU pour le développement (UNIDAP 2023-2026) et des plans locaux de développement (PCD/PRD) en vigueur .
Funding Sources: Le projet pilote de digitalisation l’Association MANN-GÃƆ (https://www.mann-ga.org/) a été entièrement financé par les revenus issus des cotisations des membres et des droits d'adhésion forfaitaire. A cela, s'ajoutent un apport en industrie d'un Expert Senior indépendant du digital , à titre gratuit. Quand aux droits forfaitaires d'hébergement du site chez Webador qui s'élèvent à 21€ par mois, ils sont assurés par un Avocat du Barreau de Ouagadougou qui a souhaite garder l'anonymat dans ses œuvres de bienfaisance. La conception du site a couté au total : 2008 USD

Summary: This project aims to digitalize 425 civil society organizations in Burkina Faso, focusing on groups led by women, youth, and persons with disabilities. The initiative is well-aligned with SDGs but lacks detailed strategies for scaling beyond the pilot phase.

Title: MSME Empowerment & Local Digital Innovation: Solutions that enable MSMEs to access digital markets, finance, and tools
Subtitle: Empowering MSMEs in Yemen with digital finance, tools, and market access to drive inclusive growth and local economic resilience.
Problem Statement: In Yemen, many micro, small, and medium enterprises (MSMEs) face severe barriers to entering the digital economy. Limited access to digital finance, lack of technical skills, poor internet infrastructure, and insufficient market linkages restrict their ability to grow and compete. Women- and youth-led businesses are particularly excluded, deepening economic inequality and limiting community resilience. Without targeted support, these enterprises risk being left behind in an increasingly digital global marketplace.
Solution Overview:
The Yemen Microfinance Network’s MSME Empowerment & Local Digital Innovation initiative equips micro, small, and medium enterprises with the skills, tools, and market connections needed to thrive in the digital economy. The solution combines digital financial literacy, e-wallet adoption, and online market access with tailored training and mentoring.

How it Works:

Capacity Building – MSME owners receive training through the Microfinance Academy, Yemen’s first digital learning platform for microfinance, covering digital finance, e-commerce, and business development.

Digital Finance Access – In partnership with financial service providers, participants are onboarded to secure and user-friendly e-wallets, enabling digital transactions, savings, and access to microfinance.

Market Linkages – Businesses are connected to digital marketplaces and online platforms to expand customer reach locally and internationally.

Ongoing Support – Mentorship, technical assistance, and peer learning networks ensure continuous improvement and adaptation to market needs.

Methodologies and Technologies Used:

Blended learning approach combining interactive e-learning, mobile-based modules, and in-person coaching.

Mobile money and e-wallet platforms integrated with training to encourage immediate application of skills.

Data-driven monitoring using dashboards to track progress, adoption rates, and market engagement.

Partnerships and Collaboration Models:

Local MSMEs and cooperatives – Direct beneficiaries and co-creators of digital solutions.

Financial institutions and mobile money providers – Facilitate access to digital finance tools and secure transactions.

Government agencies and local authorities – Support policy alignment and infrastructure development.

International partners (UN agencies, INGOs) – Provide technical expertise, funding, and access to global market networks.

This collaborative, scalable approach ensures that MSMEs—especially those led by women and youth—gain the digital tools, market access, and financial services needed to drive inclusive and resilient economic growth in Yemen.
Solution Provider(s): Solution Provider(s):  Yemen Microfinance Network (YMN) – A national umbrella organization dedicated to enhancing financial inclusion, supporting MSMEs, and promoting sustainable economic development through capacity building, digital innovation, and partnerships. (Sector: Microfinance, Capacity Building, Digital Financial Services)  Social Fund for Development (SFD) – Yemen’s leading development agency supporting livelihoods, community development, and financial inclusion initiatives, with extensive experience in rural and vulnerable communities. (Sector: Development, Livelihoods, Finance)  [Local Financial Institution / Mobile Money Provider, e.g., Al Kuraimi Islamic Bank or Mobile Money Partner] – Provides secure, accessible e-wallet and mobile payment solutions to MSMEs. (Sector: Financial Services, Digital Payments)  Microfinance Institutions (e.g., Azal, Al Wataniya, Nama, Al Tawasul) – Deliver microloans, savings products, and financial literacy support tailored for MSMEs. (Sector: Microfinance)
Implementation location(s): Yemen – Nationwide coverage across 22 governorates and rural districts through local microfinance institutions and community partners.
Implementation timeline(s): Planned duration – 12 months from project start date.
Duration to pilot in a new geography: 12 months to pilot the solution in a new geography, including setup, training, deployment, and initial monitoring.
SDGs addressed: SDG 1 (No Poverty);SDG 8 (Decent Work and Economic Growth);SDG 11 (Sustainable Cities and Communities);
Desired impact:
Solution Objectives:

Equip MSMEs—especially women- and youth-led businesses—with the digital finance skills, tools, and platforms needed to access markets and financial services.

Increase the adoption of e-wallets and mobile money to improve financial inclusion and reduce cash dependency.

Strengthen MSMEs’ ability to compete in local, national, and international digital markets.

Foster sustainable, inclusive economic growth in underserved and rural areas of Yemen.

Key Achievements / Expected Impacts:

1,000+ MSMEs trained in digital financial literacy, e-commerce, and online market access within 12 months.

60% adoption rate of e-wallets among targeted MSMEs, enabling secure transactions and access to credit.

At least 40% women-owned businesses benefiting from training and digital market linkages.

Creation of 200+ new or improved jobs through enhanced business growth and market access.

Increased sales and revenue for participating MSMEs by an average of 20% within the first year.

Strengthened local economic resilience through diversified income sources and reduced barriers to market entry.
Key technologies:
Key Technologies Used:

Mobile Money & E-Wallet Platforms – Secure, user-friendly digital payment systems enabling MSMEs to transact, save, and access credit.

E-Learning Platform (Microfinance Academy) – An interactive online learning system delivering digital finance, e-commerce, and business skills training.

Data Analytics Dashboards – Real-time monitoring of MSME participation, digital tool adoption, and market engagement for improved decision-making.

Cloud-Based Collaboration Tools – Facilitate remote mentoring, peer-to-peer learning, and coordination between partners and beneficiaries.
Unique Characteristics:
Unique / Differentiated Characteristics:

Integrated Approach – Combines digital financial literacy, access to e-wallets, and digital market linkages in one comprehensive package for MSMEs.

Local-Global Partnership Model – Leverages strong grassroots networks in Yemen, partnerships with local MFIs and mobile money providers, and collaboration with international organizations for scaling.

Inclusive Design – Specifically targets women- and youth-led enterprises, with culturally adapted training materials and flexible delivery modes to overcome gender and geographic barriers.

Proven Digital Learning Platform – The Microfinance Academy, the first of its kind in the Arab world, enables scalable, low-cost, and continuous skill development.

Sustainability Focus – Embeds business mentoring and ongoing market access support to ensure long-term economic benefits beyond initial training.
Sustainable Change:
ustainable, Systemic Change Contribution:
Our solution addresses the root barriers preventing MSMEs from participating in the digital economy—limited skills, lack of access to digital finance, and weak market linkages. By integrating capacity building, digital tool adoption, and market access support, the initiative not only empowers individual businesses but also strengthens the broader economic ecosystem.

Theory of Change:

Inputs: Digital literacy training, access to e-wallets, market linkage facilitation, and mentoring.

Activities: Training MSMEs through the Microfinance Academy, onboarding them to secure digital payment platforms, connecting them to e-commerce and local/international markets, and providing ongoing technical support.

Outputs: Increased number of MSMEs with digital skills, active e-wallet accounts, and access to new markets.

Outcomes: Improved business revenues, job creation, and greater participation of women and youth in the digital economy.

Impact: A more inclusive, resilient, and sustainable economy where MSMEs are active digital market participants, reducing inequality and fostering long-term economic growth.

Follow-On Effects:

Greater adoption of digital finance and e-commerce at the community level.

Strengthened partnerships between financial institutions, technology providers, and MSMEs.

Policy momentum for inclusive digital infrastructure and SME support programs.

Future phases are expected to be supported through a blended funding model combining international donor contributions, private sector partnerships, and cost-sharing with local financial institutions.

Title: KayCare+ – Inclusive Digital Chronic Care for Underserved Communities
Subtitle: A low-cost, AI-assisted mobile and WhatsApp-based health platform integrating functional medicine, telehealth, and patient education to manage chronic diseases in underserved areas of Kenya
Problem Statement:
In Kenya, millions of people living in low- and middle-income communities face limited access to affordable, quality healthcare—particularly for chronic diseases such as diabetes, hypertension, and thyroid disorders. The shortage of specialists in rural areas forces patients to travel long distances, miss work, and incur high costs, while poor health literacy leads to late diagnosis and poor disease management.

The digital divide further excludes vulnerable groups, as most health innovations require high-cost smartphones, reliable internet, or urban proximity. Informal workers, women, and people in underserved regions are disproportionately affected, resulting in preventable complications, reduced productivity, and persistent poverty cycles.
Solution Overview:
Kay’s Wellness Centre offers an AI-enabled, WhatsApp-based integrative healthcare platform designed to bring chronic disease management, wellness education, and health monitoring directly to underserved communities in Kenya. The solution leverages low-cost, widely accessible digital channels to break geographical, financial, and literacy barriers in healthcare access.

How it Works

WhatsApp Health Assistant – A chatbot available in English and Kiswahili offers:

Symptom screening and guidance on when to seek in-person care.

Personalized lifestyle and nutrition recommendations based on functional medicine principles.

Reminders for medication, follow-up appointments, and wellness check-ins.

Hybrid Care Model – Users can book appointments for physical checkups at Kay’s Wellness Centre or via teleconsultations with doctors and specialists.

Dance for Health & Mobility Program – Weekly group and individual dance sessions at the centre promote physical activity for clients with chronic conditions such as hypertension, diabetes, arthritis, and obesity. This fun, culturally engaging approach improves mobility, cardiovascular health, mood, and adherence to healthy lifestyle changes.

Community-Based Wellness Hubs – Mobile clinics and partner spaces (e.g., fitness instructors, herbal product vendors) integrate physical mobility and nutrition services with chronic care.

Data-Driven Health Insights – Aggregated, anonymized data informs local health trends and policy advocacy.

Methodologies & Technologies Used

Low-Bandwidth AI Chatbot on WhatsApp for accessibility on basic smartphones.

Integrative & Functional Medicine Framework to address root causes of chronic diseases.

Cloud-Based Electronic Medical Records (EMR) for secure, seamless patient follow-up.

SMS & Voice Call Integration for clients without consistent internet access.

Dance Therapy Principles adapted for African community settings to improve compliance with exercise recommendations.

Partnerships & Collaboration Models

Local Partnerships – Collaboration with community health workers, fitness professionals, dance instructors, and herbal product suppliers to offer a holistic approach.

Digital Health Partners – Integration with open-source telemedicine platforms for specialist consultations.

Public Health Agencies & NGOs – Engagement to scale outreach and incorporate solution into broader health initiatives.

Private Sector – Partnerships with local pharmacies and wellness product vendors for subsidized pricing.

This inclusive model ensures no one is excluded from the digital health economy, empowering patients to take charge of their health while creating community-based jobs in wellness, dance therapy, and digital health support.
Solution Provider(s): Kay’s Wellness Centre – A Kenyan-based chronic care clinic and wellness hub specializing in integrative and functional medicine for the prevention and management of chronic diseases such as diabetes, hypertension, obesity, and autoimmune conditions. Title: ScribeIt – Focus-Powered Learning for Everyone
Subtitle: Smart tool that turns online lectures into summaries and quizzes, helping learners stay focused
Problem Statement: Millions of learners, especially people with ADHD, struggle to stay focused during online lectures, leading to knowledge gaps and reduced educational opportunities. This limits personal and professional growth, and deepens digital inequality.
Solution Overview:
ScribeIt is a browser extension designed to help learners fully engage with online lectures without losing focus.

How it works: When the lecture starts, the user activates the extension. It records and processes the lecture’s audio in real-time. After the lecture ends, the user receives an email with a link to a structured summary and an interactive quiz, plus scheduled reminders to review the material.

Methodologies & technologies: Speech-to-text transcription, Natural Language Processing (NLP) for summarization, AI-powered quiz generation, email automation.

Partnerships & collaboration: Open to collaboration with educational platforms, ADHD advocacy groups, and universities to adapt content for neurodiverse learners and underserved communities.

Title: Farm2Go
Subtitle: WFP's digital solution to support smallholder farmer programme activities. Farm2Go is linking farmers to markets while building skills and evidence for change.
Problem Statement:
Smallholder farmers produce roughly one-third of the world’s food and are the backbone of agriculture in most low- and middle-income countries. Yet, hundreds of millions remain in poverty because they lack access to fair, transparent, and reliable markets. Even when they can sell, they often have little bargaining power, face cultural biases (especially women farmers), and lack timely and accurate market information to negotiate better prices.

Digital agriculture tools could help, but most existing solutions:
- Are designed without a real understanding of smallholder farmers’ needs.
- Depend on costly devices, expensive data, and stable connectivity, barriers in rural areas.
- Fail to scale beyond pilots due to commercial models unsuited for underserved markets.

Farmers themselves often lack smartphones, or the digital literacy needed to use such tools. This excludes them from the benefits of digital agriculture unless intermediaries bridge the gap.

Farm2Go tackles these challenges by embedding an offline-capable, low-cost digital marketplace into WFP’s smallholder farmer programmes. It connects cooperatives with trusted buyers, such as schools, and sends farmers SMS updates on their produce sales, building trust and transparency. It also delivers capacity-strengthening content to Aggregators, enabling them to train farmers on market practices, post-harvest handling, and climate-smart techniques, even when farmers cannot access the app themselves.

Crucially, Farm2Go addresses another gap: the lack of reliable data. The platform collects information on production, sales, and market engagement over time, creating access to reports for WFP and partners. This allows for better decision-making, more targeted support, and the ability to measure how training and capacity building translate into improved farmer outcomes, such as higher yields, increased sales, and stronger market linkages.

Beyond immediate benefits, Farm2Go establishes the foundation for sustainable digital agriculture systems in a country. By working with governments during implementation, it helps them understand the infrastructure, resources, and skills needed to set up, manage, and scale such solutions, ensuring that when WFP steps back, there is a strong national framework to continue supporting farmers digitally.
Solution Overview:
1. How the Solution Works
Farm2Go is a mobile and web-based platform designed to connect smallholder farmers to reliable markets while building their capacity to improve production and sales.

Aggregator Role – Local farmer cooperatives use the Farm2Go mobile app (Android, offline-capable) to:
- Register farmers and their produce.
- Record stock at aggregation centres.
- Receive and respond to offers from buyers.
- Share training and best-practice information with farmers.

Smallholder Farmer – Many farmers, often lacking smartphones or digital skills, get SMS alerts when their aggregator updates stock, offers, or completes sales. This creates transparency, trust, and inclusion without direct app access.

Buyer Role – Traders, schools, and institutional buyers utilise the Farm2Go web platform to:
- Browse available produce from aggregators within an e-commerce-style interface.
- Submit offers and negotiate terms such as quantity, price, delivery location, and timing.

WFP and Partners Role - Access their Farm2Go web portal to:
- Configure the platform for their country context
- Manage access for Aggregators and Buyers
- Monitor adoption
- Create and publish capacity-building content for Aggregators on market information, climate-smart agriculture, and post-harvest loss reduction. These materials will enable them to train farmers during meetings or field visits, ensuring that knowledge reaches even those without smart devices.
- Access dashboards and specific reports on Tableau to inform decision-making and evaluate the impact of training on farmer performance.

---
2. Methodologies and Technologies Used
* Programme-Embedded Approach – Farm2Go is not a standalone app; it is embedded into WFP smallholder farmer support activities such as market linkage, homegrown school feeding, and climate resilience programmes. This ensures alignment with local context and long-term adoption.

* User-Centric Development – The solution, launched in 2022, was refined through multiple iterations based on feedback from aggregators, buyers, and WFP country teams. Pilot learnings guided modifications to better support fresh produce markets, operate effectively in low-connectivity environments, and enhance ease of use for first-time smartphone users.

* Offline-First Technology – Built using React Native (mobile) and Django/Python (backend), Farm2Go works offline and syncs data when connectivity is available.
* Low Data Requirements – Optimised for entry-level Android devices and minimal monthly data usage (~1GB/month).
* Localisation – Integrated with Transifex for multi-language support, enabling quick translation into local languages.
* Privacy By Design – Uses WFP's standards for managing personal identifiable information, ensuring data security best-practices are followed. 

---
3. Partnerships and Collaboration Models
* Internal WFP Collaboration
- Smallholder Farmer Support Unit – Strategic guidance and integration into WFP agricultural market support.
- Homegrown School Feeding Team – Schools act as institutional buyers on Farm2Go, creating guaranteed local demand.
- Climate & Resilience Team – Integrates climate-smart content into the InfoHub.
- Gender Unit – Advises on strategies to ensure women farmers benefit equally.
* External Partnerships
- Government Ministries of Agriculture – Engaged early to align with national digital agriculture strategies and secure early endorsement and buy-in for sustainability.
Solution Provider(s): This is an internally developed solution. WFP pays external technical vendors to develop and maintain the solution. It is hosted on AWS where we have an agreement for favourable rates.
Implementation location(s): Bangladesh, Rwanda, Mozambique, Philippines, Somalia, Uganda, Cuba, Nicaragua, Guinea, Haiti, Malawi, Zimbabwe, Sudan
Implementation timeline(s): We started in 2022 in Mozambique, Bangladesh and Rwanda. Since then we've introduced Farm2Go to 10 new countries.
Duration to pilot in a new geography: A 6-month pilot will ensure that it overlaps with a harvest season and give the Aggregators an opportunity to sell some produce to potential buyers.
SDGs addressed: SDG 2 (Zero Hunger);SDG 5 (Gender Equality);SDG 1 (No Poverty);
Desired impact:
Farm2Go aims to:
1. Increase market access for smallholder farmers by connecting them with reliable buyers, including schools and institutional markets, to secure fair and transparent trade.
2. Enhance trust and transparency in transactions through SMS notifications and digital records—ensuring farmers know what is sold, at what price, and to whom.
3. Strengthen capacity of aggregators and farmers by delivering market, post-harvest, and climate-smart agriculture content through the InfoHub, enabling knowledge transfer even to farmers without smartphones.
4. Generate reliable, real-time market data to support WFP, government, and partner decision-making, while monitoring long-term improvements in yields, sales, and market access.
5. Promote gender equity by reducing cultural barriers, allowing women to participate in markets anonymously and on equal terms.
6. Build sustainable national digital agriculture systems by working alongside governments to develop the skills, infrastructure, and processes required to manage such platforms beyond WFP’s direct involvement.
---
Key Achievements and Impacts (as of August 2025)
Global reach:
- 471 registered aggregators and 45,035 farmers onboarded across 10 countries.
- 6,294,230 kg of produce recorded, valued at USD 11,766,967.
- 9,222 stock collections and 3,542 offers received from buyers.
- 1,253 exchanges completed, generating USD 491,848 in payments to aggregators and USD 689,045 in payments to farmers.

Recognition:
- Selected by the UN Global Pulse Scale Accelerator as a UN innovation with the potential to scale.
- Highlighted by CGIAR at the ICTforAg Conference as a top-five solution for increasing women’s participation in digital agriculture.
- Featured in a BBC podcast showcasing how Farm2Go empowers women farmers in Bangladesh to bypass gender bias in traditional markets, earning up to 10% more for their products through the digital marketplace.
Key technologies: Farm2Go is built using React Native for the mobile app and Django (Python) for the backend, both WFP-endorsed technology stacks. It is offline-capable, optimised for entry-level Android devices, and hosted securely on AWS with PostgreSQL for data storage. The platform uses WFP’s Customer Identity and Access Management (CIAM) for secure logins, integrates with Transifex for multilingual support, and connects to WFP’s Tableau and DOTS dashboards for real-time reporting. Farm2Go is designed to integrate with other solutions via APIs, enabling interoperability with government, partner, and private sector systems.
Unique Characteristics: Farm2Go is unique because it is embedded in WFP’s programmes rather than operating as a standalone app, ensuring implementation ownership and adoption in real market systems. It bridges the digital divide by allowing farmers without smartphones to participate through SMS updates, while aggregators use the offline-capable mobile app to manage transactions. The built-in InfoHub delivers market, post-harvest, and climate-smart agriculture content so aggregators can train farmers directly, combining digital market linkage with on-the-ground capacity building. Designed for rural realities, Farm2Go works fully offline, supports multiple languages via Transifex, and integrates with WFP’s data systems for real-time decision-making. It is built to interoperate with other platforms via APIs, making it adaptable to national systems, and operates under a sustainable cost-sharing model with early government engagement to prepare for long-term ownership.
Sustainable Change:
Farm2Go creates sustainable, systemic change by embedding a digital marketplace and training tool directly into WFP’s smallholder farmer programmes, ensuring that technology is introduced alongside market access support, capacity building, and policy engagement. By connecting cooperatives to reliable buyers and delivering tailored training content through the InfoHub, it strengthens farmer organisations’ ability to access better markets, negotiate fair prices, and improve product quality—without requiring farmers themselves to own smartphones. The platform also generates reliable, real-time market data that enables governments, partners, and WFP to make evidence-based decisions and track progress over time.

Theory of Change:
1. Inputs: Farm2Go platform, training for aggregators, integration with WFP programmes, and early government engagement.
2. Activities: Aggregators register farmers and produce, facilitate sales with buyers, and deliver training on market, post-harvest, and climate-smart practices; data is collected and shared via dashboards.
3. Outputs: Increased transparency in transactions, improved farmer skills, access to new markets, and a growing dataset on production and sales trends.
4. Outcomes: Higher sales volumes and prices for farmers, reduced market discrimination (especially for women), and stronger farmer organisations able to operate independently.
5. Impact: Sustainable national digital agriculture systems, with governments equipped to manage or integrate Farm2Go (or other interoperable solutions) into their own strategies - leading to lasting improvements in farmer livelihoods and food system resilience.
The desired follow-on effect is that, once WFP steps back, governments and partners will have both the digital infrastructure and the local capacity to sustain and expand the solution, enabling it to benefit future generations of farmers without ongoing external management.
Funding Sources:
Farm2Go has been funded through a combination of internal WFP resources, donor contributions, and innovation grants, ensuring both initial deployment and ongoing maintenance across multiple countries.
WFP Country Office Programme Budgets – Many implementations are financed through country-level programme funds, particularly from Smallholder Agricultural Market Support (SAMS), Homegrown School Feeding, and Climate Resilience activities. Each Country Office using Farm2Go contributes USD 30,000 annually to cover hosting, security, maintenance, technical support, and continuous improvement.
Donor-Funded Projects – Specific deployments have been supported by targeted donor funding, for example:
African Development Bank (AfDB) – Provided funding for the Sudan implementation to ensure Farm2Go is deployed so 600 aggregators can register 200,000 farmers.
Mastercard Foundation – Funded the development of the Youth in Work module in Mozambique.
Swiss Agency for Development and Cooperation – Supported traceability feature development in Bangladesh.
Japanese Government – Funded adoption activities in the Philippines.
European Union – Co-funded digital market linkage activities in Bangladesh.
Innovation Grants –
UN Global Pulse – Awarded a grant for Farm2Go after winning the Scale Accelerator strategy, recognising its potential as a scalable WFP corporate solution.
WFP Innovation Accelerator – Provided early-stage development and scale-up funding, including resources from the John Deere Foundation for piloting in Latin America and the Caribbean.
Testimonials and Endorsements:

After negotiation, when the price was finalised, we sent the produces to them. We got two or three taka more profit by selling our produces here than in the market. Title: FlexPaie
Subtitle: M-commerce/e-commerce platform for unbanked merchants integrated with digital payment system for instant payment, combining prepaid card, mobile money and traditional bank account for cash-in/cash-out
Problem Statement:
1-	Market access barriers: Farmers crop often spoil at the source because producers lack access to sales markets, and potential buyers are unaware of their existence. This reflects a critical gap in marker linkages (purchase channel) and communication.
2-	Weak business structures: Access to credit is limited as most small and medium businesses operate informally, with no accounting systems, no bank account, no transaction traceability, and little visibility into operations, required by credit institutions.
3-	Capital flow constraints: Circulation of capital is severely hindered by reliance on cash transactions. Cash handling logistics are particularly challenging in areas without roads or banking infrastructure especially when compounded by political instability.
Solution Overview:
1.	Merchant KYC (know Your Customer) using face-id and contactless fingerprint for biometric identification 
2.	Issuance of prepaid card used as merchant wallet integrated to biometric data (partnership with Visa, local Bank for BIN sponsorship and Thales)
3.	Merchants Marketplace integrated with marketing tools using social media, available in web and mobile version: showing products grouped by merchant, availability, location, price, include a dedicated dashboard per merchant … (google maps showing products location)
4.	Some merchants are equipped with Android devices to manage their commerce activity, from order to payment using Mobile money or Tap to pay 
5.	Consumer M-commerce Mobile application app allowing buyers to access products available on marketplace using multiple type of payment: bank cards, mobile-money, QR-code and USSD for basic phone
6.	Delivery system integrated to marketplace app using motorcycle for small packages, car and truck for big package and delivery drone for inaccessible area 
7.	cross-border digital money movement and Bulk payment for employees payroll

Partnerships and collaboration models
-	Tech5: Digital ID supplier
-	Thales: Card supplier
-	Visa Inc.: Strategic partner
-	MobiIoT: Android devices supplier
-	Mobile money operators (Mpesa, Orange Money, Airtel Money, afrimoney): Payment aggregator partnership
-	Ecobank, Access Bank: BIN sponsor partnership
Solution Provider(s): Visa Inc. :  Global payment network (https://usa.visa.com), Vodacash: Mpesa mobile money operator, Airtel Money: mobile money operator, Orange Money: mobile money operator, Afrimoney: mobile money operator
Duration to pilot in a new geography: 6 – 9 months
SDGs addressed: SDG 1 (No Poverty);SDG 8 (Decent Work and Economic Growth);SDG 10 (Reduced Inequalities);
Desired impact:
1- Solution Objectives
•	Enhance financial inclusion by providing unbanked rural populations with a secure and accessible digital commerce platform.
•	Facilitate market access for smallholder producers and micro-entrepreneurs by enabling direct, cashless transactions with buyers and suppliers.
•	Improve access to credit by creating digital transaction records that serve as a basis for credit scoring and formal financial engagement.
•	Reduce economic inefficiencies linked to cash handling, such as high transport costs, theft risk, and transaction delays.
•	Promote gender equity by ensuring that women, who are disproportionately excluded from formal finance, have equal access to the platform.

2- Key Achievements Aimed 
•	Platform deployment: Rolled out in different rural communities (ex. Those working with UNDP – WFP) across DRC.
•	User base growth: 1.200,000 users per year, of which at least 30% are women.
•	Transaction volume: Facilitated digital transactions, equivalent to USD 100 million in value.
•	Market linkages: Connected producers directly with buyers, reducing post-harvest losses initially by an estimated 18%.
•	Credit facilitation: Enabled microloans through partner financial institutions using digital transaction histories as a basis for eligibility.

3. Impacts
•	Economic empowerment: Users report increase in monthly business revenue due to expanded market access and faster payment cycles.
•	Operational efficiency: Reduced cash-related transport costs for traders in target areas without banking infrastructure.
•	Financial resilience: users have started saving regularly through mobile wallet features, providing a buffer against income shocks.
•	Women’s inclusion: Women-led enterprises using the platform report greater control over income and improved household decision-making power.
•	Community-level change: Local economies are becoming more interconnected and structured, improving prospects for future investment and development.
Key technologies: Cloud for hosting applications, digital identity for KYC and compliance (AML/CTF), digital payment, delivery drone, digital transformation
Unique Characteristics: End to End digital commerce for unbaked and rural communities integrating local and international interoperable payment channels (bank cards, mobile money, QR-code, USSD) and logistic options depending on location (moto, drone …)
Sustainable Change:
Contribution to Sustainable, Systematic Change
The digital commerce platform addresses structural barriers that keep rural, unbanked populations excluded from economic opportunity. By creating a secure, accessible, and traceable transaction system, it sets in motion a cycle of financial inclusion, market integration, and local economic growth.

Pathway of Change
1- Immediate Outputs
•	Unbanked individuals gain access to a simple, low-cost digital commerce tool.
•	Transactions shift from cash-based to digital, reducing theft risk and logistical costs.
•	Buyers and sellers can connect directly, regardless of geographic distance.

2- Intermediate Outcomes (6–24 months)
•	Digital transaction records create financial identities, enabling access to credit and other financial services.
•	Market linkages expand, increasing sales opportunities and reducing post-harvest losses.
•	Local businesses become more organized, with better visibility and traceability of operations.
•	Women and marginalized groups participate more actively in the economy.

3- Long-Term Impact (2–5 years)
•	Sustainable livelihoods: Increased and more stable household incomes.
•	Economic resilience: Communities less vulnerable to shocks due to savings, credit, and diversified markets.
•	Formalization of the informal economy: More structured trade, enabling taxation, investment, and public service delivery.
•	Digital ecosystem growth: Emergence of complementary services (insurance, remittances, e-commerce) built on the payment platform.

Desired Follow-on Effects
•	Replication & scaling: The model expands to other rural regions and sectors (agriculture, crafts, services).
•	Financial sector transformation: Financial institutions adapt their services to include rural, low-income clients.
•	Policy impact: Governments adopt digital financial inclusion as a strategic pillar for rural development.
•	Social cohesion: Stronger community networks as trade and cooperation increase within and between villages.

Title: ECOBOX INNOV
Subtitle: EcoBox Innov conçoit des boxes connectées et mobiles pour stocker et conserver les produits horticoles et le lait, réduisant ainsi les pertes post-récolte.
Problem Statement: Chaque année, environ 37 % de la production agricole en Afrique est perdue après la récolte, représentant une perte économique estimée à environ 48 milliards de dollars américains, selon l'Organisation des Nations Unies pour l'alimentation et l'agriculture (FAO). Les producteurs horticoles et laitiers manquent de solutions de stockage adaptées et de gestion à distance, limitant la conservation des produits et la sécurité alimentaire.
Solution Overview:
Description détaillée du fonctionnement :
EcoBox Innov développe des boxes connectées et mobiles, alimentées par panneaux solaires, pour stocker et conserver les produits horticoles et le lait. Ces boxes permettent de réduire considérablement les pertes post-récolte grâce à un contrôle automatisé de la température et de l’humidité, garantissant des conditions optimales pour chaque produit.

Chaque box est reliée à une application mobile intuitive qui facilite la gestion à distance : les producteurs peuvent suivre leurs stocks en temps réel, recevoir des alertes sur l’état des produits, planifier les collectes et les approvisionnements, et même accéder à un marché en ligne pour vendre leurs produits. L’application intègre également des modules de productivité et d’organisation économique, permettant aux utilisateurs d’optimiser la gestion de leur production et de leurs ventes.

Grâce à cette connexion intelligente, les boxes peuvent être activées, contrôlées et surveillées à distance, offrant une solution durable, pratique et autonome. EcoBox Innov combine ainsi innovation technologique, énergie renouvelable et inclusion économique, contribuant à réduire les pertes agricoles et à renforcer la sécurité alimentaire en Afrique.
Solution Provider(s): Enda Énergie : Organisation non gouvernementale sénégalaise membre du réseau Enda Tiers Monde, spécialisée dans les solutions énergétiques durables et l’accompagnement des populations vers l’autonomie énergétique ;  Heifer International : ONG internationale œuvrant pour l’autosuffisance alimentaire et la sécurité économique des communautés rurales, notamment en Afrique de l’Ouest, en fournissant des formations agricoles et en facilitant l’accès aux marchés;  Réseau Billital Maroobé (RBM) : Organisation régionale ouest-africaine regroupant des éleveurs et pasteurs, œuvrant pour la défense de leurs intérêts économiques, politiques, sociaux et culturels. Le RBM milite pour la sécurisation de l’économie pastorale, l’intégration des éleveurs dans les processus politiques et la gestion durable des ressources naturelles.
Implementation timeline(s): Test pilote en cours depuis août 2025
Duration to pilot in a new geography: La mise en œuvre d’un pilote de notre solution dans une nouvelle zone géographique est estimée à 3 à 6 mois, incluant l’installation du box, la formation des utilisateurs et le suivi des résultats.
SDGs addressed: SDG 2 (Zero Hunger);SDG 7 (Affordable and Clean Energy);SDG 9 (Industry, Innovation, and Infrastructure);
Desired impact:
Réduire les pertes post-récolte des produits horticoles et du lait.	

 -Améliorer la sécurité alimentaire des communautés locales.

-Faciliter la gestion, la collecte, l'approvisionnement et la commercialisation des produits via une application mobile.

-Promouvoir l'utilisation d'une énergie.
Key technologies: IoT (Internet des objets),IA, Analytique de données.
Unique Characteristics: ECOBOX INNOV se distingue par ses boîtes mobiles et connectées, alimentées par des panneaux solaires, qui permettent de conserver et de transporter les produits horticoles et le lait. L'application mobile intégrée à l'IA facilite la gestion, la collecte, l'approvisionnement et la commercialisation, tandis que l'analyse des données optimise les opérations. Le marché en ligne et les partenariats stratégiques renforcent l'inclusion économique et la viabilité de la solution.
Sustainable Change: ECOBOX INNOV crée un changement systémique durable en réduisant le gaspillage alimentaire, en améliorant la sécurité alimentaire et les revenus des producteurs, et en renforçant la résilience et l'efficacité des chaînes d'approvisionnement locales.
Funding Sources: La solution ECO BOX INNOV a été financée grâce à des contributions des ONG partenaires telles que Enda Énergie, Heifer International et RBM, ainsi qu'à la participation financière directe des quatre membres de l'équipe. Ce modèle combinant un soutien externe et un investissement interne a permis de développer le prototype et de tester la solution à petite échelle.
Testimonials and Endorsements: https://www.linkedin.com/posts/sokhna-badem-diakhate-a5227a49_agriculturedurable-innovation-pnud-activity-7359634236582027264-SKZQ?utm_source=share&utm_medium=member_ios&rcm=ACoAAD677r0BKEhiZ-Jo8CVf4vw7oKOgtTydIjI
Further comments/feedback: Nous remercions l’équipe pour ce questionnaire clair et structuré.
Primary thematic focus area: Stable and Resilient Digital Supply Chains
Summary: EcoBox Innov develops mobile, solar-powered, connected storage units for horticultural products and milk to reduce post-harvest losses in Africa. These smart boxes integrate IoT and AI to control temperature and humidity, ensuring optimal preservation. Linked to a mobile app, the solution enables producers to monitor stocks in real time, receive alerts, plan logistics, and access online marketplaces. Strategic partnerships with NGOs and farmer networks support adoption, while the solution contributes to food security, supply chain resilience, and sustainable agricultural practices.

Title: adgboinsure
Subtitle: Our technology brings entire communities together into digital health insurance ecosystems centered around Primary Health Centres. With unified enrollment, payment, and benefit management, we ensure equitable access to care at the grassroots level.
Problem Statement:
Nigeria's health care system is not the most efficient or reliable. Its people suffer from high out-of-pocket healthcare expenses
because of low health insurance adoption (less than 8%), dissatisfaction with existing health schemes from those who are
insured, deteriorating medical facilities, Healthcare workers' strikes and brain drain because of low salaries and low budget
allocation from the government, lack of awareness and trust in health insurance schemes and much more.
Solution Overview: We aim to revolutionize healthcare access in Nigeria through Community Health Insurance, ensuring every community member gets quality healthcare starting from the grassroots to the top. We aim to provide affordable, accessible, and comprehensive health insurance to Nigerian communities, leveraging technology, state health insurance agencies and local POS agents. Our solution starts off with a quick and simple registration e-form that POS agents or customers use to register to their community health insurance(CHI). POS agents, well-known in Nigeria as everyday financial service providers and are usually vendors that are on every street in the country. They offer a high-potential but underutilized channel for health insurance outreach. They have become integral to daily transactions since the 2023 cash scarcity which manifested as chronic ATM failures with their presence revolutionizing access to cash and financial services.
Solution Provider(s): Oyo State Health Insurance Agency (OYSHIA) – A subnational government agency responsible for implementing health insurance schemes across Oyo State. OYSHIA provides regulatory backing, technical support, and alignment with state healthcare financing policies. Oyo State Primary Health Care Board (OSPHCB) – State-level public health authority responsible for PHC management, providing access to PHCs for piloting and ensuring alignment with state PHC systems.
Duration to pilot in a new geography: 3 months
SDGs addressed: SDG 3 (Good Health and Well-being);SDG 11 (Sustainable Cities and Communities);SDG 17 (Partnerships for the Goals);
Desired impact:
Increase enrollment and retention in the Oyo State Community Health Insurance (CHI) scheme through digital tools and trained local agents.

Strengthen the capacity of PHCs by integrating affordable, community-driven health financing mechanisms.

Improve health access equity by reducing out-of-pocket health expenditures for vulnerable households in both urban and peri-urban communities.

Enhance community participation and awareness through structured engagement with Ward Development Committees (WDCs), community leaders, and media outreach.

Key Achievements / Expected Impacts

Enrollment Impact: Target of 500–1,000 new CHI enrollees within 3 months in Apete and Aba Emu PHCs.

System Strengthening: Introduction of a digital enrollment platform localized for PHC usage, reducing manual bottlenecks in data collection, reporting, and payments.

Affordability & Equity: Families enrolled at ₦15,000 ($16) per household annually, significantly reducing catastrophic out-of-pocket health spending.

Community Engagement: Establishment of structured partnerships with Ward Development Committees, improving accountability and sustainability of the CHI scheme.
Key technologies:
Mobile & Web-based Platform: For registration, premium collection, and benefit tracking by enrollees and agents.

POS-integration: Allowing agents to collect premiums digitally,  and allowing enrollees to make follow up payment anywhere in the country easily.

Call Center & WhatsApp Engagement with agents: For real-time customer support, enrollment reminders, and community feedback.

Backend Data Integration: Ensuring alignment with Oyo State Health Insurance Agency (OYSHIA) systems for reporting and monitoring.
Unique Characteristics:
Localized Digital Model: Unlike generic health insurance systems, AdugboInsure is customized for PHCs, integrating digital enrollment directly into primary healthcare operations.

Agent Network + Technology: Blends human-centered community agents with digital platforms, ensuring access for populations with limited digital literacy.

Flexible Financing Mechanism: Annual household premiums collected through micro-payment options via POS and mobile money, removing cost barriers.

Public-Private Partnership Approach: Built in collaboration with OYSHIA and PHC Boards, ensuring policy alignment and systemic adoption potential across all PHCs in Oyo State.
Sustainable Change:
Problem: Low enrollment in community health insurance due to lack of awareness, high out-of-pocket costs, and limited digital tools for PHCs.

Inputs (Solution Deployment):

Digital platform for enrollment and payment.

Trained community agents, call/WhatsApp support.

Awareness campaigns and WDC/community engagement.

Partnership with OYSHIA and PHC Board for policy alignment.

Outputs (Immediate Effects):

Increased awareness of CHI in target communities.

Simplified, transparent enrollment and payment processes.

Improved data for PHCs and OYSHIA on uptake and utilization.

Outcomes (Medium-Term Effects):

Significant growth in CHI enrollment and retention.

Reduced out-of-pocket expenditure for low-income households.

Strengthened PHC capacity and trust through digitalized processes.

Impact (Long-Term Systemic Change):

Sustainable financing model for PHCs across Oyo State.

Expansion of community-based health insurance beyond pilot communities.

Progress toward Universal Health Coverage (UHC) in Nigeria by building trust in government-led health insurance schemes.
Funding Sources:
project is currently funded through bootstrapping and done R&D into the
digital solution with in 2 projects in university college hospital Ibadan (UCH): Psychosis in Ancestrally Diverse Settings (PADS) and International Research Programme on Psychosis in Diverse Setting (INTREPID) studies.
Testimonials and Endorsements: none
Further comments/feedback: none
Primary thematic focus area: Enabling Policies & Regulatory Innovation
Summary: AdgboInsure is a community-driven digital health insurance ecosystem for Nigeria, designed around Primary Health Centres (PHCs). It integrates digital enrollment, premium collection via POS agents, benefit tracking, and call/WhatsApp-based support. By leveraging trusted community POS agents and aligning with state health insurance agencies, it expands coverage, reduces out-of-pocket spending, and strengthens PHC systems. The pilot focuses on Oyo State, targeting rapid enrollment growth, affordability (₦15,000 per household annually), and improved accountability through structured community engagement.

Title: Yiiya Bots:- AI-mpowering Youth in  Rural communities through Indigenous wire technology.
Subtitle: Bridging the Digital Divide with Affordable, Scalable AI Education
Problem Statement: In many rural communities, children lack access to affordable STEM resources and modern technology, limiting their ability to develop critical skills for the digital age. High costs of imported robotics kits and limited digital infrastructure widen the educational gap, leaving underserved youth behind. Despite this, indigenous technologies such as wire crafting remain widely accessible and culturally relevant but are rarely integrated into modern learning. Without innovative, low-cost, and locally adaptable solutions, rural youth risk exclusion from opportunities in AI and future-oriented careers.
Solution Overview:
Yiiya Bots, delivers an innovative, affordable, and culturally relevant solution to bridge this digital and AI divide. The Yiiya robotics kits repurpose indigenous Ugandan wire car technology, crafted from wires, nuts and bottle caps that has been used by kids in rural areas to make toy cars. We have integrated AI-powered Arduino chips and mechatronics (motors, connectors), enabling onboard machine learning for applications like voice recognition and gesture control. 
A block-based mobile coding app and web app, inspired by Scratch, allows students to program AI applications with just a smartphone, using offline functionality and voice control for accessibility. 
Our solution’s utilisation of mobile technologies and indigenous wire technology which is culturally relevant fosters easy uptake and thus will enable us to achieve our mission of to equipping 1,000,000  rural youth (ages 8 -18 years) in Uganda, Tanzania, Kenya, South Sudan and Burundi with future-proof AI skills over 3 years, contributing to the Global Digital Compact’s goal of inclusive digital transformation.
Solution Provider(s): University of Michigan: Provides technical expertise for Arduino Nano AI integration and kit design optimization.,NGOs and Religious Entities: All Saints Church and local NGOs (e.g., Assure Uganda) for community outreach and workshop hosting, leveraging trust in rural areas.
Duration to pilot in a new geography: 1 year
SDGs addressed: SDG 9 (Industry, Innovation, and Infrastructure);
Desired impact:
Skilling the Youth to participate in the AI Digital Economy. The funding will enable us to offer subsidized courses and kits, conduct free AI camps and award prize kits to outstanding students. 
The skills include AI literacy, STEM and Robotics with special camps for girls who are usually left out on these skills.

Economic Empowerment - The Social Shifters prize will enable us to reach the youth and equip them to gain skills and prepare them for future employment in various sectors in STEM and AI. At later stages of the project, we plan to set up regional assembly workshop hubs which will enable vulnerable students especially girls to earn an income directly from collecting plastic waste and packaging the kits.

Plastic Pollution reduction: Our project encourages students to reuse waste like bottle caps, and other locally available materials to design their solutions. The funding will enable us to scale to different areas hence the pollution pressure will be reduced by the student’s creations.

It also promotes cultural ingenuity by encouraging the use of locally available materials like steel gauge wires and plastic wires to create socially impactful solutions.
Key technologies: Websites, AI, IoT, Robotics/Drones
Unique Characteristics:
Low cost AI-Powered Robotics: Yiiya Bots leverages the Arduino Nano’s BLE 33 Sense onboard AI for real-time applications like voice recognition and gesture-based control. This is combined with locally sourced materials like bottle caps and local steel wires which enable students to build sophisticated projects at a low cost, such as AI-driven robots, while other robotics kits like LEGO Mindstorms which are more expensive. 

AI Web & mobile app Based Coding: Our solution includes an AI text code generator that enables students to generate blocks enabling them to easily learn understand programming concepts, use sensors etc.

Inclusivity Focus: Tailored for marginalized communities, Yiiya Bots targets students at last miles who are usually not targeted by STEM programs. We work directly with rural schools, churches and local organisations while most STEM programs focus on international schools and urban areas where parents can afford expensive kits.
Sustainable Change:
1.Economic Sustainability (Affordable & Scalable Tools)

The use of indigenous wire technology (wires, nuts, bottle caps) ensures kits are cheap, repairable, and scalable within local communities.

By avoiding reliance on expensive imported robotics kits, the solution becomes financially sustainable and accessible to low-income families and schools.

2. Cultural Sustainability (Rooted in Indigenous Knowledge)

Builds on Uganda’s wire car tradition, turning a familiar, culturally relevant practice into a modern AI learning tool.

This ensures communities embrace the technology instead of seeing it as foreign or imposed.

Protects and upgrades indigenous knowledge for the 21st century.

3. Educational Sustainability (Integration into Systems)

Kits are embedded into school clubs and classrooms, not just distributed — ensuring institutional adoption.

Teachers are empowered with hands-on teaching methods, building local capacity to sustain STEM learning.

The offline-first app reduces dependence on fragile internet infrastructure, making learning continuous and resilient.

4. Community Empowerment (Systemic Reach)

Workshops and hackathons with NGOs and local centers foster community ownership of the program.

Students not only learn but create prototypes that address real community needs — embedding AI into local problem-solving.

Encourages peer-to-peer learning and intergenerational knowledge sharing.

5. Systemic Outcomes (Long-Term Change)

Over time, rural children gain 21st-century skills, enabling them to compete in the digital economy.

A pipeline of indigenous innovators and tech leaders is created, shifting Uganda from being a technology consumer to a creator.

The model is replicable across Africa, contributing to systemic change in education by combining indigenous practices + AI.
Funding Sources:
We received seed funding of $1000 from Michigan University to help us pilot the Yiiya bots kits.

These Funds have enabled us to carry out some AI outreaches in schools which have been featured on national television. 

 We have also used the funds to purchase AI powered chips to use in our free AI camps. 
The funds have also enabled us to improve features of the mobile and web apps.
Further comments/feedback: The questionnaire was easy to answer because the questions were straight
Primary thematic focus area: Inclusive Digital Innovation Skills & Entrepreneurial Talent Development
Summary: Yiiya Bots is an AI-powered, low-cost robotics and STEM education initiative leveraging indigenous Ugandan wire toy-car technology. By combining locally available materials (wires, bottle caps, nuts) with Arduino Nano BLE 33 Sense AI chips, students in rural areas can build affordable robots with machine learning features such as voice recognition and gesture control. The solution integrates with a block-based mobile/web coding app (offline-capable), enabling programming without expensive equipment. Already piloted with seed funding and school outreach, Yiiya Bots aims to reach 1,000,000 rural youth across East Africa, promoting AI literacy, economic empowerment, and sustainability by reusing waste materials. It fosters cultural relevance, accessibility, and systemic educational change, transforming indigenous play into future-proof digital skills.

Title: Code for Change: JavaScript Training for Empowerment of Out-of-School Youth in Molepolole
Subtitle: Botswana has made significant progress in education, but youth unemployment remains high, especially among out-of-school youth. In Molepolole, a large village in the Kweneng District, many young people have dropped out of school or completed secondary school without transitioning to tertiary education or employment. This group remains particularly vulnerable to poverty, substance abuse, and lack of direction.  The digital economy presents an opportunity. JavaScript, a core web development language, is in high demand globally. Providing coding education offers out-of-school youth a pathway to digital entrepreneurship, freelancing, and remote employment. Moreover, equipping them with tech skills helps address local problems through digital solutions.
Problem Statement:
A high number of out-of-school youths in Molepolole are unemployed and lack practical, marketable digital skills. Many are disconnected from opportunities in the digital economy due to barriers such as lack of training centers, financial resources, and mentorship. This leads to increased poverty, social vulnerability, and loss of potential human capital.
There is a growing population of out-of-school youth in Molepolole who lack skills, direction, and opportunity. They are disproportionately affected by:

High unemployment
Limited access to further education or training
Lack of marketable, in-demand digital skills
Limited engagement in problem-solving in their communities
These issues have led to a rise in social ills including substance abuse, crime, and youth disengagement from national development efforts.
Solution Overview:
Project Goal: To equip 100 out-of-school youth in Molepolole with JavaScript coding skills, enabling them to develop community-focused web applications and digital solutions while improving their employability, entrepreneurial capacity, and digital literacy.

Project Objective- To empower out-of-school youth in Molepolole by providing them with practical JavaScript coding skills, entrepreneurship training, and a platform to develop digital solutions for community challenges.
This program addresses:

-Youth unemployment by building coding skills aligned with the global digital economy.
-Community problems through tech-based solutions (e.g., reporting apps, education platforms).
-Digital inclusion by bringing tech to underserved populations.
