Title: Luma: Empowering Inclusion Through Youth-led Digital Finance in South Sudan
Subtitle: Luma is a youth-led fintech startup from South Sudan that promotes inclusive digital financial services for underserved and unbanked communities.
Problem Statement: In South Sudan, a majority of youths and marginalized communities lack access to formal financial services due to limited infrastructure, low digital literacy, and economic exclusion. This hinders entrepreneurship saving and economic participation especially in remote and post-conflict areas.
Solution Overview:
Solution overview Luma a digital financial bridge for the landlocked youth: 
Luma is a youth led digital fintech solution from South Sudan South Sudan addressing the structural exclusion of youth and marginalized groups from the formal economy in one of the world’s most vulnerable landlocked developing countries LLDCs. In a context where financial infrastructure is minimal connectivity is poor and traditional banking systems fails to reach remote and conflict affected populations luma provide a local design inclusive mobile first platform for savings credit and digital payments. How the solution works
1. Accessible registration youth and informal workers register via mobile USSD/app or through local youth agent trained by luma 
2. Community savings and loans users join digital savings groups contribute regularly and access rotating credit agent with fair community based terms. 
3. Mobile wallet integration Luma integrates with existing mobile platform for seamless deposits withdrawal and transfers eliminating the need for traditional bank accounts. 
4. Local language and literacy support built in financial literacy modules supported low literacy users in local languages enhancing both financial and digital skills.
5. Decentralized credit scoping behavior based trusts driven credit scoping allow financial invisible users to access micro loans. 
Methodologies and Technologies 
Human centered design co-created with rural youth and women.
Mobile first architecture with USSD and android compatibility 
Open source backend PHP MySQL cloud based analytics and API integration.
Offline functionality for last mile service delivery. 
Partnership and collaboration models
Rebuild Initiative Youth Association coordinates grassroots mobilization digital training and youth engagement.
Telecom operators and mobile money providers enable USSD services and secure financial integration. 
Government Entities for regulatory support and policy advocacy for youth inclusion in the digital economy. 
LLDC3 stakeholders and donors engage foot cross border scalability research collaboration and South Sudan learning.
Solution Provider(s): RIYA, Zain
Implementation location(s): The luma digital financial platform has already piloted and implemented in South Sudan specifically in selected communities within and surrounding areas as well as with youth groups and informal savings cooperatives operating in refugee-returnee and Peri-urban zones. Thee pilot focused on building trust testing USSD based access and gathering feedback from unbanked youth women’s and small scale entrepreneurs.
Implementation timeline(s): The luma solution was conceptualized in late 2023 with initial prototyping and community co-design in 2024 followed by pilot implementation in 2025 in selected areas of Juba and surrounding communities in South Sudan. The platform is currently in the early scaling phase 2024-2025 focusing on expanding to more rural and low connectivity areas while building strategic partnerships for broader national and regional impact.
Duration to pilot in a new geography: The estimated duration to pilot luma in a new geography is 6 to 9 months.
SDGs addressed: SDG 1 (No Poverty);SDG 9 (Industry, Innovation, and Infrastructure);SDG 2 (Zero Hunger);
Desired impact:
Luma aims to drive inclusive economic empowerment by bridging the financial access gap for unbanked populations in South Sudan and other landlocked developing countries. The platform is designed to make digital financial services accessible affordable and locally driven especially for youth women and informal workers in low connectivity and conflict affected areas. Solution objectives 
Enhance financial inclusion 
Generate youth employment 
Improve financial and digital literacy 
Empower informal economics 
Promotes scalable models 
Key achievement
2000 user onboarded during the pilot in Juba 
40 plus youth employed as luma 
150 digital savings groups 
30,000 plus savings pooled and tracked
Key technologies:
Blockchain is planned to expand 
1. Transparent community savings and lending ledger 
Smart contract
Unique Characteristics:
USSD first design for the underserved 
Luma is built primarily on USSD technology ensuring full functionality on basic mobile a critical differentiator in rural and low connectivity areas where smartphones and internet access are rare. Scalable across LLDC and humanitarian settings
Sustainable Change:
Luma foster sustainable systemic change by addressing financial exclusion at its root through a combination of technology community empowerment and policy engagement 
1.Building local capacity and ownership 
2.Inclusive digital infrastructure 
3.Alternatively credit system for the unbanked 
4.Integration with policy and institutional frameworks.
Funding Sources: Fundraising and my own personal savings
Testimonials and Endorsements: None
Further comments/feedback: Thanks
Primary thematic focus area: MSME Empowerment & Local Digital Innovation
Summary: Luma is a youth-led fintech startup from South Sudan that provides inclusive, mobile-first digital financial services for underserved and unbanked communities. Built with USSD accessibility, offline functionality, and local language support, the platform enables registration, community savings groups, mobile wallet integration, and behavior-based microcredit. Piloted in Juba and surrounding areas, Luma has already onboarded 2,000 users, employed 40 youth, and tracked over $30,000 in pooled savings. The initiative emphasizes human-centered design, partnerships with telecoms, youth associations, and government, and plans for blockchain-based transparent savings ledgers to enhance scalability and trust.

Title: "Empower Connect'
Subtitle: GNBI  "Empower Connect," a comprehensive, user-friendly, and culturally relevant digital platform designed to be the central hub for women, youth, and MSMEs in the target communities. Empower Connect will directly address financial inclusion, digital literacy, and market access through integrated modules
Problem Statement:
Despite South Africa's economic progress, significant disparities persist, particularly in the target regions:
•Limpopo, Mpumalanga (Coal Mining Communities): These areas face high unemployment due to declining traditional industries, with limited diversification opportunities. Digital infrastructure is often poor, and communities lack access to formal financial services and diversified markets beyond local consumption.
•Gauteng (Townships): While closer to economic hubs, townships are characterized by high youth unemployment, a large informal sector, and limited access to formal credit and sophisticated digital tools for business growth. Digital literacy varies widely, often hindering entrepreneurial potential.
•Northwest (Bojanala District): Heavily reliant on mining, this district experiences economic vulnerability and limited opportunities for youth and women outside the mining sector. Access to digital skills training and broad market platforms is scarce.
•Eastern Cape (Buffalo City Municipality): Marked by persistent poverty and high unemployment, particularly among youth and women. MSMEs struggle with limited access to capital, business development support, and digital channels to reach wider customer bases.Demographic Data:
These regions collectively represent millions of South Africans, with:
•High Youth Unemployment: Often exceeding 50% among those aged 18-35.
•Prevalence of Informal MSMEs: A significant portion of economic activity occurs in the informal sector, limiting access to formal financing and growth opportunities.
•Digital Divide: While smartphone penetration is increasing, effective digital literacy for business application remains low. Many lack access to affordable data, reliable internet, and the skills to leverage digital tools for financial management or market expansion.
•Financial Exclusion: A substantial percentage of the population, especially women and informal traders, remain unbanked or underbanked, relying on cash and informal lending, which stifles growth.
Solution Overview:
GNBI proposes "Empower Connect," a comprehensive, user-friendly, and culturally relevant digital platform designed to be the central hub for women, youth, and MSMEs in the target communities. Empower Connect will directly address financial inclusion, digital literacy, and market access through integrated modules:

Project Description:
Empower Connect will be a mobile-first, web-responsive platform, accessible via smartphones and low-cost data plans. It will feature an intuitive interface, available in multiple local languages, ensuring maximum accessibility for users with varying levels of digital proficiency.Key Solution Components:
Financial Inclusion Module:
Digital Wallet & Micro-Lending Integration: Facilitate secure digital transactions, peer-to-peer payments, and integration with micro-finance institutions for accessible, low-interest micro-loans and savings products. This will formalise financial activities and build credit histories.
Financial Literacy Hub: Interactive modules, short video tutorials, and gamified content on budgeting, savings, debt management, investment basics, and understanding formal financial products.
Grant & Funding Navigator: A curated database of available grants, tenders, and funding opportunities, with simplified application guides and direct links.
Digital Literacy & Skills Development Module:
Interactive Learning Paths: Self-paced modules on essential digital skills, including using productivity tools (spreadsheets, word processors), navigating online platforms, cybersecurity basics, and digital marketing fundamentals.
Business Skills Training: Short courses on e-commerce management, online customer service, supply chain digitization, and data analytics for small businesses.
Mentorship & Peer Learning Forums: Virtual spaces for users to connect with mentors, ask questions, share experiences, and learn from peers, fostering a supportive digital community.
Market Access & E-commerce Module:
Local Digital Marketplace: A dedicated e-commerce platform where MSMEs can list and sell their products and services directly to consumers, both locally and nationally. This will include features for product cataloguing, order management, and secure payment processing.
Supply Chain Linkages: Facilitate connections between small producers/suppliers and larger buyers, helping MSMEs integrate into formal supply chains.
Digital Marketing Tools: Simple, guided tools for creating social media campaigns, understanding customer analytics, and optimizing online presence to reach broader markets.
Solution Provider(s): Great North Business Incubator(GNBI), Educational Institutions,  Business Chambers, Wavecraft designers, Tech App designers, Small Enteprises development agency, National Youth Development Agency , Local Economic Development Agencies, Financial institutions
Duration to pilot in a new geography: 24 months
SDGs addressed: SDG 8 (Decent Work and Economic Growth);SDG 9 (Industry, Innovation, and Infrastructure);SDG 17 (Partnerships for the Goals);
Desired impact:
Empower Connect will be a mobile-first, web-responsive platform, accessible via smartphones and low-cost data plans. It will feature an intuitive interface, available in multiple local languages, ensuring maximum accessibility for users with varying levels of digital proficiency.Empower Connect is projected to deliver significant, measurable impacts:
Economic Empowerment:
5,000+ MSMEs Supported: Direct engagement and support for at least 5,000 MSMEs within 24 months.
1,500+ New Jobs Created: Facilitating job creation through business growth and expansion.
20% Average Revenue Increase: For participating MSMEs within 12 months of consistent platform engagement.
Enhanced Financial Inclusion:
3,000+ Individuals Formally Banked/Financially Included: Through access to digital wallets and micro-finance products.
Increased Access to Capital: Facilitating over $1 million in micro-loans and grants accessed by MSMEs.
Improved Digital Literacy:
3,000+ Individuals Digitally Literate: Equipping women, youth, and entrepreneurs with essential digital skills for business and personal growth.
Increased Digital Adoption: Leading to more efficient business operations and broader market reach.
Expanded Market Access:
500+ MSMEs Actively Selling Online: Connecting local businesses to national and potentially international markets.
Diversified Income Streams: Reducing reliance on single industries and local markets.
Community Resilience: Fostering a culture of innovation, self-reliance, and sustainable economic development within the target communities.
Key technologies: "Empower Connect," a comprehensive, user-friendly, and culturally relevant digital platform designed to be the central hub for women, youth, and MSMEs in the target communities. Empower Connect will directly address financial inclusion, digital literacy, and market access through integrated modules
Unique Characteristics:
Empower Connect is designed with scalability at its core, ensuring long-term sustainability and broad reach:
•Cloud-Native Architecture: Built on a flexible, scalable cloud infrastructure (e.g., AWS, Google Cloud), allowing for rapid expansion of user capacity and features without significant upfront hardware investment.
•Modular Design: The platform's modular components (Financial, Literacy, Market Access) allow for independent development, deployment, and future integration of new features or partnerships.
•API-First Approach: Open APIs will enable seamless integration with existing financial service providers, government databases, and other relevant digital tools, fostering an ecosystem of support.
Sustainable Change:
Technological Evolution and Cost Optimization:
Agile Development & Iteration: Maintain an agile development approach to continuously update and improve the platform based on user feedback and technological advancements, ensuring it remains competitive and valuable.
Open-Source Components: Utilize open-source technologies where feasible to reduce licensing costs and foster a collaborative development environment.
Cloud Cost Management: Implement robust cloud cost optimization strategies to manage infrastructure expenses efficiently as the platform scales.
Data-Driven Decision Making: Use analytics to identify features that deliver the most value and optimize resource allocation, ensuring that development efforts are focused on high-impact areas.
Funding Sources: Through grant funding from Finance institutions and DFIDs
Testimonials and Endorsements: Not available
Further comments/feedback: The questionnaire is thought provoking .
Primary thematic focus area: MSME Empowerment & Local Digital Innovation
Summary: Empower Connect is a mobile-first, cloud-based digital platform proposed by Great North Business Incubator (GNBI) to empower women, youth, and MSMEs in South Africa (Limpopo, Mpumalanga, Gauteng, Northwest, and Eastern Cape). It integrates financial inclusion (digital wallet, micro-loans, literacy), digital skills training, and market access (e-commerce marketplace, supply chain linkages, digital marketing tools). With strong local institutional partners, it aims to support 5,000+ MSMEs, create 1,500 jobs, and bank 3,000+ unbanked individuals within 24 months.

Title: From Nature to Nourishment. Providing natural nourishing solutions from local roots
Subtitle: At AM Foods Ventures Limited, we’re an agro-innovative processing company committed to transforming local crops into healthier, climate-conscious food solutions. Our mission is to blend taste with convenience, reduce post-harvest losses, and promote sustainable nutrition.  We specialize in exploring the full value of the dates fruit, processing it into natural sweeteners like Dates Powder and Dates Syrup, natural and healthier alternatives to refined sugar. Our dates are sustainably sourced. We go beyond sweeteners—upcycling dates seeds into a rich, caffeine-free coffee-like beverage, reducing food waste and supporting a circular economy. Our low-energy, minimal processing approach cuts emissions and avoids the heavy refining used in conventional sugar production.  In addition, we process natural local flours and instant drinks from crops like soybeans, maize, millet, and plantain—adding value, reducing waste, and offering convenient, nutritious options for every household.  At AM Foods, we’re building a future where food is nourishing, sustainable, and proudly local.
Problem Statement:
Our solution seeks to tackle issues and problems to prevent post harvest losses, unhealthy dietary habits, environmental degradation and promoting innovative usage of indigenous agro products for food.
We process agro products into shelf-stable flours, sweeteners and natural drinks in powdered forms, extending their value and reducing food waste.
The rising cases of diabetes, obesity and other diet related illnesses in Nigeria and the world at large, are linked to excessive consumption of refined sugar and overly processed foods. We offer minimally processed natural sweeteners as a healthier alternative.
Traditional sugar production is resource intensive and contributes to high carbon emissions, contrary to Dates processing. We up-cycle the dates seeds to further reduce our environmental footprints prints.
Nutritious local crops are often overlooked and so we innovate in modern convenient forms to blend taste with convenience
Solution Overview:
How Our Solution Works

At AM Foods, we’re solving everyday food and nutrition problems by transforming locally grown crops into healthier, more convenient, and climate-smart products. We process dates, soybeans, beans, tigernut, millet, maize, plantain, and more—turning them into natural sweeteners, food flours, and instant drinks that are safe, nutritious, and easy to use for every home.

We take what’s often wasted or underused—like date seeds—and turn them into something of value, like a rich, caffeine-free coffee alternative. That way, we reduce waste, cut post-harvest losses, and support a more circular food economy.

---
Our Approach

Natural Processing: We use low-energy, minimal processing to retain nutrients and reduce emissions.

Sustainability First: Our dates are sourced using water-efficient methods suited to Nigeria’s climate.

Healthy for All: Our products are safe for children and diabetics, with no additives or refined sugar.

From Waste to Worth: We upcycle by-products like date seeds into new, useful products.
---
Technologies & Methods

-Roasting & milling for date-seed coffee

-Drying, milling, and sieving for flours

-Quality control at every step

---
Partnerships & Collaboration

Farmers: We work with small holder farmers to ensure quality and promote sustainable practices.

Communities: We engage women and youth groups for training and small-scale processing.

Retailers & Health Outlets: We collaborate with health stores, supermarkets, NGOs and schools to make our products accessible.

Researchers: We explore product development with local food scientists and universities.
Solution Provider(s): NEPWAN (NGO) for supply of our micronutrient product (Soy Plus Mix), Hmedix supermarket, Catholic Women Organization group Chikakore etc
Duration to pilot in a new geography: 2 months
SDGs addressed: SDG 2 (Zero Hunger);SDG 3 (Good Health and Well-being);SDG 12 (Responsible Consumption and Production);
Desired impact:
Solution Objectives

At AM Foods, our mission is to offer food solutions that are healthy, convenient, and climate-smart—made from crops grown right here in Nigeria. Through innovative agro-processing, we turn underutilized local crops into nutritious products that reduce waste, promote better eating, and support smallholder farmers.

Our key objectives:

Promote Healthier Eating
Offer plant-based, minimally processed alternatives safe for children and diabetics.

Reduce Food Waste & Post-Harvest Losses
Turn perishable crops into shelf-stable products, and upcycle waste like date seeds.

Support Environmental Sustainability
Use low-energy processing methods and climate-resilient crops like dates.

Empower Local Farmers & Communities
Source directly from farmers and train women and youth in food processing.
Key technologies: Hammer mills and dehydrators
Unique Characteristics:
What Makes AM Foods’ Solution Unique

At AM Foods Ventures Limited, our innovation lies in how we blend local resources, smart processing, and inclusive partnerships to offer food solutions that are good for people, farmers, and the planet. We’re not just replacing unhealthy or imported products—we’re reshaping how food is made and valued in Nigeria.
1. Circular Food Innovation
We don't waste—we upcycle. One of our standout innovations is turning date seeds, which are typically discarded, into a nutritious, caffeine-free coffee alternative. This “waste-to-worth” approach reduces pressure on landfills, supports a circular economy, and introduces new, healthy beverage options to the market.

2. Climate-Smart Product Design

Our focus on climate-resilient crops like dates, millet, and soy reduces dependence on water- and energy-intensive ingredients like sugar cane or imported cereals. Our minimal-processing techniques use less energy and avoid heavy refining, helping to lower our carbon footprints.

3. Inclusive & Localized Business Model

We’ve built a community-first model that works directly with small holder farmers, especially in northern Nigeria, offering stable offtake agreements and seasonal support. We also work with women and youth-led cooperatives in processing and packaging, promoting local job creation and skill building.

4. Affordable & Health-Driven Alternatives

Our products are not just innovative—they’re affordable, safe for children and diabetics, and tailored to everyday Nigerian diets. We’re making healthier options accessible without compromising on taste or convenience.

5. Lean Digital Integration

We use WhatsApp and digital tools to manage inventory, connect with customers, and coordinate farmer supply. This lean-tech approach keeps our operations agile and community-driven while expanding our reach affordably.
Sustainable Change:
How Our Solution Drives Sustainable, Systemic Change
At AM Foods, we believe sustainable change starts with making better food choices easier, local, and accessible. By transforming underused local crops into healthy, shelf-stable products, we’re reducing waste, improving nutrition, and creating value across the food chain.

Our Theory of Change is simple but powerful:
1. We process climate-smart crops like dates and grains into affordable, healthy foods. More families make better dietary choices, reducing sugar-related diseases.

2. We upcycle agro by-products like date seeds into new products →
→ Less food waste, lower emissions, and more circular production systems.

3. We work directly with small holder farmers and women/youth processors →
→ Stronger local economies, better livelihoods, and more inclusive food systems.

4. We minimize processing and use low-energy techniques →
→ Reduced environmental impact and a lower carbon footprint.

The long-term effect is a healthier population, stronger rural communities, and a more resilient, climate-conscious food economy—powered by everyday foods people already know and love.

It reduces post-harvest losses, promotes climate-smart nutrition, and empowers smallholder farmers and women/youth cooperatives.

Title: Aralangan CBST Market Hub: A Digital Platform for Forest-Friendly and Community-Based Enterprises
Subtitle: Digitally Empowering Indigenous, Women-led, and Cooperative Enterprises in Palawan, Philippines
Problem Statement: Rural and Indigenous communities in Palawan face significant barriers to market access, digital adoption, and inclusive economic participation. Local MSMEs, often women-led, forest-dependent, and cooperative-managed, lack platforms to reach ethical markets, access financing, or build visibility for their sustainable products. Meanwhile, most digital marketplaces are urban-centric, extractive, and not built to reflect Indigenous stewardship, cooperative governance, or conservation values.
Solution Overview:
Solution Overview: 
The Aralangan CBST Market Hub is a place-based digital solution that connects forest-dependent and community-owned enterprises to wider ethical markets, donors, and learning networks through a mobile-first, story-rich platform. It is co-created by Indigenous Peoples, cooperatives, and sustainability advocates in Palawan, Philippines—a globally significant biodiversity corridor facing high poverty, limited infrastructure, and weak digital access.

More than an e-commerce tool, Aralangan is designed as a digital ecosystem that elevates community voices, supports regenerative livelihoods, and enables transparent, data-informed engagement between local producers and global allies.

Methodologies and Technologies Used:
>Participatory Co-Design: Built with and for the communities, ensuring relevance, ownership, and cultural compatibility.
>Agile Development: Built in modular stages allowing scale and customization per region or cooperative.
>Progressive Web App (PWA): Usable even in low-signal areas, optimized for mobile-first rural usage.
>Geotagging & Mapping: Each product, service, or community story is connected to a real location helping promote visibility, trust, and responsible tourism.
>QR Code + Traceability Layer: Physical products can be tagged with codes that lead back to digital profiles of the producers and their stories.
>E-commerce Integration: Basic functions for inventory, payment, and logistics coordination are embedded or linked to existing financial platforms.
>Integrated Impact Tracker: A built-in feature that allows community enterprises to log and display real-time social, environmental, and economic impact data. Indicators include gender and youth participation, household income growth, forest product volumes, and cooperative contributions to conservation. Data is visualized through a simple dashboard and tied to each enterprise’s profile—strengthening transparency, donor engagement, and results-based storytelling.
>Future Phases: will explore blockchain to verify ethical sourcing, AI for auto-curated storytelling, and microlearning modules for local upskilling.

Partnerships and Collaboration Models:
Aralangan is powered through a multi-stakeholder platform approach, led by the cooperative SSFMPC and CBOs/IPOs partners. Core collaboration models include:
>Cooperative-led platform governance: Community enterprises manage and upload their own content and products through training and shared protocols.
>Rotating community “market weeks”: Each month, a different community is featured to avoid competition and promote diverse cultural and ecological narratives.
>Community Content Creation: Trained youth or storytellers within each community help gather and post content, increasing local employment and voice.
>Revenue Sharing Model: A fixed percentage of platform earnings are shared back with contributors and used for conservation or community funds.
Solution Provider(s): Community and Indigenous Partners: Sabang Sea Ferry Multi-Purpose Cooperative (SSFMPC) A rural cooperative in Sabang, Puerto Princesa, leading inclusive enterprises in community-based tourism, agroforestry, and NTFP marketing. SSFMPC anchors the Aralangan platform and ensures cooperative governance and continuity,  Samahan ng mga Tribu sa Kayasan (SATRIKA) A Tagbanua and Batak Indigenous Peoples’ organization, SATRIKA manages almaciga and rattan-based enterprises and is a lead content and product contributor to the platform, Tinig ng mga Katutubo sa Cabayugan (TiKCa) A grassroots IP organization representing Tagbanua communities in Cabayugan, advocating for ancestral domain recognition and the revival of traditional livelihoods, Puerto Princesa Community-Based Sustainable Tourism (CBST) Federation A city-wide federation with 31 CBST groups, acting as both beneficiaries and contributors to the platform’s services (e.g., community tours, homestays, eco-cultural products). Local Government and National Agencies: Puerto Princesa City Tourism Department Facilitates the promotion, policy alignment, and accreditation of community tourism sites featured on the platform, and supports capacity-building for CBST groups, Department of Trade and Industry (DTI) – Palawan Provides product development, entrepreneurship training, and enterprise support to MSMEs and community enterprises linked to Aralangan, Department of Information and Communications Technology (DICT) – MIMAROPA Supports rural digital access, ICT trainings, and platform readiness through local implementation of the national digital inclusion program. Platform and Development Team: Aralangan Project Team A transdisciplinary group of sustainability advocates, digital creatives, cooperative facilitators, and community organizers behind the platform design and implementation. The team combines experience in digital storytelling, regenerative enterprise development, and IP rights advocacy.
Duration to pilot in a new geography: Between 10-12 months.
SDGs addressed: SDG 1 (No Poverty);SDG 12 (Responsible Consumption and Production);SDG 11 (Sustainable Cities and Communities);
Desired impact:
Solution Objectives
> Digital Inclusion - Equip rural, Indigenous, and forest-dependent communities with mobile-first tools to access markets, share stories, and track impact.
> Enterprise Growth - Increase visibility and sales of community-based enterprises by connecting them to ethical buyers, donors, and learning platforms.
> Inclusive Economic Participation - Promote economic empowerment for women, youth, and Indigenous Peoples through traceable livelihoods and cooperative ownership models.
> Environmental Stewardship - Strengthen conservation-based enterprises by tracking and incentivizing sustainable harvesting, biodiversity protection, and carbon sequestration.
> Data-Driven Governance - Provide real-time grassroots data to inform local policies, donor strategies, and climate-adaptive planning.

Expected Key Impacts (upon pilot in one locality, scaled within 12–18 months)
> 25–50 forest-dependent producers and weavers digitally onboarded, with traceable product pages and QR-linked profiles
> 20% increase in sales for at least three community enterprises due to digital visibility and direct buyer access
> 50%+ women and youth participation across digital onboarding, storytelling, and enterprise roles
Real-time dashboards showing metrics such as forest product volumes, income per household, and cooperative equity
> 1 metric ton CO₂-equivalent of emissions avoided or offset through sustainable sourcing and avoided transport footprints
> Digital literacy tools accessed by at least 80% of enrolled users during the pilot phase
> 1,000+ site visitors/month by Year 2 from ethical market networks and donor audiences
Enhanced data for ancestral domain management and CBST (community-based sustainable tourism) planning, via geotagged layers and visual maps
Key technologies:
Key Technologies Used
The Aralangan CBST Market Hub is built as a mobile-first, place-based digital platform integrating multiple appropriate technologies tailored to underserved and low-connectivity areas:
>Progressive Web App (PWA): A lightweight, mobile-optimized platform that works across devices and can function even in low-signal environments—ideal for rural and forest-dependent communities.
>Geotagging & GIS Mapping: Products, producers, and tourism services are linked to real locations, enabling storytelling, trust-building, and traceability. This also supports environmental monitoring and CBST planning.
>QR Code + Traceability Layer: Each physical product or service includes a QR code that links to the digital profile of the producer, cooperative, and story—promoting transparency and ethical sourcing.
>Basic E-Commerce Integration: Inventory tracking, digital payments (via GCash, etc.), and logistics coordination are integrated or linked to existing platforms, supporting local MSMEs and cooperatives.
>Participatory Impact Tracker (planned): Future modules will integrate grassroots impact metrics such as income growth, forest cover protection, and gender participation using low-code dashboards and survey-based inputs.
>Blockchain (exploratory): In future phases, blockchain will be explored to verify ethical sourcing, ensure supply chain transparency, and document non-timber forest product (NTFP) flows.
>AI for Auto-Curated Storytelling (future): Text-to-voice, captioning, and auto-summarization tools will be piloted to reduce barriers to content generation and amplify Indigenous and women-led narratives.
Unique Characteristics:
The Aralangan CBST Market Hub stands out as an inclusive, place-based digital solution that bridges the gap between forest-dependent communities and the digital economy. Its uniqueness lies in both its approach and its architecture:

1. Community-Led and Culturally Grounded Co-Creation
Unlike typical top-down platforms, Aralangan is co-created with Indigenous Peoples, cooperatives, and local governments in Palawan. Every feature is rooted in cultural relevance, land-based identity, and cooperative values, ensuring legitimacy, adoption, and sustainability.
2. Multi-Stakeholder Partnership Model
The project brings together grassroots producers, digital creatives, technologists, and policymakers under one ecosystem. This ecosystem model ensures shared ownership, equitable benefits, and wide replicability.
3. Place-Based Impact + Digital Traceability
By using geotagging, QR codes, and community storytelling, Aralangan enables traceable ethical commerce—connecting buyers directly to producers and their landscapes. This builds trust, transparency, and conservation value into every transaction.
4. Modular Tech Stack with Offline Functionality
The Progressive Web App (PWA) architecture makes it accessible even in low-signal areas. The modular design allows replication in other geographies and integration of local cooperative databases, making it scalable yet contextualized.
5. Participatory Impact Tracking
The platform will include a grassroots Impact Tracker that aligns local indicators (income, forest conservation, gender inclusion) with global SDGs. This bottom-up data collection helps communities make their own progress visible and with hope, fundable.
6. Ethical Market Meets Learning Network
It’s not just a marketplace—it’s a story-rich platform that connects local producers with donors, ethical consumers, and youth microlearners through interactive modules and storytelling. This creates a virtuous cycle of commerce, learning, and solidarity.
Sustainable Change:
The Aralangan CBST Market Hub is designed to create long-term, systems-level change by bridging digital, economic, and ecological divides in forest-based and Indigenous communities. It does this by restructuring access, agency, and accountability across the value chain—from production to consumption, from local stories to global solidarity.

1. If rural and Indigenous communities co-create digital tools tailored to their context…
Then they will gain digital agency, cultural relevance, and trust in technology—enabling them to lead innovation, not just receive it.
2. If local cooperatives and IP organizations are digitally connected to ethical markets and donors…
Then they can secure fair prices, stable demand, and values-aligned partnerships—strengthening livelihoods, reducing poverty, and improving business resilience.
3. If products and services are traceable and rooted in place-based storytelling…
Then consumers and partners can make informed, ethical choices, rewarding conservation-linked, community-owned efforts.
4. If local impact is tracked through a participatory, transparent system aligned with global indicators…
Then communities can communicate their outcomes, attract support, and influence public policy from the ground up.
5. If youth and women access microlearning through the platform…
Then they become local digital stewards, ensuring long-term sustainability, innovation, and leadership continuity.

Expected Systemic Shifts:
1. Economic Empowerment: Rise in incomes, reduction in exploitation, improved cooperative enterprise performance.
2. Digital Inclusion: Tech usage shifts from passive consumption to strategic livelihood tool.
3. Environmental Co-benefits: Conservation incentives built into enterprise design (e.g., sustainable harvesting, community-based tourism).
4. Social Cohesion: Strengthened Indigenous governance, inclusive leadership, intergenerational engagement.
5. Policy Influence: Community-generated data can shape funding priorities and public sector support for CBST and green MSMEs.
Funding Sources: The Aralangan CBST Market Hub builds on the foundational support provided under the FORTIFI PPSRNP  (Forest Regeneration through Inclusive Social Fencing Strategies in Puerto Princesa Subterranean River National Park) Project, funded by the Forest Foundation Philippines (FFP) from 2023 to 2025.

We appreciate that the questionnaire allows space to present context-driven, community-led digital solutions—particularly those still in the early stages of development. However, we suggest more flexibility in recognizing the complexities of place-based innovation, especially where formal infrastructure is limited, and solutions are co-created with Indigenous and rural communities.

We also commend UNIDO’s commitment to inclusivity and recommend that future calls integrate space for storytelling, visuals, or community voices to complement written submissions. This would help surface the lived realities, values, and informal innovation ecosystems that shape digital inclusion in the Global South.

Thank you for creating this opportunity. We look forward to engaging with peers and partners through this platform

The solution emphasizes traceability (geotagging, QR codes), participatory impact tracking, and cooperative governance, going beyond e-commerce toward an ecosystem of sustainable livelihoods, conservation incentives, and storytelling. Name of your organization: Greater Kamuli Farmers Agribusiness Cooperative Society Limited
Title: ShambaSmart Investors App for Youth led cooperative Block Framing
Subtitle: A digital platform connecting investors, youth, and cooperatives for inclusive, insured, and transparent block farming in Africa
Problem Statement: In Africa, idle land, unemployed youth, and cautious investors reflect a broken agricultural system. Existing digital tools lack practical, field-based application and youth remain jobless not due to lack of work but due to the absence of structured, value-driven systems. True development must begin with collective efforts to industrializing agriculture through inclusive, practical, and transparent solutions
Solution Overview:
ShambaSmart Investors App for Youth-led Cooperative Block Farming is a digital platform that organizes youth, landowners, and cooperatives into structured block farms, connects them to investors, and ensures real-time transparency, profitability, and impact. It bridges gaps in trust, coordination, and accountability using practical field-based digital tools.
How the Solution Works:
1.	Block Farm Mapping: Idle land is mapped through cooperatives and landowners, verified using GIS tools, and divided into manageable blocks for youth-led farming.
2.	Youth Profiling & Deployment: The app registers and profiles youth (especially agricultural graduates), assigning them to specific farm blocks with digital work plans and reporting tasks.
3.	Investor Matching & Insurance: Investors select crop cycles based on cost-benefit analysis uploaded by agronomists. Funds are insured (3%) and returns structured (10%, 5%, 2.5%) based on entry point.
4.	Real-Time Monitoring: Agronomists input crop updates, progress reports, and health checks. Investors, cooperatives, and youth access dashboards for full-cycle visibility.
5.	Produce Aggregation & Value Addition: Harvested produce is bulked, sorted, and routed for local or export markets. Value-added processing (drying, branding) is integrated to boost returns.
6.	Profit Sharing: After investment recovery, surplus is distributed: 70% to youth, 15% to investors, 15% to the system/cooperative.

Technologies Used:
Mobile-first application (Android & Web).
Offline-first data entry with cloud sync.
GIS mapping for land and youth deployment.
Automated logic for ROI calculations and surplus sharing.
Investor dashboard with real-time metrics.
Insurance tracking engine for risk cover.

Methodology:
Cooperative-led planning and validation.
Youth mobilization through profiling and app-based training.
Transparent agronomic workflows and digital accountability.
Tiered investment structure with traceability and ESG compliance.

Partnership & Collaboration Models:
Cooperatives: Provide land, governance, and aggregation.
Youth groups: Serve as trained, paid farm managers.
Agronomists: Offer advisory and field monitoring.
DIT Uganda: Supports certification and digital training.
Investors & SACCOs: Fund input cycles with insurance-backed ROI.
Local government & private sector: Support value chains, irrigation, and market linkages.
Solution Provider(s): Innovation team,Greater Kamuli Agribusiness Farmers Cooperative Society , Local government Irrigation schemes ,Agrovision She farmers
Duration to pilot in a new geography: 3 years
SDGs addressed: SDG 1 (No Poverty);SDG 2 (Zero Hunger);SDG 13 (Climate Action);
Desired impact:
Solution Objectives:
Digitally organize youth-led cooperative block farming for higher productivity and income generation.
Connect investors to transparent, insured farming opportunities with guaranteed phased returns.
Transform idle land into productive agri-enterprises through structured land aggregation.
Industrialize agriculture by linking production to value addition, certification, and markets.
Create dignified, tech-enabled rural employment while fostering climate-smart practices.

Key Achievements & Impact (Targeted):
Employment Generation: Create 50,000+ jobs for youth (especially agri-graduates) as certified block farm managers within 3 years.
Land Utilization: Convert over 100,000 acres of idle land into productive horticultural blocks through cooperatives and landowner partnerships.
GHG Reductions: Promote regenerative farming, solar-powered irrigation, and organic input practices targeting a 20–30% reduction in emissions per acre compared to conventional methods.
Investment Mobilization: Attract over ~USD 5,200,000 in farming investments through phased, insured digital investor participation.
Insurance Cover: De-risk 100% of investor funds through a grant-backed Investment Insurance Fund (3% charge per cycle).
Digital Inclusion: Onboard 3,000+ users (youth, cooperatives, landowners, agronomists, and investors) to the ShambaSmart platform.
Market Value Addition: Boost produce income by 30–50% through aggregation, drying, branding, and export targeting.
Key technologies:
ShambaSmart leverages a blend of inclusive digital technologies to enable transparency, efficiency, and scalability in youth-led cooperative block farming:
1. Web & Mobile Application (Cross-Platform)
Core interface for youth, investors, agronomists, and cooperatives.
Supports real-time crop updates, digital worklogs, investment tracking, and surplus distribution.
2. IoT-Enabled Smart Farming Tools
Integrated with solar-powered irrigation and sensors (soil moisture, weather, water flow) for remote farm monitoring and efficient resource use.
Enables precision agriculture for yield optimization and GHG reduction.
3. Blockchain-Inspired Logic (for Transparency)
While not full block chain, the app uses smart contract logic to manage:
Transparent profit-sharing, automated investment tracking, Surplus distribution and investor pay out schedules
4. Investment Insurance Engine
A rule-based algorithm that calculates and applies a 3% insurance fee to protect investor funds, pooled and backed by grants/donors.
5. AI-Driven Crop Planning (Future Integration)
Plans are in place to incorporate AI models to analyze crop performance, predict pest/disease outbreaks, and guide investor decisions based on historical yield and climate data.
Unique Characteristics:
ShambaSmart stands out as a practical, inclusive digital agri-tech solution that uniquely integrates cooperative farming models with investor confidence and youth employment. Its innovations lie in the fusion of technology, business models, and local realities, specifically:
1. Cooperative-Led Block Farming Model
Unlike typical agri-tech tools, ShambaSmart is rooted in community-owned cooperative structures, enabling shared resources, transparent governance, and inclusive ownership for youth, landowners, and investors.
2. Youth-Centred Investment Logic
Youth are not labourers they are profit-sharing partners. After investment recovery, they retain 70% of the surplus, promoting dignity, motivation, and retention.
3. Phased Investor Return System + Insurance Fund
A guaranteed ROI structure (10%, 5%, 2.5%) based on farming cycle stages builds investor confidence.
A 3% insurance charge goes into a pooled fund to cover risks and rare among youth-based agri-projects.
4. Embedded Work Culture Tools
The app includes farm work logs, timetables, agronomist reports, and DIT-linked certification for professionalizing youth agri-employment.
5. Tech-Aided Transparency without High-Cost Block chain
While blockchain is often inaccessible for rural use, ShambaSmart uses automated, auditable logic to deliver the same transparency benefits at low cost.
6. Inclusive Produce Aggregation + Value Addition
It not only aggregates crops for market but builds systems for on-site value addition, improving earnings and reducing post-harvest losses.
7. Designed for Real-World Deployment
The app’s core strength lies in practical implementation with farmer cooperatives, local governments, youth groups, and landowners not just digital demos or pilots.
Sustainable Change:
ShambaSmart aims to transform Africa’s agricultural sector by digitizing and industrializing cooperative-led block farming through youth engagement, investor confidence, and agritech tools. Our Theory of Change is built around five interconnected pillars of impact:

2. Activities (What We Do):

Digitize farm planning, reporting, and crop tracking.
Aggregate investments and provide phased ROI.
Aggregate produce and build value addition systems.
Certify youth and integrate them into formal agri-employment.

3. Immediate Outcomes (Short-Term):
5,000+ youth employed in dignified agri-jobs.
Increased investor inflow due to transparency and insurance.
Idle land converted into productive block farms.
Increased cooperative income and digital visibility.
Youth trained and certified with market-ready skills.

4. Intermediate Outcomes (Medium-Term):
Reduction in rural youth unemployment and urban migration.
Boost in horticultural productivity and exports.
More women and youth owning shares in agribusinesses.
Improved investor trust in smallholder farming systems.
Higher household incomes and resilience to climate shocks.

5. Systemic Change (Long-Term Impact):
Agricultural industrialization from the grassroots, led by youth.
Policy influence through cooperative data aggregation and ESG compliance.
Emergence of Smart Farming Hubs with solar irrigation and tech adoption.
Strengthened rural economies through multi-stakeholder models.
A replicable digital ecosystem for climate-smart, youth-led agribusiness in Africa.

Name of your organization: Rescue the Child and Youth Ethiopia (RCY)
Title: Click & Grow: Digital Inclusion for Local Entrepreneurs
Subtitle: Click & Grow" is a digital inclusion and entrepreneurship initiative designed to empower marginalized youth and MSMEs in North Shewa Zone, Amhara Region. By establishing rural innovation hubs, delivering tailored digital skills training, and connecting micro-enterprises to digital platforms, the project addresses the region's significant digital divide. This solution offers a scalable and inclusive model for fostering digital transformation in underserved communities.
Problem Statement: Despite the rapid growth of digital technologies, many women, youth, and micro-entrepreneurs in North Shewa Zone remain digitally excluded. Barriers such as limited access to digital tools, low digital literacy, and lack of tailored platforms hinder their participation in the digital economy. This exclusion deepens socioeconomic inequalities, limits job creation, and restricts local innovation. To ensure equitable growth, there is an urgent need for inclusive digital solutions that empower underserved communities with the skills, tools, and networks needed to thrive in the digital age.
Solution Overview:
Project Title: Click & Grow: Digital Inclusion for Local Entrepreneurs
Implementing Entity: Rescue the Child and Youth (RCY)
Target Area: North Shewa Zone, Amhara Region, Ethiopia

1. How the Solution Works
“Click & Grow” is a hybrid digital empowerment initiative designed to bridge the digital divide among women, youth, and micro-entrepreneurs in marginalized rural and peri-urban communities of North Shewa. The solution works by:

Identifying and training local entrepreneurs on digital literacy, e-commerce, and online business management.

Developing a tailored digital platform (accessible via mobile and low-bandwidth internet) to allow users to promote, market, and sell their products and services locally and beyond.

Providing business development and digital mentorship, enabling continuous skill-building, networking, and access to finance and markets.

Offering physical digital hubs (Digital Access Points) equipped with computers, internet, and support personnel for those with limited device access.

2. Methodologies and Technologies Used
Human-Centered Design (HCD): We co-create the platform and training content with the target communities to ensure relevance, accessibility, and usability.

Mobile-First Technology: The solution is optimized for low-spec Android phones, SMS, and USSD interfaces to overcome connectivity and device barriers.

Blended Learning Model: Combines online modules with face-to-face training at community hubs to ensure inclusive participation, especially for digitally inexperienced users.

Data Collection Tools: Digital surveys and monitoring dashboards help track user progress, access, and outcomes.

E-commerce and Marketplace Tools: Lightweight web-app to enable cataloguing, payments (via mobile money), and visibility of local businesses.

AI-Driven Guidance (in future iterations): Basic AI integration for business tips, personalized learning paths, and digital coaching.

3. Partnerships and Collaboration Models
The project adopts a multi-stakeholder model that includes:

Local Government: Supports community mobilization, infrastructure access, and sustainability integration into local development plans.

Private Sector (Telcos & Fintechs): Partners like Ethio Telecom and mobile money providers collaborate to enable internet access and digital payments.

Educational Institutions: Local TVETs and universities contribute by co-developing training content and hosting internship opportunities.

CSOs and Women/Youth Associations: Help identify participants, promote the program, and foster community ownership.

UN and International Networks: Engage with UNIDO and UNCTAD platforms for visibility, knowledge sharing, and scaling opportunities.

Title: Bridging the Digital Gap in Underserved Communities
Subtitle: “Bridging the Digital Gap in Underserved Communities”:  Empowering marginalized youth and entrepreneurs with digital skills, tools, and access to unlock inclusive economic opportunities in the informal and underserved sectors.
Problem Statement: Millions of youth and micro-entrepreneurs in underserved communities, especially in informal sectors like Jua Kali, face limited access to digital skills, tools and online markets. This digital divide excludes them from economic opportunities, limits business growth and widens inequality. Low connectivity, lack of training infrastructure and limited awareness of digital platforms continue to hinder their participation in the digital economy.
Solution Overview:
Solution Overview

Valid Dream Mentorship is a community-driven digital empowerment initiative focused on bridging the digital economic divide for youth and informal entrepreneurs in underserved areas, particularly within Kenya's Jua Kali sector. The solution combines digital literacy training, mentorship and access to mobile-friendly tools to help beneficiaries meaningfully engage with and benefit from the digital economy.

How the Solution Works:
The program operates in three phases:

1. Digital Literacy & Skills Training – Participants receive training in basic ICT, online safety, digital financial tools, e-commerce, social media marketing and mobile apps for business.


2. Mentorship & Business Development – Through a network of volunteer mentors and local partners, participants get one-on-one or group coaching on branding, online customer engagement and leveraging digital platforms for growth.


3. Access to Opportunities & Platforms – Graduates are connected to marketplaces, freelance gigs, digital service providers and accelerator programs to support long-term economic participation.



Methodologies and Technologies Used:

Mobile-first approach – All content is delivered via low-data, mobile-friendly platforms like WhatsApp, SMS and web-based micro-learning portals.

Localized curriculum – Training materials are tailored to the realities of informal sector entrepreneurs, often in local languages.

Hybrid delivery – Both in-person and virtual methods are used to increase reach and adapt to connectivity levels.


Partnerships and Collaboration Models:

Local CBOs and youth groups – For community mobilization and trust-building.

Tech partners – Collaborations with local tech hubs and mobile service providers enable affordable or subsidized access to tools and devices.

Mentor network – Volunteer professionals provide mentorship on digital tools, entrepreneurship and financial literacy.

Government and SME agencies – Where possible, the initiative aligns with national youth, ICT and enterprise development policies to enhance impact and scalability.

Universities onboarded to Nanaade gain access to dashboards to track student engagement and outcomes. Employers benefit from efficient, data-informed hiring through a recruiter dashboard that matches candidates to roles based on skill relevance and hiring priorities.
Technologies include machine learning (for job-candidate matching and skill-gap detection), cloud-based architecture, and real-time labour market data integration.

Title: Smart Algae Innovation Hub: Data-Driven Solutions for Inclusive Green Growth
Subtitle: Harnessing data, IoT, and blockchain to transform algae into a driver of food security, clean water, green jobs, and inclusive participation in the digital economy.
Problem Statement: Millions face food insecurity, unemployment, and water pollution worsened by climate change and poor resource management. Untreated wastewater fuels harmful algal blooms, while vulnerable communities lack access to sustainable livelihoods and digital tools. These challenges reinforce poverty, malnutrition, and exclusion from the digital economy. Current approaches are fragmented, with limited data-driven solutions to make algae cultivation scalable, transparent, and inclusive. There is a pressing need for innovative technologies that not only address environmental degradation but also create pathways for youth empowerment, climate resilience, and equitable economic opportunities in underserved regions.
Solution Overview: Project Alsight is a data-driven platform that leverages machine learning, IoT, geospatial analysis, and blockchain to transform algae cultivation into a driver of food security, clean water, and inclusive green jobs. Through predictive models and IoT sensors, the solution monitors growth cycles, nutrient dynamics, and carbon sequestration to enable smarter farming decisions. The Alsight Simulator, a digital twin tool, provides decision support for optimal harvesting and system efficiency, while Algaecoin, a blockchain-based token, ensures transparency and traceability in algae value chains. Alongside technology, the Alsight Academy and Podcast build digital literacy, leadership, and entrepreneurship among youth. Our collaborative model engages researchers, local farmers, youth innovators, NGOs, and investors, ensuring technological feasibility, community ownership, and inclusive participation in the digital economy.

Geospatial analysis and satellite data support site selection and climate adaptation strategies. Blockchain technology, through Algaecoin, ensures traceability, trust, and transparency in algae value chains. Together, these technologies form an ecosystem that enhances sustainability, fosters digital inclusion, and drives socio-economic impact in vulnerable communities.

Title: “Easy Digital Customs and Shipping for Small Traders in Liberia”
Subtitle: We help small traders in Liberia use easy digital tools to clear goods, save money, and grow their businesses through fair customs and shipping services.
Problem Statement: In Liberia, many small and rural traders struggle with customs and shipping. The process is slow, costly, and often confusing. These traders do not have easy access to digital tools or clear information. This makes it hard for them to move their goods on time, grow their businesses, or compete in the market. Women and young traders are especially affected because they have fewer resources and support. Without a better system, many small businesses will continue to face these challenges.
Solution Overview:
Solution Overview

Our solution helps small and rural traders in Liberia move their goods faster and cheaper through customs and shipping. Many traders face delays and high costs because they don’t have clear information or easy ways to handle paperwork. We use simple digital tools and personal support to fix these problems.

How it works:
We guide traders step by step through the whole process of clearing goods and shipping. We help them prepare the right documents and explain customs rules in easy language. Traders get regular updates through mobile messages, so they know when to act and avoid delays. We also help them use fair prices and avoid extra fees.

Methodologies and technologies used:
We use tools that work on phones, like SMS and WhatsApp, because many traders don’t have computers or internet. We create simple checklists and forms that traders can follow to fill out customs paperwork correctly. Our system uses the “first-in, first-out” method, which means goods that arrive first get sent out first, making the process fair for everyone.

Partnerships and collaboration:
We work closely with customs offices, shipping companies, the Ministry of Commerce and Industry and port agents to make sure our traders get fast and fair service. We also team up with local business groups and community leaders to train traders, especially women and young people, on how to use our tools and understand trade rules. These partnerships help us fix problems quickly and lower costs for traders.
Solution Provider(s): Solution Providers:  Exclusive Logistics Liberia: This company supports small traders and Indigenous businesses by helping them with shipping and customs clearance. They guide clients through the complicated steps needed to move goods, making the process easier, faster, and fairer. They also provide advice on trade rules and help reduce extra costs or delays.  APM Terminals Liberia: This is the main company that manages cargo at Liberia’s largest port. They handle the loading and unloading of containers and goods from ships. Their work ensures that goods arrive and leave the port smoothly, which is important for traders to get their products on time.  MedTech Liberia: MedTech works under contract with the Liberia Revenue Authority (LRA). Their job is to check imported goods to make sure they meet safety and health standards. They also calculate the value of the goods and issue reports called the Clean Report of Findings (CRF) or Non-Negotiable Report of Findings (NNRF). These reports help determine how much customs duty should be paid and how the goods are classified for trade.  Global Tracking and Maritime Solution (GTMS): GTMS provides container tracking numbers (CTN) to all exporters and importers. This allows traders to track where their containers are during shipping, which helps them plan better and reduces the risk of lost or delayed shipments.  The Liberia Revenue Authority (LRA): The LRA is the government agency in charge of collecting taxes, including customs duties, in the trade sector. They oversee the proper collection of fees to support government services and ensure trade laws are followed.  Ministry of Commerce and Industry, Liberia: This government office creates and enforces trade policies. They work to make sure businesses operate fairly and have the support they need to grow. They also help improve trade environments by setting clear rules and promoting business development.  Local Business Groups: These are community organizations that support small and rural traders. They provide training on trade rules, help traders understand customs processes, and offer networking opportunities. Their work is important to help marginalized traders succeed in the market.
Implementation location(s): The solution is currently implemented in Liberia, mainly in Monrovia, including the port areas like Bushrod Island and surrounding communities where Exclusive Logistics Liberia operates.
Implementation timeline(s): The solution has been implemented since February 2021 and is ongoing.
Duration to pilot in a new geography: We started implementing the solution in February 2021, and it is still ongoing. To pilot the solution in a new area, we estimate it will take about 6 to 9 months. This time includes setting up local partnerships, training traders, and testing the digital tools and processes to make sure everything works well.
SDGs addressed: SDG 9 (Industry, Innovation, and Infrastructure);SDG 10 (Reduced Inequalities);SDG 8 (Decent Work and Economic Growth);
Desired impact:

Support Small and Indigenous Traders:
Exclusive Logistics Liberia aims to help small and Indigenous business owners clear their goods through customs without delays or unfair charges. Many of these traders face high fees, long waiting times, and a limited understanding of customs rules. We support them so they can save time, reduce costs, and run their businesses more smoothly.

Simplify the Customs and Shipping Process:
We guide traders through each step of the customs and port process using simple instructions and tools like checklists, WhatsApp messages, and one-on-one guidance. This reduces errors and confusion, especially for first-time importers.

Key Technologies Used by Exclusive Logistics Liberia

Exclusive Logistics Liberia uses simple and affordable technologies to help small and Indigenous traders move their goods through customs without delays or confusion. These tools help us organize documents, communicate with clients, and work better with government agencies.

ASYCUDA World System (LRA)

We use the ASYCUDA World system from the Liberia Revenue Authority (LRA) to process customs declarations. This system helps us submit and track all required trade and customs documents online. It makes the customs process faster, more transparent, and helps avoid errors or delays.

WhatsApp and SMS

We use WhatsApp and text messages to send quick updates to clients about their shipments, customs clearance progress, and any documents they need to provide. This makes communication faster and easier, especially for traders with basic phones.

Google Forms

We use Google Forms to collect important details from our clients, such as shipment information and contact data. This helps us prepare customs paperwork faster and with fewer mistakes.

Google Sheets and Microsoft Excel

We use spreadsheets to keep track of client information, customs steps, and shipping timelines. This makes our work more organized and helps us follow up on every shipment properly.

Google Drive and Dropbox

We use these tools to store and share important documents like invoices, waybills, and customs reports. Clients and team members can access these files anytime, which reduces the risk of lost paperwork.

These technologies allow us to offer a low-cost, efficient, and user-friendly service to clients, especially those in rural or underserved areas. As we grow, we plan to adopt more digital tools to improve our service quality and reach more traders across Liberia.
