Title: Malian School Information Software (MSIS)
Subtitle: The MSIS (Malian School Information Software) project is a major initiative by DigitAfrika, designed to modernize and optimize information management within Malian schools.
Problem Statement:
The surge in the number of private educational institutions in Mali, complementing the public network, highlights major challenges in managing their information systems (IS). These obstacles hinder administrative and pedagogical efficiency, directly impacting the quality of education.

The main difficulties identified are as follows:

- Administrative burden: Current administrative processes are often outdated, time-consuming, and poorly suited to the demands of modern management.
- Insufficient digital infrastructure: A glaring lack of adequate IT equipment, limited access to high-speed internet, and outdated network infrastructure impede any digitization efforts.
- Lack of technical skills : Mali faces a shortage of qualified IT professionals. Additionally, low adoption of digital tools by end-users compromises the deployment and effective use of IS.
- Data security vulnerabilities : Systems are generally exposed to cyberattacks, and compliance with personal data protection regulations is inadequate, exposing institutions to significant risks in terms of confidentiality and data integrity.

These challenges are compounded by issues of governance and organizational culture. In the public sector, the lack of a strategic vision for IS, cumbersome procedures, and resistance to change slow down modernization efforts. The reliability of collected data is also a concern, limiting the effectiveness of IS for decision-making. In the private sector, particularly among SMEs, the level of digitization remains very low, often due to a lack of financial resources and access to suitable funding.

In summary, the digital ecosystem of Malian educational institutions, both public and private, remains immature.
Solution Overview:
To overcome these challenges, DigitAfrika proposes three short-term solutions for partner educational institutions, centered around the following axes:

1. Development of an Integrated Digital Platform
To alleviate the administrative burden and optimize the management of educational institutions, DigitAfrika has developed a comprehensive digital solution. This platform aims to digitize all school management processes, from student enrollment to timetable and grade management. This will significantly reduce processing times for files and administrative procedures within our partner institutions under the MSIS project.

2. Establishment of Robust Digital Infrastructure
Improving the digital infrastructure of these educational institutions is essential. To achieve this, DigitAfrika will closely collaborate with them to establish robust digital infrastructure. This includes installing high-speed internet coverage (fiber optic) and acquiring suitable new IT equipment. These actions will lay the essential foundation for a successful transition to modern and accessible solutions.

3. Deployment and Continuous Monitoring of the Platform
Following the design phase, we will proceed with the deployment of the new school management platform. This step will be followed by a rigorous monitoring phase. During this period, DigitAfrika will closely monitor the performance of the new digital solution to proactively detect and address any potential system failures or bugs during its use by our partners. Our goal is to ensure optimal performance and smooth operation of the platform.

As MSIS is an application whose role will be to dematerialize all school management processes, the following players will be involved: students, parents, teachers and administration;
Solution Provider(s): Our main partners in the MSIS project are as follows :  Public and private educational institutions in Mali, the Government of the Republic of Mali, and local and international NGOs working in the field of education.
Implementation location(s): IfThe pilot phase of our digital solution is planned for this year in the Republic of Mali, more specifically in the region of Ségou and the city of Ségou. During this school year, we will work with a dozen schools to study the behavior of our digital solution and then proceed to scale it up in other regions of Mali in the years to come.
Implementation timeline(s): The pilot phase will begin in September 2025 and end in August 2026.
Duration to pilot in a new geography: The estimated duration of the pilot phase of our digital solution is one year. For the MSIS pilot phase, we plan to collaborate with around ten schools in the city of Ségou, Mali.
SDGs addressed: SDG 4 (Quality Education);SDG 9 (Industry, Innovation, and Infrastructure);
Desired impact: The main objective of the MSIS project is to develop and deploy a comprehensive centralized school management application. This digital solution aims to digitize all administrative and pedagogical processes related to school management, whether public or private. This significantly reduces information processing time and facilitates decision-making for learning.
Key technologies:
The key technologies used to build our platform are as follows:

- Frontend : HTML / CSS using the Bootstrap library.
- Backend: PHP using the Laravel framework and Ajax.
- Database: MySQL.
- Hosting: The new platform will be hosted on a cloud server to enable access by all establishments.
- Security: Authentication, data encryption.
Unique Characteristics:
What makes our digital solution unique and innovative is that all data from all institutions will be centralized in a single location, and this data is then analyzed in a dynamic dashboard to facilitate decision-making.  
It is the only solution that enables the management of all schools in Mali at a low cost.
Sustainable Change:
Thanks to the MSIS project, we anticipate the following results:
1. a significant reduction in information processing time within schools, thanks to the implementation of a single school management platform.
2. personalized support for our partners in setting up solid, appropriate IT infrastructures.
3. continuous monitoring of the use of our digital solution, to analyze its behavior, identify areas for improvement and make any necessary corrections.
Funding Sources: The MSIS application was developed with DigitAfrika's own resources and funds. For future implementations, we are counting on the support of institutions, NGOs and the Malian government to deploy this solution throughout Mali.
Primary thematic focus area: Inclusive Digital Innovation Skills & Entrepreneurial Talent Development
Summary: The MSIS (Malian School Information Software) project by DigitAfrika aims to digitize and centralize school management processes in Mali. It provides an integrated platform covering enrollment, timetables, grading, and reporting, while also upgrading digital infrastructure in schools. The pilot will begin in Ségou (2025–2026) with about 10 schools, with plans for nationwide rollout. It is designed to improve efficiency, data security, and decision-making across public and private education sectors.

Title: Limkokwing Innovation: Empowering Creative Leaders for Tomorrow’s World
Subtitle: Inspiring academic excellence and innovation, our university empowers students to become leaders and changemakers in a global society.
Problem Statement: Student entrepreneurs face challenges such as limited access to mentorship, funding, and hands-on experience, restricting their ability to launch innovative startups and thrive in a competitive market.
Solution Overview:
Our solution empowers student entrepreneurs by creating an integrated ecosystem that combines mentorship, practical training, and access to funding and digital tools. Through this platform, students develop real-world business skills and transform innovative ideas into viable startups.

How it works:

Mentorship & Coaching: Experienced entrepreneurs and industry experts provide guidance through workshops, one-on-one coaching, and networking events.

Practical Training: Hands-on modules covering business planning, digital marketing, financial management, and product development are integrated into the curriculum.

Access to Funding: A dedicated student startup fund and partnerships with angel investors and venture capitalists offer seed capital and growth opportunities.

Innovation Hub: A creative space equipped with cutting-edge digital tools and collaboration zones supports prototype development and teamwork.

Digital Platform: An online portal facilitates project submissions, peer collaboration, mentor matching, and resource sharing.

Methodologies and Technologies Used:

Design Thinking and Lean Startup methodologies to foster iterative innovation and customer-focused business models.

Use of collaborative software like Slack, Trello, and Google Workspace to enhance communication and project management.

Deployment of digital marketing tools (e.g., Canva, Mailchimp) and e-commerce platforms to support go-to-market strategies.

Access to cloud computing and AI-powered analytics to optimize product development and market research.

Partnerships and Collaboration Models:

Collaboration with local and international business incubators to provide extended support and exposure.

Strategic alliances with government entrepreneurship programs and NGOs to increase funding and outreach.

Partnership with Limkokwing’s Innovation Hub to leverage existing infrastructure and expertise.

Engagement with alumni entrepreneurs to build a strong mentorship network and foster a community of practice.
Solution Provider(s): Solution Provider(s):  Limkokwing University of Creative Technology — A globally recognized university known for fostering creativity, innovation, and entrepreneurship among students through cutting-edge programs. Sector: Education & Innovation.  Limkokwing Innovation Hub — The university’s dedicated innovation and incubation center, providing students with access to technology, mentorship, and collaborative spaces to develop and launch entrepreneurial ventures. Sector: Technology Incubation & Startup Support.
Implementation timeline(s): The solution operates on a continuous semester basis, restarting every 4-6 months aligned with the academic calendar. Each semester includes onboarding, training, mentorship, and project development phases, ensuring ongoing support and innovation opportunities for student entrepreneurs.
SDGs addressed: SDG 4 (Quality Education);SDG 8 (Decent Work and Economic Growth);SDG 9 (Industry, Innovation, and Infrastructure);
Desired impact:
Solution Objectives:

Empower student entrepreneurs with practical skills, mentorship, and resources to successfully launch and scale innovative startups.

Foster a vibrant entrepreneurial ecosystem within the university that encourages creativity, collaboration, and problem-solving.

Increase student-led startup creation and sustainability through access to funding and market opportunities.

Enhance employability and economic participation of graduates by equipping them with entrepreneurial mindsets and experience.

Key Achievements / Impacts:

Enabled the launch of over 50 student startups within the first two academic years.

Created 150+ mentorship connections between students and industry experts.

Facilitated access to seed funding totaling $100,000 for early-stage student ventures.

Increased student entrepreneur employment rate by 30% within one year of graduation.

Fostered a collaborative innovation community with participation from over 500 students annually.
Key technologies:
Cloud Computing: Enables scalable access to digital tools, collaboration platforms, and data storage for student projects and startups.

Artificial Intelligence (AI): Used for market analysis, customer insights, and personalized mentorship matching.

Collaboration Tools: Platforms like Slack, Trello, and Google Workspace facilitate teamwork, project management, and communication.

Digital Marketing Tools: Software such as Canva, Mailchimp, and social media analytics help students create and manage marketing campaigns.

E-commerce Platforms: Support online sales and business operations for student startups.

Learning Management Systems (LMS): Integrate entrepreneurship training modules and track student progress.

Prototyping Technologies: Access to 3D printing and design software within the Innovation Hub to create product prototypes.
Unique Characteristics:
Integrated Innovation Ecosystem: Combines academic learning, practical mentorship, funding access, and incubation under one roof—creating a seamless journey from idea to startup launch.

University-Driven Innovation Hub: Leverages Limkokwing’s dedicated Innovation Hub as a dynamic space equipped with cutting-edge technology and creative resources tailored specifically for student entrepreneurs.

Collaborative Partnership Model: Strong alliances with government bodies, local investors, and international tech hubs ensure diversified support, funding, and market access.

Flexible Semester-Based Program: Designed to align with academic cycles, allowing continuous onboarding and engagement that adapts to students’ schedules.

Mentorship Matching Powered by AI: Uses AI algorithms to pair students with mentors who best fit their industry focus, skill gaps, and business goals.

Funding Mechanism with Seed Capital and Investor Network: Unique combination of university seed funds plus access to an angel investor network accelerates startup growth.

Hands-On, Experiential Learning: Emphasis on real-world problem solving through design thinking and lean startup methodologies integrated into curriculum and innovation activities.
Sustainable Change:
Our solution fosters a lasting entrepreneurial culture by equipping students with the skills, mindset, and resources to create innovative businesses that address real-world challenges. By nurturing student entrepreneurs, we catalyze a ripple effect that strengthens local economies, drives job creation, and encourages continuous innovation.

Theory of Change:

Inputs: Access to education, mentorship, funding, and technology through Limkokwing’s Innovation Hub and partnerships.

Activities: Training programs, mentorship matching, startup incubation, and networking events integrated into the academic cycle.

Outputs: Increased number of student-led startups, enhanced entrepreneurial skills, and stronger support networks.

Outcomes: Graduates launch sustainable businesses, generate employment, and contribute to economic diversification.

Impact: A self-sustaining entrepreneurial ecosystem develops, driving systemic economic growth, social empowerment, and innovation across communities and sectors.
Primary thematic focus area: Inclusive Digital Innovation Skills & Entrepreneurial Talent Development
Summary: Limkokwing Innovation est une initiative universitaire au stade pilote (Q17) qui vise à transformer les étudiants en entrepreneurs en leur offrant un écosystème complet intégrant mentorat, formation pratique, fonds de démarrage et hub d’innovation (Q12, Q19, Q23). Déployé à Freetown, Sierra Leone (Q18), le programme a déjà soutenu la création de plus de 50 startups étudiantes, généré 150 connexions de mentorat et mobilisé 100 000 USD en financement initial (Q21). Le modèle, basé sur un calendrier académique semestriel (Q19), est innovant grâce à l’intégration universitaire directe et l’usage d’IA pour l’appariement des mentors (Q19, Q23). Bien que le potentiel de systémicité soit clair, le projet souffre d’une dépendance aux infrastructures universitaires et d’un manque de stratégie financière externe documentée (Q27).

Title: Rondpoint Numérique : connecter les talents africains à l’économie digitale
Subtitle: Une plateforme inclusive de formation, d’innovation et de commerce numérique pour les jeunes et les femmes d’Afrique centrale.
Problem Statement: En Afrique centrale, des millions de jeunes, femmes et micro-entrepreneurs sont exclus de l’économie numérique faute d’accès à la formation, aux outils et aux marchés. Cette fracture limite leur potentiel économique, renforce la pauvreté et empêche une participation équitable à l’économie mondiale.
Solution Overview:
Rondpoint Numérique est une plateforme hybride (en ligne et physique) portée par Rondpoint Tech, qui vise à démocratiser l'accès à l’économie numérique en formant, connectant et accompagnant les talents des zones rurales et semi-urbaines.
🔧 Fonctionnement :

Un espace numérique accessible via mobile, ordinateurs ou centres connectés (cybercafés solidaires).

Modules de formation certifiante (développement web, e-commerce, IA, cybersécurité).

Un mini-incubateur pour projets digitaux locaux.

Une marketplace permettant aux bénéficiaires de vendre leurs produits/services en ligne.


🧰 Technologies utilisées :

Progressive Web App (PWA) pour accès sans forte connectivité.

IA locale pour assistant vocal en langues locales.

Système d’apprentissage personnalisé basé sur les données (LXP).


🤝 Partenariats :

Université de Maroua, Université de Doba

Cybercafés communautaires

Coopératives féminines locales

Associations étudiantes, ONG de jeunesse, startups africaines
Solution Provider(s): Rondpoint Tech (startup tech/éducation), Université de Maroua (académie), Université de Doba, Coopérative des Femmes de Doba, Association des Jeunes pour la Paix (société civile)
Duration to pilot in a new geography: 3 à 6 mois (selon les partenariats locaux disponibles)
SDGs addressed: SDG 4 (Quality Education);SDG 8 (Decent Work and Economic Growth);SDG 10 (Reduced Inequalities);
Desired impact:
Objectifs :

Former 10 000 jeunes et femmes d’ici 2026.

Créer 1 000 emplois directs et 3 000 indirects via le digital.

Augmenter de 50 % les revenus des micro-entrepreneurs accompagnés.


📊 Impacts à ce jour :

1 200 jeunes formés (dont 40 % de femmes)

2 centres numériques communautaires créés

60 projets incubés

Lancement d’un “marché vert digital” pour produits agroécologiques
Key technologies:
Intelligence artificielle (assistant vocal multilingue)

Progressive Web App (optimisée pour mobile & connexion faible)

Open-source LMS (Moodle, WordPress)

Chatbots éducatifs & commerce WhatsApp Business
Unique Characteristics:
Modèle hybride (plateforme numérique + espace physique)

Ancrage local et communautaire (formateurs issus du milieu)

Inclusivité linguistique et technologique (traduction, accès USSD)

Auto-financement partiel par les services premium et la marketplace

Approche de micro-certification + accompagnement post-formation
Sustainable Change:
Rondpoint Numérique transforme la dynamique locale : de consommateurs passifs, les jeunes deviennent acteurs du numérique local.

Notre théorie du changement repose sur :

Former → Connecter → Accompagner → Autonomiser.
En renforçant les capacités numériques locales, nous changeons durablement la trajectoire économique de communautés exclues.


Ce modèle est réplicable dans toutes les zones rurales africaines, avec un faible coût d’adaptation. Il catalyse la création de micro-économies digitales durables et inclusives.
Funding Sources:
Notre solution a été principalement financée à travers :

Autofinancement par Rondpoint Tech, notamment via les revenus issus des formations, services numériques et ventes de matériel.

Petites contributions communautaires (ex. : frais de participation symboliques aux formations).

Soutien logistique en nature de la part de l’Université de Maroua (accès aux locaux, matériel) et de cybercafés partenaires.

Appuis ponctuels de partenaires associatifs et ONG locales pour la mobilisation communautaire.


Nous sommes actuellement en recherche de partenariats techniques et financiers pour l’extension régionale de la solution.
Testimonials and Endorsements:

— Mazina didam calvin, entrepreneure à Doba, Tchad

📢 « Les formations que j’ai suivies avec Rondpoint m’ont permis de décrocher un stage dans une entreprise numérique à Maroua. Je n’avais aucune compétence avant cela. »
— Hamadou Issa, étudiant formé en développement web

📢 « Ce projet change réellement les choses. Il donne aux jeunes de notre région des outils concrets pour s’en sortir. C’est une révolution silencieuse. »
— Dr. Barka Mahamat, Enseignant à l’Université de Maroua
Further comments/feedback:
Ce questionnaire est bien structuré et pertinent. Il met en valeur les initiatives locales et les solutions africaines adaptées aux réalités de terrain. Nous espérons que davantage de projets portés par des jeunes innovateurs africains recevront une reconnaissance mondiale.

Nous suggérons d’ajouter à l’avenir une option permettant de co-construire des prototypes avec les agences de l’ONU, pour faciliter les synergies Nord-Sud et Sud-Sud.

Merci pour cette opportunité d’amplifier notre impact.
Primary thematic focus area: Inclusive Digital Innovation Skills & Entrepreneurial Talent Development
Summary: Rondpoint Numérique est une plateforme hybride (en ligne et centres physiques) déployée au Cameroun (Maroua) et au Tchad (Doba), visant à réduire la fracture numérique en Afrique centrale (Q11, Q18). Depuis 2021 (Q19), elle offre des formations certifiantes (web, IA, cybersécurité), un mini-incubateur et une marketplace pour micro-entrepreneurs (Q12). À ce jour, 1 200 jeunes formés (dont 40 % de femmes), 60 projets incubés et 2 centres numériques ouverts (Q21). La solution repose sur des technologies adaptées aux faibles connexions : Progressive Web App, assistant vocal IA multilingue, chatbots éducatifs et LMS open source (Q20). Son modèle repose sur un ancrage communautaire, l’inclusion linguistique et un co-financement via services premium et marketplace (Q22, Q27).

Title: Empowering Eastern Visayas through Digital Intelligence in Production and Education
Subtitle: Empowering people and industries in Eastern Visayas through digital intelligence, smart manufacturing, and technical education to promote inclusive growth and Industry 4.0 readiness.
Problem Statement: The solution addresses key challenges such as the lack of access to modern Industry 4.0 technologies, limited digital skills among students and workers, outdated technical education, and weak industry-academe linkages. These issues hinder inclusive economic growth and industrial competitiveness in Eastern Visayas, particularly for marginalized communities and MSMEs.
Solution Overview:
Detailed Description of How the Solution Works
The solution empowers people and processes in Eastern Visayas by integrating digital intelligence and smart manufacturing systems into technical and vocational education. The centerpiece is the establishment of a Digital Intelligence and Industry 4.0 Learning Hub at Eastern Visayas State University (EVSU), which serves as a regional training and innovation center.

Through this hub, students, faculty, and local industries gain hands-on experience with smart production technologies using Festo Didactic’s advanced cyber-physical systems. The training programs are designed to simulate real-world manufacturing environments, enabling participants to understand, apply, and innovate with Industry 4.0 principles such as automation, data-driven decision-making, and human-machine collaboration.

The hub also serves as a capacity-building platform for local MSMEs, women, and out-of-school youth, promoting inclusive participation in the digital economy. All learning modules are aligned with international certification standards, ensuring global relevance and local impact.

Methodologies and Technologies Used
Methodologies:
Competency-Based Technical Education: Focused on practical application and skill mastery.
Blended Learning: Combines face-to-face hands-on training with digital content and simulation-based instruction.
Train-the-Trainer Programs: Builds long-term capacity among faculty and local trainers.
Experiential Learning: Real-time simulations and project-based learning using smart systems.
Community Outreach & MSME Extension: Delivers targeted programs for disadvantaged groups.
Technologies:
Festo Didactic Cyber-Physical Factory (CP Factory): A modular training and simulation system replicating Industry 4.0 environments.
Digital Twins: Virtual replicas of manufacturing processes for safe and repeatable training.
Industrial Internet of Things (IIoT): Integration of sensors and connected systems for real-time monitoring and automation.
PLC (Programmable Logic Controllers): Used for automation and control training.
AI and Data Analytics Modules: For predictive maintenance, quality control, and smart decision-making.

Partnerships and Collaboration Models
1. Eastern Visayas State University (EVSU)
Project host and lead implementer
Provides physical infrastructure, administrative support, and teaching staff
Facilitates local stakeholder engagement and sustainability planning

2. United Nations Industrial Development Organization (UNIDO)
Technical cooperation and implementation guidance
Resource mobilization and global knowledge-sharing
Monitoring, evaluation, and alignment with SDG and Global Digital Compact targets

3. Festo Didactic SE
Technology partner supplying smart manufacturing training systems
Provides faculty training, curriculum co-development, and international certification programs
Ensures system scalability and continuous innovation

4. Local Government Units and Industry Partners (MSMEs, Chambers of Commerce, etc.)
Beneficiaries of skills development and innovation support
Co-develop applied projects and offer internship pathways for students
May co-invest in training for their workforce

5. National Government Agencies (e.g., TESDA, DTI, CHED)
Support for policy alignment, standards, and possible funding extensions
Accreditation and scaling of the model across other regions
Solution Provider(s): Eastern Visayas State University (EVSU) – A leading state university in the Philippines, specializing in engineering, technology, and applied sciences. Sector: Higher Education and Research  United Nations Industrial Development Organization (UNIDO) – A specialized UN agency promoting inclusive and sustainable industrial development. Sector: International Development and Industrial Cooperation  Festo Didactic SE – A global leader in industrial education and training systems, focused on automation and technical learning solutions. Sector: Industrial Technology and Technical Education  Provincial Government of Leyte – The local government authority responsible for development planning, support services, and community engagement in Leyte province. Sector: Local Governance and Public Administration  Micro, Small, and Medium Enterprises (MSMEs) in Eastern Visayas – Regional businesses involved in manufacturing, services, and trade that benefit from workforce upskilling and technological support. Sector: Private Sector and Local Industry  Technical Education and Skills Development Authority (TESDA) – The national government agency tasked with managing and supervising technical education and skills development in the Philippines. Sector: Workforce Development and Vocational Training  Department of Trade and Industry (DTI) – The government agency promoting trade, industry, and entrepreneurship development. Sector: Economic Development and Industry Support  Commission on Higher Education (CHED) – The national regulatory body overseeing higher education institutions and programs in the Philippines. Sector: Higher Education Policy and Governance
Duration to pilot in a new geography: 12 months
SDGs addressed: SDG 4 (Quality Education);SDG 8 (Decent Work and Economic Growth);SDG 9 (Industry, Innovation, and Infrastructure);
Desired impact:
Desired Impact of the Solution:
The solution aims to catalyze inclusive industrial growth and workforce transformation in Eastern Visayas through digital intelligence and smart technical education. It seeks to bridge the digital divide, empower local industries, and develop a future-ready workforce aligned with global Industry 4.0 standards. This will contribute to sustainable development, regional competitiveness, and poverty reduction in a historically underserved region.

Solution Objectives:
(a) Establish a regional Digital Intelligence and Industry 4.0 Learning Hub at Eastern Visayas State University (EVSU) to train students, faculty, and MSMEs in advanced production and automation systems.
(b) Upskill at least 300 students and 50 faculty members annually through hands-on training in smart manufacturing, IoT, and digital twin technologies.
(c) Empower 100 MSME workers, women, and out-of-school youth per year through targeted digital skills and entrepreneurship programs.
(d) Promote innovation and industry-academe collaboration by developing applied learning projects and partnerships with local businesses.
(e) Support the region’s transition to a knowledge-based, tech-driven economy, aligned with the Sustainable Development Goals (SDGs).

Key Achievements or Impacts (Quantifiable Targets):
1. Establishment of 1 fully equipped Industry 4.0 learning lab featuring Festo Didactic cyber-physical systems, digital twin platforms, and IIoT infrastructure.
2. 300+ students trained annually in digital manufacturing and automation skills.
3. 50+ faculty members upskilled and certified as trainers in smart factory operations and digital pedagogy.
4. 100 MSME technicians, women, and youth empowered per year through targeted training and inclusion programs.
5. At least 10 collaborative projects annually between EVSU and local businesses to apply Industry 4.0 technologies in real-world settings.
6. Potential 15–25% increase in MSME productivity through improved digital process integration.
7. Job creation in the region, with graduates equipped for roles in manufacturing, automation, and digital services sectors.
8. Improved regional competitiveness, positioning Eastern Visayas as a hub for smart technical education in the Visayas.
Key technologies:
The solution leverages advanced Industry 4.0 technologies to modernize technical education and production systems in Eastern Visayas. These technologies simulate smart manufacturing environments and enable learners to develop real-world competencies in digital intelligence.

1. Cyber-Physical Systems (CPS) – Festo CP Factory
A modular, flexible factory simulation system that replicates a real smart production line.
Integrates mechanical systems with sensors, actuators, and software for process control and monitoring.
Used for hands-on learning in mechatronics, logistics, and automation.

2. Industrial Internet of Things (IIoT)
Connects machines, sensors, and devices to collect and exchange production data in real time.
Enables remote monitoring, process optimization, and predictive maintenance in smart factories.

3. Programmable Logic Controllers (PLC)
Industrial-grade control systems used to automate machinery and factory processes.
Learners gain skills in PLC programming, troubleshooting, and industrial automation.

4. Digital Twin Technology
Virtual replicas of physical systems that allow users to simulate, analyze, and optimize production processes.
Enhances learning by enabling experimentation in a risk-free digital environment.

5. Artificial Intelligence (AI) and Data Analytics
Applied in smart factory environments for pattern recognition, process optimization, and decision-making.
Used in training modules related to predictive quality control, energy management, and fault detection.

6. Human-Machine Interfaces (HMI)
Interfaces that allow operators to interact with machines via graphical control systems.
Builds competency in monitoring, diagnostics, and human-centered automation.
Unique Characteristics:
This solution stands out for its integrated approach to inclusive digital transformation, combining cutting-edge technologies with innovative partnerships, education models, and capacity-building strategies tailored to underserved regions like Eastern Visayas. Below are its key differentiators:

1. Education–Industry–Development Partnership Model
The solution is built on a Triple Helix collaboration between academia (EVSU), international development (UNIDO), and industry (Festo Didactic SE).
This model ensures that training is demand-driven, aligned with real industry needs, and globally benchmarked, while also addressing local socio-economic gaps.

2. Inclusive and Scalable Talent Development Framework
Prioritizes women, MSMEs, and out-of-school youth, ensuring that the benefits of Industry 4.0 are accessible to disadvantaged and underrepresented groups.
Uses a train-the-trainer model, enabling sustainable and scalable replication across other universities and regions in the Philippines.

3. Application of Real-World Industry 4.0 Technologies in Education
Unlike conventional TVET programs, this solution fully integrates operational cyber-physical systems, IoT, digital twins, and AI into classroom instruction and hands-on training.
Learners simulate and optimize real production environments, gaining practical, globally competitive skills.

4. Regional Innovation Hub with MSME Linkage
The learning center at EVSU serves not only as an academic facility but also as a technical extension hub for local MSMEs, offering support in digitalization, process optimization, and workforce training.
Facilitates applied research and co-developed projects that directly contribute to local economic development.

5. Alignment with Global Frameworks and Local Needs
Aligns with the UN’s Global Digital Compact Objective 2 (expanding inclusion in the digital economy), SDGs, and the Philippine national innovation and digital economy agendas.
Designed to be regionally adaptive while maintaining global quality standards, thanks to Festo’s internationally recognized training systems and UNIDO’s development expertise.

6. Potential for Blended Financing and Public–Private Investment
Opens opportunities for blended finance models, combining government investment (e.g., from CHED, DTI, or TESDA), development aid (via UNIDO), and private sector co-financing (e.g., from partner industries or tech donors).
This model reduces dependency on a single funding source and enhances long-term sustainability.
Sustainable Change:
The solution contributes to sustainable, systemic change by embedding digital intelligence and Industry 4.0 competencies into the core of Eastern Visayas' technical education and local production systems. It transforms not only the way people learn and work, but also how institutions, industries, and communities engage with the digital economy—enabling long-term economic inclusion and resilience.

Theory of Change: Pathway to Impact
1. Inputs / Enablers
Deployment of Festo Didactic cyber-physical systems and digital learning tools
Technical and strategic support from UNIDO
Local commitment and infrastructure from EVSU
Engagement from government (TESDA, CHED, DTI) and MSMEs
Inclusive program design targeting marginalized groups

2. Activities
Establishment of a Digital Intelligence & Industry 4.0 Learning Hub
Capacity-building for faculty, students, MSMEs, women, and out-of-school youth
Development of applied, competency-based learning modules
Implementation of collaborative projects between EVSU and local industries
Outreach and technical support to MSMEs in digital adoption

3. Outputs
1 fully operational smart training center
300+ students and 50+ faculty trained annually
100+ MSME workers, women, and youth upskilled yearly
Active innovation and extension services delivered to MSMEs
Cross-sector knowledge sharing and model replication

4. Immediate Outcomes
Enhanced workforce readiness in Industry 4.0
Improved productivity and competitiveness of local MSMEs
Strengthened linkages between academia and industry
More inclusive access to digital technologies and careers

5. Long-Term Impact
Sustainable, inclusive industrial growth in Eastern Visayas
A resilient, digitally competent workforce adaptable to future disruptions
Reduced regional inequality in digital education and economic participation
Scalable model that can be replicated in other underserved regions of the Philippines and beyond

Systemic Change Drivers
Institutionalization: EVSU embeds the training system into formal curricula, ensuring ongoing capacity-building beyond the initial intervention.

Policy Integration: National agencies (TESDA, CHED, DTI) can adopt and scale the approach through public policy and funding.

Industry Engagement: MSMEs become not just beneficiaries but collaborators in shaping talent pipelines and innovation projects.

Social Inclusion: Targeting women, youth, and marginalized communities fosters equity, creating a digitally empowered society, not just a skilled workforce.

Title: Empowering Rural Women through Sustainable Fashion and Digital Access
Subtitle: Eco Artisan connects marginalized women to digital markets through eco-conscious entrepreneurship.
Problem Statement: In Pakistan’s remote Gilgit-Baltistan region, women face limited access to formal employment, digital infrastructure, and economic independence. Post-flood recovery efforts have overlooked long-term, inclusive economic empowerment, particularly for rural women with no access to mainstream marketplaces.
Solution Overview: Eco Artisan is a women-led social enterprise that transforms textile waste into sustainable fashion while empowering rural women, particularly those affected by floods and unemployed artisans, with digital literacy, eco-entrepreneurship, and ethical production skills. The initiative addresses both economic exclusion and digital marginalization by providing hands-on training in upcycling, sustainable fashion design, product photography, content creation, and online storytelling. Women are equipped to showcase and sell their products using digital platforms, such as Instagram, Facebook, and WhatsApp, thereby creating new income streams and market access in previously disconnected regions. Eco Artisan also collaborates with other youth-led organizations, including Green Army Pakistan, to expand the impact through climate awareness campaigns, SDG education, and joint community engagement programs. Together, these efforts form a holistic, scalable model that bridges the digital economic divide while promoting gender equity and environmental sustainability.
Solution Provider(s): Eco Artisan – A women-led social enterprise working in the sustainable fashion and social entrepreneurship sector, empowering rural and flood-affected women through digital literacy, upcycling, and market access. Green Army Pakistan – A youth-led climate action group promoting environmental awareness, SDG advocacy, and community mobilization in Pakistan. IFRC Limitless Academy – An initiative by the International Federation of Red Cross and Red Crescent Societies that provided funding and innovation support to Eco Artisan. ARROW (Asia-Pacific Resource and Research Centre for Women) – A regional advocacy organization that funded Eco Artisan’s representation at the APFSD Youth Forum in Bangkok, Thailand, amplifying young women’s voices in sustainable development. IDEAS (Institute of Development and Economic Alternatives) – A research and policy organization that supported Eco Artisan’s participation in the Women Economic Conference in Sri Lanka, promoting inclusive economic policies and youth leadership.
Implementation location(s): Gilgit-Baltistan, Pakistan — Specifically in the Skardu and Ghanche districts, where the initiative has trained and engaged flood-affected and rural women artisans. Outreach and digital promotion are also managed from Rawalpindi and Chakwal, supporting coordination and scaling.
Implementation timeline(s): August 2021 – Present (Ongoing)  The solution was launched in August 2021 and has been continuously evolving through training programs, digital campaigns, international partnerships, and on-ground implementation in Gilgit-Baltistan and beyond.
Duration to pilot in a new geography: 4 to 6 months  This duration includes initial community assessment, partnership development, recruitment and training of local women, setup of digital infrastructure, and the launch of pilot production and marketing through online platforms.
SDGs addressed: SDG 5 (Gender Equality);SDG 8 (Decent Work and Economic Growth);SDG 13 (Climate Action);
Desired impact: The primary objective of Eco Artisan is to empower marginalized women—particularly in flood-affected and remote areas by equipping them with digital literacy, sustainable fashion skills, and entrepreneurial tools to access and thrive in the digital economy. The solution aims to create climate-resilient livelihoods by transforming textile waste into eco-friendly products while simultaneously promoting gender equality and circular economy principles. Since its inception in August 2021, Eco Artisan has trained and engaged over 50 women artisans, generated over $10,000 in sustainable product sales, and improved financial independence for nearly 30% of its participants. The initiative has also reduced textile waste by repurposing discarded materials into sellable fashion items, contributing to responsible consumption and production. By integrating local talent with digital tools and global platforms, Eco Artisan seeks to create inclusive, long-term impact through economic empowerment, climate action, and social innovation.
Key technologies: Eco Artisan primarily leverages accessible and low-cost digital technologies to empower women artisans in remote areas. These include smartphones, social media platforms (such as Instagram, Facebook, and WhatsApp) for marketing and outreach, and Canva for designing promotional content. Training also involves the use of digital photography tools, Google Workspace, and video conferencing apps like Zoom for virtual mentorship and collaboration. While the solution currently focuses on simple, user-friendly technologies suitable for low-connectivity areas, it is designed to scale using e-commerce tools and possibly integrate AI-driven content optimization and mobile commerce platforms in future phases.
Unique Characteristics: Eco Artisan stands out through its intersectional approach that combines sustainable fashion, women’s empowerment, and digital inclusion in climate-affected, underserved regions. Unlike conventional models, Eco Artisan uses a community-led business model that reinvests earnings into local skill-building and capacity development. The initiative operates with minimal infrastructure, relying on accessible digital tools to bridge rural artisans with global consumers making it highly adaptable and scalable in low-resource settings. Its partnerships with youth-led climate organizations, educational institutions, and global platforms such as the IFRC Limitless Academy and APFSD Youth Forum allow for cross-sector collaboration that amplifies reach and credibility. The model’s uniqueness also lies in empowering women as both producers and digital entrepreneurs, fostering ownership, confidence, and sustainability from the ground up.
Sustainable Change: Eco Artisan contributes to sustainable, systemic change by addressing the root causes of economic and digital exclusion among women in climate-vulnerable regions. By providing women with skills in sustainable fashion, digital literacy, and entrepreneurship, the solution builds long-term capacity and resilience within communities. The desired follow-on effects include the creation of self-sustaining micro-enterprises, increased participation of women in the digital economy, and intergenerational knowledge transfer, where trained women become mentors for others in their communities. As women gain income and confidence, local attitudes toward gender roles begin to shift, fostering a more inclusive socio-economic environment. On a broader level, the replication of this model in other marginalized areas can contribute to a network of eco-conscious, digitally connected women entrepreneurs, driving grassroots innovation, climate action, and sustainable economic growth across regions.
Primary thematic focus area: Inclusive Digital Innovation Skills & Entrepreneurial Talent Development
Summary: Eco Artisan est une entreprise sociale dirigée par des femmes au Pakistan, qui combine mode durable et inclusion numérique pour autonomiser les femmes rurales et sinistrées par les inondations. Le projet forme les artisanes à l’upcycling textile, au design éthique, à la photographie produit, à la narration numérique et à la vente via les réseaux sociaux. Depuis 2021, il a formé plus de 50 femmes, généré plus de 10 000 USD de ventes et favorisé l’indépendance financière de 30% des participantes. L’initiative repose sur des outils accessibles (smartphones, WhatsApp, Instagram, Canva) et des partenariats avec des ONG et plateformes régionales, créant un modèle scalable d’économie circulaire et inclusive (Q11, Q13, Q17).

Title: Connecting Rural Schools to the Internet via Starlink for Digital Education Access
Subtitle: Providing high-speed Internet to rural schools in South Kivu to enhance digital equity, improve educational governance, and strengthen teaching and learning quality.
Problem Statement: Most rural schools in South Kivu lack Internet access, preventing students and teachers from reaching quality educational resources and information. This digital divide worsens education inequality and hinders the development of data-based planning and school management systems.
Solution Overview:
The solution aims to connect school sub-divisions and educational inspectorates in South Kivu to high-speed Internet using Starlink satellite technology. This connectivity will enable:

Stable Internet in remote, underserved areas

A centralized digital database for schools and the Ministry of Primary, Secondary, and Technical Education (EPST)

Teacher training in digital literacy and tools

Integration of local data into national school governance systems
Solution Provider(s): Satellite Internet (Starlink)  Cloud-based educational data management platforms  Low-power local Wi-Fi networks  Offline-capable digital learning resources.  Collaboration with provincial education authorities  Engagement with local communities and traditional leaders  Partnerships with technical service providers and donors
Implementation location(s): South Kivu Province, Democratic Republic of Congo – Kabare, Walungu and Kalehe territories (targeted school inspectorates)
Implementation timeline(s): Preparation Phase: January – August 2026. Pilot Launch: Planned for September 2026
Duration to pilot in a new geography: 4 to 6 months, including local assessment, technical deployment, training, and initial data collection
SDGs addressed: SDG 4 (Quality Education);SDG 9 (Industry, Innovation, and Infrastructure);SDG 10 (Reduced Inequalities);
Desired impact:
Improve access to digital education in underserved rural areas

Centralize educational data to strengthen governance

Reduce the rural-urban digital divide
Key technologies:
15 inspectorates connected

Indirect Internet access to over 500 schools

Improved education planning and monitoring

150+ teachers trained in digital tools
Unique Characteristics:
Use of Starlink to overcome telecom infrastructure limitations

Full integration with Ministry of Education governance systems

Community-driven approach with ecosystem focus (tech, governance, training)

High scalability and replicability potential across other rural regions
Sustainable Change: This solution lays the foundation for a digitally connected, modern school system in rural areas. It enables evidence-based planning, real-time school monitoring, improved teacher capacity, and equitable access to knowledge. It supports systemic transformation in rural education through connectivity, innovation, and data integration – with potential ripple effects in gender inclusion, youth skills development, and community resilience.
Funding Sources: Our solution has been primarily funded through internal contributions from Kivu Kwetu asbl, local community fundraising, and in-kind support from partners, including local education authorities and IT volunteers. We are currently seeking additional funding from international donors and digital inclusion programs to scale the solution across all sub-divisions of the EPST in South Kivu.
Testimonials and Endorsements:
"Connecting our school to the internet has transformed the way we teach and learn. Teachers can now access updated resources, and students are more motivated than ever."
– Mr. Jean-Paul, Headmaster, EPST Kabare Sub-division

"This project gives hope to rural children who were left behind. With online access, we now feel part of the global learning community."
– Aline M., student, Walungu
Further comments/feedback: Thank you for this opportunity to showcase grassroots innovations from underserved regions. The questionnaire was well-structured and inclusive. We suggest integrating more space for visual demonstrations (e.g., uploading files) and allowing offline submissions to accommodate applicants from regions with unstable connectivity—like the one our solution aims to support.
Primary thematic focus area: Inclusive Digital Innovation Skills & Entrepreneurial Talent Development
Summary: This solution proposes connecting rural schools in South Kivu to the internet via Starlink, enabling data-driven governance and improved teaching capacity (Q13). A strength is its integration with Ministry of Education systems and direct impact on over 500 schools and 150 teachers (Q22). A weakness is that funding relies mainly on internal contributions and community fundraising, with limited secured external support (Q27).

Title: Building Trust in Africa-Europe B2B Partnerships
Subtitle: Omedema is a digital platform using AI-driven matching and blockchain-secured contracts to connect European businesses with African freelancers and SMEs, enabling trusted, high-impact B2B partnerships.
Problem Statement: European companies face high entry barriers in African markets due to fragmented networks, unreliable partner information, and complex contract processes, while African freelancers and SMEs struggle to access vetted international opportunities and fair, secure engagements. Omedema addresses these gaps by offering a unified, trust-by-design platform that streamlines partner discovery, verification, and contract execution.
Solution Overview: Omedema is a modular, AI- and blockchain-powered platform that connects European buyers with vetted African freelancers and SMEs, prioritizing projects with strong environmental and social impact. Our AI matching engine weights ESG credentials alongside skills and sector fit, surfacing “green” opportunities in clean tech, circular economy and resource-efficient initiatives. Local partners validate sustainability claims, ensure transparent and milestone-based collaborations.
Solution Provider(s): By partnering with regional green incubators, training providers and impact investors, Omedema cultivates a community committed to low-carbon, inclusive growth—enabling scalable, trust-by-design cooperation for sustainable development.
Duration to pilot in a new geography: 1 year
SDGs addressed: SDG 10 (Reduced Inequalities);SDG 9 (Industry, Innovation, and Infrastructure);SDG 17 (Partnerships for the Goals);
Desired impact: Omedema aims to (1) lower market-entry barriers for European buyers and African providers by streamlining partner discovery and validation; (2) accelerate the transition to sustainable business by prioritizing clean-tech, circular-economy, and low-carbon projects; and (3) drive inclusive economic empowerment for freelancers and SMEs—especially women and youth—through secure, transparent collaborations. the solution is under MVP
Key technologies: Omedema combines AI-driven matching, permissioned-blockchain smart contracts, and a open APIs.
Unique Characteristics: Omedema’s hybrid model uniquely combines AI-powered matching with local partner validation, underpinned by blockchain-enabled smart contracts that automate ESG-aligned milestones. Its modular microservices and open-API design allow rapid localization and integration of value-added services, while a success-based fee structure reinvests in training and green-tech capacity. Anchored by partnerships with chambers of commerce, incubators, and legal and assessment experts, this ecosystem ensures credible, scalable, trust-by-design collaborations across borders.
Sustainable Change: Omedema’s Theory of Change starts with lowering entry barriers and building local capacity: by vetting and matching SMEs and freelancers to quality opportunities, we generate reliable early wins that build trust. As users succeed, network effects accelerate platform adoption, increasing transaction volume and attracting impact-focused investors. This growth funds reinvestment in training and green‐tech partnerships, which strengthens skills and embeds sustainability practices. Over time, a self-sustaining ecosystem emerges—local businesses scale, cross-border value chains deepen, and regional policy makers recognize the platform as a model for inclusive, low-carbon economic development—catalyzing systemic shifts toward resilient, equitable markets.
Funding Sources: Omedema’s funding strategy combines innovation-focused grants (Bpifrance, France 2030, ADEME, Horizon Europe, AFD/FASEP), regional development and trust-fund programs
Testimonials and Endorsements: www.omedema.com
Primary thematic focus area: MSME Empowerment & Local Digital Innovation
Summary: Omedema est une plateforme numérique B2B qui connecte des entreprises européennes avec des freelances et PME africaines via un système de mise en relation alimenté par l’IA et des contrats intelligents sécurisés par blockchain. La solution réduit les barrières d’entrée, vérifie les partenaires et priorise les projets à impact environnemental et social positif (Q12, Q13).

Title: Green Future Skills: Empowering Jordan's Youth & Women.
Subtitle: Empowering Jordanian youth and women with green skills in renewable energy and sustainable agriculture to combat unemployment and environmental challenges, creating a sustainable economy
Problem Statement: this project addresses huge environmental and economic challenges in Jordan, which is the high unemployment rate among youth and women, particularly in underprivileged areas. This is happening alongside a severe scarcity of water resources, a decline in agricultural land quality, and rising energy costs. The project aims to tackle these problems by connecting sustainable solutions with labor market needs, thereby creating economic opportunities within the growing "green economy"
Solution Overview:
The "Green Future Skills" program is a 12-month initiative that addresses high unemployment among Jordanian youth and women and refugees, as well as the country's environmental and economic challenges. The program works by providing specialized vocational training in renewable energy and sustainable agriculture. 

The project aims to train 200 young men and women, with a 50% female participation rate, between the ages of 18 and 30. The program focuses on less-developed governorates in Jordan, with a target of 60 to 70 trainees per governorate. The training is a blend of technical skills, such as installing and maintaining solar energy systems and using water-saving irrigation techniques, and soft skills like entrepreneurship and digital literacy. As a practical component, trainees will implement 10 small community projects, such as installing solar systems or creating home gardens.

Methodologies and Technologies Used
The project's methodology is a combination of theoretical and practical training.

Curriculum Development: Training curricula will be prepared in collaboration with experts.

Technical Training: The technical training includes courses on photovoltaic solar energy systems (installation, operation, and maintenance) and sustainable agriculture techniques, including water harvesting.

Practical Application: Participants will apply their learned skills through practical projects in local communities. This hands-on experience is a key part of the program.

Soft Skills Integration: The program includes workshops on entrepreneurship, project management, and digital skills to enhance the employability and career prospects of the trainees.

Partnerships and Collaboration Models
The program emphasizes building a network of partnerships to ensure the long-term success of the beneficiaries.

Training & Employment: The project aims to build a network of partnerships between graduates and local companies and NGOs. This collaboration will facilitate job placement and networking opportunities for trainees.

Job Fairs: The project will organize job fairs and meetings to connect graduates with potential employers.

Mentorship: The program will provide guidance and mentorship for participants who are interested in starting their own projects.
Solution Provider(s): the sole solution provider is MAP Canada - Jordan Office
Duration to pilot in a new geography: The estimated time to implement the "Green Future Skills" program is 12 months. The project is designed to be implemented over this period, covering all three phases: Preparation and Planning (Months 1-2) , Training and Capacity Building (Months 3-9) , and Networking and Employment (Months 10-12)
SDGs addressed: SDG 8 (Decent Work and Economic Growth);SDG 5 (Gender Equality);SDG 4 (Quality Education);
Desired impact:
To empower young people and women in Jordan both economically and socially. This will be achieved by providing them with specialized technical skills in two key sectors: renewable energy and sustainable agriculture.

The specific, quantifiable objectives of the project are:

To train 200 young people, with 50% being female, between the ages of 18 and 30 in solar energy and organic farming skills within 12 months.

To implement 10 small community projects, such as installing solar systems for community centers or creating home gardens with water-saving irrigation, as a part of the practical training.

To build a partnership network between graduates, local companies, and NGOs to make it easier for trainees to find jobs and connect with others in the field.

Key Achievements and Impacts
The project aims to achieve the following key results and impacts:

Employment and Economic Growth: The program is expected to empower 200 individuals with in-demand technical skills, which should increase their opportunities for employment and income. It also seeks to encourage entrepreneurship within the "green sector".

Community and Environmental Impact: The project will implement 10 community-based projects as part of the training, which will provide hands-on experience and benefit local communities. The project also aims to raise community awareness of sustainable solutions. 
While specific numbers for GHG reductions or energy savings are not provided, the focus on renewable energy and sustainable agriculture implies a positive environmental impact
Key technologies:
The project's key technologies are not advanced digital technologies like AI, IoT, or blockchain. Instead, the solution focuses on practical, hands-on technologies related to renewable energy and sustainable agriculture.

Renewable Energy Technology: The project will train participants on the installation, operation, and maintenance of photovoltaic (PV) solar energy systems.

Sustainable Agriculture Technology: Trainees will learn sustainable agriculture techniques and water harvesting.

Digital Skills: The training also includes workshops on digital skills.
Unique Characteristics:
Focus on Underserved Populations and Regions
The program specifically targets unemployed or job-seeking Jordanian and refugee youth and women between the ages of 18 and 30. It intentionally focuses on less-developed governorates in Jordan, such as the southern or eastern regions, to ensure a more equitable distribution of opportunities.

Holistic Training Model
The training goes beyond just technical skills. While it provides specialized courses in 

photovoltaic solar energy systems and sustainable agriculture , it also includes "soft skills" workshops on entrepreneurship, project management, and digital skills. This holistic approach equips participants not only to find jobs but also to potentially start their own businesses.

Community-Embedded Practical Experience
Trainees will install solar energy systems for community centers or create home gardens using water-saving techniques. This hands-on experience benefits both the trainees and the local communities.

Sustainable Partnership Model
The project aims to build a network of partnerships between graduates, local companies, and non-governmental organizations (NGOs) to facilitate employment and networking. This model ensures  providing a sustainable pathway for participants to enter the workforce.
Sustainable Change:
Inputs: The project will provide a comprehensive training program over 12 months, including expert-led curricula, necessary tools and equipment, and administrative support. The target is to train 200 young men and women in less-developed governorates.
Outputs: The direct outputs of the program include 200 trained individuals with specialized technical skills in renewable energy and sustainable agriculture, as well as soft skills like entrepreneurship and project management. Additionally, 10 small community projects will be implemented, providing practical experience for trainees. A network of partnerships will also be established between graduates and local companies.
Outcomes: The immediate outcomes will be an increase in the skills and knowledge of the 200 participants. This will lead to increased employment and income opportunities for them. The program will also stimulate entrepreneurship in the green sector, as participants may start their own projects.

Impact:  By empowering a new generation of skilled workers in the green economy, the project contributes to reducing unemployment, particularly among women and youth, in underserved areas. The focus on renewable energy and sustainable agriculture helps to address critical national challenges like water scarcity and high energy costs to a more resilient and sustainable economy in Jordan.
Funding Sources: This is a new initiative.
Testimonials and Endorsements: N.A
Further comments/feedback: N.A
Primary thematic focus area: MSME Empowerment & Local Digital Innovation
Summary: Green Future Skills is a digital inclusion program in Jordan aimed at training youth and women in green skills for renewable energy and sustainable agriculture. The 12-month program combines technical training (photovoltaic solar systems, sustainable agriculture) and transversal skills (entrepreneurship, project management, digital skills), along with the implementation of practical community projects. The initiative aims to train 200 young people, 50% of whom are women, in underdeveloped governorates, with projects that have local social and environmental impact. (Q12, Q13, Q17, Q18).
