Title: The East Africa AI and Digital Rights Training for Advocates
Subtitle: Building legal capacity for ethical AI governance and digital rights protection in East Africa
Problem Statement: Despite the rapid integration of artificial intelligence (AI) and emerging technologies across East Africa, legal professionals remain largely unprepared to navigate the ethical, regulatory, and human rights challenges these innovations pose. Fragmented AI governance, weak digital rights protections, and a lack of structured legal training have left a critical gap in professional competence. Without urgent capacity-building interventions, lawyers risk ethical breaches, compromised client trust, and irrelevance in a digitally evolving legal landscape—hindering their ability to safeguard rights, promote justice, and influence AI policy development across the region.
Solution Overview:
Solution Overview

The East Africa AI and Digital Rights Training (EAADTR) is a training program  designed to equip lawyers across the East African region with the knowledge, skills, and ethical grounding required to engage with artificial intelligence (AI) and defend digital rights in an evolving technological landscape.

How the Solution Works:

The EAADTR program empowers lawyers to understand, interpret, and influence AI governance. Through expert-led sessions, interactive case simulations, and policy drafting exercises, participants gain hands-on experience in identifying and litigating digital rights violations, integrating AI into legal workflows responsibly, and shaping national and regional tech policy frameworks.
Methodologies and Technologies Used:

•	Interactive Learning Modules: Blended training combining lectures, breakout sessions, and real-world simulations to build applied legal skills.
•	Case Studies and Scenario-Based Exercises: Focused on AI misuse, algorithmic discrimination, data protection failures, and cross-border litigation strategy.
•	Legal Tech Demonstrations: Participants engage with AI tools used in legal research, predictive analytics, and document automation to understand opportunities and risks.
•	Digital Rights Toolkits: Practical resources for evidence gathering, forum selection, and policy engagement on emerging technology issues.
•	AI Forum: the training culminates into a forum which brings together different stakeholders including policy makers, CSOs, tech developers and companies to discuss the intersection of law and emerging technologies 

Partnerships and Collaboration Models:

EAADTR is implemented through a regional partnership model that brings together a diverse consortium of stakeholders:
•	ALP East Africa (Lead Implementer): Legal training design, coordination, and delivery.
•	Paradigm Initiative (PIN): Digital rights and inclusion expertise, content development.
•	CIPESA: Research and policy engagement on digital rights, particularly data protection and surveillance.
•	East Africa Law Society: Regional coordination and outreach to bar associations.
•	Thomson Reuters Foundation: international legal standards integration.

Together, these partnerships foster a cross-sector and cross-border learning ecosystem that bridges the gap between AI innovation and human rights protection—preparing East African lawyers to lead in shaping a just and inclusive digital future.
Solution Provider(s): Paradigm Initiative (PIN) – A Pan-African non-profit organization dedicated to advancing digital rights, digital inclusion, and responsible technology use across Africa, with a focus on policy advocacy, digital literacy, and civic engagement in the tech space, Collaboration on International ICT Policy for East and Southern Africa (CIPESA) – A regional non-profit organization working to promote inclusive ICT policy and advance digital rights in Africa through research, advocacy, and capacity building, East Africa Law Society (EALS) – A regional umbrella body for national bar associations and law societies in East Africa, supporting professional development, regional legal integration, and the rule of law, and Thomson Reuters Foundation / TrustLaw – The charitable arm of Thomson Reuters, supporting free legal assistance and strategic litigation on public interest issues globally, including media freedom, human rights, and the rule of law.
Implementation location(s): East Africa: Uganda, Kenya, Tanzania, Rwanda and South Sudan
Duration to pilot in a new geography: Program is to be delivered annualy, (one week in the month of July)
SDGs addressed: SDG 16 (Peace, Justice, and Strong Institutions);
Desired impact:
Solution Objectives:

•	Equip legal professionals across East Africa with practical, ethical, and strategic skills to navigate the complex intersection of artificial intelligence (AI), digital rights, and the law.
•	Strengthen regional legal capacity in AI governance, data protection, and strategic litigation.
•	Promote responsible and rights-based AI development and deployment through cross-border collaboration and advocacy.
•	Support policy coherence, regulatory reform, and inclusive technology governance in the East African Community (EAC).

Key Achievements and Impacts:

• Capacity Building: Trained over 9 lawyers from Uganda, Kenya, Tanzania, Rwanda and South Sudan in July 2025, strengthening their ability to handle AI-related legal and human rights issues.
• Cross-Border Collaboration: Fostered partnerships among law societies, civil society, and policy institutions to promote harmonized legal frameworks on AI governance.
• Strategic Litigation: Initiated collaborative litigation efforts and knowledge sharing on unlawful digital practices, contributing to ongoing digital rights enforcement.
• Professional Development: Enhanced AI literacy and ethical competence among legal professionals, reducing risks of malpractice and misuse of AI technologies.
• Sustainable Impact: Established an annual training model with growing regional demand, ensuring long-term scalability and knowledge transfer.
Key technologies: AI
Unique Characteristics:
Unique and Differentiated Characteristics of Our Solution:
•	Regionally Tailored Approach: Unlike generic AI or legal trainings, our solution is specifically designed for the East African context, addressing the unique socio-legal, regulatory, and technological challenges facing the region’s digital ecosystem.

•	Multidisciplinary Collaboration: The program uniquely brings together diverse stakeholders—legal practitioners, policymakers, technologists, civil society, and academia—fostering cross-sector dialogue and holistic understanding of AI’s impact on rights and governance.

•	Strategic Litigation Focus: Beyond training, the solution actively supports and facilitates cross-border strategic litigation and advocacy to safeguard digital rights, enabling practical application of knowledge to real-world cases.

•	 Strong Partnership Model: Anchored by leading organizations like ALP East Africa, Paradigm Initiative, CIPESA, East Africa Law Society, and the Thomson Reuters Foundation, the collaboration leverages complementary expertise and extensive regional networks for greater impact.

•	Sustainability and Scalability: Delivered as an annual flagship event with growing regional participation and institutional support, the program is designed for long-term sustainability and potential replication across other African regions.
Sustainable Change:
Our solution contributes to sustainable, systemic change through a clear Theory of Change centered on building lasting capacity in AI governance and digital rights protection, fostering collaborative networks, and driving inclusive, rights-based technology regulation across East Africa.

Capacity Building of Legal Professionals: By equipping lawyers with practical skills and ethical frameworks on AI governance, digital rights, and strategic litigation, the program cultivates a knowledgeable cohort prepared to defend digital rights and uphold justice in the evolving digital landscape.

Institutionalizing Ethical AI and Digital Rights Practices: Aligning training with international standards and regional realities, the initiative promotes responsible AI use and robust protection of digital rights, reducing risks of misuse, digital harms, and erosion of privacy and freedom of expression.

Strengthening Regional Collaboration and Networks: Through multidisciplinary dialogue and partnerships among legal practitioners, policymakers, civil society, and technologists, the program nurtures a sustainable ecosystem for knowledge sharing and coordinated responses to digital rights challenges.

Empowering Strategic Litigation and Policy Advocacy: The enhanced skills and connections enable effective litigation and policy engagement to safeguard digital rights and challenge unlawful or unethical technology practices, driving systemic improvements in regional governance.

Scalability and Institutional Embedding: Although the program was launched on a small scale last month, its design allows for growth through additional funding and stakeholder support. Anchored in key regional institutions, it aims to scale knowledge transfer and embed digital rights and AI governance into East Africa’s legal and policy frameworks over time.

Follow-On Effects:

Strengthened protection and promotion of digital rights across East Africa.

Increased awareness and capacity among legal professionals and institutions on AI’s socio-legal impacts.

More coherent and rights-respecting AI regulatory environments.

Empowered communities benefiting from fair, transparent, and accountable AI applications.

A replicable regional model for integrating technology, law, and human rights to drive sustainable, systemic change.

This phased approach ensures that as the program expands, it will continue to align technological advancement with the fundamental protection of digital rights, fostering long-term, inclusive transformation in the region.
Funding Sources: The solution has primarily been funded through generous support from our key partners and collaborators. We rely on these partnerships to provide the necessary financial resources for program development, training delivery, and capacity-building activities. As the initiative grows, we continue to seek additional funding to scale our impact and sustain long-term operations.

Title: MathScend AI: An Inclusive, Multilingual AI Powered Platform for STEM Education
Subtitle: MathScend AI is a multilingual, AI powered platform that makes STEM concepts like derivatives visual and accessible, empowering African learners for the digital economy.
Problem Statement: Many students and educators across Africa struggle to access quality STEM education due to language barriers, lack of localized resources, and limited exposure to interactive digital tools. This gap creates a ripple effect, and as such, fewer learners develop foundational STEM competencies, which in turn limits their future participation in high-growth digital sectors. The traditional teaching of calculus and derivatives relies on abstract methods, creating barriers for students from under-resourced schools. Language inclusivity is another challenge, as most learning content is only available in English, leaving out learners who are more comfortable in indigenous African languages. Without targeted interventions, these gaps will widen digital inequality and restrict access to economic opportunities in data science, AI, engineering, and other sectors, driving the digital economy.
Solution Overview:
How the solution works:
MathScend AI is an interactive learning platform that makes abstract calculus concepts, such as derivatives, easy to understand. Learners can select or input a function, visualize graphs, and explore animated tangent lines that show how slopes change. A built-in AI tutor responds to user questions with step-by-step explanations in multiple languages (English, Zulu, Sesotho, Afrikaans, Igbo, Yoruba, and Hausa), making STEM content accessible to diverse learners.
Methodologies and technologies used:
1.	AI Integration: Uses large language models (LLaMA-like architecture) for multilingual explanations.
2.	Visualization Tools: Python libraries (Matplotlib, Streamlit) create interactive graphs and dashboards.
3.	User-centric design: Based on APOS theory to guide learning through Action, Process, Object, and Schema stages.
4.	Lightweight architecture: Optimized for low bandwidth environments and mobile access.
Partnerships and collaboration models:
We collaborate with educators, curriculum experts, and EdTech trainers to co-create localized content. We plan to partner with teacher training institutions, the Department of Education, and NGOs to pilot the platform in classrooms and scale adoption across regions.
Solution Provider(s): Mathscend AI (Lead Organization): An education technology and research company focused on developing AI powered learning tools for STEM education. Sector: EdTech / Research & Innovation; Central University of Technology, Free State, South Africa: Academic collaborators providing curriculum alignment and pedagogical input. Sector: Higher Education; Department of Basic Education, Free State, South Africa: Policy and implementation partners supporting pilot programs and scale up. Sector: Public Education / Government; Mathscend Center for Innovation and Applied Research, Free State, South Africa: Supporting outreach, capacity building, and equitable access. Sector: Non profit / Education Development.
Implementation location(s): Not applicable (Pilot ready: We plan pilot in South Africa)
Implementation timeline(s): Not applicable (pilot implementation planned for 2025/2026 in South Africa)
Duration to pilot in a new geography: Approximately 6–9 months to pilot in a new geography, including localization, stakeholder onboarding, teacher training, and initial classroom deployment.  Duration Breakdown: 1–2 months: Localization (language adaptation, curriculum alignment); 2–3 months: Partnership building and teacher training; 3–4 months: Live classroom pilot, data collection, and refinement.
SDGs addressed: SDG 4 (Quality Education);SDG 9 (Industry, Innovation, and Infrastructure);SDG 10 (Reduced Inequalities);
Desired impact:
Solution Objectives
To design a learning platform; To empower students, especially in under-resourced schools, to develop a strong conceptual understanding of calculus and related STEM Education Topics; To foster digital skills and innovation capacity that prepare learners for future employment in the digital economy; To reduce educational inequalities by offering localized content in English, Zulu, Sesotho, Afrikaans, and Igbo.
Key Achievements or Intended Impacts
Reach and inclusion: Pilot deployment to impact at least 10,000 learners and 500 teachers in South Africa within 12 months, with expansion to 3 additional African countries within 2 years; 	Learning outcomes: Achieve a 30% improvement in test performance on calculus and derivative concepts among participating learners; Employment generation: Create opportunities for local EdTech developers, content translators, and teacher trainers engaged in the rollout;  Innovation impact: Build a replicable model that contributes to Africa’s inclusive digital innovation ecosystem, inspiring further EdTech solutions.
Key technologies:
Artificial Intelligence (AI):
Our solution leverages large language models (LLaMA-like architectures) to provide real-time, multilingual explanations and adaptive tutoring.
Data Visualization and Interactive Learning Tools:
Our solution is built with Python libraries such as Matplotlib and Streamlit to plot functions, animate derivative slopes, and create an intuitive learning dashboard.
Cloud-based Web Technologies:
Hosting and deployment on lightweight, scalable web platforms to ensure accessibility even in low-bandwidth environments.
Unique Characteristics:
Unique and Differentiated Characteristics
(a) Multilingual AI Tutor:
Unlike most existing STEM tools, MathScend AI provides real-time explanations in English, Zulu, Sesotho, Afrikaans, and Igbo, breaking language barriers and fostering inclusivity.
(b) Conceptual Visualization Approach:
MathScend AI integrates dynamic graphing and animated derivative exploration to move beyond procedural computation, enabling deep conceptual understanding aligned with APOS learning stages (Action, Process, Object, Schema).
(c) Lightweight & Scalable Design:
Mathscend AI is built with Python and Streamlit, optimized for low-bandwidth environments, making it practical for schools with limited infrastructure.
(d) Responsible AI by Design:
MathScend AI has a transparent step-by-step reasoning, no sensitive data collection, and a strong focus on ethical AI use in education.
(e) Collaborative Implementation Model:
MathScend AI was co-developed with educators and local partners, ensuring curriculum alignment and sustainable adoption, while creating opportunities for local content creators and trainers.
Sustainable Change:
Contribution to Sustainable, Systemic Change:
MathScend AI addresses a foundational barrier in African education, such as a lack of accessible, high-quality STEM instruction. By equipping students and teachers with a multilingual, AI-powered tool that makes abstract concepts tangible, the solution creates a ripple effect across education systems and the broader economy.
Theory of Change:
a.	Inputs:
The deployment of an interactive AI learning platform, training for teachers, and integration into school curricula.
b.	Immediate Outputs:
Students engage with visual, language-inclusive explanations of derivatives and other STEM topics,
and teachers gain digital competencies and confidence in using AI-assisted methods.
c.	Intermediate Outcomes:
Improved learner performance and conceptual understanding in mathematics, increased digital literacy, and exposure to emerging technologies among youth and educators.
d.	Long-term Impact:
A stronger pipeline of students prepared for STEM fields, greater participation of marginalized groups in the digital economy, and a shift in education systems toward data-driven, inclusive, and innovative teaching practices.
Sustainable change:
MathScend AI platform’s design enables continuous content updates, multilingual scalability, and local educator involvement, ensuring that improvements persist beyond initial pilots and become embedded in teaching and learning ecosystems.
Funding Sources: To date, the development of MathScend AI has been primarily self-funded by the founder, with in-kind contributions from collaborators and volunteer educators who supported content validation and early testing. No external grants or institutional funding have yet been secured. The prototype has been developed through personal investment in software development, cloud hosting, and initial user testing, positioning the solution as pilot-ready for scale with future funding support.
Testimonials and Endorsements: Testimonials are currently being collected as part of upcoming pilot activities. Early feedback from educators and peers has been highly positive, highlighting the platform’s clarity and multilingual support.
Further comments/feedback: The questionnaire is well structured and clear. It effectively guides applicants to articulate their solution, impact, and scalability. I appreciate the opportunity to showcase MathScend AI and look forward to engaging further. Thank you for considering innovative, inclusive solutions from Africa.
Primary thematic focus area: Inclusive Digital Innovation Skills & Entrepreneurial Talent Development
Summary: MathScend AI is a multilingual, AI-powered STEM education platform that simplifies abstract concepts like derivatives through interactive visualizations and an AI tutor supporting multiple African languages. The solution aims to reduce barriers in STEM learning for under-resourced schools, improve test scores, and build digital skills critical for Africa’s future workforce. Strengths: strong problem alignment, pedagogically sound (APOS theory), multilingual focus, and lightweight architecture for low-bandwidth settings. Weaknesses: early-stage (pilot not yet launched), limited evidence of large-scale impact, and reliance on future funding to validate scalability.

Title: Evedust – Digital Empowerment for Vocational Workers
Subtitle: A mobile-first platform bridging the digital divide for informal and vocational workers globally.
Problem Statement: Vocational workers across emerging markets face digital exclusion, lack of visibility, insecure payments, and limited access to training or job opportunities. Existing platforms ignore language, literacy, and infrastructure barriers, excluding millions from participating in the digital economy.
Solution Overview:
Evedust will be a next-generation, mobile-first platform designed to connect vocational workers across the globe to dignified digital work.

The solution will allow any service worker—from a barber in Lagos to a mechanic in São Paulo—to create a verified digital portfolio, get matched to clients using AI, receive payments through in-app escrow, and access voice-enabled training modules—even without internet access.

Technologies to be deployed:

AI-powered matching engine for real-time, skills-based client-worker connection

Voice-first navigation for semi-literate users

Multilingual natural language interface for seamless cross-border communication

Offline-first architecture for rural and low-bandwidth regions

Digital wallet and escrow integration (Paystack, M-Pesa, Stripe)

Collaboration model:
Evedust will forge strategic partnerships with governments, training institutes, telcos, fintech companies, and global NGOs to ensure adoption, scale, and impact. The platform will act as a digital bridge between informal talent and formal economic opportunity.
Solution Provider(s): Evedust Digital Solutions (Lead Proponent) – A pre-launch inclusive technology company focused on building platforms for the underserved informal workforce. Partner Organizations (planned collaborations):  National Directorate of Employment (Nigeria) – Public sector vocational training and job creation  Safaricom/M-Pesa – Financial inclusion and digital payments in East Africa  Skill India Mission – Vocational skills and livelihoods program (India)  Paystack – Digital payment infrastructure in West Africa  International Labour Organization (ILO) – Policy and labor standards expertise (developmental partner)
Duration to pilot in a new geography: A full pilot can be launched in 6 to 9 months, including localization, partner onboarding, and beta testing in selected urban centers.
SDGs addressed: SDG 8 (Decent Work and Economic Growth);SDG 9 (Industry, Innovation, and Infrastructure);SDG 10 (Reduced Inequalities);
Desired impact: Evedust aims to digitally onboard 1 million vocational workers within three years, enabling over 10 million job connections, with verified payment security and training in 100+ languages. It will empower women, youth, and marginalized workers to formalize their trade, grow income predictability, and participate in a dignified, digital global workforce.
Key technologies: Evedust will integrate AI/ML for personalized matching and learning, voice-to-text NLP interfaces for semi-literate users, multilingual auto-translation for cross-border communication, and escrow-enabled digital wallets built with regional payment partners. Offline-first design and mobile edge computing will ensure accessibility regardless of geography or infrastructure.
Unique Characteristics: Evedust’s strength lies in its human-centered design—voice interfaces for the semi-literate, gamified upskilling, and decentralized access that meets the informal economy where it is. Unlike elite gig platforms, it will be built from the ground up for resilience, inclusivity, and scale—offering digital identity, verified work history, and access to financial tools for the world’s most essential workers.
Sustainable Change: Evedust will spark systemic transformation by turning informal work into recognized, verifiable digital labor. As workers gain digital reputations, access to clients, and financial independence, entire local economies will formalize. Governments and institutions will gain data for inclusive policymaking, while youth and women will see new pathways into the global economy. This is not just a product—it’s a movement toward a truly inclusive future of work.
Funding Sources: As Evedust is currently in the concept stage, we have not yet received formal funding. However, foundational development efforts have been self-financed by the core founding team. We are actively seeking catalytic funding from international development organizations, digital inclusion accelerators, and impact-driven investors to build the MVP and pilot in high-need regions. Future funding will be diversified through partnerships with global institutions, equity investments, and mission-aligned grants.
Testimonials and Endorsements: As the platform has not yet launched, we do not yet have user testimonials. However, we have received strong expressions of interest from vocational training centers in Nigeria, digital inclusion NGOs in Africa, and microfinance enablers who are eager to partner once the MVP is developed. Testimonials will be gathered during pilot implementation phases and integrated into our growth storytelling.
Further comments/feedback: This questionnaire has been thoughtfully structured to align with impact innovation frameworks. However, for early-stage, pre-product ventures like ours, we recommend adding a section for "anticipated ecosystem support needs" or "MVP-stage readiness plans" to help distinguish between concept-stage scalability potential and already-implemented solutions. We greatly appreciate the opportunity to participate and look forward to future engagements within the Global Digital Compact ecosystem.
Primary thematic focus area: Inclusive Digital Innovation Skills & Entrepreneurial Talent Development
Summary: Evedust is an idea-stage, mobile-first digital empowerment platform designed for vocational and informal workers globally. It provides AI-powered job matching, voice-first navigation for semi-literate users, multilingual NLP for cross-border communication, escrow-enabled payments, and offline-first architecture. Developed by Evedust Digital Solutions, the concept foresees partnerships with training institutes, fintechs (M-Pesa, Paystack), and global agencies (ILO). The aim is to onboard 1M workers in 3 years, with over 10M job connections, focusing on inclusivity, resilience, and financial empowerment for the underserved informal workforce.

Title: Transforming Poultry Waste: A Climate-Smart Circular Economy Solution
Subtitle: I want to transform COCO RICO Poultry Farm into a circular economy business in Niger, converting poultry waste into biofertilizers and green energy to combat pollution and support technological development.
Problem Statement: The poultry industry, while vital for food production, poses significant environmental challenges due to pollution from waste such as manure, feathers, and unusable carcasses. These byproducts, if not properly managed, contaminate soil and groundwater, contributing to ecological degradation and health risks in surrounding communities. The lack of sustainable waste management solutions in the sector exacerbates pollution, undermining both environmental quality and the long-term viability of poultry farming. Our solution addresses these critical issues by introducing a circular economy model that transforms poultry waste into valuable biofertilizers and green energy, thereby reducing pollution and promoting sustainable rural development.
Solution Overview: Within COCO RICO Ferme Avicole in Maradi, Niger, I have undertaken a strategic transformation to address the environmental challenges posed by poultry farming, a traditionally polluting activity. The innovation consists of repositioning the company as a circular economy enterprise specializing in the collection, treatment, and valorization of poultry waste manure, feathers, and unusable carcasses into biofertilizers and green energy (biogas). This approach aims to reduce soil and groundwater pollution while promoting rural energy autonomy. The methodology is based on survey and data collection before developing a geolocated digital database that maps local poultry farms and enables real-time monitoring of waste flows. This digital infrastructure facilitates coordinated collection logistics and optimizes traceability of raw materials for sustainable processing. Technologically, the project relies on validated processes developed in partnership with agronomy faculties and applied science laboratories, alongside the integration of green technologies offered by startups specializing in the circular economy and renewable energy. These collaborations ensure technical and environmental adaptation to local conditions. Financially and institutionally, the project has been supported since its inception by the Tony Elumelu Foundation (TEF) and the United Nations Development Programme (UNDP), who provided crucial seed funding as well as entrepreneurial training and coaching that strengthened the project’s foundation. Additionally, the project is strongly anchored territorially through support from local authorities, who facilitate site access and community awareness, as well as poultry sector stakeholders, whose involvement is crucial for model adoption and supply chain structuring. This multisectoral approach aims to create a sustainable, inclusive ecosystem with significant climate impact, enhancing the resilience of rural communities to climate change.
Solution Provider(s): COCO RICO Ferme Avicole: Social and environmental entrepreneurship in poultry production and waste valorization, Niger; Tony Elumelu Foundation (TEF): Pan-African entrepreneurship support organization providing funding, training, and mentorship; United Nations Development Programme (UNDP): International development agency focusing on poverty reduction, sustainable development, and capacity building; AREN (Association pour la Redynamisation de l’Élevage au Niger): Local NGO specializing in livestock revitalization and sustainable animal husbandry practices in Niger, Faculty of Agronomy and Applied Sciences (Local Universities based in Maradi, Tahoua and Niamey): Academic institutions supporting research and technical validation of waste treatment processes; Green Technology Startups: Private sector companies specializing in circular economy solutions and renewable energy technologies; Local and Regional Authorities: Government bodies facilitating implementation, regulatory compliance, and community engagement; Poultry Sector Stakeholders: Producers, cooperatives, and market operators involved in waste generation and supply chain integration.
Duration to pilot in a new geography: The estimated duration to pilot the solution in a new geography is 6 to 9 months. This timeframe includes 1 to 2 months for initial stakeholder mapping, site identification, and community engagement; 2 to 3 months for setting up the digital infrastructure, developing the poultry waste database, and launching training programs for local youth; and 3 to 4 months for full deployment of collection logistics, pilot testing of waste transformation processes, and monitoring of impact indicators. This phased approach ensures adaptability to local conditions while validating the model’s scalability and inclusiveness.
SDGs addressed: SDG 8 (Decent Work and Economic Growth);SDG 11 (Sustainable Cities and Communities);SDG 12 (Responsible Consumption and Production);
Desired impact: The primary goal of this solution is to transform the challenges associated with poultry waste into economic, social, and environmental opportunities through an inclusive digital approach. The project envisions creating a geolocated database of urban poultry production sites to facilitate the collection, traceability, and transformation of generated waste. It also aims to structure and empower informal sector actors particularly youth by providing training, digital tools, and green employment opportunities within a circular and sustainable economy framework. The project anticipates a progressive reduction in mismanaged poultry waste in urban areas, with the goal of decreasing uncollected poultry waste by 40% within the first three years. It also foresees the creation of 100 direct green jobs for young people involved in waste collection, management, and valorization. Environmentally, the initiative aims to reduce emissions from decomposing organic waste while improving the sanitary conditions of poultry markets. Socially, integrating underprivileged youth into a professionalized waste management system will contribute to long-term resilience and poverty alleviation. This initiative aligns with multiple SDGs, including SDG 11 (sustainable cities), SDG 12 (responsible consumption and production), and SDG 13 (climate action).
Key technologies: Our solution leverages a combination of accessible and scalable technologies to drive inclusive digital transformation in poultry waste management. Key among these is Geospatial Information Systems (GIS), used to map and monitor poultry production and waste hotspots across urban and peri-urban areas. This spatial intelligence supports efficient logistics for waste collection and environmental risk assessment. We also integrate mobile-based data collection platforms for real-time reporting and tracking of waste generation by poultry actors. These tools feed into a centralized digital dashboard that visualizes trends and informs decision-making for local governments and partners. In future iterations, we aim to incorporate Internet of Things (IoT) sensors to monitor waste levels and environmental indicators, and AI-driven analytics to predict waste patterns and optimize recycling strategies. The platform is designed to be open-source and modular, allowing for easy replication, integration with municipal systems, and localization to different contexts across Africa.
Unique Characteristics: Our solution stands out through its integration of digital technology, circular economy principles, and community empowerment into the underexplored domain of poultry waste management. What makes it truly unique is the data-driven approach to environmental and economic sustainability: we combine geospatial mapping, digital monitoring, and mobile-based data collection to identify, track, and optimize the collection and transformation of poultry waste in rapidly urbanizing zones. This allows for real-time decision-making and scalable environmental impact assessments. Moreover, the hybrid business model merges social entrepreneurship and inclusive green innovation. It enables informal workers particularly youth and women who dominate the poultry value chain, to transition from precarious labor to formalized micro-enterprises through training, cooperative-based partnerships, and revenue-sharing models. Financial sustainability is ensured through value-added waste products (organic fertilizer, biogas) and digital service subscriptions. Our innovation also builds strategic linkages with municipalities, agritech hubs, and green economy stakeholders, allowing for replication in other agri-waste sectors and across developing countries
Sustainable Change: Our solution promotes sustainable systemic change by structuring the management of waste from poultry farming through a digital, inclusive, and community-based approach. By developing a digital platform for mapping poultry production and waste collection areas, we are creating an ecosystem that transforms these residues into valuable resources (compost, biogas, agricultural inputs). This process helps to address two challenges: increasing pollution in rapidly developing urban areas, and the economic exclusion of young people and women who work mainly in the informal sector, often without protection or sustainable prospects. By professionalizing their practices and providing them with appropriate digital tools, we are strengthening their ability to participate in a green economy. This model generates a virtuous cycle of long-term effects. It brings about a change in behavior among stakeholders in the poultry sector through awareness-raising and training in sustainable waste management. It creates green job opportunities, improves public health in production areas, and contributes to reducing greenhouse gas emissions. In addition, the use of digital data makes it possible to adjust interventions, monitor pollution trends, and support public policies. This solution, aligned with the SDGs and the African Union's Climate Strategy, can be easily adapted to other agricultural value chains, thereby strengthening the economic and environmental resilience of communities across the continent.
Funding Sources: The initial creation of COCO RICO Ferme Avicole was made possible through a grant from the Tony Elumelu Foundation (TEF) in partnership with the United Nations Development Programme (UNDP). This funding supported a purely economic business model focused on poultry production. The ongoing transformation of the enterprise towards a social, green tech, and climate action-oriented model is currently being financed internally by the company, while actively seeking additional funding from potential donors and partners to scale and sustain this innovative approach.
Testimonials and Endorsements: Not available
Primary thematic focus area: Stable and Resilient Digital Supply Chains
Summary: Transforming Poultry Waste is a Niger-based initiative repositioning COCO RICO Poultry Farm into a circular economy enterprise. The model converts poultry waste (manure, feathers, carcasses) into biofertilizers and green energy while reducing pollution. A geospatial digital database enables mapping and tracking of waste flows, improving collection logistics and traceability. The project is backed by TEF and UNDP, with involvement of local universities, green tech startups, and local authorities. Its integrated approach combines digital infrastructure, circular economy practices, and youth/women empowerment for climate-smart rural development.

Title: East African Business Hub: A Digital Launchpad for MSME Growth
Subtitle: A digital platform supporting East African MSMEs with affordable online presence, digital transactions, and sustainable market access to grow and thrive in the digital economy.
Problem Statement: Despite being the backbone of East Africa’s economy and accounting for the majority of private sector employment, millions of MSMEs, particularly those led by women and youth, continue to face significant barriers to growth and sustainability. These challenges include limited digital visibility, poor access to broader markets, weak product positioning, minimal adoption of ICT tools, and exclusion from formal financial systems. The lack of tailored digital support and market integration leaves many MSMEs uncompetitive, with high failure rates and limited capacity to scale. Without targeted, inclusive, and technology-driven interventions, these systemic barriers will continue to hinder the transformative potential of MSMEs in driving equitable and sustainable economic development across the region.
Solution Overview:
The East African Business Hub (EAB-Hub) is an inclusive, smart digital platform developed by Brish Media Empire, in partnership with the Uganda Small Scale Industries Association (USSIA), to support Micro, Small, and Medium Enterprises (MSMEs) across East Africa. Purposefully designed to empower MSMEs particularly those led by women and youth. The platform will provide affordable, accessible digital tools that enhance business visibility, expand market access, and foster long-term sustainability. Through EAB-Hub, entrepreneurs can establish a professional online presence, promote their products and services, engage in digital transactions, and build sustainable market linkages across the region.
At the core of the solution is a mobile-first, cloud-based platform that enables each MSME to create a personalized, interactive digital business page hosted on a unique subdomain. These pages incorporate multimedia element such as: images, videos, and text descriptions, and are seamlessly integrated with social media and e-commerce features, allowing real-time customer engagement and direct online transactions. To ensure contextual relevance, the platform categorizes MSMEs into key sectors including agriculture, manufacturing, construction, education, health, and finance, enabling the delivery of tailored services, insights, and capacity-building content.

Entrepreneurs using the EAB-Hub will benefit from a comprehensive suite of digital tools and support services. These include AI-powered business insights that provide pricing recommendations, sales forecasts, and marketing suggestions; and gamified digital marketing training delivered through interactive modules, quizzes, and certifications. The platform also features a multilingual, voice-enabled interface, along with USSD access, ensuring inclusivity for users in low-connectivity and low-literacy environments, particularly in rural and underserved communities. Additional features such as e-commerce integration, search engine optimization (SEO), email marketing, and social media integration further support MSMEs in expanding their digital reach and strengthening their brand visibility across local and regional markets.
Technologically, EAB-Hub will be anchored in a scalable, cloud-based infrastructure optimized for mobile accessibility. It will leverage artificial intelligence, e-learning methodologies, and omnichannel communication strategies to deliver a seamless and consistent user experience across web, mobile, SMS, and voice platforms. These innovations collectively lower barriers to digital participation and enable MSMEs to grow sustainably within a rapidly evolving digital economy.

The success and scalability of EAB-Hub will made possible through a strong, multi-stakeholder collaboration. The platform is anchored in a collaborative ecosystem involving MSME associations, cooperatives, fintech providers, content creators, media agencies, local governments, innovation hubs, and development partners. This ecosystem brings together actors from the public, private, and development sectors to drive MSME outreach, digital financial inclusion, content promotion, policy alignment, and regional scale-up. Through these strategic partnerships, EAB-Hub ensures broad-based impact, inclusivity, and long-term sustainability.
Solution Provider(s): The East African Business Hub (EAB-Hub) is led by Brish Media Empire, in strategic partnership with the Uganda Small Scale Industries Association (USSIA), and supported by a network of prospective partners across the public, private, and innovation sectors. These partners bring diverse expertise to support the development, deployment, and sustainability of the platform. USSIA, as a national umbrella organization, plays a vital role in supporting small-scale and cottage industries in Uganda. It provides hands-on training, enterprise development services, and advocacy for the informal and small business sector. Brish Media Empire complements this by offering robust capabilities in digital marketing, content development, e-commerce integration, and MSME capacity building, ensuring the platform is both technically sound and user-centric. The project also envisions collaboration with other key institutions. The Uganda Manufacturers Association (UMA) contributes through its extensive network of manufacturing businesses, promoting industrial growth and regional market linkages. The Private Sector Foundation Uganda (PSFU) strengthens policy alignment and public-private engagement, while also supporting enterprise competitiveness and investment facilitation. Title: Feasibility3D for design, simulations and spill quantification essentials in the oil and gas ecosystem
Subtitle: This is a platform designed to provide advanced tools for the design, analysis, and optimization of oil and gas pipelines and associated resources, leveraging state-of-the-art modeling techniques and algorithms. The project seeks to address critical challenges in pipeline engineering, enhance safety standards, and optimize resource utilization in the oil and gas sector. It is a comprehensive software solution that empowers engineers and stakeholders in the oil and gas industry to design, simulate, analyze and quantify spills relating to oil and gas operations with unprecedented accuracy and efficiency.
Problem Statement: The oil and gas industry relies heavily on pipeline infrastructure to transport hydrocarbons efficiently and safely across vast distances. However, designing, modeling, simulating, and managing these pipelines present significant challenges due to complex operational, environmental, and safety considerations. Feasibility 3D platform is created to ensure ease of design and analysis where stakeholders have the freedom of expressing their intents through familiar domain representations and are not encumbered with syntax complexities to express their design intents for productivity.
Solution Overview:
1.	Feasibility 3D Value Proposition
Feasibility3D solves a scale limitation inherent to legacy conventional modelling, analysis and simulation systems in the oil and gas industry. Today, modern modeling and simulation software e.g. OLGA, PIPESIM can handle global scale. Modeling and simulation software were designed to be rigid, associated with steep learning curves and maintain data validity despite system failures and mishaps. Instead of rigidity, and being saddled with syntactic bottlenecks, Feasibility3D stores its data in reusable collections. A collection that allows the domain expert to easily streamline from familiar notations an entire pipeline lifecycle, ensuring efficiency, safety, and reliability in the exploration, production, and transportation of oil and gas resources.

2.	Feasibility 3D Software Status 
Feasibility3D, developed by Feasibility Giant Company Limited, is an advanced 3D modeling application tailored specifically for the modeling and simulation of oil and gas pipelines. This cutting-edge software empowers engineers and designers with specialized tools to create precise virtual representations of pipeline systems. Feasibility3D facilitates comprehensive analysis, visualization, and optimization of pipeline layouts, flow dynamics, and structural integrity. From initial design conception to operational simulation and maintenance planning. This software is capable of handling the following details:

a.	Accurate 3D Modeling: It creates precise virtual representations of oil and gas pipeline systems.
b.	Specialized Tools: Provide engineers and designers with specialized tools tailored for pipeline modeling and simulation, including panels for Fluid dynamics calculations, and pipeline measurement scaling.
c.	Comprehensive Analysis: It performs in-depth analysis of pipeline layouts, flow dynamics, and structural integrity.
d.	Visualization: Visualize pipeline systems in 3D to better understand their configuration and behavior.
e.	Optimization: It is useful in optimizing pipeline designs for efficiency, safety, and cost-effectiveness.
f.	Operational Simulation: Simulate pipeline operations to predict performance under different conditions.
g.	Maintenance Planning: Assist in planning maintenance activities to ensure the continued reliability of pipeline systems.
 
3.	Needed Collaboration
a.	We need to connect with the industry to enable us build in the exact critical components that will meet the target
b.	We need to actualize the real world realities by placing our software to task in the industry
c.	We need more industry expertise to wholly critique our efforts, so that we can come up with a workable standard. Therefore, in addition we need more coordinated and resource sharing collaboration in the following areas.
a.	Multiphase Flow Representation: Recreating Multiphase Fluid flow is very possible, but a very time consuming aspect of the project, so we need your attention.
b.	Relevant Data: The project is in need of relevant data involving calculations made for similar purposes using real life values. For certain criteria like Slugging, etc., Pipeline pressure, Flow Assurance, Leak detection, Spill Quantification and the likes, so, we need your support.
c.	Resource Intensiveness: Depending on the scaling of the pipeline models created and the number of flow pathways, etc., the resource intensiveness would be more incremental on the system, and so, we need your input.

Key Objectives:

1. Optimized Pipeline Design: Develop a system that automates and optimizes pipeline design by integrating factors such as terrain, material selection, fluid dynamics, and cost constraints, ensuring safe and efficient configurations.

2. Accurate Modeling and Simulation: Create advanced modeling tools capable of simulating multi-phase flow, corrosion, and environmental impacts (e.g., temperature, seismic activity) to predict pipeline performance and identify potential failure points.

Geographic Information Systems (GIS) to integrate geospatial data for terrain analysis, route optimization, and environmental impact assessment. Artificial Intelligence (AI) and Machine Learning (ML) to optimize design parameters, predicts maintenance needs, and enhances spill detection/quantification. Internet of Things (IoT) and Sensor Technologies to enable real-time monitoring of pipeline conditions (e.g., pressure, temperature, leaks).

1.	Integrated End-to-End Workflow; combines pipeline design, modeling, simulation, and spill quantification into a single platform, seamlessly linking all stages from conceptual design to operational monitoring. Unlike traditional systems that rely on disparate tools for design (e.g., CAD), simulation (e.g., CFD), and monitoring, this system provides a unified interface, reducing data silos and improving efficiency.

Geospatial and Environmental Integration: Incorporates GIS technology to analyze terrain, seismic risks, and environmental constraints, ensuring designs account for real-world conditions and regulatory requirements. This sets a precedent for sustainable engineering practices, influencing standards and policies.

This drives industry-wide adoption of standardized, transparent practices, fostering systemic regulatory alignment.

Title: Hermplify: Powering Women & MSMEs in Africa’s Digital Economy
Subtitle: Helping African women and small businesses grow by giving them digital tools, skills, and access to finance so they can succeed in today’s online economy.
Problem Statement:
Many women and small business owners in Africa are left behind in today’s digital world.

They don’t have the tools, knowledge, or money to take part in the digital economy.

Most of them can’t afford training, don’t know how to use digital platforms, and don’t have access to funding or support networks.

This keeps them stuck in poverty or low income.

Without help, they can't grow their businesses, reach more customers, or improve their lives.

This is a major challenge that affects entire families and communities.

We are solving this problem.
Solution Overview:
Hermplify is a simple digital platform that helps women and small businesses grow.

Users can open a free business wallet, learn online, and access funding — all in one place using a smartphone.

We use AI to suggest what each user needs: training, support, or financial help.

The platform runs on cloud servers, uses APIs to connect with mobile money and ID verification tools, and supports USSD for people without smartphones (coming soon).

We work with partners like HP LIFE and EntryLevel to offer free business and tech courses.

We plan to partner with telcos like MTN to reach more users with zero-data access and MoMo.
Solution Provider(s): Hermplify is working with the following key partners:  HP LIFE (Hewlett-Packard Learning Initiative for Entrepreneurs) – a global tech company offering free business and digital skills training. Sector: Technology, Education.  EntryLevel – a digital learning platform that helps people learn in-demand tech and business skills through hands-on experience. Sector: Education, Workforce Development.  Smile Identity – an identity verification company that helps us confirm user identities securely using face recognition. Sector: Identity Verification, Fintech.  We’re also in talks with mobile money platforms and local cooperatives to expand our reach.
Implementation location(s): Nigeria - Lagos, Rivers, Abuja Benin Republic - Cotonou
Implementation timeline(s): The solution started in January 2024 and is still running.  We launched the learning platform in March 2024, started onboarding users in April 2024, and began our KYC and community pilot in June 2024.
Duration to pilot in a new geography: We can pilot our solution in a new location within 4 to 6 weeks.  This includes setup, onboarding, community engagement, and testing.
SDGs addressed: SDG 3 (Good Health and Well-being);SDG 1 (No Poverty);SDG 4 (Quality Education);
Desired impact:
Our goal is to help 1 million women in Africa grow their businesses, earn more money, and get access to better health, education, and funding.

We want to reduce poverty, improve women’s income by 40%, and create 100,000 new jobs through training, access to markets, and digital tools.
Key technologies:
We use AI to help women get business advice, training, and funding faster.

Our platform also uses cloud technology to store data safely and make it easy to access from anywhere.

We plan to add blockchain later to track funding and ensure transparency.
Unique Characteristics:
Our solution is built for African women.

We combine access to funding, business training, health tools, and a support community—all in one place.

Unlike others, we use AI to give personalized help at scale.

We partner with global learning platforms like HP LIFE and EntryLevel to offer free skills training.

We also plan to introduce a shared-revenue model so women can earn while they learn and grow.

No one is bringing all these pieces together the way we do-for women, by women.
Sustainable Change:
Our solution gives women the tools to grow steady income, access healthcare, and learn skills that last for life.

This leads to better homes, healthier families, and stronger communities.

As more women grow businesses and earn money, they lift others up too-creating jobs and mentoring girls.

Over time, this reduces poverty, improves education, and cuts down on maternal and infant deaths.

We believe when you help one woman, she helps many more. That's how real change spreads-person to person, home to home.
Funding Sources:
We have funded the solution using personal savings, small donations, and support from local community leaders.

We also got free resources from partners like EntryLevel and HP LIFE, who help us train women and girls.

So far, we’ve not received any major grant or investor funding. We’ve done a lot with very little.

With the right support now, we can reach more women, faster, and with greater impact.

Title: VIEI City Systems
Subtitle: The Vendor Integration and Empowerment Initiative (VIEI) City Systems
Problem Statement:
For more than two decades, Zimbabwe has endured persistent economic crises, resulting in an unemployment rate exceeding 70%. These conditions have fueled the emergence of a dual economy, where formal and informal sectors operate side by side. With limited job creation and constrained access to formal systems, the informal economy particularly informal vendors and MSMEs has grown exponentially, becoming a core survival mechanism for urban populations.

Government attempts to eliminate street vending in major cities like Harare have consistently failed, highlighting the resilience of informal enterprise in the face of economic instability. Efforts to formalize MSMEs have met resistance, driven largely by mistrust between vendors and local authorities who are often viewed as exploitative, corrupt, or dismissive of the livelihoods informal traders rely on. Existing interventions have lacked sustainable incentives and meaningful support for vendors, leaving a vacuum in inclusive urban development.

The Vendor Integration & Empowerment Initiative (VEIE) City Systems addresses this gap by offering a pro-vendor solution that prioritizes formalization through digital tools, fair zoning policies, and scalable incentives. It reimagines informal enterprise as a strategic pillar of the urban economy, not a threat unlocking pathways for legitimacy, opportunity, and systemic change.
Solution Overview:
The Vendor Integration and Empowerment Initiative (VIEI) City Systems is an initiative aimed at establishing a digital informal vendor management system for organizing, digitizing and integrating informal vendors into the formal economy as a pathway for enhancing MSMEs empowerment, improving urban governance, regulatory compliance and economic development in Zimbabwe. 

The VIEI City Systems will catalyse local digital innovation to empower and integrate urban informal MSMEs into the formal economy. Digital innovation will help to advance informal vendor business mapping, formal registration, regulatory compliance, and inclusive city governance. 

Main activities will include the development of the digital informal vendor management system, mobilization of vendors, development of the digital vendor registry by way of geo-tagging and permit management, vendor zoning and provision of informal vendor empowerment and support services. This will help to empower informal vendors and integrating them in the formal economy for national economic development in Zimbabwe.

We will partner with the government through the Ministry of Women Affairs Community Development and SMEs; telecoms companies (Econet and NetOne) for hosting of our USSD access code; the City of Harare (pilot) and other local councils as we scale in other towns and cities.
Solution Provider(s): Green for Sustainability Initiative Trust (Civil Society Organization which promotes entrepreneurship, innovation and green local economic development); City of Harare (local authority); Central Registry (SME registration); Ministry of Women Affairs Community Development and SMEs; Econet Wireless and NetOne (telecoms companies).
Duration to pilot in a new geography: 18 months
SDGs addressed: SDG 11 (Sustainable Cities and Communities);SDG 9 (Industry, Innovation, and Infrastructure);SDG 8 (Decent Work and Economic Growth);
Desired impact:
(i) To promote digital formalization of urban informal MSMEs through the establishment of a mobile-first informal vendor registration system that maps and profiles vendors across urban zones and simplify permit issuance, renewals, and compliance tracking via mobile payments and geo-tagged platforms.

(ii) To strengthen urban MSMEs governance through smart zoning and digital informal vendor data management systems while enabling city councils to make evidence-based decisions on sanitation, congestion, and resource allocation.

(iii) To empower urban informal vendors and MSMEs through access to digital technical and financial support services and market linkages

This will lead to:

Expected results
(i)	Formalization of 10,000 urban MSME vendors within the first 18 months, reducing shadow economy risks.
(ii)	Increased vendor income by 25-40% through digital payments, transparent zoning, reduced conflict between vendors and enforcement agents, and dispute resolution.
(iii)	Increased government revenue through enhanced MSMEs formalization, permit renewal and compliance
(iv) Improved decent employment
Key technologies: We leverage on AI and IoT to bridge the digital divide for informal MSMEs.
Unique Characteristics:
The system will have unique characteristics as follows: 

(i)	It provides a mobile-first, vendor-centric design which is tailored for low-tech environments with USSD, SMS, and WhatsApp interfaces.
(ii)	It provides a dynamic zoning intelligence showing real-time vending zone status (Green, Yellow, Red) based on congestion, sanitation, and safety metrics thereby enabling flexible relocation, adaptive permitting, and conflict mitigation with city stakeholders.
(iii)	It enables geo-tagged compliance for permit renewals 
(iv)	Scalability through modular architecture which can be easily replicable in other municipalities with plug-and-play modules.
(v)	Offers an inclusive governance platform whereby vendors are involved in decision-making via polls, grievance redressal, and live feedback. This will build mutual trust between vendors and authorities, reducing friction and enforcement challenges.
Sustainable Change: The VEIE City Systems is more than a solution, it’s a movement toward urban equity, economic justice, and digital inclusion. At its core, the system formalizes informal MSMEs not just to count vendors, but to empower them. Through mobile-first platforms and smart zoning, cities shift from reactive enforcement to proactive enablement. Vendors are no longer seen as obstacles to urban order, but as micro-entrepreneurs driving local economies. By embedding vendor operations into digital city planning tools, the system rewires governance itself. Real-time mapping, geo-tagging, and analytics replace paper-based permits with agile decision-making giving cities the pulse of their own informal sectors. The impact ripples outward: vendors gain access to microfinance, training, and cooperatives unlocking opportunities that compound over generations. Social exclusion gives way to recognition. Transactional vending gives way to resilient enterprise and because it's mobile, modular, and multilingual, the system is built to scale not just across neighborhoods but across nations. It’s the digital backbone for inclusive urban development. In short, VEIE is not a tech fix, it is a systems shift from invisibility to inclusion, from fragmentation to coordination, and from survival to sustainable growth.
Funding Sources: none
Primary thematic focus area: Inclusive Digital Innovation Skills & Entrepreneurial Talent Development
Summary: The VIEI City Systems seeks to digitally integrate informal vendors into the formal economy in Zimbabwe. Its strengths lie in its vendor-focused, mobile-first design and the innovative use of zoning intelligence. However, its scalability and clear financial strategy need further development.

Title: Des routes recyclées pour une mobilité urbaine immédiate
Subtitle: Une solution écologique, rapide et inclusive pour désenclaver les zones urbaines
Problem Statement: L’urbanisation rapide en Côte d’Ivoire engendre une saturation des voies, un enclavement de nombreux quartiers et un manque criant d’infrastructures d’accès rapides, durables et accessibles à tous, notamment aux populations défavorisées.
Solution Overview: VALORPLAST est un système de chaussées modulaires et recyclées, conçu pour créer rapidement des routes temporaires dans les zones urbaines enclavées, sans travaux lourds. Fabriqués à partir de déchets plastiques valorisés, les modules sont faciles à installer, résistants, réutilisables et adaptés aux contextes urbains denses. Cette solution offre une réponse écologique, économique et inclusive aux défis de mobilité urbaine en Afrique.
Solution Provider(s): SN KANIAN TECHNOLOGIES – Entreprise ivoirienne spécialisée dans la valorisation des déchets industriels et municipaux, la fabrication de pavés écologiques et le développement de solutions d’infrastructures modulaires durables. Acteur principal du projet, en charge de la conception, de la fabrication des modules VALORPLAST et de la coordination terrain.
Duration to pilot in a new geography: 3 A 6 MOIS
SDGs addressed: SDG 11 (Sustainable Cities and Communities);SDG 13 (Climate Action);SDG 9 (Industry, Innovation, and Infrastructure);
Desired impact:
Valorisation de 50 à 100 tonnes de déchets plastiques par mois dans la phase pilote.

 Réduction estimée de 120 à 180 tonnes équivalent CO₂/an, grâce au recyclage, à la réduction des trajets et à l’évitement de l’incinération ou de l’enfouissement.

 Installation de 5 000 à 10 000 m² de chaussées temporaires VALORPLAST dans les 6 premiers mois d’opération.

 Création de 50 emplois directs (fabrication, logistique, installation) et plus de 100 emplois indirects (collecte, sous-traitance, maintenance).

 Amélioration de la mobilité de plus de 10 000 habitants dans les quartiers ciblés.
Key technologies:
Technologie de recyclage plastique à basse température
 Transformation de déchets plastiques post-consommation en pavés et modules de revêtement, avec une consommation énergétique réduite.

Système modulaire VALORPLAST
 Chaussées démontables et réutilisables, conçues pour être posées sans génie civil ni béton, et s’adaptant à tous types de sols urbains.

Intégration de capteurs intelligents (puces RFID ou IoT)
Suivi de l’installation, de la fréquentation, des conditions d’utilisation et de l’usure des modules pour une maintenance prédictive.

Approche low-tech participative
Utilisation d’équipements simples et robustes adaptés à des opérateurs locaux peu qualifiés, favorisant une appropriation rapide de la solution.
Unique Characteristics:
Une innovation au croisement de l’environnement, de la mobilité et de l’inclusion
VALORPLAST est l’une des rares solutions à combiner valorisation des déchets plastiques et création d’infrastructures de mobilité modulaires, tout en générant des emplois locaux accessibles, notamment aux femmes et aux jeunes.

Un modèle modulaire, réutilisable et sans génie civil
Contrairement aux routes classiques, les modules VALORPLAST sont faciles à poser, retirer et réutiliser, sans terrassement ni béton, ce qui réduit considérablement les coûts, les délais et les impacts environnementaux.

Technologie propre et traçable
Grâce à l’intégration de puces intelligentes (RFID / IoT), chaque module peut être géolocalisé, suivi en temps réel, et entretenu de manière prédictive une avancée technologique rare dans les infrastructures urbaines temporaires en Afrique.

Un modèle économique circulaire et socialement intégré
Les matières premières sont issues de déchets collectés localement, transformées par une main-d'œuvre locale formée, et les revenus générés sont en partie réinvestis dans l’expansion du système et la sensibilisation communautaire. Ce modèle permet de lier rentabilité, impact social et écologie.

Un potentiel de réplication rapide et à bas coût
Grâce à son caractère modulaire et low-tech, la solution peut être adaptée à d'autres villes ou pays, même en zones à faible infrastructure ou en contexte d’urgence humanitaire.
Sustainable Change:
Notre solution agit à la fois en amont, au cœur et en aval du système, pour transformer durablement la manière dont les villes africaines gèrent les déchets et conçoivent la mobilité urbaine.
 Répond à un besoin urgent de mobilité et de gestion des déchets
Structure un écosystème local d’économie circulaire
Accélère la transition vers des villes plus inclusives, résilientes et écologiques
En partant d’un projet local à fort impact visible, nous visons à influencer les pratiques, les mentalités et les politiques pour faire de l’innovation circulaire un pilier central du développement urbain en Afrique.
Primary thematic focus area: Innovation Acceleration & Knowledge Sharing
Summary: VALORPLAST offers an innovative, eco-friendly solution to improve urban mobility by transforming waste plastics into modular, temporary roadways. The solution’s emphasis on recycling, local job creation, and modularity is a strength, though it lacks detailed financial sustainability and scalability plans.

Title: JIMITI CRAFT: AI-Driven Digital Enterprise Ecosystem for Inclusive Woodcraft Design and E-Commerce
Subtitle: Digitally transforming Jimma’s woodcraft industry by connecting artisans, designers, and workshops to global markets through AI and e-commerce.
Problem Statement: Jimma’s celebrated woodcraft industry faces significant challenges due to reliance on traditional, outdated designs, limited market exposure, and disconnected production networks. Artisans often lack access to current design trends, digital technologies, and wider markets, which stifles creativity and innovation. Meanwhile, skilled young designers and graduates find it difficult to collaborate effectively with local workshops. At the same time, both local and international buyers have limited access to authentic, high-quality Jimma woodcraft products. The lack of a unified digital platform hinders collaboration, adaptation to evolving market trends, and participation in e-commerce, thereby restricting the industry’s potential for growth and global competitiveness.
Solution Overview:
Our solution, JIMITI CRAFT, is an AI-driven digital enterprise ecosystem designed to transform Jimma’s traditional woodcraft industry by connecting artisans, designers, workshops, and buyers on a single online platform. This virtual hub enables local artisans to showcase and sell their handcrafted products while allowing designers to upload or create digital woodcraft designs. For artisans who may lack advanced technical skills, AI-powered design tools assist by converting simple text prompts into detailed, production-ready designs and by recommending trending styles based on global market data.

The platform features a built-in e-commerce marketplace where artisans and designers can sell directly to local, national, and international customers, supported by secure digital payment integrations including Telebirr. Government-owned and private workshops are integrated into the system as production partners, offering manufacturing services that help scale up artisans’ output efficiently.

Jimma University plays a central role in this ecosystem by hosting the platform on its data center, providing technical support, and coordinating training programs to build digital literacy, design capabilities, and entrepreneurial skills among artisans, students, and graduates. The collaboration extends to local woodcraft associations and artisans who contribute their expertise and products, as well as regional logistics partners who facilitate timely delivery and market access.

Together, these partnerships foster a sustainable, technology-enabled community that encourages innovation, enhances market access, and helps preserve Jimma’s rich cultural heritage, ultimately driving inclusive economic growth and elevating the woodcraft sector to compete on national and global stages.
Solution Provider(s): The key partners involved in this solution include Jimma University, a leading Ethiopian higher education and research institution specializing in technology, design, and community development, providing platform hosting, technical expertise, and capacity-building programs; the Jimma Woodcraft Artisans, a local organization representing skilled woodcraft artisans and small enterprises dedicated to preserving and modernizing traditional crafts; Local Government Technical and Vocational Education and Training (TVET) Centers, which offer practical skills training, workshops, and certification for artisans and graduates in woodcraft and related fields; and regional logistics and export partners, private sector companies specializing in product distribution and delivery services to facilitate local, national, and international market access.
Duration to pilot in a new geography: 1.5 year
SDGs addressed: SDG 9 (Industry, Innovation, and Infrastructure);SDG 8 (Decent Work and Economic Growth);SDG 17 (Partnerships for the Goals);
Desired impact:
Solution Objectives:

The primary objectives of this solution are to digitally transform Jimma’s woodcraft industry by connecting artisans, designers, and manufacturers through an AI-driven platform that fosters creativity, market access, and sustainable growth. It aims to empower local artisans and young designers with digital tools and skills, enable seamless collaboration between stakeholders, and open new national and international markets via e-commerce.

Impact of the Solution 

The solution is expected to generate significant employment opportunities by creating numerous direct and indirect jobs for artisans, designers, and logistics providers over the coming years. It aims to increase the average income of participating artisans and designers by expanding their market access and diversifying revenue streams through sales of both physical woodcraft products and digital designs. The project will also focus on skills development by training hundreds of artisans, graduates, and students in digital design, AI-assisted creativity, and e-commerce best practices. By enabling a wide network of woodcraft producers to reach new local, national, and global customers through the platform, the solution will significantly expand market reach. Additionally, it will revitalize Jimma’s traditional woodcraft industry by blending cultural heritage with contemporary, globally trending designs, ensuring cultural sustainability. The project also promotes environmentally responsible practices by encouraging sustainable wood sourcing and efficient production methods, which are expected to reduce material waste substantially.
Key technologies: The key technologies utilized in our solution include Artificial Intelligence (AI), Computer-Aided Design (CAD), e-commerce platforms, cloud computing, and digital payment systems. AI powers design generation by transforming simple text prompts into detailed woodcraft designs, analyzes global design trends to keep artisans up to date, and facilitates buyer-product matchmaking to connect customers with the right artisans. CAD tools enable precise digital modeling of woodcraft designs, allowing for efficient prototyping and production. The e-commerce platform provides a secure marketplace for artisans and designers to sell physical products and digital designs, integrated with digital payment systems such as Telebirr to support smooth local and international transactions. Cloud computing, hosted on Jimma University’s data center, ensures scalable and secure storage of designs, product catalogs, and transaction data. Additionally, mobile and web applications offer accessible interfaces for artisans, designers, and buyers, while collaboration tools foster real-time communication and coordination among stakeholders.
Unique Characteristics:
Our solution stands out due to its innovative integration of advanced technologies with a strong public-private partnership model that bridges academia, local artisans, government workshops, and private sector logistics. Unlike traditional craft marketplaces, it leverages AI-powered design tools to boost creativity and help artisans generate modern, trending woodcraft designs, making advanced technology accessible even to those with limited digital skills. The platform uniquely combines the sale of both physical products and digital design files, creating diversified income streams for artisans and designers alike.

A key differentiator is the collaboration between Jimma University as the technology and network hub, local government technical training centers, artisan associations, and private logistics companies, fostering a sustainable ecosystem that supports production, capacity building, and market access. Additionally, the integration of digital payment solutions like Telebirr facilitates secure, convenient, and efficient local and international transactions, addressing common payment barriers in emerging markets. This blend of technological innovation, inclusive business models, and strategic partnerships positions the solution as a replicable blueprint for driving inclusive digital transformation in traditional industries.
Sustainable Change:
By digitally connecting Jimma’s woodcraft artisans, designers, workshops, and buyers through an AI-driven platform, the solution creates an inclusive ecosystem that empowers local communities with skills, market access, and collaborative opportunities. As artisans gain digital literacy and access to modern design tools, their creativity and product quality improve, enabling them to compete in broader markets. This increased market participation generates higher incomes, fostering economic resilience and reducing poverty.

Simultaneously, involving university students and graduates in design and platform development cultivates a continuous innovation pipeline, ensuring the ecosystem adapts to evolving market demands. The integration of government workshops and private sector partners strengthens local production capacity and supply chains, promoting sustainable industry growth.

Over time, this inclusive digital transformation leads to a self-sustaining woodcraft economy that preserves cultural heritage while driving modernization, improving livelihoods, and encouraging environmentally responsible practices. The model’s replicability offers pathways for similar traditional sectors to leverage technology for systemic, long-term economic and social development.
Funding Sources: As this solution is newly proposed, it has not yet received prior funding. However, the foundational research, platform development, and initial stakeholder engagement have been supported by institutional resources from Jimma University, including in-kind contributions such as technical expertise, infrastructure, and student involvement through internships and academic projects.
