Title: accessible cybersecurity scanner
Subtitle: Making the cybersecurity industry accessible. Ensuring no one is exposed to security vulnerabilities because of a lack of accessibility
Problem Statement: Accessibility in cybersecurity is a critical and often overlooked challenge. The omission of digital accessibility poses a substantial threat to the cybersecurity industry. At least one in five people experiences permanent, temporary, or situational disability. This means one in five people is likely to be excluded from cybersecurity protection or forced to resort to workarounds that only compound vulnerabilities. This lapse not only leaves a significant portion (16% according to WHO) of the global population at risk but also hinders the overall effectiveness of cybersecurity measures.
Solution Overview: An accessibility scanner tailored for the cybersecurity industry. In addition to our core product, the scanner, we will also be offering training, mentorship, tooling, accessibility assessments, audits, and consulting. Our methodology is to draw awareness to the intersection between accessibility and cybersecurity, highlighting the ways a lack of accessibility could increase cybersecurity risks for people, process, and products. We achieve this through advocacy, training, and audits of cybersecurity products and services for accessibility compliance. We will partner with cybersecurity vendors to ensure that talents can use their work tools without barriers. We intend to partner with disability communities and groups to inspire talents to consider a cybersecurity career. Our team is made up of cybersecurity professionals with lived experience ranging from blindness to deafness and neurodivergent.
Solution Provider(s): UNESCO
Duration to pilot in a new geography: Our solution is digital.
SDGs addressed: SDG 10 (Reduced Inequalities);SDG 9 (Industry, Innovation, and Infrastructure);SDG 8 (Decent Work and Economic Growth);
Desired impact: For a challenge affecting at least one billion people, accessibility in cybersecurity should be by design and not an afterthought. The Fezzant team is a unique blend of professionals with technical expertise and/or lived experience at the nexus of accessibility and cybersecurity. Our one-year impact would be achieving at least 30% awareness about the need for digital accessibility amongst cybersecurity companies. This would translate to at least 3 in every 10 cybersecurity companies being aware of the essential role accessibility plays in cybersecurity. Our five-year impact sees the Fezzant team dedicated to significantly reducing the critical accessibility gap (1 billion wide) in the cybersecurity industry.
Key technologies: The scanner is a web browser extension. In addition, we leverage AI for finding vulnerabilities and suggesting remediation when generating scan reports.
Unique Characteristics: We are at the nexus of two independent industries: accessibility and cybersecurity. Most competitors focus on one or the other, Fezzant focuses on the middle ground, digital accessibility in cybersecurity.
Sustainable Change: We envision a change in the cybersecurity industry where accessibility is built into product and service developments. Talents are not excluded because of inaccessible work tools, study, and assessment labs.
Funding Sources: UNESCO grant to build out a prototype.
Primary thematic focus area: Inclusive Digital Innovation Skills & Entrepreneurial Talent Development
Summary: This solution aims to address the critical issue of accessibility in the cybersecurity industry, which has often been overlooked despite its significant impact on a large portion of the global population. By providing a scanner tailored for cybersecurity products and services, along with training and advocacy, the platform seeks to integrate accessibility into the development of cybersecurity tools. However, the solution's scalability and long-term impact depend on broader industry buy-in and the availability of sufficient resources for widespread implementation.

Name of your organization: Eastern Africa Academy of Childhood Disabilities
Title: Digital Opportunities For All (DOFA): Enhancing Economic Participation of Persons with Disabilities
Subtitle: An assessment of digital participation of persons living with disabilities and the challenges encountered in transitioning into the workforce
Problem Statement: In an increasingly digital world, the potential for technology to bridge economic divides is immense. However, this potential is often unrealized for marginalized groups, particularly individuals with disabilities, who have limited access to digital services. For individuals with disabilities, the implications of the digital divide are particularly pronounced. Barriers to access can exacerbate existing inequalities, limiting opportunities for education, employment, and social participation. The importance of accessibility cannot be overstated, as it serves as the foundation for inclusive digital transformation. When digital platforms and tools are designed with accessibility in mind, they empower individuals with disabilities to participate fully in the digital economy. This includes access to online education, employment opportunities, and social networks. The importance of digital accessibility cannot be overstated, as it serves as the foundation for inclusive digital transformation.
Solution Overview:
A. PROPOSED SOLUTIONS:
1. Facilitating Transitions into Digital Employment:
One effective strategy is the establishment of partnerships between educational institutions, employers, and community organizations. These partnerships can create pathways for internships, apprenticeships, and job placements that specifically target individuals with disabilities. By providing real-world experience and mentorship, these initiatives can enhance employability and foster a sense of belonging in the workplace.

2. Disability Policy and Advocacy
To achieve a disability-inclusive digital transformation, robust policy frameworks and advocacy efforts are essential. Policymakers play a critical role in establishing regulations and standards that promote accessibility and inclusion in the digital space. This includes enforcing existing laws, such as the Persons with Disabilities Act 2025, newly passed in Kenya, and developing new policies that address the evolving needs of individuals with disabilities in a digital economy.

3. Promoting Digital Skills and inclusive design principles
The integration of digital skills training into existing educational frameworks is essential for ensuring that adolescents with disabilities are equipped to transition into the workforce. By prioritizing digital skills development, we can create a more equitable environment where individuals with disabilities can compete on equal footing with their peers.
Inclusive design principles emphasize the importance of user-centered design processes that involve individuals with disabilities in the development of digital solutions. 

B. METHODOLOGIES
A mixed-methods approach is envisaged, integrating both qualitative and quantitative methodologies. This dual approach allows for a more nuanced understanding of the complexities surrounding digital accessibility and inclusion for people with disabilities. The qualitative component focuses on gathering in-depth insights from participants, while the quantitative aspect aims to quantify the impact of digital solutions on economic empowerment and inclusion.

Qualitative Methods and data collection tools
Semi-Structured Interviews and Focus Group Discussions will explore the lived experiences of youth with disabilities as they navigate the digital landscape with a focus on accessibility, digital literacy and the extent to which digital solutions contribute to participants' economic empowerment

Quantitative Methods and data collection tools
Surveys using semi-structured questionnaires will be used to measure the effectiveness of various digital solutions. This aspect of the research aims to identify patterns and correlations between digital accessibility initiatives and economic outcomes for individuals with disabilities. By collecting numerical data, the study seeks to provide empirical evidence that supports the qualitative findings 

Participant Selection and Inclusion Criteria with appropriate ethical considerations of informed consent, confidentiality and dignity
The study will target a diverse group of individuals with disabilities, ensuring representation across various demographics, including age, gender, socioeconomic status, and types of disabilities.
1. Individuals aged 15 to 35 (youth) with a documented disability.
2. Participants who have experience using digital technologies, whether for personal, educational, or employment purposes.
3. A willingness to share their experiences and insights regarding digital accessibility and inclusion.

Data Analysis 
Qualitative methods will generate themes which will be coded and grouped
Quantitative methods will utilize descriptive and inferential statistics with graphs and charts 

Partnerships and Stakeholder Engagement
The study seeks to collaborate with organizations that work directly with individuals with disabilities as well as educational institutions and employers.
Solution Provider(s): Eastern African Academy of Childhood Disabilities, World Rehabilitation Alliance, Aga Khan University, Nairobi, Ministry of Health kenya, Acorn schools
Duration to pilot in a new geography: 6 months
SDGs addressed: SDG 17 (Partnerships for the Goals);SDG 10 (Reduced Inequalities);SDG 9 (Industry, Innovation, and Infrastructure);
Desired impact:
1. Policy recommendations to increase uptake of digital disability inclusive strategies

2. Creation of targeted training programs for enhancing digital skills among individuals with disabilities to be adopted by academic institutions and employers
Key technologies: Digital questionnaires on AI supported platforms
Unique Characteristics: Involvement of academic institutions, employment agencies, government representation and disability inclusive organizations with the initiatives being led by persons living with disability...rather than solutions being prescribed by non-disabled groups
Sustainable Change:
1. Employment generation and inclusion for persons with disabilities
2. Improved capacity and independence amongst disabled communities
Funding Sources:
This solution is novel to Kenya and has not been assessed.

In other parts of the world, such initiatives have been state-driven
Testimonials and Endorsements: Not available
Further comments/feedback: The questionnaire is very concise and captures all the salient points.
Primary thematic focus area: Enabling Policies & Regulatory Innovation
Summary: Digital Opportunities for All (DOFA) is a proof-of-concept initiative in Kenya aiming to enhance the digital and economic participation of persons with disabilities. It proposes a mixed-methods research and action framework to understand barriers and co-develop pathways for digital skills training, inclusive design, policy advocacy, and employment transitions. By working with government (Ministry of Health), academia (Aga Khan University), and disability organizations, DOFA seeks to generate evidence-based policy recommendations, foster digital accessibility standards, and create targeted training programs. Its distinctiveness lies in being led by persons with disabilities themselves, ensuring authentic representation and bottom-up inclusion in shaping solutions.

Title: Tekuwami: Bridging Digital Gaps for MSMEs and Inclusive Innovation in Africa
Subtitle: A next-generation digital platform enabling MSMEs and institutions to collect, analyze, and act on field data in real time—empowering inclusive growth across Africa.
Problem Statement: Across Africa, MSMEs and institutions struggle with fragmented, manual, and paper-based data collection systems, leading to inefficiencies, limited access to real-time insights, and barriers to evidence-based decision-making. Many organizations—especially those in underserved or remote regions—lack affordable, scalable digital tools that work in low-connectivity environments. This digital divide limits their capacity to deliver services efficiently, reach marginalized communities, and participate fully in the digital economy.
Solution Overview:
Tekuwami is a modular, AI-powered digital platform designed to empower MSMEs and institutions with end-to-end field data collection, workflow automation, and real-time analytics. The platform enables users to design, deploy, and manage custom digital forms and workflows for various sectors—including health, agriculture, urban planning, and humanitarian interventions—without coding skills.

How it Works:
Tekuwami provides a cloud-based web portal and a mobile app, both accessible in low-bandwidth environments. Institutions and MSMEs can create digital forms, assign data collection tasks, and monitor progress in real time. Field agents use the mobile app to capture structured data, GPS locations, images, and more—even offline. All submissions are securely synced to the cloud when connectivity is available, ensuring robust data integrity and accessibility.

Methodologies and Technologies:

AI-driven Form Builder: Institutions can auto-generate forms based on their requirements using GPT-powered field mapping and validation.

Cloud-Native Architecture: Built on Firebase and Flutter, ensuring high scalability, security, and cross-platform compatibility.

Offline-First Design: Data collection and syncing are optimized for environments with intermittent connectivity.

Role-Based Access Controls: Enables secure, permissioned collaboration among super admins, institutional admins, and field agents.

Real-Time Analytics: Instant dashboards provide actionable insights for evidence-based decision-making.

Partnerships and Collaboration Models:
Tekuwami collaborates with local and international NGOs, government agencies, universities, and private sector partners to tailor solutions for specific sectors and geographies. The platform supports integration with partner systems via APIs and encourages co-creation with stakeholders, empowering local institutions to innovate and scale digital transformation according to their unique needs.
Solution Provider(s): Tekuwami – An Ethiopian-born digital platform delivering AI-powered field data collection and workflow management solutions for MSMEs, government agencies, NGOs, and humanitarian organizations. Tekuwami empowers institutions with scalable, secure, and user-friendly digital tools for real-time data-driven decision-making across sectors such as health, agriculture, urban planning, and public services.  Aries Finance and Management PLC – A private Ethiopian firm providing financial advisory, management consulting, and capacity-building services to MSMEs, public institutions, and development partners, with a focus on driving sustainable growth and effective resource management in the African context.
Implementation location(s): Ethiopia – Currently implemented with select institutions and MSMEs in Addis Ababa and Mekelle, with expansion plans to additional regions across Ethiopia.
Implementation timeline(s): Pilot implementation began in March 2025 and is ongoing as of July 2025.
Duration to pilot in a new geography: The typical duration to pilot Tekuwami in a new geography is 3 to 6 months, depending on project scope, partner readiness, and customization requirements.The typical duration to pilot Tekuwami in a new geography is 3 to 6 months, depending on project scope, partner readiness, and customization requirements.
SDGs addressed: SDG 8 (Decent Work and Economic Growth);SDG 9 (Industry, Innovation, and Infrastructure);SDG 10 (Reduced Inequalities);
Desired impact:
Solution Objectives:

Empower MSMEs and institutions to transition from manual to digital, data-driven operations.

Enhance efficiency, transparency, and evidence-based decision-making for organizations in Africa.

Promote digital inclusion and capacity-building, especially for underserved communities, women, and youth.

Facilitated data-driven service delivery to marginalized communities in Ethiopia, expanding access to digital tools for economic and social development.
Key technologies:
Key Technologies Used:

Artificial Intelligence (AI):
Tekuwami leverages AI-powered form generation and smart field mapping to automate and optimize digital data collection and workflow processes.

Cloud Computing:
Built on scalable, secure cloud infrastructure (Firebase), enabling real-time data storage, syncing, and analytics.

Mobile Technology:
The solution includes a cross-platform mobile app (built with Flutter) for field data collection, supporting offline data capture and seamless syncing when connectivity is available.

Geolocation/GPS:
Integrated GPS features allow for location-based data collection and mapping, enhancing the accuracy and context of field submissions.

Data Analytics:
Real-time dashboards and analytics tools provide actionable insights to institutions and MSMEs, supporting evidence-based decision-making.
Unique Characteristics:
Tekuwami stands out through the following unique features:

AI-Driven Dynamic Form Builder:
Institutions and MSMEs can generate customized digital forms automatically from simple prompts, streamlining configuration and reducing technical barriers.

Offline-First, Low-Connectivity Design:
The platform is built for Africa’s realities, enabling full functionality in remote and low-bandwidth areas—ensuring inclusion for even the most underserved regions.

Modular, Scalable Platform:
Tekuwami supports multiple use cases and sectors (health, agriculture, urban planning, etc.) through a flexible, no-code environment, allowing rapid adaptation to partners’ needs.

Inclusive Business Model:
Offers affordable access for MSMEs and non-profits, and encourages co-creation with local partners to tailor solutions, share capacity, and foster digital skills.

Seamless Collaboration & Real-Time Analytics:
Role-based access controls, workflow automation, and instant analytics empower organizations to act quickly and collaboratively, accelerating impact.
Sustainable Change:
By equipping MSMEs and institutions with accessible, AI-powered digital tools for field data collection and workflow management, Tekuwami enables organizations to operate more efficiently, transparently, and inclusively. This transition away from manual, paper-based processes leads to:

The platform’s modular, sector-agnostic design allows rapid replication and scaling across regions, sectors, and partners, multiplying positive impact.

Strengthened local ecosystems:
By fostering collaboration among MSMEs, government, and development partners, Tekuwami accelerates digital inclusion, economic growth, and the creation of new market opportunities.

Resilient, adaptive systems:
Organizations become better equipped to respond to emerging challenges, support marginalized groups, and sustain improvements beyond initial deployment.

In summary: Tekuwami catalyzes a sustainable shift toward digital, data-driven operations, creating ripple effects that empower local actors, foster continuous innovation, and build resilient, inclusive economies over time.

Name of your organization: WASTELOGIC AND RECYCLING CONCEPTS NIGERIA ENTERPRISE
Title: WASTELOGIC: A Smart Circular Platform for Inclusive Digital Waste Economy
Subtitle: WASTELOGIC is a smart digital platform connecting waste generators to collectors, empowering MSMEs and underserved communities through inclusive, trackable, and sustainable waste solutions.
Problem Statement: WASTELOGIC addresses key challenges in waste management, including poor waste disposal practices, lack of digital access for waste pickers and MSMEs, exclusion from carbon credit systems, and limited data for effective recycling. It tackles the digital divide in environmental services by connecting underserved communities to a circular economy model, enabling traceable collection, income generation, and climate impact accountability.
Solution Overview:
Solution Overview – WASTELOGIC

1. How the Solution Works:
WASTELOGIC is a smart, inclusive digital platform designed to revolutionize waste management by connecting waste generators (households, offices, restaurants, estates) with local waste collectors and recyclers. Users can schedule pickups via a mobile app or USSD code, track collection in real-time, and earn incentives or carbon credit points based on waste quantity and type. Waste collectors, many of whom are women and youth in underserved communities, get digitally registered, trained, and equipped to operate professionally and earn income. The platform aggregates waste data to enable traceable recycling, carbon credit generation, and environmental reporting.

2. Methodologies and Technologies Used:
	•	Geo-location & Real-Time Tracking: Enables users and waste collectors to track pickup activities and map waste flows.
	•	Mobile App & USSD Access: Ensures accessibility for both smartphone and feature phone users, bridging the digital divide.
	•	Digital ID & QR Code for Collectors: Ensures transparency and traceability in collections.
	•	Data Analytics Dashboard: Gathers and analyzes data on waste types, volumes, and collection trends for reporting and optimization.
	•	Carbon Credit Integration: Tracks emissions reduced via recycled waste and connects the data to carbon offset opportunities.
	•	Gamification & Incentives: Users receive reward points for consistent recycling, encouraging behavioral change.

3. Partnerships and Collaboration Models:
	•	Waste360Nigeria (Partner Recycler): Supports sorting, logistics, and end-user recycling.
	•	Federal University Lokoja (Academic Partner): Collaborates on training, research, and tech support.

Title: JumpToPC Personal computing solution to provide access to modern digital learning and productivity tools
Subtitle: An affordable and accessible personal computing solution to provide access to modern digital learning and productivity tools.  During the past decade India has entered a digital revolution as online services provide access to education, finance, employment and political participation. However, 80% of the population lacks the basic digital skills and tools to participate in and benefit from the Digital India revolution. The COVID-19 pandemic has promoted digital inclusion for some, but has left large swaths further behind. Girls are disproportionately affected since they are often excluded from accessing computers outside of the home.  JumpToPC is a practical and scalable solution that provides the means for India’s digitally excluded to learn and use digital services. With an experience tailored for first-time computer users, JumpToPC pairs with a smartphone and television to create an affordable home computer. It is compatible with most digital learning content, and offers a platform to build and distribute new content, making it adaptable to the specific needs of underserved communities in India and globally.
Problem Statement: Full inclusion in the digital economy means that students and workers are equipped with accessible technology and digital knowhow. Only 10% of Indian households have broadband internet and half as many own a computer, leaving 1.3 billion people, the bottom billion, without the means to fully participate in the digital economy. On the other hand, the Government of India has made aggressive moves toward digitisation of government services, healthcare and education, and India is home to the world’s largest IT workforce in the only economic sector with positive growth prior to the pandemic. Smartphone ownership is rapidly increasing and expected to reach nearly 1 billion devices by 2025, driven in part by the world’s most affordable mobile data rates. However, viewing, tapping and swiping won’t lead to full digital inclusion. Post COVID-19, the need for remote learning and work-from-home tools have risen exponentially. Smartphones are an adequate solution to consume content, but they aren’t suitable for interactive learning, problem-solving in maths or learning digital skills - a must for entry-level jobs. In the absence of technology, infrastructure and training targeted toward the digitally illiterate, the global digital divide will continue to grow wider.
Solution Overview:
Digital content is expanding at an unprecedented rate, and many households already have most of the devices needed to access them. JumpToPC technology augments these, enabling learners to jump across the digital divide. The solution consists of three components: a device that wirelessly pairs the user’s existing smartphone and television, a mobile application that transforms the mobile OS into a big screen desktop experience, and peripherals that allow the user to interact in the digital environment.

JumpToPC includes technology advances that are responsive to her needs. The hardware connects any smartphone to any television, including old CRTs, using a peer-to-peer wireless protocol that does not require external WiFi. The base peripheral set includes a keyboard and mouse designed for mobile-first users. Each user receives a set of compatible applications (e.g. browser, word processor, spreadsheet, content), and can easily add from the curated JumpToPC Library as she advances. Users can also receive free content recommendations driven by JumpToPC’s recommendation engine. The pairing also works without any Internet connectivity, making it a perfect solution in those low-to-no connectivity areas.

JumpToPC can be implemented at an institutional level with additional custom-built features including e-classroom software, video and voice peripherals and pre-installed offline content.
Solution Provider(s): JumpToPC provides an opportunity for underserved students, entrepreneurs, families and other digitally curious people to own and use technology that is currently unaffordable and unfamiliar. Alongside our distribution partner, Greenway Appliances, we have spent most of the past decade serving underserved Indian communities with life-improving household products. JumpToPC was born from conversations with students, teachers, mothers, fathers, business-men and -women, local leaders in these communities, and developed with their regular input, testing and feedback. During JumpToPC user acceptance testing, we learned about women who were hired for at-home data entry jobs, students who could participate in remote courses, and girls who were writing their first Python scripts. We recognize that for many families, inclusion in the digital economy can effectively begin with youth. Therefore, we are focusing on serving students’ needs, especially given the urgency brought by the pandemic.  While most technology companies serve India’s top 10% income earners, the stories from JumpToPC’s first users have motivated us to further develop technology tailored for them. With an average annual income of 40,000 INR (525 USD), the bottom 50% of Indian households cannot afford laptop and desktop computers, so we targeted a price of 20% the price of a low-cost laptop. For example, we have seen smartphones quickly become one of the first luxury goods purchases for low-income families. Therefore, we designed JumpToPC’s peripherals and user interface for mobile-first users. This is how we knew that quick adoption would depend on minimal behavioural changes. English language comprehension is often low in these communities, so we are adapting JumpToPC for regional languages. JumpToPC is an in-home solution, comprising devices that she is innately familiar with, and lowering barriers for her to be included in the digital economy.
Implementation location(s): JumpToPC is currently being piloted in several communities in India, but primarily by approximately 3000 users in Western Karnataka where our team has extensive work experience and knowledge of the local culture and languages. Prior to the COVID-19 pandemic, we completed development of the basic JumpToPC setup and demonstrated it at dozens of schools, NGOs and clubs in Karnataka. Many of the first JumpToPC users came from those demonstrations. During the pandemic, we ceased in-person and hosted regular virtual demonstrations with many attendees representing schools and educational NGOs serving low-income and rural communities.
Implementation timeline(s): JumpToPC is currently in use in approximately 3000 households for learning and working from home. On average we see that there are at least two users per home. Our users are both those who have bought directly from us, as well as those who have received it from the schools or NGOs that have partnered with us.   In the next one year, we aim to reach at least 50,000 households and we are on track to scale to 1 million households in the next 5 years. How are you measuring your progress toward your impact goals?      Total number of units distributed - This is easily measured, and we collate the user demographics. This helps us to define our user set as well as calculate our reach, and in turn impact. Daily and Monthly Active Usage on our app is also taken into account.       Completion of basic digital tools tutorials - We measure this via our app analytics, and ensure that every user has completed it. This includes typing, mouse skills and preparing an age-appropriate word document. This is accounted as becoming digitally literate as per the National Digital Literacy Mission developed by the Government of India.      Completion of foundational skills especially in literacy and mathematics, based on national curriculum levels - We are adding grade-appropriate tests that can be accredited and help students graduate classes without having to repeat years especially with at-home learning or missed schooling. In our next phase, we will also curate these in multiple regional languages.       Completion rates for boys and girls - We measure this by dividing the total number of all students who logged-in for the first time vs the number of boys/girls who have completed certain predetermined levels - this helps us calculate dropout rates by gender.       Set up impact measurement trackers with our allied schools and foundations, along the same lines as above. We also build certain customised services and analytics basis feedback or requests from our partners.
Duration to pilot in a new geography: 8Months
SDGs addressed: SDG 4 (Quality Education);SDG 8 (Decent Work and Economic Growth);SDG 9 (Industry, Innovation, and Infrastructure);

Our users are both those who have bought directly from us, as well as those who have received it from the schools or NGOs that have partnered with us. 

In the next one year, we aim to reach at least 50,000 households and we are on track to scale to 1 million households in the next 5 years.

How we are measuring our progress toward our impact goals

    Total number of units distributed - This is easily measured, and we collate the user demographics. This helps us to define our user set as well as calculate our reach, and in turn impact. Daily and Monthly Active Usage on our app is also taken into account. 

    Completion of basic digital tools tutorials - We measure this via our app analytics, and ensure that every user has completed it. This includes typing, mouse skills and preparing an age-appropriate word document. This is accounted as becoming digitally literate as per the National Digital Literacy Mission developed by the Government of India.

    Completion of foundational skills especially in literacy and mathematics, based on national curriculum levels - We are adding grade-appropriate tests that can be accredited and help students graduate classes without having to repeat years especially with at-home learning or missed schooling. In our next phase, we will also curate these in multiple regional languages. 

    Completion rates for boys and girls - We measure this by dividing the total number of all students who logged-in for the first time vs the number of boys/girls who have completed certain predetermined levels - this helps us calculate dropout rates by gender. 

    Set up impact measurement trackers with our allied schools and foundations, along the same lines as above. We also build certain customised services and analytics basis feedback or requests from our partners.

JumpToPC’s innovation arises from scarcity in low-income households, every family’s desire to create a better future for their children, and the recent increase in penetration of mobile technology. With an average annual income of 40,000 INR (525 USD), the bottom 50% of Indian households cannot afford conventional computers. However, with an average 20% of their income spent on education, JumpToPC fits within household constraints as an educational investment. By focusing on this cost constraint, we took a different approach compared to competitors like Sentio and Nexdock who pair the smartphone with a laptop shell. Since 70% of Indian households already own a television, JumpToPC leverages that for the display instead of a dedicated monitor, eliminating 15% of the cost of a computer. 

In addition, India has the cheapest mobile data in the world and fastest growing smartphone ownership, which serves as the processor and storage in JumpToPC, eliminating an additional 50% cost. The display adapter functions similarly to a Chromecast and Fire TV stick, but meets the specific needs of our target customers by using a secure peer-to-peer wireless connection instead of WiFi, no subscription- or pay-wall, and easy setup with local customer support. Today, all Indians are familiar with using mobile applications including ShareChat, WhatsApp and TikTok, which was not the case when products like One Laptop Per Child, Aakash tablet, and Intel’s Classmate PC were introduced. JumpToPC is built in Android for the mobile-first user to make their transition to digital literacy easier.

Title: NextGen Code: Inclusive Digital Startups for Woman Empowerment
Subtitle: A gender-inclusive digital startup platform enabling women in underserved communities to access training, tools, and mentorship—driving innovation, economic participation, and digital leadership.
Problem Statement: Women in rural and underserved areas of Bangladesh face significant barriers in accessing and utilizing digital tools and fintech services. The lack of digital literacy, limited training opportunities, and poor connectivity exclude them from the benefits of the growing digital economy. Women entrepreneurs struggle to start or grow digital businesses due to insufficient skills, resources, and mentorship. These challenges limit their economic participation, leadership, and financial independence in the digital space.
Solution Overview:
“NextGen Code” is a digital capacity-building initiative aimed at empowering underserved women entrepreneurs in rural Bangladesh through inclusive, mobile-first digital startup training. The solution works by combining mobile-based learning modules, community-led mentoring, and access to fintech tools in local languages.

We utilize a low-bandwidth progressive web app (PWA) that delivers video, SMS, and interactive quizzes, allowing women with basic mobile phones or weak internet to fully participate. The curriculum includes digital literacy, e-commerce, mobile banking, and digital marketing.

Our approach follows a blended model, combining online modules with offline support via community facilitators. The solution includes progress tracking, peer networks, and guided startup toolkits.

Key partnerships involve:

Local NGOs for mobilization and offline support

Tech firms for app and content development

Financial institutions for fintech integration and business support

Women-led networks to ensure community ownership and feedback

This collaborative and locally adapted model ensures sustainability, relevance, and replicability.
Solution Provider(s): Bhagni Nivedita Manchya (BNM) (BNM) – A women-led NGO working to empower rural women in Bangladesh through economic and digital literacy (Civil Society / Gender). TechBridge Solutions Ltd. – A tech firm that develops mobile-based learning platforms and fintech tools for inclusive access (Private Sector / ICT). Grameen Bank Digital Division – A financial institution offering digital finance and micro-credit for women in underserved regions (Finance / Inclusive Banking). Women in Digital Network Bangladesh – A gender-focused network promoting digital education, e-commerce, and IT careers for women (Gender / ICT Education).

10,000 women trained in digital literacy, fintech, and entrepreneurship.

200+ women-led digital startups launched and operational.

30% of trained women will gain employment or start earning within 6 months.

Title: TrackMe: Transforming every day environmental actions into impactful rewards.
Subtitle: TrackMe is a simple, AI-powered mobile app designed to fight plastic pollution at the source, even without internet access.TrackMe empowers everyday Cameroonians to fight plastic pollution while earning rewards. Citizens use their smartphones to take photos of plastic waste, and our app automatically identifies the type of plastic and rewards them with tokens. The app works without internet connection and helps waste collection teams know exactly where to find plastic waste for cleanup.
Problem Statement:
Cameroon produces over 600,000 tonnes of plastic waste annually, but more than 80% remains unmanaged, particularly in informal settlements where no system exists to detect plastic at the point of discard (MinEPDED, 2023).

This unmanaged waste flows into waterways, clogs drainage systems, and pollutes ecosystems, leading to increased flood risk and negative health impacts in urban areas.

TrackMe bridges this critical gap by enabling citizens to identify and report plastic waste at the source, before it causes environmental or public health damage.
Solution Overview:
TrackMe is a simple, AI-powered mobile app designed to fight plastic pollution at the source, even without internet access.
How TrackMe Works
A. For Citizens
1. Take a Photo : Snap a picture of plastic waste anywhere
2. Get Instant Results : The app identifies what type of plastic it is
3. Earn Rewards :Receive tokens that can be exchanged for airtime, goods/cash
4. Track Impact : See how much waste you have helped identify and remove.


B. For Waste Collection Teams

1. Real-time Alerts :Get notified immediately when waste is reported nearby
2. Live Map : See all reported waste locations on an interactive map
3. Route Planning :Optimize collection routes for maximum efficiency
4. Status Updates : Mark waste as collected, update citizens automatically.

C. For Management and Partners

1. Live Dashboard: Monitor plastic waste patterns across Cameroon
2. Impact Reports:Track tonnes of waste identified and collected
3. Community Engagement: See user participation and regional activity.

Technology Used
Our solution uses five main technologies;
1. Flutter for mobile app platform development. Fluuter builds apps that work on all Android devices with one codebase. It was chosen because its;
-Cost-effective for development
- High performance on older phones
- Easy to maintain and update

2.TensorFlow Lite for smart plastic identification system
 -What it does: Automatically recognizes different types of plastic (bottles, bags,
containers, etc.) from photos
 -How it works: AI model trained on thousands of plastic images learns to identify patterns.
- Key benefit: Works offline on the device with internet needed for identification
-Accuracy: 85%+ correct identification rate
- Device support: Optimized for older smartphones (Android 6.0+).

3. Circle Wallet Integration for digital token management for payment and rewards.
-What it does: Manages user reward tokens and enables easy redemption
- How users access: Simple wallet interface within the TrackMe app
- Redemption options:
 Mobile airtime top-up
 Cash withdrawal at partner locations.
Goods at participating gift shops
-Security: Bank-level encryption and fraud protection.
-Local currency: Tokens can be converted to CFA Francs.

4.Supabase a modern database with instant updates for database management and real-time updates: 
- What it stores: User data, waste reports, collection status, rewards
- Real-time feature: Collection teams get instant notifications when waste is reported
- Backup and security: Automatic data backup with enterprise-grade security
- Offline sync: Data saved locally when no internet, uploads automatically when
connected.

5.Mapbox an advanced mapping platform for maps production and location tracking : It key components includes;
-Visual features: Beautiful, customizable maps with waste location pins
- Offline maps: Works without internet connection
- Heat maps: Shows areas with highest plastic waste concentration
-Route optimization: Helps collection teams plan efficient pickup routes
- GPS accuracy: Precise location tracking for waste reports.


Budget for Development: Total Investment Required: $35,000 
1. App Development ($30,000): This covers the core mobile app build across three phases.
2.Technology Infrastructure ($3,000): Allocated for setting up crucial services like Supabase database, Mapbox maps, and Circle Wallet.
3. AI Model Training($1,500):Dedicated to developing and optimizing the TensorFlow Lite plastic identification model.
4. User Rewards Pool($500):An initial fund for early user incentives and testing of the rewards system.

Key technologies:
Our solution uses five main technologies;
1. Flutter for mobile app platform development. Fluuter builds apps that work on all Android devices with one codebase. It was chosen because its;
-Cost-effective for development

- Easy to maintain and update

2.TensorFlow Lite for smart plastic identification system
 -What it does: Automatically recognizes different types of plastic (bottles, bags,

 Mobile airtime top-up
 Cash withdrawal at partner locations.

2. AI-powered plastic identification: Enhancing accuracy and efficiency in waste reporting.
3.Real-time coordination: Streamlining waste collection and team communication.
 4.Digital token wallet: Providing a secure and convenient reward system.

Name of your organization: Fine Art Void [running the project named "Museums at Fingertips" (MaF)]
Title: Quality museum education with no borders for all abilities
Subtitle: Lining up the global museum education virtually with the local physical gallery/museum on-site and improving social life across countries with cultural exchange
Problem Statement: Mission of this project is to nurture inclusion, diversity and equity towards the people of visually impairment (VI) through art education and building empathy between the public, especially students and people with different visual abilities. The project also provides quality arts “edu-tainment” (educational entertainment) to improve quality of life.
Solution Overview:
The lack of networking opportunities for people with different visual abilities to get to understand each other and the limited museum education resources for VI, especially touch art with audio description (AD) which they can spend enough time to learn, the services and products in my project could be a good tool and experience to bridge up different groups as “Art is for ALL”.

There are many international museum around the world open their collections with 3D scanned data for educational usage, e.g. British Museum, my proposed project is to select 5 popular museums worldwide which share 3D scan models to be printed, 10 selected models from each museum, audio descriptions in Cantonese will be accompanied (my training certificate in audio description (AD) with the Arts with the Disabled Association Hong Kong (ADAHK) and related work experience in CV as attached), Talks and Workshops will be hold with the 3D printed models in schools and communities. 

Co-create the learning experience while developing the AD for the tangible art collections from different museums. It provides a valuable opportunity for students with different visual abilities to communicate and build empathy through discussion. Students will have the chance to learn about the accessible museum services from professionals, e.g. materials developed by museum educators, which they may apply the knowledge in their daily life.

The creative element of the proposed solution is that I use the official open sources of 3D model data from museums, then use the 3D print with the relevant materials e.g. polyester, ceramics, PVC coated with metals, as the touch sense of different materials is important when making tangible artefacts (this factor is less focus in current practice). Also, training in audio description will be introduced.

Title: L'accès abordable et de qualité : Développer des solutions pour rendre l'internet haut débit, les appareils numériques et les services connexes plus accessibles financièrement, en particulier dans les zones rurales et mal desservies.
Subtitle: Les compétences numériques : Mettre en place des programmes de formation pour développer les compétences numériques de base et avancées, en ciblant les populations les plus vulnérables (femmes, personnes âgées, personnes handicapées, etc.).
Problem Statement:
Accès limité ou coûteux : Une grande partie de la population mondiale, en particulier dans les zones rurales ou les pays en développement, n'a pas accès à une connexion internet fiable, rapide et abordable, ni aux appareils nécessaires (smartphones, ordinateurs). Le coût de l'accès peut être un frein insurmontable.
Manque de compétences numériques : Même avec un accès, de nombreuses personnes ne possèdent pas les compétences de base pour utiliser les outils numériques, naviguer sur internet en toute sécurité, ou exploiter les opportunités offertes par le numérique. Cela touche particulièrement les populations âgées, les femmes, les personnes peu éduquées ou issues de milieux défavorisés.
Infrastructures insuffisantes : Dans de nombreuses régions, l'absence d'infrastructures de communication robustes (fibre optique, couverture mobile) rend difficile, voire impossible, le déploiement de services numériques.
Solution Overview:
Accès Connecté et Abordable :
Déploiement d'Infrastructures Hybrides : Nous utilisons une combinaison de technologies pour assurer une couverture étendue. Dans les zones urbaines et périurbaines, nous renforçons l'accès à la fibre optique et à la 5G. Pour les zones rurales et isolées, nous déployons des solutions innovantes comme les réseaux communautaires Wi-Fi alimentés par des énergies renouvelables (solaire), les satellites à basse orbite (LEO) pour une connectivité rapide, et les technologies radio à longue portée (LoRaWAN) pour l'internet des objets (IoT) à faible coût.
Points d'Accès Publics et Communautaires : Nous établissons des "Hubs Numériques Communautaires" équipés d'ordinateurs, de tablettes et de points Wi-Fi gratuits ou à très faible coût. Ces hubs servent de centres névralgiques pour l'accès à internet, la formation et le support technique.
Subventions et Modèles de Financement Innovants : En collaboration avec les gouvernements et les opérateurs, nous mettons en place des subventions ciblées pour l'achat d'appareils à faible coût (smartphones reconditionnés, tablettes éducatives) et des forfaits internet abordables. Nous explorons des modèles de paiement à l'usage (pay-as-you-go) pour rendre la connectivité accessible même aux budgets limités.
Renforcement des Compétences Numériques :
Programmes de Formation Adaptés : Nous développons des modules de formation modulaires et contextualisés, allant de l'alphabétisation numérique de base (utilisation d'un smartphone, navigation web, communication en ligne) aux compétences avancées (e-commerce, marketing numérique, bureautique, bases de la programmation).
Approche Pédagogique Inclusive : Les formations sont dispensées en plusieurs langues locales, avec des formats adaptés (vidéos, tutoriels interactifs, sessions en présentiel) et des facilitateurs locaux formés pour accompagner les apprenants. Nous utilisons des outils d'apprentissage gamifiés pour rendre l'expérience engageante et des plateformes d'apprentissage en ligne (LMS) accessibles hors ligne pour les zones à faible connectivité.
Certification et Reconnaissance : Nous travaillons avec des institutions éducatives et des entreprises pour offrir des certifications reconnues, augmentant ainsi l'employabilité des participants. Un système de passeport de compétences numériques basé sur la blockchain est envisagé pour garantir la portabilité et la vérifiabilité des acquis.
Facilitation des Opportunités Économiques et Sociales :
Plateforme d'Inclusion Financière Numérique : Nous développons une application mobile conviviale qui agrège des services financiers essentiels (paiements mobiles, micro-crédits, épargne, assurance) auprès de partenaires bancaires et de FinTechs. Cette plateforme intègre des fonctionnalités de conseil financier simple et des alertes personnalisées.
Marketplace Locale et Soutien à l'Entrepreneuriat : Création d'une plateforme d'e-commerce locale permettant aux petites entreprises et aux artisans de vendre leurs produits et services en ligne. Nous offrons un accompagnement à la numérisation des TPE/PME, y compris la création de vitrines numériques, la gestion des commandes et le marketing digital.
Mise en Relation Emploi/Formation : Intégration d'un module de mise en relation entre les bénéficiaires formés et les opportunités d'emploi ou de missions en ligne (crowdworking, micro-tâches), en partenariat avec des entreprises et des plateformes de freelancing.
Accès aux Services Publics et de Santé : Collaboration avec les gouvernements pour numériser et rendre accessibles certains services publics (démarches administratives, informations sanitaires, télémédecine basique) via les Hubs Numériques et la plateforme mobile.

Title: Inclusive Digital Platform for Eco-Cooking and Agroecology in Rural Guinea.
Subtitle: An inclusive digital platform that trains rural women in clean cookstove production and agroecology, while connecting them to local markets—even with low or no internet access.
Problem Statement: In rural Guinea, women lack access to training, markets, and digital tools to adopt and promote clean cookstoves and agroecological practices. This limits income opportunities and worsens deforestation and health risks from traditional cooking methods.
Solution Overview:
The solution is an inclusive digital platform—accessible online and offline via mobile or low-bandwidth devices—that provides rural women and youth with practical training on the fabrication of improved cookstoves and agroecological techniques. The platform includes video tutorials in local languages, step-by-step guides, and peer-to-peer learning spaces. Participants can showcase and sell their products (cookstoves, compost, seedlings, etc.) through a built-in marketplace, connecting them to local consumers and NGOs.
Methodologies and Technologies Used:
•	Blended Training Approach: Combines in-person workshops with offline-accessible digital content.
•	Human-Centered Design: Developed with input from rural women, artisans, and farmers.
•	Low-Tech Access: USSD/SMS features and downloadable content to reach users without reliable internet.
•	Agroecological Principles: Promotes sustainable, locally adapted farming and energy practices.
•	Digital Literacy Tools: Basic modules to enhance users’ digital skills and autonomy.
Partnerships and Collaboration Models:
•	Local NGOs (e.g., APPEG Guinée): Facilitate training and community mobilization.
•	Agroecological farms and artisan networks: Act as training hubs and local mentors.
•	Tech developers: Build and maintain the platform with a focus on offline functionality.
•	Government agencies and municipalities: Support scaling through policy alignment and access to public infrastructure.
•	Women’s groups and youth associations: Serve as entry points for community-based implementation.
Solution Provider(s): APPEG Guinée (Association pour la Promotion de la Paix, l’Environnement et le Genre) – A Guinean NGO working in community development, environmental protection, and women’s empowerment, Consortium APAC Guinée – A national platform promoting the recognition and protection of community-conserved areas (ICCAs), active in biodiversity and sustainable land governance, Local Agroecological Farms – Practical hubs for training in sustainable farming and composting, Women and Youth Artisans’ Cooperatives – Community-based groups supporting skills development and local entrepreneurship, Independent Tech Developers – Providing digital solutions adapted to low-connectivity contexts.
Implementation location(s): Diembéra, Saliya-École District, Bantignel Sous-prefecture, Pita Prefecture, Mamou Region, Republic of Guinea. The first phase is 16 months from June 2023 to September 2024 in search of the realization of the second phase.
Implementation timeline(s): The estimated time to implement the full solution is 16 to 18 months, covering development, pilot testing, training, and initial market integration.
Duration to pilot in a new geography: The estimated time to implement the full solution is 16 to 18 months, covering development, pilot testing, training, and initial market integration.
SDGs addressed: SDG 10 (Reduced Inequalities);SDG 13 (Climate Action);SDG 5 (Gender Equality);
Desired impact:
Solution Objectives:
•	Empower rural women and youth with skills in improved cookstove fabrication and agroecological practices.
•	Increase household incomes through access to local and digital markets.
•	Reduce reliance on traditional biomass fuels, lowering deforestation and indoor air pollution.
•	Strengthen community resilience by promoting sustainable agriculture and clean energy.
•	Foster digital inclusion and knowledge sharing in low-connectivity rural areas.
Key Achievements / Impacts:
• Train at least 500 rural women and artisans within 16 months.
• Increase average participant income by 30% through product sales on the platform.
• Reduce firewood consumption by 70% among beneficiary households using improved cookstoves.
• Lower greenhouse gas emissions by an estimated 250 tons CO₂ equivalent annually.
• Create 60 new local jobs linked to cookstove production and agroecological farming.
• Enable digital access and literacy for over 80% of platform users despite low internet connectivity.
Key Technologies Used in the Solution
•	Mobile and Web Platform: A lightweight digital platform optimized for low-bandwidth and offline use, enabling access to training content and marketplace features via smartphones and basic mobile phones.
•	USSD and SMS Technology: To reach users without internet access, allowing navigation, learning prompts, and market transactions through simple text or menu-based commands.
•	Video and Multimedia Content: Pre-recorded, localized tutorials and demonstrations accessible offline to facilitate practical learning.
•	Cloud-based Content Management: For easy updates and remote management of training modules and marketplace listings.
•	Data Analytics (basic): To monitor user engagement, track sales, and assess impact metrics.
•	Digital Literacy Tools: Integrated simple modules to improve users’ comfort with technology and digital communication.
Note: The solution currently does not rely on advanced technologies like AI, IoT, or blockchain but is designed to be scalable and adaptable for future tech integration.

Title: Catalyst Craft
Subtitle: Igniting Zambia's Industrial Future
Problem Statement:
70 percent of Zambia’s population is below the age of 35 years of age translating 14 million people within the population of 19 million people (Zamstats, 2022). These youths and adolescents are at risk of facing high youth unemployment compared to the 19 percent of young people are facing today labour force survey 2023.ith over 350,000 young people entering the job market each year, fewer than 10% securing formal employment opportunities (MOF, 2023). Despite the country producing over 28,000 graduates annually, most youths in Zambia lack practical entrepreneurial skills, especially in the agriculture and mining sectors two of Zambia’s most economically strategic but underutilized industries with great potential to develop the country. 
By 2024, over 65% of Zambia’s population is under the age of 25 (World Bank), yet less than 15% of youth-run businesses receive technical support, mentorship, or funding, limiting their capacity to scale or even launch. Additionally, academic institutions rarely integrate entrepreneurship into their core curriculum, leaving graduates unprepared to generate or create self-employment or contribute to industrial growth. 
If this gap is not addressed, Zambia risks continued economic stagnation, youth frustration, and underutilization of Zambia’s natural resources and human capital. Therefore, youth projects development platform YPDP through the Catalyst Craft project aims to address this gap by equipping at least a total of 1000 youths aged 18-30 years by 2030. These will gain practical entrepreneurship skills, mentorship, and access to business development opportunities in agriculture and mining, to support at least 60% of them to develop viable business ventures by December 2026.
Solution Overview:
Catalyst Craft Zambia is a five-year project, it is a youth empowerment initiative designed and implemented by the Youth Projects Development Platform (YPDP) to contribute directly to the strategic goal of empowering 1,000 youths and young people with financial literacy skills, entrepreneurial skills, business knowledge, and sustainable enterprise development by 2030. The project aims to transform youth from passive job seekers into active job creators, with a primary focus on production, value addition in agriculture, mining and tourism industries of Zambia’s most vital but underutilized economic sectors by local Youth. 

OVERALL GOAL 
To build entrepreneurial capacity and promote sustainable youth-led businesses that contribute to economic development in Zambia. 

OBJECTIVES 
1)	Train 1000 youths in entrepreneurship, innovation, and sustainable business development by 2030. 
2)	Support at least 60% of participants to launch or scale up viable business ventures in posttraining. 
3)	To foster a collaborative ecosystem for youth entrepreneurs through mentorship, peer networks, and investor linkages.
4)	Advocate for better policies to support local businesses to thrive. 

STRATEGIC ALIGNMENT WITH NATIONAL AND INTERNATIONAL FRAMEWORKS 
The Catalyst Craft Zambia (2026–2030) project is firmly rooted in Zambia’s national priorities and legal frameworks, while also aligning with regional and international development agendas. Designed to train and empower 1,000 youth over five years, the project contributes meaningfully to Zambia’s socioeconomic transformation goals by promoting inclusive entrepreneurship, formalizing youth-led businesses, and strengthening policy advocacy and civic engagement among young people. 
At the national level, the project directly supports the implementation of the 8th National Development Plan (8NDP), particularly the pillar on Economic Transformation and Job Creation. The 8NDP calls for expanded employment opportunities, enterprise growth, and increased participation of young people and women in productive sectors. Catalyst Craft Zambia addresses these priorities by equipping 200 youth annually with entrepreneurial, leadership, and innovation skills, and by supporting the launch and formal registration of at least 50 youth-led businesses most of them in agriculture and mining value chains. Additionally, the project aligns with the Human and Social Development Pillar of the 8NDP by promoting skills development, mentorship, and mindset transformation among youth.

Through digital tools, pitch events, and a mentorship-driven ecosystem, the project reimagines youth development as a vehicle for national economic transformation locally grounded, youth-led, and future-focused.
Sustainable Change:
The sustainability of the Catalyst Craft Zambia project is central to ensuring long-term impact beyond the initial five-year implementation phase. YPDP has designed a multi-dimensional sustainability strategy that incorporates institutional capacity-building, youth leadership, partnerships, policy integration, and financial resilience. 
1.	Trainer-of-Trainers (ToT) Model 
Each year, at least 10 outstanding participants will be selected and trained as peer facilitators. These ToTs will serve as future trainers, mentors, and advocates ensuring the continuation of the program even beyond external funding. Over five years, this will build a pool of 50+ trained youth facilitators embedded within communities. 
2.	Ongoing Mentorship Network 
YPDP will maintain a structured mentorship system by engaging a network of at least 30 business professionals, alumni, and cooperative leaders. This mentorship structure will support new and existing youth-led businesses through one-on-one coaching, group sessions, and post-launch technical support. 
3.	Institutional Partnerships and Integration 
YPDP will work to integrate Catalyst Craft modules into the entrepreneurship programs of universities, technical colleges, and community youth centers. Through formal Memorandums of Understanding (MoUs), the program can be adapted for institutional ownership, ensuring continuity through national education systems. 
4.	Advocacy for Policy and Curriculum Integration 
The project will advocate for the inclusion of entrepreneurship and cooperative development in 
Zambia’s secondary and tertiary education curricula. Youth voices will influence local and national policy processes, helping institutionalize youth enterprise development as a national priority. 
5.	Resource Mobilization and Financial Sustainability 
The project will pursue diverse funding sources including donor grants, corporate social responsibility (CSR) partnerships, and social enterprise models (e.g., participant-led cooperatives generating income). A portion of alumni-run businesses will contribute to a Catalyst Enterprise Fund, supporting future cohorts.

Le projet ambitionne de former 1 000 jeunes d’ici 2030, en soutenant au moins 60% à créer des entreprises viables (Q12, Q21). Actuellement en phase pilote à Lusaka, deux cohortes (2024–2025) ont déjà impliqué 130 jeunes (Q17, Q19). La méthodologie intègre formation, mentorat, plaidoyer politique, formalisation légale, et un modèle ToT pour assurer la durabilité (Q23). Aligné sur le 8e Plan national de développement et Vision 2030, il contribue aux ODD 1, 8, 17 (Q20).

Title: GUIGOU-SÉCH : Digitaliser la chaîne alimentaire pour réduire le gaspillage
Subtitle: GUIGOU-SÉCH connecte les petits producteurs à une économie circulaire grâce à la lyophilisation et une plateforme digitale de traçabilité des fruits invendus.
Problem Statement: En Guinée, des tonnes de fruits sont perdues chaque année faute de moyens de conservation, tandis que les petits producteurs restent invisibles dans les circuits économiques. L’absence d’outils de transformation adaptés et de traçabilité limite leur accès aux marchés, creusant les inégalités économiques. GUIGOU-SÉCH répond à ce double défi : réduire le gaspillage alimentaire et connecter les producteurs à une économie numérique inclusive.
Solution Overview: GUIGOU-SÉCH est une solution intégrée qui combine transformation agroalimentaire et digitalisation pour lutter contre les pertes post-récolte et renforcer l’inclusion économique des petits producteurs. Elle repose sur la lyophilisation de fruits invendus ou abîmés, un procédé de conservation à froid qui préserve les qualités nutritionnelles et prolonge la durée de vie des produits. Cette technologie est adaptée à des unités  décentralisées. En parallèle, une application numérique permet de cartographier les producteurs, suivre les disponibilités en fruits invendu, assurer la traçabilité des produits transformés. Cette base de données constitue un levier pour l’analyse des tendances agricoles et l’interconnexion entre les acteurs. La solution mobilise des méthodologies telles que le séchage sous vide à basse température, la collecte de données en temps réel via mobile, l’utilisation d’emballages traçables, et l’application de normes simplifiées de contrôle qualité.
Solution Provider(s): Saboutech: ( incubateur) organisation spécialisée dans la formation, le développement de modèles économiques durables et le renforcement de capacités des entrepreneurs, secteur : Appui à l’entrepreneuriat et à l’innovation.Producteurs agricoles locaux : (coopératives informelles et marchés urbains de Conakry et Kindia), acteurs de première ligne pour l’approvisionnement en matières premières, secteur : agriculture vivrière. Techniciens en agroalimentaire (indépendants et rattachés à des centres de formation technique), impliqués dans les procédés de transformation, l’assurance qualité et le prototypage, secteur : industrie agroalimentaire. Programme de Développement de Prototypes (PDP) des UniPods: initiative visant à appuyer les projets innovants à fort potentiel de structuration locale, secteur : développement de l’entrepreneuriat et innovation frugale.
Duration to pilot in a new geography: 3 à 6 mois (Ce délai inclut : identification des producteurs, installation d'une unité pilote de lyophilisation, formation locale, déploiement de l’application de collecte de données, test de marché.)
SDGs addressed: SDG 2 (Zero Hunger);SDG 8 (Decent Work and Economic Growth);SDG 12 (Responsible Consumption and Production);
Desired impact: La solution GUIGOU-SÉCH vise à réduire significativement le gaspillage alimentaire en valorisant entre 50 et 70 % des fruits invendus ou abîmés grâce à la lyophilisation, tout en renforçant l’inclusion économique des petits producteurs. En combinant transformation agroalimentaire et traçabilité numérique, elle permet à ces derniers d’intégrer les circuits commerciaux et de tirer un revenu stable de leurs excédents. Après la finalisation du prototypage, l’unité semi-industrielle prévue permettra de récupérer environ 10 tonnes de fruits par an, de créer entre 5 et 10 emplois directs (notamment pour les jeunes et les femmes), et de recenser 100 à 200 producteurs via une application mobile dédiée. Cette approche favorise une économie circulaire locale et contribue à la réduction des émissions de gaz à effet de serre en limitant les pertes post-récolte et la décomposition des fruits invendus.
Key technologies: La solution GUIGOU-SÉCH s’appuie sur une combinaison de technologies accessibles et adaptées aux contextes locaux. La technologie principale est la lyophilisation (séchage par sublimation à basse température), utilisée pour transformer les fruits tout en conservant leurs qualités nutritionnelles. Le procédé inclut le contrôle des paramètres clés tels que la température, la pression et le temps de séchage, permettant une standardisation de la qualité des produits. En parallèle, une application mobile légère est utilisée pour le recensement des producteurs, la collecte de données agricoles, et la traçabilité des matières premières jusqu’au produit fini. Cette application intègre des fonctionnalités de géolocalisation, de stockage de données offline, et de génération de QR codes pour assurer le suivi logistique. À terme, la solution pourra intégrer des outils d’intelligence artificielle légère pour anticiper les périodes de récolte, optimiser la planification de la transformation, et visualiser les tendances agricoles locales.
Unique Characteristics: La solution GUIGOU-SÉCH repose sur l’introduction stratégique de la lyophilisation dans le contexte local, en rupture avec les méthodes traditionnelles de conservation : (séchage solaire) qui souvent efficace mais limité, altère la qualité nutritionnelle et organoleptique des fruits . Grâce à cette technologie, les fruits conservent jusqu’à 98 % de leurs nutriments, sans recours à la chaleur ni à des conservateurs chimiques, tout en prolongeant leur durée de vie de plusieurs années. Ce saut technologique s’accompagne d’un modèle circulaire basé sur le réemploi de fruits invendus ou en surplus, permettant d’assainir les pertes post-récolte et de soutenir le revenu des producteurs locaux. En parallèle, l’intégration d’une application numérique vient professionnaliser la chaîne d’approvisionnement : elle recense les producteurs, suit la saisonnalité et anticipe les flux, facilitant une planification fine de la transformation. Ce système intelligent lie directement le terrain à l’unité semi-industrielle, créant une boucle vertueuse entre technologie, territoire et impact.
Sustainable Change:
La solution GUIGOU-SÉCH vise à créer un changement durable et systémique en réorganisant la chaîne de valeur des fruits périssables à partir de la réduction des pertes post-récolte. Le déploiement de notre unité pilote de lyophilisation permettra de démontrer la viabilité d’un modèle qui transforme les surplus et invendus en produits à haute valeur ajoutée, allongeant leur durée de vie tout en préservant leurs qualités nutritionnelles. Ce processus amorce une transition vers une agriculture plus résiliente, car il offre un débouché sécurisé et rémunérateur aux petits producteurs.
À moyen terme, l’intégration de notre application numérique permettra une meilleure planification agricole grâce à la collecte de données sur la production locale (quantités, variétés, calendriers), renforçant ainsi la transparence et l’efficacité des circuits de distribution. Ce système crée une dynamique circulaire locale, dans laquelle les fruits ne sont plus gaspillés, mais valorisés en continu, avec un impact positif sur la sécurité alimentaire, l’emploi rural, et la réduction des déchets organiques.
À long terme, la réplication de ce modèle dans d’autres régions permettra de bâtir un écosystème décentralisé de micro-unités de transformation interconnectées, capable de répondre aux enjeux de nutrition, de climat, et de développement territorial durable en Afrique de l’Ouest.
Funding Sources: Jusqu'à présent, la solution a été financée grâce à une combinaison de ressources personnelles, à l’appui technique de mon université ainsi qu’à l’accompagnement de l’incubateur Saboutech. En outre, nous avons participé à plusieurs concours entrepreneuriaux dans lesquels notre projet a été reconnu comme lauréat, ce qui a permis de renforcer notre crédibilité et de bénéficier de ressources complémentaires pour développer les aspects techniques et stratégiques de la solution.
Testimonials and Endorsements:
