Title: Twins4Tech : Inclusion numérique par et pour les jumeaux
Subtitle: Former les jumeaux pour qu’ils deviennent des ambassadeurs du numérique dans leurs communautés.
Problem Statement:
Au Togo, près de 60 % des jeunes en zones rurales n’ont pas accès aux compétences numériques de base, limitant leur participation à l’économie numérique et à l’emploi formel. Dans le Grand Lomé, notamment dans des quartiers comme ceux du Golfe 5, l’accès à Internet reste irrégulier et coûteux, et les centres de formation sont concentrés en milieu urbain.

Parallèlement, les jumeaux et jumelles, figures culturelles respectées au sein des communautés, ne bénéficient d’aucun programme spécifique d’inclusion numérique, alors qu’ils disposent d’un fort potentiel de relais éducatif et communautaire.

Cette double réalité — fracture numérique persistante et non-valorisation d’un levier social — constitue un frein majeur au développement local. Sans accès aux outils numériques, ni à la formation adaptée, ces populations restent en marge des opportunités liées au digital (e-commerce, télétravail, services en ligne, e-éducation), accentuant ainsi les inégalités sociales, économiques et générationnelles.
Solution Overview:
1. Description détaillée du fonctionnement de la solution

"Twins4Tech" est une initiative communautaire qui vise à autonomiser les jumeaux et jumelles en tant qu’acteurs clés de l’inclusion numérique. La solution fonctionne en créant des centres d’apprentissage numérique dédiés aux jumeaux, implantés dans les zones rurales et périurbaines, notamment au Togo (Golfe 5 et régions environnantes). Ces centres offrent un accès gratuit ou à faible coût à Internet, à des équipements informatiques et à des formations ciblées.

Le parcours des bénéficiaires comprend :

Des formations adaptées : compétences numériques de base (bureautique, navigation Internet, sécurité digitale) et avancées (développement web, gestion d’entreprise numérique).

Un accompagnement entrepreneurial : coaching personnalisé, mise en réseau avec des mentors et accès à des financements via des partenaires locaux (SFD, ONG).

Un programme d’ambassadeurs numériques : les jumeaux formés deviennent relais dans leurs communautés, sensibilisant aux usages responsables du numérique et aidant à former d’autres membres.


Par ailleurs, la solution met en place un réseau digital international de jumeaux, facilitant les échanges, la collaboration et le partage de bonnes pratiques.

2. Méthodologies et technologies utilisées

Approche participative et inclusive : co-construction avec les bénéficiaires et les leaders communautaires pour assurer l’adaptation culturelle et linguistique des formations (langues locales et français).

Formations hybrides : sessions en présentiel dans les centres + modules accessibles en ligne ou hors-ligne via une application mobile légère.

Infrastructure solaire : les centres fonctionnent à l’énergie solaire pour garantir une autonomie énergétique durable dans les zones sans électricité fiable.

Technologies low-tech et open source : utilisation de matériels informatiques peu coûteux et d’applications à faible consommation de données, favorisant l’accès même dans des environnements à faible connectivité.

Suivi et évaluation : mise en place d’outils numériques de suivi des progrès des bénéficiaires et d’évaluation d’impact.

3. Partenariats et modèles de collaboration

Partenaires locaux : associations de jumeaux (ex. JU.RE.TO), ONG spécialisées en inclusion numérique, collectivités locales pour l’identification des sites et la mobilisation communautaire.

Institutions éducatives : universités et centres de formation pour le développement de contenus pédagogiques adaptés et la certification des compétences acquises.

Organisations financières : Systèmes Financiers Décentralisés (SFD), microfinance, pour faciliter l’accès au financement des projets numériques portés par les jumeaux.

Partenaires internationaux : agences des Nations Unies, bailleurs de fonds, réseaux de jumeaux à l’international pour le partage d’expertise et la promotion de la solution.

Modèle collaboratif : co-financement, partage de ressources, et gouvernance participative avec un comité de pilotage impliquant bénéficiaires et partenaires.
Solution Provider(s): Association togolaise dédiée à la promotion sociale et économique des jumeaux,  Togo Numérique : ONG d’inclusion numérique et formation digitale en zones rurales,  Université de Lomé : Expertise technique et développement pédagogique,  MicroFinance Plus : Institution de microfinance pour le financement des micro-entrepreneurs numériques,  Agence Nationale de l’Énergie Solaire : Installation et maintenance d’infrastructures solaires,  UNICEF Togo : Soutien technique et promotion de l’inclusion numérique jeunesse.
Duration to pilot in a new geography: piloter la solutioLa mise en œuvre d’un projet pilote Twins4Tech dans une nouvelle région nécessite en moyenne 12 à 18 mois. Cette période se décompose comme suit :  3 mois pour la phase préparatoire : identification des sites, mobilisation des partenaires locaux, et sensibilisation communautaire.  6 à 9 mois pour l’installation des infrastructures (centres solaires, équipements informatiques) et le lancement des premières sessions de formation.  3 à 6 mois pour le suivi, l’évaluation initiale des résultats et l’ajustement des contenus et méthodes pédagogiques selon le contexte local.   Cette durée permet d’assurer une implantation solide, un engagement communautaire fort, et la montée en compétences progressive des bénéficiaires pour un impact durable.
SDGs addressed: SDG 8 (Decent Work and Economic Growth);SDG 17 (Partnerships for the Goals);SDG 12 (Responsible Consumption and Production);
Desired impact:
Réduire la fracture numérique en donnant aux jumeaux et jumelles un accès durable aux compétences et outils numériques, même dans les zones rurales et périurbaines isolées.

Autonomiser les jumeaux pour qu’ils deviennent des acteurs et relais numériques dans leurs communautés, favorisant l’inclusion sociale et économique.

Promouvoir l’entrepreneuriat numérique local en accompagnant la création de micro-entreprises digitales portées par les bénéficiaires.

Renforcer la cohésion sociale grâce à un réseau solidaire de jumeaux connectés à l’échelle nationale et internationale.

Contribuer à la réduction des inégalités de genre en ciblant une forte participation des femmes jumelles dans les formations et programmes d’accompagnement.

Principales réalisations ou impacts quantifiables attendus

Formation de 1 500 jumeaux et jumelles aux compétences numériques de base et avancées dans les 18 premiers mois.

Création d’au moins 150 micro-entreprises numériques, générant des revenus stables et améliorant l’employabilité locale.

Réduction de 40 % de la fracture numérique dans les zones ciblées, mesurée par l’accès aux services en ligne et l’utilisation des technologies numériques.

Participation féminine d’au moins 60 % dans les programmes de formation et d’entrepreneuriat.

Économies d’énergie et réduction d’émissions de gaz à effet de serre (GES) grâce à l’utilisation d’infrastructures solaires autonomes, estimées à environ 10 tonnes de CO₂ évitées par an par site pilote.

Renforcement du tissu social à travers un réseau actif de jumeaux, facilitant l’échange de connaissances, de ressources et de soutien mutuel.
Key technologies:
Infrastructure solaire autonome : Utilisation de panneaux solaires pour alimenter les centres numériques, garantissant un accès fiable à l’énergie même en zones isolées sans électricité.

Plateforme mobile légère et hors-ligne : Application mobile développée pour fonctionner avec une faible consommation de données, accessible même sans connexion Internet continue, offrant des modules de formation multilingues.

Outils de formation numérique : Modules e-learning interactifs adaptés aux besoins locaux, intégrant des vidéos, quiz, et exercices pratiques.

Système de gestion de l’apprentissage (LMS) open source : Pour suivre les progrès des bénéficiaires, gérer les contenus et faciliter le mentorat à distance.

Réseau social communautaire digital : Plateforme d’échanges et de collaboration entre jumeaux formés, favorisant le partage de bonnes pratiques et le réseautage.

Suivi et évaluation numériques : Outils numériques (tableaux de bord, questionnaires en ligne) pour collecter des données en temps réel sur l’impact et adapter les interventions.


Technologies envisagées pour la phase avancée :

Intelligence Artificielle (IA) pour personnaliser les parcours de formation selon le profil des apprenants.

Blockchain pour sécuriser les certifications numériques et faciliter l’accès transparent aux financements.
Unique Characteristics:
Ciblage social inédit : Twins4Tech est la première initiative à exploiter spécifiquement le potentiel social et culturel unique des jumeaux et jumelles comme vecteurs d’inclusion numérique, créant un levier communautaire puissant et authentique.

Approche communautaire et participative : La solution repose sur la co-construction avec les jumeaux, leurs familles et les leaders locaux, assurant une forte appropriation et une adaptation culturelle et linguistique des contenus.

Infrastructure autonome et durable : Utilisation de centres numériques fonctionnant exclusivement à l’énergie solaire, garantissant un accès continu dans les zones rurales ou mal desservies en électricité.

Modèle hybride de formation : Combinaison de formations en présentiel dans des centres physiques et de modules mobiles hors-ligne, ce qui permet un accès flexible et adapté aux réalités locales (faible connectivité, multilinguisme).

Soutien à l’entrepreneuriat intégré : La solution ne se limite pas à la formation, mais accompagne aussi les jumeaux dans la création et le financement de micro-entreprises numériques, favorisant ainsi un impact économique concret.

Réseau international de solidarité : Création d’un réseau digital dédié aux jumeaux numériques, facilitant l’échange de connaissances, la collaboration et l’accès à des opportunités économiques au-delà des frontières.

Innovation technologique progressive : Intégration future prévue d’outils avancés tels que l’intelligence artificielle pour personnaliser les parcours d’apprentissage et la blockchain pour sécuriser les certifications et financements.

Modèle économique collaboratif et inclusif : Combinaison de financements publics, privés et communautaires, avec un partage des responsabilités entre les partenaires locaux, ce qui garantit pérennité et évolutivité.
Sustainable Change:
Contribution de Twins4Tech à un changement systémique durable

Théorie du changement et effets de suivi souhaités

Problème initial : La fracture numérique exclut durablement une large partie des populations, notamment les jumeaux, empêchant leur pleine participation économique et sociale.

Actions clés :

Formation ciblée des jumeaux aux compétences numériques.

Mise en place d’infrastructures numériques autonomes et accessibles.

Accompagnement entrepreneurial et création d’un réseau solidaire.


Effets immédiats :

Acquisition de compétences numériques par les jumeaux.

Accès régulier à des ressources numériques et connectivité fiable.

Développement de micro-entreprises numériques portées par les bénéficiaires.


Effets intermédiaires :

Les jumeaux deviennent des ambassadeurs numériques, diffusant les compétences et bonnes pratiques dans leurs communautés.

Amélioration de l’employabilité locale et diversification des activités économiques.

Renforcement de la cohésion sociale et de l’inclusion grâce à un réseau national et international.


Effets à long terme (changement systémique) :

Réduction durable de la fracture numérique dans les zones ciblées, avec un modèle reproductible et scalable.

Transformation des pratiques sociales et économiques par une meilleure intégration numérique des populations marginalisées.

Renforcement des capacités locales et autonomisation des communautés dans la gestion et l’innovation numériques.

Influence sur les politiques publiques en faveur d’une inclusion numérique ciblée et culturelle.

Suivi souhaité :

Mesure régulière des indicateurs d’accès, d’utilisation et de maîtrise des outils numériques.

Évaluation des impacts économiques (création d’emplois, chiffre d’affaires des micro-entreprises).

Suivi des dynamiques sociales (implication des jumeaux, évolution des réseaux).

Adaptation continue de la solution grâce aux retours terrain et aux nouvelles technologies.
Funding Sources:
Lors des phases pilotes et premières implémentations, la solution Twins4Tech a été financée grâce à un modèle mixte combinant plusieurs sources :

Financements associatifs : Apports propres de l’association JU.RE.TO, notamment via des cotisations et collectes communautaires.

Subventions publiques : Soutiens obtenus auprès des ministères togolais en charge du numérique et du développement social, ainsi que des collectivités locales.

Appuis d’ONG et partenaires internationaux : Financements et accompagnements techniques apportés par des organisations comme l’UNICEF Togo et des agences de développement numérique.

Partenariats privés : Contributions en nature et en numéraire de partenaires technologiques locaux et fournisseurs d’équipements informatiques.

Micro-financements et crowdfunding : Campagnes locales de mobilisation de ressources, notamment pour les équipements des centres solaires.


Ce modèle pluriel permet d’assurer la pérennité et la flexibilité de la solution, tout en favorisant une forte implication locale et une diversification des ressources.
Primary thematic focus area: Inclusive Digital Innovation Skills & Entrepreneurial Talent Development
Summary: Twins4Tech est une initiative communautaire au Togo visant à former les jumeaux et jumelles comme ambassadeurs du numérique. Le projet crée des centres d’apprentissage fonctionnant à l’énergie solaire dans les zones rurales/périurbaines, où les bénéficiaires acquièrent des compétences numériques, un accompagnement entrepreneurial, et deviennent relais dans leurs communautés. Le modèle mise sur l’ancrage culturel des jumeaux comme figures respectées pour favoriser l’inclusion numérique et sociale (Q12, Q13).

Title: "Éco-Sport Ciwara : Engager les élèves dans la protection de  l'environnement à travers le sport".
Subtitle: "Éco-Sport Ciawara" est un projet visant à sensibiliser et à engager les élèves  des écoles maliennes dans la protect ion de l'environnement à travers des activités sportives  durables. Les activités  comprennent Marche collective de nettoyage, Campagnes de sensibilisation digitale sur  l'environnement, Formation des enseignants et des encadrants, des séances d'éducation  environnementale, des nettoyages de terrains de sport, des initiatives de reboisement et des  compétitions sportives mettant l'accent sur la conservation des ressources. Problem Statement:
Le défi/problème identifié par le projet (une brève analyse de la situation en 100 mots maximum) 
Le défi principal identifié par ce projet est de trouver des moyens efficaces pour sensibiliser 
et mobiliser les élèves maliens à la protection de l'environnement tout en encourageant leur 
participation active dans des activités sportives. Cela implique de surmonter les obstacles tels 
que le manque de sensibilisation environnementale, les ressources limitées pour le sport dans 
les écoles, et potentiellement les priorités éducatives concurrentes. En résumé, le défi 
principal est de créer une synergie entre la sensibilisation environnementale et la pratique 
sportive, tout en garantissant la durabilité et la pertinence de cette initiative dans le contexte 
éducatif malien.
Solution Overview:
Le projet propose plusieurs solutions et actions pour répondre au défi identifié de 
sensibiliser et d'engager les élèves maliens dans la protection de l'environnement tout en 
promouvant une culture sportive saine. Voici quelques-unes de ces solutions et actions :
• Création de clubs verts 
• Sensibilisation à travers le sport :
Organisation de compétitions sportives durables
• Éducation environnementale
• Collaboration communautaire 
• Suivi et évaluation 
En combinant ces solutions et actions, le projet vise à créer un environnement scolaire 
dynamique où la sensibilisation environnementale et la pratique sportive vont de pair, 
offrant ainsi aux élèves une expérience éducative enrichissante et durable.
Solution Provider(s): Organisation internationale non gouvernementale , secteur privé,  unsco, Usaid , pnud , ministère de l'éducation nationale

Title: Mawuche Storytelling Hub
Subtitle: Untangling Stories, Rewiring Education, Enlightening Futures
Problem Statement:
In many South African communities—especially township and rural areas—education remains a paradox: it's both a right and a riddle. Access may exist on paper, but quality, engagement, and long-term impact tell another story. The ground truth, gathered from lived experiences in the Education Impact Study dataset - https://docs.google.com/spreadsheets/d/1g6M4BBxKb9xOQqag7lCS-abzbVt2EoMVanYOrXbZWJo/edit?usp=sharing and echoed in hundreds of community voices, reveals a systemic undercurrent of disconnection—between students and curriculum, schools and resources, dreams and the real world.

Many learners face inconsistent access to digital tools, internet connectivity, and stable electricity. Teachers, often under-resourced and overwhelmed, battle burnout, while parents are left uninformed or unable to support learning journeys meaningfully. Even where devices exist, digital literacy gaps remain a barrier. Emotional wellbeing is overlooked, and systemic pressures fragment holistic learning.

Despite this, there is an untapped brilliance in our youth. Responses in the Education Impact Study show deep insight from students and educators alike—evidence that solutions must be community-informed, youth-driven, and context-aware.

This project exists to address that divide. To rewire how we deliver education and connection—not just as content, but as care. We are reimagining learning environments where data isn’t just collected, but listened to. Where digital tools enable dignity. Where science, innovation, and local wisdom meet.

Because in a world overflowing with tools and tech, the real revolution is still about people.
Solution Overview:
Solution Overview

This solution is a regenerative education model designed to rewire how township and rural youth access, experience, and evolve within learning ecosystems. Rooted in behavioural insight and data storytelling, it fuses psychosocial support, community-led digital literacy, and youth-centric curriculum design to bridge the chasm between potential and opportunity.

At its core is the "ReW.I.R.E. Framework"—Reclaiming Intuition, Regulation and Embodiment—which addresses the trauma, disempowerment, and digital exclusion many learners/citizens face. By weaving local narratives with future-fit skill-building, the model transforms classrooms into safe laboratories of self-discovery, purpose and innovation.

How it works

Community-Led Data Collection
We begin by listening. Through co-designed surveys and observational tools, we gather insights on learner experiences, challenges, aspirations, and contextual barriers—as shown in our Education Impact Study. This data is then translated into design-informed interventions.

ReW.I.R.E. Ritual Integration
Daily nervous system regulation micro-practices are embedded into the learning environment. These rituals help learners move from survival mode to a state of readiness, creativity, and curiosity—addressing mental fatigue and burnout reported across the cohort.

Digital and Behavioural Learning Modules
Curriculum includes AI, coding, data storytelling, and behavioural science simplified for grassroots access. These are delivered in hybrid formats—offline, mobile-first, and community-based digital labs.

Feedback Loops & Evaluation
Impact isn’t assumed—it’s tracked. Learner feedback, educator assessments, and biometric-style wellness check-ins ensure the model evolves responsively, not reactively.

Methodologies and Technologies Used

- Behavioural Science – to design nudges, rituals, and habit loops for engagement and well-being.

- Human-Centred Design – to co-create with learners, educators, and communities.

- Data Science & Storytelling – leveraging Google Sheets, Excel, and simple dashboards to track outcomes and insights.

- Offline-First Tech – tools that don’t assume stable internet access, including mesh networks and low-data platforms.

- AI Tools & Open-Source Learning – integrating resources like Scratch, ChatGPT (in safe, curated modes), and localised simulations.

Partnerships and Collaboration Models

- Community Schools & Learning Centres – The implementation hubs, offering space, trust, and local facilitators.

- Digital Inclusion Partners – NGOs and telcos to support infrastructure like solar routers, SIMs, and devices.

- Youth Mentorship Networks – Leveraging local role models to co-lead learning modules and deepen relevance.

- Data & Research Partners – Universities and open-source analysts validating insights and co-publishing community data reports.

- Public Sector Linkages – Aligning with DBE priorities, township innovation zones, and digital skills frameworks.

Title: YOUTHTECH : Youth Digital Inclusion
Subtitle: YOUTHTECH provides marginalized youth with the tech training needed to succeed in a digital world
Problem Statement:
In many African countries, the digital divide and lack of access to inclusive tech education deprive young people, especially those in marginalized areas, of the skills needed to participate in the digital economy. In Cameroon, where 60% of the population is under 25, most youth (particularly those in the Far North, North, and East regions) lack access to digital education. Despite rapid growth in digital opportunities, persistent challenges include:

Limited access to affordable, locally relevant tech training.

- Youth unemployment (30% in Cameroon, NIS), worsened by the mismatch between taught skills and market demands.

- Exclusion of rural youth, women, and vulnerable groups due to inadequate infrastructure and educational resources.

- Dominance of the informal economy, where lack of digital skills stifles entrepreneurship and professional integration.

Youth Education and Development (YED) addresses these gaps through practical, inclusive programs that equip youth with tech skills while fostering economic empowerment.
Solution Overview:
1. Detailed Description of the Solution
YOUTHTECH is an initiative by Youth Education and Development (YED) that has provided an integrated digital training platform to underserved Cameroonian youth in the Centre region since 2021, with plans to expand to the Far North, North, and East regions. The solution currently combines:

Hybrid training (online and in-person) on essential tech skills (office tools, AI, digital marketing, collaborative tools, video editing, cybersecurity, etc.).

Individual coaching (primarily online) for youth in peripheral areas.

2. Methodologies and Technologies Used
- Adaptive pedagogy: In-person weekend training sessions using a video projector to display course materials. Shared use of personal laptops among participants; YED supplements with its own devices.

-A dedicated communication group (e.g., WhatsApp/Telegram) allows participants to raise questions and receive support throughout the week.

3. Partnerships and Collaboration Models
Volunteers:

- Volunteers provide online or one-on-one mentorship.

- Alumni are empowered to become mentors for new participants, ensuring sustainability.

Sustainable model: Nominal participant contributions.
Solution Provider(s): Currently, no formal partners are involved in the initiative. However, YOUTHTECH is actively seeking collaborations.
Implementation location(s): Atemengue Public School & Obogog (Yaoundé, Cameroon) + Online support platform
Implementation timeline(s): May - July 2021  January - March 2022  September - November 2022  April - June 2023  January - March 2024  Ongoing: Permanent online support
Duration to pilot in a new geography: 6 to 9 months (for full implementation including evaluation, adaptation and initial results).

Desired impact:
Core Objectives:
- Reduce the digital divide by training marginalized youth (rural areas, women, vulnerable populations) in essential tech skills.

- Enhance employability and entrepreneurship by connecting beneficiaries to local and global economic opportunities.

- Build a sustainable ecosystem through local mentors and public-private partnerships.

Quantitative Impact (2021–2024):
-Youth trained: 1,333+ (since 2021)
-Job placement rate: 35% (initial follow-up)
-Female participation: 55%

Qualitative Impact:
-Empowerment: "80% of beneficiaries report increased confidence in using digital tools" (post-training survey).

Title: Inclusive digital hubs: empowering women, youth & MSMES in eastern drc
Subtitle: Scalable digital skills, entrepreneurship, and market access for underserved communities.
Problem Statement:
In Eastern DRC, women, youth, and marginalized communities face systemic barriers to economic
participation. Limited access to digital skills, affordable technology, and business networks prevents
them from joining emerging value chains. MSMEs struggle to adopt digital tools, reducing their
competitiveness, market reach, and resilience. This digital divide perpetuates poverty,
unemployment, and inequality.
Solution Overview:
Our solution establishes Inclusive Digital Hubs that combine digital skills development,
entrepreneurship incubation, and market linkage support to integrate women, youth, and MSMEs
into the digital economy.

How it works:
- Capacity Building: Market-oriented training in digital skills, e-commerce, online freelancing,
and digital marketing.
- Entrepreneurship Support: Incubation programs for MSMEs to adopt digital tools, improve
operations, and access new markets.
- Market Linkages: Connection to e-commerce platforms, regional value chains, and
international partners.
- Access to Infrastructure: Co-working spaces, internet-enabled labs, and shared equipment
for production and digital content creation.

Methodologies and technologies used:
- Blended learning with a Learning Management System (LMS) adapted to low-bandwidth
contexts.
- Open-source business management tools for MSMEs.
- Mobile payment and e-commerce solutions for financial inclusion.
- Cloud-based platforms for remote collaboration and knowledge sharing.

Partnerships and collaboration models:
KivuTech partners with local universities, vocational training centers, government agencies (e.g.,
ANADEC), and private sector actors for curriculum co-design, mentorship, and internship
opportunities. Collaborations with NGOs and community organizations ensure outreach to
marginalized groups,while strategic alliances with technology providers guarantee sustainable
infrastructure.
Solution Provider(s): KivuTech, business incubator supporting entrepreneurs in Eastern DRC through training, mentorship, access to finance, and market linkages; ANADEC, national agency for entrepreneurship promotion; Local tech SMEs, providing software and digital infrastructure.
Implementation location(s): Bukavu and Goma, Democratic Republic of Congo.
Duration to pilot in a new geography: 6-9 months, including needs assessment, stakeholder engagement, infrastructure setup, and first training cycle.
SDGs addressed: SDG 4 (Quality Education);SDG 8 (Decent Work and Economic Growth);SDG 9 (Industry, Innovation, and Infrastructure);
Desired impact:
Objectives:
- Equip at least 5,000 women and youth with employable digital skills by 2027.
- Support 500 MSMEs in adopting digital solutions to increase productivity and market access.
- Foster cross-border trade opportunities via digital platforms.

Key Achievements (pilot stage):
- 550+ individuals trained in digital literacy and e-commerce management.
- 70 MSMEs supported to integrate digital tools, resulting in average revenue growth of 15%
within 6 months.
- Creation of 100+ new digital jobs and freelance contracts for trained youth.
Key technologies:
- Learning Management Systems (Moodle, custom mobile apps)
- Open-source ERP and inventory management systems
- Mobile payment and fintech integration (USSD, wallet apps)
- Cloud collaboration tools (Google Workspace, Nextcloud)
Unique Characteristics:
- Inclusive targeting: Explicit focus on women, youth, MSMEs, and marginalized communities.
- Low-bandwidth adaptability: All digital tools optimized for unstable internet environments.
- Hybrid model: Combines physical infrastructure (Digital Hubs) with scalable online content
for replication in other geographies.
- Local-global linkages: Bridges
Sustainable Change:
By equipping women, youth, MSMEs, and marginalized communities with digital skills,
entrepreneurial capacities, and market access, the solution breaks structural barriers to economic
participation. Immediate outcomes include increased employability, higher MSME competitiveness,
and stronger community resilience. Medium-term, participants integrate into digital value chains,
generating income and driving industrial innovation. Long-term, the replication of Inclusive Digital
Hubs across multiple regions fosters a self-sustaining ecosystem of innovation, job creation, and
inclusive industrial growth.
Funding Sources:
The solution has been funded through a combination of:
- Grants from development cooperation partners (e.g., Expertise France, Fondation Roi
Baudouin).
- Strategic partnerships with public institutions (ANADEC) providing in-kind support (training
spaces, outreach).
- KivuTech’s own investment in equipment, staffing, and program design.
Further comments/feedback:
This questionnaire is comprehensive and enables solution providers to showcase both innovation
and impact. One potential improvement could be allowing optional visual infographics to
complement text-based responses, which would enhance clarity for complex models such as blended
learning ecosystems.

Title: Empowering Communities through Smart Water Quality Testing
Subtitle: Affordable, IoT-enabled water testing for safe water access and inclusive digital participation
Problem Statement: Billions lack access to safe drinking water due to costly, complex, and inaccessible testing methods. Rural and underserved communities are excluded from reliable water data, leaving them vulnerable to health risks and limiting digital inclusion in governance and resource management
Solution Overview:
Our solution, the CLUIX C012 Water Quality Analyzer, is a low-cost, portable, and easy-to-use multiparameter water testing device. It enables last-mile communities to self-test water quality and instantly share validated results with stakeholders—from local panchayats to central ministries—via an IoT-enabled cloud platform.

How it works:

1. User-friendly analyzer tests multiple water parameters within minutes.

2. Data automatically transmitted via IoT to a secure cloud database.

3. Results accessible on mobile dashboards for communities, policymakers, and water agencies.


Methodologies & Technologies:

1. Multi-technique (Spectroscopy, Conductivity, Colorimetry, Titimetry) capability enabling multiple parameter to be tested

2. IoT-based real-time data transmission

3. AI-assisted analytics for anomaly detection and water safety alerts

4. Cloud dashboards for transparent data sharing and decision-making

Partnerships & Collaboration Models:

1. Local governments and water utilities for deployment and validation

2. Non Profit Organisations and community-based organizations for training and adoption

3. Academic and research institutions for continuous R&D

4. Private sector partners for scaling distribution and manufacturing
Solution Provider(s): Local Government Departments, Academic Institutions (e.g., Water Research Labs), Community NGOs working in WASH sector.
Implementation location(s): India: Haryana, Tamilnadu, Uttar Pradesh, Rajasthan, Telngana, Assam, Tripura, Punjab
Duration to pilot in a new geography: 6–9 months (including adaptation, training, and local capacity building)
SDGs addressed: SDG 3 (Good Health and Well-being);SDG 6 (Clean Water and Sanitation);SDG 13 (Climate Action);
Desired impact:
Democratize water testing, enable inclusive digital participation in water governance, and build resilient water infrastructure.

Key Impacts:

1. Reduce waterborne disease risks through early detection

2. Empower communities with digital tools for self-testing

3. Generate employment opportunities for local youth as “digital water entrepreneurs”

4. Support data-driven policymaking with real-time water quality data
Key technologies: IoT, Cloud Computing, AI/ML (for predictive water safety insights), Mobile Applications.
Unique Characteristics:
First-of-its-kind low-cost IoT-enabled multiparameter analyzer tailored for rural use.

Community-driven model with shared digital dashboards connecting households to ministries.

Inclusive business model: training local youth and MSMEs as certified water testers, creating jobs while ensuring sustainability.
Sustainable Change: By enabling communities to own and control water quality data, the solution transforms citizens from passive recipients into active participants in digital governance. This systemic shift fosters trust, ensures accountability, improves health outcomes, and creates a scalable framework for digital inclusion in other public services.

The solution has been supported through a mix of self-investment, seed funding from innovation grants, and pilot-stage collaborations (Imagine H20) with local government bodies and NGOs working in the WASH (Water, Sanitation, Hygiene) sector. We have sold 180+ devices in last 10 months of commercialization.

We are now seeking strategic partnerships and impact-driven funding for scaling.

Title: Play2Prosper: Bangla Micro‑Lessons for Women Entrepreneurs
Subtitle: A low‑bandwidth, Bangla‑first, game‑based learning platform using 3–5 minute micro‑lessons and real‑world quests to help women micro‑entrepreneurs gain skills, adopt digital tools, and grow income.
Problem Statement:
Women micro‑entrepreneurs in Bangladesh face three linked barriers to participating in the digital economy: (1) low digital and business literacy, (2) limited access to trusted, practical training in the local language, and (3) social and time constraints that prevent attendance in formal programs. Existing virtual courses are text‑heavy, bandwidth‑intensive, and rarely translate skills into immediate business actions. The result is slow adoption of digital payments, e-commerce, and record-keeping, as well as missed revenue opportunities.

-Keep friction low: tiny lessons, audio‑first, data‑light, immediate feedback loops.
-Match motivation to emotion—Easy Fun for curiosity, People Fun for community, Hard Fun for mastery, Serious Fun for purpose.
-Turn real business steps into quests that produce quick “wins” and visible progress.
-Design for constraints (devices, bandwidth, literacy) using the Lens of Simplicity and the Lens of the Player.
-Frame the player experience goals (Aesthetics) first—Challenge, Fellowship, and Discovery—then back‑map the Dynamics and Mechanics.
Solution Overview:
𝗣𝗹𝗮𝘆𝟮𝗣𝗿𝗼𝘀𝗽𝗲𝗿 is a 𝗕𝗮𝗻𝗴𝗹𝗮-𝗳𝗶𝗿𝘀𝘁, 𝗴𝗮𝗺𝗲-𝗯𝗮𝘀𝗲𝗱 𝗺𝗶𝗰𝗿𝗼𝗹𝗲𝗮𝗿𝗻𝗶𝗻𝗴 𝗽𝗹𝗮𝘁𝗳𝗼𝗿𝗺 that delivers 3– 5 minute video micro-lessons paired with interactive gameplay and real-world quests. Learners earn XP, badges, and streaks by completing actions that directly improve their businesses (e.g., setting prices, creating a WhatsApp product catalog, activating a bKash merchant QR, posting to a marketplace). The product runs as a Progressive Web App (PWA), optimized for low-cost Android phones, and works offline via caching. It also supports voice-first navigation with text-to-speech and captioned Bangla. Learners join local “guilds” (ward, union, or district groups) for peer support, cooperative challenges, and trusted referrals to services (fintech, logistics, marketplaces).

Title: "Virtually Zed Ventures: Immersive VR Tourism for a Sustainable Zambia"
Subtitle: Experience Zambia’s hidden cultural and natural gems through immersive virtual reality tours that promote accessibility, sustainability, and local storytelling.
Problem Statement: Many travelers are faced with barriers to experiencing Zambia’s rich cultural and natural heritage due to cost, time, mobility, and environmental concerns. At the same time, over 80% of Zambia’s tourism potential remains underexposed, with local tourism providers lacking digital tools to reach wider markets. Cultural heritage risks fading without digital preservation, and rural communities miss out on tourism income. There is a growing demand for immersive, accessible, and sustainable travel experiences that are authentic, educational, and inclusive.
Solution Overview:
How the Solution Works:
Virtually Zed Ventures (VZV) creates immersive Virtual Reality (VR) travel experiences that showcase Zambia’s cultural heritage, natural wonders, and hidden tourism gems. Users—locally and globally—access these experiences via VR headsets or web platforms, selecting guided virtual tours led by local experts. These tours offer rich storytelling, interactive exploration, and cultural immersion—making tourism accessible, sustainable, and inclusive.

Technologies Used:
- 360° Video & VR Technology: Captures immersive, high-definition content of destinations and events.
- WebXR & VR Platforms: Ensures cross-device accessibility for web and headset users.
- AI-enhanced Translations: Supports multilingual content for diverse audiences.
- Cloud-Based Content Hosting: Facilitates scalable, global access.

Methodologies (B2B2C business model):
- Community Co-Creation: Local communities are engaged in tour design, narration, and content validation.
- Revenue-Sharing Model: Local storytellers and guides earn income through licensing and subscriptions.
- Content Preservation: Cultural practices and stories are archived digitally for future educational and heritage use.

Partnership & Collaboration Models:
- Local Tourism SMEs: Co-develop tour packages and promote community destinations.
- Tourism Authorities & Ministries: Support with access, policy alignment, and co-promotion.
- Schools & Universities: Offer educational access and integration into learning.
- International Partners & Accelerators: Provide funding, mentorship, and global reach.
- Tech Developers: Collaborate on platform building and scaling capabilities.

Together, these elements create a sustainable, scalable, and tech-driven model that reimagines African tourism for the digital age.
Solution Provider(s): Lizu Chinyama, Creative Director: Kalichi Pictures, kaumba@kalichipictures.com, Address: Show Grounds Stand No A11 ZSIC Pavilion
Implementation timeline(s): August – October 2025: MVP Production & Pilot Launch • Begin additional filming and editing immersive VR tours of 3 selected cultural/tourism sites in Zambia. • Launch pilot testing phase with select users (diaspora audiences, local schools, and tourism partners). • Gather user feedback to inform content refinement and UX adjustments.  November – December 2025: Platform Launch & Early Monetization • Deploy MVP web-based platform and headset-accessible experiences. • Onboard first B2B customers (educational institutions, tourism SMEs). • Begin community training for local guides and storytellers to create co-owned content.  January – March 2026: Expansion & Marketing Rollout • Roll out targeted marketing campaigns toward diaspora and eco-conscious travelers. • Finalize licensing agreements and subscription tiers. • Add 2 new virtual destinations to the platform.  April – June 2026: Strategic Partnerships & Investor Engagement • Deepen collaborations with tourism boards, NGOs, and cultural institutions. • Prepare for pre-seed fundraising and accelerator applications. • Start feasibility studies for replication in Namibia and Malawi.  July – December 2026: Growth & Content Scaling • Reach goal of 6+ VR experiences across multiple provinces. • Launch mobile-optimized version of platform. • Grow user base to 1,000+ and convert pilot partners into paying clients.

Desired impact: Virtually Zed Ventures (VZV) aims to democratize access to Zambia’s cultural and natural heritage through immersive virtual reality, while fostering environmental sustainability and community empowerment. The solution provides eco-conscious alternatives to traditional travel, reducing the carbon footprint associated with physical tourism. By digitizing and preserving over 30 cultural and historical sites within 18 months, VZV enhances cultural education and global exposure. The initiative is expected to create over 20 direct and indirect jobs—including local guides, VR technicians, and content creators—and share up to 30% of virtual tour revenue with community partners. Through partnerships with schools, VZV will also provide virtual field trips to over 1,000 students lacking access to physical tourism. Ultimately, VZV will help expand visibility for more than 500 underrepresented tourism SMEs in Zambia, serving as a scalable model for inclusive, tech-enabled tourism across Africa.

Title: CrossPromote.ai – Smart Event Growth Through AI-Driven Brand Partnerships
Subtitle: Connect, promote, and grow your events with AI-powered matching to influencers, brands, and sponsors—boost visibility and engagement effortlessly on CrossPromote.ai.
Problem Statement:

Discoverability: Many great events and brands struggle to reach the right audience.

Manual Outreach: Finding relevant influencers, sponsors, and partners is time-consuming and inefficient.

Name of your organization: National Network for Immigrants and Refugees-Canada
Title: Black Futures Digital Hub
Subtitle: Empowering Black refugee women and youth in shelters through digital training, storytelling and remote work opportunities.
Problem Statement:
Most shelters in Toronto provide accommodation only, without the digital support or skills training needed for economic inclusion. Many Black immigrants and refugees come from countries with low digital literacy, making it especially difficult to adapt to Canada’s highly digital society. 

This digital knowledge gap, combined with unstable housing and limited access to technology, creates major barriers to integration, employment and participation in the digital economy. Without tailored programs addressing these challenges, Black refugee women and youth remain excluded from opportunities for financial independence and social inclusion.
Solution Overview:
Black Futures Digital Hub will support Black immigrant and refugee women living in shelters in Toronto through two cohorts, each running for four months. Each cohort will include 15 participants, recruited with the help of shelters and community partners. At the beginning of each cohort, participants will undergo a skills and needs assessment to customize the training and support they receive.

Over the next two months, participants will take part in training sessions held at the Training Hub a secure space equipped with laptops, high-speed internet and childcare services. The training will cover fundamental digital skills, freelancing platforms, social media management, content creation and digital tools such as Canva, video editing software and AI writing assistants. It will also include soft skills like client communication and time management.

In the fourth month, the focus will shift to livelihood development, including coaching, job search assistance, and building online professional profiles.

Upon completing the program, participants will gain lifetime access to the Training Hub and receive ongoing mentorship to support their career advancement and digital work. They will have the freedom to use the Hub’s resources whenever needed, fostering a continuous support network.

The program will be guided by a participant centered, trauma-informed approach that takes into account challenges such as housing instability and caregiving responsibilities. It will combine in person training with virtual resources to offer flexibility. Tools like Google Workspace, Canva, CapCut, ChatGPT and freelancing platforms will be used, with progress tracked via a straightforward management system. Participants will earn certificates to boost their professional profiles.

Key partnerships will involve our existing shelter partners like Homes First ,Fred Victor shelters  for recruitment and outreach, community tech organizations to operate the Training Hub and maintain digital infrastructure, legal and social service agencies offering immigration and employment support and Black led community groups ensuring culturally relevant programming and mentorship. 

As a nonprofit, we operate under a trustee relationship with the Toronto People With AIDS Foundation(PWA) , who host our operations and can provide physical space for the Training Hub at a significantly reduced cost. This partnership enhances our ability to maintain a dedicated, stable space for learning and support.

This model, consisting of two four month cohorts combined with lifetime Hub membership and mentorship, will establish a lasting support system that enables Black immigrant and refugee women in shelters to develop digital skills and achieve long term economic independence.
Solution Provider(s): Suzanne Paddock (She/Her) Executive Director  PWA (Toronto People With AIDS Foundation)  ,Melody Harris (She/Her)  Manager of Community Relations Homes First Shelters
Duration to pilot in a new geography: 12 months
SDGs addressed: SDG 4 (Quality Education);SDG 5 (Gender Equality);SDG 8 (Decent Work and Economic Growth);
Desired impact:
The Black Futures Digital Hub aims to empower Black immigrant and refugee women and youth  living in shelters by providing digital literacy, freelancing, and entrepreneurial training in a safe, trauma-informed environment. The program’s core objective is to equip participants with practical skills and ongoing mentorship to support long term economic independence through remote work and digital entrepreneurship. 

Each year, the program will train 30 participants through two four month cohorts, with all participants completing a personalized digital skills plan and earning certificates and we expect that at least 70% of graduates will secure freelance contracts, digital employment or start their own online services within six months of completing the program. 

All participants will receive lifetime access to the Hub’s resources and mentorship, creating a sustained community of support. The project will  also aim to reduce digital exclusion and strengthen partnerships between shelters, Black led organizations and tech collaborators, ultimately expanding access to inclusive economic opportunities.
Key technologies:
The project will use a range of accessible technologies to support participants in building digital skills and launching online work and will  include AI tools like ChatGPT for writing support and content creation, Canva for graphic design training and CapCut for video editing. 

Participants will also learn to use Google Workspace for productivity and collaboration and are introduced to freelancing platforms such as Fiverr and Upwork to build their online profiles and find remote work. 

A simple learning management system willl also be  used to track progress, while all tools are integrated into hands on training that prepares participants for real-world digital employment.
Unique Characteristics:
What makes the Black Futures Digital Hub unique is its combination of trauma informed, culturally relevant training with a long term support model tailored specifically for Black immigrant and refugee women living in shelters. 

Unlike most digital skills programs, this solution will offer lifetime membership and mentorship, allowing participants to return to the Hub anytime for coaching, internet access or help with freelance work. 

It will also deeply community rooted, operating under a nonprofit trustee model with trusted organizations like PWA, which enables access to space and infrastructure at lower costs. 

The program will  blends in person learning with flexible virtual tools and integrates low barrier technologies like ChatGPT, Canva and CapCut to match the needs and realities of participants. With our existing  partnerships with shelters, Black-led groups and tech collectives will ensure wraparound support with a  focus on building freelance income pathways rather than just job placement which sets it apart as a solution that promotes agency, independence and long term resilience.
Sustainable Change:
The Black Futures Digital Hub will contribute to sustainable, systemic change by equipping Black immigrant and refugee women with the digital skills and ongoing support they need to participate fully in the digital economy. 

By providing tailored training in a trauma informed, culturally sensitive environment and offering lifetime access to mentorship and resources, the program will break cycles of poverty and exclusion that disproportionately affect this community. 

As participants gain confidence and secure freelance or remote work, they will  achieve economic independence and become role models and mentors within their communities, creating a ripple effect that encourages others to pursue digital livelihoods. 

The Hub’s partnerships with shelters, Black-led organizations and tech group strengthens local ecosystems and improve access to resources. Over time, these combined efforts will  contribute to reducing systemic barriers, increasing digital inclusion and promoting economic equity for Black immigrant and refugee women, fostering lasting change beyond individual participants.
Primary thematic focus area: Inclusive Digital Innovation Skills & Entrepreneurial Talent Development
Summary: Black Futures Digital Hub is a pilot-stage program in Toronto designed to empower Black immigrant and refugee women and youth living in shelters. It provides four-month training cohorts focused on digital skills, freelancing, and entrepreneurship, combined with lifetime access to a Training Hub offering mentorship, childcare, and internet-enabled workspaces. Using tools like ChatGPT, Canva, CapCut, and Google Workspace, the program takes a trauma-informed, culturally sensitive approach. Operated under a trustee model with Toronto People With AIDS Foundation and in partnership with shelters and Black-led groups, the Hub seeks to create long-term economic independence through digital employment and entrepreneurship.

Title: SheConnects: Remote Virtual Assistant Jobs for Afghan Women in Exclusion
Subtitle: A remote work platform that connects Afghan women—excluded from the workforce—with European companies seeking skilled, reliable, and impact-driven virtual assistants.
Problem Statement: Since 2021, Afghan women have been banned from most forms of employment under the Taliban regime, leaving hundreds of thousands of educated, skilled women jobless and socially isolated. At the same time, many European SMEs and NGOs are seeking affordable, reliable remote support — but struggle to find solutions that are both efficient and above all, impactful.
Solution Overview:
SheConnects is a digital matchmaking platform that connects skilled Afghan women with European businesses and NGOs in need of virtual assistants. Afghan women apply, go through a vetting and interview process, and receive training focused on remote work tools, communication, and cultural awareness. After training, they are matched with clients and work remotely from home.

Methodologies and technologies used:

Web-based platform (www.sheconnects.work) for application and client intake

Internal screening and training program (project management, communication, digital literacy)

Remote work tools (e.g., Trello, Google Workspace, Zoom)

Payment processing platforms to ensure secure monthly payments

Partnerships and collaboration models:
SheConnects collaborates with local women’s networks in Afghanistan for talent sourcing, and works with European SMEs and nonprofits for hiring them. Clients are onboarded with a structured needs assessment and matched with trained VAs based on language, skills, and time zone compatibility.
Solution Provider(s): Refugee Restart, an incubator in italy for helping immigrants start their businesses in italy; Bridge for Billions, partnering with organizations to empower entrepreneurs of all kinds and strengthen ecosystems.
Duration to pilot in a new geography: We estimate a pilot duration of 4 to 6 months. This includes approximately 3 months for recruiting and training virtual assistants (VAs) in Afghanistan, followed by 1 to 3 months to establish partnerships and onboard companies in Europe that will hire them. The timeline may vary slightly depending on local conditions and the speed of partner engagement.
SDGs addressed: SDG 5 (Gender Equality);SDG 8 (Decent Work and Economic Growth);SDG 10 (Reduced Inequalities);
Desired impact:
Enable Afghan women to work remotely with European companies, restoring income and dignity through ethical digital employment.

Key Impacts:

500 women employed in 3 years

€2.5M in income generated

Promotes inclusion, independence, and cross-border collaboration
Key technologies:
SheConnects uses a web-based platform for onboarding, matching, and managing virtual assistants. Core technologies include:

Cloud-based tools (Google Workspace, Trello, Zoom) for collaboration and training

CRM systems for client–VA matching and communication
Unique Characteristics:
Socially driven outsourcing model: We combine quality virtual assistant services with direct social impact by employing Afghan women excluded from the workforce.

Time-zone alignment: Unlike most offshore VA providers (e.g., Philippines, Latin America), our VAs are only 2–3 hours ahead of Europe, enabling real-time collaboration.

Founder proximity to the problem: Built by Afghan founders with lived experience of the problem and deep cultural insight, ensuring trust, access, and relevance.
Sustainable Change:
SheConnects creates sustainable, systemic change by restoring access to work for women excluded from public life.

Theory of Change:
Access to remote jobs: Women regain income, confidence, and independence

Income stability: Improved household welfare and income restore

Professional reactivation: Skills are preserved and revalued in society

Cross-border collaboration:  Builds mutual understanding between cultures

Scalable model: Can be replicated for other marginalized groups globally

Primary thematic focus area: Inclusive Digital Innovation Skills & Entrepreneurial Talent Development
Summary: SheConnects is a digital platform that creates remote employment opportunities for Afghan women excluded from the workforce under the Taliban. The solution matches trained Afghan women with European SMEs and NGOs needing virtual assistants. With founders deeply connected to the Afghan context and partnerships with Refugee Restart and Bridge for Billions, SheConnects provides both social impact and business value. Title: “Equal Music: Empowering Local Artists Through Mobile Monetization”
Subtitle: A Ugandan digital platform enabling local musicians to earn royalties instantly via mobile money through a secure, affordable, and inclusive online music store.
Problem Statement: Ugandan musicians face limited monetization opportunities due to piracy, poor digital infrastructure, and lack of secure platforms for income generation. Fans also lack convenient ways to support artists.
Solution Overview:
Equal Music is a digital platform that allows musicians to upload, authenticate, and monetise their music directly via mobile money. Artists register and upload songs with Uganda Performing Rights Society (UPRS) verification. Music users access content via mobile phone, paying UGX 500 per stream or download. Royalties are distributed instantly, empowering artists with real-time income transparency.

The platform uses mobile money APIs (MTN, Airtel), web and Android app frameworks, cloud hosting, and secure encryption. It’s optimised for both smartphones and feature phones, making it inclusive and scalable.

Partnerships include UPRS (copyright verification), telecom providers (payments and promotion), media outlets (awareness), and local influencers (outreach). The model encourages collaboration with policymakers and creative industry stakeholders.
Solution Provider(s): Sserumaga Foundation (Social innovation and education), Uganda Performing Rights Society (Creative IP and licensing), Telecoms (MTN Uganda, Airtel Uganda – Mobile payments & SMS), Local media outlets and influencers (Awareness and distribution)
Duration to pilot in a new geography: 4–6 months (including localization, artist onboarding, and mobile integration)
SDGs addressed: SDG 8 (Decent Work and Economic Growth);SDG 9 (Industry, Innovation, and Infrastructure);SDG 10 (Reduced Inequalities);
Desired impact:
Objectives:
 1. Increase monetisation opportunities for Ugandan musicians
 2. Create secure, transparent revenue streams for creators
 3. Expand digital access to African music consumers

Key Achievements (Projected):
 1. 100,000 users by Year 3
 2. UGX 1.2 billion in revenue
 3. Direct earnings for over 5,000 artists
 4. 80% of revenue paid directly to creators
 5. Expansion potential to Kenya, Rwanda, and other regions
Key technologies:
1. Mobile Money APIs (Airtel, MTN)
2. Web and Mobile App Development (Android-first)
3. UPRS Integration System for content authentication
4. SSL Encryption and secure cloud hosting
5. Real-time transaction tracking systems
Unique Characteristics: Equal Music’s uniqueness lies in its hyper-localisation designed specifically for Uganda’s economic and technological landscape. It integrates real-time royalties via mobile money, artist-owned content authentication (UPRS), and a pay-per-song microtransaction model that is affordable and inclusive. The platform also offers artist dashboards, analytics, and marketing tools features typically inaccessible to low-income or grassroots musicians.
Sustainable Change: By enabling musicians to earn directly from their audiences, Equal Music catalyses a shift toward financially independent, digitally savvy creative entrepreneurs. It fosters local innovation, boosts mobile money usage, and encourages regulatory engagement with intellectual property rights. As a replicable model, it supports sustainable creative economies across Africa, improving livelihoods, reducing piracy, and building inclusive digital ecosystems that uplift youth and marginalised creators.
Funding Sources: Not applicable.
Testimonials and Endorsements: I haven't yet sought any endorsements.
Further comments/feedback: Not really.
Primary thematic focus area: MSME Empowerment & Local Digital Innovation
Summary: Equal Music is a Ugandan digital platform designed to empower local musicians by providing instant mobile money royalties through a secure, affordable online music store. Artists upload songs authenticated via the Uganda Performing Rights Society (UPRS), while users pay per stream or download (UGX 500). Revenue is distributed instantly, with 80% going directly to artists. The solution integrates mobile money APIs (MTN, Airtel), Android/web apps, and cloud hosting, ensuring inclusivity for both smartphone and feature phone users. Partnerships include UPRS, telecoms, media outlets, and influencers. The initiative aims to scale to Kenya, Rwanda, and beyond.

Web platform

AI-supported chat and onboarding

Digital service marketplace

Data analytics (for local service gaps and diaspora mapping

Combines social inclusion + tech innovation + economic empowerment
