Summary: Karibu Plus is a Kenyan-developed digital relocation and integration platform designed for migrants, returnees, and global professionals moving to Africa. It centralizes services such as housing, financial onboarding, legal aid, healthcare, language support, and employment connections in one web/mobile platform. Using AI-assisted onboarding, multilingual chat, diaspora mapping, and a curated service marketplace, it aims to reduce fragmentation and promote inclusive economic participation. The MVP is planned for pilot rollout in 2025, with expansion to Rwanda and South Africa.

Title: Exportplug
Subtitle: Connecting African food producers to verified global buyers for seamless, trusted export transactions
Problem Statement: Small and medium-scale African exporters face significant challenges accessing global markets due to limited visibility, complex export procedures, lack of trust between buyers and sellers, and difficulty complying with international trade standards. This leads to missed opportunities, low revenue, and limited economic growth.
Solution Overview:
Exportplug is an online marketplace that makes it easier for African businesses to export agricultural and non-oil products. It connects verified local producers and manufacturers with trusted buyers around the world. Exportplug allows exporters to showcase their products, receive inquiries, negotiate deals, and complete transactions in one place. The platform supports important processes such as product quality checks, secure payments, real-time shipment tracking, and the generation of export documents and invoices. By making the export journey more transparent and efficient, Exportplug helps small and medium-sized businesses overcome the common barriers to entering international markets.

The platform is built using modern web technologies such as React JavaScript and Java Spring Boot, which ensure fast performance and the ability to scale as more users join. Exportplug also uses artificial intelligence to recommend products to buyers and match them with reliable suppliers based on preferences and past activity. The company works closely with logistics providers like DHL (Dalsey, Hillblom and Lynn), the Nigerian Export Promotion Council, the National Agency for Food and Drug Administration and Control, and financial institutions that offer payment protection and export financing. Exportplug also trains and deploys field agents who help local businesses with product onboarding, packaging, and meeting export requirements. These partnerships ensure that every exporter, no matter their size or location, has a clear path to reaching buyers beyond their borders.
Solution Provider(s): NEPC
Duration to pilot in a new geography: Exportplug can be piloted in a new geography within 8 to 12 weeks. This includes market research, onboarding of local exporters, integration with logistics and regulatory partners, training field agents, and launching a localized platform version tailored to the region’s trade requirements and product categories.
SDGs addressed: SDG 2 (Zero Hunger);SDG 3 (Good Health and Well-being);SDG 9 (Industry, Innovation, and Infrastructure);
Desired impact:
Exportplug is designed to drive inclusive trade by connecting African agricultural and non-oil product exporters with trusted global buyers. The platform’s main objectives are to simplify the export process, increase market access for small and medium-sized businesses, and promote transparency and compliance in international trade. Exportplug provides tools for secure payments, real-time logistics tracking, and automated documentation, helping exporters reduce transaction costs and navigate trade regulations more easily. By digitizing the value chain, Exportplug supports economic diversification, encourages foreign exchange inflow, and strengthens Africa’s position in the global export market.

Since launching its minimum viable product, Exportplug has onboarded over 100 verified exporters and agents, listed more than 50 export-ready products, and reduced the time it takes to complete an export transaction by up to 40%. It has created over 120 direct and indirect jobs through its growing network of logistics providers, software developers, product designers, and trained field agents. Exportplug integrates with regulatory bodies like the Nigerian Export Promotion Council and the National Agency for Food and Drug Administration and Control to ensure product quality and compliance. Within the next year, it aims to facilitate over \$1 million in verified exports and expand operations into two new African countries.
Key technologies:
Exportplug uses a mix of reliable and modern technologies to make exporting easier for African businesses. The platform is built with React JavaScript on the frontend and Java Spring Boot on the backend. This setup helps ensure fast performance, strong security, and the ability to scale as more users and products are added.

To improve how buyers find products, Exportplug is integrating artificial intelligence. The system learns from buyer preferences and browsing behavior to recommend the most relevant export-ready products. In future updates, we plan to introduce blockchain technology to increase transparency, especially for tracking shipments, verifying payments, and handling contracts securely. We’re also exploring the use of Internet of Things (IoT) devices to help monitor sensitive goods, like fresh produce, during transport by tracking storage conditions such as temperature and humidity.

Another key feature is the smart invoice and documentation tool, which helps exporters automatically generate the right paperwork based on their product and destination country. All these technologies come together to reduce delays, improve trust, and make it easier for African exporters to meet global trade standards.
Unique Characteristics: What makes Exportplug unique is its all-in-one approach to solving the real challenges African exporters face. Unlike typical listing platforms, Exportplug combines verified buyer-seller matchmaking, automated export documentation, and quality assurance into one seamless experience. It also uses AI to recommend products and blockchain (in development) for secure, transparent transactions. Beyond tech, Exportplug partners with local agents, trade bodies, and logistics companies to support even rural exporters. Its flexible payment and financing options, along with regulatory support, help small businesses overcome barriers and compete globally making Exportplug not just a platform, but a growth partner.
Sustainable Change:
Exportplug creates sustainable, systemic change by addressing the root barriers that limit African exporters lack of access to global markets, poor infrastructure, and limited compliance support. By digitizing the export process and connecting local producers with verified international buyers, the platform helps small and medium businesses grow beyond local limitations.

The desired follow-on effects include increased income for farmers and manufacturers, job creation across the export value chain, and greater foreign exchange earnings for African economies. Over time, as more exporters succeed, communities gain economic stability, and countries diversify away from oil dependency. Exportplug’s model also encourages better product standards and transparency, setting a new norm for African trade that is digital, efficient, and trusted.
Funding Sources: We were funded by Tony Elumelu Foundation in 2024 with $5000 and won a Grant of 20 Million Naira for Nigeria AFCFTA HACKATHON
Primary thematic focus area: MSME Empowerment & Local Digital Innovation
Summary: Exportplug is a pilot-ready online marketplace from Nigeria that connects African agricultural and non-oil exporters with verified global buyers. Strengths: MVP already launched, 100+ exporters onboarded, practical integration with regulators and logistics partners, AI-driven product matching, strong early traction with grants. Weaknesses: limited funding base, operations still concentrated in Nigeria, and blockchain/IoT features remain under development.

Title: Pathway to Empowerment-Nurturing Future Digital Media Innovation
Subtitle: A community-driven digital media lab empowering rural youth in Western Kenya with creative skills, tech access, and entrepreneurial training for inclusive economic growth.
Problem Statement: Rural youth in Western Kenya lack access to digital tools, creative training, and economic opportunities. This digital divide limits their potential to express themselves, build careers, and participate in the digital economy. Many talented young people remain unheard, unemployed, or under-skilled due to systemic barriers in education, infrastructure, and mentorship.
Solution Overview:
Sebas Media Lab is a creative digital hub located in Butula, Western Kenya, designed to empower rural youth through hands-on training in storytelling, podcasting, digital editing, and photography. Our model blends digital literacy with entrepreneurship, giving marginalized young people tools to earn an income and build visibility for their communities.

1. How it works:
The lab offers structured bootcamps, peer mentorship, and access to equipment such as cameras, laptops, and editing software. Participants develop digital content, podcasts, short films, blogs and gain practical business and tech skills that are immediately applicable.

2. Technologies used:

a) Audio-visual recording & editing tools (e.g. Adobe Suite, Audacity)
b) Open-source learning platforms for digital skills (e.g. Canva, Anchor, YouTube Studio)
c) Cloud collaboration tools (e.g. Google Workspace, Trello)

3. Methodologies:

a) Project-based learning
b) Peer-to-peer mentorship
c) Community storytelling and co-creation
d) Lean startup and human-centered design approaches

4. Partnerships and collaboration:
We collaborate with AscentChange International, local schools, churches, youth groups, and digital mentors. We also leverage networks like the DOSZ Ambassador Program and alumni from Bridge for Billions to share expertise, amplify content, and provide long-term mentorship.

Together, these components form a sustainable, scalable model for digital inclusion and youth empowerment in underserved communities.
Solution Provider(s): Sebas Media Lab (Social Enterprise- Media/Creative Economy), AscentChange International (Non-profit Organization- Education, Youth Empowerment, and Community Development), Bridge for Billions (Entrepreneurship Support Organization- Business Incubation and Mentorship), DOSZ Ambassador Program- Hungary (Academic Network- International PhD Student Support and Scientific Collaboration), E4Impact Foundation (Social Enterprise Accelerator- Impact Entrepreneurship and Sustainable Development in Africa), Gile Foundation (Non-profit Organization – Academic and Professional Research Support, Social Inclusion, and Capacity Building in Emerging Economies), Local Youth Groups and Schools in Butula, Busia County, Western & Nyanza region of Kenya (Community-Based Organizations- Education and Civic Engagement)
Duration to pilot in a new geography: 12 month
SDGs addressed: SDG 4 (Quality Education);SDG 8 (Decent Work and Economic Growth);SDG 9 (Industry, Innovation, and Infrastructure);
Desired impact:
1. Solution Objectives:
Sebas Media Lab aims to bridge the rural digital divide by equipping marginalized youth in Western Kenya with creative digital media skills. The objective is to create a sustainable ecosystem that fosters storytelling, entrepreneurship, and digital empowerment.

2. Key Achievements and Impacts:

a) Digital Literacy: Trained over 100 youth in foundational digital media skills through workshops, mentorship, and community bootcamps.
b) Employment Generation: Enabled 20+ participants to start freelance careers or internships in podcasting, videography, and editing.
c) Local Innovation: Developed and piloted a locally-run media studio model that offers affordable editing, recording, and training services.
d) Inclusion: Reached young women, out-of-school youth, and underserved communities, increasing access to digital platforms and economic participation.
e) Community Engagement: Conducted local storytelling projects that promote cultural preservation and civic engagement.

Future scaling of the solution targets the creation of 300+ new digital jobs by 2027 and a network of rural media labs driving visibility and inclusive innovation across the region.
Key technologies:
Sebas Media Lab leverages accessible and cost-effective digital technologies to deliver its solution. Key technologies include:

a) Audio-Visual Production Tools: Use of digital cameras, audio recorders, podcasting microphones, and video editing software (e.g., Adobe Premiere Pro, Audacity, DaVinci Resolve) to train youth in content creation.
b) Cloud-Based Collaboration: Google Workspace and other cloud tools for remote mentoring, file sharing, and co-creation of projects.
c) Social Media Platforms: Tools like YouTube, Instagram, TikTok, and Facebook are used for publishing youth stories and amplifying impact.
d) Basic AI Tools: Introduction to generative AI and voice-enhancement software to support digital storytelling and editing efficiency.
e) Low-Code Tools: Platforms like Canva, CapCut, and mobile editing apps for entry-level creative work.

These tools are selected for accessibility, scalability, and alignment with youth needs in low-resource settings.
Unique Characteristics:
Sebas Media Lab stands out for its community-rooted, youth-led approach to digital empowerment in rural Kenya. What makes the solution unique:

a) Hybrid Model: Combines creative training, studio services, and social entrepreneurship under one roof to support skills-building and self-sustenance.
b) Local Ownership: Operated by local mentors and youth changemakers to ensure cultural relevance and long-term community investment.
c) Flexible Access: Offers mobile, on-site, and digital formats for training, enabling reach in low-connectivity regions.
d) Value-Based Storytelling: Empowers marginalized voices through storytelling that promotes identity, resilience, and inclusion.
e) Partnership-Driven: Collaborates with organizations like AscentChange International, E4Impact Foundation, and Gile Foundation to scale mentorship, business incubation, and creative enterprise pathways.

Unlike typical digital upskilling programs, Sebas Media Lab is designed as a scalable social venture—not just training youth, but equipping them to earn, innovate, and lead.
Sustainable Change:
Sebas Media Lab’s Theory of Change is rooted in the belief that equipping rural youth with digital and storytelling skills leads to self-reliance, local innovation, and social transformation.

By providing access to creative tools, mentorship, and entrepreneurial training, the Lab empowers youth to tell their own stories, build careers in the digital economy, and inspire others within their communities. As they become content creators, freelancers, and changemakers, they catalyze:

a) Economic Inclusion: Youth generate income through creative work, reducing rural unemployment and dependency.
b) Civic Engagement: Locally-produced media sparks dialogue on social issues, amplifies community voices, and promotes cultural preservation.
c) Education Reform: The Lab’s hands-on, community-based learning model complements traditional education systems with relevant, future-ready skills.
d) Replicable Model: Once proven, the Lab will be replicated in other underserved areas through local leadership and strategic partnerships.

Over time, this creates a ripple effect from individual empowerment to resilient, self-driven communities connected through purpose, technology, and storytelling.
Funding Sources: The initial phases of Sebas Media Lab have been funded through personal savings, support from family members, and contributions from well-wishers who believe in the vision of empowering rural youth through creative digital skills.
Testimonials and Endorsements: We have not yet conducted the pilot phase of Sebas Media Lab, so we do not have testimonials or formal endorsements to share at this time. However, we’ve received consistent verbal appreciation and informal feedback from community members, youth participants, and local partners who have engaged in our initiatives. We plan to gather and share documented testimonials from participants, community stakeholders, and partners to inform our growth and demonstrate impact in the near future we expand and become more structured.
Further comments/feedback: Thank you for the opportunity to share our initiative through this well-structured and thoughtful questionnaire. The questions allowed for deep reflection on our mission, impact, and growth strategy. We appreciate the focus on inclusive innovation and look forward to opportunities for collaboration and learning through this global platform.
Primary thematic focus area: Inclusive Digital Innovation Skills & Entrepreneurial Talent Development
Summary: Sebas Media Lab est un hub créatif situé à Butula, au Kenya occidental, qui vise à réduire la fracture numérique rurale en formant les jeunes marginalisés aux compétences médiatiques numériques (storytelling, podcasting, édition, photographie) et à l’entrepreneuriat (Q12, Q19). À travers des bootcamps, du mentorat par les pairs, l’accès à des équipements et des partenariats avec des ONG et incubateurs, le projet cherche à générer des opportunités d’emploi, promouvoir l’inclusion et développer un modèle de studio communautaire durable.

Title: OSIA est une IA générative 100% Camerounaise qui vise à perfectionner le système d’orientation scolaire ainsi que le rendement scolaire au Cameroun en particulier et en Afrique en général à travers un package de trois services innovants
Subtitle: OSIA (Orientation scolaire via l’intelligence artificielle) est une solution innovante, efficace et rapide à ce fléau social qui gangrène et nuit à des millions de jeunes apprenants africains sans cesse victimes de la mauvaise orientation scolaire
Problem Statement: La mauvaise orientation scolaire , l’inadéquation formation-emploi; la baisse du rendement scolaire, le taux de chômage de plus en plus élevé
Solution Overview:
Nous offrons trois services innovants pour solutionner ce problème à savoir: 
-Un VPO verdict prévisionnel d’orientation qui est un document concis et conçu par notre IA à partir des notes de classe annuelles, des tests psychotechniques de chaque afin de proposer une orientation qui sied à ses capacités réelles et donner ses différents profils(scientifiques m, littéraires, techniques ou même psychologiques…Etc)
Un CHATBOT ou répétiteur virtuel bien entrainé avec tous les programmes scolaires en vigueur au Cameroun et qui offre ainsi une assistance rapide, fluide et très explicite aux apprenants en fonction de leur niveau scolaires
- Une grosse banque numérique d’épreuves et corrigés afin de permettre aux apprenants de mieux s’entraîner avec des anciens sujets des meilleurs écoles du Cameroun.
Pour y arriver nous utilisons une open source que nous avons tropicalisée avec des données locales afin de contextualiser notre IA
Notre cible est estimée à environ 03 millions d’apprenants au Cameroun et il s’agit essentiellement des jeunes apprenants
Solution Provider(s): Les parents d’élèves, et surtout des chefs d’établissement (écoles et collèges…Etc)
Duration to pilot in a new geography: 04-06 mois
SDGs addressed: SDG 4 (Quality Education);SDG 8 (Decent Work and Economic Growth);SDG 9 (Industry, Innovation, and Infrastructure);
Desired impact: Nous comptons à moyen terme familiariser les jeunes apprenants à l’usage d’une IA locale éthique fiable et utile (OSIA), et de souscrire 50.000 users actifs sur notre plateforme d’ici fin 2026 et réaliser un chiffre affaires annuel de 3000*50.000=150.000.000 Fcfa
Key technologies: IA
Unique Characteristics: Nous avons un Bussiness model raffiné car très réaliste, bien ficelé, et surtout une stratégie marketing de proximité, d’ailleurs nous avons clairement identifié nos cibles (Fondateurs d’écoles et collèges susceptibles d’intégrer progressivement notre IA dans leur système scolaire ) à un prix imbattable soit 3000 Fcfa/an/apprenant
Sustainable Change: Grâce au verdict prévisionnel d’orientation, nous allons révolutionner le système actuel  d’orientation scolaire vétuste, inefficace et obsolète en vigueur au Cameroun, car notre solution proposera de façon personnalisée pour chaque apprenants un tunnel cohérent d’orientation, ce qui nous permettra de sauver l’avenir de millions de jeunes apprenants
Funding Sources: À partir des économies personnelles ou fonds propres, également grâce aux prix d’excellence remportés (Orange Cameroun POESAM), Pfs-Banque mondial; Awitai (UNESCO)…Etc
Further comments/feedback: https://teleasu.tv/innovation-tech-osia-remporte-le-premier-prix-poesam-2025/
Primary thematic focus area: MSME Empowerment & Local Digital Innovation
Summary: OSIA est une solution d’IA générative développée au Cameroun pour améliorer l’orientation scolaire et le rendement académique. Elle propose trois services : (1) un verdict prévisionnel d’orientation basé sur les notes et tests psychotechniques, (2) un chatbot/répétiteur virtuel aligné sur les programmes scolaires camerounais, et (3) une banque numérique d’épreuves corrigées (Q13). Ciblant 3M d’apprenants, OSIA ambitionne de compter 50.000 utilisateurs actifs d’ici 2026 et de moderniser le système d’orientation scolaire (Q17, Q21).

Name of your organization: CERVIA SA – Centre d’Entrepreneuriat et de Renforcement pour la Valorisation de l’Innovation Verte et Accompagnement
Title: Green : L’innovation verte entre les mains des jeunes
Subtitle: Une solution inclusive qui connecte les jeunes entrepreneurs verts aux outils numériques pour développer des activités durables, locales et innovantes.   - Green favorise l'accès des jeunes et des femmes aux opportunités numériques pour accélérer l'entrepreneuriat vert et réduire les inégalités.  - Un pont entre écologie et technologie pour des jeunes acteurs du changement en milieu rural.  - Quand inclusion numérique et entrepreneuriat vert se rencontrent pour bâtir un avenir durable.  - Renforcer les compétences numériques des jeunes green-preneurs pour un impact local durable.
Problem Statement:
Dans de nombreuses zones rurales et semi-urbaines, les jeunes et les femmes engagés dans l’entrepreneuriat vert font face à une triple exclusion :

un accès limité aux outils numériques,
un manque de compétences digitales,
et une faible connexion aux réseaux de financement et de marché.

Cette fracture numérique freine leur potentiel d’innovation, d’autonomisation économique et de participation aux initiatives durables. Sans accompagnement adapté, ces porteurs de solutions locales peinent à se développer, à se connecter et à valoriser leurs initiatives à plus grande échelle
Solution Provider(s): SNV – Organisation Néerlandaise de Développement Profil : Organisation internationale de développement active au Mali depuis plusieurs décennies. Secteur : Agriculture durable, entrepreneuriat vert, inclusion économique des jeunes et des femmes
Duration to pilot in a new geography: La durée estimée pour piloter la solution dans une nouvelle géographie est de 6 à 9 mois.  Ce délai comprend :  1 à 2 mois pour l’analyse du contexte local, la mobilisation des parties prenantes et la sélection des bénéficiaires ;  3 à 4 mois pour le déploiement des formations, l’équipement numérique et l’accompagnement technique ;  2 à 3 mois pour le suivi-évaluation, l’ajustement de la solution et la préparation à l’extension ou à la pérennisation.
SDGs addressed: SDG 17 (Partnerships for the Goals);SDG 8 (Decent Work and Economic Growth);SDG 2 (Zero Hunger);
Desired impact:
Objectifs de la solution :

Réduire la fracture numérique en zone rurale et semi-urbaine, en particulier chez les jeunes et les femmes.

Renforcer les capacités des entrepreneurs verts à travers la formation numérique et l’accompagnement technique.

Favoriser l’insertion économique durable grâce à l’innovation et aux outils numériques adaptés.

Contribuer à la transition verte locale en appuyant des projets à faible impact environnemental.

Promouvoir l’égalité de genre et la lutte contre les violences basées sur le genre (VBG).
Key technologies:
1 - Smartphones et applications mobiles : Utilisation d’outils accessibles tels que WhatsApp Business, Facebook, TikTok, Canva, Google Forms et Google Sheets pour la communication, la formation, la gestion, la vente et le suivi.

2 - Outils numériques d’e-learning et de formation hybride : Utilisation de plateformes de formation à distance et de vidéos pédagogiques pour renforcer les compétences des jeunes et des femmes entrepreneurs, même en zone faiblement connectée.

3 - Technologies d’énergie renouvelable (solaire) : Appui à l’utilisation de kits solaires intelligents pour alimenter les équipements numériques dans les zones non électrifiées.

4 - Outils de collecte et d’analyse de données : Formulaires en ligne (Google Forms, KoboToolbox) pour les enquêtes de terrain, l’évaluation des besoins et le suivi des performances.

5 - Réseaux sociaux comme plateformes de marché : Valorisation des produits verts via TikTok, Facebook Marketplace et WhatsApp, en remplaçant les canaux physiques par des canaux numériques accessibles.
Unique Characteristics:
Caractéristiques uniques et différenciées de la solution Green :

1 Intégration de l’économie verte et du numérique : la solution combine deux leviers de transformation : la transition écologique et l’inclusion numérique. Elle cible les jeunes et femmes entrepreneurs verts, souvent exclus des dispositifs classiques, en leur offrant un accompagnement adapté aux réalités locales.

2 Utilisation stratégique des outils numériques simples et accessibles : la solution mise sur des technologies disponibles et maîtrisables (WhatsApp, TikTok, Facebook, Google Forms), permettant une prise en main rapide, même dans des zones rurales faiblement connectées. Cela favorise une appropriation immédiate et une réduction rapide de la fracture numérique.

3 Modèle de partenariat communautaire
La solution repose sur une approche multi-acteurs impliquant :

Des ONG internationales (ex : SNV) pour l’expertise et le financement,

Des acteurs locaux (collectivités, groupements de femmes/jeunes) pour l’ancrage territorial,

Des entreprises tech et prestataires locaux pour le renforcement des compétences.

4 Modèle économique hybride et durable
Les jeunes entrepreneurs sont accompagnés dans la viabilisation économique de leurs activités via :

La valorisation de produits/services verts,

La commercialisation via les réseaux sociaux,

La mise en réseau avec des clients et partenaires à travers des plateformes digitales.

5 Focus sur la paix et l’égalité de genre
La solution intègre des actions de sensibilisation sur les VBG, la promotion du leadership féminin, et la gestion pacifique des conflits communautaires, renforçant ainsi la cohésion sociale.

6  Suivi-évaluation numérique en temps réel : l’utilisation de KoboToolbox, LogAlto Google Sheets ou Power BI permet un suivi participatif des progrès, facilitant l’adaptation continue de la solution.
Sustainable Change:
Contribution au changement systémique durable – Théorie du changement

La solution vise à transformer durablement les conditions d’accès à l’économie numérique et verte pour les jeunes et les femmes, en s’attaquant à trois leviers systémiques :

1. Renforcement des capacités locales

En dotant les jeunes et femmes d’outils numériques, de connaissances entrepreneuriales et de compétences en innovation verte, la solution développe un capital humain local fort, capable d’agir, d’innover et de transmettre.

Effet durable attendu : des communautés plus autonomes, capables de générer leurs propres solutions à long terme.

2. Inclusion économique et sociale

La solution contribue à réduire les inégalités structurelles en créant un accès équitable à la formation, au financement, aux marchés et à l’information.

Elle favorise également l’autonomisation des femmes et la lutte contre les VBG, renforçant la cohésion sociale.

Effet durable attendu : un tissu économique local plus résilient, juste et inclusif.

3. Transformation des écosystèmes locaux

Par ses partenariats multi-acteurs (ONG, autorités locales, entreprises, société civile), la solution renforce les institutions locales et introduit une culture de collaboration autour de l’innovation verte et numérique.

Effet durable attendu : un écosystème propice à l’essaimage de la solution dans d'autres zones ou secteurs, même après le retrait des acteurs externes.

Vision à long terme :

 Une jeunesse formée, connectée et engagée dans des activités économiques vertes, soutenue par un environnement numérique inclusif, avec des relais communautaires solides et une gouvernance locale participative.
Funding Sources:
Le financement s’est basé sur un modèle hybride combinant :

Dons institutionnels internationaux,

Partenariats territoriaux,

Contributions locales en nature,
ce qui garantit flexibilité, ancrage local et potentiel de pérennisation.

Title: Prediction for maximum food in the Growth Pattern of Fish (Nile Tilapia) and Plant (Lettuce) in a Prototype-Safe, Automated Aquaponics Environment Using Deep Learning.
Subtitle: Maximization of food production all year round as well as conservation of water using machine learning techniques. A more sustainable way for organic food production with individuals, entrepreneurs, educators, missions and governments to provide food all year round with small land space-no soil and less water.
Problem Statement:
Traditional agriculture has existed for thousands of years, but since the 1950s, agricultural food production has shifted away from small-scale local growers and towards the advent of the industrial farm, which has changed both the landscape and the food itself. Industrial agriculture has done a fantastic job of producing large amounts of food at reasonable prices, but it is not without flaws.  A large portion of this water is lost to runoff and evaporation during application. 
People will need to find a means to produce increasing quantities of food in a sustainable manner as the world's population grows. When compared to conventional agriculture, aquaponics systems have the ability to produce enormous amounts of food in a little amount of space. Also, can be labour-intensive due to the fact that the inside environment of an aquaponics system must be properly maintained. The approach is to design and build a clever and long-lasting aquaponics system with the use of technology that can produce a large amount of food in a little amount of space.
Solution Overview: Aquaponics is a hybrid of two technologies: recirculating aquaculture (fish farms) and hydroponics (soil-free crop production). The fish waste supplies an organic food supply for the developing plants, while the plants act as a natural filter for the fish's water. The highly nutritious effluents from the culture tank are used as a fertilizer for the hydroponics system in aquaponics. Normally, these nutrients in the fish tanks will build up in high levels. A successfully installed prototype aquaponics system can continuously check the water quality, fish and plant growth. The prototype can significantly reduce labour and operating costs when used on a wide scale, increase productivity, and increase profitability, all of which help create more livable and sustainable communities.
Solution Provider(s): The Action plan is tailored to Asante Bekwai Traditional area in the Ashanti region of Ghana, where i have identified Adubirem-a town in Amansie east to train local farmers.
Duration to pilot in a new geography: THREE MONTHS
SDGs addressed: SDG 2 (Zero Hunger);SDG 8 (Decent Work and Economic Growth);SDG 9 (Industry, Innovation, and Infrastructure);
Desired impact: The goal is to create an aquaponics system that is as self-sustaining as possible while also being adaptable to a variety of conditions. The aquaponics system must be able to maintain its occupants alive. This means that the temperature cannot be too high or too cold, that the water must be clean enough for the fish to survive, and that the plants must have enough nutrients and light from the grow lamps to thrive. The processes of measuring water quality and the amount of light needed for plant and fish to survive will be applied using machine learning algorithms to give accurate prediction on plant and fish growth and provide large portion of food in a controlled environment to solve issues in food security. Also, a system to maintain a healthy environment between plant and fish life by testing and predicting the water quality, hence water temperature to achieve all year food production.
Key technologies: Machine learning, Internet of Things
Unique Characteristics: Technological innovations, Entrepreneurial skills, Transferable Skills, ICT Convergence, Business innovations and Employment readiness
Sustainable Change: Sustainable agriculture, Proper usage of land and water, skills and training and employable skills
Primary thematic focus area: Innovation Acceleration & Knowledge Sharing
Summary: This project develops a prototype aquaponics system that integrates deep learning, IoT, and automated monitoring to maximize food production (fish: Nile Tilapia, plants: lettuce) while conserving water (Q13). It targets sustainable organic food production in Ghana, training local farmers in aquaponics techniques (Q14). Currently at Proof-of-Concept stage (Q16).

Name of your organization: OMOLARA INSTITUTO DE ESTUDOS PESQUISA DESENVOLVIMENTO SOCIO CULTURAL E SUSTENTABILIDADE
Title: Kemns Cash Inclusão Financeira Afrocentrada para Mulheres Negras
Subtitle: Kemns Cash is an inclusive, Afro-centric, and community-based fintech solution geared toward Black women entrepreneurs with low levels of education and unfamiliarity with digital tools.
Problem Statement:
Black women in vulnerable situations face significant barriers in financial management,
access to credit, and support against violence and discrimination Datashows high financial exclusion and low representation in the market The eed for a platform that integrates financial tools and rights protection is urgent.
Solution Overview:
Kemns Cash is a voice-command financial management app designed to empower Black women entrepreneurs with low or no literacy and limited access to digital technologies. Developed by Instituto Omolara Brasil, the app uses artificial intelligence, machine learning, and blockchain to simplify business operations, strengthen financial control, and provide access to educational content, microcredit, and community support.

Its intuitive and inclusive design allows users to manage income, expenses, and pricing using voice inputs and accessible interfaces — even offline. The platform is also inclusive of women with low or no vision. Additionally, it features a "Kemns Acolhe" section, which offers information and support to women facing gender-based violence or racism.

Integrated with the Kizomba Empreendedora Program, which supports hundreds of Black women entrepreneurs in vulnerable territories, Kemns Cash is both a technological solution and a social innovation. Its monetization strategy reinvests 100% of its profits into training, microcredit, and the expansion of the ecosystem of Black women-led businesses.
Solution Provider(s): We are currently seeking philanthropic investment or technical/financial partnerships to build our MVP (Minimum Viable Product), expand our community network, and scale the impact of Kemns Cash as a transformative tool for economic justice and gender equality
Duration to pilot in a new geography: quatro meses
SDGs addressed: SDG 5 (Gender Equality);SDG 8 (Decent Work and Economic Growth);SDG 10 (Reduced Inequalities);
Desired impact:
Kemns Cash aims to promote financial, digital, and economic inclusion for Black women entrepreneurs in Brazil who face barriers such as low literacy, limited digital access, and financial exclusion. Using an inclusive voice-activated mobile app powered by artificial intelligence, the solution empowers women in marginalized communities to take control of their businesses, access digital financial services, and grow sustainable enterprises.
Key Impacts and Achievements: 
 Reducing Digital Exclusion: Provides an intuitive platform tailored for users with low or no literacy, including those with visual impairments.
Works offline to reach areas with low connectivity, ensuring broader access.
 Economic Empowerment and Job Creation: Trains and empowers up to 4000 Black women entrepreneurs by 2027.
Supports the creation, formalization, or growth of 800 community-based businesses, directly contributing to income generation in underserved areas.
 Inclusive Credit Access: 
Introduces a Community Solvency Index, using alternative data such as transaction records, training engagement, and consistency, to assess creditworthiness.
Expected to reduce business dropout rates by up to 40% due to improved financial control and credit access.
Circular Reinvestment Model: The business model reinvests 100% of profits into training, microcredit, community networks, and platform maintenance, reinforcing long-term impact.
Key technologies:
What are the main technologies used in your solution?
Kemns Cash integrates accessible and high-impact technologies, including:

Inclusive Artificial Intelligence (AI):
Powers personalized financial insights, risk analysis using alternative data, and recommendation systems tailored to the realities of underserved entrepreneurs.

Natural Language Processing (NLP):
Voice command technology allows women with low digital literacy or visual impairment to record transactions, set prices, and access educational content without needing to type or navigate complex interfaces.

Machine Learning:
Learns from user behavior and generates a Community Solvency Index, a new metric designed to help banks and fintechs evaluate credit risk in a socially contextualized way.

Blockchain (under development):
Will ensure security and traceability of financial transactions within the app, reducing fraud and increasing trust.

Offline-First Architecture:
The app is designed for low-connectivity environments, allowing users to record data offline and synchronize once internet access is available.

API-Ready Infrastructure:
Enables secure and documented integration with banks, fintechs, and social impact institutions, boosting interoperability and scale.
Unique Characteristics:
Kemns Cash stands out for combining financial inclusion, African oral tradition, inclusive AI, and circular reinvestment into a single transformative solution. Its key differentiators include:

Afrocentric and Accessible Tech Model:
Uses voice commands and inclusive AI rooted in African oral tradition, allowing women with low literacy or no vision to manage their businesses independently.

Community Solvency Index:
Introduces a new credit risk analysis metric based on alternative data (cash flow, community engagement, training), designed for use by banks to enable fair microcredit access.

Offline Architecture + Simple Language:
Designed for areas with low connectivity and low literacy, making it highly adaptable to digitally excluded contexts.

Circular Reinvestment Model (Social Profit):
100% of profits are reinvested into training, microcredit, and impact scaling. The app also tracks social indicators like empowerment, formalization, and care.

Embedded in a Community-Based Program (Kizomba Empreendedora):
Linked to a program serving over 470 Black women entrepreneurs, enabling real-world testing, community feedback, and collective validation.

Support Module for Gender and Racial Violence (Kemns Acolhe):
Offers direct support and guidance for women facing violence or racism, reinforcing its commitment to dignity, care, and ancestral wellbeing.
Sustainable Change:
Kemns Cash is grounded in a Theory of Change that links digital access, economic justice, Black women’s autonomy, and systemic transformation. Its impact is designed to generate deep, lasting change at multiple levels:

1. Individual Level:
Black women entrepreneurs gain access to an intuitive financial management tool, allowing them to organize, understand, and grow their businesses.

Increases in economic autonomy, digital literacy, and access to fair credit.

2. Community Level:
Strengthening of solidarity networks among Black women entrepreneurs in underserved communities.

Creation of peer-based economic ecosystems grounded in knowledge sharing, mutual support, and conscious consumption.

3. Systemic Level:
Introduction of new solvency metrics into credit scoring models, based on alternative data such as real cash flow, consistency, and community engagement.

Stimulates the development of inclusive financial products tailored to women at the base of the pyramid.

Promotes Afrocentric technology as a legitimate and powerful field of social and economic innovation.

4. Sustainability:
A profit reinvestment model ensures long-term project viability and impact.

Strategic partnerships with fintechs, businesses, and impact funds support scale and financial autonomy.

Mid-to-long-term outcomes:
Reduction in racial and gender inequalities in the digital economy.

Formalization and scaling of thousands of Black women-led businesses.

Integration of Afrocentric social technologies into public policies and financial syste.
Funding Sources: Kemns Cash is a social and financial technology solution developed by the Omolara Institute Brazil. It was designed based on active listening to these women in peripheral territories, taking into account the real barriers they face in their daily lives to maintain financial control of their businesses and personal lives. It is in the ideation phase; we have not yet received any funding for the PMV creation, although it is being built by professionals in the area who are partners of the Omolara Institute.
Further comments/feedback: Objective questionnaire, easy to answer
Primary thematic focus area: MSME Empowerment & Local Digital Innovation
Summary: Kemns Cash is an inclusive, Afro-centric fintech solution designed to empower Black women entrepreneurs in marginalized communities by providing voice-command financial tools and microcredit. Its key strengths lie in its focus on accessibility, financial inclusion, and community reinvestment. However, the lack of funding and a clear path to scalability raises concerns about its long-term viability.

Title: Theorem Network: Empowering Global Financial and Social Inclusion
Subtitle: A super-app, digital identity, and satellite connectivity ecosystem providing microcredits, low-cost remittances, and skill-sharing to empower women, youth, MSMEs, and marginalized communities in the digital economy
Problem Statement: Theorem Network addresses the exclusion of over three billion unbanked and unidentified individuals from the global economy due to barriers like limited digital infrastructure, technological skills, and market access, particularly in rural and marginalized regions. These challenges restrict financial and social inclusion, hindering economic empowerment for women, youth, MSMEs, and marginalized communities
Solution Overview:
How the Solution Works: Theorem Network is an ecosystem promoting financial and social inclusion through a super-app, Digital Identity (DID-KYC) protocol, and satellite connectivity with offline payment capabilities. The super-app offers a digital wallet, social network, time bank for skill exchange, and social calls to action, providing microcredits, low-cost remittances (<1%), crowdfunding, and financial training with user-friendly interfaces (e.g., biometric). The DID-KYC protocol enables verified, reusable digital identities for unbanked populations to access financial services. Satellite connectivity and offline payment protocols ensure continuous access in areas without internet, syncing transactions when connectivity is restored. The CHARIFI micro-lending component offers collateral-free group loans (€10-€1,000, APR 3-8%), with interest reducible through community activities via the time bank.

Methodologies and Technologies Used: The solution leverages blockchain for secure digital identities (DID-KYC), stablecoins ($THEURO, TUSD) for stable transactions, satellite connectivity for offline access, and a mobile platform with biometric interfaces for accessibility. The time bank and social calls to action use gamified incentives to foster community engagement.

Partnerships and Collaboration Models: Theorem Network collaborates with NGOs to localize solutions and distribute social credits, local institutions and states to provide DID-KYC protocols and stablecoins for inclusive regulations, and the UNIDO AIM Global Community for technology transfer and MSME support. The ecosystem is interoperable, allowing integration with other digital platforms for scalability.
Solution Provider(s): commercio.network (Private Sector, Blockchain and Digital Identity Solutions), Namirial (Private Sector, Digital Trust Services and e-Signature Solutions), Altea (Private Sector, IT Consulting and Digital Transformation), Inaz (Private Sector, HR Management and Payroll Software), Zucchetti (Private Sector, Software Solutions for Business and HR Management)
Duration to pilot in a new geography: Based on the implementation plan (CHARIFI pilot in Q4 2025 and Phase 1 launch in 2026), an estimated duration of 6-12 months is reasonable for setting up the super-app, DID-KYC, and offline payment systems in a new region, considering partnerships and localization needs. Further clarification from Theorem Network would confirm this estimate
SDGs addressed: SDG 1 (No Poverty);SDG 8 (Decent Work and Economic Growth);SDG 10 (Reduced Inequalities);
Desired impact:
Solution Objectives: Theorem Network aims to bridge the digital divide for over three billion unbanked and unidentified individuals by providing equitable access to financial services, digital identities, and learning opportunities. It focuses on empowering women, youth, MSMEs, and marginalized communities through microcredits, digital market access, and community-driven initiatives like the time bank and CHARIFI.

Key Achievements or Impacts: The solution targets reaching 500,000 users by 2028 in regions with high financial exclusion (e.g., Sub-Saharan Africa, Southeast Asia). It enables women entrepreneurs to access collateral-free microcredits, supports MSMEs with digital market tools, and includes marginalized communities via monetizable social credits. Quantifiable impacts (e.g., number of loans issued, employment generated) are not yet specified, as the solution is at the MVP stage with a pilot planned for Q4 2025. The CHARIFI model promotes sustainability through low-interest loans (APR 3-8%) and community engagement.
Key technologies:
Blockchain for secure DID-KYC protocols

Stablecoins ($THEURO, TUSD) for stable transactions

Satellite connectivity for offline access

Mobile platform with biometric interfaces for accessibility

Gamified systems for time bank and social calls to action
Unique Characteristics:
Innovative Business Model: CHARIFI’s social micro-lending offers collateral-free loans with interest reducible through community activities, fostering a virtuous cycle of economic and social empowerment.

Technological Breakthroughs: Combines blockchain-based DID-KYC, satellite-enabled offline payments, and a super-app with biometric interfaces to ensure accessibility for low-literacy users.

Community-Driven Approach: The time bank and social calls to action incentivize skill exchange and community participation, unique in fostering solidarity alongside financial inclusion.

Interoperability and Scalability: Modular components (super-app, DID-KYC, CHARIFI) are adaptable to local contexts via territorial tokens (ART) and interoperable with other platforms.
Sustainable Change:
Theorem Network’s Theory of Change posits that providing accessible digital tools (super-app, DID-KYC, offline payments) and community-driven incentives (CHARIFI, time bank) will empower unbanked populations, particularly women, youth, and MSMEs, to participate in the digital economy. This leads to:

Economic Empowerment: Microcredits and digital market access increase income and job opportunities, reducing poverty (SDG 1).

Social Inclusion: Digital identities and community activities reduce inequalities (SDG 10) and foster gender equality (SDG 5).

Capacity Building: Financial and digital training programs enhance skills (SDG 4), enabling sustainable entrepreneurship.

Systemic Resilience: Satellite connectivity and stablecoins ensure continuity in crises, while partnerships with NGOs and institutions localize and scale impact. The non-profit CHARIFI model and transparent governance ensure long-term sustainability, creating a replicable framework for global digital inclusion.
Funding Sources: Private Contributors
Testimonials and Endorsements: Not defined at the moment
Further comments/feedback:
The questionnaire for the Global Call for Solutions for an Inclusive Digital Economy is well-designed, providing a robust framework to evaluate solutions aimed at promoting inclusive digital economies. Its structured format effectively captures essential aspects such as the problem statement, solution mechanics, technological innovations, and alignment with global objectives like the Sustainable Development Goals (SDGs) and the Global Digital Compact. The clear delineation of thematic focus areas and detailed requirements for scalability, partnerships, and impact helps ensure comprehensive submissions. However, to further improve the submission experience, particularly for solutions at early stages like Theorem Network’s MVP, the following suggestions are offered:

Flexibility for Early-Stage Solutions: For solutions at the MVP or pilot-ready stage, some sections, such as specific implementation locations and timelines, may be challenging to complete with precision. Including options to indicate "planned" or "to be determined" locations/timelines would better accommodate projects still in development.
Testimonial and Endorsement Guidance: Requesting testimonials can be difficult for pre-pilot solutions where stakeholder feedback may not yet be formalized. Providing guidance to submit preliminary endorsements, such as expressions of interest from potential partners or communities, could make this section more accessible.
Partner Specification: The requirement to list detailed partner profiles and sectors may be restrictive when partnerships are still being formalized. Allowing submitters to note "partnerships in negotiation" or to update partner details post-submission could streamline the process.
Character Limits and Clarity: While character limits for the title and subtitle are clear, additional guidance on balancing brevity with descriptive content could help submitters craft impactful responses without sacrificing detail.

Theorem Network values the opportunity to participate in this initiative and believes the questionnaire effectively supports the goal of identifying innovative solutions for global digital inclusion. Incorporating more flexibility for early-stage projects would further enhance its inclusivity and accessibility for emerging solutions.
Primary thematic focus area: MSME Empowerment & Local Digital Innovation
Summary: Theorem Network is an emerging global ecosystem designed to promote financial and social inclusion for unbanked and marginalized populations. Its super-app integrates digital wallets, microcredits, low-cost remittances, crowdfunding, and community skill-sharing features. Core innovations include blockchain-based reusable digital identities (DID-KYC), satellite-enabled offline payments, and the CHARIFI micro-lending model, which reduces interest rates through community activities. With pilot implementation planned for late 2025, the solution aims to reach 500,000 users by 2028, empowering women, youth, MSMEs, and marginalized groups worldwide.

Title: SMART FARMS AQUAPONICS, cultivate anywhere
Subtitle: SMART FARMS AQUAPONICS: Producing fish and vegetables in the city thanks to sustainable, innovative and climate-friendly technology.
Solution Overview:
1. Detailed description of the solution’s operation

SMART FARMS AQUAPONICS is an intelligent aquaponic farm that combines fish farming (mainly tilapia) and the cultivation of vegetables (tomatoes, salads...) in a closed cycle.

-Fish waste is transformed into nutrients by nitrifying bacteria, used directly by plants.
-The plants purify the water before it returns to the fish ponds.
-This cycle significantly reduces water use and eliminates the use of chemical fertilizers and pesticides.
-A mobile application allows real-time monitoring of parameters (water quality, fish growth, crop condition) and sends alerts for optimal management.

2. Methodologies and technologies used

-Aquaponics above ground for sustainable and urban production.
-IoT sensors to measure pH, temperature, water level and dissolved oxygen.
-Mobile application as a management and monitoring tool accessible to producers.
-Modular and movable model for flexible installation in different contexts (urban, school, community).

3. Partnerships and collaborative models (forecasting)

We do not yet have formal partnerships. However, we plan to develop strategic collaborations with:

Public institutions (Ministry of Agriculture, municipalities) for regulatory and logistical support.
-Schools and training centers to integrate aquaponics into education and train young people.
-Associations of women and young people to strengthen socio-economic inclusion.
-Local energy and IoT startups to support technology integration.
Solution Provider(s): SMART FARMS AQUAPONICS does not yet have official partners.
Implementation location(s): Our SMART FARMS AQUAPONICS project was installed in Côte d'Ivoire in Abidjan in the commune of Port-Bouët, where we have already produced tilapia and salad that we have marketed, thus validating the feasibility of the system.
Implementation timeline(s): Duration of the first phase: Start: February 15, 2023 End: February 15, 2024. This first phase allowed to install the system in Port-Bouët, Abidjan, and to produce tilapia and salads, validating the feasibility of our solution. The following phases will aim at extension and deployment on a larger scale.
Duration to pilot in a new geography: We estimate that a pilot phase in a new geographical area can be implemented over a period of 12 months.  This duration includes: 3 months for the installation of the system and the initial training of beneficiaries, 6 months for pilot operation and production monitoring (fish and vegetables), 3 months for the evaluation of results, the optimization of the system and the preparation for a possible extension.
SDGs addressed: SDG 9 (Industry, Innovation, and Infrastructure);SDG 13 (Climate Action);SDG 2 (Zero Hunger);
Desired impact:
Objectives of the solution:

-Ensure sustainable food security through local production of fresh fish and vegetables.
-Reduce dependence on imports and stabilize food prices.
-Promote smart and climate-friendly urban agriculture.
-Create green jobs and promote the socio-economic integration of young people and women.

Main expected impacts:

-Estimated annual production: up to 1.5 tons of tilapia and 3 tons of vegetables per deployed aquaponic unit.
-Reduction of up to 80% in water consumption compared to conventional agriculture.
-Elimination of the use of chemical fertilizers as a direct contribution to reducing GHG emissions and preserving soils.
-Creation of 5 to 10 direct and indirect jobs per installation (installation, technical monitoring, marketing).
-Contribution to urban resilience and social inclusion by making healthy and affordable food accessible.
Key technologies:
Key technologies used:

-Intelligent aquaponics: integration of closed systems combining aquaculture (fish) and hydroponics (market gardening).
-IoT (Internet of Things): sensors for real-time monitoring of water quality, temperature, pH and plant growth.
-Mobile application: user interface for data monitoring, alert in case of anomalies, and operator training.
Unique Characteristics:
Unique/differentiated features of the solution:
SMART FARMS AQUAPONICS innovates with a circular production model combining aquaculture and soilless market garden crops in a closed system, saving water and without chemicals.
Technologically, the solution integrates IoT sensors for monitoring water quality and growth, as well as a mobile application for real-time management, training, and digital inclusion of operators.
Regarding financing mechanisms, we adopt a hybrid approach based on the sale and installation of modular aquaponics systems, paid training for young and female entrepreneurs, as well as strategic partnerships with public and private institutions, ensuring both the accessibility and economic sustainability of the model.

This unique combination of advanced technology, environmental sustainability and inclusive business model aligns our solution with:

-SDG 2 (Zero Hunger): access to healthy and affordable food;
-SDG 9 (Industry, innovation and infrastructure): development of modern digital and agricultural infrastructures;
-SDG 13 (Climate action): contribution to a resilient and low carbon agriculture.
Sustainable Change: SMART FARMS AQUAPONICS creates sustainable change by combining local food production, digital innovation and climate-friendly practices. IoT sensors and the mobile application allow operators to acquire digital skills and manage production efficiently. The modular and replicable model promotes social inclusion, job creation, and urban resilience, generating a sustainable systemic impact aligned with SDGs 2, 9, and 13.
Funding Sources: AGRI GREEN GIRL benefited from support from MTN Côte d'Ivoire, which allowed to finance and develop a functional prototype of our aquaponic solution. This support made possible the first successful test, with lettuce cultivation and fish farming, thus confirming the technical and commercial viability of our system. Logistically, we have installed all the necessary infrastructure, including tanks for aquaculture and culture bins for plants, ensuring efficient implementation of the prototype.
Testimonials and Endorsements:
We had the opportunity to receive the first fish and lettuces produced by SMART FARMS AQUAPONICS. This initiative clearly demonstrates the viability and potential of their aquaponic system to provide quality fresh products.
Source: MTN Ivory Coast
Further comments/feedback: The questionnaire is clear and well structured, allowing for an efficient presentation of the technical, social and environmental aspects of the project. We particularly appreciate the focus on innovation, sustainability and inclusion, which are at the heart of SMART FARMS AQUAPONICS. We hope that this approach will make it possible to highlight concrete and replicable solutions to meet the food and climate challenges in Ivory Coast and in Africa.
Primary thematic focus area: Stable and Resilient Digital Supply Chains
Summary: SMART FARMS AQUAPONICS introduces intelligent aquaponic systems in Côte d'Ivoire to produce fish (tilapia) and vegetables in a sustainable, climate-friendly way. By integrating aquaculture and hydroponics in closed cycles, the system reduces water use by up to 80%, eliminates chemical fertilizers, and leverages IoT sensors with a mobile app for real-time monitoring. The modular design allows deployment in urban and peri-urban settings, creating green jobs and contributing to food security, climate resilience, and digital inclusion.

Title: MirrorHR, an epilepsy research kit
Subtitle: A free and co-designed application that help families manage epilepsy
Problem Statement: Epilepsy research is fragmented and hospitals and physicians are limited by the care often provided in silos and the lack of unified access needed for analysis and trending of large scale data. Each patient is unique and families are often forced to choose between conventional treatment pathways that are widely accepted but may not necessarily respond better to the patient's needs, compared to taking high risks with untested studies and ideas that might work better.
Solution Overview: MirrorHR is a mobile app connected to a wearable device that sends alerts when anomalous activity might indicate a seizure, so caregivers no longer have to hover over their son. It helps allay the biggest fear that a seizure could lead to what is called SUDEP, or sudden unexpected death in epilepsy.
Solution Provider(s): Fightthestroke Foundation, FTS srl, Microsoft Garage, PBSF
SDGs addressed: SDG 3 (Good Health and Well-being);SDG 10 (Reduced Inequalities);SDG 11 (Sustainable Cities and Communities);
Desired impact: Limit racing in the emergency rooms and help to control trigger factors for epilepsy
Key technologies: AI
Unique Characteristics: Co-developed with end users, now distributed globally for free, unique devices that help owning back own data and reduce frequency and intensity of seizures.
Sustainable Change: If a seizure is about to happen, parents can catch it at the onset and take immediate actions, such as preventing falls or other trauma and making sure the child doesn’t swallow vomit. It means there’s less likelihood the parents will have to rush to the emergency room or miss the seizure entirely. The biometric data and daily videologs are stored in a Microsoft Azure-powered FHIR Server. Machine learning and data visualization techniques are applied to this information to offer parents and doctors easy-to-read visuals and insights using Power BI tools.
Funding Sources: Fundad by Fightthestroke Foundation
Testimonials and Endorsements: https://www.fightthestroke.org/mirrorhr-eng
Primary thematic focus area: Innovation Acceleration & Knowledge Sharing
Summary: MirrorHR is a mobile app and wearable solution co-designed with families to support epilepsy management and research. It provides real-time seizure alerts, data logging, and analysis to reduce risks (e.g., SUDEP), ease caregiver burden, and support physicians with unified datasets. Strengths include a strong user-centered approach, global distribution (free), and integration with Microsoft Azure and Power BI for health data insights. Weaknesses include limited detail on clinical validation, sustainability of free distribution, and scalability strategy for new geographies.

Title: Smart and inclusive transport by mobile application
Subtitle: A multi-service digital platform for urban transportation, delivery, and youth employment via a membership system
Problem Statement:
Problem Statement
African populations, especially youth and women, face limited access to digital mobility services, high unemployment, road insecurity, and a lack of inclusive economic opportunities. The informal transport sector remains largely unregulated, inefficient, and prone to corruption.
Solution Overview:
Auto Express is a multifunctional mobile application offering:

On-demand transportation services (taxis, motorcycles, carpooling),

Delivery services (documents, parcels, food),
