Name of your organization: Ministry of Production, Foreign Trade, Investment and Fisheries
Title: Conecta Territorios: Digital Inclusion for Local Entrepreneurs
Subtitle: Empowering small businesses with digital tools, training, and e-commerce to bridge territorial gaps and boost competitiveness in underserved regions.
Problem Statement: Many rural and underserved territories face persistent barriers to economic inclusion, such as lack of access to digital tools, business training, formal markets, and up-to-date records of local economic actors. Micro and small enterprises—especially those led by women and youth—often operate informally, remain disconnected from national value chains, and lack visibility to potential customers and support services. These challenges limit their productivity, scalability, and resilience. Public institutions also face difficulties in identifying and supporting these actors effectively due to fragmented or outdated data.
Solution Overview:
How the solution works:
Conecta Territorios is a digital geoportal developed by Ecuador’s Ministry of Production, Foreign Trade, Investment and Fisheries to foster inclusive economic development. Its “Capacity-Building Module” enables entrepreneurs—especially from rural and underserved territories—to register their businesses, geolocate their economic activity, upload product photos, and provide key business information. Upon administrator validation, users gain access to tailored online training in areas such as digital marketing, financial management, and e-commerce readiness. The system is designed to eventually integrate a payment gateway, enabling direct transactions and product visibility across regions.

Methodologies and technologies used:
The platform is built using R + Shiny for rapid web development and modular design. It integrates interactive maps via Leaflet, form validation with shinyFeedback, and stores all business data in a cloud-based PostgreSQL database via Supabase. All user inputs—business profile, coordinates, and products—are validated and stored securely, with future scalability supported through Docker containers and potential deployment in public cloud or institutional servers.

Partnerships and collaboration models:
The initiative is led by the Territorial Competitiveness Directorate in collaboration with local governments in pilot cantons. It has engaged entrepreneurs, youth organizations, and technical teams in co-design and testing. The project is structured to integrate with broader national strategies for digital transformation and public-private collaboration, and is open to scaling through international cooperation and institutional partnerships.
Solution Provider(s): Ministry of Production, Foreign Trade, Investment and Fisheries of Ecuador (MPCEIP) – Government institution responsible for promoting productive development, investment, and trade. Leads national policies on industrial competitiveness and digital inclusion. Public sector / Economic development / Digital transformation.  Territorial Competitiveness Directorate (DCT) – Technical unit within MPCEIP focused on regional competitiveness, data-driven policy, and inclusion of underserved territories. Public sector / Territorial development / Digital ecosystems.  Local Governments of Pilot Cantons (e.g., Alausí, Guamote, Chunchi) – Municipal actors that facilitate user engagement and promote local economic participation. Local government / Community engagement / MSME promotion.
Duration to pilot in a new geography: The estimated duration to pilot the solution in a new geography is approximately 8 to 12 weeks. This includes stakeholder alignment, localization of content, infrastructure setup, user onboarding, and training. The timeline can be shortened with strong institutional support and existing digital infrastructure.
SDGs addressed: SDG 1 (No Poverty);SDG 8 (Decent Work and Economic Growth);SDG 11 (Sustainable Cities and Communities);
Desired impact:
Solution Objectives:
- Promote digital inclusion among micro and small enterprises (MSMEs), especially in rural and underserved territories.
- Facilitate access to business training, market visibility, and formalization tools through an integrated digital platform.
- Strengthen public-sector capacity to identify, support, and connect local economic actors.
- Enable future integration of payment systems and data-driven value chain analysis.

Key Achievements / Impacts:
- Over 150 businesses registered and geolocated in the first pilot phase (2025).
- 70% of registered users completed full business profiles, including photos and sector data.
- Developed a cloud-based, scalable system accessible by public institutions and local governments.
- Created the foundation for employment generation by connecting producers to wider markets.
-Enabled policy targeting by providing updated, georeferenced data on MSMEs in vulnerable cantons.

Future phases aim to integrate e-commerce and expand nationwide, potentially reaching 5,000 MSMEs by 2026.
Key technologies:
The solution leverages a set of open-source and cloud-based technologies designed for modularity, scalability, and accessibility:
- R + Shiny: Used for building the web interface and server logic, enabling rapid development and deployment of interactive applications.
- PostgreSQL (via Supabase): A cloud-hosted relational database used to store business data, product details, and geolocation coordinates in real time.
- Leaflet + leaflet.extras2: For interactive geospatial mapping and location capture of registered businesses.
- ShinyFeedback + shinyjs: For front-end validation and enhanced user experience in dynamic forms.
- Docker (planned): To enable scalable deployment across servers or public cloud environments.
- (Upcoming) Payment Gateway Integration: The system is designed to integrate third-party payment platforms to facilitate e-commerce functionalities.

While the current phase does not include advanced technologies like AI or blockchain, the modular design allows for future integration of AI-powered recommendations, market analytics, or supply chain optimization tools.
Unique Characteristics:
- Territorial focus with geospatial intelligence: Unlike most platforms, this solution is grounded in territorial competitiveness data and geolocation. It allows for spatial targeting of MSMEs in structurally excluded regions, enabling place-based policy and investment strategies.
- Integrated ecosystem approach: The platform goes beyond registration. It connects business profiling, interactive mapping, digital training, and (soon) e-commerce capabilities in a single modular system.
- Public sector–driven with scalability: Led by a national government institution, the solution is designed for public use, scalability, and sustainability. It can be replicated by other ministries, local governments, or international cooperation actors.
- Low-cost, open-source architecture: Built using open-source tools (R, Shiny, PostgreSQL), it offers a cost-effective and adaptable model for countries with limited digital infrastructure.
- Validated access to training and financing: By including administrator-level validation, it ensures that only verified businesses gain access to targeted training modules—strengthening accountability and impact tracking.
- Future-ready design: The platform is ready to integrate payment systems and AI-based market tools, making it flexible for evolving digital ecosystems.
Sustainable Change:
The solution addresses structural barriers to economic inclusion by enabling micro and small businesses, especially in rural and underserved areas, to be visible, validated, and connected to digital markets and training systems. By digitizing the business ecosystem at the local level and linking it to national support tools, the platform creates a foundation for long-term systemic transformation.

Inputs:
- Public sector leadership and digital infrastructure
- Open-source, modular technologies
- Territorial competitiveness data
- Collaboration with local governments and stakeholders

Activities:
- Business registration with geolocation and product visibility
- Administrator-led validation process
- Access to tailored digital training and (future) e-commerce
- Use of data for public policy targeting and investment attraction

Outputs:
- Structured, real-time registry of local businesses
- Greater access to digital tools and entrepreneurial knowledge
- Strengthened linkages between local producers and markets
- Data-enabled policy design and program evaluation

Outcomes:
- Increased digital and economic inclusion of vulnerable groups
- Improved productivity and sustainability of local businesses
- Replicable governance model for territorial digital inclusion

Impact (Long-term):
- Systemic reduction of territorial economic gaps
- Increased resilience and competitiveness of rural MSMEs
- Institutionalization of digital tools for inclusive development policy
Funding Sources: The solution has been fully funded through public investment by the Government of Ecuador, specifically by the Ministry of Production, Foreign Trade, Investment and Fisheries (MPCEIP). Funding was allocated from the national budget under strategic initiatives for territorial competitiveness and digital transformation. The project has not yet received external or private funding but is structured to allow for international cooperation, donor support, and multilateral partnerships in future scaling phases.
Testimonials and Endorsements: In 2025, the solution was awarded the Digital and Logistics Innovation Prize by the Logistics Association of Ecuador (Asociación Logística del Ecuador - ALE), recognizing it as one of the most impactful digital initiatives for strengthening local production systems and improving connectivity between small producers and broader markets.
Primary thematic focus area: MSME Empowerment & Local Digital Innovation
Summary: Conecta Territorios is a government-led geoportal in Ecuador enabling MSMEs to register, geolocate, and access training, with future integration of e-commerce. Its strengths are strong public-sector leadership, territorial focus, and early traction with 150+ businesses; weaknesses include prototype maturity and lack of private/external funding.

Title: Rural Roots, Future Coders & Creators: Girls' Tech Connect
Subtitle: Bridging the rural digital divide by providing foundational digital literacy, coding skills, and an entrepreneurial mindset for future-ready careers and innovation to girls in remote communities.
Problem Statement: Girls in rural areas frequently experience severe digital exclusion due to limited internet access, lack of tech education infrastructure, and socio-economic barriers. This denies them crucial digital literacy and entrepreneurial opportunities, perpetuating inequality and limiting their potential contributions to the inclusive digital economy.
Solution Overview:
Rural Roots, Future Coders & Creators: Girls' Tech Connect is a comprehensive, multi-phase digital empowerment program designed to equip adolescent girls in underserved rural communities with essential digital literacy, coding proficiency, and an entrepreneurial mindset. The solution works through a blended learning approach, combining localized physical hubs with accessible digital content, mentorship, and practical project-based learning.


1. Community Tech Hub Establishment: In selected rural communities, we will establish dedicated "Tech Connect Hubs." These hubs will serve as physical learning spaces, providing reliable internet access, charging stations for devices, and a safe, conducive environment for learning. Each hub will be equipped with refurbished or new laptops/tablets.

2. Foundational Digital Literacy: The program begins with foundational digital literacy modules. Girls will learn internet navigation, safe online practices, basic computer operations, word processing, and digital communication tools (e.g., email, online collaboration platforms). This phase ensures all participants have a solid groundwork.

3. Introduction to Coding & Computational Thinking: Building on digital literacy, girls will be introduced to computational thinking and visual programming languages. This will progress to foundational skills in text-based languages such as Python for web development basics using simplified, project-based curricula.

4. Entrepreneurial Skill Development: Integrated into the tech training are modules focused on entrepreneurial thinking. Girls will learn problem-solving, design thinking, basic business concepts, digital marketing for small businesses, and how to identify and leverage digital tools for income generation within their communities

5. Mentorship and Role Models: A crucial component is the establishment of a robust mentorship program. Experienced female tech professionals (from NezaTech's network and partners) will provide virtual and, where possible, in-person mentorship.

6. Project-Based Learning & Showcasing: Learning will be highly practical. Girls will work on real-world projects relevant to their communities (e.g., creating a simple website for a local business, developing a digital solution for a community challenge).

7. Pathways to Further Opportunities: The program aims to create pathways for advanced learning and economic opportunities. 


B. Methodologies:

1. Blended Learning Methodology

2. Project-Based Learning (PBL)

3. Gamification

4. Community-Led Approach


C. Technologies:

1. Connectivity: Satellite internet solutions (e.g., Starlink, local providers' solutions) complemented by mobile hotspots.

2. Hardware: Low-cost, durable laptops or tablets (e.g., refurbished devices).

3. Software/Platforms:

- Learning Management System (LMS)

- Coding Environments: Scratch (for beginners) and web development tools (HTML, CSS editors).

- Productivity Tools: For word processing and spreadsheets and more

- Communication: Secure messaging apps and video conferencing tools for mentorship and collaboration.

- Content Development: Locally relevant digital curricula, developed in collaboration with subject matter experts


D. Partnerships and Collaboration Models:

1. Local Community Leaders & Organizations:

2. Telecommunication Companies/ISPs:
Role: Provision of discounted or pro-bono internet connectivity

Model: Corporate Social Responsibility (CSR) partnerships, joint ventures for rural connectivity expansion.

3. Hardware Manufacturers/Distributors & Tech Companies:
Role: Donation or subsidized provision of computing devices (laptops, tablets), technical support, software licenses, and employee volunteering for mentorship.

4. Individual Volunteers, Educators & Mentors:

5. Government Agencies (Local, Regional, National):
Role: Policy support, regulatory alignment, potential co-funding, recognition of program certifications, and integration into national digital literacy strategies.
Solution Provider(s): NezaTech Africa (Social Enterprise; Education Technology (EdTech), Digital Skills Development), Telecommunications company (not gotten yet), Hardware Manufacturers (not gotten yet)
Duration to pilot in a new geography: 3 - 6 months
SDGs addressed: SDG 4 (Quality Education);SDG 5 (Gender Equality);SDG 8 (Decent Work and Economic Growth);
Desired impact:
Desired Impact: To transform rural communities by empowering adolescent girls with the digital skills and entrepreneurial mindset necessary to thrive in and contribute to Nigeria's inclusive digital economy, closing the digital gender gap.

Solution Objectives & Key Impacts (Estimated 3 Year Target):

1. Digital Empowerment: Directly train over 50,000 rural girls aged 10-18 in foundational digital literacy, coding, and computational thinking.

2. Access & Infrastructure: Establish 50 Community Tech Hubs across underserved rural regions, providing reliable internet access to over 250,000 community members (including program participants).

3. Skill Proficiency: Achieve an 85% completion rate for digital literacy modules and a 70% proficiency rate in basic coding skills among participants.

4. Entrepreneurial Innovation: Enable at least 15% of participants (approx. 7,500 girls) to develop and showcase digital projects or initiate small, digitally-enabled entrepreneurial ventures.

5. Economic Opportunity: Facilitate pathways to further education or income generation for 20% of graduates, fostering over 10,000 new digital livelihood opportunities indirectly.

6. Digital Inclusion: Reduce digital exclusion by 30% in target communities, evidenced by increased digital service adoption and participation.
Key technologies:
The key technologies underpinning the "Rural Roots, Future Coders & Creators: Girls' Tech Connect" solution are:

1. Diverse Connectivity Solutions: Utilizing a mix of satellite internet (e.g., Starlink) and mobile hotspots to ensure reliable internet access in remote community hubs.

2. Accessible Hardware: Deployment of low-cost, durable devices, including refurbished laptops and tablets, to bridge the equipment gap.

3. Blended Learning Platforms: Implementation of Learning Management Systems (LMS) for structured content delivery, combined with visual (e.g., Scratch) and text-based (e.g., HTML, CSS editors) coding environments for practical skill development.

4. Productivity & Communication Tools: Standard software for word processing and spreadsheets, alongside secure messaging and video conferencing for collaboration and mentorship.
Unique Characteristics:
Unique/Differentiated Characteristics:

1. Integrated Rural Hubs & Blended Learning: Combines dedicated physical tech hubs in underserved rural communities with a tailored blended learning model, directly tackling access and infrastructure barriers unique to remote areas.

2. Entrepreneurial Skills for Local Impact: Goes beyond basic digital literacy and coding to embed practical entrepreneurial thinking, empowering girls to identify and create digital solutions for their own community challenges and generate local income.

3. Community-Led & Multi-Stakeholder Partnership Model: Driven by deep local community engagement and formalized partnerships with telecom companies, hardware providers, and government agencies to ensure sustainable connectivity, resource provision, and policy integration.

4. Targeted Female Mentorship: Leverages a robust network of female tech professionals to provide crucial role models and direct guidance, inspiring and retaining adolescent girls in tech pathways.
Sustainable Change:
Rural Roots, Future Coders & Creators: Girls' Tech Connect creates sustainable, systemic change by:

1. Building Local Capacity & Infrastructure:

Theory of Change: Establishing community-owned Tech Hubs provides permanent, accessible digital infrastructure. This transforms communities into self-sustaining centers for ongoing digital learning, internet access, and innovation, beyond the initial program cohort.

2. Fostering a Self-Reinforcing Ecosystem:

Theory of Change: Empowered girls become digital ambassadors and entrepreneurs, inspiring peers, creating local digital solutions, and generating economic activity. This cultivates a new generation of female tech leaders who can mentor others, ensuring continued skill development and digital adoption within their communities.

3. Catalyzing Broader Digital Inclusion & Economic Growth:

Theory of Change: By demonstrating the tangible benefits of digital skills (e.g., through project-based learning and entrepreneurial ventures), the solution drives wider community engagement and investment in digital literacy. This leads to increased local digital service utilization, new micro-businesses, and ultimately, a more robust and inclusive rural digital economy.

Partnerships (In-kind & Financial)

Philanthropic Donations: From individual major donors and crowdfunding campaigns.

Summary: Girls' Tech Connect is a concept-stage program aiming to bridge the rural digital divide by equipping adolescent girls in underserved Nigerian communities with foundational digital literacy, coding skills, and entrepreneurial mindsets. The model combines community-based tech hubs, blended learning, mentorship from female tech professionals, and project-based activities to foster digital inclusion, entrepreneurship, and long-term socio-economic empowerment.

Title: Sebaga Africa
Subtitle: Taking Africa to the World
Problem Statement: Sebaga Africa addresses the challenge of limited market access and visibility for African artisans and small-scale producers, particularly women and youth. Despite the richness of African culture and the uniqueness of its handmade products, many artisans struggle to reach broader markets due to inadequate digital infrastructure, lack of e-commerce skills, and limited logistical support. This results in low income, underutilized talent, and loss of cultural heritage. Additionally, consumers—both local and international—often face difficulties accessing authentic, ethically sourced African goods in a centralized and trustworthy platform. Sebaga Africa bridges this gap by offering a curated digital marketplace that connects artisans directly with buyers, enabling them to showcase and sell their products globally. Through integrated logistics, capacity building, and digital tools, we empower producers to grow sustainable businesses while preserving Africa’s rich cultural identity.
Solution Overview:
Sebaga Africa is a digital marketplace that connects African artisans, creatives, and small-scale producers to global and local consumers. Our platform provides an inclusive e-commerce solution tailored to amplify African-made products while empowering underserved producers—particularly women and youth.

How the Solution Works:
Producers register on the Sebaga Africa platform and create digital storefronts to showcase their products. Each product listing includes detailed descriptions, images, pricing, and origin stories, helping to preserve the cultural context. Customers browse, place orders, and pay securely through the platform. Sebaga Africa facilitates the end-to-end process, including order tracking and delivery logistics.

Technologies Used:
We utilize a mobile-responsive web platform built on open-source technologies such as Laravel and the Farmart framework. Our backend integrates secure payment gateways and inventory management systems. We are working towards integrating AI-powered tools for product recommendations and automated translations to enhance accessibility and global appeal.

Methodologies:
Our approach centers around human-centered design, ensuring the platform is intuitive for low-digital-literacy users. We conduct regular feedback loops with vendors and buyers to optimize functionality. Additionally, we offer onboarding and capacity-building workshops to help vendors with product photography, pricing strategies, and digital marketing.

Partnerships and Collaboration Models:
Sebaga Africa collaborates with local artisans’ cooperatives, creative hubs, and NGOs to identify and onboard talent. We partner with logistics providers for efficient delivery and with financial institutions to support vendor payments and financial literacy. Our ecosystem model also involves collaboration with government agencies and development partners to expand digital access and promote inclusive trade policies.

By combining technology with empowerment and local partnerships, Sebaga Africa offers a sustainable, scalable model for boosting Africa’s creative economy and bridging the digital trade divide.
Solution Provider(s): a
Duration to pilot in a new geography: a
SDGs addressed: SDG 17 (Partnerships for the Goals);SDG 9 (Industry, Innovation, and Infrastructure);SDG 8 (Decent Work and Economic Growth);
Desired impact:
Solution Objectives:

-To provide market access and digital visibility for African artisans, especially women and youth.

-To promote the preservation and global appreciation of African cultural heritage through commerce.

-To generate sustainable income and employment for small-scale producers.

-To bridge the digital divide by equipping artisans with e-commerce and digital skills.

-To create a centralized, trustworthy platform for sourcing authentic African-made products.

Key Achievements & Impacts:

-Employment Generation: Sebaga Africa has onboarded artisans and small businesses across Botswana and Africa, with 70% being women and youth-led.

Digital Empowerment: Through our training programs, over 100 vendors have been trained in basic digital literacy, online selling, and branding.

Market Access: Products listed on Sebaga Africa have reached customers in five countries through pilot sales, increasing average artisan income by up to 40% during peak periods.

Cultural Promotion: The platform showcases over 100 unique handmade products that reflect diverse African traditions and craftsmanship.

Sustainability Goals: By promoting handmade, locally sourced, and low-carbon products, Sebaga Africa supports climate-conscious consumer behavior and circular economy principles.

Community Impact: Through partnerships with cooperatives and NGOs, we have facilitated group income-generating projects and expanded artisan networks.

Overall, Sebaga Africa aims to scale this impact across the continent, contributing to inclusive economic growth, job creation, and digital transformation within the creative and cultural sectors.
Key technologies:
Sebaga Africa leverages a range of digital technologies to deliver an inclusive and scalable e-commerce solution tailored for African artisans and producers. Below is an overview of the core technologies used:

E-Commerce Platform (Web & Mobile):
Built on the Laravel PHP framework and the Farmart e-commerce template, our platform is mobile-responsive, ensuring accessibility for users with smartphones. It supports multi-vendor functionality, enabling individual producers to manage their digital storefronts.

Secure Payment Integration:
We use secure, locally-adapted payment gateways that support mobile money, bank transfers, and card payments to facilitate inclusive transactions across diverse user bases.

Cloud Hosting & Content Delivery:
Our solution is hosted on scalable cloud infrastructure, ensuring fast loading times, reliability, and global reach. Content Delivery Networks (CDNs) help deliver product images and media efficiently.

AI-Driven Features (Upcoming):
We are working on integrating AI-powered tools to support personalized product recommendations, automated translations for wider accessibility, and inventory management support for vendors.

Data Analytics:
We utilize analytics tools to monitor user behavior, sales trends, and vendor performance. These insights are used to improve customer experience, optimize marketing strategies, and support vendor training.

Logistics and Order Tracking Integrations:
Partnerships with local logistics providers enable integrated order tracking systems and automated notifications for both vendors and buyers.

Digital Training Tools:
We use cloud-based platforms such as Google Workspace and Canva for virtual vendor training, onboarding, and content creation.

By combining these technologies, Sebaga Africa offers a holistic, user-friendly solution that drives economic empowerment, cultural visibility, and digital inclusion across the continent.
Unique Characteristics:
Sebaga Africa stands out through a combination of inclusive design, community-centered partnerships, and tailored technological integration. Key differentiators include:

Culturally Rooted Digital Marketplace:
Unlike generic e-commerce platforms, Sebaga Africa is curated specifically for African-made products, placing cultural identity, storytelling, and authenticity at the core of the shopping experience. Each product is accompanied by its origin story, preserving and promoting African heritage.

Inclusive Business Model:
Our platform prioritizes underrepresented groups—especially women and youth—through targeted onboarding, mentorship, and revenue-sharing models that ensure artisans benefit fairly from sales. We also offer vendor-friendly terms, such as zero setup fees and flexible commission structures.

Tech Accessibility for Low-Digital-Literacy Users:
The platform is designed with a simple user interface and mobile-first approach, making it accessible even to users with basic digital skills. We also provide capacity-building workshops and one-on-one digital support.

Integrated Ecosystem Approach:
Sebaga Africa doesn’t operate in isolation. We work closely with artisan cooperatives, NGOs, logistics providers, and development partners to create an ecosystem that supports artisans from production to packaging, marketing, and distribution.

Scalable and Modular Tech Infrastructure:
The use of open-source frameworks allows for cost-effective scalability. Our planned integration of AI for personalized shopping, translation, and smart inventory management will further optimize both vendor and customer experience.

Sustainable and Ethical Commerce Focus:
We promote eco-conscious and ethically sourced products, supporting a circular economy and sustainable production practices.

Impact-Driven Financing Models:
We are exploring partnerships with microfinance institutions and social impact investors to provide artisans with working capital and business development support.

Together, these elements make Sebaga Africa not just a marketplace, but a digital empowerment engine for Africa’s creative economy.

Sebaga Africa is designed to catalyze long-term, systemic change by transforming how African artisans and small-scale producers access markets, generate income, and participate in the digital economy.

Long-term Impact:

Sebaga Africa’s theory of change ultimately supports equitable growth, cultural sustainability, and long-term resilience of local creative economies.

Title: AKABOXI
Subtitle: Akaboxi provides rural communities organized in Village Savings and Loan Association groups with a robust and secure way of handling savings from agricultural proceeds at every stage of the agricultural value chain, savings money kept in boxes, to be managed and monitored by use of a Digitized Financial Inclusion system (Akaboxitech system). A new technology that replaces the rudimentary way of keeping money in boxes and in people’s homes to a more secure, reliable and easy to monitor savings and transactions. The solution enables the financially excluded vulnerable poor access finance from formal financial institutions. The system credit scores each individual member in the group and enables the group to open an account in a formal financial institution within their reach. Akaboxi provides a holistic package access to ready markets, closing the financial gap, trainings) to small holder farmers aimed at increased productivity, increased savings hence improved livelihoods.
Problem Statement: Smallholder farmers in rural communities face challenges of access to finance their small agricultural projects. As a result, they organize themselves informally in Village Savings and Loan Association groups (VSLAs). They hold savings and credit meetings every week in groups of 30 people on average, where each person saves as little as $0.30, kept in metallic boxes and usually held by VSLA leaders for safekeeping. These vulnerable groups face challenges such as low savings, monetary theft and insecurity, improper record keeping, and lack of awareness as a result of high illiteracy levels. Another common issue is that a farmer’s financial records can be altered by others, affecting the accuracy and security of financial information for smallholder farmers.
Solution Overview:
KABOXI is a digital financial inclusion system that enables smallholder farmers in rural communities to manage and monitor their financial savings together. It provides communities with a robust and secure way of handling savings using a digitalized financial inclusion system, which is an easier, more reliable way to monitor savings and transactions. AKABOXI digitally manages the financial records of these smallholder farmers, fills their financial gap, and helps engage partners to provide cheap and affordable agricultural inputs, access to ready market links, and low insurance premiums.
kaboxi assigns every individual member in the group with Identity Cards (ID) for clear identification capturing the necessary demographic information about each member. This ID card embedded with Near Field Communication (NFC) technology which is used for identification of each member in the specific group which is also used for transactions either during saving and borrowing of money. The system is linked to each member's mobile money wallet which they can use to withdraw money from any mobile money outlet in their location. Akaboxi improves security for women savings, monitors transactions and saves time. A receipt is issued out for every transaction that the farmer makes. These transactions include depositing money, account balances for each individual saver, outstanding loan balances and the system sends messages to everyone who owns any kind of phone and is a member of the registered group.    

We target the small holder farmers in rural communities. The financially excluded vulnerable people who live in rural areas. We enable digital financial inclusion of marginalized rural communities especially women and youth by digitizing Village Savings and Loan Associations (VSLAs).

These are organized in VSLAs and are over 2 Million in Uganda.

These people are often not eligible or cannot afford access to formal financial services and thus resort to pulling their savings together in boxes and give loans to their fellow group members, which limits their access to capital that could foster their investment in better livelihoods. This exclusion is a result of stringent traditional banking conditions, lack of collateral, long distances to banking facilities, financial illiteracy, low productivity leading to low savings, high costs of account operations, and high-interest rates. These people save the money collected and borrowed in boxes under their leader’s groups bed or in the roofs of their house which is not safe (of fire or theft for instance).  

A research was made in 2018 to understand their needs. We do constant monitoring and trainings and every end of the training, a follow-up report is made based on findings from the surveys that are done regularly.

Our system is customized for VSLAs. We have a strong team that does research and development based on the users needs.

Title: TRAVADA: Traveler’s Assistance and Digital Access
Subtitle: The One-Stop Interurban Bus Travel Platform : Digitizing Cameroon’s Road Transport Industry
Problem Statement: Cameroon’s interurban road travel industry is vibrant, as most mid and low income earners use travel agencies for traveling for their various businesses. Sadly, as observed, this industry is still lagging behind in technological advancement. Even the major agencies still have little to no online presence, leaving customers hopelessly reliant on the manual way of ticket buying.
Solution Overview:
The Travada app is our solution which seeks to bridge this gap and proffer a solution. TRAVADA is an app that provides a synchronized platform, bringing together all the players in the transport industry on one platform. With TRAVADA, customers are provided with all the information they need about the various agencies on a single platform, and enables them effect booking and payment online, thus eliminating the need for passengers queuing up at the agencies’ premises, which is always time consuming, a financial burden and a great inconvenience for the passengers.
Through TRAVADA, when a customer downloads and registers with the app, they are provided with all the information they need about all the transport agencies on one single platform. They are provided information such as, but not limited to, each agency’s daily schedule, travel routes and destinations, pricing structure, customer care and relation, and more importantly, seamless online booking and ticketing as well as e-payment options. It also offers the customer the advantage of comparing rates and suitability of travel schedules between the various agencies, thus boosting competitiveness in pricing, and greater efficiency of services amongst the agencies.
The Travada app was built using React Native Android (Java with Android SDK), cloud-hosted RESTful APIs, and integrates MTN/Orange Money SDKs for payments while using HTTPS/TLS for secure data handling. It offers a lightweight, secure booking platform tailored for the Cameroon, as well as African interurban transport without collecting or sharing user data.
We made key partnerships with the ministry of transport, as well as 3 transport companies so far and are working on more.
Solution Provider(s): Dr. Divine Mbamome, Director of road transport , Cameroon, Mr Fabrice Abunde, executive director, Oasis transport agency, Mr Penn Junior, CEO, Grand Jeannot Express
Duration to pilot in a new geography: 9 months
SDGs addressed: SDG 9 (Industry, Innovation, and Infrastructure);SDG 8 (Decent Work and Economic Growth);SDG 17 (Partnerships for the Goals);
Desired impact:
The main objective of Travada is to increase digital accessibility and convenience to travelers by 75% by the end of 2026, while also enabling transport operators to efficiently manage their fleets and schedules more conveniently. 
So far, we have been able to decrease unemployment, Save passengers 4+ hours/week, boosts agency revenues by 30% (efficiency gains),and reduce paper use and unnecessary travel to agencies.
Key technologies: Travada was built using React Native Android, cloud-hosted RESTful APIs, and integrates MTN/Orange Money SDKs for payments while using HTTPS/TLS for secure data handling
Unique Characteristics: Our solution is quite unique because  we are the pioneers to build a single platform that unites agencies, making booking to any travel  agency very convenient and cheap. Also we partner directly with the bus companies before including them in our platform, making us quite unique from the other competitors
Sustainable Change: As a result of Travada, any transport company in Cameroon, and eventually, Africa, would be able to sign up on our platform and digitize their systems, thereby making booking very efficient and easy for their clients, also making most of their processes automated and easy to book keep and for easy  auditing. This approach is far more sustainable than their current modus operandi and can be done from anywhere in the country  and/or continent.
Funding Sources: Most of the funding have been from personal savings of the team and  the Tony Elumelu Grant awarded in 2022.
Testimonials and Endorsements: None yet
Further comments/feedback: Thank you for the opportunity to apply. The questionnaire is very well structured and detailed.

Summary: TRAVADA is a mobile app digitizing Cameroon’s interurban bus travel industry by centralizing booking, payments, and schedules. Built with React Native and integrating MTN/Orange Money, it allows passengers to compare agencies, book tickets online, and pay securely. The MVP is piloted in Bamenda, Douala, and Limbe, with partnerships established with the Ministry of Transport and three bus companies. Strengths: strong local relevance, tangible efficiency gains (75% increased accessibility target, 30% revenue boost for agencies), and government/industry partnerships. Weaknesses: early stage (MVP only), limited institutional uptake so far, and dependency on broader operator buy-in for scale.

Title: Supporting Disadvantaged Communities in Zimbabwe Through Digital Inclusion
Subtitle: transforming lives and communities through the power of technology.
Problem Statement:
In an increasingly digital world, access to technology and the internet is no longer a luxury but a necessity. This proposal aims to address the pressing issue of digital exclusion faced by disadvantaged communities in Zimbabwe. By focusing on enhancing digital literacy and providing access to technology, we can empower these communities to participate fully in the global economy and society. 
The initiative seeks to bridge the digital divide, ensuring that everyone, regardless of their socio-economic status, has the opportunity to benefit from the digital age. The proposal outlines a comprehensive plan to implement digital inclusion strategies that will not only provide access to technology but also equip individuals with the skills needed to navigate the digital landscape. By fostering an environment where technology is accessible and usable, we can create pathways for education, employment, and social engagement.This initiative is not just about providing tools; it is about transforming lives and communities through the power of technology.
Zimbabwe is home to a diverse population, yet many communities face significant challenges that hinder their development. Disadvantaged communities, particularly in rural areas, often lack access to basic services such as education, healthcare, and economic opportunities. The digital divide exacerbates these challenges, as limited access to technology and the internet restricts their ability to connect with essential resources and information. In these communities, many individuals are unaware of the potential benefits that technology can bring. Without access to digital tools, they miss out on educational opportunities, job prospects, and vital information that could improve their quality of life. The lack of digital literacy further compounds these issues, creating a cycle of poverty and exclusion that is difficult to break. Addressing these disparities is crucial for fostering sustainable development and improving the overall well-being of disadvantaged populations in Zimbabwe.
 The Importance of Digital Inclusion
Digital inclusion is essential for empowering individuals and communities in today’s world. It enables people to access information, communicate effectively, and participate in economic activities. For disadvantaged communities in Zimbabwe, digital inclusion can serve as a catalyst for change, opening doors to education, employment, and social services that were previously out of reach. Moreover, digital inclusion promotes equality by ensuring that all individuals have the opportunity to engage with technology. It helps bridge the gap between those who have access to digital resources and those who do not. By fostering an inclusive digital environment, we can create a more equitable society where everyone has the chance to thrive. 
This initiative recognizes that technology is a powerful tool for social change and aims to harness its potential for the benefit of marginalized communities.
Solution Overview:
Proposed Solutions for Digital Inclusion
To address the issue of digital exclusion in Zimbabwe, we propose a multi-faceted approach that includes providing access to technology, enhancing digital literacy, and creating supportive community networks. First, we will establish community technology centers equipped with computers and internet access. These centers will serve as hubs for learning and collaboration, allowing individuals to gain hands-on experience with technology. 
In addition to providing access, we will implement training programs focused on digital literacy. These programs will cover essential skills such as using computers, navigating the internet, and understanding online safety. By equipping individuals with these skills, we empower them to utilize technology effectively in their daily lives.
Furthermore, we will foster partnerships with local organizations and schools to ensure that our efforts are sustainable and reach a wider audience.
 Implementation Plan
The implementation plan for this initiative will be carried out in several phases. The first phase involves conducting a needs assessment in targeted communities to identify specific barriers to digital inclusion. This assessment will help us tailor our approach to meet the unique needs of each community. 
Once we have gathered data from the needs assessment, we will proceed with establishing community technology centers in strategic locations. These centers will be staffed by trained facilitators who can provide guidance and support to users. Concurrently, we will develop and launch digital literacy training programs that cater to various age groups and skill levels. 
Throughout the implementation process, we will engage with community members to gather feedback and make necessary adjustments. This participatory approach ensures that our initiatives remain relevant and effective in addressing the needs of disadvantaged populations.

Title: FASODIGI – Digital Platform for Women’s Skills, Beauty and Impact
Subtitle: A digital platform empowering women through natural cosmetics, vocational beauty training, and local fashion — for inclusive growth and economic autonomy in Guinea.
Problem Statement: A digital platform empowering women through natural cosmetics, beauty training, and civic engagement for inclusive and sustainable local development.
Solution Overview:
FAGMUS (Fati Global Multiservices) is a women-led Guinean enterprise committed to promoting local skills, women’s economic empowerment, and professional training in wellness and beauty.

Through the FASODIGI project, FAGMUS is launching an inclusive digital platform that integrates three complementary business units:

FATISPA: a beauty and wellness center offering vocational training. The project aims to digitize training modules (hair styling, aesthetics, soap making, etc.) to make them more accessible to young women, even remotely.

NATULIX: a natural cosmetics brand. The project includes the creation of an e-commerce space for selling locally made, traceable products, with a simplified ordering and payment system.

FATIBoutique: an initiative to promote and sell African clothing, with a digital catalogue to showcase local creators and expand their reach.

All components will be connected through a single mobile-first digital platform designed for low-bandwidth use. It will be built using open-source technologies.

FAGMUS plans to partner with women’s cooperatives, local developers, and professional trainers to ensure co-creation and long-term sustainability.
Solution Provider(s): COFEM – Coalition des Femmes et Filles de Matoto (women’s empowerment NGO, social inclusion sector),  GUINETIC – Groupement des entreprises du numérique de Guinée (ICT professionals network, digital innovation sector),  Coopérative ARTISANA Guinéenne (women-led cooperative, artisanal production and fashion sector),  ADJEG – Association des Jeunes pour l’Entrepreneuriat en Guinée (youth-focused entrepreneurship NGO, business development sector),  Maison de la Presse de Guinée (independent media hub, communication and civic engagement sector),  Développeurs Solidaires Guinée (freelance tech network, digital design and low-tech solutions),  Centre FATISPA – Centre de Soins et de Formation Esthétique (training and wellness center, vocational education sector),  Marque NATULIX (natural cosmetics initiative, green economy and women’s entrepreneurship), ...
Implementation location(s): Currently under preparation. Core components implemented in Conakry, Guinea (Ratoma Municipality), through the activities of NATULIX, FATISPA, and FATIBoutique.
Implementation timeline(s): Core activities started in 2020 (product testing and local training). Operational structure established in 2022 with ongoing activities. Digital platform development planned for 2025–2026.
Duration to pilot in a new geography: Approximately 6 to 9 months, including contextual analysis, partner onboarding, digital adaptation, pilot launch, and initial evaluation.
SDGs addressed: SDG 5 (Gender Equality);SDG 8 (Decent Work and Economic Growth);SDG 9 (Industry, Innovation, and Infrastructure);
Desired impact:
FASODIGI aims to empower women and youth through digital access to vocational training, economic opportunity, and product visibility. The platform connects natural cosmetics, wellness skills, and traditional fashion to inclusive growth.

Key Impacts (estimated over 24 months):

Train 150+ young women in beauty and natural product processing

Digitally certify at least 80 beneficiaries through e-learning modules

Generate employment for 15+ women through NATULIX and FATIBoutique

Expand market reach to 10,000+ online users (local + diaspora)

Promote eco-responsible consumption via local natural products

Strengthen digital inclusion for underserved communities in Guinea
Key technologies:
FASODIGI uses mobile-first, open-source and SaaS technologies to ensure accessibility and scalability. The solution integrates:

WordPress LMS: to host and deliver online training modules with tracking and certification

WooCommerce or Shopify: for managing digital storefronts for NATULIX and FATIBoutique, enabling online sales and secure payments

Low-data video tools: such as unlisted YouTube or open-source video hosting for tutorials

Responsive design: optimized for mobile devices and low-connectivity environments

Analytics tools: to monitor user engagement, course completion, and sales performance

While no advanced technologies such as AI or blockchain are currently used, future iterations may explore machine learning for personalized learning paths and product traceability.
Unique Characteristics:
FASODIGI stands out by combining local entrepreneurship, inclusive training, and digital commerce within a single women-led platform. Its unique features include:

Integrated model: links natural cosmetics, wellness training, and African fashion through a shared digital infrastructure.

Grassroots approach: built from real operational businesses (NATULIX, FATISPA, FATIBoutique), not just a prototype.

Women-centered scaling: developed and tested with women from vulnerable backgrounds, with pathways to formal employment and self-employment.

Flexible e-learning: accessible even in low-connectivity zones, with culturally relevant content and peer mentoring.

Economic + cultural impact: bridges traditional knowledge, digital inclusion and local production for long-term community empowerment.
Sustainable Change:
FASODIGI promotes long-term, systemic change by embedding digital innovation in three interlinked pillars: natural product value chains, women's vocational training, and cultural entrepreneurship.

Theory of Change:

Skills access → Young women gain marketable skills through mobile learning

Economic activation → Trained women enter the workforce or create micro-enterprises

Visibility & distribution → NATULIX and FATIBoutique connect them to local and diaspora markets

Cultural empowerment → Promotes pride in local resources, crafts, and aesthetics

Digital ecosystem → Inspires replication and digital upskilling across sectors

The model reduces economic exclusion, promotes responsible consumption, and lays the groundwork for a local digital economy powered by women.
Funding Sources: To date, the solution has been entirely self-funded by the founder through personal savings and reinvestment of revenue from existing business activities (NATULIX, FATISPA, and FATIBoutique). No external grants or loans have yet been used. The pilot digital platform will require seed funding to expand operations and reach.
Testimonials and Endorsements:
The solution has received strong positive feedback from users and trainees. NATULIX customers report visible improvements in their skin after a few days of use. One client stated: “My skin became soft again thanks to your soap.”

FATISPA training participants also shared transformative experiences. A former trainee recently launched her own beauty salon in Conakry and shared her story on social media. Others have testified to gaining both technical skills and confidence, especially after dreadlock styling workshops.

These testimonials illustrate the real-life impact of the solution on health, income generation, and women's empowerment. They demonstrate trust, relevance, and potential for scale.
Further comments/feedback: This questionnaire provides a clear and structured way to present impactful grassroots solutions. It encourages both strategic thinking and inclusive storytelling. Thank you for giving visibility to African women-led initiatives. We would welcome opportunities for mentorship, networking, and feedback from the evaluation team.
Primary thematic focus area: Inclusive Digital Innovation Skills & Entrepreneurial Talent Development
Summary: FASODIGI is a women-led platform in Guinea combining vocational beauty training, natural cosmetics, and African fashion e-commerce. Its strength lies in being rooted in existing enterprises (NATULIX, FATISPA, FATIBoutique), while its weakness is reliance on self-funding, limiting scaling capacity.

Title: StoryImpactX: The Global Storytelling Engine
Subtitle: AI-powered storytelling platform enabling organisations to gather high-quality, user-generated impact stories from diverse voices—anywhere, anytime.
Problem Statement: Storytelling is one of the most powerful tools for driving social transformation. It humanises data, builds empathy, and bridges divides by making complex issues personal and relatable. In the context of social inclusion, environmental sustainability, and governance, storytelling gives voice to those often unheard, amplifying grassroots experiences, exposing inequalities, and showcasing locally driven solutions. Yet, the stories that shape policy and public perception are too often curated by institutions far removed from lived realities. StoryImpactX changes this by placing storytelling power directly into the hands of communities while giving organisations the structure and control they need. By leveraging AI and smartphones to guide and standardise the process, and enabling diverse voices to participate regardless of location or skill level, the platform democratises narrative creation. It empowers marginalised individuals to become agents of change, provides real-time, context-rich insights for decision-makers, and accelerates impact communication for organisations working toward the Sustainable Development. In doing so, StoryImpactX becomes more than a digital tool, it becomes a bridge between people, policy, and progress globally.
Solution Overview:
1. How the Solution Works
StoryImpactX is an AI-powered digital storytelling platform designed to empower organisations and communities to collaboratively create, collect, and share high-impact stories that drive social inclusion, sustainability, and governance transparency. The platform operates through two core interfaces:

Mobile Application (for end users):
Assigned storytellers log in via secure credentials. The app guides them through a structured, step-by-step storytelling journey using AI-powered prompts that support composition, lighting, framing, and even sound quality. The user is led to record, reflect, and submit video or audio narratives tailored to an organisation’s defined objective.

Administrative Web Interface (for organisations):
Organisations set specific storytelling objectives, parameters, and data collection goals. Administrators can assign users, track submissions, review content, and use AI-enhanced editing and curation tools (e.g., captioning, transcription, keyword tagging) to refine narratives for strategic use across campaigns, reports, and digital channels.

This two-sided approach ensures that storytelling is both purpose-driven and inclusive, combining the authenticity of community voices with the clarity of structured, goal-aligned communication.


2. Methodologies and Technologies Used
Human-Centred Design (HCD):
Developed with user feedback loops from both storytellers and organisational partners to ensure accessibility, relevance, and ease of use.

AI-Powered Story Assistance:
AI modules guide users through lighting, framing, and sound enhancement. Natural Language Processing (NLP) and computer vision are integrated to assist in editing, auto-captioning, tagging, and content analysis.

Data-Driven Story Mapping:
Stories are geotagged and indexed by theme, sector, and SDG alignment, enabling visual storytelling dashboards and impact mapping.

Offline Capability & Cloud Syncing:
The app works offline and syncs automatically when connectivity is restored — crucial for rural or under-connected regions.

Digital Literacy & Upskilling Components:
In-app tutorials and micro-learning modules on storytelling, digital skills, and ethical media practices are built in to support creator development and employability.


3. Partnerships and Collaboration Models
a. Organisational Partners:
NGOs, government agencies, CSR departments, social enterprises, and international development bodies are the primary clients. They define narrative goals and deploy the app through their networks.

b. Community-Based Collaborators:
Grassroots organisations and local leaders help onboard and train storytellers, ensuring cultural sensitivity and local engagement.

c. Technology Partners:
Collaborations with AI developers, cloud service providers, and mobile UX experts to ensure ongoing platform innovation and reliability.

d. Academic & Training Institutions:
Partnerships with universities, media training institutes, and digital inclusion programs provide a pipeline for storytelling talent and research insights.

e. Creator & Impact Networks:
A curated network of digital storytellers, filmmakers, and SDG advocates contribute content, mentor new users, and amplify stories globally.
Solution Provider(s): Sustainow Media Lab Ltd – Sustainability communications and storytelling company; sectors: digital media, sustainability, climate, development, Media Citizens Front (MCF) – Nonprofit initiative; sectors: media literacy, civic engagement, digital democracy, Do For Love UK Ltd – Technology development company; sectors: software development, digital solutions, innovation.
Duration to pilot in a new geography: 8 months
SDGs addressed: SDG 17 (Partnerships for the Goals);SDG 9 (Industry, Innovation, and Infrastructure);
Desired impact:
Empower underrepresented communities to tell their own stories and contribute to global conversations on sustainability, social justice, and development.

Standardise and simplify impact storytelling for organisations working in areas such as climate change, health, gender equality, livelihoods, and governance.

Strengthen digital skills and entrepreneurial pathways for grassroots storytellers, especially youth and women in underserved regions.

Accelerate content-driven insights that inform more inclusive, responsive, and transparent policy and program decisions.

Promote visibility and voice for community-led solutions aligned with the Sustainable Development Goals (SDGs).
Key technologies:
AI is at the core of the platform, enabling smart, guided, and efficient storytelling at both user and administrator levels.

AI-Assisted Story Creation:
Helps users with real-time prompts for lighting, framing, sound, and visual composition, increasing the quality of user-generated stories.

Natural Language Processing (NLP):
Enables automatic transcription, captioning, keyword tagging, and sentiment analysis of video/audio submissions.

Content Curation & Editing Tools:
Administrators use AI-powered editing features to clean, enhance, and organise large volumes of incoming content.

Trend & Preference Analysis:
AI modules analyse content engagement and user behavior to optimise future storytelling techniques and prompts.
Unique Characteristics:
Client-Directed Content Creation: Unlike user-driven platforms, organisations set storytelling goals, ensuring content aligns with specific impact and SDG objectives.

AI-Guided Storytelling: Real-time prompts help users with lighting, framing, and sound—making high-quality storytelling accessible to non-experts.

Inclusive & Scalable Design: Mobile-first with offline functionality, enabling widespread participation from remote or underserved communities.

Built-In Upskilling & Employment: Offers digital training and paid story gigs, turning storytellers into empowered creators and entrepreneurs.

Real-Time Impact Mapping: Stories are geotagged and linked to SDGs, helping organisations visualise and report their impact globally.

Cost-Efficient & Collaborative: Reduces the need for field crews while enabling partnerships with NGOs, tech partners, and academia for wide-scale deployment.
Sustainable Change: StoryImpactX contributes to systemic change by transforming how impact is documented, shared, and acted upon, especially in underserved communities. By equipping individuals with digital storytelling tools and linking their voices to institutional goals, the platform bridges the gap between grassroots realities and decision-making spaces. It enables inclusive communication, builds local capacity, and amplifies marginalised voices, creating long-term shifts in how development, sustainability, and governance are communicated and shaped.
Funding Sources: Research has been funded by Sustainow Media Lab Ltd
Testimonials and Endorsements: Not Applicable (Concept stage)
Primary thematic focus area: Innovation Acceleration & Knowledge Sharing
Summary: StoryImpactX is an AI-powered storytelling platform at concept stage, designed to democratize impact storytelling by enabling grassroots communities to capture and share narratives aligned with SDG objectives. Strengths: strong alignment with digital inclusion, highly innovative AI-guided storytelling, and clear institutional use cases for NGOs and development partners. Weaknesses: still at idea stage with no implementation or testimonials, limited validation of feasibility in diverse contexts, and funding remains minimal.

Title: SENOWA est une plateforme de e-commerce agroalimentaire qui transforme l’expérience des courses alimentaires grâce à la technologie. En un clic, les femmes actives et familles sénégalaises peuvent commander des produits frais, de qualité, livrés chez elles de façon rapide et personnalisée. Grâce à son application intelligente, à ses algorithmes de recommandation et à une logistique optimisée, SENOWA fait gagner du temps, de la sérénité et de la confiance.
Subtitle: Plateforme de e-commerce spécialisé dans la vente de produits agro-alimentaires frais et de qualité (légumes, poissons, viandes, épices), conçu pour répondre aux besoins mensuels des consommateurs, en particulier des femmes actives de classe moyen-supérieure. SENOWA propose un service de livraison personnalisé et rapide, permettant d'économiser du temps précieux.  Chez SENOWA, notre modèle économique est centré sur la fourniture d'une plateforme e-commerce dédiée à la vente de produits agro-alimentaires frais et de qualité, spécialement conçue pour répondre aux besoins mensuels des consommateurs, en mettant l'accent sur les femmes actives de classe moyen-supérieure et les familles nombreuses. Nous ciblons nos clients à travers un éventail de couleurs spécifiques : #FF9900 pour les femmes actives et #56B224 pour les familles nombreuses, offrant ainsi des propositions de valeur adaptées à chaque segment. Nous exploitons divers canaux pour atteindre nos clients, incluant un site web optimisé (#0A58A5), une application mobile pour les commandes en déplacement (#0A58A5) et les réseaux sociaux pour la promotion et le support client (#0A58A5). Notre relation avec les clients est renforcée par un service client disponible 24/7 et des programmes de fidélité, tous deux marqués par le code couleur #0A58A5. Nos activités clés englobent la gestion rigoureuse de la chaîne d'approvisionnement pour garantir la fraîcheur des produits, le développement et la maintenance de notre plateforme technologique, et un marketing digital ciblé.
Problem Statement:
Aujourd’hui, de nombreuses femmes actives, mères de famille et urbains débordés se retrouvent dans une situation difficile :
Elles doivent gérer le travail, les enfants, les tâches ménagères, tout en cuisinant et en s’assurant que la famille mange bien.
Faire les courses devient un fardeau chronophage, avec des produits parfois de mauvaise qualité, mal conservés, sans traçabilité.
Et aucune plateforme fiable n’existe pour commander simplement des produits naturels et locaux à distance.
Solution Overview:
1. Description détaillée du fonctionnement de la solution

SENOWA est une solution hybride (digitale + physique) qui facilite l’accès aux produits agroalimentaires locaux et naturels pour les consommateurs urbains, tout en valorisant la production rurale.

Elle fonctionne selon un modèle en 4 étapes :

Collecte locale et transformation artisanale

SENOWA s’approvisionne directement auprès de petits producteurs ou de coopératives rurales.

Les produits sont ensuite transformés (huile pressée, néré séché et broyé, miel filtré) dans des unités artisanales respectant les règles d’hygiène.

Conditionnement et étiquetage professionnel

Chaque produit est conditionné (bouteilles, sachets, pots) avec des étiquettes précisant la traçabilité, les informations nutritionnelles et la date de production.

Commercialisation numérique et physique

Les clients passent commande via WhatsApp, Facebook, ou dans des kiosques solaires SENOWA implantés dans des zones urbaines.

Une boutique mobile ou fixe permet aussi de toucher une clientèle locale (marché, école, quartier résidentiel).

Livraison rapide et personnalisée

SENOWA assure la livraison à domicile, au bureau ou en point relais, avec un suivi client via téléphone ou messagerie.

2. Méthodologies et technologies utilisées

🔹 Méthodologie :
Approche centrée sur l’utilisateur (Design Thinking) : Les produits et services sont conçus à partir des besoins réels des femmes actives, des familles nombreuses et des clients urbains.

Méthode lean startup : Test rapide des formats, canaux et prix pour ajuster l’offre en temps réel.

🔹 Technologies :
WhatsApp Business : gestion de commandes, catalogue produits, suivi client.

Facebook & Instagram : promotion, publicité ciblée, interaction avec les clients.

Excel / Google Sheets : suivi des stocks, planning de livraison.

Mini-CRM local (à venir) : suivi client, historique des commandes.

Kiosques SENOWA autonomes : kiosques physiques en bois avec panneau solaire et frigo intégré pour exposer et vendre les produits sur site.

3. Partenariats et modèles de collaboration

🔹 Partenariats existants et visés :
Producteurs agricoles locaux (femmes transformatrices de néré, producteurs d’huile, apiculteurs) : achat en direct ou en dépôt-vente.

Artisans pour la fabrication des kiosques (menuisiers, installateurs solaires).

Techniciens agroalimentaires ou associations rurales : accompagnement pour le respect des normes d’hygiène.

Plateformes numériques : utilisation d’outils gratuits (Meta, WhatsApp, Canva) pour professionnaliser la communication.

🔹 Modèle de collaboration :
Gagnant-gagnant : les producteurs sont sécurisés par une demande régulière, les clients accèdent à des produits fiables, et SENOWA agit comme un pont commercial équitable.

Réseau d’agents-relais locaux : des vendeuses ou micro-entrepreneures peuvent représenter SENOWA et vendre les produits via commission.

Possibilité de partenariat avec ONG ou projets agricoles pour équiper les coopératives en matériel ou kiosques SENOWA.

SENOWA dispose d’une maquette fonctionnelle de sa plateforme numérique, pensée pour une utilisation simple et accessible :

Caractéristiques de la maquette :
Page d’accueil personnalisée : message de bienvenue, suggestion de produits selon le profil du client.

Catalogue interactif : huiles, néré, miel, légumes, viande, poisson, visibles par catégorie.

Panier intelligent : qui mémorise les achats fréquents pour faciliter les futures commandes.

Option de livraison : choix entre retrait au kiosque ou livraison à domicile.

Paiement mobile intégré : via Orange Money, Wave, Free Money.
Solution Provider(s): Coumba DIOP (SENOWA – Sen Noflayu Wagne), promotrice du projet, spécialisée dans l'agroalimentaire local et l'entrepreneuriat féminin ; Productrices rurales du Gandon et de Ndiabène Ndialbé, spécialisées dans la transformation artisanale de produits agroalimentaires (huile, nététou, miel) ; Menuisiers et artisans locaux de Saint-Louis, spécialisés dans la fabrication de kiosques écologiques ; Technicien solaire indépendant, opérant dans l’installation de systèmes photovoltaïques pour petits équipements ruraux ; Graphistes et développeurs bénévoles / consultants juniors en design numérique, spécialisés dans la conception de maquettes UX/UI pour applications e-commerce locales ; Utilisateurs testeurs urbains (clients pilotes), femmes actives et familles ciblées à Saint-Louis pour le retour d’expérience.
Implementation location(s): Le projet SENOWA est actuellement mis en œuvre à Saint-Louis du Sénégal, plus précisément dans le quartier HLM. Les premières ventes ont été réalisées auprès de clients résidant à Saint-Louis ville, Ndiolofène et Pikine Sor Diagne et à Dakar. La collecte et la transformation des produits (huile de palme, poudre de néré, miel) se font en collaboration avec des transformatrices locales situées dans la commune de Saint louis, et au Sud du sénégal le marché de Diaobé
Implementation timeline(s): La solution SENOWA est en cours de mise en œuvre depuis le mois de mai 2024. Les premières actions pilotes (approvisionnement, conditionnement, premières ventes et tests de livraison) ont été réalisées entre mai et juillet 2024 à Saint-Louis. La phase d’expansion progressive (communication digitale, test de kiosque, maquette numérique) est prévue en décembre 2025.
Duration to pilot in a new geography: Durée estimée pour tester la solution dans une nouvelle région :  La mise en œuvre pilote de la solution SENOWA dans une nouvelle région géographique nécessite en moyenne 3 à 4 mois, répartis comme suit :  Mois 1 : Identification des producteurs et partenaires locaux, mobilisation communautaire, collecte initiale des produits.  Mois 2 : Mise en place d’un point de vente (ex. kiosque solaire), test logistique, formation sur le conditionnement.  Mois 3 : Lancement du test de commercialisation via WhatsApp/Facebook, premières ventes, ajustements selon les retours clients.  Mois 4 : Évaluation de la demande, adaptation du stock, structuration du modèle local, validation pour extension.  📍 Exemple de région cible pour extension : Thiès, Louga ou Ziguinchor.
SDGs addressed: SDG 2 (Zero Hunger);SDG 8 (Decent Work and Economic Growth);SDG 12 (Responsible Consumption and Production);
Desired impact:
Objectifs de la solution SENOWA

Faciliter l’accès des consommateurs urbains à des produits alimentaires naturels, locaux et sains, via une plateforme de vente simple et accessible.

Valoriser les productions agricoles rurales (néré, huile de palme, miel, etc.) par la transformation, le conditionnement et la vente directe.

Réduire les pertes post-récolte grâce à un circuit de collecte, de transformation artisanale et de distribution rapide.

Créer des opportunités économiques locales, notamment pour les femmes rurales, jeunes transformateurs et livreurs urbains.

Promouvoir la consommation responsable, en favorisant les circuits courts et les produits sans transformation industrielle.

Principaux impacts attendus (quantifiables)

Accès à l’alimentation
+1 000 ménages urbains auront accès à des produits sains, naturels et traçables via SENOWA d’ici 12 mois.

Réduction de 50 % du temps moyen consacré aux courses alimentaires chez les femmes actives clientes.

Impact économique et social

Création directe d’au moins 10 emplois (collecte, conditionnement, livraison, animation digitale).

Augmentation de 30 à 50 % du revenu des petits producteurs ou transformatrices partenaires.

Mise en place de kiosques solaires autonomes, gérés par des femmes ou jeunes entrepreneurs locaux.

 Impact environnemental (ODD 12)

Réduction estimée de 70 à 80 % des pertes post-récolte pour les produits partenaires transformés.

Diminution de l’usage de conservateurs chimiques ou emballages plastiques non recyclables, remplacés par des conditionnements simples et durables.

Promotion de la consommation de produits locaux, réduisant l’empreinte carbone liée à l’importation ou au transport longue distance.
Key technologies:
Technologies clés utilisées dans la solution SENOWA

1. Technologies numériques de commerce en ligne (e-commerce de proximité)
WhatsApp Business : outil central pour la gestion des commandes, la communication client, l’affichage du catalogue produit, le suivi et la fidélisation.

Facebook/Instagram : canaux de marketing digital et de prospection géolocalisée.

Formulaires et tableurs intelligents (Google Forms / Sheets / Excel) : pour la gestion des commandes, du stock et du suivi logistique.

Technologie solaire pour la vente physique

Utilisation de kiosques autonomes alimentés par panneaux solaires, permettant :

L’alimentation de petits réfrigérateurs pour conserver les produits frais (poisson, viande, jus naturels).

L’éclairage en zones rurales ou urbaines sans réseau électrique fiable.

Prototypage d’une plateforme mobile (MVP en cours)

Maquette d’une application mobile SENOWA : interface utilisateur simple pour commander les produits, choisir son mode de livraison, payer par mobile money et recevoir des recommandations personnalisées.

Prévisions futures d’intégration :

Système de panier intelligent (algorithme simple basé sur les habitudes de commande).

QR code pour chaque produit avec origine, date de production et conseils d’utilisation.


Technologies envisagées à moyen terme

Géolocalisation des clients et livreurs (via API Google Maps ou services locaux).

Micro-CRM pour suivre l’historique des achats et automatiser la relance client.

Système de prévision de la demande pour optimiser la production et éviter les pertes.
Unique Characteristics:
Double approche : numérique + proximité terrain

SENOWA combine le canal digital (WhatsApp, Facebook, application) avec un modèle de kiosque physique solaire, ce qui permet :

D’atteindre aussi bien les clients connectés que ceux sans accès stable à internet,

De maintenir un lien humain avec les clients tout en optimisant la gestion via le digital.

Spécialisation sur les produits du terroir naturel, locaux et transformés

Contrairement aux plateformes généralistes, SENOWA se distingue par :

Une offre ciblée sur les produits du terroir sénégalais (huile rouge, néré, miel, légumes frais…),

Une valorisation de la chaîne locale de production et transformation artisanale,

Une traçabilité et un conditionnement respectueux des traditions.

Kiosque autonome en énergie, innovant et multifonctionnel

Le kiosque SENOWA, alimenté par énergie solaire, permet :

La vente locale sans dépendance au réseau électrique,

Le stockage de produits frais (frigo),

L’accueil des clients, la présentation des produits, et la distribution.

Ce modèle peut être répliqué dans toutes les régions du Sénégal, même dans des zones rurales ou périurbaines mal desservies.

Modèle économique agile et solidaire

Vente directe sans intermédiaires, avec partage équitable de valeur avec les producteurs,

Intégration de micro-agents commerciaux de quartier (livreurs, revendeuses),

Possibilité d’abonnements ou paniers hebdomadaires prépayés, adaptés aux familles urbaines.

 Partenariats communautaires et production participative

SENOWA travaille avec des groupements de femmes transformatrices et des artisans locaux pour produire, conditionner et distribuer les produits.

Cette approche favorise l’emploi local, l’autonomisation des femmes et la résilience des communautés rurales.

Vision numérique inclusive et évolutive

Utilisation d’outils simples (WhatsApp, mobile money) pour les premiers clients,

Évolution vers une plateforme numérique complète avec panier intelligent, système de géolocalisation, QR codes produits, etc.
Sustainable Change:
Contribution de SENOWA à un changement durable et systémique

Objectif principal :

Créer un écosystème local de production, transformation, distribution et consommation durable de produits agroalimentaires, en connectant les producteurs ruraux et les consommateurs urbains via une solution numérique accessible et inclusive.

Théorie du changement de SENOWA
Si :
Les petits producteurs et transformatrices rurales sont formés, connectés à un canal de distribution structuré et valorisés à travers une plateforme comme SENOWA,

Les consommateurs urbains accèdent facilement à des produits locaux sains, traçables et abordables via une solution numérique simple (WhatsApp, Facebook, application mobile),

Et si la solution est soutenue par un modèle économique inclusif, reposant sur des kiosques solaires, un système logistique local, et une chaîne courte,

Alors :
Les pertes post-récolte sont réduites grâce à la transformation et au stockage local,

Les revenus des producteurs augmentent, ce qui stimule la production agricole locale,

Les urbains adoptent une consommation plus responsable basée sur des produits locaux et non transformés industriellement,

De nouveaux emplois sont créés localement dans la transformation, la logistique, la distribution et le numérique,

Et l’on assiste à une réduction des inégalités économiques et alimentaires entre zones rurales et urbaines.

Effets secondaires souhaités (changements systémiques)

Autonomisation économique des femmes rurales impliquées dans la chaîne de valeur.

Émergence d’un nouveau modèle de commerce équitable local, inspirant d'autres initiatives communautaires ou régionales.

Structuration des marchés locaux grâce à la standardisation, la traçabilité et la régularité de la demande.

Transformation des habitudes alimentaires urbaines vers des produits plus naturels, nutritifs et issus de circuits courts.

Réduction de l’empreinte carbone du système alimentaire urbain par la promotion du local et l’utilisation de kiosques solaires.
Funding Sources:
Le projet SENOWA a été lancé grâce à un financement personnel de la promotrice Coumba DIOP, principalement destiné à l’achat de matières premières (huile de palme, néré, miel), au conditionnement, à la communication de proximité et à la création de la première maquette numérique.

Le développement initial s’est appuyé sur :

À ce jour, aucun financement externe ou institutionnel n’a encore été mobilisé, mais le projet est prêt à être renforcé et structuré grâce à un appui technique et/ou financier.
