Title: Foreign Grants And More
Subtitle: Capacity strengthening platform for young people who struggle to access foreign grants and fully funded conferences.
Problem Statement:
Every year, millions of MSMEs alone shut down due to lack of funding support to sustain their operations in the first 3 years. They lack the necessary skills to communicate their business traction, impact, and solution to funding organizations. 

They find it difficult to customize and apply the generic investment readiness programs they enroll in to fit their business model and industry. 

And there are no comprehensive platforms where they can access ongoing international funding opportunities that can support their R&D and expansion plans.
Solution Overview:
Our AI-powered SaaS platform enables social impact leaders, MSMEs, and NGOs to access the necessary skills and resources they need to raise grant funding for their projects and access fully funded industry-related conferences, forums, and summits where they can exhibit their products/services and participate in policy development conversations for their industry. 

It has a database that is updated daily with foreign grants and other fully funded international opportunities that over 1,500 users currently have access to from across 62 countries in the world. 

There is also a section where users can get recommendations of development organizations, government agencies, donors, and similar organizations in their thematic area, industry, and/or country.

AI technology is integrated to help us customize the pdf learning materials we upload backend to fit the needs and industry of each user. Instead of giving them access to generic learning resources, they can learn with their organization as case study and in the context of their focus area. AI also helps with accessibility like converting the content from text-speech-sign language for the hearing impaired in Arabic, French, and English language.

In the future, we can extend this concept to fit other hard skills and enable other skills development organizations to equip young people with in-demand technical skills, vocational skills,  soft skills, and entrepreneurial skills that fit specific contexts.
Solution Provider(s): not applicable
Duration to pilot in a new geography: 2 months
SDGs addressed: SDG 8 (Decent Work and Economic Growth);SDG 9 (Industry, Innovation, and Infrastructure);SDG 4 (Quality Education);
Desired impact: The solution objectives is to improve the learning outcomes of founders, accelerate business growth, and impact employment rate.
Key technologies: AI technology
Unique Characteristics:
We use AI technology to customize generic learnin materials for learners from different backgrounds and experience levels. Our system does not offer generic learning resources to our customers. They learn based on their context.

Our business model is B2B and we generate revenue from subscirptions. 

We only publish verified international funding opportunities on our database.

AI makes it easy for the hearing impaired to access our product in Arabic, French, and English.

We do not depend on irrelevant adverts to generate revenue.
Sustainable Change: Our theory of change is to nurture and connect young people to learn in-demand skills based on their own context, develop their innovative ideas, research and advocate, mobilise and engage communities, collaborate and co-create innovative solutions, for the SDGs, leading to change in systemic, collective, community, and individual levels.
Funding Sources: Personal/founder savings

Title: FoodSaverTech – Plateforme digitale pour une chaîne alimentaire zéro gaspillage
Subtitle: Réduire le gaspillage alimentaire par la technologie et l’intelligence collective locale.
Problem Statement: Dans les pays du Sud, une part importante de la production agroalimentaire est gaspillée à cause d’un manque de coordination, de technologies de suivi, et d’accès à l’information pour les petits acteurs. Cela nuit à la durabilité des systèmes alimentaires et aggrave l’insécurité alimentaire.
Solution Overview:
FoodSaverTech est une solution numérique conçue pour optimiser la gestion des flux alimentaires et réduire les pertes tout au long de la chaîne agroalimentaire.
Elle repose sur :

Une plateforme mobile/web pour cartographier les pertes et identifier les points critiques de gaspillage.

Un système de gestion intelligent (basé sur l’IA) pour proposer des stratégies de réduction adaptées (ex : revalorisation, redistribution, transformation secondaire).

Un module collaboratif qui connecte producteurs, transformateurs, ONG et consommateurs pour échanger des excédents ou des ressources (ex : invendus).
Méthodologie et technologies :

Diagnostic terrain basé sur des données collectées localement via mobile.

Analyse algorithmique (IA) pour générer des recommandations en temps réel.

Cartographie interactive via SIG.

Modèle de collaboration :

Collaboration entre universités, coopératives agricoles, entreprises agroalimentaires et collectivités locales.
Solution Provider(s): Université Hassan II
Implementation location(s): Région de Casablanca-Settat (Maroc) – pilotes dans les zones rurales et périrubaines
Duration to pilot in a new geography: 4 à 6 mois pour une mise en œuvre pilote dans une nouvelle région
SDGs addressed: SDG 2 (Zero Hunger);SDG 9 (Industry, Innovation, and Infrastructure);SDG 12 (Responsible Consumption and Production);
Desired impact:
Objectifs :

Réduction du gaspillage de 20 % chez les coopératives et MPME partenaires.

Sensibilisation de 5 000 personnes via l’application.

Création de 50 emplois directs liés à la logistique inversée et à la valorisation des invendus.

Résultats attendus à 2 ans :

1 000 tonnes d’aliments sauvés de la perte ou du gaspillage.

Création de 3 circuits de redistribution locaux.
Key technologies:
Intelligence Artificielle (diagnostic et recommandations)

SIG (cartographie des pertes)

Application mobile low-data (fonctionne hors ligne pour zones rurales)
Unique Characteristics:
Approche inclusive centrée sur les petits producteurs et les MPME

Utilisation de la technologie pour une cause sociale et environnementale

Synergie entre innovation locale, intelligence collective et science des données
Sustainable Change:
Créant un écosystème numérique de lutte contre le gaspillage

Favorisant l’autonomisation des MPME via des outils simples et accessibles

Instaurant une logique circulaire de valorisation des ressources au niveau local
Funding Sources: Financement par fonds de recherche universitaire
Testimonials and Endorsements: Cette plateforme a réduit notre gaspillage et amélioré nos revenus
Further comments/feedback: Questionnaire clair et complet. Ajouter une section sur les défis serait utile.
Primary thematic focus area: Innovation Acceleration & Knowledge Sharing
Summary: FoodSaverTech est une plateforme numérique visant à réduire le gaspillage alimentaire dans les pays du Sud. Elle combine une application mobile/web, un système d’IA pour identifier et proposer des solutions de revalorisation ou redistribution, et un module collaboratif reliant producteurs, transformateurs, ONG et consommateurs. Développée par l’Université Hassan II, la solution est en phase prototype dans la région Casablanca-Settat. L’objectif est de réduire le gaspillage de 20 % chez les coopératives partenaires, sauver 1 000 tonnes d’aliments en 2 ans et créer 50 emplois liés à la logistique inversée et la valorisation des invendus (Q11, Q13, Q17).

Title: galyimmo est une plateform Saas pour la gestion immobilière au complet
Subtitle: GalyImmo est une solution tout en un pour une gestion immobilière plus complete et trasparente.
Problem Statement:
En Guinée, la gestion immobilière souffre d'un manque de digitalisation, entraînant des 
inefficacités critiques. En effet, 80 % des propriétaires et gestionnaires utilisent des méthodes 
manuelles telles que des carnets ou Excel. Cela entraîne des retards de paiement (30 % des 
loyers sont payés en retard) et une opacité dans la gestion des charges et de la maintenance
Solution Overview:
GALYIMMO est une plateforme SaaS tout-en-un qui digitalise la gestion immobilière via :
 Centralisation : Gestion des biens, locataires, contrats, et paiements.
 Automatisation : Alertes de retard et rappels de renouvellement.
 IA intégrée : Prédiction des loyers optimaux et assistant intelligent (chatbot).
 Transparence : Tableau de bord financier en temps réel.
Solution Provider(s): Djomy (paiements).  Nimba SMS (notifications).  1000TechLearder(réseaux, talents)
Duration to pilot in a new geography: 3 months
SDGs addressed: SDG 9 (Industry, Innovation, and Infrastructure);SDG 11 (Sustainable Cities and Communities);
Desired impact:
ODD 8 : Création de 15 emplois directs.
 ODD 5 : 40 % de femmes formées à la digitalisation.
 ODD 11 : Réduction des conflits propriétaire/locataire (-50 %)
Key technologies:
Backend Symfony 7 : API sécurisée avec Swagger.
 Mobile Flutter : Accessibilité hors-ligne pour zones peu connectées.
 IA : Analyse des tendances du marché pour fixer les loyers et chatbot pour guider les 
utilisateurs (ex : « Comment déclarer une panne ? »).
Unique Characteristics:
Adaptation locale (paiements mobiles, multilingue).
 Approche "Freemium" pour l'inclusion.
Sustainable Change:
Étude terrain montre que 90 % des gestionnaires veulent digitaliser mais manquent d'outils 
adaptés.
ET notre solution intègre de l'IA pour bien aider les utilisateur .
Primary thematic focus area: Inclusive Digital Innovation Skills & Entrepreneurial Talent Development
Summary: GalyImmo is an all-in-one SaaS platform designed to digitize property management in Guinea, addressing inefficiencies caused by manual processes. Its use of AI and mobile accessibility is a unique strength. However, it lacks a clear financial sustainability strategy and needs further details on its scalability beyond the MVP phase.

Title: Distribution équilibrée des services numériques aux peuples africains démunis
Subtitle: l’accessibilité liée à une couverture réseau adaptée en zones éloignées et une réduction significative de forfaits de communication est très indispensable aux peuples démunis
Problem Statement: l’Afrique démunie est généralement victime du déséquilibre des services numériques : moindre débit de connexion, très peu d’avantages accordés aux opérateurs numériques de télécommunication qui fait qu'ils génèrent les revenus très dérisoires y relatifs. Mais aussi les consommateurs des services ont du mal à satisfaire leur besoin de communication à cause du tarif élevé infligé par les Sociétés de Télécommunication mobile et/ou de fibre optique. Un bon nombre ne peut donc pas avoir accès sur internet, en grande partie les femmes/filles en milieux moins avancés. Leur économie ne peut aucunement relever du numérique à l'instar de l'agriculture, il en est le cas même des femmes intellectuelles. Ceci serait favorisé par l'absence d'une politique adéquate de collaboration étroite entre Acteurs Etatiques et Acteurs Privés
Solution Overview:
On peut envisager une solution en soutenant les Entrepreneurs numériques dans le contexte de promotion du genre; en facilitant l'accès aux services de payement numérique pour les populations vulnérables; en dispensant des formations adaptées aux différentes générations comme les jeunes, les femmes, les personnes âgées et handicapés; en déployant une infrastructure importante dans les milieux ruraux, etc.
S'agissant de la méthodologie, adoptons une mise en place d'un environnement numérique de confiance où les données sont protégées, renforcement des capacités et sensibilisation sur les avantages du numérique.
Concernant le partenariat, la collaboration entre les parties notamment les acteurs privés et acteurs publics doit au préalable ressortir d'un cadre légal et institutionnel du pays afin d'y accorder du sérieux ce qui fera que même les Sociétés fournisseurs des services numériques aient une discipline d'adaptation des services numériques vendus
Solution Provider(s): Les partenaires sont encore à identifier
Duration to pilot in a new geography: 24 mois
SDGs addressed: SDG 1 (No Poverty);SDG 10 (Reduced Inequalities);SDG 11 (Sustainable Cities and Communities);
Desired impact: Croissance économique des populations desservies adéquatement, communication numérique accessible par toutes catégories des communautés, voire rurales, la frustration de l'inégalité de communication entre les sexe sensiblement réduite
Key technologies: l'intelligence artificielle en priorité
Unique Characteristics: le partenariat règlementé et renforcé entre les parties : le public et le privé fondé sur la base de la croissance économique des démunis
Sustainable Change: les packages offerts par les fournisseurs des services numériques deviendront consistants, c'est-à-dire, pour le cas du numérique en RDC par exemple un lot vendu à 10USD par mois, atteindre cette période. Il ne sera donc plus éphémère ou non en fonction de consommation, plutôt en fonction du timing y dédié. La validité sera désormais appliquée in extenso

Title: VectorWatch AI: Forecasting Human and Agricultural Vector-Borne Risks to Protect Lives and Economies
Subtitle: AI-powered app predicting malaria and vector-borne disease surges by linking climate and vector data, sending alerts to boost bed net use, communities’ awareness, preventive action, and therefore, protect lives and economies.
Problem Statement: Cameroon and other vulnerable countries face rising threats from vector-borne diseases such as malaria, dengue, and livestock infections spread by ticks and tsetse flies. These diseases not only endanger public health but also undermine agricultural productivity, weaken exports like cocoa and coffee, and place heavy burdens on national economies. Current surveillance systems are fragmented, slow, and rarely integrate climate and vector data, leaving communities and authorities unprepared for outbreaks. Without predictive tools and early warnings, both lives and economies remain at risk.
Solution Overview:
Description

VectorWatch AI is an AI-powered early warning system that combines climate, environmental, and epidemiological data to forecast vector-borne disease risks affecting both humans and agriculture. The platform integrates real-time data from health facilities, IoT sensors, meteorological APIs, and field reports. Machine learning models analyze these inputs to predict surges in malaria, dengue, and other infectious diseases, while also tracking vectors that threaten livestock and agricultural productivity (such as ticks and tsetse flies). This is particularly critical in Cameroon, where outbreaks reduce farmer productivity and put major export sectors like cocoa, coffee, and livestock at risk. Communities, health workers, and authorities receive timely alerts via SMS, mobile apps, and dashboards, enabling rapid preventive action such as scaling up LLIN (Long Lasting Insecticidal Net) use, improving water management, or protecting livestock. In doing so, VectorWatch AI not only safeguards public health but also protects livelihoods and strengthens national economies dependent on agriculture and exports.

Methodologies and technologies used

IoT and Remote Sensing: Connected sensors and satellite data monitor water levels, air quality, vegetation indices, and other environmental and climate change parameters relevant to vector proliferation.

Mobile and Offline-First Tools: Health workers and farmers report cases or conditions through mobile apps that function in low-connectivity areas.

AI and Predictive Modeling: Machine learning and deep learning algorithms forecast disease surges by correlating climate signals (rainfall, temperature, humidity) with vector dynamics and case data.

GIS and Risk Mapping: Interactive maps visualize disease risks across regions, supporting targeted interventions (Vaccination programmes, livestock etc..).

Secure Data Systems: Cloud-based architecture with encryption ensures interoperability with existing tool such as :  DHIS2 : District Health Information System 2 which is a platform for collecting and transmitting health data, used across all health districts in Cameroon for the surveillance of infectious diseases etc...

Partnerships and collaboration models

VectorWatch AI is built on a multi-sectoral, One Health approach : which is a globally recognized framework promoted by WHO, FAO, OIE, and UNEP. This approach emphasizes the interconnection between human health, animal health, and environmental health. By combining climate and vector data across these three dimensions, VectorWatch AI strengthens coordinated prevention, ensuring that outbreaks affecting people, livestock, and ecosystems are anticipated early and managed effectively.

To achieve this, the project will mobilize:

Institutional Partners: Ministries of Health, Environment, and Agriculture integrate the platform into national surveillance frameworks.

Operational Partners: Hospitals, clinics, veterinary services, and local health workers provide ground-level data.

Community Partners: Farmer cooperatives and NGOs help disseminate alerts and encourage preventive practices (LLIN use, livestock protection).

Technology and Research Partners: Startups and academic institutions specializing in AI, IoT, and data science contribute to system design and continuous improvement.

International Partners: Organizations like WHO, FAO, and the World Bank can leverage the platform to align with malaria elimination, food security, and climate resilience goals.
Solution Provider(s): 1. Institutional Partnerships  Ministries of Health for integrating the platform into national surveillance systems (e.g., DHIS2, IDSR).  Meteorological and hydrological agencies such as Cameroon’s Direction de la Météorologie Nationale (DMN), in coordination with the Ministry of Environment, Protection of Nature and Sustainable Development (MINEPDED), to provide access to climate and environmental datasets essential for predictive modeling.  2. Operational Partnerships  Networks of health workers and research institutions such as the Center for Research in Infectious Diseases (CRID) and the Organisation de Coordination pour la Lutte contre les Endémies en Afrique Centrale (OCEAC) (where we already have entries) , supporting real-time field data collection and literature reviews on vector proliferation conditions.  Hospitals, clinics, veterinary services, and laboratories (from the targeted piloting zones in Cameroon) as primary sources of confirmed case data for both human and livestock health.  3. Technological and Academic Partnerships  Startups specializing in IoT, AI, data science, and GIS for the design and deployment of the innovative platform.  Vendors in Africa:   Ignitia (West Africa): Provides tropical weather forecasts via SMS tailored for farmers (e.g., rainfall, storms, drought). Their localized forecasts are useful for predicting mosquito/vector breeding conditions.  Viamo (Pan-Africa): A digital communication platform delivering voice and SMS-based data collection and alerts, often in local languages. Useful for sending outbreak alerts and gathering field-level health/agriculture info.  Safi Analytics (Kenya): Works with IoT sensors and data dashboards to provide environmental and productivity insights for agriculture and energy systems. Can support monitoring of vector habitats (humidity, water levels).
Duration to pilot in a new geography: 12 months
SDGs addressed: SDG 13 (Climate Action);SDG 3 (Good Health and Well-being);SDG 8 (Decent Work and Economic Growth);
Desired impact:
Solution Objectives

- Anticipate and reduce outbreaks of vector-borne diseases such as malaria, dengue, and livestock-related infections (ticks, tsetse).

- Strengthen resilience of farming and rural communities by linking climate, environmental, and epidemiological data to actionable early warnings.

- Protect livelihoods and major export sectors (cocoa, coffee, livestock) by reducing labor losses, safeguarding agricultural productivity, and stabilizing local economies.

- Foster inclusive digital innovation by engaging youth and women in data collection, awareness, and digital management.

Key Achievements / Expected Impacts

- Health impact: Reduce detection and response time for outbreaks by 15–20%, enabling faster interventions and reducing morbidity and mortality.

- Economic impact: Protect farmer productivity and reduce income losses in cocoa, coffee, and livestock sectors, contributing to 10–15% savings in public health and agricultural costs in intervention zones.

- Employment & inclusion: Create at least 10 local jobs during the pilot phase, prioritizing youth and women as community health workers, digital data managers, and outreach agents.

- Environmental & climate resilience: Integrate climate data into health surveillance, strengthening community preparedness against climate-driven disease risks.

- Systemic change: Establish a scalable, One Health–based model that can be replicated across African countries, linking human, animal, and environmental health through an open-source platform.
Key technologies:
Artificial Intelligence (AI) & Machine Learning

- Predictive algorithms analyze health, climate, and environmental data to forecast vector-borne disease outbreaks.
- Detects correlations between rainfall, humidity, temperature, and disease incidence to generate early warnings.

Internet of Things (IoT) & Environmental Sensors

- Connected devices measure local conditions such as rainfall, temperature, humidity, and water quality.
- IoT-enabled stations and community devices provide ground-truth data in high-risk areas.

Remote Sensing & Geographic Information Systems (GIS)

- Free and open access Satellite imagery (e.g., Sentinel, MODIS etc..) and GIS mapping identify vector breeding habitats and visualize disease risks.
- Vegetation indices, surface water mapping, and air quality data support environmental risk assessment.

Mobile & Offline-First Applications

- Mobile apps for health workers, veterinarians, and farmers to report cases and conditions, even in low-connectivity zones.
- SMS and voice-based alerts reach vulnerable communities and other groups directly.

Cloud Computing & Secure Databases

Open-Source Integration

Unique Characteristics: VectorWatch AI is unique because it bridges human, animal, and environmental health through a 'One Health' approach, forecasting not only malaria  but also a range of vector-borne threats such as dengue, yellow fever, ticks, tsetse flies, Berry Borer, leaf miner... By combining AI, IoT sensors, and free satellite data with local health and meteorological systems, it delivers timely, low-connectivity alerts to communities while safeguarding key exports like coffee, cocoa, and livestock. Designed to directly respond to Africa’s urgent need for integrated, climate-informed disease and pest surveillance, it protects both lives and economies through an open-source, scalable model that can be replicated across the continent.
Sustainable Change:
VectorWatch AI delivers integrated early warnings to communities, health workers, farmers, and veterinarians, enabling timely preventive actions that drive systemic transformation.

At the community level, SMS and app alerts increase LLIN usage and awareness, which has been shown to reduce malaria prevalence (SMS reminders in Nigeria improved treatment adherence by ~10–14%). Farmers receive tailored alerts on pest and vector surges affecting crops like cocoa and coffee, or livestock diseases linked to ticks and tsetse flies. This allows them to apply preventive treatments, improve farm practices, and avoid significant income losses. Veterinarians act swiftly to protect animal health and productivity.

The result is fewer human infections, healthier livestock, stronger crop yields, and protected household incomes, securing both livelihoods and key export economies. The platform builds on a One Health, open-source, scalable model, strengthening national surveillance systems (e.g., DHIS2) and aligning with WHO’s 2030 agenda for resilient health systems.

Over time, the follow-on effects include:

Behavioral change: Communities and farmers adopt proactive preventive measures.

Economic resilience: Farmers and exporters reduce losses from vector impacts.

Institutional strengthening: Local and national agencies gain robust climate-health surveillance.

Regional scalability: The model can be replicated across Africa, ensuring systemic resilience.

Title: Kilimara: Empowering African Farmers with Digital & Market Access
Subtitle: Kilimara is a digital platform that empowers African farmers and cooperatives, promotes local products, ensures transparency, and connects them to sustainable markets.
Problem Statement:
Across Africa, farmers and cooperatives face limited access to markets, weak organizational structures, and lack of transparency in value chains. Most transactions remain informal, reducing producers’ bargaining power and leading to post-harvest losses, low incomes, and exclusion from profitable markets. Women and young farmers, who play a critical role in local food systems, are often the most marginalized due to limited digital and financial inclusion.

Moreover, local products struggle to compete in visibility and traceability, preventing them from meeting buyers’ quality and sustainability requirements. Climate change further exacerbates these challenges, increasing uncertainty in production and threatening livelihoods.

Kilimara addresses these issues by providing an inclusive digital solution that strengthens cooperative management, promotes local products, connects farmers to reliable markets, and integrates transparency and climate-smart practices across agricultural value chains.
Solution Overview:
Detail Description
Kilimara is a digital platform for Farmers and cooperatives use to register members, track production, manage contributions, monitor sales, and ensure full traceability. Mara connects them directly with buyers at local, regional, and international levels, highlighting local products with information on origin, quality, and packaging. 
Methodologies and technologies used
The solution is designed with local users feedback, for low-connectivity rural environments, with offline-first features and user-friendly interfaces adapted to low literacy levels (icons, tutorials). It promotes sustainable practices. Technologies include mobile and web applications, cloud-based storage with offline synchronization, and analytics dashboards for cooperatives and partners.
Partnerships and collaboration models
Kilimara operate through multi-stakeholder collaboration: cooperatives, farmers’ organizations, local authorities, NGOs, and private sector actors (buyers, input suppliers, logistics providers). Institutional partnerships with GIZ, ministries, and academic partners ensure scalability and policy alignment. The business model combines affordable subscriptions, marketplace transaction fees, and strategic partnerships, ensuring long-term sustainability.
Solution Provider(s): GIZ (Deutsche Gesellschaft für Internationale Zusammenarbeit) – Technical and institutional partner supporting training, cooperative strengthening, and digital adoption. Sector: Development cooperation, capacity building. national chamber of commerce (Trade – Côte d’Ivoire) – Institutional partners supporting deployment, regulatory integration, and alignment with national strategies. Sector: Public policy, agriculture, environment. Farmer Cooperatives & Federations (Côte d’Ivoire - CNOFECI, ) – Primary beneficiaries and implementation partners ensuring adoption, local anchorage, and relevance.

SDGs addressed: SDG 5 (Gender Equality);SDG 8 (Decent Work and Economic Growth);SDG 9 (Industry, Innovation, and Infrastructure);
Desired impact:
Solution Objectives

Economic inclusion: increase smallholder and cooperative incomes by enabling direct, fair market access for local products.

Resilient value chains: improve traceability, logistics coordination, and reduce post-harvest losses.

Digital inclusion & skills: equip women and youth with practical, offline-first tools and training.


Key Achievements / Target KPIs (12 months)

Reach & adoption: onboard 10,000 farmers and 400 cooperatives; ≥50% women, ≥40% youth among trainees/users.

Market outcomes: facilitate ≥15,000 orders/transactions for local products.
 
Traceability & efficiency: 100% of listed products tagged with origin/quality; -30% order-to-cash time; +15% transport load factor through route/aggregation optimization.

Loss reduction: -10 percentage points in post-harvest losses for targeted value chains (e.g., fresh produce).

Jobs: create ≈80 direct jobs (ambassadeurs, relais staff, commercial managers, trainers).
Key technologies:
Key technology(ies) used

Mobile & Web (offline-first): Android + responsive web/PWA with on-device storage (e.g., SQLite) and sync when online.
Data & sync layer: APIs (REST/GraphQL), background queues, versioning & conflict resolution (timestamps/LWW) for multi-user edits.
Traceability: auditable logs; GS1-aligned data fields.
Analytics & dashboards: Cloud data store/warehouse, KPI dashboards for coops/partners.
Low-connectivity channels: SMS/USSD/WhatsApp bots, push notifications, multi-language UI.
Security & privacy: TLS, encryption at rest, RBAC, audit trails; GDPR-style data minimization.

Title: Donner l’accès aux étudiants comoriens aux formations en ligne et au numérique
Subtitle: Faciliter l’accès des jeunes comoriens aux formations en ligne et aux compétences numériques malgré le manque d’équipements et d’informations.
Problem Statement: Dans notre village, de nombreux jeunes réussissent chaque année le baccalauréat, mais il existe très peu de formations supérieures accessibles, notamment au niveau Master. Beaucoup d’étudiants ignorent qu’il existe des cours gratuits en ligne et des bourses pour poursuivre leurs études. De plus, l’accès à Internet et aux ordinateurs est très limité, ce qui empêche les jeunes de développer leurs compétences numériques et de se préparer aux métiers du futur.
Solution Overview:
Nous voulons aider les étudiants comoriens à apprendre en ligne. Au début, nous allons installer 5 ordinateurs et 2 projecteurs avec internet. Les étudiants pourront suivre des cours gratuits, apprendre les langues et chercher des bourses. Nous organiserons des petites formations pour leur apprendre à utiliser internet et les cours en ligne.
Plus tard, nous voulons créer des centres numériques dans les bibliothèques pour aider plus d’étudiants et proposer des formations en cybersécurité et finance digitale. Cela préparera les jeunes à travailler dans les métiers numériques et à aider le pays.
Méthodes et technologies :
Former les étudiants avec des ateliers pratiques et un suivi simple.
Utiliser des ordinateurs, projecteurs, internet, et des cours gratuits en ligne (MOOCs, langues, informatique).
Partenaires et collaboration :
Écoles et mairie : pour identifier les étudiants et soutenir le projet.
Bibliothèques : pour accueillir les centres numériques.
Organisations internationales : pour la formation et le savoir-faire.
Bailleurs de fonds : pour financer les ordinateurs, internet et le matériel.
Cette solution permet aux jeunes d’apprendre facilement, de chercher des bourses, et de se préparer pour l’avenir numérique de leur pays.
Solution Provider(s): Écoles du village, Mairie du village, Bibliothèques locales, Organisations internationales de formation (ex. UNESCO, ONUDI), Bailleurs de fonds pour le matériel et Internet (ex. Fondation MasterCard, Banque Islamique de Développement), Plateformes de cours en ligne gratuites (ex. Coursera, edX, Khan Academy).
Implementation location(s): Le projet a déjà été mis en œuvre en ligne pour les étudiants comoriens. La mise en œuvre physique est prévue dans le village de Mde Bambao, aux Comores, incluant trois écoles et les bibliothèques locales.
Implementation timeline(s): La solution a commencé en 2022, après une formation en marketing numérique, et elle est toujours en cours.
Duration to pilot in a new geography: Pour lancer la solution dans une nouvelle zone, il faudra environ 6 à 12 mois.  Les 3 premiers mois pour installer les outils numériques, former les enseignants et sensibiliser la communauté.  Les 3 à 6 mois suivants pour accompagner les étudiants, tester la plateforme et assurer un bon suivi.  Après une année complète, la solution peut fonctionner de manière autonome et être reproduite ailleurs.
SDGs addressed: SDG 4 (Quality Education);SDG 8 (Decent Work and Economic Growth);SDG 9 (Industry, Innovation, and Infrastructure);
Desired impact:
Permettre aux étudiants comoriens d’accéder à des formations en ligne et de développer des compétences numériques.
Former les jeunes aux métiers du futur, comme la cybersécurité et la finance digitale.
Aider les étudiants à trouver des bourses et poursuivre leurs études supérieures.
Principales réalisations ou impacts :
À 1 an : au moins 100 étudiants formés aux bases du numérique, 50 étudiants suivent des cours de langues, plusieurs commencent à postuler à des bourses.
À 3 ans : plus de 500 étudiants formés, création de centres numériques dans les bibliothèques, début des formations en cybersécurité.
À 5‑10 ans : de jeunes experts comoriens en sécurité numérique et finance digitale, retour au pays de boursiers qualifiés, contribution au développement économique et digital du village et du pays.
Ces impacts permettront de réduire la fracture numérique, de préparer les jeunes aux emplois du futur et de favoriser le développement durable dans la communauté.
Key technologies:
Ordinateurs et projecteurs connectés à Internet pour permettre l’accès aux cours en ligne.
Plateformes d’apprentissage en ligne (MOOCs, cours gratuits) pour les langues, l’informatique et les sciences.
Logiciels éducatifs pour la bureautique, la programmation et le développement numérique.
Outils de communication en ligne (email, messagerie, visioconférence) pour le suivi et le tutorat.
Cybersécurité de base pour protéger les données des étudiants et le matériel informatique.
Unique Characteristics:
Le projet est le premier dans le village de Mde Bambao qui combine l’éducation en ligne et l’accès à la technologie pour les jeunes.
Il est conçu pour réduire la fracture numérique dans une zone où les bibliothèques et écoles n’ont pas encore de centre digital moderne.
La solution mise sur l’accompagnement des étudiants (formation, bourses, suivi) et pas seulement sur la mise à disposition de matériel.
Le financement est basé sur la collaboration avec des partenaires internationaux (Banque Islamique de Développement, associations locales) ce qui rend le modèle durable.
L’accent est mis sur des domaines stratégiques et rares aux Comores : cybersécurité, finance digitale, et compétences numériques avancées.
Sustainable Change: Notre projet aide les jeunes à apprendre le numérique et à partager ce savoir avec d’autres. Petit à petit, cela change la façon d’étudier dans le village, car les écoles commencent à utiliser Internet et les outils modernes. Les étudiants qui réussissent pourront trouver un travail ou aider la communauté. Avec le temps, le projet pourra aussi être fait dans d’autres villages, pour que plus de jeunes aient les mêmes chances.
Funding Sources: La solution a été financée principalement par des contributions personnelles, avec l’appui de petits dons communautaires. Une partie des outils a aussi été soutenue par des formations suivies gratuitement en ligne (marketing numérique).
Testimonials and Endorsements:
« Grâce à cette solution, nos élèves ont accès à des documents numériques qu’ils n’avaient pas avant. Cela aide beaucoup pour leurs études. » — Enseignant, École publique de Mde Bambao.
« Je peux enfin lire et apprendre depuis mon téléphone sans aller loin. » — Élève bénéficiaire, 2023.
« Le projet donne de l’espoir aux jeunes et montre que le numérique peut vraiment aider notre village. » — Responsable communautaire local.

Primary thematic focus area: Inclusive Digital Innovation Skills & Entrepreneurial Talent Development
Summary: This project seeks to provide young Comorian students, particularly in the village of Mde Bambao, with access to digital education and online learning opportunities. Initially deploying five computers, two projectors, and internet connectivity, it enables students to follow free online courses, learn languages, and apply for scholarships. Over time, the initiative aims to establish digital learning centers in libraries, expand training into areas such as cybersecurity and digital finance, and create pathways for youth to participate in the digital economy. By focusing on awareness, training, and access to resources, the project reduces the digital divide and prepares young people for future employment opportunities while fostering sustainable community development.

Title: Novatrax: Powering Africa’s Gaming and Creative Tech Revolution

Key Challenges Addressed
Africa’s gaming ecosystem faces limited local content, scarce funding, skills gaps, and underrepresentation in global markets. Youth often lack platforms to turn creativity into sustainable careers, while investors see the industry as high-risk due to weak infrastructure and visibility.

Novatrax Solution
Novatrax tackles these issues by building world-class games rooted in African culture, creating jobs and training opportunities for youth, and fostering an ecosystem where gaming drives innovation. Through scalable projects and Web3 integration, we de-risk investment, open new revenue streams, and position Africa as a competitive hub in the global creative economy.
Solution Overview:
How the Solution Works
Novatrax is building Africa’s first scalable gaming and creative technology studio that develops culturally relevant games while integrating Web3 and AI to unlock new opportunities. Our games are designed with African stories, art styles, and experiences at their core, ensuring global audiences connect with authentic content. Players engage through mobile, while Web3 integration enables digital asset ownership, player-driven economies, and new monetization models. AI enhances gameplay personalization, adaptive difficulty, and smart community tools, ensuring a modern and engaging user experience.

Methodologies and Technologies Used

Game Development Frameworks: Unity and Unreal Engine for scalable, cross-platform game development.

Web3 Integration: Wallet integration, NFTs, and token-based reward systems to foster true player ownership and circular economies.

Artificial Intelligence: AI-driven matchmaking, in-game personalization, player behavior insights, and moderation for healthier communities.

Scalable Deployment: Cloud-based infrastructure for global reach and seamless user experiences.

Partnerships and Collaboration Models

Creative Industry Partnerships: Collaborations with African musicians, artists, and storytellers to embed culture and amplify reach.

Technology Collaborations: Partnerships with Web3 firms for blockchain integration and AI research labs for adaptive gameplay features.

Ecosystem Building: Working with universities and training hubs to upskill youth in game design, AI, and blockchain.

Industry Alliances: Strategic collaborations with entertainment brands, esports organizations, and investor networks to drive adoption and market visibility.

Title: Quaha - Learn to Inspire
Subtitle: Quaha is a mobile-first, gamified education app providing access to higher educuation courses to help gain access to skills , earn certificates and access to opportunity.
Problem Statement: The prevailing issue is the limited accessibility of quality education, skills  development programs, and employment opportunities for a growing Youth population, resulting in challenges for both graduates and non-graduates to acquire necessary skills and knowledge for employability.I am trying to solve the problems of accessibility to localised educational courses content by making some of the learning material relatable using african examples. I am also trying to resolve the problem of a low retention and completion rate of online courses globally from less 10 percent to target 70 percent. I am slo trying to solve the problem of making higher education inclusive and affordable to anyone with a decent smart phone regardless of their location.
Solution Overview:
Quaha wants to revolutionise education and skill development by providing practical,  relevant, and engaging bite-sized content courses , gamified with innovative  technology, to make up-skilling accessible, affordable, and enjoyable for learners and the workforce of all generations . Learners can download the Quaha mobile app on their smart phone , upon signing up the learner receives our Virtual currency called Quoins. These Quoins can be used to unlock courses, modules and play quizzes. When a learner completes a module or course the learners will receive a certificate and a skills badges which they can use to upload on their resume or start their own business with the knowledge acquired. 

The methodologies we are using are 1) Micro-learning : Learners can do short , bit-sized courses that are broken down into modules.This is intentional to making learning retention high 2) Gamification of Learning :  Learners will earn quoins for answering question correctly , referring friends , completing courses and complete modules and daily learning streaks. This is designed to keep learners engaged , rewarded and motivated to keep learning. 3) Out-come based learning : Learners will learn courses that embrace real world learning that will prepare learners for the employment opportunities and entrepreneurship. We have resources that accompany the learning material such as pdf's, hyperlinks, articles etc 4) Mobile-First : The Quaha app is designed to enable educational access to anyone in under-resourced part of the world. The app is designed for low data usage to make learning affordable .
Technology: 1) Proprietary Learning Management System :  Quaha has its own LMS that enables us to upload and manage all course and quiz content. It also enables us to track progress, upload skills upload certificates, manage quoins rewarded and data analytics.


Quaha operates on a dual business model that generates revenue through both learners (B2C) and 
partnerships (B2B) We offer unlimited access to courses, supported by seamlessly integrated advertisements
Revenue Sources
Business-to-Customer (B2C):
In-App Purchases: Users buy courses, modules, certifications and quizzes using Qrowns (real money) or earned Quoins.
Advertising Revenue: Integrated ads within free learning modules and quizzes generate income while ensuring accessibility.
Business-to-Business (B2B):
Corporate Sponsorships: Branded courses and quizzes tailored for corporate partners.
Partnerships: Customised learning programs for NGOs, institutions, and organisations.
In-App Advertising: Banner and video ads on high-visibility pages, such as course and quiz modules.
Marketplace Commissions (Future): Revenue from products, internships, and career opportunities offered via the Quaha platform.
Quaha Publisher Program:
P1: Biannual subscription for brands to integrate Quaha Quiz games exclusively within the platform.
P2: Annual subscription allowing brands to use Quaha games in commercial offerings, with analytics, marketing, and advertising support included.
Partnership Models for Course Production:
Course Creation & Revenue Sharing: Quaha collaborates with partners to produce courses, retaining intellectual property and copyrights while partners receive a majority revenue share.
Content Adjustment: Quaha customises content for partners, sharing revenue and charging additional fees for repeated courses.
Partner-Provided Content: Partners supply their content while Partner retains IP, Quaha taking an initial revenue share and partner splitting excess revenue beyond a set threshold.
Sustainability
User Engagement: Gamified learning encourages continuous app usage, driving ad impressions and in-app purchases.
Scalability: Accessible pricing broadens the user base, increasing platform appeal for advertisers and sponsors.
Diverse Income Streams: Long-term partnerships, corporate sponsorships, and future marketplace opportunities provide financial stability and growth potential.
Solution Provider(s): We are self-funded and self sustained.
Implementation location(s): The users of the mobile application are all over the world in countries such as South Africa, USA, India, Malawi, Botswana, Vietnam,UK, Germany, Ukraine , Indonesia, Hong Kong ,Ireland, China, Saudi Arabia, Malaysia, Bangladesh, Canada , Kenya, Lesotho, Mexico, Mozambique, Netherlands, Pakistan , Romania , South Korea, Sudan , Tunisia,Yemen ,France and Thailand.
Implementation timeline(s): We we went Live in November 2024
Duration to pilot in a new geography: 1 months per country.
SDGs addressed: SDG 4 (Quality Education);SDG 10 (Reduced Inequalities);SDG 8 (Decent Work and Economic Growth);
Desired impact: Quaha will provide access to higher education to underserved communities.Through Quaha the communities will be able to further their education and thus make a positive impact in their families or in their respective communities whether it will be through learners getting access to job opportunities or starting their own businesses which I believe will employ people in their community, and reducing the unemployment challenges and economically uplifting  africa and the globe .
Key technologies:
Key Technologies Used for Quaha’s Solution: 
Proprietary Learning Management System (LMS)
Built in-house to support mobile-first delivery, gamified learning, and micro-course management.

Handles user progress tracking, content delivery, certification, and analytics.

Android/IOS Mobile App (Flutter)
Designed for low-data, offline-friendly environments.

Interfaces directly with the LMS to deliver seamless learning, quizzes, rewards, and certificates.

Gamification Engine
In-app virtual currency system (Quoins) to reward learning actions (e.g. quizzes, referrals, course completions).

Supports user motivation, progress milestones, and engagement tracking.

Digital Certificate and skills badge Generator
Auto-generates downloadable, shareable certificates for completed courses, integrated with user profiles.

Backend Infrastructure (Scalable Cloud-based Architecture)
Designed for high concurrency and modular growth.

Secure APIs for course content, user activity, and future third-party integration (e.g., institutions, employers).

Data Analytics & Insights Engine
Tracks learner engagement, content performance, quiz performance, and referral metrics.

Supports impact measurement, adaptive learning, and continuous course improvement.
Unique Characteristics:
1. Gamified Learning & Rewards System (Quoins Economy)
Quaha uses a virtual in-app currency (Quoins) to reward learning actions such as completing courses, answering quizzes, referring friends, and daily logins.

Learners can redeem Quoins to unlock premium courses, certificates, and future features—creating a self-sustaining loop of engagement and access.

No traditional tuition fees, removing financial barriers to education and shifting to an “earn-to-learn” model.

2. Mobile-First & Low-Data Learning for Underserved Communities
Unlike traditional e-learning platforms that assume laptop or high-speed internet access, Quaha is built for mobile users in low-bandwidth environments.

Courses are delivered in bite-sized, friendly modules, making it ideal for youth in under-resourced areas.

3. Job-Ready courses and Entrepreneurial Focus
Quaha focuses on practical, outcome-driven short courses in entrepreneurship, digital skills, and career development—not academic theory.

The platform provides business tools, templates, and startup guides to help users immediately apply their learning.

4. Flexible B2B/B2G Partnership Model
Quaha allows corporates, NGOs, governments, and educational institutions to:

Sponsor branded or impact-focused courses

Fund reward systems (Quoins)

Sponsor in-app quizzes and ad placements

Partner on upskilling, job-readiness, and ESG initiatives

This model creates shared value across the education, employment, and private sectors.

5. Alternative Financing Mechanism for Learners
Learners don’t need upfront payment—they earn access through engagement (learn-to-earn).

This model democratises education for youth who can’t afford traditional platforms or tuition.

6. Proprietary LMS Designed for Scale
Quaha’s backend includes a custom-built LMS specifically tailored for mobile learning, gamification, and in-app engagement.

It will support multi-tenant deployment, enabling white-label or institutional rollouts in the near future.

7. Social Impact + Scalable Monetisation
Quaha is aligned with SDGs (education, employment, inclusion) and is designed to scale across African markets with other emerging markets in mind.

Monetisation comes from in-app purchases, sponsored content, advertising, and future marketplace transactions .
Sustainable Change:
Millions of africans and other nations in emerging nations have challenges of access to quality, affordable, practical education that prepares people to be job-ready and entrepreneurship ready.Formal education is expensive, hard to access especially for those living in rural communities.
Quaha is a mobile-first education platform that is focused on job-readiness, entrepreneurship and digital skills for the future. Quaha reduces the barriers to entry from a cost and access point of view.Learners are rewarded with Quoins for completing modules, courses, quizzes and for referring friends. Learners will receive additional content, skills badges and certificates. This creates a sustainable learn to earn ecosystem.This encourages consistency, completions, continuity and removes the requirement for upfront fees thus making education accessible to those in underserved communities. Over time this will lead to people having access to employment and entrepreneurship opportunities to start their own businesses thus up-skilling the targeted population. With partners such as corporates, NGO's ,Institutions who we expect to sponsor quizzes , courses and to advertise, this will lead to a sustainable financing system/ model which will thus making education affordable to those using the Quaha app.Quaha's data insights and certification system allows partners to maintain their sustainability goals and their ESG goals with real education outcomes in the real world.
Funding Sources: I used my provident fund from my previous employment to fund the Quaha platform from design to implementation.
Further comments/feedback: You can download the "Quaha" app on Google Playstore or Huawei Gallery today.

Summary: Quaha is a mobile-first, gamified education platform designed to make higher education and job-ready skills accessible and affordable, especially for underserved youth in Africa. The solution leverages micro-learning, gamification (through its virtual currency Quoins), and a proprietary learning management system to improve course engagement and completion rates. Since its launch in November 2024, Quaha has begun piloting globally, including in Africa, Asia, and Europe. Its dual B2C/B2B model combines in-app purchases, advertising, and partnerships with corporates, NGOs, and governments, aiming to create sustainable education access at scale.

Title: Cross-Border Inclusive Commerce Hub for MSMEs (SEA)
Subtitle: AI-assisted export and payments enablement hub for B40/women-led MSMEs and potentially, legal migrant workers, leveraging interoperable QR rails and digital IDs in Malaysia and SEA.
Problem Statement: Across the Global South, MSMEs and informal sellers struggle to digitize, access markets, and receive affordable cross-border payments. In Malaysia and SEA, gaps include: low export-readiness among MSMEs, high remittance costs (often >5%), language barriers, fragmented regulations, and limited access to shariah-compliant microfinance. B40 and women entrepreneurs lack market intelligence and working capital; migrants and refugees face documentation/eKYC hurdles and limited financial inclusion.
Solution Overview:
We propose an Inclusive Digital Economy Hub that integrates three components:

AI Export Coach and Market Intel: An AI agent trained on trusted trade datasets (ITC Market Finder, Export Potential Map, Global Trade Helpdesk) plus local policy alerts. It outputs product–market fit, HS codes, buyer lists, and go-to-market steps in Malay/English/Mandarin/Bahasa Indonesia.

Inclusive Payments & Remittances Toolkit (this to discuss with partner potential as integration need some API and if there's easier way to do this): Merchant onboarding with eKYC via MyKad/MyDigital ID where possible; QR acceptance and cross-border payments using ASEAN QR linkages (DuitNow–PayNow–QRIS; PromptPay; QR Ph). Features include remittance comparison, transparent fees, and offline-first receipts for low-connectivity areas.

Capacity & Credit Readiness: Micro-courses for export marketing, digital storefronts, and record-keeping; shariah-compliant micro-invoice templates; referral pathways to microfinance partners.

Delivery and partnership 
Lead: ESM Agency (Malaysia), with 15+ years of market research, B2B lead gen, and training; co-trainer for ITC’s DEEP pilot; multilingual capabilities; track record with SMEs and corporates.
Payment Partners: Community of Malaysian PSPs/acquirers connected to PayNet/DuitNow; regional PSPs for cross-border routing.
Inclusion Partners: NGOs serving migrants/refugees (e.g., Tenaganita, UNHCR-linked community groups), community organizations in Sabah/Sarawak and Klang Valley.
Policy/Institutional Partners: SME Corp-linked programs; Islamic microfinance providers for shariah-compliant working capital; universities/accelerators for talent pipelines.
Alignment: Bank Negara Malaysia eKYC frameworks; MyDigital ID roadmap; ASEAN RPC milestones for QR interoperability.
Solution Provider(s): ESM Agency (market research/training, AI go-to-market), Payment Service Providers (DuitNow acquirers), Islamic microfinance partner (e.g., Amanah Ikhtiar Malaysia or equivalent), MSME associations (SME Corp-linked programs), NGO partners (migrant/refugee support), ITC tool alignment.

Title: Powernest Initiative
Subtitle: Solving Africa’s Power Crisis one PowerNest at a Time
Problem Statement: Millions of Africans suffer from the issue of inadequate power supply on-a daily basis. Even when there is power, frequent blackouts, terrible infrastructure and lack of adaptation to the individual needs of people make it unreliable and inefficient. Single plant and grid models are used for multiple different localities and communities. Some communities are neglected in general and have no connection to national or state grids. My project aims to resolve this issue into two ways.
Solution Overview:
How the solution works.
Every community is different, so we start on the ground. Before building anything, the team checks: Natural resources
	•	How much sunlight does the area get daily?
	•	Is the wind strong and consistent, especially at night?
	•	Is there a stream or small river that could support micro-hydro?
	•	What waste streams exist (market waste, animal dung, crop residue) that could support biogas?
	•	Community energy needs
	•	What’s the daily routine of power use? (Homes at night, markets during the day, welders in the afternoon, schools in the morning.)
This study makes sure each plant is designed to fit the local environment and lifestyle, not a one-size-fits-all model.

Next we Pick the Right Mix of Technologies
From the study, we then choose the best combination:
	•	Solar PV: Always the backbone. Panels on rooftops, carports, or open land where space allows.
	•	Wind: Only added if the site has proven wind data — typically hilly or open plateau areas. Helps balance solar at night.
	•	Battery Storage: Always included. Keeps supply running when sun or wind drops. Size depends on demand pattern.
	•	Backup Generator (biogas, biomass, or gas): Sits idle most of the time, but available when renewable + batteries can’t cope.
	•	Optional Micro-hydro: Where small rivers or streams exist, can add stable baseline power.
So the “energy recipe” changes from site to site:
	•	A market town might be solar + batteries + a gas genset.
	•	A fishing village might be solar + batteries + micro-hydro + biogas from fish waste.
	•	A windy plateau might be solar + wind + smaller batteries.

Optimized Interruption Technology (OIT) – The Brain: OIT is what makes the system reliable. Without it, even hybrid plants still blink or trip when switching sources. With OIT, the power feels like a strong city grid.
	•	Seamless switching: If clouds cover the sun, OIT quietly shifts to batteries before power drops. If batteries run low at night, OIT wakes the generator without lights blinking.
	•	Load prioritization: It knows which loads are critical (clinics, pumps, fridges) and protects them first. Non-critical loads (like decorative lighting) can be dropped temporarily.
	•	Motor protection: For welders, pumps, and mills, OIT smooths out dips so equipment isn’t damaged.
	•	Islanding: If the national grid is nearby but unstable, OIT lets the mini-grid run independently, then reconnect cleanly when the main grid stabilizes.
	•	Blackout scheduling: To reduce load on the grids, OIT schedules blackouts based on the date collected Im the community’s power usage routines, always when there is significantly less power usage or consumption. This is because 24/7 power may not be feasible in African countries but 18 hours power with 6 hours schedules blackout is a tolerable and negotiable starting point. This also helps prevent random blackouts as consumers and communities are informed ahead of time of the lack it schedule.

Methodologies and Technologies Used
	•	Site study: measure solar, wind, water, waste; map energy use; note land/security.
	•	System design: model the cheapest reliable mix with tools like HOMER Pro.
	•	Deployment: build modular plants that can expand or interconnect later.
	•	OIT integration: configure for each community’s critical loads 
	•	Community ownership: energy committees, trained local technicians, transparent pay-as-you-go metering.
Technologies
	•	Solar PV (mono panels) for baseline power.
	•	Wind turbines in windy areas.
	•	Battery storage: lithium-ion (daily cycling), flow batteries (longer backup).
	•	Backup gensets: biogas/biomass where waste exists, gas in peri-urban hubs.
	•	OIT: solid-state transfer switches, smart inverters, AI forecasting, IoT demand response, microgrid controllers.
	•	Smart meters & IoT for billing, monitoring, and load control.
Partnership model: The project is delivered through a Public–Private–Community Partnership, combining government support, private expertise and international investments.
Solution Provider(s): Nil
Duration to pilot in a new geography: The project can be deployed in phases over 3–5 years. The first 12–18 months cover site assessments, community engagement, regulatory approvals, and pilot installations. Years 2–3 focus on scaling across multiple communities with standardized designs adapted to local conditions. By years 4–5, the networks are fully operational, interconnected where possible, and managed largely by trained community teams. This phased approach ensures the solution is practical, affordable, and sustainable.
SDGs addressed: SDG 7 (Affordable and Clean Energy);SDG 9 (Industry, Innovation, and Infrastructure);
Desired impact:
Solution Objectives
Our goal is simple: give communities reliable, clean power that actually fits their reality. Each system is built around what the community already has, its geography, its resources, and its daily needs. By moving away from diesel and unstable grids, we’re not just powering homes and businesses, we’re also giving people ownership through training and participation. The bigger picture is to prove that this model can be scaled anywhere, showing that clean energy doesn’t have to be one-size-fits-all.

Key Achievements and Impacts
The change on the ground will be real. Families and businesses will have steady electricity and spend up to half as much compared to running generators. Emissions will drop sharply, in some cases by almost half, and at the same time new jobs will open up for young technicians, operators, and service providers in the community. What really builds confidence is the optimized interruption technology, people will see that even when there are supply shifts, the power stays on. And even where there are blackouts, they are orderly and scheduled. It makes them trust the system, and that trust is what keeps the project growing.
Key technologies:
Technologies (The Toolkit We Use)
	•	Solar PV Panels
	•	Monocrystalline (high efficiency, long lifespan).
	•	Rooftop, ground-mounted, or carport depending on land.
	•	Wind Turbines
	•	Small-to-medium scale (20–100 kW).
	•	Installed only where wind resource data proves it’s worth it.
	•	Battery Energy Storage (BESS)
	•	Lithium-ion for daily cycling.
	•	Flow batteries (like vanadium redox) for long-duration backup where needed.
	•	Backup Generators
	•	Biogas or biomass gensets where agricultural/market waste is available.
	•	Gas gensets in peri-urban areas for last-resort reliability.
	
Optimized Interruption Technology (OIT)
	•	Solid-State Transfer Switches (SSTS): millisecond switching, no flicker.
	•	Smart Inverters: sync solar/wind/battery seamlessly with the grid or gensets.
	•	Microgrid Controllers: the digital brain that balances supply and demand.
	•	AI Forecasting: predicts cloud cover, wind drops, and demand spikes in advance.
	•	IoT Demand Response: manages loads automatically (e.g., shifting water pumping to sunny hours).
	•	Smart Meters and IoT Controls
	•	Pay-as-you-go or prepaid models.
	•	Remote monitoring, real-time fault detection, and instant load control.
Unique Characteristics:
Power plants and grids are built to the specifications of the localities that need them. It gets rid of the “one model fits all” approach used by most electricity generation and regulatory bodies across Africa. OPTIMIZED INTERRUPTION TECHNOLOGY is a technology I have personally designed. It is the backbone of the grids or plants. It can;
•	Schedule blackouts smartly → planned, minimal, and evenly distributed so no community is unfairly affected.
	•	Reduce blackout time → cuts downtime compared to traditional grids, making outages shorter and less disruptive.
	•	Switch smoothly → shifts power between solar, batteries, and backup with little or no flicker.
	•	Balance supply and demand → spreads available energy fairly across households and businesses.
	•	Protect appliances → reduces damage from sudden surges or drops.
	•	Stabilize renewables → smooths out solar and wind fluctuations so power feels more reliable.
	•	Predict usage patterns → uses data to plan interruptions and adjust loads in advance.
	•	Build trust → communities know when blackouts will happen and see they’re shorter, so confidence in the system grows.
Sustainable Change:
Sustainable, Systemic Change and Theory of Change
Our solution drives systemic change by moving communities from unreliable fossil-based power to clean, locally tailored hybrid mini-grids. This shift cuts emissions, lowers household costs, and creates jobs while giving people the skills to manage their own energy.

The follow-on effect is a ripple: one community proves the model, others adopt it, and over time connected grids reduce pressure on national systems. The theory of change is simple: reliable clean power lead to empowered communities which lead to new opportunities which lead to scalable transformation.
Primary thematic focus area: Innovation Acceleration & Knowledge Sharing
Summary: The Powernest Initiative is a community-driven hybrid mini-grid solution tailored to Africa’s diverse local contexts. It combines solar PV, wind, micro-hydro, biogas/biomass, and battery storage with an innovative Optimized Interruption Technology (OIT) that ensures seamless switching, load prioritization, and scheduled blackouts. The approach emphasizes site-specific design, affordability, and community ownership through public–private–community partnerships. Though still at proof-of-concept stage, the initiative aims to deliver reliable, clean, and adaptable power to underserved communities, reduce reliance on fossil fuels, cut emissions, and create local jobs and trust in renewable energy systems.

Subtitle: Building digital skills and entrepreneurial talent among women, youth, and marginalized groups to spark inclusive innovation and drive community‑level opportunities.
Problem Statement:
Inclusive Digital Innovation Skills & Entrepreneurial Talent Development for Women in Eastern Province

In today’s fast‑changing world, digital skills and innovation are no longer optional—they are essential tools for growth, income generation, and participation in the modern economy. Yet, many women in Eastern Province, Zambia, still face serious barriers that prevent them from taking full advantage of these opportunities. This initiative seeks to change that by equipping women with the knowledge, tools, and confidence they need to thrive in the digital age.

Key Challenges Women Face in Eastern Province

Across Chipata, Katete, and other parts of Eastern Province, women remain a vibrant backbone of the community. They farm, trade, run small businesses, and care for families. However, a lack of digital literacy limits their ability to access wider markets or use online tools to grow their enterprises. Many women are not familiar with basic computer skills or mobile applications that could help them save money, keep records, or promote their products.

Connectivity is another challenge. Rural areas often lack reliable internet services and affordable devices. Even when connectivity is available, many women have not had training on how to use these tools effectively and safely. Cultural barriers also play a role, with some women discouraged from learning about technology or pursuing new business ideas. Without targeted support, these barriers leave women behind while others move forward in the digital economy.

How This Solution Responds to the Challenges

The Inclusive Digital Innovation Skills & Entrepreneurial Talent Development program is designed with women in mind. It starts at the community level, meeting women where they are and building on their strengths.

1. Digital Skills Training:
Through workshops and community learning circles, women will gain practical knowledge in using smartphones, computers, and internet platforms. Training will cover essential areas such as online safety, basic record‑keeping, and using digital marketplaces to sell goods and services.


2. Entrepreneurial Support:
Women will learn how to turn skills into income. Sessions will cover how to brand products, market through social media, and use mobile money systems for safer transactions. Practical demonstrations will show how even small village‑based businesses can reach customers beyond their immediate area.


3. Community Tech Hubs:
The initiative plans to establish or strengthen community tech hubs where women can access devices, internet, and mentorship. These hubs will become safe spaces for experimentation, collaboration, and learning—places where women can try out new ideas, meet role models, and develop confidence in their abilities.


4. Inclusion of Marginalized Voices:
Special attention will be given to women with disabilities and young mothers who often face additional barriers. Materials will be adapted for accessibility, and flexible learning schedules will ensure more women can participate without abandoning family responsibilities.



Expected Benefits for Women

By addressing the digital gap, this program will help women in Eastern Province access new economic opportunities. Farmers can learn how to check market prices online before selling crops, ensuring they get fair value. Market traders can advertise products on WhatsApp or Facebook, reaching customers in urban areas without leaving their villages. Craft makers can learn how to photograph and share their products, expanding their reach far beyond local fairs.

In addition, improved digital skills will help women access government services, learn about health and education opportunities, and even engage in community decision‑making through digital platforms. This empowerment is not only about technology; it is about giving women the tools to have a stronger voice in shaping their futures.

Title: Waiyor
Subtitle: A mobile wallet-powered platform enabling everyday Liberians to invest in local MSMEs, fostering inclusive finance and economic growth through accessible digital tools.
Problem Statement: In Liberia, over 86% of MSMEs lack access to formal financing due to collateral requirements, while millions of mobile money users have no investment options. This disconnect limits economic growth, financial inclusion, and entrepreneurship. Traditional banking systems exclude informal and rural businesses, and there are few platforms enabling low-income individuals to participate in investment or wealth creation. Waiyor addresses this gap by offering a mobile-based solution that bridges unbanked populations and underfunded MSMEs, enabling inclusive access to capital and sustainable economic empowerment.
Solution Overview:
How the Solution Works:

Waiyor is a mobile wallet-powered investment platform that connects everyday Liberians, including mobile money users with underserved MSMEs seeking capital. Users can browse vetted SMEs via a mobile app or USSD menu, choose investment packages (fixed or custom), and contribute funds directly through integrated mobile money services (MTN and Orange). Investors receive regular ROI updates via in-app and SMS notifications. SMEs apply through the app, and their submissions are reviewed through a combination of AI analysis and manual verification (for larger amounts). The platform ensures transparency through an admin dashboard that manages transactions, updates, and approvals.

Methodologies and Technologies Used:

User-Centered Design: Figma wireframes prioritize accessibility, simplicity, and trust for both smartphone and USSD users.
Mobile Money Integration: Leveraging APIs from MTN and Orange Money for seamless transactions.
AI-Powered SME Screening: Preliminary risk assessments and categorization based on data inputs (revenue, traction, sector, etc.).
USSD Accessibility: Enables participation from rural and low-literacy populations without smartphones or internet access.
Secure Cloud Infrastructure: Built on Microsoft Azure credits, ensuring scalability, data security, and uptime.
KYC/AML Compliance Layer: Basic KYC is triggered at the investment stage to meet financial regulations.

Partnerships and Collaboration Models:

Mobile Network Operators (planned): MTN Liberia and Orange Liberia for payment integrations and co-promotion.
SME Incubators/Accelerators: Planned partnerships with local business development hubs for SME pipeline quality and capacity building.
Diaspora Networks: Engaging Liberian diaspora investors to participate via mobile/web-based options.
Development Institutions (prospective): Intending to partner with UNDP, UNCDF, and local regulatory bodies to enhance financial literacy and digital trust.
Tecfa Inc. (Parent Company): Overseas development, compliance, and platform governance, ensuring mission alignment with inclusive digital growth.

Democratize Access to Investment: Enable everyday mobile money users especially youth, women, and rural populations to invest in local MSMEs with as little as $5.

Bridge MSME Financing Gaps: Provide an alternative financing channel for MSMEs that lack access to traditional loans or venture capital.

Promote Inclusive Digital Finance: Expand digital financial services to underserved communities via mobile app and USSD.

Stimulate Local Economic Growth: Drive job creation and income generation by funding scalable small businesses.

Key technologies:
Key Technologies Used in Waiyor

Mobile Money Integration (Fintech APIs)
Waiyor connects with mobile money platforms such as MTN and Orange Money using their APIs. This allows users to make investments and receive returns directly through their mobile wallets.

USSD Technology
Waiyor uses USSD (Unstructured Supplementary Service Data) to provide access for users without smartphones or internet. This simple text-based menu works on any mobile phone, making the platform inclusive.

AI-Powered Risk Analysis
Artificial Intelligence is used to analyze SME applications based on factors like revenue, business history, and growth potential. It helps categorize businesses by risk and supports informed decision-making.

Cloud Computing (Microsoft Azure)
The platform runs on Microsoft Azure for secure hosting, data storage, fraud monitoring, and scalability. This ensures stable performance and protection of user data.

Secure Data Handling and KYC Layer
Waiyor uses data encryption and Know Your Customer tools to verify users, prevent fraud, and comply with financial regulations.

Web and Mobile Technologies (React, Node.js)
The platform is built using modern web technologies to ensure fast performance, responsive design, and secure access across mobile and desktop devices.
Unique Characteristics:
Unique and Differentiated Characteristics of Waiyor

Inclusive Micro-Investment Model
Waiyor allows anyone with a mobile phone to invest in local businesses with as little as 5 USD. This opens up investment opportunities to low-income and unbanked populations who are typically excluded from formal financial systems.

Dual Access via App and USSD
The platform is accessible both through a mobile app and a USSD interface. This ensures that people in rural areas or without internet access can still participate fully, making Waiyor highly inclusive.

AI-Supported SME Screening
Waiyor uses AI to pre-screen SME applications based on business data, reducing human bias and speeding up the onboarding process while maintaining reliability.

Grassroots Financing Mechanism
Unlike traditional lending or crowdfunding platforms, Waiyor creates a closed-loop system where mobile money users directly support local MSMEs and receive returns. This community-driven investment cycle supports local economies.

Early Partnership with Telecom Operators
By working with MTN and Orange Money from the start, Waiyor is building a strong foundation for trusted mobile money integration, increasing adoption and reach.

Designed for Replication in Emerging Markets
Waiyor’s model is adaptable to other mobile-money-dominant countries across Africa and the Global South, making it a scalable and exportable solution for inclusive digital finance.
