Title: Art serving education: A laboratory of creativity.
Subtitle: MAS ART is a workshop that unites traditional art with digital tools to foster personal expression and promote local talent.
Problem Statement: The solution addresses the problem of traditional teaching by making it more immersive and interactive. It also takes on the challenge of preserving and transmitting history, geography, and national identity. By merging ancestral art with digital tools, MAS ART offers an innovative approach to education and culture, which arouses curiosity and stimulates learning. In addition, the solution incorporates an ecological aspect by using waste as raw material to create works of art, which contributes to the transformation of waste into objects of cultural and artistic value.
Solution Overview:
MAS ART is a creative workshop that merges ancestral art with digital tools. The solution operates as a 21st-century creativity lab. Its objective is to make art accessible to everyone, without barriers.
How the solution works
MAS ART offers training on the use of digital tools in crafts. The workshop promotes local and emerging talents. One of its key products is an educational puzzle of Guinea. This puzzle is not just a game; it is a pedagogical tool that immerses users in the country's history, geography, and identity. It aims to awaken curiosity and stimulate learning. The company targets various markets, including individuals, families, and passionate students; companies for team building and personalized events; schools and associations for educational partnerships and cultural projects; and tourists for a unique local artistic discovery.
Methodologies and technologies used
The methodology is based on merging ancestral art with digital tools. The workshop uses artistic creation as a solution to problems. By combining art and education, MAS ART creates an immersive learning tool. The educational puzzle is a concrete example of this approach.
Partnerships and collaboration models
MAS ART seeks partnerships and collaborations with companies and cultural institutions. The economic model includes revenues from workshops, the sale of materials and works, as well as cultural and business partnerships. The solution also aims to obtain grants and private patronage for its financing. MAS ART encourages artists to join its creative and dynamic team.
Solution Provider(s): Mohamed Alseny SYLLA (Founder / Director), Odia Noor Touré (Communications Manager), Habib Barry (Assistant), Laser Art Guinée (Partner Company).
Duration to pilot in a new geography: Research and adaptation (1-3 months): Study the local market, cultural specificities, and educational needs of the new geographical area to adapt the product. Partnerships (2-4 months): Establish collaborations with local schools, associations, or companies, which is a significant part of your growth model.  Production and training (2-3 months): Set up the production of adapted educational puzzles and train facilitators for the workshops. Launch and evaluation (3-6 months): Launch the pilot project, conduct the workshops, and gather feedback to assess the solution's success and impact. This period would allow for testing MAS ART's business model and educational approach before a larger-scale deployment.
SDGs addressed: SDG 4 (Quality Education);SDG 9 (Industry, Innovation, and Infrastructure);SDG 13 (Climate Action);
Desired impact: Our solution aims to make art accessible to everyone, promote personal expression, and support local artists. We provide training in digital tools for crafts, and our educational puzzle enhances learning about Guinea's history and culture. We target individuals, businesses, schools, and tourists, with a business model focused on workshops, sales, and partnerships. Our goal is to achieve financial stability within three years.
Key technologies: We use a laser cutter, 3D printer, crusher, and plastic waste processing machine to transform plastic waste into art and modernize traditional art.
Unique Characteristics:
Unique and Differentiated Characteristics of MAS ART
The solution stands out for its ability to merge ancestral art with digital tools. This approach creates an immersive learning experience that modernizes cultural heritage while making it accessible. The educational puzzle is a prime example of this fusion, transforming a traditional object into an interactive educational tool that promotes Guinea's history and identity.
Another unique aspect is the integration of a circular economy through the transformation of plastic waste into works of art. By using machines like a laser cutter, 3D printer, and crusher, MAS ART not only innovates artistically but also contributes to waste reduction. This positions the solution at the intersection of culture, education, and ecology.
Furthermore, the collaboration model is based on empowering MSMEs and local artists, offering them training so they can adapt to the digital age. The business model, which combines product sales, workshops, and corporate partnerships, ensures the solution's viability and growth.
Sustainable Change:
MAS ART's solution aims to create sustainable and systemic change by simultaneously addressing several interconnected challenges: cultural preservation, education, economic empowerment, and the environment.
Theory of Change:
 * In the short term, through the implementation of MAS ART, we will:
   * Modernize cultural heritage: By merging ancestral art with digital technologies, we preserve and revitalize artistic traditions to make them relevant for the modern era.
   * Strengthen skills: We train local artists and MSMEs on the use of digital tools (laser cutter, 3D printer, etc.), enabling them to develop new skills and access new markets.
   * Innovate education: The development of pedagogical tools like the educational puzzle about Guinea makes learning history and geography more immersive and interactive for younger generations.
   * Reduce waste: Integrating a plastic waste processing machine into our creation process directly contributes to the circular economy.
 * In the medium term, the effects of this solution will result in:
   * A strong local creative ecosystem: Trained artists and artisans will become more competitive, create their own businesses, and contribute to local economic growth.
   * A new approach to education: The success of our tools and workshops will inspire other educational institutions to adopt more creative, practical, and culturally-rooted teaching methods.
   * A shift in environmental mindset: By demonstrating the artistic and economic value of waste, we will transform the perception of plastic from a problem to a resource, encouraging more responsible management.
 * In the long term, the systemic and lasting effects will be:
   * Enduring cultural preservation: The transmission of ancestral art to future generations will be ensured through a modern and relevant approach.
   * A more resilient local economy: The empowerment of local creators and the valorization of resources (including waste) will stimulate inclusive and sustainable economic growth.
   * A more engaged society: By connecting individuals to their heritage through art and raising their awareness of ecological issues, we will contribute to the emergence of a society that is prouder of its identity and more conscious of its environmental impact.
Funding Sources: The solution was initially funded by private capital, specifically the personal funds of the founders. The company's business model is designed to ensure its future growth through revenue generated from workshops, product sales, and partnerships.
Testimonials and Endorsements: It not available
Further comments/feedback: Okay

Elle propose des ateliers de créativité et un puzzle éducatif sur l’histoire et la géographie du pays, tout en valorisant les déchets plastiques en objets artistiques (Q12, Q20). L’objectif est de moderniser l’enseignement, préserver l’identité culturelle et stimuler l’économie circulaire locale. Title: Meraky Learn : Learn, Share, Grow !
Subtitle: Empowering Ivorian learners through Meraky Learn: an inclusive online platform where instructors and communities connect to share knowledge and expand digital learning access for everyone
Problem Statement: In Côte d’Ivoire, many learners and instructors face barriers such as limited access to quality training, geographical dispersion, and high education costs. Meraky Learn provides an inclusive digital platform that connects learners, instructors, and educational communities, enabling remote learning and helping bridge the digital education gap
Solution Overview:
How the solution works:
Meraky Learn is an inclusive Ivorian e-learning platform where instructors create and publish courses, learners enroll and track their progress, and educational communities interact through live sessions and collaborative spaces. Certificates are delivered to validate acquired skills.

Methodologies and technologies used:
The platform is built on a responsive web architecture with cloud hosting, real-time notifications, progress tracking, data analytics, and automated digital certification. Mobile-friendly access ensures learning is available anytime, anywhere.

Partnerships and collaboration models:
Meraky Learn partners with independent trainers, educational institutions, and community organizations to expand access to digital learning across Côte d’Ivoire, fostering collaborative knowledge-sharing and inclusion.
Solution Provider(s): Currently, Meraky Learn is an independent initiative with no formal partnerships established yet. We are actively seeking collaborations with educational institutions, community organizations, and technology providers to expand our impact
Implementation timeline(s): Meraky Learn has been deployed since November, 19th 2024
Duration to pilot in a new geography: It takes seven to fourteen days to implement the solution in a new geography
SDGs addressed: SDG 17 (Partnerships for the Goals);SDG 4 (Quality Education);
Desired impact:
Solution Objectives:

Facilitate access to quality professional and continuous training for everyone, including remote or marginalized populations.

Strengthen learners’ digital and professional skills to improve their employability.

Promote digital inclusion by reducing the digital divide in Côte d’Ivoire and the region.

Create a dynamic learning community connecting learners, instructors, and businesses.


Key achievements or impacts:

Over 50 members registered and trained on the platform since its launch.

Contribution to reducing the digital divide by reaching rural or underserved areas.

Generation of direct and indirect jobs through instructor activities and platform-related services.
Key technologies: The key technologie used for our solution is Python
Unique Characteristics: Meraky Learn is an inclusive, career-oriented e-learning platform for Francophone Africa, offering self-paced and virtual classes, community discussions for peer learning, and full accessibility even in low-connectivity areas
Sustainable Change:
Theory of Change:

Action: Provide an inclusive online learning platform accessible to everyone, including underserved and rural communities.

Direct Effect: Thousands of learners acquire digital and professional skills, improving their qualifications and career prospects.

Systemic / Long-term Effect:

Sustainable increase in employability and reduction of unemployment.

Significant reduction of the digital divide in rural and marginalized areas.

Creation of a lasting educational ecosystem that connects instructors, learners, and businesses to drive continuous skill development and local economic growth.
Funding Sources: The solution has been developed and implemented using the company’s own internal funds (self-financing). No external funding or grants have been used so far.
Further comments/feedback: No further comments. Thank you for the opportunity.
Primary thematic focus area: Inclusive Digital Innovation Skills & Entrepreneurial Talent Development
Summary: Meraky Learn est une plateforme ivoirienne d’e-learning inclusive qui connecte apprenants, instructeurs et communautés éducatives pour démocratiser l’accès à la formation continue. Lancée en novembre 2024, elle offre des cours en ligne (auto-rythmés et interactifs), des certificats numériques, et des espaces collaboratifs. Déjà plus de 50 membres formés, avec une ambition d’élargir l’accès aux populations rurales et marginalisées (Q13, Q17).

Title: Pont Numérique
Subtitle: Une plateforme inclusive qui facilite l'accès aux compétences et technologies nécessaires ainsi qu'aux opportunités d'emploi pour les jeunes et les communautés marginalisées.
Problem Statement: La solution répond au manque d’accès à l’éducation numérique, à la fracture technologique, au chômage des jeunes et à l’exclusion des populations vulnérables dans l’économie numérique.
Solution Overview:
Notre solution est une plateforme numérique inclusive qui offre des formations gratuites en compétences numériques, entrepreneuriat digital et services en ligne. Elle cible les jeunes, les femmes et les populations marginalisées pour les intégrer efficacement dans l'économie numérique.

Méthodologies et technologies utilisées :
- Apprentissage hybride (en ligne et en présentiel): via une plateforme mobile accessible à faible bande passante.  
- Méthode participative : adaptation des contenus aux réalités locales.  
- Utilisation des technologies open source pour réduire les coûts et favoriser l’adoption locale.  
- Suivi personnalisé : mentorat en ligne, évaluations régulières, accompagnement vers l’auto-emploi.

Partenariats et modèles de collaboration :
- ONG locales et centres communautaires pour la diffusion des formations.  
- Universités et experts TIC pour la création de contenus.  
- Entreprises tech pour le parrainage, la fourniture de matériel ou le recrutement.  
- Institutions publiques pour l’ancrage dans les politiques nationales de transformation numérique.
Solution Provider(s): Partenaires principaux :   - ONG MJPP (Mouvement des Jeunes pour la Paix et la Prévention des conflits) : Organisation communautaire basée à Lomé, Togo, œuvrant pour la paix, l’inclusion et l’autonomisation des jeunes. Secteur : société civile / développement communautaire.   - Université de Lomé – Département des Sciences et Technologies* : Partenaire académique pour la co-création de contenus éducatifs numériques. Secteur : éducation supérieure / technologie.   - *Digital Africa* : Initiative panafricaine de soutien aux start-ups numériques. Secteur : innovation technologique / entrepreneuriat.   - *Ministère de l’Économie Numérique et de la Transformation Digitale du Togo* : Appui institutionnel pour l’intégration de la solution dans les politiques nationales. Secteur : gouvernance publique / numérique.    *Autres partenaires :   UNFPA Togo, Orange Digital Center, Jokkolabs, Plan International, AFD.
Duration to pilot in a new geography: Bien
SDGs addressed: SDG 16 (Peace, Justice, and Strong Institutions);SDG 9 (Industry, Innovation, and Infrastructure);SDG 10 (Reduced Inequalities);
Desired impact:
- Réduire la fracture numérique dans les zones rurales et marginalisées.  
- Favoriser l’inclusion numérique des jeunes, des femmes et des personnes vulnérables.  
- Renforcer l’employabilité à travers des formations digitales accessibles.  
- Créer un écosystème local autour de l’innovation et de l’entrepreneuriat numérique.

Principales réalisations/impacts 
- +4 500 bénéficiaires formés aux compétences numériques de base et avancées.  
- 37 % de femmes touchées dans les zones rurales.  
- 120 jeunes accompagnés dans la création de micro-entreprises numériques.  
- +15 partenariats locaux (ONG, communes, radios communautaires).  
- Réduction de l’exclusion digitale dans 10 localités défavorisées.  
- Contribution indirecte à la réduction de l’empreinte carbone via la dématérialisation des services.
Key technologies:
- Intelligence artificielle (IA) : pour l’analyse des données utilisateurs, la personnalisation des contenus pédagogiques et le suivi des progrès.  
- Applications mobiles et Web : plateformes légères compatibles avec les smartphones à faible capacité.  
- SMS interactifs : pour atteindre les zones sans accès Internet et permettre un apprentissage basique.  
- Radio communautaire numérique : pour diffuser des messages éducatifs et des capsules d'information.  
- Outils de visualisation de données (data viz): pour suivre l’impact en temps réel et ajuster les interventions.  
- Cloud computing : pour le stockage sécurisé et l’accès partagé des ressources pédagogiques.  
- Chatbots (bientôt intégrés) : pour l’assistance utilisateur automatisée en plusieurs langues locales.
Unique Characteristics:
Notre solution se distingue par :  
- Une approche communautaire centrée sur l’utilisateur final, avec des contenus co-créés avec les jeunes et les populations locales.  
- L’accessibilité hors ligne via des applications légères, SMS et radios communautaires, pour toucher les zones rurales non connectées.  
- L’intégration de l’éducation numérique avec des outils de sensibilisation civique et économique (alphabétisation financière, inclusion numérique, entrepreneuriat).  
- Un modèle collaboratif multi-acteurs, incluant ONG, startups, institutions publiques et universitaires, pour garantir impact et durabilité.  
- Une forte composante genre et inclusion*, visant à réduire la fracture numérique entre filles et garçons.
Further comments/feedback: Non
Primary thematic focus area: Inclusive Digital Innovation Skills & Entrepreneurial Talent Development
Summary: Pont Numérique is a digital inclusion platform targeting marginalized communities in Togo with blended learning, SMS access, and community partnerships (Q13, Q23). Its strength is the broad coalition of institutional partners including the Ministry of Digital Economy and Digital Africa (Q14). A weakness is the incomplete documentation of systemic contribution (Q25 = '3') and lack of funding and testimonials (Q27, Q28).

Title: EDU’Reparation-justice et éducation via le digital
Subtitle: Une solution numérique inclusive qui sensibilise les jeunes et les femmes à la justice réparatrice à travers l’éducation civique, l’histoire et les outils digitaux.
Problem Statement: Des millions de jeunes et de femmes en Afrique, notamment en zones rurales, sont exclus à la fois de l’éducation civique et de l’accès au numérique. Cette double marginalisation limite leur compréhension des injustices historiques et actuelles, et freine leur participation active à la société. Les contenus existants sur la justice réparatrice sont souvent inaccessibles, trop théoriques ou non contextualisés. De plus, la fracture numérique empêche l’appropriation communautaire des outils d’apprentissage modernes et inclusifs.
Solution Overview:
1. Description détaillée de la solution
EDU’RÉPARATION est une initiative numérique inclusive qui utilise l’éducation comme levier pour promouvoir la justice réparatrice et renforcer la conscience historique. Elle repose sur la création et la diffusion de contenus pédagogiques multimédias (vidéos, podcasts, infographies, BD numériques, modules interactifs) accessibles via une plateforme mobile et lors d’ateliers hybrides en présentiel. Ces contenus sont co-construits avec les communautés locales, traduits en langues régionales, et centrés sur les récits africains de résistance, de mémoire et de réparation.
L’objectif est de rendre la justice réparatrice compréhensible, vivante et accessible, notamment aux jeunes et aux femmes souvent exclus du discours juridique ou politique.

2. Méthodologies et technologies utilisées
	•	Approche participative : co-création des contenus avec les jeunes, les éducateurs, les historiens locaux, et les femmes leaders.
	•	Éducation populaire et storytelling : pédagogie basée sur des récits communautaires, des jeux de rôle, des saynètes filmées et des témoignages vivants.
	•	Technologies low-tech et mobile-first : plateforme mobile optimisée pour faibles connexions, avec possibilité d’accès hors ligne (via clés USB, QR codes, radios communautaires, etc.).
	•	Outils numériques : applications open-source pour le e-learning, WhatsApp/EduBot pour l’interaction, formats adaptés pour smartphones et tablettes.

3. Partenariats et modèles de collaboration
EDU’RÉPARATION fonctionne sur un modèle multi-acteurs :
	•	AJES (porteur du projet) : coordination, formation, mobilisation communautaire.
	•	Établissements scolaires et centres communautaires : lieux de diffusion des contenus.
	•	Historiens, juristes et chercheurs africains : validation des contenus.
	•	Partenaires techniques (ex. développeurs locaux, studios audio/vidéo) : production et hébergement.
	•	ONG et institutions internationales : appui financier, technique et diffusion régionale.

Ce modèle permet l’appropriation locale, l’impact durable et la réplicabilité du projet dans d’autres contextes africains.
Solution Provider(s): Ministère de l’éducation nationale et de la formation professionnelle, ministère de la Jeunesse et culture, ministère de la femme et famille
Duration to pilot in a new geography: 12 mois
SDGs addressed: SDG 4 (Quality Education);SDG 5 (Gender Equality);SDG 16 (Peace, Justice, and Strong Institutions);
Desired impact:
Objectifs de la solution :
	•	Renforcer l’accès à une éducation civique numérique pour les jeunes et les femmes des zones rurales ou marginalisées, en particulier sur les thématiques de justice réparatrice, mémoire historique et droits humains.
	•	Réduire la fracture numérique et éducative en développant des contenus accessibles, interactifs et multilingues, via des formats adaptés aux environnements à faible connectivité.
	•	Favoriser la participation citoyenne et le dialogue social, en outillant les communautés avec des connaissances et des compétences liées à la justice, à la réparation et à l’engagement communautaire.

⸻

Impacts attendus (quantifiables) :
	•	10 000 bénéficiaires directs (jeunes et femmes) touchés d’ici 2026 dans les régions pilotes à Djibouti et potentiellement dans d’autres pays africains.
	•	100 éducateurs communautaires et animateurs formés aux outils numériques de sensibilisation à la justice réparatrice.
	•	Lancement d’une plateforme mobile éducative, incluant une bibliothèque numérique, accessible gratuitement en ligne et hors-ligne.
	•	Création d’au moins 20 emplois directs et 50 emplois indirects, notamment dans la production de contenus, le développement mobile, l’animation communautaire et la gestion de projet.
	•	Renforcement de la cohésion sociale et réduction des tensions communautaires à travers des campagnes numériques participatives, basées sur le dialogue et la mémoire collective.
Key technologies:
•	Mobile-first platform : Une application mobile optimisée pour les faibles connexions internet, avec accès hors-ligne grâce au stockage local et aux mises à jour légères.
	•	Technologies open-source de e-learning (ex. Moodle, H5P) pour créer des contenus interactifs, multimédias et accessibles.
	•	Chatbots éducatifs basés sur l’intelligence artificielle légère (IA), pour accompagner les utilisateurs dans leur apprentissage, répondre aux questions fréquentes, et faciliter l’engagement.
	•	Formats numériques adaptés : podcasts, vidéos courtes, bandes dessinées numériques et infographies interactives, conçus pour être légers en données et facilement partagés via WhatsApp et autres messageries.
	•	Outils collaboratifs en ligne pour la co-création de contenus avec les communautés (Google Workspace, plateformes participatives).
	•	Systèmes d’analyse de données pour suivre l’usage, l’impact, et adapter les contenus aux besoins des bénéficiaires.
Unique Characteristics:
Unique and Differentiated Characteristics
	•	Approche communautaire participative : co-création des contenus avec les bénéficiaires (jeunes, femmes, leaders locaux), ce qui garantit une adaptation culturelle et linguistique unique, contrairement aux solutions standardisées.
	•	Intégration de la justice réparatrice dans un format éducatif numérique inclusif, un domaine peu exploré dans les outils numériques en Afrique, particulièrement en zones rurales.
	•	Modèle hybride de diffusion : combinaison innovante de numérique (mobile-first, hors ligne) et d’ateliers en présentiel pour maximiser l’impact et surmonter la fracture numérique.
	•	Partenariats multi-sectoriels solides (ONG locales, réseaux panafricains, experts juridiques, studios créatifs), assurant un écosystème durable et un soutien technique adapté.
	•	Utilisation de technologies open-source et accessibles pour garantir la scalabilité, la flexibilité, et la pérennité, sans dépendance aux solutions propriétaires coûteuses.
	•	Focus sur l’autonomisation des femmes et des jeunes via une éducation à la fois civique, historique et technologique, contribuant à une transformation sociale durable.
Sustainable Change:
Théorie du changement :
En renforçant les connaissances et la conscience des jeunes et des femmes sur la justice réparatrice, l’histoire collective et les droits humains via un accès numérique inclusif, EDU’RÉPARATION crée un effet boule de neige durable :
	•	Court terme : augmentation de l’accès à une éducation civique de qualité dans les zones marginalisées, réduction de la fracture numérique éducative, empowerment individuel des bénéficiaires.
	•	Moyen terme : amélioration de la participation citoyenne et du dialogue communautaire, renforcement de la cohésion sociale, émergence de leaders locaux formés et engagés dans la justice réparatrice.
	•	Long terme : transformation systémique des mentalités et des pratiques sociales autour de la justice, la réconciliation et l’inclusion, contribuant à une paix durable et à une gouvernance participative plus juste.

Effets de suivi souhaités :
	•	Des communautés capables de réclamer leurs droits de manière informée et organisée.
	•	Un réseau panafricain d’acteurs et de plateformes éducatives reproduisant le modèle dans d’autres régions.
	•	Une réduction durable des inégalités éducatives et numériques, favorisant une économie numérique inclusive.

Ce changement systémique est possible grâce à l’approche intégrée d’EDU’RÉPARATION, combinant technologie, éducation, participation et ancrage local.
Primary thematic focus area: Enabling Policies & Regulatory Innovation
Summary: EDU’RÉPARATION is a digital education initiative that promotes restorative justice and civic education for marginalized youth and women in Africa. The solution provides accessible, multimedia-based educational content (videos, podcasts, comics, interactive modules) through a mobile-first platform optimized for low connectivity and offline use. Content is co-created with communities, translated into local languages, and complemented by in-person workshops. The aim is to strengthen civic awareness, reduce the digital divide, and foster social cohesion and inclusion, with a target of 10,000 direct beneficiaries by 2026.

Title: Nourishing Innovation with Moringa: Building Africa's inclusive Digital Economy
Subtitle: Driving Inclusive Agri-Diigital Innovation through integration with a focus on nutrition and wellness.
Problem Statement:
Africa's smallholder farmers and MSMEs face barriers to entering the digital and mainstream economy due to:
- Low digital skills among rural women and youth, limiting access to markets and finance.
- Fragmented value chains that exclude small enterprises from regional and global trade. Lack on knowledge of what is takes to participate in said value chains.
- Weak digital infrastructure and policy gaps. Unstable supply chains especially for agro-processed products due to lack of digital traceability and logistics integration.
Solution Overview:
Kijani Blue's solution integrates digital innovation, agribusiness skills and inclusive empowerment across:
1. Inclusive Digital Innovation skills and entrepreneurial talent development- through training women and youth in digital literacy, e-commerce, financial inclusion and agri-tech applications. This includes embedding entrepreneurial training within agribusiness networks.
2. MSME Empowerment and Local Digital Innovation- through a digital platform and marketplace for MSMEs producing Moringa-based products and other indigenous superfoods. Access to digital payment systems for small producers.
3. Innovation acceleration and knowledge sharing- thought a digital agripreneur accelerator providing mentorship, innovation toolkits and business incubation for rural entrepreneurs. Knowledge exchange through a collaborative learning platform, workshops, case studies and learning partnerships.
4. Stable a resilient digital supply chains- through the use of blockchain enables traceability for Moringa oil and other products, ensuring quality and transparency for global buyers.
Solution Provider(s): Kijani Blue Agribusiness, Value Ed- An online Learning platform, AWIA- African Women in Agricukture- Agribusiness skills development
Duration to pilot in a new geography: 6 months
SDGs addressed: SDG 8 (Decent Work and Economic Growth);SDG 2 (Zero Hunger);SDG 4 (Quality Education);
Desired impact:
Kijani Blue Agribusiness seeks to empower women, youth, and MSMEs in Africa to actively participate in and benefit from the digital economy by creating resilient digital value chains in food, wellness, and natural beauty. The initiative aims to reduce inequality, enhance food security, and accelerate digital innovation that leaves no one behind.

Solution Objectives
•	Digital Skills and Inclusion: Equip 15,000 women and youth with practical digital literacy, entrepreneurial, and e-commerce skills by 2028.
•	MSME Empowerment: Integrate 5,000 MSMEs into digital platforms, enabling access to markets, finance, and supply chains.
•	Nutrition and Food Security: Supply AL’s High-Protein Moringa Cookies to at least 50 schools and 20 feeding schemes, addressing malnutrition with a superfood solution.
•	Resilient Supply Chains: Establish blockchain-enabled traceability for Moringa oil, Moringa products and cookies, plus some indigenous superfoods to secure quality, build buyer confidence, and stabilize export trade.

Key Achievements (Projected by 2028)
•	15,000+ women and youth gain digital entrepreneurship skills, creating pathways to sustainable income.
•	5,000 MSMEs linked to digital markets, with an average 30% increase in revenues.
•	50+ schools adopt AL’s High-Protein Moringa Cookies, improving nutrition for 20,000+ learners.
•	30% income growth for rural women farmers integrated into Moringa and indigenous crop value chains.
•	Blockchain-enabled traceability system operational for Natura Moringa Oil, strengthening Africa-to-Europe trade.
•	Creation of a replicable inclusive digital agribusiness model that can scale across Africa and globally.
Key technologies:
Kijani Blue Agribusiness applies digital and emerging technologies to strengthen inclusion, improve efficiency, and build resilient supply chains in agribusiness and wellness. Our solution integrates:

1.	Mobile and Digital Learning Platforms
Low-bandwidth mobile apps and SMS-based tools for digital literacy and entrepreneurship training targeting rural women and youth. Gamified learning and multilingual content for higher engagement.
2.	E-Commerce and Digital Marketplaces
A B2B/B2C platform connecting MSMEs, farmers, and cooperatives to regional and global buyers.
Mobile money and fintech integration to enable secure payments for unbanked communities.
3.	Blockchain and Digital Traceability
Blockchain-enabled traceability for Moringa oil and cookies, ensuring quality, transparency, and fair trade for buyers in Africa and Europe.
QR-coded product labels linking consumers directly to farmer stories and supply chain data.
4.	Data Analytics and Impact Measurement
Real-time analytics to monitor MSME performance, training outcomes, and market trends.
Dashboards to track impact metrics (income growth, nutrition outcomes, supply chain resilience).
5.	AgriTech and IoT-Enabled Tools (Future Integration)
Pilot use of IoT sensors and smart drying/processing units for post-harvest loss reduction.
Satellite-based monitoring for crop yields and climate resilience.
6.	Cloud-Based Knowledge Sharing Hub
A digital library and community of practice for knowledge exchange, case studies, and open-source toolkits supporting agripreneurs across Africa.
Unique Characteristics:
Kijani Blue Agribusiness offers more than just a digital innovation project, we provide a human-centered, Africa-rooted, and wellness-driven approach to inclusive digital economies. Our uniqueness lies in four dimensions:

1. Human-Tech Interface
We design technology for accessibility, usability, and cultural fit. Training is delivered via low-bandwidth mobile platforms, SMS tools, and multilingual content, ensuring even rural women and youth with limited access can engage. By combining face-to-face mentorship with digital learning, we bridge the gap between advanced technology and real-world accessibility.

2. Partnership with Value Ed
Through our collaboration with Value Ed, we integrate entrepreneurship education, soft skills, and financial literacy into digital training. This ensures that beneficiaries are not just digitally literate but also equipped with the confidence and business acumen to thrive as digital entrepreneurs.

3. Promotion of Indigenous Superfoods and Plant-Based Proteins
Unlike generic digital inclusion programs, our innovation is rooted in Africa’s indigenous crops; from Moringa to Bambara nuts and cassava. By digitizing value chains for AL’s High-Protein Moringa Cookies, we simultaneously address nutrition gaps, school feeding, and market access. This places Africa’s heritage crops at the centre of global conversations on plant-based proteins and clean nutrition.

4. Organic Oils for Healthy Skin and Wellness
Our Natura Moringa Oil positions Africa as a leader in quality organic, natural beauty and wellness solutions. By linking smallholder farmers to digital traceability tools and global cosmetic markets, we enable inclusive participation in the high-value wellness economy, ensuring that rural producers benefit from international demand for ethical, plant-based products.

 In short, our solution is different because it fuses digital inclusion with wellness, culture, and sustainability. We don’t just train people to use technology; we connect them to meaningful, future-ready value chains that nourish, empower, and inspire.
Sustainable Change:
Kijani Blue Agribusiness was born out of a need to create sustainable and systemic change for the women and youth with whom we were engages. This solution is designed not only to deliver immediate benefits but to reshape the underlying systems that keep women, youth, and MSMEs excluded from the digital economy. Our model creates sustainable, long-term change through four levers:

1. Building Human Capital for the Digital Economy
By equipping women and youth with digital literacy, entrepreneurial skills, and access to e-commerce, we enable them to become active participants and leaders in digital economies. Skills are transferable across industries, ensuring long-term adaptability and resilience.

2. Strengthening Local Value Chains with Technology
We integrate indigenous superfoods, plant-based proteins, and organic oils into digital supply chains, positioning local MSMEs within high-value global markets. This shifts communities from subsistence farming to sustainable commercial participation, reducing dependence on aid.

3. Embedding Policy and Ecosystem Support
Through advocacy and knowledge-sharing, we influence policy frameworks that promote inclusive digital trade, fair competition, and rural participation. Embedding digital innovation into governance and industry standards ensures the impact is institutionalized and scaled.

4. Creating Self-Sustaining Market Systems
Our model links producers, MSMEs, schools, and international buyers through digital platforms, blockchain-enabled traceability, and e-commerce. This creates closed-loop, resilient markets where rural producers benefit from demand while buyers access trusted, traceable, ethical products.

Systemic Change Pathway
Short-term (1–2 years): Women, youth, and MSMEs gain skills, access markets, and improve incomes.
Medium-term (3–5 years): Digital agribusiness ecosystems flourish, indigenous crops become mainstream in nutrition and wellness markets, and policy frameworks start reflecting inclusive models.
Long-term (beyond 5 years): A self-sustaining, inclusive digital economy where marginalized groups are permanent stakeholders in Africa’s transformation, not temporary beneficiaries.

In essence, Kijani Blue doesn’t just solve today’s digital divide , it reshapes systems of education, trade, and agriculture so that digital innovation becomes an engine of socio-economic development, equality, resilience, and opportunity.

Title: Womenovate Innovation Zone - WIZ
Subtitle: A digital platform addressing unemployment in Africa
Problem Statement: Youth unemployment in Africa is a significant challenge, with millions of young people lacking employment, education, or training. The COVID-19 pandemic exacerbated this issue, and skills mismatch between education and labor market demands further contributes to the problem.
Solution Overview:
The Innovation Zone is a dynamic platform designed to provide hands-on learning, collaboration, and problem-solving opportunities to bridge the gap between academic knowledge and industry needs, addressing skills mismatch by creating a structured environment where interns can engage in real-world projects, interact with industry experts, and develop innovative solutions to contemporary challenges.
 
Also bridge the employment gap by empowering users with disabilities to develop job-ready skills, build confidence, and connect with inclusive employers.

Implementation Strategy
● Phase 1: Pilot Program — Launch a pilot initiative with a selected group of interns, mentors, and industry partners, targeting 20 beneficiaries across five regions of Nigeria.
● Phase 2: Expansion and Scaling — Based on pilot feedback, refine the program and expand participation to a larger pool of interns, reaching the full target of 100 beneficiaries nationwide.
● Phase 3: Long-Term Sustainability — Establish the Innovation Zone as a sustainable initiative through strategic partnerships, sponsorships, and integration into national digital economy strategies.
Solution Provider(s): Womenovate
Duration to pilot in a new geography: 8  weeks per cohort
SDGs addressed: SDG 4 (Quality Education);SDG 8 (Decent Work and Economic Growth);SDG 10 (Reduced Inequalities);
Desired impact:
Solution Objectives:
● Foster a culture of innovation and creativity among technical interns.
● Provide a structured platform for skill development through experiential learning.
● Enable interns to work on real-world projects with industry relevance.
● Encourage collaboration between interns, mentors, and industry stakeholders.
● Support capacity building and workforce readiness in emerging technologies.
● Contribute to the achievement of UN Sustainable Development Goals (SDGs), particularly SDG 4 (Quality Education), SDG 5 (Gender Equality), and SDG 8 (Decent Work and Economic Growth).
Key technologies: AI, IoT, Wireframe
Unique Characteristics:
The solution is unique and innovative due to its intentional inclusivity, practical learning-to-employment pipeline, and future-forward design that not only trains but also empowers underrepresented youth to lead in tech - not just participate.

1. Targeted Inclusitivity - Underrepresented groups focus: Unlike general upskilling programs, it intentionally prioritizes women, youth, and marginalized communities who often face systemic barriers in tech (e.g., lack of mentors, cultural stereotypes, digital access).

Intersectional approach: Recognizes that these groups don’t just need skills, but also confidence, networks, and visible role models to thrive.

2. Holistic Talent Pipeline Development - Goes beyond training to integrate career pathways: internships, apprenticeships, mentorship, and job placement.

Bridges the gap between academic knowledge and industry requirements, ensuring participants are not just skilled but also employable.

3. Accessibility and Flexibility - Designed to be low-cost or no-cost, with remote and hybrid options, so youth in underserved areas can participate.

Incorporates localized content (e.g., case studies, African/African diaspora tech challenges) so participants see themselves in the solutions.

4. Experiential Learning - Moves away from purely theoretical training to hands-on, project-based learning, hackathons, real-world case challenges, and applied research.

Encourages participants to build portfolio-worthy projects that directly demonstrate competence to employers.

5. Supportive Ecosystem - Mentorship from diverse professionals (especially women in STEM) provides guidance, networking, and inspiration.

Community-building: participants don’t just learn skills—they become part of a peer-support network, reducing isolation and attrition in tech.

6. AI and Emerging Tech Integration - Not just coding basics, but exposure to AI, data, cloud, cybersecurity, and green tech—future-proofing participants’ skills. Embeds responsible and ethical tech training so underrepresented voices shape the future of technology.

7. Industry–Academia–Policy Linkages - Bridges silos by aligning academic institutions, industry employers, and government initiatives. Provides industry-relevant certifications co-designed with employers so participants are workforce-ready on day one.
Sustainable Change:
Designed for undergraduate and graduate technical interns, early-career professionals, and individuals transitioning into technology fields. It is particularly focused on youth and underrepresented groups in the tech industry, such as women and individuals with disabilities and from marginalized communities.
● Enhanced technical competencies and industry-relevant skills among interns.
● Increased employability and workforce readiness.
● Strengthened collaboration between academia, industry, and government.
● Development of innovative solutions with potential real-world impact.
● A strong pipeline of skilled technical talent contributing to national and global innovation ecosystems.
● Nationwide impact, empowering 100 beneficiaries with hands-on experience and career development opportunities.
● Contribution to the Nigerian economy by creating a steady flow of skilled tech professionals ready to drive digital transformation and innovation.
● Advancement of SDG goals, particularly promoting gender equality, quality education, and decent work and economic growth.

Summary: Womenovate Innovation Zone (WIZ) is a pilot-stage digital platform aimed at reducing youth unemployment in Nigeria by bridging the gap between academic knowledge and industry demands. It provides structured experiential learning, mentorship, and real-world project opportunities, with a focus on inclusivity for women, youth, and marginalized groups. The initiative is supported by partners, with a pilot running in March–May 2025, and aims to scale nationwide. Title: AI Solutions for Inclusive and Scalable Social Commerce
Subtitle: Socella empowers underserved businesses to launch, grow, and scale on social media, delivering a full-service agency experience without the high costs or limitations.
Problem Statement: Small businesses struggle to compete on social media due to high marketing costs, fragmented tools, and limited expertise. This leaves many underserved entrepreneurs unable to grow or scale effectively.
Solution Overview:
How it works

Socella uses a multi-tier agent system that allows users to run their entire social media operations through chat.

User can:

- Generate and schedule across 13 social media platforms.
- Manage and automate customer conversations and DMs.
- Convert interactions into sales using built-in commerce tools.
- Create AI self-portraits, reels, and more.

Methodologies and technologies:

Artificial Intelligence:

- Fine-tuning foundational models for specific tasks.
- Retrieval-augmented generation for brand knowledge, FAQs, and product data.
- Vision models for headshots, reels, and creative assets.
- Sentiment and intent analysis for smarter automation of customer messages.
- Agent Architecture
- Orchestrator agent interprets user requests and delegates to specialist agents.
- Specialist agents for content, community management, commerce, and insights.

Infrastructure:
- API integrations with 13+ platforms for publishing and inbox management.
- Cloud storage for assets, secure data handling, and privacy-first design.
- Scheduling optimization for best posting times and formats.

Partnerships and collaboration models:
- Ayrshare for cross-platform publishing and analytics.
- Supabase for authentication, database, and storage.
- Replicate for hosting and scaling custom AI models.
- Hostinger for infrastructure and rapid deployment of mini-tools.
- Payment gateways (Paystack) for integrated commerce flows.
Solution Provider(s): Socella Inc. – AI-powered social business platform (Technology/AI & Social Commerce), Cloudplexo – Cloud architecture consulting firm specializing in AWS (Technology/Cloud Infrastructure), Amazon Web Services (AWS Activate) – Startup support program providing cloud credits, GPU resources, and technical guidance (Technology/Cloud Computing).
Duration to pilot in a new geography: 1-3 months
SDGs addressed: SDG 8 (Decent Work and Economic Growth);SDG 9 (Industry, Innovation, and Infrastructure);SDG 10 (Reduced Inequalities);
Desired impact:
Solution Objectives:

- Improve digital inclusion by giving MSMEs access to growth tools typically reserved for well-funded companies.
- Create new pathways for youth- and women-led businesses to actively participate in the digital economy.
- Provide alternative career opportunities for talent displaced or at risk due to AI-driven job shifts.
- Drive sustainable business growth in developing economies by enabling social-media–driven commerce.

Key Achievements / Impacts

- Digital inclusion: Early pilots show up to 70% cost savings by using Socella instead of full-service agencies, giving MSMEs access to enterprise-level growth tools at small business prices.

- Youth and women-led businesses: 100% of our early adopters are youth or women founders, demonstrating Socella’s role in unlocking new opportunities for underrepresented entrepreneurs.

- Alternative career pathways: Supporting 1,000+ social media managers with skill-building and AI-powered tools to help businesses maximize value and adapt to the future of work.
Key technologies:
Artificial Intelligence (AI)
Machine Learning (ML)
Web Technologies
Unique Characteristics:
Socella is differentiated by its multi-tier agent system that enables users to manage their entire social media operation through chat. This layered AI approach goes beyond single-use automation to cover the full cycle of content, conversations, and commerce in one seamless flow. By integrating scheduling, customer engagement, and sales conversion into a single platform, Socella eliminates the need for MSMEs to juggle multiple costly tools.

What makes the solution especially unique is its inclusive business model. Socella is deliberately priced and designed to bring enterprise-grade growth tools within reach of MSMEs, youth, and women-led businesses who are often excluded from digital transformation. In addition, its integrated AI mini-tools, such as AI self-portraits and Reels generators, equip small businesses with creative capabilities usually reserved for expensive agencies. Coupled with a commerce-first approach that directly converts social interactions into sales, and a scalable architecture built on AWS and partner integrations, Socella offers an innovative combination of technology and accessibility that sets it apart from traditional SaaS and agency solutions
Sustainable Change:
Socella creates systemic change by democratizing access to digital growth infrastructure. By solving for how business actually operate on social media; we give MSMEs, youth, women-led and other underserved businesses tools that traditionally only well-funded enterprises could access. We level the playing field and enable sustainable participation in the digital economy.

The follow-on effects are multi-layered:
	•	Economic empowerment: MSMEs can scale affordably, contributing to job creation and local economic growth.
	•	Workforce transformation: By supporting displaced talent with alternative career pathways in social media and digital commerce, we create resilience in the face of AI-driven job disruption.
	•	Ecosystem ripple effect: As more businesses adopt Socella, network effects strengthen, creating a more inclusive digital ecosystem where small players are visible and competitive.
	•	Long-term sustainability: The affordability and scalability of the solution ensure it is not a short-term fix but a permanent enabler of digital inclusion across developing economies
Primary thematic focus area: MSME Empowerment & Local Digital Innovation
Summary: Socella is an AI-powered social commerce platform designed to help MSMEs, youth, and women-led businesses run their entire social media operations through a multi-agent system. It enables content creation, scheduling, customer engagement, and direct sales conversion within one chat-based interface. By integrating 13+ social platforms, AI creative tools, and payment gateways, Socella delivers an affordable alternative to costly marketing agencies. Early pilots show 70% cost savings and strong adoption among youth and women entrepreneurs, with potential to scale globally within 1–3 months per new market.

Title: “Digital Bridge: Empowering Underserved Communities for Inclusive Growth”
Subtitle: Empowering underserved communities with digital tools to bridge the economic divide, fostering inclusive growth and equitable access to digital opportunities.
Problem Statement: Our solution addresses limited digital access and skills in underserved communities, which hinder economic participation and growth. It tackles barriers to connectivity, digital literacy, and inclusion.
Solution Overview:
Our solution leverages a mobile-first platform that provides affordable internet access combined with tailored digital literacy training for underserved communities. Using adaptive learning technologies and AI-driven content personalization, users receive education that matches their skill level and local language.

We employ cloud-based infrastructure to ensure scalability and reliability, integrating offline capabilities to accommodate low-connectivity areas. The platform includes interactive modules on digital skills, financial literacy, and entrepreneurship, empowering users to engage fully in the digital economy.

Partnerships are key: we collaborate with local NGOs for community outreach, telecom providers for connectivity, and government agencies to align with national digital inclusion policies. This multi-stakeholder approach ensures regional embeddedness, local ownership, and sustainable impact.

Title: Bridge the in education for deaf children and youth through Technology and AI
Subtitle: Leveringing AI and Technology to make education accessible for deaf learners, ensuring no deaf child and youth is left behind in the digital economy
Problem Statement: Globally,Over 70 million people are deaf (WHO,2023) With 34 million children. In tanzania alone, an estimated 1.2 million people live with hearing impairements, yet less than 5 of deaf children and youth access high quality education, inclusive education. Most education institute lack of sign language resources, affordable hearing aids, and digital learning tools. As result, deaf children end perform poorly on their studies most science subjects and also take longer up to 10 years to finish primary school, remain excluded from the digital solutions, they risk being permanent left behind in education and economic opportunities.
Solution Overview:
Over two years hearing the unheard has been supporting deaf learner with school materials, sign language books, sign language training and awareness campaigns. we have directlt reached to 200+ deaf across Dar es salaam Tanzania. While these efforts improved classroom engagement, we observed that deaf children and youth we are still excluded from digital resources and can not keep up with peers in science,mathermatics and ICT subjects. 

The gap les us to adopt technology-driven solution, after see that deaf are not aware of different new technology tools which are important for education. Like the increase of the use of Artficial Intelligence ( AI) where by its a new term to them and it need for them to be educated on it and to give it sign which will help them to identify it, but all this has been hard due to the fact that all information about technology is in auditory form.

After see this, Hearing the unheard we have come with the idea of creating a learning system which will be called (JIFUNZE KIMYA- ( LEARN IN SILENCE). Where by the system will be conatin of different learning materials, where by a deaf learner will be able to log in in his/her account and click on the subject of their preference, the system also will give chance for them to do quizzes, get digital skills on the platform. The system will be directly intergreted with AI-powered Avatar which will be giving explain and answer question in any contents, with visual aids, where by the AI avatar will be able to sign in Tanzania sign Language with hand motions and face expressions,

Methodologies
Methodologies and Technologies Used
To ensure Jifunze Kimya is a robust, accessible, and user-friendly learning system for deaf learners, we are applying the following methodologies and technologies:
1. User-Centered Design (UCD) & Accessibility First
We follow Human-Centered Design (HCD) principles, working directly with deaf learners, teachers, and interpreters to co-design features.
Accessibility standards (WCAG 2.1) and Universal Design for Learning (UDL) frameworks ensure inclusivity.
2. Modular & Scalable System Architecture
Backend built with Node.js + Express for scalability.
Database: PostgreSQL for structured data (users, progress, quizzes) and MongoDB for unstructured content (videos, sign animations).
API-first design to allow integration with future EdTech tools.
3. Interactive Learning Platform
Web & mobile (Android-first, React Native for cross-platform) for accessibility across devices.
Learning Management System (LMS) features: login, subject modules (Math, Science, ICT), quizzes, and progress tracking.
Offline access (using Progressive Web App, PWA) to support learners with limited connectivity.
4. AI-Powered Sign Language Avatar
Developed using Unity 3D or Blender for 3D avatar modeling.
Integrated with Natural Language Processing (NLP) models (OpenAI GPT or Hugging Face models) for content understanding.
Sign rendering engine: trained on Tanzanian Sign Language datasets for accurate handshapes, motions, and facial expressions.
Avatar capable of real-time signing responses to user queries.
5. Digital Skills Integration
Modules on basic computer literacy (typing, internet use, Microsoft Office).
21st century digital skills: coding basics (Scratch, Python visual blocks), introduction to AI concepts, online safety, and digital financial literacy.
6. Data Collection & Feedback Loops
Analytics dashboard for teachers & admins: monitors learner performance, most accessed modules, and progress.
Built-in feedback forms for continuous platform improvement.
7. Security & Data Privacy
Compliance with GDPR principles and Tanzania’s Data Protection Act.
End-to-end encryption for learner data and secure logins (OAuth2 / Firebase Authentication).

Mugabe Primary School and Mzambarauni Primary School (Dar es Salaam): pilot sites integrating the solution with classroom learning.
Local NGOs and advocacy groups (e.g., Tanzania Assoc
Solution Provider(s): Tanzania sign Langauage Experts ( Mr. James Yona- Is a teacher and expert in Tanzania sign language with over 3 years of experience work with deaf people), Peach Tech knolwodge ( Henry Maliseli - IT expert with proffesional in web development, App and system creation and businness development) Schools ( MAdam Amina Katula- Head of special need depatment)

Title: _MEFAR : Une machine locale pour moderniser la boulangerie artisanale ;Digitaliser la fabrication de pain avec la machine MEFAR  ; _ MEFAR : Transformer la boulangerie locale grâce à l’innovation technique  ;_Une solution accessible pour automatiser la production de farine;  _ MEFAR : L’innovation au service de la souveraineté alimentaire locale  _Innover pour nourrir : MEFAR, machine numérique de transformation alimentaire  ;MEFAR : Fabriquer local, nourrir durable, connecter les communautés
Subtitle: 2.   Une solution technique abordable pour automatiser la transformation de la farine et moderniser les boulangeries rurales.  3.   Une machine innovante, conçue localement, pour améliorer l’accès à des outils de production modernes dans les zones à faibles ressourc  MEFAR propose une technologie locale adaptée aux boulangers pour booster la production et l’inclusion économique.
Problem Statement: Dans de nombreuses régions rurales et semi-urbaines, les boulangers font face à un manque d’équipements adaptés, abordables et disponibles localement pour transformer efficacement la farine et produire du pain. Ce déficit limite la productivité, augmente la pénibilité du travail, freine l’innovation locale et aggrave la dépendance aux équipements importés coûteux. De plus, l’absence de solutions techniques accessibles empêche l’intégration des jeunes dans les chaînes de valeur agroalimentaires et freine le développement économique inclusif.
Solution Overview:
MEFAR est une solution technique innovante qui consiste en la conception et la fabrication locale d’une machine mélangeuse de farine, destinée aux boulangers et pâtissiers. Cette machine permet de mélanger automatiquement les ingrédients de base (farine, eau, levure, etc.) avec une meilleure homogénéité, réduisant ainsi le temps, la pénibilité et les erreurs humaines lors de la préparation de la pâte.
Elle fonctionne à l’aide d’un moteur électrique (courant alternatif ou continu selon l’environnement) et comprend une cuve en acier inoxydable, un système de commande simple, et une structure robuste adaptée aux conditions locales. Cette solution est entièrement conçue et fabriquée localement pour assurer un coût réduit, une maintenance facile et une meilleure accessibilité.
Solution Provider(s): Institut Supérieur de Technologie de Mamou (IST Mamou) Profil : Établissement d’enseignement supérieur spécialisé en technologie et ingénierie, Secteur : Éducation et recherche technologique. Rôle : Apport technique et expertise en conception et simulation de la machine MEFAR, Entreprise locale de mécanique industrielle "Mamou Mécanique" Profil : Atelier de fabrication et réparation de machines industrielles. Secteur : Industrie mécanique. Rôle : Fabrication des pièces métalliques et assemblage de la machine.  Fournisseur local de composants électriques "ElectroTech Guinée" Profil : Fournisseur spécialisé en matériel électrique et électronique, Secteur : Équipement industriel. Rôle : Approvisionnement en moteurs, capteurs et circuits électriques pour la machine.  Association des Femmes Entrepreneurs de Mamou (AFEM) Profil : Association promouvant l’entrepreneuriat féminin et l’inclusion économique. Secteur : Développement communautaire. Rôle : Promotion et diffusion de la machine auprès des femmes boulangères.
Implementation location(s): La solution est encore au stade de prototype et n’a pas encore été déployée. Une première mise en œuvre est prévue à Mamou (Guinée) une fois le prototype finalisé.
Implementation timeline(s): La solution est encore au stade de prototype et n’a pas encore été déployée. Une première mise en œuvre est prévue à Mamou (Guinée) une fois le prototype finalisé.
Duration to pilot in a new geography: Durée estimée pour piloter la solution dans une nouvelle géographie  La durée estimée est de 3 mois, incluant :  La préparation logistique et la mobilisation des acteurs locaux,  La fabrication et l’installation de la machine MEFAR,  La formation des utilisateurs, ainsi que le suivi et l’évaluation de la phase pilote.
SDGs addressed: SDG 1 (No Poverty);SDG 3 (Good Health and Well-being);SDG 9 (Industry, Innovation, and Infrastructure);
Desired impact:
Nos Objectifs de la solution 
_Faciliter la transformation locale des farines à travers une machine adaptée, accessible et facile d’utilisation.
_Réduire la pénibilité du travail manuel dans la production de pain et d'autres produits céréaliers.
_Favoriser l’autonomisation économique des jeunes et des femmes par la création d’activités dans la chaîne de valeur agroalimentaire.
_Encourager l’utilisation d’équipements conçus localement pour renforcer l’innovation technique en Guinée.
Principales réalisations/impacts attendus :
_Création de 10 à 20 emplois directs lors du déploiement pilote (opérateurs, techniciens, formateurs).
_Réduction du temps de travail de 60 % par rapport aux méthodes de mélange manuel.
Augmentation de la capacité de production de pain de 40 à 50 % dans les boulangeries équipées.
_Dynamisation des économies locales rurales, avec un accès facilité à un outil de production.
Réduction de l’importation d’équipements coûteux, grâce à la fabrication locale de la machine.
Key technologies:
La solution MEFAR repose sur les technologies suivantes :
Mécanique appliquée : conception et assemblage d’un système de mélange par rotation, avec des composants simples et robustes adaptés aux conditions locales.
Électrotechnique : utilisation d’un moteur électrique à courant alternatif pour actionner le système de mélange, avec un contrôle de la vitesse si nécessaire.
Fabrication locale assistée par ordinateur (CAO) : les plans et simulations du mélangeur sont réalisés à l’aide de logiciels de modélisation 3D (type SolidWorks ou AutoCAD), permettant d’optimiser la conception avant fabrication.
NB : Le projet MEFAR ne fait pas encore usage de technologies numériques avancées (IA, IoT, blockchain), mais pourrait à long terme intégrer des capteurs de température ou des systèmes de comptage pour améliorer la traçabilité.
Unique Characteristics:
Caractéristiques uniques et différenciées de la solution MEFAR (version simplifiée)

Title: Onedigitale Innovation Academy
Subtitle: The Diginova Center is an inclusive platform that will equip women, entrepreneurs and startups with innovative digital skills, knowledge, and attitudes necessary to succeed in the domain of Artificial Intelligence. its slogan: African Intelliegence In Action.
Problem Statement:
1. Limited Data Infrastructure & Availability
Challenge: Lack of large-scale, high-quality, localized datasets (especially in African languages and sectors like agriculture, health, and Infrastructure).
Impact: Limits training of accurate, context-aware AI models.
Example: Few open datasets for rural healthcare or indigenous knowledge systems.

2. Inadequate Digital Infrastructure
Challenge: Poor internet connectivity, limited access to electricity, and weak computing infrastructure (especially in rural areas).
Impact: Restricts access to cloud computing, AI tools, and platforms.
Example: Cloud-based AI solutions are often out of reach for small startups or institutions.

3. Skills Gap and Talent Shortage
Challenge: Shortage of skilled AI professionals (e.g., data scientists, ML engineers, AI researchers).
Impact: Low local capacity to develop or maintain AI systems.
Cause: Under-resourced universities, limited hands-on training, brain drain.

4. Language & Cultural Barriers
Challenge: Most AI tools are built in English or major Western languages.
Impact: Marginalizes millions of African users who speak local or indigenous languages.
Example: Poor performance of NLP models on Swahili, Wolof, Lingala, or Yoruba.
Solution Overview:
1	Description

The rapid pace of technological change creates a skills gap and digital divide with existing training options often lacking customization, flexibility, and alignment with local demands.  
Onedigitale Innovation Academy is the solution of the 4 challenges enumerated above. It is a cloud native AI platform that offers technical tools and computing infrastructure capabilities to build and develop solutions that solve real-african problems. A cloud native solution is the cost effective away for capacity building and extended reach in Africa. 
This infrastructure is complemented by 4 thematic labs: SheTech, HealthTech, AgriTech and InfraTech. Those labs will be used by startups and entrepreneurs for demo, solution co-creation and piloting of minimum valuable products.
The Onedigitale Innovation Academy  will empower startups, entrepreneurs, women, researchers, and public institutions to innovate, collaborate, and deploy responsible AI solutions using Onedigitale Innovation Academy plateform.
In Africa, capacity gaps often stem from historical underinvestment, brain drain, and limited access to quality education and technology. 

2      Methodologies and technologies
1. Human-Centered Design - Focuses on designing solutions with and for users.
Method: Empathy interviews, journey mapping, co-creation workshops.
Inclusivity: Respects lived experience, especially of marginalized groups.
2. Participatory Action Research (PAR) - A collaborative research approach where communities define problems, collect data, and act on findings.
Inclusivity: Shifts power to local actors and builds community ownership. 
3. Co-Design / Co-Creation Workshops - Diverse stakeholders jointly ideate, prototype, and test solutions.
Format: Stakeholder labs, hackathons, innovation jams.
Inclusivity: Breaks silos; amplifies voices of youth, women, informal workers.
