Name of your organization: ASSOCIATION SONGTAABA POUR LE DEVELOPPEMENT ASTD
Title: Global South Innovation Hub
Subtitle: A digital platform connecting innovators across the Global South to share knowledge, transfer technologies, and co-create inclusive solutions for sustainable development.
Problem Statement: In many developing countries, creative individuals and entrepreneurs often struggle to find established technologies suited to their local context. They also miss out on valuable guidance from experienced mentors and opportunities to connect with others doing similar work. This can lead to people reinventing the wheel, slower progress in implementing solutions, and difficulties in expanding their reach, particularly for women, young people, and those living in rural areas. These disconnected and fractured innovation environments ultimately impede broader progress towards a more inclusive and sustainable future.
Solution Overview:
Imagine a world where brilliant ideas from across Africa, Asia, and Latin America can easily connect and grow. That's the vision behind the Global South Innovation Hub (GSIH), a digital space designed to help innovators, entrepreneurs, and community groups in these regions share, modify, and expand successful local solutions. Think of it as a bridge connecting different innovation communities, fostering valuable knowledge exchange, guidance from experienced individuals, and the transfer of practical technologies.

The GSIH is accessible to everyone, even without a strong internet connection, through a mobile app, simple text messaging (USSD), or a website. Users can explore a shared collection of adaptable innovations—things like solar drying systems, affordable water purification methods, and mobile healthcare tools—complete with clear instructions on how to adjust them to their own needs. They can also connect with mentors who understand their specific challenges through a smart matching system. By contributing their own solutions or offering guidance, users earn "Knowledge Credits," which they can then use to access training, equipment, or increased exposure. Regular online group discussions, held in local languages such as French, English, Spanish, Arabic, Portuguese, and other regional dialects (using voice technology), further support collaboration.

The Hub leverages user-friendly technology. It utilizes a simple platform, text messaging integration for areas with limited internet access, voice-based navigation for those with lower literacy levels, and smart technology to connect users and translate content. A secure system, inspired by blockchain technology but not involving cryptocurrency, tracks contributions and credits. And, because all innovations are licensed under open-source principles, they can be freely reused and adapted.

The GSIH is built in collaboration with a network of regional centers of innovation, universities, and UN organizations. A governing body composed of representatives from the Global South ensures that the Hub remains locally driven. These partners contribute content, mentors, infrastructure, and funding, all working together to facilitate learning across borders and encourage joint innovation projects.
Solution Provider(s): University of Joseph Ki-Zerbo (Burkina Faso), research and innovation in sustainable technologies, education sector; African Institute for Mathematical Sciences (AIMS), pan-African network for science and technology advancement, STEM and innovation sector; ONUDI (United Nations Industrial Development Organization), promoting inclusive and sustainable industrial development, UN agency; UNESCO, supporting education, science and cultural innovation, UN agency; DITPA (Digital Innovation and Technology Park Agency, Senegal), fostering digital entrepreneurship and tech hubs, ICT sector; RISE (Research Institute for Sustainable Enterprise, Indonesia), advancing green and inclusive innovation, research and sustainability sector; CITE (Center for Innovation and Technological Entrepreneurship, Bolivia), supporting grassroots technological solutions, innovation and development sector.
Implementation location(s): Not applicable – the solution is currently in the ideation and design phase, with no full implementation yet. Pilot planning is underway for future deployment in Burkina Faso, Senegal, Indonesia, and Bolivia.
Implementation timeline(s): Not applicable – the solution is in the ideation phase. Development and pilot testing are scheduled to begin in Q3 2025, with a planned pilot timeline from January 2026 to June 2027
Duration to pilot in a new geography: The estimated duration to pilot the solution in a new geography is 6 to 9 months. This includes:         2 months for local partner engagement and co-design       3 months for platform localization (language, content, UI adaptation)       3–4 months for pilot implementation, user training, mentorship launch, and initial feedback collection       Ongoing monitoring and evaluation throughout the pilot phase.
SDGs addressed: SDG 17 (Partnerships for the Goals);SDG 8 (Decent Work and Economic Growth);SDG 9 (Industry, Innovation, and Infrastructure);
Desired impact:
Our solution aims to spark a rapid exchange of successful, community-driven ideas throughout the Global South. We will boost knowledge sharing and support innovators in resource-constrained environments through peer mentoring. By 2027, we envision empowering over 10,000 entrepreneurs, young people, and businesses led by women with accessible digital tools and freely available technologies. By making use of existing innovations, we hope to cut down on repetitive work and see a 50% increase in the adaptation of environmentally sound solutions. We also want to promote collaboration between countries in the Global South, leveraging digital innovation to support sustainable progress.

By 2027, we expect to see these key achievements and measurable results:

1-Global Reach: Over 500 instances of technologies being shared and implemented in different countries. For example, a solar irrigation system initially developed in Burkina Faso might be successfully adopted in Mali or Nepal.
2- Connected Community: A network of more than 10,000 innovators, with a strong emphasis on inclusion, ensuring at least 40% are women and 60% are under the age of 35.
3- Mentorship: Over 1,000 mentoring relationships established across borders, providing guidance and support to innovators.
4- Open Source Library: A collection of over 1,000 freely accessible solutions addressing critical challenges in areas like climate change adaptation, healthcare, agriculture, and renewable energy.
5- Economic Growth: Over 500 new or improved small businesses created or strengthened as a direct result of adapting successful innovations.
6- Efficiency Gains: A  30–50% reduction in the time and money needed to develop local solutions by providing access to existing designs and plans.
7- Environmental Benefits: Increased use of environmentally friendly technologies, leading to an estimated reduction of 5,000 tons of carbon dioxide emissions per year through the expanded use of clean energy and sustainable farming tools.

We will track our progress using an integrated monitoring system, gather feedback from users, and conduct annual, unbiased evaluations in partnership with universities and United Nations organizations.
Key technologies:
Key Technologies Used for the Solution: 

The Global South Innovation Hub leverages a suite of accessible, low-cost, and scalable technologies designed for inclusivity and usability in low-bandwidth and low-literacy environments: 

    USSD/SMS & Mobile-First Platform: Enables access via basic mobile phones without internet, ensuring reach in remote and underserved areas. 

    Voice Interface & Audio Navigation: Supports users with low literacy or limited reading skills through voice-guided menus in local languages (e.g., French, English, Spanish, Arabic, Mooré, Bambara). 

    Lightweight Artificial Intelligence (AI): Powers intelligent user matching for mentorship and recommends relevant solutions based on context (location, climate, language, skill level), using minimal data and processing power. 

    Automated Translation System: Facilitates multilingual content sharing through AI-driven translation between major Global South languages, improving cross-regional collaboration. 

    Blockchain-Inspired Ledger (Non-Cryptocurrency): Securely tracks user contributions (e.g., sharing a solution, mentoring) and manages "Knowledge Credits" with transparency and tamper-resistant records. 

    Offline-First Architecture: Allows content download and local use in areas with poor connectivity, with data syncing when connectivity is restored. 

    Open-Source Content Management System (CMS): Hosts and organizes blueprints, videos, and adaptation guides, enabling community-driven updates and co-creation. 
     

These technologies are integrated into a modular, scalable platform that prioritizes accessibility, energy efficiency, and local ownership, ensuring sustainable adoption across diverse geographies.
Unique Characteristics:
Unique/Differentiated Characteristics of the Solution: 

The Global South Innovation Hub stands out through its South-led, peer-to-peer innovation model, combining inclusive technology design with community-driven knowledge exchange. Key differentiators include: 

    Sud-Sud Co-Creation Model: Unlike top-down technology transfer initiatives, the Hub is built by and for innovators in the Global South, ensuring cultural relevance, contextual adaptation, and local ownership. 

    Knowledge Credits Incentive System: A novel non-monetary reward mechanism where users earn digital credits for sharing solutions or mentoring others. These credits can be redeemed for training, equipment, or visibility, fostering a circular economy of knowledge. 

    Low-Tech, High-Impact Access: The integration of USSD, SMS, and voice navigation enables participation from users without smartphones or internet-reaching rural, low-literacy, and marginalized innovators often excluded from digital platforms. 

    AI-Powered Matching Without Exclusion: Lightweight AI connects users based on shared challenges (e.g., drought-resistant farming, off-grid energy), but operates efficiently on minimal data, ensuring privacy and accessibility in low-resource settings. 

    Open-Source & Copy-Adapt Framework: Solutions are shared with clear "copy and adapt" guidelines, encouraging rapid replication and local customization—accelerating innovation cycles without reinventing the wheel. 

    Decentralized Governance with Regional Hubs: The network is co-managed by a rotating council of regional innovation hubs, ensuring equitable decision-making and avoiding centralized control. 

    Interoperability with National & Regional Ecosystems: Designed to integrate with existing innovation networks (e.g., African Union’s HUBS, ASEAN Innovation Network), amplifying reach and sustainability. 
     

This combination of inclusive design, behavioral incentives, and South-driven collaboration makes the Global South Innovation Hub a transformative model for equitable digital innovation.
Sustainable Change:
The Global South Innovation Hub is designed to catalyze sustainable, systemic change by transforming how knowledge and innovation are produced, shared, and scaled across the Global South. Its Theory of Change is rooted in decentralization, equity, and local agency: 
 
🌱 Theory of Change: Pathway to Systemic Impact 

1. Short-Term (0–18 months): Access & Connection
-  By lowering technological and linguistic barriers, the Hub connects isolated innovators to a global peer network.
-  Result: Increased access to proven solutions and mentorship, reducing duplication and accelerating learning. 

2. Medium-Term (18–36 months): Adaptation & Empowerment
- Users adapt and localize solutions (e.g., a water purification system from Indonesia applied in Burkina Faso).
- Women, youth, and rural entrepreneurs gain visibility, skills, and recognition through Knowledge Credits.
 Result: Rise in grassroots innovation, stronger local innovation ecosystems, and greater inclusion of marginalized voices. 

3. Long-Term (3–5 years): Systemic Shift in Innovation Culture
-  A self-sustaining culture of open-source collaboration emerges across borders.
- Governments and funders begin to support locally-led innovation as a development priority.
- Regional hubs replicate the model, creating a decentralized, resilient network of knowledge sovereignty.
➡️ Result: Reduced dependency on external technologies; increased South-South cooperation; innovation becomes inclusive, circular, and climate-resilient. 
 
🔁 Desired Follow-On Effects 

  -  Policy Influence: National innovation strategies begin to integrate open knowledge-sharing platforms and peer mentorship as core components.
    - Economic Resilience: Local economies strengthen through the rapid scaling of affordable, context-specific technologies (e.g., solar tools, agro-processors).
    - Gender Equity: Women innovators gain equal access to knowledge and networks, increasing their participation in tech and entrepreneurship.
    - Environmental Sustainability: Faster diffusion of green technologies (e.g., clean cookstoves, rainwater harvesting) contributes to climate adaptation.
    UN & Multilateral Adoption: The model is integrated into UN development programs as a best practice for inclusive digital transformation.
Funding Sources:
The Global South Innovation Hub is currently in the ideation and design phase and has not yet received large-scale funding. Initial development and concept validation have been supported through: 

    In-kind contributions from academic partners (e.g., University of Joseph Ki-Zerbo, African Institute for Mathematical Sciences) including technical expertise, research time, and local coordination.  
    Small seed grants from regional innovation funds and development incubators focused on digital inclusion and sustainable technology.  
    Pro bono support from tech developers and designers within the Global South innovation network.  
    Planned pilot funding is being sought from international development agencies, climate funds, and foundations supporting South-South cooperation and digital equity.
     
No major institutional or private investor funding has been secured to date, ensuring the solution remains community-driven and free from commercial constraints. Future financing will prioritize grants, multilateral support (e.g., UN funds, GCF), and public-private partnerships aligned with sustainable development goals.
Primary thematic focus area: Innovation Acceleration & Knowledge Sharing
Summary: The Global South Innovation Hub (GSIH) is a digital platform in ideation phase aiming to connect innovators across Africa, Asia, and Latin America for knowledge sharing, mentorship, and technology transfer (Q13, Q16). Its main strength is its inclusive South-South collaboration model and low-tech accessibility (Q23, Q24). Its main weakness is being at idea stage (Q17) with no implementation yet and no endorsements (Q28).

Title: AI Art Certification & Archive System
Subtitle: A credibility-driven certification, scoring, and archival system for AI-generated art.
Problem Statement: The rise of AI-generated art has outpaced systems for recognition, certification, and archiving, leaving creators—especially those blending human and machine creativity—without a framework to verify authorship, protect value, or ensure ethical creation and distribution.
Solution Overview:
The ThAI Art Certification & Archive System proposes a governance-based, expert-reviewed model for AI art certification and long-term archival. The system mimics the logic of Korea’s Copyright Commission and the Michelin Guide to evaluate human-AI collaborative works. Key features:

Certification Committee: Experts from AI, digital ethics, law, and art critique AI-generated works to assess the level of human creativity involved.

Scoring Model: Inspired by storytelling-based Michelin ratings, each certified piece is scored on originality, ethical sourcing of prompts/data, and human intentionality.

Blockchain Archive: Leveraging blockchain (e.g. Adobe’s C2PA, Niio Art’s infrastructure) to store provenance, creator rights, and metadata.

Platform Integration: Certified art can be tagged on digital platforms (e.g., VogueSnap, Marpple) to ensure visibility and credibility.

Incentives: Reward mechanisms for artists producing ethically guided AI works.

Methodologies:

Participatory design and digital policy prototyping

Peer and expert review systems

Blockchain-based registration and verification

Creative commons-inspired licensing options

Collaboration Models:

Partnerships with digital art platforms (Niio Art), Web3 developers, AI ethics scholars, and public cultural agencies

Cross-sector input to set evaluation criteria, similar to creative industry standards (e.g., publishing, food, fashion)
Solution Provider(s): Space Ba (media art hub), Niio Art (global digital art platform), Korea Copyright Commission (model reference), Adobe (tech partner – blockchain provenance), Korean art-tech researchers, art critics, and creative AI practitioners.
Implementation timeline(s): Not applicable (project is in pre-prototyping and partner outreach phase)
Duration to pilot in a new geography: 6–9 months to develop prototype and test in partnership with 1–2 digital art platforms or institutions.
SDGs addressed: SDG 8 (Decent Work and Economic Growth);SDG 9 (Industry, Innovation, and Infrastructure);SDG 16 (Peace, Justice, and Strong Institutions);
Desired impact:
Objectives:

Establish trusted norms and certification methods for AI-generated artworks

Increase transparency and traceability in digital art sales

Protect hybrid human-AI creators and prevent exploitative or plagiaristic misuse of AI tools

Key Impacts:

Creation of a trusted rating system to increase market value of certified AI art

Development of ethical and legal guidance frameworks for AI artists

Empowerment of local creatives and MSMEs using AI art tools by giving them legitimacy and archive access
Key technologies:
AI: Generative AI in art creation

Blockchain: For verification, metadata storage, and rights management

Digital Curation Platforms: e.g., Niio Art, Adobe C2PA

Smart Contracts: Licensing and attribution via Web3-based mechanisms
Unique Characteristics:
Applies a Michelin-style rating model to creative industries, using storytelling and ethics as score inputs

Embeds policy thinking into art-tech innovation, inspired by copyright governance models

Offers interoperability with both centralized (art platforms) and decentralized (NFT/blockchain) ecosystems

Encourages a human-centric AI value chain through certification and incentives
Sustainable Change:
By building a trusted certification and archival infrastructure for AI art, this solution will:

Reduce risk of misattribution or unethical commercialization

Incentivize responsible AI art development and fair compensation

Foster institutional trust in creative AI use, allowing public and private actors (museums, education, brands) to engage confidently

Lead to wider cultural legitimacy and economic resilience for AI-enhanced creators globally
Funding Sources:
This solution is currently in the concept development stage and has not yet received formal funding. However, it builds upon previous non-profit and public-private initiatives in the art-tech ecosystem, such as Space Ba (a hybrid art space supporting media artists in Korea), and collaborations with global platforms like Niio Art.
Initial outreach for co-development partnerships and pilot funding is being prepared for public innovation grants (e.g., Art Council Korea, Korea Creative Content Agency), and private foundations supporting digital cultural infrastructure and AI ethics.
Testimonials and Endorsements:
While the project is in its early stages, informal endorsements have been received from professionals in the art-tech and copyright policy sectors:

“This idea addresses a critical need in today’s rapidly evolving AI art space. There’s real potential for building legitimacy and fairness in hybrid creative practices.”
  – Art critic and professor, Korea National University of Arts

“A Michelin-style certification for AI art is a brilliant way to bring cultural weight and trust to a field that desperately needs standards.”
  – Creative AI curator, Niio Art Korea
Further comments/feedback:
This questionnaire was well-structured and thoughtfully designed. It encouraged deep reflection on the intersection of digital innovation, cultural policy, and ethics in AI.
We would appreciate opportunities to connect with other UNDP-supported projects in creative AI governance or inclusive innovation for cultural MSMEs, especially in the Asia-Pacific region.

A strength is its novel governance-driven approach with cross-sector partners, while a weakness is that it remains in proof-of-concept stage with no pilot implementation or secured funding.

Name of your organization: SUSTAINABLE DEVELOPMENT FOR VULNERABLE PEOPLES IN BANGLADESH(SDVP), Govt. NGO Bureau Reg. no-2858
Title: Freelaning job an alternative way to employment generation.
Subtitle: Skill Manpower
Problem Statement:
One in every 10 of Bangladesh's 44 million young people is unemployed, according to research by World Vision Bangladesh. Moreover, thousands of graduates who are finishing their studies at different public and private universities in Bangladesh are failing to find suitable positions in the job market each year.
As a result, the rate of educated unemployment in the country is increasing exponentially. However, these young unemployed people can easily start their career by taking some IT training and freelancing online. By doing so, they not only make a living but also contribute to the economy by earning a salary in a valuable foreign currency.
Rapid digitalization and a high rate of educated unemployment have made Bangladesh the second largest exporter of online labour.
With the advent of rapid digitalization, many developing countries like Bangladesh are focusing on the digital economy: a global market for digital outsourcing.
The digitalization of a country's economy not only drives innovation in its service industry, it also fuels domestic job opportunities, enabling faster economic growth. In the quest to lower costs and risks, many large corporations in developed nations like the US, UK and Australia are turning to IT outsourcing from countries including Bangladesh, leading to a recent boom in freelancing.
Freelancing jobs include everything from computer programming to web design, tax preparation, and search engine optimization. This has generated a wide range of new opportunities for people in emerging markets that did not previously exist. Asia has become the number-one region for providing outsourcing services to the rest of the world.
Solution Overview:
Bangladesh is one of the few countries in Asia that has a huge youth population. Of its 163 million people, almost 65% are under the age of 25. This vast, young and strong human resource, however, is still lacking in the knowledge necessary to thrive in the competitive global market.
Although freelancing as a career has gained in popularity over the last few years, thousands of Bangladesh's young people are in need of proper training and government support to help them take advantage of this opportunity.
The government should focus on turning unemployed young people into tech-savvy workers and engage them in IT-based freelancing. In this way, the government of Bangladesh can attain its goal of translating the vision of Digital Bangladesh into a reality by focusing on human capital development for the global digital economy.
Government initiatives to develop the ICT service sector, such as creating a high-tech park in every district, coupled with the low-cost workforce, have made Bangladesh a key player in the global outsourcing market.
Nevertheless, several challenges hinder the growth of this industry in Bangladesh. The absence of an uninterrupted power supply is still a major problem for the country. Freelancing work, like complex coding for software development, requires a high level of concentration, which is often shattered by the frequent power cuts.
A lack of quality internet services, along with higher broadband prices, is a major problem for freelancers in rural areas. In spite of having broadband connections in some areas, freelancers often find it too slow to suit their work.
The lack of an easy payment system - especially for receiving payments from foreign clients - is another problem for this fast-growing industry.
And women's participation in freelancing, although increasing gradually, is still not high enough.
A lot of women in Bangladesh, including highly educated women, often sacrifice their careers in order to take care of their families. Freelancing is becoming a preferred career option for many Bangladeshi women, as it provides them with an opportunity to work from home.
Bangladeshi women who are looking to take a step out of their traditional domestic roles are finding freelance jobs to be a great solution. Research shows that in terms of the quality of the work, Bangladesh's female freelancers have started gaining more credibility than their male counterparts. Increasing women's participation in freelancing is therefore boosting trust in the sector.

Duration to pilot in a new geography: 24  Months
SDGs addressed: SDG 10 (Reduced Inequalities);SDG 8 (Decent Work and Economic Growth);SDG 1 (No Poverty);
Desired impact: Employment generation.
Key technologies:
Freelancing offers many advantages, including the freedom to choose clients and projects, access to the global market, and flexibility over location. Most importantly, freelancers can avoid the long, frustrating hours commuting in traffic in the Bangladeshi capital of Dhaka.
Consequently, freelancing has become a popular career option for many Bangladeshi people, offering a new and flexible source of income that suits their lifestyles.
The rapid digitalization of Bangladesh - including easy internet access in urban areas and government and non-government initiatives to promote freelancing - has contributed to the recent growth of this way of working.
As a result, Bangladesh has already become the second-largest supplier of online labour, according to the Oxford Internet Institute (OII). About 500,000 active freelancers are working regularly, out of 650,000 registered freelancers in the country; between them they are generating $100 million annually, according to the ICT Division of Bangladesh.
India is the largest supplier of online labour, with close to 24% of total global freelance workers, followed by Bangladesh (16%) and the US (12%). Different countries focus on different sectors of freelancing services. For instance, technology and software development is dominated by Indian freelancers, while Bangladesh is the top supplier of sales and marketing support services.

Summary: This project aims to address Bangladesh’s high youth unemployment by equipping marginalized groups with ICT and freelancing skills to access global digital work opportunities. It builds on Bangladesh’s position as the world’s 2nd largest supplier of online labour. The initiative emphasizes poverty reduction, women’s participation, and sustainable employment. Strengths: clear alignment with national priorities, demonstrated experience (15+ years of training), and strong potential for social inclusion. Weaknesses: the proposal is broad and lacks a clear technological innovation component, systemic change model is underdeveloped, and evidence of impact is anecdotal rather than data-driven.

Title: Universal Health Records resident with patient and not with hospitals
Subtitle: A universal health records system that promotes privacy and ubiquity
Problem Statement: Hospitals hold and host patient records. When a patient needs to go to a new hospital, they have to reregister with the new hospital, sometimes redo tests. How about we have a system that allows a patient hold their own records, share securely with hospitals and doctors. Our system gives patients this right to share their medical records with hospitals and diagnostic centres.
Solution Overview: This system runs on blockchain and will give the user rights to share access to their medical records. The medical records will have different sharing rights, so when sharing with a diagnostic centre, all they will see will be the tests the user wants to do. When sharing with a doctor which is not your resident hospital, they will have access to basics like medical situations, and the ability to enter medical records.
Solution Provider(s): Securepoint Technologies Ltd, AWS
Duration to pilot in a new geography: 18 months
SDGs addressed: SDG 3 (Good Health and Well-being);SDG 5 (Gender Equality);SDG 10 (Reduced Inequalities);
Desired impact: improved Access to healthcare, climate change, reducing paper files in hospitals
Key technologies: AI, blockchain
Unique Characteristics: The solution will be a freemium, with people who want better access to pay a subscription. Hospitals will be able to register their patient and they will charge a fee for the registration
Sustainable Change: Our solution will change the way patient records are done, and shared
Funding Sources: Savings from co-founders, profit from current solutions
Primary thematic focus area: Enabling Policies & Regulatory Innovation
Summary: Universal Health Records is a concept-stage blockchain-based health data platform designed to shift ownership of medical records from hospitals to patients. Patients would hold their records, granting selective and secure access to doctors, hospitals, and diagnostic centers. The solution envisions a freemium model with subscription upgrades, and fees for hospitals registering patients. It emphasizes privacy, interoperability, and empowerment of patients in managing their healthcare data.

Title: SolidarSanté – Digital solidarity engineering for equity in rural health

Full or partial coverage of medical costs.

Title: From smoke to green entrepreneurs.
Subtitle: Our initiative aims to transition at 50 households that produce charcoal traditionally to clean energy agents. We aim to achieve this by conducting intensive training to the locals on effects of traditional charcoal production and usage for cooking. Diversifying sources of cooking energy by introducing clean bioethanol, green stoves and charcoal briquettes is our solution.
Problem Statement:
By transitioning charcoal producing households to clean energy entrepreneurs, we address the following challenges
1. Deforestation caused by traditional charcoal production in Samburu, that is contributing to the worsening aridity and suffering of the entire pastoral communities in the County and the entire Northern Kenya.
2. Respiratory diseases like chronic coughs and TB that are caused by charcoal production and usage that is mostly affecting women. 
3. Greenhouse gases emission to the atmosphere that is causing global warming and increasing droughts season in the pastoral lands of Samburu.
4. Poor economic cycle of charcoal production - traditional charcoal production over a period of 20 years have proven to be a hand-to-mouth type of livelihood practice. With more profitable, reliable and sustainable clean energy enterprises, livelihood will change for the best for these families.
Solution Overview:
We aim to implement our solutions in the following ways:
1. Carry out a pilot test for the installation of bioethanol refill stations in a high charcoal production spot in Samburu East and carry it for a period of 3 months. 
2. With financial support, we aim to introduce affordable green stoves and establish a local charcoal briquette manufacturing as additional alternatives to replace traditionally produces charcoal.
3, Conduct intensive education and trainings sessions to the target producer households and the local vendors who are the main charcoal buyers so as to fight behavioral resistance and increase the rates of clean energy acceptability.
4. Partner with Kenya Forest Service Administration office at the local level together with Samburu County Government so as to ensure, regulation and monitoring of charcoal production. With at least 70% transition scale achieved, we aim for policy reforms to restrict charcoal production.
5. With at least 50% transition achieved, we will work with the Health Clinical officers at County and sub-County levels to increase monitoring of local vendors like restaurants, hotels, butchery stores, on the type of cooking energy used.
6. Conduct quarterly surveys to access the statistics of cooking energy transition and landscape in Samburu.
Solution Provider(s): Greener Minds Households' Initiative
Duration to pilot in a new geography: 6 months
SDGs addressed: SDG 7 (Affordable and Clean Energy);SDG 13 (Climate Action);SDG 8 (Decent Work and Economic Growth);
Desired impact:
We aim to achieve the following objectives:
1. By our first year, obtain a 50% transition of our target households from traditional charcoal production to clean energy enterprise.
2. Obtain at least a 50% of vendor-behavioral change and acceptance of clean energy alternatives for cooking.
3. With a full transition of 25 households to clean energy agents, we will achieve a cut of 21.6 tons annually of CHG reduction and we will be able to save 2400 trees (dry matter) used for charcoal production annually.
4. We will be able to provide a more sustainable, healthy and profitable business opportunity for at least 25 women and youth involved in charcoal production and in a single town in our first year of full scale operation. This will provide a chance for children to study in schools and mothers to spend time around their families.
5. We will achieve a significant reduction in respiratory infections in women involved in traditional charcoal production occupation.
Key technologies: We will utilize the pay-as-you-go technology system in our sell for clean bioethanol to our customer which enables an affordable purchase of energy and easy payment via mobile phones.
Unique Characteristics: With this innovative idea of transitioning from traditional charcoal production to clean energy, we will be  able to measure the amount of CO2 equivalent that we have reduced and claim a compensation, with the finance used to economically empower our households and support our initiative.
Sustainable Change:
1. Improved level of incomes for the households that have transitioned to cleaner energy.
2. Reduced environmental pollution and increases forest regeneration capacity
3. Reduced incidences of respiratory infections
4. Reduced food insecurity from the unreliable charcoal selling business.
5. Increased job opportunities for youths and women in briquettes manufacturing and clean bioethanol enterprises.
Funding Sources: not applicable
Testimonials and Endorsements: not applicable.
Further comments/feedback: With financial support to implement our initiative, we will partner with KOKO Networks, local retailer and distributors to support our clean energy solutions and look for more investments from carbon credits.
Primary thematic focus area: Stable and Resilient Digital Supply Chains
Summary: From Smoke to Green Entrepreneurs est une initiative au stade d’idée visant à transformer 50 ménages producteurs de charbon traditionnel à Samburu (Kenya) en entrepreneurs d’énergie propre (Q11). La solution propose : stations de bioéthanol en mode PAYG, distribution de foyers améliorés, production locale de briquettes vertes, et formations intensives sur les risques sanitaires/environnementaux (Q13, Q20). L’initiative prévoit aussi un plaidoyer pour des réformes politiques via la collaboration avec Kenya Forest Service et le gouvernement du comté (Q13). Les impacts attendus incluent : 50 % de transition des ménages la première année, réduction annuelle de 21,6 tCO₂eq, sauvegarde de 2 400 arbres, baisse des infections respiratoires, et autonomisation économique de femmes et jeunes (Q16, Q23).

Title: Enhancing the planning and production of events in Nigeria by leveraging digital technology.
Subtitle: Events with Anthonia is a growing event planning and management company based in Nigeria, committed to creating exceptional experiences for every occasion. Since our launch in November 2022, we have successfully planned and coordinated diverse events — from weddings and corporate conferences to exhibitions, concerts, and religious gatherings — including the high-profile Air Force @ 59 celebration attended by Nigeria’s Vice President.       We combine creativity, meticulous planning, and innovative solutions to deliver seamless, memorable events that reflect each client’s unique vision. With expertise in project management, vendor relations, and budget optimization, we thrive under pressure and consistently exceed expectations. Our passion for originality and excellence, coupled with a strong understanding of the latest trends and technologies, ensures every event is both flawless and impactful.        At Events with Anthonia, our mission is to design unforgettable moments while fostering sustainability, supporting our community, and raising the standard of event production in Nigeria. We are driven by a vision to become the leading event planning and management company in Nigeria within five years — trusted for creativity, professionalism, and unparalleled attention to detail.
Problem Statement:
Nigeria’s event industry is vibrant yet fragmented, leaving both event center owners and event vendors struggling to reach their full potential. Event center owners often operate at a loss or shut down entirely due to low patronage, driven by inadequate marketing and poor online visibility. As a result, many are unable to showcase the full range of their creativity, expertise, or unique offerings, leaving their spaces underutilized.

Similarly, event vendors — decorators, caterers, photographers, and others — face limited opportunities to connect with clients who value their services. Without effective platforms to market their skills and demonstrate value, they are forced to rely on word-of-mouth referrals and informal networks, which restrict growth and sustainability.

On the client side, people searching for quality, affordable event centers and vendors encounter frustration and inefficiency. The lack of accessible, transparent information means clients spend more time and money yet often remain dissatisfied due to insufficient options or poor service matches.

This disconnects between service providers and clients underscores the urgent need for innovative solutions that improve visibility, foster trust, and create seamless connections within the event ecosystem.
Solution Overview:
To address the disconnect between event service providers and clients in Nigeria’s event industry, we are building a comprehensive digital marketplace platform — accessible via both a website and a mobile application— designed to seamlessly connect event center owners, event vendors, and clients. 

This platform will serve as a one-stop hub where event centers and vendors can create professional profiles, showcase their products and services, and reach a wider audience. Clients, in turn, can easily browse, compare, and book vetted event centers and vendors based on location, budget, ratings, and service offerings — saving time and money while ensuring quality.                                  Methodologies & Approach 

Our solution adopts a user-centered design approach, ensuring the platform is intuitive and accessible across devices. Key features include: 

* Verified listings for event centers and vendors, with photos, descriptions, and pricing
* Search and filter tools for clients to find services by category, location, and budget
* Client reviews and ratings to build trust and transparency
* Booking and inquiry management tools for seamless transactions
* Admin dashboard for monitoring activity, resolving disputes, and maintaining quality control

We will use an agile development methodology, releasing the platform in phases and iterating based on user feedback to continuously improve functionality and user experience. 

Technologies 
The platform will leverage:
* Modern web and mobile frameworks (React for web; React Native/Flutter for mobile)
* Cloud infrastructure (AWS or Azure) for scalability and reliability
* Secure payment gateways to facilitate transactions
* AI-driven recommendation engines in later phases to enhance personalization                  Partnerships & Collaborations 

We aim to collaborate with:
* Professional event associations to onboard verified vendors and centers
* Digital marketing agencies to drive platform awareness and adoption
* Financial institutions and fintech to offer integrated payment solutions and potential credit options for bookings
* Training institutions to upskill vendors on best practices in customer service and digital marketing

Through these strategic partnerships, we will strengthen the platform’s credibility, expand reach, and empower vendors to deliver better services.

Ultimately, our marketplace platform will elevate the standard of events in Nigeria by improving visibility, fostering trust, and creating meaningful connections between providers and clients — unlocking the full potential of the industry.
Solution Provider(s): Osekhale Anthonia Omotesele
Duration to pilot in a new geography: 6 Months
SDGs addressed: SDG 8 (Decent Work and Economic Growth);SDG 9 (Industry, Innovation, and Infrastructure);SDG 17 (Partnerships for the Goals);
Desired impact:
The core desire of this innovation is to transform Nigeria’s event industry by creating a centralized digital marketplace that improves visibility, access, and efficiency for both event service providers and clients. By bridging the gap between demand and supply in the event ecosystem, our platform aims to digitally empower local businesses, elevate service quality, and make event planning more accessible and affordable.                                                                                                                  

Key Objectives 
1. Enhance Visibility & Accessibility: 
   Provide event centers and vendors — especially small businesses — with an affordable platform to showcase their offerings and reach a wider audience.

2. Standardize Service Delivery: 
   Improve the quality and professionalism of event services through verified listings, client reviews, and access to vendor training.

 Employment Generation 
Our platform will directly and indirectly contribute to job creation and economic growth by:

  Creating direct employment opportunities within our team, including roles in tech development, customer service, content moderation, marketing, and operations.

This innovation seeks not just to improve the efficiency of event planning but to build a more inclusive, tech-enabled, and economically viable event ecosystem in Nigeria.
Key technologies:
To ensure scalability, security, and a seamless user experience, our digital marketplace platform is built with modern, industry-standard technology 
1. Web & Mobile Frameworks

React.js — for building a fast, responsive, and user-friendly web interface.
React Native or Flutter — to develop cross-platform mobile applications for both Android and iOS, ensuring consistent performance and experience.

 2. Backend & APIs
 Node.js (or Python/Django) — for building a robust, scalable backend that handles business logic, data processing, and API endpoints.
RESTful APIs (or GraphQL) — to enable seamless communication between the frontend and backend, and with third-party services.

PostgreSQL (or MySQL) — as a reliable relational database to store user accounts, vendor profiles, listings, reviews, and transactions.
Cloud storage (AWS S3, Google Cloud Storage, or Azure Blob) — to securely store and serve images, videos, and documents uploaded by vendors and clients.

AWS, Microsoft Azure, or Google Cloud Platform— for hosting the platform, enabling scalability, high availability, and cost efficiency.

* Data encryption (SSL/TLS) to protect user data during transmission.
* Role-based access controls to protect sensitive administrative operations.

 6. Payments Integration
* Payment gateways (e.g., Pay stack, Flutter wave, Stripe) to enable secure online payments, escrow services, and settlement to vendors.

7. Analytics & Recommendations

* AI-driven recommendation engine (in later phases) to suggest relevant vendors and venues to clients based on preferences and past behavior.

8. Content Management & Admin Tools

* Administrative dashboards for platform moderation, vendor verification, user support, and reporting.
* Notification system via email and push notifications to keep users engaged and informed.


These technologies together ensure that the platform is:
-  Scalable for growth
- Reliable even under heavy usage
- Secure for all users
-  Easy and intuitive to use
-  Future-ready for advanced features like AI and predictive analytics
Unique Characteristics:

 Unlike general classifieds or social media, this platform is purpose-built for Nigeria’s event ecosystem — catering specifically to both event centers and event vendors in one integrated hub.

2. Verified & Trustworthy Listings

Each vendor and event center is vetted before going live, ensuring quality and building client confidence — addressing the trust gap common in informal referrals.

 From discovery to booking and reviews, clients enjoy a seamless, transparent experience — saving time, reducing costs, and avoiding disappointing outcomes.

7. Community & Training Support
 Beyond just listings, the platform plans to partner with training organizations to upskill vendors, promote industry best practices, and foster a supportive community for long-term growth.

8. Future-Ready with AI & Insights
 The solution is designed to evolve — incorporating AI-driven recommendations, data analytics, and industry insights to continually improve user experience and business outcomes.

 Why This Matters
Your solution doesn’t just digitize event planning — it builds trust, empowers small businesses, and creates an inclusive, sustainable ecosystem tailored to Nigeria’s unique event industry challenges and opportunities.
Sustainable Change:
Our digital marketplace is designed not just as a transactional platform but as a catalyst for long-term, systemic improvement in Nigeria’s event industry. We create sustainable change through the following:

 1. Empowering Small Businesses & Entrepreneurs
By providing affordable digital visibility to event vendors and event centers, we empower thousands of small and medium enterprises (SMEs), many of them owned by women and youth. This helps them grow sustainably, create jobs, and contribute to the local economy.

 2. Promoting Digital Inclusion
Our platform brings traditionally offline businesses into the digital economy, equipping them with the tools and exposure they need to compete in today’s market. This helps build a more inclusive, modernized event ecosystem.

 5. Supporting Skills Development
Through planned partnerships with training organizations, we help vendors upskill in areas like customer service, digital marketing, and sustainability — strengthening their businesses and ensuring they can adapt to changing market needs.

 6. Driving Economic Growth & Job Creation
By increasing demand for event services and improving supply efficiency, we stimulate more business activity, creating direct and indirect employment across the industry — from tech jobs on our platform to field jobs in the event supply chain.

 7. Environmental and Social Responsibility
We promote responsible practices by encouraging vendors to adopt eco-friendly event solutions and by supporting socially impactful initiatives such as community-based events and inclusive hiring.

 In summary, our solution addresses **root causes — lack of visibility, low trust, and poor access to markets — rather than symptoms. By empowering providers, educating consumers, and fostering accountability, we help build a vibrant, professional, and sustainable event ecosystem in Nigeria that will continue to thrive long into the future.

Title: Unlocking your Digital Potential: Mobile Videography for All
Subtitle: Unlocking Your Digital Potential: Mobile Videography for All empowers underserved communities with affordable, easy-to-learn mobile video skills to create, share, and thrive in the digital economy.
Problem Statement: Over 5.5 billion people around the world use social media, but many people—especially women, youth, and small businesses—don’t have the skills or tools they need to take part in the digital economy. At the same time, 2.14 billion people are shopping online, and those who can't create content for digital platforms miss out on important opportunities. This gap in digital skills makes it harder for these communities to grow, get noticed, and succeed. By teaching mobile videography, we can help them unlock their potential and participate in the digital world.
Solution Overview:
Detailed Description of How the Solution Works
Delivery Mode:
The solution will be delivered online, providing practical, hands-on training in mobile videography.

Skill Development Workshops:
Target Audience: Women, youth, MSMEs, and marginalized communities, particularly those who may lack access to professional equipment and training.
The workshops will cover basic to intermediate mobile videography, starting from the essentials of filming and moving to advanced editing techniques.
Participants will learn to shoot high-quality video footage, edit with CapCut, and create engaging content tailored for various digital platforms.
Training Modules:
Module 1: Introduction to Mobile Videography
Learn the basics of using a smartphone for filming: shooting techniques, lighting, and audio tips.
Module 2: Editing with CapCut
Focus on creating scroll-stopping footage for personal or business use. Participants will dive into advanced editing features, transitions, and techniques to produce professional-looking videos on their smartphones.
Module 3: Content Strategy for Social Media
Tailoring content for platforms like Instagram, TikTok, and YouTube, focusing on engaging audiences and leveraging trends.
Module 4: Monetizing Content
Learn how to use videos to promote products, services, and businesses, including securing brand deals and generating income from content.
Practical Assignments and Feedback:
Throughout the program, participants will create real-world video content and receive actionable feedback on each piece to continuously improve their skills.

Community Building:
A dedicated Telegram group will be set up for participants to share work, ask questions, and engage with each other. This group will provide a safe space for ongoing learning, collaboration, and networking.
Live Q&A sessions and peer-to-peer feedback will further enhance the learning experience.
Methodologies and Technologies Used

Mobile Videography Apps:
CapCut will be the primary app for video editing. It’s user-friendly, accessible, and allows participants to create high-quality videos directly from their smartphones.
Basic mobile apps may also be introduced for specific tasks, such as InShot or iMovie, based on participant needs.

Online Platforms:
Zoom will be used for live training sessions.
YouTube will host pre-recorded tutorials for convenient on-demand access.
Google Drive will serve as the hub for sharing resources, assignments, and training materials.
Canva will help participants create engaging visuals like thumbnails and social media posts to complement their videos.
Collaboration and Community Engagement:
Telegram will be the primary platform for community engagement. It will allow participants to connect without needing to share personal contact details, making it safer and more accessible for everyone.

Having taught over 200 people how to edit videos on their phones through the She Leads Africa Initiative, I bring practical, hands-on experience to the table. As both a content creator and mobile phone videographer, I’m uniquely qualified to guide participants in mastering the skills needed to create impactful digital content. My experience ensures that the training isn’t just theoretical but based on real-world techniques and insights that will help participants succeed. 


Timeline and Duration
The program will span 6 weeks from start to finish:

Week 1–2: Introduction to Mobile Videography and Basic Editing
Participants will learn basic filming techniques and get hands-on practice with CapCut for editing.
Week 3–4: Advanced Editing and Content Strategy
Focus on creating scroll-stopping footage and learning how to tailor content for different social media platforms. Participants will also dive deeper into advanced editing techniques.
Week 5: Monetizing Content
Participants will explore strategies to use their videos for business promotion and how to monetize their content through platforms, partnerships, and brand deals.
Week 6: Final Projects.
Solution Provider(s): She Leads Africa – A global community that empowers young African women through mentorship, learning resources, and networking opportunities. Sector: Digital education, women empowerment. CapCut – A mobile video editing app that provides a user-friendly platform for video editing on smartphones. Sector: Technology, digital content creation.
Duration to pilot in a new geography: 6 weeks
SDGs addressed: SDG 4 (Quality Education);SDG 5 (Gender Equality);SDG 8 (Decent Work and Economic Growth);
Desired impact:
Objectives:
1. Empower underserved communities with mobile videography skills for content creation
2. Bridge the digital divide by offering accessible, mobile-based training in video editing.
3. Foster economic empowerment by enabling participants to monetize content and grow their businesses.

Title: Ferme agroécologique intégrée
Subtitle: Le projet de la Ferme Patin a pour ambition d’établir une ferme agroécologique dans la province du Ziro au Centre-Ouest du Burkina Faso. Le projet est implanté sur une superficie de 16 hectares au sein du village de Tiabien dans la commune  de Sapouy. La ferme agroécologique intégrée est constituée des composants suivants : 1. Une Maison d’hôtes sur une superficie d’un (1) hectare. 2. Une Terre des Savoirs sur une superficie de quatre (4) hectares contenant un Jardin médicinal et un Centre de formation. 3. Un Verger sur une superficie de cinq (5) hectares. 4. Un Champ de maraichéculture sur une superficie d’un (1) hectare. 5. Une Zone agro-avicole sur une superficie de cinq (5) hectares.
Problem Statement:
1. Inégalités d'accès à la technologie : Dans de nombreuses régions, l'accès à Internet et aux technologies numériques est limité par des infrastructures insuffisantes ou des coûts élevés. Cette inégalité d'accès empêche une partie de la population de bénéficier des opportunités offertes par l'économie numérique, créant ainsi un fossé entre ceux qui peuvent participer à cette économie et ceux qui en sont exclus.
2. Compétences numériques insuffisantes : Malgré l'accès à la technologie, de nombreuses personnes manquent des compétences nécessaires pour utiliser efficacement ces outils numériques. Cela peut les empêcher de trouver des emplois dans des secteurs de plus en plus numérisés ou de créer leurs propres enterprises, limitant ainsi leurs perspectives économiques.
3. Exclusion sociale et économique : Les populations marginalisées, telles que les femmes, les personnes handicapées et les minorités, peuvent être particulièrement touchées par l'exclusion de l'économie numérique. Des solutions inclusives sont nécessaires pour s'assurer que ces groupes puissent participer pleinement et bénéficier des avantages de la transformation numérique.
Solution Overview:
1. Description détaillée du fonctionnement de la solution
La solution peut se décliner en plusieurs volets intégrés :
- Plateforme d'accès numérique : Une plateforme centrale qui offre des ressources éducatives, des outils et des services numériques accessibles à tous. Cela inclut des cours en ligne sur les compétences numériques, des informations sur l'entrepreneuriat, et des outils de mise en réseau.
- Formation et accompagnement : Des modules de formation sont offerts sur les compétences numériques de base, la cybersécurité et la gestion d'entreprise. Des accompagnateurs locaux peuvent également offrir une assistance personnalisée, aidant les utilisateurs à naviguer sur la plateforme et à développer leurs compétences.
- Accès à l'Internet et aux outils : Des partenariats avec des fournisseurs d'accès Internet et des entreprises de technologie peuvent permettre de fournir un accès gratuit ou à faible coût à Internet et aux appareils nécessaires pour accéder aux services numériques.
- Sensibilisation et inclusion : Des campagnes de sensibilisation ciblant les groupes marginalisés sont mises en place pour les inciter à participer à l'économie numérique. Cela peut inclure des événements communautaires, des ateliers et des sessions d'information.
 2. Méthodologies et technologies utilisées
- Approche participative : Impliquer les communautés locales dans la conception et l'implémentation de la solution afin de s'assurer qu'elle répond à leurs besoins spécifiques.
- Apprentissage mixte : Utilisation d'une combinaison de cours en ligne et de sessions en présentiel pour garantir un apprentissage efficace et accessible.
- Technologies numériques : Développement de la plateforme à l'aide de technologies modernes telles que le cloud computing pour l'hébergement, des outils de gestion de contenu pour les ressources éducatives, et des applications mobiles pour accéder aux services depuis n'importe quel appareil.
- Analyse de données : Utilisation d'outils d'analyse de données pour suivre l'engagement des utilisateurs et l'impact des formations, permettant ainsi d'ajuster et d'améliorer continuellement les offres.
# 3. Partenariats et modèles de collaboration
- Partenariats avec des ONGs locales : Collaborer avec des organisations non gouvernementales qui travaillent déjà dans les communautés ciblées pour maximiser l'impact et garantir l'adhésion des utilisateurs.
- Collaboration avec le secteur privé : Engager des entreprises technologiques pour fournir des ressources, des formations et possiblement sponsoriser l'accès aux technologies.
- Alignement avec les gouvernements : Travailler avec les administrations locales pour aligner les initiatives sur les politiques publiques existantes en matière d'inclusion numérique et de développement économique.
- Partenariats académiques : Collaborer avec des établissements d'enseignement supérieur pour garantir que les curriculums de formation soient à jour et répondent aux besoins du marché du travail.
Solution Provider(s): 1. Organisations non gouvernementales (ONG) : L'association NEKENEDOUANA qui travaillent sur des projets d'inclusion sociale et numérique. 2. Entreprises technologiques : La Société PALOBDE SARL qui Fournis de solutions numériques, de matériel informatique ou d'accès à Internet. 3. Institutions académiques : Universités et écoles professionnelles qui offrent des formations ou des recherches dans le domaine des compétences numériques. 4. Gouvernements locaux: Mairie de Sapouy. Direction provinciale de l'agriculture biologique. 5. Fonds et philanthropies : Le fonds Kuna wili.
Implementation location(s): Village de Tiabien. Commune de Sapouy. Province du Ziro. Région du NANDO. Burkina Fasohttps://maps.app.goo.gl/kZJ6vFxmrGWpwWH29?g_st=awb
Duration to pilot in a new geography: Deux années
SDGs addressed: SDG 2 (Zero Hunger);SDG 8 (Decent Work and Economic Growth);SDG 12 (Responsible Consumption and Production);
Desired impact:
Objectifs de la ferme agroécologique intégrée:
1. Amélioration de la biodiversité : Promouvoir la diversité des cultures et de la faune sur la ferme pour maintenir des écosystèmes sains.
2. Sécurisation alimentaire : Produire des aliments sains et nutritifs pour répondre aux besoins alimentaires des communautés locales.
3. Réduction des intrants chimiques : Limiter l'utilisation d'engrais et de pesticides chimiques pour protéger les sols, l'eau et la santé humaine.
4. Conservation des ressources naturelles : Optimiser l'utilisation de l'eau et des sols en utilisant des techniques comme la récupération de l'eau de pluie et le compostage.
5. Renforcement de la résilience climatique : Adapter les pratiques agricoles aux changements climatiques en utilisant des méthodes durables et en diversifiant les cultures.
6. Création de valeur et de revenus pour les agriculteurs : Augmenter la rentabilité des exploitations agricoles en améliorant les rendements et en réduisant les coûts.
 Principaux résultats et impacts quantifiables
1. Réduction des émissions de GES :
   - Objectif : Réduction de 20-30 % des émissions de gaz à effet de serre liées à l'agriculture par l'adoption de pratiques agroécologiques.
   - Impact : Transition vers des systèmes de production qui restituent le carbone dans le sol grâce à des pratiques telles que le semis direct et la rotation des cultures.
2. Économies d'énergie :
   - Objectif : Réduction de 15-25 % de la consommation d'énergie sur la ferme en réduisant l'utilisation de machines et en adoptant des techniques manuelles et écologiques.
   - Impact : Promotion de techniques de culture régénératrices qui diminuent le besoin d'intrants énergétiques externes.
3. Création d'emplois :
   - Objectif : Génération de 10-20 % d'emplois supplémentaires dans les communautés locales grâce à la diversification des activités et à l'implémentation de pratiques agroécologiques.
   - Impact : Formation et employement dans des secteurs complémentaires, comme le traitement des déchets organiques et la transformation alimentaire.
4. Amélioration de la qualité de l'eau :
   - Objectif : Réduction de 30-40 % de la pollution des eaux due aux intrants agricoles en adoptant des pratiques naturelles de fertilisation et de lutte contre les nuisibles.
   - Impact : Meilleure qualité de l'eau pour les communautés environnantes et la faune.
5. Rendements agricoles durables :
   - Objectif : Augmentation des rendements de 10-20 % sur les cultures grâce à l'amélioration des pratiques de gestion des sols et de la biodiversité.
   - Impact : Garantir la sécurité alimentaire tout en répondant à la demande locale.
Key technologies:
La ferme agroécologique intégrée tire parti de diverses technologies clés pour optimiser les pratiques agricoles, améliorer la durabilité et augmenter la productivité. Voici un aperçu des technologies utilisées :
 1. Internet des Objets (IoT)
- Capteurs intelligents : Utilisés pour surveiller les conditions du sol, l'humidité, la température et les niveaux de nutriments en temps réel. Ces données aident à prendre des décisions éclairées sur l'irrigation et la fertilisation.
- Systèmes d'irrigation automatisés : Permettent une gestion plus efficace des ressources en eau en s'adaptant aux besoins spécifiques des cultures et en réduisant le gaspillage.
 2. Drones et imagerie par satellite:
- Surveillance des cultures : Les drones dotés de capteurs peuvent fournir des images haute résolution des champs afin de surveiller la santé des cultures, détecter les maladies et évaluer la vigueur des plantes.
- Cartographie des sols et analyses : Permet d’identifier les zones qui nécessitent des interventions spécifiques, optimisant ainsi les rendements.
 3. Intelligence Artificielle (IA):
- Analyse de données : Utilisation d’algorithmes d’apprentissage automatique pour analyser les données collectées par les capteurs et prédire les performances des cultures, les rendements et les besoins en intrants.
- Systèmes de recommandation : Guides pour les agriculteurs sur les meilleures pratiques culturales basées sur des données historiques et des prévisions.
 4. Blockchain:
- Traçabilité des produits : Permet un suivi transparent des produits agricoles du champ à la table, renforçant la confiance des consommateurs et garantissant la qualité des aliments.
- Contrats intelligents : Garantissent des transactions sécurisées entre les producteurs et les distributeurs, facilitant les accords de vente et les paiements.
 5. Agriculture de Précision:
- Gestion des ressources : Utilisation de technologies pour appliquer des intrants (eau, engrais, pesticides) de manière ciblée, ce qui réduit le gaspillage et augmente l'efficacité.
- Outils de modélisation de croissance : Modèles pour simuler le développement des cultures et évaluer les impacts des différentes pratiques de gestion.
 6. Systèmes de gestion de données:
- Plateformes d'analyse et de gestion : Des logiciels qui centralisent les données provenant de différentes sources (capteurs IoT, drones, etc.) pour une analyse approfondie et une prise de décision efficace.
 7. Techniques de biocontrôle:
- Utilisation de micro-organismes : Intégration de bactéries bénéfiques et de champignons pour améliorer la santé des sols et lutter contre les maladies des cultures, réduisant ainsi la dépendance aux pesticides chimiques.
Unique Characteristics:
La ferme agroécologique intégrée se distingue par plusieurs caractéristiques uniques et innovantes qui favorisent une approche durable et efficace de l'agriculture. Voici un aperçu des aspects qui rendent ce modèle distinctif :
 1. Modèles commerciaux et de partenariat
- Coopératives multipartites : La ferme peut fonctionner comme une coopérative incluant des agriculteurs, des consommateurs et des entrepreneurs locaux, favorisant un modèle économique circulaire où les profits sont partagés entre les parties prenantes.
- Partenariats avec des ONGs et des institutions académiques : Collaboration avec des organisations qui apportent des compétences techniques et des ressources pour la formation, la recherche et le développement de pratiques agroécologiques.
- Intégration des chaînes de valeur : De la production à la distribution, le modèle permet d'intégrer les étapes de transformation et de commercialisation, garantissant ainsi des prix équitables pour les producteurs tout en répondant aux attentes des consommateurs.
 2. Mécanismes de financement innovants
- Financement participatif (crowdfunding) : Utilisation de plateformes de financement participatif pour lever des fonds pour des projets spécifiques au sein de la ferme, permettant à la communauté de s'engager et de soutenir les initiatives locales.
- Microcrédit et financements verts : Mise en place de systèmes de microcrédit pour les agriculteurs afin de financer les investissements initiaux dans des technologies durables ou des pratiques agricoles innovantes.
- Subventions et incitations gouvernementales : Collaboration avec des institutions publiques pour obtenir des subventions destinées à promouvoir l'agriculture durable et à soutenir les initiatives d'inclusion sociale.
 3. Avancées technologiques
- Utilisation avancée de l'IA et des données : L'exploitation de l'intelligence artificielle pour la prise de décision en temps réel et l’analyse prédictive permet de maximiser les rendements tout en minimisant l'impact environnemental.
- Systèmes informatiques de gestion intégrée : Ces systèmes permettent de centraliser les données de production, de sales, et de gestion des ressources, facilitant une gestion plus transparente et efficace des opérations agricoles.
- Applications mobiles pour les agriculteurs : Développement d'applications adaptées aux agriculteurs pour leur fournir des conseils personnalisés sur les pratiques culturales, la météo, et le marché.
 4. Approche systémique et durable
- Synergie entre la culture et l'élevage : Intégration d’éléments de polyculture-élevage où les déchets des animaux sont utilisés comme engrais pour les cultures, et les résidus des cultures alimentent le bétail, créant ainsi un écosystème fermé.
- Gestion intégrée des ressources naturelles : Mettre en œuvre des outils de gestion durable de l'eau et du sol qui permettent de conserver et de restaurer les ressources naturelles tout en facilitant la productivité.
5. Axé sur la communauté
- Engagement communautaire : Des initiatives visant à inclure les membres de la communauté locale dans la gestion de la ferme, en leur offrant une formation et des opportunités d’emploi, renforçant ainsi les liens sociaux et économiques.
- Éducation et sensibilisation : Organisation de programmes éducatifs pour les agriculteurs et les consommateurs sur les avantages de l'agroécologie, favorisant une culture de durabilité au sein de la communauté.
Sustainable Change:
La ferme agroécologique intégrée joue un rôle crucial dans la création d'un changement systémique durable en intégrant une série de pratiques qui touchent non seulement la productivité agricole, mais également la communauté, l'environnement et l'économie. Voici comment cette ferme contribue à ce changement systémique, accompagnée des effets de suivi souhaités en lien avec la théorie du changement.
 1. Changement de paradigme en agriculture:
- Promotion des pratiques durables : En intégrant des méthodes agroécologiques, la ferme démontre des techniques qui mettent l’accent sur la régénération des sols, la biodiversité et la conservation des ressources, incitant d'autres agriculteurs à adopter ces pratiques.
- Inspiration et éducation : En servant de modèle, la ferme peut éduquer d'autres agriculteurs et parties prenantes sur les avantages de l'agroécologie, encourageant un movement collectif vers des pratiques agricoles plus durables.
 2. Renforcement des communautés:
- Création de réseaux locaux : La ferme agit comme un catalyseur pour construire des réseaux de solidarité entre agriculteurs, consommateurs et organisations locales, renforçant ainsi les liens sociaux et économiques.
- Autonomisation économique : En fournissant des formations et des ressources aux agriculteurs, la ferme contribue à l'autonomie économique, permettant aux producteurs de diversifier leurs revenus et d'améliorer leur qualité de vie.
 3. Résilience et adaptation aux changements climatiques
- Diversification des cultures : En promouvant la diversité des cultures, la ferme aide à réduire la vulnérabilité face aux chocs climatiques et économiques, augmentant ainsi la résilience des systèmes agricoles.
- Pratiques de gestion durable : La mise en œuvre de méthodes comme la récupération des eaux de pluie et la gestion intégrée des ressources naturelles aide à adapter les pratiques agricoles aux conditions climatiques changeantes.
 4. Impact environnemental positif
- Amélioration de la santé des sols : Les pratiques agroécologiques renforcent la santé des sols et la biodiversité, favorisant la séquestration du carbone et la réduction des émissions de gaz à effet de serre, contribuant ainsi à atténuer les changements climatiques.
- Qualité de l'eau et de l'air : En réduisant l'utilisation d'intrants chimiques et en pratiquant des méthodes de lutte biologique, la ferme contribue à la purification de l'eau et à l'amélioration de la qualité de l'air.
Effets de suivi souhaités (Théorie du changement):
Les effets de suivi souhaités résultant du déploiement de la ferme agroécologique intégrée peuvent inclure :
1. Adoption élargie de pratiques agroécologiques : Un pourcentage croissant d'agriculteurs voisins adoptent des techniques similaires basées sur les succès démontrés par la ferme.
2. Amélioration des indicateurs socio-économiques : Mesure de l'augmentation des revenus des agriculteurs et de la réduction de la pauvreté dans les communautés locales.
3. Renforcement de la biodiversité : Surveillance des populations d'espèces et amélioration de la santé écosystémique autour de la ferme, avec un impact mesurable sur la faune et flore locale.
4. Réduction des émissions de GES : Évaluation de la diminution des émissions de gaz à effet de serre directement liée aux pratiques mises en œuvre dans la ferme.
5. Résilience accrue face aux chocs climatiques : Capacité mesurée des agriculteurs à s'adapter aux variations climatiques, avec une réduction des pertes liées aux aléas climatiques.
6. Satisfaction et engagement communautaire : Augmentation de la participation des membres de la communauté dans les initiatives agroécologiques, mesurée par des sondages de satisfaction et des taux de participation.

Title: MeuBêst, connecter les éleveurs africains à l'intelligence agricole
Subtitle: MeuBêst est un outil numérique d'adaptation et d'atténuation climatique au Bénin et en Afrique de l'Ouest. Une application mobile multilingue (Français, Anglais, Fon, Bariba, Peulh, Fufulde) et inclusive avec une synthèse vocale qui offre quatre fonctions clés : Dis moi quand semer, Bien nourrir mes animaux, Mon Véto, Allo ATDA
Problem Statement:
Depuis 2010 plus de 15 000 décès ont été enregistré à la suite de conflits entre les communautés d'éleveurs et d'agriculteurs en Afrique subsaharienne. MeuBêst mobile pensée pour améliorer la résilience des agro-éleveurs face aux changements climatiques et aux conflits agropastoraux croissants, dans un contexte où la raréfaction des ressources et la mobilité non encadrée des troupeaux provoquent des tensions et d'important dégâts économiques et humains. Ces acteurs  sont confrontés à des problématiques communes :

- Manque de connaissances pratiques sur la valorisation de résidus agricoles

- Difficulté à trouver un vétérinaire de confiance, lenteur des réponses

- Mauvais calendrier agricoles, semis inadaptés

- Délai d'accès aux agents techniques long, manque d'accompagnement.

Le résultats attendus incluent l'amélioration des pratiques agricoles et d'alimentation animale, et une sédentarité encadrée des troupeaux.
Solution Overview:
MeuBêst est une application mobile multilingue (Français, Anglais, Fon, Bariba, Peulh, Fufulde) avec une synthèse vocale et qui offre quatre fonctions clés : 

- une interface "Dis moi quand semer" automatisée et générée par IA en fonction des conditions climatiques et du type de culture (riz, maïs, soja, sorgho)

- une interface "Bien nourrir mes animaux" avec un protocole détaillé de chaque étape de production, les quantités et les traitements (ex. Images d'illustration de production de balles de paille traitées à l'urée)

- une interface "Mon Véto" pour que l'éleveur en un clic, contacte un vétérinaire fiable dans sa commune 

- une interface "Allo ATDA" où l'utilisateur peut contacter l'Agence Territoriale de Développement Agricole de sa commune pour accéder à des informations, conseils, assistance ou faire un signalement 

Le projet MeuBêst a connu des étapes importantes :

- Construction du projet au sein de l'Établissement Spécialisé de la Francophonie pour l'Administration et le Management (ESFAM), agence de l'AUF à Sofia en Bulgarie, de mai 2023 à mai 2024.

- Finaliste du concours de startups Petit Poucet 2024 à Paris.

La prochaine étape sera le développement de l'application MeuBêst et sa diffusion au profit des communautés rurales 

Le projet MeuBêst intégrera le cadre GEDI (Gender Equality and Diversity Inclusion) de manière transversale, à la fois dans sa conception technologique, sa gouvernance et sa mise en œuvre sur le terrain. 

Concrètement, les actions suivantes seront menées pour garantir l’appropriation effective des principes GEDI :

1. Co-conception inclusive de l’interface utilisateur:
L’application MeuBêst sera conçue avec des interfaces adaptées aux profils de femmes rurales, souvent peu alphabétisées, à travers des contenus visuels, vocaux (en langues locales : fon, bariba, peulh, fulfulde) et interactifs. Des ateliers de co-design seront organisés avec des femmes agricultrices et transformatrices pour intégrer leurs besoins spécifiques.

2. Accès équitable aux données et services:
Les fonctionnalités de l’application (valorisation de résidus agricoles pour l'alimentation des ruminants, conseils vétérinaires, conseils techniques agricoles, recommandation de date de semis) seront testées avec un échantillon représentatif incluant au moins 50 % de femmes utilisatrices.
