Name of your organization: LES BÉNÉVOLES DE L'ÉDUCATION AUX MÉDIAS ET À L'INFORMATION (BEMI)
Title: "DÉSINFOX Connect : Autonomiser les jeunes contre la désinformation numérique"
Subtitle: A digital educational program that trains young people to detect, analyze, and counter online disinformation, thereby strengthening their inclusion and digital citizenship.
Problem Statement: The solution addresses the proliferation of online disinformation, the low digital literacy of young people and their vulnerability to manipulated content, thus reinforcing the information divide.
Solution Provider(s): Volunteers for Media and Information Education (BEMI): Ivorian organization specializing in training, awareness-raising, and support for young people and educational stakeholders on issues related to media literacy, digital citizenship, and the fight against disinformation. Active in the education, media, youth, and digital development sectors.  Other partners: Canal France International (media cooperation sector), Côte d'Ivoire Ministry of Youth (youth and citizenship sector), Félix Houphouët-Boigny University (higher education sector), UNESCO International (culture, education, and information sector), and local media partners (Fraternité Matin, RTI, etc.).
Duration to pilot in a new geography: The estimated time to test the DÉSINFOX Connect solution in a new geographic area is six months, broken down as follows:  1 month: participatory local assessment (analysis of the digital context and youth needs, stakeholder mapping);  2 months: adaptation of content and tools, mobilization of local partners, training of trainers and community representatives;  3 months: pilot implementation (training, digital campaigns, content production, participatory monitoring and evaluation).  This period allows for validation of the solution's local anchoring, educational effectiveness, and transferability.
SDGs addressed: SDG 4 (Quality Education);SDG 5 (Gender Equality);SDG 10 (Reduced Inequalities);
Desired impact:
The main objective of the DÉSINFOX Connect solution is to strengthen the digital inclusion of young people by developing their media and information literacy skills, enabling them to identify, analyze, and counter disinformation, while stimulating their online civic engagement. Through this approach, the solution aims to reduce young people's vulnerability to toxic content, improve their resilience to information manipulation, and promote critical and responsible use of digital technologies.

Expected impacts include the direct training of more than 1,500 young people over a 12-month period, at least 50% of whom will be young women; the creation of 30 local MIL ambassador groups in schools and universities; the production of more than 200 verified digital content assets (videos, articles, awareness capsules); and an estimated indirect reach of 100,000 young people reached through social media and digital campaigns. The solution also aims to create around ten technical or animation jobs in the pilot areas, and to contribute to the emergence of a local ecosystem to fight against disinformation.
Key technologies: The DÉSINFOX Connect solution relies primarily on accessible and proven digital technologies in the fields of information verification and media literacy. It uses artificial intelligence tools for the automated analysis of online content, such as algorithms for detecting fake content and recognizing manipulated images or videos. In addition, interactive web and mobile platforms enable the delivery of training modules, skills assessment via adaptive quizzes, and online collaboration between participants. The solution also integrates open-source fact-checking tools (such as InVID or ClaimReview) and community management systems to facilitate moderation and secure content sharing. Although blockchain is not directly used, the solution remains open to the future integration of traceability technologies to ensure data transparency.
Unique Characteristics:
The uniqueness of DÉSINFOX Connect lies in its integrated, community-based approach, which combines practical training, active youth participation, and a strong local presence. 
Unlike many initiatives focused solely on awareness-raising, this solution engages young people not only as beneficiaries but also as co-producers of verified content, thus fostering real and sustainable empowerment. Its multi-stakeholder partnership model involving NGOs, public institutions, universities, and media outlets ensures collaborative governance and local ownership, guaranteeing the project's sustainability and adaptability to diverse contexts. Furthermore, the combined use of artificial intelligence technologies for fact-checking, along with accessible open-source tools, makes the solution both innovative and accessible, avoiding costly reliance on proprietary platforms. Finally, its hybrid training program (in-person, online, and digital campaigns) allows for gradual, flexible skills development adapted to realities on the ground, particularly in areas with low connectivity.
Sustainable Change:
DÉSINFOX Connect aims for lasting systemic change by transforming information dynamics at the very foundation of youth communities. Its theory of change is based on the idea that by strengthening young people's media and digital literacy, they become critical actors capable of deconstructing and combating disinformation, thereby reducing the spread of toxic content and improving the quality of local public debate.

By developing a network of trained and autonomous local ambassadors, the solution creates a sustainable leveraging effect, where skills transfer occurs continuously and decentralized, fostering collective resilience in the face of digital manipulation. The multi-stakeholder partnership ensures that educational and public institutions sustainably integrate these skills into their curricula and policies, thus creating an environment conducive to a responsible digital culture.

In the medium and long term, this process aims to significantly reduce inequalities in access to reliable information, strengthen social cohesion and trust in institutions, and support the construction of an inclusive digital society, where young people play an active role in information governance. This structural change translates into a sustainable improvement in the quality of the information ecosystem, a strengthening of citizen participation and a limitation of the harmful effects of disinformation on democratic processes.
Funding Sources: The DÉSINFOX Connect solution has not yet been implemented. However, its development and design were primarily funded through internal resources provided by the sponsoring organization, the Media and Information Education Volunteers (BEMI), as well as technical and logistical support from partnerships with academic institutions and specialized NGOs. At this stage, no external funding dedicated to a pilot phase or regional deployment has yet been secured. Efforts are underway to solicit funding from international donors and cooperation organizations to ensure the implementation and expansion of the solution.
Testimonials and Endorsements:
Since the DÉSINFOX Connect solution has not yet been deployed, there are no direct testimonials from beneficiaries. However, key stakeholders involved in the design highlighted its potential. For example, a university trainer involved in the project stated: "This hybrid approach, combining training and active youth participation, is a real opportunity to strengthen their critical thinking in the face of disinformation, a major challenge of our time."

A representative of a partner organization added: "Désinfox Connect's collaborative model creates a sustainable framework that will anchor these skills in local educational practices, thus fostering profound and lasting change."

These recommendations illustrate the partners' confidence in the relevance and expected impact of the solution once deployed.
Further comments/feedback: The questionnaire is generally well structured and comprehensively covers the essential aspects for presenting an innovative solution for an inclusive digital economy. However, it could be made clearer by further specifying certain key concepts, in particular the distinction between technological innovation and social innovation, in order to more precisely guide responses. Furthermore, a section dedicated to the assessment of potential risks related to the implementation of the solution (technical, social, financial) would be a relevant addition to anticipate obstacles and demonstrate the robustness of the project. Finally, it would be useful to include a section on monitoring and impact indicators, which would facilitate a better assessment of the long-term viability and effectiveness of the solutions submitted.
Primary thematic focus area: Inclusive Digital Innovation Skills & Entrepreneurial Talent Development
Summary: DÉSINFOX Connect proposes an integrated educational approach to fight disinformation by training youth as fact-checkers and digital literacy ambassadors. Its strengths lie in its innovative pedagogy, strong multi-stakeholder partnerships, and clear expected quantitative targets. The main weakness is that it remains at the idea/concept stage, with no pilot implementation yet, which limits feasibility evidence.

Title: Inclusive Solar Tricycles E-Mobility Pilot Project for Women, Persons with Disabilities (PWDs), and Youth Empowerment in Zambia and Nigeria
Subtitle: Digital tricycles for easy mobility
Problem Statement:
In many rural and peri-urban areas of Zambia and Nigeria, mobility remains a persistent and critical challenge. The lack of reliable, affordable, and inclusive transport solutions severely limits access to essential services such as healthcare, education, and markets—especially for women, youth, and persons with disabilities (PWDs). This limited access undermines socio-economic development and entrenches existing inequalities.
1. Mobility Challenges
In rural Zambia, over 70% of the population resides in dispersed communities with poor or non-existent road infrastructure, making transport difficult and costly. Public transport is often unreliable or unavailable, forcing residents to walk long distances—up to 10–15 km daily—to reach clinics, schools, or trading centers. Similarly, in northern Nigeria and other rural parts of the country, insecurity, fuel scarcity, and poor infrastructure worsen the situation. For women and girls, these challenges are heightened by social norms and safety concerns, limiting their economic and educational participation.
2. High Poverty Levels
Both Zambia and Nigeria have high poverty rates, particularly in rural areas. In Zambia, over 54% of the population lives below the poverty line, while in Nigeria, rural poverty is widespread, with millions lacking access to basic infrastructure and livelihoods. For women, youth, and PWDs, the lack of affordable transport creates a significant barrier to employment, healthcare, and income-generating activities, perpetuating exclusion and poverty.
3. Climate Change and Environmental Stress
Climate change is exacerbating vulnerabilities. Extreme weather events such as floods, prolonged droughts, and rising temperatures are disrupting agricultural livelihoods—the primary income source for rural populations. These conditions highlight the urgent need for low-emission, climate-resilient transport alternatives. Continued reliance on fossil fuel-based transport also contributes to greenhouse gas emissions and air pollution in these regions.

Why This Project Is Innovative
This project is highly innovative because it combines inclusive mobility, green technology, and community empowerment in a unique and scalable way. By integrating solar-powered electric tricycles (e-trikes) tailored specifically for women, PWDs, and youth, the initiative breaks away from traditional transport models that often exclude marginalized groups. The use of solar charging hubs, IoT-enabled diagnostics, and Pay-As-You-Go (PAYG) mobile payment systems represents a smart, sustainable solution grounded in local realities. Additionally, by training youth in assembly and maintenance, the project builds long-term local capacity and creates green jobs—paving the way for a new, inclusive e-mobility ecosystem in Sub-Saharan Africa. Its replicable model and alignment with the Sustainable Development Goals (SDGs) make it a blueprint for socially just and climate-smart transportation innovation.

CEJ designs solar-powered e-tricycles for women, youth, and PWDs, supports zero-emission transport, and builds solar charging hubs in underserved areas. Title: Grahaye Climat+
Subtitle: A digital solution empowering schools, youth, and communities with climate data and education for sustainable futures.
Problem Statement: In Chad and across Africa, access to climate education, environmental data, and digital tools remains limited. Schools and communities lack resources to understand climate risks, manage environmental information, and prepare youth for the digital economy. This digital divide exacerbates inequalities and limits participation in sustainable development.
Solution Overview:
Grahaye Climat+ is a web and mobile platform designed to provide schools, students, and communities with digital tools for climate education, data access, and inclusive participation in the green economy.
How it works: The platform integrates APIs (NASA, Google, local data) for real-time climate and environmental information, combined with educational resources, digital classrooms, and community reporting features.
Methodologies & technologies: MERN stack (MongoDB, Express, React, Node.js), PostgreSQL, API integrations, secure cloud deployment (Vercel, Render).
Partnership model: Collaboration with local schools, universities, community groups, and climate NGOs. Open for partnerships with governments and UN agencies for scaling.
Solution Provider(s): Aldôlo (startup, Chad, digital innovation), in collaboration with a young innovators’ team including Rondouba Mbaiadem Rochto (Founder), Keimadji Casimir (Data Analyst), Ali Moussa Kadjallah (Frontend Developer), Djegolbe Reoukaoude (Community Manager), Bekainyogoto Vangila (Backend Developer).
Implementation location(s): N’Djamena, Chad (initial prototype testing with schools and communities)
Duration to pilot in a new geography: 6 to 9 months (including contextual adaptation, stakeholder engagement, deployment, and training)
SDGs addressed: SDG 4 (Quality Education);SDG 9 (Industry, Innovation, and Infrastructure);SDG 13 (Climate Action);
Desired impact:
Objectives: Bridge the digital divide in climate education, empower youth with digital skills, and foster community engagement in sustainable development.
Expected impacts: Improved digital literacy for 10,000+ students within 3 years, increased awareness on climate issues in schools and communities, integration of climate data into education and decision-making.

Title: AGRISOL CONNECT: Smart Digital Platform for Inclusive Agroforestry
Subtitle: A mobile-first digital platform empowering rural women and youth with tools for smart farming, agroforestry, food processing, and market access in underserved areas.
Problem Statement: In many rural areas of Mali and Sub-Saharan Africa, smallholder farmers, especially women and youth, face limited access to information, markets, training, and digital tools. These constraints lead to low productivity, post-harvest losses, weak value chain integration, and persistent poverty. Moreover, most available digital solutions are not adapted to local languages, literacy levels, or rural connectivity challenges. The digital economic divide continues to exclude rural communities from growth opportunities, hindering inclusive and sustainable development.
Solution Overview:
AGRISOL CONNECT is an inclusive, mobile-first digital platform designed by AGRIDEV Mali to empower rural women and youth in agriculture and agroforestry. It bridges the digital economic divide by providing accessible tools for smart farming, food processing, training, and market access, even in low-connectivity and low-literacy environments.

1. How the Solution Works
AGRISOL CONNECT combines a mobile application (with offline capabilities) and a web dashboard to deliver localized services to smallholder farmers, women-led cooperatives, and rural agro-processors. The app offers:
Agroforestry guidance: Step-by-step instructions for planting and managing moringa, baobab, hibiscus, ginger, and other species, with local climate adaptation tips.
Transformation tutorials: Audio-visual guides for producing powder, tea, syrup, juice, and chips using local raw materials.
Voice-based navigation: Information in local languages (Bambara, Fulani, French) using audio messages and pictograms to support low-literacy users.
Market linkage: A simple marketplace tool for farmers and processors to connect with buyers and cooperatives.
Training modules: Offline mini-courses in agri-business, agroecology, food safety (HACCP), and entrepreneurship.
Financing access: In-app forms and guidance to link users to microfinance, grants, and UN-supported funds.
2. Methodologies and Technologies Used
User-centered design: Developed through field interviews with rural women and youth to ensure cultural and linguistic relevance.
Progressive Web App (PWA): Lightweight, works offline, and syncs data when connectivity is available.
Vice-based interface: Text-to-speech and interactive voice response (IVR) systems for non-literate users.
GIS and weather data integration: To give crop-specific, localized agricultural advice.
Modular learning system: Bite-sized training content with quizzes, badges, and printable certificates.
AI-based recommendation engine (Phase II): Will suggest optimal planting periods, techniques, and market prices based on user data and location.
3. Partnerships and Collaboration Models
Local Cooperatives: Women-led groups co-create content, serve as ambassadors, and provide feedback loops.
Telecom operators & digital hubs: To expand network coverage and distribute low-cost sartphones with the app pre-installed.
Technical institutions & NGOs: Co-develop training modules and support capacity-building efforts (e.g., with FAO, GIZ, or local universities).
Financial institutions: Partnerships with microfinance institutions and digital banks for credit access and mobile payments.
UNIDO & UN agencies: As scaling and validation partners through pilot projects, certification programs, and matchmaking initiatives.
Solution Provider(s): AGRIDEV Mali (Agro-industrial SME specializing in agroforestry and agro-processing, focused on women’s empowerment and sustainable agriculture in Mali), Coopérative Agricole des Femmes de Sébénikoro (Women-led cooperative supporting agroforestry, local transformation, and inclusive entrepreneurship), ADCE Mali – Association pour le Développement de la Culture Entrepreneuriale (Non-profit organization promoting youth and women entrepreneurship in agriculture and green innovation), Tunel Group Industrial Cooling Systems (Private sector partner providing expertise in solar cold storage and post-harvest preservation technologies), API-Mali (Public Agency for Investment Promotion, supporting formalization and business development in rural areas), Institut d’Économie Rurale (IER Mali) – Research institute contributing to agroecology, farming systems, and technology adaptation), Local microfinance institutions (e.g., Kafo Jiginew, Nyèsigiso) – Financial inclusion partners enabling access to credit and digital payments), GIZ (Deutsche Gesellschaft für Internationale Zusammenarbeit – Supporting rural digital transformation and capacity-building), UNIDO Mali Country Office – Strategic support for scaling, certification, and UN platform integration).
Implementation location(s): This clearly indicates that the solution has not yet been implemented in any location. Let me know if you need help formulating the next section!
Duration to pilot in a new geography: Estimated duration: 6 to 9 months  This includes:  2 months for co-creation workshops, content adaptation, and local language integration  2 months for digital platform development and testing  1 month for onboarding of users (cooperatives, farmers, processors)  2 to 4 months for field deployment, feedback collection, and performance monitoring
SDGs addressed: SDG 5 (Gender Equality);SDG 8 (Decent Work and Economic Growth);SDG 9 (Industry, Innovation, and Infrastructure);
Desired impact:
AGRISOL CONNECT aims to:

Bridge the digital divide in rural areas by providing inclusive, locally-adapted digital tools for smallholder farmers and agro-processors.
Empower women and youth through digital access to training, agroecological techniques, food processing methods, and entrepreneurship support.
Improve productivity and reduce post-harvest losses via data-driven agroforestry practices, food safety guidance, and market access tools.
Foster climate-smart agriculture and sustainable land use through better decision-making, agroforestry promotion, and resource optimization.
Key Achievements / Anticipated Impacts
Since the solution is currently at the Idea/Concept stage, the following are projected impacts after pilot implementation:

 5,000+ rural women and youth trained and digitally onboarded within 2 years.
 10,000 hectares of agroforestry (moringa, baobab, hibiscus, ginger) monitored and supported through the platform.
30% reduction in post-harvest losses among users through better preservation, processing, and cold storage guidance.
500+ rural microenterprises supported with market access, HACCP-compliant training, and digital entrepreneurship modules.
Estimated GHG reduction of 120–150 tons CO₂/year through agroforestry carbon sequestration and reduced food waste (in pilot zones).
 Improved circular economy practices through localized processing and responsible consumption education.
Key technologies:
Key Technologies Used
AGRISOL CONNECT integrates the following technologies to ensure accessibility, intelligence, and scalability:
Progressive Web App (PWA): A lightweight mobile-first platform that works offline and synchronizes when connectivity is available, ensuring access in low-infrastructure rural areas.
Voice-Based Interface & Local Language Integration: Uses text-to-speech and Interactive Voice Response (IVR) systems to serve users with low literacy levels, supporting French, Bambara, Fulani, and other local languages.
Artificial Intelligence (AI – Planned Phase): A simple recommendation engine will use user data, geolocation, and seasonal trends to suggest optimized planting schedules, processing techniques, and market pricing.
Geolocation and Weather API: Real-time weather alerts and location-based advice to enhance climate resilience in farming and agroforestry.
QR Code & Batch Tracking (Planned): Enables basic traceability of processed products for quality assurance, HACCP compliance, and future integration with e-certification systems.
Unique Characteristics:
AGRISOL CONNECT stands out through a combination of technological inclusivity, local adaptation, and an integrated value chain approach. Key differentiators include:
Digital Inclusion for Non-Literate Users: Unlike many agri-tech platforms, AGRISOL CONNECT is designed from the ground up to be usable by people with low literacy levels, using voice navigation, pictograms, and local languages.
Women-First Design Approach: The solution is co-created with women-led cooperatives, with content tailored to the specific needs of female agro-processors and farmers, addressing gender inequality in rural entrepreneurship.
Agroforestry + Transformation + Market in One Platform: It integrates agroecological advisory, food processing guidance, and digital market access in a single mobile tool—offering a complete farm-to-market pathway.
Community-Based Deployment Model: AGRISOL CONNECT leverages local cooperatives and community agents as trainers, testers, and data contributors—ensuring grassroots ownership and trust.
Inclusive Financing Linkages: Through partnerships with microfinance institutions and digital finance providers, the platform supports credit scoring tools, savings groups, and grant opportunities for underserved entrepreneurs.
Offline-first Technology Strategy: Recognizing rural connectivity constraints, the platform uses Progressive Web App (PWA) architecture and IVR-based training to ensure functionality with or without internet.
Scalability across Francophone Africa: Its modular, language-adaptable design makes it easily replicable across other rural regions in the UEMOA and Sahel zones.
Sustainable Change:

Which leads to:

Strengthened rural entrepreneurship ecosystems, with local cooperatives as digital service hubs

Digital ecosystems that leave no one behind, by reaching even non-literate populations

This systemic change is sustainable because:

Title: EmpowerEd
Subtitle: Empowering teachers in small Nigerian schools with AI training to enhance lesson planning, activity creation, and educational quality.
Problem Statement: The Nigerian education sector faces significant challenges, particularly in public schools, where overcrowding and inadequate resources have resulted in subpar learning outcomes. Many children struggle to read and write at a basic level, hindering their future prospects. In response, small private schools have emerged to fill the gap, driven by passionate educators. However, these schools often lack the resources to employ qualified teachers, relying on makeshift solutions. The integration of technology, specifically Artificial Intelligence (AI), could be a game-changer. Yet, many teachers in these schools are unfamiliar with AI tools, unable to harness their potential to enhance lesson planning, activity creation, and overall educational quality. This knowledge gap limits the effectiveness of these schools, perpetuating educational disparities. Without support, these schools risk falling further behind, exacerbating the existing educational crisis. Our project seeks to address this pressing issue by providing training and support for teachers in small schools, empowering them to effectively utilize AI tools and improve educational outcomes for their students.
Solution Overview:
Our project solution involves a multi-faceted approach to empower teachers in small schools to effectively utilize Artificial Intelligence (AI) tools, enhancing educational outcomes for students. We will:

1. Develop a tailored training program for teachers on AI tools, focusing on lesson planning, activity creation, and student assessment.
2. Provide access to AI-powered educational resources and platforms, curated to support the Nigerian curriculum.
3. Offer ongoing mentorship and support to ensure teachers' successful integration of AI tools into their teaching practices.
4. Foster a community of practice among participating schools, facilitating knowledge sharing and collaboration.
5. Monitor and evaluate the impact of AI integration on student learning outcomes, informing future project development.

By equipping teachers with the skills and resources needed to harness AI, we aim to improve educational quality, increase student engagement, and bridge the knowledge gap in small schools across Nigeria. Our solution is scalable, sustainable, and adaptable to the needs of diverse educational settings.

We will implement our project through a multi-channel approach, including:

1. Webinars: Bimonthly online sessions teaching AI tool utilization, focusing on free resources like Canva, Magic School, and ChatGPT. Sessions will cover lesson planning, activity creation, and teaching unfamiliar subjects.
2. Mentorship Class: One-on-one guidance and support for teachers to ensure successful AI integration.
3. WhatsApp Group: A dedicated platform for teachers to ask questions, share experiences, and access updated teaching resources, news, and global best practices.
4. Resource Sharing: Curated AI-powered educational resources, aligned with the Nigerian curriculum, will be shared through the WhatsApp group and webinars.
5. Community Building: Regular virtual meetups and discussions to foster collaboration, address challenges, and celebrate successes.
6. Feedback Mechanism: Continuous evaluation and feedback collection to refine our approach and ensure project effectiveness.
7. Partnerships: Collaborations with educational organizations and platforms to expand our reach and provide teachers with access to additional resources and expertise.

By leveraging these channels, we aim to empower teachers, enhance educational quality, and promote sustainable project impact.

Title: Ecosolar is an innovative AI-powered digital platform (mobile and web) dedicated to the distribution of solar solutions for households and individuals. It allows users to discover, purchase, and install solar systems tailored to their energy needs.
Subtitle: The mobile app offers a wide range of products, such as solar panels, storage batteries, solar water pumps, and accessories, while providing detailed information on energy efficiency and savings. It simplifies the purchasing process, facilitates installation and maintenance, and provides real-time monitoring of energy consumption, thus contributing to the energy transition and reducing energy costs.
Problem Statement:
The innovative EcoSolar project aims to address a critical challenge: limited, unstable, or nonexistent access to reliable and sustainable electricity in many areas, particularly rural and peri-urban areas, in Cameroon.

The identified problems are:

- Unequal access and fluctuating quality of electricity: many communities and areas remain unconnected or poorly served.
- Lack of centralized information on available solar solutions and their cost-effectiveness.
- Difficulties for users to identify reliable solar products suited to their needs.
Solution Overview:
EcoSolar offers a centralized digital platform that provides:

- Easy access to solar equipment categorized by product range.
- Integrated AI-powered solar kit and solar water pump simulators for a better choice of suitable solutions.
- Online ordering with 24/7 technical support.
- Adapted financing and payment options (direct purchase, 24-time payment plan, 4-time payment plan, leasing, and bank credit, etc.)
- Implementation of solar energy training and awareness programs.
- Integration of accurate mapping and data on solar installations in Cameroon and Africa.

EcoSolar makes solar energy more accessible, transparent, and tailored to everyone's needs with just one click.

IProject Objectives
- Promote the adoption of home solar energy through an accessible, smart, and mobile platform.
- Offer a sustainable business model based on the distribution of solar solutions, subscriptions, and complementary services.
- Contribute to reducing household energy costs while supporting the energy transition.
Key technologies: The EcoSolar platform leverages key technologies to maximize its impact. It integrates AI with the Solar Kit and Pump Simulator, an intuitive mobile app for managing consumption and services, and IoT sensors for real-time performance monitoring. A cloud system ensures data storage and analysis, while mobile payment solutions facilitate subscriptions.

Title: Extending Augmented Reality to Churches
Subtitle: This is a new feature that helps preserve the heritage of churches across the world by extending augmented reality to the phones of visitors.
Problem Statement: The Sustainable Development Goal (SDG) 11 relates to sustainable cities and communities. SDG 11.4 in particular has the aim to "strengthen efforts to protect and safeguard the world’s cultural and natural heritage". A significant part of the world's heritage is tied and associated with churches. For example, many UNESCO World Heritage sites are churches, such as Cologne Cathedral and the Sagrada Familia. This solution addresses the information gap that visitors and tourists have with the churches they visit by enriching the experience with the help of augmented reality (AR). Augmented reality is a technology that enables digital objects to appear as if they interact with the physical, real world. In the present case, augmented reality is used to enrich the experience of the visit to the church by a tourist or worshipper by providing greater context on the heritage and history of the church. Furthermore, the feature also contributes to local economies by connecting tour guides with those wanting a physical human to walk them through the church.
Solution Overview: The feature in our app utilises augmented reality (AR) with mobile phones so that when a visitor or tourist visits a church, they can hover the phone over the church to find out either about the heritage of the church or what a particular statue or painting is about. Churches are important hubs when it comes to history - both local and global - and a lot of this is missed by those who visit. The feature aims to change that. At a more technical level, the augmented reality feature is powered by ARKit for iOS mobile devices and ARCore for Android mobile devices. The feature also aims to connect local tour guides who know about the church with those who visit wanting more information about the church, thereby creating an additional revenue stream for local economies.
Solution Provider(s): ChurchMapped Limited
SDGs addressed: SDG 11 (Sustainable Cities and Communities);SDG 9 (Industry, Innovation, and Infrastructure);SDG 8 (Decent Work and Economic Growth);
Desired impact: The desired impact of the solution is exactly as articulated in SDG 11.4: to strengthen and preserve cultural heritage. In this case, this is being done with churches. Another desired impact of the solution is to enhance knowledge about churches and associated monuments among the population. Additionally, another impact the solution is striving for is to help boost local economies. We also hope the solution will help enhance the visibility of our organisation.
Key technologies: The feature will be available on both Android and iOS devices and it utilises augmented reality (AR).
Unique Characteristics: We were shortlisted in the International Telecommunication Union and United Nations' 1st Citiverse Challenge out of 48 other startups. We believe our solution is unique in that we are using augmented reality technology in a new way in a space that is typically considered as traditional. The Challenge is still ongoing and we aspire to win.
Sustainable Change: The solution contributes to sustainable, systemic change by helping people understand the importance of churches as heritage sites and the connection they have with the local community. Currently, information on churches is usually hard to find: we're aiming to change that.
Funding Sources: We are a privately funded company and the solution is being funded by the revenues we earn as a company.

Visitors can hover their phones over a church, statue, or painting to access contextual heritage insights, while also connecting with local tour guides for in-person experiences. The solution aligns with SDG 11.4 on protecting cultural heritage, and additionally aims to generate revenue opportunities for local communities. The initiative has been recognized by the ITU and UN Citiverse Challenge, highlighting its innovative approach in applying AR to cultural preservation.

Ce projet vise à développer une plateforme numérique d'inscription scolaire, qui permettra une gestion simplifiée des inscriptions, de la carte scolaire et de la distribution des bulletins scolaires.té spécialisée dans le domaine de l'éducation et du développement humain. Nous avons une équipe de professionnels expérimentés dans la conception et la mise en œuvre de programmes éducatifs adaptés aux contextes locaux. Notre expertise couvre différents aspects tels que la formation des enseignants, l'innovation pédagogique, l'utilisation des technologies de l'information et de la communication (TIC) en éducation et la promotion de la qualité dans les établissements scolaires.
Subtitle: Nous sommes ravis de soumettre notre candidature pour le projet d'innovation de logiciels visant à créer une plateforme numérique pour la gestion des écoles et des élèves au Niger. Notre équipe est composée d'experts passionnés par l'éducation et la technologie, avec une expérience significative dans le développement de solutions numériques pour l'amélioration de la qualité de l'éducation.Le Niger, avec une population jeune et en croissance rapide, fait face à des défis importants dans le secteur de l'éducation, notamment en matière de gestion des données scolaires, de suivi des performances des élèves et de modernisation des systèmes éducatifs. Ce projet vise à introduire une plateforme numérique innovante pour améliorer la transparence, l'efficacité et l'accessibilité des services éducatifs à travers le pays.
Problem Statement:
Accès inégal à l’éducation
   - De nombreux élèves, en particulier ceux issus de milieux défavorisés, rencontrent des obstacles à l'accès à l'information et aux ressources éducatives. La solution facilite l'inscription en ligne et l'accès aux ressources scolaires, réduisant ainsi les inégalités.
Manque de transparence et de communication
   - Les parents et les éducateurs peuvent avoir des difficultés à suivre les progrès des élèves et à obtenir des informations pertinentes sur leurs performances. La plateforme centralise les données, offrant des rapports clairs et des canaux de communication efficaces entre les parties prenantes.
Gestion inefficace des données
   - Les établissements scolaires utilisent souvent des systèmes manuels ou désuets pour gérer les informations des élèves, ce qui entraîne des erreurs et une perte de temps. La solution propose une gestion automatisée et structurée des données, améliorant ainsi l'efficacité administrative.
Personnalisation de l'apprentissage
   - Chaque élève a des besoins différents en matière d'apprentissage. La solution permet d'adapter les programmes éducatifs en fonction des performances et des préférences individuelles, favorisant un apprentissage personnalisé.
Rétention et engagement des élèves
   - Le désengagement des élèves est un défi majeur dans l'éducation. En fournissant des fonctionnalités interactives et un accès facile aux ressources, la plateforme peut rendre l'apprentissage plus engageant et motivant.
Évaluation et suivi des performances
   - Les méthodes traditionnelles d'évaluation peuvent être lentes et peu réactives. La solution offre des outils d'analyse et de suivi en temps réel, permettant aux éducateurs d'évaluer rapidement la performance des élèves et d'ajuster les stratégies pédagogiques.
Adaptation au changement technologique
   - La rapidité des évolutions technologiques pose un défi pour les écoles qui doivent s'adapter. La solution intègre des outils modernes et des ressources numériques, aidant ainsi les établissements à rester à jour et pertinents dans un environnement éducatif en constante évolution.
Manque de ressources de soutien pour les enseignants
   - Les enseignants peuvent ne pas avoir accès à une formation continue adéquate sur les nouvelles technologies et les méthodes d'enseignement. La plateforme peut proposer des ressources de développement professionnel et des formations en ligne, leur permettant de se former en continu.
Ces défis sont cruciaux pour garantir un système éducatif efficace, équitable et adaptable. La solution logicielle vise à répondre à ces problèmes de manière innovante et durable.
Solution Overview:
Simplification des Inscriptions Développer une interface conviviale pour les familles, facilitant les démarches d'inscription dans les écoles publiques.
Gestion de la Carte Scolaire : Intégrer une fonctionnalité permettant de visualiser les zones de carte scolaire, d'attribuer les établissements en fonction de la géolocalisation, et d'informer les familles sur les établissements disponibles.
Bulletins Numériques  Créer un système permettant aux enseignants de publier et aux parents d'accéder aux bulletins scolaires au format numérique, réduisant ainsi l'utilisation de papier et améliorant la communication entre l’école et les familles.
Utilisation des QR Codes Intégrer des QR codes sur les documents officiels qui permettront un accès rapide à des informations pertinentes via smartphones, facilitant ainsi le processus de communication.
Analyse des Besoins Réaliser une enquête auprès des parents, élèves et enseignants pour identifier les besoins et les attentes vis-à-vis de la plateforme.
Développement Technique Collaborer avec des experts en informatique pour créer la plateforme, en s'assurant qu'elle soit sécurisée, évolutive et facile d'utilisation.
Phase de Test  Mettre en place une version bêta de la plateforme dans quelques établissements pour recueillir les retours d'expérience et apporter des améliorations.
Formation Organiser des sessions de formation pour les enseignants et le personnel administratif sur l'utilisation de la plateforme.
Lancement Une fois les tests et les formations réalisés, lancer officiellement la plateforme à l'échelle départementale ou nationale.

Title: DigiAgricMart: AI-assisted Digital Marketing for Rural Farmers in Nigeria
Subtitle: Code named DigiAgricMart, is an AI-assisted digital marketing platform (e-commerce) for smallholder farmers in Nigeria.
Problem Statement: Smallholder farmers in the rural of Nigeria lack access to market, transparent pricing, sustainable income and real-time market information. There post-harvest losses, limited storage and exploitative trade practices. There is currently no digital marketing platform that could solve the  challenges in the rural communities of Nigeria, hence the need for this project.
Solution Overview: DigiAgricMart will be designed as Progressive Web App (PWA) and mobile-first (Android), to be accessible offline with background sync for low-bandwidth rural areas. The platform would provide for onboarding, product listing, smart matching algorithm, order management system, and agro-logistics integration. There will be digital wallet and payments, inventory and pricing tools, feedback and analytic dashboard. The core technology to be employed at the frontend and backend, include:  ReactJS, Flutter for mobile, HTML5 PWA for frontend and Node.js / Django, PostgreSQL, Firebase for the backend. AI features would provide for Product categorization, demand prediction, voice search (to support local language). Collaboration will be sought from ICT Centre and Agricultural Engineering Department of the Federal Polytehnic, Idah.  Farmers’ Cooperative Societies, Government Agencies - Small and Medium Entreprises Development Agency (SMEDAN) of Nigeria, as well as National Information Technology Development Agency (NITDA), Nigeria shall be part of the partnership in this project. The model is multi-stakeholder to follow, majorly the Public-Private Partnership (PPP) model.
Solution Provider(s): Information and Communication Centre (The Federal Polytechnic, Idah – academia), Department of Agricultural Engineering (The Federal Polytechnic, Idah -  academia), National Information Technology Development Agency (NITDA), Nigeria (Goverument Agency – Public) and Small and Medium Entreprises Development Agency (SMEDAN) of Nigeria (Government Agency – Public).
Duration to pilot in a new geography: Six Months
SDGs addressed: SDG 1 (No Poverty);SDG 2 (Zero Hunger);SDG 9 (Industry, Innovation, and Infrastructure);
Desired impact: The platform is aimed at digitally connecting rural agro-entrepreneurs (smallholder farmers) to formal markets, logistics, and financial services through a user-friendly, inclusive digital platform which will enhance income, reduces post-harvest losses, and strengthens agro-value chains in Nigeria and Africa generally.
Key technologies: Mobile-First and Progressive Web Application (PWA), Artificial Intelligence (AI), Multilingual and Voice Interface Technologies and Fintech and Payments Integration. Others are Logistics and Location Technologies, Analytics and Monitoring Dashboard and Offline-First and Low-Bandwidth optimization.
Unique Characteristics: DigiAgricMart would be the first AI-assisted Digital Marketing Platform in Nigeria tailored to the specific challenges of rural agricultural commerce. The platform leverages advanced technology and inclusive design to address digital exclusion, market inefficiencies, and financial inaccessibility.
Sustainable Change: DigiAgricMart will address structural barriers in rural agricultural economies with technology-driven, inclusive, and locally embedded solutions. This would be done by Market System Transformation (Agricultural Value Chain), Digital Inclusion for the Underserved, Financial Access and Inclusion, Localized Logistics Infrastructure and Youth Engagement and Job Creation.
Funding Sources: Not applicable
Testimonials and Endorsements: Not available
Further comments/feedback: Not available
Primary thematic focus area: MSME Empowerment & Local Digital Innovation
Summary: DigiAgricMart is an AI-assisted e-commerce platform concept designed to connect smallholder farmers in rural Nigeria to markets, logistics, and financial services. It proposes a mobile-first Progressive Web App with AI features for product categorization, demand prediction, and voice search in local languages. Strengths: directly addresses systemic issues of market access and farmer exploitation, integrates multiple technologies (AI, PWA, fintech), and aligns well with SDG1, SDG2, and SDG9. Weaknesses: idea-stage only, no pilot or prototype, limited evidence of funding, and heavy dependence on multiple institutional partners without demonstrated commitments.

Title: EduConnect Africa: Digital Learning for All
Subtitle: A bilingual digital platform empowering inclusive education in West Africa.
Problem Statement: In West Africa, particularly in Francophone countries like Senegal and Côte d'Ivoire, limited access to digital education tools and linguistic barriers hinder inclusive learning, exacerbating the digital economic divide. Rural communities and underserved populations lack affordable, scalable solutions to access quality education, limiting economic opportunities and social mobility.
Solution Overview:
Description: EduConnect Africa is a bilingual (French-English) digital platform delivering accessible, high-quality education content to underserved communities in West Africa. It provides interactive courses, teacher training, and entrepreneurial skills development, tailored to local contexts.
Methodologies and Technologies: The platform uses cloud-based e-learning modules, mobile apps, and offline access capabilities to reach remote areas. AI-driven analytics personalize learning paths, while gamification enhances engagement.
Partnerships and Collaboration Models: SDA collaborates with UN agencies (e.g., UNESCO), local governments, and private sector partners (e.g., telecom providers) to ensure content relevance and infrastructure support. Community-based organizations facilitate grassroots adoption.

Implementation location(s): Not applicable (prototype stage, planned pilots in Senegal and Guinea).
Implementation timeline(s): Not applicable (prototype stage, planned pilots in Senegal and Guinea).
Duration to pilot in a new geography: 6-9 months to deploy a pilot in Senegal or Guinea, including stakeholder onboarding, content localization, and infrastructure setup.
SDGs addressed: SDG 4 (Quality Education);SDG 8 (Decent Work and Economic Growth);SDG 10 (Reduced Inequalities);
Desired impact:
To provide affordable, bilingual digital education to 50,000 learners in West Africa within two years, enhancing employability and entrepreneurial skills.

Key Achievements: Projected to increase digital literacy by 30% in pilot communities, create 1,000 indirect jobs through MSME training, and reduce educational disparities for rural and female learners.
Key technologies: AI for personalized learning, cloud-based platforms for scalability, mobile apps for accessibility, and offline-enabled tools for remote areas.
Unique Characteristics: EduConnect Africa’s bilingual (French-English) approach ensures cultural and linguistic relevance in Francophone West Africa. Its offline functionality addresses connectivity challenges, while partnerships with telecoms and UN agencies ensure scalability and credibility. The platform’s focus on entrepreneurial skills fosters economic inclusion.
Sustainable Change: EduConnect Africa’s Theory of Change posits that accessible, bilingual digital education will empower underserved communities, particularly women and rural youth, to gain skills for employment and entrepreneurship. This drives economic inclusion, reduces inequalities, and strengthens local economies. Follow-on effects include increased MSME activity, improved digital infrastructure, and policy advocacy for inclusive education, aligning with the Global Digital Compact’s goals.

Name of your organization: Department of Science and Technology – Forest Products Research and Development Institute
Title: eForestCrafts: Digital Marketplace & Skills Network for Sustainable Forest-based Indigenous Crafts
Subtitle: A digital marketplace and skills hub connecting Philippine forest-based indigenous artisans to global opportunities.
Problem Statement: Philippine forest-based indigenous crafts face declining visibility and market access in the global economy. Many artisans, especially from indigenous and rural communities, struggle with limited digital literacy, poor connectivity, and lack of access to online marketplaces. These challenges result in low income, exploitation by middlemen, and the gradual loss of traditional skills and cultural heritage. Furthermore, buyers often lack assurance of product authenticity, sustainability, and fair trade practices. Without an inclusive digital platform, these crafts risk disappearing from both local and international markets.
Solution Overview:
eForestCrafts is a digital marketplace and capacity-building platform that connects Philippine forest-based indigenous artisans directly with local and global buyers. It addresses the issues of limited market access, lack of authenticity verification, and low digital literacy through an integrated, inclusive approach.

How the Solution Works
●	Online Marketplace – Showcases forest-based crafts (e.g., bamboo musical instruments, wood carving, natural fiber products) with artisan profiles, cultural narratives, and verified sustainability and authenticity claims.
●	Skills Development Module – Offers training on digital marketing, forest product processing, finishing techniques, and quality standards through videos, manuals, and webinars in both Filipino and local languages.
●	Verification & Labeling – Utilizes QR codes and blockchain-backed records to authenticate product origin, materials, and artisan identity, ensuring transparency and trust for buyers.
●	Community Engagement – Facilitates partnerships with local government units (LGUs), NGOs, and cooperatives to onboard artisans, support logistics, and maintain cultural integrity.

Methodologies and Technologies Used
●	E-commerce Platform – Mobile-responsive website and Android/iOS apps designed for low-bandwidth access.
●	Digital Storytelling – Multimedia profiles highlighting artisan heritage and cultural context.
●	Blockchain/QR Authentication – Secure tracking of product provenance and sustainability compliance.
●	AI-Assisted Tools – Automated translation, design mockups, and price suggestions for international markets.
●	Learning Management System (LMS) – For structured artisan training on craft enhancement and entrepreneurship.

Partnerships and Collaboration Models
●	DOST-FPRDI – Provides training on forest product processing, finishing, and quality standards; develops technical manuals and training videos; verifies sustainability and authenticity; and coordinates with LGUs, NGOs, and cooperatives.
●	Local Government Units & Cooperatives – Mobilize artisans, provide community spaces for training, and support logistics.
●	NGOs and Cultural Organizations – Assist in cultural preservation, fair trade compliance, and outreach to indigenous communities.
●	Tech Partners – Offer app development, blockchain integration, and hosting solutions.
●	Academic Institutions – Contribute research on sustainable materials, craft innovation, and market trends.
Solution Provider(s): Department of Trade and Industry (DTI) – One Town, One Product (OTOP) Program - supports MSMEs and local crafts industries through capacity building and market linkage - Public Sector, The National Commission on Indigenous Peoples - will provide policy guidance and legal oversight, and coordinate among cultural institutions and communities - Cultural Sector,  Department of Information and Communications Technology (DICT) - provides digital skills training, ICT infrastructure, and e-commerce support - Public/Tech Sector,  University of the Philippines Los Baños (UPLB) - expertise in forestry, rural development, and sustainable livelihoods - Academic/Research Sector
Duration to pilot in a new geography: 12 months
SDGs addressed: SDG 8 (Decent Work and Economic Growth);SDG 10 (Reduced Inequalities);SDG 12 (Responsible Consumption and Production);
Desired impact:
Solution Objectives
●	Empower indigenous and rural artisans in the Philippines by providing equitable access to global markets.
●	Preserve and promote forest-based crafts and cultural heritage through sustainable production.
●	Integrate digital technologies to enhance visibility, traceability, and competitiveness of indigenous products.
●	Foster inclusive economic growth while promoting sustainable forest resource management.

Key Achievements/Impacts (Targeted)
●	Employment Generation: Create or enhance livelihoods for at least 500 indigenous artisans within the first 2 years of operation.
●	Income Growth: Increase participating artisans’ average income by 30–50% through higher-value market access.
●	Market Reach: Facilitate 1,000+ verified product listings from indigenous communities on the platform during the pilot phase.
●	Environmental Sustainability: Ensure that 100% of listed crafts meet sustainability standards, reducing the use of non-renewable or illegal forest materials.
●	Cultural Preservation: Digitally document at least 50 traditional crafting techniques to safeguard indigenous knowledge for future generations.
●	Partnership Expansion: Establish 10+ active partnerships with local government units (LGUs), NGOs, cooperatives, and international fair trade networks.
Key technologies:
eForestCrafts integrates a combination of digital tools and emerging technologies to ensure accessibility, transparency, and global reach:
●	E-commerce Platform & Mobile Application – A user-friendly web and mobile interface tailored for low-bandwidth environments, enabling artisans to easily list products, manage inventory, and process orders.
●	Blockchain-based Traceability – Provides verifiable records of product origin, materials used, and artisan identity to assure buyers of authenticity and sustainability.
●	Digital Payment Systems – Secure and inclusive payment gateways that support multiple currencies and mobile wallets for both local and international transactions.
●	AI-powered Product Tagging & Translation – Automates product categorization, generates multilingual descriptions, and improves search visibility in global markets.
●	AR/VR Craft Experience – Immersive storytelling tools that allow customers to virtually “visit” workshops, view the crafting process, and appreciate cultural context.
●	Cloud-based Learning Management System (LMS) – Hosts training modules, videos, and technical manuals for artisan skill enhancement and quality assurance.
Unique Characteristics: eForestCrafts stands out by blending digital innovation with cultural preservation to create a truly inclusive, sustainable marketplace for forest-based indigenous crafts in the Philippines. Unlike generic e-commerce platforms, it integrates blockchain traceability to guarantee authenticity, ensuring artisans receive rightful recognition and fair compensation. Its immersive AR/VR storytelling showcases not just the product but the heritage and craftsmanship behind it, deepening buyer appreciation. The solution is co-created with Indigenous people and rural communities, with training and quality standards provided by expert partners to raise market readiness. Additionally, its inclusive business model prioritizes low-income and marginalized artisans by offering low listing fees, shared marketing resources, and mobile-friendly access for areas with limited connectivity. This combination of cultural integrity, technological transparency, and equitable market access makes eForestCrafts a unique bridge between tradition and the global digital economy.
Sustainable Change: eForestCrafts fosters long-term systemic change by digitally empowering Indigenous people and rural artisans to access global markets while preserving traditional forest-based craftsmanship. By integrating blockchain verification, the platform builds lasting consumer trust and deters cultural exploitation, ensuring artisans retain ownership of their heritage. Skills development and quality training enhance product competitiveness, enabling continuous market participation without dependency on intermediaries. As income streams stabilize, communities are incentivized to sustainably manage forest resources, linking economic prosperity with environmental stewardship. Over time, this creates a self-reinforcing cycle where cultural preservation, sustainable livelihoods, and forest conservation feed into each other, reducing poverty, strengthening cultural identity, and ensuring environmental protection for future generations.
Primary thematic focus area: MSME Empowerment & Local Digital Innovation
Summary: eForestCrafts is an idea-stage digital marketplace and skills hub aimed at connecting Philippine indigenous forest-based artisans to global buyers. It integrates e-commerce, blockchain traceability, and digital training to preserve cultural heritage and enhance artisans’ incomes. Its strength lies in the cultural preservation and sustainability emphasis, while its weakness is the very early stage of development, with no funding, pilots, or endorsements yet secured.

Title: EduConnect+ App
Subtitle: EduConnect+ is an all-in-one AI-powered educational learning assistant that blends real-time messaging for guided digital study and AI-powered homework support for vulnerable students in marginalized underserved communities.
Problem Statement: In Zimbabwe and across Africa, significant disparities persist between rural and urban students. Learners in rural, underserved areas face compounded challenges including limited access to digital devices, unreliable internet connectivity, and scarce academic support resources. These systemic barriers severely impact their academic performance and exam pass rates, deepening the educational divide and perpetuating long-term inequality in opportunities. Rural children in under resourced communities have limited opportunities for school homework support due to limited internet access and their parents, mostly less educated, do not comprehend the new education curriculum to adequately support students. The EduConnect+ App comes in to bridge this gap.
Solution Overview:
EduConnect+ is an AI powered Learning Assistant and chatbot designed to specially support underserved rural learners with limited access to quality school homework support. It is multilingual with text- and voice-based features for easy accessibility by young learners in under-resourced communities who have limited access to strong internet. 

Loaded with syllabus information for multiple subjects, this homework study buddy provides exam revision support, step-by-step homework guidance, chat and voice tips adjusted to student’s comprehension of information, knowledge and ideas. Parents in rural underserved communities don’t need to worry about their children’s homework, they just have to guide them as children get AI-powered assistance. 

The bot works via WhatsApp and SMS to allow accessibility with limited or low bandwidth internet to enhance digital inclusion. 

We partner with the Ministry of Education, NGOs and the private sector to deliver the chatbot to primary users in under-served, under-resourced local communities.
Solution Provider(s): Green for Sustainability Initiative Trust: This is a non-profit organization which promotes green growth, youth empowerment and sustainable development.
Duration to pilot in a new geography: 6 months (to build and deploy the solution)
SDGs addressed: SDG 4 (Quality Education);SDG 10 (Reduced Inequalities);
Desired impact:
(i) To expand equitable access to digital learning for young learners in rural and underserved communities
(ii) To strengthen academic support and engagement
(iii) To bridge the digital and educational gap between rural and urban students
Key technologies: Key technology used is AI.
Unique Characteristics: The solution uses text- and voice-based features to support students in underserved communities which have limited connectivity. It can be used via WhatsApp and text on any form of mobile devices and bridges the technology and digital divide between urban and rural students.
Sustainable Change:
Our solution immediately increases access to quality education and learning resources for students in underserved communities. It increases digital literacy among learners while providing access and opportunities to students with limited connectivity. 

Our solution narrows educational achievement gap between rural and urban students thereby fostering equity in access to quality education. It reduces systemic educational inequalities across Zimbabwe and Africa while enhancing a more inclusive and resilient digital education system.
Primary thematic focus area: Inclusive Digital Innovation Skills & Entrepreneurial Talent Development
Summary: EduConnect+ is an AI-powered educational assistant designed to support homework and exam preparation for underserved learners in rural Zimbabwe and Africa. It works via WhatsApp and SMS to overcome connectivity barriers, offering multilingual, text- and voice-based support. Strengths: clear focus on bridging rural-urban education divides, highly accessible through low-bandwidth channels, and strong alignment with SDG4 and SDG10. Weaknesses: still at idea stage with no prototype, limited technical details beyond 'AI', no evidence of pilot results, and no secured funding.

Ultimately, it builds dignity, opportunity, and trust while creating long-term resilience in developing economies, with potential for global replication.
Key technologies: Key technologies include: Artificial Intelligence (for personalized learning and data-driven insights), Mobile and Cloud-based Platforms (ensuring accessibility and scalability), and Blockchain-enabled tools (supporting transparency and sustainability reporting). These technologies are applied in a modular way, allowing the solution to be adapted and replicated in different contexts.
Unique Characteristics: What makes this solution unique is the integration of digital skills with sustainability expertise, circular economy innovation and accountability mechanisms. Unlike many initiatives focusing solely on training or entrepreneurship, our model links skills directly to livelihoods, transparency, and resilience. It addresses not only inclusion in the digital economy, but also crime prevention, gender-based violence reduction, and trust-building, creating a holistic and scalable pathway from local empowerment to global impact.
Sustainable Change:
Through training, networks and transparent reporting practices, immediate outputs include increased skills, new circular economy solutions and stronger partnerships. These lead to outcomes such as greater economic independence, reduced exclusion, crime and violence prevention, and improved trust in institutions. In the long term, the solution contributes to an inclusive digital economy, sustainable growth, resilient communities and fairer global systems. 

Solution contributes to systemic change by linking individual empowerment with institutional transformation and environmental sustainability. By equipping women, youth and MSMEs with digital skills, entrepreneurship tools and sustainability expertise, we address not only livelihoods but also social justice, human rights, and resilience. Title: Coding and Artificial Intelligence Skills for Youth
Subtitle: This solution focuses on equipping youth with coding and artificial intelligence skills  for their livelihoods.
Problem Statement: Kenya and Africa in general experience high levels of youth unemployment. This results to idleness, drug abuse, desperation and crime. The problem is made worse by the lack of resources for self employment and opportunities for the creation of sustainable livelihoods.
Solution Overview:
Description of the Solution
This solution proposes to provide youth with training to impart them with practical coding and artificial intelligence skills in an effort to provide them with a sustainable livelihood. This training will be offered online to avoid unnecessary travel and ensure the largest number possible of youth are involved in the programme. The training programme will be divided into three categories: beginner, intermediate and advanced and will be offered over a period of six months. The youth undertaking the programme will progress sequentially through the three stages. It is envisioned that at the end of the training the youth will be able to develop their own apps and artificial intelligence tools from which they can sustainable livelihoods through subscriptions, adverts and product sales. The apps and artificial intelligence tools will also aid the participants in finding solutions to local and international problems. 

Methodologies and Technologies Used
The training will be conducted online so as to capture as large a number as possible by eliminating the need for travel, the youth will partake of the training from respective diverse locations as long as they can access an internet enabled device (preferably a laptop) and a stable internet connection. the training will be facilitated through one of the many video conferencing tools available. The youth shall be charged a nominal fee in order to run the programme, but this will be an option of last resort only if adequate financing cannot be obtained to provide scholarships to the youth

Partnerships and Collaborations 
The solution will partner and collaborate with: youth, coding and artificial intelligence instructors, gadgets providers and if possible global leaders in internet based products.

Shem Mbandu, Senior Lecturer of Cyber Security and Dean, School of Computing and Mathematics, the Co-operative University of Kenya  PhD in Cyber Security, Master of Science in Information Systems, Bachelor of Education in Educational Technology, 3. Ezra Opande,  Qualifications: Software Engineering, ALX

The solution intends to achieve the following objectives:

2. To provide youth with skills to create a sustainable source of income.
3. To keep youth occupied with productive activities and away from drugs and crime.
4. To expose youth to the potential of coding and artificial intelligence in improving their lives. 
5. To increase the digital output of the African continent and contribute to the transformation of the world. 
6. To provide youth with the digital skills necessary to create apps and artificial intelligence tools to solve local and international problems. 

By the end of the first year, the solution intends to: 
1. recruit at least 200,000 youth into the programme
2. facilitate the development of atleast 100 world class apps and/or artificial intelligence product by youth enlisted in the programme
