Title: NumidAi, Helping constructors go green
Subtitle: NumidAI is an AI-powered platform that measures, analyzes, and optimizes the carbon footprint of construction projects. It helps architects, engineers, and developers design green buildings, select local eco-materials, and quantify how much CO₂ they can save through better energy use, insulation, and nature integration.
Problem Statement:
The construction sector generates 40% of global CO₂ emissions (The Carbon Trust, 2024).
In Algeria and MENA, we still don’t have enough tools to measure and track this impact.
what are Eco-friendly solutions that exist in the market, what it costs, or how to transition.
Solution Overview:
NumidAI is an AI-powered platform that helps construction professionals in the MENA region design low-carbon, climate-resilient buildings. It calculates and optimizes the carbon footprint of projects using life-cycle assessment and local data, offering tailored recommendations for eco-materials, passive design, energy efficiency, and water-saving solutions.

Focused on Algeria as a first market ; ranked 51st in the CCPI with medium emissions and low renewable energy use; NumidAI responds to critical regional challenges like heat, water scarcity, and fast urban growth.

A key value of the solution is its ability to combine climate adaptation with cultural identity, promoting sustainable practices that respect local architecture, privacy needs, and thermal comfort.

The platform follows a freemium business model ; offering core features for free to ensure accessibility, while advanced tools, analytics, and integrations are available through paid plans. It is open-source at its core, encouraging collaboration with local universities, developers, and green industries. After launching in Algeria, we plan to expand to Gulf countries, where emissions are highest and the need for practical decarbonization tools is urgent.
Solution Provider(s): The project is led by Fella Bouti and Ikram Bichbiche, developed under NumidAI, a subsidiary of EcoTashira LLC, a company specialized in sustainable construction materials and green design.  Key Partners:  Together for Blue and Green Organization – Algerian NGO promoting ecological transition and sustainable development. (Nonprofit / Environmental Sector)  OML MENA (One Million Leaders – Middle East and North Africa) – A regional program of the NELIS global network, supporting sustainability leadership and innovation across the MENA region. (Support Program / Education & SDGs)
Duration to pilot in a new geography: 3-6 MONTHS (by 2026)
SDGs addressed: SDG 9 (Industry, Innovation, and Infrastructure);SDG 11 (Sustainable Cities and Communities);SDG 13 (Climate Action);
Desired impact:
Objectives:

Reduce carbon footprint in the construction sector
Promote the use of green building materials and sustainable design practices
Protect natural resources and promote circular economy principles
Support climate adaptation in hot and water-scarce regions like MENA
Facilitate data-driven decisions for low-carbon, resilient urban development
Lead a green transition toward sustainable building 

Expected Impacts:

Up to 30% reduction in gaz emissions per building through better material choices and energy efficiency
Encourage the use of local, low-impact materials, reducing transport emissions and supporting local industries
Water savings through the promotion of economic irrigation systems and nature-based solutions
Job creation in green construction, design, and material innovation sectors
Raise awareness and build capacity among professionals on sustainable building standards
Key technologies:
Artificial Intelligence (AI): To calculate carbon footprint and suggest optimized green alternatives.

Life Cycle Assessment (LCA): To assess the environmental impact of materials and design choices.

Geolocation Data: To adapt recommendations to Algeria’s local climate and resource availability.
Unique Characteristics:
Our solution is unique because it focuses on adaptation to dry climates and natural resource availability by region. For example, we don’t propose construction with wood in MENA regions where wood is rare and needs to be protected. The same applies to irrigation systems, water use, and vegetation ; everything depends on local resources and climate constraints.
We promote nature-based solutions, efficient resource use, and affordable local materials, making our approach both sustainable and adapted to the realities of the region.
Sustainable Change:
Our solution aims to create sustainable, systemic change by involving more stakeholders in the green transition. We encourage professionals and decision-makers to adopt sustainable behaviors, invest in clean energy, and protect water and natural resources for future generations.

Only with promoting long-term construction practices ; that are well adapted to heatwaves and environmentally responsible, we can help shift the entire sector toward low-impact, climate-resilient models. The desired outcome is a mindset and market shift where sustainability becomes standard ; leading to greener cities, better living conditions, and stronger climate action across the region.
Funding Sources: The development of NumidAI is currently self-funded. We are using personal resources from our own incomes, and part of the investment comes from EcoTashira LLC, the parent company. This initial funding supports the first version of the platform and early-stage development.
Testimonials and Endorsements: We are currently in the creation and data collection phase, and the solution has not yet been tested in the field. Therefore, no testimonials or endorsements are available at this stage. However, we have received strong interest and informal support from professionals in architecture, construction, and sustainability sectors, who are ready to engage in the pilot phase once the platform is launched.
Further comments/feedback: We are still in the early stage of development, but we are fully committed to bringing this solution to life as soon as possible. The prototype is nearly ready, and we’re entering a critical phase where support and trust will make a real difference. We appreciate the opportunity to share our vision and welcome any feedback that could help us move forward effectively.
Primary thematic focus area: MSME Empowerment & Local Digital Innovation
Summary: NumidAI is an AI-powered platform concept designed to measure and optimize the carbon footprint of construction projects in Algeria and the MENA region. A strength is its clear focus on regional adaptation to dry climates and local materials, while a weakness is its idea-stage maturity with no pilot, quantified results, or endorsements yet.

Title: Token Afya: Wellness Rewards for a Healthier Workforce
Subtitle: Incentivizing healthy behavior through blockchain-based, non-speculative wellness tokens.
Problem Statement: In Kenya and similar regions, the private healthcare sector is fragmented and reactive, with minimal incentives for preventative care. High costs, low insurance penetration, and chronic disease burdens continue to rise due to a lack of sustained wellness engagement and aligned stakeholder collaboration.
Solution Overview:
Token Afya is a blockchain-based platform that rewards individuals for healthy behaviors — like gym visits, attending wellness workshops, or completing health check-ups — with non-speculative, non-exchangeable digital tokens. These tokens can be redeemed within a curated ecosystem including fitness centers, clinics, and community events.

Methodologies & Technologies:

Tokenization of wellness activities via smart contracts

Closed-loop, fiat-free ecosystem (non-tradable utility tokens)

Behavioral nudges through gamification and rewards

Partner validation & tracking through QR/NFC and activity logs

Partnerships & Collaboration Models:
Token Afya will be  co-developed with fitness centers, clinics, NGOs, and insurers. We establish joint pilots (e.g., 6-month rollouts) where partners track wellness participation, share engagement data, and collaborate on strategic CSR alignment. NGOs and insurers help plug ecosystem gaps in underrepresented communities.
Solution Provider(s): We have approached AAR insurance for a pilot agreement- still in discussions. Emory hospital, equity foundation  for its clinics network and The hale hospital.
Implementation timeline(s): Fureai Kippu- Elder care point system in the 1990s
Duration to pilot in a new geography: six months
SDGs addressed: SDG 3 (Good Health and Well-being);SDG 10 (Reduced Inequalities);SDG 9 (Industry, Innovation, and Infrastructure);
Desired impact:
Objectives:

Foster healthier behavior across underserved populations

Reduce future healthcare costs for insurers and providers

Create alternative income for wellness-oriented MSMEs

Key Achievements (Pilot Goals):

1,000+ tokenized wellness activities completed

20% increase in gym and clinic engagement

2x weekly member retention for participating fitness centers

Measurable savings in outpatient care costs via preventative routines
Key technologies:
Blockchain (non-tradable utility tokens for internal use only)

QR/NFC for attendance validation

Data dashboards for real-time engagement metrics

Mobile-accessible user interface (no app download required)
Unique Characteristics:
Closed-loop, non-speculative token design: no exchange or fiat cash-out, ensuring long-term behavioral focus rather than crypto speculation

Integrated wellness ecosystem: bridges private sector, insurers, clinics, and NGOs

Low-cost deployment: tech-light model avoids smartphone dependence or heavy onboarding

CSR-aligned design: enables NGOs to plug gaps through token sponsorships
Sustainable Change: Token Afya aligns incentives across the fragmented health sector by rewarding positive behavior before illness occurs. Over time, this creates a preventative culture, reduces insurance strain, increases access to wellness resources for low-income groups, and encourages employers and gyms to invest in health as a shared value. Through scalable local ecosystems, it transforms wellness into an economically sustainable habit, not a luxury.
Funding Sources: We are currently bootstrapping
Testimonials and Endorsements: we dont any endorsement yet.
Further comments/feedback: Well structured, easy to fill in even for a start up in its early stages.
Primary thematic focus area: Enabling Policies & Regulatory Innovation
Summary: Token Afya introduces a closed-loop blockchain rewards system to incentivize healthy behaviors, offering a fresh approach to preventative care. Its strength lies in its innovative non-speculative token model, but its weakness is the very early maturity stage with no pilot data, confirmed partners, or clear resource strategy.

Title: Inclusive Career AI: Empowering Careers Through AI Guidance
Subtitle: AI-powered platform offering personalized career guidance and skills training for youth, women, and underserved communities worldwide.
Problem Statement: Millions of youth, women, and marginalized individuals face barriers to accessing relevant career guidance, skills training, and job opportunities. Traditional counseling is often costly, inaccessible, or not tailored to individual needs, leaving many without clear career pathways. This digital divide perpetuates unemployment, underemployment, and economic inequality.
Solution Overview:
Inclusive Career AI is a multilingual platform designed to provide career guidance and skills development opportunities for youth, women, and underserved communities. By combining global and local labor market data with information users share about their skills, interests, and aspirations, it generates tailored career pathways and connects people with relevant learning resources.

The process is straightforward: users complete a short questionnaire through a mobile or web interface. Based on their responses and real-time labor market insights, the platform recommends suitable career options, identifies the skills needed to succeed in those roles, and suggests affordable or free training opportunities. Alongside this, it offers access to volunteer mentors so users can benefit from personalized advice and industry insights.

Technically, the solution draws on data analysis and natural language processing to understand and respond to users in multiple languages, while also offering low-bandwidth access through SMS and USSD for those with limited internet connectivity. To ensure real-world impact, the initiative works with educational institutions, NGOs, and employment agencies to deliver localized training and opportunities, and partners with private sector employers to open direct pathways to internships and jobs.
Solution Provider(s): Inclusive Career AI – Independent social innovation initiative focused on inclusive career guidance and digital skills development (Digital technology, education, workforce development), LinkedIn – Professional networking platform supporting mentorship connections and industry insights (Technology and professional networking), Coursera – Global online learning provider offering access to affordable skills training and certifications (Education technology), Iran Technical and Vocational Training Organization – National provider of vocational skills training and career development programs (Government / vocational training), UN Volunteers – Network of volunteers providing mentorship, coaching, and support (International development and volunteerism)
Implementation location(s): Not applicable – planned initial implementation in Tehran, Iran, with potential for global scale.
Duration to pilot in a new geography: 6–9 months – including localization of content, partnership building, user onboarding, and pilot evaluation.
SDGs addressed: SDG 4 (Quality Education);SDG 5 (Gender Equality);SDG 8 (Decent Work and Economic Growth);
Desired impact:
The primary objective of Inclusive Career AI is to make personalized career guidance and skills development accessible to youth, women, and underserved communities worldwide, regardless of their location, language, or economic background. The solution aims to reduce barriers to employment by connecting individuals with relevant job opportunities, affordable training, and mentorship networks.

In its initial pilot phase, the platform is expected to help at least 1,000 users identify viable career paths, close skill gaps, and connect with employment or entrepreneurship opportunities. Within three years of scaling, the goal is to reach over 100,000 users globally, enabling measurable improvements in employability and income levels for target groups. Beyond individual outcomes, the solution seeks to contribute to stronger local economies by supporting MSMEs with skilled talent and fostering more inclusive, diverse participation in the digital workforce.
Key technologies: The solution leverages artificial intelligence to analyze user profiles, assess skills, and match individuals with suitable career paths. Natural language processing enables multilingual interaction, making the platform accessible to users in diverse linguistic contexts. Labor market analytics are used to align recommendations with real-time job demand, ensuring relevance and impact. The platform is designed to function in both high- and low-connectivity environments, offering SMS and USSD access for users with limited internet availability.
Unique Characteristics: Inclusive Career AI stands out for its ability to deliver highly personalized career guidance at scale, tailored to the needs of underrepresented groups who are often excluded from traditional counseling and training programs. Unlike generic job-matching tools, it combines AI-driven recommendations with local labor market data, ensuring that advice is relevant to each user’s context. Its multilingual, low-bandwidth design allows full functionality through SMS and USSD, making it accessible even in regions with limited internet access. The integrated mentorship network connects users with real professionals, adding a human element that strengthens learning and career outcomes. Its open partnership approach—working with educational institutions, NGOs, government agencies, and employers—creates a collaborative ecosystem that amplifies reach and long-term sustainability.
Sustainable Change:
Inclusive Career AI contributes to sustainable, systemic change by addressing structural barriers to employment and skills development. By making personalized career guidance and affordable training accessible to underserved populations, it helps close the digital and opportunity divide. The solution empowers individuals to enter or re-enter the workforce with market-relevant skills, which in turn strengthens local economies and increases diversity in the labor market.

Over time, its integration with educational institutions, NGOs, and private sector employers creates a feedback loop: trained and empowered individuals fill critical skill gaps, employers gain access to more diverse talent, and local training providers adapt to evolving job market needs. This systemic approach ensures that the benefits persist beyond initial deployment, fostering inclusive economic growth, reducing inequalities, and building resilience in communities worldwide.
Testimonials and Endorsements: The solution has been self-funded during its concept and design phase. No external funding has been secured yet; however, we plan to seek support from international development agencies, impact investors, and public-private partnerships for the pilot and scale-up phases.
Further comments/feedback: Thank you for providing this opportunity to share innovative solutions that promote inclusive digital economies. The questionnaire was clear and well-structured, and it allowed me to present my solution effectively.
Primary thematic focus area: Inclusive Digital Innovation Skills & Entrepreneurial Talent Development
Summary: Inclusive Career AI proposes an AI-powered career guidance platform for underserved groups (Q13), with ambitions to scale globally from an initial pilot in Iran (Q16, Q18). Its strength lies in the inclusive and multilingual design leveraging low-bandwidth access and mentorship integration (Q13, Q23, Q24). A major weakness is that it remains at concept stage without pilots, secured funding, or concrete partnerships implemented (Q17, Q27).

Title: Rural IT Center
Subtitle: Helping farmer and other in rural area to access and learn about useful internet resources
Problem Statement: Many areas outside the main cities have minimal access to the internet and even less access to training on how to how to find and use useful resources on the internet that might assist them in farming and agriculture, ecotourism, banking and financial services, health resources, and other business and work opportunities.
Solution Overview: We want to offer training on accessing and using the internet in the rural center of Amedi.  There is a technical institute there that offers degrees in a range of subjects, including IT.  KURDS NGO would hold sessions with local people to find out what training would be of the most use to them, and then work with professionals at the technical institute to design the training.  The training would initially be delivered by both KURDS NGO and institute staff at the institute, at times that do not overlap with the degree programs, and adjusted based on student feedback. Ultimately it would be good to provide such centers across the governorate.
Solution Provider(s): . The technical institute in Amedi is a branch of Duhok Polytechnic University (DPU).  DPU is comprised of six technical institutes (of which Amedi is one) and five technical colleges.  The Technical Institute of Amedi consists of the departments of IT, Marketing Management, Disease Analysis and Animal Resources, Tourism Management, Statistics and Information, and Business Management.
Duration to pilot in a new geography: One year
SDGs addressed: SDG 8 (Decent Work and Economic Growth);SDG 11 (Sustainable Cities and Communities);SDG 15 (Life on Land);
Desired impact: This desired impact of this project is to improve knowledge about accessing and using resources on the internet to increase agricultural production and ecotourism, improve understanding of banking/finance and health resources, and to do these in environmentally sustainable and climate resilient ways.  This technological upgrading should help to create and diversify jobs, providing economic growth.  As this project is in rural areas it should also help to slow or stop the migration of people to urban centers.

Unique Characteristics: We plan on using existing resources in rural centers to provide the location for training new internet users.  We want to reach those who live within approximately 50 kilometers of the centers.  We will be working with rural populations in order to identify their technological and information needs, eg, farmers and those in the agricultural areas might want to learn smart farming technology or those involved in tourism might wish to access ecosystem restoration information in order to become ecotourist destinations.  Further, learning about new technologies and systems might also encourage new businesses to form in order to provide those technologies and/or systems.
Sustainable Change: We believe that training people in how to access internet resources will improve their practical skills and encourage people to use those resources to improve their incomes, create jobs, and improve community resilience, including environmental sustainability.  By embedding the training centers in existing facilities, the program should be sustainable and lasting.
Funding Sources: Not applicable
Testimonials and Endorsements: Not applicable

Further, rural areas along the border with Türkiye have faced frequent bombardment by the Turks in the last couple of decades.  With the new peace deal this year, this has now ceased, and there is an opportunity to improve the agricultural, tourism, and other sectors, and training in the new digital economy should be part of the new stage for these areas.

Title: MyCircle: Africa’s Next-Gen Platform for Group Wealth
Subtitle: MyCircle empowers African communities with smart group savings, instant payouts, and secure digital identity. All in one easy-to-use platform
Problem Statement: Millions of Africans, especially in rural areas, struggle with financial exclusion due to limited banking facilities, low access to digital payment tools, and lack of convenient, secure platforms for group savings and transactions. This leaves communities dependent on informal methods that are often inefficient, risky, and restrict their ability to grow wealth collectively.
Solution Overview:
MyCircle, is an all-in-one fintech platform designed to empower African communities with financial inclusion, secure digital identity, and simplified group savings. Users can create or join savings circles (stokvels), manage contributions, and access instant payouts directly through the platform. MyCircle leverages blockchain technology to ensure secure, transparent, and tamper-proof transaction records, while NFC-enabled devices, to provide seamless identity verification and payout authorization.

The platform combines mobile-friendly apps with offline-ready features to reach rural areas where traditional banking access is limited. Users can transact with minimal fees and small amounts, ensuring that even low-income members can participate. MyCircle also integrates automated savings tracking, goal setting, and notifications to encourage financial discipline and collective wealth growth.

While partnerships and collaborations are still in development, the platform is designed to integrate with banks, payment providers, and local community organizations to maximize reach, trust, and adoption.
Solution Provider(s): Currently, there are no active partners, however MyCircle plans to collaborate with banks, payment providers, and local community organizations in the future to expand reach and adoption.
Duration to pilot in a new geography: The estimated duration to pilot MyCircle in a new geography is 3–6 months. This includes onboarding users, testing platform functionality, training local communities, and gathering feedback for optimization before full-scale rollout.
SDGs addressed: SDG 1 (No Poverty);SDG 10 (Reduced Inequalities);SDG 8 (Decent Work and Economic Growth);
Desired impact:
> Promote financial inclusion across underserved and rural African communities.

> Simplify group savings and payouts through secure, digital platforms.

> Empower communities to grow collective wealth and improve economic resilience.

> Introduce reliable digital identity verification for secure financial transactions.

Key Achievements / Impacts (Projected):

> Financial Inclusion: Reach over 500,000 users within the first 12 months in pilot regions.

> Savings Growth: Enable communities to collectively save millions of rands annually.

> Employment & Entrepreneurship: Support informal traders and small businesses by providing digital payment solutions.

> Reduced Inequality: Expand access to financial services in rural areas lacking banking infrastructure.

> Digital Adoption: Promote adoption of secure fintech tools, enhancing trust and transparency in community savings.
Key technologies:
1) Blockchain: Ensures secure, transparent, and tamper-proof transaction records for group savings and payouts.

2) NFC (Near Field Communication): Enables identity verification and payout authorization via rings, bracelets, or dongles.

3) Mobile & Web Platforms: User-friendly apps for savings management, goal tracking, and instant transactions.

4) Offline-Ready Features: Allows users in rural areas with limited connectivity to access and record transactions.

Title: Kijiji Soko
Subtitle: Mobile-first marketplace and impact dashboard for women-led MSMEs producing sustainable goods in rural Africa.
Problem Statement: Many small, women-led MSMEs in rural Africa face multiple structural barriers: they lack digital visibility, struggle to access funding, and are often excluded from global value chains despite producing sustainable, high-quality products. Without tools to validate environmental or social impact, they cannot build trust with buyers or donors. Most available platforms are too complex, costly, or reliant on high connectivity, leaving them digitally marginalized.
Solution Overview:
Local Market Link & TrustBox is a mobile-first solution that empowers sustainable MSMEs, especially women-led enterprises, by combining access to markets, trust-building, and ESG data tools into a single user-friendly platform.

Key features:

- Mobile digital marketplace for direct product sales (B2C), designed for low-data environments.

- Integration with mobile money, local logistics, and micro-grant opportunities.

- TrustBox module – a micro-dashboard for each verified “Sustainable Seller”, including:

                 - Number of verified sustainable product sales

                 - Estimated CO₂ or water savings (via simplified calculators)

                 - Social impact badges (e.g., employs youth, people with disabilities, women)

                 - Auto-generated QR code for each profile and product, linking to transparent SDG-aligned information

                 - Anonymized ESG and SDG impact data available to donors and buyers

Technologies used:

- Low-data mobile interface

- Google Firebase or open-source backend

- TrustBox QR dashboards

- Optional blockchain signature for verified origin

- Carbon & water footprint calculators (simple, product-linked)

Implementation model:

- Piloted in Nairobi, Kenya with 10 women-led MSMEs

- Support by local NGOs, digital inclusion programs, and fintech partners

- Design for replicability in other African regions (e.g., Uganda, Ghana)
Solution Provider(s): GrantHub s.r.o. (digital platform design, funding strategy), Local logistics & fintech partners – onboarding & operational infrastructure (TBC),  regional innovation hub in Kenya, local women’s cooperatives and chambers of commerce (implementation and outreach)
Duration to pilot in a new geography: 6-9 months depending on local partnership readiness and device/internet accessibility
SDGs addressed: SDG 8 (Decent Work and Economic Growth);SDG 9 (Industry, Innovation, and Infrastructure);SDG 12 (Responsible Consumption and Production);
Desired impact:
Solution Objectives:

- Empower small, sustainable MSMEs, especially women-led businesses in rural and underserved regions, to participate in digital markets and global value chains.

- Enable verified, trust-based visibility of environmental and social impact through an easy-to-use mobile dashboard ("TrustBox").

- Create a reliable data layer that connects local producers with global ESG and SDG reporting frameworks, supporting transparency and donor confidence.

Key Impacts and Expected Results (Pilot + 2-Year Horizon):

 Economic Empowerment:
– At least 100 MSMEs onboarded within the first 2 years
– ≥30% increase in average revenue for participating MSMEs within 6 months of onboarding
– 60% of users reporting improved access to funding or new buyers after gaining "Sustainable Seller" status

Environmental Data Generation:
– Over 10,000 data points aggregated on CO₂ and water footprint of local products
– Real-time dashboards providing estimated environmental impact of individual MSMEs

Social Impact:
– Inclusion of at least 150 women and 30 youth across pilot and scale-up phase
– Tracking of employment generation with badges for inclusive hiring (e.g., number of women, people with disabilities employed)

Trust & SDG Reporting:
– 80+ “TrustBox” dashboards created with anonymized and verifiable data for donors and buyers
– ESG metrics aligned with SDG 8, 9, and 12, improving reporting capabilities for local actors and enabling evidence-based funding

Systemic Replicability:
– Fully documented and localized pilot in Kisumu County, Kenya
– Scalable toolkit for replication in at least 2 new African regions by 2027, tailored for low-data, low-literacy settings

This solution bridges the gap between digital access, market opportunity, and ESG readiness, turning local sustainable production into a global development asset.
Key technologies:
1. Mobile-First Progressive Web App (PWA)

- Lightweight application accessible via browser or home-screen shortcut

- Optimized for low-end Android devices and low-bandwidth settings

- Icon- and voice-assisted interface in local languages

- Offline functionality with sync-on-connection logic


2. Firebase or Supabase Backend (Open-Source Option)

- Cloud-based backend for managing user data, transactions, TrustBox analytics

- Real-time sync of product data and dashboard metrics

- Role-based access control for sellers, admins, and verifiers

- Backup and export capabilities for anonymized ESG datasets


3. TrustBox Micro-Dashboard Generator

- Automatic dashboard creation for each MSME

- Embedded calculators for estimated CO₂ and water footprints based on product type

- Badge-based social impact recognition (e.g., number of women/youth employed)

- Dashboard shareable via link or printable summary


4. QR Code–Based Product Passports

- Unique QR codes linked to each verified sustainable product

- Displays seller profile, TrustBox data, product origin, and materials

- Supports tagging for carbon and social impact attributes


5. Integration APIs for Mobile Payments & Logistics

- API connectors for local fintechs (e.g., M-Pesa)

- Plug-ins for logistics providers and e-commerce marketplaces

- Modular structure allows future connections with grant/funding databases


6. Optional Blockchain Signature Layer

- Hashes ESG declarations and product metadata onto public blockchain

- Generates immutable transaction logs for selected high-value products or buyers

- Smart-contract ready structure for future incentive schemes
Unique Characteristics:
Combines commerce + impact verification + funding visibility in one accessible interface

Works in low-connectivity, low-literacy settings

Built on a “trust by design” principle for local sellers

Incentivizes local-to-global commerce while generating SDG-aligned data

Easy to scale, plug-and-play for other regions with existing MSME networks
Sustainable Change:
The project creates a scalable and replicable system to empower sustainable MSMEs through verified digital presence, market access, and impact visibility. It enables long-term systemic inclusion of marginalized producers by providing:

- A trust layer for buyers, donors, and regulators

- A data layer for ESG and SDG reporting

- A market layer for direct income generation
Together, these layers strengthen local economies, improve funding readiness, and promote sustainable consumption and production at the grassroots level.
Funding Sources:
This solution is in the early concept phase and has not yet received external funding. It has been developed pro bono by the core team of GrantHub s.r.o. (Czech Republic) and local collaborators under the emerging Impact Lab Africa initiative.

We are currently preparing a proposal to establish an Impact Lab in Nairobi (Kenya),  a community-based centre for training, mentorship, and entrepreneurial support, focused particularly on women and youth. The Lab will provide digital tools, access to markets, and funding guidance to help local innovators become financially self-reliant and develop sustainable micro-businesses.

In this context, we are also exploring the creation of a registered NGO in Kenya, which would coordinate local operations, build partnerships, and expand the model to other underserved regions through structured pilot phases.

To realise this vision, we are actively seeking seed funding from international donors through initiatives such as the Global Digital Compact, digital inclusion accelerators, or climate-resilient MSME support programmes.
Testimonials and Endorsements: not applicable
Further comments/feedback: This questionnaire is comprehensive and encourages systemic thinking. We appreciate the opportunity to contribute a grassroots concept with the potential to scale across multiple low-resource communities. One suggestion: include a section to upload visuals (e.g. concept sketch or interface mock-up), which may help communicate early-stage solutions more effectively.
Primary thematic focus area: MSME Empowerment & Local Digital Innovation
Summary: Kijiji Soko proposes a low‑data digital marketplace with a ‘TrustBox’ profile for rural MSMEs. It addresses a real access gap, but it is early-stage with no funding, limited partners, and qualitative impact framing.

Title: Silver Passport: Voice-First AI for Preserving Ancestral Knowledge
Subtitle: An offline-ready, AI-powered storytelling platform that safeguards oral traditions and life stories of elders.
Problem Statement: Aging and Indigenous communities face the loss of ancestral knowledge due to globalization, language erosion, and the absence of culturally-sensitive digital tools. Over 67% of elders feel their life stories are unheard (UNFPA, 2022).
Solution Overview:
Silver Passport is a voice-first, AI-powered platform that enables elders to narrate, preserve, and share life stories and community knowledge. Inspired by NASA’s Golden Record, it functions like a “Shazam for life stories,” converting oral narratives into structured, searchable digital legacies.

AI-driven memory prompts

Emotional indexing

Voice recognition and offline functionality

Consent-first data management and co-ownership features

Community-led story co-creation with cultural centers and caregivers

Collaboration with NASA Space Apps Collective, International Center for Journalists, and French Alliance Chiclayo.

Preserve oral heritage and ancestral knowledge at risk of extinction

Empower elders with voice and agency in the digital economy

Promote intergenerational connectivity through storytelling
500+ stories recorded in pilot phase

Engagement of 150–250 elders per geography

Integration with 5–10 elder care institutions

Potential 70% satisfaction and retention rate post-pilot
Key technologies:
Artificial Intelligence (AI)

Natural Language Processing (NLP)

Voice-first Interface

Offline Mobile Access

Consent-first data architecture

AI-driven prompts tailored to cultural memory

Co-ownership and royalty-sharing model for content

Offline functionality for digital inclusion in rural areas

Elevating local voices in policymaking, culture, and digital archives

Strengthening intergenerational ties and educational systems

Catalyzing new markets for cultural storytelling and ethical AI

Supporting governments in meeting digital inclusion and cultural preservation targets

Name of your organization: NGO ASFEM (Association for the Upliftment of Malian Women)
Title: DigiMentora Mali: Cross-Mentoring Network for Women's Digital Empowerment
Subtitle: Connecting Malian Women Leaders with Francophone African Digital Experts through Adaptive Platforms to Transform Local Value Chains
Problem Statement: In Mali, women entrepreneurs face significant barriers that greatly limit their access to and participation in the digital economy. The adult literacy rate among Malian women remains low, estimated at around 22 to 26% according to various recent sources, and is significantly lower than that of men, which creates a primary obstacle to their digital inclusion. This gap is even more pronounced in rural areas, where access to education and training is limited, notably due to socio-economic and cultural factors and educational priorities that often disadvantage girls. In addition, internet access is restricted; fewer than 5% of women use the internet regularly, reflecting a critical lack of infrastructure, suitable tools, and digital skills. These digital disparities are accompanied by the strong predominance of women in agriculture, where they constitute about 58% of the workforce. Yet women remain confined to informal activities related to artisanal processing of agricultural products such as shea butter and tomatoes, which are generally characterized by low added value, little recognition in formal markets, and limited economic margins. This economic marginalization is worsened by the absence of structured mentoring networks and skills transfer systems adapted to local realities. The lack of these mechanisms impedes the development of the technical and entrepreneurial know-how essential to modernize these traditional value chains and effectively integrate emerging digital markets. This context thus calls for innovative solutions that combine training, mentorship support, multilingual digital inclusion, and cultural adaptation to open new economic opportunities for rural Malian women.
Solution Overview:
- Detailed Description of Operation
DigiMentora Mali will create a hybrid mentoring ecosystem connecting 200 Malian women entrepreneurs specializing in the shea sector in Kolondièba and the tomato sector in Kita with 50 digital experts from Francophone Africa. This program is based on an adaptive multilingual digital platform offering French, Bambara, and Soninké languages, optimized for use on mobile devices with low connectivity. It includes virtual cross-mentoring sessions held every two weeks through interactive videoconferences, designed to encourage direct and dynamic exchanges between mentors and mentees. Additionally, regional peer support groups will be formed, grouping participants according to their geographic areas and specific sectors, to strengthen local mutual support. Finally, the program will integrate comprehensive training modules covering digital leadership, soft skills development, e-commerce techniques, as well as local product processing, aimed at enhancing the entrepreneurial and digital capacities of the participants.
- Methodologies Employed
The methodologies will rely on a peer mentoring approach, promoting exchange and collaborative learning through "learning circles." The program also adopts a cascading training model by preparing local multipliers who relay knowledge within their communities. Mobile learning (m-learning) is central to the approach, with content specifically adapted to low-connectivity contexts to ensure inclusive and flexible access. Furthermore, continuous evaluation will be implemented using digital performance indicators, allowing real-time tracking of participants’ progress and adjustments of support according to identified needs.
- Partnerships and Collaboration Models
Partnerships and collaboration models will be structured around a strategic partnership with Mali Shi, which provides recognized technical expertise in the shea sector. The project will work closely with local cooperatives such as COOPROKASI in Siby and COPROKAZAN, which play a key role in providing field support to women entrepreneurs. An alliance will also be established with Orange Mali and the United Nations Development Programme (UNDP) Mali, providing the digital infrastructure necessary for the effective implementation of digital tools. Moreover, the network of mentors consists of female experts from communities including Women Tech Mali, FEMNET, and iCodeVillage, ensuring technical support and quality guidance tailored to Francophone African realities.
- Implementation by Zones
The project implementation will be targeted in two distinct zones. In Kolondièba, 100 women will benefit from in-depth training focused on shea processing, including mastering techniques required for organic certification and developing e-commerce skills for marketing derived cosmetic products. Meanwhile, in Kita, a separate group of 100 women will be trained in tomato processing into paste or powder, proper packaging techniques, and online sales strategies, aiming to optimize their access to digital markets and add value to their local products.
Solution Provider(s): The ASFEM is a Malian civil society organization dedicated to the economic empowerment of rural women. It primarily focuses on strengthening women’s capacities in agricultural and digital entrepreneurship by providing tailored training, technical support, and facilitating their access to local and digital markets. ASFEM plays a key role in community mobilization and the development of support networks for women, thus contributing to their economic and social inclusion.  Key partners involved in this project include:  Mali Folkecenter, an NGO specializing in sustainable development;  Orange Mali, a telecommunications company providing digital infrastructure;  Cooperative of Shea Butter Producers of Zantiébougou (COPROKAZAN), known for its fair-trade practices in the shea industry;  Women Tech Mali, a network of women digital experts offering technical support and advocacy in the digital sector;  FEMNET, a pan-African feminist network supporting women's rights and digital inclusion.
Implementation location(s): Kolondièba, Bougouni region, Mali  Kita, Kita region, Mali  Bamako (headquarters and coordination), Mali
Implementation timeline(s): Pilot phase: January 2026 – December 2027 (24 months)  Expansion phase: January 2028 – December 2030
Duration to pilot in a new geography: 18 months (6 months of preparation and cultural adaptation, 12 months of full implementation)
SDGs addressed: SDG 5 (Gender Equality);SDG 8 (Decent Work and Economic Growth);SDG 10 (Reduced Inequalities);
Desired impact:
- Solution Objectives:
Economically empower 200 women entrepreneurs through digital technology
Create 400 direct and indirect jobs in the shea and tomato value chains
Increase participants’ income by an average of 150%
Establish 50 formalized women-led businesses
- Key Quantifiable Achievements:
Income: Average increase from 35,000 to 80,000 FCFA/month per participant
Production: 1,600 tons of nuts processed annually (shea), 500 tons of tomatoes processed annually
Employment: 400 new jobs created (75% for young women)
Training: 200 women certified in digital skills, 50 mentors trained
Environmental impact: 30% reduction in post-harvest losses due to improved processing
Formalization: 50 new officially registered enterprises
Key technologies:
The solution will rely on an adaptive technological ecosystem integrating:

- Communication Technologies
Responsive web platform optimized for 2G/3G mobile networks
Progressive Web App (PWA) mobile application functioning offline
Videoconferencing system adapted to low bandwidth
Automated SMS and multilingual push notifications
- Training Technologies
Learning Management System (LMS) tailored to African contexts
Augmented reality for technical training on product processing
Interactive e-learning modules with video/audio support
Digital badge system and blockchain certification
- E-commerce Technologies
Integrated marketplace platform with mobile money payment
Inventory management and product traceability tools
Customer Relationship Management (CRM) system
Analytics and business intelligence tools for performance monitoring
Unique Characteristics:
- Innovative Partnership Model
The innovative partnership model will be based on creating the first cross-border mentoring network in Francophone Africa, specifically dedicated to the empowerment of rural women. This model will adopt a unique hybrid approach that combines international expertise in digital technologies and leadership with traditional knowledge and local practices. Furthermore, the technological platform will integrate national languages such as Bambara and Soninké, ensuring optimal cultural and linguistic accessibility for all participants, regardless of their rural or urban context. This integration will promote genuine digital inclusion and strengthen community ownership of the tools and content.

- Sustainable Financing Model
The sustainable financing model will rely on a progressive subscription system implemented after the training phase, requiring a contribution equivalent to 1% of the revenue generated by the participants. In addition, the project will collect commissions on sales made via the integrated marketplace, ranging from 3% to 5%, thereby ensuring a lasting revenue source for the maintenance and development of the platform. Moreover, strong partnerships will be established with local microfinance institutions that will offer loans tailored to the specific needs of rural women entrepreneurs, facilitating access to financing and stimulating the growth of their economic activities.

- Technological Innovation
DigiMentora Mali’s technological innovation will notably rely on a multilingual conversational artificial intelligence available 24/7, providing personalized and accessible user support to facilitate continuous guidance for participants. Blockchain technology will be used to ensure transparent and tamper-proof traceability of products, especially those certified organic and fair-trade, guaranteeing integrity and trust throughout the supply chain—from producer to end consumer. The project will also integrate IoT (Internet of Things) devices for real-time monitoring and tracking of quality parameters related to product processing, such as temperature and humidity, thereby ensuring compliance with standards. Finally, machine learning will be employed to optimize the matching process between mentors and mentees, taking into account their profiles, needs, and preferences to maximize the relevance and effectiveness of the mentorship.

- Culturally Adapted Approach
The project's approach will be carefully adapted to the cultural context of rural Malian women. It will take into account agricultural calendars to respect critical periods of sowing, cultivation, and harvesting, thus avoiding conflicts with participants’ professional activities. Likewise, family obligations—including household management and caregiving—will be integrated into the planning of training and activities to ensure optimal participation. The project will also be founded on the inclusion of traditional chiefs and community leaders, recognized authority figures, to encourage local buy-in and facilitate acceptance of the program within communities. Finally, trainings and support will be delivered through already existing solidarity groups such as networks, savings groups ("tontines"), and cooperatives, providing a natural framework of trust and mutual aid conducive to collective learning and sustainability of actions.
Sustainable Change:
- Theory of Change
DigiMentora Mali’s contribution to sustainable systemic change will be based on a multi-level theory of change. At the individual level, participating women will develop digital, entrepreneurial, and leadership skills that will increase their economic autonomy as well as their decision-making power within their households and communities. At the community level, the formalization of economic activities and the creation of local jobs will strengthen social cohesion and help reduce rural exodus, especially among young women. At the sectoral level, the modernization of the shea and tomato value chains through digital integration will generate a beneficial ripple effect on other agricultural sectors, broadly stimulating innovation and technology adoption. Finally, at the institutional level, the model’s success will positively influence public policies supporting digital inclusion and the empowerment of rural women, inspiring the implementation of similar programs in the sub-region, with an amplified impact on the socio-economic development of rural Mali and the improvement of women’s living conditions.

- Long-Term Multiplier Effects
The long-term multiplier effects of DigiMentora Mali will manifest through several key dynamics. First, knowledge transfer will become a virtuous cycle, as women participating in the program progressively become mentors themselves, thereby sustainably strengthening human capital and mutual support within communities. Second, the project will foster the emergence of a local innovation ecosystem, notably through the creation of women-led startups in the Malian agritech sector, leveraging digital technologies to modernize agricultural and commercial practices. Third, the program will induce profound normative change, positively shifting social perceptions regarding the role and place of women in the digital economy, contributing to improved gender equality. Finally, the success and robustness of the model will allow its gradual geographic replication, first to other regions of Mali, then to neighboring Sahelian countries, thus extending its impact on a regional scale and reinforcing the economic resilience of rural women across the Sahel.

Title: Osusu: Digital Layaway Platform Making Food Affordable & Accessible
Subtitle: Affordable layaway food bundles helping low-income workers and SMEs beat inflation, improve purchasing power, and secure essential food through digital fintech solutions.
Problem Statement: Soaring food inflation has eroded household purchasing power in Nigeria and across Africa. Many families must choose between food and other critical expenses, while traditional informal systems (like “ajo”) no longer guarantee value security. Over 50% of income now goes to food, and price volatility leaves millions vulnerable to hunger and financial stress.
Solution Overview:
How it works:
Osusu is a digital layaway and food-commerce platform that lets users lock in today’s prices and pay in installments for essential food bundles. Payments are made seamlessly through mobile wallets, agents, or payroll deductions (for SMEs), with redemption at partnered wholesalers and retailers.

Methodologies & Technologies:

Fintech APIs for payments and embedded wallets (PalmPay, OPay, Paystack).

E-commerce engine for food bundling, inventory, and pricing.

AI-driven demand forecasting and pricing intelligence.

Agent network across communities for last-mile access.

Partnerships & Collaboration:

FCMGs (Nestlé, Unilever, Dangote) for bundled food supply.

Logistics leaders (GIG Logistics, Kwik, Fez) for distribution.

Financial partners (Paystack, Habari, fintech wallets) for payments integration.

SMEs & corporates to onboard employees into Osusu Enterprise.

This inclusive model improves financial resilience, reduces hunger risk, and builds predictable demand pipelines for suppliers.
Solution Provider(s): 15. Solution Provider(s)  Osusu (PacknPay Technologies Ltd) – fintech & food-commerce startup, Nigeria.  Nestlé Nigeria Plc, Unilever Nigeria Plc, Dangote Foods Ltd – FMCG supply partners.  GIG Logistics, Kwik, Fez Logistics – logistics/distribution partners.  Paystack Habari – fintech/payment integration partners.  SMEs & HR Platforms  – corporate onboarding of employees.
Duration to pilot in a new geography: 90days
SDGs addressed: SDG 1 (No Poverty);SDG 2 (Zero Hunger);SDG 8 (Decent Work and Economic Growth);
Desired impact:
Protect purchasing power by letting households lock today’s food prices and pay in small installments.

Increase access & inclusion via agent-led onboarding for underbanked users and simple wallet/USSD payments.

Stabilize last-mile supply through bundled procurement with FMCGs and logistics partners.

Enable employer welfare via Osusu Enterprise (“pay-small-small” staff plans).
Key technologies:
Core stack: React (web), Flutter (mobile), Node.js/Express (APIs), PostgreSQL & MongoDB (data).

Cloud & DevOps: Docker containers on DigitalOcean, CI/CD pipelines, role-based access.

Payments & KYC: Integrations with Flutterwave, Paystack, Mono (mandates, account linking).

Messaging: Termii/Twilio for SMS alerts and payment reminders (offline-friendly).
Unique Characteristics:
Price-lock innovation: Users lock today’s prices on essentials and pay over time—directly addressing inflation volatility.

Dual-rail distribution: Agents + embedded wallets/USSD ensure reach across low-connectivity and underbanked segments.

Enterprise channel: “Paysmallsmall for Companies” lets employers offer staff food bundles as a welfare benefit—solving household stress without salary increases.

Supply-side resilience: FMCG partnerships and pooled procurement reduce stockouts and improve unit economics.
Sustainable Change:
Inputs:
Osusu platform (apps/APIs), agent network, FMCG & logistics partners, wallet/USSD rails, employer programs.

Activities:
Bundle curation & price-lock, agent onboarding, user enrollment (consumer & employer), installment collection, consolidated fulfillment, SMS reminders, data-driven procurement.

Outputs (12–24 months):

Thousands of completed food plans; higher repeat rates.

Expanded agent livelihoods; employer cohorts onboarded.

Stable offtake for FMCGs; fewer stockouts for retailers.

Outcomes (2–5 years):

Improved household food security and budgeting discipline; reduced reliance on predatory loans.

Financial inclusion for underbanked users via digital payment histories and mandates.

Resilient local supply chains through aggregated demand and predictable fulfillment.

Employer productivity gains via lower financial stress.

Long-term Impact (systemic):

A scalable, interest-free alternative to consumer debt that shields purchasing power from inflation.

Formalization of the informal economy with auditable transaction data—enabling future access to credit on fairer terms.

Replicable model across Africa & diaspora (wallets/remittances), aligning with SDG 2 (Zero Hunger), SDG 8 (Decent Work), SDG 9 (Industry/Innovation), SDG 10 (Reduced Inequalities).
Funding Sources: Founders’ capital & sweat equity (2024–2025): Product build, early pilots and market launch, agent onboarding.
Further comments/feedback: We welcome the programme’s focus on inclusive digital economies. Osusu directly advances SDG 2, 8, 9, and 10 by protecting food purchasing power, formalizing informal commerce, and enabling agent livelihoods.
